summary: Collagen is a protein constituting about 30% of the body’s protein, providing structural support to skin, tendons and bones. The body makes collagen from the amino acids glycine and proline plus vitamin C, zinc and copper. About 28 collagen types exist; the most common are I, II, III, IV and V. Collagen supplements are extracted from animal sources (marine, bovine, porcine, chicken) and provide mainly types I, II and III. Hydrolysed collagen is considered most effective for absorption. Reported benefits include skin hydration and firmness, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, increased bone density in postmenopausal women, reduced joint pain and muscle repair support; limited mouse data suggest possible hair growth. Safe dosages studied are 2.5 g/day for skin and joint health, 5 g/day for bone density, 15 g/day with resistance training for muscle mass, and up to 40 mg/day for joint health. Manufacturers advise a minimum 12‑week trial. Collagen synthesis can be supported by a diet rich in protein, vitamin C foods and bone broth.

XYZprinting invites customers to booth #2142 at the Fort Worth Convention Center (April 24‑28 2018) to see the MfgPro220 xPF printer, $19,950 with a 16‑liter build volume, double competition. The printer uses software and sensors for diagnostics and cloud control. It uses learning for slicing geometries. XYZprinting announced a partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D: BEGO will exclusively market a Nexa3D dental printer made by XYZprinting, and Nexa3D will develop the technology. XYZprinting has invested in Nexa3D and will sell its printers. The printer uses LSPc technology and a structured‑light matrix achieving up to 1Z cm/min, cutting cycles from hours to minutes. XYZprinting is backed by New Kinpo Group, a $36 billion conglomerate with 8,500 engineers. Nexa3D makes ultrafast stereolithography printers using LSPc.

Sensient Technologies (SXT) reported $0.80 EPS, beating $0.78 consensus by $0.02; net margin 9.13%, ROE 16.73%. Market cap $3.48B, PE 27.90, beta 0.92; 12‑month range $54.49‑$83.38; 50‑day MA $77.45, 200‑day MA $75.83. Quarterly dividend $0.30 (annualized $1.20, yield 1.53%) payable March 1, ex‑dividend Feb 3. DPR 42.70%. KeyCorp raised price target to $84 (overweight); Zacks upgraded from sell to hold. Sensient makes colors, flavors and fragrances for food, beverage, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and specialty chemicals.

This lecture introduces MIT's Discrete Stochastic Processes course. The professor emphasizes that the primary challenge in probability theory is not solving well-posed problems but finding appropriate models for real-world situations involving uncertainty, such as business, economics, and biology. He uses games of chance as examples because they are repeatable, allowing intuitive probability understanding. The lecture notes that models are imperfect but necessary—using a simple model is preferable to using no model, though one should remain aware of a model's limitations. The professor cautions that even mathematically sophisticated PhDs have caused financial disasters by applying sound probability theory to flawed models.

The lecture then covers discrete stochastic processes, which are probability models where sample points represent sequences of random variables in time. Key processes to be studied include counting processes, Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov chains, and martingales. The course applies these to communication systems, networks, computer systems, queuing theory, risk management, and catastrophe management.

Probability models consist of three components: a sample space, a collection of events (subsets of the sample space), and probability measures. Kolmogorov's axioms (1933) provide the mathematical foundation: probabilities are non-negative, the sample space has probability 1, and the probability of a countable union of disjoint events equals the sum of their individual probabilities. Events must satisfy closure properties under countable unions and complements, with the empty set included as an event.

Independent events are defined by the condition that the probability of their intersection equals the product of their individual probabilities. When combining probability models, the combined sample space is the Cartesian product of individual spaces, allowing independent experiments to be modeled together.

Random variables are functions from the sample space to real numbers, where the set of sample points mapping to values less than or equal to any given real number must be an event. This condition ensures probabilities can be assigned. Random variables are characterized by distribution functions, which are non-decreasing from 0 to 1, and may have probability mass functions (discrete case) or probability density functions (continuous case). The lecture concludes with a theoretical discussion emphasizing the importance of understanding axioms and learning to prove results in probability theory.

A new Weather Channel app uses IBM mesh networking technology to send messages directly between phones during emergencies when mobile networks fail. The app uses Bluetooth and Wi-Fi to relay messages across 200-500 feet between devices without overloading networks or draining battery. IBM uses digital signatures for security. The app, launched in Asia, Latin America and Africa, is 3.2MB and works on 2G networks. Challenges include achieving critical mass of users with the app installed.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Q1 2016 Form 10‑Q, reporting total revenues of $1.15 billion (automotive $1.03 billion, services and other $121 million), a 22% gross margin, and a net loss of $282.3 million ($2.13 per diluted share). As of March 31 2016, total assets were $9.19 billion, total liabilities $8.18 billion, and cash and cash equivalents $1.44 billion. The company continues to invest in Model X production ramp, Model 3 development, the Gigafactory, and expansion of its retail and Supercharger network, targeting 500,000‑vehicle production capacity by 2018.

The bill would donate 20,000 acres of public land for each Senator and Representative in the current Congress, plus an additional 20,000 acres for each Representative to which a State is entitled under the 1860 census. Based on current membership, the donation would total about 6,060,000 acres, valued at $7,575,000 at the minimum price of $1.25 per acre. The stated purpose is to endow at least one college per State that emphasizes agriculture and the mechanic arts while allowing other scientific or classical studies. States must establish such a college within five years or lose the grant and reimburse the United States for any land already sold. States without public lands within their borders would receive land scrip equal to their share, which they must sell and apply only to the prescribed purposes. An estimated 580,000 acres will be taken directly, leaving 5,480,000 acres to be supplied by scrip. All grants are conditioned on States replacing any loss of the fund.

The President objects to the bill on six grounds. First, the Treasury would lose most of the projected $5,000,000 annual revenue from land sales because the market would be flooded with scrip, driving prices well below $1.25. Second, the donation blurs the distinction between Federal and State authority, encouraging States to depend on Federal funds and eroding fiscal responsibility. Third, the low price of scrip would tempt speculators to acquire the best public lands, raising costs for actual settlers and harming new States. Fourth, the Federal Government has no constitutional power to enforce the intended use of the money, so the fund could be diverted. Fifth, the creation of numerous federally endowed colleges would undercut existing institutions that already struggle financially; the President suggests directly endowing chairs of agriculture and the mechanic arts in existing colleges instead. Sixth, the Constitution does not grant Congress authority to give away public lands for state education; the “dispose of” clause authorizes sales, not gifts, and lands purchased with tax‑derived money are subject to the same limitations. The President therefore returns the bill, declaring it both inexpedient and unconstitutional.

In November 2016, Bell Academy's PE teacher Joyce Aycock secured a Mississippi Alliance for Health, PE, Recreation and Dance grant from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi, funding a PE building behind the school built by parent volunteers and community members. The building, equipped with basketballs, mats, stack cups, hula‑hoops, gives students an indoor space, ending prior outdoor classes on concrete and noisy open‑area lessons. Aycock will add a horizontal rock‑climbing wall before the ribbon‑cutting at 9:30 a.m. Friday and thanks parents and community for support.

Bethesda announced Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus for Nintendo Switch on June 29, available digitally and physically; the physical cartridge requires a download. The first‑person shooter originally launched on PS4, Xbox One, and PC in October 2017, with sales initially slow but a praised story. The Switch version aims to attract new audiences and repeat buyers and needs a microSD for storage. Bethesda also released Doom and Skyrim on Switch in November, showing its commitment to Nintendo’s hybrid console, which achieved the largest install base of any console in its first twelve months.

Drive concept uses a two‑receiver combo: a 10‑12 yd basic route (often an in‑cut) from the X receiver and a 3‑4 yd shallow crossing route from the slot receiver trailing under the linebacker level. This creates a triangle read for the QB, stresses LB‑level defenders, and can be the primary or secondary read. It works well versus man coverage (receivers stay on the move) and Cover 4 (post can pull the safety), but struggles versus Cover 2 and Cover 3 where many low defenders clog the area. Coaching points give landmarks and movement for each position in both man and zone looks. QB progression is: (1) go route by X, (2) shallow cross by slot, (3) basic by TE, (4) check‑down to RB, with a pre‑snap peek at the post. Variations pair Drive with a bunch formation for rubs or attach it to the backside of other pass schemes as a quick outlet against blitzes.

Council traffic bosses say they are acting to ease congestion around Southway and Tamerton Foliot. They are co‑ordinating scheduled utility work, requesting night or off‑peak timings and limiting temporary signals (South West Water’s works limited to 9.30 am‑2.30 pm). To keep traffic moving they have suspended bus‑lane restrictions on Tavistock Road, run simultaneous construction and weekend/night work, adjusted George Junction signals for more straight‑ahead green time, and reviewed Budshead Roundabout by converting its slip‑road to a give‑way layout and planning lane‑marking changes. After central‑reserve kerb work finishes in the next few weeks, traffic management will shift and extra signs will encourage main‑carriageway drivers to let side‑road traffic merge. All roadworks are posted on the council’s website and publicised through email alerts, media and digital signs.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS into college and university systems ahead of free higher education rollout. NSFAS has faced delayed payments causing protests at tertiary institutions. Minister Naledi Pandor acknowledged unacceptable delays for continuing students and instructed her department to resolve outstanding cases urgently, citing significant challenges with system integration affecting registration data submission. Government allocated R7.2bn in 2018 for bursaries (R4.6bn for university students, R2.6bn for TVET students), with NSFAS baseline funding set to increase from R9.9bn in 2017-18 to R35.3bn in 2020-21. Additional R105m will strengthen NSFAS administrative capacity. DA spokesperson Belinda Bozzoli criticized the minister for failing to answer key questions about how many students haven't received allowances and when they will be paid.

ADT is said to be undervalued relative to Verisure, with strong revenue growth, improving profitability, a high proportion of recurring revenue, partnerships with Google and State Farm, ongoing debt reduction, and aggressive share buybacks that raise shareholder yield to 11%. Customer churn and stagnant subscriber growth remain challenges, though ADT is investing in AI, remote assistance, and smart‑home offerings to improve retention. Peer analysis indicates a 12–14x P/E could generate over 33% upside from current levels.

Diplomats reported that Korean rebel Kim Ok‑kiun was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong‑oo, handed to Chinese authorities and sent to Korea. In Tokyo, a man claiming a royal seal to kill a refugee was arrested; Hong took refuge at the legation and was forcibly removed by police. Kim’s body and Hong’s remains arrived at Chemulpo, taken to Seoul and mutilated, prompting a protest that diplomats declined to join. Unrest against oppressive officials spread in southern provinces; troops were sent but ineffective. The legation requested naval visits to deter disorder, protect missionaries, and a Korean chargé d'affaires urged ship visits.

Joe Bryant's fantasy football newsletter provides Week 10 matchup analysis for NFL teams, categorizing games into sections for passing and rushing matchups. Categories include Locks, Prime Matchups, Even Matchups, Downside Matchups, and Defensive Slam Dunks, indicating whether games favor the offense or defense. The newsletter discusses player performances, injury updates, and statistical rankings from recent weeks to advise fantasy football decisions.

VCEK (Versioned Chip Endorsement Key) certificates are X.509v3 certificates used in AMD's SEV-SNP technology. The certificate chain consists of AMD Root Key (ARK) as root CA, AMD SEV Key (ASK) as intermediate CA, and VCEK as the leaf certificate. VCEK certificates are generated on request and contain TCB (Trusted Compute Base) information, with validity from one day before issuance to seven years after. ARK and ASK certificates are valid for 25 years. The KDS (Key Distribution System) provides an HTTP interface at https://kdsintf.amd.com for retrieving certificates, certificate chains, and CRLs (Certificate Revocation Lists) following RFC 5280. Different processor families use different hwID lengths: Family 19h (Milan, Genoa, Siena) uses 64 bytes, while Family 1Ah (Turin) uses 8 bytes. The system supports pre-fetching certificates to enable seamless security firmware upgrades.

Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player USMNT roster for October friendlies in Austin and Commerce City, Colorado. Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie headline the squad. Pulisic is in strong form with six goals for AC Milan, while McKennie returns after an absence. Antonee Robinson is recalled following injury. Several players were excluded due to injuries or lack of international form.

UPMSP will release UP Board 10th and 12th results 2018 on 29 April at 12:30 pm via upresults.nic.in. Results can be accessed online or by SMS UP10/UP12 to 56263. In 2016‑17, 34.04 lakh students sat Class 10 (81.6% pass) and 26.25 lakh sat Intermediate (81.6% pass).

Player cited frustration with scoring and defensive breakdowns in recent tight games, emphasizing need to improve D-zone play against Hasek's aggressive style. Detroit's adjustments made it tougher, though Arturs played well. Coaching will make changes as needed.

The invention discloses a vehicle radar sensing system that employs a two‑dimensional array of multiple transmitting and receiving antennas and applies two‑dimensional multiple‑input multiple‑output (MIMO) processing to enlarge the virtual aperture, providing enhanced angular resolution in both horizontal and vertical directions. In a preferred embodiment the array comprises three rows of four transmitting antennas and four columns of four receiving antennas, yielding 192 virtual receivers. A control processes the outputs of the array to detect objects in the field of sensing and may interface with driver‑assistance or autonomous‑driving functions such as blind‑spot detection, parking assist, pedestrian detection, or automatic emergency braking. The system can be combined with camera data, generate visual, audible, or haptic alerts, and may utilize aspects of related patents.

Jennifer Thompson identified Ronald Cotton as her attacker; he was convicted of her rape. Eleven years later, post‑conviction DNA testing showed the true perpetrator was Bobby Poole, who later raped six other women while imprisoned with Cotton. After his exoneration, Thompson apologized and they became best friends; both now participate in the Healing Justice organization, sharing their stories.

Russia's central bank cut key rate to 9.25% from 9.75%, deeper than forecast, and expects inflation to fall to 4% by end‑2017. It plans further gradual cuts in Q2‑Q3. The rouble fell to 57.19 then recovered. Next meeting June 16.

The Oct. 15 paycheck for 1.3 million active‑duty service members could become a decisive catalyst for ending the U.S. government shutdown. Goldman Sachs economists Ronnie Walker and Alec Phillips noted the payment date may pressure both the White House and Congress to compromise before missing it, with prediction markets assigning a 71 % probability that the shutdown extends past Oct. 14. Missing a military pay period could stir public anger and likely trigger a temporary continuing resolution to keep the government funded. NEC Director Kevin Hassett warned that President Trump may adopt “sharp measures” if the next funding bill fails. Other looming deadlines—such as the Oct. 13 expiration of WIC benefits, potential TSA delays, and mortgage payment disruptions for service members—could add pressure, while the Nov. 1 Obamacare enrollment start and the Nov. 21 congressional break for Thanksgiving serve as additional forcing events. Analysts at Pimco described the situation as the first full shutdown since 2013, emphasizing that reopenings are harder than shutdowns, and the risk of a prolonged stalemate remains.

Scientists fabricated hybrid superconducting microwave circuits by depositing 100 nm NbN on n‑doped Si/Si0.7Ge0.3 wafers and patterning coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators using e‑beam lithography, CF4/Ar anisotropic dry etch, and a novel deep reactive‑ion etch that recesses the SiGe buffer in the CPW gaps to shift high‑electric‑field regions away from charge‑noise sources. Two quarter‑wave resonators were measured with fundamental frequencies of ~5.04–5.60 GHz and internal quality factors (Qi) ranging from ~500 to ~1064 in the single‑photon regime; external coupling (Qc) remained design‑controlled. Power‑dependent spectroscopy showed resonance‑frequency shifts up to 700 kHz due to TLS saturation, while temperature studies (50 mK–1.7 K) revealed that TLS loss dominates at low power and that temperature‑independent scattering loss (grain boundaries, dislocations, substrate conductivity) is the dominant mechanism. Over four cooldown cycles spanning two years, Qi remained stable, indicating robust, aging‑resistant devices. Compared with other SiGe/Ge‑based CPW resonators, the NbN/Si‑SiGe platform yields comparable Qi with reduced error bars, and deep‑gap etching mitigates loss by moving noisy interfaces from high‑field regions. This CMOS‑compatible platform combines NbN’s high Tc, magnetic‑field tolerance, and robustness with SiGe quantum wells, offering a scalable pathway to hybrid superconducting–semiconductor quantum circuits.

Monday began the first of seven days of the 2025 World Grand Prix of Darts with eight matches. Rob Cross won a last‑leg set‑3 decider against Nijman, Ratajski upset the top seed with a 95.94 average, Menzies knocked out the #8 seed, and Cullen came back from 0‑2 down to beat James Wade 2‑0.

Major Ghana gold miners (Newmont, Gold Fields, AngloGold Ashanti) back tests to certify exports. Ghana, Africa’s second‑largest gold producer, earned $5.78 billion from gold exports in 2017, up 17.6 % from 2016. The tests enforce a law requiring the PMMC to certify exports and give officials access. President Akufo‑Addo says about $5 billion of gold revenue to the UAE is unaccounted for, with observers linking it to smuggled artisanal gold. A ban on small‑scale mining remains.

Edina School District in Minnesota introduces the concept of white privilege to kindergarten through the Melanin Project, where K‑2 students trace their hands, color them to match their skin tone and post a message encouraging equality. Separately, Michigan State University religious studies professor Shreena Gandhi co‑authored an article arguing that yoga practice in the United States is linked to white supremacy and colonialism.

President Carter concludes his term by thanking Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, and the American people for the opportunity to serve. He affirms the nation's inner strength, principles, and ability to meet future challenges. He describes the presidency as powerful yet constrained by law and public consent, emphasizes the importance of democratic debate and criticism, and warns that special‑interest groups fragment political purpose and endanger the common good. He calls for preserving the constitutional authority of the presidency as the only official representing all citizens, and pledges to support the president‑elect.

Turning to global issues, Carter outlines three major concerns: nuclear weapons, environmental stewardship, and human rights. He notes that for 35 years the world has lived under the nuclear shadow, that arsenals are growing and the risk of catastrophic war is increasing, and stresses the need for both strong U.S. military capability and international efforts to control and reduce nuclear stockpiles. He highlights that rocket technology also enables peaceful space exploration, allowing a view of Earth as a small, fragile globe whose unity transcends borders.

Carter then discusses the environment, warning of dangers to air, water, land, and resources from depletion, pollution, overpopulation, and soil erosion. He argues these problems are solvable with courage and foresight. He also addresses human rights, stating that America was founded on the idea of individual rights, and must protect liberties at home and abroad, including education, health care, equal opportunity, and freedom from discrimination. He describes the current era as a time of transition marked by tensions and competition, urging that historic principles not be abandoned.

Carter concludes by expressing gratitude to citizens, noting his continued efforts regarding American hostages in Iran, his intention to support the new president, and his plan to return home as a private citizen dedicated to the nation's founding values.

A diverse workforce reflects the global market, but subconscious biases can undermine hiring. Studies show men are hired more often for math tasks despite equal performance, resumes with white‑sounding names receive about 50 % more callbacks than African‑American‑sounding names, and non‑English surnames reduce interview invitations. To counter bias, review job ad language for behavior‑focused descriptions, remove names from résumés, use skill tests before gathering other information, and scrutinize interview gut feelings for hidden prejudice. The article was written by Gillian Burdett for CBS Small Business Pulse.

Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship has provided high‑dosage virtual tutoring to over 40 communities, training more than 5,500 tutors who delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized instruction. Academic gains were up to 2.5 times the expected rate for middle‑school math and three times faster for elementary reading. The program emphasizes structured training and ongoing coaching, uses technology to expand relationships rather than replace them, and has become a teacher‑recruitment pipeline: research shows that tutoring triples the likelihood of applying to Teach For America’s teaching program, especially among men, people of color, and non‑education majors. Since its launch, 550 Ignite fellows have joined the TFA corps, with 280 new teachers entering classrooms this year, illustrating tutoring’s potential to accelerate both student learning and future educator recruitment.

China’s foreign exchange regulator said capital outflow pressure eased in 2016 and the yuan’s flexibility will increase in 2017. The yuan fell 6.5 percent against the dollar in 2016 but has risen about 1 percent this year. Final data showed a 2016 current‑account surplus of $196.4 bn (1.8 percent of GDP, down from 10 percent in 2007) and a capital‑and‑financial‑account surplus of $26.3 bn.

Amazon.com, Inc., founded by Jeff Bezos and launched on July 16, 1995, grew from an online bookstore to the fourth-largest U.S. public company by its 20th IPO anniversary in 2017. The company's IPO in 1997 raised $54 million at $18 per share, eventually delivering a 64,000% shareholder return over 20 years with a market capitalization of $458 billion. Amazon expanded beyond books into various product categories and acquired companies like Audible (2008), Zappos (2009), and Quidsi (2010). It introduced the Prime membership program in 2005, which grew to include streaming services, free shipping, and other benefits, with Prime Day becoming a major sales event. Amazon diversified into devices (Kindle, Fire tablets, Echo) and cloud services through Amazon Web Services (AWS), which started in 2006 and became a major revenue driver. Despite failures like the Fire Phone, Amazon maintained a long-term focus on market leadership over short-term profitability. Financially, cumulative net income from 1997-2016 was $4.9 billion, with 60% earned in 2015-16, as total net sales reached $135.987 billion in 2016, with AWS contributing $12.219 billion in sales and $3.108 billion in operating income.

Microsoft Corporation is a technology company whose mission is to empower every person and organization to achieve more. The company operates in three reportable segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It offers a broad range of software, services, devices, and solutions, including operating systems, productivity applications (Office), server products (Azure, SQL Server, Windows Server), cloud services, devices (Surface, Xbox), search (Bing), and professional networking (LinkedIn). Microsoft’s strategy focuses on reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud and edge platform, and creating more personal computing experiences. The company’s intelligent cloud segment includes Azure, server products, and enterprise services; its more personal computing segment includes Windows licensing, devices, gaming, and search. Competition is intense across all markets, with rivals such as Apple, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and Salesforce, among others. The COVID‑19 pandemic has impacted the company’s operations and financial results, with uncertainties about its duration and economic effects. Microsoft is addressing environmental sustainability, including commitments to become carbon negative by 2030 and to invest in carbon reduction initiatives, as well as programs to advance racial justice and expand digital skills. The company employs approximately 163,000 people worldwide, with executive leadership including CEO Satya Nadella and other senior executives. The 2020 Form 10‑K details risk factors related to competition, cloud services execution, intellectual property, cybersecurity, data privacy, and regulatory matters, among others. Microsoft’s financial reporting covers fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, with segments aligned to the company’s internal organization and strategic objectives.

Ethereum’s enshrined Proposer‑Builder Separation (ePBS, EIP‑7732) removes off‑chain relay trust but introduces a “free option” for builders: after committing to a block header at slot start, a builder can withhold the execution payload or blobs until later PTC deadlines and thereby make the slot empty if external information (e.g., CEX price moves) makes the trade unprofitable, with no protocol penalty.  

The authors model the option and derive predictions: option value and exercise probability increase with (i) the length of the option window, (ii) market volatility, (iii) the share of CEX‑DEX arbitrage value in the block, and (iv) decreasing atomic on‑chain MEV.  

Empirical analysis of historical Ethereum blocks (Jan 2024–Mar 2025) shows that with an 8‑second window the option is profitable in 0.82 % of blocks on average, but on high‑volatility days the exercise rate rises to 5.5 % and accounts for ~80 % of missed blocks. Option value is highly skewed (median 0.84 ETH, peak >40 ETH). Builder heterogeneity matters: large builders (Titan, beaverbuild) have low exercise rates (<0.8 %) because they have diverse order flow, while smaller builders dominated by CEX‑DEX flow show rates up to 23 %. Trailing MEV reduces exercise in consecutive slots (≈63 % of otherwise exercised options remain unused).  

Two mitigation strategies are evaluated:  

1. Shortening the option window. Reducing the window from 8 s to 6 s cuts the exercise probability by >33 %; to 4 s by >50 %; to 2 s by >77 %. The reduction is strongest for CEX‑DEX‑heavy blocks, but shortening also weakens the scalability benefit of ePBS by limiting time for L1 execution and L2 blob propagation.  

2. Penalties. Static penalties of 0.075 ETH, 0.15 ETH and 0.5 ETH lower the average exercise probability by ~75 %, 83 % and 87 % respectively, but raise entry barriers for new builders. A dynamic penalty mechanism based on online gradient descent achieves a target exercise rate of 0.1 % with an average penalty of 0.104 ETH, matching the effectiveness of a high static penalty while adapting to market conditions.  

The free option degrades network liveness precisely when volatility is high, harms liquidity providers by forcing exercises in favorable market moves, and distorts DEX price signals. Both mitigations involve trade‑offs between liveness, scalability, and builder entry costs; robust protocol‑level incentives are required to limit option exercise across varying market conditions.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for discovering regulatory T cells (T‑regs), immune cells that suppress excessive immune responses, prevent autoimmune disease and help maintain fetal tolerance during pregnancy. Brunkow and Ramsdell identified a mutation that causes fatal autoimmunity in male mouse pups and its human equivalent; Sakaguchi first described T‑regs in 1995. The prize, worth 11 million Swedish kronor (over $1.1 million), was announced by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute on 6 October. Ongoing research aims to harness T‑regs to treat autoimmune, inflammatory and other conditions where the immune system is overactive or misdirected.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon on October 25, 2001. Fastow was placed on leave of absence amid an SEC inquiry into partnerships he ran (LJM Cayman and LJM2). The company disclosed a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and $1.01 billion in third-quarter losses. Enron's stock fell to $16.41 (down 17%), having lost about half its value since October 16. Analysts issued sell recommendations and multiple shareholder lawsuits were filed. Kenneth Lay said the replacement was necessary to restore investor confidence. Fastow had run the partnerships while serving as CFO, raising conflict-of-interest concerns.
Deputies investigated a road rage incident on US 77 involving a white Dodge Ram waving a gun; Isaac Torgerson was arrested at Estes Gate for aggravated assault.

The Yankees have inserted Paul Goldschmidt into the starting lineup for ALDS Game 4 against the Blue Jays, batting him sixth at first base while Ben Rice moves to the bench. They will open with Louis Varland and follow with a bullpen game. Goldschmidt, 38, has started only one postseason game and posted a .274 average and .731 OPS with 31 doubles and 10 homers in the regular season. Rice, 26, started all three prior games, going 2‑for‑11 with a double, two RBIs, a walk and five strikeouts in the series, and hit .255 with an .836 OPS, 28 doubles and 26 homers during the year. The move provides the Yankees additional bench flexibility and a potential pinch‑hit option for either Austin Wells or Goldschmidt.

Temu resumed direct shipping from China after pausing over the summer. The de minimis rule previously allowed packages under $800 to ship duty-free from overseas, which benefited Chinese e-commerce platforms. After Trump imposed tariffs on Chinese goods, Temu and Shein adapted by shipping from US warehouses to avoid fees. The author placed an order and received it without extra tariff fees. Prices on similar platforms increased by about 30% following the tariffs.

Donnell Gibson, a behavior intervention specialist at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul, was recognized as an Excellent Educator. Gibson, who grew up homeless, saved a family of 10 by entering a burning house three times in April 2015, earning the Fire Department's highest honor. He now mentors young African-American men through the Gibson Foundation he founded, using basketball and motivational speakers to help students focus on school. He credits his high school principal for seeing his potential.

A class‑action lawsuit was filed on October 23 2001 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas on behalf of investors who bought Enron common stock between January 18 2000 and October 17 2001. The complaint alleges that Enron and certain officers violated Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by issuing material misrepresentations about the company’s Broadband Services, related‑party transactions with limited partnerships managed by the chief financial officer, and timely asset write‑downs, leading to a $1.01 billion after‑tax charge (a $1.11 loss per diluted share) in the third quarter of 2001 and a drop in Enron’s share price. Enron insiders reportedly sold more than $73 million of their personal shares during the class period.

Also on October 23, Enron disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information about the company’s transactions with partnerships managed by a senior officer (CFO Andrew Fastow). Enron said it would cooperate fully. The SEC inquiry sent Enron’s stock down $5.40, to $20.65, on heavy trading; the price later fell further to $19.79. The company asked Citigroup to arrange a $750 million loan as a precaution, and Moody’s placed all $13 billion of Enron’s long‑term debt on watch for a possible downgrade. Enron relies on a $3 billion commercial‑paper program for day‑to‑day financing.

Analysts largely kept “buy” or “strong buy” ratings, though a few cut ratings to “hold” or “reduce.” On an investor conference call CEO Kenneth Lay declined to raise earnings guidance despite a planned 60‑million‑share reduction from the termination of a Fastow‑run partnership (LJM2), which caused a $1.2 billion equity reduction. Lay disputed an investor’s valuation of water assets held by a trust (Marlin II) and accused the caller of driving the stock down.

Other news items include the WTO confirming its Qatar conference despite security concerns, 3M reporting a 21 percent profit decline, copper prices near a 15‑year low, Bombardier noting increased use of regional jets, Swissair receiving a $4 billion rescue package, Aliant shedding 140 non‑union jobs, and AES Corp. complaining to India’s prime minister about state‑level interference with its power operations.

Metastatic castration‑resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) frequently develops resistance to androgen‑signaling inhibitors and to the taxane chemotherapies docetaxel and cabazitaxel. A third of patients are intrinsically refractory, and those who respond ultimately acquire resistance. The mechanisms underlying taxane activity and resistance are incompletely understood.

AR wild‑type (wt) and splice variants (ARv567, AR‑V7) associate differently with microtubules (MTs). ARv567 is largely MT‑bound, sensitive to docetaxel and its nuclear accumulation is blocked by paclitaxel; AR‑V7 is less MT‑associated and confers docetaxel resistance in xenograft models. Thus, AR transcriptional activity depends on MT cytoskeleton dynamics.

A computational platform was developed to quantify MT polymerization dynamics in living cells by automated tracking of EB1/EB3 comet trajectories from high‑resolution confocal time‑lapse sequences. EB1 comets serve as markers of growing MT plus‑ends; detection uses band‑pass filtering, shape‑based scoring, Kalman filter tracking, and spatiotemporal clustering to resolve growth, pause, and shortening phases.

In M12 isogenic PC cell lines expressing GFP‑tagged AR‑wt or AR‑V7, AR‑wt expression caused a modest decrease in EB1 speeds (≈16 µm/min) and MT slowdown near the cell edge, whereas AR‑V7 expression increased speeds >40 % (≈24 µm/min) with no edge slowdown, indicating differential MT regulation in taxane‑sensitive versus resistant cells.

Patient‑derived organoids were generated from primary, lymph‑node, and metastatic prostate tumor tissues (UCSF‑PR, UCSF‑LN, UCSF‑PCa). Selection for tumor cells over normal epithelium employed a twin‑needle biopsy and differential concentrations of Y‑27632 ROCK inhibitor; high‑grade tumors required lower inhibitor concentrations. Organoids were transduced to express EB1ΔC‑2xEGFP for live‑cell MT dynamics analysis.

Increased MT dynamicity and up‑regulation of the MT polymerization inhibitor Op18 (STMN1) correlated with taxane resistance in androgen‑independent PC. Low‑dose paclitaxel paradoxically increased MT polymerization rates, while high doses stabilized MTs, highlighting nonlinear dose‑dependent effects.

The tumor suppressor pVHL attenuates MT turnover by reducing polymerization and shrinkage rates and inhibiting catastrophe events. VHL mutations increased MT dynamics and reduced drug susceptibility; pVHL30 protected MTs from depolymerization by nocodazole, whereas pVHL19 had a milder effect. Both pVHL isoforms maintain primary cilia, and their MT‑stabilizing function is independent of HIF1α degradation.

GSK3β phosphorylates pVHL at Ser‑68/72, inactivating its MT‑stabilizing activity. In quiescent cells, GSK3β‑mediated phosphorylation raised MT turnover to levels observed in VHL‑deficient proliferating cells, and GSK3 inhibition restored pVHL function, lowering MT turnover. Different GSK3 isoforms (α vs β) are elevated in early versus advanced disease, suggesting isoform‑specific therapeutic targets.

Circular Hough transform analysis of drug‑treated cells quantified MT bundling as a hallmark of taxane activity. BRCA1‑knockdown A549 cells showed reduced bundling (27 % vs 83 % in parental cells) and lower MT ring intensity (≈70 % reduction), indicating a second resistance mechanism.

Live‑cell MT dynamics were correlated with gene‑expression signatures of 70 MT‑regulating genes in patient organoids. Hierarchical clustering revealed Op18 up‑regulation in a metastatic organoid with attenuated MT growth rates. These patterns may guide matching of patients to specific tubulin inhibitors.

Proposed workflow integrates patient‑derived organoids, ex vivo MT dynamics profiling, transcriptomics, and patient‑derived xenograft testing to anticipate resistance, select optimal drug regimens, and evaluate combination therapies (e.g., GSK3 inhibitors, NAD+, ferroptosis inducers, AR‑targeting PROTACs, and immune checkpoint blockade with expanded TILs).

Collectively, the studies demonstrate that quantitative MT dynamics provide a functional readout of drug susceptibility, that both accelerated and decelerated MT turnover are hallmarks of resistance, and that integrating MT dynamics with molecular signatures could enable personalized treatment for advanced prostate cancer.

California's energy crisis in February 2001 involved Governor Gray Davis negotiating with utilities (Edison, PG&E, SDG&E) facing nearly $13 billion in debts due to high wholesale power costs and rate caps. Davis proposed the state purchase 26,000 miles of transmission lines for $4.5-7 billion to help stabilize utilities. Davis announced a tentative $2.7 billion deal with Edison for its grid plus 10-year cheap power sales. Progress with PG&E was described as difficult. The state was spending approximately $50 million daily on power purchases, with costs potentially reaching $3 billion by mid-March. GOP leaders struggled to craft alternative solutions while avoiding contradictions to their deregulation stance. Legislators introduced bills for alternative energy price reductions and proposed discounts for residents near power plants. Some lawmakers returned utility campaign contributions. After 40 days of power alerts, the state saw its first day without emergencies on February 23, though officials warned the crisis was far from resolved. Consumer advocates criticized the plans as giveaways. Republicans sought to use the crisis politically against Davis in the 2002 gubernatorial race. The Public Utilities Commission ruled utilities were not responsible for revenue shortfalls, potentially shifting costs to taxpayers. Small power producers agreed to price cuts.

Hungary is a European country with a population of 9.7 million, facing a negative natural increase rate. Its government is a multiparty parliamentary democracy with a prime minister holding significant power. The economy has shifted from agriculture to industry and services, with recent policies like Orbanomics reducing unemployment. Education is a priority, with compulsory schooling from ages 6 to 16, including pre-primary, primary, secondary, and post-secondary levels. Teacher training for general education requires bachelor's degrees, with recent reforms to undivided teacher education programs. Special education in Hungary began in 1802 and has evolved, with over 88,000 special education needs students in 2019, 60% educated inclusively. Diagnosis involves a committee, with final placement decisions made by parents. Special education teachers undergo four-year university programs with specializations. Current issues include diagnosis procedures, building accessibility, and inclusion in schools. Teacher preparation faces challenges like frontal teaching methods, low pay compared to OECD standards, and high attrition rates. Laws such as the Hungarian Act on Public Education of 2011 have improved rights for students with disabilities. Recommendations focus on improving teacher training for disabilities, increasing school accessibility, and enhancing inclusion practices to benefit student outcomes.

Donchian Channels, created by Richard Donchian in the mid‑20th century, consist of an upper band (the highest high of the last N bars) and a lower band (the lowest low of the last N bars). Originally a trend‑following tool for commodities and currencies, they rely on breakouts above the upper band or below the lower band. Curtis Faith’s Turtle backtests (1996‑2007) on currencies, commodities and Treasuries showed simple Donchian strategies achieving CAGRs of 29 % to 57 %.

Testing a basic long‑only Donchian system on the S&P 500 from 1960 to 2021 produced an unleveraged CAGR of 4.57 % versus 7.15 % for buy‑and‑hold, but with a lower maximum drawdown. Optimization found the best results using a 40‑day upper band and a 20‑day lower band.

Inverting the indicator for a mean‑reversion approach on SPY (1993‑2021) gave a best CAGR of 9.16 % with a 5‑day look‑back; a 15‑day look‑back also performed well and reduced curve‑fitting risk. This version displayed small drawdowns and a high win rate, and the results were roughly out‑of‑sample because an overnight strategy based on the approach had been used for seven years.

Visually similar to Bollinger Bands, Donchian Channels differ in calculation and can yield different backtest outcomes. Overall, Donchian Channels appear effective as a trend‑following indicator for commodities and currencies, and as a mean‑reversion indicator for stocks.

President Ronald Reagan, speaking at the University of Virginia, praised Thomas Jefferson as the university’s founder and the chief advocate of free inquiry, science, and popular government in American higher education, noting Jefferson’s epitaph and his use of balanced, symmetric architecture as a metaphor for balanced governance. He described a worldwide shift toward democracy and market‑oriented economies, citing Freedom House data that the number of “not free” countries fell from 71 to 50 while free or partly free nations rose from 92 to 117, with over 90 percent of the world’s population now living in democratic or democratizing states. Reagan highlighted U.S. foreign‑policy achievements: the INF treaty, a START agreement calling for 50‑percent cuts in strategic weapons, progress on nuclear‑testing and chemical‑weapons talks, and Soviet troop reductions announced at the UN; successful resolutions of regional conflicts including Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan, Vietnamese troops leaving Cambodia, a U.S.‑mediated Cuban troop withdrawal from Angola, and the end of the Gulf war; and human‑rights advances in the Soviet Union such as the release of political prisoners, easing of state economic controls, and greater freedoms to publish, emigrate, and practice religion. He offered three reflections: (1) trust but verify, maintain military strength, avoid bad treaties, and speak candidly about differences; (2) Soviet reforms were not inevitable and resulted from Western resolve and Gorbachev’s choices; (3) effective foreign policy requires cooperation between the Executive and Congress while respecting their distinct constitutional roles. He concluded by quoting Jefferson’s and Adams’s letters and noting their shared death on July 4, 1826, fifty years after the Declaration of Independence. During the Q&A, Reagan discussed granting most‑favored‑nation status to the USSR, emphasizing that deeds must match words; described progress toward Middle‑East peace, noting the PLO’s acceptance of Israel’s right to exist and UN resolutions; outlined a firm anti‑terrorism policy; advised young people to register and vote; highlighted his administration’s restoration of military readiness, the creation of 19 million jobs, tax‑rate reductions that increased revenue, and the reduction of federal paperwork by 600 million man‑hours; and said he planned to remain active after leaving office as a speaker and possibly an author.

Rapid identification of chest X‑ray (CXR) abnormalities suggestive of lung cancer is essential for improving patient outcomes. In England over 8 million CXRs are performed annually, yet lung‑cancer prevalence in primary‑care‑requested CXRs is about 1.4%. To address high reporting demand and radiology workforce shortages, AI has been proposed as a tool to flag suspicious CXRs. This study aimed to develop a systematic, evidence‑based method for selecting which AI‑detected CXR findings should be prioritised.  

The work was conducted across seven acute care trusts in Greater Manchester using two cohorts: a retrospective cohort of 1,282 patients with confirmed lung cancer and an abnormal CXR (June 2020–June 2022), and a prospective cohort of 13,802 consecutive primary‑care CXRs (June–July 2024) in which the Annalise Container CXR AI (124 possible findings) ran in shadow mode. An Excel‑based tool calculated the prevalence ratio of each finding between the cancer cohort and the referral cohort. Findings were classified into CRITICAL, HIGH and STANDARD groups, and three prioritisation strategies were compared: (1) 19 HIGH‑priority findings with a prevalence ratio >5; (2) all HIGH‑priority findings with ratio >2; (3) a final set refined by clinical judgement.  

Performance metrics were derived using cohort 1 for sensitivity and cohort 2 for specificity (assuming 1% cancer prevalence). Results are shown in the table. Strategy 1 achieved sensitivity 92.82% and specificity 87.21% but missed more cancers. Strategy 2 had the highest sensitivity (97.27%) but lowest specificity (62.68%). Strategy 3 offered a balance: sensitivity 95.87%, specificity 79.11%, PPV 4.43%, NPV 99.95%, with about 23 CXRs requiring reporting to detect one cancer case.  

The most informative findings included solitary lung mass, mediastinal mass, diffuse airspace opacities, cavitating mass, hilar lymphadenopathy and multiple nodules. Higher prevalence of bone‑related abnormalities in the cancer cohort reflected the older age of that group.  

The study demonstrates a reproducible, data‑driven approach to AI‑based CXR prioritisation, using shadow‑mode evaluation to ensure patient safety. It provides a framework for selecting findings that maximise sensitivity and NPV while accepting a lower PPV. Limitations include single‑region data and reliance on assumed prevalence for cohort 2. External validation and broader implementation are planned. This method could serve as a blueprint for integrating AI into radiology workflows to improve early lung‑cancer detection.

Non‑Farm Payrolls (NFP) is a monthly report released by the US Department of Labor on the first Friday at 8:30 am ET. It measures the number of new jobs added in the previous month across all non‑agricultural businesses, excluding private households, federal government, farms and non‑profit organisations. The headline figure is the net change in non‑farm employment, while the report also includes the unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, total hours worked and sector‑by‑sector breakdowns.

Because the NFP figure is tightly linked to Federal Reserve policy, it consistently triggers the largest market moves of any monthly data release. A reading that beats consensus is interpreted as positive for the US economy and the USD, prompting forex traders to go long USD‑based pairs (e.g. USD/JPY) and short USD‑quote pairs (e.g. EUR/USD). A reading below expectations is seen as negative for the USD and produces opposite positioning.

The bond market is most sensitive: stronger job growth raises expectations of a Fed interest‑rate increase, which pushes bond yields higher and depresses bond prices (including Treasuries, municipal bonds and mortgage‑backed securities). Conversely, a weaker NFP figure tends to support bond prices.

Equity markets also react. Positive NFP results boost bullish sentiment, encouraging investment in US stocks, ETFs and indices such as the S&P 500, Dow 30 and Nasdaq 100. Negative results reduce optimism and investment activity.

Commodity markets are affected: higher NFP can lift demand for oil, gas and energy, while gold futures and spot prices move with changes in USD strength and inflation expectations.

Back‑testing shows that on the day of release the SPY ETF (tracking the S&P 500) averaged a 0.09 % gain, while the TLT bond ETF averaged a –0.02 % loss. Over the following one to five trading days both instruments posted negative average returns, indicating no consistent short‑term edge in trading the NFP number.

Overall, the NFP report is a key indicator of US employment and economic health, with wide‑ranging effects on forex, equity, bond and commodity markets, but exploiting its movements through systematic trading strategies has proven difficult.

The lecture discusses pseudorandom graphs and eigenvalue conditions. It defines n, d, lambda graphs as d-regular graphs where all eigenvalues except the top one are bounded in absolute value by lambda. Cayley graphs are introduced as examples, with Paley graphs (Cayley graphs of cyclic groups modulo prime p using quadratic residues) shown to have small eigenvalues. The eigenvalues of Cayley graphs on cyclic groups correspond to Fourier coefficients. A theorem by Conlon and Zhao states that for Cayley graphs, the discrepancy condition (DISC) and eigenvalue condition (EIG) are equivalent up to constant factors. The proof uses Grothendieck's inequality, which bounds the ratio between a discrete bilinear form and its semidefinite relaxation. The Alon-Boppana bound states that for any d-regular graph, the second largest eigenvalue in absolute value is at least 2√(d−1)−o(1) as n grows. Two proofs are provided: one via the Courant-Fischer min-max principle constructing vectors around vertices, and another via the trace method counting closed walks, both showing lambda_2 ≥ 2√(d−1)−o(1). This bound is tight and relates to the spectral radius of the infinite d-regular tree.

The case involves a $1,400 promissory note given by Hepner to Kil-Tone Company and endorsed to Bridgeton National Bank. Hepner claimed the note was obtained through fraud and that the bank's cashier (who was also Kil-Tone's treasurer) knew of the fraud, making this knowledge attributable to the bank. The passage details the AMD AGESA firmware interface specification, describing a set of procedures and data structures used during platform initialization. It defines functions for reading event logs, creating and releasing parameter blocks, and initializing processor cores at various boot stages: Reset, Early, Env, Post, Late, Ready‑To‑Boot and S3 resume. Each function is documented with input/output structures, status codes (SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, FATAL), and dependencies such as stack availability, heap usage, and core‑to‑core communication requirements. The interface also specifies a collection of call‑out routines that the host environment must implement, including memory allocation/deallocation (AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer), buffer location (AgesaLocateBuffer), system reset (Reset2), SPD reading (ReadSpd), AP task dispatch (AgesaRunFcnOnAllAps, AmdLateRunApTask), and optional hooks for voltage adjustment, PCIe clock request, and IDS data retrieval. Platform customization is achieved through build configuration options (e.g., BLDOPT_REMOVE_UDIMMS_SUPPORT, BLDOPT_REMOVE_ECC_SUPPORT) that enable or disable feature modules, and through build configuration elements (e.g., BLDCFG_VRM_CURRENT_LIMIT, BLDCFG_CPU_FREQUENCY_LIMIT) that set VRM capabilities, frequency limits, memory interleaving, ACPI table generation, and controller enable/disable flags for SATA, USB (XHCI), IDE, GPP, and integrated graphics. The passage also enumerates many parameter fields for processor, northbridge, graphics, FCH, display, and memory initialization, along with rules for execution cache region allocation and status reporting.

APP_CMD (CMD55) causes the next command to be interpreted as an application‑specific command (ACMD); certain ACMDs are reserved and ACMD41 has special APP_CMD status handling. GEN_CMD (CMD56) is blank. CMD6 (Switch Function) switches or expands card functions via four function groups (Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit); it is mandatory for spec v1.10+ and only valid in the Transfer state, returning an R1 response plus 512 bits of status data within 8 clocks. CMD6 supports Mode 0 (query supported functions) and Mode 1 (set functions); each group has 16 branches with Function 0 as default and 0xF leaving the current function unchanged; status includes support bits, function‑selection results and maximum current/power, plus busy‑status bits. Power‑Limit default is 0.72 W; removable cards may go up to 1.80 W, UHS‑I cards limited to 1.44 W and UHS‑II up to 1.80 W; hosts must verify max consumption before Mode 1 and UHS‑II requires group 4 but not groups 1 and 3. High‑Speed mode (25 MB/s) is entered by CMD6 at 50 MHz and is optional; the host must drive only one card in this mode. Command System reserves CMD34‑37, CMD50, CMD57 for extensions; selecting “standard” makes them illegal, “vendor‑specific” makes behavior vendor‑defined and “mobile e‑commerce” follows Part A1. CMD8 initializes v2.00+ cards, checks voltage and must be issued before ACMD41; the card returns R7 with voltage range and check pattern or no response if voltage unsupported. CCS=0 denotes SDSC (byte addressing) and CCS=1 denotes SDHC/SDXC (block addressing with fixed 512 B blocks, no partial/misaligned access). The host may lower or stop the clock after providing 8 clocks following a transaction; after ACMD41 the host must supply continuous 100‑400 kHz clock or poll busy ≤50 ms; a clock edge is required to release a busy card’s DAT line. CRC7 protects commands/responses (G(x)=x⁷+x³+1) and CRC16 protects data blocks (G(x)=x¹⁶+x¹²+x⁵+1); CRC or illegal‑command failures cause no response and set the appropriate status bit. Read timeout is the lesser of 100 ms or 100×(TAAC+NSAC); write timeout is the lesser of 250 ms or 100×program time; write‑busy limits are typically 250 ms, up to 500 ms for the final block or after CMD12/CMD23, and 250 ms during speed‑class write; UHS‑II busy after a Data Burst ≤1 s. UHS‑II modifies several commands (e.g., CMD13 not during transfer, TLEN stops data, CMD3 returns Device ID). Commands are 48‑bit with start/direction bits, 6‑bit index, 32‑bit argument, 7‑bit CRC and end bit; they are grouped into classes indicated by CCC bits; classes 0, 2, 4, 5, 8 are mandatory, class 7 (except CMD40) mandatory for SDHC/SDXC. Responses include R1/R1b (48 bit), R2 (CID/CSD, 136 bit), R3 (OCR, 48 bit), R6 (RCA, 48 bit) and R7 (voltage, 48 bit); all except R3 use CRC7. Three status fields exist: Card Status (R1), SD Status (512 bits) and Task Status (R1 with CMD13 b[15]=1). SD Status contains speed‑class, AU size, erase parameters, UHS/Video speed grades, command‑queue support and performance‑enhancement information. Write‑protection hierarchy and timing sections are blank. Speed‑class methods are optional and include Speed Class (Classes 2, 4, 6, 10), UHS Speed Grade (Grade 1, 3) and Video Speed Class (V6‑V90); they define AU and RU units, write performance (Pw) and move performance (Pm), FAT update cycles, buffer sizing and measurement conditions. SDXC uses exFAT, larger AU (up to 64 MB), no Pm, CI updates and CMD20 control commands (Start Recording, Update DIR, Update CI); CMD20 support is mandatory for SDXC, optional for SDHC, and an example recording sequence is provided.

The 1985 Heckler Report documented that Black people in the United States experienced roughly 60,000 excess deaths per year compared with White people, attributing the disparity to social determinants, acquired risk factors, access barriers and structural racism rather than biological differences. To provide a unifying metric for accountability, this study quantified excess deaths and years of potential life lost (YPLL) for non‑Hispanic Black versus non‑Hispanic White individuals using CDC WONDER data from 1999–2020 and National Center for Health Statistics life tables.

Over the 22‑year period, the mean annual excess mortality rate was 148.6 per 100,000 for Black females and 284.2 per 100,000 for Black males, corresponding to approximately 658,000 excess deaths among Black females and 1.15 million among Black males. The mean excess YPLL rate was 7,932 per 100,000 for Black females and 11,579 per 100,000 for Black males, totaling roughly 35 million excess YPLL among Black females and 47 million among Black males.

Temporal trends showed a steady decline in excess mortality and YPLL from 1999 to the early 2010s, followed by a plateau through 2019 and a sharp rise in 2020 that restored levels close to those of 1999. Age‑adjusted mortality rate ratios ranged from 1.13–1.31 for females and 1.21–1.40 for males. The leading cause of excess mortality was heart disease for both sexes; cancer, diabetes, HIV (males), assault and cerebrovascular disease also contributed. Perinatal conditions showed the highest YPLL rates.

In 2020, COVID‑19 added 47 excess deaths per 100,000 Black females and 80 per 100,000 Black males, and 1,759 and 2,572 excess YPLL per 100,000 respectively. Mortality and YPLL disparities were greatest among infants (Black‑White rate ratios >2.3) and increased with age after early adulthood, peaking in the 65–79 age group.

The authors conclude that excess deaths and YPLL among Black people persist at a scale that warrants national attention, that recent progress has been fragile and largely reversed by the pandemic, and that annual reporting of race‑based YPLL could serve as a metric for health‑equity accountability and stimulate new strategies to close the gap.

One police officer and two Barrio 18 gang members were killed and eight officers were wounded in a clash in San Salvador while a tactical unit searched for illegal weapons. One of the dead gunmen was identified as a Barrio 18 leader in Panchimalco linked to more than a dozen murders. All eight wounded officers suffered superficial bullet wounds; four were treated and released, and the other four are expected to leave the hospital within a week. El Salvador recorded 60 homicides per 100,000 inhabitants in 2017, one of the world’s highest rates.

Japan's government upgraded its business sentiment assessment in April for the first time in four months, based on the Bank of Japan's tankan survey showing corporate mood improved. Big manufacturers' confidence reached a one-and-a-half year high for a second consecutive quarter. The overall assessment of gradual economic recovery remained unchanged, with exports, factory output, consumer spending, and capital expenditure all showing signs of recovery. Uncertainty remains regarding overseas economies and financial markets.

A 26-year-old man has been charged with assault with a weapon following a suspicious death at an Aroland First Nation residence. Greenstone OPP responded to reports of an injured male on Friday. The victim was taken to hospital but died of his injuries. Multiple police units are investigating, and a postmortem examination will be conducted.

Comcast abandoned its bid for most of Twenty‑First Century Fox assets, leaving Disney as the sole suitor for the over $40 bn deal; negotiations with Disney are ongoing and could be finalized this month.

A Simple Moving Average (SMA) is the arithmetic mean of an asset’s closing price over a specified number of periods (SMA = (P1 + … + Pn)/n). As new price data appear the earliest observation is dropped and the average is recomputed, producing a continuously updated line that smooths price fluctuations. A rising SMA indicates an upward price trend, a falling SMA a downward trend, and a flat SMA with price crossing above and below signals a sideways market. Longer‑period SMAs (e.g., 100‑ or 200‑day) act as dynamic support or resistance levels and reduce sensitivity to daily noise, while shorter‑period SMAs react quickly and generate more trading signals, increasing trade frequency. The SMA is a lagging indicator because it uses past prices; its lag can be reduced by shortening the period but at the cost of more false signals. The exponential moving average (EMA) assigns greater weight to recent prices, providing faster reactions than the SMA, which treats all periods equally. Traders can apply SMAs to non‑price series such as volume or economic indicators to reveal underlying trends, but seasonal or cyclical patterns may make the SMA misleading because it does not account for those regular fluctuations. The choice of starting point can skew the SMA in volatile markets, and an SMA can theoretically be zero only if the price closes at zero throughout the period, a practical impossibility. Backtesting SMA strategies shows that short‑term mean‑reversion (buying when the close falls below a short SMA) yields higher returns than buying when the price rises above a short SMA, with a 5‑day SMA producing a CAGR of 8.34 %. Conversely, long‑term trend‑following (buying when the close crosses above a long SMA) becomes more profitable as the period lengthens; a 200‑day SMA yields a CAGR of 7.89 % with a maximum drawdown about half that of buy‑and‑hold, and the best result recorded is buying on a cross above the 200‑day SMA and holding for 200 days, delivering an average return of 10.93 % per trade (dividends excluded). Combining multiple SMA periods or using an SMA as a trend filter alongside other indicators can improve signal reliability. No single SMA period is universally optimal; backtesting each asset is required to find the most effective time frame. Both SMA and EMA are common, but many traders prefer the SMA for its simplicity and smoother depiction of long‑term trends, while the EMA is favored for short‑term strategies needing rapid response. Moving averages have been used for decades; systematic trend‑following with moving averages gained prominence in the 1970s with computerization, though their effectiveness has declined as more market participants have adopted similar methods.

Colleges and universities are preparing for possible unrest around the Oct. 7 anniversary of the 2023 Hamas attacks. Columbia University requires protest plans at least two business days in advance and has suspended same‑day and alumni guest passes. The University of Maryland has limited campus access to students and faculty with ID cards, and a student group plans a week of solidarity events, including a teach‑in and sit‑in. Demonstrations are also expected at other schools.

Thirty‑seven lawyers, ten incoming partners, have moved from Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft to Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe. They will work in Orrick’s new Charlotte office, London, Washington, D.C., New York offices, focusing on collateralized loan obligations and asset‑backed lending. Bloomberg Law reported a “lawyer exodus” from Cadwalader, counting 33 partners who left the firm this year; eight are part of the Orrick group. Law360 documented at least 23 partner defections this year. Recruiters said partners are moving to firms with broader service offerings and cross‑selling platforms. Cadwalader’s revenue ranking fell from No. 39 in 2007 to No. 85 in 2024, partly because its capital‑markets and finance practices are sensitive to interest‑rate changes. Despite posting $3.7 million profit per equity partner in 2024 and a strong brand, the firm has lost nearly a fifth of its partnership this year. It has responded by adding a second managing partner and hiring to bolster core practices.

The passage describes embodiments of a communication system enabling carrier aggregation and multi-connectivity in 5G networks. It details OFDM radio resources, frame structures with subframes and slots, and supports multiple numerologies and bandwidth parts (BWPs). The system includes base stations (gNB, eLTE eNB) and wireless devices with multi-carrier capabilities. Multi-connectivity allows a user equipment to connect to multiple base stations via master and secondary roles, managing radio resources through master cell groups (MCG) and secondary cell groups (SCG). Timing advance groups (TAGs) synchronize uplink transmissions across serving cells. Random access procedures and PUCCH configurations for cells are described. Tight interworking between 5G RAN and LTE RAN enables resource sharing via interfaces like Xn and Xx. Bandwidth adaptation supports dynamic switching between configured BWPs, with default BWPs for load balancing and connectivity maintenance. The system incorporates various protocols including NR RRC, PDCP, RLC, and MAC, with support for bearers like MCG, SCG, and split bearers.

Yahoo's AOL is in advanced talks to be sold to Italy's Bending Spoons for about $1.4 billion, a price representing 0.8 % of what AOL paid for Time Warner in 2001. Bending Spoons, which already has over 300 million monthly users and recently agreed to take Vimeo private for $1.38 billion, would gain AOL's user base and advertising reach; AOL's traffic rose 20 % year‑over‑year among younger users. Tesla delivered a record 497,100 vehicles in Q3, beating a 448,000 estimate and locking in the expiring $7,500 EV tax credit; production was 447,000 units, mostly Model Y and Model 3. Caterpillar has surged 32 % year‑to‑date, boosted by demand for its turbines and mining equipment for data‑center power and copper, with Bank of America raising its price target to $517. Wedbush identified Tenable, Qualys, SentinelOne, Elastic and C3.ai as prime AI‑driven takeover targets as smaller firms struggle with rising costs. Berkshire Hathaway is buying Occidental Petroleum's chemical business for $9.7 billion cash; Occidental will use most of the proceeds to reduce debt, saving over $350 million in annual interest. September job cuts fell 37 % from August to 54,064, the highest year‑to‑date total since 2020, while planned hires are down 58 % from the prior year. A new licensing model for FICO scores is expected to cut per‑score fees by up to 50 %. AI music‑label negotiations continue, with startups and larger players discussing micropayment structures for AI‑generated tracks.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on April 3, 2015, disclosing a press release regarding its results of operations and financial condition under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report is signed by CFO Deepak Ahuja.

Speaker thanks predecessor, cites inauguration ceremony reflecting inner spiritual strength, and notes use of the 1789 Bible and a maternal Bible containing Micah’s call to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God. The inauguration marks a new beginning that depends on the people; the nation’s 200‑year‑old dream of liberty and spirituality awaits fulfillment. The address calls for unity, trust, and shared learning, work, prayer and sacrifices, affirms faith in the American dream, and urges renewed commitment to basic principles while insisting government be both competent and compassionate. It stresses personal liberty, equal opportunity, absolute human rights, fair laws, preservation of natural beauty, and warns that “more” is not always better. Domestic strength is linked to foreign influence; a democratic example, quiet strength based on noble ideas, and the fight against poverty, ignorance and injustice are highlighted. The speaker reaffirms moral responsibility to support freedom abroad, pledges to limit arms, moves toward nuclear disarmament, and expresses hope that the nation will build lasting peace on shared values, affirming its enduring moral strength and expanding American dream.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 study comparing convalescent plasma (4 units, ~800-1000 mL) plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in 489 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (2:1 allocation). The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on Day 15. No significant difference was observed between groups (convalescent plasma: 83.7% vs control: 84.1%, odds ratio 0.99, p=0.976). Secondary endpoints also showed no significant differences in mortality, clinical status, or other outcomes. Safety profiles were similar between groups, with transfusion-related side effects reported in 5.9% of intervention patients. The study concluded that early administration of high-titer convalescent plasma did not significantly improve clinical outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

A prospective hospital-based study conducted at three Dar es Salaam regional referral hospitals (December 2021 – July 2022) examined 228 adult patients with acute intestinal obstruction. The study found a male-to-female ratio of 3:1, median age of 34 years, and median hospital stay of 4 days. The most common surgical diagnoses were adhesions (98 cases), hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20). Overall, 76% of patients were discharged home, 9% developed surgical site infections, and the mortality rate was 5.3%. The study suggests changing epidemiology of intestinal obstruction causes in developing countries, as adhesions—typically associated with developed countries—were most frequent, possibly due to referral bias. No significant differences in surgical outcomes were observed across the three hospitals. Limitations include potential referral bias and use of odds ratios rather than absolute risks.

Averaging down is an investment method where a trader buys additional shares of a stock after its price falls, lowering the average purchase price. By reducing the breakeven point, a smaller price increase is needed to become profitable, but the strategy does not eliminate loss; the stock must still rise. Whether to average down depends on the trader’s goals, time horizon, and confidence in the underlying company. For long‑term investors who believe in a company’s value, averaging down can be part of a planned scale‑in strategy; for short‑term traders without deep knowledge of the business, it may increase risk. A backtest on SPY using RSI signals and a two‑position scale‑in showed smoother equity and higher risk‑adjusted returns compared with a single‑position approach, but the benefit depends on the asset’s tendency toward mean reversion. Stocks are considered the most suitable asset class for averaging down, while other markets may not behave similarly. The strategy is not universally advisable; it requires a clear plan, risk management, and, ideally, prior backtesting.

Since 2008 the Personalized Medicine Conference has been held annually in South San Francisco, co‑organized by San Francisco State University’s Department of Biology, alumni and the City of South San Francisco. The June 2 2017 edition, Personalized Medicine 10.0, titled “Has It Changed Your Life?”, will review a decade of topics, assess past predictions and explore future directions. The meeting covers clinical advances, study design, business, regulatory and ethical issues, as well as bioinformatics, oncology, epigenetics, rare‑disease genomics, sequencing technologies, microbiome, gene therapy and genome editing. Amylynne Santiago Volker, founder of the Nicholas Volker One In A Billion Foundation and mother of the first person saved by genetic sequencing, will deliver the opening keynote, noting the need for provider training and insurance coverage for routine DNA sequencing. The conference originated from a collaboration between Michael A. Goldman and three Genentech alumni. Speakers include researchers, clinicians and industry executives. Registration is open to students, professionals and the public; details are available via Eventbrite and the conference website.

Therapeutic antibodies must achieve both strong target binding and favorable developability properties such as thermostability and low hydrophobicity. While structure‑based diffusion models assist non‑iterative antibody engineering, antibodies still require costly iterative refinement. Bayesian optimization (BO) provides an uncertainty‑aware approach suited to the low‑data, high‑experiment‑cost regime, but its success depends on the choice of surrogate model and acquisition function. Prior work has not incorporated structural information, despite its benefits for non‑Bayesian iterative optimization, and it is unclear which antibody properties benefit most. This work investigates how to embed structural information into BO surrogate models, identifies tasks where it helps, compares antibody‑specific and general protein structural models, and assesses its necessity. A novel protein language‑model “soft constraint” is introduced to incorporate sequence‑only prior information.

Aberdeen Emerging Markets Equity Income Fund, Inc. (ticker AEF) resulted from the April 30 2018 consolidation of seven emerging‑markets funds into the former Aberdeen Chile Fund and now trades on the NYSE American exchange. The fund follows a multi‑cap emerging‑markets equity‑income strategy, committing at least 80% of net assets to emerging‑market equities to generate current income and long‑term capital appreciation; leverage is permitted but not currently used. As a closed‑end fund, shares may trade above or below net asset value and there is no assurance the fund will meet its investment objective. The figures are unaudited.

Police released suspect photo of Steve Stephens, 37, and asked who sees his vehicle to call 9‑1‑1 after he shot and killed Robert Godwin Sr., live‑streaming Facebook and forcing victim to say Joy Lane. CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge acceleration were associated with cardiovascular disease, pulmonary function decline, and frailty, while Horvath age showed no significant associations. CXR-Age associations were robust in adults as young as 45, unlike DNAm PhenoAge. Proteomic analysis revealed distinct protein associations for each clock, including shared association with CDH13. CXR-Age could enable opportunistic biological age screening using routine chest X-rays, potentially improving medical decisions currently based on chronological age. Limitations include lack of longitudinal data and uncertain generalizability.

PhenoID, a transformer-based pipeline, extracts and normalizes dysmorphology exam findings to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms from EHR data. It comprises an extractor (detects dysmorphic spans) and a normalizer (maps spans to HPO IDs). Trained on 3,826 annotated observations, it achieves state-of-the-art F1 of 0.717, outperforming six existing systems. Errors stem from imperfect ontology coverage, descriptive phrasing, and limited semantic understanding. Span extraction limits performance, with normalizer achieving 0.82 F1 when given gold truth spans. The system handles overlapping and disjoint terms but struggles with combined cases. Negation detection is highly accurate (98.4%). Future work explores LLMs to improve extraction and generalization.

SpaceX’s Falcon 9 will launch HPE’s “Spaceborne Computer,” a commercial supercomputer, to the International Space Station on Monday. The system can perform about one trillion calculations per second—30–100 times more powerful than a typical desktop—and will test onboard data processing to reduce Earth‑space communication bottlenecks for high‑resolution satellite imagery. Unlike previous space computers, it uses standard hardware with software that monitors radiation and makes adjustments to stay safe. Engineers expect the computer to be powered on around September 4 and will run 2½‑hour functional tests before a year‑long evaluation. Success could enable more powerful space computers and future use on Mars missions where communication delays are a challenge.
