Researchers manipulated a nutrient used by malaria parasites in the drinking water of drug‑treated mice and found that limiting this resource prevented the emergence of drug‑resistant strains even when resistance was present. Competition between drug‑sensitive and resistant parasites drove the effect: without the nutrient, resistant parasites failed to grow in mixed infections, while limiting the nutrient alone did not eliminate resistant parasites in single‑strain infections. The study demonstrates that ecological manipulation can extend the useful life of existing drugs and suggests identifying nutrients that resistant strains require more of, then integrating resource‑limiting interventions into drug‑development pipelines. The work was supported by the Institute of General Medical Science.

StatsCan reported London‑St. Thomas unemployment rose to 5.5 % in September, labour force down from a year ago. About 75 % of residents aged 25‑54 are employed, lowest among Ontario cities. King’s College study found roughly half of working adults have permanent jobs; rest are part‑time, temporary, contract or self‑employed. Precarious work linked to stress, poorer health and strained family life, especially youth and minorities. Men 25‑54 participation fell to 76.9 %, low. Ontario added 35,000 jobs, lowering its rate to 5.6 %, lowest since 2000. Canada’s rate stayed at 6.2 %. A survey of 800 London residents confirmed only half have secure employment and showed depression among precarious workers.

The passage describes a method and apparatus for automatic, near‑real‑time classification of objects represented by three‑dimensional (3D) point clouds generated by a chirped LIDAR system. In the disclosed method a 3D point cloud of an object is obtained, a surface normal is extracted at a point to define a translational‑ and rotational‑invariant coordinate system, and values of one or more feature variables (α, β, θ, ρ, ψ) are measured in that coordinate system. A first classification statistic (a spin image) is computed from the feature variables and matched to a set of spin‑image templates for N known classes using linear discriminant analysis (LDA) dimensionality reduction and a k‑d tree nearest‑neighbor search. A second classification statistic (a covariance matrix) is computed from the same feature variables and matched to a set of covariance matrices arranged in clusters, each cluster representing one of the N classes, again using a k‑d tree nearest‑neighbor search. If the first and second classifiers assign different classes, a third classification statistic (iterative closest point, ICP) is computed by fitting the point cloud to occluded model point clouds for only the two conflicting classes; the class that yields the smallest root‑mean‑square distance is selected. After the object is assigned to a class, a device is operated based on that class (e.g., display of the class, control of a vehicle, or guidance of a projectile). The apparatus comprises a laser source, an optical splitter that produces transmitted and reference signals, an optical coupler that directs the transmitted beam and receives the return signal, a balanced photodetector that receives the reference and return signals, and a processor that performs the classification steps. The classification method is validated experimentally with five object classes (cone, cube, pipe, box, pistol) and with a more challenging set of similar objects, achieving high correct‑classification rates.

NVIDIA's RTX 50 series, built on the Blackwell architecture, introduces FP4 quantization to halve memory usage while delivering over twice the performance of the previous generation, enabling models like FLUX.dev to run on a broader range of GPUs. The new fourth‑generation RT Cores double ray‑triangle intersection throughput and support features such as the Opacity Micromap Engine, Linear Swept Spheres for hair, and Mega Geometry for real‑time ray tracing of Nanite‑style high‑detail meshes. Mega Geometry addresses cluster‑based LOD updates and high object counts via Cluster‑Level Acceleration Structures and Partitioned TLAS, reducing BVH build overhead by two orders of magnitude. The architecture also adds Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 for better GPU utilization, an AI Management Processor that offloads scheduling from the CPU, and enhanced video capabilities including 4:2:2 chroma sampling, ninth‑generation NVENC with AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and DisplayPort 2.1b for up to 80 Gbps. Power‑management improvements include fine‑grain power gating, accelerated frequency switching 1000× faster, and low‑latency sleep states that can yield up to 50 % power savings. DLSS 4 introduces Multi‑Frame Generation generating up to three extra frames per rendered frame, a transformer‑based model for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction and DLAA, and reduced VRAM usage. Neural shaders are integrated via the Cooperative Vectors API, enabling RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7× compression), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (real‑time subsurface scattering) and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI face rendering). The flagship GB202 chip contains 92.2 B transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090, with other variants GB203 and GB205 powering the RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5070 respectively.

Cell phone ownership among children varies widely by country. In Germany, 51% of 6‑13‑year‑olds own a mobile phone, but few have smartphones before high school. In the US, 45% of children 10‑12 have a smartphone with a service plan; 22% start at age 10, 15% at 9 or 11, and 16% at 8. In Europe, 46% of 9‑16‑year‑olds own a smartphone, with differences in school restrictions (Italy and the UK limit use; Denmark uses them for class work). Children in Portugal were most affected by cost‑saving measures. South Korean data show 72% of 11‑12‑year‑olds own a smartphone, spending up to 5.4 hours/day; Taiwanese ownership rises from 45% at age 11 to 71% at 15. Turkish parents differ: 19.5% think ages 6‑11 are appropriate, 59.8% prefer 12‑17. In South Africa, 81% of secondary‑school students have a phone; Ghana has 18.8% of boys and 12.9% of girls; Malawi 10.4% of boys and 6.2% of girls. Australian primary‑school children have a median phone‑ownership age of 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no universally correct age for a first phone, recommends limiting digital media for children under 18‑24 months to video‑chatting, limiting screen time for 2‑5‑year‑olds to one hour daily, and advises monitoring content, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping meals screen‑free.

The passage discusses the development of a new classical embedded atom method (EAM) potential for the ternary W-H-He system for radiation damage simulations in fusion reactors. Tungsten is a candidate plasma-facing material but faces challenges from irradiation damage, gas bubble formation, embrittlement, and tritium retention. Existing potentials (Bonny, Yang, Li) have limitations including overestimated relaxation volumes and imprecise void descriptions. The new potential extends the Mason W-H potential (which accurately reproduces DFT binding energies and relaxation volumes) to include helium interactions. The fitting method uses a generalized Finnis-Sinclair potential with negative electron density values, a loss function balancing defect and gaseous properties, and an importance sampling optimization algorithm combining Gaussian Mixture Models with Simplex minimization. DFT data was sourced from literature and generated using VASP with specific computational parameters. The parameterization incorporates ZBL stopping model priors, constraints on W-He interactions, specialized functional forms for helium embedding, and balanced fitting to both low-pressure virial coefficients and high-pressure hcp helium DFT data. The H-He potential was fitted to DFT dimer binding energies.

Metlakatla Indian Community grant writer Alexis Wagner is one of five residents from Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat and Metlakatla being trained as home energy assessors for a $25 program run by the Renewable Energy Alaska Project (REAP) in partnership with Southeast tribes. Using a tablet, they inventory appliances, windows, occupancy and body heat to identify low‑cost improvements such as LED light replacements, insulated coffee pots and other “energy‑vampire” reductions. The assessments aim to cut electric bills by roughly 10 % for diesel‑dependent households. The Home Energy Leader Program runs through July 31 and seeks to make energy upgrades more affordable and accessible in remote Alaskan villages.

Commercial property owners in Southern Nevada have been charged several trash fees by Republic Services without approval from local lawmakers. The Las Vegas City Council plans to introduce an ordinance to codify these fees, which include a $65.10 commercial container delivery fee, a $65.10 removal fee, a $100.15 exchange fee, and a $107.42 industrial dry run fee. Republic Services, the sole waste hauler in Clark County and the cities of Las Vegas, North Las Vegas and Henderson, reports these supplemental fees annually to municipalities, but elected officials say they cannot recall approving them. Some cities indicated the ordinance will address the issue, while Henderson officials said the fees possibly violate the ordinance.

This Mendelian randomization (MR) study examined causal relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM). Using GWAS summary data from European populations, bidirectional MR analyses were performed. First, causal relationships between 211 gut microbiota taxa and FM were assessed. Six taxa showed causal effects: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales were associated with reduced FM risk (protective), while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 increased FM susceptibility (risk). No reverse causality was detected.

Second, MR analysis of 1,400 plasma metabolites identified 82 metabolites associated with FM (44 known, 24 metabolite ratios, 14 unknown). Among known metabolites, categories included 10 amino acids, 2 carbohydrates, 2 cofactors/vitamins, 19 lipids, 2 nucleotides, and 9 exogenous substances. Pathway enrichment highlighted three main metabolic pathways: caffeine metabolism, α‑linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism, and synthesis/secretion/inactivation of glucagon‑like peptide‑1 (GLP‑1) and incretin. In the caffeine pathway, 5‑Acetylamino‑6‑formylamino‑3‑methyluracil (AFMU) appeared protective, whereas 7‑Methylxanthine and 1‑Methylxanthine were risk‑associated. In the ALA pathway, eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and stearidonic acid (SDA) were protective. In the GLP‑1 pathway, EPA and oleoyl‑ethanolamide (Oleoyl‑EA) were identified, with EPA protective and Oleoyl‑EA risk‑associated.

Third, MR analysis of the six gut microbiota taxa against the 82 metabolites revealed multiple causal relationships. Family Enterobacteriaceae and order Enterobacteriales were linked to 2,3‑dihydroxypyridine, 1‑stearoyl‑2‑oleoyl‑GPE (18:0/18:1), palmitoylcholine, and the threonine to α‑ketobutyrate ratio. Mediation analysis using multivariable MR indicated that 2,3‑dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine mediated 14.91% and 12.34% of the effect of Enterobacteriaceae/Enterobacteriales on FM, respectively.

The discussion emphasizes that disruptions in caffeine metabolism, ALA metabolism, and GLP‑1/incretin pathways may contribute to FM pathogenesis via inflammation, oxidative stress, and energy metabolism. Oxalate may also be a potential risk factor for FM. Dietary recommendations derived from the findings include limiting caffeine intake, increasing omega‑3 fatty acid consumption, adopting a low glycemic index diet, and reducing high‑oxalate foods.

Limitations include lack of demographic details for subgroup analysis, reliance on European ancestry cohorts, and need for further experimental validation. In conclusion, this MR study identified specific protective and risk gut microbiota taxa, 82 FM‑associated plasma metabolites, and two mediating metabolites (2,3‑dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine), linking gut microbiota to FM through metabolic pathways and suggesting potential dietary interventions.

Guinness partners with Arsenal striker Thierry Henry for its Made of Black campaign in Nigeria and Africa, promoting those embodying the Made of Black spirit. Henry, a PFA Player and three‑time FWA Footballer of Year, will headline activations and EPL broadcasts. MTV Base campaign defines Black as an attitude.

This patent application discloses magnet management systems for MRI-compatible implantable medical devices, particularly hearing prostheses such as cochlear implants. The devices include a magnet apparatus and a body encompassing the magnet, with structural components configured to move away from one another upon initial rotation of the magnet when subjected to external magnetic fields during MRI imaging. This movement limits further rotation of the magnet beyond the initial rotation by creating resistance through an elastomeric body material surrounding the components. The structural components include plates that sandwich the magnet, where torque applied to the magnet creates a camming action driving the plates apart, which is counterbalanced when the plates reach equilibrium due to resistance from the body. The housing may be made of silicone or other elastomeric material, and in some embodiments includes a slit for magnet insertion and removal. The devices resist rotation of the magnet relative to the body in at least one plane when subjected to externally generated magnetic fields that impart torque onto the magnet. The teachings are applicable to cochlear implants, bone conduction devices, middle ear implants, and other sensory supplement medical devices.

Activist investor TCI cut Zodiac Aerospace's valuation to 7-10 euros from 10 euros, citing a first-half loss and unrealistic forecasts, while pressuring Safran to drop its buyout offer above 10 euros.

Shares rose over 3% after the announcement. Dell plans to ship $20 billion worth of AI servers in fiscal 2026, double last year's sales.

Three bullish candlestick patterns—Bearish Engulfing Pattern, Three Outside Down Pattern, and Bullish Harami—were backtested on the S&P 500 (SPY) from 1993 to October 2021. The Bearish Engulfing Pattern showed the highest CAGR at 5% with a 71% win ratio over 296 trades, the Three Outside Down Pattern had a 78% win ratio over 112 trades, and the Bullish Harami had a 76% win ratio over 306 trades. The author argues that while many candlestick patterns lack quantified tests, these three patterns demonstrate positive results and can be used in trading strategies.

Turkish authorities issued detention warrants for 133 former public servants over alleged links to the Gülen movement, citing ByLock app usage. Warrants targeted personnel from the Finance and Labor ministries across 11 provinces. Additional detentions included 14 women, 18 teachers, and 19 military personnel in separate operations. Since the July 15, 2016 coup attempt, 50,510 people have been arrested and 169,013 face legal proceedings on coup charges, with over 150,000 suspended or dismissed.

QuantifiedStrategies.com’s recent posts describe market‑timing models and trading strategies—including Sy Harding’s seasonal timing, Yale Hirsch’s best six‑months model, the Coppock Curve, Fabian model, PENTAD model, SuperTrend indicator, and Bitcoin timing—along with related topics such as backtesting, regime indicators, risk management and algorithmic trading; the site is managed by full‑time traders Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette.
Appellants withdrew their appeal from Supreme Court orders by stipulation; the Court ordered the appeal withdrawn.

The Titan V outperforms the Titan Xp and GTX 1080 Ti in benchmarks like Fire Strike (32,774 vs ~28,000 points) despite lower clocks, using Volta architecture with HBM2 memory (652.8 GB/s bandwidth). Moyes urged Sunderland's relegation‑threatened players to create chances for Jermain Defoe, who has 14 of the club's 24 league goals. Sunderland have one win in 11 games, sit bottom, seven points from safety with 10 left; four are against bottom‑six sides. Next: at Watford, home vs Leicester, then home vs Manchester United.

RSI (Relative Strength Index) measures price momentum via gains and losses over a period; its values range 0‑100, with above 70 indicating overbought and below 30 oversold, and it generates bullish/bearish divergence signals. Backtests show RSI works best on very short periods (2‑3 days) for short‑term trading. ADX (Average Directional Movement Index) is a non‑directional indicator developed by Welles J. Wilder that estimates trend strength using DMI+, DMI‑, and ADX components; optimal performance uses short periods of 5‑10 days and a threshold around 30‑40 for strong trends. IBS (Internal Bar Strength) gauges the closing price’s position between the bar’s high and low (0‑1 scale); low values are bullish and high values bearish, serving as a mean‑reversion tool. Simple IBS strategy (buy when IBS <0.2, sell when IBS >0.8) yields a profit factor of 1.92. Backtests on QQQ (Nasdaq‑100 proxy) for IBS produced an average 0.78% per trade, 12.1% CAGR, 38% market exposure, and 32% risk‑adjusted return. On SPY, RSI achieved 0.98% avg gain, 7.5% CAGR, 41% exposure, 18% risk‑adjusted return; ADX achieved 6.5% CAGR, 63% exposure, 10.3% risk‑adjusted return. Combining two of the three indicators on SPY yielded 270 trades, 0.86% avg gain, 56% risk‑adjusted return with only 14% exposure; the only losing year was 2018 (-5.5%). On QQQ the combined approach produced 1.3% avg gain with no losing years since 2000. The passage notes that no “Holy Grail” trading strategy exists, but RSI, ADX, and IBS are among the best short‑term indicators, complementing each other for mean‑reversion and trend‑following strategies.

Former Glenwood School in Erie is now Erie Federal Credit Union’s headquarters and ninth branch. The credit union held a ribbon‑cutting today. Services include banking, loans, a drive‑through ATM and a community room retaining the school’s feel. CEO Brian Waugaman noted local contractors and historic preservation. Beluga whales Qila and Aurora died at Vancouver Aquarium in November 2016 from an unidentified toxin, not bacteria or viruses; researchers collected their DNA to sequence a beluga genome, which may aid preservation and conservation. The study was published in Genes.

Citadel Securities hired Anthony Cronin from Societe Generale to head Treasuries trading in Europe, expanding market-making across European and Asian hours. The firm, which began dealing in off-the-run Treasuries last year, aims to become a primary dealer and one of the top global dealers in U.S. government debt. It has 100 U.S. Treasuries clients across 17 countries and expects that number to double. Since starting direct market-making with investors in 2016, it has tripled counterparties to over 450 and quadrupled average daily volume. In 2017, it traded $6 trillion in Treasuries. It also recently hired Michele How for fixed-income sales in London and Daniel Gottlander from Citigroup to lead U.S. interest-rate swaps trading.

After last year's Brexit and Trump surprises, France's National Front leader Marine Le Pen may profit from recent unrest before the spring presidential election. Conservative rival François Fillon is weakened by a scandal over his wife's parliamentary salary. In February, a black youth alleged police rape, sparking riots in French suburbs; nearly 250 arrests and over 50 violent incidents in roughly 30 towns near Paris occurred in one night, per a secret interior report. The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures momentum by subtracting a longer exponential moving average (typically 10‑day) from a shorter one (3‑day) of the Accumulation/Distribution Line (ADL). The ADL is derived from a money‑flow multiplier, money‑flow volume and a cumulative sum. The oscillator oscillates around zero; values above zero indicate buying pressure and below zero selling pressure. Entry signals are generated by zero‑line crossovers and by bullish or bearish divergences.  

Backtests on the S&P 500 of three strategies produced modest results. A basic zero‑crossover strategy with optimized 10‑day/20‑day averages yielded a 2.4% CAGR over 20 years. The inverse approach using 10‑day/50‑day averages generated 287 trades, an average gain of 0.54 % per trade, a profit factor of 1.76 and a maximum drawdown of 37 %. A strategy combining the oscillator with a two‑day RSI below 5 (or RSI below 20 with the oscillator above zero) produced about 216 trades, a 0.3 % average per trade, a profit factor of 1.6 and drawdowns of 17–18 %.  

Overall, the tested Chaikin Oscillator strategies demonstrated limited predictive power on the S&P 500, although the indicator can still reflect accumulation versus distribution.

Players acknowledged frustration with scoring despite creating opportunities, noting missed chances like a crossbar hit. They expressed relief at avoiding extensive travel in the Eastern Conference, believing road games help them focus better. Zach Parise cited turnovers and perimeter passing as issues needing correction, while emphasizing they controlled play but need to execute better and take more shots. Brock Ternes, a University of Kansas researcher, surveyed 864 Kansans and found private well owners (48%) water more during droughts than municipal customers (52%). Well ownership correlates with increased irrigation use and varying conservation. Ternes says higher water‑supply awareness leads to consumption, but does not disqualify them as environmentalists. The High Plains Aquifer is over‑pumped and may not support irrigation in southwestern Kansas within 25 years unless pumping declines. He suggests groundwater stewardship requires timing of extractions and that well owners are a social group with drought responses. Ternes will present at the 2017 ASA meeting in Montreal.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS) that uses artificial‑intelligence and machine‑learning techniques to safely control autonomous vehicle operations. The AVMS receives sensor data from on‑board and remote sensors, builds and maintains a multi‑layered, three‑dimensional internal map of the vehicle’s environment, and generates a plan of action to achieve a goal while considering safety. To improve safety the system evaluates “what‑if” scenarios by creating modified copies of the internal map, determines confidence scores for AI‑model predictions by comparing inferring data to training data, and dynamically controls sensor behavior (e.g., field of view, resolution, data rate) via instructions sent through a sensor interface. The system also uses reinforcement‑learning models governed by a safety sanity index and interruptible commands to override unsafe actions. The AVMS comprises subsystems for sensor interface, localization, perception, planning, control, and information output, each communicating through defined interfaces. The disclosed embodiments include methods, systems, and non‑transitory computer‑readable media. The application is a continuation of earlier related filings.

Leon Cooperman, chairman and CEO of Omega Family Office, says we are in the late innings of a bull market where bubbles can form and risks rise. He cited Warren Buffett's 1999 warning about crowds attracted to stocks by momentum rather than fundamentals. Cooperman noted that investor mood and AI valuations are similar to that warning period, calling AI valuations "ridiculously high." Several large U.S. school districts recently approved teachers union contracts providing raises but later discovered insufficient funds to cover them. Philadelphia Public Schools narrowly avoided a strike in August by agreeing to 3% annual raises, then sought permission to borrow up to $1.5 billion to meet contractual and other expenses, incurring about $15 million in extra interest due to a state budget delay. Methods and apparatus for providing ACK/NACK feedback in a wireless network with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station sends to a user equipment (UE) information indicating PDCCH monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether ACK/NACK feedback across TRPs is allowed, rules for performing ACK/NACK feedback bundling across TRPs, and a DAI definition for interpreting DAIs transmitted by the TRPs (indicating whether DAIs are joint across TRPs or independent per TRP). The UE receives this configuration and, when bundling is allowed, determines a codebook size and transmits a joint ACK/NACK feedback in a PUCCH based on the rules, or transmits individual ACK/NACK feedbacks to each TRP. In multi-TRP scenarios, DAIs can be joint (count across all TRPs and carriers) or independent (count per TRP), affecting codebook size determination. The disclosure covers both joint and separate feedback configurations, with details on determining codebook size from PDCCH monitoring occasions and DAI values.

C‑BerryTrans is a C++ code that computes the Berry curvature (Ω) and the related anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) directly from WIEN2k output. It extracts eigenvalues and momentum‑matrix elements from WIEN2k, evaluates Ω with a Kubo‑like formula, and integrates Ω over the full Brillouin zone weighted by the Fermi‑Dirac distribution for AHC and by an entropy function for ANC. Calculations are parallelized over k‑points using OpenMP, and band‑resolved Ω is stored in compact binary files, enabling fast post‑processing of AHC/ANC for a range of temperatures and chemical potentials in a single run. Input parameters (case, struct num, kmesh, temperature/energy windows, spin‑polarization flag, number of threads, etc.) are defined in a dedicated input file; a utility module generates the required k‑list for the full BZ and modifies WIEN2k input files to limit the energy window, reducing computational cost. The workflow consists of (i) Ω computation, (ii) binary storage of band‑resolved Ω, and (iii) post‑processing via the postBerryTrans command to obtain σ_AHC or α_ANC for specified ranges. The implementation uses standard C++ libraries (cmath, vector, chrono, omp.h, cstdlib, string) and can be extended to other DFT packages. Validation was performed on Fe, Pd, Fe₃Al and Co₂FeAl, and a visualization module (berryTrans plot.py) is provided for interactive display of weighted Ω distributions.

The passage introduces a hybrid Method of Moments (MoM) and Generalized Scattering Matrix (GSM) framework for analyzing multiscale electromagnetic problems involving antennas embedded in large structures like radomes, reflectors, or biological tissues. Traditional hybrid approaches model the large structure with T-matrix and the antenna with MoM, but this becomes inefficient for large irregular environments. The proposed method inverts these roles, solving the large environment with MoM while representing the antenna via its GSM. This reduces unknowns by encapsulating antenna details in a compact GSM representation and enables modular reuse of antenna data. The framework can extend to specialized variants including a GSM-PO hybrid for large reflectors and a GSM + T-matrix hybrid. The approach aims to bridge full-wave rigor with system-level efficiency, offering a versatile tool for advanced antenna system design.

The Single/Double Offense uses double and down screens to free shooters. NBA teams prefer "Show and Recover" over switching to prevent mismatches. The defense involves dictating shooter direction away from their preferred side, with specific show and recover techniques against double and single screens. After screens, defenders recover to deny post positions and maintain ball-man vision. Total disruption is achieved through wing traps that force offensive players into freelance situations. Contact switches, snuggle denials, and triangle positions are used in defensive rotations to counter the offense's various options.

Pop singer Helgi Bjornsson, known for the 1980s hit “I Do Like the Rain,” defended the song on national TV as Reykjavik endures its worst May‑June weather in a century. Ermotti added that UBS will keep providing annual shareholder guidance, and analysts view the stance as a sign of financial strength while warning that balancing regulatory compliance with investor expectations could be challenging if market conditions deteriorate.

The Russian naval officer seized the American bark Cape Horn Pigeon on 10 September at 46°30′ N, 146°35′ E, about 125 miles off Sagalien Island, for whaling in the closed Okhotsk Sea. The vessel was taken to Vladivostok, where the crew was landed without food or shelter. Captain Scullen claimed $45,000 for profit from five whales lost; the Imperial ministry of marine regarded $2,500 as sufficient indemnification for the actual loss caused by the temporary detention. A U.S. chargé d'affaires alleged that the crew was left without lodging, but the Russian authorities stated that the captain himself had declined the assistance offered. The United States legation requested an investigation and humanitarian aid. Employer Identification No. 94-2404110) headquartered at One Apple Park Way, Cupertino, California. Services include the App Store, Mac App Store, TV App Store, Watch App Store, Apple Music, Apple TV+ (launched November 2019), Apple Arcade, Apple Card, Apple News+, Apple Pay, and iCloud. President Trump told the UN General Assembly that the United States, the world’s most powerful nation after spending over $2.5 trillion to rebuild its military, emphasizes sovereignty, patriotism, and national foundations. He highlighted domestic achievements: the lowest unemployment in over half a century, six million jobs added, rising wages, a 2.5‑million‑person reduction in poverty, and the United States becoming the leading oil and gas producer. On trade, he cited the US‑Mexico‑Canada Agreement replacing NAFTA, new deals with Japan and the UK, and said the US imposed $500 billion in tariffs on Chinese goods while accusing China of failing to liberalize, stealing intellectual property, and causing a loss of 4.2 million manufacturing jobs and $15 trillion in trade deficits. He announced the withdrawal from the Iran nuclear deal, new sanctions on Iran, and a coalition of 55 countries supporting the Venezuelan opposition while describing Venezuela’s humanitarian crisis. He discussed illegal immigration, border‑security cooperation with Mexico and Central American nations, and condemned open‑border activism. He warned that socialism and communism have killed millions and affirmed America will never become socialist. The speech also covered support for LGBTQ rights, women’s economic empowerment, religious freedom, opposition to taxpayer‑funded abortion, and the refusal to ratify the UN Arms Trade Treaty while upholding the Second Amendment. He concluded by urging world leaders to prioritize their nations’ sovereignty and prosperity.

The lecture restates the Weierstrass M‑test: if a sequence of functions \(f_j\) on a subset of \(\mathbb R\) satisfies \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) for all \(x\) and \(\sum M_j\) converges, then \(\sum f_j\) converges uniformly. An example shows that the series \(\sum\cos(160^j x/4^j)\) is bounded by \(4^{-j}\) and therefore converges uniformly to a continuous function.  

A series of functions converges uniformly precisely when its partial sums converge uniformly. For a power series \(\sum a_j (x-x_0)^j\) with radius of convergence \(\rho\), the lecture proves that on any closed interval \([x_0-R,x_0+R]\) with \(0<R<\rho\) the series converges uniformly; the proof applies the M‑test after bounding the terms by \(|a_j|R^j\) and using the root test (since \(R/\rho<1\)). Consequently, inside the radius the series can be differentiated and integrated term by term, and termwise differentiation preserves the radius \(\rho\).  

The lecture then states the Weierstrass Approximation Theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) is a uniform limit of polynomials. The proof constructs a “delta‑like” sequence \(q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n\) with \(\int_{-1}^1 q_n=1\) that concentrates near the origin, defines \(p_n(x)=\int_0^1 f(t)q_n(t-x)\,dt\), shows each \(p_n\) is a polynomial, and uses uniform continuity of \(f\) together with the properties of \(q_n\) to prove \(p_n\to f\) uniformly on \([0,1]\).

Louisville officials warn residents not to set off fireworks on Independence Day because the smoke creates particle pollution that can linger, aggravate asthma and other respiratory issues, and sometimes exceeds federal air‑quality limits. Airborne and exploding fireworks are illegal within city limits. The combined effect of many small fireworks can produce more pollution than the city’s own display; the last exceedance occurred in 2015.

The court found claims 1, 2, and 3 of the Curtis & Cook patent (No. 285,116) for portable elevated railroads void for anticipation based on evidence of prior use at Camden Iron Works in 1866. Claim 4, covering a main elevated track in combination with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler, was found valid and infringed by the defendant's structure. The defendant failed to rebut the presumption of patentability, and a decree was entered in the plaintiff's favor regarding claim 4.

The Whiteness Group at Kenyon College, founded by student Juniper Cruz, a Queer Afro‑Latinx Muslim, aims to address white privilege and educate on deconstructing whiteness for anti‑racist action. The group, run through the Snowden Multicultural Center, drew about 50 students to its first meeting. Ground rules prohibit white members from asking people of color questions and require whites to answer such questions themselves. A second meeting featured chaplain Rachel Kessler, who wrote that shame or fear among whites are unproductive for combating racism. The group seeks to foster sustainable activism.

The Supreme Court appeared largely sympathetic to a Colorado counselor challenging the state's ban on conversion therapy for minors. A majority of justices seemed to agree with the counselor, Kaley Chiles, that the ban discriminates against her based on views she expresses in therapy. However, several justices suggested sending the case back to lower courts for further examination rather than striking down the law outright. Key issues debated included whether Chiles has standing given no enforcement, whether the ban regulates speech or medical treatment, and potential viewpoint discrimination. Chiles argues she helps clients reduce unwanted attractions or become comfortable with their bodies, while Colorado contends the law protects minors from harmful practices.

Data strobe pins DDR[0]_DQS[3:0] and DDR[1]_DQS[3:0] are outputs when writing and inputs when reading DDR memory, synchronizing 32‑bit bus transfers. Chip‑select pins have on‑die termination with pulldown active during reset, disabled after release. Some pins have pullup enabled in reset, disabled after reset, and may switch to pulldown after reset. Data mask pins DDR[1]_DQM[3:0] correspond to upper, middle, and lower bytes. I, O, Z, S, GND, A, MM, DSIS denote signal types; IPD, IPU, DIS denote internal pull states.

This study developed a cost-effective citizen science approach to monitor microbial contamination in household tap water across China. Fifty tap water samples were collected from 19 provinces between December 2020 and August 2021, including opportunistic samples after the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa. Using a culture-independent 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding approach optimized for low-biomass samples, 22 of 50 samples tested positive for microbial DNA, yielding 7,635 Amplicon Sequence Variants. Pathogenic bacteria including Mycobacterium spp., Acinetobacter spp., and Legionella spp. were detected in all PCR-positive samples. Additional pathogens (Salmonella enterica) and toxin-producing cyanobacteria (Microcystis spp.) were found in samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou following extreme weather events. The study demonstrates the utility of citizen science in enhancing microbial monitoring and supporting water safety public health strategies.

After losing the finals, the speaker was disappointed yet happy for his brother’s win. He values the off‑ice time with his teammate’s family, emphasizes trust as the key factor for their line’s cohesion throughout the season, and credits both goalies, especially Giggy, for their team’s success.

Dr. Pasvolsky said respect for international obligations inherent in proposals and might be enumerated; Honduras and Chile ambassadors discussed inclusion of “respect for treaties” in proposals, disagreeing on whether it is part of international law; Venezuela corrected a misattribution; minutes approved. Sixteen years ago a pickup crashed near California‑Mexico border, leaving Mexican boy, 18‑20, in San Diego hospital; nurses named him Pancho. Story spread, and McAllen woman recognized his photo on Facebook group, messaging Houston cousin asking if he was Gilberto.

Quarters coverage is a 4‑deep, 3‑underneath zone that uses cornerbacks on the #1 receivers, safeties on the #2 receivers while reacting to run plays, outside linebackers on the flats, and a middle linebacker as the hook defender. The scheme is designed to stop pass‑heavy offenses and allow fast, responsive play. Offenses exploit it by throwing to the flats and the deep middle of the field, using QB reads of linebacker drops, hitch routes, and aggressive safety play for play‑action shots. Overload concepts, 3‑level play‑action reads, and clearing safeties to open the middle of the field also stress the coverage. Five example plays illustrate these ideas: a BYU PA Wide Zone double‑verts sluggo, a Texas Red‑Zone stick with backside option route, an Ohio State 2×2 shallow sting, a Georgia 2×2 Colt Y leak, and a Wake Forest trips‑bunch play‑action slot cross.

Child care academies in North Carolina are providing accelerated pathways for early childhood educators. Operating in 11 counties, these programs lasting two to six weeks offer training at little to no cost to participants. Two models exist: the classroom-ready model requires 20+ hours and qualifies graduates to work in licensed facilities, while the teaching credential model additionally provides college credit (EDU 3119) that transfers to all 58 community colleges, qualifying graduates as lead teachers.

The programs address staffing shortages affecting 60% of licensed child care providers in the state. A $1.476 million pilot for expansion was included in the House budget but did not make the final version. The Division of Child Development and Early Education offers grants up to $50,000 for colleges implementing academies.

Programs in Wayne and Johnston counties receive Camber Foundation funding (~$1,040 per student) and have graduated 63 students, with most entering child care or pursuing further education. McDowell County's teaching credential academy cost $500-600 per student, with six graduates and four entering classrooms directly. Durham County's six-week bilingual program cost $1,264 per student and was oversubscribed with 140 applicants for 20 slots.

The academies aim to address workforce gaps while providing debt-free entry into the field, with opportunities for continued education toward associate degrees. More than a dozen additional community colleges have expressed interest in developing programs.

The passage is a continuation patent application describing object sortation systems and methods. The invention provides a method of processing objects using a programmable motion device that acquires an object from a plurality of mixed objects at an input area, perceives identifying indicia on the object, assigns an intermediate station to a destination location responsive to the indicia, and moves the acquired object toward the intermediate station. An object processing system is also disclosed that includes at least one programmable motion device for acquiring an object and a processor for dynamically assigning an intermediate location for the object, where the intermediate location is dynamically associated with a destination location. Another method includes acquiring an object from an input station, identifying the object, assigning an intermediate station responsive to the indicia, and moving the object using a first automated carriage toward the intermediate station, with the intermediate station associated with a destination location.

The disclosed systems employ robotic arms or other programmable motion devices, perception units (cameras, scanners, drop‑camera units) to read object indicia, stacks of collection bins, and central controllers that assign and reassign bins to destinations based on heuristics, historical trends, and real‑time system state. Bins are not pre‑assigned to fixed destinations; instead, the correspondence between intermediate containers (bins) and final destinations is changed dynamically during sortation. When a bin is full or its destination is unlikely to receive further objects, the bin is emptied and the contents are forwarded for further processing (e.g., bagging, transport).

Several embodiments are detailed: (i) single‑input‑conveyor systems with multiple sorting stations each having a robot, perception unit, and collection bins; (ii) circulating‑conveyor input loops where multiple sorters pick objects from a buffer and may return objects to the buffer; (iii) multi‑input‑conveyor and multi‑output‑conveyor configurations; (iv) shuttle‑wing sorters using reciprocally moving carriages that carry an object to a designated collection bin and tip the carriage to deposit the object; (v) scaled systems with four or eight shuttle‑wing stations, multiple robotic arms, and up to 64 collection bins, with the ability to add further parallel cells. The shuttle‑wing sorter reduces cost per divert to the hundreds‑of‑dollars range compared with prior‑art automated diverts costing thousands. The invention allows fewer sorter outputs than destinations, reduced space requirements, flexible ordering of object handling, scalability by adding sorters or parallel cells, and robustness against single‑sorter failure. Dynamic bin allocation leverages historical data, object physical characteristics, facility location, and downstream demand to optimize assignment. Human workers may still interact with bins for emptying or labeling, but the system minimizes manual labor. The overall control process continuously assigns new collection bins based on system parameters, updates object counts, and signals when bins are ready for further processing or for a human to empty. The disclosed approach aims to achieve high throughput, low cost per divert, and reduced reliance on human labor compared with conventional sortation methods.

The passage describes the SEV‑ES/SEV‑SNP Guest‑Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol used for VMGEXIT‑based communication. It defines a set of MSR‑protocol request/response functions:

* AP reset hold – the guest can request that an AP be placed in an HLT loop awaiting an INIT‑SIPI‑SIPI sequence; not allowed for SNP guests with Restricted Injection.  
* Preferred GHCB GPA – the guest asks the hypervisor for its preferred GPA; the hypervisor returns a GFN or a marker indicating no preference.  
* Register GHCB GPA – the guest registers a vCPU’s GHCB GPA before first use; the hypervisor accepts or rejects it; any previous registration is automatically removed; a mismatch must cause guest termination.  
* Unregister GHCB GPA – the guest can unregister the current GPA; the hypervisor returns the unregistered GFN, zero, or a rejection marker.  
* Page State Change – the guest supplies a Page State Change structure in the GHCB shared buffer to request private/shared transitions, PSMASH (split a 2 MiB page into 4 KiB pages), or UNSMASH (merge 4 KiB pages) for SEV‑SNP; the hypervisor updates the RMP table and returns status in SW_EXITINFO2; cur_entry/end_entry track progress.  
* Run VMPL – the guest requests execution at a specific VMPL level; availability depends on the SEV‑SNP Multi‑VMPL feature.  
* Hypervisor Feature Support – the guest queries a feature bitmap.  
* Termination – the guest requests termination with a reason code; the hypervisor should comply and may place the guest in an HLT or SHUTDOWN loop.

NAE (Non‑Automatic Exit) events are all exits that cause a #VC exception when an SEV‑ES guest runs. The guest copies minimum state (SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2, and relevant registers) into the GHCB, sets the corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits, and issues VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit, updates SW_EXITINFO fields, and returns results; the guest copies results back, advances RIP, and may inject a requested exception. Specific handling is defined for MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, IOIO_PROT (IN/OUT), #NPF/MMIO accesses, and CPUID‑intercepted instructions.

GHCB negotiation examples are provided for SEV‑ES and SEV‑SNP guests. In both cases the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 before the first VMRUN; the guest determines the encryption‑bit position via CPUID (or an MSR) and allocates a GHCB page marked shared. The guest then uses the MSR protocol to obtain a preferred GPA (if desired) and to register the GHCB GPA before writing MSR 0xc001_0130 with the GPA.

For SEV‑SNP the protocol includes a Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area that stores per‑VMPL message sequence numbers (expanded from 32‑bit to 64‑bit in a later API version) and a Guest Usage field. An EFI configuration table GUID and structure are defined for passing the secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

The SNP Guest Request NAE event lets a guest invoke the SNP_GUEST_REQUEST API through the hypervisor. It requires two hypervisor‑owned (shared) pages for request and response; the hypervisor translates the guest physical addresses to system physical addresses, assigns the response page to firmware with RMPUPDATE, processes the request, reclaims the page with SNP_PAGE_RECLAIM, and returns the firmware return code in SW_EXITINFO2. Rate‑limiting is recommended and the message sequence number must be incremented to avoid IV reuse in AES‑GCM encryption.

The document also specifies the format of the Page State Change structure (up to 253 entries), the encoding of SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2 error codes, and the mapping of VALID_BITMAP bits to GHCB field offsets. It defines the minimum required state for each NAE event, the rules for resetting VALID_BITMAP before each exit, and the standard steps for the guest #VC handler (disable preemption/interrupts, update GHCB, invoke VMGEXIT, copy back results, advance RIP).

The lecture covers smart contracts and decentralized applications (DApps) in MIT's Blockchain and Money course. Professor defines smart contracts as "promises specified in digital form" (Nick Szabo, 1996), noting they may not be "smart" or legally "contracts." The class reviews technical features comparing Ethereum to Bitcoin: Ethereum is Turing complete, account-based with state transitions, while Bitcoin uses UTXO. Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin created it at age 19; its monetary policy changed from 5 to 3 to 2 Ether per block versus Bitcoin's fixed supply. Major platforms include Ethereum ($22B market cap), EOS ($5B), and NEO (China-based). Current DApp usage remains limited (top gambling site has 1,500 daily users). ICOs raised $20-28B with thousands proposed, many failing or proving fraudulent.

Guest lecturer Larry Lessig explains contract law fundamentals: contracts involve promises exchanged for performance; the state is always present as enforcer; contracts contain implied terms enforced by law. He argues blockchain can substitute for underdeveloped legal systems and enable new markets by lowering transaction costs, citing flight delay insurance as an example. However, he emphasizes that ambiguity in contracts serves valuable purposes—allowing judges to interpret terms ex post—which smart contracts may eliminate, potentially increasing costs for complex agreements. Lessig concludes that courts must develop technical sophistication to evaluate code-based contracts, and the legal system will remain involved despite blockchain's capabilities.

In Morris v. Scott, the court held that an action on the case for malicious prosecution can lie even if the court lacked jurisdiction, provided malice and falsehood are the gravamen and the arrest is claimed as a consequence. Morris sued Scott for maliciously prosecuting him without probable cause, leading to his arrest and acquittal. The lower court nonsuited Morris for failing to aver jurisdiction. The appellate court reversed, citing authorities supporting such actions without jurisdiction and referencing a statute allowing case for trespasses affecting person or property. A new trial was ordered.

Lower highs and lower lows indicate a short‑term reversal. In backtests on the S&P 500, gold and long‑term Treasuries, holding positions longer improves average gains because of long‑term drift. A one‑day entry after a single lower‑high/lower‑low bar yields modest returns; a two‑day consecutive pattern slightly improves results in equities but not in commodities or bonds. A three‑day pattern raises average gain, profit factor and produces a low maximum drawdown. The pattern is a typical short‑term reversal, especially effective in stocks.

The court denies plaintiffs' motion to enforce a settlement agreement. Three former D.C. Department of Corrections employees sued claiming retaliatory termination for speaking to the media about the halfway-house system. Five days before the October 2001 trial, the parties reached a tentative settlement for $625,000 in exchange for dismissing First Amendment claims. The plaintiffs subsequently moved to enforce the settlement, asserting it also included their re-enrollment into the retirement system. The court finds that while the parties agreed to the $625,000 payment, they never reached a "meeting of the minds" regarding re-enrollment. The defendants never committed to re-enrollment, raised concerns about allowing non-working plaintiffs to participate in a retirement program, and never initiated the process. The absence of a written agreement and conflicting evidence about what was discussed further demonstrate no mutual assent on this issue. The court denies the motion to enforce and gives plaintiffs until September 9, 2002 to either accept the $625,000 without retirement benefits or reject the settlement and proceed to trial.

Collagen is a structural protein that makes up about 30% of the body’s protein, produced from amino acids glycine and proline together with vitamin C, zinc and copper. Natural collagen declines with age, leading many to consider supplements. The body contains about 28 collagen types; types I, II and III are the main forms in oral supplements. Collagen supplements are derived from animal sources: marine (fish, jellyfish, sponges) high in types I and III; bovine (cow) and porcine (pig) also types I and III; and chicken (type II). Hydrolysed collagen, broken into low‑molecular‑weight peptides, is considered most effective because it is quickly absorbed. Reported benefits include improved skin elasticity, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, increased bone density in post‑menopausal women, joint‑pain relief, tendon and ligament support, and possible hair growth (limited animal research). Effective daily doses are roughly 2.5 g for joint and skin health, 5 g for bone density in osteopenic/post‑menopausal individuals, and 15 g for muscle mass with resistance training. Manufacturers recommend a 12‑week minimum use and third‑party testing. Collagen production can be supported by eating protein‑rich foods, vitamin C‑rich fruits and vegetables, and bone broth.

Midline Option is an option play where the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman to decide whether to hand off to a fullback through the A‑gap or keep the ball and run through the B‑gap. Its primary strength is that the offense does not need to block that single defender, making it an effective complement to inside/outside veer schemes and creating confusion with motion. A key weakness is that the quarterback often runs into the defense, requiring a rugged runner; therefore, play‑callers must weigh the risk. The play can be run from various formations, including Flexbone sets, and a “Follow” variation adds an extra lead blocker for short‑yardage situations.

Trend Micro uncovered 89 malicious Google Chrome extensions in the official store affecting over 423,000 users. The extensions formed a botnet called Droidclub, injecting ads and exploit kits, and using a Yandex Metrica JavaScript library to record and replay victims’ browsing sessions. They can capture form data such as names, credit‑card numbers, CVV numbers, email addresses and phone numbers, excluding passwords. Earlier versions also injected Coinhive code to secretly mine Monero. The extensions spread via social‑engineering tricks and block removal by redirecting users to fake uninstall pages. Trend Micro notified Google and Cloudflare, which removed the extensions and took down the servers. Google says it blocks over 1,000 malicious extensions per month and invites user reports of suspicious extensions. The report follows similar findings by ICEBRG (four extensions with 500,000+ installs) and the discovery of Archive Poster running Coinhive in December 2017.

Soccer formations dictate player placement to balance defense and attack. Choice depends on number of players (age‑specific rules), player skill and coach’s tactical comfort. Over the past century the game has shifted toward fewer forwards, more balanced spacing, all‑around skills, greater fitness and short passes. In an 11‑a‑side match there are 10 field players; formations are denoted by the count of defenders‑midfielders‑forwards (e.g., 4‑3‑3, 4‑4‑2, 3‑4‑3). Newer notations include 4‑3‑2‑1 and 4‑6. U.S. Soccer recommends 4‑3‑3 and 4‑4‑2 for U15‑U19, 4‑3‑3 for U13‑U14, 3‑2‑3 for U9‑U12 9‑a‑side; lower ages leave formation to coach discretion. Formation, position names, placement and tactics are interlinked, requiring coaches to know positions, initially assign players and present a diagram of the intended formation.

The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope captured NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy 102 million light‑years away in Scorpius. Its center glows yellow with older, lower‑mass stars, while its spiral arms host bright blue clusters of young, massive stars; the galaxy’s colors reflect differences in stellar ages, masses and temperatures. Hubble observed the galaxy while surveying recent supernovae, and NGC 6000 has hosted two events—SN 2007ch and SN 2010as—whose faint afterglows remain detectable. An asteroid drifting across Hubble’s field of view left four thin blue‑red streaks from sequential filtered exposures. The resulting image portrays stellar life cycles together with a chance solar‑system interloper.

Patterns for distributed systems provide value by allowing developers to learn from others' mistakes, establishing shared vocabularies for communication, and enabling reusable components. Single-node patterns (sidecar, ambassador, adapter) group containers on the same machine with tight coupling. The sidecar pattern augments existing application containers, example use cases: adding HTTPS to legacy services via nginx proxies, and dynamic configuration synchronization. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between application containers and external services, such as client-side sharding with twemproxy for Redis or service discovery and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern modifies application interfaces to conform to standardized expectations for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus exporters for Redis), logging (e.g., Fluentd normalization), and health checks (e.g., MySQL query-based checks). Multi-node patterns include replicated load-balanced services for stateless applications, session-tracked services for user affinity, and sharded services for scaling stateful data storage (e.g., sharded caches and Memcache deployments). Implementation details include Kubernetes Deployments, Services, StatefulSets, ConfigMaps, and Secrets. Replicated services benefit from readiness probes and can be enhanced with caching layers (Varnish), SSL termination (nginx), and rate limiting. Sharded services improve storage utilization by distributing data across multiple replicas, with sharding functions (hashing and modulo) determining request routing. Patterns enable modularity, reusability, and maintainability through containerization.

The speaker assumes the office of President, takes the constitutional oath, and promises to rely on divine aid while acknowledging the historic tendency of office‑holders to break campaign pledges. He affirms that the Constitution rests on popular sovereignty, that government powers are limited to those expressly granted, and that individual citizens retain unalienable rights. He identifies defects in the Constitution, especially the eligibility for a second Presidential term, and declares that he will not accept a second term, arguing that short terms prevent the growth of a dangerous love of power. He explains that the veto power is a conservative instrument, to be used only to protect the Constitution, to prevent hasty legislation that ignores the popular will, and to safeguard minority rights; early Presidents employed it only for constitutional objections. He warns that the concentration of power in the executive, especially through patronage and control of the Treasury, threatens liberty, and he pledges to keep the Treasury Secretary independent, to inform Congress of any removal, and to enforce a ban on federal officers influencing elections. He advocates protecting press freedom, opposing the use of government presses for partisan purposes, and insists the President should not originate finance measures. He cautions that an exclusive metallic currency would halt social mobility, encourage usury, and damage the economy. He calls for forbearance among the states, emphasizing that District of Columbia residents are free citizens, not subjects, and that attempts by one state to control the domestic institutions of another risk disunion and civil war. He stresses that union, nurtured by a spirit of liberty and mutual confidence, is the essential guarantee of all other interests, and warns that parties become destructive beyond a certain point; he seeks a unity of the whole country rather than partisan loyalty. He expresses deep reverence for Christianity, seeing sound morals and religious liberty as vital to happiness, and thanks the Almighty for the blessings of civil and religious freedom. Concluding, he reaffirms his pledge to discharge his duties according to the best of his ability, confident in the support of a just and generous people.

Riverton Investment Corp. v. United States involved a tax refund dispute over whether payments RIC made in the 1990s to buy back management stockholders' stock were deductible compensation or non-deductible stock redemptions. The court determined that the stock was never fully "transferred" to the management stockholders in the 1980s because the Management Stockholder's Agreement restrictions—prohibiting transfer to anyone but RIC or family members, and fixing the buy-back price at 60% of book value with a guaranteed minimum—permanently restricted ownership. These non-lapse restrictions meant no taxable transfer occurred. The payments were therefore deductible as compensation, not redemptions. The court sustained RIC's objections, rejected the Magistrate Judge's recommendation, granted RIC's motion for summary judgment, and entered judgment in RIC's favor.

Patterns in software development provide reusable solutions to common problems, enable teams to learn from others' mistakes, provide shared vocabulary, and create modular components. Single-node container patterns include the sidecar pattern (augmenting applications with auxiliary containers), ambassador pattern (broker interactions with external services), and adapter pattern (modifying interfaces to conform to standards). Multi-node distributed patterns include replicated load-balanced services for reliability and scaling, and sharded services for handling large stateful datasets. These patterns help regularize distributed system development, improving reliability and agility in modern software architecture.

The study presents a structured framework for evaluating and ranking the impacts of digitalization on higher‑education quality, focusing on Vietnam. It distinguishes digitization (conversion of analog to digital), digitalization (adoption of digital tools within existing processes), and digital transformation (fundamental rethinking of educational models). Five criteria are identified: technological infrastructure, accessibility of digital resources, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and adaptability/innovation. The Spherical Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (SFAHP) is applied using pairwise comparisons from nine education experts. Steps include hierarchical construction, spherical fuzzy judgment matrices, consistency verification (threshold 10 %), weight derivation via fuzzy aggregation, and defuzzification. The resulting priority weights are: pedagogical integration = 0.236 (rank 1), student engagement = 0.212 (rank 2), accessibility of digital resources = 0.203 (rank 3), adaptability and innovation = 0.184 (rank 4), and technological infrastructure = 0.165 (rank 5). The analysis emphasizes that pedagogical integration is the most crucial factor, followed by student engagement, while highlighting the need for equitable digital access, adaptable and innovative practices, and robust infrastructure, especially in underserved regions. Strategic recommendations include fostering collaboration between educators and technologists, promoting interactive and personalized learning, enhancing digital accessibility, and investing in professional development in digital pedagogy. Limitations note reliance on expert evaluations and suggest future research incorporate broader stakeholder perspectives and explore how evolving digital pedagogy may affect prioritization. No external funding was received, and derived data are available from the corresponding author on request.
