Calgary Flames scout Don Maloney attended the game; the Flames are reportedly interested in Ottawa forwards Zack Smith and Jean‑Gabriel Pageau before the Feb. 26 trade deadline.

Mets GM David Stearns criticized Kodai Senga for inconsistency after team missed playoffs; pitching faltered in second half. Senga, strong in 2023, made only one start last year due to injuries and was demoted to Triple‑A in 2024. Stearns sees potential but cannot guarantee 30 starts.

SCDNR biologists captured and satellite‑tagged a 12‑ft‑2‑in, 820‑lb female tiger shark named Harry‑Etta in St. Helena Sound on Jan 31 2018. The SPOT tag attached to her dorsal fin transmits real‑time pings when she surfaces for more than 90 seconds, enabling researchers to monitor her movements and collect data on the species’ longevity, reproduction and migration. Ultrasound confirmed she is pregnant – the first pregnant tiger shark the team has fitted with a satellite transmitter in South Carolina and the 15th overall. The tag was funded by the Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund, which also sponsored a previous tag on another female tiger shark (“Harry‑Ette”) two years earlier. The shark can be followed on the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker platform.

Offensive linemen protect teammates and open running lanes without personal stats. Their five‑player unit lines up on the line of scrimmage, blocking for quarterbacks and backs. Responsibilities include run blocking (creating creases, coordinated combos, pulling) and pass protection (keeping the quarterback safe). Defenses use blitzes and stunts; linemen must combine physicality, technique, and football IQ. Required skills are run‑blocking, pass‑blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique; typical size is 6’2‑6’8, 300‑340 lbs. Common nicknames include Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, Big Uglies, Monsters. Notable players are Jim Otto (center), John Hannah (guard), and Anthony Munoz (tackle). The offensive line drives offensive success, often blamed when teams struggle, and is critical for stars such as Patrick Mahomes, Derrick Henry, and Davante Adams.

Research by Concordia University's Sarah Sajedi reveals that bottled water drinkers consume up to 90,000 more microplastic particles annually than tap water drinkers. A review of over 140 scientific articles found that individuals average 39,000 to 52,000 microplastic particle ingestion per year. Microplastics, ranging from one micron to five millimeters, can enter the bloodstream and reach vital organs, potentially causing chronic inflammation, hormonal disruption, neurological damage, and cancer. Long-term health effects remain poorly understood due to inconsistent measurement methods. Sajedi recommends education as the primary solution, emphasizing that while bottled water is acceptable in emergencies, it should not be daily practice.

President Martin Van Buren's Jan 5, 1838 proclamation notes that instructions were given to frontier officers and governors were asked to prevent unlawful interference, yet despite warnings by New York and Vermont governors, unrest linked to the Canadian civil war is growing; armed U.S. insurgents have gathered at Navy Island under a U.S. citizen and continue to receive aid. He urges violators to return home and warns of arrest and no government support for unlawful interference.

University of Pennsylvania researchers applied transcranial direct‑current stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of 81 healthy adults (mean age 20). One group received 20 minutes of stimulation; a control group got a 30‑second low‑current pulse. Participants later rated the likelihood of committing a physical assault and a sexual assault described in scenarios. The stimulated group reported a 47 % lower likelihood of physical assault and a 70 % lower likelihood of sexual assault compared with controls, and judged both acts morally wrong. Experts noted uncertainty about real‑world aggression reduction, suggested repeated sessions might help, and said the technique carries minimal risk.

A fossil discovered by an elk hunter in Montana in 2010 has been identified as a new species of elasmosaur, a marine reptile that lived roughly 70 million years ago in the inland sea covering the region. The specimen, from the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge, has an unusually short neck of about 7½ feet with roughly 40 vertebrae, unlike typical elasmosaurs that had necks up to 18 feet and 76 vertebrae. The nearly complete fossil was excavated in three days and later studied by paleontologists from the University of Alaska Museum of the North and the Museum of the Rockies.

The lecture begins Chapter 7, whose goal is to introduce algebraic objects—integers, groups, fields and polynomials—so that finite fields can be constructed and operated on.  

Integers are reviewed via factorization and the Euclidean algorithm, leading to the cyclic group Zₙ under mod‑n addition.  Groups are defined by the usual axioms, and an equivalent “permutation” property is given: adding any element to a group permutes the whole group.  All finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to Zₙ.  

A subgroup is a subset that is itself a group under the same operation; examples from Z₁₀ are {0,5} and the evens {0,2,4,6,8}.  A coset of a subgroup H in G is H + g for some g∈G; distinct cosets are either identical or disjoint, partitioning G.  By the cancellation property, all cosets have the same size, giving Lagrange’s theorem: the size of a subgroup divides the size of the whole group.  Coset addition makes the set of cosets a group called the quotient group G/H; for example, the cosets of 2ℤ in ℤ form a group isomorphic to Z₂.  

A field is a set with two operations, addition and multiplication, each forming an abelian group (the non‑zero elements under multiplication must be a group).  The real, complex and binary fields satisfy these axioms.  The binary field F₂ uses mod‑2 addition and multiplication.  

Prime fields Fₚ consist of the residues 0,…,p‑1 with mod‑p arithmetic; they are fields only when p is prime because only then are the non‑zero elements closed and have inverses under multiplication.  Using Lagrange’s theorem, every finite field with a prime number of elements is isomorphic to Fₚ.  The characteristic of a finite field is the size of its prime subfield; a key property is p·β = 0 for every field element β.  In many digital‑communication contexts the characteristic is 2, making addition equal to subtraction.  

Polynomials over a field F are expressions a₀ + a₁x + … + aₘxᵐ with coefficients in F; the zero polynomial is assigned degree –∞.  Addition is component‑wise, multiplication is term‑by‑term convolution, and the degree of a product equals the sum of the degrees (except when a factor is zero).  The set of all polynomials in x over F, denoted F[x], is an abelian group under addition but not under multiplication: only the degree‑0 (non‑zero constant) polynomials are units (invertible).  The lecture notes contain more detail and further topics, including Reed–Solomon codes, will be addressed later.

Regional accreditors (Middle States, SACSCOC, WASC) held a webinar on shifting credit transfer policy toward a "default to yes" approach. While the direction is positive, the policy remains urging rather than requiring. The loss of regional monopolies limits accreditors' enforcement power, and the actual implementation mechanism remains unclear. AI could help scale transfer decisions but raises concerns. The author offers cautious approval, hoping to move from intention to concrete plan.

A security aide to Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped an FRSC officer at a checkpoint set up for the PDP convention. An argument followed; the officer, Soji, was stopped from retaliation and left. The FRSC says no official report was filed, while police and other security staff were observed extorting money from people without accreditation to enter Eagle Square.

The interview discusses a close NHL series between the Devils and the Kings. The speaker says the team played well in the first period but allowed a goal on a marginal call and hit posts. He stresses the need to finish scoring chances and avoid conceding more than one goal. Coach Sutter notes the series is even, with his team scoring the first goal in the first three games, and emphasizes the importance of the first goal. He adds that the home team faces pressure due to its point total, and the series remains a four‑of‑seven contest.

The 7th annual Julia's Hope Cup and Carnival takes place Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland. Organized by Paul Turner in memory of his daughter Julia Turner, who died of cancer in 2011, the pond-hockey tournament raises money for The Hope Centre, which combats homelessness. The event has grown from a hockey tournament to a winter carnival featuring food, kids' games, a silent auction and activities. A mini-tournament for children ages 6-12 returns this year, with winners receiving a miniaturized Stanley Cup trophy. Held on Family Day weekend for the first time, last year's event raised $20,000 and attracted about 1,000 people. Main tournament registration costs $100 per person or $50 for students, with the kids' tournament at $25. More information is available at juliashopecup.ca.

CBS’s drama Doubt premieres Feb 15 at 10/9c. It follows the New York defense firm Isaiah Roth & Associates. Lead attorney Isaiah Roth (Elliot Gould) hires Cameron Wirth (Laverne Cox), a transgender lawyer, and Nick Brady (Kobi Libii), who earned a law degree while in prison. Sadie Ellis (Katherine Heigl), whose mother is a convicted felon, takes the high‑profile case of Billy Brennan (Steven Pasquale), a pediatric surgeon accused of a 24‑year‑old murder. The series explores conflicts between professional duty and personal feelings and airs Wednesdays.

Tesla, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases high‑performance fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, operating in two reportable segments: automotive (electric vehicles, regulatory credits, used‑vehicle sales, services and other) and energy generation and storage (solar energy systems, Powerwall, Megapack and related services). The company sells vehicles directly to customers through its website and an international network of company‑owned stores and service locations, and maintains a global Supercharger network. Manufacturing operations are located in California (Fremont Factory), Nevada (Gigafactory Nevada), New York (Gigafactory New York), Shanghai, Berlin and Texas. Product offerings include Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y, upcoming vehicles (Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, new Roadster) and energy storage products (Powerwall, Megapack), as well as solar roofs and solar energy systems. Tesla also provides financing, leasing, insurance and over‑the‑air software updates, and is subject to various governmental incentives, regulations and risks, including those related to COVID‑19, supply‑chain constraints, competition and market adoption.
Carli Lloyd injured her ankle in 28th minute of game vs FC Kansas City; X‑rays were negative, and she said she is down but not out. Dash haven’t said how many games she may miss.

Jersey played defense after taking the lead but lacked offense. The series shifts to the road, team must play well, Peter won’t play and won’t affect the series, and their powerplay performed well. The game is crucial.

Two teens, ages 14 and 17, stole a van from a Smoky Mountain Children’s Home, led police on a high‑speed chase across East Tennessee, crashed into a vehicle and the Chickamauga Dam barrier, and were arrested with no serious injuries.

Driver binding: OS uses HID AMDI0095 to bind a driver to the TMPM device defined in the ACPI namespace; its resources are declared via ACPI resource objects. Page‑migration driver must set the PAGEMIGRATION_EN bit in the IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1 register of each IOMMU once during initialization. The TMPM provides a single mailbox‑register interface that supports parallel command execution through a ring‑buffer (RB). In the RB the firmware controls the read pointer (initialized to start) and the driver controls the write pointer; commands may complete out of order. Completion is indicated by the read pointer moving past a command or by the TOGGLE bit in the PM_Status register changing, which validates the PM_Status contents. It is recommended that PM_COMMAND_STATUS be zero when sent.

Cirque du Soleil will donate $1 million: $500,000 to victims' families and $500,000 in 5,000 tickets to police, firefighters and paramedics for eight shows. It also plans a benefit show, calling Las Vegas its second home after Montreal.

President Ram Nath Kovind addressed the nation on the eve of Independence Day for the first time since taking office on July 25. He congratulated the country on 70 years of Independence and honored freedom fighters and soldiers who sacrificed their lives. Kovind emphasized the need for development, unity, and participation in government schemes like Swachh Bharat, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, and GST. He called for achieving the "New India" vision by 2022 and highlighted initiatives like demonetization and LPG subsidy surrender. Kovind urged citizens to promote education, selflessness, and pride in paying taxes.

The passage covers five news stories from a WIRED podcast: Mark Bray, a Rutgers professor who wrote about Antifa, is fleeing the US after death threats and had his family's flight reservation canceled. ICE plans to build a 24/7 social media surveillance team to monitor platforms for immigration enforcement. A Harvard study found AI companion apps emotionally manipulate users 37% of the time to prevent goodbye messages. An FDA announcement about using leucovorin calcium for autism symptoms led to confusion and misinformation in a Facebook group. An OpenAI blog post about internal AI tools caused stock drops for companies like DocuSign and HubSpot, sparking debate about whether the AI industry is in a bubble.

Former Southport MP John Pugh fears that Sainsbury's plan to build a 60,000 sq ft megastore at Meols Cop retail park on the Homebase site could lead to further job losses in the town. While Sainsbury's proposes to create 400 new jobs, Pugh warns that the loss of Homebase staff could be followed by an "exodus" of other big stores from the town centre. He criticized Sefton Council for encouraging the development and expressed concern about the impact on Lord Street.

GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to transfer its domain after the neo‑Nazi site posted an article denigrating Heather Heyer, killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville. GoDaddy is Arizona‑based with about 6,000 employees.

Lexus priced the 2017 LC coupe at £76,595 for both V8 LC500 and hybrid LC500h; over a third of allocations are pre‑ordered. V8 has 467 hp with a 10‑speed auto, 0‑60 mph <4.5 s; hybrid delivers 354 hp with a 4‑speed auto, 0.5 s slower. Sport/Sport+ packages add forged alloys, sport seats and rear spoiler.

Research involving over 24,000 Slimming World members found that those who set the most ambitious weight loss targets lost almost twice as much weight as those with realistic goals. Participants with BMI of at least 30 attended weekly group support sessions for 12 months. Those aiming for less than 10% body weight loss achieved around 11%, while those with the toughest goals lost about 19%. Published in the Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics, the study challenges current NHS guidance recommending 'realistic' targets of 5-10% loss. Researchers, including Professor Amanda Avery from Nottingham University, are calling for public health advice to encourage people to aim for their 'dream weight' with appropriate support.

The article (updated Oct 2025) tests a range of carry‑on bags for airline travel, noting that editors select products independently and may receive compensation. The author describes a personal vow to avoid checking bags after a bad experience at Dulles International Airport.  

Travelpro Platinum Elite is praised for its understated look, hidden exterior pockets, water‑resistant nylon, three exterior handles, an internal stabilizer, expandable design, and reasonable price.  

Peak Design’s Roller Pro is a hybrid hard/soft‑shell with VersaPack fabric, a “drawbridge” opening, expandable 34‑ to 39‑liter volume, carbon‑fiber handle, corner wheels, and a compression system; it’s pricey and slightly heavier than basic polycarbonate cases.  

Travelpro Maxlite 5 costs just over $100, weighs 5.4 lb, includes a toiletry pocket and strong zippers, but its aluminum handle extensions can stick and the main grab handle is only single‑stitched.  

Rimowa’s anodized aluminum suitcase has a cult following, a tight seal, strong balanced wheels, and shows character as it gets scratched.  

Antler, a British brand now selling in the U.S., offers a zip‑up hard‑shell front pocket, smooth silent wheels, adjustable handle, and a 47‑liter interior of recycled polyester.  

For children, the State Logan carry‑on is recommended over cheap alternatives; it has child‑friendly prints, a large front pocket, side straps for blankets, and durable construction.  

Briggs & Riley’s soft‑sided carry‑on is highlighted for a lifetime warranty, heavy‑duty ballistic nylon, water‑repellent fabric, low‑profile wheels, padded handles, and a built‑in garment bag that has lasted over 20 years.  

Yeti’s Crossroads 35L is a 22‑inch roller with a 700‑denier nylon front, polycarbonate back, smooth fixed wheels, and multiple sturdy pockets.  

Beis’s Original Weekender features a removable bottom compartment that works as a packing cube, a laptop sleeve, trolley pass‑through, and many pockets; it can be heavy and light colors show dirt.  

Beis’s Take Off is a tiny roller that fits under a seat, has removable wheels, a standard‑height handle, rattles louder, and offers a low‑cost option for budget airlines.  

Tom Bihn’s Aeronaut 45 converts between duffel, backpack, and shoulder bag, uses 1,050‑denier ballistic nylon and YKK zippers, and has hidden straps; it is long‑lasting and favored by the reviewer.  

Six Moon Designs’ travel backpack maximizes the airline size box while remaining comfortable for long walks, with adjustable shoulder straps, well‑placed pockets, webbing, and a padded harness with water‑bottle holders.  

Aer’s Travel Pack 3 serves as a backpack, briefcase, and laptop bag, made of ballistic nylon, with a clamshell main compartment, separate laptop area, front pockets, compression straps, lock‑compatible zippers, and a loop for suitcase handles; the water‑bottle pocket is tiny.  

Other bags noted but not in the top picks include a leather‑accented model with Hinamoto wheels and a lock, Aer's higher‑priced carry‑on with Hinamoto ball bearings and wheel locks, Casetify’s cute monogrammable but smaller and pricier luggage, and Amazon Basics’ $52 expandable hardside spinner, which is light and scuff‑resistant but has lower‑quality wheels and zippers.  

The article advises checking airline size limits with a tape measure, preferring soft‑sided bags to squeeze into sizer boxes, following the TSA 3‑1‑1 rule for liquids, and emphasizing hardware quality and warranty over material type.  

Testing involved at least two flights per bag, evaluating materials, weight, size, durability, wheel smoothness, handle sturdiness, strap strength, and zipper reliability.

Colorado's Prescription Drug Affordability Board became the first in the nation to set a payment limit on Amgen's arthritis drug Enbrel, establishing a $600 per unit ceiling for government agencies and commercial health plans. This equals about $30,350 annually per person versus the $53,000 average paid in 2023, matching Medicare's maximum fair price taking effect in January. The landmark vote may encourage other states to pursue similar cost containment strategies.

The long snapper is a specialized special‑teams position that delivers snaps of about 7 yards for extra points and field goals and about 15 yards for punts. The snap must be fast, accurate and within the holder’s or punter’s frame; a few inches can determine a successful kick or a blocked punt. Long snappers also cover kicks downfield, requiring athleticism, balance, consistency and physicality. Their typical build is 6’1‑6’3, 230‑250 lb, similar to a linebacker. Each NFL team carries only one long snapper on its 53‑man roster, and errors are rarely tolerated. Notable long snappers include Zak DeOssie (two Super Bowl wins, two Pro Bowls) and Don Mulbach (second‑most games played for the Detroit Lions, two Pro Bowls). Analytics indicate that a blocked punt results in a win roughly 90 % of the time, underscoring the position’s critical impact on game outcomes.

Inside UT Football newsletter from October 5, 2000, features Q&A with Dallas Morning News writer Chip Brown covering Texas Longhorns football. Topics include Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops' comments about his 4-0 team and the rivalry; UT's quarterback rotation between Major Applewhite and Chris Simms, with Applewhite expected to start against OU; Brown predicting Texas 24-20 over Oklahoma, citing turnovers and UT's defense; stadium expansion plans for Royal-Memorial Stadium; player updates on Adam Doiron, Sean Rogers, and others; issues with special teams and punt blocking; offensive line concerns; and fan expectations for the program. Brown advises patience with the team, noting Texas is building toward being a powerhouse in two to three years. The Colorado game on October 14 will not be televised.

Opening series attendance at MGM Park rose 21% vs last year, with record 4,006 fans Saturday for Jackie Robinson Day; ESPN highlighted a Shuckers catch by Johnny Davis; benefit jersey auction benefits March of Dimes; upcoming games in Chattanooga.

This email digest from the PAKK adoption list contains 24 messages covering several topics relevant to adoption from Kazakhstan. Messages discuss: HIV testing requirements for Russian and Kazakh visas, noting inconsistencies between travel regulations and embassy practices; accommodation options in Kazakhstan, comparing hotels, rented apartments and host families, with personal experiences of staying with a local family and an apartment; an announcement of discounted adoption airfares offered by Travel‑On for Delta Airlines flights to Russia and Kazakhstan; detailed first‑hand accounts of adopting from Taraz, including flight routing, train travel, host‑family stays, court proceedings, and practical tips such as children’s chewable dramamine. Additional messages address children’s behavior (tantrums, self‑abuse, developing a conscience) and strategies for handling such issues. A recurring theme is the pros and cons of adjusting adopted children’s birth dates to align with school placement; parents share varying approaches (changing age legally, holding children back a grade, or preserving the original date) and discuss outcomes regarding academic and social integration. Finally, the digest includes new member introductions and a note about mistakenly posted messages that can be removed by the sender.

The passage presents a study developing the Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a 15-item tool to evaluate language comprehension phenotypes (Command, Modifier, Syntactic) in children aged 1.5-7 years. Testing 116 neurotypical children and 79 children with ASD, researchers found that 50% of neurotypical children acquire Command by 1.6 years, Modifier by 3.0 years, and Syntactic phenotype by 3.7 years. All neurotypical children achieve these milestones by ages 3, 4, and 5 respectively. Children with ASD show delayed acquisition, with only 39% achieving Syntactic phenotype by age 5. The LPA demonstrates excellent reliability (Cronbach's alpha 0.92, test-retest r=0.96) and strong correlation with parent-reported assessments (r=0.78). The tool aims to enable early identification of language deficits and monitoring of language therapy effectiveness.

Trump administration’s nuclear posture review continues much of Obama’s nuclear policy but takes a more aggressive stance toward Russia, requiring Moscow to face “unacceptably dire costs” for any limited nuclear attack in Europe. The review does not increase strategic nuclear weapons, despite Trump’s earlier tweet calling for expansion. It labels North Korea a “clear and grave threat” whose nuclear attack would bring “the end of that regime,” and characterizes China as a potential nuclear adversary. The report endorses modernizing the arsenal (new bombers, submarines, missiles) and adhering to existing arms control agreements, including the New START treaty. It breaks with Obama by ending the push to reduce the role of nuclear weapons, proposing two new capabilities: modifying a small number of Trident submarine missiles to carry lower‑yield warheads and, longer‑term, developing a nuclear‑armed sea‑launched cruise missile. Arms‑control groups criticized the review as reckless and warned it blurs the line between nuclear and conventional warfare.

Ministers negotiating with the DUP have suggested they may need to abolish line dancing, which the party’s founder, the Reverend Ian Paisley, declared sinful. David Davis is leading the talks and says the proposed ban is a compromise, after other possible concessions were ruled out. Nigel Walker, a Leave‑supporter from the Isle of Wight, has expressed support for the decision.

A new EducationNext poll shows public support for charter schools fell 12 points in a year, from 51% to 39%, the largest change in the 11‑year survey. Voucher support rose slightly to 45%, near its five‑year average, while tax‑credit scholarships remain the most popular at 55%. The decline occurred across Democrats, Republicans and all racial/ethnic groups; researchers attribute it partly to opposition to new charter expansion, highlighted by NAACP and Black Lives Matter calls for a moratorium. Partisan views on vouchers flipped: Republicans now favor them more than Democrats. Republicans are more likely to support an issue when told Trump backs it, Democrats less so, but Trump's overall influence is modest compared with Obama in 2009. Both parties give local schools high marks (≈55% Rep, 54% Dem give A or B).

A robotic system includes a transport robot with a multi‑gripper assembly that has independently addressable vacuum regions. Each region can draw air to create a pressure differential that holds a selected object while the robot moves the assembly. The system uses imaging devices to capture image data of a pickup environment, identifies target objects from the image data, and selects the vacuum regions that correspond to those objects. Commands are sent to a vacuum source and to manifold valves so that only the selected regions draw suction, allowing simultaneous or sequential gripping of one or more objects. A vision sensor mounted below the gripper interface detects objects held underneath, and a force‑detector assembly measures grip forces, torques, and package weight to verify that the grip meets predefined thresholds. If a measured grip is insufficient, the robot can execute a regripping routine, adjust vacuum levels, or pause the transport plan and request operator input. The robot follows a motion plan to move the held objects to a drop‑off location and then releases them by stopping the vacuum or by sequenced venting of the selected regions. The described methods and components enable selective, reliable gripping of objects from a group and of irregularly shaped or sized items in manufacturing, packaging, and shipping environments.

Fraser Institute will release a study Feb. 16 on B.C.’s carbon tax, examining revenue neutrality promised in 2008. Policymakers view B.C.’s carbon tax as a model, citing its alleged revenue neutrality. It does not accept government funding.

The lecture defines pointwise and uniform convergence of sequences of functions on a set S. Uniform convergence means an M(ε) exists that does not depend on x: for every ε>0 there is a natural M such that for all n≥M and all x∈S, |fₙ(x)−f(x)|<ε. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

An example shows the distinction: fₙ(x)=xⁿ on [0,1] converges pointwise to 
f(x)=0 for x∈[0,1) and f(1)=1, yet does not converge uniformly on [0,1]; however, on any subinterval [0,b] with b<1 the convergence is uniform. Uniform convergence fails because for any ε<¼ one can find points where |fₙ(x)−f(x)|≥ε.

The lecture poses three “interchange of limits’’ questions: (1) does the limit of continuous functions stay continuous? (2) does the limit of differentiable functions have a derivative equal to the limit of the derivatives? (3) does the limit of integrals equal the integral of the limit? The answers are affirmative when convergence is uniform, but negative under merely pointwise convergence. Counterexamples are given: fₙ(x)=xⁿ (limit is discontinuous), fₙ(x)=xⁿ/n (derivative of the limit differs from the limit of derivatives), and a “tent’’ sequence (the integral of the limit does not equal the limit of the integrals).

Theorems are proved: a uniformly convergent sequence of continuous functions has a continuous limit; the integral of the uniform limit equals the limit of the integrals; if fₙ are continuously differentiable, converge uniformly to f, and their derivatives converge uniformly to g, then f is continuously differentiable and f′=g. The Weierstrass M‑test is stated: if |fⱼ(x)|≤Mⱼ for all x∈S and ΣMⱼ converges, then Σfⱼ converges uniformly on S.

The De'Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is discounted $200, now $1,300. It has a built‑in touchscreen for selecting milk‑based drinks, an automatic grinder, a “bean adapt” function that lets users dial in settings for each bean type, and a swappable hopper for two bean varieties. The machine includes an integrated milk frother that produces silky micro‑foam, though it doesn’t reach the temperature of a traditional steam wand. While easier to use than a manual portafilter setup, it does not match the potential quality of a classic espresso machine.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee recognized by UNHCR, describes his experience in Papua New Guinea’s Manus Island detention centre since arriving in October 2013. He was placed in the Delta compound, a cramped metal shipping container housing around 300 men with only five toilets and one washing machine. Detainees faced constant queuing for meals, water, toilets and razor exchanges, often under extreme heat or rain. Prayers were performed on the floor in front of toilets because no dedicated space existed. He later moved to Mike compound, which held over 400 men; it had a small TV room, inadequate ventilation and no air‑conditioning in sleeping areas. Food was frequently thrown away while he and others hid fruit to survive evenings of hunger. Restrictions on phone calls and slow internet limited communication with families. He recounts thoughts of suicide, emotional distress and coping through writing, quoting the idiom “the pen is mightier than the sword”. He emphasizes indefinite detention, repeated loss of birthdays and a desire for freedom and safety in Australia.

Total solar eclipses were historically viewed as ominous. Ancient Greeks saw them as the gods' anger, Vikings as possible apocalypses, and Chinese as a dragon devouring the Sun, prompting noisy protests. In 1878, many Americans in the eclipse path panicked, some believing it was Christ’s return; one father killed his son and himself. The Gospels describe a darkened sky at Jesus’s crucifixion, and some modern Christians now fear the August 21 eclipse signals the end times. Sister Mary Elizabeth, a cloistered nun, tells callers the event is not a bad omen and plans to watch it from her monastery near totality. In Islamic tradition, an eclipse coincided with the death of Muhammad’s son Ibrahim; Muhammad taught it was merely a sign of God, not a response to human death. Author David Baron describes a total eclipse as an alien, awe‑inspiring experience that makes people feel small, like standing on the Grand Canyon rim times a million.

The Triangle offense attacks the Diamond & One defense by isolating the "Star" player in the middle, forcing one-on-one situations against a defender unprepared for post defense. The offense uses high post entry, inside triangle action, kick out passes, and lob exchanges to create open shots and layups. Successful execution requires coordination, high post isolations, back cuts, interior passing, and spot up shooting ability. Players must function as a unit with proper timing and communication. Scouting opponents and deploying various alignments prevents defenders from focusing on one set.

Funnel-web spider found in Springwood, NSW, Blue Mountains, identified as the world’s most venomous spider. Spider about 5 cm across, common along Australia’s east coast from Queensland to NSW, with a new species recently discovered in northern Tasmania. Funnel‑webs have large fangs that can pierce fingernails; bites cause rapid nausea, muscle cramps, sweating and numbness, and can be fatal within 15 minutes due to nervous‑system shutdown. Australian Museum records 13 deaths; an antivenene introduced in 1981 has prevented further fatalities. Males are seen in cooler evenings during mating season searching for females. They prefer cool, damp environments such as pools, bathrooms and laundries, and can survive underwater for days. Experts advise leaving them alone, wearing gloves when gardening and seeking immediate medical care if bitten. The venom primarily threatens insects, other spiders and primates; larger animals and treated humans are unlikely to die.

The speaker reaffirms his oath to uphold the Constitution, enumerating its purposes—union, justice, tranquility, defense, general welfare, and liberty—and noting that over thirty‑six years the Constitution has been administered successfully, with the nation’s population growing from four to twelve million, its territory expanding to the Pacific, new states admitted, treaties concluded, commerce flourishing, and internal improvements such as roads and military science advancing. Although party divisions arose from theoretical, foreign‑policy, and geographic differences, the experiment has been crowned with success; ten years of peace have healed most animosities and a broad consensus now supports the Constitution’s principles. The predecessor’s administration achieved peace and defensive preparation, exact justice abroad, reduction of internal taxes and the national debt, the reduction and professionalization of the armed forces, the peaceful acquisition of the Floridas, recognition of Latin American independence, progress in fortifications, navy growth, suppression of the slave trade, and efforts to civilize Indian tribes and explore the interior. The speaker intends to continue internal improvements, rely on legislative guidance, executive assistance, state cooperation, and the people’s support, trusting in divine providence for the country’s future.

KGI analyst Ming‑Chi Kuo reports that the 2017 Apple Watch will keep the same design, marking three generations of the same form factor. In an optimization trial using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework, 97 children aged 9–12 years with insufficient sleep (baseline 7.7 h per weeknight) were randomized to a 2⁵ factorial design testing five candidate components: sleep‑goal setting (guideline‑based ≥9.25 h vs personalized ≥baseline + 45 min), child‑directed loss‑framed financial incentive, caregiver‑directed loss‑framed incentive, screen‑time reduction messaging, and daily‑routine messaging. All participants received the core intervention (sleep tracking via Fitbit and weekly performance feedback). The primary outcome was change in weeknight sleep duration; the optimization criterion was an increase of ≥30 minutes.

Overall, weeknight sleep increased 24 minutes during the 7‑week intervention and 21 minutes during the 2‑week follow‑up. No single component setting met the criterion. Interaction analysis identified two component combinations that achieved ≥30‑minute increases: (1) core + caregiver‑directed incentive + screen‑time messaging + routine messaging (any sleep goal) – weeknight sleep increased 39.6 minutes (intervention) and 33.2 minutes (follow‑up); (2) core + caregiver‑directed incentive + routine messaging (any sleep goal) – increased 32.0 minutes (intervention) and 26.6 minutes (follow‑up). The caregiver‑directed loss‑framed incentive was essential; the child‑directed incentive was ineffective and redundant. Guideline‑based and personalized sleep goals performed comparably, with guideline‑based being slightly more favorable.

Limitations include a single‑site, predominantly non‑Hispanic White sample, reduced data capture for Black participants, short follow‑up, and use of a single‑sensor commercial tracker. The next step is evaluation of the optimized package in a randomized controlled trial. The findings suggest that a mobile health platform incorporating sleep tracking, performance feedback, a caregiver‑directed loss‑framed incentive, and routine‑promoting messaging (with optional screen‑time reduction) can increase children’s weeknight sleep duration by at least 30 minutes.

This study investigates nanoscale plasticity of single‑crystalline α‑titanium under spherical nanoindentation by coupling molecular‑dynamics simulations with orientation‑resolved Schmid‑factor mapping. Three crystal orientations ([0001] basal, [10̅10] prismatic, and [2̅110] a‑plane) were indented at 10 K, 300 K and 600 K using an EAM potential and a rigid 12 nm radius indenter. Load‑displacement curves show elastic Hertzian loading followed by pop‑in for the basal orientation and smoother nucleation for prismatic orientations; contact pressure decreases with temperature. Dislocation analysis identifies dominant basal a‑type dislocations (1/3⟨1̅210⟩) with c‑type, prismatic and pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ contributions; the HCP→BCC transformation occurs under high stress, most pronounced at low temperature. Schmid‑factor maps link high resolved shear stress to plastic zones beneath the indenter, while shear‑strain maps reveal basal and prismatic slip, with pyramidal slip activated at higher temperature. Surface morphologies evolve from localized circular pile‑up (basal) to dual‑lobe (prismatic) and asymmetric patterns (a‑plane), with increasing temperature promoting diffusion and recovery. Dislocation density is highest in the [0001] orientation (≈0.86–1.52 ×10¹⁶ m⁻²) and decreases with temperature for prismatic orientations (≈0.41–0.45 ×10¹⁶ m⁻²). The results demonstrate that temperature and crystallographic orientation jointly control slip system activation, phase transformation propensity, and residual defect structures in α‑titanium.

This document describes physical layer preamble signaling designs for wireless communication protocols (such as IEEE 802.11be/EHT and later versions). The document defines specific formatting options for Trigger-Based (TB), Single User (SU), Multi-User (MU), and unified SU/MU PPDUs, including methods for signaling channel puncturing patterns and spatial reuse.

High Post Split Offense is a simple, flexible system used at all levels, featuring a 2‑3 high alignment that enables quick post splits, down screens and back cuts. The offense creates baseline space, gives all five players scoring chances, removes weak‑side defensive help and promotes strong offensive rebounding. It operates in four phases: (1) high post split with options such as split, fake split, back cut and two‑same‑side; (2) down screens by the wings for the guards, with reads for defender chase, cheat, switch or show‑and‑recover and counters such as curl, fade, back cut, screen‑and‑roll or slip; (3) high post isolation where the post pivots to a triple‑threat position, has a green light to shoot or drive, and can use automatic lob, wing feeds, post exchange or screen exchange; (4) strong post ups against smaller defenders with entry variations including flop/back‑cut, wing pass, wing double‑away and post single/double. Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, non‑verbal communication, timing and defensive recognition. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, hustle and boxing out. Even teams not using the offense must understand how to defend it.

A method for forming a semiconductor device includes arranging a plurality of interconnect structures on a carrier substrate, encapsulating the structures in a first encapsulant, exposing contact areas on opposite sides of the structures, electrically coupling at least one semiconductor component of each of a plurality of semiconductor dies to one or more of the interconnect structures using direct metal‑to‑metal bonding or solder bonding, encasing the dies and portions of the first encapsulant in a second encapsulant, removing the carrier substrate, and bonding a plurality of external contacts to first sides of the interconnect structures. The interconnect structures may be discrete substrates or a single universal interconnect structure, and semiconductor dies such as processor dies, memory cubes and controllers may be placed over one or more structures, sometimes bridging adjacent structures. Underfill may be applied by capillary flow or moldable underfill, and redistribution layers may be formed over the structures to interconnect the dies. The process yields multi‑die InFO packages supporting super‑large package sizes (>70 mm × 70 mm) for high‑performance computing applications with reduced coefficient‑of‑thermal‑expansion mismatch stress and improved board‑level reliability.

Paula Norrell, a female employee of Waste Away Group, Inc., filed suit alleging gender discrimination under Title VII after she was not promoted to district sales manager for the combined Montgomery‑Opelika district in 2001. Norrell, who had been hired as an inside sales representative in 1996, subsequently promoted to customer service manager (1997) and district sales manager for the Opelika district (1998), applied for the new position, was interviewed, but the company selected male employee Terry White. Norrell claimed the refusal to promote her constituted disparate‑treatment discrimination and that the company’s employment practices had a disparate‑impact on women.

The court found that Norrell established a prima facie case of discrimination, but that Waste Away articulated a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason—White possessed prior experience as district sales manager for the combined district, had outside‑sales experience, and was deemed more qualified. The court examined Norrell’s evidence of pretext, including statements by supervisor Malphrus and manager Johnson concerning her pregnancy and work‑family balance, and concluded those remarks were stray comments unrelated to the promotion decision and did not show discriminatory animus. No genuine issue of material fact existed as to pretext, and Norrell conceded the disparate‑impact claim after discovery.

The district court granted Waste Away’s motion for summary judgment on both claims, entered final judgment for the defendant, and taxed costs against Norrell.

Triangle Post Offense is a basketball system created, developed and refined by Tex Winter. It bases its actions on defensive reads rather than fixed plays, relies on sound principles, precise court spacing (players stay 15‑20 ft apart) and fundamental execution. The offense consists of a sideline triangle on one side of the court combined with a two‑player weakside “two‑game” on the other; every player remains involved and must understand the options for each spot. Its three core components are entry, sideline triangle and weakside two‑game.  

Entries can be any pass or dribble that initiates the formation, including guard‑outside cut, guard‑inside cut, dribble‑clear, off‑guard cut, post‑pop, base‑screen, ball‑reversal, dribble‑weave and post exchange. Sideline triangle actions produce quick‑hitting post split options (basic post split, high post split, post isolation, corner split, screen‑and‑roll) and set up strong post ups by using the “Line of Deployment.”  

The weakside two‑game provides a series of pass and dribble entries with corresponding reads and counters such as hand‑off & drive, pull‑up jump shot, roll‑post isolation, wing isolation, fake hand‑off, cut opposite and lob pass. When the defense overplays—fronting, sagging, double‑team‑ing, denying reversal or backdoor passes—the offense automatically generates counters (over‑the‑top passes, dribble penetration, drop‑passes, kick‑out passes, back‑door cuts).  

Coaches teach the system using a whole‑part‑whole method and run drills that cover two‑player entries, weakside two‑game, sideline triangle play and combined 4‑on‑4/5‑on‑5 scrimmages. Game strategy emphasizes scouting the opponent, varying entries to prevent defender focus and remaining alert to defensive adjustments throughout the contest.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, consist of a 20‑period simple moving average plus/minus a multiple of its standard deviation, forming upper and lower bands. They visualize asset volatility and help estimate reversals or trend continuations. The bands are calculated in TradingView using the ta.sma() and ta.stedv() functions; users can adjust the period, multiplier, and price source. Disadvantages include false signals, limited effectiveness in range‑bound markets, signal delays, and sensitivity to settings. A breakout strategy based on band breaches is one common approach. Although Bollinger Bands are easy to use, implementing a profitable system requires defining clear rules, backtesting, and risk management. TradingView provides tools to quickly prototype strategies such as breakout, mean reversion, or squeeze, but performance depends on the chosen parameters and time frame.

The public domain must be protected from illegal seizure, Indians treated fairly with a path to citizenship, and polygamy suppressed. Immigration laws will bar non‑citizen laborers with customs repugnant to American civilization. Civil‑service reform is demanded, requiring merit over partisan service. Freedmen are guaranteed full citizenship rights. The speaker concludes by calling for practical, united action to secure the benefits of the Republic, acknowledging divine guidance.

The TPS7H500x-SP series is a family of radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers for space applications, consisting of four devices: TPS7H5001-SP (dual output, full-featured), TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP (both single output), and TPS7H5004-SP (dual output for push-pull/full-bridge topologies). All controllers feature a 0.613-V reference with +0.7%/-1% accuracy and configurable switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz with external clock synchronization capability. Operating input voltage ranges from 4 V to 14 V, and startup requires VLDO exceeding 3.55 V, internal reference availability, EN pin above 0.6 V, FAULT pin below 0.6 V, and junction temperature below 175°C. The controllers support internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary operating modes for switching frequency control. Output voltage is programmed via resistor divider to the 0.613-V reference. Soft-start is controlled by an external capacitor, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating when the SS pin exceeds 1 V. Dead time is fixed at 50 ns for TPS7H5003-SP but programmable for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP. Leading edge blank time is configurable on most devices. Maximum duty cycle is set via the DCL pin (floating for 75%, connected to VLDO for 100%, or AVSS for 50% depending on device). The controllers implement peak current mode control with hiccup mode protection when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart at 160°C. The series supports buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies, optimized for GaN power semiconductors.

Jane Goodall assembled a unique collection of chimpanzee skeletons at Gombe National Park. After death, carcasses were placed in a tin drum where insects removed soft tissue, leaving clean bones linked to each individual’s known sex, age, weight and life history. This dataset allowed researchers to examine how development shapes skeletal anatomy and offered a new perspective on ancient hominid fossils. When asked about relevance to Lucy’s 3.2‑million‑year‑old partial skeleton, Goodall responded that they simply do not know. She explained her principle: “When you’re working in the field, you shouldn’t waste anything.” The collection includes Flo, a dominant matriarch whose skeleton was larger than most Gombe chimps yet lighter than a smaller male, illustrating the difficulty of estimating body mass from bone size, and who displayed bone loss different from human osteoporosis while giving birth near age 50, mirroring recent evidence of menopause in wild female chimps. Goodall’s refusal to discard remains continued to provide scientific insights long after she moved from fieldwork to activism.

The second week of motherhood is described as especially difficult after the initial endorphin‑filled week. Support from visitors and medication fades, leaving mothers to confront severe sleep deprivation, painful breastfeeding (raw, bleeding nipples), insufficient milk production causing babies to lose or fail to gain weight, and feelings of isolation when visitors stop coming. Babies’ two‑week growth spurts lead to frequent, uninterpretable crying, which adds stress. Emotional rawness often causes arguments with partners over minor issues, and infants may refuse to sleep, demanding constant feeding or holding, making the mother feel like an object rather than a parent.

On June 15, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Whole Foods Market, Inc. and Walnut Merger Sub, Inc., an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Amazon. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Whole Foods Market, with Whole Foods Market surviving. Each Whole Foods Market share will be converted into $42.00 in cash. The merger is subject to conditions including Whole Foods Market shareholder approval, expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, and Competition Act (Canada) clearance. Amazon plans to finance the merger primarily through debt, including a commitment letter for a $13.7 billion senior unsecured bridge term loan facility from Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Goldman Sachs Lending Partners LLC, Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated, and Bank of America, N.A. The agreement includes a termination fee of $400 million payable by Whole Foods Market under certain circumstances. The merger has an outside date of February 15, 2018, extendable once for 90 days. Amazon issued a joint press release with Whole Foods Market on June 16, 2017 announcing the transaction. Forward-looking statements noted that the transaction is subject to various risks including potential failure to obtain required approvals, financing challenges, and other business uncertainties.

A follow‑through day is a market‑timing signal that identifies the start of a new uptrend after a correction or bear market. It occurs on Day 4 or later of a rally attempt when a major index (e.g., S&P 500, Nasdaq) closes significantly higher than the prior day and volume also increases. To detect it, an investor first marks a Day 1 when the index closes higher during a correction; Days 2 and 3 must not fall below Day 1’s low, otherwise the rally attempt fails and the process restarts. The follow‑through day itself is marked by a large price gain and higher volume, confirming that selling pressure has subsided and a new uptrend has begun.

Early signs that the signal may fail include the index dropping below the Day 1 low (or a new low for the whole period) and a second follow‑through day closing below the previous one’s low. Such conditions are considered sell signals.

Backtesting the strategy on the S&P 500 (using SPY) shows poor short‑term results because the market tends to mean‑revert; performance improves modestly with a filter such as a 25‑day RSI below 55. The method was developed by William J. O’Neil for stock‑specific analysis rather than index trading, and historically no bull market has started without a follow‑through day.

Practical guidelines advise monitoring the index during a correction, waiting for a valid rally attempt, entering a partial position on a confirmed follow‑through day, and managing risk by studying leading stocks and sentiment. The signal is not a guarantee of the absolute market low and should be used in conjunction with other analysis.

The double top pattern is a bearish reversal chart pattern consisting of two swing highs at roughly the same level and a neckline connecting the intervening swing low, with that level acting as resistance and the neckline as support. When price breaks below the neckline, it signals a potential downward reversal, prompting traders to close longs or open shorts. Research by Thomas Bulkowski found only 39% of double top formations reach their profit target, indicating the strategy is difficult due to the market's upward bias, making shorting challenging.

Moody's downgraded Enron's senior unsecured debt to Baa2 (two levels above junk) and placed its ratings on review for further downgrade. Enron's stock fell to around $13-14, near seven-year lows, having lost more than half its value in two weeks. The energy trader drew down approximately $3 billion in credit lines and was negotiating for an additional $1-2 billion in new credit. Concerns arose over undisclosed partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, prompting an SEC inquiry and his resignation. European energy companies froze dealings with Enron due to credit concerns. Moody's cited deteriorating financial flexibility and reduced valuations in several businesses. Analysts viewed the credit request as a sign of weakness, though some research firms said Enron bonds were not likely to fall to junk status.

Retired Metro Police homicide detective Phil Ramos viewed the newly released 1 October police body‑camera videos and described the detectives’ tension and stress as they approached Stephen Paddock’s hotel room, noting audible anxiety and visible sweat. He said forgetting to turn on the body camera was understandable in such a nightmare scenario, and that an accidental firearm discharge was unsurprising given the readiness for a firefight. Ramos also expressed surprise that the footage lacked timestamps and emphasized that the videos show only part of the night, so conclusions should not be drawn from them alone.

A heat wave over Northeast will move west after July 4 to southern California. Excessive heat warning through Tuesday; New York heat index 106 °F. Seven‑day heat wave began Saturday; New England set record highs. One heat‑related death reported (Pennsylvania woman); another death under investigation (Kansas City man). New York air quality alert issued. Storm front will cool East Coast before heat spreads to central United States, reaching Los Angeles and San Diego Friday.

In March 2024, a paper titled “Crossing the Partisan Divide in Education Policy” notes that pandemic‑induced learning loss, heightened political pressure, and post‑2020 racial reckoning have moved education from traditional bipartisan support into a highly polarized environment. It argues that, despite this division, cross‑partisan collaboration is possible and identifies five factors that enable successful cross‑partisan education policy: (1) problems and solutions must be easy to communicate and appeal broadly; (2) policies must be responsive to local context and supported by visible local champions; (3) policymakers need political cover—protection from higher authority, a constituency, or a deadline—to take risky positions; (4) both sides must be able to claim a win, allowing each party to point to different achievements; and (5) strategic use of media can accelerate policy adoption.

Illustrative examples include the “science of reading” movement sparked by the American Public Media podcast Sold a Story, which spurred 15 states to pass reading‑instruction laws; state‑run teacher apprenticeship programs that tap federal labor funding in traditionally Republican states; the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, which grew from military‑family needs and has gained cross‑partisan support; career‑and‑technical‑education (CTE) initiatives tailored to local workforce demands, such as Idaho’s Idaho Career Ready Students Program and North Carolina’s Short‑Term Workforce Development Grant; and recent civics‑education legislation in states like Indiana, Oregon, Utah, and Georgia, which has garnered support across the political spectrum.

The paper also offers additional guidance for advocates: understand the political landscape, align problem definitions, gauge urgency, avoid threatening frontline staff, and frame policies as expansions rather than restrictions. It cautions against value‑signaling, mission creep, and over‑extension, urging organizations to prioritize and check assumptions.

The conclusion emphasizes that, while federal gridlock persists, substantive cross‑partisan education reforms are occurring in many states, demonstrating that collaboration is both realistic and achievable in the current political climate.

Microsoft Q1 FY2022 (ended September 30, 2021) financial results: Total revenue $45,317 million (up 22% year-over-year), net income $20,505 million (up 48%), operating income $20,238 million (up 27%). Revenue breakdown: Product $16,631 million, Service and other $28,686 million. Segment revenue: Productivity and Business Processes $15,039 million (up 22%), Intelligent Cloud $16,964 million (up 31%), More Personal Computing $13,314 million (up 12%). Diluted earnings per share $2.71. Total assets $335,418 million, cash and cash equivalents $19,165 million. Stockholders' equity $151,978 million.

A systematic review and meta-analysis assessed Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) seroprevalence in Ethiopia using five studies (2016-2023) with 335,821 subjects. The pooled seroprevalence was 12.35%, with highest rates in SNNPR (43.6%) and lowest in Dire Dawa (~12%). Risk factors included occupation (farmers highest at 49.7%), age (adults highest), education (attended formal education higher), and sex (variable results). No vaccine or antiviral exists; treatment is symptomatic with vector control. Ethiopia faces limited healthcare infrastructure affecting disease detection. The review highlights Chikungunya as a persistent public health concern requiring proactive readiness, collaboration, and public awareness campaigns.

The Colts have nine picks in the 2018 NFL Draft, with the No. 6 overall selection being critical to general manager Chris Ballard's rebuild. The top prospects for their first-round pick are Bradley Chubb (EDGE from NC State), Quenton Nelson (IOL from Notre Dame), and Saquon Barkley (RB from Penn State), each of whom could help address the team's needs, particularly protecting quarterback Andrew Luck.

The book "Designing Distributed Systems" by Brendan Burns explains distributed system patterns using containers and container orchestration. It begins with single-node patterns: the sidecar pattern, where a container augments an application; the ambassador pattern, which brokers interactions between an application and external services; and the adapter pattern, which standardizes application interfaces. These patterns promote modularity, reusability, and separation of concerns. The book then covers multi-node patterns, including replicated load-balanced services for reliability and scaling, sharded services for handling large datasets, and microservices architectures that decouple components through defined APIs. It emphasizes that patterns provide shared vocabularies, reusable components, and lessons learned from others, enabling more efficient and reliable distributed system development. Tools like Kubernetes are used to deploy these patterns, with concrete examples for implementing sidecars, ambassadors, adapters, caches, and SSL termination layers.

The Piotroski F-Score, developed by Joseph Piotroski, is a stock selection method using 9 financial criteria (profitability, liquidity, efficiency) to identify undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals. Stocks scoring 8-9 are considered strong. Backtests on NYSE stocks (1974-2014) show Alpha Architect's version yielded 13.3% annual returns versus 11.2% for the S&P 500. For cheap stocks (bottom 20% by price) with scores above 6, returns reached 15.9%. The strategy reduces risk by focusing on financially strong companies and should be used with other research. Implementation involves calculating the score, selecting high-scoring stocks, diversifying, and monitoring investments.

Patrick McCaffery, a 6-foot-8 four-star forward from Iowa City West, committed to the University of Iowa. He is ranked 30th nationally by Rivals, the highest-rated recruit since 2003. McCaffery cited family and his father's coaching style as reasons, noting the freedom to play and fastbreak system. He helped West win a Class 4A state title, averaging 13.8 points on 60.6% shooting, and is targeting 2019 recruits D.J. Carton, Trace Jackson-Davis, and Tyrell Terry. He is working to increase his weight from 165 to 175 pounds for Big Ten play.

The Supreme Court appears inclined to allow trial judges to limit defense attorneys’ overnight discussions with clients who are still testifying. In David Villarreal’s murder trial, the trial court prohibited his lawyer from discussing his testimony while permitting discussion of trial strategy. Villarreal appealed, claiming the restriction violated his Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance; Texas courts upheld the conviction. During Monday’s oral argument, justices debated where to draw the line between permissible trial‑strategy advice and prohibited coaching of testimony. Some justices indicated the court could ban direct discussion of the client’s testimony while allowing talk about strategic consequences; others questioned whether such a line could be drawn. Texas proposes distinguishing “management” of testimony from other matters, while the United States advocates a bright‑line rule barring any discussion of the defendant’s testimony.

Containers on a single node can be grouped to enforce resource isolation, delineate team ownership, and achieve separation of concerns. Three single‑node patterns formalize these groupings:

**Sidecar pattern** – a helper container augments an application container without the application’s knowledge. Uses include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration files, exposing a /topz‑style resource monitor, and implementing a simple PaaS that pulls code from a Git repository.

**Ambassador pattern** – a container brokers interactions between the application and the external world. Examples: a client‑side ambassador routes requests to sharded Redis or Memcached, a service‑broker ambassador discovers MySQL in different environments, and a request‑splitting ambassador sends a fraction of traffic to an experimental version.

**Adapter pattern** – a container modifies the application’s interface to conform to a standard. Applications include adapting Redis to the Prometheus metrics format, normalizing heterogeneous log formats with Fluentd, and providing rich health checks for MySQL by exposing an HTTP endpoint.

To make containers modular and reusable, they should be parameterized via environment variables, define a stable API surface, and be documented in the Dockerfile with EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL directives.

At the multi‑node level, **replicated load‑balanced stateless services** provide redundancy, scale, and session affinity; they can be extended with a caching tier (Varnish) for performance and an SSL‑termination tier (nginx) for security. **Sharded services** split data across independent shards; a client‑side ambassador routes requests, and consistent hashing limits resharding impact. A **sharded, replicated cache** combines both patterns to improve hit rates and resilience.

These patterns enable independent deployment, team decoupling, and consistent tooling across diverse applications.

The lecture reviews the history of lower‑bound results for the predecessor problem (Ajtai 1988, Miltersen, Beame & Fich, Xiau, Sen 2003, Patrascu & Thorup) and argues that the known upper bounds (Van Emde Boas and fusion tries) are essentially optimal up to a log log factor. It recasts the static colored‑predecessor problem as a communication‑complexity game between Alice (the query, holding a w‑bit word) and Bob (the data structure, holding n elements). In the cell‑probe model each memory read is a round of communication with Alice sending ≤ log s bits and Bob replying with a w‑bit word.

The proof uses the round‑elimination lemma: a protocol for the “f^k” version of the problem (Alice has k inputs, Bob knows an index i) can have its first message eliminated at the cost of increasing the error by at most √(a/k) when Alice speaks first or √(b/k) when Bob speaks first. Repeating this t times removes t messages, shrinking the word size by a factor of ≈ a·t² in an Alice‑to‑Bob step and the universe size by a factor of ≈ b·t² in a Bob‑to‑Alice step. The process must stop when w becomes O(log w) or n becomes constant, otherwise all messages would be eliminated and the error would be ≥ ½, a contradiction. This yields the lower bound  

Ω(min(log_a w, log_b n)).

For polynomial‑space structures (a = Θ(log n), b = w) the bound becomes Ω(min(log w / log log w, log_w n)). Hence Van Emde Boas is optimal when w is small, and fusion tries are optimal when w is large; together they are optimal up to the log log factor for static, randomized colored‑predecessor data structures.

The passage describes a report and appendix that bring the narrative up to the revolution of January 17, 1893, and notes that a later report transmits a treaty signed February 14, 1893 by the U.S. Secretary of State and the Hawaiian Provisional Government. It presents a chronological list of diplomatic papers and a bibliography of sources on U.S.–Hawaii relations from 1826 to 1891, including works on treaties, histories, directories, and congressional reports. The passage also reproduces the 1826 Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation between the United States and the Sandwich Islands, signed at Honolulu on December 23, 1826, and includes excerpts of letters that discuss the poor condition of foreign protection and arrangements to secure American claims and protect seamen.

Striker Rudy Gestede says Middlesbrough must believe they can end a slump to avoid relegation. Middlesbrough are 19th, lowest scorers (22 goals), six points from safety. Arsenal, sixth, have won one of last five and lost 3‑0 to Crystal Palace. Gestede stresses positivity and focus.

NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x architecture, comprising the GA102 and GA104 GPUs, builds on Turing by doubling FP32 throughput, delivering up to 2× higher raster graphics and ray‑tracing performance. The GA102 die has 28.3 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors (SMs) with 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑generation RT cores, and 336 third‑generation Tensor cores; the GA104 die is used in the GeForce RTX 3070. Key features include: double‑speed FP32 operations on both SM datapaths, second‑generation RT cores that double ray/triangle intersection rate, third‑generation Tensor cores supporting TF32, fine‑grained structured sparsity, and AI‑accelerated features such as DLSS 8K, denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast and Canvas; larger unified L1/shared memory (128 KB per SM) and doubled L1 bandwidth; GDDR6X memory (up to 24 GB on RTX 3090, 48 GB on RTX A6000) with up to 1.5× more bandwidth than predecessor; third‑generation NVLink providing 56.25 GB/s per direction (112.5 GB/s total) and PCIe Gen 4 host interface delivering up to 64 GB/s; ROPs relocated to GPC, increasing total to 112 ROPs. The architecture is up to 1.9× more power‑efficient than Turing. Products include GeForce RTX 3090 (8K @60 fps with 24 GB GDDR6X), RTX 3080 (≈2× performance vs RTX 2080), RTX 3070 (≈RTX 2080 Ti performance), and data‑center GPUs RTX A6000 and A40 (48 GB GDDR6, NVLink‑scalable to 96 GB).

The study assessed SARS‑CoV‑2 mRNA vaccine responses in 40 participants: 13 healthy controls and 27 rheumatoid‑arthritis (RA) patients treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab. Antibody and cellular analyses showed that rituximab‑treated individuals had near‑complete loss of anti‑spike antibodies and reduced vaccine‑induced CD4⁺ T‑cell activation; abatacept treatment significantly lowered spike‑specific and neutralizing antibody levels and decreased IgG class‑switching of RBD‑specific memory B cells, while the proportion of activated RBD‑specific B cells and CD4⁺ T cells producing IL‑2, IFNγ, and IL‑21 was reduced; MTX‑treated subjects displayed a modest reduction in spike‑specific CD4⁺ T‑cell activation but no major alterations in antibody titers, B‑cell numbers, or class‑switching. Across all RA cohorts, vaccine responses differed from healthy controls, with abatacept showing the most pronounced impairment of T‑cell help for B cells. The authors suggest that temporary cessation of abatacept when clinically feasible may improve vaccine‑induced protection.

Danantara to launch at least eight waste-to-power projects in Indonesia by October, starting in Jakarta with plans to expand across Java and Bali. Indonesia produces 35 million tonnes of waste annually, with 61% poorly managed. Each plant will process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily, generating 15 megawatts of electricity at a cost of approximately $180 million per facility. PLN will purchase the electricity for national grid integration. The initiative aligns with Indonesia's target of 453 megawatts from waste-to-energy facilities requiring $2.72 billion in investment. The program supports Danantara's dual mandate of financial returns and addressing national priorities including pollution control, waste reduction, and energy security.

MTN and four banks plan to raise a total of GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange within six months, the largest simultaneous capital‑raising in the exchange’s near‑30‑year history. MTN is selling a 35 % stake for GH¢3.48 billion, while Access Bank, the Agricultural Development Bank, Republic Bank and Societe Generale are seeking GH¢1.19 billion via rights issues to meet the Bank of Ghana’s December 2018 capital requirement of GH¢400 million. Economists warn that failure to meet the targets would exceed the market’s capacity, and the timing of the multiple offers is risky because the MTN IPO could absorb most available liquidity, prompting banks to need a backup plan. Pension assets now exceed GH¢21 billion, providing a cushion, but analysts say foreign participation will be needed to cover the bulk of the demand, as institutional investors may be able to absorb only about GH¢1.5 billion. While foreign inflows could stabilise the cedi, repatriation of dividends could further weaken the currency.

The study developed and formally validated an Arabic version of the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) for Saudi Arabian patients with dentofacial deformities. The OQLQ contains 22 items across four domains (social aspects of deformity, facial aesthetics, oral function, awareness of dentofacial aesthetics) scored on a 4‑point Likert scale (total 0–88); higher scores indicate poorer quality of life. After forward‑backward translation and expert committee review, 74 adults (mean age 30 ± 4.6 years, 62 % female) completed the questionnaire before or after orthognathic treatment, 15 patients repeated it after two weeks for test‑retest reliability, and 12 completed it both before and after surgery for responsiveness. Internal consistency across the cohort was excellent (Cronbach α = 0.92). Test‑retest correlations ranged from 0.601 to 0.879 (overall = 0.859). Validity was supported by weak but significant correlations between overall OQLQ and facial‑esthetics scores and patient satisfaction, and by lower OQLQ scores in patients reporting improved appearance after surgery. Responsiveness was shown by significantly lower overall OQLQ scores after surgery (median 34 vs 10, p < 0.0001) and improvement in the facial‑esthetics subdomain in the paired analysis (p = 0.03). The Arabic OQLQ demonstrated reliable, valid and responsive measurement of quality‑of‑life changes in orthognathic patients, though limitations include small test‑retest and paired samples, single‑center recruitment, and lack of convergent/discriminant validity testing.

The Supreme Court will decide whether the ex post facto clause applies to restitution under the 1996 Mandatory Victims Restitution Act in the case of Holsey Ellingburg, a bank robber. The ex post facto clause prevents punishment for conduct that was legal when committed and traditionally applies only to criminal punishments, not civil remedies. Several factors make the restitution look criminal: it's imposed as part of the criminal sentence, uses criminal procedures, gives victims little role, and failure to pay results in incarceration. The MVRA itself describes restitution as serving punitive purposes. The government concedes that restitution is criminal for purposes of the ex post facto clause, and a court-appointed amicus defends the decision below.
Delta plans to acquire up to 32% of Grupo Aeroméxico, raising its stake to 49%, pending approvals.
Appeal dismissed on motion of appellant, with consent of appellee, no costs.

Tradeshift raised $250M in Series E funding, led by Goldman Sachs and PSP Investments, with HSBC and others. Total funding surpasses $400M; valuation exceeds $1.1B. Mikkel Hippe Brun joins board. CEO says investment will fuel growth; Goldman notes rise in B2B transactions.

Steve Pearse, a former CEO, entrepreneur, and angel investor with background in telecommunications, IT, and health science, discusses startup fundamentals. He has raised over $250 million across six rounds and built successful companies including Time Warner Telecom and Bay Networks before selling his Silicon Valley startup for $2.7 billion. Startup success statistics show approximately one out of ten succeeds, with investors seeking tenfold returns while six typically fail.

Exits require either going public or acquisition. Startups succeed because employees work for stock and share common goals. Effective pitches need strong signals to punch through noise, using simple language explainable to third graders. Key pitch elements include a hook, solution, technology explanation, business model, marketing strategy, competitive analysis, team credentials, financials, timeline, and final offer requesting money.

Hooks require seven seconds of engagement; presenters should avoid jargon, focus on customer pain points, and convert technology benefits to dollar values. The best presenter (preferably the CEO or founder) should pitch with confidence, eye contact, and audience engagement while managing technical team members to prevent derailing into details.

Companies should raise money six months before needing it, approaching multiple VCs simultaneously to create competitive tension. Brand-name investors often provide better value than their financial terms suggest. Cash flow is critical, and companies must remain flexible enough to pivot based on customer feedback. Speed to market matters more than patents, and first movers typically win. Team chemistry and focus on core objectives are essential while avoiding distractions.
