The player says the team feels more comfortable now, must bring its game and legs to the rink after early struggles; a deep lineup of four lines, six defensemen, and solid goaltending gives confidence. Strong road record, owner commitment, and trade‑deadline additions have helped. A teammate who overcame injuries is praised as the best player on the team. The focus is on the next game, with excitement and confidence in the series.

This systematic review examined how personality traits influence student satisfaction and success in online higher education. It identified 23 studies (all level IV evidence) organized into three themes: the interaction between personality and online education, comparisons across different class formats, and student choices regarding class format. The review found that conscientiousness, openness, and agreeableness positively correlate with academic success and satisfaction, while neuroticism negatively affects outcomes. Extraversion influences preferences for face-to-face learning but does not directly impact grades. No studies focused on occupational therapy programs, indicating a significant research gap in that field. The review highlights the importance of self-regulation, universal design for learning, and tailored support to accommodate diverse personality traits in online education.

In 1977 Leeds held the UK's first Reclaim the Night march, organized by the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group in response to women's fear after Peter Sutcliffe's murders. On November 12, about 60 women marched in each of two Leeds routes, with similar marches in 10 other towns. Slogans included “No Curfew on Women, Curfew on Men.” Marches continued for over a decade, revived in 2004. The event now inspires the theatre piece “The Darkest Corners” by RashDash, a cabaret/physical theatre performance with live music, part of the Transform 17 festival. It runs April 20–22 in a Holbeck car park and draws on global female activism to celebrate 40 years of collective women's rights action.

Adjunct instructors at Southwestern College held a rally demanding equal pay and benefits. Attendance was low; speakers outnumbered the audience. Adjuncts teach most courses, lack benefits, often work multiple campuses, traveling long distances for insufficient wages. Several speakers described financial strain, job insecurity, and limited medical coverage. President and a trustee voiced support, urging the campus community to fight for adjuncts.

- Turing GPUs add hardware support for USB Type‑C and the VirtualLink open‑industry standard, allowing a single USB‑C connector to supply power, display data, and USB for VR headsets, eliminating the multiple cables of current systems.  
- NVLink replaces the older MIO/PCIe SLI bridge on Turing; TU102 provides two x8 second‑generation NVLink links (25 GB/s each direction, 50 GB/s bidirectional) and TU104 one x8 link, enabling two‑way SLI only.  
- Turing introduces dedicated RT Cores that accelerate BVH traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, delivering roughly a ten‑fold improvement in ray‑tracing performance compared with Pascal.  
- Hybrid rendering combines rasterization for visibility with ray tracing for reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion; advanced denoising (AI‑based and non‑AI) reduces the number of rays required per pixel.  
- Tensor Cores enable the NGX deep‑learning stack, providing DLSS (standard and 2X modes trained with 64× supersampling), InPainting, AI Slow‑Mo, and AI Super Rez; NGX operates only on Turing hardware.  
- Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh shader stages, eliminating CPU draw‑call bottlenecks, supporting per‑object LOD selection, dynamic cutaways, and rendering hundreds of thousands of objects in real time.  
- Variable Rate Shading (VRS) lets developers set shading rate per 16×16‑pixel region; use cases include content‑adaptive, motion‑adaptive, and foveated shading, and VRS can also increase shading rate for MSAA.  
- Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen‑space, storing results in a texture and reusing shaded texels across frames or views, providing temporal stability and fine‑grained LOD control.  
- Multi‑View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi‑Projection to up to four views per pass (32 at API level), efficiently rendering stereo VR, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character instances in a single pass.  
- Turing includes bindless Constant Buffer and Unordered Access views (DX12 Tier 3), allows multiple resource types to co‑locate in a single heap, and adds integer execution units that operate in parallel with FP32.  
- VR experience enhancements on Turing comprise VirtualLink, MVR for stereo, VRS‑based foveated rendering, and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores for ray‑traced 3‑D sound.  
- TU104 full chip: six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 256‑bit memory, one x8 NVLink link.  
- TU106 full chip: three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 256‑bit memory, no NVLink.  
- RTX‑OPS metric combines Tensor (20 % time), FP32 (80 % time), RT (40 % of FP32 time), and INT32 (28 % of FP32 time) operations; RTX 2080 Ti achieves 78 RTX‑OPS.  
- Ray‑traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections use RTX with denoising to provide contact‑hardening shadows, correct AO, and artifact‑free glossy reflections.  
- BVH acceleration structures are built once per scene and refitted for incremental changes; denoising filters, both AI‑based and traditional, further improve image quality while reducing ray count.

Eye on AI newsletter covers several topics: Pika, founded by 26-year-old Demi Guo, launched a TikTok-like AI video app with a new Predictive Video feature and has raised $135 million at a $470 million valuation with 16.4 million users; San Francisco rents rose 6% year-over-year due to AI startup growth, with some neighborhoods seeing 13% increases; TSMC reported a 39.1% profit surge with revenue up 30.3% and raised its 2025 revenue growth forecast to mid-30% with planned capacity investments of at least $40 billion; Spotify partnered with major music labels including Sony, Universal, and Warner to develop AI music products through a new generative AI lab; and only 11% of Americans would consider using AI mental health tools, with just 8% trusting them and 4% having tried such tools.

The study compared Colombian higher education students' perceptions and preferences between online learning (OL) and emergency remote education (ERE) during COVID-19. Conducted with 88 undergraduate students from a private university, the research used surveys and content analysis. Results showed students rated OL significantly higher in most dimensions (10 of 14 items), particularly for independent activities, assessment strategies, and content quality. While most students (70-90%) held positive perceptions of both modalities, over 57% preferred OL. Notably, student-student interaction was nearly equal between modalities. Students identified advantages of OL as flexibility and structure, while ERE was valued for allowing continued learning during the pandemic. The study recommends instructor training, improved interaction design, and better assessment strategies for post-pandemic education.

Mark Cuban says Trump’s planned federal website TrumpRx.gov could be impactful if it forces pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to change their practices. The site, slated to launch early 2026, will sell prescription drugs directly to consumers at discounted rates, starting with a partnership with Pfizer that also grants the company a three‑year reprieve from pharmaceutical tariffs. The platform follows Cuban’s own Cost Plus Drugs model, which bypasses PBMs and offers average savings of about 50 %. Cuban gave the initiative a “B” grade, crediting the administration for hiring capable people but noting that PBM stock prices rose after the announcement, suggesting markets doubt the platform’s immediate effect. He warns the system remains rigged in favor of PBMs, but says if the administration forces PBM changes, Trump will deserve the credit. Public‑health experts are skeptical, noting the cash‑only model limits benefits to uninsured patients.

The Russell 2000 is a market‑weighted U.S. small‑cap index of roughly 2,000 stocks, representing about 10% of total U.S. market capitalisation. It is owned by FTSE Russell. Each year the index is reconstituted on the fourth Friday of June; preliminary constituent lists are published on June 9, 16 and 23, and the new composition takes effect after the close on that Friday.

Rebalancing adds companies that meet the index’s criteria, removes those that no longer qualify and adjusts the weights of existing holdings to reflect changes in market capitalisation. The buying and selling required can create temporary price imbalances – for example, stocks that have risen sharply (such as GameStop) need additional purchases, while declining stocks are reduced.

Historically the Russell 2000 has shown a pronounced end‑of‑June rally. A simple strategy that buys on the close of the first trading day after June 23 and sells on the close of the first trading day of July has averaged a 1.34% gain over about six trading days since 1988, outpacing the S&P 500’s 0.85% average gain over the same period. A hedged position that is long the Russell 2000 and short the S&P 500 has produced a lower average return of roughly 0.23% and has been relatively flat over recent years.

The purpose of the annual rebalancing is to keep the index aligned with its stated methodology and accurately represent the small‑cap segment of the U.S. equity market.

Digital leaders use data‑driven objectives as a coordinating mechanism across levels of the organization. These objectives are defined through a transparent process, clearly linked to company strategy, and allow teams to see how their work contributes to overall goals, creating a shared “North Star.” Implementation requires buy‑in and a combined top‑down/bottom‑up approach; mandating OKRs without engagement can become a burden, and excessive quantitative requirements can suppress intuition.  

A strong data culture aligns the firm vertically (individual and group goals to company strategy) and horizontally (cross‑functional collaboration through common data models and transparent access). Most digital leaders treat culture as the centerpiece that ties beliefs, stated values, and day‑to‑day actions together, with employee behavior reinforcing the espoused values.  

Digital laggards often lack clear goal‑strategy connections, leading to misalignment and a “culture of genius” where individuals pursue independent priorities. Changing entrenched mindsets is cited as the hardest part of transformation; compelling reasons for change must be understood.  

Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices (recognize need but lack culture/systems), insight ready (risk‑accepting culture but limited analytics capability), tech enabled (adequate technology but no experimentation mindset), and data reliant (over‑reliance on data that discourages critical thinking). Companies can target actions based on their current pattern to progress toward a strong data culture.  

Keystone Strategy is a consulting firm offering expertise in technology‑led strategy and digital transformation.

The president returned the harbor and river improvements bill to the House of Representatives with objections. The bill proposes $1,378,450 for over 40 distinct improvement projects. The president argued the Constitution does not grant the Federal Government power to construct internal improvements within states or appropriate funds for such purposes, noting several predecessors held the same view. The president contended many objects in the bill are local, not connected to foreign commerce, and some are at locations never established as ports of entry. The president identified practical concerns including consolidation of federal power at states' expense, sectional prejudices, wasteful expenditures, and injustice to states that funded their own improvements. Additionally, the president noted the country was engaged in a foreign war and questioned appropriations for non-essential objects during such time, warning the principle would lead to increasing annual appropriations and Treasury drains. While some provisions might be acceptable standing alone, the president withheld approval from the bill as a whole.

This document is a statistical analysis plan (SAP) for a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled trial (protocol ZP4207-17086) evaluating dasiglucagon versus placebo and GlucaGen® in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) for treating hypoglycemia. The primary objective is to demonstrate dasiglucagon's superiority over placebo in achieving plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase) within 45 minutes after a single 0.6 mg injection. Secondary objectives include confirming comparability to GlucaGen® and assessing safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles. The trial will enroll approximately 40 patients (20 dasiglucagon, 10 placebo, 10 GlucaGen®) at 2-3 European and 1-2 U.S. centers, with a screening period, a treatment period on Day 0, and a follow-up visit at Day 28. Statistical analyses will use SAS software (Version 9.4 or higher) and Phoenix® WinNonlin (Version 6.4 or higher) for PK/PD analyses, with all tests two-sided at the 0.05 significance level. The primary efficacy analysis will be based on the full analysis set (FAS), using Kaplan-Meier methods and a stratified log-rank test for time-to-recovery, with supportive analyses including Cox proportional hazards models and sensitivity analyses. Secondary efficacy endpoints include plasma glucose recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and changes from baseline, analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests and ANOVA. Safety analyses will cover adverse events (AEs), local tolerability, vital signs, laboratory parameters, electrocardiograms (ECGs), and immunogenicity, based on the safety analysis set. PK parameters (e.g., AUC, Cmax, Tmax) will be derived via non-compartmental analysis, and pharmacodynamic metrics include plasma glucose area under the effect curve. Data handling rules include handling of concentrations below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) and missing data, with no imputation for the primary efficacy analysis. All summaries will include treatment groups and total columns, with tables, listings, and figures formatted per ICH guidelines.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, achieving over 900 GB/s bandwidth via PAM4 signaling at up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering 936 GB/s peak memory bandwidth on the RTX 3090 and providing more than a 52 % bandwidth increase over the previous generation. The memory subsystem uses MTA encoding to limit signal transitions and improve SNR, and includes Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for GDDR6X to detect transmission errors and retry, signaling overclock limits via plateauing performance.

To address storage bottlenecks, NVIDIA RTX IO offloads game asset loading and lossless decompression to the GPU using Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, delivering up to 100× I/O performance improvement versus hard‑drive/traditional storage APIs and reducing CPU core usage from over twenty cores to near zero, which improves frame rates, shortens load times, and enables larger open‑world games.

The GA10x architecture provides second‑generation RT Cores that double ray‑triangle intersection and support motion blur, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity that double effective throughput, and doubled FP32 processing per SM; DLSS enhancements enable 8K HDR rendering.

For data centers, the A40 GPU offers up to 2× FP32 throughput, 2× ray‑tracing throughput, and up to 5× AI training throughput (10× with sparsity) versus prior Turing GPUs, features PCIe Gen4, 48 GB GDDR6 memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, supports vGPU software and Quadro Sync, and is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX platform. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU uses a GA102 with 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑generation RT cores, 336 next‑generation RT cores, 48 GB GDDR6, can be linked via NVLink for 96 GB, and includes professional certifications.

Display capabilities include 4K 120 Hz and 8K 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with DSC, plus HDCP 2.3 support. The fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder supports MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and the first hardware‑accelerated AV1 decode; the seventh‑generation NVENC encoder provides high‑quality, low‑CPU‑usage encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC, matching x264 Medium quality.

Specific products include the GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA cores, 1.5× faster than TITAN RTX) and the RTX 3070 (GA104, fastest in its class, faster than RTX 2080 Ti, uses GDDR6).

The SPY often rises the day after a down day, a short‑term pattern explained by mean reversion—asset prices tend to return to their long‑run average after moving away. A simple strategy that buys after a red day and sells after a green day exploits this effect. Backtesting on SPY (adjusted for dividends and splits) shows the red‑day strategy yields higher returns, spends less time invested and has a significantly lower maximum drawdown than a green‑day strategy or a buy‑and‑hold benchmark. The authors conclude that while momentum works over longer horizons, the S&P 500 exhibits strong mean‑reverting behavior in the short term.

According to PEN America, U.S. public schools recorded 22,810 book‑banning incidents from 2021 to 2025, sparking concern among librarians and teachers. While colleges previously avoided bans, recent actions have targeted books on diversity, gender and politics at institutions such as Franciscan University of Steubenville (barred a book about the Virgin Mary), New College of Florida (removed gender‑studies texts), the U.S. Naval Academy (banned 381 titles by Ibram X. Kendi, later restored most), and West Point (where professor Graham Parsons resigned after works by Baldwin, Morrison, Walker and others were removed). Several states now require public syllabi to flag controversial readings, and the Trump administration asked nine universities to sign a “Compact for Academic Excellence” that would mandate transforming or abolishing units that belittle conservative ideas, with loss of federal funding. Texas A&M dismissed a professor over gender‑identity content and ordered course audits. During the Carter administration, MONs were used to introduce higher-risk, higher-cost, or geographically specific operations under previously approved objectives, requiring CIA, State Department, and broader interagency coordination. The Hughes-Ryan amendment required timely congressional notification of new presidential findings, typically within 48 hours. The 1980 Intelligence Authorization Act limited notification requirements to the two intelligence committees, clarified that notification did not require congressional approval, and established the "Gang of Eight" provision allowing limited prior notice to congressional leaders in extraordinary circumstances. The passage also includes a table of contents for a Soviet Union section covering January 1983–March 1985 with references to Reagan Library documents and communications between Shultz, Clark, Dobrynin, and others regarding US-Soviet relations and Shultz's four-part agenda.

St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Company v. Conarty, opinion delivered February 3, 1913, affirmed a $10,000 judgment of the Crawford Circuit Court in favor of Fannie M. Conarty, administratrix of the estate of W. Gr. Conarty, deceased.  

The decedent, a switchman, was killed when the locomotive he was riding collided with a disabled coal car that had been loaded at Huntington, Arkansas, consigned to Texas, and was being moved for heavy repairs to Fort Smith. The car lacked proper couplers and draw‑bars. The railroad argued that the case was removable to federal court on diversity grounds, that the car was no longer engaged in interstate commerce, that the defective coupler was not the proximate cause of injury, that the widow‑administratrix could not recover for both pecuniary loss and pain‑and‑suffering, and that her testimony regarding contributions was inadmissible under the Arkansas Constitution.  

The court held that the Federal Employers’ Liability Act, as amended in 1910, expressly prohibits removal, that the car remained in interstate commerce while being switched in the yard, and that the carrier’s absolute duty under the Safety Appliance Act attached when the car was moved regardless of repair status. The defect was the direct cause of the injury, and liability attached even though the decedent was not handling the coupler. The 1910 amendment allows a single action for the benefit of the widow and next of kin that may include both loss of contributions and the deceased’s pain and suffering; no election was required because only one suit was prosecuted. The wife’s testimony about the amount of contributions was admissible as it concerned a matter collateral to the main issue of liability.  

All assignments of error were rejected, and the judgment for $10,000 was affirmed.

The phase of an optical field can be estimated by interferometry. For an unbiased estimator the variance satisfies the quantum Cramer–Rao bound Var[δ ˜ϕ]≥1/FQ, with FQ≤n(n+2) for unentangled inputs. A pair of squeezed states with total photon number n saturates this bound and yields Heisenberg scaling Var[δ ˜ϕ]∝1/n. With squeezing limited to bandwidth ΔΩ, the spectral bound is ¯Sδ ˜ϕδ ˜ϕ[Ω]≥1/(ΔΩπ n(n+2)). This bound is attained by a nonlinear estimator applied to filtered outputs of two homodyne detectors; the estimator δ ˜ϕ(t)=(˜qout1^2−˜qout2^2)/[(V+−V−)ΔΩ/π] reaches it.

Chronic hepatitis C (CHC) is associated with progression to cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma and extrahepatic complications including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Elevated risks of T2DM have been linked to CHC, cirrhosis and decompensated cirrhosis, while HCV clearance reduces this risk. Inflammation‑related markers (neutrophil‑to‑lymphocyte ratio, NLR; platelet‑to‑lymphocyte ratio, PLR) and the prognostic nutritional index (PNI) have prognostic value in various cancers.

The study assessed NLR, PLR and PNI as prognostic indicators in patients with CHC‑associated cirrhosis complicated by T2DM. Between January 2018 and December 2021, 56 CHC‑cirrhosis patients with T2DM (Group A), 85 CHC‑cirrhosis patients (Group B) and 85 T2DM patients (Group C) were recruited at Fu Yang Second People’s Hospital. Group A was stratified after 6 months of treatment into a good‑prognosis subgroup (33 patients) and a poor‑prognosis subgroup (23 patients). Laboratory data collected at admission included serum albumin, AST, ALT, platelet, lymphocyte, mononuclear and neutrophil counts; NLR, PNI and PLR were calculated as NLR = neutrophils/lymphocytes, PNI = albumin (g/L) + 5 × lymphocytes (10⁹/L), PLR = platelets/lymphocytes. The study received ethics committee approval and informed consent from all participants.

The Rubber Band strategy is a contrarian/mean-reversion method for trading stocks that identifies overbought and oversold levels using indicators like Keltner Channels or Bollinger Bands. Traders buy when price is below the lower band and sell when above the upper band, targeting the mean (middle band). A backtest example on the XLP ETF (328 trades) yielded a 6.1% CAGR, a 2 profit factor, and spent only 20% time in the market over roughly ten years. It is less effective on assets like commodities or gold.

UK university staff are in their fourth week of strikes over changes to defined‑benefit pensions. Talks have failed, prompting the UCU higher education committee to announce 14 days of strikes, expected in April‑June, the exam period. The outcome depends on negotiations between Universities UK and the UCU. The University of Edinburgh has been criticised for asking lecturers to provide old recorded lectures to replace striking‑affected teaching.

Using ADNI data, this study developed a two-stage machine learning framework to predict rates of cognitive decline and progression to dementia in non-demented individuals. The framework combined plasma biomarkers (Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL), MRI data, demographics, and baseline cognitive scores (memory, executive function, language, visuospatial) using ridge linear regression for MRI processing and random forest regression for final prediction. Four models were compared. The combined model significantly outperformed others for predicting memory decline, increasing correlation from 0.38 (basic model) to 0.50. Plasma biomarkers NfL and p-tau181 were significant predictors, while Aβ42/40 showed lower importance. MRI scores were the most important predictor for memory decline. Prediction was more accurate for individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) than cognitively unimpaired (CU) subjects. The predicted memory decline rate effectively stratified risk of progression to dementia, with the combined model showing a 33-fold higher risk for the highest versus lowest tertile in CU individuals.

A new report from the National Academy of Sciences and the National Academy of Medicine says scientists should be allowed to edit human germline DNA only to prevent serious, strongly heritable diseases, not to enhance traits. Germline editing is illegal in the United States, but CRISPR‑Cas9 is being used to modify disease genes in adult cells; a Chinese trial recently began using CRISPR to treat lung cancer, raising concerns about a competitive disadvantage for U.S. and European researchers. The 22‑member international panel recommends that germline clinical trials only proceed when no reasonable alternative exists, when the targeted gene is known to cause or strongly predispose to a serious disease, and when risks and benefits are weighed. All trials should be open to public scrutiny, address societal fairness, personal dignity and scientific integrity, and include long‑term follow‑up of edited descendants. The panel stresses that genome‑editing research is an international endeavor requiring oversight that reflects societal values in each nation’s regulatory framework. The report was co‑chaired by MIT’s Richard O. Hynes and UW‑Madison’s R. Alta Charo and included members from the United States, China, France, Israel and Italy; funding came in part from the Department of Defense and the FDA. Dr. J. Patrick Whelan described the report as a valuable step toward responsible conversation and ethical structures in the rapidly advancing field.

Arrested eight women and 15 men in May 21–27, checked 700 at locations in Yishun and Sengkang. Women charged Women’s Charter for services; S$730, phones seized. Men under Common Gaming House Act; four ran gambling den, one drink‑driving.

TeraAgent is a distributed simulation engine that extends BioDynaMo to overcome three critical restrictions: limited simulation size (~1.7 billion agents), impractical integration with MPI-based third-party software, and hardware flexibility constraints. TeraAgent divides simulation space across multiple servers using spatial partitioning, enabling agents to interact locally while distributing computation. The system introduces a novel serialization mechanism that avoids pointer deduplication, deserialization overhead, endianness conversions, and schema evolution, achieving 110× faster serialization and 37× faster deserialization compared to ROOT IO. A delta encoding scheme reduces data transfer between servers by up to 3.5× by exploiting gradual agent attribute changes between iterations. TeraAgent supports both MPI-only and MPI-hybrid parallelization modes, allowing seamless scaling from laptops to supercomputers without code modifications. Evaluation demonstrates simulations of 501.51 billion agents on 84,096 CPU cores—an 84× improvement over state-of-the-art—8× higher efficiency than Biocellion, and 39× faster in-situ visualization performance. The system enables extreme-scale agent-based simulations previously impossible due to scaling limitations.

STH infections affect over a billion people, primarily in low‑ and middle‑income countries; WHO recommends an integrated approach including preventive chemotherapy (PC), sanitation and hygiene. PC coverage has risen to ~60% of at‑risk children, reducing prevalence globally, but endemic countries must periodically conduct impact‑assessment surveys (IAS) to decide whether to continue PC. Traditional IAS are expensive, especially where resources are limited. The authors propose a model‑based geostatistical (MBG) framework that uses baseline prevalence data, environmental covariates and PC treatment history to predict prevalence at the time of an IAS. The method fits a geostatistical model to baseline data, projects the prevalence surface forward with a multi‑state Markov model that incorporates the number of effective PC rounds, and then applies local thinning to generate an estimated impact surface. Using this projected surface, a spatially‑regulated survey design is created that selects a reduced number of schools and children while respecting a minimum separation distance. Performance is evaluated by comparing classification of implementation units into endemicity classes and by the required sample size and cost. Applied to Kenya, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe, the MBG approach achieved the same classification accuracy as conventional surveys but required on average 80% fewer schools and children—cost reductions of 91% for Zimbabwe, 86% for Kenya and 62% for Sierra Leone. The authors note that the MBG method provides finely resolved prevalence maps, can help sustain STH control by identifying residual hotspots, and a manual and web application are being developed for its implementation.

Home prices rose 7.1% YoY and 1.1% MoM in May 2018, supply. 40% of the 100 largest metros and 52% of the top 50 markets were overvalued. Utah, Washington, Nevada and Idaho posted double‑digit growth. CoreLogic forecasts a 5.1% rise by 2019, prices soar in Denver, San Francisco and Seattle.

The invention provides a driver monitoring method and system for a vehicle that captures interior and exterior images with one or more cameras and processes the image data together with vehicle sensor signals. The system estimates driver attention by computing a maximum driver workload (initially a preset value that can be adjusted based on driver characteristics) and then evaluating a distraction workload and a driving workload. Inputs used for the estimation include driver identity, posture, health (e.g., biometrics), emotions, visual focus, vehicle control data, media usage, environment conditions (weather, traffic, road geometry), drowsiness indicators, and passenger activity. Each input carries a state, confidence, availability, and a calibration weight that can start at a default and evolve through testing or real‑time use. The amount of driver attention is calculated as the maximum workload minus the weighted sum of the distraction and driving workloads, expressed as a percentage between 0 and 100. Modules within the system receive these inputs, produce outputs with confidence, and include adjustable calibration functions. The system can also monitor passengers to refine driver estimates and, in autonomous‑vehicle operation, an occupant may become the driver when a takeover is required. The driver monitoring system may interface with exterior sensors (radar, lidar, cameras), communicate via vehicle‑to‑vehicle (V2V) or vehicle‑to‑infrastructure (V2X) links, and can take autonomous control (e.g., braking or steering) if a detected risk exceeds a threshold.

Shonda Rhimes has signed a deal for her Shondaland company to produce series for Netflix. Her shows (“Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal,” “How to Get Away With Murder”) will remain on ABC. Financial terms and duration were not disclosed. Rhimes, 47, has three Emmy nominations.

The American Academy of Pediatrics advises that five medical tests commonly ordered for children with growth or development concerns—hormone tests, endocrine tests, vitamin D screening, thyroid/insulin tests for overweight children, and thyroid ultrasounds—are often unnecessary for otherwise healthy children. Doctors should weigh risks and benefits before ordering these tests. Hormone tests may be unnecessary without physical puberty signs. Screening tests rarely reveal issues (1% for shorter children). Vitamin D testing applies only to patients with bone mass disorders. Thyroid testing for obese children should only occur with abnormal growth or other thyroid signs. Thyroid ultrasounds should be limited to specific cases with neck swelling, palpable nodules, or very enlarged glands.

Grassroots Leadership posted on its website letters from women held at the T. Don Hutto Residential Center in Taylor, Texas, describing conditions in immigration detention. One woman, who called the holding area “la perrera” because of chain‑link cages, said she and other women were not allowed to bathe or brush their teeth for eight days and slept on the floor under aluminum‑paper blankets. The women reported being separated from their children and not knowing their fate for up to 21 days. Additional letters from other women, including Mirian and a Guatemalan mother, expressed heartbreak and asked for help to be released and reunited with their children. One account from a woman identified as Claudia recounted crossing the river on May 21 and being separated from her son after being taken to criminal court. The anonymous writer’s lawyer said she was first detained near Hidalgo, Texas, then transferred to Laredo and finally Hutto, while her children were moved to Michigan and released to their father on June 19. ICE said it could not respond because names and facility details were redacted. Volunteers with Grassroots Leadership helped the women draft and send the letters, which are part of a petition to reunite separated families.

Pairs trading is a market‑neutral strategy that simultaneously buys one highly correlated asset and sells another to profit from temporary mispricing. Traders analyze the historical co‑movement and price difference (the “spread”) of two instruments—commonly stocks, ETFs, futures or currencies—and enter positions when the spread diverges, expecting it to revert to its historical relationship. A typical rule might be to short the stronger stock and buy the weaker when the spread widens, or vice‑versa.

Key advantages include the ability to make money in up, down or sideways markets, a high win‑ratio of small gains, and uncorrelated returns that improve overall portfolio performance. Studies report average annualized excess returns of roughly 11 % to 15.9 % for well‑selected pairs, and a high Sharpe ratio because the equity curve tends to be smoother.

Pairs trading also has notable drawbacks: it relies on leverage to achieve acceptable returns, involves commissions, slippage and borrowing costs for short positions, and can suffer from “black‑swan” events when the spread fails to converge. Different betas and fundamentals mean the strategy is not truly market‑neutral, and pairs can wander apart out‑of‑sample as companies’ fortunes diverge.

Effective pair selection hinges on high correlation (often ≥ 0.80) and, preferably, cointegration, which measures long‑term stability of the spread. Cointegration tests such as the Johansen or Engle‑Granger methods help identify pairs whose price ratio remains constant over time.

Implementation often uses technical tools (e.g., RSI, Bollinger Bands) to generate entry and exit signals, and may be automated with platforms offering real‑time data, risk management, and execution capabilities. Successful traders emphasize understanding each stock’s fundamentals, employing strict risk controls, diversifying across many pairs, and adjusting position size for beta and volatility.

In practice, simple rule‑based strategies on pairs like KO/PEP or GS/MS have shown positive returns (e.g., 113 % on a naive rule from 2000 to today) but have produced little or no gain in the last decade, illustrating diminishing edge. Overall, pairs trading remains viable for hedge funds and proprietary traders, but profitability depends on leverage, diversification, robust pair selection and disciplined risk management.

A method and apparatus for displaying a marker element in a virtual scene, a terminal, and a computer‑readable storage medium are disclosed. The terminal renders a display interface of a virtual scene containing multiple virtual items. Upon receiving a marking operation from a user account, the terminal obtains marker indication information that identifies a target virtual item marked for viewing by other user accounts in the same team. Graphic data of a marker element is then obtained according to the marker indication information, the marker element being a graphic that indicates the location of the target virtual item to teammates. The terminal renders the marker element and displays it at a designated location around the target virtual item in the display interface. The disclosed method also optionally obtains and displays distance information (straight‑line, horizontal, or height difference) between the target virtual item and the current virtual object, displays a thumbnail‑map marker icon, supports marker‑type selection, and removes the marker after a server‑determined or locally‑determined preset duration when the target item is no longer within the visible distance of the current virtual object. The invention is implemented by terminals communicating with a server that validates visibility distances and synchronizes marker indication information to the relevant team members.

Thomas Alter, a Texas State professor, was fired after a speech at a socialism conference; a judge ordered his reinstatement citing free‑speech violations, without pay. He is among faculty terminated; Michael Hook, a South Dakota professor, was reinstated after Facebook comments.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Q3 2016 10-Q report for the quarter ended September 30, 2016. Total revenues were $2.30 billion, up 145% from $936.8 million in Q3 2015, driven by increased vehicle deliveries including Model X ramp-up. The company reported net income of $21.9 million compared to a net loss of $229.9 million in Q3 2015. Cash and cash equivalents increased to $3.08 billion from $1.20 billion at year-end 2015. Lundqvist reflected on a tough loss, describing a late first‑period goal that shifted momentum. He said the team generated many chances but the opponent’s saves kept them from tying. While acknowledging he gave up three or more goals, he felt his positioning and puck tracking were solid and attributed the goals to deflections and a two‑on‑one. He emphasized belief the series can be turned around, stressed the importance of a strong start, focusing on the next shot rather than the final result, and maintaining the same overall approach with minor improvements. Lundqvist mentioned he will skate today and rest tomorrow to conserve energy, and noted the team must accept their disappointment, stay angry but move forward. He praised the opposing team’s defensive play and goaltending, saying they will need to play their best, create traffic in front of the net, get to loose pucks, and rely on some luck to earn their first win.

Researchers at La Jolla Institute for Immunology analyzed blood samples from 40 ALS patients and 28 healthy controls and found stronger T‑cell responses to the C9orf72 protein, which is tied to the most common ALS‑linked mutation. Responses to other ALS proteins (TDP‑43 and SOD1) did not differ between groups. Among patients with anti‑C9orf72 T cells, those whose cells produced higher levels of the anti‑inflammatory molecule IL‑10 had longer predicted survival. The findings indicate an autoimmune component in ALS and suggest possible new treatment approaches by modulating the immune system and using autoreactive cells to track disease progression. The authors caution that the results do not prove ALS is an autoimmune disease; self‑reactive T cells may be a consequence rather than a cause of neuronal loss. Future work will include larger studies, simpler isolation of autoreactive cells, and animal models to test whether these immune responses drive disease.

S&P 500 closed up +2.2% in July, up +7.8% YTD, marking its 3rd month back above the 10-month moving average. Market momentum remains intact but short-term technicals show early warning signs, with 50-day breadth rolling over from overbought levels. Volatility and credit spreads are seeing a seasonal upturn, investors are increasingly favoring tech stocks, and US electricity demand has reached new all-time highs. Japan is seeing a rise in cryptocurrency‑related crime while overall crime rates fall. The Jan. 26 theft of 523 million NEM coins from Coincheck, valued at ¥58 billion, sparked concerns; the FSA had previously warned Coincheck about security. Japan hosts many exchanges, recognised bitcoin as legal tender in 2017, and over 30 % of global bitcoin trading is yen‑denominated. Recent scams include ransomware and fraudulent ICOs; the FSA issued an advisory on ICO risks and Facebook banned related ads. The SEC halted a $600 million ICO in the U.S., while Japan’s regulatory framework for ICOs remains unclear.

The Ontario Liberal government, if re‑elected, plans to scrap province‑wide EQAO tests for Grades 3 and 9, remove the mandatory high‑school literacy test, and replace the remaining Grade 6 and 9 tests with less rigorous assessments. The proposals come from the “Ontario: A Learning Province” report commissioned by Premier Kathleen Wynne and released by Education Minister Indira Naidoo‑Harris, which recommends shifting more assessment responsibility to teachers. The government released the report after the June 7 election and had earlier denied intentions to eliminate the tests. The independent Ontario Education, Quality and Accountability Office (EQAO) was not consulted; EQAO officials say eliminating the primary‑division test would remove half the independent data used to track school improvement. Critics argue the changes would reduce objective measurement of student performance and accountability, noting that teachers already assess students but not the broader system. The report suggests further consultation before implementing its 18 recommendations.

For the fiscal year ending 30 June 2020 it reported assets of AUD 3,789 million, loans and advances of AUD 3,206 million, deposits and short‑term borrowings of AUD 3,019 million, net interest revenue of AUD 70.5 million, net profit after tax of AUD 18.5 million and dividends of AUD 13.6 million.

The WEA Teacher Residency Program is a union-led alternative teacher certification program in Washington State, piloted in 2023–24 to address persistent special education teacher shortages and underrepresentation of diverse educators. Using an exploratory case study design, the program involved 16 teacher residents across three districts, examining evidence-based training components, technology integration, and incentives. The program incorporates culturally responsive practices, family engagement, and Universal Design for Learning, delivered through a Hyflex model with competency-based assessments and four field placements. Mentors and coaches provide support, and emerging technologies such as AI-based simulation (Mursion) are utilized. Residents receive a living wage, health insurance, and stipends, in exchange for a three-year commitment to the district upon licensure. Funding exceeds $10.5 million from WEA, districts, and state grants. The program demonstrates a comprehensive approach to preparing special education teachers and diversifying the workforce, though scalability and long-term retention require further evaluation.

Motivate, operator of the Bay Area’s Ford GoBike program, launched 250 electric‑assist e‑bikes in San Francisco on Tuesday. The black e‑bikes, branded Ford GoBike Plus, are stationed at dozens of GoBike docks and give a noticeable boost after two to three pedal revolutions, making steep climbs like Page Street easy. The city’s hilly terrain prompted the addition, aimed at attracting new users and expanding typical ride distances from about 2 miles to 3–5 miles. The e‑bikes are part of a regional system with 287 stations and 3,600 bikes funded by the Municipal Transportation Agency, the Metropolitan Transportation Commission and Ford. Only San Francisco currently has them; no rollout schedule exists for Berkeley, Emeryville, Oakland or San Jose. Motivate emphasized its coordinated approach with the city, contrasting its rollout with the controversial sudden appearance of scooters.

The player emphasizes defensive responsibility, playing a simple game without risks, and prioritizing team wins over personal records. He notes that prior experience helps him handle the situation, and while media attention brings recognition, it can also be excessive.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Secretary Abid Majeed has directed formation of committees at provincial, district and union council levels, headed by paediatricians, to oversee the upcoming measles campaign. The campaign, scheduled to launch in October, targets 4.3 million children aged 9-59 months. The secretary emphasized effective communication, social mobilization, staff training, logistics and vaccine availability. Growing measles cases across districts prompted the initiative.

IDC sees IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics as essential for industrial enterprises to respond to disruptive changes with agility and innovation. High‑Performance Computing (HPC) is becoming a prerequisite for modern simulations and can be delivered via on‑premises systems, cloud services, or hybrid models. Effective digital transformation requires a single source of truth across the product life cycle, integrating high‑quality data from development through manufacturing, operations, and service. IDC recommends that enterprises set up virtual product and manufacturing development, develop a holistic data strategy, assess suitable HPC operating models, prioritize scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leverage external expertise. Findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT decision makers in industrial firms with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The Ayoub Sisters, aged 22 and 24, attribute their classical success to fully funded music education in Scotland, citing one‑to‑one lessons, ensemble playing and choir experience. They have recorded with Mark Ronson, performed at the BRIT Awards and released an iTunes‑chart‑topping album recorded at Abbey Road. Of Scotland’s 22 local authorities that charge for music tuition, Highland Council has transferred its service to a charity, while Clackmannanshire has doubled fees to £524 a year and West Lothian is consulting on cuts. Renfrewshire, the only one of ten authorities not charging, has increased spending, pledging £200,000. Former Royal Conservatoire head John Wallace warns council music services could disappear and the EIS reports a drop in music teachers from 1,100 to 640 over the past decade. Campaigns “Save Our Strings” and “Develop not Dismantle” have support from musicians including Evelyn Glennie, Nicola Benedetti and Paolo Nutini. The Scottish Government’s Youth Music Initiative provides free tuition for all primary pupils by Primary 6, but the Culture Secretary says decisions on further charging remain with local authorities. Campaigners say the current provision is insufficient.

Plaintiff Toy Lykins sued Aluminum Workers International Union and Local 480, alleging that defendants used his mandatory union dues for purposes other than collective bargaining, contract administration, and grievance adjustment, violating his First Amendment rights. Defendants moved for summary judgment, arguing lack of a justiciable controversy, failure to exhaust remedies, and no First Amendment violation.

The court denied defendants' motion. It held that: (1) jurisdiction was proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1337(a) because the action arose under an act regulating commerce; (2) plaintiff stated a justiciable controversy because defendants held his money and allegedly spent it in violation of his rights; (3) plaintiff was not required to exhaust statutory remedies under § 201(c) of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act; (4) governmental action existed because the union shop clause was authorized by the National Labor Relations Act; and (5) the NLRA did not authorize unions to spend dissenters' dues for political or ideological purposes unrelated to collective bargaining.

The court ordered plaintiff to amend his complaint regarding jurisdiction, denied defendants' motion for summary judgment, set discovery deadlines, and scheduled a pretrial conference and trial.

A new Gallup‑Walton Family Foundation poll finds that more than one‑in‑four U.S. public‑school teachers lack the basic materials or staffing needed to perform their jobs effectively. Nearly two‑thirds of educators report shortages of teaching assistants, aides, paraprofessionals, mental‑health resources and special‑education staff. About 24 % of teachers say they do not have enough classroom furniture, 25 % lack sufficient laptops or computers and 35 % lack adequate printing supplies; one‑third describe the process for ordering materials as difficult. Job satisfaction is strongly tied to resource adequacy: 77 % of teachers with sufficient resources are satisfied, compared with 44 % of those without. The survey, conducted with 1,989 teachers in fall 2024, 2,046 in January 2025 and 2,167 in spring 2025, shows that teachers also want more collaborative planning and opportunities to observe colleagues, yet only about one‑third receive such opportunities. Shortages affect schools regardless of income level, though wealthier schools are slightly more likely to lack paraprofessionals while lower‑income schools face greater gaps in technology and printing. Jessica Saum, a special‑education coordinator and former Arkansas Teacher of the Year, notes that paraprofessional shortages make teachers’ work harder and contribute to turnover.

He feels honored by a call from coach, Steve Yzerman and Chris Chelios, enjoys winning the Stanley Cup and hopes to repeat it, praises the coach’s excellence, notes retirement, awareness, less controversy, and time flies with missed details.

The lecture focuses on implementing linear constant coefficient difference equations as digital networks. Two graphical representations are discussed: block diagrams and signal flow graphs. Block diagrams use delay ($z^{-1}$), multiplication, and addition elements. Signal flow graphs consist of directed branches connecting numbered nodes (source, sink, and network nodes). In linear signal flow graphs, node variables equal the sum of outputs from entering branches, where each branch output is the input multiplied by a scalar or $z^{-1}$. Algebraically, these graphs correspond to matrix equations representing the system as coupled first-order difference equations, decomposed into current and delayed state matrices. A key network property is computability: a node numbering is computable if the coefficient matrix has no non-zero elements on or above the main diagonal; delay-free loops result in non-computable networks.

Ron Washington will not return as Angels manager after the team declined to pick up his contract option. Washington, 73, missed more than half of the 2025 season following quadruple bypass heart surgery but said the decision was based on team performance rather than his health. The Angels went 36-38 before he left and finished 72-90 overall, their 10th consecutive losing season. Interim manager Ray Montgomery also won't get the full-time role as the Angels search for their sixth manager in nine years. Washington went 99-137 in two seasons with Los Angeles and previously managed the Rangers from 2007-2014. Albert Pujols and Torii Hunter are considered strong candidates for the open managerial position.

The British government disavowed its occupation of the Sandwich Islands in 1843, while French and British rivalry sought to limit growing American influence, which had been expressed through early trade, naval visits, and diplomatic relations. The first Hawaiian embassy to the United States secured U.S. Secretary of State John Webster’s recognition of Hawaiian independence in December 1842, and subsequently obtained a convention between France and Great Britain on 28 November 1843, in which both powers agreed to regard the islands as independent and pledged never to take possession of any part of the territory.

Manchester United lost 2-0 at Spurs, 15 points behind City and five points above fifth. Alexis Sanchez makes debut against Huddersfield; Mourinho will address Fellaini's fitness and Pogba's touchline issue.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, built on the Ampere‑architecture GA100 (TSMC 7 nm N7) with 54.2 billion transistors, contains 108 streaming multiprocessors (SMs), 432 third‑generation Tensor Cores and 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores. It provides 40 GB of HBM2 memory (1555 GB/s bandwidth) and a 40 MB L2 cache (2.3× the L2 read bandwidth of V100). The A100 introduces fine‑grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) that doubles Tensor‑Core throughput, while new Tensor Core data‑type support includes TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8/INT4 and binary formats; TF32 runs 10× faster than V100 FP32 and 20× faster with sparsity, FP16/FP32 mixed‑precision delivers 2.5× the V100 performance (5× with sparsity), and INT8 sparse inference is up to 20× faster. The GPU’s peak mixed‑precision FP16/FP32 throughput reaches 312 TFLOPS and its FP64 throughput reaches 19.5 TFLOPS (2.5× V100). A100 can be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU instances via Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) technology, offering defined QoS and fault isolation for cloud service providers. Third‑generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 delivers 31.5 GB/s, and SR‑IOV enables virtual sharing of the PCIe link. New hardware features include asynchronous copy directly from global memory to shared memory, hardware‑accelerated asynchronous barriers, task‑graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls and compute data compression (up to 4× bandwidth and 2× capacity). The A100 integrates with NVIDIA Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand/Ethernet, CUDA 11, NGC containers and Kubernetes on GPUs, and supports mixed‑precision HPC solvers such as TCAIRS, delivering up to 4× speedup with TF32 on large matrices.

Elliott Management, with a 6% stake, said NXP is worth $135 per share, above Qualcomm's $110 offer, and that the offer undervalued NXP, noting about half its revenue comes from automotive and industrial sectors. NXP shares have risen above the offer but the spread has narrowed. Elliott retained UBS to analyze NXP. Meanwhile, Qualcomm rejected a $103bn Broadcom approach. NXP traded at $116.30, Qualcomm at $64.02.

The Japan Society of Technology Education (JSTE) developed a new framework for technology and engineering education in Japan, titled "The New Framework for Technology and Engineering Education to Create the Next Generation of Learning" (NGTE), published in 2021. This initiative responds to the global rise of STEAM education and Japan's focus on transdisciplinary learning since 2019. JSTE aimed to clarify the role of technology and engineering education within STEAM, addressing previous underestimation and connecting it to societal changes like Society 5.0.

The framework targets both general education for technological literacy among all citizens and professional education for experts. Its primary goal is to foster abilities for technological innovation and governance. NGTE expands previous technology education by incorporating engineering sciences and emphasizing connections between physical and cyber technologies (e.g., AI, IoT, robotics) to enable students to create new value in a complex society.

A survey of 1,656 junior high school students in Hyogo Prefecture revealed that while students hold positive perceptions of technology classes, they lack sufficient exploratory activities and design problem-solving experiences linked to innovation and governance. To address these issues, NGTE introduces the Triple-Loop Model of Engineering Design Process, comprising Needs Exploration, Seeds Exploration, and Creation loops, to enhance problem-solving and design thinking.

NGTE also includes a learning model for STEAM education centered on engineering design, aiming to integrate disciplines through transdisciplinary learning. Evaluation by JSTE members showed general agreement with the framework, though the concept of "engineering" required clarification by distinguishing engineering science from the engineering design process.

The development process involved academic societies assessing current learner status, interpreting it with curriculum revision directions, and proposing curriculum standards as references for national revision. Future tasks include validating NGTE through classroom practice and reforming teacher education to bridge the gap between curriculum aims and actual teaching.

Robert Cyrus Garrison was convicted of first-degree rape in Tulsa County District Court after a second trial and sentenced to 30 years. The trial court gave an instruction required by 57 O.S.Suppl.1969, § 138, which the Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals previously held unconstitutional in Williams v. State. The appellate court found the instruction erroneous but not reversible, and reduced the sentence to 15 years.

Port Hardy Secondary School senior girls soccer team qualified for BC Single A Provincials in Penticton (May 31‑June 3). An audit of state‑run Duquesne School District found former superintendent Barbara McDonnell and staff used district funds as a piggy bank, authorizing $41,000 in no‑interest loans ($22,000 to herself) without board approval, and failing to document $1.3 M in transportation reimbursements, overpaying $180,000; matter referred to the Ethics Commission.

Accepting the Republican presidential nomination, the speaker affirms belief in party government, constitutionalism, and representative popular government; opposes personal or autocratic rule; calls for a cabinet with the Vice President and cooperation with both houses of Congress. He emphasizes restoring Senate authority, safeguarding American sovereignty, and avoiding a world super‑government, while committing to an association of nations that promotes peace through justice, reduced armaments, and clarified international law. The speaker pledges to restore constitutional methods after World War I, secure formal peace with a Republican Congress, and resist any surrender of U.S. rights to a military alliance. Economically, he stresses the need for maximum production, fair wages, and honest work; supports collective bargaining that protects individual freedom; warns that rising wages without increased output threaten ruin; and calls for thrift, economy, and deflation of inflated currency. He outlines a program for rehabilitating railroads, opposes government ownership, advocates federal aid for highways and inland waterways, and supports the Panama Canal for American shipping. The speech embraces agriculture by encouraging cooperative associations, irrigation, and reclamation, and promises protection of the farmer’s interests. On domestic issues it backs a protective tariff, a strong merchant marine and navy, a small but prepared army, selective immigration, limits on child labor, women’s suffrage, and care for veterans and African‑American citizens. The nominee commits to law‑enforcement of existing laws (including the Eighteenth Amendment) and to honest, business‑like federal administration, a balanced budget, and the elimination of waste. He concludes with a call for confidence in the Republic, the preservation of liberty, and a pledge of service to the country and to God.

Between 2012 and 2018 the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers (IAM) organized Maine lobstermen into a local lodge called Lobster 207 (IAM Local 207) and a statewide marketing cooperative, the Maine Lobstering Union (MLU). The effort began after a Vinalhaven lobsterman contacted his brother, an IAM District 4 member, and received approval from IAM headquarters. Business representative David “Sully” Sullivan and organizer Joel Pitcher held open meetings, provided training at the IAM Winpisinger Center, and built membership through dockside outreach, reaching 99 signatures by February 2013 and growing to roughly 550 lobstermen by 2017, with about 250 paying dues.

Lobster 207’s goals were to give self‑employed lobstermen collective power, create a statewide co‑op, improve economic viability, protect the next generation, influence regulation, and engage in environmental stewardship.

Political victories included legislation protecting lobstermen on military duty, opposing an Army Corps dredging project, influencing dragging restrictions, electronic‑monitoring rules, and license‑fee increases, and helping defeat a Right‑to‑Work bill. Members ran for office; Robert Alley was elected and re‑elected to the Maine House of Representatives.

Economic power was pursued by incorporating a marketing co‑op (MLU) that is exempt from antitrust laws, enabling profit‑sharing, group purchasing, and price‑setting. The lecture discusses capabilities and privilege separation in operating systems, focusing on the "confused deputy" problem where a Fortran compiler inadvertently misused its "home files license" to write to privileged files, highlighting the issue of ambient authority where operations succeed if any set of privileges permits them. Capabilities are presented as an alternative where access is granted only through unforgeable tokens (like file descriptors), eliminating ambient authority by explicitly naming the privilege for each operation. Capsicum, a FreeBSD system, is described as implementing capability-based sandboxing by eliminating global namespaces (e.g., filesystem paths, PIDs) through kernel changes like cap_enter, openat, and process descriptors, supported by libcapsicum for fd lists and clean sandbox initialization. The lecture compares Capsicum with Unix mechanisms and virtual machines, noting that Capsicum provides fine-grained control but requires careful capability assignment, correct kernel implementation, and only protects code once in capability mode.

Magic Formula, introduced by Joel Greenblatt in The Little Book That Beats the Market, selects stocks by ranking companies on two metrics: earnings yield (EY) – the inverse of the P/E ratio – and return on invested capital (ROIC). Stocks are ranked separately on each metric; the sum of the two ranks determines the overall ranking, with lowest combined rank considered best. The strategy aims to buy high‑quality, undervalued firms. Implementation involves defining a universe (usually large‑ or mid‑cap listed stocks), ranking by EY and ROIC, and selecting the top‑ranked securities, either via passive index funds or active stock picking.

Backtests covering the US market from 1988‑2004 showed the top 30 stocks returned about 30.8% annually versus 12.4% for the S&P 500; the formula outperformed in 14 of 17 years. A later backtest from 1999‑2023 also outperformed the S&P 500 with a higher Sharpe ratio, though with larger drawdowns. Studies in Sweden, Finland and Norway reported similar outperformance for the upper‑half of the ranking relative to local indices.

The approach is praised for simplicity and a proven long‑term record, but critics note it relies on historical data, can overweight small‑cap or sector‑specific stocks, and often excludes transaction costs. It also lacks consideration for qualitative factors such as management quality. Risks include potential underperformance during growth‑focused markets and that past results do not guarantee future returns.

The lecture describes a step‑by‑step design of a low‑pass IIR digital filter using two mapping techniques—impulse invariance and the bilinear transformation—starting from an analog Butterworth prototype.

Analog Butterworth filters are defined by the magnitude‑squared function  
|Hₐ(jΩ)|² = 1 / [1 + (Ω/Ωc)²ᴺ] ,  
where Ωc is the cutoff frequency and N is the filter order. The frequency response is monotonic; a larger N gives a flatter passband and a sharper roll‑off. The poles of the squared‑magnitude function lie on a circle of radius Ωc (the Butterworth circle) equally spaced in angle; the left‑half‑plane poles correspond to a causal, stable analog filter.

Digital specifications are: passband 0 ≤ ω ≤ 0.2π with ≤ 1 dB ripple, stopband ω ≥ 0.3π with ≥ 15 dB attenuation.

Impulse‑invariance design: Convert digital frequencies to analog via Ω = ω/T, neglect aliasing initially, and impose the 1 dB passband and 15 dB stopband constraints on the analog Butterworth magnitude. Solving the resulting two equations yields N ≈ 5.886 and ΩcT ≈ 0.705. Because N must be an integer, N = 6 is selected; the passband constraint is met exactly, the stopband constraint is exceeded, compensating for aliasing. The analog poles are placed in the left‑half plane, then the impulse‑invariant mapping converts the analog filter to a digital filter. The resulting magnitude meets the specifications: ≈ 1 dB loss at ω = 0.2π and over 15 dB loss at ω = 0.3π.

Bilinear‑transformation design: Pre‑warp the critical digital frequencies through the bilinear warping curve (Ω = 2 tan(ω/2)) to obtain analog frequencies. With T = 1, solving the same two constraint equations gives N ≈ 5.3, again requiring N = 6. In this case the stopband specification is satisfied exactly, exceeding the passband requirement. The analog filter is mapped to digital using the bilinear transformation. The resulting filter also satisfies the specifications, with a slightly steeper stopband than the impulse‑invariant design because of frequency warping.

The parameter T is shown to be irrelevant for both methods; the final digital filter is independent of its chosen value.

The lecture notes that the low‑pass design procedure extends to band‑pass, band‑stop, and high‑pass filters via frequency transformations, and that finite‑impulse‑response designs will be covered next.

Thokozani Khupe was elected leader of a new MDC breakaway faction at an extraordinary congress in Bulawayo on Saturday. Defensive ends (DE) line up on the edge of the offensive line, usually opposite the offensive tackle, and are critical to both stopping the run and pressuring the quarterback. Their responsibilities include executing gap‑sound assignments, forcing ball carriers wide, batting passes, and recording sacks. Elite DEs combine size (6’3–6’7, 270–290 lb), strength, quickness, and technique. The position is considered the top priority on a defense because an elite DE can disrupt an offense’s passing attack, force the quarterback out of rhythm, and allow defenses to use fewer blitzes. Historically notable DEs include Reggie White (2× Defensive Player of the Year, 198 career sacks), Bruce Smith (all‑time NFL sack leader), and Dwight Freeney (noted for his speed off the snap). The role’s importance grows as offenses shift to pass‑heavy, spread formations.

TLV321x devices include an internal power‑on‑reset (POR) that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply reaches 1.65 V. The basic comparator compares the input voltage (VIN) to a reference (VREF); when VIN exceeds VREF the output switches high, and swapping the input pins inverts the logic. Propagation delay (tpLH, tpHL) is measured from the input mid‑point to the output transition and increases when the overdrive voltage (VOD) is small (<100 mV). Internal hysteresis is only 1.8 mV, so external hysteresis can be added using resistor networks. Inverting hysteresis uses three resistors referenced to VCC, with trip points VA1 and VA2 defined by the given equations; non‑inverting hysteresis uses two resistors and a reference, with thresholds VIN1 and VIN2 and hysteresis equal to VIN1–VIN2. A low‑side current‑sense application alerts when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Designers should bypass the supply with a low‑ESR 0.1 µF capacitor placed close to the device, minimize input‑output coupling, and consider series resistors and controlled‑impedance traces for fast edges. The devices can operate from split or single supplies, and input signals must stay within the recommended range. Documentation updates are available through the product folder on ti.com, and ESD handling precautions are required.

The passage describes the AMD SEV‑ES and SEV‑SNP Guest‑Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification. Its purpose is to standardize the GHCB memory area, the required Non‑Automatic Exits (NAEs) and minimum guest state exposure, and specific actions needed when running as an SEV‑ES or SEV‑SNP guest.

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page that mirrors the SEV‑ES VMCB save‑state area through offset 0x3ff. Guests and hypervisors communicate through the VMGEXIT instruction. VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AE) or Non‑Automatic Exits (NAE); NAE events always raise a #VC exception, allowing the guest to copy register state into the GHCB and invoke VMGEXIT.

Version 2 of the specification introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap (limited to 52 bits) and adds support for SEV‑SNP. The bitmap is returned before a GHCB is established and indicates optional features such as base SEV‑SNP support, AP VMSA creation, Restricted Injection (IPI and timer), APIC ID list retrieval, multi‑VMPL execution, page state change, trusted IO (TDISP), and GHCB unregistration.

The GHCB MSR protocol (MSR 0xc001_0130) uses the lower 12 bits for request/response codes. Defined request codes include: 0x001 (SEV Information), 0x002 (SEV Information via MSR), 0x004 (CPUID Request), 0x005 (CPUID Response), 0x06/0x07 (AP Reset Hold request/response), 0x10/0x11 (Preferred GHCB GPA request/response), 0x12/0x13 (Register GHCB GPA request/response), 0x14/0x15 (Page State Change request/response), 0x16/0x17 (Run VMPL request/response), 0x18/0x19 (Unregister GHCB GPA request/response), 0x080/0x081 (Hypervisor Feature Support request/response), and a termination request. The protocol requires exclusive access to the GHCB during VMGEXIT and recommends disabling interrupts and preemption.

GHCB GPA registration is mandatory for SEV‑SNP guests. Guests can query a preferred GPA, register a GPA (hypervisor updates the RMP table to make the page shared), and later unregister it. Registration automatically unregisters any previously registered GPA.

NAE event handling follows a standard pattern: the guest clears the VALID_BITMAP, sets the required state fields and SW_EXITCODE, writes the GHCB GPA to the MSR, and issues VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit, updates the GHCB with results, and resumes the guest. The VALID_BITMAP bit position is calculated as (field_offset / 8) mod 8 within a byte. Specific NAE events are documented for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, and #NPF/MMIO accesses, the latter using the SW_SCRATCH shared buffer for decrypted data transfers.

The document also specifies the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area (expanded to 64‑bit sequence numbers), the EFI SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table GUID, and the handling of NMIs, SMP booting, debug registers, SMM, and nested virtualization. A changelog notes updates across revisions 2.01–2.04, including new error codes, VLEK GUID, APIC ID list support, multi‑VMPL, page state change improvements, SEV‑TIO, and Secure AVIC.

Lasik treatment in Dubai is a widely performed eye surgery that corrects vision and eliminates the need for glasses or contact lenses. It is painless, provides immediate results, and allows patients to see clearly right after the procedure. Recovery is quick; most activities can be resumed within 24 hours without bandages or stitches.
