An international team led by scientists from Senckenberg and the University of Vienna found that alien species numbers have increased continuously worldwide over the last 200 years, with no signs of saturation. Over 45,000 first records of more than 16,000 alien species were analyzed. More than a third of introductions occurred between 1970-2014, peaking in 1996 with 585 new species recorded. Different taxonomic groups show varying trends attributed to human activities such as colonial expansion and trade globalization. The study, published in Nature Communications, indicates current mitigation efforts are insufficient and more effective prevention policies are needed.

Joe Graedon of People’s Pharmacy reported that a 5% weight loss may need a 10% calorie reduction to maintain, contributing to regain; an article addresses weight maintenance, and dMeetings offers diabetes education.

Pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) at diagnosis in 3,216 advanced cancer patients identified actionable biomarkers in 49% of cases, increasing clinical trial eligibility compared to 50-gene panel testing. Precision therapies (targeted therapy or immunotherapy) were used in 67% of patients and were associated with significantly better overall survival than chemotherapy (median 25 vs 17 months overall; 26 vs 16 months in NSCLC). This is the first report of precision therapies overtaking cytotoxic treatments in community-based care.

FoLix is the first FDA‑cleared fractional laser for hair loss. It creates microscopic scalp channels that trigger a controlled wound‑healing response, boost circulation and deliver growth signals to existing follicles. The treatment is noninvasive, requires no anesthesia, takes 20–30 minutes per in‑office session and has minimal downtime, allowing patients to return to work immediately. Typically, three to six sessions are needed in the first year (spaced a few weeks to a month apart), followed by up to two maintenance sessions per year. Cost ranges from $750 to $1,250 per session. FoLix works best for early to moderate hair loss with intact but underperforming follicles; it is not for complete baldness or scarring. Side effects can include temporary redness, tightness, scalp sensitivity and shedding. It offers a surgery‑free alternative to hair transplants and may suit those who prefer to avoid daily oral medications. A physician should be consulted before treatment to determine the underlying cause of hair loss.

The article investigates the perspectives of visually impaired students in Turkey on the distance‑education process used for professional music education. It notes that distance learning, accelerated by COVID‑19, has become the dominant educational model worldwide and outlines Turkey’s four historical phases of distance education (conceptual, mail‑based, radio‑TV, internet‑based). The study’s aim is to determine how the model is applied to visually impaired learners, assess the accessibility of technological tools and digital content, identify challenges, and evaluate effectiveness.

Methodology – A qualitative case‑study approach was employed. Data were collected via semi‑structured telephone and online interviews during COVID‑19, using questions validated by music‑education experts. The participant group consisted of seven visually impaired students who were enrolled in undergraduate or graduate music programmes at various Turkish universities; the sample represented about 80 % of the national population of visually impaired music‑department students. Content analysis was used to identify themes and codes.

Findings – Five participants were undergraduate and two graduate students, studying in Turkish Music, Musicology, Music, and Music Education departments. Most institutions delivered courses synchronously; only one participant reported asynchronous use for some subjects. Equipment used included computers, cell phones, and tablets, with all participants able to operate their devices independently. Course documents were rated sufficient by some, insufficient by others, and sometimes absent; special needs were not addressed in the materials. Assessment methods varied: several students received individual arrangements (e.g., video submissions, homework) while others followed general arrangements, with many reporting difficulties in written exams.

Strengths of distance education reported by participants included spatial and temporal flexibility and increased social acceptance. Weaknesses were low productivity, technical deficiencies such as poor sound synchronization and audio quality on video‑conference platforms, and teachers’ limited technological competence.

Students’ suggestions covered: extending lesson duration, providing regular technical support, using voice‑to‑text and screen‑reader‑compatible programs, creating audio‑based course content, improving internet infrastructure, offering accessible music‑notation software and Braille printing, enabling customizable screen settings, and ensuring quicker response from distance‑education centres.

The conclusion emphasizes that visually impaired professional music‑education students face substantial barriers in distance learning, as planning generally assumes normally developing learners. It stresses the need for specialized technological tools (screen readers, speech recognition, Braille printers, audio documents) and for cooperation with parents, professionals, and tailored materials to make distance education accessible and effective.

The United States sued Hale County, Alabama, alleging violations of the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The dispute concerned the county's change from district-based to at-large elections for County Commissioners enacted in 1965, 1971, and 1973 without obtaining federal preclearance approval as required by Section 5 of the Act. The court determined that the Voting Rights Act applies to Hale County because Alabama was designated as a covered state in 1965, automatically subjecting all its political subdivisions to the Act's requirements. The court found that the three enactments failed preclearance and are legally unenforceable. The November 2, 1976 election was permitted to proceed provisionally, and the defendants were ordered to submit the enactments to the Attorney General for review. If preclearance is denied and no successful court action is taken, the county must revert to district-based elections. The court retained jurisdiction of the case.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x architecture succeeds Turing and delivers up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Key advancements include doubled FP32 processing throughput in each SM, second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection performance, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32 and BF16 precision with structured sparsity for up to 2x throughput. The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling achieving up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth, third-generation NVLink with 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between GPUs, PCIe Gen 4 support, and RTX IO for GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets. Products based on GA10x include the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000 workstation GPU, and A40 data center GPU, all featuring hardware-accelerated AV1 decode and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

Anna Gasser won gold in women's Big Air snowboarding at the Pyeongchang Olympics, edging two-time gold medalist Jamie Anderson. Gasser, the reigning world champion, scored 96 on her final double cork 1080 jump, totaling 185.00 points. Anderson led going into the final round but failed to land her last attempt. New Zealand's Zoi Sadowski Synnott took bronze, the country's first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years.

This patent describes flexible cable assemblies for connecting electrical circuitry in a quantum computing system. The flexible cable includes an electrically insulating strip (e.g., polyimide) with a metal stripline inside and metallic grounding planes on both surfaces; it can be attached at one or both ends to a mechanically stiff circuit board (rigid board) and may include a mechanical stiffener. The cable can fan out at the ends to improve mechanical integrity and may incorporate absorptive composite material for high‑frequency filtering. The flexible cable carries DC, low‑frequency and/or high‑frequency signals and is used in a cryogenic system having multiple isothermal plates, a mixing plate and a quantum processing unit with superconducting circuits. The system may combine non‑superconducting and superconducting metal striplines, connected by compliant joints or other connectors, and can integrate components such as filters, attenuators and amplifiers on the rigid boards. Various embodiments include windows in the grounding planes aligned with absorptive material, solder‑bump or compliant‑joint connections, and clamping structures for thermal anchoring to isothermal plates.

Teagasc surveyed 314 male farmers in Ireland. 20% never consulted a doctor, 57% visited one past year, below 65% national average. 39% reported ill health (lower‑back pain, arthritis, anxiety). 20% smoked (vs 24% nationally), 88% drank alcohol, 22% binge drank (21% nationally). Farmers under 45 smoked and drank often; those 45+ reported more arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis at 13%—triple national rate. Mortality from CVD and cancers higher for farmers; factors unclear.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill last month, citing family and retirement. He resigned Sept. 2, when the New York State Commission on Judicial Conduct agreed to drop ethics charges in exchange for his resignation and a ban from judicial office. The commission alleged Nock was rude toward staff and threatened to file grievances and criminal complaints. Nock denied the allegations; his motions were denied. He served as a civil court judge from 2015 and Supreme Court justice from 2018. Anderson Kill said Nock disclosed the allegations before hiring, that no wrongdoing was found, and they were satisfied the allegations did not affect his conduct or character. His lawyer noted no findings.

Baseline C‑reactive protein (CRP) was the strongest predictor of progression to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) or death in hospitalized COVID‑19 patients in the phase 3 LIVE‑AIR trial. In the overall modified intent‑to‑treat population, lenzilumab (a GM‑CSF‑neutralizing monoclonal antibody) improved survival without ventilation (SWOV) compared with placebo (HR 1.54, 95 % CI 1.02–2.32; p = 0.0403). Subgroup analysis showed that participants with baseline CRP < 150 mg/L (≈ 78 % of the study population) derived the greatest benefit: HR 2.54 for SWOV (nominal p = 0.0009), lower incidence of IMV, ECMO, or death (OR 0.38), more ventilator‑free days (25.7 vs 22.7), shorter ICU stay, and faster recovery. No significant lenzilumab effect was observed in patients with baseline CRP ≥ 150 mg/L. Lenzilumab also reduced CRP levels more rapidly than placebo. In the CRP < 150 mg/L subgroup, grade ≥ 3 adverse events were reported in 18 % of lenzilumab‑treated participants versus 28 % in the placebo group; no treatment‑emergent serious adverse events were attributed to lenzilumab. These findings indicate that baseline CRP < 150 mg/L may be a useful biomarker to identify patients most likely to benefit from GM‑CSF neutralization with lenzilumab.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life plus 30 years for the July 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son‑in‑law. She told the court she is innocent, asserted no evidence of her participation, and said she would have stopped the killing if she had known. Judge Stephen Everett warned that her “utter lack of remorse” could affect sentencing. Prosecutors said the motive was the Adelson family’s desire to relocate Markel’s ex‑wife Wendi to South Florida. Her son Charlie Adelson and his girlfriend Katherine Magbanua were charged, and a second hit‑man pleaded guilty to second‑degree murder. Her husband Harvey Adelson also maintained her innocence.

The White House confirmed Saturday it will withdraw the nomination of Kathleen Hartnett White to chair the Council on Environmental Quality. Announced last October, White, a former Texas commission member under then‑Governor Rick Perry, faced opposition over her climate‑change skepticism, statements that particulate pollution is harmless unless inhaled directly, and praise of fossil fuels. Critics pointed to her ties to the Texas Public Policy Foundation, a think‑tank funded by Koch Industries, ExxonMobil, Chevron and other fossil‑fuel companies. The Senate had not acted on her nomination, which was resubmitted in January. Senator Tom Carper called the withdrawal the right decision.

Christopher K. Merker, PhD, CFA, describes institutional investment boards as imperfect and subject to behavioral biases. Prompted by teaching corporate governance at Marquette University, he conducted a five‑year study of public pension funds, creating a research protocol because governance data were scarce. Analysis of 35 plans representing ~14.5% of total assets showed five‑year (2008‑2012) returns ranging from 15% to –4.2% (annualized); the S&P 500 returned 1.4% and a 60/40 balanced index ~4.5%. More than half of the plans underperformed the 4.5% average. The study found that asset owner governance—codified group behavior—explained performance gaps. Key governance factors included board stability, monthly rather than quarterly meetings, a higher share of retired members, and greater staff involvement. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant. A Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient (FEQ) showed the top quintile outperforming the bottom quintile by about two to one, and each unit increase in FEQ corresponded to a 0.36% higher return over five years, indicating measurable governance quality drives investment outcomes.

Ray tracing is a computationally intensive rendering method that simulates realistic lighting with physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Historically, GPUs could not perform real-time ray tracing for games on a single GPU. NVIDIA's Turing GPUs incorporate RT Cores, enabling real-time ray tracing through about ten years of collaborative hardware and software development.

This cross‑sectional study assessed knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) of contraception among 217 female students of NTA TV College, Nigeria. About 55 % had good knowledge, 48 % good attitude and 51 % good practice; 74 % reported ever having sex. Main sources of contraceptive information were friends and the internet; the most commonly used methods were condoms and oral contraceptive pills. Fear of side effects was the most frequent reason for non‑use. Multivariable logistic regression showed that age > 19 years (aOR = 2.63) predicted good knowledge; diploma enrollment (aOR = 2.37), living off‑campus (aOR = 2.13) and good knowledge (aOR = 3.80) predicted good attitude; indigenous ethnicity (aOR = 2.37) and ever engaging in sex (aOR = 24.48) predicted good contraceptive practice. The authors conclude that levels of good KAP are relatively low and urge improved advocacy, policies and youth‑friendly sexual and reproductive health services.

FY 2017 financial results for Hui Ying Financial Holdings Corp (formerly Sino Fortune Holding Corp) show total revenues of $46.50 million, an 88.4% increase from $24.68 million in FY 2016. Net income rose to $15.27 million from $3.44 million, a 343.9% increase, with diluted EPS of $0.21 versus $0.05. Operating income increased to $17.95 million (301.6% increase) and operating margin improved to 38.6% from 18.1%. Operating expenses rose to $28.55 million (41.2% increase) with sales and marketing expense of $22.29 million (37.7% increase) representing 47.9% of revenue versus 65.6% in 2016. General and administrative expense increased to $5.94 million (88.0% increase), accounting for 12.8% of revenue. The company launched an entrusted loan business in June 2017, contributing $1.58 million in financing income (3.4% of total revenue). Chrissy Teigen has publicly shown her thigh stretch marks and explained that she comes from a stretch‑mark‑prone family, having had marks for years. She is expecting a son in June and uses a nightly 10‑15‑minute routine of Aquaphor on her elbows, coconut oil on her body and Lumière de Vie concentrate on her belly to prevent marks; her husband John Legend and daughter Luna assist with the applications. Teigen notes that her belly is the only area without stretch marks, that the Lumière products are provided for free as part of a campaign, and that every model she has worked with also has stretch marks.

Research involving 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10–15 found that girls who used social media for an hour or more by age 10 reported lower well‑being by age 15. Girls used social media more than boys at every age, with 59% of 15‑year‑old girls spending over an hour daily versus 46% of boys. Girls’ happiness scores fell almost three points (36.9 to 33.3) compared with a two‑point decline for boys (36.02 to 34.55). The study, based on 2009–2015 UK Household Panel data and published in BMC Public Health, suggests early social media exposure, especially in girls, may affect later adolescent well‑being; the association may be underestimated due to self‑reported data and school‑day only measurements.

The passage reports on Enron-related news from January 26, 2001. California faces a power crisis with rolling blackouts due to deregulation, and Enron's involvement in India's Maharashtra involves a potential payment default by the state electricity board to Enron's Dabhol Power, prompting US Ambassador mediation. Enron's stock rose on profit forecasts. Enron's "rank and yank" performance review system is causing employee dissatisfaction. Wind farms are resurging as an alternative energy source in California and West Texas, with Enron deploying windmills. The coach discusses the team's approach after losing Chris Pronger to suspension, requiring the entire group to share the void in minutes and responsibility. The team lost three key players for an extended period but has dealt with adversity historically. Chris Kunitz will be a game time decision. The coach addresses undisciplined penalties that need to be reduced while accepting necessary ones that prevent goals. The team prepared too intensely early in a game, taking multiple penalties, but the penalty killing kept them in the game. Individual players stepped up, with Teemu Selanne making key plays including a pass to Dustin Penner. The team must play desperately and match the opponent's intensity in the next game, which will be the toughest to win.

President returns House bill No. 6242 (river‑and‑harbor appropriations) unsigned, objecting that some provisions fund only local projects rather than the common defense, general welfare, or interstate commerce, which he holds exceeds Congress’s constitutional powers. He cites the rise in appropriations: $3.9 million in 1870, $6.6 million in 1875, $9.0 million in 1880, $11.5 million in 1881, and $18.7 million in the current bill. A domestic violence support group meets Tuesdays at noon, free for women survivors. Pakistan Volleyball Federation chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob has urged the federal government to build a sports complex in Abbottabad, citing moderate summer weather and the lack of air‑conditioning at Islamabad’s Liaquat Gymnasium. He criticized the Rs1.2 billion spent on the underutilized Narowal complex and called for an early, four‑month national camp for the Asian Games (Aug‑Sept). The Pakistan Sports Board will meet federation and POA officials on June 6 to finalize preparations after halting camps due to financial problems. Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi arrives Thursday to lead junior, youth and senior camps in Peshawar.

The TPS7H500x-SP are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converter design, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. To prevent subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%, slope compensation—set equal to the inductor falling current slope—is applied via the RSC pin. The datasheet details a design example for a synchronous push-pull converter (5 V output, 500 kHz switching) using GaN devices, including transformer selection (primary inductance 40 µH, turns ratio 2.5), switching device ratings, and output filtering requirements (2.3 mF capacitance to mitigate single-event transients). Frequency compensation using Type 2A topology is specified, and layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds and minimizing high di/dt switching loops. Thermal shutdown activates at approximately 175°C.

Chicago’s former Johnson Publishing headquarters received landmark status, sold for $10 million to 3L Real Estate, which will spend $20 million converting it into 150 apartments with rents $1,200–$2,700, preserving the Ebony and Jet signs. Construction begins 2018, finishes 2019. The building, previously owned by Linda Johnson Rice and Columbia College, was called a historic Black cultural center by Mayor Rahm Emanuel.

The Federal Government laid the foundation for the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said the project, linked to an MoU with the Vatican, aims to leverage science and technology for economic diversification, arguing that past neglect of these fields hindered Nigeria's growth. Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged support for the initiative.

Duane Boning welcomed students at MIT and in Singapore for MIT 2.830J / Control of Manufacturing Processes, a video‑linked class. A recording policy applies to most participants; those who prefer not to be filmed may sit in the video blind spot. When a holiday occurs at one site, the other site holds class and posts a video for the missing location; the first such holiday is Chinese New Year on Thursday.

All course material—lecture slides, readings, problem sets and assignments—is distributed via the Stellar website, which requires registration; slides are posted a day in advance and students may self‑organize printing, but no handouts are provided in class.

The course is interactive, relying on students’ industrial or experimental background. Formal prerequisites listed in the catalog (2.008, 2.810, 6152J, 6041, 15064J) indicate two expectations: substantial exposure to a manufacturing process and basic probability/statistics. No specific class is mandatory; relevant coursework or industry experience satisfies the intent.

Two required textbooks are: *Fundamentals of Semiconductor Process Control* by Gary May and Costas Spanos (available 2007) and *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control* by Douglas C. Montgomery. Both are on reserve at MIT’s library.

Assessment consists of eight weekly problem sets (≈40 % of the grade) in the first two‑thirds of the term, two quizzes (≈40 %), and a three‑student team project (≈20 %) in the final third, with no final exam. Problem sets must be individual write‑ups that explain the reasoning; collaboration on concepts is encouraged but each student must submit his/her own work. The team project requires a presentation during the last class period and a joint report.

Project topics may include process diagnosis, SPC‑based improvement, design‑of‑experiments and response‑surface modeling for optimization and robustness, and advanced applications such as yield or defect modeling. Students are encouraged to consider early possible data sets from research or work experience.

The course focuses on controlling variation and quality. The first third covers statistical process control to detect disturbances; the middle third deals with empirical modeling (design of experiments, response‑surface methods) to make processes robust; the final third addresses feedback control strategies that adjust process inputs in response to observed deviations. A generic process model is introduced comprising a workpiece, process environment, equipment settings, sensors, and a recipe or control algorithm.

Instructors: Duane Boning (lead lecturer, Prof. of EECS) and Dave Hardt (co‑lecturer, on sabbatical); teaching assistant Hayden Taylor (microsystem fabrication). Office‑hour arrangements for Cambridge and virtual office hours for Singapore will be posted on Stellar. Administrative issues are handled via Charlene Blake in EECS headquarters. Reading assignments begin with the first two chapters of the textbooks. A pro‑seminar series (2.888) is available for interested students.

CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction) is a long‑established online advertising company and affiliate network founded in 1998, consistently ranked among the top affiliate networks. It serves as an intermediary between advertisers offering products or services and publishers who promote them for commissions. CJ provides advertisers with advanced tracking, management, and payment tools, and offers publishers promotional resources such as banners and product feeds, along with detailed reporting.

The platform is free to join. Applicants must have a blog or social media profile with relevant content and an audience, and be based in the US or Canada. The sign‑up process involves creating an account, completing an application, adding payment information and any required tax certificates, and building a network profile. Once approved, publishers can browse advertisers by niche or keyword, apply to programs, and receive affiliate links after approval.

CJ pays commissions through direct deposit, check, or Payoneer, with a minimum payout of $50 (US) or $100 (outside the US) within 20 days of month‑end. CJ retains a 5–10 % commission on each sale. The network offers thousands of programs across virtually every niche, with filters for commission type, category, and country. While CJ is praised for its robust features and ease of use, it has a learning curve and a relatively strict approval process. CJ also lists alternative affiliate networks for users seeking different platforms.

The Eagles held a Monday practice at the NovaCare Complex for Thursday’s preseason game versus the Bills. Cornerback Ronald Darby, traded Friday for Jordan Matthews, took snaps Sunday. Video Output terminals provide Composite/S-Video Luminance and Chrominance amplifier outputs with Normal mode (using internal amplifier) and TVOUT Bypass mode (external amplifier), requiring external resistors and feedback connections. Supply voltages include variable core voltages (CVDD, CVDD_ARM, CVDD_DSP), 1.8V and 3.3V I/O supplies, and 1.5V/1.8V DDR supplies. Boot configuration uses BTMODE[15:0] pins to determine boot mode order and options including XIP NOR, NAND, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART modes. Pin multiplexing is controlled via PINCNTL1-PINCNTL270 registers with MUXMODE settings. Internal pullup/pulldown resistors are provided on most pins; external resistors are recommended for boot configuration pins. Device interconnect uses L3 and L4 switch fabric architecture connecting initiators to targets. PRCM module manages power domains, reset types (POR, warm reset, software reset), and clock generation via PLLs with SYSCLK and Module Clock distributions. Voltage domains include four Core Logic and four Memory domains with SmartReflex DVFS support. Supply sequencing follows specific power-up/down sequences across four supply groups. Reset sources include POR, external warm reset, emulation warm reset, watchdog reset, and software resets with priority handling. Clock sources include DEVOSC (20-30 MHz), AUXOSC, SERDES_CLKN/P, AUD_CLKIN, and CLKIN32 inputs. Interrupt controllers handle ARM Cortex-A8 (128 events) and C674x DSP (12 prioritized interrupts) interrupts.

The study aimed to translate and cross‑culturally adapt the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire‑Revised (WFQ‑R) into Modern Standard Arabic and to evaluate its measurement properties for Arabic speakers in Saudi Arabia. Using Beaton et al.’s five‑stage guidelines (forward translation, synthesis, back‑translation, expert‑committee review, and pre‑testing), 320 adults (≥18 years) were recruited; 30 participated in a pilot test of the pre‑final Arabic version (WFQ‑Ar) and 290 completed the final testing. Only one item required wording clarification and abbreviations were replaced with full words to improve clarity.  

Validity was assessed through face validity (interviews with pilot participants), content validity (expert consensus and absence of floor/ceiling effects), and construct validity using exploratory factor analysis. The Kaiser‑Meyer‑Olkin measure was 0.93, Bartlett’s test was significant, and a single factor with eigenvalue 6.01 accounted for 55.79 % of variance; all ten items loaded between 0.56 and 0.82. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.93). Test‑retest reliability was ICC = 0.94 (95 % CI 0.93–0.95); the standard error of measurement was 4.5 points (10 % of the total score). Hypothesis testing showed a moderate positive correlation (r = 0.48, p < 0.001) between WFQ‑Ar scores and a single‑item foot‑dominancy question.  

Results support the hypotheses: the Arabic version demonstrates good internal consistency, excellent test‑retest reliability, and strong construct and concurrent validity. The WFQ‑Ar was reported as clear and easy to complete. The authors conclude that the adapted questionnaire is a valid and reliable tool for assessing footedness among Arabic‑speaking populations, offering clinicians and researchers a standardized instrument for clinical and research applications.

Peace must be founded on equality of rights among nations, not on power or territory; guarantees must not recognize differences between big and small or strong and weak. Governments derive all just powers from the consent of the governed, and no one may hand peoples about as property. A united, independent, autonomous Poland should be assured inviolable security for life, worship, and development. Every great people should have a direct outlet to the sea, either through cession or neutralization of rights of way, to ensure free access to world commerce. The freedom of the seas is a sine qua non for peace, equality, and cooperation, and may require revision of established international practices. The limitation of naval armaments and, more broadly, armies, must be faced candidly and accommodated, as peace requires concession, sacrifice, and planning for peace rather than war.

Seasonal trading involves regular price patterns at specific times of the year. Silver exhibits strong seasonality, with January and July being the best months for long positions (69.5% and 63.6% positive respectively), while June and September are the worst months (31.8% and 54.4% positive). Silver prices typically rise rapidly at the beginning of the year and remain relatively flat for the remainder. The seasonality is attributed to industrial silver users placing orders at the beginning of the financial year. The backtested strategy since 2001 involves holding silver only during the two best-performing periods: December through February and July through August. This strategy holds silver 5 out of 12 months and outperforms buy-and-hold by 3.9% annually. The strategy achieves a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% compared to 7.33% for buy-and-hold, while reducing maximum drawdown from -71.65% to -23.34%. Commodities are highly seasonal due to weather and business cycles, and trading silver based on this seasonal pattern has demonstrated solid results.

The ADS868xW ADC supports internal or external voltage reference selection via the INTREF_DIS bit in RANGE_SEL_REG, defaulting to the internal 4.096V reference. The internal reference requires a 4.7µF minimum decoupling capacitor on the REFIO pin, is factory-trimmed for accuracy, and can shift during soldering reflow processes due to thermal/mechanical stress. Temperature drift specification is 0.5ppm/°C typical and 2ppm/°C maximum over -40°C to +125°C. For external reference mode, program INTREF_DIS=1, apply 4.096V at REFIO, and place 10µF minimum and 1µF capacitors on REFCAP.

The device supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges using straight-binary output format. LSB size equals FSR/2^16.

Alarm features include input alarms with user-programmable high/low thresholds and hysteresis, and AVDD alarms with fixed thresholds (low: 4.7V, high: 5.3V). Both alarm types have active and tripped flags.

The device operates in three functional states: RESET (controlled by RST pin, supporting application or power-on reset), ACQ (signal acquisition), and CONV (conversion using internal clock). Transitions are controlled by RST and CONVST/CS signals.

Communication uses multiSPI interface supporting SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S protocols, single or dual SDO modes, and source-synchronous protocols. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge and end at rising edge. Optimal frames contain 32 SCLK cycles. Configuration uses register writes via HWORD commands. Daisy-chain topology connects multiple devices with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK, sequential SDO-0 to SDI connections.

Nine configuration registers exist at addresses 00h-28h, including DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (with write key protection), SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG.

The device includes NAP and power-down modes for power saving, with specific wakeup and power-up timing requirements.

A method and system for encoding a single bitstream from an HDR video source that can be decoded by both HDR and SDR systems. The encoder receives an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and target SDR display properties to find a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values matching the reference SDR master. Two embodiments are described: encoding SDR values with metadata for inverse transform, or encoding HDR values with metadata for SDR conversion. The color volume transform can be a tone mapping function, scaling factor, 3D-LUT, or 1D-LUTs. The encoder tests candidate transforms by emulating SDR display operations and selects the one minimizing difference from reference SDR values. Metadata items communicate the transform to decoders. HDR systems use inverse transforms to reconstruct HDR values, while SDR systems present SDR values directly or after converting decoded HDR values to SDR using provided metadata. This eliminates the need for separate SDR and HDR bitstreams.

A 20-year-old model who used sunbeds up to twice weekly for two years had to have moles removed after they changed shape and color. Hexane is an unbranched hydrocarbon solvent found in the volatile fraction of plants such as guava and orange. It is derived from crude oil and exists as pure hexane (used mainly in laboratories) and solvent‑based hexane (widely used in industry). Solvent‑based hexane extracts vegetable oils from soybeans, cottonseed, rape seed, mustard seed and safflower seed, and is also employed as a cleaning agent in textile, printing, furniture and leather industries, as well as in consumer products like glues, gasoline, rubber and cement. An alternative extraction method using sodium hydroxide and methanol has been successfully applied to soybeans, though high moisture content increases methanol consumption. Hexane’s health hazards include weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache and fatigue; OSHA has set a permissible exposure limit of 500 ppm. Its ability to remove unwanted taste and odor drives demand in the edible‑oil sector, and rising population and refined‑oil demand are expected to boost hexane consumption. Asia Pacific, especially China, dominates global production and consumption, prompting manufacturers in Europe and North America to shift facilities to the region. North America and Europe are projected to grow rapidly due to high demand for rubber in automotive applications.

CSF‑tDNA analysis using CAPP‑Seq was applied to 81 CSF, blood and tissue samples from 24 patients with advanced lung cancer undergoing lumbar puncture for suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD). CSF‑tDNA variant allele fractions (VAFs) were significantly higher than plasma ctDNA VAFs (median 32.7% vs 1.8%, P < 0.0001) and the two were positively correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.45, P = 0.03). For definitive LMD diagnosis, cytology was 81.8% sensitive, MRI 80.0% sensitive, and CSF‑tDNA 91.7% sensitive. Detection of CSF‑tDNA was strongly associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 7.1, P = 0.02). In EGFR‑mutant patients receiving EGFR‑TKI therapy, resistance mutations (e.g., EGFR T790M and MET amplification) were frequently detected in peripheral blood but rarely in time‑matched CSF, indicating spatial heterogeneity of resistance mechanisms. In a prospective cohort of 12 patients treated with osimertinib for refractory LMD, patients with CNS progression showed increased CSF‑tDNA VAFs after three weeks of treatment; post‑osimertinib CSF‑tDNA VAF was strongly prognostic for CNS progression (HR = 6.2, P = 0.009). The findings indicate that CSF‑tDNA detection is feasible, may improve LMD diagnostic sensitivity, provides prognostic information, and reveals compartment‑specific resistance patterns.

In 2016‑17, 719 people were admitted to hospitals in Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly for eating disorders; among them were a boy and a girl under 10, 13 children aged 10‑12, 91 youths aged 13‑15 and 117 aged 16‑18. LLC to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured notes: $1.25 billion 0.309% notes due 2023, $1.25 billion 0.584% notes due 2024, $1.25 billion 1.550% notes due 2028, and $1.25 billion 2.000% notes due 2031. Poor medication adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, with non‑adherence rates >50% (up to 98.6%). Non‑adherence worsens chronic kidney disease management and increases mortality. Proposed strategies include simplifying regimens, improving health literacy, and applying person‑centered care (PCC) to enhance physician‑patient communication, though evidence remains limited. This study of patients undergoing hemodialysis (with or without peritoneal dialysis) at six facilities examined relationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, testing trust as a mediator. Adults capable of completing a questionnaire were included; those with dementia or blindness were excluded. The study received ethical approval from Fukushima Medical University. Adherence was measured with the Japanese ASK‑12. Data were collected between April 2022 and February 2023. No patient or public involvement occurred.

Tesla's Entry into the U.S. Auto Industry (May 1, 2019) by Donald Sull and Cate Reavis examines Tesla's position in the automotive market. In March 2016, Elon Musk unveiled the Model 3 ($35,000, 220-mile range), targeting mass production with deliveries planned for end of 2017. By 2018, pre-orders exceeded 500,000. However, production faced severe challenges: Musk described being in "production hell," working 120-hour weeks, and pausing production twice in early 2018. Financial losses were significant: Q2 2018 net loss of $743 million on $4 billion revenue, with analysts stating the need to produce 5,000 units weekly for profitability. Musk admitted excessive automation was a mistake. Investor opinions were divided; some believed Tesla would disrupt the industry, while skeptics claimed it was "on the verge of bankruptcy."

The case provides an overview of the U.S. auto industry: worth $270 billion in 2016, with sales expected to remain flat until 2021. The "Big Three" (GM, Ford, Chrysler) held 46% market share, but brand loyalty was low (80% switched brands). Barriers to entry were high ($6 billion, six years). Suppliers (tiers 1-3) were fragmented, with top five accounting for 8.1% of revenue. Customers, particularly Millennials, preferred online research and 75% considered buying online. Changing mobility trends included electrification (EVs, battery cost declines), autonomous driving (levels 0-5), connectivity, and alternative ownership like car-sharing.

Tesla, founded in 2003 by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, with Musk as chairman (2004) and CEO (2008), pursued a "Master Plan" (2006) to enter at the high end and move to mass market. Its models included the Roadster ($100,000, 2,500 sold), Model S (launched 2013, 225,000 sold by 2018), Model X (2015, 81,000 sold), and Model 3 (mass production, 500,000+ reservations but 25% deposit refunds by mid-2018). Tesla vertically integrated up to 80% of Model 3 components, manufacturing batteries at the Gigafactory (Nevada, $5 billion, Panasonic partnership) and assembling at Fremont plant. Production issues included skipping beta production, automated line problems, and 40% parts requiring rework. Tesla sold directly via company-owned stores (111 in 26 states), facing legal restrictions from dealer lobbies. It operated over 1,300 charging stations and 11,000 Superchargers. Master Plan Part Deux (2016) aimed for Level 5 autonomous vehicles and a ride-sharing platform (expected 2019). While Tesla spurred industry innovation, its long-term viability remained uncertain.

Lewis Williamson appealed a trial court's judgment favoring Town of Surf City, which closed a 20‑foot portion of North Shore Drive adjacent to both parties' properties. The closure allowed the town to use its share of the right‑of‑way for public bathroom and storage facilities needed for beach‑access improvements. Plaintiff conceded the town complied with all procedural requirements of N.C.G.S. § 160A‑299 but argued the closure was improper because the town's intent was to construct public facilities on its vested portion, relying on Wooten v. The passage describes a rotating shaft mechanism for a foldable mobile terminal comprising a main shaft assembly, a swing arm assembly, and a support assembly. Each connecting‑rod group has two connecting rods rotatably connected to the main shaft assembly, and each swing‑arm group has swing arms fixedly connected to the two housings of the terminal. The swing arms and connecting rods rotate around parallel axes and slide relative to each other, allowing support plates to rotate and enclose folding space for the flexible display, so that the folded thickness is approximately equal to the thickness of the two stacked housings. Gears on the ends of the connecting rods engage for synchronized movement. A limiting mechanism with first and second cams and an elastic part restricts rotation positions. The main shaft assembly may consist of a main inner shaft and a main outer shaft, with arc‑shaped sliding slots for the swing arms. A flexible blocking layer may be attached to the opposite surface of the main shaft assembly and inserted into the housings to improve appearance. The mobile terminal includes the rotating shaft mechanism, two housings, and a flexible display fixed to the housings.

The Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway opened a line in 1848 linking Lincoln to Grimsby via Barnetby and Market Rasen. The line was built to transport goods and fish from Grimsby docks and initially included a bridge over the River Witham at Stamp End. Designed by chief engineer John Fowler – later consulting engineer for the Forth Bridge and co‑builder of the London Underground – the bridge used box‑shaped wrought‑iron girders, making it possibly the oldest surviving wrought‑iron box‑girder railway bridge in Britain. The structure carried a double‑track railway with three spans: a 74‑ft central tubular girder span and timber side spans on the north and south banks. After the 1847 collapse of the Dee Bridge, Fowler adopted William Fairbairn’s tubular girder design for the River Witham bridge. The bridge required reinforcement in 1903 and 1948 to accommodate heavier trains, replacing the timber side spans with steel plate girders and adding a central plate girder. A steel deck was added in 1968, giving the bridge its current layout. Network Rail has recently completed a £7 m project replacing the bridge using one of the world’s biggest cranes. The line later became part of the Great Central Railway.

High S-IgG seroprevalence (95.6%) was found in 1,411 emergency department patients in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany (August-September 2022), but only 67.7% met vaccination recommendations; 45.7% reported prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. S-IgG levels correlated with neutralization against Wu01 and BA.4/5 but showed decreased accuracy for BQ.1.1. Neutralizing activity against BQ.1.1 was reduced 23.6-fold and 4.2-fold compared to Wu01 and BA.4/5, respectively; only 73.8% of participants showed detectable BQ.1.1 neutralization. Drug immunosuppression was associated with lower S-IgG levels and neutralization. Multivariable analysis identified NC-IgG status, number of vaccinations and infections, time since infection/vaccination, and S-IgG levels as most predictive for neutralizing activity. S-antigen contacts (vaccination/infection) substantially contribute to humoral immunity, but the substantial immune escape of BQ.1.1 and moderate vaccination compliance highlight the need for improved vaccine uptake.

Scientists have created parachutes inspired by the Japanese paper‑cutting art of kirigami. A thin Mylar disk perforated with concentric slits unfurls automatically when dropped, forming a lattice that creates drag and forces the payload to fall straight down regardless of its initial orientation. In laboratory tests the kirigami parachutes landed closer to a target than traditional or uncut disks and are simpler to make because they require no sewing or folding. A 60‑m drone test with a 0.5‑m parachute slowed a 1‑kg bottle from about 34 m/s to 14 m/s, demonstrating reduced fall speed. Because the devices are full of holes they produce less drag than solid parachutes; a human would need a parachute with a radius of roughly 100 m to avoid crash‑landing. The researchers suggest the design could be used for humanitarian aid drops, drone deliveries and even planetary missions, and they are exploring biodegradable materials and other modifications.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling a financial instrument within the same day, can involve stocks, futures, or forex, and includes scalping or day‑trading techniques. The aim is to profit from short‑term price movements while avoiding overnight gaps. Intraday trading is common in forex and futures due to high leverage, and also occurs in stock markets. In the US, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) designates pattern day traders as those who execute four or more day trades within five business days when those trades exceed six percent of total margin‑account trades; such traders must maintain a minimum equity of $25,000 and are limited to four times the maintenance‑margin excess as buying power. CFD trading is prohibited for US residents. Successful intraday trading requires a backtested, statistically proven trading plan and adherence to several rules: learn market mechanics, set realistic goals, avoid herd mentality, choose a regulated broker, trade only liquid stocks, stay aware of fundamentals, use a quantified/automated system, and review performance periodically. Technical indicators such as moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands and RSI are commonly employed, though their effectiveness on intraday data is limited due to market noise. Intraday trading can be profitable, but most traders lose money because the activity is a zero‑sum game and strategies are difficult to backtest reliably. An example strategy based on a series of lower lows and lower highs was backtested on WTI crude oil futures (2000‑2021) and performed poorly; reversing the logic to short positions improved results. Out‑of‑sample testing after July 2021 showed a positive average gain of 0.57% per trade, but only 21 trades were recorded. The optimal trading window is the first two hours after market open when liquidity and volatility are highest. Capital requirements depend on the instruments traded, but traders are advised to have sufficient funds to cover losses and avoid under‑capitalization. Popular intraday strategies include scalping, momentum, news‑based, and trend‑following approaches, all of which should be backtested before use. Markets with high liquidity and volatility—primarily stocks, futures, and forex—are preferred, with stocks offering the best opportunities and forex the least. Ultimately, most intraday traders lose, and those who succeed typically rely on disciplined, backtested plans.

Buck Sweep is a misdirection off‑tackle run with two pulling linemen, created by Tubby Raymond at the University of Delaware and now the signature play of the Wing‑T. The passage details blocking assignments for the 3‑4 odd front and the 4‑3 even front, and notes two variations: a Shotgun version where the quarterback shuffles and can keep the ball (popularized by Gus Malzahn at Auburn) and an I‑Wing version that uses a counter step by the tailback but retains the same blocking scheme.

Following stroke, motor deficits are heterogeneous, complicating assessment and treatment. Surface electromyography (EMG) can quantify altered muscle activation such as excessive co‑contraction and modified muscle synergies, but low‑density bipolar electrodes cannot reliably record small hand muscles. High‑density EMG (HD‑EMG) provides high‑resolution data on motor control, yet existing systems are bulky and require expertise. This work used a wearable HD‑EMG sleeve (NeuroLife) to characterize movement coordination across a range of functional tasks in seven chronic stroke survivors (60 ± 5 yr) and seven age‑matched able‑bodied adults (27 ± 1 yr). Participants performed twelve hand, wrist and forearm movements (and an additional 25 grasps only in able‑bodied participants) at 25–50 % maximal effort while EMG was recorded at 3000 Hz, pre‑processed with 60 Hz notch and 20–400 Hz band‑pass filters, and corrected for sleeve‑shift artifacts using blind‑source separation. Data were segmented into 150 ms RMS bins, mapped to a standardized medium‑size sleeve and to six forearm muscle groups, and analyzed for co‑contraction index (CCI), inter‑muscle correlation, and time‑invariant muscle synergies via non‑negative matrix factorization. Clinical assessments (Fugl‑Meyer upper‑extremity, Box‑Blocks, Modified Ashworth) were used to stratify stroke participants and to evaluate correlations with HD‑EMG features, demonstrating feasibility of these metrics as motor‑related biomarkers after stroke.

SrTiO3 exhibits distinct structural phases, including a quantum paraelectric regime at low temperatures. Using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) with a pixelated detector, polarization was mapped via asymmetry in Kikuchi band intensity. Below the antiferrodistortive transition (~105 K), local polar nanodomains emerge with a characteristic size of ~20 nm. At ~69 K, these domains show periodic spatial ordering with a length scale of ~25 nm. Upon cooling below ~40 K (quantum paraelectric regime), the polar domains fragment into smaller, disordered clusters, losing periodic order. This behavior indicates a re-entrant disordering driven by quantum fluctuations, contrasting typical domain growth with decreasing temperature. The findings reveal a complex nanoscale polar landscape in SrTiO3, linking local polarity to macroscopic anomalies and tunable ferroelectric states.
