This lecture discusses Thomson scattering theory and its applications to plasma diagnostics. The spectral density function for scattering depends on electron density fluctuations and contains both electron and ion components, with scattering occurring only from electrons while some electrons respond to ion behavior. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibilities scale with alpha squared, where alpha is the collective scattering parameter (1/(k lambda_Debye)). The plasma dispersion function w(squiggle) describes the interaction between wave phase velocity and thermal velocity, with squiggle representing the ratio of these velocities. When alpha squared approaches zero (incoherent regime), scattering reveals only individual electron distribution functions without plasma response effects. For high frequency waves where squiggle_I >> 1, ion contributions vanish and electron plasma wave resonances appear at frequencies satisfying the dispersion relation omega^2 = omega_pe^2 + 3(Te/me)k^2, with peak positions depending on density and temperature. For low frequency waves where squiggle_e << 1, ion acoustic waves emerge when zTe/TI > 3, with frequencies proportional to k*sqrt(zTe/mI), and their damping depends on electron distribution gradients. The anacoustic spectrum provides information about electron temperature, ion temperature, ion flow velocity, and electron-ion drift (allowing current measurement), while electron plasma waves provide density information. Practical considerations include avoiding velocity gradients within collection volumes, managing finite collection angles that average over multiple k vectors, and handling collision effects that damp coherent features. Current research focuses on non-Maxwellian distribution functions and multi-angle Thomson scattering measurements using advanced optical setups.

Turkey’s education administration is centralized and top‑down, based on directorates whose directors are appointed by the Ministry of National Education. This structure lacks participation, transparency, accountability and other good‑governance principles. In contrast, 16 OECD countries with higher PISA scores and GDP per capita manage education through local boards and commissions at central, provincial, district, vocational and school levels. Turkey’s 2018 PISA averages (math 454, reading 466, science 468) and GDP per capita (28 454 $) are below the OECD means (488, 487, 489; 46 173 $). This gap motivated the study, which aimed to develop a local education board model for Turkey.

The research used a mixed‑method exploratory sequential design. Qualitative data were obtained from literature and reports on education administration in 16 OECD countries selected because their PISA and GDP figures exceeded OECD averages. Quantitative data were collected through a questionnaire titled “How to Manage Education” administered to 8 118 teachers and 696 administrators in the Seyhan district of Adana (421 respondents). Test–retest reliability was r = 0.961, Cronbach’s α = 0.978.

Qualitative findings showed that all 16 countries use boards/commissions (Central Education Board, State Board, Local/Regional Boards, Higher Education Boards, Vocational Education Boards, Education Supervisory Boards, School Boards) composed of diverse stakeholders. Survey results indicated that 61.5 % of participants prefer local administration over central; 41 % think provincial education boards/commissions should drive decentralization; 61 % want elected boards/commissions; large majorities favor boards that include teachers, principals, parents, union representatives, university and NGO members, mayors, governors and other stakeholders at provincial, district, vocational, school and inspection/evaluation levels. Respondents also indicated that 22 of 27 listed duties (e.g., building maintenance, curriculum content, budgeting, personnel recruitment) should be transferred to local units, while the Ministry should retain policy‑making, law‑application procedures and regulation issuance.

Discussion highlighted that board‑based, participatory governance improves accountability, transparency, efficiency and student outcomes. Countries with such structures score above OECD averages in PISA and have higher GDP per capita. The study argues that Turkey’s centralized system should be restructured to a local‑board model.

The proposed model consists of a National Education Supreme Council (policy‑setting), a central Ministry organization (monitoring, evaluation, supervision), a Higher Education Council, Provincial/District National Education Boards/Commissions, Vocational Education Boards and School Boards. The central government would set overall policy, monitor and audit; local boards would handle implementation, budgeting, curriculum and personnel matters.

Recommendations include adopting the Local Education Boards model, conducting pilot studies in one or more provinces, and performing further qualitative, quantitative or mixed‑method research on board structure and functioning.

Limitations: the quantitative sample is limited to teachers and administrators in Seyhan district; the qualitative analysis covers only 16 of 36 OECD members; the proposed model is a general framework.
A federal judge rejected government request to delay order letting transgender people enlist from Jan 1; Pentagon preparing to accept them; Justice Department reviewing legal options.

Texas has passed a law (HB 8) to replace the STAAR standardized test with three shorter exams throughout the school year. Supporters claim this will reduce overall testing time and student stress, but critics—including teachers, parents, and education experts—fear it may increase stress and testing time, as the end-of-year test will still heavily influence school accountability ratings. The law bans practice tests and requires TEA to study reducing testing weight on ratings, but that report isn't due until 2029-30 and implementation isn't mandatory. Many schools already conduct similar assessments, so the law may codify existing practices. Educators want more relaxed testing protocols and input in exam creation.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU‑based lossless decompression, reducing CPU load and delivering up to 100× throughput and 20× lower CPU utilization. The GA10x Ampere architecture powers the GeForce RTX 30‑series, data‑center A40 and workstation RTX A6000 GPUs. It provides second‑generation RT Cores, third‑generation Tensor Cores with sparsity support, up to 2× FP32 performance and up to 5× (10× with sparsity) AI throughput. The architecture supports GDDR6X memory (first to do so) via PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 936 GB/s bandwidth on the RTX 3090. Display capabilities include 4K 120Hz and 8K 60Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC and HDMI 2.1. Fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decodes MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1, with GA10x GPUs the first to include AV1 decode, enabling 8K 60 HDR playback at about 4% CPU usage. Seventh‑generation NVENC provides hardware encoding that matches or exceeds x264 Medium preset while offloading the CPU. The A40 GPU offers 48 GB GDDR6, scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtualization (vGPU) and EGX platform compatibility. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and retries, helping users gauge memory overclock limits. The RTX A6000, based on GA102, provides 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑gen RT Cores and 336 third‑gen Tensor Cores, supports hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and can combine two cards for 96 GB of memory.

A flaw in Atlassian Jira and Confluence contains a vulnerable proxy that can be abused via SSRF to extract AWS secret keys, allowing takeover of hosted instances. NIST rated the flaw 6.1/10; Atlassian has patched it, yet many legacy deployments remain exposed. Researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen major firms with outdated, publicly accessible instances. After notification, EE, Insider, Easy Metrics, a HHS division, IEEE, Ronin and A&E Networks patched or shut down servers. Three unnamed firms remain vulnerable. The US Department of Defense also fixed two Jira instances this year. Updating Atlassian software is the recommended mitigation.

Gareth Southgate should abandon his cautious 4‑2‑3‑1 formation to avoid another early World Cup exit; England’s attack featuring Harry Kane, Marcus Rashford and Raheem Sterling lacks pace and invention, and only Dele Alli can provide the creativity needed in the No.10 role. Southgate should test a three‑centre‑back system with more aggressive wing‑backs in the friendlies against Brazil and Germany.

In the past week Spotify, Comcast and Oracle announced co‑CEO structures, continuing a trend that remains rare—about 1.2 % of the Russell 3000 index. Historical data show companies with two chief executives posted an average annual shareholder return of 9.5 % from 1996‑2020 versus 6.9 % for single‑leader firms. While the model can aid succession and broaden leadership talent, it also creates risks such as unclear accountability, potential power struggles and higher executive compensation. Examples include Chipotle’s brief co‑CEO period before reverting to a single leader, Netflix’s long‑term dual‑CEO arrangement, and Oracle’s new dual leadership under a founder‑heavy board. Experts advise that success hinges on clearly defined responsibilities, aligned strategic goals, complementary skills and strong communication. When those elements are absent, co‑CEO arrangements can become “the kiss of death,” according to leadership consultants.

NVIDIA's Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended October 25 2015 reports Q3 FY2016 revenue of $1,305 million, a 7% increase year‑over‑year, and nine‑month revenue of $3,609 million, up 5%. Gross profit for the quarter was $734 million (56.2% gross margin) and operating income $245 million (18.9% of revenue). Net income was $246 million (diluted EPS $0.44) for the quarter and $406 million (diluted EPS $0.72) for the nine‑month period.  

By segment, GPU revenue grew 12% to $1,110 million, driven by higher gaming GPU sales; Tegra revenue fell 23% to $129 million due to reduced OEM smartphone/tablet sales, partially offset by automotive growth. The “All Other” segment contributed $66 million from a patent cross‑licensing arrangement.  

Cash and cash equivalents were $471 million; marketable securities totaled $4.3 billion. The company repurchased 18 million shares under a $400 million accelerated share‑repurchase agreement (average price $21.63) and paid cash dividends of $0.0975 per share, totaling $152 million for the nine months. Remaining share‑repurchase authorization was $1.6 billion.  

Restructuring charges of $8 million were recorded in the quarter and $97 million for the nine months, related to the wind‑down of Icera modem operations; an additional $25 million to $35 million charge is expected in Q4 FY2016.  

Litigation highlights include NVIDIA’s patent‑infringement suits against Qualcomm and Samsung (ITC and Delaware) and Samsung’s counter‑claims (Virginia). A $21 million warranty charge was recorded for a voluntary recall of SHIELD 8‑inch tablets.  

New accounting standards for inventory measurement, debt issuance costs, cloud‑computing arrangements and revenue recognition are being evaluated; the revenue‑recognition standard is effective FY2019. An interest‑rate swap on the new headquarters operating lease is designated as a cash‑flow hedge.

The passage is the front‑matter of a 1902 U.S. Department of State ebook covering “Whaling and Sealing Claims Against Russia.” It describes the arrest and seizure of the American vessels “Cape Horn Pigeon,” “James Hamilton Lewis,” “C. H. White,” and “Kate and Anna” and notes that the United States presented a memorandum for indemnity to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser following an arbitration agreed upon by an exchange of notes dated September 3, 1900. Correspondence from counsel and agent Herbert H. D. Peirce to Secretary of State John Hay was transmitted to the Senate (H. C. Lodge) and printed as a public document on December 12, 1901. The ebook, released by the Office of the Historian, provides the full text of the Foreign Relations of the United States series in a portable, searchable format.

Berenice M. Brubaker filed a claim in the New York Court of Claims for damages from the State’s appropriation of her 365‑acre property near Massena for the St. Lawrence River project. The State took four parcels: (1) about 183 acres north of Middle Road on May 19 1955; (2) a 0.15‑acre permanent flooding easement on June 12 1956; (3) a 25.34‑acre fee taking on April 1 1957; and (4) a permanent easement for an electrical transmission line over 55.38 acres on May 1 1957. Claimant’s experts valued the land at $331,200–$368,275; the State’s experts placed the value at $28,000–$40,000. The court applied the United States v. Miller rule, excluding any enhancement in value attributable to the project for the first taking because no open and notorious designation of the probable taking area existed before May 13 1954. The court awarded: $32,000 for the 183‑acre tract, $100 for the 0.15‑acre easement, $39,750 for the 25.34‑acre fee taking (including $12,675 direct and $27,075 consequential damages), and $27,700 for the 55.38‑acre transmission line easement, all with interest from the respective appropriation dates.

Display device includes a substrate, a pixel electrode and an opposing electrode on the substrate, an encapsulation portion on the opposing electrode with alternating organic and inorganic layers, and a planarization layer on the encapsulation portion. The planarization layer covers at least an edge portion of the encapsulation portion where the upper surface of the encapsulation portion gradually lowers toward the device edge. The edge side surface of the planarization layer forms a larger angle with the substrate surface (equal to or larger than about 70°) than the edge side surface of the encapsulation portion (less than 45°). The planarization layer comprises an organic material, may be formed over the entire encapsulation portion or only over a portion, and its upper surface is substantially flat. Touch sensor patterns, including touch electrodes and touch wiring, may be formed on the planarization layer. The planarization layer increases the flat area available for pattern formation, reduces dead space, and lowers parasitic capacitance between the opposing electrode and the touch sensor. The encapsulation portion prevents moisture and oxygen from reaching the emission layers. Alternative embodiments include a planarization layer that exposes a part of the encapsulation portion, an edge side surface that is substantially flat or curved, and a planarization layer formed by screen printing or photolithography using a photosensitive organic material. The display device may be a top‑emission OLED with a thin‑film transistor backplane and may incorporate a capacitive touch sensor of an on‑cell type.

Defending the UCLA offense focuses on disrupting high‑post rub cuts and down‑screen actions. The NBA show‑and‑recover method has three phases: (1) a defender “shows” the cutter wide while the original defender forces the cutter behind the pick; (2) the showing defender recovers and teammates “pack” the paint; (3) the defense matches up, applies ball pressure, and crowds the low post. The all‑out SOS disruption traps the wing on the first pass, exploiting the point guard’s low‑post cut, then rotates using the near‑player concept, and ends with a match‑up applying SOS principles. Both strategies require coordinated individual fundamentals and team concepts.

During oral argument a majority of Supreme Court justices appeared inclined to reverse courts and grant Rep. Michael Bost standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing mail‑in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to 14 days later. Paul Clement, arguing for Bost, proposed a rule granting candidate standing to challenge change in election procedures. Justice Kagan rejected that approach, suggesting a lower bar: a candidate must allege the new rule puts them at an electoral disadvantage relative to former rule, without needing to prove loss. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson said Bost could not meet that test because he admitted the rule would not cause him to lose his safe seat. Several justices indicated they could accept Kagan’s standard. Clement argued Bost satisfies it by pointing to a threatened margin loss. Illinois Solicitor General Notz said she would not oppose Kagan’s test but argued Bost’s facts do not show standing. Kavanaugh and Jackson warned Notz about her concession, and Notz clarified that standing could arise if the law would affect the election outcome or, if extreme, taint the candidate’s victory. Kavanaugh warned that denying pre‑election standing would force litigation post‑election and limit suits to major parties.

Microscale four-point probe measurements in SEM were used to analyze contributions of grain interior and Si and Mg2Si precipitates to electrical resistivity in Al-Mg-Si alloys. Grain interior resistivity depends on heat treatment rather than composition, while Si and Mg2Si precipitates contribute equally to resistivity. Bulk resistivity scales linearly with solute content (Si and Mg), with linear coefficients varying by heat treatment.

Y‑Cross is a drop‑back passing concept used in the Air Raid and other offenses. It employs a post route, a crosser, and an RB flat to the boundary, creating a weak‑side flood that can produce deep shots and intermediate completions. The concept can be run from many formations, can be dressed up with play‑action and adapted to personnel (TE or a fast slot receiver). It works well against man coverage and Cover 4 by giving two routes that attack away from defenders, but is less effective against Cover 3 because the post safety occupies the middle of the field. Coaching points detail releases, landmarks (18‑22 yd for the TE), and route depths for each position, with separate cues for man (stay on the move) and zone (sit). The QB progression is post → deep crosser → RB check‑down/dig, creating high‑low reads against 2‑high looks. Variations include a post‑wheel read first, a curl‑flat tag for 1‑high defenses, and personnel tweaks to keep the read intact while using a slot receiver. The concept is praised for its flexibility and ability to stress defenses horizontally.

Bitcoin rose to a six‑week high on Tuesday, up 4.4% to $9,340 on Bitstamp, after news that institutions are entering the crypto market. Gains lifted other tokens, pushing market cap to $427 billion. Goldman Sachs hired a head; Barclays gauging interest in a trading desk. A Thomson Reuters poll shows one in five plan to trade cryptos within a year, with 70% aiming to start in 6 months. Trading volume reached $28 billion, since Feb 10, though regulatory issues remain.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls fell to five over St. Patrick’s Day weekend, continuing a three‑year decline (39 in 2016, 38 in 2017, 25 in 2018). Sgt. Harold McClure credits increased awareness and the recent arrival of Uber and Lyft; a 2016 Uber study showed 90% of riders felt the service reduced drunk driving. Police presence at festivals also encourages sober driving.

The EUR/USD pair, representing the Euro against the US Dollar, is the most traded currency pair worldwide, offering high liquidity, tight spreads, and 24‑hour availability. Its exchange rate reflects the relative health of the Eurozone and US economies, and it serves as a barometer for global economic conditions.

Fundamental drivers include interest rate differentials set by the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Federal Reserve, inflation data, GDP growth, employment reports, and broader monetary policy divergence. Central‑bank announcements and economic releases can cause sharp volatility and influence long‑term trends.

Technical analysis tools commonly applied to EUR/USD include moving averages (e.g., 9‑, 18‑, 40‑, 100‑, and 200‑day periods), Fibonacci retracement levels, support/resistance zones, candlestick patterns, and indicators such as the Average Directional Index, Average True Range, and Balance of Power. Traders often backtest these tools to evaluate their effectiveness.

Market sentiment is used primarily for short‑term strategies, while long‑term movements are guided by fundamentals. Entry and exit decisions may be based on breakout or breakdown from consolidation patterns, narrow‑range bars, pullbacks to key support or resistance, and confirmation from multiple indicators.

Multiple trading styles are discussed:
- Scalping: rapid, high‑volume trades targeting small price changes (minutes), with most participants losing money.
- Day trading: capitalizing on intraday price action; strategies include Snap Back, Double Pump, and Session High Low.
- Swing trading: holding positions for days to weeks to capture short‑to‑medium term moves; patience and disciplined risk management are emphasized.
- Position trading: long‑term holds based on macroeconomic analysis, interest‑rate differentials, and risk‑adjusted position sizing (typically ≤ 1 % of capital per trade).

Risk management practices highlighted include setting stop‑loss and take‑profit levels, proper position sizing, limiting leverage, using uncorrelated currency pairs for diversification, and regularly reviewing performance. Leverage amplifies both profits and losses, and excessive use is cited as a common mistake.

The optimal trading window occurs when the European and US sessions overlap (12:00 pm–4:00 pm GMT in summer, 1:00 pm–5:00 pm GMT in winter), providing higher liquidity and volatility.

Brokers should be evaluated for regulation, security features, trading platforms (e.g., MetaTrader 4/5), transaction costs, and customer support. Demo accounts are recommended for practicing strategies, understanding platform features, and building confidence before moving to live markets.

Key pitfalls to avoid are over‑leveraging, lacking a clear and back‑tested trading plan, insufficient risk management, ignoring demo‑account practice, and chasing unrelated news or political events without a structured approach. Continuous learning, systematic backtesting, and adapting strategies to changing market conditions are presented as essential for sustained success in EUR/USD trading.

This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education from 2020 to 2024 using citation analysis. Data was collected from the Dimensions database using keywords "artificial intelligence" and "stem education," yielding 35 journal articles from 101 documents. Publication trends show a significant increase in 2024, with 15 articles receiving 234 citations (average 15.62 per article), while no citations were recorded in 2020–2023. The United States led in contributions with 9 documents and 103 citations, followed by China with 5 documents but no citations. The most cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson (55 citations each). The International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education was the most cited journal (55 citations), and the influential article was "Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education" (55 citations). Carnegie Mellon University had the highest citations (55), followed by Indiana University of Bloomington, University of Rochester, and Utah State University (43 each). The study highlights AI's benefits in personalized learning and instructional automation, while noting challenges such as ethical concerns and AI literacy. It provides insights for researchers and educators on AI integration in STEM education.

Trump officials argue that the H‑1B program is abused and have proposed a $100,000 fee for employers seeking H‑1B visas. The proposal could affect colleges, which employed more than 16,000 H‑1B workers as of June 30, about 5 percent of total H‑1Bs for fiscal year 2025. Data show 930 colleges had at least one approved H‑1B, with half of the 16,797 approved college H‑1Bs concentrated in 50 institutions; the top 100 universities held roughly 70 percent of all college H‑1Bs. The administration’s plan does not apply to current visa holders and universities are exempt from the 85,000‑visa cap. However, if fee and cap apply, experts say many institutions cannot afford the cost, potentially limiting hiring of lecturers, researchers and physicians. Agencies may grant exemptions for hires deemed in the national interest, and higher‑education groups argue academic and medical roles meet that standard. The National Postdoc Association says the fee would create a barrier for postdocs and other employers seeking top talent.

Natural disasters like hurricanes create significant health hazards that persist long after the storms pass. Hurricanes Maria, Harvey and Irma revealed numerous dangers including contaminated floodwaters with bacteria and toxins, toxic chemical releases from industrial sites, mold infestations, and mosquito breeding grounds raising disease risks. Structural instability, downed power lines and lack of air conditioning contributed to preventable deaths. Health and economic impacts could be dramatically reduced through better prevention measures and planning. Infrastructure should be hardened, hazardous sites better secured, and electrical grids made more storm-resistant. The author argues that approaching natural disasters like a preventable disease—applying medical prevention principles to emergency preparedness—could better protect human life and health before, during and after such events.

On Feb. 25, 2018, the California Democratic Party endorsed two Democrats in targeted Southern California Republican House races: Dave Min, who won the party’s nod over four rivals to challenge Rep. Mimi Walters after a floor fight and a subsequent voice‑vote ratification by more than 2,000 delegates, and stem‑cell researcher Hans Keirstead, who secured the endorsement to face Rep. Dana Rohrabacher despite united opposition from fellow Democrats and a contested floor vote. Both endorsements give the candidates a party stamp and placement on sample ballots. In three other targeted districts, none of the preferred Democrats reached the required 60 percent threshold: Mike Levin received 53 percent for the open Darrell Issa seat, Bryan Caforio got 53 percent for the Steve Knight seat, and Jay Chen led with 47 percent for the Ed Royce seat. For statewide contests, no gubernatorial or U.S. Senate candidate achieved the 60 percent endorsement consensus; in the Senate race Kevin de León led with 54 percent versus Dianne Feinstein’s 37 percent, and in the governor’s race Lt. Gov. Gavin Newsom topped delegates with 37 percent while Antonio Villaraigosa finished fourth with 9 percent. Party Chairman Eric Bauman upheld Min’s endorsement after a challenge, and Rohrabacher‑district challenger Harley Rouda attempted a floor vote but was barred from the room.

AMD shares rose after an AI chip agreement with OpenAI. Evercore’s Emanuel outlined a bubble scenario that could drive the S&P 500 to 9,000 by 2026. Gold crossed $3,900 per ounce amid yen weakness and expectations of U.S. rate cuts. Market commentary notes seasonal weakness, reduced liquidity, tax‑loss selling and institutional rebalancing, with yields and the dollar expected to fall further, supporting commodities. The divergence between growth and value sectors is widening. The passage also promotes AI‑driven investment strategies and includes standard risk disclosures.

Coccolithophores are microscopic oceanic algae smaller than dust that capture carbon dioxide, release oxygen, and produce calcium carbonate plates (coccoliths) which form chalk and limestone, recording Earth’s climate history. They are among the most effective natural carbon regulators, generating over 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate annually and supporting marine ecosystems. Five European research institutions have established International Coccolithophore Day on October 10 to raise awareness of their planetary impact. Ongoing research at the Ruđer Bošković Institute, Heriot‑Watt University’s Lyell Centre, NORCE, MARE (University of Lisbon) and the International Nannoplankton Association focuses on their carbon‑cycling role, climate‑archive properties and responses to ocean warming and acidification. Climate change threatens their survival and the stability of dependent ecosystems.

Kimberly Jones posted a video of her son Keaton describing middle‑school bullying, including name‑calling and having milk and ham thrown at him. The video reached over 18 million views and a crowdfunding page raised more than $29,000 for his education. Athletes Delanie Walker and Tyler Byrd, entertainer Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr. and Snoop Dogg publicly offered support.

Gunmen, identified by police as Taliban fighters, kidnapped 52 farmers, mostly Uzbek community members, from three villages in Jowzjan province on Wednesday. Police blame the Taliban and say elders are negotiating for their release while a rescue operation is possible. A Taliban spokesman acknowledged the report but could not confirm it. The incident follows an attack on ICRC workers in the same province.

On June 28 2021 NVIDIA completed a corporate simplification, repatriating certain foreign intellectual‑property rights to the United States via a foreign‑subsidiary domestication. As a result, the company raised its Q2 fiscal 2022 GAAP and non‑GAAP tax‑rate outlook to 13 % (±1 %) from the prior 10 % (±1 %), and expects a discrete tax benefit of roughly $250 million to $300 million from the domestication.

Using the THIN primary‑care database and the UK Biobank, the authors performed cross‑disorder analyses to identify health‑condition and medication associations in the years before a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). The THIN cohort comprised 20 214 AD patients, 28 222 PD patients, 4 682 DLB patients and 20 214 matched controls; the UK Biobank provided replication data for 1 005 AD, 2 268 PD and 2 732 dementia cases. Twelve prediagnostic health conditions (memory problems, tremor, confusion, hallucinations, sleep disorders, constipation, anxiety, depression, falls, hypotension, urinary‑tract disorders, abnormal weight loss) and several drug classes (antihypertensives, antidiabetics, statins, laxatives, antidepressants, benzodiazepines, antipsychotics, dopamine antagonists) were examined at 0–5, 5–10 and 10–15 years before the index date.

All examined conditions occurred more frequently than in controls in the 0–5 year window for all three diseases. Constipation, sleep disorders, anxiety, urinary‑tract disorders and tremor were already elevated up to 15 years before diagnosis, with constipation and tremor being more common in PD/DLB than in AD, while memory problems predominated in AD. DLB showed the strongest prediagnostic associations with hallucinations, confusion, falls, depression, anxiety, autonomic dysfunction and neuroleptic use.

Medication analyses revealed lower prescription rates of antihypertensives (including calcium‑channel blockers, diuretics and agents acting on the renin–angiotensin system) and antidiabetic drugs before all three diseases. Laxatives, antidepressants (including serotonin‑reuptake inhibitors), benzodiazepines, dopamine antagonists and antipsychotics were prescribed more often before each disease. Beta‑blocker use was higher before PD/DLB than before AD, whereas statin use was lower before PD than before AD/DLB; this statin pattern replicated in the UK Biobank.

Among PD patients, those who developed dementia within five years of diagnosis had higher prediagnostic use of statins, laxatives, antidepressants and antipsychotics than PD patients who remained dementia‑free, while antihypertensive use was not associated with later dementia.

The authors conclude that the prodromal phase of neurodegenerative diseases extends many years before clinical diagnosis and that distinct patterns of autonomic symptoms and medication use differentiate AD, PD and DLB, suggesting a differential role for lipid‑lowering therapies in their prediagnostic stages.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Q2 2015 10-Q report for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. The company reported total revenues of $955.0 million, up 24% from $769.3 million in Q2 2014, driven by increased Model S deliveries. Net loss was $184.2 million compared to $61.9 million in the prior year period. Gross margin decreased to 22.3% from 27.7% primarily due to product mix and manufacturing costs. As of June 30, 2015, cash and cash equivalents were $1.15 billion and total assets were $6.47 billion. The company continued expanding its retail, service, and Supercharger infrastructure globally, with over 480 Supercharger locations. Model X production remained on track for late Q3 2015 delivery. The Gigafactory construction continued in Nevada with $206.6 million in costs incurred to date. Financing activities included entering a $150 million Warehouse Facility and a $500 million Credit Agreement in 2015. Due to stock price conditions, the 2018 Notes became convertible in Q3 2015. Capital expenditures for 2015 are expected to be approximately $1.5 billion. As of July 30, 2015, there were 127,142,147 shares of common stock outstanding.

Gold is a precious metal used in jewelry, ornaments, exchange and as a store of value. Gold trading means speculating on its price through futures, options, spot markets, stocks, ETFs and CFDs; most trades are cash‑settled and do not involve physical delivery. Price movements are driven by supply‑demand and macro‑political factors, allowing traders to profit from volatility and to use gold as a hedge and safe‑haven. Historically, gold was used as early as 3400 BCE and became the first official medium of exchange in Egypt around 1500 BCE. Gold coins later served as currency across the Mediterranean and Middle East. In 1946 the Bretton Woods agreement pegged gold at $35 per ounce, backing the US dollar, but the gold standard was later abandoned, leading to floating exchange rates. Futures trading began in 1972 and the first gold futures contract traded on COMEX in 1974; over‑the‑counter and online trading expanded through the 1980s. Backtesting a weekend swing‑trading strategy on GLD (2004‑Sept 2021) showed that buying at Thursday’s close and selling at Friday’s close yielded an average 0.14 % gain per trade with a profit factor of 1.4. Extending the holding to Monday’s open produced 0.19 % per trade with a profit factor of 1.3. Adding a simple parameter improved results to acceptable levels for small positions. The weekend strategy is difficult but shows promise; optimizing entry and exit timing may enhance performance. Code for the strategy and additional trading systems is available for a fee.

VNRs from EMR countries demonstrate commitment to SDG monitoring but face challenges with weak health information systems, limited data availability, and analytical capacity. Reporting comprehensiveness varies by country income level, with higher-income countries reporting on more SDGs. Maternal, neonatal, and under-5 mortality rates are the most commonly reported indicators. Data availability for SDG3 ranges from 48% to 93% among reporting countries. Key recommendations include strengthening CRVS systems, increasing investment in health information systems, and developing national survey plans to improve data quality and accessibility.

Gold rallied on Friday while miners failed to follow, with the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closing below its April high for the third consecutive day. The USD Index returned to its July high and the neck level of an inverse head-and-shoulders formation. Stocks consolidated above 6,250 and then declined below their rising support line, combining two bearish signals. The author notes the current situation resembles 2008, with gold holding relatively well amid significant volatility, the USD Index starting to rally, stocks heading lower, and weak mining stock performance.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has been fined $250,000 by the NFL for making an obscene gesture toward fans during Sunday's 37-22 victory over the Jets at MetLife Stadium. Videos showed Jones quickly flashing his middle finger late in the game after the Cowboys' fourth touchdown increased their lead to 37-14. Jones claims the gesture was "inadvertent" and was meant to be a "thumbs up" to enthusiastic Cowboys fans. He stated there was "a swarm of Cowboys fans out in front" and the gesture was made in celebration. The Cowboys are likely to appeal but have until Friday to make a final decision. This is not the first instance in which the NFL has fined an owner for poor interaction with fans, with Panthers owner David Tepper previously fined $300,000 for throwing a drink at fans and former Oilers owner Bud Adams fined $250,000 for making an obscene gesture.

A rare white moose was filmed in Värmland, Sweden. According to the BBC, only about 100 exist in the country. The moose aren't albino—white fur results from a genetic mutation, whereas albino animals have pink or red eyes. People compared it to creatures from Game of Thrones and Lord of the Rings. The twin white calves' status as albino or piebald remains unknown.
Tomorrow’s game is crucial in a long series; the team regrouped after allowing a third‑period comeback, noting they need more power‑play goals, must maintain pressure and avoid any let‑ups.

The ADS868xW ADC uses an integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise input driver and supports internal (4.096V nominal) or external 4.096V reference selected via the INTREF_DIS bit. Internal reference requires a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor on REFIO, is factory-trimmed, and is affected by thermal stress and temperature drift (typical 0.5ppm/°C). External reference uses an internal buffer with 10µF and 1µF capacitors on REFCAP. The device features input and AVDD alarms with programmable thresholds and active/tripped flags readable via pin, register, or data output. It operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by CONVST/CS and RST pins, with multiSPI interface supporting single-device and daisy-chain topologies. Programming involves 32-bit data transfer frames and nine configuration registers (addresses 00h–28h) controlling device operation, including reset, power modes (NAP, power-down), and alarm settings. The device includes power-saving modes and requires specific decoupling and layout for industrial applications.

Researchers at Princeton University and collaborators have developed an AI system called Diag2Diag that generates synthetic diagnostic data for fusion plasma, filling gaps that current sensors cannot capture. The system uses input from existing diagnostics to predict measurements for other sensors, especially in the plasma edge region (the pedestal) where stability is critical. By providing high‑resolution data without additional hardware, Diag2Diag can enhance monitoring and control of plasma, reduce the number of required diagnostics, and enable more compact and affordable fusion reactors. Tests performed on data from the DIII‑D National Fusion Facility validated the approach and showed that the synthetic data aligns with real measurements and can be more detailed than direct sensor output. The AI also supports the magnetic‑island theory for suppressing edge‑localized modes (ELMs) by revealing flattening of temperature and density in the pedestal when resonant magnetic perturbations are applied. Diag2Diag was developed in an international collaboration involving Princeton, the U.S. Department of Energy’s Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, Chung‑Ang University, Columbia University and Seoul National University, and published in Nature Communications. Potential applications extend to spacecraft, robotic surgery and other fields where diagnostic data are missing or limited. The researchers report that the system can increase reliability and lower maintenance costs for future commercial fusion power plants.

The passage notes that these tools aim to reduce the time and cost of content creation, highlights Jasper as a recommended option, and mentions the presence of affiliate links.

Origin PC introduced an Eon15‑S gaming laptop starting at $999, featuring an Nvidia GeForce 1050Ti GPU, Intel Core i3 CPU, 120GB SSD, IPS display, and 24/7 US‑based lifetime support, with upgrade options for a Core i5 and larger storage for $100 extra.

Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal. Maxwell, serving a 20-year sentence for sex trafficking of a minor, challenged a 2007 non-prosecution agreement between Jeffrey Epstein and the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida. She argued the agreement's co-conspirators clause should bind all U.S. attorney's offices nationwide. The 2nd Circuit ruled the agreement applies only to the district that made the deal. The Supreme Court refused to review the decision.

The 5‑Day Low of the Range Strategy goes long when IBS < 0.25 and the close is below the lowest low of the previous five days. From Jan 1993 to present it generated 517 trades with 309 winners (60% win ratio) and an average return of 0.46% per trade, exceeding the 0.11% average for a five‑day period. Profitability peaks at 3–7 days; exiting after five days yields a 10.76% annualized return while the market is held only 510 days versus buy‑and‑hold. The method can be adapted for short selling using a 0.75–0.9 IBS threshold, producing roughly 10% returns, though short strategies are less profitable than longs. It is simple, requires no complex tools, and recent performance has declined.

The passage describes a study evaluating the MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test for point-of-care (POC) use. It notes that standard central laboratory RT-PCR tests for COVID-19 caused delays (up to five days), required uncomfortable nasopharyngeal swabs (NPS), and exposed healthcare workers. Early POC tests still involved manual sample handling and transfer, risking contamination.

The Sal6830™ system addresses these issues by using patient self-collected saliva deposited directly into an all-in-one sealed cartridge, minimizing operator exposure and sample mix-up. The study was conducted at two clinics (Care 4 U Community Health Center in Miami and St. Mary’s Health Wagon in Virginia) with six non-laboratory trained healthcare workers (medical assistants and nurses).

The evaluation included two phases: blinded testing of spiked positive and negative saliva samples, which showed 100% concordance, and a prospective clinical study comparing the Sal6830™ (using saliva) to a standard NPS-based platform (Cepheid Xpert Xpress) on patients suspected of having COVID-19. The clinical performance showed a Positive Percent Agreement (PPA) of 87.2%, Negative Percent Agreement (NPA) of 97.2%, and an Overall Agreement of 93.3%. A usability questionnaire completed by nine non-laboratory staff indicated high confidence and ease of use, with all participants finding the system intuitive and not requiring technical support.

The authors conclude that the Sal6830™ can be used accurately by untrained healthcare workers at the POC, combining the gold-standard RT-PCR technology with non-invasive sample collection.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) is a neural shader that caches radiance to achieve high‑quality global illumination and dynamic lighting in real time. It receives path‑traced rays after one bounce, trains tiny networks on live data, infers many‑bounce lighting, reduces GPU ray‑tracing cost, improves indirect lighting quality, and adapts to diverse game scenarios.
State v. Nelson, 31760-9-III: rev & rem; Korsmo J., Siddoway CJ, Fearing J.

A voice-directed inspection system supporting multiple inspectors for business assets includes two inspection assistance devices (each with portable computer and headset), a site computer, and a host computer. The system divides inspection plans into non-overlapping sections, allowing multiple inspectors to work simultaneously on the same asset without interference. Inspectors request assignments via voice, receive audible commands for their section, and submit completion updates voice. The site computer assigns sections based on availability, qualifications, or priority, and aggregates updates for the host computer. The system uses speech recognition and synthesis for hands-free operation, with inspection assistance devices capable of barcode scanning and voice template adaptation. Inspection plans can be divided by physical parts, component systems, or other criteria to enable parallel work. The system improves efficiency by allowing continuous workflow and flexible inspector allocation.

The passage explains that the Supreme Court’s decision in New York State Rifle & Pistol Association Inc. v. Bruen created a two‑step test for Second Amendment challenges. First, a court asks whether the amendment’s plain text covers the challenger’s conduct; if it does, the government must show that its regulation is consistent with the Nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation. Critics, including Justice Breyer and lower‑court judges, argue the test is impractical because judges lack the methodological and substantive knowledge of historians. The author contends that the proper question is not whether judges are good historians but how they handle history as lawyers. Originalist scholars respond that legal evidence is relatively durable, limiting the amount of historical work required, and that judges must decide cases even when historical certainty is lacking. The plain‑text step is generally straightforward; the historical‑tradition step may require research into early‑republic regulations, but many disputes will be clear‑cut, and courts have procedural tools such as burden‑shifting to manage uncertainty. Adding means‑ends scrutiny would make judges act like legislators, an approach the Court has rejected.

The speaker, thrilled that the series is over, says the team has won the Stanley Cup, praises Buffalo for a strong series and a promising young roster, and reflects on the difficulty of the playoff grind. He notes, recalling his ten‑year‑old Cup win, that many players, including Hull and Mike, played through injuries, that veteran experience and hard‑fought effort helped the team win, and that having a full lineup made opponents wary.

The lecture introduces the "decision mentality" in poker, using credit card roulette to illustrate expected value and the law of large numbers. It covers three levels of reasoning: hand vs. hand (soul reads), hand vs. range (exploitative play), and range vs. range (optimal play/Nash equilibrium). Key concepts include effective stack size relative to blinds, position at the table, equity calculation, and antes. The professor recommends specific opening hand ranges by position (tightest at under the gun, widest at the button), and advises raising to 2.25 big blinds or going all-in when effective stacks are 12 big blinds or less with antes. The lecture includes demonstrations of equity calculations using PokerStove and Nash equilibrium concepts.

Ovarian cancer in the UK is often diagnosed late, with only one in three cases identified at the earliest stages. Nearly half of women first present as emergency cases. Key symptoms include persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary changes, and persistent pelvic or abdominal pain. Other signs may include lower back pain, digestive discomfort, post-menopausal bleeding, and fatigue. There is no routine screening test; diagnosis relies on symptom awareness. A CA-125 blood test is not used for screening but to monitor treatment or recurrence. Early detection (stage 1 or 2) offers a 95% survival rate, compared to 16% for stage 4. Ovarian Cancer Action provides a free symptom checker and downloadable symptoms diary to aid early reporting. The term "silent killer" is considered misleading, as most women diagnosed at stage 1 experienced symptoms. Ovarian cancer is the sixth most common cancer in UK women.

DryShips (DRYS) raised $14.5 million through a continuous stock offering, far below its $30 million request, selling 7.9 million shares at $1.79 average. The offering caused 16.8% dilution and left $173.4 million of equity still to be issued as of April 17 (market cap $106 million). Kalani Investors fulfilled only 48% of the two fixed‑amount requests ($5 million and $25 million), missing the target for the third consecutive period. Equity issuance represented 8.86% of traded volume, the weakest performance to date. At the current pace, completing the remaining issuance at a 15% discount would need about 54 trading days and add roughly 105.7 million shares, causing further dilution. The article notes DRYS likely will pursue debt financing and later issue the remaining equity after a price bounce. The company would need to fall nearly 30% to breach the $75 million market‑cap threshold for F‑3 eligibility.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20 2017 with 155 mph sustained winds, gusts up to 190 mph, and up to 40 inches of rain, causing island‑wide flooding, destruction of the electrical grid (3.4 million people without power), damage to aqueducts, roads, bridges, ports, airports, cell towers and fuel stations, and an estimated $82 billion in monetary damage. The hurricane also destroyed about 80 % of the island’s crops, a loss of $780 million. Indirect mortality from such emergencies is difficult to measure because guidelines and personnel training vary. Prior studies estimated excess deaths after Maria, but they cover only short periods, a limited set of causes, and do not fully account for population displacement. This research develops a semi‑parametric Poisson regression model that controls for intra‑annual variation, population displacement, and cause‑specific effects of non‑communicable diseases and other indirect causes. The model is expressed as  

\[
\log(\mu_{i,j,t}) = \log(N_t) + \beta_0 + \text{yeart} + \mathbf{p}'_t\boldsymbol{\alpha} + \mathbf{c}'_t\boldsymbol{\gamma} + (\mathbf{p}_t\!\otimes\!\mathbf{c}_t)'\boldsymbol{\omega} + f(\text{day}_t) + \epsilon_{i,j,t},
\]  

where \(p_{i,t}\) indicates pre/post‑emergency periods, \(c_{j,t}\) indicates cause of death, \(f(\text{day}_t)\) captures within‑year seasonality, and the interaction term allows cause‑specific post‑emergency effects. Coefficients are estimated by penalized likelihood with REML, and excess deaths for cause \(j\) in period \(i\) are computed as the difference between the model prediction with the post‑emergency indicator (\(p_{i,t}=1\)) and the counterfactual with \(p_{i,t}=0\), using a displacement‑adjusted population size \(N_t^*\).

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran and Garry Cullum clinched class titles in the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at Agrisea Raceway. Drysdale won the Wifiplus KZ2 title by four points over Aaron Wilson; Wilson had taken the Final after Mat Kinsman crashed early. Tim Loughran secured the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters title after Enrico van der Griend crashed in the third heat, with Brett Hollander second and van der Griend third. Garry Cullum dominated the KZ2 Restricted class, winning all heats, the Pre‑Final and Final to claim the title by 20 points over Regan Hall, while Aaron Wooley finished second in the round and third overall. 27 karts competed; kerb‑hopping penalties affected several drivers including Madeline Stewart.

NASA plans to use a nuclear device to destroy asteroid Bennu, which has a 1 in 2,700 chance of hitting Earth on September 21, 2135. Bennu is taller than the Empire State Building and orbits 54 million miles from Earth. It is one of 10,000 near-Earth objects detected by NASA, with the HAMMER spacecraft designed to either deflect smaller rocks or deploy nuclear weapons against larger asteroids.

Between 1926 and 2015, Hendrik Bessembinder’s study of 26,000 U.S. stocks found that only 43% of equities outperformed one‑month Treasury Bills over their lifetime, and just 86 stocks generated half the total equity return. Returns were highly concentrated: the top 30 stocks accounted for roughly 30% of all gains, while the median stock returned about –4% and the average equal‑weighted portfolio outperformed only because a few stocks rose sharply. A similar analysis of the Oslo Stock Exchange (1985‑2017) showed that 18 large companies explained the entire value creation, with the majority of shares underperforming risk‑free rates. These findings illustrate that most individual stocks fail to beat Treasury Bills, and the overall market’s strong performance is driven by a small minority of stocks. The suggested remedies are buying a passive fund or, for those selecting individual stocks, maintaining broad diversification.

When an injured player is ignored by the referee, a player may stop play by kicking the ball out; the referee restarts with a throw‑in for the non‑kicking team, and the thrower returns the ball throwing to opponent’s back defender. Neither side may exploit this; the receiving team must let the thrower return and the defender secure the ball before attacking. A similar courtesy applies on a dropped‑ball restart after injury.

Intelligent maintenance systems, called e‑Maintenance, aim at near‑zero downtime by using real‑time monitoring, degradation prediction, and integration with e‑Manufacturing and e‑Business. They rely on sensors, reasoning agents, wireless communication, virtual platforms and web‑enabled technologies. Research gaps include predictive intelligence algorithms, linking product‑quality variation to machine degradation, data‑to‑knowledge conversion tools, scalable informatics platforms, data‑security solutions, distributed web‑based optimisation, and workforce training. The reconfigurable maintenance concept ties product design and production‑system configuration to quality, tolerance and maintenance policy, enabling inter‑company cooperation and early failure prediction. Modular reconfigurable maintenance uses distributed management, monitoring modules and a knowledge base to transmit sensor data, detect abnormal conditions, diagnose degradation and recommend corrective actions. In today’s mass‑customisation environment, integrating such reconfigurable maintenance systems is necessary to cut costs, improve quality and sustain production reliability.

The authors acknowledge prematurely abandoning a bullish stance on US equities and present 21 charts challenging bearish views. They note market breadth is showing underlying strength. Rigel Mercantile Limited, specializing in Macro/Value Research and Systematic Trading, discloses being long US equities and VIX. The information is not investment advice and applies only to their discretionary portfolios.

The Teachers’ Union of Ireland warned teachers that adding students as Facebook friends is “ill advised” because it can erode professional distance and jeopardize careers. The union advised members to be cautious with online comments, avoid hasty or angry posts, and stay out of online feuds. It also criticized some employers for demanding 24/7 electronic responses, calling such pressure “borderline harassment,” and recommended that members not feel obligated to respond unreasonably and consider turning off devices.

VentureWire newsletter from May 17, 2001 covers venture capital and startup news. Key stories include Tahoe Networks launching with $38M first round led by Redpoint Ventures and Accel Partners; Startups.com rebranding as Startups, Inc. and cutting 30% of staff; Hermes allocating $965 million for private company investments through Botts Capital Partners; and OffRoad Capital splitting into two divisions while cutting 50% of staff. DataSynapse expects to close $15 million Series B funding. iBase, a London-based digital asset management firm, is expanding to the US with GBP 4.2 million in Series B funding.
