Multiple funding rounds were reported for companies including Algorx Pharmaceuticals, Alphamosaic, Comlase, Xora, e.Intelligence, Foundstone, and Yube. The newsletter also covers M&A activity, new product launches, and executive appointments across the venture capital ecosystem.

Fellow-Citizens: The speaker thanks the people for the confidence that appointed him, acknowledges the accountability of his office, and pledges zealous service. He will execute the laws, manage foreign and confederate relations, control revenue, and command forces while respecting the constitutional limits of executive power. He intends to preserve peace with foreign nations on fair terms and to respect the sovereignty of the separate states. He will practice strict economy in managing the public revenue to eliminate the national debt and to prevent profligacy, and will favor agriculture, commerce, and manufactures equally in taxation, with special encouragement for products essential to independence. He supports constitutional internal improvements and the spread of knowledge, and will maintain a small standing army while gradually increasing the Navy and preserving forts and arsenals. He regards the national militia as the bulwark of our defense and will protect civil liberties. He promises a just policy toward Indian tribes, and cites recent public sentiment demanding reform of federal patronage and appointment practices. He will choose officials for integrity and diligence, rely on past examples and divine providence for guidance.

Education policies in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) have been shaped by presidential discourses, Education Council decisions, and the island’s historical developments. After the 1974 Peace Operation, the TRNC restructured its education system under close ties with Turkey, adopting a Turkish model that emphasized national‑identity construction. Earlier periods included Ottoman‑era religious schooling, British colonial segregation of Turkish and Greek education, and the 1960 Republic’s attempts at educational equality amid ethnic tensions. The Turkish Cypriot Education Council has driven reforms in teacher training, curriculum regulation, school infrastructure, language instruction, and history courses, using these tools to strengthen Turkish Cypriot identity and cultural heritage. History textbooks have traditionally presented a Turkish‑identity‑centered narrative, highlighting Turkish Cypriot victimhood and portraying Greek Cypriots as aggressors, thereby polarizing the communities. Since the early 2000s, EU‑driven harmonization and bicommunal projects prompted reconciliatory reforms, introducing more pluralist and peace‑oriented curricula, but political shifts have repeatedly stalled these initiatives. Comparative presidential statements reveal distinct priorities: Rauf Denktaş stressed national identity and Turkish integration; Mehmet Ali Talat focused on European‑style reforms and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu emphasized cooperation with Turkey and technical education investment; Mustafa Akıncı highlighted multiculturalism and intercommunal dialogue; Ersin Tatar reinforced national identity and Turkish alignment. The passage recommends that future education policy adopt a multi‑perspective, scientifically neutral curriculum, formulate long‑term strategies independent of ideological swings, and balance cooperation with Turkey against TRNC‑specific needs and autonomy.

Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said India's SCO accession raised the group's profile and capacity to stabilize Central and South Asia and address Afghanistan. He called for India‑Russia trade to reach $30 billion by 2025 and defence ties. Lavrov said the US strategy in Afghanistan is unlikely to succeed, noting NATO's failure to curb extremism and drug trade. He denied Russia supports the Taliban, saying contacts aimed to extract citizens and press the group to negotiate under UN criteria. The US rejected the Moscow Process for the Six‑Plus‑One format (India, Pakistan, Iran, Russia, US, China, Afghanistan). Lavrov said a solution requires all parties—Afghan government, Taliban, neighboring states—and a smaller group of Central Asian countries.

Michael Ben’Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney in the Eastern District of Virginia, was fired last week after a false social‑media post, a note says. The note says he was handling a terrorism case on Afghanistan bombing. It warns that DOJ leadership is endangering country, prioritizing punishment of enemies over security. The firing followed a claim that Ben’Ary was aligned with Deputy AG Lisa Monaco and opposed indicting Comey.

Speaker stresses a strong start is crucial to avoid a rough night, noting the opponent is playing for its life and has been successful at home; the team wants to end the series, while the opponent aims to extend it.

Malcolm Mitchell, a New England Patriots wide receiver, caught six passes for 70 yards in the team’s 34‑28 comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons in Super Bowl XVI. The 23‑year‑old, who entered the NFL as a fourth‑round pick, faced reading difficulties in college and taught himself to read by starting with children’s books such as The Giving Tree. He developed a passion for literacy and founded Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative that aims to provide books to children in underserved communities and improve grade‑level reading in low‑performing schools. Mitchell will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance at its 20th Anniversary Summit and Gala in New York. A report cited by the organization notes that children with the lowest reading scores account for 65 % of high‑school dropouts and that 61 % of low‑income families lack age‑appropriate books. Mitchell graduated in December 2015 with a communications degree, was drafted by the Patriots in May, and has written the children’s book The Magician’s Hat. He cites his mother Pratina Woods as his key inspiration and advises youth to never give up, treat each day as an opportunity to improve, and use reading to overcome adversity.

Yandex will release Q2 2018 financial results on July 26, 2018, with a conference call at 8:00 a.m. US Eastern (3:00 p.m. Moscow, 1:00 p.m. London). Dial‑in numbers and passcode provided; replay available until Aug 2. Yandex is a NASDAQ‑listed technology company founded in 1997, operating 20 offices worldwide and offering search, transportation and other services powered by machine learning. Investor contact: Katya Zhukova; Media contact: Ilya Grabovskiy.

The passage describes a digital accessibility workshop designed for software professionals and CS educators in India, addressing a significant skills gap in accessibility expertise. The workshop was attended by 73 participants representing software engineering, education, and UX design backgrounds, with diverse professional experience levels. The one-day workshop followed a structured three-phase model with five instructional modules covering accessibility basics, design, development, testing, and teaching. Post-workshop feedback indicated strong positive reception, with 100% of participants willing to recommend the workshop, 90% rating it as highly effective and engaging, and 52% reporting significant shifts in their accessibility perception. Recommendations for future initiatives include providing pre-workshop materials, customizing content by role, incorporating case studies, encouraging peer learning, and offering continued engagement opportunities.

The article analyzes whether the Supreme Court will overturn the 1935 precedent *Humphrey’s Executor* to uphold President Trump’s firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter. It argues the Court is likely to uphold the firing without fully overturning the precedent. The Court has recently shifted from broadly endorsing independent agencies to analyzing the specific powers of individual agencies, as demonstrated in the *Seila Law* case regarding the CFPB. That analysis found the modern CFPB acted as an executive enforcement agency rather than the quasi-legislative/quasi-judicial body the 1935 FTC was. The article contends the modern FTC has evolved similarly: its rulemaking and enforcement powers have expanded dramatically, its adjudicatory powers have receded, and it operates in a partisan, ideological manner distinct from the "non-partisan body of experts" described in *Humphrey’s Executor*. The Court’s recent stay orders regarding the NLRB and MSPB indicate it will judge these agencies based on the executive nature of their current functions. Therefore, the Court is expected to uphold the firing, narrow *Humphrey’s Executor* as applied to the FTC’s current structure, and preserve the precedent for agencies like the Federal Reserve that retain the original multi-member, quasi-judicial model. The Court is described as taking a "mend it, don’t end it" approach to the 1935 decision.

Maimane delivered the speech on day one of the SONA debate. He said President Zuma’s “Radical Economic Transformation” rhetoric hides elite self‑enrichment, and accused the ANC of prioritising power, personal wealth and projects such as the Arms Deal and the Nuclear Deal for cronies. He labelled the ANC the “enemy of the people”, citing the deaths of 94 mental‑health patients at Esidimeni, the Marikana 34, and the rejection of a minute’s silence for the victims. He argued that policies on land reform and Black Economic Empowerment have been corrupted to benefit ANC cronies, pointing to a R130 million land deal that enriched two allies while 31 farm workers went unpaid. He described a “lost generation” of nearly six million unemployed black youth, 500 000 children leaving the education system annually, three million under‑25s not in education, employment or training, and 340 000 additional unemployed youths in the past year. He warned that the ANC’s nuclear and mining proposals will enrich elites and deter investment. Maimane outlined the DA’s “Rescue Plan”: improve education via teacher training, a school‑voucher system, a national education inspectorate and expanded student financial aid; create apprenticeships, internships and support for small businesses; reduce regulations and exempt low‑skill firms from minimum‑wage laws; invest in infrastructure, broadband and transport; partially privatise state‑owned enterprises with employee and citizen shares; implement mass‑inclusion BEE and transfer title deeds for land; add 50 000 police officers, specialised units and a new health plan; fight corruption by halving ministries, capping consultant spending and making tender processes transparent. He concluded that the DA seeks to move South Africa forward with hope rather than backward.

The article explains how Alexa can reduce cleaning effort: set a cleaning schedule with the Cleaning Buddy skill, order supplies automatically via voice purchasing on Amazon, control robot vacuums (e.g., Roomba, Neato) with voice commands, and use services such as Laundrapp for laundry pickup or stain‑removal skills for clothing care.

Electropolishing of superconducting radio frequency cavities introduces intergranular sloped steps with slope angles up to ~50° and heights up to 70 nm. Using atomic force microscopy and white light interferometry, researchers found these defects suppress the superheating field and enhance magnetic field concentration, limiting peak accelerating fields. The defects also reduce local impurity concentration during diffusion processes like low-temperature baking, affecting surface treatment effectiveness. The superheating field suppression and magnetic field enhancement factors depend on slope angle, step height, and material parameters. Minimizing surface roughness and step heights is essential for achieving field limits near the superheating field of niobium and next-generation cavity materials.

MIT researchers have engineered an improved prime editing system that reduces DNA editing errors by up to 60‑fold. By introducing specific Cas9 mutations and combining them, they created a version of the editor called vPE that lowers error rates from about one in seven edits to roughly one in 101–543 edits, depending on editing mode, in mouse and human cells. The approach avoids double‑strand DNA breaks, uses a single‑strand cut, and an RNA template to insert corrected sequences. The team reports that the new method could make gene therapy safer and allow treatment of many genetic diseases. They are now working to increase efficiency and develop tissue‑specific delivery systems, while encouraging other labs to adopt the editor for research. Funding came from the Life Sciences Research Foundation, the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the National Cancer Institute and the Koch Institute Support.

Police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury, eight miles from Salisbury, with critical exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with Wiltshire Police. Initial tests suggested contaminated drugs, but further analysis continues. No wider health risk is believed.

In re Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak, Bankruptcy No. 8:04‑BK‑13861‑PMG, Adversary No. 8:05‑AP‑173‑PMG (M.D. Fla. Aug. 1, 2007). The plaintiff, D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P., filed a complaint to deny the debtor’s discharge under 11 U.S.C. §§ 727(a)(2)‑(5). The debtor, a 72‑year‑old former owner of A & F Corporation (a Pennsylvania manufacturing firm), claimed net worth of $2.7 million on a March 2002 financial statement. Prior to his Chapter 7 filing in July 2004, he transferred funds to his wife, opened accounts in her name, and his schedules omitted prior bankruptcy filings, his stock in A & F, and certain income. The court found that the plaintiff did not prove fraudulent intent in the transfers, that the debtor had produced records, that the false statements were not made knowingly or fraudulently, and that the loss of assets was not satisfactorily explained but the plaintiff failed to identify specific assets. The court entered final judgment for the debtor and ordered a discharge.

Polo began in Persia more than 20 centuries ago, spread to the Middle East, Central Asia and the Far East, and its modern form derives from India where it was called sagol kangjei, kanjai‑bazee or pulu (the wooden ball). British colonists introduced it to England, and from there it reached the United States, where about 250 polo clubs now operate in 43 states. The Milwaukee Polo Club (MPC) is located in Hartland, about 26 miles west of Milwaukee, and traces its roots to a 1923 formation; the club has been at its present site for more than 20 years. Thomas Esser handles MPC’s marketing, website and media outreach. MPC describes its polo as “blue‑collar” and accessible, with members ranging from nurses and students to bartenders and retirees; spectators pay $5 (children free). Matches consist of six seven‑minute chukkers with a half‑time “divot stomp,” lasting roughly two hours. Games are scheduled weather‑dependent; unsafe footing cancels play, while off‑days feature horse demonstrations. The club stresses that horses are teammates, limiting their work, providing proper feeding, grooming and rest. MPC is at N75 W30311 County Highway VV, Hartland; phone 262‑222‑2870 or 262‑951‑8029; milwaukeepoloclub.com.

The speaker discusses hockey coaching philosophy, emphasizing preparation, focus, and execution over momentum. He notes that in a salary cap world, winning opportunities are limited and must be capitalized on. The coach highlights the importance of team depth and player development, noting how contributors like Abby, Helm, Ericsson, and Leino have been essential. He discusses matchup strategy, stating that depth provides better matchups and playing from ahead is advantageous. The speaker analyzes game performance, mentioning early defensive lapses and noting both goaltenders have performed better at home. He emphasizes team building through winning together, paying the price, and supporting each other, stating "you win together today you walk together forever." The coach also discusses the importance of enjoying playoff opportunities while they last, acknowledging two evenly matched teams in a close final series.

Austin ISD sent a memo directing staff not to share unvetted resources and prohibiting discussion of political or controversial topics. It cited heightened scrutiny due to the district's location in the state capital. School Board Vice President Saldana criticized the memo as contradictory to district commitments and said the board was not briefed. Education Austin distributed immigrant resources and held Know Your Rights seminars, arguing such information is informational, not political, and called for the district to communicate it clearly to families.

A 13‑year‑old girl was shot in an open garage in Guildford, Sydney, on Tuesday night at 9:45 pm. She was taken to Westmead Children’s Hospital in serious but stable condition. Police say the shooting was not random.

Penny stocks are low‑priced equities, typically below $5, that are mostly traded on over‑the‑counter (OTC) markets and Pink Sheets rather than on formal exchanges like NYSE or Nasdaq. The OTC market serves small companies that cannot or choose not to meet exchange listing requirements. Because they operate with limited regulation, penny‑stock companies are not required to file detailed financial reports, leading to a lack of reliable information for investors. Most penny‑stock firms have unproven or failing business models, and many end up worthless; almost all ultimately fail.

Low liquidity creates high bid‑ask spreads and slippage, making buying and selling expensive. The combination of limited data, high volatility, and minimal oversight makes penny stocks highly susceptible to scams such as pump‑and‑dump, dump‑and‑dilute, and “know‑it‑all” schemes. Success stories are rare and often linked to such fraudulent activity. Consequently, penny stocks are considered high‑risk, speculative investments where investors can lose their entire capital. The passage advises avoiding penny stocks and warns that traders without significant resources and expertise are likely to become prey for more informed or fraudulent market participants.

Senator Mark Warner says Republicans are engaged in an unprecedented campaign to undermine Robert Mueller's investigation and FBI integrity. Warner, leading the Senate Russia investigation with Sen. Richard Burr, says neither he nor Burr was permitted to view the Nunes memo before its release. He believes they were blocked because legitimate entities would question its methodology and reckless use of classified information. The House Intelligence Committee later voted along party lines to prevent Democrats from releasing their response memo. Warner says the investigation is key to defending against future cyberwarfare threats.

Two‑sided many‑to‑one matching must balance fairness for participants and for teams. The classical Gale‑Shapley stability notion (justified envy‑freeness) may be unfair to teams when participants are indifferent, as teams can receive participants of very different desirability. Recent work introduced team‑EF1 (envy‑freeness up to one participant for teams) but showed that an allocation satisfying team‑EF1 and participant‑justified EF may not exist and that deciding existence is NP‑hard.

The authors propose a new fairness notion, team‑justified EF1, which removes from a team’s bundle those participants who strictly prefer the other team before checking envy. Under ordinal preferences, they define stochastic‑dominance (SD) counterparts: team‑SD‑EF1 and team‑justified SD‑EF1.

Two simple approaches are examined. Restricting round‑robin to participants who rank a team first yields team‑justified SD‑EF1 and participant‑EF but may be highly unbalanced. An auxiliary one‑to‑one instance yields team‑justified SD‑EF1, participant‑justified EF, and balancedness, but does not guarantee swap stability.

The main algorithm (Algorithm 3) produces an allocation that simultaneously satisfies team‑justified SD‑EF1, participant‑justified EF, balancedness, and Pareto optimality (which implies swap stability). It works with ordinal preferences (including ties), creates team‑slots, maintains eligibility sets for participants, and in each iteration computes a matching that maximizes team‑slot values in round‑robin order and breaks ties by lexicographically optimizing participants’ preferences. The algorithm runs in polynomial time and reduces to round‑robin when participants are indifferent and to the Gale–Shapley algorithm when all preferences are strict.

With an augmented tie‑breaking rule, the algorithm is shown to be group‑strategyproof for participants: no coalition can misreport preferences to make all its members strictly better off.

The method extends to settings with quotas and the option for participants or teams to remain unassigned, yielding an allocation that is stable, Pareto optimal, group‑strategyproof for participants, and satisfies an extended notion of team‑justified SD‑EF1. Thus the algorithm unifies the round‑robin fair‑division method and the Gale–Shapley matching algorithm while guaranteeing fairness to both sides.

Digital laggards prioritize short‑term, process‑driven work, limit risk‑taking, hoard data, and set aspirational but unrealistic goals; their cultures discourage experimentation and rely on a “culture of genius” rather than data‑driven decisions. Digital leaders foster a learning mindset, encourage risk‑taking in controlled pockets, make data transparent across teams, and use metrics to set realistic, measurable goals. They align objectives vertically and horizontally, providing employees with autonomy while tracking progress toward shared targets. Two case studies illustrate these patterns: a regulated pharmaceutical firm created a localized experimentation team that automated compliance checks, cutting the required time by 75 % and spreading the solution across the organization; a retail company adopted real‑time sales reporting after an acquisition, enabling leaders to make data‑driven inventory and supply‑chain decisions. Research identified four organizational patterns—data novices, insight‑ready, tech‑enabled, and data‑reliant—based on culture maturity and technical capability, indicating that companies can build on existing strengths to develop a strong data culture. The findings were presented by Keystone Strategy.

The speech reviews the first century of the United States, noting the adoption of the Articles of Confederation, the creation of the Constitution, the addition of twenty‑five states, and the Civil War’s test of the Union. It states that the nation has emerged stronger, with the Constitution as supreme law while preserving state autonomy. The most important political change since 1787 is identified as the elevation of African Americans from slavery to full citizenship, which freed both races, added moral and industrial forces, and opened careers to millions. The speech acknowledges that equal suffrage remains contested, warning that denying the ballot threatens self‑government and that ignorance among voters is a danger requiring universal education; the nation bears responsibility for extending suffrage and combating illiteracy.  

Economic policies emphasized include maintaining the gold‑silver monetary basis, ensuring United States notes are redeemable, refunding the national debt at lower interest, supporting agriculture through scientific assistance, fostering manufacturing and transportation, and protecting American interests in a future interoceanic canal across the Isthmus.  

The address calls for congressional prohibition of polygamy and other criminal practices in the Territories, insisting that no ecclesiastical organization may usurp governmental powers. It also urges the establishment of civil‑service law governing tenure and removals.  

The Administration commits to upholding national authority, enforcing laws, practicing rigid economy, demanding honest service, and respecting state and reserved rights, while appealing for public support and divine blessing.

ATR trailing stop is a dynamic stop‑loss tool introduced by J. Welles Wilder that uses the average true range (ATR) to set and adjust stop levels based on price volatility. It is calculated by multiplying the current ATR by a multiplier (commonly 3.5) and subtracting the result from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions, producing tighter stops when volatility is high. The indicator helps traders determine exit points, protect profits, limit losses, and adapt to changing market conditions, and it can also provide entry signals when price breaks the trailing stop. It applies to various instruments such as stocks and futures, and ATR bands derived from ATR values are used to identify breakouts and gauge volatility intensity. The cross point where price intersects the trailing stop signals a potential trend reversal, prompting traders to reassess positions. A limitation is that the indicator does not account for past performance or price movements, so it should be combined with other analyses to manage risk effectively.

Harvard President Drew Faust announced she will step down June 30, 2018, after 11 years as the university's first female president. Her tenure ends alongside Harvard's $6.5 billion fundraising campaign, which raised $8 billion. A historian specializing in the American South and Civil War, Faust succeeded Lawrence Summers and restored campus unity after his contentious leadership. She expanded financial aid and championed both arts and sciences. Her presidency faced controversies including backlash over all-male clubs, diversity concerns, and a suspended men's soccer team. A search committee will find her replacement.

Texas A&M has had at least one first‑round NFL draft pick since 2011, and receiver Christian Kirk could become the 10th first‑round selection. Kirk is projected as a first‑round pick; USA Today listed him fourth among receivers, behind Calvin Ridley, DJ Moore and Anthony Miller, Ridley and Moore projected. He will stay home in Arizona rather than attend the draft at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. Safety Watts is a mid‑round prospect and Ratley a late‑round choice. The Aggies were young, underclassmen; the 2013‑14 recruiting under Kevin Sumlin failed, limiting recent draft picks. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson was arrested in December on aggravated‑assault, evidence‑tampering and marijuana charges, suspended for the bowl, participated in the combine but not the pro day, his draft outlook declined. The first round is Thursday in Arlington; rounds two‑three are Friday and rounds four‑seven Saturday. Prior Aggies first‑round picks include Von Miller, Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, Cedric Ogbuehi and Myles Garrett.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice retires Friday after a decades‑long career; Glenn Maleyko, current Dearborn superintendent, will succeed him, with Sue Carnell serving as interim. Rice, who took office in 2019, led through the COVID‑19 pandemic, which drove lower state and national exam scores, higher chronic absenteeism and worsening student mental health. He warns that state law lets schools count up to seven professional‑development days and up to fifteen online‑instruction days as instructional days, reducing actual teaching time below the legally required 180 days, yet no data show how many districts use these flexibilities. Despite flat NAEP results, Michigan has made incremental progress: higher enrollment in free preschool, a record 82 % high‑school graduation rate and additional funding for vulnerable students. Rice cites Mississippi’s mandatory LETRS science‑of‑reading training and early‑literacy coaches as a model and wants similar K‑5 requirements. Teacher‑preparation numbers have risen from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually, aided by state stipends, scholarships and “grow‑your‑own” programs, though shortages remain in high‑need schools.

Alphabet, owner of YouTube, agreed to pay $24.5 million to settle a lawsuit filed by Donald Trump after his account was suspended following the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. Of that amount, $22 million will go to Trump and $2.5 million to co‑plaintiffs including the American Conservative Union and several individuals. Trump sued YouTube, Twitter (now X) and Meta in July 2021, claiming his free‑speech rights were violated; his YouTube restrictions were lifted in March 2023. Trump directed that the $22 million be transferred to the Trust for the National Mall and used to fund construction of a ballroom on the White House grounds. Combined with earlier settlements with X ($10 million) and Meta ($25 million), Trump has received more than $57 million from the three platforms.

Peter Lynch is a retired money manager who ran Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, delivering a 29% annual return—more than double the S&P 500’s—and grew fund assets from $20 million to $14 billion. He popularized “invest in what you know” and “ten baggers,” and practiced a value‑oriented, fundamentals‑first approach, ignoring market‑timing and short‑term price swings. Lynch grouped stocks into six categories: slow‑growing, moderately growing, fast‑growing, cyclical, crisis‑recovery (turnaround), and undervalued‑asset (hidden‑value) companies. He preferred simple, boring businesses with clear models, often small‑cap firms overlooked by institutional investors, and evaluated them using market share, profit margins, P/E ratios and other financial metrics. The portfolio was diversified, with roughly 30‑40% in growth stocks, 10‑20% each in moderate growers and cyclicals, the remainder in turnarounds, plus a 1% stake in 500 potential candidates. Holdings were reviewed quarterly; positions were sold when price outpaced fundamentals or growth slowed, while adding to those that fell on solid fundamentals. Lynch believed individual investors could beat professionals by applying everyday knowledge of businesses.

The Vice President of the Ghana Football Association (GFA), George Afriyie, was relieved of his duties following an Executive Committee meeting on Tuesday, weeks after he announced his intention to contest the 2019 GFA presidency. The dismissal follows months of rumored conflict with GFA President Kwesi Nyantakyi, stemming from financial disagreements and accusations of connivance with a critic. Prior removals of Vice Presidents Fred Pappoe (2011) and Fred Crentsil (2015) illustrate a pattern of sidelining former lieutenants. Earlier, Afriyie was stripped of his role as head of the Black Stars Management Committee. Some Executive Committee members publicly opposed him, with Winfred Osei assuming his position. The sacking is seen as solidifying Nyantakyi's position as he contemplates a fourth term as GFA president, despite mixed performance records including three straight World Cup qualifications and a revived FA Cup.

Lenders to Enron‑promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC) met in Singapore on 7‑8 June 2001 and appointed global energy consultants Stone & Webster to evaluate the cost of suspending the project’s second phase (1,444 MW). Enron India’s managing director suggested a temporary suspension, while both Indian and foreign lenders agreed Phase I (740 MW) should restart immediately and that legal disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) should be deferred until a solution for power offtake is found. DPC offered to cut its target rate of return from 16 % to 11 % to lower the per‑unit tariff, and the Godbole renegotiation committee maintained that DPC’s return on equity should not exceed 16 % regardless of plant load factor. DPC filed a writ petition in the Bombay High Court challenging the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (MERC) jurisdiction and seeking to stay MERC’s order restraining it from reactivating an escrow account and from proceeding with arbitration. The court is scheduled to hear the petition on 11 June. Lenders formed a joint committee (IDBI, ICICI, SBI, ANZ Grindlays, ABN Amro, Citibank, Credit Suisse First Boston) to negotiate with MSEB, and a $25 million payment to the EPC contractor Bechtel is due on 18 June. Private power producers welcomed Prime Minister Vajpayee’s optimism but warned that states cannot afford DPC’s power at current tariffs, and activist Medha Patkar called for a judicial inquiry into the deal.

Scientists assessing cheetah populations in southern Africa recommend listing the species as "Endangered" on the IUCN Red List. The assessment follows a report that cheetahs have disappeared from 91 percent of their historic range.

The study uses machine learning to estimate Aedes invasive mosquito abundance in the Basque Country (northern Spain) by modeling relationships between ovitrap egg counts (2013–2023) and climate variables (temperature, humidity, precipitation) from 2016–2023. Data from three provinces were collected, but Araba was excluded due to sparse data; analysis focused on Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia. Four models were tested—GLM, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Trees—incorporating lagged variables which improved performance. Temperature showed strong correlation with egg counts (Spearman index 0.72–0.80), while humidity and precipitation were weakly correlated. Random Forest achieved highest training accuracy (R²=0.98), but GLM and SARIMAX performed best on test data (R²=0.81–0.85). Predictions suggest lower mosquito abundance in 2024 compared to 2023. The study concludes that temperature is the key climate driver of mosquito abundance, and continuous entomological surveillance is critical for accurate forecasting and public health strategies in non-endemic regions.

Coach discusses team momentum, home ice advantage, and confidence from past success in Stanley Cup Finals. Expresses pride in team's will and attitude despite injuries. Emphasizes opportunity to win and importance of staying focused on execution rather than the prize. Highlights learning from legendary players and cherishing the opportunity to share it with the community during challenging economic times. Emphasizes team unity and doing your part for the group.

The author reflects on college nearly eight years after graduation, noting they didn't take advantage of available opportunities or realize how much time they had for adventure. They acknowledge "youth wasted on the young" and note everyone does college differently. While college had wonderful aspects like exceptional people and fascinating classes, the author focuses on what they did wrong.

HPBOSE released Himachal Pradesh Class 12 Result 2018 on April 24 at 14:07 pm on its website hpbose.org; it is available via examresults.net, indiaresults.com, or by SMS (HP12ROLLNUMBER to 56263). To view online, visit the site, locate the result link, enter roll number, and download.

Feb. 14 seven more candidates qualified for the race to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price in Georgia’s 6th Congressional District, raising the total to 15. New qualifiers include Republicans Bruce Levell, David Abroms, Bob Gray, Kurt Wilson; Democrats Ragin Edwards, Richard Keatley, and Rebecca Quigg. A special election is set for April 18, with a runoff likely on June 20.

Liverpool open 2017/18 at Watford (Aug 12); Everton Dec 9, Goodison Apr 7; United home Oct 14, away Mar 10; Swansea Boxing Day; finish vs Brighton May 13 after Chelsea, Stamford Bridge; dates subject to change.

A UK study published in Thorax investigated whether CT lung cancer screening helps smokers quit. Questionnaires were sent to 2.5 million British residents aged 50‑75; 8,729 high‑risk smokers were identified and randomly invited to CT screening or not, while all received information on smoking’s health risks and quitting. At two weeks, 10 % of screened participants quit versus 5 % of controls; at two years the quit rate was 15 % versus 5 %. A normal screening result did not lower motivation, and quitters reported greater smoking‑related distress. The researchers conclude that CT screening provides a teachable moment and, when combined with other cessation support, may increase quitting among motivated smokers.

Geminids peak Wednesday night; viewing after midnight until 4 a.m. Thursday, 50 meteors/hr, best away from city lights, no telescope needed. Look south toward Gemini. A crescent moon this year enhances visibility; meteors are debris from asteroid Phaethon entering Earth’s atmosphere.

USGS awarded $4.9 million to Caltech and six other institutions to develop the ShakeAlert earthquake‑warning system for the West Coast, plus about $1 million for sensors. The system, in development since 2006, needs an estimated $38.3 million in capital and $16.1 million annually to operate. Funding was previously threatened but restored after West Coast legislators pushed for $10.2 million.

Northwestern is close to its first NCAA bid after a 66-59 upset over Wisconsin, with Chris Collins urging focus despite media attention. Point guard Bryant McIntosh and forward Vic Law warn that a loss could jeopardize bid. Northwestern hosts Maryland tomorrow night while Scottie Lindsey remains out with mono.

Valmet Oyj announced on 11 December 2017 that its Board approved a new share‑based incentive plan for employees. The plan covers discretionary periods (2018‑2020). For 2018, rewards are based on Comparable EBITA margin and orders received growth of the Services and Automation lines, and will be paid half in shares and half in cash in 2019. Executive Team is advised to hold shares equal to their gross base salary. Shares are locked for two years after each period. Termination before payment forfeits the award; termination during lock‑up requires return of shares. The plan targets 120 participants (80 senior managers, 40 management talents) and total reward is capped at 586,000 shares.

American Airlines mailed a Net SAAver Weekend Getaway promotion to Theresa Staab on 19 Nov 2001. Domestic travel is valid 30 Nov – 1 Dec 2001 and international travel 29 30 Nov 2001; tickets must be purchased by 23 Nov 2001. The email lists dozens of round‑trip domestic fares ranging from $69 (e.g., Abilene–Dallas) to $229 (e.g., Boston–San Francisco) and international fares from $219 (e.g., Boston–London) to $399 (e.g., Chicago–Tokyo). Vacation packages offered include: AA Vacations Florida Winter Specials from $115 per person (4 days/3 nights at Hyatt Orlando); the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess Sonoran Celebration Holiday Package starting at $259, which includes breakfast for two, a 10 % discount, complimentary gift wrapping and 500 AAdvantage miles; Starwood hotels (Westin, Sheraton, Four Points, St. Regis, Luxury Collection, W) at $49–$179 weekend rates (Thurs–Sun) and up to 40 % off weekday rates (Mon–Wed) until 27 Jan 2002; and Hertz last‑minute compact‑car rates from $14.99 to $17.99 per weekend day (book by noon 26 Nov, pickup before 10 Dec).
