A July survey of 202 administrators, teachers and managers at Illinois Head Start and other daycare centers found nutrition, physical activity and oral hygiene were the primary health‑promotion priorities. Fewer than one‑in‑five respondents ranked bike‑helmet use, vaccinations or sun protection among top concerns. About half of programs provided sunscreen, yet 77 % of those did not allow children to apply it themselves; many used spray sunscreens to avoid direct touching, with Head Start more likely to use sprays, but spray often directed at faces, risking inhalation or eye irritation. Most programs reported no sunburns and followed heat‑index guidelines to keep children indoors. Authors note the Illinois focus and call for greater education; experts suggest parents help by applying sunscreen, providing protective clothing and modeling behavior.

In a Denver federal civil trial, a jury found that radio host David Mueller sexually assaulted pop star Taylor Swift during a 2013 preconcert photo session. The six‑woman, two‑man jury awarded Swift the $1 she had requested and ruled that Mueller’s actions constituted assault and battery. Mueller’s own 2015 suit, which alleged Swift fabricated the accusation, was dismissed after the judge found insufficient evidence to support the claim. The jury also determined that Swift’s mother, Andrea, and her manager, Frank Bell, did not interfere with Mueller’s contract with radio station KYGO. Swift said she would donate an unspecified amount to organizations that aid sexual‑assault victims. The verdict followed closing arguments in which both sides presented differing accounts of the encounter, and the jury deliberated for one day before reaching its decision.

Angela B. Ryan, a lawyer and mother of four, recounts experiencing repeated non‑consensual touching of her pregnant belly during court proceedings over three pregnancies spanning 27 months. She describes how judges and colleagues commented on her appearance, and opposing counsel physically stroked her abdomen in front of the court, treating her body as public property. She previously judged pregnant colleagues and now acknowledges her earlier ignorance, arguing that this conduct constitutes assault despite being euphemistically called a stroke, rub, or pat. She notes that existing U.S. law—the Pregnancy Discrimination Act of 1978, Title VII, and EEOC guidance—already defines such unwelcome physical contact based on pregnancy as unlawful sex discrimination, yet the practice is rarely addressed. Referencing anthropological and public‑health research, she cites pregnancy as a “liminal state” and says stress hormones from unwanted touching affect both mother and child. Ryan calls for immediate policy changes: a clear rule prohibiting any touch of a pregnant person without explicit consent, inclusion in harassment policies, staff training, and judicial education. She concludes that the legal profession must stop treating the belly stroke as acceptable and recognize it as assault.

After two straight wins, the team says it has played better, managed the puck more effectively and created better scoring chances while keeping the puck away from the opposing goaltender. Players feel confident but not cocky, and they are focused on Thursday’s game, which they consider the most important of the series. They note that a six‑hour flight affects both teams equally and that home‑ice gives the centerman who puts his stick in last a small advantage. The squad highlights a key player who has been outstanding throughout the playoffs, providing a lift and boosting confidence. Players say the every‑other‑day schedule limits over‑thinking and that they are preparing with the same routine they used after a recent Saturday night. Both teams are strong defensively; scoring first helps, but both have shown they can come back, and the team feels especially confident in overtime.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth gathered hundreds of generals and admirals from around the globe to argue for a military overhaul, describing the force as soft and “woke.” New York Times Pentagon reporter Greg Jaffe reports on the speech.

SD Memory Card specifications cover pre-erased settings for faster multiple block writes using ACMD23; erase operations including standard erase (CMD32-33-38), discard (CMD38 with argument 00000001h), and Full User Area Logical Erase or FULE (CMD38 with argument 00000002h); write protection via mechanical switch, internal card protection, and password locking; Card Ownership Protection (COP) with PWD and FEP registers controlling lock/unlock and force erase functions; application-specific commands via APP_CMD (CMD55) preceding ACMDs; switch function command (CMD6) for access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit selection; high-speed mode (25 MB/s) at 50 MHz; CMD8 for interface condition checking; address and block length differences between SDSC (byte addressing, variable block length) and SDHC/SDXC (block addressing, fixed 512-byte blocks); bus clock control requiring 8 clock cycles after transactions; CRC protection using CRC7 for commands/responses and CRC16 for data blocks; 48-bit command format with indexed commands, arguments, and CRC; command classification into classes (0-11) defining mandatory and optional support; and state transition rules dependent on card state and command class.

Commander Chris Hadfield spent Christmas 2012 aboard the International Space Station, where he played Santa, hid cards from crew families, and encountered 16 sunrises each day because the station orbits Earth every 92 minutes. To prevent crumbs in microgravity, the crew ate a dense fruitcake made by Trappist monks, velcroed to a table. They also shared a ready‑to‑eat turkey meal, an artificial tree velcroed to a wall, and stockings filled with chocolate and nuts. Emphasizing the psychological importance of traditions, Hadfield and his U.S.‑Russian crew celebrated holidays from their own cultures. He later applied that cross‑cultural perspective to his science‑based variety show, Generator, premiering in Toronto.

A100’s L1 and shared memory give 1.5× capacity vs V100; it has 40 GB HBM2 (1555 GB/s, 73%↑), a 40 MB L2 cache (≈7× larger, 2.3× read bandwidth), residency controls, and Compute Data Compression for 4× DRAM bandwidth.

Polling for 69 of Uttarakhand's 70 seats began Wednesday; 74 lakh voters and 628 candidates vote till 5 pm. Karnaprayag seat postponed to March 9 after BSP candidate death. 30,000 security and 60,000 officials in 10,685 booths, 460 snowbound.

Sylvester Michael McGillivray sued Harry Eramian for personal injuries sustained at Eramian's bowling alley on March 10, 1938. While delivering a bowling ball with his hand near the floor, a splinter from the uneven, worn, and splintered "sliding floor" entered the plaintiff's finger. The floor was dirty, old, and had been installed from used materials two to three months before the accident. The jury returned a verdict for the plaintiff, awarding $750. The court affirmed that the defendant owed a duty to keep the premises reasonably safe, and the evidence supported a finding of negligence regarding the floor's condition. The court also found no evidence that the plaintiff's bowling technique was improper or unusual, and no evidence he observed the splinter before the injury, so contributory negligence could not be ruled as a matter of law. The defendant's requested jury instructions were properly refused as they concerned factual matters for the jury. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff.

Samsung unveiled three water-resistant Galaxy A smartphones (A3, A5, A7) - its first product launch since the Note 7 recall. The devices feature 16MP cameras with "selfie mode" and screen sizes ranging from 4.7 to 5.7 inches. Launching first in Russia, they resemble the Galaxy S line but have less processing power and max out at 32GB storage. Pricing typically starts under $400, compared to Galaxy S's $800. Samsung reportedly completed its Note 7 investigation but hasn't publicly revealed findings.

Passports are issued only by the Secretary of State. U.S. citizens abroad apply to the nearest diplomatic or consular officer; residents of insular possessions apply to the chief executive. Passports are denied to anyone not owing allegiance to the United States, including those who have only declared intent to become citizens.

Within the United States, applicants must file a sworn affidavit with the Secretary of State, attested by an authorized officer, stating birth date and place, occupation, permanent residence, and intent to travel temporarily and return to perform citizenship duties. The affidavit must include a physical description, at least one credible witness certificate, and the applicant must take the oath of allegiance.

Certain categories must submit extra documentation: persons born abroad to a U.S. citizen father, naturalized citizens, unmarried women, women married to a citizen, children of naturalized citizens, and insular residents.

After a July 4 flood killed 26 people at Camp Mystic in Kerr County, including Chloe Childress (an 18-year-old counselor and the daughter of Matthew and Wendie Childress), parents organized to push for new Texas laws. The flood resulted from 10 inches of rain falling in three hours along the Guadalupe River. Matthew Childress and other parents, including Blake Bonner whose 9-year-old daughter Lila died, connected with lobbyists and families of the victims to advocate for camp safety reforms.

The new laws require camps to move overnight cabins out of floodplains, follow weather warnings with radios, install alert systems, and train staff on emergency evacuation procedures. Parents testified before legislators about their daughters. On Sept. 5, Gov. Greg Abbott signed the bills into law during a ceremony attended by the parents, who received the pens used for signing.

Despite their advocacy success, the parents acknowledged their grief remained. Matthew Childress said the laws couldn't bring back his daughter, who had been accepted to the University of Texas at Austin. Bonner noted the accomplishment felt bittersweet because "our girls are still dead."

The excerpt describes the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processor’s L4 Fast and L4 Slow peripheral memory map regions, the DDR DMM TILER extended 4‑GByte addressing range that is usable only by the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, and the terminal‑function tables that list external signal names, pin multiplexing, pin numbers, pin types (I, O, Z, S, GND, A), internal pull‑up/pull‑down states, supply voltage sources, and boot‑configuration details for GPMC pins (including BTMODE sampling and de‑selected input states).
China launched its first talent visa for young STEM graduates as the US raised H‑1B fees to $100,000, sparking backlash.

This whitepaper discusses how AI, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), may transform social science research and how regulatory frameworks should evolve for responsible AI governance. Social scientists aim to uncover predictive patterns in human behavior, and computational social science has emerged with the availability of large-scale behavioral data. LLMs offer opportunities to synthesize research data, automate analysis through zero-shot capabilities and in-context learning, and potentially contribute to developing novel social theories. However, challenges exist, including inherent biases, quality concerns regarding LLM-generated data, and ethical risks. AI governance is needed due to threats like misinformation, deepfakes, and amplified societal biases, with existing legal frameworks struggling to keep pace with rapidly evolving technology. Current governance challenges include gaps between industry and government, lack of international consensus, and difficulties identifying emerging risks. Recommendations include fostering top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers while also implementing bottom-up approaches that engage developers and users in reporting issues. Effective governance should be human-centered, ensuring AI advances safely and aligns with ethical values. The paper is a collaborative effort by Microsoft Research Asia and academics from various institutions.

Study used cross‑sectional data from the COVID‑PCD cohort (N = 747, 60 % female, median age 27, from 49 countries) to describe diagnostic testing for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD). Overall, 92 % reported testing; 49 % of participants aged ≥ 5 had nasal nitric oxide (nNO) measurement, 75 % reported a biopsy, and 58 % reported genetic testing. Biopsy was the most common test in most countries, but genetic testing dominated in North America and France. Test use varied widely by country; German participants reported nNO most frequently (66 %) while Swiss participants reported it least (35 %). Recall of tests differed, with the highest proportion of “no recall” for nNO (18 %) and lowest for biopsy (8 %). Only 36 % of participants aged ≥ 5 reported all three tests (nNO, biopsy, genetics). Multivariable regression showed that diagnosis after 2010 was strongly associated with higher odds of each test (OR 2.2–4.7) and situs abnormalities with lower odds (OR 0.5–0.7). Age at diagnosis was not a significant predictor. The authors conclude that PCD diagnostics vary considerably worldwide, many patients have incomplete work‑up, and recent diagnosis and absence of situs abnormalities predict more comprehensive testing, highlighting the need for improved diagnostic characterization and patient education.

A federal judge rejected a lawsuit challenging the Biden-era gainful-employment rule, siding with the Education Department. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to prove graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates, with failing programs risking loss of federal financial aid. Industry groups opposed the rule while student advocacy groups praised it, and the issue will be revisited during an upcoming rule-making process.

The Third Circuit vacated the district court's order denying Mrs. Prava Chatterjee's petition to vacate a settlement and release related to her son's death in a 1975 maritime collision. The court held that Indian law applies to the validity of the special power of attorney (due to choice-of-law principles), while federal maritime law applies to the release. The court extended the Garrett standard of careful scrutiny to relatives of deceased seamen, placing the burden on shipowners to prove the release was valid. The appellate court found the district court abused its discretion by denying Mrs. Chatterjee's motion for a new commission to take testimony in India, effectively blocking her ability to substantiate claims that her signature on the power of attorney was forged. This procedural ruling denied her due process. The case was remanded with directions to invoke a commission.

Halliburton reported Q1 net income of $46 million, reversing a loss a year earlier; adjusted EPS of 41 cents met analyst expectations; revenue of $5.74 billion fell slightly short of the $5.76 billion forecast; shares rose about 6 % year‑to‑date and 10 % over the past 12 months.

National Travel and Tourism Office data show 19 percent fewer international students arrived in the U.S. in August 2025 than in the same month of 2024, while a DHS SEVIS report released in late September recorded an unexpected 0.8 percent enrollment increase, which NAFSA criticized as unreliable. Arrival figures exclude students who arrived after the semester began or who remained in the U.S. over summer. Organizations such as NAFSA forecast overall declines of about 15 percent, with particularly steep drops from Africa (‑32 %), Asia (‑24 %) and the Middle East (‑17 %). Country‑level decreases include Iran (‑86 %), India (‑44.5 %), Nigeria (‑47.8 %), and over 33 000 fewer Indian students. Experts attribute the decline to a global freeze on visa interviews and reduced processing capacity at key posts, and note that nine universities were asked to cap undergraduate international enrollment at 15 percent. They warn of significant tuition‑revenue losses for institutions and economic harm to college towns, and some predict the total decline could exceed 20 percent. William Brustein described the ongoing damage as irreparable. A clearer picture of fall enrollment is expected when the Institute of International Education releases its Fall Snapshot report in mid‑November.

Canada credits NAFTA with strong economic growth and a transformed manufacturing sector, yet current renegotiations reveal that its exports are overly reliant on North America. Although Canada has 14 free‑trade agreements (including CETA and CPTPP), exports to most non‑NAFTA markets have not grown after signing. The author argues that a new trade deal alone is insufficient; a comprehensive five‑point plan is needed: 1) improve domestic business competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; 2) ensure FTAs address non‑tariff barriers and provide strong protections for manufactured goods; 3) focus trade agreements on countries with natural business ties and compatible legal systems; 4) leverage existing integrated supply chains, as about 85 % of Canada’s value‑added exports are production parts; and 5) support small‑ and medium‑enterprise growth abroad by consolidating export‑support programs. The author urges immediate structural changes to boost Canada’s global competitiveness.

A Delhi court on July 4 deferred to July 6 the hearing on the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies (ASCPL and CMSPL) for money‑laundering linked to the Aircel‑Maxis deal. The ED alleges Karti secured FIPB clearance for a $800 million (₹3,565.91 cr) FDI while his father was finance minister, a sum far above the ₹600 cr approval limit, with the actual FDI claimed to be ₹3,565.91 cr versus a projected ₹180 cr. CMSPL received ₹90 lakh and ASCPL ₹26 lakh from Maxis/Aircel. The CBI had earlier charged Dayanidhi Maran with using his influence to help the Maxis Group acquire Aircel, but a special court later dropped those charges for lack of concrete evidence. Karti also faces charges in the INX Media case for irregular FIPB clearance up to ₹305 cr.

The speaker returned from the Crimea (Yalta) Conference and reported to Congress that the meeting produced two major achievements: a plan to defeat Germany rapidly with minimal Allied losses, and a foundation for a lasting international peace. The conference established coordinated military operations between the Allied chiefs of staff, including daily exchange of intelligence between the western and eastern fronts. Politically, the three major powers agreed on the occupation and control of Germany, including the division into four zones under a Control Council in Berlin, the complete disarmament and removal of Nazi militarism, and reparations in kind. They also reached agreement on the voting procedure for the Security Council of the future International Security Organization, with a charter to be drafted at the United Nations conference in San Francisco on April 25, 1945. Decisions on liberated areas stipulated joint responsibility of the three powers to help establish democratic governments and hold free elections, exemplified by the agreement on Poland's provisional government and its borders. France was invited to join the Control Council and the San Francisco conference as a fourth sponsor and permanent Security Council member. The speech noted continued warfare against Japan, a planned increase of the Pacific offensive, and meetings with Middle Eastern leaders to discuss common interests. The speaker emphasized that the United States must share responsibility for world peace, that the Yalta agreements represent a turning point, and that the Senate and the American public will face a decision on endorsing the emerging United Nations charter.

Coach says the player likely will not play, citing no fatigue. Replays were inconclusive; he declines to give the player's status for tomorrow. The team won second and third rounds at home and a road win; location has not impacted them. Top players were affected night. He is confident but unsure about tomorrow. The last two games were overtime.

Pokémon GO's Solstice Event provides fire and ice-themed spawns and triples XP for catching Pokémon and for landing nice, great, excellent throws, curveballs and first throws. Stacking with a discounted Lucky Egg yields up to six times XP, making active catching more efficient than evolving Pokémon with Lucky Eggs. The bonuses help casual and midcore players reach higher levels ahead of upcoming gym system changes, while Stardust remains in demand. The event's seasonal theme reflects the game's worldwide character.

Theresa May faces pressure from Conservative MPs ahead of a cabinet meeting at Chequers. Andrea Jenkyns and Jacob Rees‑Mogg warn that failing to deliver a hard Brexit would be catastrophic for the party, urging May to keep her promises to leave the single market and customs union. Some MPs fear May might compromise on her red lines, resulting in a “soft Brexit” that would keep Britain closely aligned to EU rules and limit trade deals. Remain‑supporting MPs argue a pragmatic approach is needed to avoid business disruption and border problems in Northern Ireland. Environment Secretary Michael Gove said May’s plan keeps the red lines intact and predicted a united cabinet position, playing down suggestions of resignations.

The U.S. stock market has nearly quadrupled from post-crisis lows, but signs of a more challenging environment are emerging. The S&P 500 recently experienced its longest stretch without a new all-time high since 2015-2016. The Federal Reserve has raised rates and is expected to continue tightening, unlike during previous periods of volatility when central banks provided support. Meanwhile, 2017 saw historically low volatility (3.19% of trading days with 1%+ moves), but 2018 has experienced dramatically higher volatility (39.24% of trading days with 1%+ moves in just the first portion of the year), making it on track to be among the most volatile years since World War II. The VIX spiked in February and has remained elevated, failing to return to previous lows. The author suggests markets may be building toward a top and warns that the next bear market, when it arrives, may be slow and prolonged due to limited monetary policy tools to combat it. Investors are advised to look for dangers others are not yet seeing.

Bogleheads 3 Fund Portfolio consists of three low‑cost index funds: a U.S. total stock market fund, an international stock market fund and a U.S. total bond market fund. The Bogleheads 4 Fund Portfolio adds a total international bond market fund, providing global stock and bond exposure. Both strategies follow Jack Bogle’s principle of buying the whole market with low‑cost index funds, emphasizing diversification, long‑term growth and minimal costs. Typical allocations are 50 % U.S. stocks, 30 % international stocks and 20 % U.S. bonds for the three‑fund version, and 50 % U.S. stocks, 30 % international stocks, 10 % U.S. bonds and 10 % international bonds for the four‑fund version. Suitable fund examples include VTI, VEU and BND for the three‑fund portfolio, and VTI, VEU, BND and VXIS/IXUS for the four‑fund portfolio. Backtesting shows the three‑fund portfolio earned about 7.6 % annually with a 28 % maximum drawdown, while the four‑fund portfolio earned about 7.8 % annually with a 31 % maximum drawdown. Benefits include broad diversification and low expense ratios; risks include sensitivity to market volatility and interest‑rate changes. Both portfolios are designed for long‑term, buy‑and‑hold investors and require periodic rebalancing.

CWWA conference (Oct 16‑20) focuses on water, wastewater, waste; Caribbean minister to present position at 2018 World Water Forum. Cabinet approved; over 250 delegates, 40 exhibitors. Forum will review waste management plan for United Nations General Assembly. Bulkan leads Guyana delegation, includes Ministry of Communities and GWI. Partners: IDB, United Nations Environment, Caribbean Development Bank, PAHO.

Broadcast announces a nationwide mobilization to provide unemployment relief this winter, coordinated by a new organization under Walter Gifford that works with governors, state and local agencies, and business, labor, welfare, religious and fraternal groups. Over a thousand towns and cities already have relief committees and will seek funds for work programs and direct assistance, including health and character‑building services. The federal government is expanding public works that support nearly 700,000 families, has halted immigration, and is ensuring credit to stimulate employment; states, counties and municipalities are also expanding public works and tax‑supported relief. A voluntary margin of need must be met by community giving. A similar effort last winter under Colonel Woods succeeded, but many localities face greater need this year. The speaker urges Americans to make the upcoming Thanksgiving (Nov. 26) a demonstration of shared responsibility, ensuring no hunger or cold, and recalls the national unity shown at Valley Forge and Yorktown.

LG V35 ThinQ: Snapdragon 845, 6GB RAM, 6‑inch 2880×1440 OLED, no notch, headphone jack, Gorilla Glass 5, IP68, MIL‑STD‑810G, dual 16MP rear cameras (wide‑angle) + 8MP front, AI scene selection/portrait/low‑light, Google Lens, Super Far Field Voice Recognition, 32‑bit Hi‑Fi Quad DAC (7.1), 3,300 mAh battery, Bluetooth 5.0/NFC/802.11ac Wi‑Fi/USB‑C, face+fingerprint, Quick Charge 3.0, 64/128GB storage + microSD up to 2TB, joins LG G7 ThinQ, V‑series no secondary display, pricing and release TBD.

Drug repurposing leverages existing drugs for new indications, reducing development time and cost. Knowledge graphs integrate biomedical associations (e.g., drug–target, disease–protein) and use machine‑learning embeddings to predict novel drug‑disease links. The Elsevier Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG) extracts binary relations from both open‑access (OA) and controlled‑access (CA) literature using proprietary AI NLP, containing millions of nodes and edges relevant to rare‑disease drug repurposing. Comparative analyses show that OA and CA contributions to EBKG are roughly equal in number of relations; OA share has grown sharply since 2006 and now exceeds 50 % of rare‑disease and drug‑target relations. Most relations in the graph (≈50 %) are supported by a single reference, and uncited relations accumulate exponentially in both OA and CA corpora, with no difference in citation rate or speed of first citation between the two sources. Retraction rates are higher in CA journals, and most uncited relations originate from original research articles rather than reviews or high‑throughput experiments. The authors argue that additional confidence metrics—such as citation index, discourse analysis, network alignment, or training LLMs on highly cited literature—are needed to assess the reliability of knowledge‑graph relations.

The lecture covers control charting and its relationship to hypothesis testing. Alpha (false alarm rate) sets control limits while beta (missed alarm rate) depends on sample size. Increasing sample size tightens the sampling distribution, reducing beta while maintaining the same alpha. Average Run Length (ARL) quantifies expected runs before detection: ARL0 for in-control processes and ARL1 for detecting shifts. Process capability indices CP and CPK compare process spread and centering to spec limits. Control limits differ from spec limits; control limits detect unusual events while spec limits define acceptable parts. Quality loss functions penalize deviations from target quadratically. When monitoring many parameters simultaneously, aggregate false alarm rates must be considered. The lecture also discusses challenges with n=1 sampling and introduces alternative charts (moving average, EWMA, CUSUM) for faster detection of small shifts.

Managed by Q was an on-demand office cleaning and maintenance company founded in April 2014 in New York by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian. Inspired by their dissatisfaction with poor maintenance services in their housing co-ops, the founders aimed to create a fully transparent, technology-driven solution for office management. The company’s initial goal was to aggregate demand for all goods, services, and technology required to run an office, offering cleaning, maintenance, and office supplies through a centralized platform.

Q provided cleaning services at $25 per hour with a two-hour minimum, maintenance services ranging from $40 to $80 per hour depending on complexity, and automatically refilled office supplies. Customers received a wall-mounted iPad with a customized dashboard to monitor tasks, adjust cleaning schedules, and communicate with operators. The company used an app for cleaners to access task lists, schedules, and maps.

Initially, Q used subcontractors for cleaning but switched to hiring direct employees after three months due to quality control issues and a vision for an inclusive company culture. Employees, called “operators,” included field operators (cleaners, helpers, handymen) and HQ staff. Field operators earned $12.50 per hour for cleaning, with raises every six months, plus benefits like health insurance and paid time off for those working at least 30 hours per week.

Hiring prioritized integrity and work ethic over experience, using online applications, information sessions, one-on-one interviews, and hands-on training. Training included three-hour sessions on Q’s procedures, mentorship, and quizzes. Promotion opportunities existed for operators to become mentors or supervisors.

Q’s culture emphasized transparency, community, and continuous feedback. Operators used the term “Q” to describe the company’s values, such as solving hard problems and communicating fearlessly. Town Hall meetings were held every six weeks to share updates and recognize top operators. All employees, including management, participated in at least one deep cleaning during their first week to understand the cleaning role.

The company operated with headquarters functions for software development, customer acquisition, and policy standardization, while city functions managed day-to-day operations with operational autonomy. Q Knowledge was a centralized digital repository of policies and procedures to ensure consistency across locations.

By July 2015, Q served 228 accounts in New York, 25 in Chicago, and 28 in San Francisco, with about 1% market penetration in New York and less than 1% in other cities. The company raised $17.4 million in total funding, including a $15 million Series A round in June 2015. Investors saw potential in Q’s platform business model, which could expand from cleaning to maintenance, supplies, and other services.

Growth challenges included operational complexity, the need to train and manage a workforce, and differences in real estate and labor markets across cities. Q faced copycat competitors and considered expanding into new markets (Boston, Atlanta, Washington, DC) or deepening services in existing markets. The founders were determined to preserve the company’s culture and employee-focused business model while pursuing growth.

President Trump's first State of the Union will be used by lawmakers to convey messages. Female Democratic lawmakers plan to wear black in solidarity with #MeToo, highlighting sexual harassment; Rep. Annie Kuster invited Chessy Prout, a sexual‑assault survivor, as a guest. Dozens of Dreamers protected under DACA will sit in the House gallery as invited by Democratic leaders to emphasize immigration; Rep. Kevin Cramer invited Tommy Fisher, whose company is developing a prototype border wall. At least eight Democratic lawmakers announced they will boycott the address. Bill Nye the Science Guy will attend as a guest of Rep. Jim Bridenstine, Trump's nominee for NASA administrator, amid Democratic criticism. Rep. Joe Kennedy of Massachusetts will deliver the Democratic response.

Iraq has begun an aerial bombardment of Tal Afar, west of Mosul, with a ground attack to follow. The town, next target after Mosul's recapture, had about 200,000 residents and has produced senior ISIS commanders.

The Sarahah app is an anonymous messaging platform that recently went viral on social media, though it has existed for several months and was already popular in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Users create profiles where others can send anonymous messages. The app has received roughly equal positive and negative reviews, with critics noting its potential for bullying and harassment. Privacy features include profile removal from search results and user blocking. Similar to earlier apps like Yik Yak and Secret, its long-term viability remains uncertain.
Chronological list of telegram references from Washington, Helsinki, Kuibyshev, Ankara, London, and Stockholm, January–September 1942.

The PGA848 is a monolithic high‑voltage, high‑bandwidth precision programmable‑gain instrumentation amplifier with a single‑ended output. It provides eight binary gain settings (0.5 V/V to 100 V/V) selected via three digital pins (A0‑A2) and is designed for factory automation, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test applications.

The input stage operates linearly within 3 V of either supply rail, maintaining common‑mode rejection over a range that depends on input common‑mode voltage, differential voltage, gain, and reference voltage.

A typical application drives a 16‑bit 1 MSPS SAR ADC (ADS8860). The PGA848 input stage uses ±15 V supplies; the output stage is powered from a unipolar 5.3 V supply shared with the ADC. The REF6250 5 V reference is divided to set the PGA848 REF pin at 2.5 V, buffered by an OPA192 in a dual‑feedback configuration (2 kΩ resistor, 2 nF capacitor, 20 Ω isolation) giving 86° phase margin.

Three filters are used: an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback filter with 75 pF across the internal 6.67 kΩ resistors (nominal cutoff 318 kHz), and a charge‑reservoir RC filter at the ADC inputs. High‑grade C0G capacitors are used throughout. The combined –3 dB bandwidth is nominal 318 kHz, with –0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz.

Supply recommendations: nominal ±15 V for input and output stages, output supplies clamped to input‑stage levels, and exceeding 40 V permanently damages the device.

Layout guidelines stress symmetrical input paths, local 0.1 µF bypass capacitors, separation of input traces from noisy traces, and minimization of leakage and parasitic capacitance.

Simulation support includes TINA‑TI and PSpice‑for‑TI tools; additional documentation is listed in related TI application notes and data sheets.

Tungsten (W) oxidation was investigated at 400–1050°C in dry air for fusion reactor applications. Oxidation follows parabolic then linear kinetics with activation energies of 180.4 kJ/mol and 117.5 kJ/mol, respectively. Above 600°C, voids and cracks form, leading to oxide spalling and dust generation. The oxide scale consists of three layers: inner WO2 (~30–50 nm), middle WO2.72 (10–20 µm), and outer WO2.9/WO3. Preferential oxidation occurs at specimen edges, which may exacerbate handling issues. The inner WO2 layer may act as a tritium permeation barrier, potentially explaining the low detritiation efficiency observed in JET tungsten tiles. WO3 sublimation was characterized between 750–1100°C with activation energy of 335.8 kJ/mol.

A detective in eastern Missouri was exposed to fentanyl while administering Narcan and rescue breaths to an overdose victim. He experienced headache, lightheadedness, and tingling hands. Both the detective and victim were taken to the hospital and are recovering. Police are increasingly encountering heroin mixed with fentanyl, which they say poses dangers to first responders.

Joseph Nicholson was convicted of first-degree murder in 2007 for stabbing 16-year-old Joey Tanner to death and attempting to kill his friend Jeremy Rodgers in Barrie. The Ontario Court of Appeal overturned the verdict and ordered resentencing for second-degree murder due to inadequate jury instructions. This reduces the mandatory parole ineligibility period from 25 years to 10-25 years, with the Crown requesting 16 years. The victims expected a fist fight but Nicholson used a flick knife. Nicholson apologized in court while Tanner's parents expressed ongoing pain and frustration.

The author, a psychology major with a studio art minor, details her study abroad in Florence. She describes improving Italian language skills, completing five paintings and multiple drawings on site, participating in cooking and pastry classes, and joining school trips to Siena, Pisa, Lucca. Over spring break she visited seven countries, including highlights such as the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Copenhagen, the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam, the Centre Pompidou-Metz, and a visit to her ancestor’s village Becherbach, Germany. In Switzerland she toured Adelboden and tandem paraglided near Geneva. After returning to Florence she traveled to Split, Croatia for rafting and visited Krka National Park. She reached the milestone of 20 countries by age 20, and faces final exams, apartment inspections, and reflections on leaving.

From 2 July 2018 the Turnbull Government will replace the Child Care Rebate and means‑tested Child Care Benefit with a single, means‑ and activity‑tested childcare subsidy. About 1.2 million families are eligible; up to 489,000 could lose payment unless they update their Centrelink details via myGov and provide an estimated 2018‑19 family income and combined activity hours for both parents. To qualify, each parent must do at least eight hours of work, study, volunteering or job‑search per fortnight. Households earning under $186,958 will no longer face an annual cap; higher earners will see the cap lifted from $7,500 to just over $10,000 per child. Subsidy rates taper with income, from 85 % for families on $66,958 or less to 20 % for those on $341,248–$351,248, and no subsidy above $351,248. Subsidised care hours are linked to combined activity: 8‑16 hrs → 36 hrs, 16‑48 hrs → 72 hrs, >48 hrs → 100 hrs per fortnight. Additional support is provided for vulnerable children, grandparents and families experiencing hardship. Children must be immunised, and families can use an online calculator to estimate entitlements.

Jeffing, also called the run‑walk‑run method, was created in the 1970s by Olympian Jeff Galloway. It alternates short running intervals with planned walking breaks during a workout or race. According to Dr. John Gallucci Jr., this approach lowers injury risk, improves aerobic endurance, reduces fatigue and provides built‑in muscle recovery. Beginners are advised to start with 1–2 minutes of running followed by 1–2 minutes of walking and to increase running intervals gradually while keeping walking breaks for recovery. Proper progression and good running/walking form are needed to avoid overuse injuries such as knee pain or shin splints. Jeffing can benefit long‑distance runners, aid recovery weeks and suit people with busy schedules, though it may be less suitable for athletes whose sport requires continuous high‑intensity effort. Walk breaks are presented as a performance strategy, not a sign of weakness. The article also mentions rucking and home‑gym options as related fitness topics.

Matroid theory provides a unified framework for studying combinatorial, algebraic, and topological properties of discrete structures. Key algebraic invariants include the Orlik–Solomon algebra A(M), which encodes circuit dependencies and is isomorphic to the cohomology of hyperplane arrangement complements when realizable; the holonomy Lie algebra h(M) and its quotient the holonomy Chen Lie algebra, which encode dual relations and metabelian structure; resonance varieties R^q_s(M,k) that decompose via multinets; and Koszul modules W_q(M,k) whose supports coincide with certain resonance varieties. Multinets are combinatorial partitions of a matroid’s ground set with multiplicities and base loci; they connect to Latin squares and finite group realizations via 3-nets in projective planes. Open questions concern the linearity of higher-degree resonance varieties, torsion in holonomy Lie algebras, and differences between realizable and non-realizable matroids.

The last trading day of the month has been a consistently weak day for stocks, producing an average intraday loss of about –0.11 % with a win ratio of 42 % in the S&P 500 (SPY). When $100,000 was invested only on that day from 1993 to mid‑2021, the trade returned –0.06 % on average and resulted in a negative annual CAGR of –0.8 %, compared with a typical daily gain of +0.04 % over the same period. Exiting at the open of the last trading day yields an overnight return close to the overall average (≈ +0.04 %), indicating the poor performance occurs from the open to the close. No end‑of‑month effect is observed; the day’s weakness appears structural, possibly due to profit‑taking.

Sharon Haliwell, wife of a Wigan millionaire, died by suicide in April after an addiction to sleeping pills and abuse by her husband. Coroner Prof Jennifer Leeming found poor communication between North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust teams; two mental health assessments in February indicated suicide risk, but an error prevented a referral. The trust introduced training, flagging and revised procedures. The coroner issued a prevention of death notice, noting ongoing communication concerns. Her husband questioned why she was not deemed high‑risk.

Adrenaline and experience are emphasized as key factors in a Stanley Cup “race to four,” where fatigue is said to be overridden. The team relies on veteran experience (Thornton, Carbonneau, Hatcher, Modano) and highlights strong chemistry from the Sykora‑Elias‑Arnott line. Physical play and defensive shutdowns are identified as strategies to contain opponents like Jason Arnott’s line. Joe Sakic is defended for playing well—generating offensive zone chances and scoring opportunities—even though he has not scored many goals in the early games of the series.

Anna Ryder Richardson, former Changing Rooms presenter, bought Manor House Wildlife Park near Tenby, Pembrokeshire, in 2008 for £1 million. She and her husband Colin MacDougall renovated the zoo, spending an additional £1 million on new enclosures and living for several years in a prefabricated cabin on the site. Their wildlife park was featured in Channel 4’s series Chaos at the Zoo and in a Welsh ITV programme. The couple faced severe financial pressure, constant work and marital conflict, and an incident in 2010 when a falling tree injured a three‑year‑old visitor and his mother, leading to fines exceeding £100 000. Colin took legal responsibility, and Anna says the event damaged their relationship. They have now separated; Anna is buying a dilapidated farmhouse on six acres near Bordeaux, learning French and planning to live there with her daughters. She acknowledges the stresses of the park destroyed her 16‑year marriage, though she and Colin remain friends. Anna is returning to television as co‑presenter of 60 Minute Makeover on Quest Red, seeking to rebuild her career.

Tiffany Gholston, 41, was born with a heart murmur requiring a pacemaker at age 20. She stays healthy through activity, good eating, and daily meditation. An active member of the American Heart Association's Circle of Red, she raises awareness and funds for heart health research, crediting research with saving her life.

Hackers released HBO episodes, including “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers,” and “The Deuce,” but no “Game of Thrones” material. HBO said it won’t comment, confirmed a cyber incident and ransom demands, while Time Warner awaits approval for its $85.4 billion sale to AT&T.

The passage is a collection of headlines and short descriptions from The 74, a news outlet focused on education. It includes items about an all‑girls camp in west Texas planning to reopen after deadly floods, student achievements (e.g., Jamal Roberts, Hezly Rivera), a lawsuit by the New York attorney general targeting vape distributors, school integration experiments, education funding concerns, veteran diploma programs, COVID‑19 vaccine endorsements, and various school‑reform stories. The passage also contains a request for tax‑exempt donations to The 74.

The article describes three no‑annual‑fee credit cards: Wells Fargo Active Cash (unlimited 2% cash rewards, $200 bonus after $500 spend, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, up to $600 cell‑phone protection with a $25 deductible, requires Good/Excellent credit 670‑850), Capital One Quicksilver (unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on travel booked through Capital One Travel, $300 welcome bonus, 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers, requires Good/Excellent credit), and a Citi card (2% cash back, 5% on travel booked via Citi, $200 cash back after $1,500 spend, 0% intro balance‑transfer APR for 18 months). The site discloses that it receives compensation from partner companies, its ratings favor versatile low‑cost offers, and editorial content is independent of advertisers. Advertising partners include Citi, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo; The Motley Fool holds positions in JPMorgan Chase, Target, Uber Technologies and Visa and recommends Capital One Financial.

Einstein College of Medicine researchers discovered that intense exercise suppresses appetite through temperature-sensitive TRPV1-like receptors in hypothalamic arcuate nucleus POMC neurons. About two-thirds of these neurons possess such receptors, which fire in response to heat or capsaicin. Experiments showed that infusing capsaicin into the arcuate nucleus reduced food intake, and 40 minutes of treadmill exercise decreased intake by 50 percent in normal mice but not in mice lacking these receptors. The findings indicate body temperature can regulate feeding behavior like hormones and nutrients, potentially leading to new appetite-suppression approaches.

The Supreme Court of Texas denied a writ of error application in Black v. Texas Department of Labor and Standards. The case involved enforcement of a surety's obligations under the Health Spa Act. Black claimed the trial court erred by allowing documentary evidence not timely identified in response to interrogatories. The court of appeals had found no abuse of discretion and distinguished a prior case as applicable only to witness identification, not documents. The Supreme Court clarified it was not approving this distinction or relieving parties of the duty to show good cause in the record.

Researchers from the Harvard‑Smithsonian Centre for Astrophysics and Tel Aviv University propose using a worldwide network of mobile phones and low‑cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs). Their paper, accepted by the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, describes how phones would continuously listen for FRB signals, upload data to a central site and use GPS‑based arrival‑time differences to triangulate a burst’s position to arc‑second accuracy. The team estimates a Milky Way FRB may occur roughly once every 30–1,500 years, though a repeating source could appear weekly. Citizen scientists could assist in identifying these brief, mysterious bursts.

McLaren says reliability problems that hampered testing – wheel‑nut failure, battery faults, a loose exhaust and overheating – have been resolved at Woking. Heading into the Australian Grand Prix confident of a step forward, racing director Eric Boullier reported all issues fixed, and Fernando Alonso noted the Renault‑powered MCL33 showed promise but still needs work. Boullier said the midfield is tight, they are not expecting miracles and will give this weekend.

The passage describes systems and methods for adapting radiotherapy treatment plans based on real-time biological and physiological data extracted from imaging acquired during treatment sessions. Biological activity data includes tracer uptake values (SUV), PET tracer kinetics, tissue metabolism, oxygenation levels, genetic expression, and blood flow. Treatment plans may be updated based on changes in dosimetric objectives, target geometry, or fractionation patterns. Systems include imaging modalities (PET, MRI, CT) integrated with radiation treatment systems controlled by processors that evaluate treatment plan quality using metrics like dose-volume histograms (DVH) and plan quality indices (PQI). Notifications indicate whether treatment plans meet pre-approved criteria. Methods include online, real-time, and offline adaptive radiotherapy approaches using various PET tracers to measure biological functions such as metabolism, hypoxia, DNA synthesis, and HER2 expression.

After winning his first Stanley Cup, the player thanked his teammates—especially Igor and Larry Murphy—coach Scotty, and his family, including his six‑year‑old daughter Dasha. He described his eight‑year wait, the difficulty of moving from his domestic league to the NHL, and his motivation to keep playing. He suggested bringing the Cup to Moscow to generate interest and investors for Russian hockey.

The passage describes a compilation linking the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals to United Nations Charter, emphasizing United States' role in shaping the UN's legal framework. It follows U.S. policy from early 1945 to Charter signing on 26 June, covering four phases: policy development, negotiation, debates, and drafting. The work uses minutes of U.S. Delegation (79 meetings), Big Four (12) and Big Five (29), and various documents from Department of State files, Library of Congress manuscripts, and other sources.

On March 22, 2016, NVIDIA entered into an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC, paying $500 million for 12,108,715 shares of its common stock; settlement may involve additional share deliveries or cash adjustments based on the stock’s volume‑weighted average price.

Coach discussed third-period philosophy of keeping players fresh by shortening shifts. Lineup decisions involve evaluating players like Sydor for physical impact and considering Hogue, who is progressing. Brett Hull remains doubtful due to injury, with team protecting details. Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips for AMD in its foundry business, which would be a significant win for Intel Foundry as it seeks big customers. On May 18, 2001, multiple news reports covered developments in the energy sector. A Dow Jones article reported that California faces potential loss of over 40% of power from long-term contracts after Republicans failed to support a $12.5 billion bond deal. Forward power prices in the western U.S. have been declining since Governor Gray Davis announced $43 billion in energy purchases on March 5. The contracts have declined in value by approximately 15%, representing a $6.5 billion loss. Meanwhile, options market volatility fell to its lowest level in months as investors sold options to generate income, with the VIX falling to 25.00 and Nasdaq volatility indexes reaching their lowest levels since October 2000.

In separate reports, Saudi Arabia announced selections of international oil companies for three major natural gas projects requiring approximately $25 billion in investment. Exxon Mobil, Royal Dutch/Shell, BP, and Phillips were awarded the South Ghawar project (Core Venture 1, estimated at $15 billion). Exxon Mobil was selected to lead the Red Sea project (Core Venture 2), with Occidental and Enron receiving stakes. Shell, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco were chosen for the Shaybah project (Core Venture 3). This marks the first extensive reopening of Saudi Arabia's energy sector to foreign investment since nationalization in the 1970s. Leaders for Core Ventures 1 and 3 will be announced by June 5, 2001. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the decision, stating it aligns with the Bush administration's energy plan. Chevron, ENI, and Marathon were not selected to participate.

Enron’s Steven Kean told James Hughes that the company’s involvement in Export‑Import Bank (Ex‑Im) lobbying is limited to its own project‑finance needs, having cut headcount and budget for its Washington office and moved John Hardy into Linda Robertson’s organization while continuing negotiations with Ex‑Im and OPIC on the Electrobolt project and on problem projects. Multiple news reports (WSJ, Reuters, Dow Jones) described major U.S. exporters—Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, Halliburton and others—launching an aggressive lobbying campaign to block a proposed 25% cut to Ex‑Im’s $865 million operating budget, labeling the bank “corporate welfare.” The Coalition for Employment Through Exports is leading the effort and plans to mobilize about 100,000 small suppliers; lobbyists are circulating a 1997 speech by Vice‑President Dick Cheney praising the bank. Stack Offense places two stacks near the free‑throw line, using three ballhandlers and two posts as screeners. On a wing penetration, the teammate pops off the post’s screen; if the driver cannot beat the defender, the ball goes to the pop‑out and the passer moves below the post. Players roll when overplayed or when a defender shows and recovers; they back‑cut when the passing lane is denied. If the defender does not protect the basket, the ballhandler can drive, turn the corner, or deliver a drop pass to a rolling post. Patience avoids fouls. After option, O2 and O4 reset the stack at the free‑throw line.

This study evaluated electronically prescribed nameless Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) accessibility in 335 NYC pharmacies using a secret shopper methodology. Only 40% of pharmacists were aware of EPT, and willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions was 30%. Pharmacists aware of EPT were more likely to dispense nameless prescriptions (48% vs. 18%), but only 46% adhered to NY State guidelines. National chain pharmacies showed higher EPT awareness (adjusted OR 2.58) compared to independent pharmacies. Contrary to the hypothesis, higher neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater EPT awareness (aOR up to 3.74) but not with willingness to dispense. Chlamydia incidence rates were not significantly associated with pharmacist awareness or willingness. The study concludes that significant barriers to EPT implementation exist, including limited pharmacist awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor guideline adherence, necessitating targeted educational initiatives and policy interventions to improve EPT access.

First Lady Melania Trump has made combating bullying a priority at the UN and is now acting. The ML Model Swapping (MLMS) system optimizes AI/ML models for hardware platforms by selecting and deploying models in an energy and communication efficient manner while adapting to real-time system constraints. The system uses a similarity-based subnet selection process that minimizes memory write overhead by selecting replacement subnets with the most overlap in pre-trained parameters from the current model. It includes an MLMS engine with a subnet selector and a performance auditor that monitors hardware platform conditions including power modes, system state, physical environment, and network environment. The system operates on supernets containing multiple subnets optimized for different operational conditions. A two-stage algorithm first identifies candidate replacement subnets meeting performance and constraint criteria, then selects the optimal replacement based on minimal data transfer cost. This enables ML applications to maintain performance across varying hardware conditions while reducing resource consumption.

Globalization integrates world citizens into a single social order requiring cross-cultural collaboration. English education serves as a key tool for international communication, with global issues such as health crises, environmental problems, and conflicts used as teaching materials. Curricula incorporating international topics prepare university students for global engagement.

Skinimalism is a streamlined skincare trend that encourages using only a few high‑quality, multitasking products that respect the skin’s natural barrier instead of layering many active ingredients. Dr Hazel Parkinson, a GP and founder of Dr Hazel Skin Solutions, explains that the approach focuses on targeted products such as serums containing niacinamide, hyaluronic acid or peptides, and emphasizes barrier repair over instant results. Benefits include reduced irritation and sensitivity, a more sustainable routine with less waste and lower cost, and relief from the overwhelm caused by endless product choices. While most people can adopt a skinimalist routine, those with specific concerns (acne, pigmentation, rosacea, menopausal skin) may still require targeted actives but can integrate them simply, using gentle cleansers, barrier‑supportive moisturisers and a single active. Transition advice is to eliminate products gradually, allowing 2–4 weeks for the skin to adapt and monitoring its response. The passage also briefly covers nutrient‑rich foods for healthy skin and mentions coconut oil for hair, a peer‑reviewed information disclaimer, a symptom checker and community discussions.

The study examined how anti‑seizure medication changes and seizures affect smartphone touchscreen interactions in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy. Over 185 days (May–November 2021) he used the TapCounter app, recording 718 357 touchscreen timestamps; his medication (lamotrigine and perampanel) was tapered before a five‑day video‑EEG admission and then restarted. Joint‑interval distributions of inter‑touch intervals were computed daily, transformed into a two‑dimensional space, and analysed with kernel density estimation and cluster‑based permutation testing (1000 permutations). Significant differences were found between pre‑tapering, tapering, and post‑tapering periods: tapering increased the probability of fast next‑interval dynamics, which reversed after medication restart. A focal to bilateral tonic‑clonic convulsion on day 4 of admission produced an increased probability of slow next‑interval dynamics compared with the three preceding days. The findings indicate that smartphone touchscreen patterns can reflect medication‑related and post‑ictal behavioural changes, suggesting potential for unobtrusive monitoring of neurobehavioural comorbidities in epilepsy. Limitations include the single‑case design and the need for larger cohort studies to confirm generalisability.

Market Basket, operating as DeMoulas Super Markets, began in 1917 when Greek immigrant Athanasios “Arthur” Demoulas opened a small store in Lowell, Massachusetts. The business grew through the Demoulas family; a 1954 purchase by brothers George and Mike Demoulas created the company that expanded to 14 stores by 1971. After George’s death, a family dispute erupted in the 1990s over ownership, culminating in a 1996 court ruling that gave Arthur S. Demoulas’s side a 50.5% stake and a $206 million judgment against Mike’s side. Mike’s son, Arthur T., became president in 2008 and CEO in 2008, emphasizing low prices, high wages, profit‑sharing and internal promotion.

By 2014 Market Basket operated 71 stores in Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Maine, employed 25,000 non‑union workers, generated $4.6 billion in revenue and owned 15 million square feet of real estate. The company’s model relied on high sales volume, low prices (10–22% cheaper than regional rivals) and generous employee benefits: starting wages of $12/hr for full‑time cashiers, a profit‑sharing plan that held over $612 million by end‑2014, bonuses based on tenure and a policy of promoting from within. Employee turnover was low (5% for full‑time store staff) and most managers started as part‑timers.

Corporate governance was dominated by the Demoulas family; only nine shareholders, all relatives, appointed a seven‑person board. A voting alliance gave Arthur T. effective control until 2013, when a shareholder switched sides, shifting board power to Arthur S.’s faction. In June 2014 the board fired Arthur T., along with two senior vice presidents, and appointed Felicia Thornton and James Gooch as interim co‑CEOs, citing a desire to “maximize the company’s potential.” The decision prompted immediate backlash: headquarters staff, warehouse workers and truck drivers (roughly 200, 300 and 65 respectively) walked out on July 18, 2014, and the protest lasted six weeks. Employees, customers and suppliers organized online campaigns, boycotted stores and raised funds for affected workers; sales fell more than 90% and part‑time staff were laid off.

The board fired eight managers with a combined 280 years of experience and later lost 18 senior executives who resigned. New co‑CEOs issued ultimatums, held a sparsely attended job fair and attempted to hire replacement workers, but employees refused to return unless Arthur T. was reinstated with full decision‑making authority. Governors and a congressman expressed concern, and the United Food and Commercial Workers union supported the non‑union workers.

On August 27, 2014 the board and shareholders agreed to sell Arthur S.’s 50.5% stake to Arthur T. and his family for $1.6 billion. Arthur T. was reinstated with his management team; the company financed the purchase with a $1 billion mortgage backed by its real estate and $600 million syndicated loans. Employees received a $49 million bonus in 2014, up from $44 million the prior year, and vendors and customers returned quickly, producing a short‑term sales bump.

The acquisition left Market Basket with substantial debt, raising questions about its ability to maintain low prices, high wages and the profit‑sharing plan. Employees expressed willingness to cut costs to sustain the business model, and the company continued operations under Arthur T.’s leadership. The episode illustrates how a combination of employee loyalty, customer solidarity and supplier relationships can influence corporate governance outcomes in a family‑controlled firm.

Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved rapid efficiency gains, making precise characterization of perovskite thin‑film morphology essential for performance and stability. Microscopic grain size, boundaries, and defects critically influence charge transport and recombination, yet manual interpretation of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images is labor‑intensive and subjective. Traditional machine‑learning segmentation methods struggle with blurry boundaries and low‑contrast regions, while existing deep‑learning approaches often lack scalability, demand extensive manual parameter tuning, or incur high computational cost, especially when applied to high‑resolution SEM data.

To address these limitations, we present PerovSegNet, a lightweight and high‑precision segmentation framework built on YOLOv8‑seg and tailored for SEM images of perovskite and lead‑iodide films. PerovSegNet introduces two custom modules: the Adaptive Split‑Dilated Convolution with Shuffle Block (ASDCB), which enhances multi‑scale feature extraction and boundary localization through multi‑branch dilated convolutions and channel‑attention recalibration; and the Separable Adaptive Downsampling (SAD) module, which captures fine‑scale textures and large‑scale structures via depthwise separable convolutions and adaptive pooling, reducing aliasing and preserving critical microstructural details.

A curated dataset (PerovData) of 10 994 augmented SEM images, derived from 40 manually labeled samples, was constructed and validated with UMAP to ensure class separability. Training was performed on an NVIDIA A100 GPU with standard hyper‑parameters (AdamW optimizer, 300 epochs, batch size 4, input size 640 × 640). PerovSegNet achieved an mAP@0.5 of 87.3 % and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 80.0 %, surpassing baseline models (Mask R‑CNN variants, Cascade InternImage‑XL) while using only 79 M parameters and 265 GFLOPs. Ablation studies confirmed that both ASDCB and SAD contribute independently, and their combination yields the highest accuracy and lowest computational load.

Qualitative comparisons show that PerovSegNet delineates sharper grain boundaries, reduces mask leakage in lead‑iodide regions, and improves detection of small defect areas. The framework also generates quantitative descriptors—perovskite area, lead‑iodide area, defect area and count, and shape metrics—which correlate with photovoltaic efficiency (PCE). Correlation analysis indicates strong positive association between perovskite area and PCE (r = 0.78), mild positive effect of lead‑iodide (r = 0.23), and negative impact of defect metrics (r ≈ −0.27 to −0.32). These descriptors enable data‑driven feedback for process optimization and high‑throughput screening, though limitations include observational correlations and class imbalance. PerovSegNet’s lightweight design and robust quantification capabilities offer a pathway toward real‑time quality control in perovskite manufacturing.

A University of Connecticut study found that nicotine‑based e‑cigarette vapor caused DNA damage comparable to unfiltered cigarette smoke, using a low‑cost 3D‑printed “lung‑on‑a‑chip” with human metabolic enzymes. DNA damage increased with the number of puffs. The results, published in ACS Sensors, surprised researchers, who plan further 3D‑printed platforms for toxicity screening and cancer diagnostics.

The article explains how to backtest a momentum trading strategy in Python using sector SPDR ETFs. It begins by downloading historical adjusted‑close prices with the yfinance library and resampling the data to monthly closes, then computing monthly percentage changes. Momentum is defined as the rolling 9‑month performance of each ETF, calculated with a custom function. Trading rules select the three ETFs with the highest 9‑month momentum each month and form an equally‑weighted portfolio. Portfolio returns are computed for every month from 2005 onward using a loop that calls the selection and return functions. The resulting performance is plotted against the SPY ETF for comparison. The backtest shows the strategy compounded at roughly 9.89 % per year, only marginally better than the SPY’s 9.46 % CAGR, indicating limited alpha with the chosen rules. The process includes steps for data retrieval, momentum calculation, rule implementation, and result visualization, and the article notes the strategy can be customized by changing the list of ETFs or other parameters.

The Evening Star is a bearish reversal pattern formed by three candles: a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above it, and a third bearish candle closing below the midpoint of the first. Traders confirm the pattern with tools such as trendlines, resistance levels and momentum oscillators before entering short positions, using profit targets, stop‑loss orders or indicator signals as exits. The pattern is considered more reliable when the gap is significant and the third candle is longer than the first, especially when it appears near trendlines or resistance. Backtesting resources with predefined rules and code for platforms like Amibroker, Tradestation and Python are available. Benefits include clear entry rules and high reliability, while drawbacks involve subjectivity and false signals. Risks include market volatility, over‑reliance on technical analysis, lack of diversification and potential losses. Traders often use RSI, stochastic, Bollinger Bands or other indicators and may adjust position sizing or stop‑loss placement according to market conditions and their preferred timeframe.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after allegedly shooting her 72‑year‑old son at their Fountain Hills home, motivated by a dispute over being placed in an assisted‑living facility. US education has historically adopted business models, using standardized testing and accountability (e.g., NCLB) to address perceived teacher and school failures; teacher professionalism initiatives and charter schools showed mixed results and increased segregation, with minimal gains in student test scores. The medical model of learning, rooted in biological determinism and diagnostic labeling, risks fostering fixed mindsets, stigma, and stereotype threat in students. The passage argues for reframing education around a universal problem-solving process modeled on the scientific method—involving theory creation, testing, explanation, and error correction—which mirrors natural cognitive development and supports metacognition, self-directed learning, and collaborative support at all institutional levels, rather than top-down bureaucracy or market-driven approaches.

The passage criticizes Ambassador Hartman's argument for trading INF deployment for arms control, arguing that deployment has become essential to NATO's credibility. The author contends non-deployment would embolden anti-American forces and that Hartman's reading of European mood is incorrect, citing support from Mitterrand and Italy, and likely compliance from Britain and Germany. The author recommends holding firm on the zero-zero option, deploying INF if Soviets don't change position, but remaining open to asymmetrical reductions if Soviets seriously restructure their position. The passage also documents a meeting between the Secretary and Dobrynin, where they agreed to regular consultations, a possible Foreign Ministers' meeting, and a U.S.-Soviet summit with concrete results, with Dobrynin emphasizing the need for a direct Shultz-Gromyko channel for arms control negotiations.

The passage establishes legal principles for damages in vessel collisions and detentions, stating that owners of injured vessels are entitled to compensation for loss of use during repairs, including loss of catch for whaling vessels. When market price exists, it determines recovery; otherwise, evidence of potential profits is used. The rule allows gross freight deductions for ship expenses but may fall short for lengthy repairs. Multiple cases including the Potomac, Williamson v. Barrett, and Gazelle support this principle, and it was applied to whaling ships captured by the Shenandoah.

Semiconductor crystals of Cd1‑xZnxTe1‑ySey (CZTS) are new promising materials for X‑ray and gamma‑ray radiation detectors. Cutting and polishing of these crystals creates a damaged surface layer up to ~100 µm thick, which must be removed for detector performance. Chemical polishing with a 5 % bromine‑methanol solution was used to study the effect of selenium on etching behavior. Samples with constant zinc content x≈0.1 and selenium fractions y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, 0.10 were prepared (typical size 8 × 8 × 5 mm³). Etching trajectories and average rates were measured at 19 ± 0.5 °C without stirring. The average etching rates decreased with increasing selenium: 24 µm min⁻¹ for CZT (y = 0), 18 µm min⁻¹ for CZTS2, 15 µm min⁻¹ for CZTS6 and 13 µm min⁻¹ for CZTS10. At y≈0.02 the rate dropped by ~20 %, in good agreement with a thermodynamic model that predicts V_CZTS = V_CZT (1 − 2ΔG_ex / RT); the calculated ΔG_ex ≈ 260 J mol⁻¹ gives ~22 % reduction, matching the experiment. The decrease is attributed to hardening of the crystal lattice caused by selenium addition, which strengthens covalent bonds and reduces excess Gibbs energy. The effect shows a threshold character: a small increase in selenium produces a large change in etching rate, while at higher selenium concentrations the difference between rates diminishes. Surface morphology improves after short etching (<30 s) but roughness rises after 3–5 min. Stirring was found to raise the rate by 1.5–2× and was therefore avoided. These results establish a linear thermodynamic relationship between etching rate and selenium content and provide guidelines for optimal chemical polishing of CZTS detector elements.

The Reserve Bank may investigate AFIC, claiming 25,000 and 30,000 depositors but no deposits in banks. Ambae volcano is level 3 with explosions and lava flow. The second edition of "The New Zealand Land and Food Annual" was launched at the National Field Days, edited by Professor Claire Massey with contributions from 31 experts. The book addresses sustainable food production and New Zealand's potential to lead the global green revolution. The land and food sector contributes $33 billion to the economy, with a goal to triple this value by 2025 through nutrition-driven agriculture operating within planetary boundaries. Recent OECD and Ministry for the Environment reports highlight urgency for change, as current farming and food-processing practices are deemed unsustainable.

Small‑body reservoirs in planetary systems provide the source populations for exocomets. In the Solar System these reservoirs are dynamically distinct: interior asteroids (Ayló’chaxnim, near‑Earth families, the main belt), the Jupiter Trojans and Hildas, the massive Neptune Trojan swarm, the trans‑Neptunian populations (cold classical Kuiper belt, hot classical, scattered disc, detached and extreme objects), the Centaur/Jupiter‑family comet zone, and the Oort cloud (inner ∼2 000–10⁴ au, outer >10⁴ au). Trans‑Neptunian objects are dominated by icy compositions (H₂O, CO₂, CO, CH₄, organics) while inner‑belt bodies are largely silicate‑rich. All these reservoirs originate from a planetesimal disc that survived planet formation.

Stars form in dense molecular clouds; rotation leads to protostellar discs that evolve through class 0/I/II/III stages. The cluster environment can truncate or destroy discs via external photo‑evaporation (dominant in massive, long‑lived clusters) or stellar flybys (dominant in low‑mass clusters). Protoplanetary discs have dust‑to‑gas ratios higher than the interstellar value; dust grows by sticking collisions, but bouncing and fragmentation create a barrier. The streaming instability (SI) allows pebbles to concentrate to Hill density, enabling gravitational collapse and the formation of ~100 km‑scale planetesimals (“born big”). SI requires super‑Solar metallicity and low turbulence; the resulting initial mass distribution follows shallow power laws.

The composition of planetesimals is controlled by snowlines (water ≈1–2 au, CO ≈20–30 au for Solar‑type stars) and by stellar luminosity; more luminous stars push snowlines outward. Disc chemistry evolves through freeze‑out, photodesorption and turbulent mixing, producing C/O > 1 anomalies.

Transition from protoplanetary to debris discs occurs when gas disperses; disc lifetimes scale with stellar mass (A‑type ~1–4 Myr, M/K ~5–10 Myr). Debris discs are analogues of the Kuiper belt, detected around ~20 % of nearby AFGK stars; dust masses are 10⁻³–1 M⊕, implying total masses of 0.3–300 M⊕. Collisional grinding depletes dust with age, so younger systems host more potential exocomets.

Observational constraints come from orbital distributions, color bimodality (linked to formation distance), JWST near‑IR spectra revealing compositional groups, D/H ratios (e.g., comet 67P), and in‑situ samples (Hayabusa2, Rosetta). The Oort cloud likely formed from ejected planetesimals (≈1–3 % of escapers) isotropized by Galactic tides; its population may include captured objects from the Sun’s birth cluster, and close stellar encounters can both reduce and enhance cometary influx.

Future facilities (JWST, ALMA, Rubin LSST, Roman, SPHEREx, ELT, GMT) will address open questions on the influence of the natal environment, binary stars, planetesimal formation pathways, the dominant exocomet source, debris‑disc masses, and Oort‑cloud structure.

Statistical analysis plan outlines summary statistics for plasma concentration and PK metrics by treatment group and nominal time using original and log‑scale concentrations, with overlay plots (placebo samples not analyzed for dasiglucagon/GlucaGen). Plasma glucose will be measured at pre‑dose and at 4–45 min (with ±30 s tolerance until 20 min), and the pharmacodynamic endpoint is the area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 min (AUE₀–₋₃₀ₘᵢₙ). Individual and summary glucose concentrations and change from baseline will be presented. PK/PD tables and figures will display mean and individual concentration‑time curves.

Safety analyses are based on the safety set and include: exposure (insulin administration before hypoglycemia induction, hypoglycemia induction procedure, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion, time to first IV glucose infusion), local tolerability assessments at injection sites, and adverse events. Treatment‑emergent AEs are defined as events occurring after dosing or worsening pre‑existing events; causal relationship is graded 0‑3 (related includes possible and probable), severity 1‑3 (missing severity not imputed). AEs are summarized by treatment group, MedDRA system organ class and preferred term, and special search categories (QT prolongation, hepatic disorders). Laboratory evaluations (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy test) and vital signs are summarized with descriptive statistics and categorical thresholds. ECG parameters are tabulated with QTcF categorical changes from baseline. Immunogenicity (ADA occurrence) is described descriptively.

Tables, figures and data listings are specified with formatting rules (decimal places, significant digits, footnotes). QC requirements for SAS programming include log review, output verification, dataset validation with Pinnacle 21, and documentation. Protocol changes clarify primary efficacy analysis wording and secondary efficacy terminology.

Department of State circulars address three topics: (1) passport issuance, stating that applicants need not declare an intent to return within two years, but a passport is valid for two years and may be renewed; (2) the role of secretaries as chargés d'affaires in the absence of a mission head, with expectations for leave coordination and prior State Department consultation for emergencies; and (3) an executive order prohibiting diplomatic and consular officers from publicly criticizing or charging other officers except confidentially to the Department.

Sixteen seniors from Miami Valley graduated May 20 from a seminary at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Huber Heights. 100 attendees received certificates after studying the Book of Mormon. Speakers highlighted growth and applying scripture. The program, taught by volunteers, is open to high school students.

The passage details design guidelines for a push-pull converter using the TPS7H500x-SP controller. Key component selections include: a leading edge blank time of ~50 ns (RLEB = 49.9 kΩ), soft-start capacitor of 33 nF (~7.5 ms), transformer with 2.5 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance, 170 V GaN FETs for primary switching and 80 V GaN FETs for synchronous rectification, output inductor of 0.47 μH, output capacitance of 2.3 mF using seven 330 μF polymer tantalum capacitors, and an optional secondary output filter. Overcurrent protection is set at ~35 A with a 7.5 Ω sense resistor and 1:100 current sense transformer. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A with values of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF. A slope compensation resistor of 102 kΩ and hiccup capacitor of 3.3 nF are specified. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt switching loops, keeping traces short and wide, placing bypass capacitors near the controller, and routing feedback traces away from power magnetics.
