The controller operates from 4 V to 14 V with a minimum 0.1 μF input bypass capacitor recommended.

Amazon.com, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Seattle, Washington, incorporated in 1994 and reincorporated in 1996. The company’s common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “AMZN.” Amazon operates three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019, net sales were $280,522 million, operating income was $14,541 million, and net income was $11,588 million. The company employed approximately 798,000 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2019. Amazon serves consumers through online and physical stores, sellers through marketplace programs, developers and enterprises via AWS, and content creators through various publishing services. The business is affected by seasonality, with higher sales in the fourth quarter. Key acquisitions include Whole Foods Market (2017), Ring (2018), PillPack (2018), and Souq Group (2017). Amazon faces risks including intense competition, challenges in global expansion, foreign exchange fluctuations, regulatory scrutiny, and reliance on third-party suppliers and payment processors.

Anthology Inc. has lost nearly $80 million over two years and carries over $1 billion in debt. To restructure and emerge debt-free, the company is receiving $50 million from investors to focus on its Blackboard learning management system while selling its enterprise operations, life-cycle engagement, and student success businesses to Encoura and Ellucian. The company's downfall stemmed from incorrect assumptions that colleges would purchase its full suite of products and from integration difficulties following rapid acquisitions. Market analysts say this reflects a broader shift in the education-technology market from growth-focused strategies to sustainable, modular platforms.

Yellen told senators Dodd-Frank rollback is unwarranted; banks are well‑capitalized, lending has grown past its 2008 peak, and only a few small businesses cite credit‑access issues. She said banks are profitable, resilient and not less competitive, with high‑quality capital almost doubled. She backs exempting community banks from the Volcker Rule but acknowledges their regulatory burden. She declined to comment directly on Trump’s tax and spending plans, hoping policies boost productivity and keep fiscal accounts sustainable, and said rates may rise sooner than expected.

The DAWN‑plasma trial is a randomized, open‑label, phase 2 multicenter study comparing standard of care (SOC) alone versus SOC plus convalescent plasma in hospitalized adult COVID‑19 patients, based on the WHO master protocol with WHO‑aligned outcomes and 2:1 randomization. Appendices provide protocol, amendments, and investigator details.

Germany's education system evolved from the 19th-century Prussian model through Bismarck's mandatory schooling, was shaped by Nazi ideology, and was restructured post-WWII into a three-tiered secondary system (Hauptschule, Realschule, Gymnasium). Special education emerged in the 1920s with specialized schools for students with disabilities, which were later formalized by the KMK in 1960. Currently, approximately 577,000 students attend seven categories of special schools, while inclusion rates are low (33.6% in elementary, 14.9% in secondary schools). Teacher training follows a two-phase model: university study ending in state examination, followed by a 2-year paid Referendariat internship. Germany passed the General Equal Treatment Act in 2006 and ratified the UN CRPD in 2008. Key challenges include limited inclusion, funding constraints for general education settings, teacher attitudes toward inclusion, and limited job opportunities for students with disabilities in the Hauptschule track, the lowest secondary option.

Staff at the Department of Education will be affected by mass layoffs, with Russell Vought of the Office of Management and Budget initiating the reduction in force. A department spokesperson confirmed employees will be impacted but did not specify numbers or affected offices. The Office of Federal Student Aid will not be affected. A previous round of layoffs in March affected most employees outside federal student aid, which was challenged in court but allowed by the Supreme Court in July. The latest cuts are directed by OMB and surprised department leadership. Union president Rachel Gittleman vowed to fight the layoffs, calling them an attempt to illegally dismantle the department. Democrats, including Sen. Patty Murray, argued that firing federal workers during a shutdown is unconstitutional. HHS also announced layoffs across multiple divisions.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki met in Warsaw on March 19, 2018 to discuss EU future, security and bilateral ties. Merkel said she hoped EU‑Poland talks would resolve the dispute over Poland’s judicial reforms, which triggered a censure procedure that could lead to sanctions. Morawiecki described “light in the tunnel” but stressed the need for understanding on both sides. Both leaders emphasized Europe’s need for unity, economic cooperation and more support for countries receiving many migrants. They also addressed the Skripal poisoning in Britain, with Merkel expecting strong EU conclusions and evidence pointing to Russian responsibility; Russia has rejected the allegations.

The passage describes a continuation patent application regarding metal gates of transistors with reduced resistivity. It explains that traditional polysilicon gates suffer from poly depletion effects, and metal gates are used to address this. However, tungsten nucleation layers used in metal gates have high resistivity, degrading transistor performance as devices scale down. The disclosed embodiments provide methods for forming FinFETs using cobalt-containing or metal silicide layers instead of tungsten. The process includes forming protruding fins, dummy gates, source/drain epitaxial regions, an inter-layer dielectric, replacement gate dielectrics (including high‑k dielectrics), work‑function metal layers, titanium nitride barrier layers, and cobalt or metal silicide conductive layers. The cobalt/metal silicide layers provide low resistivity (about 5.8 μΩ·cm), good adhesion to titanium nitride, resistance to acid corrosion, and lower roughness compared to tungsten. Contact plugs (source/drain and gate) are formed with similar cobalt or metal silicide layers over barrier layers, and the devices exhibit improved electrical characteristics. The summary covers the technical problem, the solution, key process steps, and material advantages as described in the passage.

OpenAI's new Sora app allows users to generate personalized AI deepfake videos of themselves and others. The app, powered by Sora 2, features a TikTok-like feed of AI-generated clips with sound. Users create digital avatars by recording themselves saying numbers and turning their heads, and can control who uses their likeness. Safety guardrails block sexual content, graphic violence, self-harm, and some copyrighted characters like Darth Vader, but marijuana use is allowed. OpenAI acknowledges addiction risks and potential for bullying. The app raises concerns about deepfake misuse despite built-in protections.

The Spinlock module provides 128 hardware spinlocks that allow a device resource to be locked with a single read access, avoiding read‑modify‑write bus transfers. The Mailbox module enables communication between the ARM Cortex‑A8, the C674x DSP and the Media Controller, supporting four‑message FIFO queues and four interrupts (one to each processor). The device integrates on‑chip memories for its two processors and uses a unified memory map across bus masters. L3 memory tables map system masters (including Cortex‑A8) to address ranges, while the C674x DSP has limited access to peripherals such as McASPx, McBSP, UARTx, I2Cx, SPIx, EDMA, GPIO/INT, GPMC, DDRx, EMAC, PCIe, Timers and USB. The address range 0x1000_0000‑0x10FF_FFFF translates to C674x internal addresses 0x0000_0000‑0x00FF_FFFF. L4 Fast and Slow peripheral regions are shown in separate tables; regions decoded internally by the Cortex‑A8 subsystem are not physically part of L4 Slow. The DDR DMM TILER provides an extra 4‑GB addressing window via a 33rd address bit, accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS; other masters can access a single 512‑MB view. Device pin tables list terminal functions, multiplexing via PINCNTL registers, internal pullup/pulldown states and supply voltages. Boot configuration is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset, latching values into the CONTROL_STATUS register; BTMODE[15:11] set GPMC CS0 defaults and BTMODE[4:0] select the primary boot mode with fallback order. Pin multiplexing is controlled by MUXMODE bits, defaulting to tri‑state. Unused input pins should be pulled and all supply pins must be connected to the correct voltage.

A study in the Journal of Consumer Psychology found that parents favor children of the same gender. Four experiments in the US and India asked parents to allocate money or raffle tickets to only one child; mothers preferred daughters and fathers preferred sons. The bias was consistent across cultures and linked to parents identifying more with same‑sex children. Over 90% of participants claimed they had no preference in interviews.

The passage describes an off‑highway recreational side‑by‑side vehicle having a frame and a rear suspension in which the left A‑arm’s pivot axis is located on the right‑hand side of the vehicle’s longitudinal centerline. The vehicle includes front and rear suspension systems with upper and lower A‑arms, anti‑roll bars, and coil‑over shock damping members; a steering system with a rack, tie rods and electric power steering; and a driveline comprising an engine, a continuously variable transmission (CVT) with inner, intermediate and outer covers, gaskets, a flywheel, a CVT air box and vibration isolators. The vehicle has a ROPS (roll‑over protection structure) with connection members and accessory attachment points, a cargo box located rearward of a side‑by‑side seating area, adjustable seats with removable bases and seat backs, a floorboard with drainage gutters and traction‑enhancing features, and a brake pedal assembly with an adjustable pedal ratio (about 5.8:1) and dual reservoirs. Additional details cover structural frame members, suspension support brackets, tie‑rod connections, front drive assembly mounting, lighting and signal components, a fuel tank positioned on the left side with a recessed filler neck, door hinges attached to the frame, and various body panels and fasteners. The vehicle may be configured as 2‑wheel or 4‑wheel drive with selectable differentials.

Top universities like MIT, Columbia, UMich, and Rochester Institute of Technology are piloting MicroMasters programs to make master's degrees more affordable. MicroMasters are online certifications costing around $1,350 versus full tuition of about $67,938. They offer rigorous coursework, new skills, and improved job prospects; companies like GE, Walmart, IBM, and Volvo recognize them. To earn a full degree, students must complete a semester on campus at full cost in a blended program. Admissions are competitive, with MIT admitting 40 students annually, and performance in online courses is weighed in decisions, helping institutions verify applicant quality.

The speaker stresses that winning tomorrow’s game is the priority, noting the team’s urgency and Ray’s comment that it will be exciting. He recalls his early NHL days, when he knew little English, and describes the fans’ strong support for the Avalanche in Colorado, especially after the Olympics. He credits Ray’s trade with bringing leadership, raising expectations, and modeling hard‑work and unselfish play, while also noting Rogie Vachon’s quick reflexes in goal.

The coach said goaltending was not the cause of the loss in the last game and that Kris Letang will not return for the remainder of the series. He explained that the decision to insert Archie into the lineup was to add energy, speed, and enthusiasm. The coach expressed confidence in the team's leadership and ability to respond, noting that the game was possibly their best overall performance in the series despite the scoreboard result. Carter Rowney was praised for his strong play at center, including faceoffs, size, physicality, and penalty killing. Regarding player combinations, the staff found limited chemistry when certain players were paired together, so they separated them to create better balance; Phil and Geno have shown chemistry and are used as a pair. The coach highlighted the importance of goaltending, noting that Pekka Rinne played exceptionally well in the last game. The coaching staff is actively adjusting lines to achieve a balanced attack and improve secondary scoring. They acknowledged a few preventable goals but emphasized that the game was closer than the final score indicated, with several high-quality chances not converted. The coach believes the team will continue to focus on controllable factors and expects players to score going forward.

NVIDIA's RTX Blackwell architecture builds on prior AI technologies to boost AI‑powered gaming and professional applications. It introduces AI‑based Neural Rendering and Neural Shading, leverages DLSS Super Resolution, Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction to increase frame rates and image quality at lower cost, and enables generative AI for dynamic terrain, physics simulation and character behaviors. Professional 3D tools gain conversational design workflows. The architecture honors mathematician David H. Blackwell.

The Boston Zone Offense, developed and refined by Tom Davis while coaching Boston College, features a single‑position system where players flip sides rather than interchange roles. The basic alignment consists of a point guard (O1), a shooting guard (O2), a baseline runner/cutter (O3), a weakside rebounder/power forward (O4) and a low‑post scorer (O5). The offense initiates with dribble penetration, emphasizes a strong low‑post attack and uses ball reversal, skip passes and controlled passing to keep the defense moving. Key principles include avoiding forced passes, eliminating unnecessary dribbling and converting defensive sags into open shots for spot‑up shooters. The offense provides counters for overplayed passes (skip passes, back cuts, cross‑court “X” passes) and specific reads for 2‑3, 1‑2‑2 and 1‑3‑1 zones, incorporating baseline cuts, post feeds, wing flashes, dribble penetration and overload tactics. This combination of overloading and spreading enables efficient attack of zone defenses.

Hawaiʻi is turning charter schools into tuition‑free preschools to meet its goal of offering preschool to all 3‑ and 4‑year‑olds by 2032. Waikīkī Community Preschool became the first private program to convert to a charter, eliminating tuition and receiving state funding through the State Public Charter School Commission. Charter preschools now operate 33 classrooms, including six at Waikīkī; the state also opened 26 classrooms on DOE campuses this fall and plans about 25 more next year. Roughly 6,700 children lack access, requiring about 330 additional classrooms in seven years. Advocates say charter status gives providers a stable funding stream and higher teacher salaries, helping address a long‑standing early‑educator shortage. However, charter funding is $171,000 per classroom, below many programs’ needs, and Waikīkī projects a $150,000–$200,000 shortfall this year, relying on fundraising. Charters must employ licensed teachers, leading to emergency hires amid a statewide shortage. Two charter preschool applications were submitted this year—Waikīkī’s was approved, Mana ‘Ulu’s was not. The commission plans to add 15 more charter classrooms by fall 2028, and $20 million has been allocated for constructing classrooms on state‑owned land, though many charters on private property do not qualify.

Ed Silverman, a senior writer at STAT, has covered the pharmaceutical industry for nearly three decades. EnGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; he previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head, oncology clinical development.

PIM Capital is a fund structuring and administration specialist that targets emerging‑market clients, offering flexible, client‑focused solutions for alternative investments and cross‑border opportunities. It operates from offices in Sub‑Saharan Africa, Mauritius and Guernsey, emphasizing locally attuned, highly nuanced services that address complexities such as grey‑listing, varied regulatory frameworks and currency volatility. The firm differentiates itself from larger administrators by taking a hands‑on approach, absorbing upfront costs, designing adaptable structures from the start and building long‑term, mutually beneficial partnerships. Its team thinks like fund managers, leveraging on‑the‑ground networks of advisers, lawyers and other professionals to create cost‑effective, jurisdiction‑specific solutions. PIM Capital’s client base has grown from smaller emerging funds to large global asset managers, and it serves both small private‑wealth firms and multi‑billion‑dollar portfolios. Christopher Erasmus (TEP) leads the Mauritius operation, providing expertise in fund and corporate structuring for high‑net‑worth individuals and corporations.  

Pan Finance, a print and online financial‑intelligence platform, provides in‑depth analysis and news to senior decision‑makers worldwide.  

The passage also includes separate headlines such as the EU pushing climate reform for development banks, the World Bank raising China’s 2025 growth forecast to 4.8%, and various corporate announcements (e.g., Fifth Third acquiring Comerica, JPMorgan integrating AI, AMD’s stock surge on an OpenAI chip deal).

Amazon.com, Inc. held its Annual Meeting of Shareholders on May 30 2018. All nine director nominees, including Jeffrey P. Bezos, were elected. Ernst & Young LLP was ratified as the company’s independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31 2018, and shareholders approved the compensation of the named executive officers. Two shareholder proposals—a policy requiring an independent board chair and a proposal regarding vote‑counting practices for shareholder proposals—were not approved.

Day trading can be profitable, but it demands systematic work, preparation, and strict discipline. The author, who has traded stocks since 2002 and earned enough to achieve FIRE, notes that most day traders lose money quickly; high turnover among participants and a long learning curve of two to three years are common. Starting with swing trading before day trading is recommended. The author’s own statistics from 2002 to May 2012 show accumulated profits with strong years in 2006 and 2009, 15‑17 losing days in those years, and the best 1 % of trading days accounting for roughly 11 % of total profit. Algorithmic trading has changed market conditions, reducing bid‑ask spreads and increasing price volatility, so day traders must either compete with algorithms or adopt strategies that are less affected by them, which can cause larger drawdowns and require longer holding periods. Court‑case data from the defunct prop firm Tuco Trading indicate low profitability among most traders. Patience, careful learning, and risk management are identified as key to succeeding in day trading.

Corporate bond auction: 58 bidders placed Rs 5,898 cr bids against Rs 3,360 cr notified, cut‑offs 15.25‑25 bps, up from 8 bps; G‑sec auction: 37 bidders for Rs 7,116 cr vs Rs 5,481 cr. Second such auction this fiscal.

The Turnaround Tuesday effect describes a market tendency for price reversals occurring from Monday's close to Tuesday's close. The passage states that if the market is down on Monday, above-average returns typically follow, while a strong Monday leads to lower subsequent returns. A historical example provided is Black Monday (October 19, 1987), when the market rebounded 5.3% on Tuesday and 9.1% on Wednesday following a dramatic Monday decline.

The article presents backtesting results on SPY from inception through September 2021, incorporating 0.03% commissions and slippage per trade. Findings indicate buying at Monday's close produces substantially higher returns than buying on other days, with Monday close being approximately twice as profitable as Tuesday close.

The strategy involves buying weakness on Mondays, though it appears effective only when Monday shows weakness. The passage notes that buying on strength on Monday is not recommended. Various trading rules and strategy versions are discussed, including approaches using filters like Intraday Breadth Strength (IBS). The author notes that while the Turnaround Tuesday strategy has been profitable for approximately 30 years, current market conditions involving geopolitical risks warrant caution. The article includes an FAQ section explaining the strategy's mechanics, effectiveness on weak Mondays, and variations for implementation.

The King appointed commissioners Allen and Carter to negotiate a reciprocity treaty, signed in Washington on January 30, 1875, ratified by Congress and proclaimed effective September 9, 1876. Disputes with Great Britain and Germany over the 1852 parity clause were resolved after diplomatic exchanges; a proposed 10 % British import duty was rejected, and the Hawaiian legislature’s support for British equal privileges prompted a ministry change and a royal admission of U.S. exclusive treaty rights. An “annexation scare” followed, prompting U.S. instructions to reassure Hawaii. Subsequent interpretation questions and fraud allegations, including British claims under the 1852 treaty, were settled by diplomatic notes. A domestic scandal caused rapid cabinet shifts, but the recall request for foreign representatives was withdrawn. The United States also assisted Hawaii’s Evangelical Association in enforcing liquor‑traffic regulations in the Ralik Islands, secured a consular agent there, helped negotiate a Hawaii‑Japan treaty, and opposed British efforts to claim treaty benefits, noting that a British commissioner in 1855 had relinquished the claim.

Femtosecond noise correlation spectroscopy was used to investigate magnon fluctuations in Sm0.7Er0.3FeO3 across the spin reorientation transition. Thermal fluctuations increase when the free energy potential softens near critical temperatures, while an external magnetic field suppresses fluctuations and increases the quasi-ferromagnetic magnon frequency by stiffening the potential. Atomistic spin model and Monte Carlo simulations confirm these trends, demonstrating that FemNoC can directly map magnetization potential landscapes and enable external tuning of ultrafast spin fluctuations for spintronic applications.

The passage describes a camera module and its molded circuit board assembly and molded photosensitive assembly together with their manufacturing methods. The module comprises a circuit board, a photosensitive element, a lens, and a molded base integrally formed on the circuit board (and optionally on the photosensitive element) by a molding process. The molded base defines a light window that provides a light path between the lens and the photosensitive element. The inner side surface of the molded base is slanted relative to the optical axis and has at least a first inclination angle (an acute angle) that facilitates demoulding and reduces stray light reflections. The outer side surface of the molded base also has a second acute inclination angle that eases removal of dividing blocks of the mould. In some embodiments the inner side surface comprises a first portion, a second portion, and a third portion, each with specified inclination angles (first α, second γ, third β) ranging from 3° to 45°. The light window forming block of the mould has a trapezoidal or multi‑step trapezoidal cross‑section with diameters increasing from bottom to top, and the base forming guide groove surrounds the block. The molding process includes placing a circuit board (or a board with a photosensitive element) in the mould, filling a liquid molding material into the base forming guide groove while preventing material from entering the space of the light‑window‑forming block, solidifying the material, and demoulding the mould so that the block leaves a light window of the required shape. The invention addresses prior‑art problems such as damage to the encapsulation portion caused by sharp‑edged mould blocks, high friction during demoulding, and stray light reflected from vertical inner walls that degrades image quality. By using acute inclination angles and a trapezoidal or stepped window, the molded base can be produced in large‑scale mass production, reduces demoulding friction, and minimizes stray light reaching the photosensitive element. The passage also describes a joint‑board array operation where an integral piece of circuit board array is moulded to form an integral piece of molded base array, which is subsequently cut into individual camera‑module assemblies. Additional features include optional lens‑actuator pin grooves, an elastic film layer on the mould bottom, and a blocking element around the photosensitive element to protect lead wires during moulding. The described camera module can be incorporated in electronic devices such as smartphones, computers, wearable devices, televisions, vehicles, cameras and monitoring devices.

David Hardt's lecture introduces a framework for understanding manufacturing processes as geometric changes, emphasizing the distinction between equipment and material, and between states (transient energy exchanges) and properties (inherent characteristics). He presents a taxonomy categorizing processes by transformation mode (removal, addition, formation, deformation), interaction type (serial vs. parallel), and energy source (mechanical, electrical, thermal, chemical). Examples include turning, injection molding, rolling, stereolithography, and chemical vapor deposition. Hardt highlights that serial processes offer greater flexibility, while parallel processes are faster but less adaptable. He discusses how variation arises from uncertainties in material properties, equipment properties, and material states, with equipment states being the most controllable. The lecture connects these concepts to process control, optimization, and the fundamental limits of different manufacturing methods.

The speaker, a member of a defending champion team, expresses pride in the group, many of whom returned from the previous year. They describe the difficulty of repeating as champions, the joy of overcoming that challenge, and the importance of sharing the success with teammates, family and friends. They highlight the team's competitive mentality, the contributions of players such as defenseman Schultzy, the impact of goaltenders (Murray and Fleury) who stole games in the playoffs, and a rookie who scored key goals. The team also overcame injuries and relied on fill‑in players and veteran additions. The speaker recounts the special moment of passing the championship trophy to a veteran who had never won a playoff game before.

The lecture explains how van der Waals forces arise between neutral atoms. Classically, neutral atoms have no net Coulomb interaction; any dipole moment costs energy, so two neutral atoms do not attract. Quantum mechanically, zero‑point fluctuations give a non‑zero ⟨d²⟩, so each atom always possesses fluctuating dipole moments. When these fluctuations become correlated, an attractive force appears. First‑order perturbation theory yields a dipole‑dipole term ∝1/R³; second‑order perturbation gives the familiar van der Waals potential ∝1/R⁶ (the C₆ coefficient). This result can be visualized using two coupled LC circuits: their zero‑point energy produces a 1/R⁶ interaction, whereas a classical LC ground state yields no effect. The same interaction can be derived from vacuum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field, which induce correlated dipole moments and, at long range, give a 1/R⁷ Casimir‑Polder potential. The short‑range 1/R⁶ law assumes instantaneous Coulomb fields, while the long‑range 1/R⁷ law includes retardation effects. A diagrammatic treatment in fourth‑order perturbation shows that the force results from exchange of virtual photon pairs. Two representative diagrams—one with photon‑dominated intermediate states (ω ≫ ω₀) and one with atom‑dominated states (ω₀ ≫ ω)—correspond to the short‑ and long‑range limits, producing the two distinct power laws. The lecture references Dan Kleppner’s treatment and indicates that further topics (interactions with metal plates) will be covered after spring break.

A cross-sectional study examined the apprehensions and potentiality of AI usage in education among 63 faculty members and administrators at Kuwait University's Faculty of Education. Results showed medium acceptance of AI (mean 3.37), with high belief that AI will benefit humanity (4.03). Most participants (58.7%) had no prior teaching experience with AI. The most important aspects of linking education to AI were data analysis, machine learning, and natural language processing. Student empowerment requirements included identifying AI use cases, evaluating AI intelligence, and identifying technical limitations (mean 4.36). Challenges and difficulties in using AI were high (mean 4.83), primarily regarding availability of suitable educational materials, lack of expertise, and subject complexity. Scenarios for AI education scored high (mean 4.82), emphasizing personalized smart teaching, smart schools, and online education. No significant differences existed by gender, academic degree, or department, though gender differences approached significance for challenges (p=.067). The study concluded that both apprehensions and potentiality are higher for integrating AI in education, with significant challenges requiring reforms in the Arab region context.

The lecture introduces risk preferences from an expected utility perspective, explaining that economics models risk aversion using concave utility functions, measured by coefficients like gamma. Stylized facts include widespread insurance purchase, willingness to accept risk for high returns, and occasional risk-seeking in lotteries. The expected utility model struggles to reconcile small-scale and large-scale risk aversion; rejecting small gambles implies unreasonably high risk aversion for large gambles (Rabin 2000). The lecture notes that alternative models like reference dependence and loss aversion will be discussed next week. It also previews Justin Sydnor's study using home insurance choices to estimate risk aversion.

Sears borrowed $100 M from Lampert’s ESL Investments, with up to $100 M; fund has loaned ~$2 B. Sears will close >300 stores, reducing to <1,140; store sales fell 11.5% and revenue fell 22% to $4.37 B.

CSUSB veteran students explain military tuition benefits: active duty members receive tuition assistance up to $4,500/year with 100% tuition paid, though military duties take priority. The Post-9/11 GI Bill provides up to 4 years of education benefits for those who served at least 90 days on active duty, covering tuition at public schools plus fees, books, and education-related expenses. The Montgomery GI Bill offers similar benefits but requires students to pay tuition, fees, and books themselves, with payments based on credit load ($1,857 for full-time, half for part-time). Veterans have 10-15 years after service to use their GI Bill benefits.

Memoranda for President Roosevelt and the American delegation for the Malta and Yalta Conferences were completed on January 16, 1945, as the "Yalta Briefing Book." A memorandum by Leo Pasvolsky records discussions with the Soviet Ambassador on the Dumbarton Oaks proposals, covering the voting formula, the Court, and dependent areas, including trusteeship and colonial problems. The Ambassador indicated Soviet interest in colonial matters despite having no colonies or colonial administration experience. Pasvolsky stated that only trusteeship questions would belong on the UN conference agenda, while colonial issues might be addressed at a special conference or by other means.

Wells was convicted of embezzlement and filed an appeal bond approved by the sheriff but not by the trial judge. Instead, another judge approved it as special judge. Under Code of Criminal Procedure 1911, article 904, the trial judge must approve the appeal bond. The bond was insufficient and the appeal was dismissed.

Defendant Alexander Shircliff and Edward O’Connor were indicted for conspiring to bribe a township trustee, in violation of R.S. 1881 §§ 2139 and 2009, to obtain O’Connor’s employment as a public‑school teacher. The trial court overruled a motion to quash, holding the indictment sufficient without alleging that any school position was vacant. The defense alleged error in denying a continuance and in the admission of evidence, but those claims were not preserved because the relevant affidavits and evidence were not included in a bill of exceptions. O’Connor was discharged to serve as a State witness. After a guilty verdict (two‑and‑one‑half years imprisonment and a $100 fine), Shircliff defaulted; a special judge, whose appointment the court presumed valid, entered judgment. The Supreme Court affirmed, finding no properly presented error.

Democrats are refusing to compromise on health care demands ahead of a meeting with Trump to avert a government shutdown. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries opposes the GOP spending proposal, insisting any deal must extend enhanced Obamacare tax credits expiring at the end of 2025. Republicans want negotiations on those credits to occur after funding is resolved. A shutdown is set for 12:01 a.m. Wednesday without a deal.

H&M reported March local‑currency sales rose 6 %, one point below the earlier 28‑day estimate, signaling difficulty meeting its 10‑15 % full‑year growth target. February sales fell for the first time in four years, and analysts described the market as tough. The retailer continues to open many stores (4,426, up 11 % year‑on‑year) despite weak demand, facing stiff competition from budget rivals such as Primark and online players. H&M shares fell 0.3 % and have dropped about 26 % over the past year.

Microsoft Corporation is a technology company focused on empowering every person and organization to achieve more. It operates through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, enterprise services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, devices, gaming, search advertising). Microsoft offers software, services, devices, and solutions globally. Its strategy centers on cloud computing, artificial intelligence, productivity tools, and personal computing devices. The company is committed to sustainability, including carbon negativity by 2030, and social initiatives such as racial equity and digital skills development. Microsoft employs approximately 221,000 people worldwide and distributes products through OEMs, direct sales, and distributors/resellers.

Leslie B. Canion v. United States (Reap. Dec. 9232, Entry No. 4135‑H, Oct. 10, 1958) was decided per stipulation. Court used foreign value per §402(c). For invoiced glassware, furniture and smokers' articles, value equals unit invoice prices plus 12.44 % plus packing. For 40 excess boxes of item 21008, value is 337 French francs each plus 12.44 % plus packing. Judgment entered.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported Q1 2016 net sales of $29.13 billion, up 28% year-over-year, with operating income of $1.07 billion (compared to $255 million in Q1 2015) and net income of $513 million (reversed from a net loss). Segment results: North America net sales $17.0 billion with operating income $588 million; International net sales $9.57 billion with operating loss $121 million; AWS net sales $2.57 billion with operating income $604 million. Cash flow from operating activities was negative $2.16 billion due to working capital changes, and capital expenditures were $1.18 billion. The company authorized a $5 billion stock repurchase program and had $8.3 billion in long-term debt outstanding. Legal proceedings include ongoing tax disputes with the IRS and European Commission. Accounting changes include adoption of new income tax standards and upcoming lease accounting updates.

The U.S. government provided over $55,000 to Cambodia for preserving 3,000-5,000 personal items belonging to prisoners at the Khmer Rouge's Tuol Sleng prison (S-21), where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed during the 1975-79 regime. The items include clothing, shoes, hats and belts, some showing blood and sweat stains. The preservation work will maintain historical evidence while preventing further deterioration. Some items will be displayed at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum to educate young Cambodians.

Connor McDavid signed a two‑year, $25 million extension with the Edmonton Oilers, worth $12.5 million per year. The 28‑year‑old captain has 1,082 points (361 goals) in 712 games, five Art Ross trophies, three Hart trophies and was the second skater to win the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP on a losing team in 2024. He was set to become an unrestricted free agent after his 11th season with the Oilers, having previously signed an eight‑year, $100 million contract in 2017. In the same news cycle, the Oilers signed defenseman Jake Walman to a seven‑year, $49 million extension and extended coach Kris Knoblauch through 2028‑29. Other moves reported include Boston retiring Zdeno Chara’s No. 33, the Lightning and Panthers combining for 312 penalty minutes in a preseason game, Matt Grzelcyk’s one‑year deal with Chicago, Kevin Ellis joining San Jose after an injury‑filled tenure in Philadelphia, and Minnesota signing goaltender Filip Gustavsson to a five‑year, $34 million contract.

NVIDIA Corporation Q1 FY19 (quarter ended April 29, 2018) financial results: Revenue increased 66% year-over-year to $3.21 billion; gross margin improved to 64.5% from 59.4%; net income rose 145% to $1.24 billion ($1.98 per diluted share). GPU segment revenue grew 77% to $2.77 billion, driven by gaming and datacenter demand. Tegra Processor segment revenue increased 33% to $442 million. Operating expenses were $773 million, up 30% year-over-year. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.30 billion. The company repurchased 3 million shares for $655 million and paid $91 million in dividends during the quarter. The board authorized up to $1.16 billion in additional share repurchases through December 2020. NVIDIA adopted the new revenue recognition accounting standard using the modified retrospective approach with no significant impact.

US objectives for dependent territories: promote advancement, encourage self‑government, safeguard security, apply non‑discriminatory treatment. A March 1943 Draft Declaration distinguished mandated/detached territories from colonies, proposed international trusteeship only for the former, and set an independence schedule. The draft was discussed with Britain at Quebec and with Britain and the Soviet Union at Moscow; British objections were recorded. Refinements were incorporated into three undisclosed documents. At the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s request the trusteeship chapter was omitted from U.S. proposals, so the issue was not addressed at Dumbarton Oaks, though governments expressed interest. The three documents are being revised in light of the Dumbarton Oaks proposals and will be submitted for Presidential approval before discussion. Diplomatic correspondence recorded U.S. gratitude for British acceptance of President’s Security Council proposal. A War Department memorandum advised settling fundamental issues among the major powers before convening a world organization and warned that raising territorial or trusteeship questions during the war could generate controversy and undermine wartime unity.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs combine rasterization, real‑time ray tracing, and AI to deliver hybrid rendering. The architecture includes dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, achieving roughly ten times the ray‑tracing throughput of Pascal GPUs while using far fewer rays per pixel when paired with denoising filters. Tensor Cores power the NGX deep‑learning stack, enabling features such as Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS) which trains on 64× supersampled reference images to infer high‑quality images from reduced input samples, providing up to a 2× performance gain on 4K DLSS versus Pascal, and a DLSS 2X mode that approaches 64×SS quality at target resolution. Other NGX capabilities include AI‑based inpainting, AI Slow‑Mo frame interpolation, and AI Super Rez upscaling (2×–8×) with higher PSNR than bicubic methods.

Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh shader stages that use a cooperative thread model, allowing developers to eliminate CPU draw‑call bottlenecks, increase the number of rendered objects by over an order of magnitude, dynamically select level‑of‑detail, and implement advanced geometry manipulations such as real‑time cutaways. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) lets developers set per‑16×16‑pixel region shading rates, supporting content‑adaptive, motion‑adaptive, and foveated rendering algorithms to reduce shading work without altering visibility sampling.

Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance by shading in texture space and reusing texels across frames, improving temporal stability and enabling fine‑grained LOD control for VR and other latency‑sensitive applications. Multi‑View Rendering expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi‑Projection to up to four views per pass (32 at API level), facilitating efficient stereo VR, cascaded shadow maps, and single‑pass instancing. Turing also adds USB Type‑C VirtualLink support and accelerates VRWorks Audio with RT‑core ray tracing for realistic reverberation.

The Turing line includes three GPU dies: TU102 (full‑feature, up to 576‑mm², 18.6 B transistors, 4608 CUDA cores, 576 Tensor cores, 72 RT cores); TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, Tesla T4; 13.6 B transistors, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor cores, 48 RT cores; 256‑bit memory, NVLink); and TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070; 10.8 B transistors, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor cores, 36 RT cores; no NVLink). TU104’s Tesla T4 variant is optimized for inference, delivering 65 FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

A workload‑based metric called RTX‑OPS aggregates peak operations of Tensor (20 % utilization), FP32 (80 %), RT (40 % of rendering time), and INT32 (35 % of rendering time) pipelines; for RTX 2080 Ti this yields ~78 RTX‑OPS.

Ray‑traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections leverage the RT cores and denoisers to produce physically correct contact hardening, superior definition, and artifact‑free glossy reflections. Advanced filtering (AI and non‑AI denoising) reduces the number of rays required per pixel, enabling real‑time deployment in games such as Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

Overall, Turing’s combination of hybrid rendering, dedicated ray‑tracing and tensor accelerators, and new shading models enables cinematic‑quality graphics at playable frame rates previously unattainable on GPU architectures.

President reports that Georgia surveyors have entered Creek Indian Territory in violation of the treaty of Washington (ratified April 22) and the Act of March 30 1802, which prohibits surveying lands secured to Indian tribes. Surveyors have been arrested by the Indians; their forbearance is hoped to prevent bloodshed. The law provides two enforcement mechanisms: military arrest of trespassers in Indian country, or civil prosecution of violators found within United States jurisdiction. After deliberation, the President opted for civil process first, directing the U.S. attorney and marshal in Georgia to prosecute the surveyors and instructing the Indian agent to assure the Creeks of protection and to urge them to avoid hostilities. Military force was withheld because the surveyors acted under state authority and employing troops risked conflict between Georgia and the Union. The President warns that continued Georgia encroachment will compel the use of military force, and asks Congress to consider whether further legislation is needed.

The passage describes container design patterns for distributed systems. The ambassador pattern (Chapter 3) involves a container that brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world, useful for client-side sharding, service brokering, and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern (Chapter 4) modifies an application's interface to conform to a standardized interface for monitoring, logging, and health checks.

Chapter 5 covers replicated load-balanced services, where stateless identical servers handle traffic through a load balancer, providing redundancy and scalability. Additional layers can add caching (for performance) and SSL termination (for security). Session-tracked services ensure user requests route to the same replica.

Chapter 6 describes sharded services, where each replica serves only a subset of requests, scaling to handle data too large for a single machine. Sharding functions determine request routing, and consistent hashing minimizes disruption when resharding. Replicated sharded caches combine both patterns for reliability.

The scatter/gather pattern (Chapter 7) achieves parallelism by sending requests to multiple nodes simultaneously, then combining results at a root node, useful for distributed search. However, increased parallelism has diminishing returns due to overhead and the "straggler" problem.

Chapter 8 discusses function-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven processing, where functions execute in response to events. Benefits include simplified deployment and automatic scaling, while challenges include operational complexity and difficulty monitoring decoupled systems.

Apple Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 26, 2015 reported net sales of $75.9 billion (up 2% year-over-year) and net income of $18.4 billion. Gross margin was $30.4 billion (40.1% of net sales), and operating income was $24.2 billion. The company declared a cash dividend of $0.52 per share and repurchased $6.9 billion of common stock. Samsung paid $548 million in December 2015 related to a patent infringement lawsuit. Geographic performance included Americas ($29.3B), Europe ($17.9B), Greater China ($18.4B), Japan ($4.8B), and Rest of Asia Pacific ($5.4B). The company noted an ongoing European Commission investigation into Irish tax arrangements and expects Q2 2016 gross margin between 39% and 39.5%. As of December 26, 2015, total assets were $293.3 billion with shareholders' equity of $128.3 billion.

AT&T plans to launch LTE‑M nationwide by the end of June, a low‑power cellular version for IoT devices. LTE‑M uses a fraction of the energy of regular LTE, can last up to 10 years on a single charge, penetrates walls up to 8 inches thicker than standard LTE, and provides about 386 kbps—sufficient for small sensor data. Examples include pallets with embedded radios for tracking, Pepsi soda fountains that report flavor preferences, and Capstone smart water meters that detect leaks or toilet malfunctions. Corporate IoT applications are considered as valuable as consumer ones. LTE‑M devices consume little data and are mostly idle, so they won’t affect network performance for other users. AT&T has not disclosed pricing, weighing per‑bit or per‑device charges.

The speaker says Detroit Red Wings have weaknesses and need better preparation for upcoming games, emphasizing the importance of capitalizing on limited chances and the power play. He notes that a key player contributes both offensively and defensively, and that during the lockout year in Magnitogorsk he observed a teammate’s growing confidence, now in his third NHL season and second finals. The speaker also describes suffering a significant injury, feeling helpless while the team struggled, and using a day‑to‑day recovery approach that allowed a return to play. He remarks that after returning he made changes that improved the club’s performance and playoff prospects, and that facing the same opponent as last year makes the series especially competitive.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 snapped a seven‑day win streak. Tesla released Model Y (under $40,000) and Model 3 (about $37,000). Model Y omits a panoramic glass roof, leather seats and light bars, costs $5,000 less than prior version, shorter range. Price cuts follow loss of $7,500 EV tax credit and competition. Tesla has not launched a new model since Cybertruck, which has popularity and recalls. Company is shifting to robotics and self‑driving, showing Cybercab (~$30,000) not yet in production, promising next‑generation Roadster and robotaxi software. Optimus robot remains unreleased; competitors sell bipedal robots. After a 36% drop, Tesla’s shares surged 40% in Q3; Musk bought $1 billion of Tesla stock in September.

The Rock Springs City Council will hold a hearing May 1 on amendments allowing restaurants to operate seasonal dining decks (May 1–Oct 31). Decks must be stored off‑season, keep sidewalk clearance, rent parking spaces, avoid fire‑hydrant blocking, limit umbrellas to table width, serve alcohol only at tables and undergo inspections. City Hall, 212 D St., 7 p.m.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch says Tarik Skubal will not pitch in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Mariners, even though Detroit faces elimination Wednesday. Skubal gave up two runs and struck out nine over seven innings in Game 2 and is being saved for a Game 5 on Oct. 10 in Seattle. Hinch calls the decision risky but will have relievers ready. A Game 4 win would set up Skubal to start Game 5.

Lego DC Super Villains was officially announced with a trailer. The game lets players create a custom villain and play alongside classic DC antagonists in a parallel universe where heroes are absent. It releases October 16 2018 on PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, with special editions offering bonus characters.

The speaker describes a veteran right‑winger as one of the league’s best players for the past two‑three years, noting his team’s recent success and his heavy ice‑time in the first period that was later reduced. He says the player is versatile, able to slide to either side of the ice when needed, and likens him to Andreychuk, emphasizing that he leads by example. The player is described as an underrated, disciplined defenseman who consistently faces the opponent’s top lines, rarely takes penalties and still plays many minutes on the power play and penalty‑kill. The coach notes a team adjustment this year: instead of protecting a young defenseman with another veteran, they brought in a young defenseman with experience, which helped the club. The coach also calls the player a big, old‑school power forward who plays the first and last minutes of periods, is healthy, from Alberta, and is good with the media. Regarding Jarome, the speaker says he historically starts slowly, improves after Christmas and this year had four goals by Christmas with none at home; his progress is attributed to taking on a leadership role beyond simply wearing the “C”. The team focuses on its own improvement and does not use schedule, ice conditions or opponent strength as excuses. The Lightning’s season has not been hindered by the ice, and veteran linesman “Scamp” remains fast, respected and controls play between whistles.

Pakistan has stopped work on three CPEC road projects after China halted funding on November 20. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal confirmed this to a parliamentary committee, which stated the projects are not abandoned but awaiting Chinese approval. Pakistan's financial strain has left it unable to continue work independently. Earlier, Pakistan had refused Chinese funding for the Diamer-Bhasha Dam and rejected yuan trading at Gwadar Port, twice snubbing Chinese officials. China cited corruption concerns as a top issue. A European think tank noted China's moves appear aimed at shifting CPEC control from civilian administration to the Pakistan Army.

The author urges national legislators to enact a graduated inheritance tax on gifts, bequests, or devises, with rates increasing with amount and remoteness of kin, while keeping the tax low on modest estates to preserve incentives for thrift and ambition. He emphasizes that such a tax is ethically proper and should be implemented gradually. The passage reviews three prior national inheritance taxes: the 1797 act (graduated, small, with kin exceptions), the 1862 act (progressively higher for more distant kin, with a $1,000 exemption), and the 1898 war‑revenue act (tax on sums over $10,000, rising with amount and kinship). The Supreme Court has upheld the constitutionality of these taxes, classifying them as excise taxes rather than direct taxes. The author contrasts inheritance taxes with income taxes, noting the latter face constitutional obstacles (the 1894 law was struck down) and may require a constitutional amendment if legislation cannot achieve the desired results.

A retrospective cohort study examined 290 coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) patients treated at a Mordovian Republic Hospital from 2017‑2021 to determine whether the number of arterial shunts and the number of internal thoracic arteries (ITA) used influence postoperative complications. Patients were 41–80 years old (mean ≈ 61 years), 85 % male, and 95.9 % underwent on‑pump surgery. BMI ranged 16–45 kg/m²; ejection fraction 29–77 ml; cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time 0–431 min; aortic cross‑clamp time 0–147 min; ICU stay 1–27 days; total stay 7–50 days. Pre‑operative risk factors included diabetes (23 %), dyspnea (19 %), arrhythmia (24 %), progressive angina (39 %), post‑myocardial‑infarction myocardial sclerosis (61 %) and left‑ventricle aneurysm (3 %). Shunt numbers: 1‑shunt = 30, 2‑shunt = 67, 3‑shunt = 119, 4‑shunt = 65, 5‑shunt = 8, 6‑shunt = 1. One ITA was used in 66 % of patients; two ITAs in 34 %. Overall postoperative complications occurred in 69 patients: 10.7 % arrhythmia, 5.0 % psychosis, 1.4 % stroke, 0.7 % myocardial infarction, 12.0 % hydrothorax, 3.2 % re‑sternotomy, 0.4 % superficial wound infection, 2.0 % deep wound infection, 3.9 % dyspnea; most frequent was hydrothorax. Five patients died (1.7 %); complication count did not differ between survivors and non‑survivors. Statistical analyses showed that older age, longer CPB and aortic cross‑clamp times, higher BMI, diabetes, lower ejection fraction, and presence of progressive angina or post‑myocardial‑infarction sclerosis were significantly associated with more complications, longer ICU and total hospital stays, and higher mortality. Two‑ITA use correlated with longer cross‑clamp and CPB times; number of shunts correlated with CPB and cross‑clamp times. No significant association was found between complication count and the number of shunts or the number of ITAs. The study concludes that elderly CABG patients are at higher risk for psychosis, arrhythmia, stroke and extended hospitalization; hydrothorax is linked to low BMI and prolonged cross‑clamp time leading to longer CPB; progressive angina and post‑myocardial‑infarction sclerosis increase overall complication risk.

The team sought four centermen, believing Tanner and Tyler, who previously played together in the American League, provided a better matchup. Coach Sutter is described as a top‑end, two‑way player and a Selke Trophy nominee, noted for his competitive, tenacious style and reliable practice habits. Kopy is highlighted for his heavy minutes, consistent performance, and elite play‑making ability, while the team emphasizes collective effort over individual stars, crediting leadership for keeping the group focused. The club views itself as experienced and playoff‑proven yet still young, with an emphasis on preparation and continuous learning. Both the team and its opponent are described as fast, and the club is currently in the Stanley Cup Finals, where several players are experiencing their first final‑game adjustment. Sutter is identified as a top goalie and a strong leader who consistently delivers and mentors younger players, and the interview notes he has not yet had his best season.

Team attributed success to playing well at home, John's key contributions after Holik departed, and overcoming injuries during the playoffs despite difficult travel. New players integrated after trades, and the team used previous playoff experience of blowing a lead to succeed this year. The player believed John deserved the Conn Smythe Trophy while acknowledging the team is not ready to call itself a dynasty but hopes for continued success.

An assignee for the benefit of creditors is not subject to arrest under section 179 of the Code in an action brought primarily to compel an accounting and distribution of funds among creditors, even though the assignee holds property in a fiduciary capacity. The statute applies only to actions primarily and simply for the recovery of money received by factors, agents, and brokers, not to actions against trustees requiring judicial determination of net amounts chargeable and distribution among multiple parties. A judgment for false imprisonment against attorneys who issued an unauthorized execution against the person of an assignee was affirmed.

Since 2007, America Saves Week, coordinated by America Saves and the American Savings Education Council, runs Feb. 27‑Mar. 4, promoting savings with themes, contests, tweet chats and resources; participants receive a toolkit and badge; Military Saves Week offered.

Following the death of his cousin Jonathan Jeffrey, Erik Brust founded JonnyPops in 2011 to create a fruity, creamy frozen treat made from fruit, real cream, cane sugar and a pinch of salt, with no additives. He and St. Olaf classmate Connor Wray tested recipes on campus, then sold the pops at Twin Cities farmers markets in 2012, later expanding to vendors, restaurants and convenience stores. By 2013 the company reached several states and Brust and Wray were named to Forbes’ “30 Under 30.” In spring 2014 they launched with about 50 Minnesota retail partners, won the MN Cup Student Division, and after graduating took the business full‑time. By 2018 they again made Forbes’ “30 Under 30.” JonnyPops now has roughly 10,000 distribution points nationwide and introduced a Delights line (dark chocolate, cold‑press coffee chocolate, cherry chocolate, vanilla mint chocolate, root‑beer float) that is natural, gluten‑free and under 200 calories. The brand’s “Better Pop for a Better World” mission places motivational messages on sticks and partners with retailers to fund addiction‑treatment organizations.

President James Monroe, in his second inaugural address, expressed gratitude for his reelection, attributing the national consensus to strong and permanent causes rather than to his own merits. He reviewed the recent war that left the nation with heavy loss of life and an added $120 million of debt, and described the post‑war effort to improve security by constructing coastal fortifications and augmenting the navy, arguing that these measures would be economical because a small regular force could hold the works while militia gathered. He affirmed the United States’ strict neutrality in the war between Spain and its South‑American colonies, noting that both parties received equal treatment in U.S. ports and that laws against illegal arming were enforced impartially; he indicated that this neutrality would be maintained even if the conflict continued. He recounted the suppression of piracy, especially the elimination of a buccaneering base at Amelia Island and incidents in Florida in 1817‑1818, and explained that clemency was shown to those who acted in ignorance of the law.

Monroe highlighted recent diplomatic achievements: a treaty with Spain that secured Florida, settled the western boundary, and provided for citizens’ claims; and an 1818 convention with Great Britain that renewed commercial relations, resolved fisheries disputes, and left West‑Indian trade restrictions in place. Negotiations with France on commerce were ongoing, and relations with the Barbary powers remained unchanged. He reported that, despite a temporary decline in revenue caused by low prices, the nation had repaid roughly $67 million of the public debt while advancing defense and other improvements, and he recommended that future revenue needs be met by internal duties and excises to reduce dependence on foreign trade.

Regarding domestic policy, Monroe called for a reformed Indian policy that would replace tribal sovereignty with individual land grants, education, and permanent funds for civil government. He assured that the United States remains at peace with all powers, warned of renewed European conflict, and pledged neutrality while upholding U.S. maritime rights. He praised the nation’s elective political system and its territorial expansion, including control of the Mississippi, acquisition of Louisiana and Florida, and the admission of new states on equal footing. Concluding, Monroe affirmed his commitment to serve the office faithfully and expressed confidence in the continued support of his fellow citizens and divine protection.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the company will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite President Trump's new $100,000 fee, which could cost Nvidia an estimated $147.3 million for 2025 approvals. In an internal memo, Huang wrote that "legal immigration remains essential" and that immigration made Nvidia's success possible. Huang, who was born in Taiwan and came to the U.S. as a child, previously spoke positively about Trump's visa changes but later said the fee "probably sets the bar a little too high." Nvidia is not in the top 10 Fortune 500 companies with the most H-1B approvals in 2025.

On October 6, analysts from BNP Paribas, Cowen, Royal Bank of Canada, Oppenheimer, Stifel, Benchmark, HC Wainwright, UBS, Mizuho and other firms raised or lowered price targets for Covestro, AdvanSix, Ascena, Basf, Costco, Deckers, New Oriental, Evonik, Inovio, Linde, Eli Lilly, Lanxess, Mallinckrodt, Netflix, Plug Power, Rite Aid, Constellation Brands, 2U, Wacker Chemie and Yum China, with ratings ranging from sell to buy, outperform, neutral and hold.

Background: SARS‑CoV‑2 infection duration is prolonged in immunosuppressed transplant recipients, and safe discontinuation of isolation should rely on viral culture or reliable surrogates (e.g., rt‑PCR Ct values). This protocol describes a systematic review to collate data on infectivity assessment in immunosuppressed patients using viral culture and to estimate the relationship between serial Ct values or other viral burden measures and the likelihood/duration of replication‑competent virus. The review focuses on solid organ or hematopoietic stem‑cell transplant recipients. Research questions address the association of Ct values and other viral burden measures with infectious virus detection, and the influence of age, sex, underlying pathology, degree of immunosuppression, vaccination status, symptoms, and disease course. Methods: searches of LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar and WHO Covid‑19 database from November 2019 to December 2021 using terms combining coronavirus/covid‑19, immunosuppression, transplant, and culture/Ct/viral load; independent title/abstract and full‑text screening by four reviewers; inclusion of primary studies reporting serial Ct values and viral culture from respiratory samples of pre‑ or post‑transplant patients; exclusion of post‑mortem, non‑respiratory, or culture‑negative studies. Data extraction, quality assessment (case definition, patient characteristics, follow‑up, PCR and culture methods), and narrative synthesis are planned; pooling is not intended due to assay variability. Funding: NIHR Evidence Synthesis Working Group [Project 569] and University of Calgary. Conflicts of interest for all authors are disclosed.

The speaker mourns the fourth presidential death, reaffirms the Constitution’s guarantee of a peaceful transition, and pledges to continue the predecessor’s goals of correcting abuses, promoting prosperity, and preserving peace. He notes the nation’s current prosperity and stable finances, sees no urgent need for a special congressional session, and declares reliance on divine guidance and the patriotism and intelligence of the American people.

Lincolnshire County Council’s new care‑leavers strategy, described by parenting manager Andrew Morris as parental‑type support, includes council‑tax discounts up to 100 % for 18‑21‑year‑olds, extends advice to age 25, funds university fees and driving licences, provides prison liaison, and has a £1.2 m leaving‑care budget covering 600 people in care and 300 care leavers, numbers rising. Help is available through the council or Barnardo’s.

A fossil from southwestern China reveals a pregnant Dinocephalosaurus, a fish‑eating marine reptile from the Triassic (~245 million years ago). The embryo’s curled posture and forward orientation prove it is a developing offspring, not swallowed prey. This archosauromorph is the first known viviparous member of its group, indicating live birth rather than egg‑laying. The ~4‑m‑long animal had a slender 1.7‑m neck, paddle‑like limbs and a small head with canine teeth. Viviparity suggests it remained fully marine, avoiding land predators while breeding. Sex determination was genetic.

Farmers State Bank of Craig sued Samuel J. Lydick to recover $3,000 on a promissory note dated March 17 1920. Lydick answered that the note was given as partial payment of a $5,000 note for stock in the Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company, which he claimed he was fraudulently induced to buy by the bank’s officer Everett J. Martin. The bank and Martin raised separate defenses. The trial court directed a verdict for the bank on Lydick’s cross‑petition seeking affirmative recovery and submitted to the jury the questions whether the bank was a holder in due course and whether Martin made fraudulent representations. The jury found the bank was a holder in due course, that Martin did not commit fraud, and that insufficient evidence supported the second count of the cross‑petition. On appeal the Supreme Court upheld the rulings, holding that under the negotiable‑instruments law a payee who takes an instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity and without notice may be a holder in due course, and affirmed the judgment.

James Schenck, President and CEO of PenFed Credit Union, was named Large Business Philanthropist of the Year by Volunteer Alexandria at its 20th annual Business Philanthropy Summit. In his speech he cited the ‘People Helping People’ philosophy and its 2,500 employees. PenFed and the PenFed Foundation donated $300,000 to Serve our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America, $15,000 to Bunker Labs, and additional funds to the Gary Sinise Foundation. The PenFed Foundation, headquartered in Alexandria, has provided over $30 million to veterans, families and caregivers since 2001. Schenck volunteers as CEO without compensation. He was elected National Credit Union Hero of the Year in 2017 and selected by HillVets as one of the 100 most influential veterans in 2015. PenFed Credit Union, founded in 1935, is America’s second‑largest federal credit union, serving over 1.6 million members with $23 billion in assets, and is federally insured.

Amazon Prime Day 2 is scheduled for October 7–8, with early deals already active. WIRED’s editors, who have hundreds of years of combined experience testing gear, are covering the sale and have added 10 new discounts on Amazon devices, cheap laptops, fitness trackers, smart bird feeders and other gadgets. Notable deals include the Apple iPad (2025, A16) for $299 (save $149) with USB‑C, Touch ID, two 12‑MP cameras and no Apple Intelligence support; the Apple iPad with M3 chip (13‑inch) as an upgrade option; the Apple iPad with A17 Pro and Apple Intelligence at a higher price; the Apple MacBook Air (M4, 2025) for $799 (save $200) featuring a fanless design, support for two 4K monitors, a 12‑MP webcam, four color choices and three storage options; the Anker MagGo Power Bank (10 K) for $70 (save $20) with a built‑in kickstand, LED display and MagSafe/Qi2 compatibility; Nimble power banks offering fast 15‑65 W charging, bioplastic construction and minimal packaging; the Arlo Pro 5S security camera for $100 (save $80) with 2K HDR video, night vision, two‑way audio and a built‑in siren (subscription required); the Essential Indoor Security Camera (2nd Gen) which remains reliable though some features are subscription‑only; and the Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024) for $300 (save $100) with a 10‑inch display, Premium Pen, AI note‑summarization and no waterproofing. Additional items on sale include earbuds, headphones, a rolling adjustable desk, a 140‑W multi‑port hub and a portable speaker with built‑in lights.

Over the past two decades, China has modernised its People’s Liberation Army to match its global ambitions, seeking hard power to protect regional claims, secure sea lanes, support initiatives like AIIB and OBOR, and counter U.S. influence in the Indo‑Pacific. The PLA’s transformation has made China more assertive, with its future use of military power still uncertain.

North Korea’s defaulted sovereign debt, with syndicated loans of around $1 billion and total obligations of about $3 billion, has been frozen for years under the world’s strictest sanctions. In 1997 BNP Paribas packaged the debt into NK Debt Corporation, creating transferable securities that were regularly traded after 2000. Prices rose to 14‑18 cents on the dollar after Kim Jong‑un’s succession in 2011 but fell again as sanctions tightened and the market effectively halted in early 2013. Recent UN sanctions banning coal, iron, lead and seafood exports further discourage trading. Holdings include the Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund, which held $15.5 million of zero‑coupon bonds maturing in 2020. Debt‑restructuring experts see little prospect for resolution, likening North Korea’s situation to Cuba’s and noting arrears several times the principal.

Latin American stocks rose on Monday, recovering from last week's selloff as U.S.-North Korea tensions eased. U.S. officials downplayed an imminent war, after last week's threats wiped about $1 trillion from global equity markets. Scotiabank strategists said geo‑political risk has fallen but warned of possible missile tests. Mexico's IPC gained 1.1% and Brazil's Bovespa reached its highest since May. Currency moves were subdued; the Mexican peso edged up 0.3% ahead of NAFTA talks, while the Brazilian real seesawed before a fiscal goal revision.

This passage describes the development of a modular AI-driven framework for multi-modal synchrotron experiments at NSLS-II. Materials characterization of complex materials like high entropy alloys requires complementary techniques such as X-ray diffraction (XRD) for long-range structure and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) for local structure. Synchrotron facilities provide advantages over lab instruments but face constraints from limited beamtime and mismatches between homogeneous mapping approaches and spatially heterogeneous samples. The researchers developed a modular framework integrating AI agents for data processing, analysis, and decision-making through Bayesian optimization. These agents are deployed as scalable services with plug-and-play capabilities and interface with existing Bluesky infrastructure including queue servers, data storage (Tiled), and adjudicators that moderate measurement requests. The system supports operating modes ranging from fully human-driven to fully autonomous while maintaining human oversight. Multi-beamline experiments demonstrated synchronous XRD and XAFS measurements on identical Al-Ni-Pt combinatorial libraries. A digital twin was developed to enable offline testing and benchmarking, where simulated campaigns showed AI-driven mapping outperforms conventional grid and random sampling approaches in resolving phase boundaries and localized features. The framework enables FAIR data practices and collaborative human-AI workflows for accelerating materials discovery.

Founded in 2015 by Rick Davis, Let’s Grow Kids was created as a time‑limited child‑care advocacy organization with a planned 2025 sunset. Davis recruited Aly Richards as leader after former Vermont governors persuaded her to join. Over its ten‑year run the group raised more than $70 million, grew to 40 staff, and helped pass Act 76 (2023), Vermont’s near‑universal child‑care law. The law opened over 100 new child‑care programs, added more than 1,000 child spaces, created 230 early‑childhood educator jobs, and made 4,000 additional children eligible for tuition assistance. The organization officially sunset on Oct 3 as scheduled. Its deadline‑driven model attracted talent, accelerated fundraising, and maintained focus during the COVID‑19 pandemic. Staff transitioned to permanent agencies including First Children’s Finance, the Vermont NAEYC chapter, the Department of Children and Families, and the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network. About 80‑90 % of Vermont families now qualify for subsidies, but full universal coverage has not yet been achieved. Leaders credit the sunset provision for the campaign’s success and view it as a possible model for other states.

Jennifer Bartell, 39, was shot and killed March 14 in Portsmouth, Va. Four arrested, including Joshua Bowen. Facebook argument led to meeting; it failed, they went to Bartell’s home, a fight erupted, and Bowen shot her. Gun was taken, but no firearm was found at scene. Neighbors called it shocking but not random.

Federal Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit claiming the Nirvana “Nevermind” album cover—a naked baby underwater—constitutes child pornography. Olguin ruled the image lacks the statutory criteria, noting only the child’s nudity and that the picture resembles a family photo of a nude child bathing. The 9th Circuit later reinstated a related suit.

A study by Florida Museum researchers found that lice parasitic on primates and humans have hosted their vitamin-producing bacterial endosymbionts continuously for 20 to 25 million years, coinciding with the divergence of great apes and old world monkeys. Sequencing genomes of symbionts from human, chimpanzee, gorilla, and red colobus monkey lice revealed extremely reduced genomes (530,000–570,000 base pairs) devoted primarily to B‑vitamin synthesis. Extensive genome remodeling over this period placed symbiosis-critical genes in close proximity, and the host specificity of lice provides clues to primate and human evolutionary history.

Using deep‑learning on more than 50 000 images from the European Mars Express HRSC camera and the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter CaSSIS camera, researchers identified dust devils and measured their motion with stereo imaging of about 300 events. The study, led by Dr. Valentin Bickel (Univ. of Bern) and colleagues, found that Martian winds and the dust devils they generate reach speeds up to 44 m/s (~160 km/h), far exceeding earlier surface‑based measurements that rarely exceeded 100 km/h. These stronger winds are shown to lift large amounts of dust into the atmosphere, influencing Mars’ weather and climate on a global scale. The results provide the first planetary‑wide, multi‑decadal data set on near‑surface wind dynamics and are considered essential for planning future landed missions, modeling atmospheric processes, and studying phenomena such as dune formation and slope streaks. The team plans to continue coordinated observations with CaSSIS and HRSC to further refine wind and dust‑cycle models.

This study examined whether resting‑state functional connectivity (FC) of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) predicts the course of ADHD symptoms in newly diagnosed adults. Fifty‑four patients underwent baseline fMRI and clinical assessment (t1) using the Wender‑Reimherr Interview (WRI); a follow‑up was performed after a mean of three years (t2). Approximately 30% of participants had discontinued stimulant medication by t2 (non‑responders, n = 20), while the remaining 34 continued treatment. Seed‑based FC analysis of the NAc showed that higher baseline symptom load correlated with reduced FC between the NAc and the right paracingulate gyrus. Over the follow‑up period, greater symptom improvement was associated with lower FC between the NAc and the right anterior insular cortex. The relationship between FC change and symptom change differed by medication status: in treated patients, higher FC between the NAc and the right posterior insula predicted improvement, whereas in non‑responders higher FC predicted deterioration. The findings indicate that NAc‑to‑default‑mode‑network and salience‑network connectivity patterns are linked to ADHD symptom trajectories and to responsiveness to stimulant medication.

Utah's Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control overcharged customers $1,161 on seven items due to a markup error when raising the markup and will refund overcharges. The department added a program to flag markup mistakes. An audit also found it failed to transfer $4.6 million to school lunch and public safety programs in November 2017, which it corrected after discovery.

In 1793, a hot, dry summer enabled the Aedes aegypti mosquito to spread yellow fever throughout Philadelphia, killing about 5,000 people (≈10 % of the city’s population). Despite attempts by physicians Benjamin Rush and Philip Physick—including bloodletting, smoke “purification” and quarantine—no effective control was found. Over a century later, mosquitoes were identified as the vector, prompting improved water, sanitation and drainage, and the last North‑American outbreak ended in New Orleans in 1905. Brazil is now experiencing its worst human yellow‑fever outbreak in decades, with at least 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths since December 2016, and cases approaching Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. A highly effective vaccine (≈99 % efficacy, usually single dose) exists, and WHO recommends vaccination for travelers to endemic areas. Penn researchers are developing Zika vaccines using DNA and mRNA platforms; one DNA vaccine entered phase I trials in August 2016 and an mRNA vaccine showed protective efficacy in mice and monkeys in pre‑clinical studies.

Rachael Caplan, 29, has Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), a rare neurological disease causing constant, severe pain that began after a hip injury in her first year of law school. CRPS affects about 9,000 Canadians per year, mostly in Ontario. It typically starts with trauma or injury and spreads, producing swelling, skin changes, temperature shifts, and can affect nails, hair, and bones. Early diagnosis is crucial; treatment success is 80‑90 % in the first three months, but after six months the disease is largely irreversible. Caplan’s pain progressed after acupuncture in 2012, and she received a diagnosis from pain specialist Dr. David Shulman on her 26th birthday.
