The case held that a conveyance by extent operates like a conveyance by deed, passing all buildings on land to the creditor regardless of their foundations. Jack owned both the land and buildings; therefore the buildings passed with the land to Brooks through the execution and to the plaintiff through his deed. Parol evidence is inadmissible to contradict written appraisement returns. The defendants' evidence that the buildings were reserved by mutual consent was properly rejected. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff.

A study of Danish births over 25 years found children of mothers with rheumatoid arthritis had nearly threefold increased risk of developing the disease and elevated risks for thyroid disease (2.2‑times) and epilepsy (1.6‑times). Researchers advise close monitoring of these children.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020. Total revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2020 was $35.0 billion, compared to $30.6 billion in the prior year period. Net income was $10.8 billion for the quarter, up from $8.8 billion in the prior year period. The company reported three segments: Productivity and Business Processes ($11.7 billion revenue), Intelligent Cloud ($12.3 billion revenue), and More Personal Computing ($11.0 billion revenue). Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $13.3 billion. As of March 31, 2020, total assets were $285.4 billion, and stockholders' equity was $114.5 billion. The company declared dividends of $0.51 per share during the quarter. COVID-19 had minimal net impact on Q3 revenue, with increased cloud usage offset by reduced advertising spend and transactional licensing in certain areas. The board authorized a $40 billion share repurchase program in September 2019, with $36.8 billion remaining as of March 31, 2020.

The passage describes video encoding and decoding techniques, focusing on intra prediction modes (directional and non-directional) and non-separable transforms (e.g., LFNST, RST). Directional modes are determined by a nominal mode and an angular offset, while non-directional modes (DC, PAETH, SMOOTH, etc.) are based on averaging neighboring samples. Non-separable transforms are applied as secondary transforms to improve coding efficiency for directional textures. Transform set selection depends on the intra prediction mode, and LFNST indices are signaled per intra-coded CU. The disclosure provides methods and apparatuses for video encoding/decoding using these techniques, with processing circuitry to handle block reconstruction based on directional or non-directional modes and non-separable transforms. The passage also references prior applications and discusses constraints like coefficient significance, block size, and ISP mode for applying LFNST, as well as line graph transforms derived from generalized graph Laplacian matrices.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 college students found that those who persistently consumed energy drinks from age 18 were significantly more likely to use cocaine or non‑medical prescription stimulants by ages 21–24. Even occasional energy‑drink consumers showed a higher stimulant‑drug risk, while non‑consumers had lower substance‑use rates. The mechanism behind this association remains unclear and requires further research.

The study examines Hungarian higher education lecturers after the post-socialist transition. Enrollment rose from under 1,000 per 100,000 inhabitants in 1990 to 2,755 by 2020, but remained below developed European levels. Institutional pluralism led to non-state share of lecturers reaching 30% by 2020, while privatization reduced public university lecturers to 25% by 2023. Demographic decline, the 2005 Bologna reform, and policy changes—including tuition fees, 2013 cuts in state support, and 2020 advanced exam requirements—shaped student numbers, with illiberal policies increasing inequality and reducing graduate rates below EU 2020 targets. Lecturer numbers correlated positively with students until 2004, then weakly negatively; the student-teacher ratio peaked at 17.9 in 2006 and fell to 10.4 in 2022. Hungarian lecturers are older than the OECD average but in the middle range internationally, with women’s proportion rising but lagging leading countries. Employment rules evolved from Soviet-era centralized qualification (1951) to the 1993 Act restoring university PhD rights, with later acts tightening requirements (e.g., habilitation, international recognition). The 2011 Act introduced a chancellor system reducing autonomy, and in 2020, 22 state universities were reorganized into public foundations, losing civil service status. Academic staff structure showed stagnation since 2005, with professor numbers falling by two-thirds by 2020 due to demographics, funding cuts, and low salaries. Lecturer salaries are based on a fixed professor salary base (unchanged at 554,400 HUF/month from 2018 to 2023 despite high inflation), lower than industry or public administration managers. Doctorate holders in academia earn less than business sector graduates until their late 30s; lifetime earnings are below the national average and only slightly above public sector levels. International salary ratios between ranks align broadly, but assistant lecturer ratios are below international practice. Hungary ranks low in doctoral student numbers (53rd worldwide share, 47th per capita), which correlates with scientific output. The study concludes that illiberal policies since 2010 halted massification, and low earnings discourage the best candidates from academia, risking future higher education and research capacity.

The Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards annually recognise accountants’ work in private and public sectors. The event includes dinner, awards by Sarah Heaney, entertainment by Britain’s Got Talent act DNA. Tickets: £1,200 for a table of ten, £1,440 for a table of twelve, £132 per person; plus VAT.

He says Detroit was his first team, which made the semifinals twice, and he has fond memories. He was excited when traded to Washington, but the move didn’t work and the team struggled. He believes in the current roster, is excited to return, mentions teammates Steve and Kocur, and notes his first trade was a shock and difficult.

Azerbaijan plans to boost honey exports, forecasting demand to rise to 2–2.5 million tonnes by 2020‑2022 from 1.5 million. Its organic honey sold at 8–8.5 k USD/tonne, with 6 tonnes exported last year; organic honey accounts for 15‑20% of demand, especially in China and Japan. Agriculture ministry will propose increased state support for beekeeping.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers’ social‑media posts commenting on the fatal shooting of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Commissioner Mike Morath described the remarks as “reprehensible and inappropriate” and said his agency would review posts to determine whether license‑sanctionable conduct occurred. Governor Greg Abbott supported the move, stating the posts could amount to incitement. Legal experts and public‑education advocates argue the investigations infringe on teachers’ First Amendment rights, noting that public‑school employees retain free‑speech protections when speaking in a personal capacity unless their comments cause a significant workplace disruption. One example cited involved a teacher who allegedly called Kirk’s death “karma.” Experts say the state would need to meet a high legal bar to prove the posts endorsed or promoted violence, and that widespread outrage alone does not constitute disruption. Critics, including the Texas American Federation of Teachers, characterize the probe as a “witch hunt” that could chill open discussion on public matters. The Education Agency has not responded to questions about how it will weigh First Amendment protections.

Marc Ó Sé says an injury-free James O'Donoghue could be a huge boost for Kerry this summer. O'Donoghue scored nine points in last Sunday's win over Clare in his return to action. Ó Sé believes O'Donoghue will be a tough challenge for defenders, and having him and Paul Geaney both performing well would be difficult for any defense to handle.

Bonds are debt securities issued by a borrower to raise capital; investors receive periodic interest payments and repayment of principal at maturity. A bond trading strategy is a systematic plan to buy or sell bonds with objectives such as capital preservation, income generation, or appreciation. Strategies include yield‑curve, duration, credit‑spread, tactical asset allocation, seasonal, price‑action and inter‑market approaches, and they differ by time horizon, risk tolerance and market conditions. Common mistakes in bond trading include insufficient market knowledge, over‑reliance on historical data, poor risk management, chasing yield without assessing credit risk, misjudging interest‑rate moves, lack of diversification, inflexibility and emotional biases. Interest rates have an inverse relationship with bond prices; rising rates push bond prices down and falling rates push them up, influencing strategies such as riding the yield curve or adjusting duration. Bonds provide diversification and typically low correlation with equities; backtests of a 20‑year Treasury ETF (TLT) show seasonal strategies can more than double buy‑and‑hold returns while being invested only about 60 % of the time. Combining TLT strategies with S&P 500 strategies improves annual returns and reduces drawdowns, illustrating the complementary benefit of bond strategies. Bond strategies can be automated using algorithmic systems that analyze market data, trends and economic indicators, though human oversight remains necessary. Day trading bonds is possible but less volatile than stocks and focuses on liquid government securities. For beginners, a simple strategy is dollar‑cost averaging, investing fixed amounts regularly to reduce the impact of market fluctuations.

Enron is in advanced talks to sell its Portland General Electric utility to Northwest Natural Gas for about $1.8 billion in cash and stock, with Northwest assuming roughly $1 billion in debt, which would give Enron a minority stake in Northwest. The discussions are delicate and face financing challenges; a deal could be announced soon. This follows a failed sale to Sierra Pacific Resources earlier in 2001. Northwest Natural confirmed the discussions. Enron is also cutting 500 jobs in Europe, about 10% of its European workforce. In India, Enron's $388 million sale of offshore oil and gas fields to BG Group may fail due to operatorship disputes with ONGC and Reliance. Tata Power is considering buying Enron's 65% stake in Dabhol Power Company, with a final decision expected in three weeks, while BSES will not buy the stake. Moody's commented on Tata Power's potential purchase. Meanwhile, Northwest Natural increased its quarterly dividend.

Microsoft Corporation filed an 8‑K on July 1 2020 announcing the retirement of Frank H. Brod as Chief Accounting Officer (CAO) effective July 31 2020, remaining through September 30 2020 to aid transition. The company appointed Alice L. Jolla, age 54, as Corporate Vice President and CAO effective the same date. Jolla has been Corporate Controller since 2014 and previously held senior accounting roles. In connection with her appointment, Jolla will receive a $1.5 million stock award vesting 6.25% quarterly under the 2017 Stock Plan.

Bitcoin fell below $8,000 since November, recovering most of the day’s losses. Since its record high of $19,511 on Dec 18 after regulated futures contracts, it has lost over half its value. Concerns include regulatory threats in India, South Korea, China and the US, a $500M theft at Japanese exchange Coincheck, and Facebook’s ad ban. Japanese authorities raided Coincheck’s offices. Analysts warned of further losses; Nouriel Roubini called Bitcoin “the mother of all bubbles.” Bitcoin is down ~21% for the week; Ripple, Ether and Litecoin each fell at least 18%.

Roseanne’s reboot was canceled after a racist tweet by its creator, and President Trump criticized ABC, saying CEO Bob Iger called Valerie Jarrett to apologize for the tweet but did not call him to apologize for negative statements about him on ABC. Iger, whose company Disney owns ABC, had previously quit Trump’s advisory council over the Paris climate accord and called Trump’s DACA decision cruel. Democratic lawmakers responded to Trump’s tweet, and Jarrett said Iger apologized and described the incident as a teaching moment, noting that the tone set by the president influences behavior.

Best Hope Services plans Nigeria’s first online trade exhibition in May to promote innovations by local inventors, scholars and entrepreneurs, letting exhibitors showcase worldwide without a venue and visitors attend from home. Prof. Joseph Mba says the e‑fair will cover expo, connect, trade and events across sectors like technology, automobiles and electronics, urging registration before May 1.

Microsoft is developing Windows 10 Polaris, a modular version built on Windows Core OS that runs only UWP apps from the Microsoft Store, unlike traditional desktop applications. Polaris will use CShell, a new interface replacing the legacy shell from Windows 95, allowing Windows to scale across devices while removing redundant features. Legacy applications won't work, but Microsoft is exploring remote virtualization to run old programs. Expected release is 2019.

The passage says the US and China share interests in peace, trade (~$3.5 billion) and technology, and both are concerned about the Soviet military buildup. Chinese leaders favor US strength but differ on Taiwan. Five Far East principles are outlined: a strategic partnership with China; peace and economic growth with Japan, PRC, ROK and Taiwan; coordinated resistance to aggression; and US‑Taiwan relations under the Taiwan Relations Act. The Act, enacted by Congress, commits the US to maintaining peace and friendly ties with Taiwan and mainland China, treats non‑peaceful resolution of Taiwan’s future as a threat, permits defensive arms sales to Taiwan, and requires US personnel to administer relations via the American Institute in Taiwan with congressional funding and oversight.

Researchers at the Institute of Synthetic Polymer Materials of the Russian Academy of Sciences, MIPT, and other institutions investigated how the molecular regularity (isotacticity) of polypropylene and its thermal treatment influence mechanical properties. Isotacticity, measured by the abundance of pentads—five‑unit isotactic segments—determines the formation of cross‑linked crystalline regions that stiffen the material. Polypropylene samples with isotacticities of 25 %, 29 %, 50 %, 72 %, 78 %, 82 % and >95 % were prepared as 0.5–0.7 mm films using two cooling methods: quenching in ice water and slow cooling at 3 °C min⁻¹. Tensile testing at 10 mm min⁻¹ revealed that elastic modulus depends on both the degree of crystallinity and the thermal history; slower cooling produces different crystallite shapes. Higher isotacticity increases crystallite content, raising the elastic modulus and overall strength. The results enable the synthesis of polypropylene with preset properties ranging from elastic to hard, as reported in Polymer.

Up to 200 Japanese or Asian American students and young professionals (ages 18‑25) will be selected for the JACL Kakehashi Program, a nine‑day trip to Japan (Dec 13‑20 or March 12‑20, 2018) with cultural activities and a homestay. Applications close Oct 9 for Trip 1 and Jan 2, 2018 for Trip 2; Japanese nationals are ineligible.

Wal‑Mart Stores Inc is bidding for clothing retailer Bonobos, its fourth acquisition of a small online clothing‑and‑accessories brand since early 2017, in a push to regain ground against Amazon.com in the fast‑growing online fashion market and to reach younger, millennial shoppers who rarely shop on Walmart.com. The company, the world’s largest brick‑and‑mortar clothing retailer with 2016 sales exceeding $23 billion, generates only about 3 percent of its total sales online and is targeting 20‑30 percent online sales growth in the second half of this year. Wal‑Mart has previously bought ShoeBuy (footwear and apparel), Moosejaw (outdoor wear) and ModCloth (women’s clothing). Analysts say the deals are currently too small to have a material impact, but they give Wal‑Mart a separate vehicle to grow with fashion brands. Amazon leads the U.S. online clothing and footwear market with $13 billion in sales in 2016 and is expected to triple its share of the U.S. apparel market over the next four years. Wal‑Mart has spent a total of $3.1 billion on e‑commerce and digital projects in its prior four fiscal years and has been investing in online retail for 15 years, yet it still lags far behind Amazon, according to retail consultants.

Materials modeling seeks atomistic structures matching experiment, but disordered materials pose challenges due to symmetry lack and statistical motif reproduction. Standard Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics methods lack experimental agreement guarantees. Reverse MC (RMC) and hybrid RMC (HRMC) improve agreement but face computational limits (few thousand atoms, billions of energy evaluations) and may produce unphysical structures. Previous MD attempts with experimental potentials suffered from poor scaling, inaccurate gradients, and neglected thermal effects. Molecular Augmented Dynamics (MAD) introduces an O(N) modified MD method using a Hamiltonian combining kinetic energy, interatomic potential, and experimental potential to efficiently generate ab-initio accurate structures matching experimental data with analytical gradients accounting for thermal broadening.

1976 AMA 500cc National Motocross at Moto‑Masters, Mexico, NY: Husqvarna’s Kent Howerton won, Yamaha’s Bob Hannah second, Suzuki’s Tony DiStefano third. 1982 High Point 250 National: 17‑year‑old Yamaha rider Ricky Johnson won; Honda took 1‑2 in the 500cc class, while Suzuki’s Alan King and Kent Howerton finished second and third in Suzuki’s last official participation. The "Drive & Kick" offense is a three-player weave using a 3-2 spread alignment. It involves dribble penetration to the basket for layups, with passing back outside and replacing positions when defenders deny penetration. The continuous action can run time off the clock and includes corner help and back cut options when defenses sag or zone.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an 8th‑generation data‑center GPU based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture. It features a GA100 chip with 54.2 billion transistors fabricated on TSMC’s 7 nm process, 108 streaming multiprocessors (SMs) each containing four third‑generation Tensor Cores, 64 FP32 CUDA cores per SM (6,912 total), 40 GB of HBM2 memory (1555 GB/s bandwidth), and a 40 MB L2 cache (2.3× the L2 bandwidth of V100). New Tensor Core data types include TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary, delivering up to 10× the FP32 FMA throughput of V100 (20× with sparsity), 2.5× FP16 mixed‑precision performance (5× with sparsity), and up to 20× INT8 inference performance with sparsity. The A100 introduces fine‑grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) that doubles Tensor Core throughput. Memory subsystems include ECC‑protected HBM2, partitioned L2 cache with residency controls, and compute data compression providing up to 4× DRAM/L2 bandwidth improvement. Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) allows the A100 to be securely partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU instances with separate L2 slices and memory controllers, enabling multi‑tenant and QoS guarantees for cloud service providers. Third‑generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total bandwidth (12 links × 25 GB/s) versus 300 GB/s for V100, and PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe bandwidth to 31.5 GB/s per direction. CUDA 11 adds hardware‑accelerated task‑graph launch, asynchronous copy to shared memory, asynchronous barriers, and L2 cache residency controls. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting MIG to provide up to 56 isolated accelerators per system for heterogeneous AI, HPC, and data‑analytics workloads.

The Housing Authority of Santa Barbara won a Gold Nugget Award at the Pacific Coast Builders Conference for Bradley Studios, a 54‑unit affordable development completed in 2012. Designed in a Craftsman style, it replaced blighted buildings and houses residents earning under 60 % of area median income. Services include mental health treatment, addiction counseling, job training and life‑skills classes. McGillivray Construction built it and Peikert Group Architects designed it.

In cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) patients from Sri Lanka, Brazil, and India, spatial transcriptomics identified myeloid cell-rich niches expressing IDO1 and CD274 (PD-L1) in the papillary dermis. Neighbourhood analysis revealed that these niches involved interactions between IDO1+/CD274+ myeloid cells, CD8+ memory T cells, and regulatory T cells (Tregs). A molecular signature including IL32, CXCL9, CCL18, and other cytokines was associated with these niches, with a core set of five genes (IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, FTH1) common across different dermal leishmaniasis forms. High abundance of IL-32+ CD8+ T cells correlated with slower rate of cure following treatment, suggesting these cells contribute to immunosuppressive microenvironments that may restrain immune-dependent chemotherapy.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill called on vaccine manufacturers to develop monovalent measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines to replace the combined MMR shot, proposing separate injections at different appointments. He referenced a post by President Trump but provided no scientific rationale. Outside experts say splitting the vaccine lacks evidence, could leave children more vulnerable, and is logistically impractical because monovalent vaccines are not currently licensed in the United States. A 2017 study found higher series completion with combination vaccines (69%) than with single‑antigen vaccines (50%). No evidence shows separate administration improves safety or efficacy; the proposal echoes the discredited Andrew Wakefield autism claim. Developing monovalent versions would require new clinical trials and FDA approval, likely taking years. The MMR vaccine has been used for over half a century with minimal side effects, though it carries a small increased risk of febrile seizure (about 1 per 3,000‑4,000 doses). Experts warn the administration’s rhetoric could lower vaccination rates, resulting in more disease and deaths.

MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers are 32-bit MCUs based on Arm Cortex-M0+, operating up to 32 MHz with up to 64 KB flash and 8 KB SRAM. They support five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with two power domains (PD1, PD0) to balance performance and power. Key peripherals include a 12‑bit 1.6 Msps ADC, comparator with 8‑bit reference DAC, temperature sensor, DMA with 3 channels, multiple timers (advanced, general‑purpose, watchdog), and communication interfaces (3 UART, 1 SPI, 2 I2C) supporting protocols like LIN, IrDA, DALI, and SMBus. Additional features include CRC‑16 accelerator, flash memory with up to 100 000 program/erase cycles, GPIO up to 45 pins, and an event manager for peripheral interconnections. The devices include debug support via Serial Wire Debug (SWD) and are provided with factory constants for calibration and device identification.

The study assessed empathy among 206 university teachers at University G, Spain, using the Spanish Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI). Overall empathy was above the theoretical midpoint, with high perspective‑taking, fantasy and empathic concern, and moderate personal distress. Female teachers scored significantly higher across all dimensions. No significant differences were found by degree programme, campus, contract status or teaching experience, though prior non‑university teaching experience was linked to higher scores on perspective‑taking, fantasy and empathic concern, and exclusively university experience to higher personal distress. Results suggest a balanced empathic profile in educators, highlight gender differences, and align with UN Sustainable Development Goal 4, while noting limited generalisability due to sample size and potential response bias.

The Department advises against dividing the General Assembly into four sections, fearing regional substructures would hinder security; decentralization proposals should be postponed until the organization is established. The Bearish Engulfing candlestick pattern consists of two candles: a small bullish candle followed by a larger bearish candle whose body completely engulfs the first candle’s body, opening above the first candle’s high and closing below its low. It appears after an uptrend, indicating a shift from bullish to bearish sentiment and a potential reversal from an uptrend to a downtrend. Traders use the pattern to identify entry and exit points: long‑position holders may close or lower stop‑loss orders, while traders seeking short positions may enter the market, placing a stop‑loss above the high of the first (white) candle and targeting a support level below current price. The recommended stop‑loss placement is above the white candle’s high.

The pattern’s win rate in the stock market (S&P 500) is reported between 55 % and 65 %, based on backtesting of historical data. Its reliability improves when confirmed by other technical indicators (e.g., moving averages, RSI, MACD), a change in market momentum, a support‑break or volume decline, or when it appears in a long‑term uptrend. Combining the pattern with filters such as an RSI reading above 60 can increase average profit per trade (example: from 0.73 % to 0.88 % on S&P 500 trades). The pattern occurs frequently: 311 instances have been recorded in the S&P 500 from 1993 to the present, making it the third most common of 75 candlestick patterns.

Risk management when using the pattern includes using stop‑loss orders, applying risk/reward ratios, proper position sizing, diversification, hedging, and maintaining a clear risk‑management plan. Potential risks are false signals, dependence on market conditions, increased volatility, and magnified losses when leverage is used.

The Bearish Engulfing pattern is similar to other bearish reversal patterns—dark‑cloud cover, evening star, and bearish harami—which also signal a potential trend reversal but differ in the specific candle formations and the strength of the bearish sentiment they indicate. Like all candlestick tools, it should be used in conjunction with other technical analysis methods and backtesting to validate its effectiveness.

The 50 EMA strategy is a technical analysis method that uses the 50‑day exponential moving average to determine trend direction and to generate buy and sell signals. The indicator is typically plotted on medium‑term charts such as the 4‑hour or daily time frame. An upward‑sloping 50 EMA with the price above it signals an uptrend (long entry), while a downward‑sloping 50 EMA with the price below signals a downtrend (short entry). Traders often confirm signals with additional oscillators such as RSI or MACD. Entry rules: go long when price crosses above the 50 EMA and exit when price falls below it; go short when price crosses below the 50 EMA and exit when price rises above it.  

Backtests of the basic 50 EMA crossover on the S&P 500 cash index from 1960 show annual returns of about 6.8% versus 7.3% for buy‑and‑hold, with a maximum drawdown of 32% compared with 56% for buy‑and‑hold. Adding a secondary indicator as a filter improves performance: a strategy using QQQ (Nasdaq‑100) produced a CAGR of 11.5% while being invested only 27% of the time, a 73% win rate, and a 22% maximum drawdown; a similar strategy on SPY (S&P 500) generated an 8.9% annual return with a 16% drawdown, invested 29% of the time. Tests on long‑term Treasury bond ETF (TLT) show modest gains (0.18% per trade).  

Advantages of the strategy include simplicity, clear signals, and suitability for medium‑term trend capture. Disadvantages include the need for confirmation with other tools and the importance of backtesting. Recommended risk management includes stop‑loss and take‑profit orders, maintaining a favorable risk‑reward ratio, and diversifying the portfolio. Platforms such as TradeStation and Amibroker are commonly used to implement the strategy.

AMD Secure RNG Library provides a high‑level API for accessing the hardware random number generators built into AMD Zen processors via the x86 RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. It offers functions to retrieve single 16‑, 32‑, or 64‑bit random values and to fetch arrays of 32‑ or 64‑bit values or arbitrary byte streams, with a user‑specified retry count for handling possible hardware failures. The library includes detection routines (is_RDRAND_supported, is_RDSEED_supported) that use CPUID to verify instruction support. Because the underlying read is a memory‑mapped I/O operation, it is slower than pure software PRNGs; for latency‑sensitive cryptography a hybrid approach can seed a software PRNG with a hardware value to combine security and performance. The API is designed to simplify low‑level instruction handling, making it suitable for cryptographic key generation, Monte‑Carlo simulations, communication protocols, gaming and other high‑performance computing applications.

In response to the Trump administration’s threats, many liberal nonprofits are preparing contingency measures such as surrendering 501(c)(3) status, relocating abroad, setting up emergency funds, merging with other groups and preparing legal challenges. KNH is Kenya’s national teaching and referral hospital at the apex of a six‑tier health system. Orthopaedic wards have recorded high bed occupancy (142 % in 2018, 138 % in 2019, 116 % in 2020), exceeding the hospital’s overall occupancy. On 1 July 2021 KNH began enforcing the Kenya Health Sector Referral Guidelines (2014), requiring written referral letters and prior concurrence for all referrals.

A pre‑posttest study compared 5‑month periods before (February–June 2021) and after (August–December 2021) guideline enforcement. A total of 468 orthopaedic facility referrals were abstracted: 220 before and 248 after. Data were collected from three admission points (Accident & Emergency, Orthopaedic Outpatient Clinic, Corporate Outpatient Care).

Most referrals originated from Nairobi County and its neighbours; over half were from government facilities and roughly half from Tier 2–4 facilities. After enforcement the overall number of referring facilities rose, but the increase was not statistically significant. Stratified analysis by tier showed a significant reduction in direct referrals from Tier II and Tier III facilities and an increase in referrals from Tier IV, V and VI facilities. Approximately 43 health facilities stopped referring patients directly to KNH; most were private (≈ 70 %) and lower‑tier (≈ 80 %). Multivariable analysis indicated that human‑resource capacity and availability, infrastructure, orthopaedic equipment and implant availability, patient preference, and financial considerations were the main factors associated with referrals. Private‑facility referrals were more driven by patient preference, whereas government‑facility referrals were more influenced by financial considerations.

The study concludes that enforcement of the national referral guidelines reduced lower‑tier facility referrals and caused many private facilities to cease direct referrals. The identified factors highlight barriers to appropriate referral behaviour. Recommendations include regular sensitisation of health facilities on referral guidelines, strengthening human‑resource capacity, developing standard operating procedures, and educating facilities on KNH’s role as a premier referral centre.

The 1‑2‑2 zone is a defensive alignment with a point at the top of the circle, two wings at the elbows, and two baseline players just above the blocks. It is especially useful against outside‑shooting teams, fast‑break situations, and late‑game leads because defenders are already in trapping positions. When the ball moves, each defender follows a prescribed shift: for instance, with the ball in the left corner X5 guards the ball, X4 covers the low post, X3 drops to the weak‑side baseline, X2 cuts off the corner‑pass, and X1 defends the high post. Comparable patterns are given for the left wing, middle, right wing, and right corner. The baseline pair works in unison, the wings operate opposite each other and cover weak‑side rebounding, and the point guards the ball out front and protects the high‑post area. Optional adjustments include: the wing may stay out to deny the return pass or drop to assist the low post; a corner trap can be executed by the wing and X4 while X1 cuts off the return pass and X2 guards the high post; on the first pass the 1‑2‑2 can switch to a 2‑1‑2, with X3 moving to the middle, X1 guarding the ball, X2 shifting, and X4 moving out; and the zone can be extended into a half‑ or full‑court press because defenders are already positioned for trapping.

Probiotics are reported to aid digestion, immune function, and nutrient absorption, and may also protect the liver from drug‑ and alcohol‑induced damage. Researchers at Emory University gave mice a diet enriched with Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) for two weeks before administering high doses of acetaminophen. The LGG‑fed mice showed an improved antioxidant response that protected the liver from oxidative damage caused by the drug. The study identified the protein Nrf2 as a key regulator of this protective effect, indicating a specific molecular mechanism. Although results in mice are promising, further human studies are required. Probiotics are not a substitute for medical treatment and should be used under a doctor’s guidance.

Enron CEO Jeff Skilling attributed the company's stock decline on March 28 to market trends against high price-to-earnings ratios, while analysts cited specific issues like broadband valuation and telecom weakness. Enron reported strong 2000 performance, rewarding Chairman Kenneth Lay with a $7 million bonus and Skilling with a $5.6 million bonus. Enron pursued international growth, presenting a thermal power plant proposal in Aomori, Japan, and advancing a power project in Lagos, Nigeria, as Nigeria announced plans to unbundle its state electricity monopoly. The United Nations 2030 Agenda and the Incheon Declaration set a vision for education by 2030, with Sustainable Development Goal 4 highlighting education as both a target and a prerequisite for the other sixteen goals. Despite a dramatic worldwide expansion of education over the past seventy years, the global state of education in 2020 fell short on three dimensions: quantitative participation, quality, and equality. Before the COVID‑19 pandemic, 258 million school‑age children (17 % of the cohort) were not attending school; quality problems were evident across input, process, output and product components, exemplified by low numeracy in England and persistent salary gaps between men and women with identical qualifications in Saudi Arabia; and stark inequalities persisted across socio‑economic, gender and ethnic lines.

The pandemic caused the closure of institutions serving roughly 91 % of the world’s students, compelling a shift to distance and online learning. This transition widened gaps for already disadvantaged learners, as shown by South African data: 29 % of learners lost all contact with teachers, 79 % of fee‑dependent schools could not collect fees, and 51 % could not send homework. At the same time, the crisis forced education systems to adopt digital technologies despite the sector’s historical inertia.

Comparative and International Education (CIE) studies education systems within societal contexts and compares them, positioning the field to investigate pandemic‑driven disruptions and technology use. Such comparative research can generate recommendations for leveraging technology to meet SDG 4 goals. However, CIE faces identified weaknesses: unresponsiveness to new opportunities, a “black‑box” over‑emphasis on external factors at the expense of classroom practice, lack of an indigenous theoretical framework, marginal presence in universities (especially in initial teacher education), persistent Northern dominance, and limited impact on policy, practice and academic discourse.

The paper concludes that achieving the 2030 education vision requires overcoming substantial obstacles, and that CIE is pivotal to harnessing technological advances, recovering from pandemic‑related setbacks and building improved education systems that surpass pre‑pandemic levels.

In Closson v. Billman et al. (1904), a contractor hired to build a house and furnish materials failed to pay for lumber, resulting in liens against the property. The appellant (Closson) was a guarantor, not surety, on the contractor's bond. The court held the guarantor was liable for the material liens because the bond required the contractor to "build, construct, and complete" the residence according to the contract, which obligated him to pay for materials and deliver the house free of liens. Since the guaranty was executed contemporaneously with the transaction, notice of acceptance was not required. The burden was on the guarantor to plead and prove omission to give notice of default and resulting damage. The judgment for defendants was affirmed.

NVIDIA has developed several shading advancements: Mesh Shading moves geometry processing from CPU to GPU, enabling more objects per scene; Variable Rate Shading (VRS) dynamically controls shading rate to improve frame rate by reducing work in low-detail regions; Texture-Space Shading caches results in memory for reuse; and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) extends stereo rendering to support multiple views with different origins in a single pass.

Systems and methods for route planning for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) based on topological maps. The system obtains a topological map and preprocesses it by modifying node information based on motion status of other vehicles (static or moving) occupying nodes in the map. Start and destination nodes are determined for the current AGV, and total costs are calculated for nodes between them using formulas incorporating weight values, distance costs, turn costs, and Manhattan distance. Route planning is performed using algorithms like A-star. The system includes modules for location obtaining, map obtaining, motion status obtaining, and route determination. Preprocessing involves first preprocessing for static AGVs (modifying node information within preset regions around them) and second preprocessing for moving AGVs (also modifying planned routes they haven't passed). This ensures routes avoid collisions with other AGVs. The system uses binary heap structures and open/closed sets for efficient path finding, with costs determined by f(n)=g(n)+h(n) formulas where costs account for weight, distance from parent nodes, and turn angles.

U.S. 1983 USSR policy calls for arms‑control standards—real reductions, equality, verifiability—including INF and START approach. Regionally, it proposes testing Soviet intentions on Afghanistan, strengthening U.S‑PRC dialogue, demanding Kampuchean settlement, pressing for Cuban withdrawal from Angola, warning about MiG deliveries to Nicaragua, and avoiding Middle‑East dialogue that gives Moscow a role. Human‑rights focus on private diplomacy to free prisoners, resolve family cases, increase Jewish emigration, and promote democracy in Poland/CSCE. Economic measures must avoid aiding Soviet military capability and be timed to strategy, possibly via Joint Commercial Commission contacts. Bilateral actions should be reciprocal, broaden access to Soviet society, and may include a cultural umbrella agreement. The dialogue process has four levels—summit, ministerial, ambassadorial and department‑level—aiming for a productive summit without premature commitment, possibly preceded by a China meeting. The conclusion says 1983 brings new challenges and opportunities, a sound policy foundation exists, an intensified dialogue will protect U.S. security while offering Soviets incentives, and continued tension would rest with Moscow if it fails to meet U.S. criteria.

W. T. Hay was adjudicated a voluntary bankrupt in 1915. Before bankruptcy he had conveyed real estate to his brother, who later conveyed an interest to Hay’s wife, Matilda. Deposit National Bank held a judgment against Hay, received a dividend in the bankruptcy, and after Hay’s discharge issued an execution on the property claimed to have been fraudulently transferred to his wife. The lower court stayed the execution as to Hay personally but refused to stay it as to the wife’s property. Hay appealed, arguing the bank had no right to execute. The Supreme Court held Hay lacked standing because he had no interest in the property and was not aggrieved; the questions of the bank’s right to proceed and the effect of a sheriff’s sale could be raised by his wife. The appeal was dismissed.

Delta offers a cyber risk assessment and support, and is a Canterbury Tech member. Samson has 12 years’ experience and a Bachelor of Commerce and Management from Lincoln University.
Ants in warmed milk create yogurt via bacterial acidification, traditional in Bulgaria and Turkey.

MacKenzie Scott’s latest round of donations includes a $42 million gift to 10,000 Degrees—her largest to that organization in its 45‑year history—supporting low‑income and largely non‑white students in the Bay Area, alongside tens of millions to Native Forward, the nation’s largest scholarship provider for Native students, and a $70 million contribution to UNCF for endowments at 37 historically Black colleges and universities. Over the past five years she has given more than $19 billion, with roughly $2 billion in 2024 alone to nearly 200 grantees focused on economic security, housing, jobs, child development, postsecondary education and health. Her philanthropy delivers large, unrestricted grants quickly and without conditions, allowing recipients to direct capital where needs are most immediate. In 2024 she introduced an open‑call process while preserving the surprise element, and has pledged to expand into mission‑aligned investments that mirror her grant priorities. She continues to emphasize trust‑based funding, repeat gifts to high‑performing organizations and endowment‑strengthening contributions for equity‑focused institutions.

Lisa Baird became NWSL commissioner on March 10, 2020. Within days, the COVID-19 pandemic forced the league to cancel preseason and evaluate contingency plans. Baird created multiple workstreams (medical, finance, competition format, host city, players, childcare, social justice) to develop a return-to-play strategy, resulting in the Challenge Cup held in Utah from June 27 to July 26, 2020—the first professional U.S. sports league to resume play during the pandemic. The league also staged a Fall Series with regional pods and secured broadcast deals with CBS and Twitch. Despite concerns about financial sustainability and player safety, the league achieved record viewership (up 493% over 2019), added new teams (Racing Louisville and Kansas City in 2021), and increased sponsorship revenue while navigating social justice issues and the departure of USWNT players to European clubs. The case examines Baird's leadership through the crisis, the NWSL's history (including failed predecessors WUSA and WPS), ongoing equal pay litigation, and future challenges including league rebrand, expansion, fan engagement, and CBA negotiations.

This study reports the synthesis of Cu-doped NiO thin films using ultra-fast spray pyrolysis (1.5 minutes) for LPG gas sensing applications. XRD analysis confirmed successful Cu incorporation into the NiO lattice without changing the cubic crystal structure, with lattice parameters increasing from 4.18 to 4.20 Å and crystallite size decreasing from 21 to 20 nm. UV-Vis spectroscopy revealed a reduction in optical bandgap from 3.70 eV to 3.65 eV upon Cu doping, while Raman and photoluminescence analyses indicated increased defect density and structural disorder. Electrical measurements demonstrated enhanced gas sensitivity, with Cu-doped NiO showing significantly higher sensitivity (1.8) compared to undoped NiO (1.3) at 5V bias voltage, attributed to improved charge transport and surface reactivity.

The passage describes AMD's AGESA (AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture) software initialization framework for processor and platform boot sequences.

Key entry points manage boot phases from reset through OS handoff: AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization; AmdInitEarly handles early configuration including optional execution cache regions; AmdInitPost initializes system memory; AmdInitEnv performs full processor and platform configuration; AmdInitLate generates ACPI/DMI/SMBIOS tables; and AmdInitRtb performs late configuration before boot.

The software operates across two build methods: binary module distribution using indirect interfaces, and source integration where host environments incorporate source files. Build customization occurs through platform-specific options files and build control files for PEI and DXE phases.

Memory initialization uses cache-as-Ram techniques before main memory becomes available, with stack procedures provided for x86-64 architectures. The Platform Security Processor (PSP) handles initialization for newer APU families.

Host environment responsibilities include allocating buffers via AgesaAllocateBuffer, managing resets, reading SPD data, and executing code on application processors. Required call-outs enable memory allocation, deallocation, buffer location, reset control, and hardware-specific data retrieval.

Configuration options cover VRM settings, PCIe topology, FCH parameters, memory timing, ECC, interleaving, voltage regulation, and display settings for platform customization.

Alek Minassian, 25, has been charged with 10 counts of first‑degree murder for the Toronto rental‑van attack that killed 10 people and injured 15. He made his first court appearance, with prosecutors announcing the charges while he sat head‑shaved and looking down. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said the incident had not altered Canada’s national threat level or security preparations for the upcoming G7 summit, and he called on Canadians to remain united and true to their freedoms and values. A makeshift memorial of flowers and messages grew at the scene, and the Canadian flag was lowered to half‑staff at Parliament and Toronto city hall. The police officer who apprehended Minassian was praised for a peaceful arrest despite his shouts of “kill me” and claims of having a gun. Victims were being identified as the city mourned, and the incident shocked Toronto’s usually peaceful streets, a multicultural city of 2.8 million. The CN Tower was darkened in remembrance.

Improving farmers requires broad education linking theory to life, training executive ability and emphasizing labor dignity; organization like the Grange benefits them economically and socially. Oregon Health & Science University scientists are using somatic cell nuclear transfer to create human eggs. In 2022 they produced three mouse pups from lab eggs derived from adult mouse skin cells. A paper in Nature Communications reports that attempts to use the same method with human cells have been mostly unsuccessful, though the team developed a “mitomeiosis” step to reduce chromosome count and avoid double‑chromosome embryos. Lead researcher Mitalipov says the technique partially works and needs refinement before clinical testing, but he remains optimistic it could help treat infertility, prevent hereditary diseases and allow same‑sex couples to have genetically related children.

A new study suggests the brain chemical dopamine plays a key role in mother-child bonding. Researchers studied 19 mothers and their babies using video recordings and brain scans. Mothers who secreted more dopamine when viewing their own babies provided more responsive care and were more sensitive to their infants' needs. Previously, bonding was linked to oxytocin. The study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Researchers say this process likely continues throughout the lifespan and may also apply to other caregivers, though further research is needed.

Trauma is defined by SAMHSA as an experience perceived as harmful or threatening that can cause lasting negative effects on mental, physical, social, emotional, or spiritual well‑being. It may be individual or collective, direct or indirect (e.g., hearing about others’ trauma). Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are traumatic events occurring before age 18; estimates indicate 50–70 % of post‑secondary students have experienced at least one ACE, 30–50 % more than one, and 12–20 % four or more. Students’ trauma histories can manifest as poor attendance, reduced academic performance, lower self‑efficacy, isolation, and higher dropout rates. Behavioral cues that may signal a trauma response include increased absences, fidgeting, disrespect or aggression toward peers or instructors, dissociation, missed deadlines, communication barriers, distrust of authority, cognitive difficulties (attention, focus, memory), and social withdrawal. Environmental triggers such as abrupt changes in lighting or sound or instructors standing behind students can provoke distress, especially for survivors of assault.

Research on occupational therapy (OT) students shows that 44.6 % experienced trauma before OT school, 31.1 % both before and during, and 24 % during school; 93 % reported that trauma affected daily routines including rest, sleep, social participation, and education. A cross‑sectional study of master’s‑level OT students found low overall severity on the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire, yet about 28 % showed potential minimization or denial of childhood trauma.

SAMHSA’s Trauma‑Informed Care (TIC) framework outlines six core principles: safety, trustworthiness and transparency, peer support, collaboration and mutuality, empowerment and voice, and recognition of cultural, historical, and gender issues. The framework includes ten implementation domains: governance/leadership, training/workforce development, cross‑sector collaboration, financing, physical environment, engagement/involvement, screening/assessment/treatment services, progress monitoring/quality assurance, policy, and evaluation. Validated tools such as the Attitudes Related to Trauma‑Informed Care (ARTIC‑35) scale can assess faculty attitudes.

Studies of the PATH simulation‑based model (professional ACEs‑informed training for health professionals) with PT and OT students showed significant gains in self‑efficacy, hope, and knowledge about ACEs and TIC. Health‑and‑wellness coaching delivered by peers is proposed as a supportive strategy for student well‑being.

Current OT curricula rarely include trauma education; only 12 of 82 entry‑level OT programs surveyed reported trauma content, primarily in pediatrics and mental health courses. TIC educational strategies recommended for OT educators include seeking trauma‑informed professional development, using predictable and flexible pedagogical approaches, incorporating de‑escalation techniques, adding self‑care modules and statements to syllabi, providing advance notice of potentially triggering content, conducting regular check‑ins, ensuring equal participation opportunities, employing simulation‑based ACEs/TIC training, recognizing student strengths, offering timely and consistent communication, embedding self‑regulation activities, designing culturally respectful learning environments, and applying universal design principles.

Potential short‑term outcomes of TIC in OT education include students feeling supported, engaged, and satisfied; long‑term outcomes may be increased retention, graduation rates, and degree attainment. Authors note that up to 75 % of students may have experienced trauma and encourage OT educators to evaluate their practices and policies to prevent re‑traumatization and to foster a supportive, empowering learning environment.

Robert Stuart has spent almost two years investigating the BBC Panorama documentary “Saving Syria’s Children.” The documentary aired a segment on 29 August 2013 claiming a Syrian fighter jet dropped a napalm‑type bomb on the playground of Urm al‑Kubra school near Aleppo while the UK Parliament debated military action. Footage of casualties arriving at Atareb hospital formed the basis of the documentary. Stuart’s analysis highlights multiple discrepancies: medical professionals question the injuries shown; reported victim numbers vary from 25 to 50 among Dr Ahsan, journalist Ian Pannell and the Hand in Hand for Syria website; and the time of the alleged attack differs by up to six hours among sources. The BBC crew’s accounts give conflicting times (around 5:30 versus “between 3 and 5”). Two British doctors appearing in the film have backgrounds in military service and pro‑rebel activities. The passage claims the combination of questionable injuries, inconsistent numbers, and timing issues suggests the footage may be fabricated and raises concerns about the reliability of similar narratives.

Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) that detect Plasmodium falciparum histidine‑rich protein 2 (PfHRP2) are the primary diagnostic tool for P. falci​parum malaria. Increasing prevalence of pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 gene deletions causes false‑negative HRP2‑based RDTs, threatening global malaria control. As of 2023, WHO reports pfhrp2/3 deletions in 40 of 47 surveyed countries, with false‑negative rates up to 80 % in the worst‑affected settings. Existing non‑HRP2 RDTs lack sensitivity or combination formats for P. falci​parum/P. vivax detection, and many countries have no WHO‑prequalified alternatives, creating a need for global risk assessments.

The study used a previously published individual‑based P. falci​parum transmission model to simulate selection and spread of pfhrp2 deletions. The model tracks infection dynamics in humans and mosquitoes, incorporates treatment‑seeking behavior, RDT use, non‑adherence to RDT results, microscopy use, HRP3 cross‑reactivity on HRP2 RDTs, and parasite fitness costs. Model parameters were sourced from WHO reports, Demographic and Health Surveys, Malaria Indicator Surveys, Malaria Atlas Project maps, Global Fund data, and a literature review. For pfhrp3 dynamics, the analysis relied on WHO Malaria Threat Maps, estimated the probability of HRP3 cross‑reactivity, and quantified linkage disequilibrium between pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 deletions.

From WHO Malaria Threat Maps, 63.5 % (95 % CI 55.1‑71.1 %) of pfhrp2‑deleted samples globally also carried pfhrp3 deletions; in Africa the proportion was 61.2 % (95 % CI 47.9‑72.7 %). The normalized linkage disequilibrium coefficient D′ was 0.762, indicating strong positive association between the two deletions. A significant inverse relationship was found between malaria prevalence and the frequency of pfhrp2 deletions among pfhrp3‑deleted samples (p < 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶), with lower prevalence regions showing higher deletion frequencies.

Parameter estimation by fitting the model to Eritrea and Ethiopia data yielded a relative fitness of pfhrp2‑deleted parasites of 96.4 % (95 % CrI 95.8‑97.0 %), implying a ~3.6 % fitness cost, and an estimated probability of 29.0 % (95 % CI 20.0‑45.0 %) that an infection with only pfhrp2 deletions would still test positive on an HRP2 RDT due to HRP3 cross‑reactivity.

The analysis identified malaria prevalence as the most important driver of selection for pfhrp2 deletions, with strongest effects below 20 % slide prevalence in 2‑10‑year‑olds. Treatment‑cascade factors (RDT non‑adherence, microscopy use, HRP3 cross‑reactivity) had similar effect sizes.

Two risk scores were produced. The “Innate Risk Score” measures the inherent speed at which false‑negative HRP2 RDTs among clinical cases would rise from 1 % to 5 % if HRP2 RDTs were the sole diagnostic, assuming deletions are already present at 1 % genotype frequency. The “Prospective Risk Score” incorporates current deletion prevalence from WHO data, RDT brand usage, and models geographic spread using a simple export rule (deletions spread from a region once ≥ 25 % of clinical cases are affected). Under the Innate scenario, 73 of 106 modelled countries have at least one first‑administrative unit predicted to reach the 5 % threshold within 20 years; high‑risk regions are concentrated in low‑transmission areas, especially the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa (e.g., Senegal, Mali). Countries with ≥ 50 % of administrative units classified as high innate risk include Eritrea (100 %), Ethiopia (100 %), Gambia, Madagascar, Namibia, South Sudan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Ghana, and others.

Under the Prospective scenario, 29 of 49 countries have at least one administrative unit predicted to reach or already exceed the 5 % threshold within 20 years. Countries with ≥ 50 % high prospective risk include Djibouti (100 %), Eritrea (100 %), Ethiopia (100 %), Senegal (100 %), Zambia, Kenya, and others. The model predicts that deletions will spread southward from the Horn of Africa through East Africa and increase in West Africa.

Uncertainty analysis shows that malaria prevalence uncertainty is the largest contributor to variation in risk predictions; for example, prevalence estimates for Yobe, Nigeria range from 10 % to 40 %, shifting risk classification from marginal to high. Interactive risk maps and a web‑based tool (DeletionRiskExplorer) allow exploration of scenarios and parameter impacts.

Key limitations include the simplistic model of inter‑regional spread, high parameter uncertainty (especially prevalence and fitness costs), constant prevalence assumption, possible non‑equilibrium dynamics of pfhrp2/3 loci, and reliance on cross‑sectional survey data that may be unrepresentative. The authors note that additional longitudinal surveillance data are needed to refine predictions.

In conclusion, the study provides an updated global risk model for pfhrp2/3 deletions, confirming a substantial threat to malaria control if HRP2‑based RDTs remain the primary diagnostic. Malaria prevalence is the dominant driver of selection, and many African countries—particularly in the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa—are at high risk of rapid increase in false‑negative results. The risk scores and interactive tool can guide prioritization of surveillance, transition to alternative RDTs, and future research and policy decisions.

Scientists fused human skin cells with enucleated donor eggs using somatic cell nuclear transfer, then combined fertilization with the molecule roscovitine to trigger a meiosis‑like reduction of chromosomes. The aim was to create functional human eggs that could eventually help treat infertility, including for women who have lost eggs and for same‑sex male couples. Some fertilized eggs formed early embryos, but none achieved the correct chromosome complement; many stopped developing before reaching the blastocyst stage. The technique is currently inefficient and high‑risk, and researchers estimate it will take at least a decade before clinical testing could be considered. A limitation is that the method requires donor egg cells, unlike other reprogramming approaches that avoid this need. The work provides proof‑of‑concept that human skin cells can be induced to halve their chromosomes, but further development and regulatory approvals, especially in the United States, would be required before any clinical application.

The lecture introduces a mechanical model for protein folding using fixed angle linkages, where protein backbones are modeled as chains with fixed edge lengths and angles. Four key problems are discussed: span (maximum and minimum distances between endpoints), flattening (existence of a flat configuration without self-intersection), flat state connectivity (reachability between flat states), and locked chains (configurations that cannot be unfolded). Finding minimum or maximum flat span is NP-hard, while orthogonal chains allow linear-time solutions for max span. Determining flat state existence is NP-hard. Whether all open chains are flat state connected remains an open problem, but positive results exist for monotone and obtuse chains. Locked configurations are known, but it is unknown if equilateral equiangular obtuse chains can be locked. A model of protein production via ribosomes as a cone is presented, showing that chains producible from such a cone are in one connected component and are flat state connected, and can be canonicalized into a configuration within a smaller cone. The FedEx and momento methods are used to prove these properties. While these results provide algorithmic insights into protein folding, the actual biological mechanism remains unresolved.

In late July 2001, California's energy crisis remained a critical issue. Governor Gray Davis faced scrutiny over his administration’s handling of the crisis. The Securities and Exchange Commission launched a preliminary inquiry into whether energy consultants advising Davis used inside information to trade stocks of power companies. Five consultants were fired for possible conflicts of interest, and Davis’s press secretary, Steve Maviglio, admitted purchasing $12,000 worth of Calpine Corp. stock, prompting calls for his termination from Republican rival Bill Jones. California’s energy situation improved due to cool weather, conservation, a recession, and federal price caps, but the state remained burdened by $43 billion in long-term power contracts deemed too expensive. Southern California Edison sought a state bailout, but legislative efforts stalled amid opposition and questions about Davis’s ties to Edison, which had contributed significantly to his campaign. Consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani, hired to improve Davis’s image, also worked for Edison and faced conflict-of-interest criticism; they later agreed to forgo payment as part of a settlement. In San Francisco, voters were set to decide on measures to create public utility districts to replace Pacific Gas and Electric Co., which was in bankruptcy. Federal regulators ordered refunds for overpriced electricity, but the amount was reduced to under $4 billion, far less than the $9 billion sought, prompting Davis to plan an appeal. Texas moved toward launching its own electricity deregulation pilot program.

Gas colic, while the least severe form, is common and can progress to colon displacement or twisting if not addressed. It results from normal fermentation of dietary fiber in the hindgut; when gas cannot pass through the large colon’s twists, pain and distension occur. Inadequate forage consumption, stall confinement, stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, insufficient exercise, dehydration, and rapid changes in forage or feed are common causes. Two widespread management practices contribute: limiting forage disrupts normal digestion, leading to acid buildup, gorging, ulcers, and excessive gas; and confining horses to stalls reduces hindgut motility, allowing gas accumulation. Stress exacerbates inflammation and can damage the digestive tract; pasture turnout mitigates stress. Gradual feed transitions, prebiotic support, and consistent feeding of any new feed (e.g., bran mash) reduce risk. Supplements such as B vitamins, yeast products, and colostrum may aid gut health. Using slow‑feeder systems and providing continuous forage availability mirrors natural grazing and helps prevent gas colic.

Newark Police are seeking public help to locate nine suspects linked to seven unsolved crimes dating back to June 2016, including shootings, robberies, and a grocery store robbery. Tips can be submitted via a tip line, website, or app and may be confidential and rewarded.

It features a 6.2‑inch FHD+ notch display, Snapdragon 845, up to 8 GB RAM, dual rear cameras (12 MP + 8 MP), 8 MP front camera, Android 8.0 Oreo (upgradeable to Android P), 3300 mAh battery with fast and AI charging. In PEOPLE v HELZER (1978), the Michigan Supreme Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not a penalty enhancement for the principal charge. The Court ruled that defendants charged with sexual delinquency must be tried before a separate jury unless waived, and are entitled to 20 peremptory challenges for that jury due to the possible life sentence, while receiving only the number appropriate to the principal charge for the initial jury. The sexual delinquency charge must be included in the original indictment before trial begins, and no reference to it may be made to the jury trying the principal charge. The defendant's conviction on gross indecency was affirmed, but the case was remanded for a hearing on sexual delinquency before a separately empaneled jury with full peremptory challenges. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, arguing the sexual delinquency statute was unconstitutional for vagueness.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on March 27, 2017 reporting that underwriters (Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, Citi, Morgan Stanley and Barclays) exercised in full their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million aggregate principal of its 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022 (the “Option Notes”). The Option Notes were sold under a Form S‑3 registration statement and issued on March 30, 2017 pursuant to a Fourth Supplemental Indenture dated March 22, 2017. In connection with the issuance, Tesla entered additional note hedge transactions with the underwriters, paying approximately $26.6 million on March 30 to reduce potential dilution and offset cash payments on conversion. Tesla also entered warrant confirmations with the same counterparties, issuing Additional Warrants that permit the purchase of up to approximately 0.8 million shares of common stock at $655.00 per share, subject to anti‑dilution adjustments, for proceeds of about $6.9 million. The warrants are separate from the notes and were issued under a Section 4(a)(2) exemption. The filing includes a legal opinion (Exhibit 5.1) and references the form of call‑option and warrant confirmations.

Turing is NVIDIA’s latest GPU architecture that combines GDDR6 memory, enhanced L2 cache, lossless compression, and a redesigned memory interface to deliver roughly 50% effective bandwidth improvement over Pascal. The new display engine supports 8K at 60 Hz, HDR, and VESA DSC, while NVENC adds H.265 8K encoding and NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 decoding. Turing introduces hardware‑based VirtualLink over USB‑C for single‑cable VR headsets and expands Multi‑View Rendering for higher‑field‑of‑view VR. NVLink replaces the previous SLI bridge, providing up to 50 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth per link. Ray tracing is accelerated by dedicated RT Cores that perform BVH traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, enabling real‑time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization with ray‑traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. Advanced denoising reduces the number of rays required. AI features are delivered through the NGX stack, featuring Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS) for up to 2× performance at equivalent image quality, InPainting, AI Slow‑Mo, and AI Super Rez up‑scaling. New shader stages include Mesh Shading for large object counts, Variable Rate Shading for content‑adaptive and motion‑adaptive shading, Texture Space Shading for decoupled visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi‑View Rendering for single‑pass stereo and multi‑projection. Turing GPUs include Tensor Cores for AI inference and support RTX‑OPS, a workload‑based metric combining FP32, Tensor, RT, and INT32 throughputs. The architecture is implemented in three dies: TU102 (full‑featured, 12 GB GDDR6, 48 SMs, 6 MB L2, NVLink), TU104 (mid‑range, 8 GB, 40 SMs, NVLink), and TU106 (entry, 8 GB, 36 SMs, no NVLink). Products include GeForce RTX 2080 Ti/2080/2070, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX series. Overall, Turing integrates memory, display, VR, ray‑tracing, AI, and shading innovations to enable hybrid rendering at real‑time frame rates.

The American Cancer Society (ACS) updated its colorectal cancer (CRC) screening guideline, lowering the recommended start age from 50 to 45 for average‑risk adults. The change is based on rising CRC incidence in people under 50, microsimulation modeling showing a favorable benefit‑to‑burden balance when screening begins at 45, and expectations that screening performance in the 45‑49 age group will be similar to that in people 50 +. The recommendation for 45‑year‑olds is designated “qualified,” while the recommendation for those 50 + remains “strong.” All positive non‑colonoscopy test results must be followed with a timely colonoscopy. Average‑risk adults in good health with >10‑year life expectancy should continue screening through age 75; screening for those 76‑85 should be individualized, and it should be discouraged after age 85. Recommended options include annual FIT, annual HSgFOBT, mt‑sDNA every 3 years, colonoscopy every 10 years, CT colonography every 5 years, and flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years; no test is prioritized. CRC incidence has fallen in people 55 + but rose 51 % in those under 50 since 1994, with death rates also increasing. Adults born around 1990 have twice the colon‑cancer risk and four times the rectal‑cancer risk of those born around 1950, and trends suggest the higher risk will persist as these cohorts age. New ACS modeling incorporating recent incidence trends shows that starting screening at 45 yields more life‑years gained and a better benefit‑burden ratio than starting at 50, and it is expected to reduce the disproportionate burden among Black, Alaska Native, and American Indian populations as well as the general average‑risk population.

Quantum spin relaxation in radical pairs is essential for quantum computing, spintronics, and quantum biophysics, with computational challenges including ensemble averaging of random initial states, exponential growth of Hilbert/Liouville space, and numerically stable long-time propagation. This work introduces three tensor network methods for modeling radical pairs: stochastic matrix product states, vectorised matrix product density operators, and locally purified MPS. The radical pair Hamiltonian includes Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and Haberkorn relaxation terms, with observables typically being electronic state populations. These methods aim to provide full quantum-mechanical treatment with manageable computational scaling.

Thai cave rescue described as one of the toughest. Twelve boys and their soccer coach were found alive after nine days inside Tham Luang Nang Non cave, trapped by rising floodwater after practice. The standard protocol in cave flooding rescues is to wait: either the trapped are alive and safe, so risking rescuers is unnecessary, or they are dead, making risk pointless.  

Most caves are limestone and can flood, especially in monsoon regions where water may persist for months. While many floods recede quickly after rain, the Thai cave may stay flooded for weeks. Surface actions include monitoring water depth, temperature, weather, diverting or pumping water, and searching for alternative entrances; divers may make contact or deliver supplies.  

The group has water but no food for nine days, leaving them weak with gastrointestinal shutdown; a sudden full meal could be fatal, so rescuers are gradually reintroducing food. Weeks are needed to recover strength, limiting ability to perform strenuous escape activities.  

Three main options are considered: teaching the boys to dive out (dangerous), drilling a new entrance (requires heavy equipment and precise mapping), or waiting for water to recede (monsoon season may delay this for weeks). If flooding remains a threat, diving may be the only option. Rescuers face intense public and media pressure, risking hasty decisions.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars defendants from directly appealing contested post-judgment restitution orders entered pursuant to plea agreements that cap restitution amounts. Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to DUI and agreed to pay restitution up to $53,653.45; when the court later ordered $40,933.45 in restitution, Hoffman attempted a direct appeal. The court ruled that such appeals must be pursued through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings rather than direct appeal. The decision rested on the legislature's intent to reduce appellate burden, the inclusion of restitution orders within "sentence" under subsection (B), and avoidance of a dual-track review system. The court disapproved prior cases that had assumed jurisdiction over similar appeals.

A blood-based test using circulating glial cells (CGCs) detected via GFAP and OLIG2 immunocytochemistry demonstrated high sensitivity (>99%) and 100% specificity for identifying glial malignancies and differentiating them from benign brain tumors and metastases in multiple validation studies involving over 850 samples. Analytical validation confirmed recovery ≥80%, detection limits of 1 cell/5 mL, sensitivity of 92.5-95%, and accuracy of 95.3-96.9%. Orthogonal FISH verification showed 100% concordance with tissue EGFR status. The test provides a non-invasive alternative to surgical biopsy for diagnosing brain tumors presenting with intracranial space-occupying lesions. The study was funded by Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited.

Carleton University in Ottawa is creating an Allan Slaight–named chair for a research and teaching program on perception and deception in the conjuring arts. Has secured a $2 million Slaight Family Foundation grant for the five‑year post, covering salary, graduate hires, travel and a digital archive. Interim president Alastair Summerlee said the aim is to investigate why people deceive and are deceived, linking the work to fake news and political persuasion. Former U.S. senator Mark Begich’s entry into Alaska’s 2018 gubernatorial race has raised concerns that a three‑way contest could hand victory to Republicans.
