Panic attacks are bursts of intense fear lasting fewer than 30 minutes, distinct from the persistent worry of anxiety, according to the DSM‑5. About 2–3 % of Americans have panic disorder; 18.1 % have any anxiety disorder. When linked to panic disorder, attacks arise without a trigger, though anyone can experience one if a clear fear is present. Symptoms include palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, nausea, dizziness, paresthesia, depersonalization, and fear of dying or losing control. Experts recommend learning the symptom list, obtaining a physical exam to rule out medical causes, and seeking professional help. Coping tools include writing “Panic attacks are not life‑threatening” on an index card or phone, adding personal mantras, visualizing panic as a wave that rises and falls (peaking at about 10 minutes), using smartphone games or relaxing music for distraction, and practicing slow, deep “full‑body” breathing daily so the technique can be employed during an attack. These strategies are described by Dr. Carolyn Rodriguez, Dr. Prakash Masand, Dr. Chuck Schaeffer, and Annie Wright.

Using the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education (NSECE) Household Survey, this analysis identified common types of searches for child care and early education (CCEE). The sample comprised 1,190 households that reported a recent CCEE search (within 24 months) for a focal child under age 6 and considered more than one provider. Up to two information sources families mentioned were recorded.

A latent class analysis (LCA) with five possible sources (friends/family with children, providers already known, social media, internet search tools, and CCR&R or other local organizations) yielded five distinct search types, each defined by two primary sources:

- **Search Type 1 (N=101):** CCR&R or friends/family (83% used a CCR&R, 31% asked friends/family).  
- **Search Type 2 (N=323):** Internet search or social media (94% used internet search, 23% used social media).  
- **Search Type 3 (N=104):** Known providers or friends/family (84% asked a known provider, 42% asked friends/family).  
- **Search Type 4 (N=243):** Social media or friends/family (93% used social media, 59% asked friends/family).  
- **Search Type 5 (N=419):** Friends/family or internet search (99% asked friends/family, 53% used internet search).

Correlational analyses showed that search type varied significantly with whether families sought information about the type of care (Search Types 1 and 2 differed from Type 5), with the presence of a child condition affecting care provision (Types 1 and 3 had higher proportions), and with geographic region (Type 3 was more common in the West; Type 5 was more common in the Northeast). No systematic differences were found across other family or child characteristics.

Limitations include reliance on the first two reported sources and a non‑representative analytic sample (higher income, more English‑speaking households). The findings indicate that families tend to cluster distinct combinations of information sources when searching for CCEE.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU, built on the Ampere architecture, integrates 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM organized as five stacks of eight dies, delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth—more than 1.7× that of the Tesla V100. The memory subsystem employs SECDED ECC to protect data and the L1 caches, register files, and L2 cache. The L2 cache is 40 MB, partitioned into two sections of 40 slices each, providing 2.3× the read bandwidth of V100 (5120 B/clk vs 2048 B/clk) and supports compute‑data‑compression for up to 4× DRAM/L2 bandwidth gains and 2× capacity. A100 has 108 SMs with third‑generation Tensor Cores delivering 16× peak mixed‑precision throughput versus FP32, and new features such as warp‑wide data sharing, k‑dimension expansion up to 4×, and an asynchronous copy instruction that bypasses L1 and the register file, along with 1.7× larger shared‑memory per SM (164 KB). The Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) capability can split a single A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated GPC, L2 slices, memory controllers and QoS, supporting multi‑tenant and single‑user scenarios. Third‑generation NVLink provides twelve 50 Gbit/s links per GPU for 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 with SR‑IOV offers additional connectivity. CUDA 11 introduces asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, CUDA Graphs, and cooperative groups to improve performance and programmability. The DGX A100 system houses eight A100 GPUs interconnected via NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 MIG‑partitioned accelerators. A100 also supports fine‑grained structured sparsity (2:4) with negligible accuracy loss for inference and training acceleration.

The lecture covers web security vulnerabilities and defenses. Shellshock exploits how CGI servers set Bash environment variables from HTTP headers, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands via specially crafted header values. Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks involve injecting malicious code through untrusted user input; defenses include browser filters, HTTP-only cookies, privilege separation using separate domains for untrusted content, content sanitization (like Django's template escaping), and Content Security Policy (CSP) headers. SQL injection attacks occur when untrusted input is directly inserted into database queries, allowing attackers to modify or delete data; mitigation requires rigorous input encoding. Cookie security involves session management risks from shared domains and the same origin policy; alternatives include stateless cookies using Message Authentication Codes (MACs) as demonstrated by Amazon Web Services. Protocol vulnerabilities include URL parsing inconsistencies between browser components (Flash vs. browser origin determination) and the "GIFAR" attack, where JAR files are embedded in GIF images to bypass same-origin checks. Covert channel attacks use timing differences to determine which websites a user has visited: CSS link color sniffing, cache timing attacks, DNS timing attacks, and rendering-based timing attacks.

The passage is a lecture transcript covering topics in coding theory, focusing on Reed-Muller codes, graphical realizations, and the sum-product algorithm. Key points include: the Hadamard transform over the binary field and its properties, such as self-inverse matrices; recursive construction of graphical realizations using simple gates like controlled NOT gates; trade-offs between cycle-free and cyclic graphical representations regarding complexity and performance; application to specific codes like the (8,4,4) Reed-Muller code; and an introduction to the sum-product algorithm for a posteriori probability decoding. The lecture also references problem sets, including difficulties with certain exercises, and mentions connections to turbo codes and capacity-approaching codes in subsequent chapters.

This preprint describes a retrospective multi-centric study using deep learning to separately model brain ageing and disease-specific effects in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients from structural MRI scans. The study included 4,392 patients for age and disease duration (DD) modelling, and a longitudinal cohort of 252 patients with early MS for validation. A model was trained to predict DD from brain MRI (DD gap), and compared with the brain-age gap (BAG) derived from healthy ageing models. The DD gap model performed well (MAE 5.63 years, R²=0.34), exceeding the explained variance of lesion and thalamic volumes. DD gap was nearly independent of BAG (r=0.06). Both DD gap and BAG were positively associated with physical disability (EDSS). The DD gap significantly added to BAG in explaining EDSS variance cross-sectionally (ΔR²=0.012) and longitudinally (ΔR²=0.064), while an alternative MS-age model did not improve on BAG. The authors conclude that the DD gap is a clinically meaningful biomarker of MS-specific brain damage that complements classical brain-age models.

The Situation Calculus is a logical framework for specifying dynamic systems such as robotics, databases, and software agents. Reiter’s successor‑state axioms solve the frame problem for actions that change the external world; Gabaldon extended this to non‑Markovian domains where action preconditions and effects may depend on past situations, and Scherl and Levesque further extended it to knowledge‑producing actions. Modern applications such as smart contracts require non‑Markovian theories that can represent obligations. This paper formalizes the obligation taxonomy from [31] within the non‑Markovian Situation Calculus by using the deontic fluent O(s′, s) introduced in [37] to capture deontic accessibility and defining Oblg(ϕ, s) ≡ (∀s′).O(s′, s) ⊃ ϕ[s′] to express that an agent must bring about ϕ. A running door‑opening example illustrates primitive actions (unlock, lock, pressButton, moveTo, notify), relevant fluents (open, locked, notifiedManager, at), action precondition axioms, and successor‑state axioms. The paper is organized into sections covering the sequential temporal Situation Calculus, deontic logic notions, formalization of obligation types, properties, violation and compensation, related work, and future directions.

Five years after the 2012 discovery of Richard III’s skeleton under a Leicester car park, several people whose lives intersected with the last Plantagenet king experienced lasting changes. Michael Ibsen, a descendant who provided a DNA sample, faced sudden fame and public recognition. Mike Mistry, the council car‑park attendant who witnessed the excavation, became an informal guide to visitors before being made redundant in 2016. Musician Ian Churchward, inspired by the discovery, re‑oriented his Devon folk‑rock band to produce multiple Richard III‑themed albums and performances. The church where Richard III was originally buried was demolished in the first half of the 16th century.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, and push-pull. Duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin: connecting to VLDO enables 100% duty cycle (three compatible devices), AVSS sets 50% limit for push-pull applications, and floating allows 75% maximum. Current sensing through CS_ILIM detects primary-side current and triggers PWM turn-off when peak current reaches COMP/2, with overcurrent threshold at 1.05 V causing hiccup mode activation. Hiccup mode involves cycle-by-cycle current limiting followed by disabled switching, controlled by CHICC capacitor (minimum 3.3 nF). External fault protection is provided via the FAULT pin with 0.6 V threshold and 0.4–1.4 µs pulse width filtering. Slope compensation is required for duty cycles above 50% to prevent subharmonic oscillation, implemented through an RSC resistor. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C with re-initiation at 160°C. The design example details a synchronous push-pull converter at 500 kHz with 5 V output using GaN devices, including calculations for RT (205 kΩ), feedback resistors (10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ), dead time (~25 ns), transformer turns ratio (2.5) and primary inductance (40 μH), output inductor (0.47 μH), output capacitance (2.3 mF with additional filtering), sense resistor (7.5 Ω), and frequency compensation (RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, CHF 47 pF). Layout guidelines emphasize feedback trace separation from power magnetics, minimized switching loop areas, separate analog and power grounds, and proper capacitor placement.

Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology and collaborators used fossil evidence and rare horizontal gene‑transfer (HGT) events to date fungal diversification. By identifying 17 HGT “older‑than/younger‑than” relationships, they calibrated a molecular clock and estimated that the common ancestor of extant fungi lived roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, well before land plants. The study indicates that ancient fungi partnered with algae, broke down rock, recycled nutrients and created primitive soils, acting as ecosystem engineers that prepared terrestrial environments for plants. Complex multicellularity evolved independently in five major groups (animals, land plants, fungi, red algae, brown algae). The revised timeline suggests a long pre‑plant fungal phase that altered Earth’s surface and enabled later plant colonisation.

In 1962 the Soviet Union withdrew missiles from Cuba after the United States demonstrated decisive strategic superiority, roughly 8 to 1. Subsequent U.S. policymakers ignored evidence of Soviet aggressive intent and a declared intention to build up forces. By the mid‑1970s the Soviets had surpassed the United States in most strategic categories. The Carter Administration’s responses to Soviet actions—including tolerating a combat brigade in Cuba, failing to prevent the Afghan invasion, and contradictory statements on Middle East defense—were characterized as weak and inconsistent. The author argues this weakness damaged U.S. credibility and alliance confidence. He calls for restoring a margin of safety through prudent defense budgets, firm deterrence, decisive anti‑terrorism measures, consultation with allies, and unwavering commitment to American principles to achieve lasting peace.

This study examined blockchain course offerings in 533 AACSB-accredited US universities. Of these, 151 (28%) offer at least one blockchain course, totaling 361 courses. The largest course category is Fundamentals & Overview (140 courses), followed by Digital Assets & Cryptocurrencies (71) and Technical Development (66). Most courses are at the undergraduate level (72%), with Computer Science (70) and Information Systems (67) departments hosting the most courses. Finance, Business & Strategy, and Law departments also offer blockchain courses, with some offered by uncommon departments like Biology, Literature, and Political Science. Larger universities are more likely to offer blockchain courses, and private universities have a higher percentage offering such courses (36%) compared to public universities (24%). Courses increasingly integrate with emerging technologies like AI, Machine Learning, and IoT. The research highlights the interdisciplinary nature of blockchain education and the need for both technical and non-technical competencies in curricula.

The device supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S) for reading data, selectable via SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in SDI_CTL_REG. Default protocol is SPI-00-S on power-up or reset. SDO_MODE[1:0] bits must be set to 00b in SDO_CTL_REG for data reading. The device optionally supports dual SDO mode (two-bit bus width) configured via SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] bits, which halves required SCLK cycles. The disclosure relates to noninvasive devices and methods for monitoring a patient's physiological information using data from multiple measurement sites. Sensors placed at different sites (e.g., a cephalic site such as the nose and a peripheral site such as a finger) each comprise a plurality of light emitters that transmit optical radiation into tissue and a plurality of photodetectors that detect the attenuated light. The photodetectors can be arranged in a three‑dimensional spatial configuration that conforms to the anatomy of the measurement site, providing diverse light path lengths and topology information indicating sensor placement. Signals from the detectors at each site are fed, in raw or minimally processed form, to a signal processor that combines the data streams and generates a single measurement of a physiological parameter such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, or glucose. The combined data allow the processor to extract multiple features (amplitude, phase, DC value, ratiometric values) and improve measurement robustness and accuracy compared with single‑site monitoring. Sensors can be implemented as finger clips or adhesive tapes and may include two to twelve or more photodetectors. Methods disclosed include transmitting light of multiple wavelengths through tissues of at least two sites, detecting the light, generating corresponding signals, and determining the single measurement by combining the signals.

A continuation of patent applications regarding torque sensing in surgical robotic wrists. The invention provides a surgical robotic component with an articulated terminal portion having a basal segment, an intermediate segment, and a distal segment connected via first, second, and third articulations. The intermediate segment contains a third articulation permitting relative rotation about third and fourth axes with first and second torque sensors for sensing torque about those axes. The wrist enables measurement of forces applied to a surgical instrument through torque sensors at multiple joints, providing force feedback to surgeons. The robot arm comprises alternating roll and pitch joints along its length, with a wrist portion that can be implemented at the distal end of a robot arm or within a surgical instrument. Additional torque sensors may be included for the first and second axes. The arrangement eliminates kinematic singularities present in prior art designs and allows the instrument shaft to extend from the wrist in a manner resembling a human wrist, facilitating translation of conventional surgical procedures to robotic methods. The torque sensors can be strain gauges, piezoelectric sensors, or magnetostrictive sensors, with outputs processed to determine applied forces for haptic feedback. Alternative arm configurations include lateral offsets between joints and various joint sequences such as RPRP, PRPRP, or RPRPRP.

The book seeks to bring pattern‑based regularization to distributed systems, analogous to earlier gains in algorithmic development and object‑oriented programming. It starts with single‑node container patterns because containers co‑located on one machine constitute the atomic building blocks. Splitting a node’s components into separate containers is motivated by resource isolation (e.g., separating latency‑sensitive user‑facing services from best‑effort background tasks), delineating team ownership, and achieving separation of concerns. Additional benefits include enabling small, focused teams, facilitating reuse of modular components, and simplifying testing, deployment, and rollback. The patterns assume tight dependencies among containers, allowing reliable co‑scheduling and optional sharing of volumes or network namespaces—a concept termed a pod in Kubernetes.

The “Combo” defense blends person‑to‑person and zone principles to counter the North Carolina Four‑Corner offense and other spread attacks that rely on dribble penetration. Three outside players (X2, X3, X1) aggressively deny passes while the two inside players (X4, X5) provide backside zone coverage. In the basic alignment, X1 plays off‑ball against O1, forcing the ball to the sideline; X2 and X3 occupy full denial positions on O2 and O3; X4 and X5 guard the baseline. Once the dribbler passes, O1 returns to a tight denial stance, X5 takes a loose on‑ball role on O5, and X4 slides to a helpside position. The defense aims to keep non‑ball handlers O4 and O5 handling the ball. If O1 penetrates the middle, X5 steps up to charge or trap the ball with X1; X4 supplies backside support, while X2 and X3 maintain denial. After the dribbler surrenders the ball, O1 resumes tight denial, X4 closes out to the ball pushing O5 toward the baseline, X5 drops back into a baseline zone, and X2, X3 continue strong denial. When a dribble is picked up, the on‑ball defender jams the handler and X4, X5 close out to O4 and O5, placing the ball handler in a disadvantage that often forces a difficult pass leading to an interception or violation. If X4 and X5 are capable ball handlers and shooters, the defense can switch to a quarter‑court 1‑3‑1 trap.

Passage describes AMD’s AGESA software interface procedures for processor and memory initialization during boot. Two stack‑less assembler routines allocate or remove pre‑memory stacks: AMD_ENABLE_STACK (sets SS:ESP, maps stack to global address space, creates UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF and configures MTRRs) and AMD_DISABLE_STACK (flushes cache lines, disables CAR mode and leaves MTRR settings unchanged). Structure management routines AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct allocate or free storage for call parameters using pre‑memory (Cache‑as‑RAM) or post‑memory (DRAM) allocation methods. Service calls provide access to DIMM SPD data, APIC and PCI base addresses, execution‑cache size, data‑eye bitmaps and system‑address translation. Boot‑flow entry points execute in sequence: AmdInitReset (minimal core init and execution‑cache allocation), AmdInitEarly (core and power‑management configuration), AmdInitPost (memory locate/initialize and transition to main memory), AmdInitEnv (peripheral, display and ACPI/DMI table generation), AmdInitRtb (event‑log retrieval) and suspend/resume procedures AmdS3Save, AmdInitResume, AmdS3Restore and AmdS3Resume (state preservation across S3). The host environment must implement required call‑outs such as AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaLocateBuffer, AgesaReadSpd, AgesaRunFcnOnAllAps, AgesaReset and platform‑specific hooks. Procedures return AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING, AGESA_ERROR or AGESA_FATAL status codes.

United Distributors, Inc. sued Airco Appliance & Hardware, Inc., Henry R. Burke, and Alfred R. Willis to recover a $3,107.82 note. Willis signed a guarantee in March 1953 to secure credit for a corporation he intended to own 50% of. Two days later he decided not to join the venture, informed the plaintiff, and the salesman returned the other signed documents; the guarantee remained with the plaintiff. Willis claimed the guarantee lacked consideration because he never became a shareholder. The court held the guarantee’s purpose was contingent on Willis’s stock ownership, which never materialized, and the plaintiff was aware of his withdrawal, thus the consideration failed and the contract was ineffective under Civil Code articles. The appellate judgment dismissing the suit as to Willis was affirmed.

VIX is a real-time index measuring implied volatility in the U.S. equity market, created by CBOE in 1993. VIX futures are futures contracts based on the VIX Index, traded on the Cboe Futures Exchange (CFE). They allow traders to speculate on volatility, diversify portfolios, and hedge against equity market risk. However, VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX; the S&P 500 VIX Short-Term Futures Index captures about half of spot movement, making long-term hedging expensive.

Key contract specifications: full contract size is the index value multiplied by $1,000, mini contract is one-tenth of that. Price quotation is in index points to three decimal places. Tick size is $50 per contract, minimum fluctuation is 0.05 per tick. Trading hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. CT, with extended sessions available. Contracts are financially settled, with trading terminating at 8:00 a.m. CT on the Wednesday 30 days prior to the third Friday of the following month.

Factors affecting VIX prices include the stock market cycle phase (VIX rises during bearish phases and falls during bullish phases) and contango/backwardation effects (futures sell at a premium when spot VIX is low, and at a discount when high). VIX futures all-time high was 80.850 in March 2020; the VIX Index all-time high was 89.53 in October 2008, and low was 8.56 in November 2017. The biggest risk in trading VIX futures is adverse price movement due to leverage, which can magnify losses.

To start trading VIX futures, one must open an account with a futures broker and fund it. CFDs are another option but are contracts with brokers rather than exchange-traded instruments and have no expiry dates. VIX ETFs also exist.

Researchers developed a simultaneous ADF‑EDS‑EELS tomography technique to obtain three‑dimensional maps of structure, chemical composition and valence states in LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2 (NCM111) cathode particles at stages of electrochemical cycling (pristine, 50, 100, 200 cycles). The method acquires ADF, EDS and EELS data in a single low‑dose tilt series, reducing beam damage and ensuring precise spatial alignment between modalities. Reconstructed 3D maps show that chemical composition (O, Mn, Co, Ni) evolves uniformly throughout primary particles, while transition‑metal segregation and valence‑state changes are strongly surface‑localized and depth‑dependent. Valence states of Mn and Co remain dominated by Mn4+ and Co3+ up to 100 cycles, but drop sharply by 200 cycles, with Mn2+ and Co2+ increasing to ~42% and ~89% respectively, consistent with a layered‑to‑spinel‑to‑rock‑salt structural transition. Quantitatively, oxygen atomic fraction stays ~66–67% up to 100 cycles then falls to 61% at 200 cycles, indicating ~34% of the volume has transformed to rock‑salt. Transition‑metal inhomogeneity decreases after 50 cycles due to ion migration, then rises again by 200 cycles due to segregation and dissolution. Depth‑profile analysis confirms that Mn and Co inhomogeneity and lower valence states are greatest near the surface. The results reveal three concurrent degradation mechanisms: structural phase transitions, transition‑metal migration and dissolution‑driven segregation, collectively governing capacity loss. The simultaneous ADF‑EDS‑EELS platform provides a generalizable route for correlated 3D structural, chemical and electronic analysis in complex functional materials.

Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. appealed a tax case regarding sales and use taxes on drilling equipment purchases. The court reaffirmed that part of a prior refund claim was barred by the statute of limitations and addressed whether the taxpayer qualified for an exemption under Indiana tax code for manufacturing machinery used in direct extraction of tangible personal property. The taxpayer, which drills water wells and installs pumps for residential, farm, and commercial use, argued that the equipment exemption applied because water is extracted for end users. The court determined the exemption was intended to prevent tax pyramiding on goods manufactured for resale, not for personal use, and found no evidence that ultimate users resold the water. Thus, the taxpayer failed to meet the exemption requirements, and the trial court's judgment in favor of the Department of Revenue was affirmed.

Elliott Wave theory, introduced by Ralph Nelson Elliott in the 1930s after analyzing 75 years of stock data, is a technical‑analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. The waves are classified into two main types: impulse (motive) waves, which follow the trend and consist of five sub‑waves (three motive and two corrective), and corrective (retracement) waves, which move opposite the trend and consist of three sub‑waves (A, B, C). Specific rules define wave formation—for example, wave 2 cannot retrace more than 100 % of wave 1, and wave 3 cannot be the shortest motive wave. Traders (day, swing, and long‑term investors) use the theory in stock, forex and commodity markets, often combined with indicators such as moving averages or oscillators. Its advantages include indicating probable future price direction; disadvantages include high subjectivity, difficulty in backtesting, lack of precise entry/exit signals, and a steep learning curve. Timeframe choice depends on the trader’s style, and the theory provides probabilities rather than certainties. Common mistakes involve mis‑counting waves and violating the defined rules.

In the Supreme Court oral argument on the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act (MVRA), justices considered whether restitution imposed on a convict is criminal or civil for purposes of the Ex Post Facto Clause. The defendant, Holsey Ellingburg, argued the MVRA, enacted after his offense, cannot be applied to increase his punishment, a position the government also supported. The Court heard from Ellingburg’s counsel, the Department of Justice, and a court‑appointed attorney defending the sentence. Justice Alito emphasized civil‑like aspects of the statute, such as allowing victims to enforce restitution as a judgment lien. Justices Kagan and Jackson stressed that inserting restitution into the criminal sentencing system makes it punitive, triggering the ex post facto clause. The author predicts the Court will likely reject applying the MVRA to Ellingburg early next year, with possible dissenting grumbling from justices favoring the lower‑court punishment.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) treatment is limited by universal resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxane chemotherapy. Approximately one-third of tumors are primarily refractory to treatment, and mCRPC refractory to tubulin inhibitors is uniformly fatal within 12-18 months. AR splice variants (ARv567, ARv7) are co-expressed in metastatic patients, with ARv7 associated with clinical taxane resistance. Computational analysis using EB1/EB3 fluorescent comet tracking reveals that AR-wt expression minimally affects microtubule dynamics while ARv7 expression increases EB1 speeds by over 40%, correlating with taxane resistance. Patient-derived organoids from primary, lymph node, and distant metastatic tissues are cultured using Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor to select tumor cells. pVHL and GSK3β cooperatively maintain microtubule dynamicity, with pVHL attenuating dynamics and GSK3β phosphorylation inactivating this function during quiescence. Small molecules including NAD+ and GSK3 inhibitors can modulate microtubule dynamics and drug susceptibility. Op18 upregulation is associated with taxane resistance in androgen-independent PC. Resistance evaluation using circular Hough transform detects drug-induced microtubule bundling, and BRCA1 knockdown reduces paclitaxel sensitivity. The authors propose correlating microtubule dynamics signatures from patient-derived tumor organoids with gene expression data to anticipate drug resistance, identify therapeutic targets, and inform personalized treatment strategies for mCRPC.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s RTX IO technology and related hardware. RTX IO works with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to move game‑asset loading and lossless decompression from the CPU to the GPU, delivering up to 100× faster I/O and reducing CPU utilization by offloading the work of dozens of cores. This improves frame rates, shortens load times, reduces stutter and pop‑in, and enables large, detailed open‑world games. The technology leverages Turing and Ampere GPUs’ DMA/copy engines, asynchronous scheduling, and GPU‑based decompression kernels.

The document then covers the NVIDIA A40 data‑center GPU, built on the GA10x Ampere architecture. It offers up to 2× the FP32 throughput, 2× ray‑tracing performance, and 5× AI throughput of the prior Turing generation, uses PCIe Gen4 for doubled bandwidth, and includes 48 GB of GDDR6 memory scalable to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink. The A40 supports virtualization (NVIDIA vGPU software) and integrates with the NVIDIA EGX platform.

Display capabilities of GA10x GPUs include 4K 120 Hz and 8K 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC and HDMI 2.1, with HDCP 2.3 protection. The fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder accelerates decoding of MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1, enabling 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. The seventh‑generation NVENC hardware encoder offloads video encoding, delivering quality comparable to x264 Medium while freeing the CPU, supporting up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding.

The GA10x architecture features second‑generation RT Cores, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory achieving up to 936 GB/s bandwidth. Specifications for the GeForce RTX 3090 (24 GB GDDR6X, GA102) and RTX 3070 (GA104, GDDR6) are provided, as is the Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature for GDDR6X overclocking. Alexis Perez pled guilty to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and was sentenced to 51 months in prison. On appeal, he challenged his sentence, arguing the district court erred by not granting him a three-level reduction for an incomplete conspiracy under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) and a minor-role reduction under U.S.S.G. § 3B1.2. The Eleventh Circuit found that Perez and his co-conspirators had taken "crucial steps" toward completing the offense—they had established a detailed plan, possessed the means to execute it, and were on the verge of execution—so the three-level reduction was properly denied. The court also concluded Perez played an "important" role in the conspiracy, being involved in planning and preparation, knowing how the fraudulent scheme would work, and receiving payment, warranting denial of a minor-role reduction. The sentence was affirmed.

Price action trading is a technical analysis method that focuses solely on past price movements plotted on charts, without indicators, to identify entry and exit points. A day trading price action strategy applies these patterns on intraday charts. Traders analyze price swing highs and lows, chart patterns (reversal, continuation, harmonic), and candlestick patterns to gauge market sentiment and behavior. Pure price action traders often use only trend lines, support/resistance, and pivot levels, while others combine price action with indicators such as moving averages, VIX, or RSI. Backtesting price action strategies is essential but difficult because patterns are hard to code and manual backtesting can be biased. An example backtest of a lower‑lows/lower‑highs strategy on WTI crude oil futures (2000‑2021) showed poor historical performance, though out‑of‑sample results after 2021 improved. Effective strategies should be quantified, tested on out‑of‑sample data, and diversified across markets and approaches. Common day trading price action strategies include trend following, breakouts, reversal trades, and scalping.

In 2016 credit‑card and auto‑loan debt raised household bills for millions. To pay off debt, cut credit‑card use, set up a spending plan, build an emergency fund and pay as much as possible each month. Use extra income such as overtime and cut unnecessary expenses like daily coffee. Prioritize high‑interest debts, then double payments on the next balance, and make lifestyle changes gradually to keep momentum.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network that exploited over 20 transsexuals recruited in Venezuela through fake "Miss Trans" competitions promising a new life in Spain. Victims were promised travel, accommodation, and breast implants, but upon arrival had documents confiscated and faced 15,000-euro debts. They were forced to live in inhumane conditions and work to pay off debts through prostitution and drug dealing. Fourteen people were arrested for managing the network, which earned up to 1 million euros over five years.

Google Doodle commemorated Max Born’s 135th birthday. Born, born into a family of upper‑class Jewish academics in Breslau (now Wrocław) in 1882, contributed fundamentally to quantum mechanics, most notably the Born Rule, which predicts probabilities of quantum measurement outcomes. He was a professor of theoretical physics at the University of Göttingen for 12 years and mentored future prominent scientists. He maintained a close friendship with Albert Einstein despite differing views on quantum theory. Forced to leave Germany when Hitler rose to power, he emigrated to England. In 1954 he received the Nobel Prize for his work on the Born Rule, which underpins modern quantum‑physics predictions. Born died on Jan 5 1970 at age 87.

Official data show UK employment rose 109,000 in the three months to April, lifting the employment rate to a joint‑record 74.8%. However, regular earnings grew only 1.7% annually, the weakest since January 2015, while consumer prices rose 2.9%, indicating falling real pay. Consumer spending is under pressure and business confidence may be undermined by post‑election uncertainty. Input‑cost inflation has moderated, suggesting consumer price inflation may peak above 3% in autumn before easing later. The Bank of England is likely to keep interest rates unchanged until the outlook clears.

The passage describes the AGESA™ software binary interface to a host BIOS. Host‑side bridge code calls the AGESA dispatcher to execute functions, and the dispatcher can invoke host procedures through a call‑out port routed by a host‑implemented router. The software is built for the UEFI phases SEC, PEI, DXE and RTP using 16‑bit, 32‑bit and 64‑bit tool sets and may be distributed as binary modules or integrated source. Host responsibilities include establishing a stack before any call, providing a call‑out router, allocating buffers via AgesaAllocateBuffer, and managing configuration options. The main entry points are AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, AmdS3Save, AmdInitResume and AmdInitRestore. Initialization coordination uses PPIs such as AMD_PEI_INIT_RESET_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI and AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI across processor and memory PEIMs. The DXE driver publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol and generates ACPI/DMI tables. Build control uses files such as <Plat>Options.c and .inf libraries, with environment variables AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir and PLATFORM_SOLUTION_NAME. Stack setup is performed by AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_STACK macros, and storage management uses AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct.

Al‑Qaida‑linked militants in Syria shot down a Russian Su‑25 fighter jet near Saraqeb, Idlib on Saturday; the pilot ejected, resisted capture, opened fire with his pistol and was killed by the militants. The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed the downing, saying the plane was hit by a portable surface‑to‑air missile in an area controlled by al‑Qaida’s Syrian branch. NVIDIA Corporation is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Santa Clara, California, dedicated to advancing visual computing. The company operates two reporting segments: GPU and Tegra Processor, based on a single graphics architecture.

NVIDIA-branded products address four markets: Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing & Cloud, and Automotive. GPU brands include GeForce for gamers, Quadro for designers, Tesla for researchers and deep learning, and GRID for cloud-based visual computing. Tegra processors power mobile devices, tablets, automotive infotainment, and gaming devices like SHIELD.

For fiscal year 2015 ended January 25, 2015, revenue was $4.68 billion, net income was $630.6 million, and cash and marketable securities were $4.62 billion. The company had 9,228 employees, with 6,658 engaged in research and development.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing strategy, utilizing foundries like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics for wafer production, and independent subcontractors for assembly, testing, and packaging.

The company's common stock trades on NASDAQ under symbol NVDA. NVIDIA initiated a quarterly cash dividend program in November 2012, currently paying $0.085 per share quarterly. The Board has authorized share repurchases up to $434.8 million through January 2016.

Key risk factors include intense competition, dependence on third-party manufacturers and subcontractors, international operations exposure, intellectual property challenges, and potential product defects. The company faces competition from AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and other semiconductor companies across its GPU and Tegra processor markets.

In September 2014, NVIDIA filed patent infringement lawsuits against Qualcomm and Samsung entities. In November 2014, Samsung filed a complaint against NVIDIA in response.

Strong mentoring relationships with adults and peers are critical for youth academic achievement, especially as COVID‑19 disruptions left many students months behind in math and reading. Survey data show that only a minority of students feel adult support at school and that mental‑health challenges frequently hinder learning. Meta‑analyses (2002, 2011, 2019, 2010) document that mentoring programs produce positive effects on attendance, grades, test scores, behavior, and school engagement. School‑based programs such as Big Brothers Big Sisters, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, and Check and Connect have demonstrated gains in grades, attendance, credits earned, and graduation rates. After‑school and community models (Quantum Opportunities, Village Model of Care, Pathways to Education) also improve GPA, graduation, and post‑secondary enrollment. Research on naturally occurring mentors—including teachers and other school personnel—finds that these relationships predict higher educational attainment, stronger school attachment, and better academic outcomes, particularly for students of color. Disparities exist: low‑income, minority, and first‑generation students report fewer mentoring relationships. Expanding quality mentoring—through both structured programs and natural relationships—requires public and private investment and supportive policies.

Researchers conducted a longitudinal evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 antibody responses in 11 nursing home residents (median age 74) during an October 2020 outbreak in Georgia, ending April 2021. Most participants developed binding antibodies (Pan-Ig, IgG, IgA, IgM) post-infection, though one participant did not. Ten participants received the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine 71–105 days post-diagnosis. Post-vaccination antibody titers, particularly IgG, were significantly higher (up to 200-fold) than post-infection levels. The study suggests nursing home residents generate robust immune responses to both infection and vaccination.

The court affirmed the Commissioner's decision allowing Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners, Inc. to register its service mark for dry cleaning and pressing services despite opposition from Lever Brothers Company. Lever Brothers, which has used the "Lux" trademark for soap products since 1900 and operates approximately 600 "Lux Laundries," claimed the marks were confusingly similar. The court found that while "Lux" is arbitrary for soap, "Thrift-D-Lux" connotes "thrift" combined with "de luxe" (an established term meaning elegance or quality) rather than "Lux." The court determined Lever Brothers failed to show it would be damaged by registration of the mark for services.

An outside day is a two‑bar price‑action pattern where the second bar’s high exceeds the previous bar’s high and its low is lower than the previous bar’s low, while the open and close of the second bar fall outside the prior bar’s open/close. The pattern signals rising volatility and stronger conviction by buyers or sellers. Four configurations exist depending on whether each bar is bullish or bearish; only those with opposite‑direction bars are called outside reversal patterns. An outside day can act as a continuation pattern when it aligns with the prevailing trend and as a reversal pattern when it opposes the previous bar, especially near support or resistance. Bullish and bearish outside days are stronger versions of the corresponding engulfing patterns and indicate a potential shift in sentiment. The outside reversal day specifically shows a high/low that surpass the prior day’s range but closes opposite to the prior bar, suggesting a trend change in an up‑ or down‑swing. To be effective it must be combined with additional technical analysis such as trend direction, support/resistance, pivot or Fibonacci levels. Backtesting on SPY (S&P 500) and other ETFs found that performance after an outside day was essentially random (average gain near 0 %), even worse than a typical day. Requiring the previous close to be higher produced a small negative return (−0.07 %), while requiring it to be lower gave a slight positive return (+0.06 %) that was not tradable. Overall, thousands of strategies testing outside‑day setups for day‑trading showed little predictive value, indicating that the pattern alone is insufficient for trading decisions.

In his inaugural address the speaker thanks President Reagan, repeats the oath taken by George Washington, and places his hand on the same Bible used by Washington, noting the nation’s 200‑year continuity. Noble et al. versus The Thompson Oil Co. to the use of Brown et al. involves a recognizance of bail in error. Key legal holdings: oyer of a record is not demandable; a valid assignment of a judgment in Pennsylvania is valid everywhere; assignees take judgment subject to existing equities and prior payments; after valid assignment, assignor has no attachable interest; a foreign attachment plaintiff stands no better than his debtor regarding attached property; courts may inquire into jurisdiction of sister state courts; judgment in rem is void without jurisdiction over property; notice to assignees after judgment does not bind them.

The case: Thompson Oil Company, a Pennsylvania corporation, recovered judgment against Snow et al. in Pennsylvania. Before the judgment was affirmed, Thompson assigned portions of it to Brown et al. and others for valuable consideration. Subsequently, Snow et al. were attached as garnishees in New York in a foreign attachment by Woods & Wright Oil Company, which claimed as creditor of Thompson. Garnishees had no notice of the assignment until after the attachment was served. New York court rendered judgment against garnishees, who paid it. Garnishees then pleaded this payment as defense in the Pennsylvania suit on the recognizance.

Court held: The assignment transferred all Thompson's interest to the assignees, who were Pennsylvania residents; the judgment's situs follows its owners' residence and was never within New York's jurisdiction. The New York court never acquired jurisdiction over the assignees or their property, rendering its judgment void as to them. The garnishees failed to follow New York Code provisions requiring substitution of claiming third parties. The Full Faith and Credit Clause permits inquiry into jurisdiction. Payment by garnishees did not bar assignees' recovery.

Judgment affirmed for defendants in error on demurrer.

Aziz Ansari says he uses a flip phone, hasn’t had email for about a decade and relies on an assistant. He hails taxis instead of using ride‑share apps, noting that a low‑tech lifestyle gives him more space to think and helps his creative work. He criticizes ChatGPT, calling it “outsourcing critical thinking” that makes people’s opinions more uniform and removes human interaction. He acknowledges his ability to live offline is a privilege, but says it keeps his head clear for writing. Other celebrities such as Christopher Nolan, Dolly Parton and Christopher Walken have described similar analog or low‑tech habits, and regular people have swapped smartphones for basic phones or landlines to reduce screen time.

James Horne, a plastic surgeon, appealed an order granting summary judgment to the New York State Department of Health. Horne's complaint alleged human rights violations under Executive Law § 296, claiming disability discrimination due to adult ADD in the revocation of his medical license. The court found the essence of Horne's action sought judicial review of the Administrative Review Board's determination to revoke his license, which must be pursued via CPLR article 78 proceeding. The court rejected Horne's argument that article 78 was not the sole means of review, interpreting "may" in Public Health Law § 230-c (5) as permissive rather than exclusive. The order was affirmed.

Northern Ireland’s health service is UK region without a minister, facing ageing population, GP shortages, drug costs and waiting lists exceeding targets. In March 83,392 patients waited a year for a first appointment. In June 2018 3,200 neurology patients were recalled and an investigation revealed inhuman treatment at Dunmurry Manor care home. RQIA faced criticism. In 2016 Rafael Bengoa proposed a reform plan, but no minister has been in post since Stormont’s collapse in January 2017.

Jurors in Nassau County Court acquitted Jasmine Copeland, 18, of all charges in the Nov. 1, 2014 stabbing death of 17‑year‑old Abbigale Thomas. Verdict came after three hours of deliberation; she was cleared of manslaughter and gang assault. Prosecutors alleged she stabbed Thomas with a steak knife during a brawl triggered by taunts; defense argued she had no contact and no blood spatter on her clothes.

The lecture is the last class of the term. Professor William Green thanks the class, notes the final exam is a week away, and reviews stochastic methods for evaluating high‑dimensional integrals. He explains that many integrals can be written as a weighting factor \(w(x)\) times a function \(f(x)\); examples include the Boltzmann distribution and Bayesian posterior densities (likelihood × prior). He describes Metropolis Monte Carlo: choosing a step size in each dimension is difficult because too large a step causes repeated rejections, while too small a step samples only a tiny region. Adaptive algorithms try to keep the acceptance ratio between 0.2 and 0.8, and it is essential to verify results against an expected order of magnitude. Statistical error scales as \(1/\sqrt{N}\), so gaining one extra significant figure requires about 100 times more samples.

He then introduces Kinetic Monte Carlo (Gillespie algorithm) for a catalytic‑surface model with a 10 × 10 lattice of sites, each site having four possible states (empty, A, B, coke). The total number of states is about \(4^{100}\) (≈ 10⁶⁰), far too large to store explicitly. Initial conditions should be sampled from a Poisson distribution, and slow or low‑probability processes (e.g., coking) can be omitted or approximated by slower diffusion to make simulations feasible.

Finally, he contrasts Molecular Dynamics (Newton’s equations, Verlet integrator, thermostats) with Metropolis Monte Carlo. Molecular dynamics uses real femtosecond time steps, is time‑accurate, and is appropriate for fast processes, but cannot reach millisecond conformational changes. Metropolis Monte Carlo avoids choosing a physical time step but sacrifices time information. He stresses that each method suits different problems, and using the wrong tool can lead to incorrect results. A brief Q&A addresses how to select weighting functions (preferably constant \(f\) and sharply peaked \(p\)) and how to perform marginal integrals over unwanted parameters.

Players say they need to start games better, after three straight two‑goal deficits they hope to score first. Gaborik notes his first return to the Garden after a trade and the building’s renovations, calling the atmosphere special. King mentions using off‑days for rest and focusing on traffic in front of the net. Both emphasize teamwork, home‑ice advantage, momentum in playoff hockey, a calm mindset and confidence in each other, and desire to avoid further comeback situations.

Zeta Global is acquiring Marigold’s enterprise software business for $325 million—its biggest acquisition. The deal includes Marigold’s Loyalty brand, email platforms Cheetah Digital and Sailthru, and marketing automation platform Selligent; Marigold will retain its SMB products (Campaign Monitor, Emma, Vuture). The purchase expands Zeta’s Fortune 500 client base and EMEA footprint, adding more than 100 large brands. Zeta will pay $100 million cash and $100 million stock upfront, with the remaining $125 million via a seller note within three months of closing. The acquisition supports Zeta’s strategy to increase multi‑service usage and leverage added loyalty data to improve targeting. Zeta projects $1.2 billion revenue this year, a 26 % rise from 2024.

Technology for detecting gastric neoplasia using methylated DNA markers identified in case-control studies. Optimal markers include 10 for tissue (ARHGEF4, ELMO1, ABCB1, CLEC11A, ST8SIA1, SFMBT2, CD1D, CYP26C1, ZNF569, C13ORF18), 30 for tissue, and 12 for plasma (ELMO1, ZNF569, C13ORF18, CD1D, ARHGEF4, SFMBT2, PPP25RC, CYP26C1, PKIA, CLEC11A, LRRC4, ST8SIA1). Methods assay methylation state in samples (gastric tissue, plasma, stool) via bisulfite treatment, sequencing, or PCR. Kits and systems for detection are provided.

Removing the 50 most hazardous objects in low‑Earth orbit would cut overall debris‑generating risk by about half; extracting the top 10 would reduce it by 30 %. The list, compiled by LeoLabs researcher Darren McKnight, is dominated by old rocket bodies: 76 % of the top 50 were placed before 2000 and 88 % are rocket bodies. They travel at ~5 mi/s in the 700–1 000 km altitude band, where collisions could trigger a Kessler cascade. Russia and the former Soviet Union contribute 34 objects, China 10, the United States 3, Europe 2 and Japan 1; Russia’s SL‑16 and SL‑8 rockets make up 30 of the 50. Since Jan 2024, 26 new rocket bodies have been abandoned in LEO, 21 of them by China, each remaining >25 years, violating the international 25‑year guideline. China’s Guowang and Thousand Sails megaconstellations use rockets that leave upper stages in orbit, potentially adding >100 such bodies in coming years. Some Chinese rockets (e.g., Long March 5 with YZ‑2 stage) can deorbit, but most do not. Active debris removal has been demonstrated (Astroscale’s ADRAS‑J) and could measurably reduce risk, but funding and market viability remain unresolved.

Petitioner Buchanan was convicted of murdering his wife in New York, sentenced to death, and his conviction was affirmed by the Court of Appeals. He sought a U.S. Supreme Court writ of error, alleging that a juror (Paradise) became mentally incapacitated during deliberations and that the jury improperly separated, violating his constitutional rights to due process and an impartial jury. The Court of Appeals reviewed conflicting medical opinions and denied a new trial, concluding that the juror’s condition did not prejudice the defendant. The Supreme Court held that the competency of a juror is a factual question it cannot review on a writ of error to a state court, and therefore denied the application.

East Dunbartonshire Council faces further strike action by GMB, Unison, and Unite affecting refuse collections July 12‑15. Council leaders express disappointment; action short of strike (working to rule, no overtime) continues. Assessments of service impacts are underway. Last month’s four‑day strike caused disruption. UNISON says the council’s failure to alter employees’ terms and conditions could result in further action.

Cerebras Systems withdrew its IPO plans on Friday, over a year after filing its prospectus. The AI chipmaker recently raised $1.1 billion in funding at an $8.1 billion valuation. The company did not provide a reason for the withdrawal but said it still aims to go public as soon as possible. Cerebras has shifted focus from selling hardware systems to providing cloud services using its chips. CEO Andrew Feldman stated the original prospectus was outdated due to AI developments. The government shutdown did not influence the decision.

The UN World Water Development Report 2018 warns that without solutions five billion people could lack adequate water by 2050, driven by growth, climate change and rising demand. It cites nature‑based solutions: China’s Sponge City (70 % rainwater recycling), India’s forest regeneration and Ukraine’s artificial wetlands. In Rajasthan, the NGO Tarun Bharat Sangh raised forest cover by 30 %, groundwater by several metres and cropland productivity; women‑led water‑harvesting raised groundwater by six metres, productive farmland from 20 % to 80 % and forest cover by 33 %. It advocates low‑cost community approaches combining soil, vegetation and structures, noting 3.6 billion people already face scarcity for at least one month yearly, projected to rise to 4.8–5.7 billion by 2050. Goal 6 of the 2030 Agenda targets universal access to safe drinking water and sanitation.

The guide compares current and recent Google Pixel phones, outlines case and accessory recommendations, and highlights key software and hardware features.

Models covered include the Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, and the previous Pixel 9 series. The Pixel 9a has a 6.3‑inch OLED, 48‑MP main + 13‑MP ultrawide + 13‑MP selfie, Tensor G4, 8 GB RAM, 5,100 mAh battery, Qi wireless charging, IP68 rating, and costs $499 with seven years of updates. The Pixel 10 adds a brighter 3,000‑nit OLED, Tensor G5, a 5× telephoto camera, louder speakers, Qi2 magnetic charging (15 W wireless, 29 W wired), eSIM‑only US models, and the same seven‑year support. The Pixel 10 Pro/Pro XL feature LTPO OLEDs (1–120 Hz, up to 3,300 nits), 16 GB RAM, vapor‑chamber cooling, a triple‑camera system (50‑MP wide, 48‑MP ultrawide, 48‑MP telephoto) with 42‑MP selfie, Pro Res Zoom up to 100×, Video Boost up to 8K, Qi2 (15 W on Pro, 25 W on Pro XL), 39 W wired charging, IP68, Wi‑Fi 7, Ultra‑Wideband, and eSIM‑only US support. The Pixel 10 Pro Fold offers a 6.4‑inch outer and 8‑inch inner LTPO OLED, same Tensor G5, a 48‑MP main + 10.5‑MP ultrawide + 10.8‑MP telephoto, Qi2, IP68, physical SIM + eSIM, durability claims (10+ years folding), but lacks the vapor chamber, Pro Res Zoom and Video Boost of the Pro models, and is priced at $1,799.

Previous generations (Pixel 9, 9 Pro, 9 Pro XL, 9 Pro Fold) use Tensor G4, lack 5× telephoto on non‑Pro models, and have no Qi2; they have been on sale for $599‑$1,499. Older A‑series (Pixel 7a, 6a) receive three‑year OS updates; a battery‑performance program has limited performance on some older A‑model phones, with free replacements or Store credit offered.

Ryan is a six‑year‑old YouTube personality whose channel “Ryan ToysReview” features him opening, playing with and reviewing toys. His parents began filming him at age three after he asked why he wasn’t on YouTube; the first video was a simple Lego Duplo train set posted in March 2015. The channel grew rapidly, especially after a viral video showing him unboxing more than 100 toys in one clip. By early 2016 it had 1 million subscribers; a year later it surpassed 5 million and now has over 10 million subscribers and 16 million views. Forbes ranked Ryan eighth among the highest‑paid YouTube entrepreneurs, estimating $11 million in revenue between June 1 2016 and June 1 2017; he tied with the comedy channel Smosh. The ten top‑earning YouTube stars collectively earned $127 million, a 80 percent increase, driven largely by massive view counts including Ryan’s 8 billion views. Ryan’s videos are described as “unboxing” content with a focus on surprise reveals (many titles contain “SURPRISE”), simple child‑centric play and no profanity or preachy commentary. The channel is largely non‑branded, with the family stating they purchase most toys and donate them after filming. Production involves filming two to three videos at a time two to three times a week, usually on weekends to fit Ryan’s pre‑school schedule. Ryan’s popularity has influenced retail, with some products gaining exposure through his endorsement. Parents report that children watch his videos for hours, often treating him as a friend, and credit his content with helping some kids develop language and imagination. The channel’s style is likened to a “miniature Mister Rogers” – upbeat, innocent and focused on simple play.

The passage describes AMD's AGESA software interface specifications, covering error handling, binary module architecture, and entry procedures for platform initialization.

Error codes range from SUCCESS (no issue) through AGESA_UNSUPPORTED, BOUNDS_CHK, ALERT, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL (stop POST), to FATAL (stop immediately). The host environment is responsible for implementing appropriate actions based on these returned status codes.

The AGESA binary module operates in 32-bit protected mode and interfaces with host BIOS through Bridge (procedural collection point), Dispatcher (entry point), and Router (CallOut re-entry point) components. Call-out operations allow AGESA code to invoke host environment procedures through a function number selection mechanism.

UEFI implementations span multiple execution phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RT), with different tool sets for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit development. Build configuration is customized through platform-specific option files.

Key entry procedures include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block storage management, AmdInitReset for basic processor initialization, AmdInitEarly for further processor configuration, AmdInitPost for memory initialization, AmdInitEnv for graphics display configuration, AmdInitLate for generating data tables, and AmdInitRtb/AmdInitResume for suspend/resume operations.

Stack procedures AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_STACK establish and remove pre-memory stack regions within cache-as-RAM storage. These are required for x86-64 architecture APUs before main memory becomes available.

All published entry functions are assured availability over time; use of unpublished internal function names is strongly discouraged as they may change between releases.

The court examined plaintiffs' motion for class certification in a case involving Baycol (Cerivastatin), a cholesterol-reducing drug linked to rhabdomyolysis. After analyzing Pennsylvania Rule of Civil Procedure 1702 requirements, the court found that numerosity was satisfied, but commonality failed for nationwide Classes II and III and Pennsylvania Classes III and IV due to individual issues of law and fact predominating. However, commonality was satisfied for Class I (Pennsylvania medical monitoring class). Typicality, adequacy of representation, and fair/efficient adjudication requirements were met for Class I. The court granted class certification only for Class I—Pennsylvania residents prescribed Baycol who have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart failure, seeking medical monitoring benefits. Certification was denied for all other proposed classes.

This patent application describes methods and apparatuses for downlink assignments for downlink control channels in wireless communications. The methods involve monitoring first and second downlink control channel candidates in first and second control resource sets (CORESETs) with different orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing symbol sets, receiving downlink assignments, determining downlink data channel allocations and demodulation reference signal symbol locations based on the assignments and the CORESET symbols, and decoding the downlink data channels. The application also covers methods for receiving indications of associated search spaces corresponding to different CORESETs with different quasi-collocation assumptions, determining monitoring occasions for associated search spaces, and monitoring downlink control channel candidates when they carry the same downlink control information. The described embodiments address multi-TRP transmissions to enhance reliability, handling multiple PDCCHs and PDSCHs carrying the same transport block, determining PDSCH demodulation reference signal locations when CORESETs collide with PDSCH allocations, and determining PUCCH resources for HARQ-ACK feedback across multiple CORESETs. The invention is applicable to 5G NR networks and wireless communication systems.

A defensive switch in soccer is a coordinated exchange of marking responsibilities between two defenders when the first defender is beaten by the ball carrier. The second defender, positioned behind and inside the first defender, calls for the switch (“Switch” or “Switch off”), moves to take the ball carrier, and the first defender sprints to cover the opponent originally marked by the second defender. Proper positioning requires the support defender to be goalside, at a correct distance, and in a defensive stance. Oral communication includes calls such as “Support,” “Jockey,” “Tackle,” and “Switch back” or “Return” to undo the switch after the play ends. Coaching instructions describe setting up stationary attacker and defenders, practicing relative movement, adding oral cues, and running scenarios (down the sideline or to the inside). Defenders may return to their original assignments as soon as the immediate play is no longer active. Switches can also occur without a dribbler when an opponent unexpectedly sprints past a defender.

Adm. Michael Rogers said the Air Force must embrace rapid continuous change and be willing to consider new ideas in organization, procurement and operations. The service has begun cross‑training active‑duty cyber defense specialists in offensive tactics, and vice‑versa, to give the force broader insight into the cyber battlespace. Tech. Sgt. Kyle Hanslovan, a cyber operator in the 175th Cyberspace Operations Group (COG) of the Maryland Air National Guard (ANG) and CEO of a cyber‑security company, suggested that the structure, composition and operational flexibility of ANG cyber units may offer ideas for evolving all cyber forces.

The 175th COG, activated in 2016 from a 35‑person detachment that performed network warfare for intelligence agencies in 2013, now has more than 200 Airmen in four squadrons: two active‑engagement squadrons (175th and 276th), a defensive squadron (275th) and an operations support squadron (275th OSS). The unit has secured city and state government networks during the Baltimore riots, conducted cyber training with Estonia, and supported the FBI, Secret Service, DHS and USCYBERCOM during the 2013 and 2017 presidential inaugurations.

Guardsmen bring civilian cyber experience—from government agencies to startup firms—that, combined with military training, gives commanders operational options not available to active‑duty only units. Col. Jori Robinson, 175th COG commander, emphasized that integrating civilian‑sector skills enhances both defensive and offensive missions and that rank transparency on the operations floor allows junior Airmen to critique senior personnel, accelerating decision‑making in a rapidly changing environment.

Hanslovan described how his early curiosity about the internet—learning to code and “borrowing” accounts—translated into real‑world cyber‑defense skills during his Air Force service. He credited the ANG’s “Innovations Program,” launched in 2017, for fostering an entrepreneurial mindset among Airmen and encouraging rapid experimentation rather than lengthy policy cycles.

The ANG’s cyber teams have excelled in civilian competitions; members won the World Series of Hacking at DEFCON’s Capture the Flag, demonstrating talent from outside the military. Col. Kevin George said combining private‑sector experience with Air Force training creates a force multiplier and that ANG persistence helps maintain skill currency as active‑duty personnel rotate.

Challenges cited include the slow acquisition timeline (months versus weeks in private industry) and retention of hands‑on cyber talent, as promotion paths often require Airmen to leave keyboard work. Robinson noted a post‑9/11 surge in enlistments has increased turnover, especially in technical fields. Both Hanslovan and Robinson argued the force needs faster hiring, broader recruitment and mechanisms to keep full‑time cyber experts, suggesting ANG units could serve as a stable talent pool while longer‑term solutions are developed. Robinson highlighted ongoing dialogue about cyber policy and workforce management as the Air Force builds its cyber capability while already operating in the domain.

The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) guarantees a free appropriate public education (FAPE) to students with disabilities, and disputes over IDEA compliance can be resolved through special education due‑process hearings. A hearing officer reviews evidence and issues a written decision that the parties must follow. Prior to the COVID‑19 pandemic, Pennsylvania was among the most litigious states for IDEA matters; suburban schools generated more hearing activity than city Local Education Agencies (LEAs), but the School District of Philadelphia (SDP) had the highest frequency of appearances. During pandemic‑related school closures, the Pennsylvania Department of Education required LEAs to continue providing FAPE while adapting to remote instruction, yet teachers reported being unable to deliver required accommodations because of limited connectivity. After the pandemic, Pennsylvania continued to experience high levels of dispute‑resolution activity, and investigations found that SDP and Pittsburgh Public Schools failed to provide FAPE and related IDEA services.

The study examines the pandemic’s influence on city LEA hearings by comparing published hearing‑officer decisions from March 16 2018 through March 15 2022. Of the 347 posted decisions, 24 duplicates were removed, leaving 323 cases; non‑city LEAs were excluded, yielding the final sample. The research addresses three questions: (1) whether city LEA hearing frequency increased post‑COVID, (2) whether hearing‑officer rulings differed before and after the pandemic, and (3) what remedies city LEAs were ordered to provide after the pandemic.

An ex‑post facto design was used, with rulings classified on a five‑point scale ranging from “Full Student” (fully in favor of the student) to “Full LEA” (fully in favor of the district). Remedies captured include Independent Educational Evaluations (IEEs), compensatory education, and financial reimbursements. Data are drawn from publicly available decisions posted by the Office for Dispute Resolution, and no IRB approval was required.

The lecture discusses model-free optimal control methods, comparing policy gradient methods (which scale to high dimensions and have guaranteed convergence but high variance) with value function methods (which are efficient and compact but can diverge when small changes in value estimates cause dramatic policy changes). The solution presented is actor-critic algorithms, which combine both approaches by maintaining a policy (actor) and value estimate (critic) simultaneously, allowing slower policy changes based on value function guidance. Key algorithms referenced include Konda and Tsitsiklis (2003), Sutton (1999), and Jan Peters' Natural Actor Critic. The lecture then presents a thesis case study of a robot called "Toddler" that learned to walk using an actor-critic approach with linear function approximation, updating once per footstep with a cost function targeting a "deadbeat controller." The robot learned to walk in about one minute, converged in 10-20 minutes, and was highly robust to disturbances, even adapting to a broken ankle. The value function estimate was found to dramatically speed up learning from 20 minutes to 2 minutes when retained between sessions.
