Natural zircon single crystals from the Mud Tank deposit, Australia (oriented ≈(100)), were shock‑loaded in recovery capsules to peak pressures of 13.6 GPa (7 mm‑thick Al projectile, 1.15 km/s) and 51.3 GPa (5 mm‑thick Al projectile, 3.3 km/s). One‑dimensional hydrodynamic calculations gave pressure‑time profiles; estimated heating was 24 °C (13.6 GPa) and 265 °C (51.3 GPa) with residual temperatures of 21 °C and 182 °C, respectively, for several porosity values (0–10 %).  

After loading, samples were examined by X‑ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, cathodoluminescence (CL), photoluminescence (PL) and scanning electron microscopy.  

At 13.6 GPa the zircon structure remained; intense fracturing occurred but no polymorph transformation was detected. CL images showed red‑tinted patches adjacent to fractures, reflecting increased defect density.  

At 51.3 GPa the material fully converted to reidite (a = 4.722 Å, c = 10.524 Å, ρ = 5.189 g cm⁻³) with the orientation relation (112)R||(200)Zrn; a minor residual zircon fraction persisted. Reidite exhibited strong mosaicism and high lattice stress (Raman ν₃z peak shifted by 5 cm⁻¹ and broadened ~six‑fold). CL of the reidite showed a broad blue band centered near 430 nm; REE³⁺ lines (Dy, Sm, Pr, Eu, Er, Tb) intensified and split, indicating at least two distinct REE sites. Numerous bright yellow luminescent speckles (2–10 µm) were confined to planar defects and are interpreted as segregation of REE³⁺ (especially Dy) on dislocations or interphase boundaries generated during the reconstructive zircon–reidite transition.  

The segregation occurred on a time scale of tens of seconds, implying vacancy‑mediated diffusion or transport along defects rather than long‑range post‑shock annealing. The U–Pb system remained undisturbed. Strong fracturing increased the material’s surface area, and part of the fractures healed after the zircon‑to‑reidite transformation. The results demonstrate that trace‑element redistribution, including REE segregation on planar defects, can accompany shock‑induced phase transitions under laboratory conditions.

The referenced patent application is a continuation of earlier applications concerning a ladar transmitter that uses an ellipsoidal reimaging mirror. Ladar (laser radar, lidar) is employed for computer‑vision tasks in autonomous vehicles, surveillance, mapping and other fields. Conventional ladar systems suffer from high cost, size, weight, power and limited range, field‑of‑view and signal‑to‑noise ratio. The inventors disclose methods to improve a scanning ladar transmitter’s gaze on desired regions of the scan area.

An optical field splitter/inverter is placed downstream of the scanning mirrors to split the field of view and invert the scan direction so that the fast part of a resonant scan occurs at the edges and the slower part resides in the middle, thereby extending dwell time on the center region. Overlapped inversion can be used to allow multiple inversions per field look direction, further increasing gaze on the centreline.

A Lissajous scan pattern is enhanced by inducing a periodic phase drift in one or both scanning mirrors. The phase drift is derived by solving a total‑least‑squares problem that minimizes scan gaps in a user‑defined region of interest (e.g., a ground‑plane zone). The drift is periodic with a harmonic sub‑period of the original pattern so that revisit time is preserved.

The patent also describes a compact beam‑scanner assembly that employs an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector (ECR) positioned between two single‑axis scanning mirrors (e.g., MEMS mirrors). The ECR reimages the spot from the first mirror onto the second, allowing both mirrors to be of similar small size and placed close together. A design formula for the coplanar‑angle (CPA) ensures that the reflected ray fan lies in a plane containing the centre of the second mirror, minimizing distortion. Optional tilt offset and near‑unity magnification maintain simplicity while increasing scan speed, maximum tilt angle and field of view.

Together, the field‑inversion, overlapped inversion, induced phase drift and ECR reimaging provide increased dwell time, higher revisit rates and reduced blindspots in targeted regions, particularly for automotive ladar applications.

The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput per clock, increases L1/shared‑memory capacity by 33 % and adds a second FP32 datapath per partition, while retaining concurrent FP32/INT32 operation. Third‑generation Tensor Cores introduce TF32 and BF16 precision modes, support fine‑grained structured sparsity that doubles matrix‑multiply throughput, and power AI features such as DLSS (now up to 8K with a 9× super‑resolution factor) and AI‑enhanced denoising. GDDR6X memory, the first consumer graphics memory to exceed 900 GB/s (up to 936 GB/s on RTX 3090), uses PAM4 signaling to double data‑rate efficiency. GA10x includes third‑generation NVLink (four × 14.0625 GB/s links, 56.25 GB/s each direction), PCIe Gen 4 host interface, and ROP partitions moved into each GPC, raising the total ROP count to 112. RTX IO leverages Microsoft DirectStorage for GPU‑based lossless decompression, offloading dozens of CPU cores and delivering up to 100× I/O throughput. Fifth‑generation NVDEC adds hardware‑accelerated AV1 decode (up to 8K60 HDR) alongside existing codec support, and seventh‑generation NVENC provides high‑quality, low‑power encoding up to 8K on HEVC. Professional GPUs include the NVIDIA A40 (48 GB GDDR6, up to 2× FP32 and 5× AI training versus Turing, NVLink‑scalable to 96 GB) and the RTX A6000 (GA102, 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 third‑gen Tensor cores, 48 GB GDDR6, hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising).

Analysis of the West African Ebola epidemic found that roughly 3 % of patients caused more than 60 % of all transmissions, a phenomenon known as superspreading. The 2014‑2016 outbreak infected over 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000, with spread driven by contact with bodily fluids of the living and the dead, especially through traditional funeral rites. Computer modeling by Benjamin Dalziel and colleagues calculated an average reproduction number of 2.39, yet transmission was highly uneven; many patients infected no one, while superspreaders were responsible for about 61 % of cases. Transmission occurred mainly among people who stayed home, and age was a key factor, with the very young and very old attracting caregivers who became infected. Superspreaders also played major roles in the SARS and MERS outbreaks. The epidemic was ultimately controlled through safe burial practices and rapid hospitalization of symptomatic individuals.

NOMA (Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access) techniques are described for enabling small data transmission by UEs in RRC idle or inactive states in LTE and NR. Methods, systems, and devices allow UEs to transmit small data via configured grant PUSCH using NOMA with contention-based radio resources broadcast via system information. NOMA parameters (DMRS ports, MA signatures) are configured to reduce collision probability. UE-specific reference bits are generated based on UE-ID and jointly encoded with information bits (using LDPC or Polar), then used as preamble or DM-RS to mitigate sequence collisions and enhance decoding performance. The transmission may use asynchronous or synchronous modes, with optional preamble/DM-RS, guard bands, and extended cyclic prefix for robustness. Procedures for small data transmission while in idle or inactive states, including configured grant resource allocation, response handling, and mapping rules, are detailed along with bit-level and symbol-level processing components such as interleaving, rate matching, modulation, spreading, and RE mapping.

The Tax Court reviewed an IRS Appeals officer’s determination permitting collection by levy of unpaid income taxes for 1994 and 1996. The petitioner, a songwriter, argued that the self‑assessed tax liabilities were inaccurate because of a dispute with record companies over royalties and asked the IRS to subpoena records from those companies. The Appeals officer declined to examine the accuracy of the assessments, concluding the underlying liabilities were not properly at issue under § 6330(c)(2)(B), verified that all applicable legal and procedural requirements were met, and determined that the proposed levy balanced the need for efficient collection with the petitioner’s legitimate concerns. The petitioner’s petition alleged errors including false information on the returns, mistakes in assessment procedures, reliance on incorrect IRS advice, failure to follow IRS procedures, and improper levy execution, but provided no specific factual basis or supporting evidence. The court found no genuine issue of material fact, holding that the petitioner failed to aver facts sufficient to show the assessments were wrong and that the law does not authorize the IRS to intervene in the royalty dispute. Summary judgment was entered for the respondent.

The case involved a burglary insurance claim on policies that contained a clause requiring the insured to keep records that allow the insurer to accurately determine the loss. The plaintiff operated a check‑cashing fund and recorded only the total amount of cash and checks each night on a scratch‑pad, without listing individual checks, payees, or amounts. After a burglary, the insurer argued the plaintiff’s record‑keeping did not satisfy the policy clause. The court held that, for a fund containing checks, the minimum required record must include sufficient detail—e.g., the name of the drawer or check number—to enable the insurer to pursue the drawers and ascertain the loss. The plaintiff’s system, which recorded only a single total, did not meet this standard, even though cash‑only cases require less extensive records. Variance reduction techniques (VRTs) and population control techniques (PCTs) are essential for efficient time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations. VRTs like implicit capture, weight windows, CADIS, and FW-CADIS modify particle weights and distributions to focus computational effort on regions of interest. PCTs such as uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC) regulate particle populations over time to manage memory and variance. The study shows that combining Cooper-Larsen weight windows with uniform combing yields significantly higher efficiency, while weight windows with weight-based combing cause memory depletion due to weight resets that misalign particles with weight windows. Implicit capture is found to underperform with uniform combing, though it works with weight-based combing. Time-dependent adaptations of steady-state VRTs, such as dynamic weight windows, improve efficiency by adapting to changing flux distributions. Proper selection of VRT and PCT combinations is critical for viable time-dependent simulations.

US language enrollment is low, especially for German and French, and programs are at risk of being cut. The article’s purpose is to re‑emphasize the “why” behind language learning by focusing on connection. ACTFL’s tagline “language connects” defines connection as an affinity, relationship, or link that can be measured qualitatively or quantitatively. Educators are urged to foster connection through imagined communities—groups of people linked by imagination—using task‑based instruction (TBI) that requires students to perform authentic, real‑world tasks while imagining themselves in the target language and culture. An example scenario involves students planning a move to a target‑language city, searching for apartments, shopping online for furniture, using public‑transit websites, and presenting their choices. Implementation guidelines include designing plausible authentic scenarios aligned with curriculum, providing autonomy, delivering just‑in‑time scaffolding, and using authentic materials for assessments. Positive outcomes include deeper cultural learning, new perspectives on cultures, increased feelings of connection and membership in target‑language communities, and continued language study beyond required years. The approach can be applied at all K‑16 levels and across languages, and sustainability is achieved by cataloging activities, collaborating among instructors, and making ongoing adjustments based on reflection and student feedback. The article concludes that fostering imagined communities gives students the essential “why” behind language learning and is key to the success of language education.

After the FBI raided the home and office of President Trump’s personal lawyer Michael Cohen in April 2018, Trump called the raid “an attack on our country” and the White House refused to rule out a future pardon for Cohen. Days later Trump granted a full pardon to former Bush‑administration aide Scooter Libby, convicted of perjury and obstruction in a classified‑leak case. The White House called it a correction of injustice; critics said it was a signal to those caught up in the Russia investigation not to cooperate.

The Constitution gives the president exclusive, broad pardon authority that has never been fully tested. Scholars disagree on limits: some say a pardon must serve public policy and is invalid if used for self‑interest or to conceal wrongdoing; others argue a corrupt motive does not invalidate a pardon, and that even a self‑pardon could be legal, though politically damaging. The Constitution makes clear that a pardon does not protect against impeachment.

Historical precedents illustrate the power’s reach: President George H.W. Bush pardoned Caspar Weinberger and others in the Iran‑Contra case shortly before trial, ending the investigation; Richard Nixon considered but did not issue a self‑pardon before resigning; Bill Clinton pardoned Marc Rich after large donations to his political interests, a decision scholars say remained valid despite alleged corrupt motives.

Alan Dershowitz said offering a pardon in exchange for silence would be inappropriate and potentially impeachable, though the pardon itself would be lawful. Reports indicate Trump’s former lawyer John Dowd discussed pardons with lawyers for former national security adviser Michael Flynn and campaign manager Paul Manafort; both were later indicted. Flynn pleaded guilty and is cooperating; Manafort has pleaded not guilty and faces separate trials.

Democratic Rep. Adam Schiff introduced the Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act, requiring public disclosure when the president pardons someone linked to an investigation targeting the president or his family; the bill is backdated to Jan 20 2017. New York’s attorney general is seeking to close a “double‑jeopardy loophole” so that state charges can proceed despite a presidential pardon, as current state law recognizes federal pardons. A pardon removes the recipient’s Fifth Amendment right against self‑incrimination for the pardoned crime, obligating testimony; false testimony can result in perjury or obstruction, and can aid a prosecution.

The study investigates whether LLM agents can develop altruistic behavior in a large-scale social dilemma using a Schelling-variant migration model with 225 agents in a 3×3 grid. Researchers identified two distinct behavioral archetypes: "Adaptive Egoists" (o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B), which default to self-interest but significantly increase altruism when exposed to social norms via a message board, and "Altruistic Optimizers" (Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek series), which consistently pursue collective welfare even at personal cost regardless of social interaction. The study finds that model choice constitutes a theoretical choice between egoistic and altruistic foundations for social simulation, with Adaptive Egoists better suited for modeling human bounded rationality and Altruistic Optimizers better for modeling idealized pro-social actors. Limitations include simplified model assumptions and homogeneous agent populations.

Background: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) accounts for 20–30 % of strokes and roughly 40 % of stroke‑related deaths. High morbidity and mortality have prompted interest in biomarkers such as resting heart rate (RHR).

Objective: To examine the association between RHR and all‑cause mortality (ACM) in ICU patients with ICH.

Methods: Retrospective analysis of 1,918 adults with ICH from the MIMIC‑IV database (ICU admissions 2011–2019). Patients were divided into four RHR quartiles (Q1–Q4). Cox proportional hazard models (three adjustment strategies), Kaplan‑Meier survival curves, restricted cubic splines (RCS), mediation analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed. Primary endpoints were ACM at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year.

Results: Higher RHR quartiles (Q3/Q4) showed greater ACM rates. RHR > 78.5 bpm was significantly associated with increased mortality, and RCS identified a threshold of 90.3 bpm. Below this value RHR appeared protective; above it, RHR predicted higher ACM (hazard ratios roughly 1.5–2.0 per quartile increase). Age modified the effect, with patients > 60 years showing a stronger association. Mediation analysis revealed a direct positive RHR–ACM relationship and a small negative indirect effect through age. RHR > 90.3 bpm had modest predictive value (AUC > 0.5).

Conclusion: In ICU patients with ICH, an RHR below 90.3 bpm may be independently protective, while an elevated RHR exceeding 90.3 bpm is associated with increased all‑cause mortality. Monitoring and controlling heart rate could inform management strategies and improve outcomes.

Turtle Trading is a trend‑following system created by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt from a 1983 training experiment. Dennis recruited 14 novice traders, gave them two weeks of instruction, and funded accounts of $500,000–$2,000,000. The core original rules were: (1) size positions inversely to market volatility using the Average True Range (ATR); (2) pyramid by adding to winning trades while keeping risk‑to‑reward below 0.5; (3) exit positions with predetermined stop‑loss levels—long when price breaks above a 20‑day high, short when it breaks below a 20‑day low. The theory assumes markets can remain in a trend until a confirmed reversal, so entries are based on breakouts and exits on opposite breakouts.

The Turtles traded a diversified basket of futures—U.S. bonds, commodities (cotton, sugar, gold, oil, etc.) and several currencies—often using leverage. Those who followed the mechanical rules generated large profits; some later founded successful firms (e.g., Chesapeake Capital). Curtis Faith’s book “Way of the Turtle” describes the six original strategies and back‑test results from 1996‑2006.

Richard Dennis earned $80 million in 1986 but lost more than half his assets in 1987‑88 and quit trading. William Eckhardt, after the experiment, started a CTA with a 17.35 % compound annual return over 20 years and acknowledged that trading can be taught.

Modern back‑tests (2007‑2022) on futures with dual moving‑average, ATR‑channel, and Bollinger‑Band breakout rules show lower returns than the 1980s but remain profitable. Trend‑following indices such as the Barclay CTA Index and the Swedish Lynx hedge fund maintain low correlation to stocks. Crypto markets have been tested with mixed results as trends have weakened. The experiment demonstrated that disciplined, mechanical trading can be learned, requires strict risk management, and typically produces low win rates with occasional large gains and extended drawdowns.

Researchers fabricated dye‑sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass‑jelly leaves (GJL). Dye extracts were mixed in five volume ratios (MP:GJL = 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, 1:3) and applied to TiO₂‑coated ITO substrates, with an iodide‑based electrolyte and a graphite counter electrode completing the cell. UV‑Vis spectroscopy showed that MP provides anthocyanin absorption (440–550 nm) and GJL provides chlorophyll absorption (610–665 nm); mixing extends the light‑harvesting window across the visible range. Morphological analysis revealed that MP‑rich films develop cracks, whereas the 1:1 and GJL‑rich ratios produce homogeneous, crack‑free coatings with uniform nanoporous structure (film thickness ≈15–20 µm). Photovoltaic testing gave power‑conversion efficiencies ranging from 2.12 % (pure GJL) to 3.50 % (1:3 ratio). The 1:3 MP:GJL blend achieved the highest efficiency, surpassing single‑dye cells (MP alone 2.75 %). Cyclic measurements showed that GJL‑rich mixtures retain performance over ten cycles, while the 1:1 mixture decays rapidly. The study concludes that a 1:3 MP:GJL ratio optimizes light absorption, dye loading and charge collection, demonstrating natural dye blends as low‑cost, eco‑friendly sensitisers for DSSCs.

The lecture discussed the LSZ theorem for extracting scattering amplitudes from correlation functions by taking the on-shell limit and truncating external propagators, with the Z factor capturing self-interaction corrections. The lecture then introduced the Dirac equation for fermions. Historical context was provided: Dirac sought to solve the Klein-Gordon equation's problems (negative probability and negative energy states) by proposing a first-order-in-time equation, requiring alpha and beta matrices to satisfy anticommutation relations. This led to gamma matrices satisfying the Clifford algebra {γμ, γν} = 2ημν. Multiple equivalent representations of gamma matrices exist under similarity transformations, with different representations convenient for different regimes. Lorentz covariance of the Dirac equation was noted to be discussed next time.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards back on patrol by April 1 during a March 21 meeting to address the lifeguard crisis. The Phuket Provincial Administration Organisation (PPAO) previously provided 37 lifeguards across 15 points on six beaches from Dec 28 to Feb 26. On Dec 12, the Governor ordered the PPAO to cease involvement. However, his new instructions assign responsibility to local administrative offices for Muang Phuket, Kathu, and Thalang districts while directing those without budget to request funds from the PPAO, conflicting with the Dec 12 order. Questions to the Governor regarding the lack of lifeguards remain unanswered.

Eric Schmidt, former Google CEO, will fund a five‑year project that uses uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) to collect data in the rough waters around Antarctica. Schmidt Sciences, founded with his wife Wendy, will spend $45 million on the effort, which seeks to improve understanding of the Southern Ocean’s role as a major carbon sink. The Southern Ocean absorbs a large share of human‑generated CO₂, yet climate models diverge for it and data are scarce due to extreme conditions and limited shipping routes. The four USVs will operate continuously, even in winter, measuring partial pressure of CO₂ and using machine learning to target data‑rich areas. All data will be made publicly available. The project is a public‑private partnership with NOAA, whose scientists co‑lead the work. Researchers note that recent cuts to federal science funding make such private‑sector support increasingly vital.

The passage describes AMD AGESA firmware procedures for processor and memory initialization. Two assembler procedures handle stack setup: the first initializes the processor and cache system to create a pre-memory stack region, maps it to global address space, sets MTRRs, and must run on all cores, returning status codes like AGESA_SUCCESS or AGESA_FATAL; the second removes the pre-memory stack, disables cache-as-RAM mode, and flushes cache lines, applicable only to the BSP. Additional procedures include AmdCreateStruct (creates storage for parameter blocks using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation methods), AmdReadSpd (obtains data eye results for DIMMs), AmdGetApic (gets APIC address for processor cores), AmdGetExeSize (returns available cache for execution caching), AmdGetPciAddress (gets base PCI address for processor dies), AmdIdentifyCore (identifies the current processor core), and AmdIdentifyDimm (identifies the DIMM corresponding to a memory address for error reporting). All procedures require a stack and operational HyperTransport links.

Lab experiments show that jostling micro‑bubbles of air and methane can generate tiny electric sparks (microlightning) sufficient to ignite methane gas, suggesting a possible cause of will‑o‑the‑wisps. Researchers bubbled methane and air through water, used photon counters and high‑speed cameras to detect weak flashes; when bubbles were made smaller and more crowded, visible zaps appeared. The sparks are attributed to triboelectric charging between differently charged bubbles. While the experiments were underwater, the findings support the idea that micro‑spark ignition could produce the hovering blue flames seen above swamps and cemeteries. The team notes that such micro‑discharges could also be harnessed to drive chemical reactions and study atmospheric pollutant transformations.

Devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK. Host SDO‑x drives device’s SDI; device feeds next, and the last returns to host. Sampling on rising edge of CONVST/CS; frame on falling edge. On SCLK launch edges the MSB is shifted out; on capture edges devices shift in the LSB. Host receives data in reverse. Frame needs 32 × N SCLK edges; shorter frames cause misconfiguration, longer frames need alignment for CONVST/CS to go high.

Solawave’s Wand is on sale for just over $100, offering targeted red‑light therapy with vibration and warmth in three‑minute sessions. It uses a single 630‑nm wavelength and has been reported by WIRED staff to tighten skin around the eyes. A Red Light Therapy Face Mask is also discounted to $227 ($122 off). All WIRED product picks are editorially independent, and the site may earn compensation.

President’s message to Congress highlights the urgent need to conserve and wisely manage the nation’s public lands and natural resources. Since 1860 the public domain has shrunk from 1.055 billion acres to 731 million acres, with an additional 368 million acres in Alaska. Early disposal policies, including the Homestead, preemption, timber‑culture, coal‑land and mining acts, led to rapid, often fraudulent, transfer of lands and fostered the impression that the domain was “legitimate prey.” Growing public concern now demands that the remaining lands be saved, classified and developed under conditions that attract private capital while preventing monopoly and abuse.

The administration continues vigorous prosecution of land‑fraud cases, withdrawal of coal lands for classification, and temporary withholding of power‑site lands; since March 4 1909, temporary withdrawals have covered 102 streams—a 229 percent increase over prior withdrawals. Current statutes are inadequate for modern disposition, so the President asks Congress to validate all existing withdrawals, authorize the Secretary of the Interior to make temporary withdrawals pending new legislation, and enact laws that separate surface rights (to be sold as agricultural land) from mineral rights (to be leased on a royalty basis with development requirements and anti‑monopoly provisions). This approach should apply to Alaska and to phosphate, oil, coal, and other mineral resources. Experimental statutes may be needed to balance public control with investment incentives.

Water‑power sites on government‑owned riparian lands should be controlled through limited‑term leases (≈50 years) with graduated rentals and renewal provisions to prevent consolidation into a monopoly. The rapid advance of electrical transmission makes water power a likely substitute for natural fuels, so retaining government authority over these sites is essential.

Soil conservation is deemed the most vital resource issue; the government should foster scientific soil management, drainage, irrigation, dry‑farming, and the reclamation of arid and semiarid lands. The recent increase of the homestead size to 320 acres in semiarid regions has expanded “dry farming” successfully. The Reclamation Act’s irrigation projects have begun on over 30 sites, but funding is insufficient, leaving settlers in distress. The President recommends issuing up to $30 million in bonds, repaid from reclamation‑fund proceeds, to complete ongoing projects.

For isolated timbered areas, existing timber‑sale acts (June 3 1878) should be repealed and timber disposed of at public sale, after which lands become subject to agricultural or mineral laws. The Secretary of the Interior’s recommendations, embodied in prepared bills, include validating past withdrawals and granting the Secretary clear authority to withdraw lands for future disposition.

The United States forest reserves, roughly 190 million acres under the Department of Agriculture, must be maintained and expanded. While 400 million acres of forest are privately owned, only 3 percent are managed scientifically; state regulation, not federal, controls private forests. A modest annual federal appropriation for reforestation at sources of navigable streams—proposed in a bill passed by the House—should be authorized for five to ten years to enhance watershed protection.

Inland waterway improvement is a key component of the conservation program. The Ohio River project calls for 54 dams to maintain a 9‑foot depth from Pittsburgh to Cairo; 7 dams are complete, 6 under construction, with $63 million still required, and the work can be finished in twelve years. Similar projects for the upper Mississippi (St. Paul to St. Louis, 6‑foot depth) and the Missouri River (Kansas City to St. Louis, 6‑foot depth; St. Louis to Cairo, 8‑foot depth) have been approved by army engineers and are ready for appropriation. Improved waterways regulate railroad rates and support cheaper transport of bulky goods, so the President urges Congress to include continuing contracts for these improvements in the river‑and‑harbor bill, positioning this Congress as the initiator of a new inland‑waterway system.

The President emphasizes that ongoing investigations into the Interior Department and the Forest Service do not delay the need for the recommended legislation. Congress is urged to act promptly on the Secretary of the Interior’s proposals, validate existing withdrawals, and grant the necessary authority to protect and develop the nation’s public lands and resources.

RTX IO integrates with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to enable GPU‑based lossless decompression of game assets, moving data from NVMe SSD directly to the GPU and offloading work that previously required many CPU cores. This yields up to 2× I/O performance, 100× throughput and 20× lower CPU utilization, allowing faster render start times and better GPU memory management.  

The NVIDIA A40 data‑center GPU, built on the GA10x Ampere architecture, offers up to 2× FP32 throughput, 2× ray‑tracing throughput and up to 5× (10× with sparsity) AI training throughput compared with Turing‑based GPUs. It includes 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink, supports virtualization with vGPU software and is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX platform.  

Ampere‑generation GPUs support high‑resolution displays via DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, delivering 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz with Display Stream Compression (DSC) 1.2a. HDCP 2.3 is also supported.  

The fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder in GA10x GPUs accelerates MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9 and the AV1 codec. GA10x is the first to provide AV1 hardware decode, enabling 8K60 HDR playback at ~4 % CPU usage versus >85 % for software decoding.  

The seventh‑generation NVENC encoder offloads video encoding from the CPU, matching the quality of x264 Medium preset while supporting 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding with low power consumption.  

Architectural highlights include second‑generation RT Cores that double ray‑triangle intersection performance, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity doubling effective throughput, and GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling reaching up to 936 GB/s bandwidth on the RTX 3090.  

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU, 24 GB GDDR6X, 10 496 CUDA cores and is ~1.5× faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 (GA104) exceeds the performance of the previous‑generation RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU offers 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, 48 GB GDDR6 (expandable to 96 GB via NVLink), hardware‑accelerated motion blur, AI denoising and supports Quadro Sync.  

Error Detection and Replay (EDR) in the GDDR6X memory interface helps users identify safe overclock limits by plateauing performance rather than crashing.  

Benchmark data shows the A40 and RTX A6000 deliver substantial gains over their predecessors in professional graphics, rendering, HPC and deep‑learning workloads. All product information is provided “as is” with no warranties.

The document standardizes the Guest‑Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) used by SEV‑ES and SEV‑SNP virtual machines. The GHCB is a single 4 KB decrypted memory page that mirrors the VMCB save‑state layout and serves as the shared communication area between a guest and its hypervisor. It defines protocol version negotiation and, in Version 2, introduces hypervisor feature advertisement that allows a guest to discover optional capabilities such as APIC ID list retrieval, multi‑VMPL support, page‑state change, SEV‑TIO, Secure AVIC, and extended guest request handling. The specification lists the required Non‑Automatic Exit (NAE) events, the minimum guest state that must be placed in the GHCB, error codes, and the handling flow for each event (e.g., CPUID, MSR, I/O, VMMCALL, page‑state change, SNP guest request, SNP extended guest request, AP creation, AP reset hold, AP jump table, #HV doorbell page, #HV IPI, #HV timer, APIC ID list, SNP run VMPL, SNP TIO, Secure AVIC, and termination). It also covers SMP booting of application processors, NMI delivery rules, hardware debug register virtualization, and host behavior for interrupt shadows and optimized end‑of‑interrupt handling. SMM and nested virtualization are explicitly out of scope for this version of the specification.

Consumer confidence measures the degree of optimism or pessimism that consumers hold about the overall economy. The Conference Board publishes a monthly Consumer Confidence Index (CCI) based on a survey of 5,000 U.S. households that answers five questions with responses of positive, negative, or neutral. The index tracks two components – a present‑situation index and an expectations index – and changes of less than 5% are considered insignificant while larger moves signal a shift in economic momentum. High confidence boosts spending, production, hiring, and market sentiment, while low confidence reduces those activities and dampens the economy.

The University of Michigan also conducts a separate monthly Consumer Sentiment Index via telephone interviews that asks respondents about personal finances and the short‑ and long‑term state of the economy. Backtests using U.S. consumer‑confidence data from the OECD (1993‑2021) show that a strategy that is long the S&P 500 when confidence is above its 12‑month moving average, and switches to cash when below, returned an 8.4% compound annual growth rate from a $10,000 initial investment compared with 10.4% for a simple buy‑and‑hold. The confidence‑based approach had a maximum drawdown of 23% versus 55% for buy‑and‑hold and was invested roughly 55% of the time.

Conversely, investing only when confidence is below its moving average produced a 1.58% annual return, growing $10,000 to $15,000 over the same 28‑year span. The backtests indicate that consumer confidence is a useful predictor of future stock‑market performance: above‑average confidence favors equity exposure, while below‑average confidence is associated with poorer returns.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, set a world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing the 2.4‑mile swim, 112‑mile bike ride and 26.2‑mile marathon in 16 hours 45 minutes 26 seconds. She learned to swim at 59, began competing in triathlons at 60 and later qualified for the full‑distance race. A former software developer, mother of two and grandmother of four, she trains about two hours daily and follows a varied diet that includes sweets. After the October 11, 2025 race she was greeted by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld, received the winner’s bowl on October 12 and says she intends to compete in Ironman events for as long as she can.

NVIDIA A40 is a data‑center GPU based on the GA10x Ampere architecture. Compared with the Turing‑based Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to 2× FP32 throughput, 2× ray‑tracing performance, and 5× (10× with sparsity) AI throughput; it uses PCIe Gen 4 for doubled bandwidth and provides 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink. The A40 includes three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, HDMI 2.1 support for 8K60/4K120, HDCP 2.3, and is compatible with NVIDIA vGPU software, Quadro Sync and the EGX platform. Video capabilities include a fifth‑generation NVDEC that hardware‑decodes MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1 (first GPU to support AV1 decode), delivering up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage, and a seventh‑generation NVENC that hardware‑encodes H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K with quality comparable to x264 Medium while offloading the CPU. The GA10x architecture provides up to 2× performance in programmable shading, ray tracing and AI, featuring second‑generation RT Cores, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, GDDR6X memory (up to 19.5 Gbps) and RTX IO with Microsoft DirectStorage for fast SSD‑to‑GPU loading. The RTX A6000, built on the same GA102 GPU, offers 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores and 48 GB GDDR6 (expandable to 96 GB via NVLink), supporting hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 24 GB GDDR6X) is up to 1.5× faster than TITAN RTX, and the RTX 3070 (GA104) exceeds the performance of the previous‑gen RTX 2080 Ti. GA10x GPUs include Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on the GDDR6X interface to manage memory‑transmission errors during overclocking. Performance data is provided for SPECviewperf 2020, Blender, V‑Ray, Redshift, Gromacs, NAMD and BERT inference/training.

Lenovo unveiled the limited‑edition ThinkPad 25 (based on T470, inspired by the 1992 700C) with retro styling, a 14‑inch FHD touchscreen, Intel Core i7‑7500U, GeForce 940MX, 16 GB DDR4, 512 GB SSD, Thunderbolt 3, fingerprint scanner, 18‑hour battery, starting at $1,899.

This passage discusses Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations for calculating thermal properties using the Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD) methods. Heat flux (HF) calculation is central to determining thermal conductivity. LAMMPS originally used incorrect HF formulas valid only for pair potentials, leading to errors with many-body interactions. Correct formulas were derived by Torii et al. for arbitrary many-body potentials but had limited implementations. The authors implemented these exact formulas in LAMMPS for both control volume and control surface heat flux calculations, including spectral decomposition. They validated the implementation using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials on various 2D and 3D systems.

COPD, a leading U.S. death cause almost exclusively caused by smoking, presents with chronic cough and shortness of breath. Diagnosis uses smoking history and pulmonary function testing. Management includes inhalers, oxygen, and pulmonary rehab; no cure, but quitting smoking prevents onset and halts progression.

The passage discusses a study evaluating distance education in sports higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on lecturers' perspectives. The study aimed to assess thoughts on distance education practices, advantages, disadvantages, challenges, management, and affecting factors. Using a qualitative approach with semi-structured interviews of 14 lecturers from sports departments in Turkish universities, data were analyzed descriptively, revealing four themes: positive aspects (e.g., time/space flexibility, technology use, resource access), negative aspects (e.g., communication issues, motivation problems, inequality of opportunity), challenges (e.g., infrastructure issues, assessment difficulties), and distance education management. Findings indicate that while distance education offers flexibility and resource access, it faces significant issues like communication problems, motivation loss, and infrastructure inadequacies, particularly for applied sports lessons. The study highlights the need for improved infrastructure, training, and management to enhance distance education effectiveness in sports higher education.

The passage reports first-principles calculations of the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in a Mn₃Sn/MgO/Mn₃Sn magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) using the Mn₃Sn(01̄10)/MgO(110) orientation. Mn₃Sn is a noncollinear antiferromagnet with a D0₁₉ structure and an inverse triangular magnetic order that breaks time-reversal symmetry, leading to momentum-dependent spin splitting. The chosen orientation is optimal for electrical switching via spin-orbit torque. By applying density functional theory and the Landauer–Büttiker formalism with a sufficiently thick MgO barrier, the study finds a TMR ratio exceeding 1000%. The high ratio is attributed to the spin polarization (primarily the x-component) of Mn₃Sn and the filtering of tunneling electrons by the MgO barrier. This work provides a practical benchmark for realizing antiferromagnetic MTJ devices with Mn₃Sn electrodes, addressing previous theoretical limitations regarding barrier thickness.

Jeff Bezos suggests future data infrastructure could be built in space to relieve land, energy and cooling constraints and to provide resilience against terrestrial disruptions. The concept responds to growing demand for cloud and AI services that strain existing data centres, which consume large amounts of electricity and water. Orbital data centres could tap solar power and bypass some terrestrial limits, but face major engineering hurdles such as radiation shielding, power storage, vacuum cooling and low‑latency communication with Earth, as well as high launch and maintenance costs. Several aerospace and technology firms are exploring orbital and lunar infrastructure, driven by falling launch costs and hardware miniaturisation. While the idea remains speculative, it highlights intensifying competition for computing power that pushes the sector beyond traditional limits.

In a study published in the Journal of Neuroscience, scientists tested barn owls' ability to locate a moving target among shifting backgrounds. The owls performed the task by grouping moving elements that share a direction, a visual processing ability previously observed only in primates. Using head cameras, researchers measured how quickly the birds turned toward a dot moving differently from others. Uniform dot direction improved performance. Neural recordings from the ocular tectum showed activity correlated with dot motion, indicating this region supports the task.

Thursday was the final day of school for students and the end of Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky’s tenure in Clark County Schools. Skorkowsky announced his retirement last fall and was succeeded this month by Dr. Jesus Jara. During his tenure, he highlighted a rise in the graduation rate from 60 % to 83 % and the addition of 10,000 magnet‑school seats. District faces a $60 million budget shortfall, and Skorkowsky urged leadership to push for 2019 legislative changes to allocate marijuana tax revenue to county where it is generated. Suicide remains a taboo in Fiji; NSAAC data show 124 suicides and 107 attempted cases in 2015, and 102 suicides and 104 attempted in 2016. From 2011 to March, 627 suicides and 694 attempted were recorded, including 56 child suicides and 97 child attempts. During RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security’s Chris Young warned that attackers are corrupting the data used to make decisions, creating “data landmines” that can cause faulty outcomes, missed opportunities and economic losses. He cited insecure home networks and IoT devices, noting the Mirai botnet, as a growing attack surface that endangers corporate systems when employees work remotely. Microsoft President Brad Smith called on the tech community to act as a “digital Switzerland,” adopting Red‑Cross‑style principles: defend only, avoid offensive actions, collaborate on attacks, protect all customers and refuse to attack civilians. He proposed a digital Geneva Convention that would bar attacks on private industry and civil infrastructure, prohibit stockpiling software vulnerabilities, and push governments to sign agreements such as the U.S‑China cyber‑espionage pact. Smith also suggested an international body drawn from private, public and academic sectors to monitor and attribute nation‑state attacks, asserting that the private sector, as the owner of cyberspace, must serve as the primary cyber responder.

The disclosed system concerns a location‑sharing platform integrated with a social network. A map‑based graphical user interface (GUI) displays a user’s avatar together with avatars of the user’s friends on a map. Location data received from a client device is used to compute the user’s current trajectory. By correlating the trajectory with the user’s historical location data, the system predicts a presumed destination and shows an icon representing that destination on the friends’ map GUIs. The predicted destination can be updated in real time, and an estimated time of arrival (ETA) may be computed from the associated trajectory pattern and factors such as speed, traffic or public‑transport schedules. If updates from the client cease, the system extrapolates the user’s position along the known pattern and continues to display the avatar. Users can control visibility by selecting groups such as “Best Friends,” “Friends” or a custom whitelist, and can chat or request arrival notifications from within the map GUI. The server side comprises an API server, an application server hosting a location‑sharing server, a messaging system and a social‑network system, with data stored in a database containing entity, message and location tables. Methods for extracting trajectory patterns from historical location data involve clustering historical trajectories, aligning and averaging them to produce representative patterns, which are then used for destination prediction, location projection and ETA updates.

The passage describes the MSPM0G microcontroller series features: an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU with pre-fetch/cache, system timer, MPU, and NVIC; five power modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with two power domains (PD1, PD0); a clock module with multiple oscillators; a DMA controller with 12 channels supporting various transfer modes; flash memory up to 512kB with ECC and sector-level endurance options; SRAM up to 128kB with write-execute partition capability; GPIO up to 93 pins with wake functionality; IOMUX for pin configuration; 12-bit ADC modules with high speed and averaging; temperature sensor and VREF; comparator, DAC, security features including AES-128/256 and TRNG; communication peripherals (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD); timers (TIMGx, TIMAx); event manager for peripheral interconnect; boot strap loader with password protection; factory constants for device identification; and development tool support.

Radyr, a Cardiff suburb without a pub since 2003, may get a micropub called the Radyr Tap after Vale of Glamorgan Brewery applied for planning permission to open it on Station Road. The plan follows a resident‑led Twitter campaign. The brewery says the venue would serve as a watering hole and celebrate local beer. Consultation ends 19 June, after which Cardiff council will decide. Managing director Phil Newbould says the pub will offer local cask ales, craft beers, wines, spirits and snacks, with no cooked food.

MIT has become the first of nine universities invited by the Trump administration to reject the "Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education," which would require institutional changes in exchange for preferential federal funding. President Sally Kornbluth announced the rejection, stating the proposal would restrict academic freedom and institutional independence. While she noted areas of agreement with the compact's stated values, she argued its premise conflicts with MIT's belief that funding should be based on merit. Other invited universities are still reviewing the proposal, while some state officials have threatened financial consequences for institutions that sign. MIT's rejection has received support from academic circles and some lawmakers.

Prosecutors released cellphone videos of Nikolas Cruz announcing plans to commit a school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School, where he killed 17 people and injured 17 others on Feb. 14. In the videos, Cruz said he wanted to kill at least 20 people using an AR-15 and discussed logistics including taking Uber and timing. He expressed anger, loneliness and hatred. Cruz is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 counts of attempted murder. Prosecutors refuse to waive the death penalty while defense seeks life without parole. The videos became public under Florida's discovery laws despite defense efforts to keep them private. Cruz attended a school for emotionally disabled children, was kicked out of Stoneman Douglas, and had a history of animal killing and his mother called 911 on him nearly 20 times.

The passage urges the addition of roughly a thousand naval officers, noting that junior officers are overworked but conduct themselves admirably; it stresses that an efficient navy is essential to avoid conflict, and that failure to maintain it invites disaster. It also reports that postal revenues rose to $121,848,047.26 in the last fiscal year, the largest increase in the service’s history, and that rural free‑delivery service has proven financially successful, boosting receipts in serviced districts by over ten percent and covering about a third of the nation’s eligible territory, prompting calls for further expansion. Finally, the passage advocates for national irrigation in the far West, scientific forest protection in public‑land states, and immediate action to stop the wasteful slaughter of wildlife such as the elk.

Donald Trump is pursuing a fossil-fuel-driven world order, replacing the liberal international system created after WWII. Domestically, he seeks to cripple renewable energy and perpetuate carbon-based economies. Abroad, he aims to form an alliance of fossil-fuel states (U.S., Russia, Saudi Arabia) while isolating green-energy powers like Germany and China. Key steps include revitalizing the U.S.-Saudi alliance through a $110 billion arms deal and downplaying human rights concerns; undermining NATO and the EU, which support the Paris climate accord; and withdrawing from the Paris agreement to boost coal and oil industries. This trilateral axis would control roughly 57% of global oil and 59% of natural gas output, concentrating immense economic and geopolitical power. Obstacles exist, including divergent interests on Syria and Iran, but Trump's efforts represent a calculated strategy to reshape global politics around energy preferences rather than ideological or civilizational lines.

Researchers blocked the protein Ant2 to reprogram T cells' energy metabolism, making them more effective at fighting cancer. The study, led by Omri Yosef and Prof. Michael Berger at Hebrew University, found that disabling Ant2 triggers a complete shift in how T cells produce and use energy, enhancing their ability to recognize and kill cancer cells. The altered T cells exhibited greater stamina, faster replication, and sharper targeting. The metabolic rewiring can be triggered through genetic modifications or drugs, opening doorways for clinical applications in cancer therapy.

Facebook took two hours to delete live videos of Steve Stephens' shooting of Robert Godwin, prompting a blog post by VP Justin Osofsky. Immigrant‑rights activist Hugo Castro vanished after a Facebook Live plea for help. In Georgia, Democrat Jon Ossoff, 30, a documentary filmmaker, raised $8.3 million to flip the 6th District.

Belgian medical students have poor knowledge and limited exposure to global surgery despite high interest in the field, according to a survey of 304 students at four universities. Global surgery, addressing surgical care disparities, is neglected in global health despite 16.9 million annual deaths from conditions requiring surgical care. The study found only 24.7% of students had prior exposure, and most (75%) wanted more exposure, preferring optional teaching, events, and clinical internships over social media. Knowledge was low; only 24% correctly identified that five billion people lack access to surgical care, and less than 13% knew the Bellwether procedures. Master’s students were less interested in additional exposure and less likely to view global surgery as relevant compared to bachelor’s students. Common obstacles to a career in global surgery included personal responsibilities, language barriers, lack of career paths, financial constraints, and mentorship gaps. The study concludes that curriculum development, including pre-clinical seminars and equitable international internships, is needed to support students pursuing global surgery careers. Limitations include non-random sampling and potential selection bias.

Fifty years after Paul Ehrlich’s 1968 book The Population Bomb began with a Delhi slum description, demographer Jack Caldwell noted similar crowding in London, Paris and New York, questioning whether fears of megacities reflect racism. Cities now house half the world’s people and are projected to reach 66 % by 2050. Urban fertility is lower than rural: Kenyan women have 4.3 children, Nairobi 2.7; Indian women 2.4, Delhi 1.6, Mumbai 1.4, lower than London’s 1.72. While cities curb population growth, they drive a consumption bomb, using three‑quarters of the planet’s materials; London alone consumes about 40 million tonnes of construction materials, 2.4 million tonnes of food, over a billion tonnes of water and produces 8 million tonnes of sewage and 4 million tonnes of waste.

Electrocardiograms (ECGs) are used to estimate echocardiogram (ECHO) variables for early disease detection, especially in resource-limited settings. Extracting ECHO-derived insights from ECGs is difficult due to signal complexity and lack of paired ECG‑ECHO data. The work proposes EchoingECG, a probabilistic student‑teacher framework that combines Probabilistic Cross‑Modal Embeddings (PCME++) with an ECHO‑CLIP teacher to enable many‑to‑many mappings and model embedding variance. By aligning ECG windows with ECHO frames and text using learned mean and variance, the model captures uncertainty and reduces reliance on large annotated datasets. Contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model that extracts structural and functional cardiac information, a knowledge‑distillation approach using ECHO‑CLIP, and experimental results demonstrating uncertainty‑aware downstream evaluation.

This article is a bibliometric analysis of academic publications on digital accessibility in education from 2013 to 2024, using data from Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC. It addresses publication trends, types, research areas, languages, educational levels, countries, and citation relationships. Publications on digital accessibility increased from 12 in 2013 to 502 in 2024, with most in Scopus. For digital accessibility in education, 924 publications were found, rising sharply post-2019. Journal articles are the dominant type, and research focuses on digital accessibility and inclusion, higher education, and computer science. English is the primary language, and higher education is the most studied level. The USA, UK, and Spain are leading contributors. Highly cited works include Gorriz (2023) and Chen Weiqin. The USA and UK are most cited countries. The study concludes that digital accessibility in education is a rapidly growing field post-pandemic, emphasizing the need for more collaboration and quality research.

OGM provides a comprehensive, high-resolution alternative to multiple sequential cytogenetic tests for hematologic malignancies, detecting all standard-of-care findings and additional clinically relevant variants in a single assay. A study testing a streamlined VIA software workflow on 10 myeloid malignancy cases found that OGM identified all SOC-detected variants and further revealed additional findings in five of six positive cases; technologist review averaged 20–45 minutes for non-complex cases and reduced analysis time by approximately 50% compared with previous methods. The workflow enabled efficient, reproducible variant classification and reporting across multiple independent reviewers, demonstrating that OGM combined with VIA can simplify cytogenomic analysis while improving detection and standardization.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model, created by Yale Hirsch, is an active market‑timing strategy that provides entry and exit signals, letting investors avoid constant market exposure and reduce risk versus a passive buy‑and‑hold approach. The model works across any asset class and was backtested over 16 years, showing a maximum drawdown of –27.27% versus –47.77% for a fully invested portfolio. A five‑asset‑class portfolio with equal weights was used for testing: stocks (U.S. large‑ and mid‑cap plus foreign large‑ and mid‑cap, represented by ETFs such as SPDR S&P 500 SPY and iShares MSCI EAFE EFA), bonds, REITs, and commodities. Stocks historically yield the highest returns; bonds lower volatility and correlation; REITs and commodities further diversify the portfolio and decrease asset correlation. Yale Hirsch founded the Hirsch Organization, authored the Stock Trader’s Almanac, and popularized seasonal concepts such as the Presidential Election Year Cycle, January Barometer, Santa Claus Rally and the Best Six Consecutive Months.

Educational disparities—gaps in opportunities, resources, and attainments caused by factors such as socioeconomic status, gender, region, ethnicity, or disability—are regarded as unjust because they depend on ascriptive, uncontrollable circumstances. The paper argues that the normative premise “educational disparities should be corrected” can be justified by luck egalitarianism, which holds that inequalities arising from brute luck (uncontrollable circumstances) are unfair and should be eliminated, while those arising from option luck (choices under individual control) remain the responsibility of the individual.  

Luck egalitarianism therefore supports a fair educational system in which the influence of brute luck on children’s education is minimized, regardless of social background. It offers a balanced approach that both compensates the disadvantaged and respects individual responsibility.

However, Elizabeth Anderson’s critiques of luck egalitarianism identify two major problems. The harshness objection contends that the theory can leave extremely harsh outcomes as the sole responsibility of the individual, even when the circumstances are severe. In education this appears when students who choose to drop out or pursue risky dreams (e.g., a musician who later seeks a high‑school diploma) receive no support despite being unable to afford it. The humiliation objection warns that compensation policies may undermine dignity and create stigma, for example by publicly attributing low achievement to “defective endowments” or by providing targeted help that makes low‑achieving students feel embarrassed.

To address the harshness objection the paper explores two values. The “fresh start” principle, proposed by Marc Fleurbaey and elaborated through dynamic luck egalitarianism (Patrick Tomlin), allows redistribution to individuals who regret past choices and wish to re‑enter education, even if the initial disadvantage stemmed from option luck, because responsibility can diminish over time. The “sufficiency” principle, drawn from sufficientarianism, sets an absolute welfare or resource threshold (e.g., guaranteeing a high‑school diploma) that society unconditionally provides, thereby avoiding harsh outcomes; the paper notes that this requires a controversial choice of threshold and that a pluralistic approach—combining sufficientarianism for basic needs with luck‑egalitarian redistribution above the threshold—can mitigate the harshness problem while preserving fairness.

To counter the humiliation objection the paper invokes the value of respect (Jonathan Wolff). Because determining eligibility for redistribution can force individuals to make “shameful revelations” about their failures, Wolff advocates unconditional cash transfers or practices that avoid humiliating recipients. In the educational context this suggests avoiding labeling low‑achieving students and considering classroom designs (e.g., proficiency‑based classes) that prevent embarrassment while still offering support.

The paper concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should not limit itself to measuring fairness‑based inequality. It should also examine: (1) whether children who have faltered or dropped out have genuine opportunities for a “fresh start” (requiring longitudinal data); (2) how many children achieve a defined sufficiency threshold and what policies secure it; (3) what forms of humiliation children experience in school settings; and (4) relational capacities such as democratic competence and healthy interpersonal relationships. Integrating normative theories of fairness, fresh start, sufficiency, and respect with empirical methods can generate new research questions and guide more comprehensive educational policy.

In March 1986 the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee denied a motion to dismiss filed by East Tennessee Equity, Ltd. and Theodore A. Erck in an adversary proceeding brought by Thomas E. DuVoisin, Liquidating Trustee of Southern Industrial Banking Corporation (SIBC). The Trustee sued under 11 U.S.C. §548 to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances, asserting the claims belonged to the estate and were retained by the Trustee under the confirmed Modified Plan of Reorganization. Defendants argued that the Trustee lacked standing and that any recovery would not be distributed equally among creditors. The court held that §1123(b) expressly authorized the Trustee to retain and enforce the estate’s claims, that the plan gave impaired unsecured creditors ownership interests (stock or stock‑purchase rights) in the successor‑in‑interest, and that recovering the transfers would increase the successor‑in‑interest’s assets, thereby augmenting the value of those ownership interests and benefiting the creditors. The court also noted that a district court had already ruled SIBC was eligible to be a debtor under the Bankruptcy Code. Consequently, the motion to dismiss was denied.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic disorder where abnormal hemoglobin forms sickle‑shaped red blood cells. The condition affects people of all backgrounds, most frequently those of sub‑Saharan African descent, and also occurs at higher rates in South/Central America, Saudi Arabia, India, Turkey, Greece and Italy; in the United States about 100,000 people have SCD. The abnormal cells die early and can block blood vessels, leading to crises (sudden severe pain), acute chest syndrome, anemia, jaundice, organ damage, strokes and other complications. Diagnosis uses a simple blood test, and newborn screening is routine in the U.S.; prenatal testing is also possible. Management includes regular vaccinations, prophylactic antibiotics in children, pain control, treatments to raise fetal hemoglobin, transfusions and, for severe cases, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Lifestyle measures—quitting smoking, limiting alcohol, balanced diet, adequate rest and regular exercise—help reduce episodes. Ongoing education and screening improve quality of life.

University of Exeter research shows the Fal oyster fishery in Cornwall survives because its hand‑hauled sail‑dredges are inefficient, preventing overfishing; motorising the fleet would increase effort nine‑fold. The fishery, Europe's only commercial sail‑driven fleet, is one of three English oyster fisheries; the others have faced temporary closures. The native European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis) is now threatened. GPS tracking and observers confirmed the low efficiency of sail dredging versus modern mechanical methods. The study appears in the Fisheries and Aquaculture Journal.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese candlestick charting method imported into the West in the late 1990s. It smooths price data by averaging open, high, low, and close values, aiming to reduce noise and highlight trends or consolidation phases. Unlike traditional candlesticks, Heikin Ashi does not show real prices and cannot be used directly for trading orders. Its popularity grew after Dan Valcu’s 2004 article. The method acts as a lagging indicator, with haOpen derived from a 3‑period exponential moving average. Researchers tested a simple cross‑over strategy on the S&P 500 (monthly), achieving a 49.4% win ratio and positive equity growth; adding an ADX filter yielded a 5.27% CAGR with low market exposure. Heikin Ashi works best on longer timeframes.

FHA loans treat married couples jointly, requiring lenders to count a spouse’s debt even if the spouse is not on the mortgage. Spouse debt is included in the debt‑to‑income ratio for both purchases and refinances, which can reduce borrowing power. The rule applies only after legal marriage; single or engaged borrowers are exempt. For separate property transactions, a quit‑claim deed is required. Borrowers with credit‑challenged spouses may consider conventional loans, which require a slightly higher down payment but do not include spousal debt.

A resurfaced 2013 YouTube video shows actress Allison Mack praising NXIVM, the organization she was arrested on April 20 for allegedly recruiting women as sex slaves. Mack discusses her desired legacy and praises JNess, a NXIVM-affiliated women's group, while mentioning personal heroes Lena Dunham and Miranda July. NXIVM founder Keith Raniere was arrested about a month earlier.

A 16‑year‑old with severe depression arrived at a Waterloo, Iowa hair salon with matted hair and asked to have it shaved off. Her stylist, student hairdresser Kayley Olson, spent 13 hours over two days untangling the hair and gave her a shoulder‑length haircut, restoring her confidence. Olson shared the experience on Facebook, where it was shared over 75,000 times, prompting discussion about mental health and praise for her compassionate care.

Side Screen is a motion offense that uses a series of continuous on‑ball side screens to stress the defense. It can be initiated by a point guard dribbling to the wing and clearing, or by passing to the wing and making a basket cut that clears to the weak side. Basic options include the wing driving over the screen, pulling up for a jumper, returning the ball to the screener cutting away, or kicking out to a spot‑up shooter. When the defense “shows and recovers,” the screener rolls to the basket and the ballhandler can pass to a teammate with a better angle. The offense also employs ball reversal, back‑cuts, and dribble hand‑offs to maintain continuity. Defensive counters are addressed: “shows and recovers” is countered with post slips, switches create outside mismatches, and double teams are strung out with a 2‑1‑2 alignment that leads to baseline or high‑post feeds. The constant movement forces the defense to cover sideline‑to‑sideline and makes boxing out difficult.

The lecture covers nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, focusing on India-Pakistan as a major flash point for potential nuclear war. Vipin Narang explains deterrence theory (deterrence by punishment versus denial), the three requirements of credibility, capability, and communication. He details how India and Pakistan acquired nuclear weapons: India's program was motivated by the 1962 China war and 1974 peaceful nuclear explosion, while Pakistan's was triggered by the 1971 war and led by AQ Khan who stole URENCO centrifuge designs. India's nuclear doctrine is assured retaliation with no first use policy, while Pakistan maintains a first use doctrine with tactical nuclear weapons to counter Indian conventional superiority. The lecture examines crises including the Kargil War (1999), Parliament attack (2001), and Mumbai attacks (2008), where India's conventional retaliation options became paralyzed by Pakistan's nuclear threats. Narang discusses escalation dominance concepts, AQ Khan's proliferation network, and US-Pakistan relations during the Afghanistan war. He concludes that the combination of proxy militant forces and nuclear weapons makes South Asia particularly unstable, while suggesting potential for a peace deal remains but spoilers prevent progress.

Kieran Trippier, a 27-year-old Tottenham wing-back, described England's penalty shootout win over Colombia as "the best feeling of my career." England was held 1-1 over 120 minutes in Moscow, with Yerry Mina scoring an injury-time equaliser after Harry Kane's penalty. Trippier converted England's fourth penalty before Eric Dier scored the winning kick. England had won only one of their previous seven penalty shootouts. Trippier said he felt confident and focused, crediting the team's spirit and self-belief. Dele Alli played through a thigh injury and praised Jordan Pickford's crucial save from Carlos Bacca, stating he showed he's a top-class keeper.

Over the past three years, global HIV treatment eligibility has shifted dramatically: UNAIDS launched the 90‑90‑90 targets in 2014 and WHO recommended universal “test‑and‑treat” in 2015. Uganda responded by expanding antiretroviral therapy (ART) beyond large public hospitals to smaller and private‑for‑profit facilities with support from PEPFAR and the Global Fund. A three‑year study examined the sustainability of these services using a nationally representative sample of 195 health facilities that participated in the first phase of ART roll‑out.

The research found that lower‑level health centres and small private clinics are relatively constrained in maintaining HIV treatment. Several such facilities discontinued services despite free antiretrovirals (ARVs), equipment support and health‑worker training. Current funding mechanisms disproportionately benefit larger, well‑established hospitals, which attract multiple donor grants, whereas many smaller facilities struggle to secure even a single funder due to demanding performance requirements.

Key barriers identified include shortages and attrition of ART‑proficient personnel, inability to meet donor reporting mandates, and irregular ARV supply. For‑profit providers often lack alignment between their organizational goals and the public‑health objective of mass ART access; some have stopped offering HIV services because donor‑supported treatment attracted long queues and a broader patient mix conflicting with their high‑end, privacy‑focused model. Patients frequently bypass nearer, smaller facilities in favour of larger hospitals that offer a wider service menu, more staff, shorter waiting times and fewer stock‑outs.

The findings indicate that without targeted interventions, smaller, rural and for‑profit facilities are likely to fail, limiting HIV treatment coverage to well‑established hospitals and undermining the scale‑up goal of using diverse service platforms (for‑profit facilities represent about half of all Ugandan health facilities). Recommendations include mentoring programmes linking large hospitals with smaller facilities, service‑purchase agreements between government and private providers, salary support for high‑volume or hard‑to‑reach for‑profit sites, and greater government financing to reduce dependence on external donors and expand fiscal space for HIV treatment.

Mechanical/visual: latch and support tabs lock lever; actuation force <3.6 kgf; pin displacement <1.0 mm; durability ≥50 cycles; 1× magnification inspection; no missing/malformed/damaged or misaligned solder balls; contacts not missing, damaged, or lacking gold plating; cover/base free of cracks/flashing; tabs intact; cover fits without gaps; latch and lever undamaged.

Electrical: contact rating 1.5 A per contact, ≤30 °C rise with ≥6 rows; LLCR ≤25 mΩ initial and final, measured on 200 daisy‑chained pairs (400 contacts) per sample; inductance: single <4 nH, two nearest and three neighboring 3 nH ±10% at 500 MHz/2 GHz; capacitance: two nearest and three neighboring <1 pF at 500 MHz/2 GHz; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10% (three‑pin S1,S2,G), 150 ps rise time if time‑domain; propagation skew <10 ps + 3 ps error for single‑ended and differential signals; crosstalk measured vs partial‑loop inductance and Maxwell capacitance; dielectric withstanding voltage ≥650 Vac; insulation resistance ≥1000 MΩ.

Corn futures are standardized contracts traded on the CME Globex exchange that obligate the buyer to purchase and the seller to deliver 5,000 bushels (full contract) or 1,000 bushels (mini contract) of corn at a pre‑agreed price quoted in U.S. cents per bushel. Full‑size contracts (symbol ZC/ZCH) have a tick value of $12.50 per 0.0025 ¢/bu; mini contracts (symbol XCH) have a tick value of $1.25 per 0.00125 ¢/bu. Trading runs Sunday‑Friday from 5:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. CT with a one‑hour break each day. Settlement is by physical delivery; most brokers automatically close positions before expiry to avoid delivery. Price‑moving factors include weather in major growing regions, USDA reports (WASDE, Prospective Planting, Grain Stocks, Crop Production) and Chinese demand, as well as broader macro data. Corn futures exhibit seasonal patterns, performing better in Jan, Feb, Apr, May, Oct, Nov, Dec than in the summer months. Successful trading requires a strategy that combines technical and fundamental analysis, precise entry/exit rules, position‑sizing and risk‑management; backtests of seasonal strategies can show profitability but also large draw‑downs (e.g., up to 70 % in one test). A second backtest of a momentum‑filtered seasonal approach yielded an average of 1.13 % per trade over 175 trades, invested 13 % of the time with a worst‑year loss of 7.9 %. The contract’s all‑time high is 831.25 ¢/bu ($8.3125) set in 2012 and the low is 100.7 ¢/bu ($1.007) in 1960. A listed corn ETF is the Teucrium Corn Fund (CORN). CFDs on corn are available through online brokers such as IG, but most CFD traders lose money.

State "affidavit of merit" statutes, which require medical malpractice plaintiffs to obtain a doctor's affidavit attesting to negligence or face dismissal, may not apply in federal court according to a Supreme Court case to be argued on Oct. 6. Harold Berk sued Delaware doctor Wilson Choy and Beebe Medical Center in federal court (as a Florida resident) for ankle and foot injuries. Delaware state courts would dismiss such cases without the required affidavit, but federal courts follow federal procedural rules rather than state procedural rules under the *Erie* doctrine. Lower courts dismissed Berk's case, finding the statute substantive. Arguments center on whether the statute conflicts with Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, particularly Rules 8, 9, and 11, and whether it is truly substantive or merely a procedural obstacle to malpractice claims. The Supreme Court will decide if states can impose these requirements in federal court.

AIRSS generates structures near minima. MINSEP and TARGVOL define minimum separation and target volume; constraints are satisfied by overlap removal then lattice and ionic optimization with a truncated Lennard‑Jones potential.

South Carolina has passed an ordinance declaring federal tariff acts null and void within the state, organized military forces, and threatened secession if the federal government uses force to collect duties after February 1, 1833. The president argues that the state's actions are revolutionary, lack constitutional justification, and must be resisted to preserve the Union and supremacy of the laws. He requests Congress to enact measures enabling the relocation of custom houses, use of military force to enforce the laws, and protection of federal officers from state prosecutions.
