In a large US hospital cohort of 19,739 plasma samples from 16,172 patients tested with the Karius plasma microbial cell‑free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing assay (April 2018–Sept 2021), 58 % of reports identified at least one pathogen (701 unique taxa) while 42 % were negative. The median time from sample receipt to reported result was 26 h and 96 % of samples yielded valid results. The test detected bacteria (including anaerobes, streptococci, enterics, staphylococci), viruses (CMV, EBV, HSV‑1, HHV‑6B, BK virus, adenoviruses, TTV), fungi (Candida spp., Pneumocystis jirovecii, Aspergillus fumigatus), and parasites (Toxoplasma gondii, Strongyloides, etc.). The top 50 taxa accounted for 69 % of all detections. The assay identified diagnostically challenging organisms such as Legionella (including non‑pneumophila species), multiple Nocardia and Mycobacterium species (including co‑detections), dimorphic fungi, and zoonotic pathogens. Quantification was reported as molecules per microliter (MPM). Results support the assay’s robustness at scale and its ability to uncover rare pathogens, but also highlight the need for diagnostic stewardship and further clinical outcome studies. Limitations include lack of comparator testing data and incomplete clinical context.

The coach said his team didn't play its best, citing poor decision-making and puck movement, but they fought back to force overtime. He emphasized that average performance isn't acceptable at this stage and they must improve and stay focused on the next game. He credited the opponent for their strong play.

NVIDIA's Q1 FY2020 (ended April 28, 2019) revenue was $2.22 billion, down 31% year-over-year, with net income of $394 million ($0.64 per diluted share), down 68%. Gross margin was 58.4%. GPU business revenue was $2.02 billion (down 27%), driven by declines in gaming and data center, with gaming revenue down 39% to $1.06 billion. Tegra Processor business revenue was $198 million (down 55%). Total cash and marketable securities were $7.80 billion. The company announced a merger agreement to acquire Mellanox Technologies for approximately $6.9 billion. Operating expenses were $938 million, up 21% year-over-year. The company adopted new lease accounting standards, recognizing $470 million in operating lease assets and $500 million in operating lease liabilities. Legal matters include settled litigation with Polaris Innovations and ZiiLabs, and ongoing securities class action and derivative lawsuits.

The passage describes a pilot study that uses a deep‑learning convolutional neural network (CNN) to identify benign and malignant thyroid nodules from ultrasound images. Thyroid nodules are solid or fluid‑filled lumps that may be benign or malignant; early detection is important because thyroid cancer can spread and cause health risks. Current diagnostic methods include physical examination, fine‑needle aspiration (FNA) – which is invasive, painful and time‑consuming – and ultrasound imaging, which provides visual information but requires expert radiologists to interpret the images.

The study employed the publicly available Thyroid Digital Image Database (TDID), which contains ultrasound images sorted by radiologists using the Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI‑RADS). Images were classified as benign (TI‑RADS 2–3) or malignant (TI‑RADS 4–5). The dataset was split into training (55 malignant, 13 benign), testing (7 malignant, 1 benign) and a validation set representing 10 % of the total. To address class imbalance, class weights favoring benign cases by a factor of roughly four were applied. Images were normalized to pixel values between 0 and 1, and augmented using rotation, shifting, and flipping; early stopping prevented over‑fitting.

A hybrid CNN model was built by combining two pre‑trained architectures, VGG‑16 and Inception v3, which were originally trained on large general‑image datasets; input images were replicated to match the required RGB dimensions. The model used binary cross‑entropy loss and was trained for ten epochs with a batch size of eight. Performance was evaluated with sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and ROC‑curve analysis. The hybrid model achieved an accuracy of 87.5 % and an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.929.

The authors note that the small, imbalanced dataset limited the model’s reliability and that larger clinical datasets could improve performance. They conclude that a CNN can accurately determine benign or malignant thyroid nodules from ultrasound images and may be used to assist or replace radiologist interpretation in thyroid cancer diagnosis.

Congress party elected Rahul Gandhi unopposed as its president, succeeding his mother Sonia Gandhi who led the party since 1998. Gandhi, great‑grandson of Jawaharlal Nehru, faces 2019 polls against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who has called him an undeserving “prince” and enjoys 90% favourable support. The announcement coincides with Gujarat elections, seen as a test for Modi amid criticism of growth and a sales tax, with Congress hoping the polls will aid its revival before 2019.

According to Hiscox's 2016 DNA of Entrepreneur report, over 4,000 small and medium firms (including >1,000 U.S.) were surveyed. Fifty percent of U.S. respondents always wanted to be their own boss, but only 37% cited earnings as a primary motive; top motivators were flexibility (68%), control (61%) and remote work (57%). Twenty‑two percent took no holiday. Despite that, 70% reported revenue growth, 68% profit growth and 73% added new customers; growth was strongest in financial services, hospitality and technology/media/telecom. U.S. optimism was highest; 23% plan to hire and 61% have no succession plan. Funding challenges persist: 17% found bank financing harder (up from 13%), 23% used personal credit cards, and alternative sources such as venture capital (11%) and peer‑to‑peer lending (15%). Oregon offers state‑backed programs (Business Oregon, OBDF, CAP, CEF, IDB, EDLF) providing direct loans, guarantees and industrial bonds. Only 34% of U.S. owners said government policies support entrepreneurs (down from 37%); they want lower taxes, more lending, subsidized training and relaxed employment laws. Thirty‑one percent reported that political instability harms business. Oregon’s economy shows full‑throttle growth, with the Bend metro posting 6.6% job growth and the state approaching full employment for the first time since 2000.

The article examines S&P 500 performance relative to interest rates. Traditional finance assumes an inverse relationship, but since the 2000s the correlation has turned more positive. Backtesting a rule that buys the index when interest rates are rising (SMA above the 10‑year yield) yields miserable compounded returns. Conversely, a rule that buys when rates are falling (SMA below the 10‑year yield) shows higher returns and less time in the market, with comparable drawdown. Performance was stronger before the 1990s than during the 2000s‑2010s, especially during quantitative easing. The analysis concludes that holding stocks when rates fall is more profitable than buying when rates rise.

Obama will deliver a farewell address in Chicago on Jan. 10, thanking supporters and reflecting on his eight years, referencing Washington’s 1796 farewell. Trump is sworn in Jan. 20 after pledging to undo Obama’s policies, and Obama seeks a smooth transition despite policy differences.

Marquez Charter Elementary reopened its temporary campus nearly nine months after the Palisades fire, becoming the first public school to return to a campus destroyed by the Palisades and Eaton fires. The site includes 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library and play areas. Enrollment has fallen about 58 percent, from roughly 310 to 130 students, with most students no longer living in the Palisades. The district estimates the temporary campus and full rebuild will cost $202.6 million, with completion by 2028; rebuilding all three damaged campuses could total around $600 million. A parent survey showed 45 percent of respondents wanted a return as soon as possible and 20 percent said they would not stay if the school remained at the shared Nora Sterry campus. Transportation and personal circumstances were cited by over half of respondents. Other schools, including Palisades Charter Elementary and Palisades Charter High School, have not yet reopened. Pasadena Unified has installed portable classrooms at several campuses but has no rebuild timeline.

The MMA Manifesto’s Middleweight Rankings (voting panel: Jeff Fox, Ryan MacDonald, Ricky Leone, Daniel Vreeland) list ten fighters, with Michael Bisping (champion, 39 points) first, followed by Luke Rockhold (35), Yoel Romero (34), and tied Chris Weidman and Jacare Souza (25 each). The study investigates the key trends and emerging areas in open education and how findings can guide policy and practice to enhance equitable access to educational resources. Using a bibliometric approach, the researchers conducted co‑citation and co‑word analyses on 402 articles retrieved from the Web of Science (topic field “Open Education”) in September 2023, employing VOSviewer software.

Co‑citation analysis identified five thematic clusters: “Evolving open education” (focused on the shift from OER to open educational practices), “OER’s role in education” (examines the evolution, sustainability and institutional integration of OER), “Adoption of open education” (covers cost‑saving benefits and student outcomes), “Educational paradigms of MOOCs” (explores learning theories and the paradox between openness and low completion rates), and “Implementation of OEP” (addresses barriers to embedding open practices in teaching).

Co‑word analysis yielded five clusters: “Blended learning in open education,” “Openness in the COVID‑19 era,” “Challenges of OER adoption,” “Inclusive digital pedagogy,” and “Collaborative online academia.” These clusters highlight emerging research directions such as scaling blended models, sustaining post‑pandemic openness, overcoming faculty resistance, promoting equity in digital learning, and fostering ICT‑mediated collaboration.

Implications emphasize open education’s dynamic nature, the benefits of OER (cost reduction, flexibility, personalized learning), and the necessity of institutional support and faculty engagement for successful implementation. Limitations include reliance on a single database (WoS), subjective interpretation of clusters, and threshold selection, with recommendations for future work combining quantitative and qualitative methods and examining contextual variations.

The OHL trading strategy uses the opening, high, and low price levels in the first few minutes of a trading session to generate intraday buy or sell signals. A buy signal occurs when the open equals the low, suggesting bullish sentiment; a sell signal occurs when the open equals the high, indicating bearish sentiment. The strategy is applied on low timeframes (1‑ to 15‑minute charts). Backtesting on S&P 500/ES futures (9:30–16:00 NY) of 1,401 trades yielded an average 0.04% gain per trade; the average rose to 0.06% when the day opened above the previous close and fell to 0.01% when it opened below. Similar tests on WTI crude oil showed a 0.12% average gain under the same open‑above‑yesterday‑close condition. The results indicate the first‑minute price configuration sets the tone for the rest of the day. Code for the strategy is included in a purchasable package of trading systems.

This paper presents a neural solver combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to address three challenges in applying PINNs to complex CAD geometries: enforcing solution conformity across multi-patch domains, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and handling geometry size/shape variations. The method uses NN-based ansatz functions operating on IGA's reference domain, with solutions mapped to the physical domain via NURBS parametrization. Ansatz functions satisfy boundary conditions, ensure differentiability within patches, and maintain continuity across patch interfaces. Training uses the variational PINN framework with the discretized energy functional as the loss function. The method's contributions include control over solution continuity, strong Dirichlet boundary condition enforcement, and natural input normalization. Efficacy is demonstrated on a 2D magnetostatics quadrupole magnet and a 3D nonlinear solid mechanics mechanical holder.

Owen Sound Foodland will start selling beer and cider in April, the first grocery store in the Owen Sound area to do so. It was chosen in an LCBO bidding process for 87 stores, raising Ontario’s beer and cider locations to 370. The 34,000‑square‑foot store on the former Towers/Zellers site in Georgian Bluffs opens March 22, adds fresh, catering, delivery and health, and expands staff from 100 to 160 employees.

First‑principles calculations are computationally expensive; machine‑learning force fields (MLFFs) provide faster alternatives. Graph‑based equivariant neural networks (GNNs) dominate MLFFs but struggle with point‑defect simulations due to oversmoothing and large supercell sizes. Non‑local interactions are important for defect structures. ADAPT (Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer) is a coordinate‑based Transformer that represents each atom as a token using a 12‑dimensional feature vector (coordinates, group, period, electronegativity, radii, valence electrons, ionization energy, electron affinity, atomic radius, molar volume). It uses separate networks for forces and energies, embeds tokens into a high‑dimensional space via MLP, and achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on silicon defect data, outperforming pretrained MLFFs such as MACE and MatterSim while requiring two orders of magnitude less training cost.

About 88% of Ireland’s firms reported earnings meeting or beating expectations, with EPS growth of 8%. Merrion noted Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil and IFG Group missed forecasts, while 16 firms including CRH, Kerry Group and FBD beat estimates. The study examines Turkish parents' experiences with emergency distance education during COVID-19. Using a survey of 2,371 parents, it finds mixed views: 57.7% positive (valuing education continuity, repetition, and health safety) and 42.3% negative (citing inadequacy, difficulty, technical problems, and inequality). Key concerns include student adaptation, lack of interaction, digital divide, and insufficient content. Parents suggest improving testing, content, and course duration, and continuing distance education as support. Recommendations focus on addressing infrastructure, reducing inequality, promoting open educational resources, and enhancing digital literacy.

Suarez recorded a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, a 0.904 WHIP and 40 saves in 70 appearances this year. The Executive Yuan plans to merge the Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission with the Ministry of Culture and Mainland Affairs Council by year-end, eliminating its separate agency status after nearly a century. No budget was proposed for the commission in the next fiscal year. The commission, founded in 1928, has continued despite a 2010 amendment excluding it. Six employees will transfer to the council while remaining staff handle affairs under the ministry. While most of the pan-green camp supports the decision, DPP legislator Tsai Yi-yu opposes merging parts into the council, preferring the commission become part of the Ministry of Culture. KMT legislator Lin Te-fu criticized the proposal as a step toward de jure independence.

The speaker notes the team values both winning and losing, takes pride in that difference, and plays a collective style with superstars like Yzerman and Fedorov working within the system. A close puck incident highlights how small margins turned the game into a loss.

Mourinho has urged Fellaini, in a contract stand‑off, to sign a new deal after he was substituted early in the Tottenham defeat; a knee injury may sideline him for up to two months. Further tests will determine its extent. Fellaini will miss United's next game against Huddersfield and risks missing the Champions League ties with Sevilla, having missed 20 games this season.

Renewable energy output fluctuates because generation depends on variable natural resources, causing grid stability challenges. Operators must keep conventional plants ready and sometimes pay consumers to use excess power to balance supply and demand. As renewable share grows, managing these fluctuations becomes harder.

Prof. Mahesh Bandi of OIST used turbulence theory and wind‑plant data to show why wind‑power fluctuations follow the same spectral pattern as wind‑speed fluctuations. He demonstrated that the similarity arises not from the speed‑power relationship but from the difference between spatial wind‑speed measurements (Kolmogorov’s 1941 result) and temporal power measurements at a fixed turbine. Large‑scale, low‑frequency eddies and smaller high‑frequency eddies cause turbines within the same eddies to produce correlated output. Consequently, geographically dispersed wind plants can smooth high‑frequency fluctuations but retain correlated low‑frequency swings, imposing a natural limit on geographic smoothing. Validation with data from Texas and Ireland wind plants confirmed this limit. The findings help estimate required reserve capacity and guide regional renewable‑mix policies.

Merger arbitrage aims to profit from the spread between a target’s market price and the acquisition offer price when a merger is announced. Investors buy target shares and, when the acquirer pays with stock, short the acquirer’s shares. Success depends on assessing deal completion likelihood, regulatory hurdles, and market conditions. Backtests of the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF (2010‑2023) show a 2.73% CAGR versus 18.52% for the S&P 500, with volatility half the market’s. The Merger Fund (since 2013) delivered a 4.46% CAGR versus 17.37% for SPY, with lower volatility. A Verdad Research study of 835 deals (2000‑2020) found an 89% deal‑closure rate, average 2.0% gain on successful deals, –2.8% loss on cancellations, and a blended 1.5% average return. The strategy is market‑neutral, provides uncorrelated returns, but requires disciplined research and continuous monitoring.

REHO films exhibit color-neutral photochromism, maintaining high transparency in the visible spectrum while losing significant transmittance upon illumination. The kinetics of this photodarkening do not conform to simple zero, first, or second-order reaction models, suggesting a complex mechanism. Electron energy loss spectroscopy indicates higher free hydrogen mobility in photochromic films compared to non-photochromic ones. The transition is best described by a two-phase exponential decay function: a fast initial decay (k1=0.016 s⁻¹) associated with local structural changes and hydrogen loss, followed by a slower decay (k2=0.001 s⁻¹) attributed to long-range hydrogen migration and lattice contraction. This two-process model provides a framework for tailoring the optical properties of REHO for applications such as smart windows.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K with the SEC on January 26 2022, disclosing that the company released its fourth‑quarter and full‑year 2021 financial results via a Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update posted on its website and attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing is made under Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) and includes Item 9.01 (Financial Statements and Exhibits). Tesla’s common stock (TSLA) trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The report is signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Congress failed to pass a continuing resolution, causing a federal shutdown at midnight Wednesday. The U.S. Department of Education says Title I and special‑education funds due Wednesday will be released, but districts that depend on certain federal grants—especially those near military installations or national parks—could face cash‑flow problems; roughly 1,100 districts serving eight million students are eligible for those funds. A shutdown lasting weeks could disrupt Head Start and school‑nutrition programs. Six Head Start grantees expecting new funding Wednesday plan to stay open for now, but longer closures are possible. Low‑income families also receive nutrition assistance through WIC, which states may have to back‑stop. The School Nutrition Association says USDA has enough money to reimburse September–October meals, and SNAP benefits should continue if the shutdown is brief. Most federal employees stop work, pausing civil‑rights investigations, regulatory work and grant‑related communications. Ongoing work such as gathering feedback on Institute of Education Sciences projects and a $500 million charter‑school award could be delayed. The Trump administration is using the pause to push for further downsizing and mass layoffs.

Chicago wheat rose 0.9% to $4.54‑3/4 per bushel, recovering from a 7.8% three‑day loss since April 2013. Corn gained 0.1% to $3.75‑1/2 and soybeans added 0.2% to $10.25. A storm brought about 1 inch of rain to Kansas, Nebraska and Colorado, aiding winter wheat. Arkansas Governor Asa Hutchinson's 42-year-old son, William Asa Hutchinson III, was arrested Monday on DWI, speeding, and implied consent charges in West Fork. He was released on $1,626 bond and is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday and again July 19. The arrest comes less than a year after a circuit judge dismissed a previous DWI conviction due to citation errors. Billionaire investor Paul Kazarian, who holds Greek debt via Japonica, says Portugal’s corporate sector is ripe for investment and opened his office in Lisbon. Both countries' Socialist governments adopted recovery policies after euro‑zone bailouts; Portugal exited its programme in 2014 and enjoys growth, while Greece receives aid until 2018. Kazarian says governments have done well, notes improvements and that Japonica bought up to €2.9 billion of Greek bonds, seeing an anomaly in pricing. The Lisbon office will target real‑estate and technology, leveraging Portugal’s property boom and growing tech sector, to help Portuguese firms expand globally.

Study examined commercial NMC/graphite coin cells (3032) cycled at 1C, 2C, and 3C rates for 278 cycles. Electrochemical testing showed 3C charging caused ~60% capacity loss (from 200 mAh to 42 mAh) and increased internal resistance to 0.34 Ω. XRD analysis revealed c-lattice parameter contraction in the dead cathode (14.27878 Å to 14.27442 Å) and expansion in the graphite anode (6.71906 Å to 6.72132 Å). Li-NRA quantified bulk lithium changes: cathode lost 1.86 × 10²² atoms/cm³ while graphite anode gained 1.38 × 10²² atoms/cm³, indicating lithium migration and plating. SEM imaging revealed cathode particle decomposition with 2.7 at.% oxygen increase and graphite surface cracking with SEI formation. EDS showed cathode density decrease from 4.624 to 4.20 g/cm³ and anode density increase from 1.99 to 2.03 g/cm³. Coulombic efficiency remained stable (~99.8%) across rates. The non-destructive Li-NRA technique effectively profiled lithium distribution, identifying lithium plating on graphite as the main degradation mechanism at high C-rates.

The Education Department announced it will rewrite two Obama-era rules governing student‑loan forgiveness – the Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment regulations – which were created to address fraud at for‑profit colleges. Secretary DeVos called the rules “overly burdensome and confusing,” and said hearings will be held in July. The department said the roughly 16,000 pending claims will be fulfilled. Eight states and the District of Columbia have sued to keep the rules in place, citing critical consumer protections. The changes follow the collapse of Corinthian Colleges (2015) and ITT Technical Institute (2016). Critics argue the revisions could shift costs to taxpayers, while industry representatives say they will protect both students and schools.

T-bills market slightly bullish due to liquidity from N300bn bond maturity; CBN raised N49.60bn on offer, over-subscribed. OBB and OVN rates fell to 1.75% and 2.50%, liquidity increased to c.N600bn positive. Kawann Short's nickname “KK” comes from his first name plus a second K added because of his size. The Panthers signed Short to a five‑year, $80 million contract, ending a year‑long negotiation and avoiding a franchise tag. The deal reinforces general manager Dave Gettleman’s “hog mollies” philosophy and is the penultimate major move of the off‑season for a franchise seeking its first Lombardi Trophy for its 80‑year‑old owner. Gettleman has said his goal is to win now, rejecting the idea of championship windows. Short’s extension is expected to maintain his sack production (17 sacks in the past two seasons) through 2021. The Panthers’ other off‑season moves reflect a win‑now approach: a one‑year contract with Julius Peppers, who has at least seven sacks in 14 of his 15 seasons; retention of the Luke Kuechly‑Thomas Davis linebacker duo; additions of 36‑year‑old safety Mike Adams, safety Kurt Coleman and cornerback Captain Munnerlyn; the average age of projected base‑defense starters is 29.45 years. On offense, Cam Newton’s recent shoulder surgery and prior injuries have prompted a shift toward quicker passes and less zone‑read under coordinator Mike Shula. The Panthers released veteran receivers Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown, signing Russell Shepard and Charles Johnson. At tackle, Michael Oher’s concussion history and a five‑year, up‑to‑$55 million deal for Matt Kalil reflect a focus on immediate help. With the No. 8 pick approaching, Carolina is eyeing offensive playmakers such as Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey or O.J. Howard to support Newton.
Battle of Alberta chess tournament held Feb. 18‑19 at U of C with 30‑40 players using FIDE rules; host U of C Chess Club charges $10 for students and $15 for non‑students.

The passage discloses a cache‑coherent switch on a chip (CCSoC) that utilizes the Compute Express Link (CXL) protocol to interconnect processors, accelerators, memory, storage, and other devices. The CCSoC provides low‑latency, cache‑coherent paths among components, enables resource sharing and pooling without CPU involvement, and supports features such as memory expansion, compression, security, erasure‑coding, and bridging to Ethernet. It comprises upstream and downstream ports, virtual hierarchies, fabric‑manager functions, and hot‑plug capabilities, and defines packet formats, opcode values, and protocol stacks (including CXL 3.0, ROCEv1/3, MPLS, IPsec, and modified L2) for communication across servers, racks, and data centers.

Sugar futures are exchange‑traded derivative contracts that obligate the buyer (seller) to receive (deliver) 112,000 lb of sugar on a future date at a pre‑agreed price. They are listed on ICE (symbol SB, No 11) and on CME Globex (symbol YO). ICE settles physically; CME settles cash. Prices are quoted in cents per pound (ICE) or US $ per pound (CME); the minimum price fluctuation is 0.0001 lb ($11.20 per contract) and contract size is 112,000 lb. Trading hours: ICE 08:30–18:00 London time (pre‑open 01:00–08:30, post‑close 18:30–23:00); CME Sun‑Fri 18:00–17:00 ET with a 60‑minute break. Retail brokers auto‑close positions before expiry to avoid delivery.  

Key price drivers include government subsidies/tariffs in major producing and consuming nations, ethanol demand (tied to oil prices), Brazil’s currency, weather and crop supply. Sugar futures show seasonal strength in February, June, July, November and December. Strategies combine technical and fundamental analysis; a back‑tested ATR‑channel breakout produced a low win‑ratio with many small gains offset by occasional large winners.  

Leverage amplifies risk—a 1 % adverse move with 20× leverage causes a 20 % loss. Historical extremes for SB are 66.00 US cents/lb (Nov 1974) and 2.63 US cents/lb (June 1985). At time of writing SB traded at 19.69 US cents/lb on ICE and $0.1976/lb on CME, giving a notional value of ~$22,131 per contract. Block minimum is 100 contracts.  

Sugar futures can be used for speculation, portfolio diversification or hedging; CFDs offer an alternative without delivery, and ETFs that track sugar are available.

Prime Day discounts on MacBooks start at $200 off. The 13-inch M4 MacBook Air (WIRED Recommends) is the best deal at $800, featuring 16GB RAM and 256GB storage, with support for two 4K external monitors. The M1 MacBook Air remains available at $600. The Supreme Court heard arguments on when police may enter a home without a warrant during emergencies. The case involves William Case, a Montana Army veteran shot by police in 2021 after officers entered his home following a call from his former girlfriend who reported suicide threats. Police saw a suicide note and empty holster before entering without a warrant. Case argues evidence should be suppressed due to the warrantless entry, while Montana courts upheld the entry as reasonable for non-criminal emergencies. The justices questioned applying a probable cause standard outside criminal contexts, with most favoring a flexible "objectively reasonable" standard for emergency entries. A decision is expected by late June or early July.

Market structure trading strategy analyzes swing highs and lows, support and resistance levels, and trendlines to interpret price movements and identify entry/exit points. The three primary market structures are trending (sustained upward or downward price movement), ranging (prices oscillate within a defined range) and consolidating (narrow range with indecision). Key components include swing highs/lows, support/resistance thresholds, and trendlines/channels. Traders use candlestick patterns (e.g., doji, engulfing) and volume analysis to detect shifts, and apply Fibonacci retracements (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%) to locate potential reversal or continuation levels. Popular entry methods are breakout trading (entering after a support/resistance break) and pullback trading (entering during retracements within an established trend). Risk management involves setting stop‑loss orders at key support/resistance and adjusting position size according to pattern strength. Additional techniques include multiple‑time‑frame analysis to confirm structures, and harmonic patterns (Gartley, Butterfly) based on Fibonacci ratios. Combining these tools can improve understanding of trend shifts and market sentiment, but backtesting is recommended.

President transmits dispatches from Minister Wise reporting that vessels are chartered or bought by Brazilian slave dealers, with English brokers, to transport slaves from Africa to Brazil using false clearances, cargo swaps, and crews replaced; goods, including coast goods, are exchanged for slaves, and vessels’ names and papers destroyed to hide involvement; penalties fall on ignorant crew while owners escape; British subjects and capital also implicated; apprenticeship policies perpetuate trade, and measures and restoration of captured Africans to Africa recommended.

Economic policies focusing on tax reductions and debt payment have increased national income to over $90 billion. Foreign relations are positive, with arbitration treaties, successful intervention in Nicaragua, and improved relations with Mexico and China. Most aborigines, Creoles and naturalized foreigners in Hawaii support annexation to United States. The king’s death, with no heir, would create a crisis that could be used to begin annexation as will of Hawaiian majority, through means, with United States approval. Hawaiian residents have been taught by American missionaries for fifty years, and Fifteenth Amendment increased annexation popularity, reflecting Puritan and democratic ideas. Native population about 45,000, down 15,000 since 1866, while 5,000–6,000 foreigners, two‑thirds from United States, dominate foreign capital and hold government offices. Their central location makes them valuable for a naval depot to protect U.S. commerce with China, Japan and Australia. Their climate yields sugar, coffee, rice, fruits, hides, goat‑skins, salt, cotton, wool, for U.S. flour, grain, lumber and manufactures. European powers seize kingdom. King, 41, weighs 300 lb, is last Kamehameha, unmarried, has no heir, and will not name a successor; United States could acquire sovereignty for a modest price, buying Crown and public lands and paying annuities to several chiefs.

A mother posted on Imgur urging parents to keep sick children home after her three‑year‑old, who has asthma and is fully vaccinated, was hospitalized in intensive care unit with RSV after playing with a sick cousin at a holiday dinner.

On June 14, 2017, Verona celebrated Flag Day at the groundbreaking of Annin Lofts, a 112‑unit apartment complex being converted from the historic Annin Flag manufacturing plant (1919‑2013). Developer Ed Russo aims to preserve the building’s character; the Verona Fire Department Honor Guard raised an American flag. The UK Foreign Office is holding only informal talks with Belgian officials about renewing the Anglo‑Belgian Congo purchase agreement. Its proposals aim to increase and diversify revenue, simplify tax payment, promote small‑medium enterprises, protect vulnerable groups and remove obsolete provisions. The work produced two executive orders and five amendment bills, covering modifications to VAT and excise duties and amendments to the CIT, VAT, CET, PIT and IDITR Acts.

After Project Maven controversy sparked protests and resignations, Google said it will draft an ethics policy explicitly banning AI in weapons, incorporating employee feedback. Eleven Ursuline High students and six adults will go to Nicaragua April 2‑8 to help locals with food, housing, home visits, cooking, child care and house construction, learning empathy and compassion.

Pet owners spend about £3,500 in the first year, Nationwide survey finds; cats £2,455, dogs £4,791, horses £12,654, fish £769, rabbits £1,802. The passage argues that improving education requires recognizing teachers’ professional identities rather than focusing only on structural reforms. Drawing on Alsup (2006) and Varghese et al. (2005), it defines “borderland discourse” as the complex negotiation between a teacher’s personal self and professional self, producing a renewed, non‑fixed identity. Teacher identity is portrayed as multiple, transient, and socially and historically situated, shaped by beliefs, emotions, and power relations.

The study examines the (re)construction of professional identities of preservice language teachers in a Letras program, emphasizing the theory‑practice gap reported by novice teachers. Two participants, Laura and Richard, illustrate this process: both experience tension between university‑based theory and school realities, leading to critical reflection and adaptation of pedagogical approaches. Their identities evolve from student/apprentice to intern teacher and finally to language teacher, a fluid, back‑and‑forth progression rather than a linear sequence.

Findings indicate that supervised internships and virtual platforms such as Moodle serve as spaces for sharing frustrations, emotions, and achievements, functioning as emotional scaffolding for identity development. The analysis concludes that narrative practices in both presence and virtual contexts offer privileged insight into how language teachers construct and negotiate their professional selves.

CFPB's final rule requires payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers can repay within 30 days and limits debits without reauthorization. Consumer advocates say it prevents lenders from profiting by setting up borrowers to fail. The CFPB found 80% of loans are not repaid on time and 15% of new loans lead to sequences of at least ten loans. Industry trade group says the rule would cut loan volume by half, force many of 16,000 stores to close, and push customers to unregulated lenders. The rule takes effect in 2019 and may be reversed by Congress; Republicans have introduced legislation to curb the agency. April Pew poll found 70% of Americans want more regulation. Robinson Cano, who had been in a slump, broke out with a 441‑foot homer, and Nelson Cruz followed with a 410‑foot shot, providing the Mariners with ample run support.

Oil prices fell on Thursday as easing Middle‑East geopolitical tensions reduced the risk premium that had supported markets; Brent crude slipped about 1.4 % to $65.07 per barrel and WTI fell to $61.55, while rising U.S. inventories and slowing demand in transport and manufacturing contributed to the decline. Analysts noted that with tensions subsiding, market focus has shifted back to fundamentals such as non‑OPEC production growth and subdued European and Asian demand, forecasting relative stability absent a resurgence of tensions. The lecture discusses coherent states of light, which are eigenstates of the annihilation operator and represent minimum uncertainty states closest to classical electromagnetic fields. Three quasi-probability distributions (Q, P, W) describe quantum states in phase space with different operator orderings. Coherent states have Poissonian statistics with a second-order correlation function g2=1, while thermal states are super-Poissonian with g2=2. Number states exhibit sub-Poissonian statistics with g2<1 and appear as rings in phase space with random phase. The Hanbury Brown Twiss experiment measures intensity correlations to distinguish classical light (g2≥1) from non-classical light (g2<1). Single photons cannot be created by simply attenuating coherent states; instead, they require single-atom sources in cavities or heralded generation through Raman transitions.

Marine heatwaves disrupt the ocean's biological carbon pump, preventing carbon from reaching the deep sea where it can be stored for millennia. Research in the Gulf of Alaska found that two successive heatwaves (2013-2015 and 2019-2020) caused plankton shifts that altered carbon cycling. During the first heatwave, carbon particles accumulated at 200 meters depth instead of sinking. During the second, carbon built up at the surface and lingered at 200-400 meters depth. Both events jammed the carbon conveyor belt, increasing the risk that carbon returns to the atmosphere. The study used robotic floats and ship-based surveys to track ocean conditions and highlights the need for sustained monitoring as marine heatwaves intensify.

Yen Bai province plans to upgrade its agro‑forestry sector by investing in processing of wood, tea, cinnamon, cassava, bamboo and camellia. It has 104 wood‑processing plants (176,000 m³/yr) targeting 300,000 furniture pieces and revenue of 850 billion VND (2020) rising to 1.7 trillion VND (2025). Tea processing uses 99 facilities (1,200 t fresh leaves/day) producing 25,000 t dry tea/yr; cassava factories produce 66,000 t flour/yr; cinnamon‑oil extractors yield 955 t/yr. The province aims to raise camellia and bamboo product value to 50 billion VND (2020) and 200 billion VND (2025), and build cattle‑meat facilities with >3,000 t/yr capacity.

In this case, the district court addressed whether actions brought by Bill Vassar, former County Attorney of Lincoln County, Oklahoma, should be dismissed because Vassar ceased office in January 1939 and his successor, Frank McVey, did not substitute as plaintiff within the six-month period required by Rule 25(d) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. The defendants argued the actions abated under Rule 25(d), which allows continuation of a case by a successor officer only if substitution occurs within six months of the successor taking office. The court found the rule's language clear and mandatory, and that no substitution was made within the required period. It concluded the actions should be dismissed without prejudice in all listed cases.

The Imperial and Royal Government of Austria‑Hungary, on behalf of itself and its allied powers, reports that it received, via the United States, the enemy states' reply to its December 12 note proposing peace negotiations. It states that the enemy rejected the proposal, calling it insincere, and gave a communication that cannot be answered. The Government asserts that its peace offer was made in good faith and aimed solely at defense, while the enemy seeks the destruction of the Austro‑Hungarian monarchy, the conquest of Alsace‑Lorraine, the partition of Turkey and the subjugation of Bulgaria. It cites the fate of the Irish, Finnish, Boer, North‑African and Greek peoples as evidence of the enemy's violation of small nations. It disclaims responsibility for the continuation of the war and declares that it will carry on the struggle until it obtains a peace that secures the existence, honor and free development of its peoples and enables European states to cooperate on a basis of equal rights.

Mario Batali has surrendered oversight of daily operations at his restaurant empire after reports of sexual misconduct spanning at least 20 years. At least four women, three of them employees, described incidents including unwanted touching. Batali acknowledged the complaints and apologized. A company spokesperson said an employee filed a complaint in October and Batali was reprimanded and required to attend training. He will also take leave from the ABC show “The Chew.” Food Network suspended plans to relaunch his show “Molto Mario.” The Batali & Bastianich Hospitality Group operates Babbo, Carnevino, Pizzeria Mozza and is a partner in Eataly. The Mario Batali Foundation advocates child nutrition and Batali opposes hydraulic fracturing.

Starbucks (SBUX) stock has been flat since late‑2015, pressured by weaker comparable‑store sales. Mobile Order & Pay accounts for over 20% of orders at some stores, creating crowding during peak hours, but new solutions deployed and comps are recovering. Limited‑time drinks such as the Unicorn and Frappuccino Happy Hour lifted sales, while loyalty‑program changes and a change in traffic counting dampened results. First dividend was $0.05 in April 2010, rising to $0.25 by November 2016, a CAGR over 26%. In China, Starbucks opens about 500 stores per year (one every 15 hours) and expects this pace for decades; comparable‑store sales rose 7% last quarter, driven by middle‑class growth.

The Grocery Basket Score (GBS) is a model that rates shopping baskets for health properties based on mortality outcomes, using dietary data from NHANES 2001–2018 linked to mortality data. It employs Cox proportional hazard models with density signals (nutrients relative to total calories) and deficiency signals (risk of nutrient deficiency), combining separate models for foods and beverages via calorie-weighted averaging. The food model penalizes saturated fats, sugar, sodium, and deficiencies in protein, vitamin C, or iron, while rewarding fiber; the beverage model penalizes calorie density. Validation on Open Food Facts items showed a correlation of 0.60 with the Nutri-Score, and stronger correlations with the AHEI (–0.62/–0.60) compared to the Nutri-Score (–0.48/–0.47). The GBS does not require manual ingredient annotation and can be deployed on retailer loyalty or digital basket programs.

Cam Newton apologized for sexist comments made to a female reporter, which resulted in the loss of his Oikos Greek Yogurt sponsorship. In a video posted October 5th, he called his words degrading, apologized to women, and said he learned a lesson from the incident.

The Fifth Circuit reversed the district court's judgment and remanded the case. The court held that debtors filing above-median income Chapter 7 bankruptcy cases may claim the IRS Local Standard vehicle ownership deduction even when they have no loan or lease payment on their vehicles. The court adopted the "plain language approach," interpreting "applicable" in 11 U.S.C. § 707(b)(2)(A)(ii)(I) to refer to the debtor's geographic region and number of vehicles, rather than requiring an actual ownership expense. The court rejected the "IRM approach," which only allowed the deduction when a debtor had a debt payment.

AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine facilitates moving pages between memory tiers, extending SEV and SNP features. It enables safe migration of DMA-targeted pages and SNP-protected guest pages, requiring IOMMU enablement. Commands support up to 128 pages via ring buffer. A Pre-Migration state is defined for SNP pages. Performance peaks at 128 pages per command. Reload procedures vary by EPYC family; Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major value 71. IOMMU structures and ring buffers cannot be migrated.
Liberty Island evacuated July 4 after a climber ascended the Statue of Liberty; six people were arrested for hanging an “Abolish I.C.E.” banner, and police negotiated the climber’s descent.

FoodSEM is a fine-tuned open-source LLM for food named-entity linking, developed to align food data with FAIR principles. It uses instruction-response data from CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA corpora annotated with Hansard taxonomy, FoodOn, and SNOMED-CT entities, enhanced with artificial instances for balance. The model is based on Llama 3 8B, fine-tuned via LoRA, and achieves F1 scores up to 98% on artificial samples, outperforming 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot baselines. On real corpora, performance varies by dataset and ontology, with higher precision than recall due to NER errors propagating to NEL. Contributions include published annotated corpora in IR format, a robust model, and a benchmark dataset for food NEL.

Checkr, founded in 2014 by Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon, began as a background check tech startup serving gig economy companies. After launch, founders noticed high rejection rates for job candidates with conviction records—disproportionately Black and Hispanic—despite fast and accurate software. This motivated a shift toward fair chance hiring, or second chance hiring, which offers fair and equal job opportunities to individuals with records without lowering hiring standards. By 2024, Checkr was valued at $5 billion, had raised $678 million, employed 1,200 people, and completed 30 million background checks annually; 4% of its own workforce were people with records.

In 2021, Checkr signed the Pledge 1%, committing 1% of employee time, products, equity, and profits annually to its fair chance mission. A Corporate Social Responsibility division, led by Ken Oliver (who spent 24 years in prison), operationalized the pledge, while the Checkr.org foundation handled advocacy and fundraising.

Roughly 80 million people in the U.S. have arrest or conviction records—over one‑third of the workforce. The justice‑impacted population is predominantly Black and Hispanic, with 1.2 million in state or federal prisons (93% male, 32% Black, 24% Hispanic). Mass incarceration costs taxpayers over $80 billion per year. Formerly incarcerated individuals face unemployment rates above 27%, lower incomes, and over 44,000 collateral consequences restricting employment, housing, and education. The unemployment and economic instability contribute to high recidivism: two‑thirds of released prisoners are rearrested within three years.

In response, the 2019 Fair Chance to Compete for Jobs Act prohibits federal agencies and contractors from requesting criminal history until after a job offer. Fifteen states mandate that private employers remove conviction history questions from applications, and 37 states and 150 cities/countries have banned the box for government jobs. The Second Chance Business Coalition, cofounded by JPMorgan Chase in 2021, had nearly 50 members by 2024, including Target, Bank of America, and GM.

Fair chance hiring benefits companies by enlarging talent pools, reducing turnover (Checkr’s fair chance attrition is 5% versus 22% for other hires), and improving performance—85% of HR professionals and 81% of business leaders report fair chance hires perform same or better. Diversity through lived experience enhances workplace culture, and diverse companies earn 2.5 times higher cash flow per employee with 35% higher productivity. With 9.5 million job openings and 6.5 million unemployed in early 2024, fair chance hiring helps address labor shortages.

Checkr offers tools aligned with its mission: Candidate Stories (launched 2020, nearly 45,000 submitted) lets candidates provide context on records; Assess (launched 2019, filtered records for over 2 million individuals) filters by conviction type, age, or recency; and an Expungement tool helps candidates clear ineligible charges. A fair chance dashboard helps customers track hiring against EEOC guidelines.

Internally, Checkr hired its first fair chance talent in 2015, growing to nearly 60 employees by 2024 through nonprofit partnerships. All employees attend the same onboarding, including a simulation on post‑release hurdles. Fair chance employees choose whether to disclose their backgrounds; some become evangelists. Employees receive 21 paid hours annually to volunteer with justice‑related organizations. In July 2023, Checkr launched a 12‑month fair chance apprenticeship program offering full benefits, mentors (one justice‑impacted, one from the team), and training on business tools.

Checkr emphasizes aligning mission with business: its mission flywheel drives impact through customers. CEO Yanisse stresses that mission success depends on business strength; companies must connect mission to revenue to sustain impact. Yanisse aims to convince more companies—especially large public firms—to adopt fair chance hiring, citing its strategic value, talent acquisition benefits, and alignment with diversity, equity, and inclusion goals.

The DAWN‑Plasma trial was a prospective, multicenter, open‑label, phase II proof‑of‑concept study that randomized 320 patients to receive four units of high‑antibody‑titer convalescent plasma plus standard of care (PLASMA+SOC) and 163 patients to standard of care alone (SOC) using a 2:1 allocation. The primary endpoint – proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on day 15 – showed no difference between groups. No statistically significant differences were observed for any secondary endpoints (including day 30 outcomes), and estimated treatment effects (odds ratios, hazard ratios, differences) were close to the identity value, indicating similar outcomes in both arms. Safety profiles were comparable: 28.13 % of PLASMA+SOC patients and 30.06 % of SOC patients experienced at least one adverse event; serious adverse events occurred in 20.62 % vs 20.68 %; fatal adverse events in 10.31 % vs 9.82 %. Treatment‑related adverse events were reported in 12 patients (3.75 % of the PLASMA+SOC group) and treatment‑related serious adverse events in 7 patients (2.19 %). Laboratory parameters (CRP, ferritin, D‑dimer) and body temperature showed no clinically meaningful differences between groups. Neutralizing‑antibody titers (NT50) rose from baseline to day 6, but the increase was not influenced by plasma treatment (adjusted difference in log₂ NT50 = 0.08, p = 0.766). Higher NT50 at baseline and at day 6 were associated with better clinical outcome, whereas the magnitude of NT50 change was not. Transfusion‑related side effects were observed in 19/320 patients (6.0 %); no transfusion‑related acute lung injury (TRALI) cases were reported. The trial concluded that early administration of high‑titer convalescent plasma did not alter the natural course of hospitalized COVID‑19 patients.

Internal ESD protection clamps inputs to within 0.2 V of the rails; a series resistor is advised when the source impedance is low and the current should be limited to ≤10 mA. The device includes an internal power‑on‑reset (POR) circuit that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply passes VPOR ≈ 1.65 V, ensuring a known start‑up for both open‑drain and push‑pull outputs.  

The basic comparator switches low when the non‑inverting input (VIN) is below the reference (VREF) and high when VIN exceeds VREF; swapping the inputs inverts the logic. Propagation delay (tpLH, tpHL) varies between transitions and lengthens as the overdrive voltage (VOD) decreases, especially below 100 mV.  

The TLV321x has only ~1.8 mV of internal hysteresis, so external hysteresis is recommended to prevent output chatter. An inverting hysteresis configuration uses a three‑resistor network with defined trip‑point equations, while a non‑inverting configuration uses a two‑resistor network and a reference, providing separate VIN1 and VIN2 thresholds whose difference equals the hysteresis.  

A typical low‑side current‑sensing circuit uses an amplifier to scale the shunt voltage and a comparator to signal an over‑current condition; bypass capacitors (0.1 µF low‑ESR) must be placed close to the V+ pin, and output and input traces should be separated to avoid coupling; a small series resistor on the output can damp ringing and controlled‑impedance routing is recommended for long paths.  

The device is ESD‑sensitive and must be handled with appropriate precautions to avoid damage.

Exchange‑traded funds (ETFs) are baskets of securities that trade on stock exchanges like individual stocks. They track indices, sectors, commodities, bonds, currencies or other asset classes and offer real‑time price updates, ticker symbols and the ability to buy or sell throughout the trading day. Unlike mutual funds, ETF shares are priced continuously and their outstanding share count can change daily through a creation‑redemption mechanism that keeps market price close to net asset value.  

ETFs have grown rapidly since the first U.S. listing (SPY) in 1993; by 2020 over 7,100 ETFs existed globally with U.S. assets exceeding $5.8 trillion. They provide diversification, low expense ratios, tax efficiency and the flexibility to employ margin, short‑selling or leverage. Common strategies include trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, pair trading, quantitative modeling, options and volatility‑based approaches. Many of these strategies are best executed with back‑testing and are suitable for both long‑ and short‑term horizons.  

Key advantages are cost‑effectiveness, liquidity and ease of trading; major risks are market volatility, tracking error and, for leveraged or inverse ETFs, amplified volatility. Liquidity determines bid‑ask spread and trading costs; lower expense ratios preserve returns. Taxation follows stock rules: short‑term gains taxed as ordinary income, long‑term gains at lower rates. ETFs can be used for day‑trading, swing‑trading, or long‑term investing, though beginners are advised to practice in demo accounts, back‑test strategies and consider broad‑market, high‑liquidity funds.

AMD Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine facilitates efficient migration of memory pages between tiers, supporting DMA-concurrent migration and SNP guest pages. It uses a ring-buffer command interface with commands: PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP, each processing up to 128 pages per batch. Driver initialization requires checking ENGINE_READY, configuring a 4KB-aligned ring buffer (1–255 pages), and enabling IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bit. Operations are asynchronous, with interrupts for queue events (RBWritePtr_Err, RBMem_Err, QfreeIntStat, QthreshIntStat, IntOnError, IntOnComplt); pause/resume is supported. Pages must be 4KB-aligned (2MB pages must be smashed), DMA-mapped pages require IOMMU host page table updates, and SNP guest pages need specific RMP states (Guest-Valid/Invalid for source, Pre-Migration for destination). Firmware reload is possible only when the ring buffer is paused and torn down, with version checks. Errors are reported per command or via MCA; multi-page batches may yield partial success with per-page status.

Udvada, a Zoroastrian village in Gujarat, gave rise to families such as the Udvadias, whose members became doctors. Dr Zarir Udvadia, a member of that family, faced bureaucratic restrictions when treating a girl from Bihar diagnosed with drug‑resistant TB in 2012. By October 2016 the girl weighed 25 kg and had failed standard drugs; Dr Udvadia recommended Bedaquiline, a powerful drug with side effects, but its use under the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme was limited to select cities, excluding her. He and the father petitioned the Delhi High Court, which ordered Bedaquiline’s administration. The treatment succeeded; the father credited Dr Udvadia’s support. Dr Udvadia reports that thousands need Bedaquiline, he treats 30 patients with a 70 % success rate, and access remains difficult. The case illustrates concerns about inflexible policies, while noting TB’s resurgence, compliance requirements, 18‑month regimen, and carrier rates.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces second‑generation RT Cores that double ray‑triangle intersection, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structured sparsity that double matrix‑multiply throughput, and a new SM design that doubles FP32 processing per clock. The SM includes 128 CUDA cores, four third‑gen Tensor Cores, one second‑gen RT Core, a 128 KB L1/shared‑memory cache and a 256 KB register file. ROP units are now attached to each GPC, raising total ROPs to 112 (up from 96 in TU102). GA10x supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling at up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering up to 936 GB/s bandwidth on a 384‑bit (12 × 32‑bit) interface, with 512 KB L2 cache per controller (6 MB total). The architecture provides third‑generation NVLink with four x4 links delivering 56.25 GB/s per direction (112.5 GB/s total) and a PCIe Gen 4 host interface offering up to 64 GB/s. Concurrent execution of RT and compute workloads is enabled, and a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray‑traced motion blur up to 8× versus Turing. RTX IO offloads storage decompression to the GPU via Microsoft DirectStorage, achieving up to 100× throughput and dramatically reducing CPU usage. Fifth‑generation NVDEC provides hardware‑accelerated decode for AV1 (first GPU to do so), H.264, HEVC, VP9, and others, while seventh‑generation NVENC encodes H.264/HEVC with quality comparable to x264 Medium and supports up to 8K HEVC. Display outputs include HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC for 8K 60 Hz. The RTX 3090 (GA102) offers 24 GB GDDR6X, the RTX A6000 and A40 provide 48 GB GDDR6 (scalable to 96 GB via NVLink), and the RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X protects memory transactions during overclocking. Overall, Ampere delivers up to ~2× programmable‑shading, ray‑tracing and AI performance and up to 1.9× power efficiency versus Turing.

Merck announced it is halting the late‑stage trial of its Alzheimer’s drug verubecestat after an independent assessment found virtually no chance of success. Decision follows Eli Lilly’s termination of its solanezumab trial, which also showed no improvement over placebo. Experts described the verubecestat failure as a substantial setback, noting hopes for the drug. About 47 million people worldwide live with dementia, a figure projected to double to 131 million by 2050. No proven treatment slows Alzheimer’s progression, and the disease’s underlying cause remains unknown. Verubecestat belongs to a class of BACE inhibitors designed to block amyloid plaque formation; its failure has raised doubts about the beta‑amyloid hypothesis. Other companies continue testing BACE inhibitors, while Biogen’s aducanumab has shown encouraging early results. Merck’s early‑stage verubecestat data are expected in February 2019, and its shares fell nearly 2 % after the announcement.

The appeal involved Edward C. Turner's six-month license revocation for refusing a breath test after a DUI arrest. The District Court modified the revocation to three months. The Supreme Court majority reversed the modification, holding the District Court lacked authority to reduce the suspension period under the statute as interpreted in State v. Kopczynski, noting a 1975 amendment created a limited hardship exception. A dissent argued § 6-211 authorized modification based on the driver's record and that Kopczynski was distinguishable. The suspension was affirmed with the modification reversed in a 5-4 decision.

Vermont City Electric (VCE) is a municipal electricity utility created in 1905 to reduce the cost of supplying power to the city. By 2008 it served roughly 16,000 residential accounts, 2,845 small commercial customers and 784 large commercial customers in an area of about 16 square miles. VCE has focused on demand‑side management (DSM) since 2000, but the 2008 economic downturn forced spending cuts and the Finance Committee limited 2009 DSM capital expenditures to $800,000.

VCE’s supply comes from three categories: owned generation (the low‑cost wood‑fired McNeil plant and the high‑cost oil‑fired VCE‑GT turbine used for peaks), medium‑term hydro‑based contracts (NYPA, NYSEG, VEPPI), and the wholesale market (ISO‑NE) whose price rises with demand. A 5.2 MW wind project is expected online in 2012 at a flat cost.

Electric load is described by a load‑duration curve divided into five blocks: Blocks 1‑2 cover the highest‑load 14 % of hours, Blocks 3‑4 cover the middle 81 % of hours, and Block 5 covers the low‑load 480 hours (about 5.5 %). Demand is forecast to grow 0.52 % per year in population and 0.22 % per year in per‑capita electricity use.

Nine DSM programs are detailed: Business New Construction, Business Existing Facilities, Residential New Construction, Residential Existing Homes, Retail Products, Commercial Smartlight, Commercial Heating & A/C, Commercial Outdoor Lighting, and an LED Streetlight Program. Each program has a 2009 direct cost, estimated MW savings per load block, and a six‑year energy‑saving effect; total annual DSM cost is about $1.03 million.

The case presents a modeling assignment: first build a linear program for the least‑cost supply plan in 2009, then extend it to a six‑year (2009‑2014) net‑present‑value model that includes the wind capacity from 2012, and finally a mixed‑integer model with binary variables to select which DSM programs to implement while respecting the $800,000 budget, also tracking carbon emissions. The analysis task is to recommend which programs to retain, assess carbon impact, and evaluate whether the budget limit influences the optimal mix.

This lecture introduces MIT's Effective Field Theory (EFT) course. Prerequisites include quantum field theory 2, with QFT 3 lecture notes posted as background. Grading consists of five biweekly problem sets and end-of-term presentations, with no exams. The course covers basic EFT concepts in the first half and soft-collinear effective theory in the second half, with no required textbook. EFT enables physicists to focus on specific energy scales and extract interesting physics at various scales, rather than learning physics purely bottom-up. The course distinguishes between "top-down" approaches, where one starts from a known high-energy theory and integrates out heavy particles, and "bottom-up" approaches, where one constructs an effective theory without knowing the high-energy completion. Key elements include identifying relevant degrees of freedom, determining symmetries, and performing power counting—the latter being as fundamental as gauge symmetry for making the theory consistent and renormalizable. Examples include non-relativistic QED, heavy quark effective theory, and chiral perturbation theory. The standard model itself is an effective field theory with infinite higher-dimensional operators.

Methods, apparatuses and systems for multi‑user (MU) transmission in wireless local‑area networks (WLANs) are disclosed. A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may contain a receiver, transmitter and processor that receive a null‑data‑packet (NDP) MU MAC PLCP protocol data unit (NDP MU MAC PPDU). The WTRU determines whether the received frame meets an NDP condition, processes an NDP signal (SIG) field that carries MU control information, generates a response based on the NDP SIG field and the control information, and transmits the response. In another embodiment the WTRU determines the NDP MAC frame type from the NDP SIG field and generates a response according to that type and the MU control information.

The disclosure addresses limitations of IEEE 802.11ac group‑ID mechanisms, which support only a limited number of downlink MU‑MIMO groups and cannot handle large clusters, mixed orthogonal frequency‑division multiple access (OFDMA) and MU‑MIMO schemes, or per‑transmission scheduling. New MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms are proposed that use a cluster ID, a membership bit‑field (N bits) and a position bit‑field (m·N bits) signaled in a clustering management frame. The position bit‑field can be updated per transmission opportunity (TxOP) either in the PLCP header/SIG field of the data packet or in an MU control frame preceding the data transmission. The mechanisms support many clusters, combinations of OFDM MU‑MIMO and OFDMA, and flexible per‑transmission resource allocation.

Two NDP MU MAC PPDU formats are described. Both include a legacy preamble (L‑STF, L‑LTF, L‑SIG) for backward compatibility. The first format contains a single HE‑NDP‑SIG field, which may be fixed‑length (Format A) or variable‑length (Format B) and carries an NDP MAC frame body, an NDP indication, a CRC and a tail. The second format adds an HE‑NDP‑SIG‑A field (common to all users) and an HE‑NDP‑SIG‑B field (user‑ or resource‑specific). Both formats convey fields such as NDP MAC Frame Type, MU mode, AP address/TA, Group ID, Duration, Sync info, Bandwidth, and NDP‑SIG‑B‑Present, and may include a Partial AID (PAID) for implicit resource allocation.

MU control frames are defined for downlink and uplink. Downlink frames include an MU‑RTS (reserve TXOP and schedule DL) and an MU‑CTS (respond to MU‑RTS). Uplink frames include an MU‑Poll (reserve TXOP and poll STAs), an uplink response/request (ULR) (respond to poll or request UL), an MU‑Schedule (schedule UL), and an MU‑ACK (acknowledge UL). A Response‑Protocol field indicates the format of the reply, whether sub‑channel‑selection or synchronization information is required, and whether users transmit simultaneously in time, frequency, code or spatial domains. STAs decode the L‑SIG length to detect an NDP frame, verify the NDP indication in the HE‑NDP‑SIG, identify intended receivers by AP address and Group/Cluster ID, prepare the appropriate response (e.g., MU‑CTS) after a SIFS, and set their NAV according to the Duration field.

The disclosure also describes an UL multi‑user channel‑access scheme using a COBRA poll, ULR, COBRA schedule and MU‑ACK, and a DL scheme using a G‑RTS and G‑CTS. By using compact NDP MAC PPDUs for control signaling and limiting control‑frame duration, the described techniques reduce MAC overhead while supporting a large number of users, mixed OFDMA/MU‑MIMO operation, and dynamic per‑transmission clustering.

The motion asks that Champion be removed from Quinton Tellis’s capital‑murder case and punished, that a September retrial be postponed and that the state attorney general take over the prosecution. Tellis is accused of burning 19‑year‑old Jessica Chambers to death on Dec. 6 2014; his first trial ended in a hung jury. The author reflects on confessions from a 10-day family road trip to several National Parks. He questions whether the weather community should convey forecasts with uncertainty ranges similar to how Yellowstone provides estimated eruption times for Old Faithful. He notes that outlets like Capital Weather Gang use graphics to show probability ranges for weather events, addressing the challenge of communicating uncertainty. Observing a bison almost charge a visitor at Yellowstone prompted him to reflect on how people often ignore warnings and prioritize familiar goals over risk awareness. At Glacier National Park, he noted the decline from over 100 glaciers in 1910 to 26 active glaciers by 2015 due to rising temperatures. He recounts an encounter with someone who dismissed climate change as "fake news" based on experiencing cold weather while camping, exemplifying how people often equate local weather with global climate patterns.

The Draw play is a run that mimics a pass look before handing off to a back, aimed at exploiting defenses expecting a throw. It works best in pass‑heavy offenses or obvious passing situations where defenders are far off the ball. Its main weakness is vulnerability to interior blitzes, which can leave unblocked rushers; offenses often pair it with an RPO to mitigate this. The passage details blocking assignments for the offensive line, tailback, quarterback, and receivers against a 3‑4 odd front and a 4‑3 even front, describing pass‑set techniques, lane‑creation moves, and route‑selling responsibilities. Two variations are noted: QB Draw, which uses an athletic quarterback’s mobility and often tags a perimeter RPO, and Lead Draw, used from 12‑personnel Strong‑I, where a tight end releases, the double team shifts, and a fullback inserts for the middle linebacker. Effectiveness of the Draw depends on consistently showing a pass threat from the formation.

Mannerheim was anxious; Finns misjudged the war. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digitalization in Moroccan education, prompting a study on the sustainability of ICT use post-pandemic. Surveying 130 primary and secondary teachers who abandoned technology after resuming face-to-face classes, the research identified barriers to sustained ICT integration: lack of devices, internet connectivity, digital resources, and training; limited technology and techno-pedagogical knowledge; and insufficient institutional support. Findings indicate that nearly half of the initial sample did not sustain ICT use despite prior reliance during the pandemic. Barriers are attributed to leadership factors rather than demographic variables like age, gender, or location. Recommendations include unifying distance learning platforms across academies, establishing effective coordination channels, developing teacher training platforms, capitalizing on pandemic-era digital content, and providing devices to learners. The study underscores the need for enhanced educational leadership to meet ISTE standards and ensure long-term ICT sustainability in Moroccan schools.

First‑principles DFT+U calculations on chromium diiodide (CrI2) monolayers and bilayers reveal that the magnetic ground state of the bilayer is the indirect BA′ stacking with intralayer stripe‑type antiferromagnetism and antiparallel interlayer alignment. In all bilayers the nearest‑neighbour in‑plane A‑B exchange remains antiferromagnetic (~−4 meV) and the intra‑chain A‑A/B‑B exchange ferromagnetic (~+2.7 meV); both increase by ~6–10 % relative to the monolayer. The symmetric in‑plane anisotropy ∆Jxy is ≈1.48 meV for A‑B bonds and ≈1.03 meV for A‑A/B‑B bonds, essentially registry‑independent. Dzyaloshinskii‑Moriya interactions appear only in indirect (inversion‑breaking) registries, with magnitudes 0.02–0.08 meV; the Heisenberg part of the interlayer coupling is one order of magnitude weaker (≈0.03–0.2 meV) and changes sign with registry and interlayer spin texture. Indirect stackings also produce a spontaneous in‑plane electric polarization of a few µC cm⁻² (up to ≈10 µC cm⁻²) that serves as a fingerprint of the stacking symmetry. Sliding between registries costs ~25–50 meV per formula unit, allowing mechanical switching of magnetic state and electric dipole. These results identify CrI2 bilayers as a model system for stacking‑controlled magnetism and magnetoelectric coupling suitable for reconfigurable 2D spintronic devices.

Soccer positions are grouped into four general categories: goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders and forwards. The goalkeeper is the only player with handling privileges within the penalty area and must wear a contrasting jersey. Defenders (backs) protect the goal, cover opponents and can start counter‑attacks. Midfielders link defense and attack, require all‑around skills and stamina. Forwards are the primary attacking force, create scoring chances and must perform under pressure. Position names often have synonyms and shorthand acronyms (e.g., G, GK, K for goalkeeper; D, B for defenders; M, MF for midfielders; F for forwards). Specific positions within each group (center backs, sweepers, attacking midfielders, strikers, etc.) depend on the team’s formation (e.g., three‑back, four‑back). Coaches select a formation, define position names and use them consistently. Young players should experience all positions to develop awareness and avoid early specialization.

A single monitoring solution should automatically discover and monitor any deployed application, requiring a common interface. Standardized interfaces exist but differ in protocol and communication style. Most monitoring tools include plugins to adapt interfaces. The adapter pattern separates the application container from an adapter container that translates its interface to the monitoring system. This decoupling improves comprehensibility and maintainability, enables independent versioning, reuse, and resources for each container.

Using Python, a Bollinger Band trading strategy was backtested. Historical data for Microsoft was obtained with the yfinance library. Pandas and numpy were imported, and Bollinger Bands were calculated as a 20‑day simple moving average plus/minus two standard deviations. A position column was created: 1 when the adjusted close fell below the lower band, –1 when it rose above the upper band, using np.where. Daily strategy returns were computed by multiplying the daily price change by the lagged position. Cumulative returns were obtained with .cumprod() and plotted as an equity curve. The strategy yielded a 2.65% annual return while being invested only 10.6% of the time. The article emphasizes demonstrating Python code rather than providing investment advice.

Scientists at Skoltech built a mathematical model of memory that examines how information is encoded and stored. Analyzing the model shows that memory capacity is maximized when concepts are represented in a seven‑dimensional conceptual space, corresponding to an optimal number of seven senses. Engrams—the basic memory units—are described by sets of features that correspond to sensory qualities; as they are repeatedly triggered, they sharpen or become diffuse, reflecting learning and forgetting. The researchers mathematically proved that engrams converge to a steady state and that the greatest number of distinct engrams occurs at seven dimensions, regardless of model specifics. The findings suggest that expanding sensory inputs could improve learning, recall, and artificial intelligence systems.

The WilliamsVixFix, introduced by Larry Williams in 2007, is a synthetic VIX that estimates price volatility for any security using the formula (Highest(Close,22) – Low) / Highest(Close,22) × 100. The 22‑day window approximates a month of trading and the indicator is a lagging, mean‑revertive measure of recent volatility. It closely mirrors the real VIX in levels, swings, magnitude and timing, and has a negative correlation with the S&P 500: high readings reflect fear and short‑term buying opportunities, low readings indicate complacency and market peaks. Multiple back‑tested strategies on the S&P 500 and QQQ produced hundreds of trades with profit factors ranging from 1.78 to 2, win rates around 75 %, and modest drawdowns, often outperforming buy‑and‑hold while being invested only ~20 % of the time. The author notes that results vary and that quantified testing is required before trading.

Melania Trump held a meeting with executives from Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google, Twitter, and the Internet Association to address cyberbullying and internet safety, her first public event on the issue. Major tech firms have policies against harassment but depend largely on user reports; Facebook provides policy guidance, Instagram links to anti‑bullying resources. Despite these efforts, harassment remains widespread—Pew found 41% of US adults were harassed online—and companies have struggled to police content at scale (Facebook billions of posts daily, YouTube 300+ hours of video per minute). Twitter introduced new policies to protect women from non‑consensual nude images after hateful tweets proliferated; Yik Yak shut down after schools banned it due to bullying. Companies balance free‑expression concerns with preventing abuse; some of President Trump’s tweets have drawn calls for removal, but Twitter has kept his account citing news value. No federal anti‑bullying law exists; state laws vary. Melania Trump’s earlier campaign pledge to fight cyberbullying contrasts with her husband’s Twitter behavior; she also focuses on child well‑being, including the opioid crisis.

This disclosure pertains to a sole structure for an article of footwear that includes an outsole with an annular cleat set and a plurality of radial cleat sets. The outsole has a plantar surface and a peripheral surface. The annular cleat set comprises a first plurality of traction elements arranged about a central axis, while each radial cleat set comprises a second plurality of traction elements aligned along a radial axis intersecting the central axis. At least one traction element in each radial set includes a peripheral cleat formed on the peripheral surface. The annular cleat set can be located on the medial side of the outsole in the ball portion of the forefoot region and includes major cleats arranged in an outer ring and minor cleats in an inner concentric ring. The major cleats have a greater height than the minor cleats, and both types exhibit a tapering width and may include reinforcing ribs. Radial cleat sets include lateral radial sets adjacent to the lateral side of the forefoot plate and an anterior radial set at the anterior end. In each lateral radial set a major cleat is positioned adjacent to the peripheral surface, a series of minor cleats decrease in size toward the central axis, and a peripheral cleat projects at an oblique angle from the peripheral surface. The anterior radial set on the medial side similarly includes a major cleat adjacent to the peripheral surface and decreasing minor cleats toward the central axis. A heel cleat set in the heel region includes major cleats around the periphery and minor cleats interior to them. The outsole may be constructed as two modular plates: a forefoot plate bearing the annular and radial cleat sets, and a heel plate bearing the heel cleat set. Each plate can be a composite of an outer shell of a first material and an inner skeleton of a second material, with optional inserts forming portions of the traction elements. The sole structure further includes a midsole with a casing and a core, a shank interposed between the forefoot and heel plates, and a cradle attached to the shank. The midsole casing extends from the anterior to posterior end and contains the core in a recess. The shank provides longitudinal rigidity and may include ribs. The disclosed arrangement provides traction in lateral and longitudinal directions, enables rotation about the central axis, and improves traction when the medial side of the sole structure is lifted from the ground.
