The edition publishes diplomatic records from the Department of State and the American Commission to Negotiate Peace, supplemented by papers of Wilson, Lansing, Bliss, White, Long, Miller, and House. The volumes are arranged in three groups covering active U.S. participation until December 9 1919, following criteria approved by Secretary Kellogg on March 26 1925. Major minutes and proceedings are printed fully; secondary material is omitted. Dr. Cyril Wynne oversaw the project, compiled by Dr. James S. Beddie, Dr. Morrison B. Giffen, and John W. Foley Jr., under Dr. Ernest R. Perkins, with editorial direction by Miss Matilda F. Axton, and support from G. Howland Shaw, Laurence C. Frank, Library of Congress, Yale University, and Hoover Library. Only three treaties were ratified by the United States: the Spitsbergen Treaty, the Liquor Traffic in Africa Convention, and the Convention revising the Berlin and Brussels Acts. It includes sections covering termination of hostilities, American preparations, representation, policies, and proposals for a League of Nations.

Research on lead-free organic ferroelectric/antiferroelectric systems in the phenyltetrazole (PHTZ) family identifies APHTZ as a canted ferroelectric with FE ordering along the a-axis coexisting with AFE ordering along the b-axis, while MPHTZ is a uniaxial antiferroelectric. Both crystals exhibit proton tautomerism where dipole formation and switching result from proton movement in double-well potentials. Pseudospin models were developed to describe their behavior, using mean field approximation to predict phase transitions, dielectric properties, and polarization switching. The models reproduce basic structural features and available experimental data, showing APHTZ exhibits single FE hysteresis loops for fields along the a-axis and predicted double loops for fields along the b-axis, while MPHTZ displays classical uniaxial AFE behavior with double hysteresis loops. Phase diagrams with tricritical points are predicted for both materials. The authors note experimental data is insufficient for definitive conclusions and recommend measurements of temperature-dependent polarization, permittivity, and phase transition properties to validate the models.

This study examined whether genetic variation in vitamin B12 metabolism influences Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, age‑at‑onset, or progression. Using the largest PD GWAS of European ancestry, pathway‑specific polygenic risk scores, rare‑variant analysis in whole‑exome/whole‑genome cohorts (AMP‑PD and UK Biobank, 4,929 cases/68,029 controls), and Mendelian randomization (MR) with B12 GWAS as exposure, the authors found no robust association of common or rare B12‑related variants with PD. Polygenic risk scores showed only nominal significance (OR≈1.03–1.06, p≈0.04–0.06) that did not survive multiple‑testing correction. A rare high‑CADD variant in CUBN (p.G3114S) was suggestively associated in AMP‑PD (OR=3.3, p=3.56×10⁻⁵) but not replicated in UK Biobank and was classified benign; TCN2 also showed a nominal signal. MR analysis found no causal effect of B12 level on PD risk, age‑at‑onset, or progression, and no genetic correlation between B12 and PD traits. Power was sufficient for risk and onset but limited for progression outcomes. The study was limited to European ancestry and underpowered for some progression analyses. The authors conclude that B12 metabolism does not have a major genetic role in PD, though low B12 in patients may result from non‑genetic factors such as gastrointestinal dysfunction or altered microbiota, and should still be managed clinically.

The lecture covers energy absorption in foams, explaining how to convert compressive stress-strain curves into energy absorption diagrams by plotting energy versus peak stress on log-log scales, normalized by the solid modulus. The diagrams consist of three regions: linear elastic behavior, a stress plateau where energy increases without increased stress, and densification where stress increases significantly. The optimal operating point is the "shoulder point," representing maximum energy absorption at the plateau stress.

These diagrams can be generated from experimental data or foam models. For elastomeric foams, a single diagram represents all foam types since both modulus and plateau stress depend on the solid modulus. Similar diagrams exist for foams with yield points, though they are specific to the ratio of solid yield strength to solid modulus.

For impact protection applications, key parameters include the protected object's mass, contact area, maximum drop height, and tolerable deceleration. Using these, peak stress can be calculated, and foam material, density, and thickness must be selected. An iterative process determines foam thickness and density, typically converging quickly.

Bicycle helmet foam selection uses material selection charts showing plateau stress versus densification strain, with expanded polystyrene at 5% density identified as effective. The lecture also briefly discusses woodpeckers' ability to withstand high decelerations (up to 1500g) due to three factors: small brain size, brain orientation providing a contact area advantage, and short impact duration. The next topic will be sandwich panels using honeycombs and foams.

The Inquiry, as of December 15, 1917, is organized with an Executive Committee of four overseeing division chiefs who manage research assistants and collaborators from various universities including Harvard, Yale, Columbia, Princeton, and others. NVIDIA Tensor Cores, introduced in Volta, give an 8× mixed‑precision speedup over FP32. Ampere‑based A100, with 108 SMs and third‑generation Tensor Cores, delivers 16× peak mixed‑precision versus FP32 FMA. Improvements improve utilization, reduce bandwidth, latency, and complexity. Deep learning workloads are long layer chains performing GEMM; each GEMM’s output is tiled across SMs. Ampere targets strong scaling, preserving workload as A100 Tensor Cores consume data 2.5× faster than V100.

Federal courts will use non‑appropriated funds to continue paying staff through Oct 17 during shutdown. Judges’ salaries, protected by Constitution, will be paid regardless of appropriations. Most proceedings will continue, but hearings may be rescheduled if DOJ attorneys are unavailable. Supreme Court also plans to rely on such funds. At least ten district courts have issued orders delaying civil cases, and some judges are refusing to pause them, including cases about IRS records, Live Nation antitrust suit, grant restrictions, layoffs and Medicaid bans. When funds run out, courts will operate under Antideficiency Act, potentially requiring staff to work without pay while each court determines staffing for core constitutional duties.

Lehman Brothers' 2007 financials showed $19 billion in net revenues, $4 billion in net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, and $282 billion in assets under management. The lecture explains leverage using mortgage examples: a 20% down payment yields 5:1 leverage, while a 5% down payment (as in subprime mortgages) yields 20:1 leverage. High leverage, such as Lehman's 16:1 ratio, means small asset declines can rapidly deplete capital. Topics include mark-to-market, subprime mortgages, adjustable rate mortgages, defaults, and bankruptcy (e.g., Lehman filing for Chapter 11 after the Fed declined to provide a backstop). The lecture discusses Fed rate cuts, inflation risks, and job prospects for finance students amid market dislocation. It then transitions to fixed income securities: definitions, examples, and market size ($6.4 trillion in mortgage-related securities, among others). Key concepts include valuation of coupon bonds and pure discount bonds (including STRIPS), and risks such as inflation, credit, timing, liquidity, and currency risk.

The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign‑aid while Congress decides on a rescission request under Impoundment Control Act. Justice Kagan, joined by Justices Sotomayor and Jackson, dissented, calling the case uncharted with high stakes. President Donald Trump welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron to the White House on Tuesday with a South Lawn ceremony, the first state visit of his administration. Trump praised the U.S.-France alliance and thanked Macron for France’s support during the recent missile strike in Syria. Macron said the two nations would fight terrorism, limit weapons of mass destruction in North Korea and Iran, and work together on climate action, noting his push to keep the United States in the Paris climate accord.

The visit included a private dinner Monday at Mount Vernon, where the presidents and their wives arrived by helicopter, toured George Washington’s home and planted an oak from the World War I Battle of Belleau Wood. Tuesday’s agenda covered security, trade and the Iran nuclear agreement. Trump has signaled possible withdrawal before a May 12 deadline, while Macron calls the deal imperfect but urges staying until a Plan B exists.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended March 31 2015. Total revenues were $939.9 million, up 51% from $620.5 million in Q1 2014, driven by higher Model S deliveries. The company reported a net loss of $154.2 million compared with $49.8 million in the prior‑year quarter; basic and diluted net loss per share was $1.22 versus $0.40. Gross margin rose to 27.7% from 25.0%, helped by increased production volume, manufacturing efficiencies and cost reductions. Research and development expenses more than doubled to $167.2 million, while selling, general and administrative expenses grew to $195.4 million, reflecting global expansion of stores, service centers and the Supercharger network. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.51 billion at quarter‑end, down from $1.91 billion at year‑end 2014, with operating cash flow negative $131.8 million and investing cash outflows of $432.3 million (primarily $426.1 million in capital expenditures). Capital spending for 2015 is expected to be about $1.5 billion, including investments in Model X production, the Gigafactory (where $146.2 million had been incurred through March 31 2015) and infrastructure. The company issued $920 million of 0.25% notes due 2019 and $1.38 billion of 1.25% notes due 2021 in early 2014, and entered a $100 million warehouse facility in March 2015, drawing $77.7 million. Model X deliveries are planned for late Q3 2015; Model 3 is targeted for 2017. Tesla is party to a securities class action appealing a dismissal, and faces other legal proceedings and various market‑risk factors detailed in the filing.

Ken Lay resigned as Enron's chairman and CEO on Jan. 23, 2002. Stephen Cooper was being considered as his successor. Investigations into Enron's collapse included congressional hearings on document shredding by Arthur Andersen, with the DOJ and FBI also probing. Enron disclosed it overstated earnings by $586 million since 1997 and had $3 billion in obligations to partnerships. The company's Australian unit faced liquidation. Former Enron employees held a rally organized by Jesse Jackson. Congress considered legislation on 401(k) rules in light of employees' lost retirement savings. Book deals were being made about Enron's downfall. Charities previously funded by Enron were adjusting to the loss of donations.

ADS9803 initialization requires register writes after power-up or reset with a free-running sampling clock. The device supports speed-boost mode enabling up to 8MSPS sampling for user-selected channel pairs while remaining channels idle. Register access uses 24-bit SPI frames with three register banks, where bank 0 is always accessible and banks 1-2 require selection via address 0x03. Daisy-chain topology connects multiple ADCs with shared CS and SCLK signals, requiring N×24 SCLKs per register write, with DAISY_CHAIN_LEN configured to exclude ADC1. The device operates as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) and no specific power-up sequence requirement. Applications include ATE with Total Unadjusted Error (TUE) specifications and bandwidth modes up to 700kHz for wide-bandwidth operation.

The OpenChart‑SE project was launched to overcome the scarcity of publicly available Swedish electronic health records (EHRs) for clinical natural language processing (NLP) research. Swedish EHRs are sensitive and difficult to access, and existing publicly released corpora are almost exclusively in English. OpenChart‑SE uses a citizen‑science approach: volunteer Swedish physicians and medical students create artificial EHRs for imagined but plausible patients seen in an emergency department.

Data were collected via a Swedish mock‑EHR form built with KoboToolbox, published on the project GitHub repository. The form mirrors real Swedish emergency‑care EHRs, containing fields for chief complaint, background, examination (with a standard “ABCDE” exam for priority‑one patients requiring immediate care), ECG/laboratory results, and assessment/diagnosis. Submissions could be anonymous or include contact details.

During the pilot phase (Nov 2021–Dec 2022), 50 artificial EHRs were gathered and reviewed by an experienced emergency physician; all passed quality control and are released as the OpenChart‑SE corpus version 1 on Zenodo. The 50 records cover a wide range of emergency‑care scenarios: 12 % describe priority‑one patients, 58 % are female, ages range 18–94 years (mean 52), and there are no pediatric cases. Most records contain some missing fields, and the most common main diagnoses are “other/unspecified abdominal pain,” “calculus of ureter,” and “dyspnea.” Text lengths vary from 954 to 2 738 characters.

The artificial records closely resemble real Swedish emergency‑department EHRs in language style and medical content, providing a valuable resource for developing and validating Swedish clinical NLP tools. The project is now open for additional submissions from trained physicians and medical students; updated versions of the corpus will be released periodically.

Particle released an LTE-enabled module for devices that were reliant on retiring 2G/3G networks, offering built‑in cloud and SIM support. LTE hardware is cheaper and provides better battery life and range for industrial and dispersed sensor networks. The module is part of Particle’s suite (device cloud, OS, developer toolkit) and includes two LTE CAT‑M1 models (B13 and B2/4/5/12), certified, low‑profile, surface‑mountable, powered by Qualcomm MDM9206 and u‑blox Sara‑R410‑02B. Evaluation kits are $89; individual modules $69. Particle serves 8,500 customers and 140,000 developers, including Engie, Ideo, Grow Labs and Keurig.

Light‑field imaging captures the full 4‑D distribution of light rays (spatial and angular information) in a single snapshot, enabling high‑speed volumetric acquisition without mechanical scanning. The underlying theory is based on the 7‑D plenoptic function, which reduces to a tractable 4‑D light‑field (L(x, y, θ, φ) or L(u, v, s, t) in two‑plane parameterization). Geometric‑optics models describe ray demultiplexing by microlens or pinhole arrays, while wave‑optics models address diffraction, interference, and high‑NA effects for high‑fidelity reconstructions. Rendering techniques such as computational refocusing, synthetic aperture, multi‑view stereoscopic output, and tomographic inversion allow digital reconstruction of 3‑D volumes from the captured light field.

In biomedical applications, three main implementations are highlighted. Light‑field microscopy (LFM) uses microlens or Fourier configurations to record 2‑D spatial and angular data in one exposure; iterative deconvolution (e.g., Richardson‑Lucy) reconstructs volumes at camera frame‑rate speeds, achieving cellular resolution in brain imaging, organelle dynamics, and subcellular studies. Fourier/extended light‑field microscopy (FLFM/XLFM) improves sampling of spatial frequencies, reducing artifacts and extending resolution across neuroscience, cell biology, and organoid research. Light‑field mesoscopy provides large‑field‑of‑view (several mm) volumetric imaging of cortical circuits and whole‑organ structures, with systems such as MesoLF, CM2, RUSH3D demonstrating functional calcium imaging and adaptive‑optics correction. Light‑field endoscopy integrates microlens or GRIN‑lens arrays into endoscopic probes to enable real‑time 3‑D visualization of tympanic membranes, vocal folds, gastrointestinal tracts, and vascular territories, either by adding a light‑field module to conventional optics or by replacing entrance optics with compact arrays; flexible fiber‑bundle approaches have explored encoding depth in intracore modal patterns.

Current challenges include the inherent trade‑off between speed, field of view, depth of field, and resolution due to the constant space‑bandwidth product of the system. Strategies to mitigate these limits involve compressive sensing, event‑based cameras, virtual scanning with deep learning, and hybrid optical‑computational designs. Meta‑optics (nanostructured metasurfaces) offers alternative demultiplexing, polarization‑multiplexed focal control, and integration with sensor chips, but optical performance still lags behind compound lenses. Deep‑learning reconstruction (fully end‑to‑end or hybrid models) accelerates volume recovery, improves resolution, and reduces artifacts, yet issues of generalization, interpretability, and training‑data dependence remain. Overall, light‑field imaging provides a scalable, snapshot‑based route to high‑speed 3‑D biomedical visualization, with ongoing advances in hardware (cameras, meta‑optics) and AI‑driven processing extending its utility across microscopy, mesoscopy, and endoscopy.

Panthers kicker Graham Gano missed three of four field goals in a loss to the Buccaneers. Gano complained about the Bucs displaying live footage of his kicks on the stadium video board and using a red background when Tampa Bay's kicker was shooting. Coach Ron Rivera also objected to a slow-motion replay of a hit being shown twice. A league official confirmed using video boards to distract kickers violates rules.

A hockey player discusses adapting to a forward position by being more creative with the puck while keeping his game simple. He focuses on creating space for his linemates and adjusting to their playing style. He emphasizes the physical and energetic nature of playoff hockey and credits team depth for players being prepared when opportunities arise. He stresses taking the series one period at a time rather than looking ahead.

The paper argues that teacher education must be reformed to meet the demands of 21st‑century classrooms. It identifies five key areas: integrating technology using the TPACK framework, fostering critical thinking and problem‑solving through constructivist methods, preparing teachers for diverse learners via inclusive and differentiated instruction, promoting collaboration and lifelong learning through professional learning communities, and addressing global challenges such as climate change and social justice. The discussion emphasizes that aligning teacher preparation with the TPACK model and constructivist principles equips educators to create interactive, equity‑focused, and inquiry‑based learning environments. Literature reviewed supports that ongoing professional development, cultural competence, and global awareness improve teaching practice and student outcomes. The authors conclude that teacher education is a continuous process that must be responsive to emerging trends and research.

On March 11, 2015, NVIDIA Corporation appointed Michael McCaffery and Persis Drell to its Board of Directors. McCaffery also joined the Board’s Audit Committee. Each new director received an initial grant of 10,656 restricted stock units vesting semi‑annually over three years from March 11, 2015, a pro‑rated annual grant of 2,361 restricted stock units vesting on May 20, 2015, and a pro‑rated cash retainer of $15,625 payable on March 11, 2015. Indemnity agreements were also entered into with each director.

Sana Bhat, a 24‑year‑old Kashmiri hotel‑management student, was diagnosed with leukemia in April 2015. Her family sold land in Srinagar to fund treatment in New Delhi, but she relapsed and died in February. In October 2016 a relative posted a Facebook appeal with her photo and a hospital certificate, raising $40,000 in a month. The appeal inspired Srinagar businessmen to launch #TwentyRupeesMiracle in February, requesting 20 rupees (≈$0.30) monthly for the Lalla Ded Charity, named after a 14th‑century Kashmiri poet. Over 50,000 donors signed up within days, and the campaign aims to double that to 100,000, generating about $30,000 monthly. Cancer cases are rising in Kashmir; SKIMS charges $600–$6,000 for treatment, while per‑capita income was $970 in 2015. The charity uses social media to verify patients and routes funds through Help Poor Voluntary Service and the Cancer Society of Kashmir. It helped an 18‑year‑old with acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy by providing $1,000 for medicines, after which he regained mobility. The initiative is described as a tribute to Sana’s battle.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on March 15, 2021, reporting that as of that date Elon Musk’s title changed to “Technoking of Tesla” and Zach Kirkhorn’s title changed to “Master of Coin,” while both continue to serve as CEO and CFO, respectively.

BitMine chair Tom Lee says the bubble has burst in digital asset treasury companies. DATs are businesses that acquire cryptocurrency holdings and operate publicly traded vehicles. Lee learned about Bitcoin at JPMorgan in 2012, founded Fundstrat, and later became chairman of BitMine, which follows MicroStrategy's model but for Ethereum. BitMine holds over 3 million Ethereum tokens (2.5% of total supply) with a goal of acquiring 5%. Lee argues Ethereum remains the "blockchain of Wall Street" but is skeptical about the broader DAT asset class as more companies launch with various cryptocurrencies.

The Italian stock market index (IT 40) tracks the 40 largest companies on the Borsa Italiana, including Monclear, Pirelli, Tenaris, Ferrari and Campari, and has shown little growth since 1998. Backtests of daily performance reveal that Tuesdays and Wednesdays generate the best returns, while Mondays and Fridays perform poorly. An end‑of‑month seasonal strategy outperforms buy‑and‑hold, delivering a 6.17% CAGR versus 4.71% while being invested only about a third of the time. Historically, March and June are the strongest months, May the weakest, with the rest of the year essentially flat. Seasonal strategies may improve performance in this largely sideways market.

The MSPM0 G‑Series 80 MHz microcontrollers include a Keystore controller for secure AES key management (up to four 128‑ or 256‑bit keys), a CRC‑P module supporting 16‑bit CRC16‑CCITT and 32‑bit CRC32‑ISO3309, a MATHACL accelerator for 32‑bit math operations, UART peripherals (UART0‑UART1, UART3‑UART7) with asynchronous communication, LIN mode, programmable baud rates, separated TX/RX FIFOs and DMA support, an I2C interface supporting 7‑/10‑bit addressing, Standard/Fast/Fast‑Plus modes up to 1 Mbit/s, SMBus 3.0, glitch filtering and separate FIFOs, an SPI peripheral supporting up to 32 Mbit/s, flexible frame sizes, PACKEN packing, and TI/Motorola/National Microwire formats, a CAN‑FD controller compliant to ISO‑11898‑1 up to 5 Mbit/s with transmit/receive buffers, a Low‑Frequency Sub‑System (LFSS_B) containing RTC_B with counters, alarms, calibration and temperature compensation, an independent watchdog timer (IWDT_B) with programmable periods, a windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) with interval mode, general‑purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) timer blocks with capture/compare, complementary PWM and fault handling, analog I/O connection details, IOMUX for pin multiplexing, a Serial Wire Debug interface, a Boot‑strap Loader (BSL) with UART/I2C options protected by a 256‑bit password, device factory constants for identification and calibration, and development tools such as LaunchPad, Code Composer Studio, IAR and Keil.

Fiat marks the 60th anniversary of the 500 Jolly Spiaggina with the limited‑run “Spiaggina ’58” (1,958 convertibles). Finished in Volare Blue with vintage logos, 16‑inch wheels, a white belt‑liner and a two‑tone interior, it offers Uconnect 7‑inch HD LIVE with Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, navigation, DAB and a 1.2‑L 69 hp Euro6D engine. The brand also released a video tribute to the 1958 song “Volare,” while Garage Italia and Pininfarina produced a showcar interpretation featuring sky‑blue/pearl white livery, a removable roof, built‑in shower, cork floor and a bench seat. The new series joins a long line of special 500 editions; the model has sold over two million units worldwide, leads the European small‑car segment since 2013 and posted its best five‑month period in 2018.

A May 1902 State Department circular announced that U.S. military occupation of Cuba had ceased and that an independent republican government under President Tomás Estrada Palma had been inaugurated; diplomatic officers were directed to convey this information. In a separate instruction, the Department asked Argentina to permit U.S. consular officers to represent Cuban interests until Cuban consuls are appointed. A congressional act of June 14 1902 amended passport statutes to allow U.S. diplomatic and consular officers to issue passports to residents of U.S. insular possessions (e.g., Puerto Rico, the Philippines, Guam) who owe allegiance to the United States; applicants must declare no other allegiance, provide affidavits from at least two witnesses, and pay the same fee as U.S. citizens.

The GST Council set a 0.1% tax on export‑procuring goods with refund. It extended AA/EPCG/EOU schemes to foreign and domestic sourcing, exempting holders from IGST and cess and deeming domestic supplies to them as exports with supplier refund. Banks and PSUs can import gold without IGST for exporters. FIEO said merchant exporters make up over 30% of exports and operate on thin margins, and an e‑wallet for exporters will launch from April 1 under DGFT norms.

The court held that mandamus is a proper remedy to compel the county treasurer to pay city tax penalties, interest, and fees held in trust for the City of Bisbee, and that the county and its supervisors are not liable. Under the 1917 statutes the treasurer must remit such amounts to the city; the later statutes govern and create a trust exempt from the statute of limitations until demand or refusal. After June 12 1931, however, a new law credits all interest, penalties, charges, and fees to the county’s general fund, so the city has no claim to amounts collected after that date. The trial court’s dismissal was reversed; the demurrer as to the treasurer (Kitchel) was overruled and the case remanded.

The speaker praised the team's performance around the net and in the defensive zone, noting battling and scrambles, rebounds and a few bounces, felt good despite difficulty with rebounds. He also mentioned the goaltender’s elite playoff performance as something to emulate.

AggregateIQ, a Canadian firm, told a Canadian parliamentary committee it is not a subsidiary of Cambridge Analytica and denies having accessed the Facebook data harvested by that company. Zack Massingham and Jeff Silvester said AIQ only places online ads and builds campaign software, does not harvest data or share client information. AIQ also denied responsibility for a violent video used in Nigeria’s 2015 election, stating it refused to distribute the material. In the Brexit campaign, AIQ worked with four groups—Vote Leave, BeLeave, Veterans for Britain and the Democratic Unionist Party—and received more than £625,000 from Vote Leave for work for BeLeave and £100,000 for Veterans for Britain. AIQ said it saw no evidence of coordinated spending between Vote Leave and BeLeave and that the funding was treated as a donation, an arrangement it called unusual but legally assured.

The Sansa Fuze manual describes how to operate the player: the hold switch disables all buttons when locked; the power switch turns the device on/off and resets it; the thumbwheel navigates menus and adjusts volume. The player has a built‑in rechargeable battery, charged via USB or optional AC/car adapter, with charging status shown on screen. Media files are transferred by dragging to the internal MUSIC folder, using Windows Media Player, or the Sansa Media Converter. Music, audiobooks, video and photos can be played, with options for repeat, shuffle, equalizer, bookmarks and slideshow settings. An FM radio and voice‑recording feature are included. Content can be deleted directly on the player or via a computer. System settings allow customization of wallpaper, backlight duration, power‑saver timer, language, date/time, brightness, USB mode, and reset to factory defaults. The manual also provides troubleshooting tips, warranty information and the end‑user software license terms.

World stocks rose to near all-time highs and the dollar extended its winning streak to 11 days following Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen's signals of a possible interest rate increase next month. MSCI's global equity index rose 0.25% to 442.4 points, its highest since May 2015. European stocks gained with banks leading the advance. The dollar index reached its longest winning streak since May 2015, while sterling fell 0.5% after UK wage growth data disappointed. U.S. Treasury yields rose and crude oil prices declined as a stronger dollar weighed on commodities. Gold also fell slightly.

More than 5,000 Maharashtra HSC students scored over 90 % in 2018. Kshirsagar Kedar Kailas, a differently‑abled student at Niwant Andh Mukta Vidyasalaya, topped her school with 80.15 % and aims for the IAS exam. Vanshika Joshi, born with a left‑leg deformity, earned 70.77 % and plans to become a banker. Night‑school results were notable: 104 of 120 candidates passed, Hirve Ashwini led girls with 70.6 % and Akash Dhindle topped overall at 79.23 % while working a 10‑hour job. Vitthal Bashweshwar Ishwarkatti, a 30‑year‑old married delivery agent, scored 75 % (third highest) after an 11‑year break and intends to study for an accounting degree.

The Software is not fault‑tolerant, not intended for high‑risk activities; SanDisk disclaims fitness and liability for such use. The Agreement is governed by California and U.S. law, and disputes must be heard in Santa Clara courts. Export must comply with regulations; amendments require written signatures. The side screen offense uses a big screening a small; if on‑ball defender caught, dribble penetration results, especially with a post‑up or shooter. Teams prefer Show & Recover. Show: X5 steps out forcing ballhandler wide, X1 chases, defenders sag. Recover: after X1 re‑establishes guard X5 returns to post and on pass out defenders close out. SOS three options: above line contact switch and smother; below baseline trap and triangle I; and All‑Out double‑team before screen with rotations. Secondary trap occurs on a pass to screener on a base roll.

Hubble captured an image of NGC 2775, a galaxy located 67 million light-years away that displays characteristics of spiral, elliptical, and lenticular types. Its smooth, featureless center resembles an elliptical galaxy, while its dusty ring of patchy stars resembles a spiral. Evidence of a hydrogen gas tail extending 100,000 light-years suggests past galactic mergers may explain its hybrid appearance.

Despite rain, a line formed early for the Crossroads of the West Gun Show at the Del Mar Fairgrounds on Saturday, drawing thousands of visitors while about 80 orange‑shirted protesters across the street held signs referencing the Parkland shooting victims. Organizers said the protest reflected renewed calls for gun control after the massacre; show owner Bob Templeton expected 8,000–10,000 attendees, more than usual, attributing the increase to the national debate. California law requires a background check and a 10‑day waiting period for gun purchases at the show, which runs through Sunday.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend that simplifies routines to focus on essential, high-quality products. Dr Hazel Parkinson, a GP and founder of Dr Hazel Skin Solutions, explains that it involves using fewer products that serve the skin's needs rather than layering multiple steps. Benefits include protecting the skin barrier, reducing irritation, less waste, and improved wellbeing. While suitable for most people, those with specific conditions like acne or hyperpigmentation may still need targeted ingredients but fewer steps. For sensitive skin, a minimal routine with a gentle cleanser, moisturizer, SPF, and one calming active is recommended. Transitioning from a complex routine should be done gradually, eliminating products one at a time over 2-4 weeks.

In November 2010, David Bradt found an elasmosaur fossil at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge, Montana, while elk hunting; a new species that shows elasmosaurs evolved longer necks. Elasmosaurs were reptiles 30 ft with paddle limbs. Inland sea had few fossils. Excavation took three days; Bradt reported the find to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Museum of the Rockies.

SARS-CoV-2 is a positive-sense single‑stranded RNA virus that has caused a global pandemic. Metagenomic next‑generation sequencing (mNGS) can detect viral pathogens without prior hypothesis, but low viral nucleic‑acid proportion in clinical samples limits sensitivity. Two strategies to address this are virus enrichment and host depletion. This study evaluated a field‑deployable mNGS workflow that combines a 15‑minute DNase I treatment with 0.22 µm filtration, nucleic‑acid extraction on a MagNA Pure system using a guanidine‑isothiocyanate‑based buffer, random amplification with a modified REPLI‑g WTA kit, and Oxford Nanopore library preparation with the Rapid Barcoding Kit. Sequencing was performed on R9.4.1 flowcells for up to 20 h. Pooled SARS‑CoV‑2‑positive swabs (median Ct ≈ 22) showed that the combined pretreatment increased the proportion of SARS‑CoV‑2 BLAST hits from 31.8 % (no pretreatment) to 99.9 % and raised genome coverage from 7.5 % to 99.3 %, a 525‑fold rise in viral reads. DNase I alone gave 95.3 % hits (94.1 % coverage) and filtration alone gave 65.4 % hits (32.8 % coverage). The combined method covered >50 % of the genome within 10 min of sequencing. In 14 individual clinical samples (Ct 18–36), samples with Ct ≤ 30 achieved 85.8–100 % coverage; higher‑Ct samples gave 40–60 % coverage. All samples were identified as clade 21J (Delta) by Nextclade; Pangolin assigned sub‑lineages for Ct < 33 but failed for Ct ≥ 33. No contaminants were detected by qPCR after extraction or amplification. The protocol avoids centrifuges, robots and thermal cyclers, aiming for field use. The authors conclude that DNase I + filtration pretreatment substantially improves viral detection with Nanopore sequencing, enabling reliable clade and lineage typing for samples with Ct < 33 and offering a rapid, portable option for point‑of‑incidence diagnostics.

Centre told Supreme Court it will grant pension revision to all Major Generals and equivalent ranks, including those retired before 2006. Bench headed by Chief Justice Dipak Misra gave three‑month compliance order and disposed of petition. Plea sought One Rank One Pension for retired armed forces personnel.

Oral communication among players during a soccer game is essential for success, requiring short, instantly recognizable words or phrases that convey both meaning and required action. Because the game moves quickly, players without the ball—especially those positioned behind the ball—usually give the calls, as they have the best view of the field and can direct play.

The passage organizes calls into four skill‑based levels plus specific groups for the Defensive Organizer (usually a center‑back, trail centre‑back, or sweeper) and the goalkeeper. Introductory calls (e.g., “Settle,” “Man‑on,” “Turn,” “Carry”) address receiving, controlling and dribbling. Basic calls (e.g., “Ball,” “Center,” “Challenge,” “Contain”) provide simple tactical cues for passing, defending and support. Intermediate calls (e.g., “Back and left,” “Go,” “Stay up,” “Mark #”) handle positioning, team coordination and specific defensive assignments. Advanced calls (e.g., “Overlap,” “Dummy,” “Trap,” “Switch”) involve strategic moves, high‑pressure tactics and complex defensive organization.

Goalkeeper and Defensive Organizer calls include directives for marking opponents by number, building walls, directing back‑pass options, and coordinating defensive shape (e.g., “Pick up (#),” “Balance,” “Push up,” “Keeper’s out,” “Goalie go”). The passage notes that many calls duplicate one another, so coaches may select preferred terms that fit their team’s age and ability level, while still ensuring every player eventually learns the full vocabulary.

Coaches are advised to teach all calls to everyone, introduce them at age‑appropriate intervals, and may develop team‑specific signs for situations such as an offside trap or noisy environments that require non‑verbal cues.

Consumer Reports (CR) testing of 23 popular protein powders and ready‑to‑drink shakes found that more than two‑thirds contained lead at levels exceeding CR’s daily safe limit; some products had up to 7.7 µg of lead per serving (1,572 % of CR’s limit). Plant‑based powders were the most contaminated, averaging about nine times the lead found in dairy‑based proteins. CR’s chemist concluded that most protein powders are not necessary to meet protein requirements and advised against daily use. The investigation also noted that contamination has increased since CR’s 2010 testing and that the industry operates in a regulatory gray area: there is no federal limit for lead in protein powders, the FDA inspected only a small fraction of manufacturers, and many brands rely on self‑testing or less stringent certifications. CR recommends that most people can obtain adequate protein from whole foods without supplements.

Hundreds of current and former Big Five bank employees have reported unethical sales tactics and excessive production pressure, including layoffs for missing revenue thresholds. Financial institutions claim to prioritize clients but must prove it. Three recommendations are: tie a portion of advisor bonuses to client satisfaction (e.g., Sun Life’s 25% metric), compensate advisors for advising against a purchase, and set minimum education requirements for the role. These changes aim to reduce perverse incentives and improve advice quality.

This IEP News compilation for July 18 2001 presents multiple news items about California’s energy situation. Stories cover the state’s push to permit new power plants, noting that 450 MW have been approved but the goal of 5,000 MW will not be met; Pacific Gas & Electric’s lawsuit seeking compensation for contracts the governor seized; a 20/20 rebate program that has delivered $7.6 million in savings for roughly 29 % of processed customers; Duke Energy’s 27 % earnings increase driven by its wholesale‑power trading business; Governor Gray Davis’s efforts to use the crisis for political advantage; competing legislative bailout plans for Southern California Edison, including proposals for state purchase of transmission lines and consumer rate increases; and an editorial suggesting that markets are self‑correcting and urging balanced energy policy that respects the environment and promotes efficiency.

The coach says he hasn't yet addressed his team, plans to talk to them after speaking to the media. After discussing a post‑game incident involving Danny that caused no injuries and will be covered by insurance, he acknowledges that Calgary earned their win while his team did not execute. He credits Marty for his effort and notes he needs to start scoring consistently. He rejects the term “must‑win,” insisting every game is important and his team will approach tomorrow’s game with the same desire to win. Reviewing tape, he says they identified Calgary’s trap and good reads but were too passive against the league’s top Western team. He emphasizes the need for a mindset shift, not major tactical changes, and expects goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin to lead the response. The team plans to stay even‑keeled, focus on the next game, and bring the required intensity.

Intermediate attacking runs in soccer extend basic concepts by requiring greater awareness, timing, and communication. Individual runs include back‑door, drifting, doubling back, holding the run, recycled run, and setting up a defender. Runs that draw an opponent away from a teammate comprise decoy runs, drawing or dragging a defender, dropping or leaving the ball, and dummy runs. Offensive switches with teammates—either called or natural—include basic horizontal switches (diagonal X pattern), vertical switches (front‑to‑back exchange), and cross‑over exchanges (right‑foot‑to‑right‑foot or left‑foot‑to‑left‑foot). After a switch, players should verbally acknowledge “switch back” when returning to original positions. Players must be ready to receive a pass, anticipate subsequent actions, and go to the ball to avoid it being cut off.

A player credited timely goals and composure, calling the win a birthday gift. Another player made an impressive play. The team emphasized aggressive forechecking in the third period, benefited from Pekka's saves and an empty‑net goal. Contributions from Freddy, Sissons, Jarnkrok and Fiddler were highlighted, and the team stressed continued improvement for the series ahead.

U.S. wages and benefits rose 2.6% in the 12 months to December 2017, the fastest pace since 2015; Q4 growth was 0.6%. Wages increased 2.5% in 2017, but economists note that wages typically rise faster at the current 4.1% unemployment level last seen in the late 1990s.

The article lists AI tools designed to automate tasks, improve workflow and increase productivity. It covers ChatGPT, DALL‑E, Lumen5, Grammarly, OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI, Surfer SEO, Zapier and Compose AI, describing each tool’s main capabilities—such as language generation, image/video creation, writing assistance, code generation/completion, SEO analysis and workflow automation—and common limitations (potential inaccuracies, biased output, resource demands, variable quality). The overall message is that these tools can streamline work across many domains but should be used with caution and reviewed before production use.

The FDA approved a second generic version of the abortion pill mifepristone, enabling a third U.S. company to produce the drug. The decision drew criticism from anti‑abortion groups and Trump‑aligned politicians urging the agency to curb access. Mifepristone, typically taken with misoprostol, accounts for roughly two‑thirds of U.S. abortions and remains widely available despite the new approval. Meanwhile, Amgen reported that its cholesterol‑lowering injection Repatha met its primary goals in a 12,000‑patient trial, reducing a composite of heart‑disease death, heart attack, and the most common stroke. Repatha, launched in 2015, generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024 and lowers LDL cholesterol. Separately, the Trump administration postponed an effort to close a Medicare drug‑price negotiation loophole.

US manufacturing and services firms expect continued economic growth and rising revenue into 2018, with manufacturing revenues projected to rise 7.8% and services sector growth at 6%. Manufacturing outlook is more optimistic with 70% of firms expecting increased earnings versus 59% in services. Over 60% of firms report difficulty finding workers, leading 44% of manufacturing and 37% of services companies to raise wages. Employment is expected to grow 1.2% in manufacturing and 1.5% in services, with wage and benefit costs increasing 2.1% and 2.6% respectively. Capital expenditures are projected to increase 2.7% in manufacturing and 3.8% in services.

Jerry Coyne cited a YouTube video as new evidence for a multiverse, but the evidence does not support a multiverse with varied physical laws needed to counter theological fine‑tuning. The author warns that relying on YouTube or Facebook sources is unreliable. A Nobel Week Dialogue talk by David Gross affirmed science’s honest, experimental approach, though the author remains uneasy.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2017. The company designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and related software, services, and accessories. Its products include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV, along with operating systems iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The company paid dividends of $12.6 billion in 2017 and $12.0 billion in 2016, expecting quarterly dividends of $0.63 per share. In May 2017, the Board increased the share repurchase authorization to $210 billion, with $44 billion remaining available as of September 30, 2017. The aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $747.5 billion as of March 31, 2017.

One in five rail passengers in Britain is resigned to poor service, according to a survey of 2,477 people. Rail complaints rose by 31% to about two million last year, with punctuality, customer service and overcrowding being the most common grievances; the regulator recorded a 13% rise in complaints per 100,000 journeys in the July‑September quarter compared with 2015. Campaign groups called for stronger enforcement while the government highlighted over £40 billion of investment, and a proposed bill aims to create a rail ombudsman to financially penalise under‑performing operators.

Scientists at Rockefeller, using C. elegans, discovered a compartmentalized cell‑death process in the tail‑spike cell. The cell’s core is first severed from its long extension, rounds up and disintegrates, while the extension disappears in two stages: the proximal part breaks into beads, the distal part retracts into a ball removed by a neighbor. The same pattern was seen in a neuron, suggesting it may be widespread. The researchers also found that the protein EFF‑1 enables phagocytes to seal around debris, aiding clearance. The findings appear in Nature Cell Biology.

Jana Partners increased its Whole Foods stake, later profiting from Amazon’s acquisition. FAANG stocks posted gains during the quarter, making Third Point’s moves appear prescient.

The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) warned that a U.S. government shutdown would force about 750,000 federal workers to be furloughed, costing roughly $400 million in daily compensation. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R‑La.) blamed Democrats for refusing to back a short‑term funding bill, saying they must “come to their senses.” House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D‑N.Y.) countered that a shutdown would be the Republicans’ decision and that Democrats are ready for a bipartisan solution. The deadlock centers on Democrats’ demand that any continuing resolution extend enhanced Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax credits, which lower insurance premiums for millions and are set to expire at the end of 2025. Republicans call the demand a made‑up issue; Johnson accused Democrats of protecting Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer’s political position. This patent application, a continuation by Tony M. Brewer, describes a multi-threaded, coarse-grained configurable computing architecture for heterogeneous computing systems. The invention addresses limitations in existing computing systems regarding computational speed, energy consumption, and heat dissipation. The architecture provides self-scheduling, dynamic self-configuration and reconfiguration, conditional branching, backpressure control for asynchronous signaling, and ordered thread execution including loop thread execution with data dependencies. The configurable circuits (tiles) include configurable computation circuits, configuration memory with instruction and spoke instruction RAMs, synchronous network inputs/outputs, asynchronous network queues, control circuits with memory control, thread control, and control registers storing completion and loop tables. Systems comprise arrays of these configurable circuits with synchronous mesh communication networks and asynchronous packet networks, along with memory interfaces, dispatch interfaces, and interconnection networks. The architecture targets compute-intensive applications such as FFTs, FIR filters, synthetic aperture radar, 5G base stations, graph analytics, machine learning, and large stencil codes. Methods for configuring these circuits and controlling multi-threaded execution are also disclosed.

The passage describes MSPM0 G-Series 80MHz microcontrollers technical documentation. The IOMUX controls peripheral function selection, IO driver/input configuration, and wake-up logic; a 5V-tolerant open drain IO type lacks a high-side driver. Serial Wire Debug (SWD) provides a two-wire debug interface. The Boot Strap Loader (BSL) enables programming via UART or I2C, protected by a 256-bit password, with invocation possible via a hardware pin, an unprogrammed reset vector, or software command. Device capabilities and factory trim data reside in a memory-mapped read-only region. Typical schematic recommendations include a 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitor across power pins, a 47kΩ pullup with 10nF capacitor on the reset pin, a 100kΩ resistor for the system oscillator correction loop, and a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE. Device prefixes X and MSP distinguish experimental and production units, respectively. Supported development tools include Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, and Keil MDK. The document also includes a revision history and ESD handling precautions.

Researchers synthesized off‑stoichiometric single crystals of YbCu1.14Se2 using a self‑flux technique. Single‑crystal X‑ray diffraction (SC‑XRD) shows Yb ions form a two‑dimensional triangular lattice in a P‑3m1 structure with lattice parameters a≈4.02 Å and c≈6.45 Å. Cu occupies the 2d Wyckoff site with ~57 % occupancy, producing bond disorder without vacancy ordering; Yb and Se sites are fully occupied. Magnetic susceptibility measurements (2–350 K, 0.1 T in‑plane) reveal a Kramers doublet ground state, effective moments of 4.48 µB at high temperature and 2.94 µB at low temperature, and Weiss temperatures indicating antiferromagnetic exchange. Specific‑heat data (0.03–10 K) show no magnetic ordering transition, a nuclear Schottky anomaly below 100 mK, and sub‑linear C/T from ~0.5 K to 5 K that follows approximately C∝T^0.95 up to 1 K; integrated entropy reaches ~85 % R ln 2. Ultra‑low‑temperature AC susceptibility exhibits a frequency‑dependent symmetric peak near Tf≈0.1 K, characteristic of spin‑glass freezing. Field‑dependent susceptibility lacks the 1/3 magnetization plateau observed in ideal triangular‑lattice delafossites, indicating departure from the pure 2D Heisenberg model. The combined results suggest a spin‑disordered ground state with bond disorder similar to YbMgGaO4, consistent with a possible random‑singlet phase in frustrated triangular magnets.

The paper proposes a class of bivariate zero-inflated Poisson models using a common inflation factor and extending the bivariate Poisson shock models of Genest et al. (2018) through comonotonic and counter-monotonic shocks, allowing both positive and negative correlations. The model formulation involves a Bernoulli inflation factor and correlated latent Poisson variables, with separate specifications for positive (BZIP+) and negative (BZIP-) dependence. Key contributions include derivation of joint probability mass and distribution functions, analysis of the dependence structure through covariance and correlation formulas, and establishment of PQD ordering properties. Estimation approaches encompass method of moments and maximum likelihood (including a two-step implementation), with asymptotic normality established. An EM algorithm is also developed for parameter estimation. Comprehensive simulations across 72 scenarios compare these methods, showing ML approaches generally outperform MoM in terms of RMSE. The model is illustrated using Australian disaster data on monthly flood, storm, and bushfire occurrences, demonstrating significant zero-inflation and dependence in the data. Extensions to higher dimensions via the multivariate comonotonic shock model are discussed.

The lecture discusses extending temporal difference (TD) learning from discrete Markov chains to continuous function approximation. While TD with discretized states converges for ergodic chains, it becomes impractical for high-dimensional systems due to exponential growth in state space discretization.

Least squares function approximation is presented as the solution. Given input/output data, one can write a least squares cost function and optimize over parameters using either gradient descent or analytical solutions for certain function classes.

Neural networks are mentioned as popular function approximators where inputs are weighted and passed through sigmoidal functions. While they can theoretically represent any function with enough neurons, the lecture notes they're not ideal for least squares optimization.

The preferred approach is linear function approximation, where output is a linear combination of potentially nonlinear basis functions. This is linear in parameters but not necessarily in inputs. Parameters appear at the output, enabling explicit solution via least squares rather than iterative gradient descent, allowing representation of arbitrary nonlinear functions with appropriate basis functions.

Common basis function choices include radial basis functions (Gaussians with different means), Fourier decomposition, polynomials, and barycentric interpolators. The lecture emphasizes choosing basis functions matching the problem structure.

Robot manipulator equations are shown to be linear in their parameters, making system identification a straightforward least squares problem. Using a pendulum example with basis functions for theta double dot, theta dot, and sine theta, parameters can be accurately estimated in one shot from noisy data.

For extending TD to function approximators, eligibility traces are maintained on parameters rather than states. The update uses the gradient of the estimate, which for linear function approximators is simply the basis function. This approach converges for linear function approximators with all lambda values between 0 and 1.

LSTD (least squares temporal difference learning) is presented as a more data-efficient alternative that collects trajectory data and solves for the steady-state solution directly, avoiding the need for learning rates or specific initial conditions. The lecture concludes that linear function approximation is the only case with strong convergence guarantees.

The Court granted AAA Nevada Insurance Company's motion for summary judgment in a case involving Defendant Vinh Chau, who was insured by AAA when he caused a car accident resulting in Benjamin Buenaventura's death. The policy contained bodily injury liability limits of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per accident. In December 2006, counsel for the Buenaventuras demanded policy limits within two weeks, but failed to identify all heirs or provide a release. AAA repeatedly attempted to contact counsel to obtain this information but received no response. When the two-week deadline passed without compliance, the Buenaventuras' counsel claimed AAA had failed to respond and later filed a wrongful death action seeking $999,997.

The Court held that AAA's policy liability is limited to $100,000 and that AAA did not act in bad faith under Nevada law. The Court found the demand letter was unreasonable because it lacked essential information needed to verify all potential claimants, and AAA had a reasonable basis for not settling within the arbitrary deadline. The Court also denied the Interveners' request for a Rule 56(f) continuance, finding no genuine issue of material fact existed regarding bad faith.

The trap play is a quick‑hitting, downhill run scheme that uses angle blocks to remove an interior defensive lineman, making it effective against aggressive pass rushers and forgiving for smaller offensive linemen. It pairs well with deceptive offenses such as the Wing‑T. Its main weakness is that a defense that squeezes interior gaps (e.g., a Bear front or an even front) can limit its success. The passage shows example blocking assignments for a 3‑4 odd front and a 4‑3 even front, and describes two variations: a Gun Trey Same‑Side Trap RPO run from the shotgun, and a Wing‑T Trap that serves as a sister play to the Buck Sweep.

The President addressed a joint session of Congress to review U.S. foreign policy, stating that his first priority is to sustain mutual trust between Americans and their government. He highlighted post‑World War II achievements: strong alliances with European democracies, Japan, and North America; improved relations with the Soviet Union, including progress on strategic arms control; an historic opening with the People’s Republic of China; and U.S. efforts that helped contain conflicts in the Middle East, opened a new dialogue with Latin America, and strengthened ties with African nations. He acknowledged setbacks and quoted President Truman’s warning about the consequences of faltering leadership, calling for national unity.

He described the critical situation in Vietnam and Cambodia after North Vietnam violated the 1973 Paris accords and the United States was legally unable to respond. He reported that South Vietnam’s defense required urgent assistance and asked Congress to appropriate $722 million for emergency military aid and $250 million for humanitarian relief, to authorize protection of Americans and endangered South Vietnamese, and to provide food and ammunition for Cambodia.

He urged Congress to lift the arms embargo on Turkey, warning that the embargo harms U.S. security interests and complicates negotiations over Cyprus, and to consider economic and military assistance for Greece. He called for amendments to the 1974 Trade Act that inadvertently penalized friendly OPEC members such as Ecuador and Venezuela.

The President affirmed U.S. commitment to Middle‑East peace, noting recent disengagement agreements and his determination to continue efforts, including reconvening the Geneva conference. He said the United States seeks a stable relationship with the Soviet Union based on mutual interest and restraint, while pursuing strategic arms control, but warned that recent economic sanctions have backfired and cost American jobs. He reaffirmed relations with the People’sRepublic of China based on the Shanghai communique and announced a planned visit later that year.

He outlined new global challenges—hunger, energy, ocean resources, and technology—highlighting U.S. leadership in creating the International Energy Agency and the need to reduce dependence on imported oil. He emphasized the importance of intelligence services for national security and the need for responsible Congressional oversight.

The President concluded by calling for unity, resolve, and a defense budget sufficient to maintain U.S. strength, quoting Abraham Lincoln to stress the historical responsibility of Congress and the Administration.

The passage documents AMD AGESA software interface specifications for BIOS developers. It describes the bridge, dispatcher, and router mechanisms for calling AGESA functions from host BIOS code, along with error logging procedures and the binary module design. The document covers the UEFI BIOS environment with four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP) across different execution modes, and explains the build tools required for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit platform initialization phases. It details processor initialization procedures including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and AmdInitResume entry points with their respective responsibilities for memory initialization, power management configuration, and hardware setup. The documentation also covers PEIM modules for processor and memory initialization, DXE drivers for late configuration and ACPI table generation, stack establishment procedures using Cache-As-Ram, and S3 resume mechanisms for saving and restoring processor state.

This patent application discloses systems and methods for dynamically providing video overlays. The application is a continuation of earlier applications claiming priority to a provisional application titled "Dynamic Video Overlays." The technology relates to processing video streams and causing the presentation of overlaid video content on client devices such as smart televisions.

The system identifies a set-top box providing video data to a client device through methods including Extended Display Identification Data (EDID) when connected via HDMI cable, user interface selection, or IP address lookup. Once identified, templates corresponding to presented information are selected, and a replacement video stream is presented while maintaining the manner in which the original video was displayed.

Video content identification uses fingerprinting techniques. A query fingerprint generator creates fingerprints of frames from the received video, which are compared against reference fingerprints in an index module. Matching can use various distance measurements including Tanimoto, Manhattan, Euclidean, Cosine, and others. Fingerprints may be single-frame or multi-frame, with multi-frame fingerprints containing collections of single-frame fingerprints with relative timings.

The system handles multiple overlay scenarios. Picture-in-picture displays present replacement video in a smaller region while passing through set-top box content. Informational bars occupy screen portions while scaling original video. Semi-transparent overlays are transferred to replacement content using calculated transparency values. The system can also match playback speed changes, applying the same fast-forward, rewind, or pause rates to replacement content.

Template generation occurs manually or programmatically. Manual generation involves analyzing menu presentations on client devices. Programmatic generation identifies known versus unknown video data regions through fingerprinting of screen areas and multi-frame analysis comparing static versus changing regions.

Detection of channel changes causes the system to cease applying overlay masks, allowing full video from the set-top box to display. When returning to identified content, the system resumes presenting replacement video. Data structures include tables for PictureinPicture, MenuOverlay, MenuBlend, and Template information, with each storing device identifiers, template identifiers, and coordinates for positioning overlay elements.

Coffee consumption is rising rapidly in Britain, driven largely by Costa, the UK chain that has become the world’s second‑largest coffee retailer after Starbucks. Costa’s UK sales reached £3.4 billion in 2016, up 37 % over five years and a further 10.4 % between 2015‑2016, with growth projected to reach 29 % by 2022. The company now operates more than 2,000 shops in the UK, roughly one for every 30,000 people, while Britain ranks only 44th worldwide in per‑capita coffee consumption. Costa opened a new roastery in Basildon, Essex, chosen for its proximity to Tilbury Docks, where beans arrive, and its quick road links to London. The site quadrupled roasting capacity to 45,000 tonnes per year, enabling the production of about 2.1 billion cups annually and handling up to 24 tonnes of beans per hour. The facility achieved a BREEAM “outstanding” design rating, uses solar panels, rainwater‑harvesting and LED lighting, and all its beans are Rainforest Alliance certified. Quality control involves infrared colour testing and moisture measurement; each incoming bag is sampled, roasted and tasted, with roughly 8 % of beans rejected each year. Costa’s blend combines arabica for acidity and aroma with robusta for body; Vietnam is the second‑largest coffee producer after Brazil. The company’s Master of Coffee, Gennaro Pellicia, whose palate is insured for £10 million, rose from barista to senior role, and the roastery trains 3,000 baristas a year, promoting from within. Robots now pack roasted coffee, increasing productivity by an estimated 25 %. The site has spare land for future expansion, giving it a projected 30‑year lifespan and supporting Costa’s ambition to open up to an additional 6,000 shops worldwide. Production staff follow a “nice and easy” philosophy that the company credits for its growth.

The lecture discusses multi-stakeholder engagement in supply chains, using palm oil as a case study. It examines palm oil's deep integration into companies' supply chains and the lack of transparency in commodity supply chains. The class analyzes the Nestlé and Greenpeace case where Greenpeace targeted brands to create publicity and consumer pressure, which proved more effective than targeting deep-tier suppliers. Students discuss various stakeholders involved: growers, mills, farmers, corporations like Nestlé and Unilever, certifying bodies like RSPO and ISPO, Indonesian government, investors, consumers, and local communities. The lecture covers multiple strategies for companies like GAR: working with NGOs like Greenpeace or Forest Trust, pursuing RSPO certification, creating sustainability reports, using celebrity advocacy, and partnering with government and industry bodies. Challenges discussed include supply chain transparency, small farmers' inability to afford certification, limited price premiums reaching farmers, and consumer awareness. The lecture also addresses industry collaborations like the Sustainability Consortium, EICC, and Sustainable Apparel Coalition, as well as the complexity of NGO-company partnerships and greenwashing concerns with certification labels.

YouTube announced four new Original series for YouTube Red, created with the YouTube Kids app in mind. The series will debut in spring 2017 and feature DanTDM, Joe and Cody of TheAtlanticCraft, L2M, and Fruit Ninja. The shows include "Hyperlinked" starring L2M, "DanTDM Creates A Big Scene," "The Kings of Atlantis," and "Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force." YouTube Kids app will also be available on LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

The Kiss of Death is a sell signal in the S&P 500 that occurs when the index drops from an all‑time high, falls below its monthly 21‑period exponential moving average (EMA), then bounces back above that EMA and subsequently drops below the recent low made just before the bounce. Since 1960 the signal has appeared five times—in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008—and each time preceded a major bear market. In September 2008 the signal correctly flagged the crash that bottomed in March 2009, while in September 2022 it triggered but the market rose instead, indicating a false signal. The backtest (starting 1967, unadjusted data) used a rule to sell when the signal fires and re‑enter when the S&P 500 closes above its 10‑month EMA. The strategy increased CAGR relative to a simple buy‑and‑hold and cut the maximum drawdown to roughly half. The authors conclude that the strategy can improve performance and may suit conservative investors who cannot tolerate large losses.

Fair Isaac (FICO) announced a new pricing model that lets mortgage lenders obtain FICO credit scores directly from the company, bypassing credit bureaus. The company will license scores to mortgage resellers who can then provide them to borrowers. On Thursday, Fair Isaac shares rose more than 20%, their biggest one‑day gain since late November. Shares of Experian, TransUnion and Equifax fell 4%–10% as investors viewed the move as potentially reducing the agencies’ role. The FICO score, used by roughly 90% of lenders, ranges from 300 to 850. The new model offers lenders two pricing options and eliminates the bureaus’ estimated 100% markup. An analyst called the change a way to improve FICO’s economics and disintermediate bureaus. FHFA Director Bill Pulte praised the move as a creative solution for consumers.

MSPM0C1105/6 are ultra‑low‑power 32‑bit MCUs based on Arm Cortex‑M0+ (32 MHz), operating -40 °C to 125 °C on 1.62–3.6 V. They integrate 64 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, oscillator, 3‑channel DMA, CRC‑16, 12‑bit 1.6 Msps ADC, comparator with DAC, 16‑bit advanced timer to 64 MHz, four 16‑bit timers, watchdog, three UART, one SPI, two I2C, and support LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus, and PMBus protocols.

According to two telegrams from the U.S. Minister in Finland (Schoenfeld) and one from the U.S. Minister in Sweden (Johnson), Finnish political sentiment is shifting toward separate peace with the Soviet Union and sympathy for the democracies. Pekkala reported that most Finns, including Field Marshal Mannerheim, the Social Democratic Party and small parties, share this view, while the Agrarian Party still believes Russia can be defeated and is indifferent to foreign policy. The Finnish Foreign Minister, Witting, said Finland depends 93 % of its imports on German goodwill and sees its situation as a “mouse in a trap,” with no intention to break German dominance for fear of starvation. Meanwhile, a Swedish telegram warns that Finnish military collapse could trigger a Swedish internal crisis, potentially empowering pro‑German forces; Soviet Minister Kollontay privately urged an immediate cessation of fighting as the only hope for peace.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on March 11, 2016 reporting an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10‑K. The error overstated the cost and net book value of the Supercharger network; the correct net book value on Dec. 31, 2015 was $166.6 million. Misstatement was limited to a section and did not affect consolidated financial statements or notes. Management deemed it immaterial. Report was signed by CFO Jason Wheeler.

Scientists have designed a taste‑based molecular sensor that releases thymol, a herb‑like flavor, when it encounters influenza virus. The sensor consists of a neuraminidase substrate linked to thymol; viral neuraminidase cleaves the bond, freeing thymol that is detected by the tongue. Lab tests with flu‑positive human saliva showed thymol release within 30 minutes and no toxicity to human or mouse cells. The researchers aim to embed the sensor in chewing gum or lozenges to enable rapid, at‑home screening before symptoms appear. Human clinical trials are planned in about two years. Funding came from the German Federal Ministry of Research and a patent has been filed with the European Patent Office.

Four leading candidates for Baltimore County executive spoke to real estate agents, builders and mortgage professionals, pledging smart growth and a streamlined development approval process. They all opposed impact fees, suggesting alternatives such as school‑capacity standards or noting fees are outdated. The candidates described the current approval process as cumbersome, with long permit waits, and called for rezoning decisions based on the master plan with an appeals process. Brochin pledged to end pay‑to‑play politics, while other candidates called developers partners. The forum, hosted by three industry groups, was the first of several this week; other primary candidates are Kevin Marron and Pat McDonough, with the primary on June 26 and early voting on June 14. The passage also contains captions about President Trump praising Mike Pompeo and about Council President Jack Young announcing affordable‑housing legislation.

The Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards are taking nominations until noon on 13 March, with the 12th ceremony scheduled for 27 April at the fully restored Edwardian Royal Hall. The hall seats 976 for shows but can accommodate about 300 for a banquet after its 7‑tonne seating is manually removed. The awards have ten categories (including Best Rural Business, Tourism, Employer of the Year, and Business Personality of the Year) and are open to businesses of any size, with each category sponsored individually and the main sponsor being estate agent Verity Frearson. Winning provides credibility and marketing impact, as illustrated by last year’s Best Small Business winner, Network Scientific, which reports increased interest after using the award status.

Robert Oscar Lopez, a former tenured professor at California State University, Northridge, resigned after eight years and now contends that academic freedom is not a virtue. He argues that the U.S. tenure system protects only a select few and does not shield most adjunct instructors, and that academic freedom does not function as a genuine safeguard, citing his own case and those of other professors such as John McAdams and George Ciccariello‑Maher as evidence of ideological persecution. Lopez claims that “academic freedom” is often used to justify extreme viewpoints rather than to promote objective truth. The article recommends reducing financial support for colleges, promoting trade schools and apprenticeship programs, and focusing on truth‑based curricula rather than defending academic freedom. It also asserts that the current higher‑education system has become a political racket that inflates tuition and produces graduates for jobs that do not require their credentials.

The first trading day of the month effect is a recognized phenomenon where the S&P 500 performs significantly better on the first trading day compared to other days, with an average gain of 0.24% versus 0.04% on a typical day. Simply buying at month close and selling on the first trading day is not viable due to instability, but adding a filter can improve the strategy to 0.35% average gain per trade with a 3% CAGR, 67% win ratio, and 5% max drawdown. The effect is likely attributed to capital inflows from pension funds, 401k contributions, and automatic savings.

The paper studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade under dominant‑strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality constraints. It frames the problem as online learning, seeking to minimize regret against the best mechanism in hindsight. Two data generation models are examined: stochastic i.i.d. valuations (possibly correlated) and an adversarial model.  

Main results:  
1. In the stochastic i.i.d. setting a polynomial‑time learning algorithm attains a near‑optimal regret of ˜O(√T) and a matching Ω(√T) lower bound, implying a sample complexity of about 1/ε² for learning an ε‑optimal mechanism.  
2. In the adversarial setting no learning algorithm can achieve sublinear regret relative to a 2/3 + ε fraction of the optimal profit, establishing a separation between the two models.  

The work also links bilateral trade to non‑excludable mechanism design, improving the regret bound for the joint ads problem from O(T^{3/4}) to ˜O(√T). Key challenges stem from the non‑parametric mechanism space and the impossibility of uniform convergence for all mechanisms; a chaining analysis is required, and simple discretization is shown to be insufficient.
The drawings show nine views of a cooling fan; broken lines indicate non‑claimed portions.

Mediation analysis in applied psychology identifies how interventions affect outcomes via intermediate variables, yet validating mediators requires rigorous methods because standard regression and structural equation modeling (SEM) assume no unmeasured confounding (sequential ignorability), which is rarely satisfied in practice. Omitted confounders can bias mediation estimates, limiting generalizability. To address this, rank‑preserving models (RPMs) based on g‑estimation relax the no‑effect‑modifier (no‑essential‑heterogeneity) assumption, allowing omitted covariates provided they do not interact with treatment or mediator. RPMs have shown robustness in detecting mediation effects but have not been extended to latent variable models, limiting their use in psychology where measurement error is common. The introduced Rank‑Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM) integrates RPM with factor‑score regression and interaction corrections, enabling SEM with latent constructs while preserving the relaxed no‑effect‑modifier assumption. RAPSEM estimates the controlled direct effect (CDE) of treatment on outcome and the controlled mediation effect (CME) of the mediator on outcome, defined within a potential outcomes framework with latent variables. The model is specified with a measurement part (latent mediator, covariates, and outcome) and a structural part, and its performance is assessed through two simulation studies comparing robustness to standard SEM under key assumption violations and evaluating power across scenarios.

He says team felt comfortable, expecting to capitalize. He praises his goalies, especially one who struggled but played, noting the need for him to be hot for three games. He sees next game as a chance to even the series, similar to San Jose. He notes team growth, highlights veteran players who score key goals while playing hurt, credits a power play. He says game plans and adjustments throughout the playoffs improved special teams and aided wins over Detroit and San Jose. He emphasizes handling adversity, staying focused, and believes raising their level will take the series. He mentions tradition.

He praises a teammate's fearlessness and daily presence on the ice, and notes the unusual excitement after a long break and media hype.
