Royal baby’s birth in the Lindo Wing at St. Mary’s Hospital cost $8,900; UK parents pay nothing for maternity care and have low maternal and infant mortality. In the US, average delivery costs $12,290, cesarean sections average $16,907, and complex cases can exceed $30,000; premature triplets can cost $870,000. US infant mortality in 2017 was 6.1 per 1,000 births, three times Japan’s, and among the worst in the OECD; US maternal mortality in 2015 was 26.4 per 100,000 births, three times the UK’s and over six times Finland’s, Denmark’s and Italy’s. US life expectancy fell to 78.7 years, below the OECD average of 80.3 years, while health spending reached $3.3 trillion, almost 18% of GDP, and costs are roughly double European levels despite similar usage. The Affordable Care Act reduced uninsured numbers, but Republican changes may cause 9 million more uninsured by 2019. Even insured Americans face high deductibles, copays and out‑of‑pocket expenses; one in three Medicare recipients spent at least 20% of income on health costs. Many turn to crowdfunding sites such as YouCaring and GoFundMe to cover expenses insurance rejects, and examples include $80,000 for a lung transplant and $43,000 for a brain tumor. US costs for a first child are about 13 times those of a UK couple, and a typical US family spends roughly 10% of its wealth on uncovered maternity costs.

This patent application relates to multi-modal user interfaces for electronic devices and digital assistants. SRAM in switchable power domains automatically enters SHUTDOWN when its power domain goes OFF, losing data, and returns to ACTIVE when the domain turns back ON; additional SRAM in the ALWAYS_ON domain can be shut down via x_MEM_PWRDN registers. Power supplies are organized into four sequencing groups (CVDD, DDR 1.5/1.8 V, 1.8 V, and 3.3 V) with required power‑up and power‑down sequences; specific timing relationships are listed in tables, and 3.3 V supplies must never exceed 1.8 V by more than 2 V during ramp‑down. The device supports Low‑Power Standby Mode with all switchable domains OFF and the ARM Cortex‑A8 in an IDLE loop at lowest frequency; PLL and analog supplies benefit from ferrite bead filters and 0.1 µF decoupling capacitors placed close to pins, with bulk caps for every ~10 power pins. System‑level resets include Power‑On Reset, External Warm Reset, Emulation Warm Reset, Watchdog Reset, Software Global Cold/Warm Resets, and Test Reset, each with specific effects and pin behaviors (most reset pins place I/Os in Hi‑Z except emulation and optionally EMAC switch pins). Reset priority order is defined, and reset isolation is supported for PCI Express and EMAC Switch modules. Clock generation uses DEV and AUX inputs from crystals or external LVCMOS sources (DEV typically 20 MHz), with twelve top‑level PLLs and an embedded PLL_ARM; all PLLs start in bypass after reset and have defined frequency limits and multiplier/divider ranges. SYSCLKs and module clocks are routed via the PRCM with maximum frequencies listed per OPP. The device has an ARM Cortex‑A8 Interrupt Controller handling up to 128 requests, and a C674x DSP interrupt controller combining 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts. Peripheral details include DCAN (CAN 2.0, two interfaces), EDMA (64 channels, 512 parameter entries), Advanced Event Triggering, IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, EMAC Switch (3‑port gigabit Ethernet with MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII support and MDIO), GPIO (four modules, up to 128 pins), GPMC (NOR/NAND flash, SRAM, error locator module for BCH), HDMI (1.3a transmitter, TMDS, audio, CEC), HDVPSS (video input/output, de‑interlacing, scaling, compositing, HDMI), and various timing specifications for these interfaces.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2× FP32 performance, second‑generation RT Cores, third‑generation Tensor Cores and GDDR6X memory support. The A40 data‑center GPU provides up to 2× FP32, 2× ray‑tracing and 5× AI throughput (10× with sparsity) versus Turing, has 48 GB memory (scalable to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink), three DP1.4 outputs, vGPU virtualization and is EGX‑compatible. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU uses a GA102 with 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑generation RT Cores, 336 third‑generation Tensor Cores, 48 GB GDDR6 and NVLink for 96 GB combined memory; it includes hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising. Ampere GPUs support 8K@60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a or HDMI 2.1 (up to 48 Gbps), and 4K120 Hz displays; they implement HDCP 2.3/1.x. The fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder accelerates MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1, enabling 8K60 HDR playback at ~4 % CPU usage. The seventh‑generation NVENC encoder provides hardware‑accelerated H.264 encoding up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K, matching x264 Medium quality with lower CPU load. Second‑generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection and support concurrent ray tracing and shading; third‑generation Tensor Cores double effective throughput with sparsity, enhancing DLSS. RTX IO with Microsoft DirectStorage reduces loading times by offloading asset decompression to the GPU. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and retries, preventing crashes during overclocking. GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) offers 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, 10 496 CUDA cores, 1.5× faster than TITAN RTX; RTX 3070 (GA104) exceeds RTX 2080 Ti performance. Both A40 and A6000 support vGPU software, Quadro Sync and NVIDIA EGX platform integration.

The lecture introduces relativistic kinematics for nuclear and particle physics, defining β = v/c and γ = 1/√(1–β²). For a massive particle the total energy is E = γ m c² and momentum p = γ m v; the invariant relation is E² = p²c² + m²c⁴ (or E² – p² = m² in natural units). Energy and momentum transform like time and space under Lorentz boosts, leaving the Mandelstam variable s = E² – p² invariant. The total mass of a system, √(E_total² – p_total²), is invariant (the same in any frame) but not conserved; total energy and total momentum are conserved in reactions. The lab frame and the center‑of‑mass frame are contrasted; in the CM frame the invariant mass equals the parent particle’s mass. The Higgs boson was discovered by calculating the invariant mass of photon pairs from its decay. Z‑boson production at LEP required a center‑of‑mass energy of ~91 GeV; a fixed‑target experiment would need a positron beam of ~45.5 GeV (since the electron mass is 0.511 MeV). Example problems include: determining the γ factor for 100 GeV electrons, calculating the binding energy of a deuteron from proton, neutron and deuteron masses, conditions for photon re‑absorption in a medium, the minimal beam energy to produce an antiproton in a proton‑fixed‑target collision, the speeds of electron and positron from a pion decay at rest, and wavelength changes in Compton scattering. Solutions to two problems are provided in backup slides.

President Arthur returns Senate Bill No. 71 (Chinese Exclusion Act) with objections, arguing it violates treaty obligations to China. The Burlingame Treaty of 1868 guaranteed Chinese subjects the right to emigrate to the United States. The 1880 treaty allowed the U.S. to "regulate, limit, or suspend" but not "absolutely prohibit" Chinese labor immigration. The President contends the bill's 20-year suspension exceeds what either party contemplated during treaty negotiations, representing a breach of national faith. He recommends Congress find alternative legislation that addresses concerns about Chinese labor competition without violating treaty rights. The President also criticizes proposed passport and registration requirements as undemocratic, suggests the suspension period should be shorter, and warns that restrictive policies may harm Pacific Coast trade relations with Asia. He advises an experimental approach with a review period rather than permanent prohibition.

Graphene flakes were grown on 700 nm single‑crystal Cu(111) films epitaxially deposited on sapphire using ambient‑pressure chemical vapor deposition at ~1020 °C with Ar/H₂/CH₄ flows. The flakes aligned in a single orientation and merged to form large‑area films. Despite the expectation that such stitched films are continuous and impermeable, scanning electron microscopy, atomic‑force microscopy (AFM) phase profiles, and Kelvin probe measurements revealed merging lines with only sub‑nanometre height contrast (<0.5 nm) and a contact‑potential‑difference increase of ~100 mV, indicating non‑seamless junctions. Wet oxidation of the Cu substrate in 90 °C water for two hours produced Cu₂O under graphene at some merging regions, detected by Raman mapping; approximately 45 % of the 122 counted merging regions showed Cu₂O signals, implying water‑permeable defects, while the remaining ~55 % remained unoxidized and are interpreted as seamless stitches. Scanning tunnelling microscopy at 4 K identified these defective junctions as overlapped bilayer regions where one flake edge lies atop the other, with step heights of ~1.2–1.4 Å on one side and ~3.3–3.5 Å on the other, consistent with a graphene monolayer stacked over a Cu step edge (~2.2 Å). Three merging types are classified: Type A seamless stitching, Type B defective stitching containing Stone–Wales or point defects, and Type C overlapped junctions. The findings show that single‑orientation stitched graphene is not defect‑free and that the water‑permeable structures could be exploited for filtration, desalination and molecular‑sieving applications.

The 1-4 "Slice" zone offense uses a high player alignment that creates matchup problems for zone defenses, allowing entry passes and quick releases to four receivers. The offense is easy to teach and learn but difficult to defend. Key actions include the Slice Cut (opposite post cutting hard to basket when point enters ball to post), Post Up Isolation (posting strong if pass not received), Low Post Feeds (feeding post when defender plays high side or skipping over fronted defender), Weakside Skip Pass Options (extra passes for open three-point shots), Ball Reversal (passing to weakside and cutting to basket with give and go actions), Wing Entry (entry passes to wings with slice cuts and post options), Wing Reversal (cross court skip passes when post up shots unavailable), and Overplay Counters (pump fakes and back cuts when defenders overplay posts or wings).

The lecture discusses how sustainable real estate (PPP: People, Planet, Profit) often fails to achieve intersection of the three bottom lines due to market failures. The first two market failures (information asymmetry, splitting incentive) were covered earlier. Today’s focus is the third: externality. Positive externality (green buildings generate societal benefits like reduced carbon emissions that developers cannot monetize) leads to undersupply because private benefits are insufficient relative to costs. Policy can internalize these external benefits through “carrots” (e.g., EU renovation wave subsidies, Massachusetts Mass Save heat pump subsidies, density bonuses like Arlington, VA’s FAR increases). Negative externality (brown buildings impose societal costs like carbon emissions that developers ignore) leads to oversupply. Policy can internalize these costs through “sticks” (e.g., carbon taxes, energy efficiency mandates, penalties). Examples include NY Local Law 97, Boston BERDO, Cambridge BEUDO, and UK minimum energy standards. Trade-offs exist between sustainability and housing affordability, particularly for low-income households. MIT aims for net zero by 2026 via carbon offsets. Coastal climate resiliency investments create positive feedback loops for wealthy areas like Miami but negative loops for poor areas like Fair Bluff, NC. Biden’s $47 billion climate resiliency funding raises moral hazard and equity concerns, prompting discussion of managed retreat as an alternative.

The paper treats the paradox of moral education as arising from tacit libertarian assumptions about free will. It shows that both causal determinism and indeterminism appear to undermine autonomy: determinism forces actions, while indeterminism makes them random, so moral responsibility seems impossible in either case. To resolve this dilemma the author turns to Harry Frankfurt’s hierarchical theory of the will. In this theory, responsibility depends not on the availability of alternative possibilities but on second‑order desires (volitional control) and the subject’s identification with the first‑order desire that motivates action. When a person’s will aligns with his/her own aspirations, the subject is morally responsible even if no alternative course of action existed. The hierarchical structure makes metaphysical facts about determinism or indeterminism irrelevant for assessing responsibility and authenticity, thereby dissolving the paradox of moral education. The paper concludes that educational practice should focus on the actual scenario of action, helping students develop an autonomous will through reflexive self‑assessment rather than relying on libertarian notions of freedom.

Marine heatwaves are prolonged periods of unusually warm water at a specific location for the time of year, occurring in any season. Since 1925 the number of marine heatwave days has risen by 54 % and their frequency and duration have increased by 34 % and 17 % respectively, with acceleration after 1982. Long‑term ocean warming explains the trend and predicts more events as temperatures rise. Recent examples include the 2011 western Australian heatwave that killed kelp and seagrass, affecting biodiversity and carbon storage; the 2012 Gulf of Maine event that shifted lobster landings and prices; and the 2014‑2016 North Pacific “Blob” that caused fishery closures, marine‑mammal strandings and harmful algal blooms. Human‑induced climate change increased the likelihood of the 2016 tropical Australian heatwave by 53‑fold and the 2015‑16 Tasman Sea heatwave by over 300‑fold. Scientists aim to quantify future changes and develop forecasts to help managers, but urgent emissions reductions are needed to limit further impacts.

Kerberos is a network authentication protocol designed for distributed systems with multiple servers and workstations. It uses a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) that stores shared keys for all entities and provides two interfaces: the initial Kerberos login and the Ticket Granting Service (TGS) for obtaining subsequent service tickets. Tickets contain the client and server names, client IP, timestamp, lifetime, and a shared session key, while authenticators prove freshness to prevent replay attacks. The initial login requires the user's password-derived key to obtain a TGS ticket, after which the password can be discarded. Kerberos version 4 had design flaws: it assumed encryption provided authentication, and allowed offline password guessing attacks since decryption success revealed correct keys. Version 5 fixes these by using separate authentication and supporting modern encryption like AES. The KDC can be replicated for availability but must be highly secured since compromising it grants full system control. The password-changing service requires a ticket obtained directly from Kerberos (not via TGS) to prevent attackers with stolen tickets from changing passwords.

The passage describes the SD Memory Card Physical‑Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. It defines command structures, card states, data‑transfer timing, error protection and performance‑class schemes.  

Force‑erase does not erase the secure area; the card stays locked and retains temporary or group write protection until all user data is cleared. Locked cards accept a limited set of commands (including CMD11 and CMD40) and reject ACMD6; CMD0 resets the bus to 1‑bit mode. Lock/Unlock functions have three types (Type 1, 2, 3) that differ by specification version, and the host must follow guidelines to avoid permanent lock‑up.  

APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the following command an application‑specific command (ACMD). Defined ACMDs are executed as such; undefined ones are treated as regular commands. Certain ACMD numbers (6, 13, 17‑26, 38‑49, 51) are reserved for proprietary use. ACMD41 is an exception – its response does not carry an APP_CMD flag.  

The Switch Function command (CMD6) provides six function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit and two reserved groups. CMD6 operates in Mode 0 (query) and Mode 1 (set). The response is a 512‑bit status block containing supported functions, selected functions, busy status and maximum current/power consumption. Power Limit defaults to 0.72 W; higher settings enable UHS‑I performance. In UHS‑II mode only Function Group 4 is mandatory and bus behavior changes require an 8‑clock switching period.  

High‑Speed mode (25 MB/s at 50 MHz) is optional and selected via CMD6. The Command System (CMD34‑37, 50, 57) is optional; when a non‑default function is selected, interpretation of these commands becomes vendor‑specific or defined by other specifications. CMD8 (Send Interface Condition) checks host voltage and returns an R7 response.  

SDSC cards use byte‑addressing and variable block length, while SDHC/SDXC cards use fixed 512‑byte block addressing and disable partial or misaligned access. The host may lower or stop the bus clock, but must provide 8 clock cycles after each transaction and keep the clock active during busy periods.  

Commands and responses are protected by CRC7; data blocks use CRC16 (generator polynomial x¹⁶+x¹²+x⁵+1). Read timeout is 100 ms or 100 × (TAAC+NSAC), whichever is smaller; write timeout is 250 ms or 100 × program time; erase timeout is derived from erase‑size/timeout fields. Write‑busy may extend to 500 ms for SDXC in specific cases; UHS‑II busy after a data burst is limited to 1 s.  

All commands are 48 bits long, start with a start bit, direction bit, 6‑bit command index, 32‑bit argument, 7‑bit CRC and an end bit. Commands belong to classes (Class 0, 2, 4, 5, 8 mandatory; Class 7 mandatory for SDHC/SDXC; others optional) and responses are R1, R2 (CID/CSD), R3 (OCR), R6 (RCA) and R7 (voltage). R1b includes an optional busy signal.  

Card Status is a 32‑bit field in the R1 response indicating errors and state; SD Status (512 bits) carries Speed Class, AU size, erase parameters, UHS mode, Video Speed Class, Application Performance Class and command‑queue depth; Task Status (32 bits) reports queued‑task information when CMD13 bit 15 is set.  

Three performance‑class schemes are defined: Speed Class (Class 0, 2, 4, 6, 10), UHS Speed Grade (U1, U3) and Video Speed Class (V6‑V90). Application Performance Class (A1) is also defined. Performance is measured using Allocation Units (AU) and Recording Units (RU); write performance (Pw), move performance (Pm) and read performance (Pr) are specified at defined clock frequencies (20 MHz for Class 2‑6, 40 MHz for Class 10). FAT update cycles consist of three writes; for SDXC the exFAT bitmap and Continuous Information (CI) updates are added, with CI write time limited to 250 ms. Measurement conditions, required parameter values and file‑system constraints are detailed for each card type.

This patent application discloses methods and systems for detecting and processing speech signals from multiple data modules simultaneously over a network. A year after the Supreme Court’s Loper Bright decision (overruling Chevron), the legal landscape for agency deference is shifting. Courts now primarily apply textualism, relying on ordinary meaning, dictionaries, grammar, and structural cues rather than agency expertise. The older Skidmore deference, while not formally overturned, appears in “shadow” form: lower courts inconsistently apply it and the Supreme Court has cited agency consistency as supporting evidence of correct interpretation. Some circuits have placed Skidmore on uncertain footing, especially in immigration and labor cases, while other domains (environmental, health) invoke it less due to shifting executive positions. Judges may use Skidmore as a legitimating tool, but it could eventually be dropped as textualist interpretation becomes routine. The Major Questions Doctrine (MQD) remains intact, integrated into ordinary meaning; the Court will not assume major delegations absent explicit statutory language. However, Justice Kavanaugh’s recent concurrence suggested a possible MQD exception for national security and foreign affairs, noting limited nondelegation constraints in those areas. This raises stakes for pending challenges to presidential tariff authority under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Scale‑in is a planned method of gradually increasing a position size as market conditions provide additional entry points, rather than entering the full position at once. Retail investors use it to buy additional shares as the price falls, lowering the average purchase price (a form of dollar‑cost averaging). Short‑term traders, such as day traders, first test the market with a small trade and add to a winning position to amplify profits while using the floating gain to cover the risk of the added trades. Institutional traders employ scale‑in to fill large orders without moving the market or attracting front‑running attention. Unlike the double‑down or Martingale strategies, which are reactive attempts to recover a losing trade, scale‑in is a pre‑planned entry strategy. The opposite of scale‑in is scale‑out, which gradually exits positions to lock in profit while leaving room for further gains. Benefits include a lower average entry price, reduced slippage and front‑running, and the ability to risk only a small amount initially. Disadvantages are the risk of not completing the intended position before a rapid market move and the possibility of a reversal after adding to a winning trade, leading to a net loss. A backtest presented in the passage shows that scaling‑in lowers CAGR but improves risk‑adjusted returns by using capital more efficiently; the author therefore prefers the scale‑in approach when the same return can be achieved with less time in the market.

In a retrospective single‑center cohort of 226 patients admitted for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (2020‑2022), 33 (15%) experienced rebleeding. Baseline characteristics and classical risk factors (systolic blood pressure, WFNS and Fisher grades, aneurysm location and size, intracerebral or intraventricular hematoma) did not differ significantly between rebleeding (RB+) and non‑rebleeding (RB‑) groups. Multivariate analysis identified two independent predictors of rebleeding: longer time from first symptom to event (0.7% increased odds per hour, p=0.008) and higher WFNS score (OR = 2.44, p=0.039). Timing analysis showed that patients whose aneurysms were secured within 24 h had a lower rebleeding rate (9% vs 21% for those secured later) and that two‑thirds of rebleeding events occurred after 24 h. Time from symptom onset to hospital admission was significantly shorter in RB‑ patients (18 h vs 60 h), while time from admission to treatment differed only by ~1 h. Prognosis at 1 and 6 months (Glasgow Outcome Scale) did not differ significantly between groups, though a trend toward better functional outcome (GOS 5) at 6 months was noted in RB‑ patients. The findings support early aneurysm securing and are consistent with current guideline recommendations for treatment within 24 h of symptom onset.

Menière’s disease (MD) is characterized by recurrent vertigo, hearing loss and other aural symptoms, and its diagnosis is complicated by episodic fluctuations; current Barany Society criteria classify patients as definite or probable MD. This study investigates whether the German 17‑item short form of the Speech, Spatial and Quality of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) is suitable for assessing hearing‑related quality of life in unilateral MD. Patients were recruited from a multicenter prospective registry (SEMM) approved by research ethics boards at LMU Munich and Greifswald University Medicine. Inclusion required fulfillment of current diagnostic criteria (definite, probable or Menière’s Characteristics); exclusion criteria included vestibular schwannoma, other vestibular disorders, prior intracranial surgery, stroke and bilateral MD. Participants underwent comprehensive vestibular testing, MRI to exclude retrocochlear pathology, pure‑tone audiometry (4‑PTA) and speech audiometry (Freiburg monosyllabic test at 65 dB HL). The SSQ17, comprising three subscales (speech hearing, spatial hearing, qualities of hearing) plus two additional questions, was completed by each patient. Internal consistency was evaluated with Cronbach’s α, and correlations between SSQ scores and audiometric variables were examined.

Of 97 patients (56.7 % female, mean age 56.2 ± 15.0 years), 75 % met criteria for definite MD and 51.6 % used hearing aids. Affected ears had a mean 4‑PTA of 51.9 dB HL versus 19.3 dB HL in unaffected ears (inter‑ear difference ≈ 32.6 dB); speech recognition scores were 33.9 % versus 86.6 % respectively. SSQ17 total score averaged 6.0 ± 2.1 (median 5.9), with subscale means of 5.3 (speech hearing), 5.1 (spatial hearing) and 7.2 (qualities of hearing). No significant differences in SSQ scores were observed among diagnostic categories. Cronbach’s α was 0.960 for the total score and 0.904–0.956 for the subscales, indicating excellent reliability. Moderate negative correlations existed between SSQ scores and pure‑tone thresholds, and moderate positive correlations were found between SSQ scores and speech recognition scores.

The SSQ17 demonstrated excellent internal consistency and correlated with objective audiometric measures, supporting its validity as a patient‑reported outcome for evaluating hearing‑related burden in unilateral MD. It provides a useful addition to clinical diagnostic tools but does not address the disability arising from vertigo, which remains a major aspect of disease impact.

This scoping review examines anti-inflammatory strategies for treating depression, covering 31 animal studies on neuroinflammatory pathways (NLRP3, NF-κB, P2X7R) and 11 clinical trials with 907 patients. Pharmacological interventions (Empagliflozin, Vitamin D analogues, natural extracts, NSAIDs) and non-pharmacological approaches (acupuncture, exercise, light therapy) were found to modulate these pathways and improve depressive symptoms in animal models. Clinical studies used anti-inflammatory drugs (Fluoxetine, Infliximab, Minocycline, Celecoxib, Vortioxetine) over 2-18 weeks, with inflammatory markers (CRP, hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α) as outcome measures. Benefits include improved treatment response in patients with high baseline inflammation and biomarker-based prediction of treatment efficacy. Challenges include substantial inter-patient variability, drug safety concerns (e.g., Celecoxib side effects), high costs (1000-1500 RMB for inflammatory testing), and limited understanding of inflammation's role in depression pathophysiology. The review concludes that anti-inflammatory strategies currently have limited research value and poor feasibility, recommending future focus shift toward non-pharmacological approaches (exercise, positive thinking) and improved research methodology, while proposing AI integration and microbot technology for personalized monitoring and treatment.

Backtests on the TLT ETF (tracking 20‑year Treasury bonds) from 2004 to August 2021 reveal two persistent calendar effects: the first seven trading days of each month produce strong negative returns, while the remaining days generate returns roughly double those of a simple buy‑and‑hold strategy. Combining a short position during the first seven days with a long position for the rest of the month yields an annual return of 10.2% versus 3.8% for buy‑and‑hold, and reduces maximum drawdown from 48% to 24%. A pure short strategy during the first seven days earns an average 0.6% per trade, an unleveraged CAGR of 5.5% and a profit factor of 2. Staying invested about two‑thirds of the month (from the close of the seventh trading day to month‑end) roughly doubles the buy‑and‑hold return. The article provides Python code for these strategies.

Enron Corp. was on the brink of the largest-ever bankruptcy filing after Dynegy Inc. withdrew from a $23 billion acquisition deal, leaving the energy trader with over $15 billion in debt and less than $2 billion in cash. Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for a congressional investigation into Enron's collapse, questioning whether it indicated broader industry issues. Enron's stock fell to 41 cents from $54.54, losing $26 billion in market value over six months. The company's European operations filed for creditor protection, and NYMEX restricted trading with Enron. Major banks including Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank, Bank of America, Citigroup, and J.P. Morgan Chase each had significant loan exposure to Enron. Enron reopened its EnronOnline trading system to allow counterparties to unwind positions. The company's global operations spanning power generation, pipelines, and metals trading employed 21,000 people, with overseas assets in Brazil, India, Europe, and elsewhere potentially complicating bankruptcy proceedings.

Digital laggards typically set only high‑level priorities with weak links to overall strategy, causing employee misalignment and deprioritization of unclear objectives. In contrast, digital leaders adopt a data‑driven culture that aligns the organization vertically (individual goals to company objectives) and horizontally (cross‑team collaboration). This culture, emphasized as a centerpiece, coordinates beliefs, values, and day‑to‑day actions, requiring consistency across levels. Changing entrenched mindsets is the hardest part of digital transformation. Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices (culture and systems lacking), insight ready (culture supportive but technology limited), tech enabled (technology present but culture risk‑averse), and data reliant (high maturity but over‑reliance on data). Firms can build on current strengths to advance their data culture.

Over the past 15 years, Seattle has recorded an increase in extreme rainstorms, according to a new study released by Seattle Public Utilities (SPU). SPU has monitored rainfall for about four decades using 17 gauges across the city; the previous major analysis was in 2003. While ordinary short showers and drizzle remain unchanged, flash storms are not necessarily worsening. Seattle’s overall precipitation rank is 44th nationally because its rain comes mainly from low, layered clouds. SPU classifies storms by duration and total rainfall and found that what used to be a once‑in‑a‑century 24‑hour storm of 4 inches now occurs roughly every 25 years, and the new threshold for a once‑in‑a‑century 24‑hour storm exceeds 5 inches. Similar shifts appear for 6‑hour and multi‑day storms, which now meet the “5‑year” and “10‑year” criteria more frequently. Residents note larger drops and longer lasting events, and construction workers report more days of uninterrupted rain. SPU plans to incorporate the updated data into the design of drainage and sewage projects; its ongoing tunnel project under the Lake Washington Ship Canal aims to keep nearly 60 million gallons of polluted water out of the canal each year. The city’s existing infrastructure was sized for lighter rain and must be upgraded. Mayor Jenny Durkan highlighted the trend while calling for climate‑action steps. The SPU results align with National Weather Service data, and NWS meteorologist Logan Johnson emphasized the need for broader flood‑preparedness efforts across Western Washington.

Blackwell architecture introduces Mega Geometry, enabling cluster‑level acceleration structures (CLAS) of up to 256 triangles, reducing BVH build cost by roughly two orders of magnitude and supporting a Partitioned Top‑Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) for scenes with many objects. New fourth‑generation RT Cores include dedicated cluster engines that compress geometry and BVH data and deliver up to twice the ray‑triangle intersection rate. Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) provide a hardware‑accelerated curve primitive that is about twice as fast as triangle‑strip approximations while using five times less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reorder efficiency, improving performance for path‑tracing and neural shading workloads. The AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC‑V scheduler on the GPU, offloads CPU scheduling, reduces latency and allows concurrent AI and graphics tasks. Video capabilities add native 4:2:2 chroma encode/decode, a ninth‑generation NVENC that improves AV1/HEVC quality by 5 % BD‑BR PSNR with an optional AV1 Ultra‑High‑Quality mode, up to three encoders and two decoders, and DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR20 supporting 8K@165 Hz or 4K@480 Hz. Power‑management innovations include fine‑grain power gating, independent voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching (1000× faster than previous generations) and a low‑latency sleep mode that enters ten times faster, delivering up to 50 % power savings for small‑language‑model inference. DLSS 4 adds Multi‑Frame Generation that creates up to three extra frames per traditionally rendered frame using a 40 % faster AI model that consumes 30 % less VRAM, and a transformer‑based neural network for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction and DLAA that doubles the parameter count for better temporal stability and detail. Neural shaders, accessed via the new Cooperative Vectors API, enable RTX Neural Materials (film‑quality assets at game frame rates), Neural Texture Compression (up to seven‑times VRAM savings), Neural Radiance Cache (real‑time indirect lighting inference), RTX Skin (real‑time subsurface scattering) and RTX Neural Faces (generative‑AI face rendering). The flagship GB202 die contains 92.2 B transistors, 12 GPCs, 192 SMs, 24 576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores and 768 Tensor cores, powering the GeForce RTX 5090; the GB203 die (45.6 B transistors, 7 GPCs, 84 SMs, 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores) drives the RTX 5080; and the GB205 die (31 B transistors, 5 GPCs, 50 SMs, 6 400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores) powers the RTX 5070. All Blackwell GPUs support DirectX 12 (via NVAPI), Vulkan extensions and OptiX 9.0, and are backward compatible with earlier RTX generations.

The 1942 Foreign Relations series is organized into six regional volumes and includes a previously published unnumbered volume on China; it is edited by E. R. Perkins. The Belgium section records a U.S.–Belgium preliminary agreement on mutual aid (June 16 1942) and a military‑service agreement (effected March‑October 1942), and details negotiations among the United States, the United Kingdom, and Belgium concerning imports from and exports to the Belgian Congo. Document 1 requests a status report on the Anglo‑Belgian economic negotiations and asks whether U.S. representation is desirable. Document 2 reports that the talks have proceeded slowly due to the death of a Belgian official, price disputes, higher offers from U.S. buyers, obstacles from powerful Congo trading interests, and the Belgians’ unmet request for a comprehensive British goods program; the British aim to coordinate policy with the United States.

NVIDIA Q2 FY2016 Summary (quarter ended July 26, 2015):

Revenue increased 5% year-over-year to $1,153M, driven by 9% growth in GPU business to $959M from strong gaming GPU sales, partially offset by 19% decline in Tegra Processor business to $128M due to reduced smartphone/tablet chip sales.

Key events: Announced voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets due to battery overheating hazard, recording $21M warranty charge. Entered $400M accelerated share repurchase agreement and paid $52M dividends. Began constructing new headquarters in Santa Clara under build-to-suit lease arrangement.

Total assets were $6,979M with $435M cash and $4,070M marketable securities. Shares outstanding: 539 million.

A driving assistance system for a vehicle utilizes sensors such as cameras, radar, or lidar to capture data representative of objects and scenes exterior to the vehicle. The system detects a rearward approaching vehicle traveling faster than the equipped vehicle and controls the equipped vehicle to accelerate to at least the speed of the approaching vehicle and/or change lanes to avoid collision. The system may operate autonomously in driver assistance or autonomous driving modes, or provide alerts to the driver to manually perform maneuvers. It can adjust speed based on factors including traffic conditions, speed limits, and vehicle conditions such as trailer towing. Decision-making may involve algorithms considering parameters such as distance, speed, and available lanes.

Mapbox, a Washington, D.C. startup that provides underlying mapping data for apps such as Snap and Instacart, announced partnerships with Microsoft, Intel’s Mobileye unit and SoftBank’s ARM Holdings to expand its services for self‑driving cars. The company, which has raised about US$228 million from SoftBank’s Vision Fund, will integrate its road‑recognition software with Microsoft Azure to offload camera data for cloud‑based algorithm training. It will also optimize its vision system on ARM chips to speed up detection of lanes, pedestrians and signs, and partner with Mobileye to stream the firm’s detailed road‑feature database into vehicles, giving them a constant map about 200 meters ahead as a backup to onboard sensors.

Payton v. County of Kane: Six former arrestees sued 19 Illinois counties challenging a bail fee authorized by state law (725 ILCS 5/110-7(b)), imposed above the bail amount for pretrial release. The district court dismissed for lack of standing. The Seventh Circuit reversed in part, finding the named plaintiffs have standing for individual claims against Kane and DuPage Counties (where they were detained) and for class claims against those two counties. For the remaining 17 counties, the appellate court discussed the "juridical link" doctrine, noting that because the fee is mandated by a state statute, defendants are instrumentally linked. The court held that once a class is properly certified, standing is assessed with reference to the class as a whole, and found no reason to preclude the class action device. The case was remanded for the district court to perform the Rule 23 analysis it previously skipped.

Researchers demonstrated NIR‑to‑visible photon upconversion using a bulk‑heterojunction sensitizer composed of a squaraine donor (DIB‑SQ) and a fullerene acceptor (PCBM) blended in a 1:3 weight ratio. The BHJ layer was spin‑coated on glass, followed by vacuum deposition of a rubrene (or rubrene doped with 0.5 vol % DBP) layer as the annihilator. Excitation at 690 nm generated charge‑transfer (CT) states at the donor–acceptor interface; non‑geminate recombination produced both singlet and triplet CT states (1CT/3CT) in a 1:3 ratio, with the long‑lived 3CT states transferring triplet energy either directly to rubrene or indirectly via molecular triplets in PCBM. Rubrene triplet states then underwent triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA), producing singlet excitons that radiatively decay, giving visible upconverted photoluminescence (≈562 nm for neat rubrene and ≈605 nm for rubrene:DBP). The upconversion quantum yield of the DIB‑SQ:PCBM(1:3)/rubrene:DBP device reached 1.36 % at an excitation intensity above 69.7 mW cm⁻², with a threshold intensity of ≈60.5 mW cm⁻²—among the lowest reported for solid‑state upconversion systems. Time‑resolved photoluminescence showed UC growth lifetimes of 1.2–1.4 µs and decay lifetimes of 9.5–14.7 µs. Transient‑absorption spectroscopy identified CT state formation, polaron signatures, and subsequent triplet populations in PCBM and rubrene. Magnetic‑field measurements showed a negative magnetophotoluminescence signal for upconverted emission, confirming TTA as the emission mechanism, whereas direct optical excitation of rubrene:DBP gave a positive signal due to singlet‑fission. The work demonstrates that exploiting 3CT states in fullerene‑based BHJs can repurpose the normally loss‑channel back‑electron‑transfer into a productive triplet‑sensitizer pathway, enabling relatively high solid‑state photon upconversion at low excitation densities and offering a route to integrate NIR‑to‑visible upconversion into practical optoelectronic devices.

The Marin Nail Trail 6 is a trail hardtail mountain bike priced at £1100, available from Marin Bikes UK. Its 6061 hydroformed aluminium frame features a 68° head angle, 120 mm Rockshox Recon fork, 655 mm top tube, short 60 mm stem and 780 mm bars, with two builds sharing the same frame across sizes small–XL and 27.5‑in or 29‑in wheels. Cable routing mixes internal and external runs, includes dropper‑post routing and dual bottle mounts. Spec highlights a SRAM GX 1×11 drivetrain with Sunrace 11‑42 cassette, Formula hubs, Marin 30 mm rims, Schwalbe Nobby Nic (front) and Racing Ralph (rear) tyres, and Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes. Reviewers describe the ride as comfortable, forgiving, with a low 311.5 mm bottom bracket, predictable handling, and a fun, upgrade‑friendly platform.

San Diego Unified School District rescinded a resolution to invite U.S. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos after the teachers’ union said her push for vouchers and profit‑driven charters threatens public schools. Board president Richard Barrera and trustee John Lee Evans had sponsored the resolution; Barrera withdrew support after union, parent and community opposition. In Washington, D.C., protesters tried to block DeVos from entering a school, clashing with police; American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten condemned the protest while urging her to visit public schools. DeVos’s confirmation required Vice President Mike Pence’s tie‑breaking Senate vote and was praised by President Trump at a White House listening session with educators from public, private, charter, Catholic, homeschool and other school settings.

The court denies the plaintiff's motion to dismiss the defendants' devolutive appeal. The three transcripts filed under the same docket number substantially comply with legal requirements as the clerk's certificate confirms they contain all proceedings, evidence, and documents. Appellants are not required to name all parties in their appeal petition—merely praying for citation of appellees is sufficient, making it the clerk's duty to issue citations to all record parties. The acquiescence of some appellants in the judgment does not divest non-acquiescing appellants of their right to appeal. The failure to make heirs of a deceased defendant parties does not prejudice the appellants' standing. The delay for the devolutive appeal has not elapsed.

Victor Wembanyama spent the offseason recovering from a career‑ and life‑threatening right‑shoulder condition that prompted a broad push to improve both physically and mentally. He played soccer in Costa Rica and Tokyo, visited NASA’s Johnson Space Center, trained with Kevin Garnett and hosted a chess‑basketball tournament in France. He also spent 10 days at a Shaolin temple in Zhenzhou, China, waking at 4:30 a.m., eating vegetarian meals, practicing Chan meditation and Shaolin Kung Fu, shaving his head, and focusing on range of motion, strength, flexibility and balance. After meeting Hakeem Olajuwon at the NCAA men’s championship game in San Antonio in April, Wembanyama worked out with the Hall‑of‑Famer in early September, completing four 2½‑hour sessions that emphasized “big‑guard” style play, the Dream Shake, tight spin moves and an undisclosed jump hook. He engaged fans by hosting supporter try‑outs, covering season‑ticket costs for top supporters and leading chants. He also participated in a community event in Ingram, Texas, after July floods, tossing T‑shirts and joining teammates in a light workout. Wembanyama said he maxed out his summer training and is ready to return to the court, while Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson and teammates praised his curiosity, work ethic and intent to expand his game and mindset.

In 2017 the Woodland Trust’s Nature’s Calendar recorded 42 spring indicators at over 1,000 UK sites; fewer reports than last year due to colder January. Volunteers have turned the project into a vital survey of climate‑change impacts on UK wildlife.

Email chain dated 12 Dec 2000, sent by Kimberly Kirkwood to a long list of recipients (including mark.guzman@enron.com) with the subject “Fwd: Fw: THIS IS SCARY!!! DO IT!!”. The message forwards a chain letter that instructs readers to make a wish after scrolling to the bottom, then claims the wish will come true in a number of minutes equal to the reader’s age. It also states that the message must be forwarded to ten additional people to obtain a major wish, warning of bad luck if not sent within five minutes. The chain contains multiple forwarded headers showing the message was passed through several other email accounts before reaching the final recipients. The email includes a confidentiality notice stating the information may be confidential and privileged.

During the Korean crisis, China asked England and Russia for help securing peace and requested US support. A British minister asked the US to initiate a joint protest at Tokyo, but the US declined unless the Tsung‑li‑Yamên requested it. The Viceroy Li later asked the US to urge other powers to request Japan withdraw its troops from Korea; the US said it could not intervene forcibly. Japan reinforced Korea with about 15,000 troops and 3,000 coolies, using merchant ships as transports. Japanese forces were described as orderly; a Japanese envoy was received by the Chinese Emperor. An incident involved Japanese interference with a British representative, and Japan presented reform demands to Korea. No fighting had yet occurred.

State Bar of Michigan e‑Journal dated May 23 2001 provides case summaries for Bankruptcy, Civil Rights, Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Negligence & Intentional Tort and Real Property; includes a Fields of Practice listing with attorney names and contact information; contains classified advertising for job positions, expert witnesses, office space and services; lists upcoming bar events and provides contact details for subscription and advertising.

Tesla, Inc. is a Delaware corporation that filed its Form 10‑K for the fiscal year ended December 31 2017. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells high‑performance fully electric vehicles—Model S, Model X and Model 3—alongside energy generation and storage products (Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2) and solar energy systems (including Solar Roof). It operates as a vertically integrated sustainable‑energy company offering end‑to‑end clean‑energy products and services. Vehicles are sold directly to consumers through company‑owned stores, galleries and online, supported by a growing global Supercharger and Destination Charging network. Manufacturing is performed at facilities in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; Gigafactory 1 in Nevada (battery and vehicle production); and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York (solar panels, in partnership with Panasonic). The company provides multi‑year warranties: four‑year/50,000‑mile new‑vehicle limited warranty, eight‑year battery/drive‑unit warranties for Model S/X (infinite mileage) and Model 3 (100k/120k miles with a 70% capacity guarantee), ten‑year “no‑defect” and energy‑retention warranty for Powerwall 2, fifteen‑year warranty for Powerpack 2, and twenty‑year installation warranties for solar leases/PPAs plus a thirty‑year warranty for Solar Roof. Financing options include loans, leases and power‑purchase agreements for vehicles and solar products. Tesla reports under two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of December 31 2017, Tesla employed 37,543 full‑time employees; 168,919,941 shares of common stock were outstanding as of February 14 2018, with the aggregate market value of non‑affiliate holdings totaling approximately $47.83 billion as of June 30 2017. The company participates in regulatory credit markets (ZEV, GHG, SREC) and benefits from various federal and state incentives for electric vehicles, energy storage and solar. The filing also outlines risks such as delays in ramping Model 3 production, reliance on single‑source suppliers, competition in the automotive, energy storage and solar markets, regulatory and legal challenges, and the limited number of vehicle nameplates in the company’s portfolio.

Inspector-General of Police Ibrahim Idris warned Ekiti state police before the July 14, 2018 governorship election not to help politicians manipulate results, stating police must ensure the voters' will prevails. He reminded officers that those who misbehaved in the 2014 election were investigated and punished, and said any officer found misbehaving will be dismissed and may face legal action. He urged the public to report police misconduct. Separately, Mobile Policemen protesting unpaid salaries in Maiduguri alleged Idris is corrupt, subjects them to inhumane treatment, and sells promotions.

Nearly 600 SUNY Oneonta students and staff attended a memorial service for Daniel William Michaels, 18, who died Dec. 3. Pastor Peter Derway led the service where memories were collected for the family and over $17,000 was raised for a scholarship in his name.

Device supports multiple Core Logic Voltage Domains each with independent Operating Performance Points (OPPs) defined by maximum frequencies and associated voltage ranges; lower frequencies reduce voltage for power savings; OPPs can be changed in real‑time without reset via Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling (DVFS). Not all OPP combinations are allowed and the maximum voltage difference between CVDD and any CVDD_x must be <150 mV. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is not supported. SRAM in switchable power domains automatically enters SHUTDOWN when its power domain goes OFF and returns to ACTIVE when the domain returns ON; additional SRAM can be shut down via registers. The device’s I/O groups (DVDD, DVDD_GPMC, DVDD_C, DVDD_SD) support independent 1.8 V or 3.3 V operation and DDR I/Os support 1.5 V or 1.8 V. Low‑Power Standby Mode turns all switchable domains OFF while the ARM executes an IDLE loop at its lowest frequency. Power supplies are organized into four sequencing groups with specific power‑up and power‑down sequences; 1.8 V supplies must be ≥ DDR supplies and 3.3 V supplies must never exceed 1.8 V by more than 2 V. The device provides multiple reset sources (Power‑On, Warm, Watchdog, Software Cold/Warm, Test) with defined priorities and isolation for PCIE and EMAC Switch. Pins enter Hi‑Z on reset except emulation pins, EMAC Switch pins (when isolated), and DDR address/control pins (driven to pull values). A Boot ROM configures pins after reset and the ARM Cortex‑A8 starts from ROM. Clock generation uses DEV and AUX inputs from crystals or external LVCMOS clocks (typically 20 MHz). The device contains 12 top‑level PLLs and 4 embedded PLLs; PLLs start in bypass after reset and require external filtering. Clock outputs, SYSCLKs, and module clocks have defined maximum frequencies based on OPP. Interrupt controllers (ARM AINTC up to 128 requests, DSP C674x up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts) and EDMA with 64 channels are provided. Peripherals include Ethernet MAC Switch (3‑port gigabit, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII), MDIO, GPIO (up to 128 pins), GPMC (NOR/NAND/ SRAM, up to 8 chip selects), DCAN, HDMI (1.3a TMDS transmitter), and JTAG (IEEE 1149.1) with AET and trace capabilities.

IAG shares fell to $8.07, extending a >4% drop linked to the Royal Commission into financial‑services misconduct. Investigations highlighted insurers denying claims (e.g., a funeral claim after a suicide) and targeting Indigenous people. No commission findings involve IAG, but its group general counsel is on leave. Completed a $525 million sale agreement, posted a result and raised its dividend 7.7%. Market confidence is low; investors should watch for further share‑price impact.

The Fresh Market Inc. named Yvonne Cowser Yancy senior vice president and chief human resources officer. Yancy brings over 20 years of HR experience, previously serving as commissioner of human resources for the City of Atlanta, where she oversaw 8,500 employees and 5,000 retirees. She will lead talent acquisition, organizational design, training, compensation and health‑wellness functions. CEO Larry Appel praised her HR expertise.

In this 1930 case, Ángel Bracero sued S. Ramírez & Co. for injuries when bags of rice fell on him while he was in the defendant's Ponce warehouse. The court found Bracero was an independent contractor. The majority reversed the lower court judgment, concluding no negligence was attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident and that the res ipsa loquitur doctrine was inapplicable given the plaintiff's and other workers' intervention with the pile. Chief Justice Del Toro dissented, arguing the evidence supported the trial court's finding that the defendant was grossly negligent in building a defective pile and failing to warn despite being timely cautioned about its condition.

Japanese bond prices fell Friday, tracking U.S. Treasuries retreat; markets awaited BOJ's April debt‑buying announcement. Treasury prices fell Thursday after Q4 GDP revision; five‑year yield to −0.125%, 10‑year to 0.065%.

Investing.com reports that the S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July, lifting its year‑to‑date gain to 7.8%, but slipped 1.6% on the first August session. August opened weakly; volatility and credit spreads showed seasonal upticks while investors kept increasing tech exposure and US electricity demand set a new all‑time high. Short‑term technicals appear fragile, though medium‑ and longer‑term trend indicators remain constructive, and the month was risk‑on with stocks up and bonds down. US large‑cap stocks placed third in monthly returns, frontier markets outperformed, and global stocks remain ahead year‑to‑date. The site’s AI‑driven stock‑picking service states that three‑quarters of its global portfolios are beating benchmarks, 98% are in the green, and its flagship Tech Titans strategy doubled the S&P 500 in 18 months, citing Super Micro Computer (+185%) and AppLovin (+157%). Related headlines note a $7 trillion price target for NVIDIA, Bitcoin above $123 k but below record highs, and Bank of America’s view that buying the S&P 500 at all‑time highs has historically carried no penalty. The site contains a disclaimer that its data may not be real‑time or accurate and that trading financial instruments involves high risk.

WiseGuyReports published "Gonorrhea - Pipeline Review, H2 2017," a pharmaceutical pipeline guide covering therapeutics under development for gonorrhea. The report provides information on therapeutics by stage of development, drug target, mechanism of action, route of administration, and molecule type. It reviews key companies involved in gonorrhea therapeutic development, including Debiopharm International SA, Entasis Therapeutics Inc, Merck & Co Inc, and Recce Ltd. Development stages include Phase III (1), Phase II (1), Preclinical (4), and Discovery (1). The guide also covers dormant and discontinued projects, drug profiles, and latest news related to pipeline therapeutics.

In 2011 Akamai, the world’s largest content‑delivery network (CDN) with $1.6 billion in revenue and a 60 % market share, faced a growing “localization challenge.” The company operated more than 100 000 servers across 78 countries, handled up to 30 % of all Internet traffic, and served global customers such as Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and the U.S. Department of Defense. Although international revenue had risen to 29 % of total sales (up from 22 % in 2006), Akamai’s market share fell sharply with distance from the United States, especially in Korea, China, and India, where local CDNs captured the majority of the market. New local entrants and “arbitrage” by multinational customers were eroding Akamai’s dominance.

CEO Charley Dublin, who also led international support, was tasked with developing solutions. The company’s decentralized, edge‑oriented server model gave it technical advantages, but operational issues limited local performance:

* **Products & sales targets** – A US‑centric product development model meant local sales teams often lacked the right offerings or faced targets set using a 40‑hour work week, creating mismatches in markets with shorter work weeks (e.g., Germany’s 37.5‑hour week) and limited network coverage (e.g., only one of France’s two ISPs).  
* **Pricing** – Prices were set globally and only currency‑converted, preventing Akamai from matching lower‑priced local competitors; in South Korea, CDNetworks undercut Akamai by a factor of ten while delivering comparable local performance.  
* **Brand awareness** – Akamai was well known in the US and parts of Europe but virtually unknown elsewhere, hindering sales in new regions.  
* **Market insight** – Headquarters lacked visibility into local conditions, and local teams did not fully understand global customer management; an acquisition of a US mobile‑content tool was rejected in Japan, where a superior native technology had existed for years.

To address these problems, Akamai reorganized in 2011. It moved from a purely functional structure to a business‑unit model (web experience, emerging products, media) and created three geographic theaters (Americas, EMEA, APJ) covering 35 countries. This allowed field managers to coordinate locally while product and pricing decisions remained global. However, tension persisted between the desire for full local responsiveness and the need to preserve a cohesive global core.

Dublin’s challenge was to determine where, how quickly, and to what extent Akamai needed to localize, balancing sales‑driven demands for total locality with centralized functions’ need to allocate resources efficiently.

Evolutionary hypergame dynamics model players with heterogeneous strategy sets in the prisoner’s dilemma with voluntary participation (C, D, L). Using a two-timescale framework—fast introspection reasoning for strategy choice and slower evolution of strategy sets—the paper analyzes tournament competitions and evolutionary simulations. Results show that stronger introspection (higher rationality) promotes cooperation, with the {C, L} strategy set dominating at high introspection in both well-mixed and spatially structured populations, while weak introspection favors defection or loner strategies. The framework extends classical evolutionary game theory by allowing both strategies and strategy sets to co-evolve.

PfK13 mutations (C469Y, A675V) were associated with decreased DHA and lumefantrine susceptibility, while PfCRT K76T mutation correlated with reduced chloroquine/amodiaquine activity. Researchers used scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to generate and detect magnetic monopoles on the surface of a three‑dimensional (3D) high‑order topological insulator. By applying a radially distributed electric field with the STM tip on a Bi(111) thin film, they observed image‑potential states (IPS) that exhibit intrinsic splitting dependent on the electric field strength. The splitting is attributed to the Zeeman interaction of the orbital magnetic moment of the IPS with the magnetic field created by the magnetic monopole, which arises from the topological magnetoelectric effect in the 3D TI. Theoretical analysis predicts the splitting energy ΔE ∝ √{n(n‑1)} / n³(n‑1/2) for principal quantum number n, and the measured ΔE for the n=2 IPS (~400 meV) is of the same order as the estimate (~204 meV). Control measurements on topologically trivial √3‑Bi and two‑dimensional topological insulator Bi(110) show no comparable IPS splitting, confirming the phenomenon requires a 3D TI with non‑zero magnetoelectric angle θ=π. The dependence of the splitting on tip current (electric field) follows the relationship I_t ∝ ΔE² exp(−a/ΔE), consistent with field‑emission transport and the formation of dyon‑like quasiparticles. The results demonstrate the creation and manipulation of magnetic monopoles in a solid‑state system, providing a new STM‑based platform for studying topological magnetoelectric effects and magnetic charge phenomena.

The passage details the new features of NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture. Blackwell adds hardware‑encode and‑decode support for YUV 4:2:2 chroma sampling, building on the prior 4:4:4 and 4:2:0 support of Ada. YUV 4:2:0 retains full luminance but only 25 % of chrominance, cutting data to half a 4:4:4 frame, while YUV 4:2:2 retains full luminance and half the chrominance, using two‑thirds the data of a 4:4:4 frame and providing twice the color resolution of 4:2:0. Higher‑end prosumer and professional cameras favor 4:2:2 because it balances color detail with file‑size and bandwidth savings, especially for HDR content and repeated color grading. The ninth‑generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5 % BD‑BR PSNR and introduces an AV1 Ultra‑High‑Quality mode that adds another 5 % improvement; it also adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding. The RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, delivering over 50 % faster export than the previous generation and 4× the speed of the RTX 3090. A sixth‑generation hardware decoder (NVDEC) doubles H.264 decoding speed and supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC decode.

DisplayPort 2.1b (UHBR 20) provides up to 80 Gbps, enabling 8K @ 165 Hz and 4K @ 480 Hz with DSC, and requires DP80LL‑certified cables. Blackwell’s Max‑Q power efficiency includes advanced power gating with multiple new levels, faster clock‑tree shutdown, and a dedicated voltage rail for GPU cores and memory that allows independent control and rail‑gated states at frame granularity, improving battery life on laptops. Accelerated frequency switching lets clocks adjust 1000× faster than earlier architectures, allowing the GPU to respond to short idle periods and free up power for higher clocks during active work. Low‑latency sleep states enter ten times faster than Ada, enabling deeper sleep and up to 50 % power savings during inference on small language models.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi‑Frame Generation (MFG) capable of producing up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame, a 40 % faster AI model, 30 % lower VRAM usage, and enhanced Flip Metering for smoother frame pacing. It also debuts a transformer‑based neural network for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, delivering twice the parameters, improved temporal stability, and better lighting detail. The fifth‑generation Tensor Cores and the AI Management Processor accelerate DLSS AI processing and scheduling.

Neural shaders integrate AI into traditional rendering pipelines. Blackwell introduces a Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan, enabling Tensor Core access from any shader type, and supports technologies such as RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC), and RTX Neural Faces. NTC achieves up to 7× VRAM compression over block‑compressed formats and, combined with Stochastic Texture Filtering, runs faster on Blackwell due to a 2× point‑sample texture‑filtering rate. Neural Radiance Cache uses tiny neural networks trained in real time to infer indirect lighting, improving performance and quality by reducing ray‑trace bounces. The present invention provides an image encoding/decoding method and apparatus using a motion vector refinement technique. The decoding method involves deriving an initial motion vector, refining it using either a merge mode-based or prediction block-based method, and generating a prediction block. The refinement derives refined L0 and L1 motion vectors by adding differences from search areas. Specific processing varies based on reference picture POC differences, including mirroring or scaling of motion vector differences. Entropy decoding of magnitude, direction, and unit information of the refined motion vector is performed. The prediction block-based method applies only under certain conditions (bi-direction merge mode, matching POC differences, block size constraints) and uses distortion calculations (SAD, SATD, SSE, MSE) to select optimal motion vectors. The encoding method mirrors the decoding steps, and a non-temporary storage medium stores the generated bitstream. The invention aims to improve image compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity during inter prediction.

Heating oil is a low‑viscosity refined crude‑oil product used mainly for heating residential and commercial buildings, with demand rising in colder months and falling in warmer months. Heating‑oil futures are standardized contracts to buy or sell a defined quantity at a preset price on a future date; they trade on ICE Futures Europe (symbol UHO, cash‑settled) and CME Globex (symbol HO, physically delivered). One contract equals 42 000 gallons (1 000 barrels), quoted in US $ per gallon with a minimum price move of $0.0001 per gallon ($4.20 per contract). Trading hours are 1:00 am‑11:00 pm London time on ICE and 5:00 pm‑4:00 pm CT on CME, with a 60‑minute daily break; the block minimum is 25 contracts. Settlement is cash on ICE and by physical delivery on CME, with final settlement on the last business day of the month before the contract month. Price drivers include weather, crude‑oil costs, refinery capacity and alternative fuel prices. All‑time high was $5.2215/gallon (April 2022) and all‑time low $0.2920/gallon (February 1999). Leverage can amplify losses; the biggest risk is adverse price movement. A backtested 168‑trade strategy showed an average gain of $370 per trade, profit factor 2.02 and 59 % win rate. An ETF tracking the market is the WisdomTree HEAT fund (Bloomberg Heating Oil Subindex). Futures allow speculation, hedging and arbitrage, and can add diversification to a trading portfolio.

An inside day occurs when today’s low is higher than yesterday’s low and today’s high is lower than yesterday’s high, placing the entire daily range inside yesterday’s range. It can appear on any time frame but is most common on daily bars. In the S&P 500, inside days have appeared about 10 % of the time since 1993.

Backtests show that buying every inside day and selling at the next open yields only a modest average gain and is not profitable on its own. Adding a filter such as the five‑day RSI below 50 raises the average gain per trade but still does not produce a viable strategy. A more refined swing‑trade rule on the S&P 500 generated 89 trades from 1993 onward, an average gain of 0.45 % per trade and a profit factor of 2.1; however, this approach works in equity markets but opposite in commodities like gold. Two consecutive inside days produced too few trades to be useful.

Overall, an inside day alone is a weak trading signal; profitable strategies require additional variables or filters to improve performance.

The damages awarded for the unlawful seizure and detention of a whaling ship are measured by the loss of the vessel's service during the brief whaling season, not by ordinary demurrage for trading vessels. The loss includes the owners' loss of returns for the entire year and the crew's loss of earnings, as crew are paid by a share of the catch (lay) and have no ownership of the catch. The appropriate measure of damages is the average catch of the vessel for the season, treated as the best evidence of the vessel's use, because the entire earnings depend on exploiting the brief opportunity. The rule does not admit speculative profits but permits use of the average catch as evidence of value. This rule was applied in the Costa Rica Packet case, where the arbitrator, a Russian official, noted that Captain Carpenter missed the best part of the whaling season due to unjustifiable detention, yet found no conclusive proof that he was forced to remain on board until April 1892.

Strength training builds muscle mass, strength and endurance, and can help maintain independence later in life. However, proper technique, adequate warm‑up and cool‑down are essential to prevent injuries. Warming up increases heart rate and blood flow, delivering more oxygen to muscles and providing a protective mechanism that makes them more resistant to strain; a rabbit study showed a warm‑up requires greater stretch force to cause a tear. Cooling down helps regulate blood flow.

Common strength‑training injuries include rotator‑cuff tears and tendinopathy, hamstring pulls (graded from pull to grade‑three tear), herniated discs (caused by sudden or repetitive poor movement), tendonitis (micro‑tear irritation from repetitive motion), tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) and golfer’s elbow (medial epicondylitis). Prevention strategies include maintaining good shoulder‑blade posture, using correct technique, progressing workout intensity gradually, warming up and stretching regularly, staying hydrated, and using ice, compression and elevation for initial injury care. Fitness coach Ollie Kerr advises against lifting weights that exceed current ability, recommends consulting a qualified instructor before starting a new programme, and suggests rest, proper diet and gradual progression to avoid injury. If pain persists, a doctor should be consulted. Research indicates that 22 minutes of moderate‑to‑vigorous daily exercise may mitigate the health effects of prolonged sitting. The content on this page is peer‑reviewed by qualified clinicians.
