Mammals and birds adapt to temperature changes 2–3 times faster than reptiles and amphibians, according to a study in Nature Ecology & Evolution. The research, led by Jonathan Rolland of the University of British Columbia, analyzed 300 million data points for 11,500 species over 270 million years. Endotherms regulate own body temperature and warm offspring, giving them higher survival during past temperature swings and allowing them to move into higher latitudes as Earth cooled. The authors note current warming is faster than past changes, and that pollution, hunting, habitat loss and invasive species drive extinction. Species are vanishing up to 10,000 times faster than baseline, with over 20,000 plants and animals at risk; a quarter of mammals and 12 % of birds are threatened. Rolland hopes the work will link macro‑ and micro‑evolutionary responses to climate change.

SNP Run VMPL NAE event enables a guest to request the hypervisor run a vCPU at a different VMPL level, associating a unique VMSA with each level; a GHCB may also be per level and the hypervisor updates VMSA and GHCB SPAs. SEV‑TIO provides trusted‑device binding, discovered via a device’s TEE‑IO PCIe capabilities; the SNP guest performs setup including device info, interface report, MMIO and IOMMU configuration. SNP TIO Guest Request NAE mirrors the SNP Guest Request but supplies unencrypted Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status; data pages are optional for measurements, certificates and TDISP attestation report, and the hypervisor returns required page count if insufficient. Secure AVIC offers a private APIC backing page per vCPU with REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions; no feature bit is required. Termination Request NAE lets the guest request termination, providing 64‑bit info in SW_EXITINFO2 and reason codes in SW_EXITINFO1. Guest identification of SEV‑ES uses CPUID with ECX[31]=1, EAX[1]=1, and EBX bits for encryption bit position and address‑space reduction. AP booting under SEV‑ES/SEV‑SNP is challenging because registers cannot be updated after measurement; solutions include reset‑vector code or a predetermined CS/IP location. The AP Jump Table conveys the AP reset vector, must be 4 KB, encrypted, page‑aligned, and communicated via SEV‑SNP Secrets Page. SNP AP Creation NAE (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013) uses VMSA pages to create or update AP state, supports vCPU hotplug and eliminates AP Reset Hold. NMI injection requires the hypervisor intercept #DB, not IRET, and the guest sends an “NMI Complete” message. Debug register virtualization is optional via the DebugVirtualization bit in SEV_FEATURES. #HV doorbell page is a shared, host‑owned page with a 16‑bit PendingEvent field and a byte NoEoiRequired field; host writes interrupt vectors, NMI, or #MC and sets NoFurtherSignal; guest acknowledges by atomic exchange of PendingEvent and clears NoEoiRequired when possible. Host emulates APIC interrupt presentation; guest validates vectors, dispatches interrupts, handles EOI via atomic exchange or VMGEXIT write to X2APIC EOI MSR, and may dispatch non‑maskable events regardless of EFLAGS.IF. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this version.

Kuwait expects to finish cleaning an oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, with no further patches reported and work continuing near shore. The cause is undisclosed. Ras al-Zour hosts a 615,000 bpd KNPC refinery. Saudi‑Kuwait joint operations say their facilities are safe and have enacted an emergency plan.

A head-mounted augmented reality system for image-guided surgery uses a tracking device to align computer-generated images of tools and patient anatomy with the actual patient, requiring alignment accuracy of about 2-3 mm. The system includes a patient marker with a unique array allowing position and orientation determination using a single camera without triangulation. When the primary tracking device loses line of sight to the patient or tool marker, data from additional tracking devices (on another head-mounted device or stationary in the operating room) is used to continue generating the augmented reality image, which may display the view from the second tracking device, fill the display with the virtual view, or continue showing the tool position while tracking head movements with an inertial measurement unit. Methods and apparatus for tracking and generating these augmented reality images are provided.

Investors, who had been shrugging off geopolitical and economic risks while focusing on economic strength and corporate profits, are now becoming skittish. Stocks fell over 2% in their worst week in two years. The catalyst was a jobs report showing rising wages, suggesting potential inflation. Investors' real concern is that cheap money from global central banks may disappear sooner than expected. Since 2009, the stock boom has been supported by historically low interest rates, which central banks slashed to encourage investment and economic growth.

Since 1900, the U.S. stock market has experienced an average of one correction per year; a correction is a decline of at least 10% but less than 20%. About 80% of corrections do not become bear markets (drops greater than 20%). The average correction has been a 13.5% drop lasting roughly 54 days. Bear markets historically have produced an average decline of 33% in the S&P 500, with more than a third falling more than 40%; their duration has ranged from about 45 days to 694 days, averaging about a year. Between 1980 and 2015, the S&P 500 fell at least 10% intra‑year in those years, ending positive in 27 of the 36 years (75%). Market declines have occurred amid major events such as wars, 9/11, and the 2008 crisis. Experts including Warren Buffett argue that long‑term growth drivers (population growth, productivity) make future market gains likely, and investors who react emotionally often lock in losses. The article encourages accepting corrections as routine, staying invested, and taking personal responsibility for investment decisions.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardened, current mode PWM controllers designed for space-grade DC-DC converter applications. These controllers support multiple topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz suitable for GaN power semiconductor designs.

The devices provide primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with approximately 150-mA peak current capability, requiring external gate drive solutions. Programmable features include dead time (TDSP and TDPS) between primary and synchronous switch transitions, duty cycle limits (50%, 75%, or 100% depending on DCL pin configuration), and leading edge blank time for noise filtering.

Current sensing is achieved through the CS_ILIM pin with a 1.05 V current limit threshold. The controllers implement peak current mode control where outputs turn off when sensed current reaches the COMP/2 voltage. Hiccup mode operation provides overcurrent protection with cycle-by-cycle limiting followed by a delay period before attempting restart.

Additional features include slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%, external fault protection with configurable thresholds, thermal shutdown at 175°C with 160°C restart threshold, and Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation using transconductance error amplifiers. The controllers operate from a 4V to 14V input supply range with minimum 0.1 µF input bypass capacitance recommended.

The passage describes a plan to reform railroad regulation and taxation through moderate, common‑sense legislation. The author argues that the government should not operate businesses but should supervise them to protect the public interest. Current laws that prohibit all combinations of capital are ineffective and harmful; the author calls for rigorous control and supervision of legitimate combinations while allowing railroads to make agreements sanctioned by the Interstate Commerce Commission and publicly disclosed. The passage notes that the Supreme Court’s rulings have made it impossible to operate railways without technically breaking the law, and it cites the Interstate Commerce Commission’s statement that joint traffic associations continue to operate despite the rulings. The author recommends amending the law to address this problem.

On taxation, the passage explains that in a federal system some taxes are best levied locally (real estate taxes, state franchise taxes), while others should be imposed nationally to avoid driving business to other jurisdictions. Historically, the national government has relied on tariffs and excise taxes. The author proposes adding a graduated inheritance tax and, if possible, a graduated income tax, arguing that the wealthy derive special benefits from the state and should bear a proportionate share of the tax burden. The passage emphasizes that any revision must distribute the burden equitably, treating rich and poor with equal justice, and must avoid injustice to either group.

Apple Inc. Q2 FY2018 (quarter ended March 31 2018) reported net sales of $61.1 billion, up 16% year‑over‑year, with net income of $13.8 billion ($2.73 diluted EPS). Gross margin was $23.4 billion (38.3%) and operating income $15.9 billion. By segment, Americas contributed $24.8 billion, Europe $13.8 billion, Greater China $13.0 billion, Japan $5.5 billion and Rest of Asia Pacific $4.0 billion. Product revenue: iPhone $38.0 billion (62% of total), Services $9.2 billion (15%). The effective tax rate fell to 14.5% following the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered the statutory rate to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax. Cash and marketable securities totaled $267.2 billion. The company repurchased $23.5 billion of common stock in the quarter and a new $100 billion repurchase program was authorized in May 2018. Apple expects Q3 FY2018 gross margin of 38.0%–38.5%.

Two teens arrested and one at large after a Frankston police pursuit. A black Subaru with stolen plates was spotted by highway patrol around 12:20am, later dumped in Bayswater car park. Three occupants fled on foot; an 18-year-old was bitten by a police dog. Both arrested teens assisting police.

On May 18, 2001, Saudi Arabia selected international oil companies including Exxon Mobil, Shell, BP, Phillips, TotalFinaElf, Conoco, Occidental, and Enron for three natural gas projects requiring approximately $25 billion in investment, marking the reopening of Saudi Arabia's energy sector to foreign investment for the first time since nationalization in the 1970s. Meanwhile, a Dow Jones article reported that California faces losing over 40% of its power from long-term contracts, and forward power prices in the western U.S. have been falling, reducing the value of the state's $43 billion in contracts by an estimated 15%. In options markets, investor volatility fell to its lowest levels in months as investors continued selling options to generate income in an expected flat market.

Sam Bankman‑Fried (SBF) co‑founded Alameda Research in 2017 with Tara Mac Aulay and Gary Wang, and later co‑founded the crypto exchange FTX with Wang in 2019. FTX grew rapidly, reporting $1.02 billion in revenue in 2021, a $32 billion valuation after a Series C round in early 2022, and more than nine million customer accounts. FTX issued its own token (FTT), with Alameda holding a large portion that was used as collateral for loans.

In 2022, amid a crypto market downturn, FTX and Alameda attempted to prop up failing firms. On Nov 2 2022, CoinDesk leaked Alameda’s balance sheet, revealing that 40 % of its assets were in FTT. Binance announced it would sell its FTT holdings, causing the token’s price to fall ~80 % in two days. A run on FTX ensued, with over $6 billion withdrawn in 72 hours. FTX paused withdrawals on Nov 8, the Bahamian regulator froze its assets, and on Nov 11 2022 FTX and about 100 affiliated entities filed for bankruptcy.

SBF was arrested on Dec 12 2022 and charged with eight criminal counts (fraud, money‑laundering, campaign‑finance offenses); he pleaded not guilty. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty; Nishad Singh pleaded guilty to six charges, admitting he wrote code that allowed FTX customer funds to be diverted to Alameda, inflated 2021 revenues by about $50 million, and made illegal political contributions at SBF’s direction.

Investigations revealed that FTX operated without an independent board, a CFO, or a functioning accounting department, and that Alameda received a nearly limitless line of credit funded by FTX customer assets. The SEC and CFTC filed civil complaints alleging undisclosed diversion of customer funds, special treatment for Alameda, and undisclosed exposure to overvalued illiquid tokens. Auditors, investors, and regulators faced scrutiny over the lack of oversight that enabled the collapse.

Penn State has ordered three student‑led outdoor clubs — the Outing Club (founded 1920), the Nittany Grotto Caving Club and the Nittany Divers SCUBA Club — to stop organizing trips, citing high risk from remote locations, poor cell service and distance from emergency services. The decision followed a two‑month risk review conducted without consulting the clubs, prompting complaints about lack of dialogue and higher costs of university‑run alternatives. The university says safety is its primary focus, staff are meeting with student leaders about the transition, and it will continue to offer its own outdoor program.

Android 8.0 Oreo, released in August, brings several features including Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, which enhances multi-tasking beyond the split-screen mode introduced in Nougat. PiP allows video content to display in a floating window while users access other apps. However, not all apps support this feature—developers must enable it. Currently supported apps include Google Chrome, Google Duo, Google Play Movies & TV, Google Play Services, Google Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC. YouTube's PiP requires a YouTube Red subscription, which is unavailable in some countries. To use PiP, users can enter full-screen mode in a supported app, swipe up to reveal navigation buttons, and tap the home button to activate the floating window. The floating window can be moved, paused, closed, or expanded back to full-screen. If PiP doesn't work, users can enable it in Settings under Apps & notifications > Advanced > Special app access > Picture-in-picture. This feature benefits power users who want to watch videos or access navigation while using other apps.

The case involves a dispute over land ownership in Navarro County, Texas. The court held that an 1839 deed from Mastín Latham to William F. Henderson was an absolute conveyance, not an executory contract, because the consideration clause referred to past services already rendered. Even if the clause created a condition subsequent, no forfeiture was properly enforced, and the grantor's right to enforce forfeiture could not be asserted by a stranger to the title. The defenses of stale demand, three-year, five-year, and ten-year statute of limitations all failed because: the deed was executed rather than executory; the ten-year period was incomplete due to constitutional exclusions; no tax payment evidence existed for the five-year defense; and the defendant's chain of title was inconsistent with his possession, which was held under Latham rather than under his own title chain, with no privity established. The judgment was reversed and remanded.
Annual Fund donations protect rule of law, build independent courts, eliminate bias, expand justice access; donors receive sticker and magnet set.

The President reported to Congress that diplomatic efforts to persuade Britain and France to revoke their edicts against U.S. commerce had failed; France provided no response and Britain rejected the proposed arrangement, leaving the embargo in effect. He stated the embargo had protected American mariners and property while allowing time for defensive preparations. Relations with Spain were paused due to its internal situation; harmony with Barbary powers was maintained except for an incident with Algiers. Indian affairs remained peaceful with tribes assisting in delivering offenders for trial. Defense works at harbors and gun-boat construction were progressing, and domestic manufacturing was expanding due to trade disruptions. Financial data showed receipts of about $18 million, enabling significant debt repayment and leaving a substantial treasury balance. The President suggested future surplus revenue could fund internal improvements and expressed confidence in the nation’s stability and future.

Ukraine and Bitfury Group signed a memorandum of understanding to place all government electronic data on a blockchain platform, described by Bitfury CEO Valery Vavilov as the largest such government blockchain deal. The partnership aims to improve transparency and efficiency, beginning with a pilot covering state registers, public services, social security, health and energy, expected later this year. Other countries with smaller blockchain initiatives include Sweden, Estonia and Georgia. Bitfury previously piloted a blockchain land‑titling project in Georgia.

The Bank of England’s “Super Thursday” will keep rates unchanged while investors watch its inflation and growth forecasts; UK bond yields hit a pre‑Brexit high and sterling has risen to near its 2016 level. Australian and New Zealand central banks face cooling housing markets, below‑target inflation and stronger currencies, while China’s upcoming data are expected to show slowing price growth and a closely watched trade surplus with the United States. The U.S. trade deficit is forecast to widen in December as strong domestic demand drives record imports, and a potential government shutdown looms on Thursday. Corporate results will highlight a growing earnings gap between Europe and the United States, with European stocks trading at a discount to U.S. peers. Emerging‑market central banks are active: Russia may cut its key rate as inflation falls below target, Mexico is expected to raise rates, Romania may hike again, and the Reserve Bank of India is likely to hold but may adopt a firmer tone after the expansionary budget.

McGreal v. Village of Orland Park: The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to the defendants. McGreal, a former police officer, claimed his firing was retaliation for protected speech at a village board meeting and that it constituted intentional infliction of emotional distress. The court found McGreal failed to provide admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his speech or that his speech motivated his termination. The court also found no evidence that the defendants' alternative explanations for the firing—lying under oath, insubordination, and reckless conduct—were pretextual. Additionally, McGreal offered no evidence that the defendants' conduct was extreme or outrageous or caused severe emotional distress, noting his own admission that his distress was "probably of the garden variety," which is insufficient under Illinois law.

HoopTactics offers out‑of‑bounds plays that aim for high‑percentage shots with two to three options and, if unavailable, flow into a predetermined continuity to avoid rushed shots. The plays are shown for baseline, sideline and full‑court situations. Full‑court out‑of‑bounds is difficult, but a prepared team can score with as little as one second left; defense often has a 5‑on‑4 advantage, so a baseline play can safely inbound under pressure. Priorities are the best player, then height and best shooter, and the best inbounder and shooters on the floor. At game end, advance the ball to mid‑court and call a timeout is preferred; otherwise use a baseline out‑of‑bounds play with the best free‑throw shooters.

Kyle Freeland threw 5 1/3 innings, doubled during a three-run fourth and earned the win as the Colorado Rockies defeated the San Francisco Giants 11‑4. The Giants lost starter Jeff Samardzija after one inning because of shoulder tightness; he was replaced by rookie Dereck Rodriguez, son of Hall‑of‑Famer Ivan Rodriguez, making his major‑league debut but leaving in the fifth after being hit on the right shin by a line drive. The Rockies got hits from every starter, including David Dahl’s first career pinch‑hit homer, Trevor Story’s run‑scoring triple and RBI doubles by Nolan Arenado, Gerardo Parra and Ian Desmond. Evan Longoria hit two solo homers and Buster Posey added a solo shot for the Giants. Errors by Giants infielder Kelby Tomlinson and a throwing miscue by Brandon Belt helped the Rockies score three unearned runs in the fourth. The Rockies have won 12 of their last 13 home games against the Giants. Madison Bumgarner is scheduled to make his second minor‑league rehab start Thursday.

Maddie Sabourin, 18, a Darlington School senior in Georgia, has been seeking a kidney match for her grandfather Sam Senseney, 63, who needs a transplant and undergoes dialysis. After family and friends tested unsuccessfully, Maddie used the Miss Georgia Outstanding Teen pageant to raise organ‑donation awareness and $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund. On her 18th birthday she learned she was a match; doctors initially deemed her too young, but she persuaded them to allow the donation. A surgery date is expected within the next month, requiring Maddie to miss three weeks of school.

The passage describes a 5G system architecture comprising 5G access networks and a 5G core network that includes network functions such as AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NEF, NRF, UDM, AUSF and N3IWF. It explains registration management (RM) and connection management (CM) states for UEs and AMF, and introduces network slicing concepts including S‑NSSAI, slice instances and slice isolation levels. The disclosed embodiments define three levels of network‑slice isolation: fully isolated (no sharing of (R)AN or core‑network functions), partly isolated with (R)AN shared, and partly isolated with (R)AN and AMF shared. The passage provides call‑flow examples and flow diagrams for UE registration in which the UE includes network‑slice isolation information in the registration request; the (R)AN forwards the request to an NRF or NSSF, which obtains subscription data from the UDM and selects an appropriate AMF based on the requested and subscribed isolation level. The selected AMF address is returned to the (R)AN, which routes the registration to the AMF and sends a registration accept to the UE. The described procedures support both 3GPP and non‑3GPP access and allow a UE to be simultaneously attached to multiple network slice instances.

Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers observed the rogue planet SIMP‑0136 and detected strong auroral activity similar to Earth’s Northern Lights and Jupiter’s, heating its upper atmosphere. The planet’s surface temperature exceeds 1,500 °C and temperature variations smaller than 5 °C were recorded, linked to subtle chemical changes that suggest storm systems like Jupiter’s Great Red Spot. Cloud coverage on SIMP‑0136 remained constant and consists of silicate grains, unlike terrestrial clouds. The observations provide the most precise atmospheric measurements of any exoplanet to date and represent the first direct detection of atmospheric property changes with rotation. The study was conducted by Trinity College Dublin’s Exo‑Aimsir group, led by Prof. Johanna Vos and lead author Dr. Evert Nasedkin, building on earlier work by Allison McCarthy’s team. Future telescopes may extend such measurements to additional brown dwarfs and exoplanets.

E. F. Joy, as assignee of a creditor, appealed a judgment rejecting his claim to set aside two deeds of gift executed by Louis Helbing to his wife Louise in May 1893. The deeds conveyed San Francisco real property on B Street and on Waller and McAllister streets and were not recorded until December 1895. At the time of the conveyances Helbing was solvent and owned other assets; he later entered the plumbing business. Between September and December 1895, before the deeds were recorded, Helbing obtained credit from W. W. Montague & Co. by representing himself as the owner of the unrecorded property. The trial court found that the deed was not made with intent to hinder, delay, or defraud Helbing’s creditors, that it was made without consideration other than love and affection, and that the plaintiff bore the burden of proving fraudulent intent. The court noted that the long delay in recording the deed was a suspicious circumstance but not alone evidence of fraud. It also excluded testimony about personal property found under the house and a sworn claim by Mrs. Helbing, ruling the evidence too remote and unrelated to the execution of the deed. The appellate court affirmed the judgment and the order denying a new trial, holding that the trial court correctly applied the burden of proof and that the excluded evidence, even if erroneous, did not warrant reversal.

Tropical Storm Nate, the 15th Atlantic system of the season, is forecast to strike the U.S. Gulf Coast as a Category 1 hurricane this weekend after crossing the Yucatan Peninsula. Louisiana declared a state of emergency, ordered evacuations of coastal and barrier‑island areas and mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops, with pumps in New Orleans being monitored. Nate has already caused 22 deaths in Latin America (at least 15 in Nicaragua, 7 in Costa Rica) and heavy rainfall. This season has produced 15 tropical cyclones, including three major hurricanes (Harvey, Irma, Maria), and September set a record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy, being about 3.5 times more active than average.

The article tests a pair‑trade strategy in SPY (S&P 500 ETF) and TLT (long‑term Treasury ETF). Entry rules: when the S&P 500 falls more than 1.25 × the 50‑day average true‑range and TLT rises by the same factor on the same day, a long SPY/short TLT position is opened and held overnight (or closed after a set number of days). Back‑testing from 2003 to June 2021 yields an erratic equity curve, a CAGR of about 1.93 %, a 60 % win‑rate and an average gain of roughly 0.18 % per round‑trip. Changing the movement thresholds or varying the holding period (best exit at the close of the third day, averaging 0.26 % per trade) does not materially improve results. The conclusion is that the strategy is not consistently profitable and therefore not considered tradeable. On 18 June 2021 both SPY and TLT moved sharply in opposite directions, illustrating the market conditions that prompted the test.

Study aim: analyse factors causing delayed discharge from a subacute Complex Discharge Unit (CDU) during the first year of the COVID‑19 pandemic at St James's Hospital, Dublin. A retrospective cross‑sectional analysis of 390 adult patients admitted March 2020–February 2021 with hospital length of stay (LOS) > 15 days was performed. Patients were predominantly > 65 years (83.6 %), female (59.7 %) and 48.2 % had > 4 comorbidities; median LOS was 19.4 days. Five factors associated with delayed discharge were identified: complications from primary diagnoses or multimorbidity (37.94 % of patients), frailty/falls requiring integrated rehabilitation (25.38 %), community service issues (14.35 %), patient‑centred needs (13.07 %) and healthcare‑associated infection (10.52 %). Kaplan–Meier and stratified Cox regression showed that age 65‑75 years, female gender and > 4 comorbidities were linked to prolonged LOS; complications arising from comorbidities and patient‑centred needs were the only factors that remained statistically significant (p < 0.05) across gender and multimorbidity strata. The authors conclude that complexities from primary diagnoses and patient‑centred needs are the main contributors to delayed discharge, highlighting areas for future contingency planning.
OpenAI is preparing to launch a stand-alone app for AI-generated videos powered by Sora 2, resembling TikTok with vertical video feeds, swipe navigation, and For You-style recommendation algorithms.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) is a passive investment approach based on Buffett’s 2013 instruction to allocate 90% of a portfolio to a low‑cost S&P 500 index ETF and 10% to short‑term government bonds. The strategy seeks long‑term growth, lower fees and reduced risk compared with actively managed funds. The 90% equity component provides exposure to the 500 largest publicly‑traded U.S. companies, which historically have delivered strong returns over long periods. The 10% bond component offers a buffer against market volatility; government bonds are considered the safest form of debt because they are backed by the government. Investors can implement the portfolio with a lump‑sum purchase or through dollar‑cost averaging, and the allocation may be adjusted over time to match individual goals, risk tolerance and time horizon. Historical backtests of a 90/10 mix of SPY with short‑term Treasury ETFs (SHY, IEI) and a longer‑duration Treasury ETF (TLT) show that increasing bond maturity raises risk but also raises return compensation, with the 10% TLT allocation closely matching the performance of a 100% equity portfolio while offering slightly lower drawdowns. The portfolio carries market‑related risks (economic changes, geopolitical events) and tax implications on capital gains and dividends that depend on individual circumstances. Past performance is not a guarantee of future results.

Bank of England research indicates a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could strengthen monetary policy transmission by making commercial banks respond faster to interest rate changes and improve quantitative easing by allowing direct asset purchases without intermediaries. The Bank is not currently planning to issue a CBDC but is researching its design.

Defendant Lawrence B. Schaub was charged with child abandonment under MCL 750.135 after allegedly attempting to sell his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for $60,000. The district court dismissed the charge, finding no evidence the child was left without care. The circuit court reversed, reinstating the charge. The Court of Appeals reversed the circuit court, holding that while sufficient evidence existed to show defendant intended to wholly abandon the child, the evidence did not establish the element of "exposure" required under the statute because the child was handed to someone who would care for her and was never without care. The matter was reversed and remanded. The dissent argued that delivering an infant to a stranger without proper investigation constitutes exposure under the statute. Following this case, the Legislature enacted MCL 750.136c prohibiting the sale or purchase of people.

U.S. consuls report that many American citizens in Cuba, especially in rural central and eastern districts, are destitute and lack food and medicine. Six to eight hundred need immediate relief. The President recommends a $50,000 appropriation under the Secretary of State for provisions and transportation home.

The acknowledgments thank staff from the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, Library of Congress, CIA, and numerous historians and editors who contributed to the volume. The sources include published presidential papers, congressional records, Department of State bulletins, and declassified White House files such as speechwriting records, WHORM subject files, transition papers, presidential papers, staff and office files, Secretary of State George Shultz’s papers, State Department lot files, and the Central Foreign Policy File, all housed at the Reagan Library, National Archives, and related facilities.

Walmart senior vice president of transformation and innovation Greg Cathey said at the UP.Summit in Bentonville, Arkansas, that the retailer plans to expand drone delivery to “most areas that we operate in,” marking a shift from limited pilots to a core component of its operations. The company has tested drones for more than five years and cites the evolving regulatory environment as making the service viable. Currently drone delivery is available at a handful of Walmart’s 4,600 U.S. stores through partnerships with Alphabet’s Wing, and in June the retailer announced an expansion to 100 stores in Atlanta, Charlotte, Houston, Orlando and Tampa. Cathey added Northwest Arkansas—near its headquarters—will also be added, and the retailer intends to add “a lot” more locations. Walmart has completed over 300,000 drone deliveries, double the 150,000 it reported in June. Widespread rollout remains years away as technical, regulatory and financial hurdles remain, including an FAA proposal to allow beyond‑visual‑line‑of‑sight flights, which is not expected to be finalized until next year.

The Golden Cross Trading Strategy uses the 50-day and 200-day moving averages. A Golden Cross occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses above the 200-day moving average, signaling a buy. When the 50-day crosses below the 200-day, it signals a sell. Backtesting on the S&P 500 since 1960 showed 33 trades over approximately 66 years, with a 79% win rate and 15.8% average trade gain. The strategy produced a 6.8% annual return with a 9.6% risk-adjusted return while invested 70% of the time. Drawdowns were lower (33%) compared to buy-and-hold (56%). An example trade showed buying the S&P 500 in July 2020 at 2867 and selling in March 2022 at 4173 for a 32.4% gain. The strategy aims to exploit the stock market's long-term uptrend while reducing losses in bear markets.

This study assessed antiretroviral therapy (ART) non-adherence among 424 HIV patients at Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda, using a cross-sectional design with structured questionnaires administered in March-April 2024. The overall non-adherence rate was 13% (55 patients), with 87% (369 patients) adhering to treatment. Multivariate analysis identified five significant factors associated with non-adherence: younger age (below 31 years) with adjusted odds ratio (AoR) of 15.462, lack of tertiary education (AoR 8.232), experiencing stigma (AoR 2.148), perceiving ART as ineffective (AoR 9.333), and failing to integrate ART into daily routines (AoR 11.180). Bivariate analysis also found associations with multiple sexual partners, longer travel and waiting times, smoking, and non-disclosure of HIV status to friends. Psycho-behavioral factors including recognizing the health risks of non-adherence and maintaining medication despite disruptions were significantly associated with better adherence. The study concludes that younger patients, those without tertiary education, individuals experiencing stigma, and those who do not incorporate ART into daily activities face higher non-adherence risks. Setting alarms as reminders showed no significant impact. The authors recommend targeted interventions for vulnerable populations and comprehensive support systems beyond simple reminders to improve adherence rates.

Plaintiff Richard A. Milan, a pro se inmate at the Indiana State Prison, sued under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 alleging that prison officials violated his due‑process and Eighth Amendment rights when they denied his visitation request on July 10, 1988. The court applied the summary‑judgment standard from Celotex Corp. v. Catrett and Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, requiring the moving party to show no genuine issue of material fact. Citing Hewitt v. Helms and Kentucky Dep’t of Corr. v. Thompson, the court held that inmates generally have no liberty interest in visitation privileges; a protected interest only arises when state law uses mandatory language limiting official discretion. The court examined the prison’s Administrative Procedure 02‑00‑104 and found it grants officials broad discretion and does not create a liberty interest. Although the prison failed to give written notice of the denial, the court ruled this procedural defect does not rise to a constitutional violation. Accordingly, summary judgment was granted in favor of the defendants.

E-learning is essential for organisations to stay competitive, aiming to deliver knowledge and skills cost‑effectively. To achieve this, a flexible governance model is needed. The paper defines e‑learning governance as providing strategic direction, ensuring objectives are met, managing risks and allocating resources (COBIT Steering Committee). It reviews e‑learning systems, ecosystems and governance, proposing a framework of structures, processes, communications and relational mechanisms, extended with a fourth element – pedagogies and instructional designs – based on De Haes and Van Grembergen’s IT governance model. Darking’s six characteristics and dimensions (constitution/balance of interests, culture of communication, credibility/attunement/trust, organisation/synchronisation, licensing/regulation, and technological dimension) are adopted to strengthen the framework. The paper also addresses information‑security governance, outlining steps to ensure security, manage risk and monitor counter‑measures. Trust in services, business activities and knowledge, together with a regulatory knowledge base covering privacy, e‑signatures and jurisdiction, are identified as critical. The authors conclude that governance is vital for e‑learning success and suggest further exploratory research.

This passage outlines a study estimating the burden of disease (BoD) from COVID-19 in the Republic of Ireland (RoI) between March 1, 2020, and February 28, 2021, using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs). DALYs are calculated by summing years of life lost (YLL) and years lived with disability (YLD). YLL is derived from deaths and remaining life expectancy using GBD 2019 life tables. YLD is computed for five health states—asymptomatic, moderate, severe, critical, and post-acute consequences—using incidence, duration, and disability weights. Data is sourced from public datasets (DATA.GOV.IE) including CSO, HPSC, HSE, and Department of Health. Ethical approval was obtained from University College Cork.

Interpretability research aims to improve transparency and trust in large language models (LLMs) and AI systems, addressing challenges such as lack of standardized evaluation frameworks, computational scalability (need for sub‑linear methods), and practical deployment across diverse contexts. A proposed framework edits concept activation vectors (CAVs) by training logistic regression classifiers on activation data to detect target concepts, enabling dynamic enhancement or suppression while preserving text fluency and handling conflicts among multiple concepts through optimization.

The passage describes a data management system using storage appliances that cache snapshots between data sources and cloud storage. Snapshots contain metadata (inode, directory, and data map records) organized in key-value stores by defined data collection. The system addresses problems with "forever incremental" snapshot strategies where stable, unchanged data blocks risk eviction due to typical caching policies, potentially violating recovery time objectives. The disclosed solutions involve creating synthetic baseline snapshots by manipulating snapshot metadata in key-value stores and refreshing eviction state data for stable data blocks. The patent details methods for snapshot creation, storage in arrays, metadata record generation, snapshot restoration (full, file-level granularity), and snapshot reclamation through merging valid records into succeeding snapshots.

Police are investigating a video of officers using a stun gun on a pregnant 17‑year‑old, Dailene Rosario, during an arrest after a fight over a video game at a Bronx apartment. She faces charges of resisting arrest, second‑degree harassment and disorderly conduct; the incident is under internal review.

The coach discusses the goaltending situation, with Martin initially struggling and Emery becoming the starter after getting healthy. He praises general manager Brian Burke for his willingness to make big trades and build the team. The team emphasizes respecting all opponents and credits its leadership group, particularly Alfredsson, Phillips, and Redden, for their composure and ability to step up. Mike Comrie is highlighted as an acquisition who improved his two-way play after initially struggling on the right side. The coach discusses his philosophy of playing four lines and six defensemen throughout the season, believing this depth will benefit the team in the playoffs. Anton Volchenkov is noted as having emerged as a leader in shot blocking after receiving more playing time following the loss of Chara.

In Shumye v. Felleke, the court rules on cross-motions for summary judgment regarding a sponsor’s obligations under Form I-864. The plaintiff, an Ethiopian citizen, seeks to enforce her former husband’s financial obligations as her sponsor. The defendant concedes the validity of the Form I-864 and the plaintiff’s right to sue for enforcement. The court analyzes the plaintiff’s income annually against the 125% federal poverty threshold. Regarding disputed income categories, the court finds: the $49,000 divorce settlement is not income; student loans are not income; student grants are income; and housing subsidies are income, while bank statements alone are insufficient to infer additional income. For 2000, 2001, 2002, 2004, and 2005, the plaintiff’s income met or exceeded the threshold, so the court grants partial summary judgment for the defendant on those years. For 2003, 2006, and 2007, the defendant’s evidence does not establish that the plaintiff’s income exceeded the threshold, and the plaintiff fails to meet her burden for her own motion. The court grants in part and denies in part the defendant’s motion and denies the plaintiff’s motion.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016. Total net sales were $30.4 billion for Q2 2016, up 31% from $23.2 billion in Q2 2015. Operating income was $1.3 billion compared to $464 million in Q2 2015. Net income was $857 million compared to $92 million in Q2 2015. Cash and cash equivalents were $12.5 billion at June 30, 2016. The company has three segments: North America (net sales $17.7 billion, operating income $702 million), International (net sales $9.8 billion, operating loss $135 million), and AWS (net sales $2.9 billion, operating income $718 million). Long-term debt was $8.3 billion. The company faces ongoing tax audits, including an IRS dispute regarding transfer pricing for 2005-2006 seeking additional tax of approximately $1.5 billion. The European Commission is investigating tax arrangements in Luxembourg. Recent accounting pronouncements include new standards for revenue recognition, leases, and stock-based compensation that will impact future financial statements.

Asian shares paused after three straight sessions of gains, with markets hoping an upswing in global growth can outlast a likely U.S. rate hike this week. Chinese banks supplied unexpectedly generous credit in November, supporting prospects for retail sales and industrial output data due later. The MSCI Asia‑Pacific index held near flat, with blue‑chip Chinese shares off 0.2% and Australia up 0.1%; Japan’s Nikkei steadied after a 25‑year high. Wall Street rose, led by technology and energy, with the Dow up 0.23%, the S&P 500 0.32% and the Nasdaq 0.51%. An explosion at New York’s Port Authority had no lasting market impact. Investors are watching the Fed’s two‑day meeting ending Wednesday and the ECB’s meeting Thursday; a JPMorgan economist expects the Fed to raise its growth forecast and possibly add a fourth 2018 rate hike, while the ECB is set to stress a low‑for‑long stance and a slower core‑inflation recovery. Despite a widening U.S.–German two‑year yield spread, the euro has risen 12% against the dollar this year, and the dollar is down 8% on a currency basket. The euro steadied at $1.1768 and the dollar at 113.48 yen; forex volumes were 35% below average. Bitcoin traded near $16,350, gold at $1,243.90 per ounce, and Brent crude rose to $65.07 a barrel after a temporary shutdown of a major North‑Sea pipeline.

Mechanical, packaging and orderable information for MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 devices is presented. Dimensions are in millimeters with tolerances per ASME Y14.5M and are subject to change without notice. The thermal pad must be soldered to the PCB; optional vias are application dependent and should be filled, plugged or tented. Laser cutting apertures with trapezoidal walls and rounded corners may improve paste release. Printed solder coverage values of 73%, 75% and 78% are noted for different package versions. Orderable part details include status, material type, RoHS compliance, lead finish options, moisture sensitivity level and part marking. Technical data, design resources and reliability information are provided as‑is with all faults disclaimed.

This paper investigates how time‑delayed feedback affects multi‑agent learning in normal‑form games. Standard optimistic Follow‑the‑Regularized‑Leader (OFTRL) achieves O(1) regret and Nash‑equilibrium convergence under full feedback, but even a one‑step delay degrades its performance to Ω(√T) regret and divergence (Theorems 6–7). The authors propose Weighted OFTRL (WOFTRL), which scales the optimistic term by a factor n∈ℕ. A Taylor‑expansion analysis shows that the delay m and weight n counteract each other; when n=m+1 the algorithm recovers O(1) regret (Corollary 11) and best‑iterate convergence to Nash equilibria in poly‑matrix zero‑sum games (Corollary 13). Empirical results on Matching Pennies, Sato’s game, and Rock‑Paper‑Scissors confirm a sharp phase transition: O(1) regret and convergence when n>m, and Ω(√T) regret or divergence when n≤m. The findings also extend to the Mirror Descent family of algorithms.

Molina Healthcare is a pure‑play government‑sponsored health insurer focusing on Medicaid and dual‑eligible populations, with strong contract wins and retention. It trades at a discount (8–9× earnings, ~0.2× EV/sales). Risks include policy changes, acquisitions, medical‑cost inflation and cash‑flow volatility, mitigated by state‑level dynamics and contract discipline. The author describes the firm as a structurally profitable compounder offering value for defensive investors, discloses a long position in MOH and provides personal disclosures. The passage also lists other article titles and includes chart data.

The speaker, a U.S. President, thanked Notre Dame for the welcome and an honorary degree, noting the record‑size graduating class. He praised Father Hesburgh’s long‑standing advocacy for human rights and the university’s Civil Rights Center, and honored Bishop Donal Lamont, Cardinal Paul Arns and Cardinal Stephen Kim for their courageous work for freedom in Rhodesia, Brazil and South Korea. The speech then set out five principles of a new American foreign policy: (1) reaffirming human rights as a fundamental U.S. commitment; (2) strengthening bonds among democratic nations; (3) engaging the Soviet Union to halt and reduce strategic nuclear arms and to promote reciprocal détente; (4) pursuing a comprehensive Middle East peace settlement based on UN resolutions; and (5) reducing the spread of nuclear weapons and limiting conventional arms sales. He emphasized that U.S. policy must be open, moral and grounded in democratic values, and that the United States will cooperate with newly influential countries in Latin America, Africa and Asia, work toward normalizing relations with the People’s Republic of China, and support a peaceful transition to majority rule in southern Africa. The president concluded that the policy aims to create a durable framework of international cooperation for the benefit of all mankind.

A study of more than 5,000 US women found that children of obese mothers were about 70 % more likely to fail fine‑motor skill tests by age 3, children of obese fathers were about 75 % more likely to fail social‑competence tests, and children of extremely obese couples were nearly three times more likely to fail problem‑solving tests. The mechanism linking parental obesity to developmental delays is unknown, but researchers suggest physicians consider parental weight when screening young children for delays.

VentureWire’s September 28 2000 issue reports major funding rounds: Warburg Pincus closed a $2.5 billion international private‑equity fund, Primus Venture Partners raised $200 million for Fund Five, Goldman Sachs launched a $250 million venture (GSVentures), Hyperchip secured $67 million in Series C, Gear.com’s president resigned and the company cut 22 jobs, and Sally Ride stepped down as president of Space.com. The newsletter also lists dozens of new money investments ranging from $1.5 million to $32.8 million across sectors including online auto, digital audio, IT job databases, web learning, e‑billing, staffing, mobile commerce, price‑optimization, wireless medical software, storage, broadband and insurance. Asia Online withdrew its IPO citing market conditions. M&A activity includes Zoho acquiring hotel liquidator NCL and Band‑X buying telecom‑stats publisher TeleGeography. New board and executive appointments were made at Logictier, Clickability, DataRise, LinuxOne, Intellego, AnywhereYouGo.com, TriStrata, GlobalNetXchange, LinkMe2, ViAir, Expanse Networks and zGraffiti. The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2× programmable‑shading, ray‑tracing and AI performance compared with the prior Turing generation. Key improvements include:

- **Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)**: each SM contains 128 CUDA cores (doubled FP32 throughput versus Turing), four third‑generation Tensor Cores and a second‑generation RT Core. The SM is partitioned into four processing blocks, both datapaths now support FP32, and the combined L1/shared‑memory capacity is 128 KB (33 % larger than Turing).

- **RT Core**: the second‑generation RT Core doubles ray‑triangle intersection testing, adds an Interpolate‑Triangle‑Position unit for hardware‑accelerated ray‑traced motion blur, and enables concurrent execution of RT and compute workloads.

- **Tensor Cores**: third‑generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, INT8/INT4 and fine‑grained structured sparsity, delivering up to 2× matrix‑multiply throughput and up to 2.7× peak FP16 tensor performance on the GeForce RTX 3080.

- **Memory subsystem**: GA10x uses GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth on the RTX 3090. The GPU integrates 12×32‑bit memory controllers, 6 MB of L2 cache, and an optional Error‑Detection‑and‑Replay (EDR) feature for memory‑overclocking.

- **Interconnect**: third‑generation NVLink provides 56.25 GB/s per direction (112.5 GB/s total) between two GPUs. PCIe Gen 4 offers a x16 slot bandwidth up to 64 GB/s.

- **Raster Operations (ROPs)**: ROPs are now part of the GPC, raising the total count to 112 (up from 96 in TU102), improving multisample anti‑aliasing and pixel fillrate.

- **Video and display**: the fifth‑generation NVDEC accelerates decoding of MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1; the seventh‑generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 8K HEVC. Display outputs support HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC for 8K60 or 4K120.

- **RTX IO**: offloads storage I/O and lossless decompression to the GPU, working with Microsoft DirectStorage to improve frame rates and reduce CPU utilization.

- **Data‑center GPUs**: the NVIDIA A40 delivers up to 2× FP32, 5× AI training (10× with sparsity), 48 GB GDDR6, and scales to 96 GB via third‑gen NVLink; it supports virtualization and Quadro Sync. The RTX A6000 (GA102) provides 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑gen RT cores, 336 third‑gen Tensor cores, 48 GB GDDR6, and hardware‑accelerated motion blur.

These features collectively constitute the generational leap of the GA10x Ampere architecture for gaming, professional visualization, AI and data‑center workloads.

The whitepaper from Microsoft Research Asia introduces "Societal AI" - a research framework aimed at ensuring AI integration into human society is harmonious, synergistic, and resilient. It outlines ten key research questions addressing fairness, safety, human-AI collaboration, evaluation, interpretability, value alignment, impact on cognition and work, social science research transformation, and regulatory frameworks. Motivated by the emergence of advanced LLMs like ChatGPT and GPT-4 in late 2022, the framework emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration between computer scientists and social scientists. The Societal AI team at Microsoft Research Asia has organized workshops, conducted joint research with global collaborators, and developed projects including DyVal for dynamic evaluation, CulturePark for cross-cultural understanding, and Concept Activation Vector methods for interpretability. Many people equate buying stocks with investing, but Benjamin Graham’s definition requires that a security purchase protect the investor’s capital and provide an adequate return; otherwise it is speculation. The author notes that his early purchase of Ask Jeeves was not an investment because he ignored the safety of his principal and lacked a margin of safety. Graham’s approach stresses buying securities only when they trade at a large discount to intrinsic value (the larger the discount, the greater the buffer against business decline) and choosing financially solid firms—those with low debt, strong liquidity, and improving balance‑sheet ratios. This “value‑investing” focus on downside protection allows the upside to follow as the price‑value gap closes, especially for out‑of‑favor companies and net‑net stocks. Whether one is an investor or a gambler depends on the process used to select securities, not the assets themselves.

The Stack Zone Offense is an overload‑based, simple‑to‑teach system that forces match‑up problems for any zone defense. It assigns specific roles to each player (point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, post) so each can concentrate on a limited set of responsibilities. The offense consists of four phases: basic overload reads, pass‑and‑cut action, high‑post roll, and ball reversal, each with built‑in reads and counters. It offers multiple entry options—basic, flop, exchange, triple‑stack, and dribble—plus a “Crunch Time” set of specials (Vegas = double‑away double screen, Back = weakside lob, Cat = 2‑1‑2 alignment for double‑team situations). The system was introduced by Mike Frink and expanded by Tom Newell’s triple‑stack alignment.

Offensive set pieces off free kicks in soccer restart play after a foul and offer a planned opportunity to score. The Laws of the Game (Law 13) require the ball to be stationary, defending players to stay at least 10 yards away, the kicker to touch the ball only once, and the ball to visibly move after contact. A direct free kick may score directly; an indirect free kick must touch at least one other player before a goal counts. Design of a set piece depends on proximity to the goal, whether the kick is direct or indirect, and the players’ skill level. Five common near‑goal starting locations (outside left/right, near left/right, near center) and three farther locations (far left/right, far center) are identified, each typically matched with a two‑ to five‑man defender wall. Common design elements include direct shots around or through the wall, simple touches, crosses, step‑over fake runs, misdirection runs, screening or “committee” groupings, single or double lateral passes, chip passes over the wall, decoy movements, “ghosting” toward goal, crashing into the penalty area, and anticipating rebounds. Players must be capable, know their responsibilities, understand if a kick is direct or indirect, and a designated dead‑ball specialist may be used for bending shots. Free kicks may be taken ceremonially (with a delay) or quickly to exploit defensive lapses; the quick free kick can be taken without waiting for the wall if the referee signals ready. In rare indirect awards near the goal line, defenders must stand on the line until the ball is touched. Practice should progress from no defenders to live defenders, enforce rules, and encourage player input. Coaches are advised to scout opponents, prepare contingencies for missing key players, keep designs simple, and study successful plays.

This document describes the AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture (AGESA) interface for host environment wrapper implementers. It defines procedure call interfaces, recommended wrapper implementations, and build options for BIOS and kernel developers. The software uses a three-level version numbering scheme (X.Y.Z) where X indicates major version, Y minor version, and Z code updates. Call mechanics utilize initializer functions that pre-fill structures with default parameters, allowing host environments to modify required or optional settings. The interface provides two build methods: binary modules for isolated compilation or source integration for direct host environment building. Error reporting occurs through return codes ranging from SUCCESS to FATAL, plus an event log system retaining the 16 most recent entries. The boot sequence progresses through system reset, ROM integrity verification, optional recovery mode, main boot initialization, optional suspend restoration, and OS boot stages. UEFI implementations span SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP phases in both 32-bit and 64-bit modes, organized into processor initialization, memory initialization, and late initialization entry points. Configuration is customized through platform-specific <Plat>Options.c files containing build options and default table entries. Binary image headers contain signatures, creator IDs, entry point offsets, relocation tables, and checksums for image validation.

The case involved a land‑sale dispute. Moore owned a tract; he orally agreed to sell it to Thompson via an agent, then orally agreed to sell it to Hunter. Moore later gave Thompson a title bond (Dec 1, 1856) and, despite notice of that bond, deeded the land to Hunter (Dec 12, 1856). Thompson tendered the purchase money and interest, demanded a deed, and was refused. The trial court ordered specific performance for Bales (Thompson’s assignee). The appellate court affirmed, applying the equity rule that a valid land‑sale contract makes the vendee the owner and the vendor a trustee holding a lien for the price, and that the contract must be enforceable by specific performance. It also held that a plaintiff seeking specific performance need only offer to bring money into court upon decree, and that a tender of purchase money and interest bars further interest unless the vendor proves the money was used. Judgment affirmed.

This study compared a commercial PCR assay with a hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow for detecting respiratory pathogens in nasopharyngeal samples from 29 patients with suspected acute upper respiratory infections. The PCR panel detected 15 microorganisms (4 bacteria, 11 viruses), while mNGS identified 44 microorganisms (27 bacteria, 2 fungi, 15 viruses). The methods showed high concordance (98.33% positive percent agreement and 100% negative percent agreement) for the 33 shared targets. However, mNGS detected 29 additional microorganisms not included in the PCR panel, including SARS-CoV-2, Coxsackievirus A, and Human rhinovirus C. Microorganisms were phenotypically classified into three groups based on pathogenic potential: group 1 (normal flora, colonizers, or contaminants), group 2 (frequently associated with respiratory disease), and group 3 (pathogenic). The findings suggest that hybridization capture-based mNGS offers advantages for broader pathogen detection and phenotypic characterization compared to traditional PCR, potentially aiding clinical decision-making for respiratory co-infections and trafficking assessment to the lower respiratory tract.

Information management is critical for industrial competitiveness; insufficient management costs about 1.5 % of sales in asset‑intensive sectors. Manual communication, incomplete standards, and lack of a scalable digital medium force enterprises to use error‑prone methods such as spreadsheets. This paper identifies the need for an architecture that enables digitally structured exchange of technical information in industrial business networks and scales to many partners with heterogeneous back‑end systems.

The proposed architecture relies on an open consortium that defines common business practices and information formats. Information mediators act as multi‑sided platforms that route messages and coordinate collaborative processes between consortium members. Each business party connects to a mediator via an adapter that maps its proprietary back‑end systems to the agreed format. The design includes a commonly agreed API, routing logic, business‑process coordination, and optional matchmaking services.

The work focuses on the lifecycle domain, especially technical information for process‑industry plants. It examines existing standards (e.g., IEC 61987, IEC 62541, ISO 15926, CFIHOS) and notes that they do not provide a concrete exchange medium.

A prototype was built on a web‑application platform implementing the mediator role. It uses configurable import/export applications that read and write spreadsheets through XML‑based mappings, analogous to adapters. Each party has a storage silo (data lobby) and tasks representing collaborative processes. Business‑taxonomy and integration libraries were developed in .NET to promote interoperability and reuse.

Experiments involved two equipment suppliers and two plant operators exchanging valve and pump data for maintenance and renewal projects. Equipment information (product data, individual device data, and attachments) was imported from back‑end systems, delivered to the plant operator site, and in some cases exported to the recipient’s back‑end, without manual mapping during execution.

The prototype demonstrated that digital, structured exchange reduces manual effort and errors and can scale to larger networks. Limitations include the absence of an open consortium, only a single mediator, and limited coverage of engineering‑design information and business‑process workflows. Future work includes establishing the consortium, extending the prototype to a mediator network, supporting additional information types, and expanding to financing, logistics, manufacturing, and marine industry.

The case concerned a challenge to a supplementary sewer assessment in Buffalo. The city initially assessed $1,058.63 for sewer construction and contracted with Randolph to complete the work. When unexpected quicksand was encountered, increasing costs beyond the contract price, Randolph stopped work. The common council authorized an additional $588.13 payment and ordered a second assessment on benefited properties. Property owners challenged this assessment as illegal. The court held that under the city charter, which permits further assessments when initial amounts prove insufficient, the supplementary assessment was authorized. The order granting a new trial was affirmed.

This research examines how peer mentoring helps PETE students develop 21st-century skills in a movement education course. Conducted as a case study with 3 peer mentors and 25 first-year students at a Turkish university, the study used storytelling and gamification over 14 weeks. Three themes emerged: peer learners excluded non-contributing members while peer mentors divided responsibilities to keep everyone engaged; both groups created storytelling content, enhancing accountability and awareness of teaching roles; and narrative structure connected learning to daily life, making knowledge more permanent. Peer mentors provided feedback inside and outside class, while social media platforms supported the learning ecosystem. The study found that peer mentoring offers real teaching experience during undergraduate education and serves as a bridge between students and faculty. Storytelling proved effective for permanent learning and linking content to daily experiences. Researchers recommend integrating peer mentoring and storytelling into undergraduate programs across all grade levels to prepare teacher candidates for professional practice.

The Korean diet is rooted in traditional Korean foods and emphasizes whole, unprocessed ingredients such as vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, fermented products (e.g., kimchi, doenjang, gochujang) and small portions of broth‑based dishes. It limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats and dairy. The diet is low in calories and saturated fat, high in fibre, provides probiotics and antioxidants, and can aid weight loss, but its reliance on fermented condiments can increase sodium intake (a concern for hypertension) and its avoidance of dairy results in lower calcium. Carbohydrate‑rich foods such as rice require portion control, especially for blood‑sugar management, and spicy ingredients may irritate some digestive systems. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low‑carb or gluten‑free needs by substituting protein sources, reducing rice portions and using gluten‑free soy sauce or rice noodles. Regular physical activity is also part of the overall approach.

The SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification describes communication between AMD SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. The protocol uses MSR 0xc001_0130 for guest-hypervisor communication, with the GHCB address required to be 4K-aligned and the lower 12 bits encoding protocol information. Hypervisor features are advertised via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap. Key NAE (Non-Automatic Exit) events include CPUID requests, MSR operations, IO protection faults, VMMCALL hypercalls, page state changes, and SNP guest requests. Page state change operations support making pages private or shared, and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints for 2MB/4K conversions. For SEV-SNP, GPA registration is required and the protocol supports guest requests to firmware with optional certificate data returns. AP booting uses either AP reset hold or SNP AP creation mechanisms. The #HV restricted injection feature uses a doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for interrupt delivery. Secure AVIC supports guest-owned APIC backing pages. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this specification.

Pumpkin is a fruit in the Cucurbitaceae family that is highly nutritious, providing fibre, iron, vitamin B3, alpha‑ and beta‑carotene, vitamin E, lutein + zeaxanthin and potassium. One cup of cooked pumpkin (baked, boiled or roasted) contains about 52 kcal, 3 g fibre, 13 g carbohydrate, 1.48 mg iron, 595 mg potassium, 5.4 mg beta‑carotene, 7 mg alpha‑carotene, 2.5 mg lutein + zeaxanthin and 2 mg vitamin E, with potassium exceeding that of a large banana. Carotenoids give pumpkin its orange colour and have anti‑cancer and anti‑inflammatory properties; they may help reduce the risk of several cancers and age‑related macular degeneration, support eye health, and contribute to cardiovascular health by aiding blood‑pressure regulation. Regular consumption of pumpkin may also support immune function, brain health and cognitive function. The author, Doug Cook RD, MPH, is a registered dietitian and functional nutritionist.

A systematic review of 270 studies on the social science of large language models (LLMs) identified three stable, interpretable research themes via unsupervised clustering: LLM as Social Minds (mind-like capacities, moral/social reasoning, self-regulation, and strategic/deceptive behavior), LLM Societies (multi-agent interactions, emergent social structures, cooperation, collective epistemics, and institutional design), and LLM–Human Interactions (trust, perception, affect, collaboration, learning, productivity, and interactional risks). A tripartite taxonomy emerged from sentence-BERT embeddings, K-means clustering, and LDA topic modeling, aligning closely with expert classifications (Macro-F1 = 0.954, NMI = 0.811, ARI = 0.867). The PRISMA-compliant review spanned computer science, psychology, sociology, HCI, economics, and interdisciplinary venues, with most studies from 2023–2025. The taxonomy offers a cumulative map for integrating fragmented work, guides evidentiary standards across levels, and suggests future directions including anti-shortcut stress tests for mind-level claims, pre-registered institutional counterfactuals for society-level studies, and transparency/verification affordances for human–LLM interaction research. Limitations include English-language-only coverage and a September 2025 cutoff.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide describes optional extensions to AMD’s SEV and SNP that enable a hardware engine, TMPM, to perform page migration between memory tiers while keeping guest physical addresses unchanged. The engine requires IOMMU enablement and is verified via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register. TMPM solves two key challenges: pausing DMA traffic during page copies and acting as a trusted agent for SNP‑protected guest pages. Commands such as PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (for concurrent DMA), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (for SNP guests), and PM_NOOP support moving groups of pages; a single command can move up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with no order‑dependence and per‑page status reporting (PM_SUCCESS, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS, etc.). A Pre‑Migration RMP state facilitates SNP page migration. Performance is highest with ≥16 pages per command, optimal at 128 pages, and the ring buffer should be kept ahead of the engine, with interrupts requested only at the end of a command sequence. IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU private address spaces, ring buffers, and argument pages cannot be migrated. All system physical addresses must be 4 kB aligned. TMPM firmware can be reloaded after pausing operations and tearing down the ring buffer; reload requires the same or higher firmware version and checks ENGINE_READY; Family 19h reports a FW_VER_Major value of 71.

A collaboration between University College London’s Institute of Education and the LGBTQ+ charity Diversity Role Models delivered a year‑long knowledge‑exchange project (Oct 2023–June 2024) to equip citizenship student teachers with trans‑inclusive practices. Workshops introduced the “actualise” method (making topics concrete) and storytelling to build empathy. Student teachers used the Equality Act 2010, Human Rights Act 1998 and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child as rights‑based frames for teaching LGBTQ+ identities, but most actualisations focused on sexual orientation and lacked confidence in discussing gender identity. Increased media hostility and two DfE draft guidance documents (December 2023 gender‑questioning children; May 2024 RSHE ban on gender‑identity teaching) were identified as barriers that could force outing and limit lawful instruction. Despite these challenges, participants found that rights‑based citizenship education, paired with personal counter‑stories and whole‑school strategies (visibility, restorative behaviour policies, anti‑bullying rules, Pride clubs, upstander training), can create safe, rights‑respecting environments for trans youth. International frameworks such as the Yogyakarta Principles+10 and UNESCO guidance support curriculum inclusion and teacher training. The project highlighted the need for specialist teachers, civil‑society partnerships and ongoing professional development to embed trans inclusion across schools.

Charles Jones sued Orin S. Bacon, executor of James McKechnie’s estate, claiming McKechnie promised to indemnify Jones for endorsing notes of Jones’s son‑in‑law Sherman Kingsbury. Jones endorsed a $15,000 note in 1885 and later a $20,000 note in 1888, and gave mortgages as collateral, but Kingsbury defaulted and McKechnie failed to pay. The only surviving witness to the alleged agreements besides Jones was Kingsbury. Over the defendant’s objection, the trial court admitted evidence that McKechnie and Kingsbury were speculating in hops and that McKechnie refused a 40‑cent‑per‑pound offer for the hops that would have cleared Kingsbury’s debts. The Supreme Court, General Term, Fifth Department, held this evidence was irrelevant to the indemnity claim and served only to arouse jury sympathy and prejudice, constituting reversible error. The judgment for $16,369.69 and the order denying a new trial were reversed, and a new trial was ordered, with costs to abide the event.

FIRE (Financial Independent Retire Early) describes individuals who aim to live on capital withdrawals after leaving work. The article stresses that retirees and FIRE participants are fragile because any negative surprise can devastate their lifestyle, especially if they have long horizons (40+ years). Key risks are sequence‑of‑returns risk, withdrawal‑rate decisions, and insufficient diversification.

A 2000 example illustrates the danger: a couple with a $1 million portfolio withdrew $50 000 (5 % of initial capital) annually, invested passively in U.S. large‑cap stocks, and ended up broke by 2017 despite later bull markets. Their failures stemmed from a high withdrawal rate, poor diversification, and an unlucky early sequence of returns that eroded compounding.

Sequence risk means the order in which annual returns occur affects long‑term outcomes; a few early losses can permanently impair compounding. Monte Carlo simulations of the S&P 500’s 120 yearly returns (1901‑2020) show a median growth near 9.5 % but a 10 % chance of a CAGR below ~3 % and a 10 % chance above ~16.5 %.

William Bengen’s 4 % rule (1994) found that withdrawing 4 % yearly historically allowed retirees to avoid depletion. Norway’s sovereign wealth fund now uses a 3 % rate to accommodate lower expected returns. However, FIRE participants need even more conservative rates because longer timeframes increase exposure to black‑swans and unfavorable return sequences.

Diversification can offset higher withdrawal rates; a mix of assets (e.g., U.S. large caps, REITs, emerging markets, gold, long‑term Treasuries) improves sustainability. Still, correlations shift, so past performance does not guarantee future results.

To reduce sequence risk, the article recommends living modestly, spending less than desired, and maintaining a large margin of safety. Edward Thorp’s analysis suggests a 2 % inflation‑adjusted withdrawal limit for “forever” payouts to avoid early‑stage market declines wiping out a portfolio.

Overall, the likelihood of going broke as a retiree or FIRE depends on planning, conservative withdrawal rates, diversification, and the margin of safety built into the strategy.

The study examined the relationship between the self‑report PTSD Checklist (PCL‑5) and the clinician‑administered PTSD Scale (CAPS‑5) in 100 adults (56 men, 44 women). Participants were either veterans or civilians who had experienced military or civilian trauma; they completed PCL‑5 followed by CAPS‑5. Overall severity scores on CAPS‑5 did not differ by sex or trauma type. Correlation between PCL‑5 and CAPS‑5 was strong overall (Rho = 0.815), but females showed a markedly stronger correlation (Rho = 0.907) than males (Rho = 0.655). Odds ratios for PCL‑5 predicting CAPS‑5 were higher for women (144.6) than men (11.8). Males deviated significantly from the ideal regression line (mean difference ≈ 12.5, p = 0.001), whereas females did not (mean difference ≈ 1.07, p = 0.51). Using PCL‑5 alone misclassified 26.8 % of men (13 false positives, 2 false negatives) versus 11.4 % of women (4 false positives, 1 false negative). Civilian trauma participants had a stronger PCL‑5/CAPS‑5 correlation (Rho = 0.885) than military trauma participants (Rho = 0.523); this pattern held within each sex. Authors note that symptom severity was similar across groups, suggesting that the weaker correlation in men stems from reporting or interpretation differences rather than actual severity differences. Limitations include the modest sample size and regional focus. The findings indicate that sex and trauma type should be considered when interpreting PCL‑5 results, and that clinicians should use caution when relying solely on PCL‑5 for PTSD diagnosis, especially in male and military populations. Further research is needed to determine the causes of these discrepancies.

Channel 4’s documentary The Super Orgasm follows five women who claim to experience up to 100 orgasms in a single encounter. The women include an engineering student who reported over 60 orgasms and a mother who says she has only had such experiences with her husband. Researchers conducted three experiments: an arousal booth measuring pupil dilation and genital blood flow (Gerulf Rieger), a brain‑wave study monitoring alpha activity during porn viewing (Nicole Prause), and a functional MRI test tracking cerebral blood flow (Barry Komisaruk and Nan Wise). Results indicated the women were easily aroused, that alpha waves remained elevated during multiple orgasms, and that multi‑orgasmic women showed increased blood flow in over 30 brain regions, unlike women with a single orgasm. Experts critique the documentary as lacking scientific rigor – small sample, no control group, and no clear distinction between “super” and multiple orgasms. They note that most women are unlikely to achieve such high numbers and caution that the suggestion all women could is misleading.

During the lecture the professor continued the discussion of continuity by restating the epsilon–delta definition. He presented a three‑part theorem that relates continuity to limits of functions and to convergence of sequences.

1. If c is not a cluster point of the domain S, any function f:S→R is continuous at c.

2. If c is a cluster point of S, f is continuous at c iff lim_{x→c}f(x)=f(c).

3. f is continuous at c iff for every sequence (x_n)⊂S with x_n→c we have f(x_n)→f(c).

The proof of part 1 uses the definition of cluster point to show that the only point of S near c is c itself. Part 2 follows directly from the definition of limit. Part 3 is proved in two directions: the forward direction applies the epsilon–delta definition, the reverse direction uses a contradiction argument that builds a sequence x_n with |x_n−c|<1/n and |f(x_n)−f(c)|≥ε₀.

The theorem is then applied to show that sine is continuous everywhere: by the identity
sin x−sin c=2 sin((x−c)/2) cos((x+c)/2) and the bound |sin t|≤|t| one chooses δ=ε.
Cosine continuity is obtained from sin using cos x=sin(x+π/2) and the sequential characterization.

An example of a function discontinuous at every point is f(x)=1 for irrational x and f(x)=0 for rational x. Using the density of rationals and irrationals, for any c one can construct a sequence (x_n)→c with f(x_n) not converging to f(c), violating the sequential characterization.

Algebraic operations preserve continuity: if f and g are continuous at c then so are f+g, f·g, and f/g (provided g≠0). Continuity is also preserved under composition: if g is continuous at c and f is continuous at g(c) then f∘g is continuous at c. Consequently, x^n for any n∈ℕ and all polynomials are continuous, and the function 1/(3+sin⁴x) is continuous.

The lecture ends with a preview of the next topics: the extreme‑value theorem (min/max theorems) and the intermediate‑value theorem for continuous functions on intervals.
