The lecture covers Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), a methodology for quantifying environmental impacts of products. LCA consists of four stages: goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation. The methodology was developed by Coca-Cola in 1969, gained attention in the 1970s, and became standardized in the 1990s after "hired gun studies" made false environmental claims, leading to ISO 14040 standards. Two types of LCA exist: attributional (static snapshot) and consequential (change-oriented). Key concepts include functional units, system boundaries, cut-off rules, allocation problems, and sensitivity analysis. The hand dryer study (comparing Dyson Airblade, Xlerator, and paper towels) is used as an example, illustrating challenges such as data access limitations, assumptions about drying time, electricity use, and the need for third-party verification for comparative claims.

A new report from the Children's Rights Alliance, conducted by Dublin City University researchers, examines how homelessness affects children's education in the greater Dublin area. The study found parents must choose between buying food or paying travel costs so children can attend school in their original community. Children reportedly go to school hungry, in dirty clothes, and sometimes fall asleep in class after rising at 5:30am. The report recommends free school travel, funding for school meals and psychological assessments, and limiting families' time in emergency accommodation to six months.

This cross‑sectional baseline survey combined with a randomized controlled open‑label trial examined malaria, malnutrition and the effect of intermittent preventive therapy (IPTsc) on nutritional status in school‑age children (5–15 years) in Muheza District, Tanzania. 1,566 children were recruited, randomised to dihydroartemisinin‑piperaquine (DP), artesunate‑amodiaquine (ASAQ) or standard‑care control, and followed for 20 months. At baseline, malaria prevalence was 27 %; 23 % of 5‑10‑year‑olds were underweight, 21 % of all participants were stunted and 28 % were thin. Logistic regression showed that children with malaria had 78 % higher odds of stunting (adjusted OR = 1.78) and those from low socioeconomic households had 50 % higher odds of being underweight (adjusted OR = 1.50). Linear mixed‑model analysis found no significant differences in mean weight, height or BMI over time between the DP, ASAQ and control groups. The study concludes that malaria and malnutrition coexist as a substantial double burden and that IPTsc alone does not improve growth; integrated community‑based nutritional programmes alongside malaria control are recommended.

NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture combines dedicated hardware for ray tracing (RT Cores), AI (Tensor Cores), and traditional rendering (CUDA cores) to enable real-time hybrid rendering. It supports Variable Rate Shading (VRS), Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) for performance optimization and VR applications. Turing GPUs (TU102, TU104, TU106) offer significant performance gains over Pascal, particularly in ray tracing and AI tasks, with features like GDDR6 memory, larger caches, and enhanced video encoding. The architecture is used in data centers (Tesla T4), gaming (GeForce RTX), and professional visualization (Quadro RTX), and includes AI-based image enhancement technologies such as DLSS, InPainting, and AI Super Rez. Turing enables real-time ray tracing with denoising and hybrid rendering, improving shadow, reflection, and ambient occlusion realism.

This study compared humoral and cellular immune responses elicited by Covishield (adenovirus vectored vaccine) and Covaxin (inactivated vaccine) in 691 Indian adults (18–45 years) across four sites between June 2021 and January 2022. Participants were stratified by baseline serostatus (seronegative or seropositive based on anti-spike antibodies).

In seronegative individuals, Covishield induced higher seroconversion rates (93.2% after dose 1, 98.3% after dose 2) compared to Covaxin (36.6% and 74.4% respectively). In seropositive individuals, Covishield again showed higher seroconversion (95.2% and 91.7%) versus Covaxin (51.8% and 66.9%), with 37.4% of seropositive Covaxin recipients showing no response. Higher pre-vaccination antibody titers were associated with non-responsiveness in both groups.

Covishield produced significantly higher geometric mean titers (GMT) of anti-spike antibodies than Covaxin in both seronegative and seropositive groups at all timepoints. Neutralizing antibody assays showed significant increases for Covishield but not for Covaxin. In the earliest cohort, Covishield elicited higher frequencies of both spike-specific CD4 and CD8 T cells, while Covaxin primarily elicited CD4 responses.

The Omicron wave complicated durability assessments. Cohorts vaccinated during the Omicron wave showed comparable antibody titers between vaccines, likely due to asymptomatic infection boosting responses. Neither vaccine induced strong Omicron-specific antibodies; however, prior exposure (seropositive status) and exposure to the Delta variant improved Omicron-specific responses.

Overall, Covishield elicited stronger and broader humoral and cellular immune responses against SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to Covaxin, with serostatus and timing of vaccination relative to variant waves influencing outcomes.

The player, in his first Stanley Cup finals, says he was overexcited and must stay calm to play his regular game. The Yankee concept is a pro‑style shot play that uses a post‑dig combination from opposite sides of the formation to stress safeties and linebackers. It is usually run from heavier personnel to force 1‑high safety looks, creating a natural high‑low on the free safety. The concept works well against Cover 1 and Cover 3 but is less effective against Cover 2 and Cover 4. QB progression is post → dig → crosser → check‑down, with three underneath options available. Variations include a 2×2 set with shallow crossers and a version adding whip routes to pull linebacker coverage.

A worst‑case climate scenario called a “pulse” could cause Antarctic and Greenland glaciers that back ice sheets to collapse, pouring massive ice into oceans and producing extremely rapid global sea‑level rise. Current projections for Miami predict up to 7–8 ft of rise by 2100, but a pulse could bring 10–30 ft and more superstorms. A recent study in Science Advances found that in the Amundsen Sea (West Antarctica) and Sabrina Coast (East Antarctica) warm water is pooling beneath ice, counteracting the normal cooling that creates Antarctic bottom water. The warm‑water feedback accelerates glacier melt and may have contributed to a 16‑ft sea‑level rise at the end of the last glacial period. Loss of Antarctic bottom water would slow ocean currents, increasing storm intensity, while rising temperatures from fossil‑fuel burning make ice‑shelf collapse and a pulse more likely.

Traditional apprenticeship programs in construction are highly selective, favoring applicants with prior knowledge and excluding many motivated learners. Pre‑apprenticeships address this by offering short‑term exposure to multiple careers, building technical and professional skills, providing mentorship and industry‑recognized credentials, and preparing participants for entry assessments. However, these programs lack stable funding and are not required to track outcomes, limiting their capacity and ability to attract investment. Suggested solutions include income‑contingent financing for wrap‑around support such as transportation, childcare and lost wages, with repayment tied to earnings increases; employers and unions could co‑invest or repay such loans, creating a pipeline of diverse talent. Expanding data collection to demonstrate program success is also recommended. Realizing these goals requires coordinated investment from employers, unions, government and philanthropy to broaden access to construction pathways, fill in‑demand jobs and promote economic mobility.

An AI tool called Waldo successfully scanned 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing harmful side effects. Researchers verified that 86% of a sample of 250 flagged posts actually represented problematic experiences. The tool outperformed ChatGPT, producing 18 times fewer false positives. According to researchers, Waldo demonstrates that social media can provide valuable public health information that government agencies like the CDC typically don't monitor, potentially helping protect consumers from harmful products. The tool was developed by researchers including Richard Lomotey from Penn State, John Ayers from UC San Diego, and Karan Desai from the University of Michigan. It was published in PLOS Digital Health on September 30, 2025.

The paper presents Robodoc, a prototype medical chatbot that integrates multiple AI models using OpenAI's large language models (LLMs). The author used Google's Teachable Machine for transfer learning to build image-based models for detecting pneumonia from X-rays and retinal conditions (Drusen, CNV, DME) from OCT images. A diabetes detection model was created using TensorFlow.js. The system operates through text messages or image uploads, with OpenAI's function calling feature enabling intelligent model selection. Built using Angular (TypeScript), the chatbot decouples the machine learning models from the interface, allowing independent updates. Results demonstrate good integration with minor deviations in classification and urgent case handling. The author argues this approach addresses bioinformatics' integration challenges, enabling researchers to package models into accessible chatbots without complex infrastructure. Limitations include unpredictable LLM outputs and risks of misdiagnosis, requiring human oversight. The work represents an alternative to classical UI/UX, suggesting chatbots may become primary interfaces for medical AI models. The future of AI lies in public APIs enabling complex, low-cost applications accessible to researchers without extensive computational resources.

Most surveyed enterprises (87%) favor external HPC infrastructures, while 74% operate or plan own HPC in colocation datacenters. 43% use or plan to use innovation partners, and only 6% currently have on‑premises HPC, with 28% planning such use within two years.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture adds Tensor Cores with FP16, INT8 and INT4 precision for AI inference, enabling NGX features such as Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Super Rez and AI Slow‑Mo. Turing also introduces a dedicated RT Core per SM for real‑time ray‑tracing; combined with hybrid rendering (rasterization + ray tracing), BVH traversal, and denoising, it produces physically correct reflections, shadows and ambient occlusion. The memory subsystem uses GDDR6 at 14 Gbps, larger L2 caches (6 MB on TU102) and lossless compression, delivering roughly 50 % higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. The display engine supports 8 K @ 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, HDR tone‑mapping, and enhanced NVENC/NVDEC video encode/decode. New shading techniques include mesh shading for object‑level parallelism, variable‑rate shading (VRS) for adaptive quality, texture‑space shading (TSS) for decoupled visibility/appearance sampling, and multi‑view rendering (MVR) for VR. Turing GPUs include NVLink for high‑speed GPU interconnects and VirtualLink for single‑cable VR headsets. The TU102, TU104 and TU106 chips contain 13.6 – 10.8 billion transistors, up to 576 Tensor Cores and 48 RT Cores, delivering up to 40× inference performance and >50× energy efficiency versus CPU‑based solutions. The RTX‑OPS metric combines FP32, Tensor, RT and INT32 operations to represent hybrid rendering workloads.

Swing trading holds positions from one day to a few weeks, longer than day trading but shorter than position trading. The recommended time frame for swing‑trading indicators is 1–15 days; longer horizons increase drawdowns.

Risk‑adjusted return is defined as the geometric annual return divided by market‑exposure (time in the market). The ratio of risk‑adjusted return to maximum drawdown (RAR/MDD) above 2 is considered good.

The article backtests six popular indicators on SPY using Amibroker, ranking results by profit factor and trade count. The indicators are: Relative Strength Index (RSI), Internal Bar Strength (IBS), Stochastic (%K), Bollinger Bands, WilliamsVixFix and Williams %R.

- RSI: a 2‑day look‑back with entry below 10 and exit above 60 performed poorly after 2015 with large drawdowns.
- IBS: a 2‑day moving average of IBS with entry below 0.3 and exit above 0.8 produced a steady equity curve despite a 2008‑2009 drawdown.
- Stochastic %K: look‑back ≤5 days and entry at 10, exit at 70 showed strong performance but may be curve‑fitted.
- Bollinger Bands: mean‑reversion entries on lower‑band break and upper‑band exit; optimal look‑back 6–10 days; an 8‑day, 1‑sd entry and 1.8‑sd exit gave good returns but high drawdowns.
- WilliamsVixFix: a 10‑day look‑back yielded ≈8.5 % CAGR with ≈50 % exposure but frequent large drawdowns.
- Williams %R: a mean‑reversion oscillator that works best with a longer look‑back (≈10 days), entry at –90, exit at –80, holding about three days; equity curve shows low drawdowns, only two negative years since 1993, and the lowest average max drawdown among the tested indicators.

Based on the backtests, Williams %R is ranked as the best swing‑trading indicator because it provides the most stable and solid results across variables and the lowest average maximum drawdown, leading to superior risk‑adjusted returns. The three top indicators (Williams %R, IBS, and Stochastic) are considered roughly equal, with risk‑adjusted performance serving as the primary ranking criterion.

The present invention relates to a video signal encoding/decoding method and apparatus that aim to improve intra‑prediction and inter‑prediction efficiency, reduce overhead, and increase motion‑vector precision. In the decoding method, it is first determined whether the current block is merged with a neighboring block; motion information and a weight prediction parameter are obtained (inherited from the neighbor if merged, otherwise decoded from the bitstream). A reference block is selected based on the motion information, and a prediction block is generated by applying the weight prediction parameter. The precision of a motion vector may be increased using reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block. For intra‑prediction, the decoder reconstructs the intra‑prediction mode, performs prediction, decides whether to correct the prediction sample using neighboring reconstructed pixel areas, and derives correction coefficients by regression analysis using a similar previously decoded block. The encoder performs corresponding decisions and encodes flags indicating block merging, weight‑prediction control, correction use, intra‑prediction mode candidates, and difference values for parameters. The invention also supports dividing a current block into sub‑blocks, deriving weight‑prediction parameter sets from upper and left reconstructed pixel areas, and encoding index or offset information to select the best weight prediction parameter.

Organized patriotism, replacing local pride with national loyalty, is essential for a nation’s growth. Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers operate in primary-secondary mode via the SYNC pin, where the primary uses the RT pin to set the switching frequency and outputs a clock signal at twice that frequency on SYNC, while the secondary uses that SYNC signal as its clock input with its RT pin left floating. This mode enables synchronizing two independent converters (requiring no other connections) or designing a single interleaved converter with parallel phases (requiring additional connections for VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC). The secondary inverts the clock signal, creating a phase shift of 90° or 270° between corresponding outputs.

Python is a popular language for finance used to backtest trading strategies. This article demonstrates how to backtest a MACD (Moving Average Convergence/Divergence) strategy by downloading Apple historical data from Yahoo Finance, calculating the MACD (12‑period EMA minus 26‑period EMA) and its signal line (9‑period EMA of MACD), generating regime entries based on a positive histogram, and computing returns. The strategy achieved a 15.04% CAGR versus 19.07% for buy‑and‑hold, while being invested only 51.13% of the time. Results are for informational purposes and can be adapted to other indicators.

The paper introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic module that transforms camera-centered 3D skeletons into a canonical body-centered frame to address viewpoint-dependent variability in monocular pose estimation. The architecture uses parallel GCN and Transformer branches fused via cross-attention and adaptive gating to predict a global 6D rotation converted to an SO(3) rotation matrix plus an optional residual correction. Trained with synthetic rotations and a composite loss function (reconstruction, geodesic rotation, cycle consistency, perceptual, and regularization terms), it achieves approximately 27% MPJPE reduction and 5-6× improvement in rotation error on the MM-Fi dataset (S2/S3 protocols). On TotalCapture, canonicalized poses produce wrist acceleration signals that more closely match IMU ground truth than geometric baselines, enabling more reliable kinematic analysis for rehabilitation, sports science, and VR training applications.

The IRS reports progress on tax‑related ID fraud but warns consumers to watch for scams. Under the new federal tax law, payroll withholding tables were updated in February, and about 90 % of workers should see some extra cash in their paychecks. The extra amount varies by income, filing status, number of children and the number of withholding allowances claimed on the W‑4. For example, a married couple earning $90,000 with two children under 17 could receive roughly $61 more per semi‑monthly paycheck ($1,468.70 more for the year) and a larger tax refund ($2,008.94 vs. $780.64). A single worker earning $35,000 with no children could see about $32 more per paycheck ($763 more for the year). The child tax credit doubled to $2,000 per qualifying child, allowing more higher‑income families to claim the full credit. Employers must use the new tables by Feb 15, and a revised W‑4 form is expected in early spring. Taxpayers may need to adjust withholding using the IRS calculator, especially since the standard deduction rose to $24,000 for married couples and $12,000 for singles, a $10,000 cap now applies to state and local tax deductions, and home‑equity‑loan interest is no longer deductible. Bonus checks are now withheld at 22 % instead of 25 %, reducing withholding on, for example, a $5,000 bonus from $1,250 to $1,100.

Christian Brothers defensive lineman Bill Norton, a 6‑foot‑6, 270‑pound four‑star prospect ranked 11th nationally as a strong‑side defensive end, committed to Georgia, choosing the Bulldogs over several major programs after a visit to Tennessee.

The passage presents a bibliometric analysis of wartime and online education research in African higher education institutions. The study used Scopus database to analyze publications between 2000-2024, identifying 53 relevant articles after screening. Key findings reveal significant geographic disparities: the United States leads with 21 publications, followed by Ukraine with 10, while no African countries appear in the initial search results. Further analysis limited to wartime, education, and online learning identified only three countries (Ukraine, Austria, United States) with no African representation. Publications have increased from one in 2009 to 12 in 2023, with most research appearing in social sciences (55%) and arts/humanities (25%). The study highlights a critical research gap regarding wartime and online education specifically in Africa, despite over three-quarters of African nations experiencing armed conflicts in the past three decades. Recommendations include further research on brain drain impacts, psychological effects on students and faculty, and inclusive online learning for people with disabilities in conflict-affected African universities. Limitations include reliance solely on Scopus database and exclusion of other databases like Web of Science or ScienceDirect.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic Party operative known for pranks targeting Richard Nixon, died at 94 in Tucson, Arizona. Among his notable stunts were bogus fortune cookies at a Republican fundraiser and infiltrating a 1962 Nixon campaign event in Chinatown with a sign referencing the Hughes loan. Tuck also worked on Robert Kennedy's 1968 presidential campaign and ran for California Senate in 1966, receiving 10% of the primary vote.

Mathieu Henderson, a Brantford native, finished his four‑year OHL career with Flint Firebirds, recording a breakout season of 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games to rank ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring. He noted the league passed quickly, especially the final year, and his season ended when Flint lost the opening playoff round to the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds. Henderson recalled feeling nervous as a rookie in Plymouth but quickly felt part of the team. After three seasons, the franchise relocated to Flint in 2015‑16; commissioner David Branch suspended owner Rolf Nilsen for five years after the owner repeatedly fired the head coach despite player protests. Henderson improved his defensive play, raising his plus/minus from –45 to –7, and scored the Firebirds’ only post‑season goal. During the OHL playoffs he received an offer from the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays, played three games, but had no roster spot for the ECHL playoffs. He is deciding whether to pursue pro hockey in North America or Europe or attend school, crediting his parents for his success.

The lecture covers VCG mechanisms and Google's online advertising auction. VCG implements utilitarian solutions in dominant strategies by charging bidders the negative externality they impose on others, but is not budget balanced and requires bidders to submit preferences over enormous outcome spaces. Google uses a Generalized Second Price (GSP) auction where advertisers submit single per-click bids and pay the next highest bid. Unlike VCG, truthful bidding is not an equilibrium—bidders shade their bids. However, the lecture presents the Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz theorem showing that GSP equilibrium payments exactly replicate VCG payments, making it ex post efficient and stable, which prevents costly repricing. The Athey-Ellison paper extends this model to endogenize ad slot values through consumer search with heterogeneous search costs. It demonstrates that reserve prices can improve welfare by signaling ad quality to consumers, and that consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price. The lecture also briefly discusses papers by Anderson-Renault and Armstrong-Zhou on endogenous pricing and platform information design.

GST is scheduled for July 1. The civil aviation ministry has requested a two‑month deferral, citing airlines’ need for more time to update their systems. Airlines, including Air India, are concerned about compliance, especially taxation of aircraft parts, and possible higher costs. The finance ministry has denied rumors of a delay.

The passage describes a data intake and query system, such as Splunk Enterprise, that collects, indexes, and searches machine-generated data. The system uses forwarders to ingest data, indexers to parse, timestamp, and store events in data stores, and search heads to process queries. Events are organized into time-based buckets, and the system supports late-binding schemas for flexible field extraction at search time. Acceleration techniques include parallel query processing, keyword indices, high-performance analytics stores (summarization tables), and accelerated report generation. The system enables users to analyze massive volumes of minimally processed data, create data models for structured searches, and generate reports and visualizations. Applications include security threat detection and data center monitoring. Deployment options include on-premises installations and cloud-based services.

The IRS announced higher 2026 federal income tax brackets and increased standard deductions to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single filers. The top 37% rate applies to taxable income above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for joint filers. Additional changes include higher long‑term capital gains brackets, increased estate and gift tax exemptions, and revised eligibility for the earned income tax credit. The SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) is a communication mechanism between AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypted virtual machines and their hypervisor. The GHCB is accessed via MSR 0xc001_0130, which contains the guest physical address of a 4K-aligned GHCB page.

The hypervisor establishes initial capabilities by setting GHCBData fields: bits [63:48] for maximum protocol version, bits [47:32] for minimum protocol version, and bits [31:24] for the SEV page table encryption bit number. The guest negotiates a protocol version within this range and may terminate if unsupported.

Key GHCB operations include: CPUID requests for retrieving CPU information before the GHCB is established; SEV information requests; GHCB GPA registration, unregistration, and preferred GPA queries for SEV-SNP guests; page state changes allowing guests to request transitioning pages between private and shared states; and SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request events for communicating with SEV firmware.

The specification defines numerous Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events handled via VMGEXIT, including AP Reset Hold, AP Creation, AP Jump Table management, #HV doorbell page operations, #HV timer support, APIC ID list retrieval, VMPL level changes, Secure AVIC backing page management, MSR and I/O protection, VMMCALL hypercalls, and page fault handling.

SEV-SNP introduces additional features including multi-VMPL support, Restricted Injection using #HV doorbell pages with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, and SNP AP Creation for simplified AP booting. The doorbell page format includes a 16-bit PendingEvent field with vector number and non-maskable event indicators, plus a NoEoiRequired byte for optimized end-of-interrupt handling.

Guests must initialize page tables with the encryption bit, mark GHCB pages as shared, and register the GHCB GPA before first use in SEV-SNP. vCPU hotplug is only supported via SNP AP Creation.

Substance use disorders (SUD) affect approximately 7% of the US population annually with high relapse rates. This study examined perineuronal nets (PNNs) and extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules in postmortem hippocampus samples from human subjects with SUD (n=20), SUD with comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD) (n=24), MDD (n=20), and controls (n=20), plus rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration. PNN densities were significantly increased in CA1 stratum oriens of subjects with SUD, along with increased PNNs in CA2, CA3, and CA4 regions. Subjects with SUD showed decreased ECM proteolytic gene expression (Mmp9, Ctss) and increased expression of the synaptic marker Vamp2 and CSPG synthesis molecule Chsy1. Parvalbumin (Pvb) gene expression was increased across all diagnostic groups. In contrast, subjects with MDD alone showed decreased PNNs in CA1 with increased PNNs in CA4, and subjects with comorbid SUD/MDD showed intermediate or opposing effects. Rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol self-administration exhibited increased hippocampal PNNs, supporting the human findings. These results suggest that increased PNNs may stabilize contextual reward memories in SUD, representing potential therapeutic targets for context-induced relapse, while MDD produces generally opposite effects that can mask or modify SUD-related changes.

The invention provides systems and methods for automated localization and classification of abnormalities (e.g., lesions, fractures, bleeding) in medical images. In one embodiment, a multi‑task network comprising a trained localization network and a trained classification network is jointly learned in a two‑phase training procedure: the localization network (an encoder‑decoder) generates a pixelwise heat map of the abnormality, and the classification network receives the heat map together with the original image to produce a binary malignancy classification. The multi‑task network can be extended to a multi‑modality fusion network that processes multiple mpMRI contrasts (T2‑weighted, DWI, ADC, DCE) with separate encoder‑decoders, combines their localization maps, and then classifies. A regression variant adds a scoring map (e.g., PI‑RADS) and uses a patch‑based approach for multi‑class lesion scoring.

Another embodiment detects abnormalities by deleting portions of an input image to create incomplete images, then uses a trained GAN to synthesize the deleted portions as normal tissue. The synthesized image that most closely resembles healthy tissue is selected as the normal reference; comparing it with the original image yields a localization map of the abnormality.

A further embodiment trains deep learning models on multi‑site datasets. During the training stage, additional site sub‑datasets are reordered by similarity to the main dataset, and a pretrained model is iteratively fine‑tuned only when each sub‑dataset improves performance. In the deployment stage, a small labeled deployment set is reordered by sample uncertainty, and the model is selectively refined using only samples that improve performance, ensuring generalization to unlabeled data.

All methods can be implemented on a computer system with processors, memory, storage, and optional image acquisition hardware.

Offensive goal kicks aim to retain possession and launch an attack after the defending team wins the ball. A goal kick is awarded when the ball crosses the defenders’ goal line after last being touched by an attacker; it is taken from anywhere in the goal area with the ball stationary, and opponents must stay outside the penalty area until the kick is taken. The ball becomes live as soon as it is kicked and visibly moves, and any player may then play it except the original kicker, as defined by Law 16.

For young players (generally 10‑and‑under), fields are reduced in size and a “build‑out line” is introduced: defenders must retreat behind the line before contesting the ball. Teams typically use a designated kicker at the outermost corner of the goal area to pass to a dribbler or to a target receiver positioned along the sideline; the receiver dribbles upfield or passes to a secondary receiver. Players are taught to keep the ball wide and upfield and never to send it across their own goal.

For players 11‑and‑older, the secondary receiver becomes a direct target and the kicker chooses between two or three target players based on defensive coverage; if both targets are covered the ball is kicked short so the far target can meet it. A midfielder may be added as a third option, and the goalkeeper may signal which side the kick will be taken from.

At the adult level all options are available: short passes to advancing teammates, deep targets, and the goalkeeper usually takes the kick. Goal kicks are a direct restart; a goal can be scored without the ball touching another player, and unusual wind conditions have led to goals or corners. Coaches must position targets appropriately and emphasize forceful movement to the ball.

The passage discusses the Random Walk Trading Strategy, which is based on the Random Walk Theory. This theory assumes stock prices move randomly and unpredictably, making historical price analysis ineffective. The strategy involves random entry and exit points, operating on the assumption that there is a 50% probability a stock will rise or fall. A key component of the strategy is diversification—investing in a broad range of stocks or a market index fund to mitigate risk. The passage relates the strategy to the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH), noting that while they differ in premise (random vs. efficient), both conclude it is nearly impossible to consistently outperform the market. Burton Malkiel popularized the concept in his book "A Random Walk Down Wall Street." The passage also describes backtests of the strategy, showing positive results in S&P 500 stocks (SPY) but poor results in gold (GLD).

From its earliest contact the United States opposed foreign aggression in Hawaii and viewed annexation as a possible contingency. In 1850 Lord Palmerston suggested a U.S. protectorate or integration of the islands. In 1851 a sealed deed of cession was prepared for use if France attacked. In 1854 Secretary Marcy advocated annexation and a draft treaty was agreed, but foreign influence on the heir and the death of King Kamehameha III blocked it. In 1867 Seward instructed the Honolulu minister to receive Hawaiian overtures, stating annexation outweighs reciprocity. President Johnson (1868) saw reciprocity as desirable until voluntary admission. President Grant (1871) asked the Senate for its view on annexation, and in 1873 Fish urged not to discourage annexation sentiment. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, U.S. policy protected exclusive commercial rights and supported the Hawaiian government. In 1881 Blaine endorsed benevolent neutrality and, if impractical, an avowedly American solution. The earliest official U.S. presence was the appointment of John C. Jones as agent for commerce and seamen on September 19 1820.

Official mpg figures from manufacturers are not reliable; they come from the NEDC test, which has not been updated since 1997 and contains many loopholes. The test omits sustained motorway driving, permits use of eco modes, turns off accessories, allows removal of items such as roof rails, lets tyre pressures exceed recommendations and lets manufacturers arbitrarily reduce results by 4%. From September 2017 the NEDC is being replaced by the WLTP cycle, a tougher procedure that should close these gaps.

Which? runs its own fuel‑economy tests using the WLTP cycle, performing a cold and a hot test plus a motorway‑speed test to capture real‑world consumption. Cars are tested in their default start‑up mode, with air‑conditioning, lights and radio on, and tyres are inflated to the manufacturer’s specification; no adjustments are made at the end. Hybrid vehicles follow the same cycles, with non‑plug‑in hybrids starting at 60‑70% charge and plug‑ins starting fully charged until charge falls below 50%.

Emissions such as NOx, CO, HC and PM are measured; any vehicle with very high pollution cannot become a Best Buy. To detect cheating, Which? uses a Portable Emissions Measuring System (PEMS) on the road when lab NOx readings seem suspicious. Which? publishes real‑world mpg data for over 700 vehicles, testing about 120 new cars each year.

The analysis addresses endogeneity by leveraging variation in reopening dates, uses cellphone mobility data, and reweights observations based on colleges’ likelihood of selecting a given modality.

Viral genome sequencing has shifted toward near‑real‑time analysis, enabling public‑health responses to emerging SARS‑CoV‑2 variants. However, sequencing is heavily concentrated: 10 % of countries generated >90 % of sequences, and most sequences came from the United States and United Kingdom. Sparse and heterogeneous data limit reliable early characterization and real‑time prevalence estimates, especially in low‑capacity regions.

To address this, the authors developed a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial model that pools all available sequences across countries. The model estimates (i) within‑country variant prevalence, (ii) within‑country growth rates, and (iii) a global fitness advantage for each variant, while accounting for regional heterogeneity and data sparsity. Country‑specific fitness estimates shrink toward the global mean, reducing over‑fitting to noisy early data.

Applying the model to SARS‑CoV‑2, they show that BA.5 has the highest global weekly fitness advantage (~0.94) relative to BA.2, followed by BA.4 (~0.67) and BA.2.12.1 (~0.45); BA.1’s advantage is negative. Growth rates vary markedly across countries (e.g., higher in the United States and United Kingdom than in India or South Africa). Validation using retrospective data for BA.5’s emergence in Portugal demonstrates that the multicountry model yields lower Brier scores and more stable fitness estimates than a single‑country multinomial regression, especially when sequences are few.

The approach is general: it can be applied to other pathogens (e.g., influenza) and sub‑national scales, and it complements capacity‑building efforts by extracting more information from existing data. Limitations include assumptions of random sampling, correct lineage assignment, constant generation intervals, and no change in fitness over the modeling window.

The authors have implemented a live dashboard providing real‑time global and country‑level variant fitness estimates and prevalence nowcasts to support public‑health decision‑making.

The paper studies Gorenstein‑projective modules over the ring Z[ε]=Z[T]/(T^2) of dual integers. It focuses on the category G‑proj_Z[ε] and shows it is equivalent to the categories of torsionless Z[ε]‑modules, perfect differential structures of abelian groups, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups; this category lacks the Krull‑Remak‑Schmidt property. The stable category of G‑proj_Z[ε] modulo projectives is related to the derived category of Z and to results of Buchweitz and of Honma–Usui. Theorem 1.2.1 states that the stable category of G‑proj_Z[ε] is equivalent to four other categories: submodules of a free Z[ε]‑module modulo projectives, the orbit category Db(Z)/[1], the homotopy category of perfect differential structures, and the stable category of perfect differential structures; the theorem holds for any principal ideal domain. A chain of categories Cb(F)→G‑proj_Z[ε]→Db(Z)/[1]→Ab connects bounded complexes of free abelian groups, Gorenstein‑projective modules, derived category, and finite abelian groups via dense functors σ, π, φ. Composing these functors yields a commutative cube whose faces correspond to the listed equivalences.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis received the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in a macroscopic electric circuit built on a chilled Josephson junction. Since the discovery, tech companies and researchers have used similar circuits as the quantum bits, or qubits, that make up quantum computers. The prize, worth over $1.1 million, was awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences and split among Clarke (UC Berkeley), Martinis (UC Santa Barbara) and Devoret (Yale University and UC Santa Barbara).

Enron shares fell sharply on October 30, 2001, dropping to their lowest level in over eight years after Moody's Investors Service downgraded the company's credit rating to two notches above junk status. The stock lost about 19% of its value, trading around $11, and has declined 83% year-to-date. Moody's lowered Enron's long-term credit rating to "Baa2" from "Baa1" and placed its commercial paper rating on review for possible downgrade. Insurance premiums for Enron bonds doubled as investors sought protection against potential default. The company is lobbying banks for new credit lines after tapping its $3.3 billion credit facilities. Enron lost approximately $15 billion in market capitalization amid disclosures about off-balance-sheet partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, which triggered an SEC investigation. Fastow was ousted last week. Meanwhile, new CFO Jeff McMahon discussed Enron's ambitions to expand in forest products trading, aiming to become one of the largest newsprint marketers in North America. The company reported a $1.01 billion loss two weeks ago, including equity charges related to partnership investments. Major utilities including AEP, Exelon, and Northeast Utilities said they are monitoring their trading exposure to Enron while continuing to do business with the company. Consumer confidence in the U.S. fell to its lowest level in over seven years in October, contributing to broader market declines.

The passage describes design procedures for a push‑pull converter using the TPS7H500x‑SP space‑grade controllers. An 80‑V GaN FET is chosen for the synchronous rectifier with a parallel Schottky diode to reduce soft‑start current and dead‑time losses. The RCD clamp is sized using an overshoot factor (KCLAMP = 1.5 for 50 % allowable overshoot), leakage inductance, and peak primary current. The output inductor is set to 0.47 µH for a 40 % ripple target, and the minimum output capacitance of 1.3 mF is increased to 2.3 mF to mitigate radiation‑induced single‑event transients. An optional LC filter (inductor plus ceramic capacitance) is placed downstream of the main inductor, with its resonant frequency chosen above the crossover but below the switching frequency and ESR zero; a damping resistor can be added if high‑frequency peaking occurs. Cycle‑by‑cycle current limiting begins at roughly 35 A, using a 7.5 Ω sense resistor (RCS) and a 1:100 current‑sense transformer. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF, and Type 2A compensation is implemented with RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF; slope compensation uses a 102 kΩ resistor. Power‑supply recommendations include a 4–14 V input range, a minimum 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor, and separation of analog (AVSS) and power grounds. Layout guidelines advise routing feedback away from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing switch‑node copper area, shortening high‑di/dt loops, using wide high‑current traces (≥15 mil/A), placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, keeping resistor dividers near the device, separating high‑dv/dt signals from sensitive pins, adding RC filtering on CS_ILIM, routing SYNC away from noise‑sensitive pins, and connecting the CFP package backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias. Application curves for soft‑start and load‑step response are referenced. Related documentation covers evaluation modules, radiation reports (TID and SEE), and neutron displacement characterization. Revision history notes the addition of QMLP options and updates to device options.

The MSPM0 G-Series 80MHz microcontrollers feature a PMU for power regulation and supervision, a CKM providing multiple oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, HFXT, SYSPLL), and clocks like MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, HFCLK, HSCLK, and CANCLK. The DMA controller offers 6 full-feature channels and 6 basic channels with support for various data transfer sizes and triggers, including stride mode and ping-pong buffer support. An event manager handles peripheral-to-CPU, peripheral-to-DMA, and peripheral-to-peripheral events through static and programmable routes. Memory includes dual-bank flash up to 512KB with ECC protection, up to 128KB SRAM split into ECC-protected and configurable banks, and supports write-execute partitioning. Peripherals include up to 93 GPIO pins, IOMUX for pin configuration, dual 12-bit ADCs with 4Msps and HW averaging, temperature sensor, VREF, comparators, 12-bit DAC, security features (AES-128/256, firewalls, secure key storage, CRC), TRNG, AESADV accelerator, keystore, CRC module, MATHACL, UART (UART0-UART1, UART3-UART7), I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS (RTC_B, IWDT), WWDT, and TIMx (TIMGx and TIMAx) timers. Additional features include SWD debug interface, BSL for programming via UART/I2C, and factory constants for device identification and trim data. Development tools include Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, and MSPM0 SDK.

The Open Source Definition (OSD) was published in early February 1998, formalizing a movement built on Richard Stallman's free‑software advocacy. The Open Source Initiative was founded on 3 February 1998 after Netscape released its code; Christine Peterson proposed the term “open source” there, adopted on 5 February 1998, and Bruce Perens announced the OSD on 9 February 1998. The term avoided the ambiguity of “free” and offered a commercially palatable alternative to free software, both aiming to make source code available under user‑freedom licenses. Today major tech firms—Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, Microsoft—depend on open‑source code such as Linux and Darwin, and open‑source projects, once aimed at cloning proprietary software, now drive innovation. Microsoft, once calling Linux “cancer”, has since embraced open source.

J. Bernstorff’s note says the blockade may end if a reasonable conference is arranged. Document 31 records that German Ambassador Zimmermann handed over a submarine‑warfare note and maps, stating Bernstorff had been instructed to give Germany’s peace terms confidentially to the President and urging the President to stay quiet for two months while submarine warfare forces England to seek terms; he described Lloyd George as the Entente leader and warned of exhausted Europe confronting Japan. Ambassador Gerard replied that the documents seemed lawyer‑drafted, he did not know the outcome and always worked for peace. Document 32 reports the Greek Government’s announcement that the Entente would allow essential food imports pending the lifting of the blockade, while noting that a large stock of rifles remains unaccounted for. Document 33 transmits Austria‑Hungary’s request that the United States consider its defensive stance, its readiness for Wilson‑proposed “peace without victory,” and its insistence that the Entente abandon its dismemberment plan; it states submarine warfare cannot be technically altered and that Wilson should use US influence and economic leverage to bring the Entente to accept the proposed basis.

Storage technologies are promoted as a means to increase renewables and reduce fossil reliance. A storage system takes power when cheap or excess and returns it later, incurring capital and operating costs, including round‑trip efficiency losses. Key technologies include lithium‑ion batteries (efficient at small scale, costs falling toward US$600/kWh), pumped hydro (large‑scale, cheap ~A$100/kWh), flywheels (low efficiency, fast dispatch, grid frequency support) and others such as compressed air, cryogenic and flow batteries, each suited to different grid roles. For a home with a 4.5 kW PV system and variable tariffs, a 7 kWh battery must cost under A$7,000 (~A$1,000/kWh) to save money; current costs are A$1,000–3,000/kWh, close to break‑even. Retail rate spreads overstate wholesale differences; a flat 25 c/kWh tariff would require ~A$300/kWh for viability. Electricity demand in the National Electricity Market has fallen since 2009, limiting network‑cost benefits of storage. Pumped hydro already costs around A$100/kWh with 1,500 MW installed, but distributed lithium‑ion may dominate due to consumer preferences rather than pure economics.

Bitcoin’s price rose nearly 100% since early December, with swings of up to 40% gains and a ~20% loss in recent days. The K‑diet is based on Korea’s traditional eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods such as fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, fermented foods (kimchi, doenjang, gochujang) and healthy fats. Allowed foods include seasonal produce, legumes, soy, rice, noodles, broth‑based soups and seasonings. The diet limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats and dairy, and promotes physical activity. Benefits include high fibre, low calories and saturated fats, and antioxidants from plant‑based and fermented foods, supporting digestion and weight loss. Drawbacks include high sodium from fermented condiments (unsuitable for hypertension), low calcium due to lack of dairy, possible irritation from spices, and high carbohydrate content requiring portion control. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low‑carb or gluten‑free needs.
Guide offers new soccer players rules on positioning, ball work, and team tactics.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with an integrated analog front-end.

The device supports a speed-boost mode enabling sampling rates up to 8MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair while the remaining six channels remain idle. The SPI configuration interface uses three 16-bit register banks, with bank 0 always accessible and banks 1 and 2 selected by writing to register address 0x03. Register read and write operations use specific 24-bit SPI frames.

Multiple ADS9803 devices can be configured in a daisy-chain topology, sharing a single CS and SCLK line. The SDO output of each device connects to the SDI input of the next, and the daisy-chain length is set via the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register. Operations on the chain require N × 24 SCLK cycles, where N is the number of devices.

The device is intended for ATE applications, achieving a total unadjusted error (TUE) of less than 0.01% with calibration and full-scale settling within 10µs. It requires three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) and recommends specific layout practices such as using decoupling capacitors near power pins and separating analog and digital signal paths.

Objective: To develop a predictive model for shunt‑dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Methods: Retrospective cohort study of 118 consecutive aSAH patients who underwent aneurysm obliteration (clipping or coiling) at Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital (January 2013–October 2021). After excluding 9 patients (8 in‑hospital deaths, 1 incomplete data), 109 patients were analyzed. Variables included age, gender, BMI, treatment modality, aneurysm location, Fisher grade, Hunt‑Hess scale (HHS), eGFR, neutrophil‑lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet‑lymphocyte ratio (PLR), platelet‑neutrophil ratio (PNR), and new neurological deficits. All patients received an external ventricular drainage (EVD) challenge (EVD closure with ICP monitoring for 72 h); failure led to VP shunt placement. Univariate analysis identified variables with p < 0.1, which were entered into multivariate logistic regression. A nomogram was constructed from the final model. Results: Three variables remained independent predictors of SDHC: age ≥ 65 years (OR 3.94, 95% CI 1.41–11.00, p = 0.009), clipping versus coiling (OR 4.36, 95% CI 1.81–10.53, p = 0.001), and HHS ≥ 3 (OR 3.59, 95% CI 1.50–8.61, p = 0.004). The model’s discriminative ability was an AUC of 0.753 (95% CI 0.66–0.84). The nomogram assigned 1 point to each factor, allowing total‑score estimation of SDHC probability. Conclusions: SDHC occurs in 17.2%–31.2% of aSAH patients. Age ≥ 65, clipping treatment, and HHS ≥ 3 are independent risk factors. A bedside nomogram based on these factors estimates individual SDHC risk. Limitations include retrospective design and modest sample size; prospective validation is required.

An international team from the University of Utah, Northeastern University, the University of the Philippines, Sultan Kudarat State University and Drexel University obtained live Kuphus polythalamia specimens in a lagoon in the Philippines. The bivalve lives in five‑foot shells, consumes hydrogen sulfide and uses microbes to convert the gas into carbon, unlike wood‑eating relatives. Researchers will study gill microbes for antimicrobials; results published in PNAS. Haygood, Altamia and Distel note the species evolved from wood‑eating shipworms and may be a addition to family tree.

DAX 40 is Germany’s main stock index, made up of 40 blue‑chip companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (e.g., Adidas, Airbus, Allianz, Munich Re, SAP, Deutsche Bank, BMW). Founded in July 1988, it now has a market capitalisation of roughly $1.25 trillion and has returned about 5.36 % per year since inception. U.S. investors can access the German market via the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG), which holds large‑ and mid‑size German firms, with its biggest positions in SAP, Siemens and Allianz, and charges a 0.50 % expense ratio. Historical monthly returns of EWG show the strongest performance in the final quarter, while the rest of the year the ETF trades sideways. The seasonal strategy limits holdings to the last three months (Q4) each year. Back‑testing the strategy on EWG (adjusted for dividends and splits) demonstrates better returns than a buy‑and‑hold approach over recent decades. The article also includes FAQs describing the DAX 40 composition, EWG’s relevance for U.S. investors, and how historical performance informs trading strategies.

Climate change is causing earlier, warmer and drier springs in the northern Rocky Mountains, reducing cold‑water habitat for native cutthroat trout. Introduced rainbow trout are moving into these warming streams and interbreeding with cutthroats, producing hybrids that lack the locally adapted traits and have lower survival rates. Hybridization is widespread, especially where rainbow trout have been stocked for decades. Some states are removing rainbow trout to protect cutthroat populations, because once the native genome is lost it cannot be restored.

Long-term outdoor exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE) is linked to a modest increase in Parkinson’s disease risk among older U.S. adults, according to a nationwide study of over 1.1 million Medicare beneficiaries. The highest TCE exposure group (0.14–8.66 µg/m³) had a 10 % higher risk of Parkinson’s compared with the lowest exposure group (0.005–0.01 µg/m³), after adjusting for age, smoking and fine particulate air pollution. TCE is an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning that persists in air, water and soil nationwide. Elevated TCE “hot‑spots” were identified in the Rust Belt and other pockets; analysis of the three largest TCE‑emitting facilities showed higher risk closer to the sources. The study shows an association, not causation, and is limited to Medicare‑aged individuals and 2002 outdoor exposure estimates.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden used machine‑learning and advanced supercomputer simulations to determine the low‑temperature crystal structure of formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI₃), a leading halide perovskite for next‑generation solar cells. Global electricity consumption is rising sharply, with projections that electricity will exceed 50 % of total energy use within 25 years, driving demand for efficient, durable solar technologies. Halide perovskites are prized for their high light‑absorption and flexibility, but their instability has hindered practical deployment; mixing two perovskite types can improve stability, yet deeper knowledge of each component is required. The Chalmers team identified the previously elusive low‑temperature phase of FAPbI₃, showing that formamidinium molecules become trapped in a semi‑stable state as the material cools. By combining conventional modelling with machine‑learning, they ran simulations thousands of times longer than before, covering millions of atoms, and validated results experimentally by cooling the material to –200 °C with collaborators at the University of Birmingham. Their findings, published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society (14 August 2025), resolve a fundamental structural question and provide guidance for engineering FAPbI₃ and related mixtures into stable, ultra‑thin, flexible solar cells that could coat mobile devices or entire buildings.

COVID‑19 emerged in Wuhan in early 2020, was declared a pandemic by WHO on 11 March 2020, and reached Turkey the same day. The pandemic forced a worldwide shift to virtual education; Turkey implemented distance learning through the Education Informatics Network (EBA TV) via TRT and the Ministry of National Education. Virtual education offers flexibility but also reduces in‑person interaction, limits immediate problem‑solving, and can cause motivation, socialization, and equity problems. Students with disabilities, many of whom receive services in inclusive settings, were particularly affected. Pre‑pandemic inclusive education in Turkey already suffered from insufficient support rooms, limited expertise, inadequate equipment, large class sizes, and insufficient individualization of instruction.

The study aimed to examine, from primary‑school teachers’ perspectives, the participation of students with disabilities who continued inclusive education during virtual learning, the problems they encountered, and potential solutions. Using a qualitative phenomenology design, ten general‑education teachers in two Marmara‑region provinces were purposively sampled and interviewed with a semi‑structured form (eight open‑ended questions); data were audio‑recorded, transcribed, and content‑analyzed.

Findings showed teachers initially informed parents, used EBA and Zoom, and sought parental support. They tried various applications, hybrid schedules, and sent materials via WhatsApp. Student attendance varied: many participated independently with parental assistance, some attended only basic courses or were absent due to parental illiteracy, internet issues, or lack of devices. Teachers reported challenges in including students and monitoring their progress, including not knowing the student, low socialization, difficulty tracking homework, keeping cameras on, and needing extensive family help. Large class sizes, limited one‑on‑one time, poor teacher‑parent communication, and inadequate resources were identified as reasons. Some teachers experienced no problems because families provided strong support and used EBA’s tracking features.

In following lesson activities and assignments, teachers noted students’ reluctance to watch EBA TV, low interaction, lack of engaging content, and occasional behavioral issues. Disadvantaged districts, parental illiteracy, and technology gaps compounded difficulties. Teachers applied solutions such as hybrid scheduling, flexible support sessions, video feedback on home work, and frequent phone motivation. Suggested solutions included providing devices and internet for low‑income families, ensuring school continuity especially for students with disabilities, fostering both academic and social development, using EBA support points for emotional encouragement, and coordinating with rehabilitation centers.

The study concludes that parental support is crucial for virtual inclusive education and that adequate resources, clear teacher‑parent collaboration, and targeted training are needed to address participation, monitoring, and engagement challenges. Future research is recommended to explore experiences of diverse student groups, compare outcomes with typically developing peers, and examine quantitative factors influencing virtual‑education effectiveness.

Definition of youth (UN: 15‑24) and skills (hard/soft) are provided. Experiential learning, including co‑op, integrates curriculum, work experience and coordination. Youth unemployment in Nigeria rose sharply, reaching levels higher than most regions by 2021; youth rates are roughly double total rates. Employment‑to‑population ratios are lower for youth; informality, high NEET rates (28% vs 13% OECD) and gender disparities are noted, with higher unemployment among the educated and in urban areas. Co‑op originated in industrialized countries and has been adopted in some sub‑Saharan institutions; core dimensions are integrated curriculum, learning from work, and logistical coordination. Two main models exist: alternating semesters and parallel work‑study; benefits for students, employers, institutions and society are documented, mainly from North America and the UK. Nigerian government responses include SIWES (short, vacation‑based), SURE‑P (internship and vocational schemes) and N‑SIP (N‑Power). Reviews show positive impacts but also challenges such as poor placement and funding gaps. The paper argues that co‑op can complement these programs by aligning training with industry needs, leveraging existing infrastructure and mitigating costs through government grants or tax credits. Adoption of the alternating model is recommended, and further research on management structures and applicability is needed.

Omicron (PANGO lineage B.1.1.529, BA.1/BA.2) was first identified in Botswana and South Africa in late November 2021 and designated a VOC on 26 November 2021. It showed higher transmissibility than Delta, linked to a shorter serial interval, increased immune evasion and enhanced replication in the upper airway. The variant quickly reached major travel hubs, including New York and London, despite restrictions on flights from several southern African countries. In England the first confirmed case was on 27 November 2021; prevalence peaked first in Greater London in mid‑December and later in other regions, creating a north‑to‑south gradient by early January 2022.

Phylogenomic analysis of 115 622 Omicron genomes (48 615 from England) identified at least 6 455 independent introductions; 69.9 % were singletons with no detectable onward transmission. The eight largest transmission lineages accounted for over 60 % of English genomes, six of them imported before the southern‑African travel restrictions. Early introductions (5–13 November 2021) produced ~80 % of Omicron BA.1 infections in England by end‑January 2022, despite representing only ~6 % of total introductions. Importation intensity grew exponentially until early December, driven mainly by air passengers from the United States; the average weekly estimated importation intensity from the US was about four‑fold higher than from South Africa during the restriction period.

Spatially explicit phylogeographic reconstruction showed Greater London as the central source of long‑distance viral movements, frequently exporting lineages to the Midlands, North West and North East from early December. Short‑range (<50 km) movements declined over time, while mid‑to‑long‑range (50–300 km and >300 km) movements increased during the New Year period. A discrete phylogeographic GLM confirmed that population‑size‑dependent “gravity” dynamics and a London‑origin predictor shaped the expansion phase, while aggregated mobility became the dominant predictor in the post‑expansion phase.

Human mobility fell 20–50 % across all spatial scales from mid‑December to early January 2022, coinciding with “Plan B” measures, holiday mixing and behavioural responses to rising case numbers. A statistical model estimated that for every unit increase in weekly COVID‑19 cases per 100 people at a major hub, mobility to/from that hub decreased by ~12 %, with stronger reductions for shorter distances (≈20 % at 50 km). The study concludes that travel restrictions implemented after local transmission were largely ineffective, and that early introductions, human mobility patterns and behavioural responses were key determinants of the Omicron BA.1 wave in England.

The TLV321/2x family are low‑power comparators that consume 40 µA per channel with a 40 ns propagation delay, detecting fast voltage and current transients while maintaining low power. Two output options are available: the TLV321x provides a push‑pull (sink‑source) output, and the TLV322x provides an open‑drain (sink‑only) output that can be pulled up to 5.5 V independent of the supply voltage.

The input voltage range extends from 200 mV below V– to 200 mV above V+, and the differential input must stay within this range to avoid phase‑inversion. Inputs include an ESD clamp to V+ that limits the voltage to 0.2 V beyond the rails; the input current should be limited to 10 mA or less by adding a series resistor. Unused inputs must not be tied together; they should be tied to any voltage within the specified range with at least a 50 mV differential to prevent high‑frequency chatter.

The devices contain 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis; additional external hysteresis can be applied using resistor networks (inverting or non‑inverting configurations) to prevent output chatter near the threshold. The output is treated as a high‑speed digital signal; proper layout, bypass capacitors, and short series resistors on inputs and outputs are recommended to avoid ringing and oscillations. The push‑pull output must never be shorted to the opposite rail, and the open‑drain pull‑up resistor should be set between 100 µA and 1 mA.

A Power‑On Reset (POR) holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply voltage reaches 1.65 V, after which the comparator output reflects the differential input state. Propagation delay is affected by overdrive voltage (smaller overdrive yields longer delay), and rise/fall times are in the tens of nanoseconds.

Typical applications include low‑side current sensing, where the comparator alerts when an amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. A stable, low‑noise supply with bypass capacitors placed close to the supply pin, minimized coupling between inputs and outputs, and series output resistors for long traces are essential for reliable operation.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture powers GeForce RTX 30‑series consumer GPUs and the data‑center A40/RTX A6000 workstations. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third‑generation Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, one second‑generation RT Core, and 128 KB of unified L1/shared memory; the SM is split into four partitions, each with its own register file, L0 cache, warp scheduler and dispatch unit. GA10x doubles FP32 throughput versus Turing by enabling FP32 on both datapaths in each partition, delivering 128 FP32 ops per clock per SM. The L1 data cache grows to 128 KB per SM and shared‑memory bandwidth doubles to 128 bytes/clock.

The memory subsystem uses 12 × 32‑bit controllers (384‑bit total) with 6 MB of L2 cache. ROP units are moved into the GPC, providing 112 ROPs on a full GA102 (7 GPCs × 16 ROPs), improving multisample anti‑aliasing and pixel fill‑rate.

Second‑generation RT Cores double ray‑triangle intersection rates versus Turing and add a dedicated Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware‑accelerated motion blur, achieving up to 8× faster motion‑blur rendering. The RT Core also supports concurrent execution of ray‑tracing and graphics or compute workloads.

Third‑generation Tensor Cores introduce TF32 and BF16 precisions, and a fine‑grained structured‑sparsity feature that doubles matrix‑multiplication throughput for sparse networks. With sparsity enabled, the RTX 3080 reaches 238 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS.

GDDR6X memory, co‑developed with Micron, uses PAM4 signaling to achieve data rates up to 19.5 Gb/s and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s on the RTX 3090. NVIDIA RTX IO leverages Microsoft DirectStorage to offload game asset loading and lossless decompression to the GPU, delivering up to 100× throughput and 20× lower CPU utilization.

Display capabilities include HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, supporting 8K 60 Hz and 4K 120 Hz. The fifth‑generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decode alongside H.264, HEVC, VP9, and the seventh‑generation NVENC enables high‑quality, low‑power video encoding up to 8K HEVC.

For data‑center workloads, the A40 delivers up to 2× FP32 and ray‑tracing performance, 5× AI training (10× with sparsity) versus the Quadro RTX 6000, and includes 48 GB GDDR6 with third‑generation NVLink for 96 GB combined memory. The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB GDDR6, hardware‑accelerated motion blur, AI denoising, and supports professional certifications. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X protects memory transactions during overclocking.

The passage analyzes originalism as a method of constitutional interpretation and its application to a current Supreme Court case involving Louisiana’s majority‑Black congressional district. It contends that the Court’s “racial predominance” doctrine, which invalidates districts drawn primarily on race, cannot be justified by the original public meaning of either the Fourteenth or Fifteenth Amendments. The author notes that the Fourteenth Amendment’s equal‑protection language was not originally understood to limit how states draw districts, and that the Fifteenth Amendment’s text only prohibits denying or abridging an individual’s right to vote, not the mere grouping of voters by race. Therefore, the doctrine lacks an originalist foundation. Nevertheless, the doctrine remains precedent, and under the principle of stare decisis the Court would normally follow it unless it becomes unworkable or conflicts with other law. The passage highlights an existing tension between the “racial predominance” rule and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which permits vote‑dilution claims. The author argues that a consistent originalist approach would eliminate the “racial predominance” doctrine, thereby resolving the conflict and preserving Congress’s authority to enforce voting rights through statutory amendments. The author urges Justice Barrett, a self‑described originalist, to address these originalist and stare‑decisis considerations in the Louisiana case and to persuade her colleagues to do the same.

Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index surveys over 100 independent market newsletters weekly, reporting the percentages of advisors that are bullish, bearish, and expecting a correction. It also provides weekly figures of stocks above their 10‑week and 30‑week moving averages, useful for short‑term and major market turns. The index, created in 1963 by AW Cohen, was originally intended to signal when most advisors were bullish as the best time to be long, but advisors proved mostly wrong at turning points, so the investment community now uses it as a contrarian indicator. Bullish readings above 55 % indicate excessive optimism and are considered bearish for the market; readings below 35 % indicate excessive pessimism and are seen as bullish. Weekly readings above 70 % signal an overbought market and below 30 % an oversold market, with a trend change signaled when the numbers cross 30 or 70. The AAII Sentiment Survey polls individual investors, whereas the Investors Intelligence Index polls professional advisors and commentators. The index is published by Chartcraft and is widely followed by the financial media as a long‑standing contrarian tool since 1963.

During the first day of the U.S. government shutdown, Department of Education (DOE) employees set neutral out‑of‑office messages stating they could not reply until the shutdown ended. Within hours the messages were altered without consent to blame Senate Democrats for the lapse in appropriations. Employees reverted to the neutral text, but the department re‑applied the partisan language. Sources say the Department of Labor also received similar partisan suggested language. Experts say the forced partisan language could violate the Hatch Act, which restricts political activity by federal employees. The DOE press office responded to a request for comment with the same partisan out‑of‑office message.

The passage argues that the "out-of-school children" (OOSC) indicator, which measures formal school enrollment, inadequately captures educational exclusion. Using Afghanistan as a case study, the author advocates replacing OOSC with an "out-of-education children" (OOEC) indicator encompassing formal, informal, and non-formal learning pathways. The OOSC indicator allegedly privileges formal schooling while marginalizing alternative systems like madrasas and community-based programs. Afghanistan's education challenges include geographic disparities affecting rural provinces, nomadic children's limited access, child labor forcing children out of school, and inadequate accommodations for children with disabilities. The proposed OOEC indicator aims to broaden understanding of educational challenges, catalyze system transformation, and reimagine education as an interconnected ecosystem. Implementing this shift would require fundamental changes to data systems, credentialing, inter-agency collaboration, and resource allocation to recognize diverse pathways and address systemic barriers to education.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables patching of selected AMD firmware without system reboot. Three version identifiers track patches: SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), per‑component Security Patch Level (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run‑once code. AMD cryptographically signs all SFS packages; customers may optionally co‑sign to maintain their own root‑of‑trust for update. SFS is configured in BIOS via two flags (SFS_ENABLE and SFS_COSIGN_REQUIRED) and requires a 2 MB‑aligned TEE command buffer and a customer‑provided deployment agent. The ASP verifies the customer signature (if present), then the AMD signature, loads the executable patch, and updates version information. Packages are not persistent across reboots and must be reapplied after reset; they use the naming scheme fam_<family>-<AGESA‑Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run in parallel with normal system traffic with minimal performance impact; SEV/SEV‑ES virtual machines must pause and restart for firmware updates, while SEV‑SNP VMs can continue operating.

Passport applicants must take an oath of allegiance to the United States and provide a personal description (age, stature, forehead, eyes, nose, mouth, chin, hair, complexion, face) with at least one credible witness’s affidavit confirming identity. Native citizens submit the basic application; persons born abroad prove their father’s U.S. citizenship; naturalized citizens present their certificate of naturalization and details of emigration and naturalization; women declare marital status and, if married to a citizen, include the husband’s naturalization information; children of naturalized citizens submit the parent’s certificate and same details. Residents of insular possessions affirm U.S. allegiance and provide two witness affidavits. Passports expire after two years and may be renewed; a prior passport can replace a naturalization certificate if the prior application was adequate. One passport may cover a spouse, minor children, and servants; other companions need separate passports. Professional titles are omitted. Officials may refuse passports for unlawful or improper purposes. Fees: $1.00 for the passport, $0.50 for the application in duplicate, $0.50 for administering the oath.

Archaeologists from the Great Mayan Aquifer Project, led by Guillermo de Anda, will clear a centuries‑old sealed tunnel beneath the El Castillo pyramid at Chichen Itza to reach a hidden cenote identified two years ago by Mexican scientist René Chávez Segura. The tunnel was blocked by the Maya, who regularly sealed important caves. Cenotes are water‑filled sinkholes that provide the only fresh‑water source in the Yucatán and were seen as the entrance to the underworld in Maya cosmology, which comprised three layers (heavens, earth, underworld). Offerings, including human sacrifice, were made to maintain cosmic balance. Previous study of bones from the Sacred Cenote found that roughly 80 % of victims were children aged 3‑11 from low‑status groups, many showing signs of anemia and malnutrition. The expected excavation will take about three months; the team hopes the hidden cenote may represent a fifth direction or “axis mundi,” symbolizing the Maya’s Tree of Life, and could yield further insights into their beliefs.
Lab tests show microbubbles create lightning igniting methane to form will-o’-the-wisps over swamps.

Europe, through EU’s Global Gateway, announced a €545 million ($636 million) package to boost renewable energy and electrification in Africa. Projects include a high‑voltage transmission line in Côte d’Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydro development in Lesotho, and mini‑grids in Madagascar, aiming to expand electricity access and shift the continent off fossil fuels. EU says it could create 38 million green jobs by 2030. Global Gateway, launched in 2021, prioritises Africa and counters China’s Belt and Road Initiative, which has invested over $1.3 trillion and wields influence. Africa holds key minerals (cobalt in the DRC, lithium in Zimbabwe, copper in Zambia, manganese in Gabon) where Chinese firms are already active. In the first half of 2025 Belt and Road energy contracts in Africa reached $39 billion and China exported 15 GW of solar panels to the continent, a 60 % year‑on‑year rise. United States responded with the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment, supporting solar plants in Angola, wind storage in Kenya and a nickel plant in Tanzania. West is also building the Lobito railway linking Zambia’s copper and DRC cobalt to Angola’s port. Africa’s decarbonization is essential for net‑zero goals, with Von der Leyen saying Africa’s choices today shape the world’s future.
