During the 2020–2021 school year in Epirus, Greece, a quantitative survey examined 82 kindergarten teachers’ views on distance education after its forced implementation due to the COVID‑19 pandemic. The sample was mostly female, with 55.6 % having 15–25 years of service and about 31 % over 25 years; most held a bachelor’s degree (76.5 %) and roughly a third possessed Level B ICT certification. The questionnaire assessed familiarity with distance education, prior experience, tools used, and opinions on its integration.

Descriptive results showed that over three‑quarters of teachers reported little or no familiarity with distance education before the pandemic and 91.5 % had never used it in kindergarten prior to COVID‑19. Synchronous platforms (mainly Webex, used by 88.9 %) were preferred over asynchronous methods; email and Viber were also common.

Teachers highlighted major obstacles: insufficient digital infrastructure (65 % reported severe problems), limited internet and technology access for both staff and families (73 %), and difficulty for preschool children to use tools independently (78 %). Large majorities judged distance education less effective than conventional teaching for developing social skills (86 %) and for implementing psychomotor activities (90 %). About half felt it only suits emergency situations; only a minority saw it promoting individualized learning or student interest.

Statistical analysis revealed a significant relationship between ICT certification level and pre‑pandemic familiarity: Level B certificate holders were more familiar than uncertified teachers (Kruskal‑Wallis = 7.001, p = 0.030). No significant correlation was found between years of service and ICT literacy (Spearman ρ = 0.109, p = 0.331).

The discussion notes that teachers view distance education as inadequate for preschool, emphasizing the need for adult supervision, parental involvement, better school infrastructure, and targeted professional development. The authors conclude that distance education in kindergarten faces substantial barriers and recommend state investment in technology, teacher training, and family support. Generalizability is limited to the Epirus region.

A Take a Knee Chart helps football coaches decide when to run the take a knee play to run out the clock. The offense lines up in formation; the quarterback snaps and kneels, counting as a run so the clock continues and the play clock resets. The play is used when the offense leads and the opponent has no timeouts, so they cannot stop the clock. The chart shows positions and movement. Clock management is a coaching duty, noting that college and high school football use a 40‑second play clock and lack a two‑minute warning. Completed passes keep the clock, while incomplete passes stop it, giving the opponent time.

The captions describe the third round of the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee held in Oxon Hill, Maryland on May 30, 2018. Participants range from 9 to 15 years old and come from various U.S. states as well as South Korea. Some successfully spelled words such as “bonspiel,” “slickensides,” “aspirator,” “heliosis,” “revivification,” “sclerotic,” and “deliverable,” while others misspelled words including “giddily,” “abandonedly,” “finial,” “frustraneous,” “transude,” “athleisure,” and others. ML²B (Multilingual Machine Learning Benchmark) is introduced as the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs on generating complete ML pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. It extends 30 Kaggle competitions (24 public, 6 private) into 13 languages, creating 390 unique evaluation instances across tabular, text, and image modalities in 12 domains. Five LLMs were evaluated across two execution frameworks (AIDE with 3 agents, ML Master with 2 hybrids). Results revealed substantial 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks. English remains the strongest anchor language, while low-resource languages like Kazakh, Belarusian, and Romanian exhibit higher failure rates. Domain complexity interacts with cross-lingual performance, with tabular classification and regression showing greater instability than image categorization. Hybrid architectures partially mitigate low-resource limitations but do not eliminate cross-lingual disparities. The modular grading interface curbs preprocessing leakage by construction, and static analysis identified potential leakage in 5.9% of submissions. Six private competitions help reduce benchmark data leakage to LLM pretraining corpora.

Amazon.com, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Seattle, Washington, whose common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol AMZN. The company operates three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through online and physical retail, third‑party seller services, cloud computing, advertising, and device sales. As of December 31 2018, Amazon employed approximately 647,500 full‑time and part‑time employees worldwide and maintained global facilities including fulfillment centers, data centers, office space, and 527 physical stores (520 in North America and 7 internationally), primarily under the Whole Foods Market brand acquired in August 2017. For the fiscal year ended December 31 2018, consolidated net sales were $232.9 billion (North America $141.4 billion, International $65.9 billion, AWS $25.7 billion), operating income was $12.4 billion (North America $7.3 billion, International loss of $2.1 billion, AWS $7.3 billion), and net income was $10.1 billion. Cash provided by operating activities was $30.7 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $41.3 billion at year‑end. The company faces intense competition across its retail, cloud, and device businesses and identifies numerous risks including rapid growth, seasonality, foreign‑exchange exposure, regulatory changes, litigation, and reliance on key personnel. No material unresolved staff comments or mine‑safety disclosures were reported. Executive officers include Jeffrey P. Bezos (President, CEO, and Chairman), Andrew R. Jassy (CEO AWS), Brian T. Olsavsky (CFO), and others. As of January 23 2019, 491.2 million shares of common stock were outstanding.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to generate buy signals when price moves above it and sell signals when it moves below. It applies to stocks, forex, commodities, and crypto markets. Backtesting shows it works well in trending assets like Bitcoin but underperforms in mean-reverting markets like stocks. Combining it with indicators like RSI or Bollinger Bands can improve signal confirmation. Risk management includes stop-loss orders and position sizing. Adding a 200-day moving average as a trend filter can reduce trades and increase average gains but may not make it profitable in stock markets.

Mark Palmer forwarded a class action complaint filed by Pamela Gordon against major energy companies (Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and others) alleging they manipulated California's wholesale electricity market in 2000 through improper use of real-time data, withholding generation capacity, and scheduling transmission flows to create artificial shortages. This resulted in wholesale electricity prices soaring from $32.31/MWh in August 1999 to $166.24/MWh in August 2000, causing retail rates for San Diego Gas & Electric customers to triple and resulting in over $4 billion in overcharges during summer 2000. The complaint cites FERC's finding that prices were "unjust and unreasonable" and includes causes of action for antitrust violations (Cartwright Act), unfair business practices, consumer legal remedies act violations, and unconscionability.

Passage argues that law’s effectiveness often hinges on enacting statutes lacking public excitement because interested parties oppose them. The Government has shifted to criminal prosecution in trust and interstate‑commerce cases where success is plausible, after initially using civil actions. Criminal penalties, especially imprisonment and heavy fines, have produced deterrence. Judge Holt of a New York district court emphasized a recent case where a railroad granted rebates amounting to over one‑fifth of the tariff, deliberately and over months, with the intent to drive competitors out. The court described the offense as more serious than common crimes because it was premeditated, committed by educated businesspeople on behalf of a corporation that enjoys state‑granted privileges and must treat citizens equally. It noted difficulty of proof, few prior prosecutions, and imposed a penalty proportional to the gravity, placing the principal penalty on the corporation rather than the individual traffic manager.

MU hosted its annual Veterans Day ceremony as part of the National Remembrance Day Roll Call. Keynote speaker Col. Konektadong Pinoy Act became law on August 24, 2025, aiming to remove barriers to competition in the Philippine telecom market and enable Virtual Network Operators to compete with PLDT. PLDT, a market leader in fixed‑line and mobile broadband, faces new entrants during a period of declining profitability and slowing growth. Capital Cycle analysis suggests the law could cause excess investment in a mature, highly penetrated industry, further depressing profitability. Despite PHI's attractive valuation, the author views the threat of new entrants as sufficient reason to avoid investing in the company.

Passports expire two years after issuance; a new passport requires a new application, and a naturalized citizen may use old passport instead of a naturalization certificate if original application had sufficient naturalization data. A passport may cover applicant’s spouse, minor children and servants if ages and allegiance are listed; others need separate passports. Fee is one dollar, payable by currency or postal money order to disbursing clerk; checks are not accepted. Department does not obtain visas for passports; blank forms are supplied to applicants. Address communications to Passport Bureau. Secretary of State may deny a passport for unlawful or improper purpose. In insular possessions, applications are made to chief executive or, if abroad, to a diplomatic or consular officer abroad; passports are not issued to non‑citizens or those who have only declared intent, and applications must be a sworn affidavit with required personal details.

Small group differentiation is an instructional approach that tailors content, process, products, and learning environment to meet diverse student needs in elementary and higher education. Supported by constructivism and sociocultural theory, it addresses increasing demographic diversity (e.g., U.S. public school enrollment in fall 2018 was 47% White, 15% Black, 27% Hispanic, and 5% Asian; the share speaking a language other than English rose from 11% in 1980 to 20.3% in 2010, with English language learners exceeding 10% in ten states) and disability prevalence (e.g., 15% of public‑school students receiving IDEA services, 32% with specific learning disabilities). Effective differentiation relies on flexible goals, ongoing assessment, respectful challenging tasks, collaboration, and student autonomy. Implementation challenges include time‑intensive planning, large class sizes, limited administrative support, and a one‑size‑fits‑all culture in higher education. Research gaps exist regarding comparative effectiveness and longitudinal outcomes. Future studies could examine long‑term impacts and learning‑style‑based strategies.

The Atlas of Human-AI Interaction is a framework using large language models to synthesize empirical findings from over 1,000 human-AI interaction research papers. The system extracted 2,037 findings structured as triplets (cause, relationship, effect) and built a knowledge graph with 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges. It provides three visualization modes: 3D Graph View for landscape exploration, Cause-Effect View for relationship tracing, and Paper View for detailed investigation. Analysis identified 24 thematic clusters across human, AI, and concept types, and found five concepts at structural holes (LLM, generative AI, trust, chatbot, agent) representing integration opportunities across disconnected research communities. A user study with 20 experts showed Atlas helped identify research gaps and discover cross-disciplinary connections, though participants noted limitations in domain-specific applicability and need for deeper information and temporal analysis. The study concludes Atlas offers value for researchers and practitioners but requires further development for broader adoption.

The 4-3 defense, popular in the NFL and at all football levels, features four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs. The 3-technique defensive tackle is considered the most critical position. Personnel include 5-technique defensive ends, a 1-technique nose guard (the largest lineman), a 3-technique tackle, and linebackers ranging from the biggest (Sam) to smallest and most athletic (Will). Strengths include strong run defense due to seven defenders in the box and gap-sound assignments, while weaknesses involve vulnerability to modern spread offenses and personnel specificity, often requiring a nickel package. Offenses attack it by spreading the field and forcing linebackers out of the box or using extra blockers to outflank the edge. Common blitzes include the Will edge blitz and zone blitz with a dropping defensive end. Popular coverages are Tampa 2 (with a deep-dropping Mike linebacker) and Cover 3. Notable teams using the 4-3 include the early 2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers (famous for Tampa 2), the 2006 Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic HS in Illinois, which won multiple state titles with the defense under coach Mike Bukovsky.

Pan Finance, a global financial intelligence platform with over 200,000 readers in 150 countries, publishes a series of news items covering banking M&A (Fifth Third acquires Comerica for $10.9B, Santander UK CEO departure before TSB merger), AI market developments (Bank of England warns of AI bubble risk, Google launches Gemini Enterprise for corporate clients), commodity movements (gold above $4,000, oil price fall), infrastructure investments (Poland $5.5B NATO fuel link, U.S. freezes $18B New York funds), and other corporate stories (AMD chip deal, Tesla affordable EV speculation, Bezos space data‑centre plan, OpenAI $500B valuation). The featured article details Google’s new AI platform, Gemini Enterprise, offering advanced Gemini Ultra models, enterprise‑grade data governance, security and compliance tools, and integration with Google Cloud and Workspace. The product targets finance, healthcare and manufacturing sectors, competing with Microsoft, Amazon and OpenAI while emphasising transparency and accountability as differentiators. Google aims to monetise AI advances by enabling scalable enterprise deployment but faces challenges in proving reliability and delivering measurable returns.

Ray Dalio’s All‑Weather Portfolio was created by Bridgewater Associates to perform in any economic climate—inflation, deflation, or stagflation—by diversifying across stocks, bonds, and commodities. It uses a risk‑parity approach, balancing asset‑class risk rather than seeking maximum total return, which results in a defensive, “sleep‑well‑at‑night” profile. Typical allocations include a large share of bonds, modest stock exposure, and a smaller commodity component, often implemented with low‑cost ETFs such as TLT, IEF, VNQ, GLD, and DBC. Rebalancing is recommended at least once a year (quarterly at most) and is best done in a tax‑deferred account. Back‑tests from 1970 to 2022 show lower annual returns than equities (CAGR roughly 4–5 % versus 6–7 % for the S&P 500) but substantially smaller maximum drawdowns (≈17 % vs. 55 % for stocks). During major sell‑offs—2008/09 crisis, the March 2020 Covid‑19 crash, and the 2022 bear market—the portfolio fell 12–17 % while the S&P 500 dropped 33–55 %. Leveraging the strategy can raise returns (CAGR ~6.5 % at 1.5× leverage) but increases drawdowns to ~25 %. The All‑Weather Portfolio suits retirees, FIRE‑oriented investors, and risk‑averse individuals seeking capital preservation over aggressive growth. It does not guarantee future performance, and its high bond allocation can suffer when bonds sell off, as seen in 2022.

Mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding $31 per month per child in child support, arguing it was too low and that abatement during father's visitation was improper. The appellate court increased support to $65 per month per child, effective from the decision date, finding the original amount insufficient despite acknowledging that father's expenses during visitation should be factored in. No costs to either party.

‘Please, Continue (Hamlet)’ by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, premiered in Switzerland in 2011, is staged at the Melbourne Festival in a courtroom with judges and barristers; a jury of twelve audience members delivers a guilty or not‑guilty verdict within 20 minutes. Duyvendak, a visual‑arts artist, and Bernat were united by interest in Guantanamo trial transcripts, prompting them to study criminal trials in France and Switzerland and film 12 Angry Men. Their production inserts a fictional Hamlet case into a trial setting, adapting to each country’s legal system and performed in jury‑system countries. A case of a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father, unredacted from a lawyer friend, provides context; creators’ opposing views on conviction are used to provoke audience deliberation. Performances show how legal reasoning can shift audience opinions and reveal the complexity of justice, attracting legal professionals to observe the effect.

A systematic review and bibliometric analysis of 270 journal articles on the metaverse in education (Scopus, 2015‑July 2024) identified three main research questions. The study applied PRISMA guidelines, used VOSviewer for visualisation, and required English‑language journal articles, published between 2015 and 2024, focusing on the metaverse and education. Publication trends showed no articles before 2020, a modest rise in 2020–2021 (four per year), a sharp increase in 2022 (36 articles) and a peak in 2023 (131 articles), with 91 articles already recorded in 2024. South Korea, China and the United States were the most productive countries in terms of article count, while South Korea, the United Kingdom and China led in citation impact. The journals contributing the most articles were IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies (21 articles, 237 citations) and Sustainability (Switzerland) (18 articles, 447 citations). The most cited article was Dwivedi et al. (2022) (890 citations). Keyword co‑occurrence analysis produced six clusters, with the most frequent terms being “metaverse” (192), “virtual reality” (54), “education” (28), “augmented reality” (23) and “artificial intelligence” (18). Thematic clusters revealed two broad research areas: the use of metaverse technologies to create immersive virtual learning environments (e.g., medical, engineering, primary education applications) and investigations of users’ perceptions and attitudes, often employing the Technology Acceptance Model. The discussion notes that metaverse platforms enhance learner engagement and motivation but are still limited by a lack of longitudinal studies and geographic concentration in East Asia and the United States. The authors conclude that the metaverse offers transformative, time‑ and space‑independent educational possibilities and recommend future research on long‑term outcomes, scalability and cross‑cultural implementation.

Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department affirmed the lower court order on December 10, 1912, in Jones v. Dow, awarding respondent $10 costs and disbursements. Justice Thomas dissented, stating the ex parte order deprived plaintiff of a statutory right to reply. Justice Carr did not vote.

During Severe Weather Awareness Week, Michigan emergency officials urge residents to join a statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday. Kelenske advises finding low cover and interior rooms, conducting drills, monitoring broadcasts and distinguishing watches from warnings; signs include a dark sky, large hail and a freight‑train roar. Residents should also prepare 72‑hour emergency kits with water, food, a NOAA weather radio and essential documents. If severe weather hits April 19, the drill moves to Thursday 1 p.m.

Good transition defense starts with sound offensive habits: protecting the ball, taking high‑percentage shots, securing offensive rebounds, and maintaining defensive balance so opponents cannot push the ball. When these offensive elements are in place, fast‑break opportunities are limited. Transition defense itself follows a set of core principles: players must “seek the level of the ball,” sprint back with constant ball vision, never retreat with their backs to the ball, and play up the lane between their opponent and the ball. Defenders are taught to jam the rebounder, deny the outlet pass to the primary ballhandler, force the offense into extra passes, and contain dribble penetration toward the sideline. Outnumbered situations (2‑on‑1, 3‑on‑2, and breakaways) are handled by containing the dribbler, forcing passes, taking charges, and sprinting back to create a numerical advantage; a successful stop in these moments is called a “Really Big Play.” After any turnover, missed shot, blocked shot, or missed free throw, the closest defender jams the rebounder, the point‑guard’s defender denies the outlet, and the remaining players sprint back to protect the basket, matching up against the nearest offensive players. Sideline “pushpoint” pressure slows the ballhandler, and secondary defenders assume helpside positions to prevent easy lay‑ups. Game strategy emphasizes taking care of the ball, hard offensive rebounding, scouting the opponent’s early‑offense patterns, denying the primary ballhandler, immediately substituting players who jog back, and applying full‑court or half‑court pressure after made baskets. Coaching objectives focus on developing awareness of transition importance, good shot selection, rebounding effort, defensive balance, sprinting back, and the ability to defend out‑numbered situations. Teaching uses the whole‑part‑whole method, and drills are designed to improve sprint‑back, contain, jam, outlet‑denial, and transition‑game execution.

The document specifies the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for communication between SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors via VMGEXIT. The VALID_BITMAP field indicates which GHCB fields contain valid data, with guests and hypervisors required to clear and set appropriate bits before each NAE event. VMGEXIT processing requires disabling interrupts and preemption when updating the GHCB. NAE events include: Page State Change (for private/shared page conversion and PSMASH/UNSMASH operations); SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request (using request/response pages and certificate data identified by GUIDs); AP Creation (creating vCPUs with VMSA pages via RMPADJUST); #HV Doorbell Page (registering guest physical addresses for hypervisor injection exceptions); #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, and APIC ID List (providing virtual APIC functionality); SNP Run VMPL (changing VMPL levels); SNP TIO Guest Request (binding trusted devices with MMIO validation and TDISP support); Secure AVIC (managing guest-owned APIC backing pages); and Termination Request. Guest identification of SEV-ES support requires specific CPUID and MSR values. SMP booting under SEV-ES requires the AP Reset Hold mechanism since hypervisors cannot update measured registers; SEV-SNP provides the AP Creation NAE event as an alternative. The AP Jump Table mechanism allows UEFI to communicate AP boot vectors to the OS. SNP Restricted Injection limits host interrupt delivery to #HV doorbell notifications, using PendingEvent (vector number and NMI/MC flags) and NoEoiRequired fields for optimized EOI handling. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this specification.

During Alcohol Awareness Month, the Navy promotes Pier Pressure app to help Sailors make responsible drinking choices. The app tracks drink types and counts, estimates calories and push‑ups needed to burn them, integrates Uber and Lyft for safe rides, and has been used over 30,000 times. Available on iTunes and Google Play.

Dow fell 424 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq dropped 1.3% and 1.7% respectively. Caterpillar rose on earnings then fell 6.2% after CFO said first quarter would be high‑water mark. 3M fell 7% and Alphabet fell 5% despite profit increase. 10‑year Treasury yield rose above 3%, raising concerns of Fed tightening.

Appellants Hemsell and Columbian Fuel Corporation appealed a $30,890 judgment for appellees in a wrongful death suit after J. W. Summers died in a car collision with Hemsell, an employee of the corporation. The appellate court reversed the judgment due to errors in jury charges: (1) the charge for the wife's damages assumed a 34½-year life expectancy; (2) the charge for the mother's damages assumed a 20-year life expectancy; (3) the charge for the minor son allowed non-pecuniary recovery for loss of love and care; (4) the charge for the minor daughter included a specific item for college education without sufficient evidence and was on the weight of evidence; (5) the court failed to instruct the jury to exclude sorrow and grief; and (6) counsel made improper remarks that the court should have struck. The court also upheld the refusal to submit sole proximate cause and new and independent cause issues. The case was remanded.

A security researcher discovered a pre‑installed keylogger in Synaptics touchpad drivers shipped on hundreds of HP notebook, tablet and other device models. HP confirmed the finding, released patches for more than 450 products, and stated that no customer data was accessed. The keylogger is disabled by default but could be activated by modifying a registry entry. This is the second keylogger issue for HP in 2017; in May a similar debug‑trace keylogger was found in Conexant audio drivers.

Police in Xinjiang’s Pishan County shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five and injured ten. Authorities called the attackers thugs, restored order and opened an investigation. Previous similar incidents include a 2015 colliery attack killing 16 and a 2014 Kunming station attack killing 31.

Four MLS matches had early and late kickoffs. Bořek Dočkal, a Czech import, posted a goal and two assists in a win over Chicago; Union unbeaten in four, conceding two goals. Ilsinho scored after a move on Bastian Schweinsteiger, and New England earned a draw via Bunbury's penalty.

Johnny Juzang scored 20 points in 14 minutes in the Timberwolves' preseason, earning a roster spot on a non‑guaranteed contract. The 24‑year‑old former third‑team All‑American has shot over 38% from three over the past two seasons, and JJ Redick said he could become a long‑term bench shooter for Minnesota. The Wolves' young bench includes Rob Dillingham and Terrence Shannon Jr. Juzang is 9‑of‑15 from three this preseason.

Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic researchers compiled peer‑reviewed evidence and a guideline recommending elimination of the widely used CK‑MB blood test for evaluating suspected heart attacks. Their report, published in JAMA Internal Medicine, cites ACC/European guidelines and five studies showing CK‑MB is no longer an effective cardiac damage biomarker and can be safely removed from practice. The work is the first of a series of implementation guides from the High Value Practice Academic Alliance (HVPAA), a coalition of over 80 academic institutions across 15 specialties. The guideline outlines four steps to phase out CK‑MB: a hospital‑wide education campaign, partnership with cardiology, emergency medicine, internal medicine and laboratory stakeholders to remove CK‑MB from standard order sets, creation of a best‑practice alert in electronic ordering systems, and monitoring of test use and patient outcomes. Despite prior recommendations, a 2013 survey found 77 % of U.S. labs still use CK‑MB, adding an estimated $416 million annually to diagnostic costs. Cardiac troponin, identified as the optimal biomarker since 2000, is a stronger predictor of mortality and disease severity.

Researchers used smoothed-particle hydrodynamic simulations combined with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer to create synthetic observations of a collapsing prestellar core modeled as a critical Bonnor-Ebert sphere. They compared infall velocities derived from molecular line profiles using the Myers et al. (1996) method with the actual mass-weighted velocities in the simulation. The study found that calculated infall velocities significantly underestimate true values, often by an order of magnitude, depending on the molecular tracer and aperture size. CS lines provided estimates closest to the true velocity but only reached about half the actual value, while HCO+ lines produced values up to ten times lower. The authors conclude that mass accretion rates derived from these observational techniques likely underestimate true values by potentially an order of magnitude, and suggest that non-thermal velocity dispersion from optically thin lines may serve as a more reliable diagnostic of infall speed in simple systems.

An Indian‑origin surgeon, Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri, was banned from UK practice after a tribunal found he abused his position by sending a love letter to a patient; he was struck off the register and plans to appeal.

Tesla, Inc. reported that effective March 11 2021 Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking, now leading the Tesla Semi program and its related charging and servicing networks.

Sony launched an instant rebate and trade‑in program in the US through Sept 30 2017, offering up to $300 savings on select full‑frame cameras, an extra $500 with a trade‑in, up to $200 on A7 bodies and up to $100 on select lenses, with free shipping. Discounted models include Alpha a7R II, a7S II and their 24‑70mm f/4 kits, with lens discounts up to $100.

Compass Minerals International (CMP) holds a "Buy" rating due to attractive valuation and operational improvements. Revenue and volumes are rising in salt and plant nutrition segments, while cost-cutting initiatives are boosting cash flow and EBITDA. Despite higher net debt and leverage compared to industry peers, the stock trades at lower valuation multiples. Management projects continued top-line growth for 2025, though leverage risk limits the rating to "Buy" rather than "Strong Buy."

The CANSLIM method, developed by William O'Neill of Investor's Business Daily, is an acronym for seven criteria used to identify strong-performing stocks. Backtests show it has beaten the S&P 500 since 2003 (18% CAGR vs 9%), but this outperformance comes with higher volatility and larger drawdowns, possibly due to its small-cap exposure. The IBD 50 provides a weekly list of 50 stocks meeting CANSLIM criteria. The method focuses on long-term investing through strong fundamentals, positive earnings, growth, institutional sponsorship, and stocks in uptrends. Risks include market volatility and potential capital loss. Recent performance has underperformed the S&P 500, and backtesting the method is difficult due to its requirement for both fundamental and technical data.

Player says they needed a win and credited Rucchin’s two goals and the team’s overall effort. He notes they started well, kept control, and will stay consistent in preparation, with Mike helping them stay ready. He says the first two games in New Jersey were atypical and that returning to Anaheim restored their legs and performance. He emphasizes tightening defensively, leading by example rather than speaking up, and recalls a hard stick hit he recovered from quickly after a medical check. He describes playoff competition as intense and acknowledges fond memories of a comeback win involving Rucchin.

After the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge welcomed their third child, a baby boy born on St George's Day at St Mary's Hospital, Paddington, weighing 8 lb 7 oz, Peter Crouch posted a joke about the photo that received over 22,000 retweets. Abbey Clancy replied, and Crystal Palace posted a tweet about the name.

Mark Jackson (former player and coach, now ESPN analyst) and Jeff Van Gundy warn that Golden State’s habit of trailing early and relying on a “Superman” switch to come back is a concern. The Warriors led the NBA in third‑quarter scoring and overcame a 17‑point first‑quarter deficit in Game 6 of the Western Conference finals, outscoring Houston 64‑25 in the second half. They also erased a 15‑point second‑quarter deficit in Game 7 (58‑38 second‑half). However, in Games 2, 4 and 5 they failed to flip the switch, losing despite defensive lapses and turnovers. Both coaches note that repeatedly digging early holes can eventually catch up with a team. Historical examples of comeback performers (Silky Sullivan, Dave Wottle, the Oakland A’s) illustrate this pattern.

Closed‑end equity mutual funds listed on exchanges trade at discounts to net asset values (NAVs). Investors buy at these discounts to profit at maturity, but liquidity forces sellers to accept them. Discount size depends on maturity and tax treatment: under a year yields larger discounts; over a year, smaller ones (5‑15% for five‑year, 5‑7% for three‑year). Examples include Reliance Close Ended Fund Series A (10 % discount) and HDFC Equity Opportunities Fund (6 % discount). Experts suggest focusing on schemes with assets above Rs 250 crore.

Airbus CEO Tom Enders announced at the DLD tech conference a plan to test an autonomous flying car prototype (Project Vahana) that aims to transport multiple riders in a helicopter‑style vehicle and reduce urban congestion. The vehicle will use clean technology and lower infrastructure costs; a functional prototype is targeted by 2017 and service by 2021. Other firms such as Uber, Urban Aeronautics (Cormorant) and AeroMobil (3.0) are also developing VTOL or convertible flying vehicles, with investments from Skype co‑founder (10 million) and Google co‑founder Larry Page.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Ben’Ary was abruptly fired while prosecuting a terrorism case involving the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. A note attributed to Ben’Ary posted on his door said the dismissal stemmed from a false social‑media claim by a pro‑Trump commentator linking him to former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco. The letter accused DOJ’s political leadership of prioritizing punishment of the President’s perceived enemies over national security and of removing career officials from U.S. attorney offices and the FBI, thereby making America less safe.

A light emitting diode device and a method of manufacturing it are disclosed. The device comprises a thin film transistor substrate having a plurality of light emitting areas, a first and a second diode electrode on the substrate, a first passivation pattern between the electrodes, a plurality of micro light emitting diodes on the first passivation pattern, and first and second bridge patterns that electrically connect the first and second diode electrodes to the micro LEDs, respectively. Each micro LED includes a cylindrical light‑emitting material with a protective layer and a p‑type semiconductor layer, an intermediate layer and an n‑type semiconductor layer. The sidewalls of each micro LED and the sidewall of the first passivation pattern lie on the same plane, reducing step height and preventing breakage of the bridge patterns. The manufacturing method forms the first passivation pattern, micro LEDs, and a second passivation pattern using a single mask process that includes two etching steps: a first anisotropic etch and a second more isotropic etch that uses an oxygen‑containing additive gas, thereby aligning the sidewalls and completing the device.

MLB wild‑card series feature three winner‑take‑all Game 3s on Thursday, the second time in baseball history such a scenario occurs. The Yankees won Game 2 to force a decisive game against the Red Sox, while the Guardians and Dodgers also forced Game 3s. The Tigers left a franchise‑record 15 baserunners in Game 2 and are 3‑for‑38 with runners in scoring position over three recent elimination games. The Padres‑Cubs series will hinge on bullpens, with Yu Darvish (2.56 ERA in six postseason starts) and Jameson Taillon (1.57 ERA in six recent starts) expected on short leashes. The Red Sox used six relievers in Game 2 and have limited options for Game 3, while the Yankees’ potent lineup could exploit early departures by Boston pitchers.

Aspen is replacing its Fourth of July fireworks with a 50‑drone show in Wagner Park on July 4 at 21:15 local time (03:15 GMT), citing wildfire risk and fire restrictions. The 15‑minute display is organized by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association and was inspired by the 2018 Winter Olympics drone show.

The United States national debt surpassed $21 trillion, adding $73 billion in a single day, $215 billion in February, and over $1 trillion in six months. Debt growth outpaced GDP: the economy grew 2.5% in real terms while debt rose 6%, expanding 36% faster proportionally. Over ten years, debt grew from $9.4 trillion to $21 trillion (123% increase) while GDP rose from $14.5 trillion to $19.7 trillion (36%). Debt is owed to Social Security, banks, and the Federal Reserve; default would cause severe financial crisis. Public attitudes toward debt range from ignoring it to believing it irrelevant to making preparations.

Jio Galaxy Club offers Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 (Rs 8,190) and Galaxy J7 Duo (Rs 16,990) with a Rs 2,750 cashback each via 55 Rs 50 vouchers. J2 buyers get 100GB extra data on Rs 198/299 plans, reducing its price to Rs 5,440; J7 Duo buyers receive double data (4GB/day on Rs 198, 6GB/day on Rs 299). Offers valid until 30 September, sold online and offline. J2 specs: 5‑inch qHD, Snapdragon 425, 2GB RAM, 8MP/5MP cameras, 2600mAh. J7 Duo specs: 5.5‑inch HD, Exynos 7 series, 4GB RAM, 13MP/5MP cameras, 3000mAh.

CFPB final rules require payday and auto‑title lenders to verify borrowers can repay within 30 days and limit account debits. Consumer groups say the rules target a model that relies on rollovers and rates exceeding 300 percent; a CFPB study found over 80 percent of loans are rolled over and 15 percent become sequences of ten or more loans. Agency estimates rules could halve loan volume and force the 16,000 stores in 35 states to close; fifteen states already ban such lenders. Industry group warns rule would devastate industry and push borrowers to unregulated markets. The rules take effect in 2019 and may be reversed by Congress, where Republicans have introduced legislation to weaken the agency. A Pew poll shows 70 percent of U.S. adults favor tighter regulation of payday lenders.

Sarcomas comprise over 170 mesenchymal tumors with limited response to first‑line chemotherapy (≈20%). Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) shows variable activity; predictive biomarkers in sarcomas are lacking because microsatellite instability is rare and tumor mutation burden is low. Epigenetic regulation of transposable elements (TEs) can affect antitumor immunity. This study tested whether baseline immune infiltrates and clinical outcomes after ICI are linked to TE expression and epigenetic regulators.  

Pre‑treatment biopsies from 67 patients with >10 sarcoma subtypes enrolled in three ICI trials were profiled by RNA‑sequencing. Unsupervised hierarchical clustering of immune cell estimates identified two groups: immune‑hot and immune‑cold. Immune‑hot tumors had higher overall response rates (30% vs 8.1%) and longer progression‑free survival (median 3.65 months vs 1.7 months). Immune‑hot status correlated with elevated checkpoint gene expression (CD274, CTLA4, LAG3) and matched previously described sarcoma immune classes.  

Lasso logistic regression showed that expression of 1002 intergenic TEs (R²=0.29) and 532 epigenetic regulators (R²=0.19) better predicted immune type than a model using only subtype and batch. Signature features included six TE subfamilies (MER57F, MER45A, Tigger17a, MER61F, LTR104_Mam, HERVL74.int) and the transcription factor IKZF1. TE score and IKZF1 expression correlated positively with innate immune pathways (cGAS‑STING, type I/II interferon, antigen processing, CD8⁺ T‑cell effector) and with PD‑L1. Conditional independence analysis indicated that TEs largely drive immune type and interact with IKZF1.  

In an independent TCGA cohort of 190 sarcomas, immune‑hot tumors showed improved overall survival (37.5 months vs 25.5 months) and similar TE/IKZF1 associations. Limitations include the small, heterogeneous cohort and differences between the validation cohort (untreated primary tumors) and the original ICI‑treated patients. The findings suggest that pretreatment immune status predicts ICI response and that TE de‑repression and IKZF1 expression may serve as biomarkers; targeting epigenetic silencing of TEs could be explored to convert immune‑cold sarcomas to an immune‑hot phenotype.

A writing program at Seattle Children’s, run by the Pediatric Advanced Care Team, helps parents like Meagan Holt cope with their child’s terminal condition (Zellweger Syndrome) by journaling with a coach, providing an emotional outlet and a sense of empowerment, calm and relief. The program relies on donations.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on October 27, 2022, announcing its third‑quarter 2022 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information on non‑GAAP measures (Exhibit 99.2). The company’s common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol AMZN. The report is signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath town‑centre store after 33 years, citing insufficient free parking, rising business rates, and persistent anti‑social behaviour linked to a bench placed outside a cheap‑liquor shop after a street‑improvement scheme. The company says staff have had to deal with fights, vandalism, drug needles and public fouling, and many customers now avoid the area. The council states that the street works were completed for the town’s benefit, the bench was removed about a year ago after being used for anti‑social behaviour, and a 600‑space multi‑storey car park offers free parking after 3 pm. The Welsh Government notes that business‑rate relief schemes support nearly 15 000 small firms in Wales. Happy Home Furnishers intends to continue trading at other sites and may seek a new Neath location.

The study investigates physics teachers’ scepticism toward physics education research (SSSE) and its relation to teaching practice. It notes a gap in research on teachers’ perspectives and two motivations: the theory‑practice gap and the assumed value of evidence‑based teaching. The paper defines SSSE as scepticism about any positive impact of science‑education research on teaching.

The research addresses three questions: (1) teachers’ attitudes toward the value of physics‑education research; (2) types of teachers who are sceptical; (3) associations between professional variables and SSSE.

A two‑step mixed‑methods design was used. Step 1 involved guideline‑based interviews with 13 in‑service German physics teachers (average teaching experience ≈ 12.5 years). Content analysis yielded seven main attitude categories (e.g., research is relevant, research is too theoretical, findings cannot be implemented, poor researcher‑practitioner cooperation). Sceptical attitudes predominated, though some teachers expressed positive views.

Step 2 surveyed 174 German/Austrian physics teachers (mean age ≈ 44.5 years, mean experience ≈ 14.6 years). Twenty‑two Likert‑scale items were derived from interview categories. Exploratory factor analysis identified four factors: relevance for the individual teacher, feasibility of findings for practice, relevance for general teaching practice, and cooperation between research and schools. Latent profile analysis (LPA) of the 14 retained items produced a four‑profile solution: “Sceptical Ones” (14 %), “Uncertain Ones” (27 %), “Undersupplied Ones” (41 %), and “Research Advocates” (18 %). Profiles differed in scepticism levels but all showed scepticism about researcher‑practitioner cooperation.

Multinomial logistic regression with teaching experience, teacher‑education type, school type, doctoral degree, and frequency of reading instructional journals as predictors (reference: Sceptical Ones) showed only frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership (higher reading frequency increased odds of belonging to Uncertain Ones or Research Advocates). Other professional variables did not reach significance.

Limitations include the small, purposeful interview sample, convenience sampling in the survey, possible Hawthorne effect, and reliance on modal assignment in LPA.

The authors conclude that many physics teachers are sceptical about the practical value of research and the research‑practice link, and suggest integrating research more visibly into teacher education and improving communication between researchers and practitioners.

Ravens trade outside linebacker Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth‑round pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman. Oweh, 26, recorded a career‑high 10 sacks last season but has zero sacks in five games this season, seeing a career‑low 45% of defensive snaps; he will be an unrestricted free agent after the season. The move frees roughly $8 million in cap space. Baltimore, which is allowing an NFL‑high 35.4 points per game and ranks 31st in pass defense (262.4 yards per game), also signed veteran safety Gardner‑Johnson and added another safety to the practice squad. Gilman, 28, was a key part of the Chargers’ top‑ranked defense last season, thriving as a deep safety before moving to nickel, and the Chargers needed an edge rusher more than a safety. Oweh gives the Chargers a young pass‑rusher with an 11% pressure rate (33rd in the NFL, second‑highest on the team). The Ravens are 1‑4, matching the worst start in franchise history.

At the 18th VADA Forum in Lilongwe, Treasury Secretary Ben Botolo urged African nations to adopt electronic fiscal devices to combat tax noncompliance, citing cash economies as a barrier. Malawi noted progress in electronic monitoring and a pending Tax Administration Act. VADA chair Henry Saka called for measures to fight tax evasion. VADA has members—Malawi, Zambia, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda—and supports other countries.

The lecture continues the discussion of the scalar‑field propagator, which can be interpreted either as a transition amplitude for a particle to go from one space‑time point to another or as a correlation function of the field. The two-point functions G⁺(x,x′) and G⁻(x,x′) are introduced, together with the retarded, advanced and Feynman propagators G_R, G_A and G_F. These are obtained by different ways of going around the poles of the Fourier representation in the complex ω plane; equivalently one uses the “ε‑prescription” to move the singularities infinitesimally above or below the real axis. G_R is proportional to θ(t−t′), G_A to θ(t′−t), and G_F contains both time‑ordered and anti‑ordered contributions.

In the free‑field theory the vacuum n‑point correlation functions factor into sums of products of the two‑point function because creation and annihilation operators must be paired. Operators such as φ², φ³ or the Hamiltonian density are composite operators; they become singular when multiplied at the same point and require renormalization.

To introduce interactions the simplest term added to the Lagrangian is λ φ⁴. The resulting equation of motion is nonlinear and cannot be solved exactly, so one treats λ as a small coupling and expands perturbatively.

Scattering experiments are the primary means to probe interactions. The S‑matrix is defined as the evolution operator from t = −∞ to t = +∞, connecting initial and final states of free particles. Writing S = 1 + iT, momentum conservation forces a delta function into T, and the remaining part M_{αβ} is the scattering amplitude. The S‑matrix is unitary (probability preserving) and commutes with any symmetry generator of the Hamiltonian.

The LSZ reduction formula states that the scattering amplitude M_{αβ} can be extracted from time‑ordered vacuum expectation values of the fields. The next step will be to develop the path‑integral formulation for handling interacting theories.

A sidelink positioning method and apparatus for communication systems where terminal devices determine positions using sidelink signals instead of relying solely on network device measurements. In June 2014 a Wall Street Journal article reported that Hertz Global Holdings would have to restate its 2011–2013 financial statements because accounting problems were more extensive than earlier disclosed; Hertz’s stock fell about 9% that day. Auto‑industry analyst Abby Devins investigated whether the issues were connected to Hertz’s large rental fleet and how they might affect future vehicle‑acquisition plans.

The U.S. car‑rental industry generated roughly $36 billion in revenue in 2013, with three companies—Enterprise Holdings, Avis Budget Group and Hertz Global Holdings—together holding about 71% of the market. Hertz originated in 1918, was sold to John D. Hertz in 1923, later owned by General Motors and Ford, bought by a private‑equity group in 2005 and taken public again in 2006. By the end of 2013 it operated ~12,000 locations in 145 countries, employed ~30,000 people and owned a fleet of more than 700,000 cars (524,000 in the U.S., 179,500 internationally).

From a single‑brand, on‑airport business‑travel focus, Hertz expanded into a multi‑brand portfolio (Hertz, Dollar, Thrifty, Firefly) after acquiring Dollar Thrifty in 2012 and entered the Chinese market via a 20% stake in China Auto Rental. It also provides commercial fleet leasing and management services through the Donlen subsidiary and runs an industrial‑equipment rental business.

From 2011 to 2013 Hertz’s total revenue grew about 30% and net income more than doubled; depreciation represented roughly 25% of total expenses, and revenue‑earning equipment accounted for over half of total assets. The company’s stock generally tracked the S&P 500 until mid‑2012, after which it outperformed, and Hertz posted record revenue and EBITDA in 2013.

Depreciation of revenue‑earning equipment is calculated using estimated useful life and residual value; Hertz applies straight‑line depreciation over the expected holding period and adjusts rates quarterly for market conditions such as vehicle age, mileage and manufacturer incentives. The fleet includes program cars (with manufacturer‑guaranteed depreciation) and non‑program cars (subject to residual‑value risk).

Exhibits provide historical useful‑life ranges, program‑car purchase percentages, used‑vehicle value indices and financial data for Hertz and competitor Avis Budget Group from 2006 through 2013, including gross revenue‑earning equipment, depreciation expense, gains or losses on asset sales, and income before taxes.

Devins compiled comparable data for Hertz and Avis to assess how depreciation practices might relate to Hertz’s larger‑than‑anticipated accounting adjustments.

The passage discusses AI’s multifaceted societal impact across four domains: human cognition and learning, social division of labor, social science research, and regulatory frameworks.

**AI and Human Cognition**
AI augments cognitive abilities, learning capacity, and creativity, but poses risks such as over-reliance, which may undermine critical thinking and skill internalization. Mitigation involves selective delegation of tasks, encouraging active learning, and fostering critical mindsets. AI can personalize education, shifting focus from rote memorization to adaptive, interactive learning. However, concerns remain about whether AI will replace human intelligence, requiring efforts to position AI as an enhancer of cognition rather than a replacement.

**Reformation of Social Division of Labor**
AI reduces knowledge scarcity, blurring job boundaries and challenging traditional social structures built on specialized knowledge. The rise of the gig economy, enabled by algorithmic management, offers flexibility but lacks labor protections, risking worker exploitation. Policies like flexible contracts and tailored welfare systems are suggested. AI also shifts collaboration toward dynamic, network-based models, empowering individuals as independent innovators and fostering cross-industry partnerships.

**AI in Social Science Research**
AI, particularly LLMs, offers scalable data synthesis and automated analysis, reducing barriers to research. LLMs can simulate demographic behaviors and assist with stance detection, sentiment analysis, and coding tasks. However, risks include biases, oversimplification, and ethical concerns like misinformation generation. LLMs may aid in hypothesis generation for social theories but require human oversight to ensure validity. Effective human-AI collaboration is emphasized.

**Regulatory Evolution**
Rapid AI advancement creates legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, deepfakes, and bias amplification. Existing frameworks struggle with AI’s complexity, and gaps exist between technology developers, policymakers, and international regulators. Proposed solutions include top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and governments, alongside bottom-up mechanisms for continuous risk reporting and regulation updates. The goal is human-centered, safe, and trustworthy AI development through inclusive governance.

Unused inputs of the TLV321/2x comparators must not be tied together; instead each input must be connected to any voltage within the specified input range that provides a minimum of 50 mV differential (e.g., ground on one input and a reference or V+ on the other). The device includes 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis (VHYST) that, together with the threshold (VTH) and offset (VOS), defines the actual trip points and reduces sensitivity to noise.

The family offers two output stages. The push‑pull output (TLV321x) can both source and sink current, eliminating the need for an external pull‑up, and must never be connected to another output. Direct shorts to the opposite supply can cause thermal runaway; a series current‑limiting resistor is recommended if shorts are possible. Unused push‑pull outputs must be left floating. The open‑drain output (TLV322x) is a sinking‑only stage that allows the logic level to be pulled up to any external voltage up to 5.5 V independent of the comparator supply; TI recommends pull‑up resistor currents between 100 µA and 1 mA, with lower values improving rise time at the cost of higher VOL and power dissipation. Large pull‑up resistors (>1 MΩ) create exponential rise times due to RC time constants. Shorts to a voltage source must be avoided; a current‑limiting resistor is advised. Unused open‑drain outputs may be left floating or tied to V‑.

ESD protection clamps inputs to ±0.2 V beyond the rails; for low‑impedance sources a series resistor should limit transient currents to ≤10 mA. An internal power‑on‑reset (POR) holds the output low for up to 32 µs after VPOR reaches 1.65 V, ensuring a known start‑up state for both output types.

Propagation delay (tpLH, tpHL) is measured from the midpoint of the input transition to the output and can differ between rising and falling edges; smaller overdrive voltages (especially <100 mV) increase delay. The output must be treated as a high‑speed digital device, and proper layout techniques are required.

External hysteresis can be added to prevent chatter when the input is near the offset voltage. For an inverting configuration a three‑resistor network referenced to VCC defines high‑to‑low (VA1) and low‑to‑high (VA2) trip voltages and total hysteresis (ΔVA). For a non‑inverting configuration a two‑resistor network with a reference voltage provides VIN1 and VIN2 thresholds; hysteresis equals VIN1 – VIN2. Both configurations add to the internal 1.8 mV hysteresis.

A typical low‑side current‑sensing circuit uses an amplifier to amplify the shunt voltage and a comparator to detect an over‑current threshold; bypass capacitors (0.1 µF low‑ESR) must be placed close to each device’s supply pin, and narrow output current pulses require a solid ground plane. Layout guidelines include minimizing input‑output coupling, using series resistors on inputs, adding a low‑value series resistor on outputs to damp ringing, and employing controlled‑impedance traces with back‑termination for long routes.

Reference design notes (SBOA219, SNOA997, SBOA313) and application briefs provide further detail on hysteresis circuits. Support resources include TI E2E forums, product‑folder notification registration, and the listed trademarks.

President Andrew Johnson transmitted to the House of Representatives additional correspondence with General U.S. Grant and written statements from five Cabinet members describing a Cabinet meeting on January 14, 1868. The meeting concerned Grant’s role as Secretary of War ad interim following the suspension of Edwin Stanton. Johnson alleged that Grant had agreed either to stay in office until a court decided the matter or to return the office to the President before the Senate acted, and that Grant later violated this understanding by surrendering the office to Stanton, which Johnson labeled insubordination. Grant replied that his decision was based on his legal interpretation of the Tenure of Office Act, asserting that he could not continue in the role after the Senate refused to concur, and denied any intent to disobey a direct order of the President, instead offering an interpretation of what constituted satisfactory evidence of presidential sanction for War‑Department orders. The five Cabinet officers—Gideon Welles, Hugh McCulloch, Alexander W. Randall, O. H. Browning and William H. Seward—each confirmed Johnson’s version of the conversation, noting Grant’s admissions and the alleged prior understanding about retaining or returning the office. Accompanying documents show the Treasury and Post Office departments treating Stanton as the lawful Secretary of War and requesting military assistance from Grant, indicating recognition of Stanton’s authority. In a final letter Grant maintained that he never intended to disobey a legal order of the President, only sought clarification of ambiguous instructions, and denied the charge of insubordination.

A study at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences in Dubai investigated medical students' perceptions of a curriculum-based resilience skills building course. Using qualitative phenomenological methodology, researchers analyzed reflective essays from 37 Year 4 MBBS students. The six-hour course, designed using constructivism experiential learning theory, covered topics including mindfulness, meditation, cognitive behavioral therapy, emotional intelligence, and mental toughness. Thematic analysis identified three interlinked themes: Awareness (understanding resilience), Application (practicing resilience skills), and Appraisal (evaluating the course and exercises). Students reported that the course enhanced their awareness, enabled them to apply resilience techniques in daily life, and improved their mental health and academic performance. The findings support integrating resilience skills building into medical curricula to help future healthcare professionals manage stress and prevent burnout.

The lecture discusses regulating dominant digital platforms through the lens of industrial organization economics. It examines why traditional Chicago School arguments about platform self-regulation fail, particularly due to zero lower bound constraints preventing negative pricing to consumers. The lecture covers the Digital Market Act's approach to ensuring contestability and fairness through obligations on designated platforms, including requirements for interoperability, data portability, and non-discrimination. It explores access pricing theories including the Efficient Component Pricing Rule adapted for two-sided markets, noting that optimal access charges depend on ancillary benefits but face implementation challenges due to information asymmetries and the need for simple regulatory rules. The discussion also addresses platform foreclosure risks, multihoming strategies, and concerns about entry deterrence through acquisitions.

The lecture introduces the Real Analysis course (18.100A). Its primary goals are to give students experience reading and writing proofs and to prove statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. After a brief review of sets, the instructor defines a set as a collection of objects called elements, introduces the empty set, and presents notation for membership (∈), non‑membership, subset (⊆), equality of sets (mutual subsets), proper subset, complement, union (∪), intersection (∩), set difference (\), and disjoint sets. The natural numbers, integers, rationals, and real numbers are defined, with a note that the real numbers will be rigorously constructed later as the first major goal of the course.

The first theorem presented is DeMorgan’s Laws. The instructor explains the general structure of a proof (assume hypotheses P, use definitions and logic, conclude Q) and proves the first law by showing the two required subset inclusions. The lecture then moves to mathematical induction, stating the well‑ordering axiom (every non‑empty subset of ℕ has a least element) and proving the induction theorem: if a statement Pₙ holds for n = 1 (base case) and whenever Pₘ holds then Pₘ₊₁ holds (inductive step), then Pₙ holds for all natural numbers. The proof uses well‑ordering and contradiction.

Two inductive examples are given: (1) the geometric series formula for c ≠ 1, and (2) the inequality (1 + c)ⁿ ≥ 1 + n c for any real c ≥ –1. The instructor notes that basic algebraic properties of real numbers may be used, but calculus concepts such as continuity or differentiation are not yet available.

The analysis, based on data from Voyager 2 and ground‑ and space‑based telescopes, including Hubble and NASA’s Infrared Telescope Facility, incorporated the planet’s hazes, clouds, and seasonal changes to refine the energy‑budget calculation. The study, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society and consistent with a separate NASA‑funded estimate, suggests the heat is modest relative to Neptune. The finding informs models of solar‑system evolution and the behavior of exoplanets of similar size.

The study developed and externally validated three machine learning (ML) models to predict pulmonary restriction from spirometry, demographic, and anthropometric data, and compared their accuracy and equity with the current guideline method that uses the forced vital capacity lower limit of normal (FVC LLN) to exclude restriction. Pulmonary function tests (PFTs) with both static and dynamic lung volume measurements from two academic health systems were used: 42 462 PFTs for model development (2000–2023) and 24 524 PFTs for external validation. Patients younger than 18 or older than 80 years were excluded, and restriction was defined by a total lung capacity below the lower limit of normal. Race‑neutral Global Lung Initiative equations were applied to calculate spirometric z‑scores.

Three ML architectures—logistic regression, random forest, and boosted tree—were trained using 10‑fold cross‑validation repeated five times, with hyper‑parameter tuning to maximize area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Predictors included age, height, weight, sex, multiple spirometric indices (FEV0.5, FEV1, FEV3, FEV6, FVC, FEV1/FVC, FEF25‑75, FEFMax, and expiratory time), and demographic variables. The primary performance metric was negative predictive value (NPV); sensitivity, specificity, and additional threshold‑independent metrics (AUC‑ROC, AUC‑PR, integrated calibration index, scaled Brier score) were also assessed. Model performance was compared between non‑Hispanic Black and non‑Hispanic White patients to evaluate equity. Decision curve analysis was performed to compare clinical utility.

The random forest model showed the highest overall performance. In the validation cohort, its NPV was 88.3 % (95 % CI 87.8–88.9 %) versus 72.7 % (95 % CI 72.1–73.3 %) for the FVC LLN. Sensitivity was 83.3 % vs 46.0 % and specificity was 82.9 % vs 94.4 % for the random forest and FVC LLN, respectively. The random forest excluded the need for static lung volume measurement in 56.7 % of tests compared with 78.4 % for the FVC LLN. Discrimination (AUC‑ROC = 0.91) was excellent, but calibration was poor (integrated calibration index = 0.17). Equity improved: the NPV ratio of non‑Hispanic Black to non‑Hispanic White patients rose from 62 % (FVC LLN) to 82 % (random forest). Decision curve analysis indicated that the random forest model was preferred for most plausible threshold values, except for a narrow range (0.59–0.76) where the FVC LLN was favored.

Limitations include possible over‑estimation of restriction probability due to higher prevalence in academic settings, potential ascertainment bias, and restricted racial diversity in the validation set (only non‑Hispanic Black and White patients). Model code is open source and model objects are publicly available.

In conclusion, using an ML model to exclude restriction from spirometry improves both accuracy (higher NPV) and equity (more consistent performance across racial groups) compared with the current FVC LLN approach, although adoption would increase the proportion of tests requiring static lung volume measurement.

G. M. Cox sued Judge George W. Burnham alleging the judge lacked jurisdiction to grant a liquor permit because the hearing took place in a term after the application was filed. The case concerned a 1901 application by pharmacist P. E. L. Bell in Benton county, a remonstrance filed by Cox and other citizens, and multiple continuances of the case. Interpreting the relevant statutes (Code §§ 2387‑2389, 2431), the court found that the provisions requiring applications to be heard at the first term are not mandatory; the court retains discretion to set hearing dates and to continue matters when its business so requires. An adjournment of the term does not automatically dismiss the proceeding, and in the absence of a showing to the contrary the court presumes cause for the continuances. The hearing held at the September term before Judge Burnham was regular, not evasive, and the remonstrants did not obtain separate representation. Consequently, the court held that jurisdiction was not lost and dismissed the plaintiff’s claim.

This meta-analysis examined 13 studies on AI technologies in education across eight countries (Taiwan, Australia, Turkey, China, Iran, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland) published between January 2015 and July 2024. Using PRISMA guidelines, the study evaluated overall effect sizes for AI applications including chatbots, generative AI, virtual reality, and learning management systems. The overall effect size was 0.86 (95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001), indicating a large positive impact of AI technologies on educational outcomes. Chatbots and generative AI showed the highest effect size (1.02, 95% CI [0.45, 1.59], p < 0.0001), while online learning and virtual reality showed 0.79 (p < 0.07), and learning management systems showed 0.62 (p < 0.05). The researchers applied novel algorithmic approaches including Naive Bayes-based algorithms, TF-IDF variants, and BERT-based search algorithms, and developed a weighted hybrid model combining random and fixed effects (effect size 0.88, 95% CI [0.48, 1.29], p < 0.0001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I² values 54.03% to 93.23%), with publication bias noted. Findings indicate that AI technologies, particularly chatbots and generative AI, significantly enhance educational outcomes across diverse contexts. The study recommends careful implementation considering specific educational contexts and student needs, and calls for future research with larger sample sizes and longer intervention periods. Authors include Jincheng Zhang, Dr. Thada Jantakoon, and Dr. Rukthin Laoha, with no competing interests, and ethics approval from the Canadian Center of Science and Education.

Probiotic foods introduce beneficial bacteria that aid digestion and nutrient absorption, promoting gut health. Nuts and seeds are dense in minerals, fatty acids and vitamin E, which aids cell repair after infection. Incorporating these foods into a daily diet, including Mediterranean‑style options, can naturally strengthen the immune system. The information is peer‑reviewed.

Danish study of 4,741 mothers found that children of older mothers (average age 30.9) displayed fewer behavioural, social and emotional difficulties at ages 7 and 11, but not at 15. CAR T cell therapies with enhanced efficacy are provided by disrupting methylcytosine dioxygenase genes (Tet1, Tet2, Tet3) in engineered immune effector cells. Disruption of a single allele of a Tet gene reduces total 5‑hydroxymethylcytosine (5‑hmC) levels, which is associated with enhanced proliferation, regulation of effector cytokine production and degranulation, thereby increasing CAR T cell function. The invention provides compositions and methods for bolstering therapeutic efficacy of CAR‑expressing cells.

The cells are engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising an antigen‑binding domain, a transmembrane domain, and an intracellular signaling domain, and have reduced or eliminated expression and/or function of Tet1, Tet2 and/or Tet3. The antigen‑binding domain can bind a tumor antigen selected from a large group including CD19, CD123, CD22, CD30, BCMA, GD2, HER2, MUC1, and many others; in one embodiment the antigen is CD19. The transmembrane domain may comprise SEQ ID NO:12 or a sequence with 95–99% identity thereto, and the intracellular signaling domain may contain primary signaling domains (e.g., CD3ζ) and/or costimulatory signaling domains (e.g., 4‑1BB, CD28, OX40). Hinge regions, leader sequences, and specific SEQ ID NOS for various domains are disclosed.

Inhibitors of Tet1, Tet2 and/or Tet3 include: (1) gene‑editing systems (CRISPR/Cas9, zinc‑finger nucleases, TALENs, meganucleases) targeted to sites within the Tet gene or its regulatory elements; (2) nucleic acids encoding such systems; (3) siRNA or shRNA molecules specific for Tet mRNA; (4) small‑molecule inhibitors; (5) dominant‑negative Tet proteins or binding partners thereof; and (6) combinations thereof. Targeting can be directed to early or late exons/introns of Tet2 (e.g., exon 3 or exon 9), and guide RNA sequences are provided in tables.

Methods are disclosed for increasing therapeutic efficacy of a CAR‑expressing cell by decreasing 5‑hmC levels via contacting the cell with a Tet inhibitor (e.g., a Tet2 inhibitor). Contact can occur ex vivo or in vivo, either before delivery of the CAR nucleic acid or after administration to a subject. The methods are applicable to treatment of diseases associated with tumor‑antigen expression, including hematologic cancers (e.g., CLL, ALL, AML, multiple myeloma, non‑Hodgkin lymphoma) and solid tumors (e.g., lung, breast, colorectal, melanoma, pancreatic, head‑and‑neck cancers).

Also provided are methods of manufacturing a CAR‑expressing cell by integrating CAR‑encoding nucleic acid into a Tet gene locus (e.g., within an intron of Tet2) so that Tet expression is reduced, or by ex‑vivo contact with a Tet inhibitor. Vectors encoding both a CAR and a Tet inhibitor (e.g., separated by a 2A site) are disclosed, as are compositions for ex‑vivo manufacture comprising a Tet inhibitor (e.g., N‑[3‑[7‑(2,5‑dimethyl‑2H‑pyrazol‑3‑ylamino)‑1‑methyl‑2‑oxo‑1,4‑dihydro‑2H‑pyrimido[4,5‑d]pyrimidin‑3‑yl]‑4‑methylphenyl]‑3‑trifluoromethyl‑benzamide, 2‑[(2,6‑dichloro‑3‑methylphenyl)amino]benzoic acid, or 2‑hydroxyglutarate).

The cell populations described contain a higher percentage of Tscm cells (CD45RA⁺CD62L⁺CCR7⁺CD27⁺CD95⁺) compared with control populations lacking Tet disruption. Experimental data from a CLL patient show that CAR19 insertion into the Tet2 locus (between exons 9 and 10) produces fusion transcripts, reduces Tet2 function, and results in clonal expansion of CAR⁺ T cells with decreased 5‑hmC and 5‑fC levels. Knockdown of TET2 by shRNA in normal T cells reduces 5‑hmC, promotes Tscm expansion, and enhances antigen‑dependent proliferation, IL‑2 and interferon‑γ production, and degranulation. CRISPR/Cas9 editing of Tet2 in CAR T cells increases CAR expression and improves functional responses. The disclosed gene‑editing systems and inhibitors are specific for Tet genes and can be used to generate CAR‑expressing cells with improved therapeutic efficacy.

Russian math after‑school programs, especially the Russian School of Mathematics (RSM), are expanding across the United States, with RSM reporting 22,000 students, 15 branches in Massachusetts and 40 overall. The growth is driven by parents seeking deeper conceptual understanding, dissatisfaction with school curricula, and concern that children will fall behind without additional instruction. RSM’s curriculum, originally based on Soviet teaching traditions, emphasizes early abstract reasoning, introduction of algebra and geometry, and understanding why operations work rather than rote memorization. Founded in 1997 in Newton by Russian immigrant Inessa Rifkin, the school charges about $2,000 per year for weekly classes. While many families enroll for enrichment, some parents report pressure to keep up with peers, creating an “arms race” of after‑school math instruction. The rise of Russian math has created challenges for public schools: teachers encounter classrooms where a quarter of students have already covered new material, and gaps in preparation may widen between affluent and lower‑income families. Some educators note that students can become overconfident despite partial understanding, yet also observe overall growth in the number of students comfortable with math, for example a rise in honors‑class enrollment in Newton South High School. Research on the effectiveness of Russian‑style teaching methods remains limited, and the long‑term impact on the U.S. education system is still uncertain.

The passage describes a metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) workflow using HostEL and AmpRE kits for rapid pathogen detection in plasma. HostEL depletes human background via magnetic bead-immobilized nucleases after selective lysis, while AmpRE enables single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation in under 4 hours. Analytical validation using spiked plasma showed a limit of detection of 70,000 cells/mL with ~4-fold enrichment of non-human reads and preserved pathogen composition. With HostEL treatment, sensitivity and specificity reached 96% and 96%, respectively, compared to 82% and 97% without treatment. Clinical validation on 42 plasma samples achieved 93% agreement with qPCR results. Both DNA viruses (Hepatitis B, CMV, EBV) and RNA viruses (Hepatitis C, Dengue, HIV) were detected. The workflow was tested on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq platforms, with a total turnaround time of 27 hours (or 13 hours on MiniSeq). The method reduces time, cost, and effort, enabling unbiased detection of bacteria, fungi, and both DNA and RNA viruses as a potential first-line diagnostic for infectious diseases.

Backtesting of NIFTY 50 data from 2007 shows a positive end‑of‑month effect. Results are reasonably robust across small variations of entry and exit days, though some curve fitting is present. The effect parallels the turn‑of‑the‑month effect observed in US stocks.
