The US government supports his specific claim but opposes a blanket rule granting candidates automatic standing.

The study evaluated the Happy Ring, a novel finger-worn wearable device with multiple physiological sensors (electrodermal activity, accelerometry, photoplethysmography, temperature), testing two machine learning scoring approaches (Generalized and Personalized) against polysomnography (PSG) and other consumer devices (Fitbit, Whoop, Oura, Actiwatch) in 36 healthy adults across 77 nights (lab and home settings). The personalized approach demonstrated superior specificity (83% vs. 70% generalized) and improved sleep stage classification accuracy compared to other devices, while maintaining high sensitivity (~93-94%). The Happy Ring performed comparably or better than existing consumer sleep-tracking devices for sleep-wake detection and staging. The personalized algorithm represents a dynamic, user-adaptive approach that significantly improves wake detection, particularly important for healthy populations with high sleep efficiency.

The iCVS model infers hidden cardiovascular states from arterial and venous pressure waveforms sampled at the bedside, requiring only patient age and weight. It extracts five observables—mean arterial and venous pressures, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure—using both fast (beat‑by‑beat) and slow (minutes) timescales. The model consists of a one‑chamber heart pump, arterial and venous compliance compartments, a peripheral resistor, and three regulatory components: a pressure‑dependent baroreflex (Sb), an independent autonomic component (S), and a non‑autonomic modulation of systemic vascular resistance (MSVR). Volume changes are represented by Iex. Fifteen hidden parameters relate the observables to arterial and venous pressure dynamics via ordinary differential equations. Parameter estimation is performed on 300‑second segments using constrained nonlinear optimization, with physiological bounds derived from age and weight. The model was validated on waveform data from ten critically‑ill children in a pediatric intensive care unit, including patients with hypovolemic, distributive, and cardiogenic shock and hemodynamically stable controls. Results showed that the model correctly identified negative Iex in patients with documented bleeding, negative MSVR in distributive shock, reduced contractility in cardiogenic dysfunction, and stable parameters in controls, with Pearson correlations between reconstructed and measured observables ranging from 0.71 to 0.94. iCVS enables real‑time estimation of hidden states and shock classification without requiring invasive measurements beyond routine pressure catheters. Limitations include simplifying assumptions about ventricular pressure, neglect of positive‑pressure ventilation effects, and the need for larger prospective validation to define diagnostic thresholds. The authors propose future integration of iCVS with machine‑learning modules to create hybrid decision‑support tools for bedside management of cardiovascular instability.

Speaker outlines his long‑standing support for a downward revision of the Dingley tariff, arguing that excessive rates foster monopolies. The Payne Tariff Bill, resulting from a year‑long investigation by the House Ways and Means Committee, altered 874 of the 2,024 dutiable items: 654 rates were reduced, 220 increased and 1,150 left unchanged. Detailed tables show that the decreases applied to articles worth roughly $5 billion in consumption, while the increases affected mainly luxuries valued at about $580 million and a smaller amount of non‑luxury goods. The speaker maintains the bill fulfills the Republican platform’s promise to cut excessive rates while still protecting industry, and that it is the best tariff bill the party has passed. He acknowledges that the wool schedule was not reduced because of strong interests, and that the cotton schedule was adjusted to correct inequities. The act also imposed a 1 % corporate excise tax, added a maximum/minimum provision to combat foreign discrimination, and established free trade with the Philippines within limited quotas. Citing party solidarity and the need to avoid delaying other reforms, the speaker explains his decision to sign the bill despite incomplete reductions. He has appointed an impartial tariff board to collect data for any future revision, urging that the current law be allowed to operate before another revision is attempted.

China’s domestic debt has risen to about 328 % of GDP, driven by massive stimulus, loose credit and shadow banking. The debt is largely internal and shielded by a closed capital account, which has so far prevented a currency crisis but has produced capital misallocation and may require drastic policy intervention. At the same time, China has become a major external creditor, financing infrastructure and supporting friendly governments through the Belt and Road Initiative, often with political strings attached. Notable recipients include Venezuela (over $60 bn), Argentina, Kenya (a costly railway operating far below capacity), Laos (a high‑speed railway partly financed by loans), Sri Lanka (a 99‑year port lease) and Pakistan ($2 bn). Many of these loans lack viable repayment sources, fueling political resentment and prompting new governments to re‑evaluate commitments. The pattern mirrors the 1970s–80s Latin American debt crisis, where cheap capital from oil windfalls funded unsustainable projects. A similar supply shock today stems from China’s cheap labour and massive dollar reserves, making it likely that many Belt and Road loans will become unserviceable, prompting calls for debt write‑offs and leaving China holding large amounts of uncollectable debt.

The ADS9803 has three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. Use 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors close to each power-supply pin, avoiding vias between pins and capacitors. Keep analog signals and references away from digital lines and noise sources. Connect GND and REFM pins to a ground plane with short connections. Texas Instruments provides development tools, E2E support forums, and documentation notifications. Two dietitians share tips for celebrating Diwali healthily while managing diabetes, heart health, or weight. Planning ahead and setting realistic targets like maintaining weight or limiting gains to under 1 kilo over the five-day festival is recommended. Use smaller plates for portion control, limit high-fat fried foods, and choose heart-healthy ingredients like lentils, wholegrains, and colorful vegetables. Replace ghee, butter, or coconut oil with unsaturated oils; use wholemeal flour instead of refined flour; and choose lean proteins. For sweets, limit intake or make them yourself using unsaturated fats, fresh fruit, and dried fruit instead of refined sugars. If diabetic, eat sweets with protein and fiber to prevent blood sugar spikes, and monitor levels regularly. Limit high-calorie and sugary drinks, and alcohol which can contribute to weight issues and dangerous blood sugar drops. Stay active with family activities and don't skip meals. Ask loved ones for support by requesting healthier food gifts or cooking healthy recipes together.

Foams are widely used for thermal insulation due to their low thermal conductivity, which arises from a high volume fraction of gas and low solid volume fraction. Small cell sizes reduce convection and radiation heat transfer. The thermal conductivity of foam includes contributions from solid conduction, gas conduction, convection, and radiation. Solid conduction is a fraction of the solid's conductivity times its volume fraction, while gas conduction dominates and often uses low-conductivity gases, though aging occurs as gas diffuses out. Convection is negligible in typical foams because cell sizes are small (Rayleigh number < 1000 for cell sizes below 20 mm). Radiation contribution increases as relative density decreases. An optimal relative density minimizes thermal conductivity due to trade-offs between solid and radiation contributions. Aerogels achieve even lower conductivity through pore sizes smaller than the mean free path of air. Foams also have good thermal shock resistance because of their low modulus.

The invention discloses a blockchain‑based system and method for issuing, buying, and reselling tokenized securities. A tokenized‑securities offering entity operates a server that communicates with investors’ user devices through a GUI. The server provides a link to one or more accreditation agencies, synchronizes with their databases in real time, and maintains an up‑to‑date whitelist (and a blacklist) of accredited investors. After verifying an investor’s accreditation status, the server sends a link to a tokenized‑securities contract deployed on the blockchain. The investor reviews the contract’s documents, accepts the terms, and transfers a predetermined amount of cryptocurrency from a uniquely identified digital wallet to an escrow account on the blockchain. The contract includes an escrow function that releases the securities token to the investor and the funds to the offering entity when a preset threshold (date, number of investors, minimum raise, etc.) is satisfied.  

Tokens are subject to a rest period (e.g., six months to one year) before they can be traded on a secondary market, and the system enforces SEC rules (e.g., Rule 144) to prevent the investor from acting as a broker‑dealer. After the rest period, a token market allows asks and bids, with the server enforcing compliance, suspending trading, and reversing transactions for non‑compliant investors.  

The tokens, called BITE (Blockchain Instrument for Transferrable Equity), can represent various securities such as common or preferred stock, options, warrants, convertible notes, or restricted stock units. BITE tokens include optional conversion rights, dividend‑distribution equivalents, automatic conversion upon a qualified financing, and a liquidity‑event option.  

The platform uses smart contracts (proxy, escrow, aggregate, and standard contracts) to manage ownership transfer, encrypt sensitive data, and lock contract terms. Document hashes are recorded on the blockchain to prove review. The server can access third‑party accreditation services and a blockchain oracle to retrieve and normalize accreditation information.  

The process follows discrete stages: registration (legal name, email, uniquely identified account, accreditation ID), verification (whitelist/blacklist comparison), review (mandatory and non‑mandatory documents), acceptance (terms, OFAC, AML/KYC), and purchase (cryptocurrency transfer to escrow, token release). A programmable timeline includes promotion, presale (with discounts), offering, rest, and trading periods; pricing may be locked at the time of purchase. The system also supports self‑accreditation, real‑time whitelist updates, and the ability to burn unsold tokens or reverse funds if minimum thresholds are not met.

El artículo analiza la expresión de las emociones en las cuentas corporativas de Twitter de Acciona e Iberdrola (IBEX 35) para identificar los sistemas léxicos y las estructuras figurativas que conceptualizan o evocan emociones. Las preguntas de investigación abordan los tipos de emociones predominantes, las unidades verbales implicadas, las metáforas employed, y su relación con la misión, visión y valores de las empresas.

El corpus está formado por 798 tuits (400 de Acciona, 398 de Iberdrola) publicados entre el 1 de abril y el 30 de junio de 2016, que abarcan juntas de accionistas, informes anuales y eventos de sostenibilidad, entre otros. El total de palabras asciende a 111 720.

La metodología combina análisis del discurso con una taxonomía de 14 categorías de emociones adaptadas de Storm y Storm (1987) y del grupo Grid (Sherer et al., 2013), basadas en las ocho emociones básicas de Plutchik. Los tuits se clasifican en informativos/neutros y emocionales (descriptivos o evocativos). Se emplean herramientas como twdocs para la extracción y un pretest de 30 tuits por empresa.

Los resultados muestran que la mayoría de los tuits son emocionales: 66,5 % en Acciona y 73,62 % en Iberdrola. La emoción más frecuente en ambas cuentas es el orgullo (≈27 %). Le siguen alegría‑felicidad‑optimismo e interés. Las emociones negativas (miedo, preocupación, tristeza, ira) representan solo el 4,7 % en Acciona y el 3,7 % en Iberdrola. El léxico más frecuente para cada emoción se vincula con términos como energía, luz, renovable (alegría) o sostenible, renovable (confianza).

El análisis метафóрико revela que la alegría se conceptualiza mediante el dominio fuente “luz” (subdominios energía, sol, calor), el orgullo se evoca a través de dominios relacionados con la innovación y la sostenibilidad, y la confianza se provoca con el hashtag #RecuerdoSOStenible y la metáfora yin‑yang. En Iberdrola, el color verde funciona como metonimia del equipo humano y del compromiso ambiental.

Las conclusiones confirman la validez de los corpus de microblog corporativo para el estudio lingüístico de las emociones en contextos organizacionales; se constata el predominio de emociones de valencia positiva, cuya expresión metafórica se ajusta a la misión, visión y valores de cada empresa, reforzando así su identidad corporativa.

A machine learning tool predicting 1-year overall survival for pediatric diffuse midline gliomas (DMG) using MRI achieved 77-85% accuracy. Homogeneous whole tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and larger post-radiation therapy tumor core to whole tumor volume ratio were identified as indicators of worse prognosis. The automatic method segments DMG subregions, extracts radiomic features, and was trained and validated on multisequence MRI data from two centers. It shows potential for improving patient risk stratification and therapeutic management in clinical trials.

The “Pound Cake” offense is a set of tactics designed to attack a Box & One defense by isolating the star player 1‑on‑1 in the low post. The primary option is a post‑isolation where the star draws a defender; if the defender helps, the star can drop‑pass to a back‑cutter for a lay‑up. When a shot isn’t available, teammates set “base screens” (O4 and O5) that let the star roll to the basket or break to a pop‑out position. A series of reads (curl, fade, back‑cut, screen‑and‑roll) and ball‑reversal actions are used to create open looks. Additional variants include a screener pop after the base screen, guard‑basket cuts, a pop‑out 1‑on‑1 isolation, and double mid‑screen “Horns” actions. Effective execution requires coordinated off‑ball screens, timing, non‑verbal communication, and a set of breakdown drills (post‑isolation, base screens, scrimmaging). Scouts are advised to study the opponent’s defensive reads and adapt alignments during the game. The Box & One defense itself consists of four players in a box zone and one “chaser” who aggressively denies the ball to a single opponent.

The U.S. Supreme Court will decide whether a trial court violated a criminal defendant's Sixth Amendment rights by prohibiting his lawyers from discussing his ongoing testimony with him during an overnight recess. David Villarreal was convicted of murder and sentenced to 60 years after stabbing his boyfriend, claiming self-defense. During his trial, the judge prohibited him from conferring with his attorneys about his testimony during an overnight recess. Villarreal argues this violated his right to effective assistance of counsel. The case involves conflicting Supreme Court precedents from 1976 and 1989 and questions about the workability of restricting lawyer-client communications. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals upheld the restriction. The U.S. government filed a brief supporting Texas's position.

President Kennedy reported that Soviet Premier Khrushchev’s warnings, aide‑memoire on Berlin, subsequent speeches, and a new Soviet military‑budget increase have prompted a series of U.S. and NATO decisions. He affirmed that the United States will defend its legal rights in West Berlin, which derive from the WWII victory and repeated agreements, and that a NATO commitment protects the city. The Administration stated it will resist any Soviet attempt to end U.S. rights or access, while remaining open to negotiations that do not compromise those rights.

To back this stance, the President announced several measures:

1. Request $3.247 billion in additional appropriations for the armed forces for the current fiscal year.  
2. Raise the Army’s authorized strength from 875,000 to about one million.  
3. Increase active‑duty Navy end‑strength by 29,000 and Air Force by 63,000.  
4. Double and triple draft calls, obtain authority to order selected Ready‑Reserve units and individual reservists to active duty, and activate air‑transport and Air National Guard tactical squadrons.  
5. Retain or reactivate ships and aircraft, expand tactical airpower, sealift, airlift, and anti‑submarine capabilities, and delay the deactivation of B‑47 bombers.  
6. Allocate roughly $1.8 billion for non‑nuclear weapons, ammunition, and equipment.  

An additional $207 million was requested for civil‑defence, covering shelter identification, stocking, warning‑system upgrades, and a household warning device. The new defence requests total $3.454 billion, raising the defence budget to $47.5 billion—an increase of $6 billion since January—with an expected deficit over $5 billion. Officials indicated the economy can absorb the spending, noting recent recovery, stable prices, an improved gold position, and a budget deficit smaller than in the 1958 recession. The President pledged a balanced budget in January and said higher taxes could be sought if required; he also called for closing tax loopholes on expense accounts, overseas income, dividends, interest, and cooperatives.

On diplomacy, the United States said it is willing to discuss Berlin in any forum, submit legal rights to international adjudication, and hold a free vote in the city, while emphasizing that Soviet security concerns after past invasions could be accommodated in arrangements that preserve peace and freedom. The Administration stressed it will maintain assistance to developing nations, pursue realistic disarmament, and avoid letting a single crisis undermine broader responsibilities.

Kennedy asked for public support, citizen involvement, and prayers, underscoring that the policy combines firm defence with a readiness to seek a negotiated settlement that does not surrender U.S. rights.

Early Offense consists of three sequential phases: an initial push, an offensive flow, and a continuity phase. The push tries to advance the ball before the defense organizes, creating outnumbered or mismatched situations. If the push does not yield a good shot, the team flows into the set offense; if that also fails, it transitions to a continuity style as the shot clock declines. Success requires counter‑pressure, breaking on every possession, playing tenacious defense, securing rebounds, and pushing the ball quickly with passes rather than dribbles. Point guard must advance the ball into the front court in 3‑5 seconds, wings run wide lanes, and players look for mismatches and quick shots. The transition starts with good defense, and a safe outlet pass is essential. Players must stay balanced, get the ball to their best scorers, and aggressively rebound missed shots.

The study employed a single‑group post‑test design with five beginner guitar students (ages 18–33, no prior instruction) to test an eight‑week activity‑based lesson plan. The plan, derived from the 5E model adapted to three stages (introduction, development, evaluation), covered four topics: major scales, minor scales, chords, and arpeggios. Each weekly session lasted 50 minutes, totalling 16 instructional hours delivered online in one‑on‑one format. Content and difficulty were reviewed and approved by three field experts. Evaluation consisted of a 10‑item theoretical knowledge test (each item worth 10 points) and a 10‑item performance test assessed on pitch/duration, tempo, technique, and musicality (total 100 points). Theoretical scores contributed 40 % and performance scores 60 % to each student’s overall result; success levels ranged from “Very Unsuccessful” (0–30) to “Very Good” (81–100). The theoretical test mean was 92 points (individual scores: 90, 80, 100, 90, 100). Chapter averages (weighted scores) were 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, placing all students in the “Very Good” category. The class average reached 93.6. The authors conclude that the activity‑based instructional approach produced successful learning outcomes for the study group during the Covid‑19 pandemic.

The Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) is defined as the co‑evolution of a Business Ecosystem and a Digital Ecosystem. It passes through three main phases – formation, evolution, and dissipation – with formation being critical for successful transactions. During formation, business entities search for partners and rely on negotiation to establish contracts. The Contract Net Protocol (CNP), originally introduced for distributed problem solving, is widely used for DBE negotiation because it is lightweight, flexible, and easy to implement. CNP consists of a sequence of steps (task identification, announcement, processing, bidding, bid processing, awarding, execution, termination) and was later extended by FIPA with minor additions.

To improve contract reliability, the paper proposes the Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), which adds quality‑evaluation steps for both the initiator and the participant during the negotiation process. Quality is assessed on three pillars: reliability, trust, and reputation, and is managed by a Quality Backbone Engine. The extension introduces extra time (Tq) into the negotiation timeline, but the authors argue that this trade‑off enhances overall performance, reduces uncertainty, and increases confidence among business alliances. Future work will focus on using CNQP to negotiate service‑level parameters between entities.

Offensive tackles line up at the ends of the offensive line and are responsible for run and pass blocking, often facing the opponent’s best pass rusher without immediate help from other linemen. Their primary duties are to block defensive linemen and linebackers, using footwork, hand placement, coordination, agility, and functional strength to protect the quarterback’s pocket and create running lanes. Typical NFL tackles stand 6’3‑6’8, weigh 300‑340 lb, and possess a thick, lengthy build. The position is abbreviated OT or T and carries nicknames such as Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, and Big Uglies. The term “tackle” originated from early football when edge defenders tackled ball carriers on outside runs. Offensive tackles make up two of the five offensive line spots and typically play the same spot throughout a game. Notable tackles include Jonathan Ogden (11‑time Pro Bowler, Super Bowl champion), Anthony Munoz (Hall of Fame, 13‑year Bengal starter), and Joe Thomas (10 straight Pro Bowls, over 10,000 consecutive snaps). The left tackle often protects the quarterback’s blind side and is considered a team’s most talented lineman.

The Gaia hypothesis, introduced by James Lovelock in the 1970s, proposes Earth as a self‑regulating organism where life interacts with inorganic processes to keep the planet in a state where life can persist. University of Exeter researchers refined the theory with 'sequential selection'—short‑lived destabilizing episodes lead to stable states, after which further stabilizing traits arise via 'selection by survival alone.' Their model identifies two mechanisms providing stabilising properties, explains the accumulation of stabilising mechanisms over 3.5 billion years and resolves the objection that natural selection cannot generate planetary stability. The paper, titled 'Selection for Gaia across multiple scales,' published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution, involves Tim Lenton, Dave Wilkinson and James Dyke, and could inform climate‑change response and the search for life elsewhere.

Hard-to-borrow stocks in the US typically underperform over 3-, 6-, and 12-month periods, while general collateral stocks yield positive returns. In Japan and Europe, hard-to-borrow stocks do not systematically underperform. Small-cap stocks perform particularly poorly. However, exploiting this negative edge through short selling is likely unprofitable due to difficulties in obtaining a short locate. Short selling requires borrowing shares, paying fees that can range from 1% to 50%. Stocks become hard to borrow due to limited supply, high demand, regulatory restrictions, and high borrowing costs. Factors affecting borrowing fees include stock size, stability, liquidity, and volatility, with larger, stable, liquid stocks having lower fees. For example, GameStop's short-borrow fee rose from 1% in 2019 to 34% in 2021 during a short squeeze. Hard-to-borrow stocks make short selling challenging and expensive.

Trading time frames range from tick data to years, with daily bars recommended as the best starting point for most traders. Time frames serve as diversification tools to spread risk and optimize capital use. Traders should be agnostic in choosing time frames based on their strategy and goals. Day traders typically use minutes to hours, swing traders use days to weeks, trend followers use days to months, and investors use years to decades. Daily bars offer simplicity in backtesting and help identify market inefficiencies. Trading multiple time frames can offset losses in one area with gains in another, potentially reducing overall drawdowns. The choice of time frame depends on individual preferences, trading goals, and the specific strategy being implemented.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine identified a secondary heat-producing system in brown fat that can burn calories independently of exercise. This backup “heater” relies on peroxisomes, cellular structures that multiply in the cold and metabolize fatty acids via the enzyme acyl‑CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). Peroxisomes proliferate in the cold and compensate when mitochondria's uncoupling protein 1 is absent. Mice lacking ACOX2 in brown fat showed reduced cold tolerance, lower body temperature, impaired insulin sensitivity and greater weight gain on a high‑fat diet. Conversely, mice engineered to overproduce ACOX2 displayed increased heat generation, better cold tolerance, improved insulin sensitivity and weight control. The ACOX2 pathway metabolizes certain branched fatty acids that are present in dairy products, human breast milk and produced by gut microbes, suggesting that dietary or probiotic interventions could boost this heat‑production route. The researchers note that the mechanism appears relevant to humans, as higher circulating levels of these fatty acids correlate with lower body mass index. A provisional patent has been filed targeting ACOX2 activation for obesity and metabolic disease. The work was supported by the National Institutes of Health.

Both the Chicago Blackhawks and Philadelphia Flyers have rebuilt quickly, with Chicago relying on strong drafting and key acquisitions such as Marian Hossa and goaltender Antti Niemi, while Philadelphia constructed its defense through trades and free‑agent signings, acquiring Kimmo Timonen, Chris Pronger, Matt Carle and Braydon Coburn. The Flyers enter the finals with a sense of desperation and underdog motivation, aided by a “never‑say‑die” attitude attributed to Richards and Pronger, despite age concerns for some veterans. NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, built on the Ampere GA100 architecture using TSMC 7 nm N7, contains 54.2 billion transistors, up to 108 streaming multiprocessors (SMs) each with 64 FP32 CUDA cores and four third‑generation Tensor Cores, and 192 KB combined L1/shared memory per SM. The GPU adds support for TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4 and binary data types; Tensor Cores deliver up to 2.5× mixed‑precision FP16/FP32 performance and 5× with fine‑grained structured sparsity compared with Tesla V100, and TF32 runs 10× faster than V100 FP32 FMA. Sparsity (2‑out‑of‑4 pattern) doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero operands.

Memory subsystem includes 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM (1555 GB/s bandwidth) and a 40 MB L2 cache (2.3× the bandwidth of V100). L2 residency controls let programmers mark data as persisting, and compute data compression provides up to 4× improvement in DRAM and L2 bandwidth and up to 2× L2 capacity.

Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) partitions a single A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances; each instance receives its own SMs, L2 slices, memory controllers and DRAM bandwidth, guaranteeing QoS and fault isolation for multi‑tenant cloud services.

Third‑generation NVLink offers twelve links with 600 GB/s total bandwidth (double V100) and improved error detection. PCIe Gen 4 with SR‑IOV and enhanced error‑containment features further improve reliability.

CUDA 11 enables asynchronous copy from global to shared memory, asynchronous barriers, task‑graph acceleration to reduce launch latency, L2 cache residency control, and warp‑wide reductions. Hardware accelerators for JPEG decoding (NVJPG), optical‑flow, and five NVDEC units boost video processing.

The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs linked by NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and scaling to thousands of GPUs via Mellanox InfiniBand; MIG provides up to 56 fully isolated accelerators in a single 6U chassis.

James Swan’s lecture focuses on numerical optimization methods. Steepest descent finds minima by moving opposite to the gradient with an optimal step size derived from a quadratic Taylor approximation, but it can be slow and may fail on flat or cliff-like landscapes. Linear equations Ax=b can be posed as quadratic optimization problems requiring a symmetric positive‑definite matrix A. Conjugate gradient improves on steepest descent by choosing search directions that are orthogonal to past gradients (conjugate directions), preserving prior minimization and solving linear systems in n iterations, requiring only matrix‑vector products. For nonlinear equations grad f=0, Newton‑Raphson uses the Hessian to achieve quadratic convergence but may not descend if the Hessian has negative eigenvalues. Trust‑region methods combine both by using a radius R_i around the current point: if a Newton‑Raphson step stays within R_i and reduces the objective, it is taken; otherwise, a steepest‑descent or boundary step is chosen. The trust‑region size adapts based on whether the quadratic approximation over‑ or under‑estimates the actual function reduction. Matlab’s solvers employ such heuristics, including dogleg strategies, to robustly find minima.

Recent research from Harvard T.H. Couples who ate fish or shellfish at least twice a week achieved a 92 % conception rate within a year, and those consuming eight or more seafood servings per month reported 22 % more frequent intercourse than average. The study’s authors are uncertain of the mechanism, noting that zinc, present in oysters, correlates with testosterone in humans and improves sexual performance in rats, but they did not measure zinc intake. They suggest that couples sharing more seafood meals may spend more time together, providing a behavioral explanation. Additional surveys indicate 54 % of millennials equate food with sex, compared with 42 % of Baby Boomers. A dating‑site analysis found that mentioning guacamole in messages raised reply rates by 114 %. A published study reported that apple consumption can improve female sexual arousal and lubrication. A 2011 study reported that men think about sex every 28 minutes and women every 50 minutes, while women think about food every 62 minutes and men every 38 minutes.

Enron Corp. replaced chief financial officer Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, former treasurer and head of the industrial‑markets group, after a steep stock drop and the start of a Securities and Exchange Commission informal inquiry into Fastow’s related‑party transactions with two partnerships he ran (LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co‑Investment). Williams %R, created by Larry Williams, is an oscillator ranging from 0 to -100 that compares the current close to the highest high over a look‑back period, functioning as a mean‑reversion tool. Its formula is (highest high – close) / (highest high – lowest low) × –100.

Backtesting on S&P 500 (SPY) with look‑back periods from 2 to 25 days gave profit factors above 2; 2‑day look‑back delivered a CAGR of 11.9% (vs. 10.3% buy‑and‑hold), 22% market exposure, 598 trades, 0.6% average gain per trade, 17% max drawdown, profit factor 2.2, risk‑adjusted return 52%, and did not work for shorts.

Compared with the RSI, Williams %R achieved a higher CAGR (11.9% vs 7.3%). A second strategy on Nasdaq with an extra indicator attained a CAGR of 13.4%, 14% exposure, 251 trades, 78% win rate, profit factor 3.2, Sharpe 2.9, and risk‑adjusted return 96%.

Conclusion: Williams %R is an underappreciated indicator that outperforms RSI and Stochastics in the tested strategies.

Study investigated the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure and blood‑brain barrier (BBB) leakage in humans using 7 T dynamic contrast‑enhanced (DCE) MRI. Twenty‑three patients with essential hypertension and twenty age‑ and sex‑matched normotensive controls were enrolled; hypertension was defined as systolic ≥ 135 mmHg or diastolic ≥ 85 mmHg, or current antihypertensive medication. BBB leakage was quantified with Patlak analysis to obtain leakage rate Ki and plasma volume fraction vp in total grey matter, cortical grey matter, deep grey matter and white matter regions. No significant difference in Ki was found between hypertensive and control groups after adjustment for age and sex, whereas vp was significantly higher in hypertensive patients in grey‑matter regions. Ki showed positive relations with systolic, diastolic and mean arterial pressure in cortical and total grey matter, but not in white matter or deep grey matter. These associations remained significant after further adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, medication use and cerebral small‑vessel disease (cSVD) score. Subgroup analysis revealed lower Ki in normotensive medicated patients compared with the pooled hypertensive groups, indicating a potential protective effect of antihypertensive treatment. The findings suggest that continuous blood‑pressure levels, rather than a binary hypertension diagnosis, are linked to increased BBB leakage in grey matter. Strengths include early BBB assessment before visible neurovascular damage and use of high‑field MRI; limitations involve the 30‑minute BP measurement, low cSVD burden in the cohort and small subgroup sizes.

Data write operations require a minimum of 32 SCLKs. Read protocols are divided into three categories: legacy SPI-compatible with single SDO, legacy SPI-compatible with dual SDO, and source-synchronous (SRC). The four legacy SPI protocols are SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S, with SPI-00-S as the default protocol on power-up or reset. Protocol selection is performed by programming the SDI_MODE[1:0] bits in the SDI_CTL_REG register. To read data using the selected SPI protocol, the SDO_MODE[1:0] bits in the SDO_CTL_REG register must be set to 00b.

Modern portfolio theory explains that combining non-perfectly correlated securities creates an efficient frontier (bullet-shaped curve) where rational investors prefer the upper branch (higher return for given risk). Individual securities typically lie inside this frontier, making diversification optimal. Adding more securities shifts the frontier leftward (improving risk-return trade-offs). Combining a risk-free asset with any portfolio yields a straight line; the tangency portfolio provides the highest Sharpe ratio and is preferred by all rational investors regardless of risk aversion. In equilibrium, this tangency portfolio must be the market portfolio (all assets weighted by market capitalization). This leads to the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM): expected return equals the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium, where beta measures systematic risk as the covariance between an asset and the market divided by market variance. This framework determines appropriate discount rates for capital budgeting decisions.

Belarus’s out‑of‑school education (OSE) is a legally‑defined part of the national lifelong‑learning system. Its development has three historical phases: early‑20th‑century literacy drives, a Soviet‑era construction of a comprehensive OSE infrastructure (labor, outdoor practice, talent identification), and post‑1991 integration of EU lifelong‑learning concepts.  

Legislative guarantees centre on the 2011 amendments to the Code of the Republic of Belarus about Education, which define OSE for children and youth as additional education that develops personality, creative abilities, moral, physical and professional qualities, and organises free time. The Code and subsequent decrees (e.g., “Regulations on Out‑of‑school Education for Children and Adolescents” 2017, “Lifelong Learning Plan” 2011) mandate non‑discriminatory access, state funding, protection of institutions from closure or leasing, and curricula covering art, technology, social practice, patriotism, ecological awareness and safety.  

By the end of 2021 Belarus had 318 public OSE institutions: 185 comprehensive (providing multidisciplinary training at lower fees) and 133 specialized, including regional study tours (62), ecosystem protection (30), physical training (15), science‑technology (13), professional (9) and art (4). Comprehensive institutions are preferred because they reduce travel and cost; specialized institutions focus on patriotism, environmental education and physical health.  

OSE aims to cultivate four core abilities in students: mastering information‑technology knowledge, developing social personality, surviving in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong learning. Representative institutions illustrate these goals: the Minsk State Children’s Palace offers age‑specific IT and robotics courses; the Belarusian Youth League organizes nationwide sports, volunteer services and anti‑vice campaigns; study‑tour and cultural‑exchange activities foster cross‑cultural understanding; the Belarusian Firefighters Association promotes safety awareness and career exploration.  

State‑run OSE institutions remain the first choice for most families because of lower fees, stable quality, and links to academic competitions that can guarantee university admission. Belarus’s blend of Soviet‑era systematic OSE with EU lifelong‑learning principles, strong legislation, clear cultivation objectives, and broad participation offers lessons for other countries seeking to optimise public out‑of‑school education.

Four overnight trading strategies for the S&P 500 buy at the close and sell at the next day’s open, using short holding periods to keep drawdowns small. Strategy 1 enters on a new n‑day low and requires the close to be above the 200‑day moving average; it generated an 8.43 % profit with a 29 % win rate, and omitting the moving‑average filter degrades the equity curve. Strategy 2 also triggers on a new n‑day low with two extra variables, producing a 12.69 % profit, 14 % win rate and a profit factor of 2.6 with a smooth equity curve; the inverse short version is erratic and not tradeable. Strategy 3 uses three different variables, delivering a profit factor of roughly 3.8 and a steadily rising equity curve. Strategy 4 modifies strategy 3 by holding to the close if SPY opens lower than –0.1 % and exiting at the open otherwise, boosting results; in recent years holding to the close has been profitable even when SPY opens up, a change from earlier behavior. All strategies benefit from brief exposure, limiting drawdowns, though overnight gaps can cause single‑digit losses.

The study examined dropout tendencies among students at Turkish public universities, using a descriptive correlational design grounded in Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model. Data were collected in the 2023–2024 academic year via the “School Dropout Scale in Higher Education” (adapted to Turkish) and a demographic form. The sample comprised 1,061 undergraduate and preparatory students (58.2 % female, 41.8 % male), selected by simple random sampling from public universities.

The overall mean dropout‑tendency score was 2.67 (SD = 0.58), indicating a moderate level. No significant gender difference was found. Significant differences emerged by year of study: third‑year and higher students showed higher dropout tendencies than preparatory and first/second‑year students. Students studying outside metropolitan cities reported higher dropout tendencies than those in metropolitan areas. Working while studying was associated with higher dropout tendency. Having close friends who had dropped out correlated with higher dropout intention. Correlations with socioeconomic and academic variables showed that lower school‑attendance frequency, lower parental education (both mothers and fathers), lower GPA, lower family income, and higher number of siblings were each significantly associated with greater dropout tendency.

All six subdimensions of the scale (Social, Academic, Faculty Members, Health & Wellbeing, Institutional, Financial) correlated positively with the overall dropout tendency (r = .696 to .776). Subdimension scores were higher for non‑metropolitan students in Social, Health & Wellbeing, Institutional, and Financial areas.

The findings support Tinto’s model in the Turkish context and highlight demographic, academic, and environmental factors influencing dropout. The authors recommend that institutions—particularly in non‑metropolitan regions—implement retention strategies such as academic mentoring, financial support, and mental‑health services, monitor attendance, and target at‑risk students early. They note that the study’s cross‑sectional, self‑report design limits causal inference and suggest that future research employ longitudinal or mixed‑method approaches to explore personal, institutional, and contextual interactions over time.

ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires were synthesized by depositing MoO3 or WO3 precursor layers on ZnSe nanowires via DC magnetron sputtering, followed by selenization in a three-zone furnace. XRD, XPS, and Raman confirmed successful conversion to TMD shells with no residual oxide peaks. TEM analysis revealed that at lower selenization temperatures (600°C for MoSe2, 700°C for WSe2), uniform 2 nm conformal shells formed, while higher temperatures (650°C and 750°C) produced discontinuous shells with protruding TMD crystals 20-50 nm in size. Photoluminescence showed characteristic emissions from both ZnSe and the TMD components. The temperature-dependent morphology shift is attributed to a transition from solid-state reaction at lower temperatures to gas-phase reaction and nucleation at higher temperatures.

Researchers from Princeton led by Geoffrey Dann discovered that ATP‑dependent ISWI chromatin remodelers use the nucleosome’s acidic patch—a negatively charged surface formed by histones H2A and H2B—to remodel chromatin, a mechanism not previously implicated in remodeling. High‑throughput screening revealed that chemical modifications on histones adjacent to the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity, and that other chromatin remodelers also employ this feature, indicating it may be a general requirement. The study, published in Nature, provides extensive data on regulatory inputs for ISWI and suggests the acidic patch could be a target for cancer therapies, as mutations in this region occur in certain cancers.

Japan indicated willingness to help Korea become independent and to assist its reforms, and sent troops to protect its legation and nationals. China reported that its forces entered Korea at Korea’s request to suppress southern rebels; after Chun‑Chu was recaptured and the rebels dispersed, China intended to withdraw its troops. The 1885 Tien‑Tsin agreement stipulated simultaneous withdrawal of the two nations’ troops, but Japan refused, leaving its forces in Seoul and Chemulpo. Diplomatic notes exchanged among Korean, Japanese, Chinese and other foreign representatives in Seoul recorded these positions, expressed concern for peace and order, and thanked the mediators for their efforts.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon warned at Italian Tech Week that stock markets are likely to see a drawdown in the next 12–24 months, citing AI-driven capital formation that could follow the pattern of past tech booms. He said much deployed capital may not deliver returns, and investors, excited by AI, are overlooking risks, leading to a market reset. Solomon called the situation similar to the late‑1990s dotcom bubble and noted other investors also flagged an AI “industrial bubble.” Despite the warning, he remains optimistic about AI’s long‑term potential.

University of Oxford scientists using the Gemini North telescope detected hydrogen sulphide in Uranus’s cloud tops, confirming the planet’s rotten‑egg smell. Unlike Jupiter and Saturn, which contain ammonia, Uranus’s hydrogen sulphide reflects differences in planetary formation conditions. Researchers noted that a human descending into Uranus’s clouds would encounter a foul odor, −200 °C temperatures, and suffocation long before the smell.

The authors present EduVidQA, a dataset of 5,252 QA pairs from educational lecture videos (270 real-world questions from YouTube, 4,982 synthetic pairs from NPTEL), designed to benchmark MLLMs on answering student questions from online lectures. Their preliminary study found that while 67.9% of students wanted to ask questions while watching videos, only 17% actually asked in comments sections. They developed qualitative evaluation metrics (Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking, and Using Pedagogical Techniques) based on student preference studies, and benchmarked six state-of-the-art MLLMs, finding that finetuning smaller open-source models on synthetic data can match or outperform larger closed models. The work addresses the lack of interactive learning in online educational videos by providing a dataset and framework for developing expert-level question answering systems.

Cameroon plans to restore 12 million ha of deforested land by 2030 under the Bonn Challenge, with 183 partners including local councils, NGOs and businesses. In a joint session of Congress the President presented a ten‑point anti‑inflation program. 1) Food: call for maximum farm production, removal of acreage limits for rice, peanuts, cotton, guarantee fuel and fertilizer, review marketing orders, and monitor exports. 2) Energy: create a National Energy Board under the Secretary of the Interior, cut foreign oil imports by 1 million barrels per day by end‑1975, promote domestic coal, nuclear and renewable power, set a 1980 target to replace oil‑fired electricity, push a 40 % mileage improvement, deregulate natural gas, use Naval petroleum reserves, amend the Clean Air Act, and pass surface‑mining legislation. 3) Restrictive practices: strengthen antitrust enforcement, raise maximum penalties to $1 million for corporations and $100 000 for individuals, create a National Commission on Regulatory Reform, require inflation‑impact statements for all executive and congressional proposals, and monitor wages and prices without imposing controls. 4) Capital: expand the 10 % investment tax credit, make preferred‑stock dividends fully deductible, and liberalize capital‑gains taxes. 5) Unemployment: extend unemployment benefits (13 weeks for exhausted claimants, 26 weeks for uncovered workers) funded from the Treasury, and create a Community Improvement Corps that activates when national unemployment exceeds 6 %. 6) Housing: authorize federal purchase of most home mortgages and immediately allocate $3 billion to finance about 100 000 homes. 7) Thrift institutions: work with Congress to relieve mortgage‑credit shortages. 8) International: seek early passage of a trade reform bill and continue cooperation with allies. 9) Taxes & spending: impose a one‑year 5 % surcharge on corporate and high‑income individuals, exempt those earning under $15 000, set a $300 billion FY 1975 spending target, and submit rescissions/deferrals to meet it. 10) Volunteer effort: launch a “WIN” mobilization urging citizens to cut food waste, drive 5 % fewer miles, car‑pool, and share resources. The President declared that fiscal discipline and citizen participation are essential to defeat inflation.

This paper addresses memory management challenges in long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) agents using Large Language Models. The authors identify two critical problems: memory inflation from growing dialogue history and contextual degradation where older information is lost from context windows, causing inconsistent agent behavior.

The proposed solution is a hybrid memory system with three components: Working Memory for immediate context, Episodic Memory as a vector database storing fine-grained interactions, and Semantic Memory containing distilled concepts. The core innovation is an "Intelligent Decay" mechanism that evaluates each memory entry using a utility score formula: S(Mi) = αRi + βEi + γUi, combining recency (time decay), relevance (semantic similarity to current task), and user utility (human-assigned importance).

The system includes a visualization interface allowing non-technical users to directly manage agent memory by pinning, forgetting, or consolidating entries. This Human-in-the-Loop approach enables users to correct flawed memories and prevent error propagation.

Experiments comparing three strategies over 500 turns showed hybrid system achieved 92.5% task completion rate versus 81.4% for basic retrieval-augmented generation and 65.2% for sliding window. Token cost decreased by 22% compared to basic RAG while contradiction rate dropped to 1.2% from 5.5% and 18.1%. The system demonstrated "self-evolution" through maintained and improved performance over time, contrasting with the "self-degradation" observed in naive memory-add approaches.

AP Creation NAE (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013) lets an SEV‑SNP guest create, add, update or destroy a vCPU at a specified VMPL level. The guest must first issue RMPADJUST to mark a page as a VMSA. Two forms exist: a VMSA that is not used until an INIT‑SIPI sequence, and a VMSA that is installed immediately, making the vCPU runnable. The hypervisor validates the VMPL level and APIC ID, uses the VMSA page’s system physical address, and returns an error if the operation fails; the vCPU cannot run until a VMSA is successfully (re)assigned. AP Creation enables vCPU hotplug and removes the need for an AP Reset Hold NAE under Restricted Injection.

#HV Doorbell Page NAE (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014) registers a shared page for the #HV injection exception when Restricted Injection is enabled. Actions: GET_PREFERRED returns a hypervisor‑preferred GPA or 0xffff_ffff_ffff_ffff; SET supplies a page‑aligned GPA (may be the preferred value) and the hypervisor accepts or rejects it; QUERY returns the currently set GPA or 0; CLEAR removes the doorbell page and the guest should make the page private again.

#HV Timer NAE provides emulated APIC timer support. SET writes timer registers (Timer LVT, Divide Configuration, Timer Initial Count) according to a MASK; GET reads the registers. Interrupts are delivered via #HV; if Restricted Injection is disabled the hypervisor may return a #GP exception.

APIC ID List NAE allows the guest to retrieve all APIC IDs of the guest. The guest supplies contiguous shared pages; the hypervisor returns in RAX the required number of pages if the supplied space is insufficient. The list format is a 4‑byte count followed by 4‑byte entries.

AP Jump Table NAE uses SET (UEFI) and GET (OS) actions to store/retrieve the address of a 4 KB, page‑aligned, encrypted jump table used to start APs after UEFI hands control to the OS. The address is communicated via the SEV‑SNP Secrets Page.

Secure AVIC provides guest‑owned APIC backing pages per vCPU. REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE informs the hypervisor of the page‑aligned GPA; the hypervisor must keep it present in the NPT while the vCPU runs. UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE removes that requirement and returns the previously set GPA. No feature flag is required; Secure AVIC support is implied by the SEV_FEATURES VMSA bit.

Termination Request NAE lets the guest request termination. SW_EXITINFO1[3:0] specifies the reason‑code set, and SW_EXITINFO1[11:4] the code; reason‑code set 0x0 and code 0x01 are defined. SW_EXITINFO2 carries 64‑bit termination data.

Guest identification of SEV‑ES: the hypervisor sets CPUID ECX[31] (under hypervisor), EAX[1] (SEV support), EBX[5:0] (encryption‑bit position) and EBX[11:6] (reduction in physical‑address space bits).

SMP booting challenges: under SEV‑ES and SEV‑SNP the hypervisor cannot modify registers after measurement, so traditional INIT‑SIPI sequences are replaced by AP Creation (when supported) or AP Reset Hold. Methods for setting the initial CS:IP include writing a memory location at the reset vector or using a fixed hypervisor‑known location. On first AP reset the hypervisor runs the vCPU with its initial registers; on subsequent resets the guest updates the GHCB and issues the AP Reset Hold request. After a SIPI the guest transitions to real mode and executes at the vector supplied by the OS via the AP jump table.

#HV Doorbell page structure: bytes 0‑1 hold a 16‑bit PendingEvent field (bit 15 = NoFurtherSignal, bits 14‑10 reserved, bit 9 = #MC, bit 8 = NMI, bits 7‑0 = interrupt vector); byte 2 holds NoEoiRequired; bytes 3‑63 are reserved. The page is hypervisor‑owned and accessed with C=0. Host writes the pending vector, sets NoFurtherSignal when delivering NMI/#MC, and sets NoEoiRequired when no further pending interrupts exist. Guest atomically exchanges PendingEvent to acknowledge and clears NoEoiRequired to perform an implicit EOI; otherwise it writes the X2APIC EOI MSR via VMGEXIT.

Host behavior: emulates APIC interrupt presentation, writes the highest‑priority ready vector, records presented vectors and NoEoiRequired state, and performs EOI cycles when NoEoiRequired transitions from non‑zero to zero. Guest behavior: handles #HV at any time, must atomically retrieve the pending vector, assumes the interrupt is acknowledged, and performs EOI by clearing NoEoiRequired or by a register write.

SEV‑TIO extension enables binding trusted devices. A guest request includes a PCI ID, MMIO range with desired RMP state, and TDISP status. Data pages provide optional nonce, measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report; the hypervisor returns the required page count in RBX if insufficient.

Debug register virtualization: if hardware supports DebugVirtualization, the VMSA bit enables it and the hypervisor clears all debug‑register intercepts; otherwise the hypervisor intercepts DR7 reads/writes and caches the value.

SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this version.

Unsupported NAE events cause the #VC handler to issue a VMGEXIT with the “Unsupported Event” exit code.

Cape Horn Pigeon was a bark built in 1854 in Dartmouth, Mass., for whaling and owned by J. & W. R. Wing. As of 10 Sept 1892 the ownership was divided among J. & W. R. Wing (4 /64), Thomas M. Hart (2 /64), John Wing (2 /64), Edward F. Potter (11 /64), Edward F. Potter as executor (8 /64), Michael Baker as administrator (4 /64), George W. Collins (1 /64), Charles C. Church (2 /64), and the former interest of Alexander H. Seabury (10 /64) conveyed to Louisa B. Haskell; subsequent conveyances gave J. & W. R. Wing 20 /64. All owners were native U.S. citizens. The ship carried a crew of 31 (30 seamen plus the captain) paid a share of net proceeds; several crew members assigned their claims to the owners in return for advances, and most were in debt to the vessel. The bark measured 201 42/100 tons and was fitted out at San Francisco in December 1891 for a one‑year whaling voyage to Japan and the Okhotsk Sea, equipped solely for whaling with no sealing gear or intent.

Turing GPUs improve video‑encoding quality compared with Pascal and software x264, enabling 4K streaming on typical CPUs and reducing CPU utilization. Turing includes hardware support for USB Type‑C and VirtualLink, an open industry standard that delivers power, display (four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes) and SuperSpeed USB‑3 data through a single USB‑C connector, simplifying VR headset cabling and allowing VR on small‑form‑factor devices.  

NVLink replaces the prior MIO/PCIe SLI interface. The TU102 GPU provides two x8 second‑generation NVLink links (25 GB/s per direction each, 50 GB/s bidirectional per link) while TU104 has one x8 link; Turing supports only 2‑way SLI, not 3‑ or 4‑way configurations.  

Ray tracing is enabled by dedicated RT Cores in each SM of TU102, TU104 and TU106. Turing implements a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization with real‑time ray tracing. RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, freeing CUDA cores for other work. Turing delivers >10 Giga Rays / sec—roughly ten times faster than Pascal’s software ray‑tracing—while denoising filters reduce the number of rays needed per pixel.  

The NGX stack leverages Turing’s Tensor Cores for AI‑based features: Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS) trained on 64× supersampled ground‑truth images can double performance versus Pascal while maintaining near‑64×SS quality; DLSS 2X approaches 64×SS quality at target resolution. Additional NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow‑Mo and AI Super Rez (real‑time 1080p‑to‑4K upscaling with 1‑2 dB higher PSNR than bicubic).  

Mesh shading introduces Task and Mesh shader stages with a cooperative thread model, eliminating CPU draw‑call bottlenecks and enabling rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects; it supports dynamic level‑of‑detail selection and cut‑away effects.  

Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows developers to set shading rates per 16×16‑pixel region, supporting content‑adaptive, motion‑adaptive, and foveated rendering, and can increase MSAA shading rates.  

Texture Space Shading decouples shading from screen‑space pixels, storing results as texels for reuse across frames and providing fine‑grained LOD control for shading‑rate management.  

Multi‑View Rendering extends Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi‑Projection to up to four views per pass (32 at API level), removing restrictions on view‑dependent attributes and enabling efficient single‑pass stereo and cascaded shadow rendering for VR.  

Turing supports Tier 3 bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views; multiple resource types can share a single heap.  

VR enhancements include VirtualLink, MVR for stereo, VRS‑based foveated rendering, and RT‑Core‑accelerated VRWorks Audio for spatial sound.  

Architecturally, the full TU102 chip has 48 SMs, 13.6 B transistors, 4608 CUDA cores, 576 Tensor cores and 48 RT cores, with two NVLink x8 links. TU104 has six GPCs, 48 SMs, 13.6 B transistors, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor cores, 48 RT cores and one NVLink x8 link. TU106 has three GPCs, 36 SMs, 10.8 B transistors, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor cores, 36 RT cores and no NVLink. Each SM includes 64 CUDA cores, a 256 KB register file, a 96 KB L1/shared cache and four texture units.  

RTX‑OPS combines operation counts weighted by workload: Tensor ops (20 % of frame time), FP32 (80 %), RT ops (40 % of 80 % = 32 %) and INT32 ops (28 % of 80 % = 22.4 %). For an RTX 2080 Ti this yields 78 RTX‑OPS.  

Ray tracing works by casting rays from the camera through each pixel; a BVH acceleration structure reduces the number of triangle tests, and denoising improves visual quality. Turing’s RT Cores perform BVH traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, enabling real‑time performance on a single GPU.  

Ray‑traced shadows provide correct contact‑hardening from area lights, replacing shadow maps; ambient occlusion grounds objects; reflections produce artifact‑free glossy reflections. Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider demonstrate RTX‑based shadows, reflections and lighting effects.  

Overall, Turing combines dedicated ray‑tracing (RT) and AI (Tensor) cores with hybrid rendering, new shading models (mesh shading, VRS, texture‑space shading, multi‑view rendering) and VirtualLink connectivity to deliver real‑time, cinematic‑quality graphics for games and professional applications.

The study examines structural and policy-related barriers to medical oxygen access in Peru. Peru’s health system is fragmented, with public, social security, and private subsystems overseen by the Ministry of Health, and governance is decentralized across 24 regions, with political and economic power concentrated in Lima. Medical oxygen was added to the essential medicines list in 2010 with a purity requirement of >99%, a policy trap that limited market competition—six companies (dominated by Linde‑Praxair and Air Products groups) supplied 92.6% of government contracts from 2008 to 2020. Political instability (7 presidents and 17 health ministers between 2016‑2022) hampered coordinated responses. During the COVID‑19 pandemic, Peru experienced the highest excess mortality globally in 2020 (413.4 per 100,000), and oxygen demand surged, revealing severe shortages and inequities, especially in Andean and jungle regions where production and distribution were limited. The government’s response was slow; lowering the purity standard to 93% required two laws, three ministerial resolutions, and seven months. A lack of accurate data and a national oxygen strategy further hindered crisis management. Civil society, notably the Respira Peru initiative, donated 496 oxygen plants, but many remain unused, broken, or abandoned due to maintenance funding gaps, legal clearance delays, and insufficient technical personnel. The authors recommend establishing a national oxygen system to ensure sustainable supply, equitable distribution, equipment maintenance, and trained staffing for future health emergencies.

The speaker tells the Council that improving the Nation’s moral and spiritual life is its purpose, and that political success depends on the people’s religious convictions. He describes modern life as complex, creating new opportunities for crime and misuse of government, while post‑war conditions weaken old restraints and increase lawlessness. He argues that government can maintain order and justice but cannot alone produce the public resolve to obey the law; that resolve comes from religion. Education reduces ignorance and vice, but intellectual progress without moral growth merely amplifies harmful capacity. Historically, clergymen such as Thomas Shepherd, Thomas Hooker and John Wise shaped American education and government through religious teaching. He emphasizes that government legitimacy rests on a common conscience grounded in belief in God, and that democracy fails without faith. Concluding, he asserts that only a broader commitment to religion can enforce law, reform individuals and preserve the Nation’s enlightened civilization.

A scoping review of 65 articles published 2012–2024 examined socioeconomic status (SES) measurement methods in sub‑Saharan African health research. The review found 41 SES measures grouped into 11 categories; the asset‑based wealth index (61.9% of studies), especially the Wealth Index calculated via principal component analysis, was the most common. South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana contributed the most articles. Cross‑sectional and cohort designs dominated, and major research themes were SES assessment and maternal/child health. Findings indicate variability in SES measures complicates cross‑study comparisons and policy application, and the authors recommend moving toward standardized SES measurement across Africa while allowing local adaptation.

Researchers using 3D modeling and field experiments confirmed that Rapa Nui’s moai statues were moved upright by a rocking “walk” motion with rope and only a few people. A 4.35‑ton replica with a forward lean and D‑shaped base was transported 100 m in about 40 minutes by 18 people, and the island’s concave roads (≈4.5 m wide) provided stabilization, supporting the hypothesis that the statues were not dragged lying down. The study highlights the innovative engineering of the ancient Rapa Nui people.

Sudan, the world's last male northern white rhinoceros, was euthanized on Monday in Kenya at age 45 after a severe leg infection left him unable to stand. Captured in Sudan at two years old in 1975, he was moved from Dvůr Králové Zoo in the Czech Republic to the Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya in 2009, together with the two remaining females, Najin and Fatu. Once abundant across Uganda, Chad, southwestern Sudan, the Central African Republic and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the subspecies numbered about 2,000 in 1960 but war‑funded poaching drove it to extinction in the wild. Caretaker Joseph Thaida described Sudan as affectionate and gentle, noting his curiosity toward visitors and his adoption of natural behaviors such as horn sharpening and mud wallowing. Sudan never reproduced with the females. Veterinarian Dr. Steve Ngulu said sperm was collected, but both remaining females are incapable of gestation: one is sterile and the other cannot carry a calf. Scientists plan to retrieve eggs, fertilize them and implant the embryo in a southern white rhino – a procedure never attempted and risky to the females.

Ethiopia has made progress reducing maternal mortality (MMR fell from 871 to 412 per 100,000 live births between 2000–2016) but still faces large disparities in the use of essential maternal services; about half of pregnant women do not receive antenatal care or deliver in health facilities, with utilization varying by region, wealth, and other factors. To address this, the study aimed to develop a Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) that identifies pregnant women at higher risk of not using services, to create vulnerability indexes, and to test how vulnerability scores relate to essential service utilization.

The study was a community‑based quasi‑experiment conducted in Oromia, Ethiopia (early 2024). Four woredas were selected (two treatment, two control). Household visits screened 1,614 homes, yielding 1,189 pregnant women with ≥5 months gestation; 470 were sampled for detailed vulnerability assessment. A 20‑item structured questionnaire was built from literature and secondary analysis of the 2019 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey, covering economic, social, and service‑access dimensions. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, reliability testing (Cronbach’s α and Kuder‑Richardson‑20), and fit‑index assessment were used to reduce items.

Four items were retained for urban‑rural settings (rural residence, house not made of corrugated iron, woman’s lack of a mobile phone, distance to a health facility >30 minutes) and six items for rural settings (woman’s and husband’s illiteracy, house not made of corrugated iron, woman’s and household’s mobile‑phone ownership, distance to a health facility). Both sets showed factor loadings >0.3, internal reliability ≈0.60, and acceptable model fit (RMSEA ≤0.06, CFI ≥ 0.94, TLI ≥ 0.90). Higher composite vulnerability scores were associated with lower health‑facility delivery and fewer antenatal‑care visits; women scoring ≥3 points (urban‑rural) or ≥1 point (rural) were more likely to deliver at home. Mediation analysis indicated that the effect of vulnerability on facility delivery was partly mediated through antenatal‑care utilization.

The MVST enables front‑line health workers to classify pregnant women by degree of vulnerability, facilitating targeted, cost‑effective interventions. Limitations noted include potential lack of universal applicability, the dynamic nature of vulnerability, and the need for validation against health outcomes. The authors conclude that this is the first tool in Ethiopia to integrate holistic factors for identifying underserved pregnant women and recommend further development and validation across low‑ and middle‑income settings.
