New York’s early‑intervention program, which provides speech, physical and occupational therapy to about 70,000 children from birth to age 3, has not given providers a substantive pay increase in three decades. Reimbursement rates for a standard 30‑minute visit fell from an average of $79 in 1994 to $69 in 2022, and therapists with master’s degrees typically earn $50,000–$70,000—far less than comparable roles in other settings. Two statewide rate cuts (10 % in 2010 and 5 % in 2011) followed a decade‑long freeze, and special‑education teachers were excluded from a modest 2022 bump. In 2024 the legislature authorized a 5 % rate increase for in‑person services and an additional 4 % for rural/underserved areas, but the 5 % increase still requires federal Medicaid approval; the 4 % was approved in September but implementation is pending. Proposed Medicaid cuts by the Trump administration could further delay or reduce rate boosts.

Providers report that travel, paperwork, lesson planning and equipment are largely uncompensated, and many have left for higher‑paying jobs—e.g., occupational therapists moving to nursing homes for an additional $30,000. The loss of staff has caused service gaps, especially in rural regions where families such as Katie Wheeler’s daughter have gone months without therapy. A 2025 pay cut for virtual providers prompted many to quit. Research shows timely early‑intervention improves children’s outcomes; when services are delayed, children enter school with lower skills.

Advocates attribute the stagnation to the program’s low political visibility, past fraud concerns, and the largely female, home‑based workforce. The Children’s Agenda reports that reimbursement rates would need a 240 % increase to regain the purchasing power of the early 1990s. Provider representatives, including veteran teacher Emily Lengen and former physical‑therapist Sandra Ribeiro, describe a “dire” situation where many are paid less now than when they entered the field, yet they continue working because they love the work. Similar pay and staffing problems are reported in Texas, Rhode Island and Illinois, where the number of speech therapists fell 13 % and physical therapists 16 % between 2018 and 2023.
Appeal dismissed; see People v Seaberg, 74 NY2d 1; JJ. concur.

People in the United States consume more protein than the recommended 0.8 g per kilogram of body weight, but dietary guidelines treat all whole‑food protein sources as equivalent. Recent research shows this assumption is inaccurate: animal foods (meat, dairy, eggs) contain higher‑quality proteins—higher essential amino‑acid density and better bioavailability—than most plant foods, and animal protein produces greater muscle‑protein synthesis in controlled feeding studies. Consequently, many adults, especially those over 70, may not obtain enough high‑quality protein, raising the risk of muscle loss, weakness and sarcopenia. Nutrition scientists propose refocusing guidelines on essential amino acids rather than total protein; a tool called EAA‑9 scores foods by the limiting essential amino‑acid content, indicating that a single egg provides a score of ~15.8 % while a tablespoon of peanut butter scores only ~4 %, and that much larger quantities of plant foods are needed to match an egg’s protein benefit. Strategies to improve protein quality include combining complementary plant proteins (e.g., beans with rice), processing methods such as soaking, sprouting or fermentation, and choosing softer or ground animal products for older adults. The Netherlands offers a model that reduces meat intake while recommending weekly legumes, fish, dairy, nuts and daily fruits and vegetables, and advises non‑meat eaters to increase protein or obtain it from dairy and eggs. Experts suggest updating dietary guidance to focus on essential amino‑acid adequacy, tailoring recommendations to age and health status, and providing clear, practical meal models to help people meet protein needs while reducing meat consumption.

The article connects transformer variants with formal language theory, logic, and circuit complexity. Unique Hard Attention Transformers (UHAT) are strictly contained in AC0 and are characterized by first‑order logic over strings with monadic numerical predicates (FO[Mon]), capturing star‑free regular languages and even palindromes. Average Hard Attention Transformers (AHAT) are bounded by TC0; Counting LTL extended with unary predicates is expressible by AHAT with positional encodings, and its fragment Kt[#] is captured by masked NoPE‑AHAT. NoPE‑AHAT recognizes exactly permutation‑invariant languages with semi‑algebraic Parikh images. Hard‑attention models give upper bounds for softmax transformers; uniform‑attention layers (AHAT[U]) are simulable by softmax, implying that Kt[#] languages and permutation‑invariant semi‑algebraic languages are also recognizable by softmax transformers. Verification of masked UHAT without positional encodings is EXPSPACE‑complete, while emptiness of NoPE‑AHAT is undecidable. Expressibility does not guarantee efficient trainability: PARITY can be expressed but is hard to train, whereas MAJ is trainable. A formal version of the RASP‑L conjecture, linking length generalization to limit transformers and Kt[#], has been proved, highlighting open challenges in the growing field of Formal Languages and Neural Networks.

The lecture discusses gender discrimination and identity, covering reasons to study gender differences (equality, efficiency, preference formation), persistent gender wage gaps (20-30% even after controlling for education and work time), and causes of female labor market gains (education, technology, labor demand shifts, reduced discrimination). It uses blind auditions in orchestras (Goldin and Rouse) as an example of a technological solution that increased female hiring. The lecture then explores how beliefs contribute to discrimination, citing Sarsons (2019) showing physicians update beliefs differently for male and female surgeons, penalizing women more for bad outcomes and rewarding them less for good outcomes. Gender identity norms (Bertrand et al., 2015) are discussed, where prescriptions like men earning more than wives lead to a "missing mass" in couples where wives earn more, resulting in lower marriage rates, higher divorce, and wives working less. The impact of children on women's earnings (about 20% long-run penalty) and the transmission of identity norms through generations are noted. Gender-neutral policies, like tenure clock stopping, may unintentionally favor men if unenforced. Finally, women are more likely to volunteer for and be asked to do non-promotable tasks, amplifying gender gaps. Overall, biased beliefs and identity concerns play a significant role in persistent gender disparities.

The passage documents the ADS868xW series 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end and precision reference. Key topics include: the device transitions from ACQ to CONV state on the CONVST/CS rising edge, with conversion time varying between tconv_min and tconv_max. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge and end at the subsequent rising edge, with optimal frames requiring exactly 32 SCLK cycles. The device supports nine configuration registers (addresses 00h-28h) and operates using SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) with options for single or dual SDO modes, plus source-synchronous protocols. Write operations require unlocking the RST_PWRCTL_REG register by first writing 69h to address 05h. The device includes programmable input and AVDD alarms with user-configurable thresholds and hysteresis. Power-saving options include NAP mode and power-down mode with register control. Power supply recommendations include decoupling AVDD with 10µF and 1µF capacitors and DVDD with a minimum 10µF capacitor, with specific PCB layout guidelines for separating analog and digital sections.

Findings indicate that lack of awareness, self-doubt, stigma, and discrimination impede help-seeking and can constitute epistemic injustice. Recommendations include raising awareness, mitigating stigma, improving primary care access, and establishing dedicated Long Covid services.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy monitors the S&P 500 for three consecutive daily declines. A trade is entered at the close of the third down day and exited at the next day’s open (or close in an alternative version). Backtesting from 1993 shows 661 trades, an average gain of 0.13 % per trade, a 65 % win rate, and an 8 % maximum drawdown. Exiting at the close improves average gain to 0.24 % but lowers win rate to 61 % and raises max drawdown to 17 %. A March 2022 modified version reduces market exposure, achieving a 0.35 % average gain, a 60 % win rate, and a 10 % max drawdown, and produced a 0.3 % average gain across 35 trades during the 2022 bear market. The strategy also applies to Nasdaq 100 and other stocks, but with reduced effectiveness.

Double‑down is a stock‑trading tactic in which a trader adds a second position equal in size to an existing losing long position when the price falls, aiming to lower the average entry price and recover losses faster if the price rebounds. In the example, buying 100 shares at $136 and then another 100 shares at $100 allows breakeven after a $18 rise (half the decline). The strategy focuses on price rather than on the odds of success, often creating a mental bias.

The double‑down differs from the Martingale strategy: Martingale doubles the position size after each loss, raising risk more sharply, while double‑down adds the same size as the initial trade. It also differs from the repair strategy, which uses call options.

Backtesting on SPY (a mean‑reverting asset) showed that doubling down improved performance: 236 trades with an average gain of 0.97% versus 518 trades with 0.56% for a non‑doubling approach, and the larger the price fall, the larger the expected gains. Testing on HYG (a trend‑following asset) produced the opposite result: fewer trades but a larger average loss (‑0.22% vs ‑0.19%), indicating double‑down is unsuitable for assets that trend rather than revert.

Overall, double‑down can be effective in mean‑reverting markets but is generally considered a bias‑driven move, rarely part of a rational trading plan, and carries the risk of large losses if the market continues to decline.

Low‑side current sensing uses an amplifier to amplify the voltage drop across a shunt resistor and a comparator to generate a logic‑high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Bypass capacitors (0.1 µF, low‑ESR ceramic) must be placed directly between the V+ pin and ground at each device to suppress supply ringing and false triggers caused by fast output edges (tens of nanoseconds). The circuit can operate from split supplies (V+ and V‑) or single supply (V+ and GND); with split supplies the output swings low to V‑. A stable, low‑noise supply and careful layout—keeping output and input traces apart, using a series resistor (<100 Ω) to dampen ringing, and employing controlled‑impedance back‑terminated traces for long runs—are essential for accurate comparator operation. Documentation updates are available via TI’s website notifications, and design support can be obtained from the TI E2E™ forums. ESD handling precautions are required, and mechanical packaging dimensions are defined in millimeters.

The paper investigates the emergence of a new productivity paradox driven by the Internet of Things (IoT) and the dual nature of information and communication technology (ICT). It reviews earlier productivity paradox debates (Solow, Brynjolfsson) and notes that the Internet’s characteristics (freebies, easy copying, mass standardization) cause ICT prices to fall, leading to declining marginal productivity for high‑R&D‑intensive firms. These firms therefore shift their value creation from captured GDP (monetized revenues) to uncaptured GDP (un‑monetized value such as consumer surplus, free services, and new goods) while trying to maintain technology prices.

Empirical analysis of the top 500 global ICT firms from 2005‑2016 shows a bi‑polarization: high‑R&D‑intensive firms (HRIFs) fall into a vicious cycle where increased R&D leads to lower marginal productivity, whereas low‑R&D‑intensive firms enjoy a virtuous cycle. The authors attribute this trend to the Internet‑driven price decrease (the “two‑faced” nature of ICT) and a shift in consumer preferences toward supra‑functionality beyond pure economic value.

To counteract the productivity decline, leading ICT firms (Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, Amazon) activate a self‑propagating function that enhances functionality development by harnessing “soft innovation resources”: (1) a preference for supra‑functionality, (2) leveraging sleeping resources (e.g., Uber‑style ridesharing), (3) building trust through overdrawing past information (e.g., digital education), (4) delivering utmost gratification from past experiences (commodification of experiences), (5) invoking memories and future dreams (e.g., streaming‑live music co‑evolution), and (6) tapping untapped resources such as women’s potential. These resources enable “soft value addition” that supports uncaptured GDP without large additional investment.

The study concludes that global ICT firms must transition from traditional ICT‑driven functionality strategies to sophisticated digital business strategies, recognizing the trap of ICT advancement and increasing dependence on uncaptured GDP. Successful firms employ trust‑based ICT‑driven disruptive business models with a consolidated challenge to social demand, leveraging soft innovation resources to create self‑propagating functionality development and thereby sustain market value.

Nuclear binding energies explain nuclear stability and abundance patterns. Binding energy is calculated by subtracting the actual nuclear mass from the sum of constituent nucleon masses. Average binding energy per nucleon is approximately 7.5-9 MeV for most nuclei, with a maximum around iron. This curve explains why fusion (combining light nuclei) and fission (splitting heavy nuclei) release energy.

The Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, also called the liquid-drop model, parameterizes binding energy with five terms: the volume term (dominant, ~16 MeV per nucleon, indicating short-range nuclear forces), the surface term (reduced binding for surface nucleons, proportional to A^(2/3)), the Coulomb term (proton repulsion), the asymmetry term (preferring equal numbers of protons and neutrons due to the Pauli exclusion principle), and the pairing term (favoring even numbers of protons and neutrons to minimize energy).

The overlap in soccer is a tactic where a wing fullback sprints past the midfielder along the sideline into the attack, creating an unmarked player opportunity. If the overlapping player is covered, the defender typically leaves their position, freeing another attacker. The midfielder remains in attack position (distinguishing it from a "vertical offensive switch"). The overlap requires space and is performed near the sideline where vertical and width room exists. It can be initiated with the midfielder or fullback having possession. The usual result is a cross toward the end-line or a pass back to the midfielder if covered. An "underlap" variant has the fullback sprinting inside the midfielder, typically resulting in a free inside player who can shoot. After both plays, the back defender returns to their original position. Coaches should vary between overlap and underlap to keep defenses guessing.

Ross Nelson v. Peter John (1906): This case concerned restrictions on alienation of lands allotted to Puyallup tribal Indians under the 1854 treaty. The court held that such restrictions were valid and not void as repugnant to the grant because government policy made Indians wards requiring protection. The Bland Act conferring citizenship did not impliedly repeal the restrictions. Contracts conveying allotted lands made before removal of restrictions are void. The Act of Congress of March 3, 1893, permitted removal of restrictions but only after ten years. Plaintiff Nelson sued for specific performance of a land contract with Indian allottees dated March 9, 1892. The trial court sustained a demurrer, and the Washington Supreme Court affirmed, rejecting arguments that restrictions were invalid, impliedly repealed, or removed by state legislation with Congressional consent.

The passage presents a mathematical framework for modeling SARS-CoV-2 transmission using a nine-compartment SEIR-like system of ordinary differential equations (including susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic, mildly, severely, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased individuals). The main results establish the well-posedness, uniqueness, and non-negativity of solutions for the model over time intervals, and demonstrate that the parameter-to-solution map is continuous, injective, and Fréchet differentiable.

RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC) uses neural shaders to compress material textures, reducing memory usage from 1110 MB to 333 MB (over 3×) while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) adds randomness to sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré, and on Blackwell GPUs provides higher‑order filtering at a single point sample, benefiting from a 2× increase in point‑sampled texture filtering rate. Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) employs a neural shader to cache radiance after the first bounce and infers final lighting for many bounces, training on live game data to deliver real‑time global illumination and dynamic lighting while reducing GPU load. RTX Skin brings film‑style subsurface scattering to real‑time path‑traced games for translucent materials, and RTX Neural Faces applies a real‑time generative AI model to a rasterized face plus pose data, trained on thousands of offline images and optimized with TensorRT, to produce more natural facial rendering. The Blackwell architecture comprises three GPU dies: GB202 (flagship, 92.2 B transistors, 12 GPCs, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, 512‑bit memory), GB203 (high‑end, 45.6 B transistors, 7 GPCs, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, 256‑bit memory) and GB205 (entry, 31 B transistors, 5 GPCs, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, 192‑bit memory). The GeForce RTX 50 series includes the RTX 5090 (GB202), RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti (GB203) and RTX 5070 (GB205), each with specifications compared to prior generations.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine discovered a backup heat‑producing system in brown fat that can burn calories independently of the mitochondria‑based uncoupling protein 1. This system involves peroxisomes that multiply upon cold exposure and generate heat through the enzyme acyl‑CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). Mice lacking ACOX2 in brown fat showed reduced cold tolerance, lower body temperature, poorer insulin sensitivity and greater weight gain on a high‑fat diet, whereas mice with elevated ACOX2 had increased heat production, better cold tolerance, improved insulin sensitivity and weight control. The fatty acids metabolized by ACOX2 are present in dairy, breast milk and produced by gut microbes, suggesting that dietary or drug interventions targeting this pathway could boost metabolism and aid weight loss. Although the work was performed in mice, human data hint at a similar link between these fatty acids and lower body mass index.

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI) was created in 2003 by Standard & Poor’s. It comprises the same 500 U.S. companies as the market‑cap‑weighted S&P 500 but assigns each stock an equal 0.2% weight at each quarterly rebalance, instead of weighting by market value. Sector weights are therefore determined by the number of stocks in each sector. ETFs tracking the two indexes are the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) and the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY); RSP must be rebalanced to keep equal weighting. Historically the equal‑weight index outperformed the market‑cap index, a result attributed to the small‑cap effect—smaller companies grow faster than larger ones—but this outperformance stopped in the last decade. RSP’s expense ratio (0.20%/yr) is higher than SPY’s (0.0945%). A $10,000 investment in RSP in 2004 grew to about $60,000 after 18 years (dividends reinvested) versus roughly $55,000 for SPY, and the gap widens over time. Daily return differences between the ETFs are larger during market turbulence such as 2008 and 2020, and equal‑weight positioning can offset losses from large‑cap declines.

Choked jets in core-collapse supernovae with Blue Supergiant/Red Supergiant progenitors may produce high-energy neutrinos via hadronic interactions in dense stellar material. The passage describes relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of jet propagation, cocoon dynamics, and shock formation, using a stellar setup with specified density profiles, jet injection parameters (luminosity, opening angle, magnetization, engine duration), and a shock‑finding algorithm. It presents scaling relations for breakout and choking times derived from 39,000 one‑dimensional models, initial results for a specific Blue Supergiant case (R⋆=50 R⊙, M⋆=15 M⊙, L=10⁵¹ erg/s, Γ₀=7, σ≈10⁻², engine time 5 s), and shows a double‑shock structure (termination shock, cocoon shock, internal collimation shock) with evolving Mach numbers. The jet chokes within about a minute, and future work will explore additional progenitor and jet parameters to assess neutrino detectability from such choked‑GRB events.

VR: VirtualLink USB‑C eliminates multiple cables; Multi‑View Rendering expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi‑Projection to four views and up to 32 at API level; Variable Rate Shading enables foveated rendering; VRWorks Audio uses RT Cores for ray‑traced audio.

The lecture continues the discussion of the massive Sudakov form factor in SCET for the LHC, highlighting the need for an additional rapidity regulator (nu) besides dimensional regularization to handle 1/eta poles. Factorization involves a hard function (Wilson coefficient), collinear functions (cn, cn bar), and a soft function, with physical observables requiring cancellation of cutoffs. Renormalization group evolution must be performed in a two-dimensional mu-nu space to sum large logarithms, with modes localized at specific points (hard at mu~q, collinear at mu~m and nu~q, soft at mu~m and nu~m). The evolution kernels connect initial conditions to a common point, and path independence follows from commutativity of mu and nu derivatives. Anomalous dimensions are derived by requiring bare objects independent of mu and nu, yielding simple evolution kernels (exponentials with Sudakov logs). Applications include Higgs production (gg to Higgs with pt distribution, SCET2, involving rapidity divergences and transverse-momentum-dependent PDFs) and Drell-Yan (pp to l+ l-), with three kinematic cases: inclusive (standard PDFs, SCET1), threshold endpoint (soft function, summing logs of 1-tau), and isolated (measuring small plus momentum in hemispheres, leading to beam functions as matrix elements of chi bar chi with both large and small momentum arguments). Beam functions appear in processes with initial state radiation and jets.

The lecture discusses effective coding gain for signal constellations. The effective coding gain measures the gap between a given signal set and baseline 2-PAM at a fixed probability of bit error of 10^-5. Using the union bound estimate P_b ≈ K_b·Q(√(2γ_c·E_b/N_0)), where K_b is the average number of nearest neighbors per information bit and γ_c is the nominal coding gain (d_min²/(4E_b)), one can plot performance curves by shifting the baseline horizontally by γ_c and vertically by K_b.

A rule of thumb states effective coding gain ≈ nominal coding gain in dB minus 0.2·log₂(K_b), meaning each factor-of-two increase in K_b costs 0.2 dB. Examples show 2-PAM and 4-QAM both have 0 dB effective coding gain, while a 4-point constellation in 3 dimensions (from a 3×4 Cartesian product) achieves approximately 1 dB.

Orthogonal signal sets, where signals are pairwise orthogonal with constant distance between any two points, approach the Shannon limit as M→∞ but have two major drawbacks: spectral efficiency (2log₂M/M) approaches zero, and decoding complexity (M log M operations per symbol) is exponential in transmitted bits. Simplex signal sets, derived by subtracting the mean from orthogonal sets, form equilateral triangles and tetrahedra. Bi-orthogonal signal sets double the number of points by adding negatives of orthogonal signals, doubling nearest neighbors.

The lecture introduces binary block codes for Chapter 6, where K input bits are encoded into N bits, then mapped to binary symbols ±α. This separates coding from modulation. In the power-limited regime, binary signaling loses at most 0.2 dB compared to optimal signaling, making this architecture practical.

The PSY-COVID study analyzed predictor variables for compliance with COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 Spanish adults during the first wave of the pandemic (May-June 2020). Markov cohort‑state‑transition models (MCSTMs) are widely used in cost‑effectiveness modelling; their core element is the transition probability matrix (TPM). Estimating TPMs is difficult when data come from multiple sources, have unequal observation intervals, or contain missing transitions. An existing uniform‑weight EM algorithm (Craig & Sendi) handles unequal intervals but can increase transition‑state variance and affect probabilistic sensitivity analysis. The present work proposes an optimized, weighted EM algorithm that chooses weights to minimize the variance of a model output (e.g., the incremental cost‑effectiveness ratio, ICER).  

During the E‑step each multi‑step transition‑count matrix C(s) is decomposed into estimated 1‑step counts Ĉ(s→1); the M‑step recomputes the TPM by row‑normalizing a combined estimate. Unlike the uniform sum, the combined estimate is a weighted sum (Equation 2) where weights are selected via a grid search over the 3‑simplex to minimize the variance of the chosen output function. Uncertainty around the TPM is obtained with Efron’s bootstrap; bootstrap replicates of the TPM are generated, the ICER is computed for each, and its variance is used to guide the weight optimization.

A proof‑of‑concept example uses a 3‑state Markov model (Healthy, Unhealthy, Death) with a monthly cycle. Simulated data include 1‑month, 2‑month and 3‑month transition‑count matrices (C(1), C(2), C(3)) created from missed health‑state reports (assumed missing at random). The algorithm adjusts weights over 5 000 bootstrap samples; convergence is achieved when the step size reaches 0.01. Compared with the uniform‑weight method, the optimized weights reduced ICER variance by 15.2 % and increased the probability of cost‑effectiveness at a £20 000/QALY threshold by 3 percentage points, while the mean ICER remained similar.

The authors note that weighting is appropriate only when source data are similar; pooling heterogeneous studies may bias the TPM. They recommend a stepwise approach: assess pooling feasibility, apply both uniform and weighted methods, check for precision gains without accuracy loss, and validate weights with experts if needed. Further statistical validation with real‑world or trial data is identified as a next step.

A multi‑criteria integer model is presented to optimize ambulance station locations by maximizing population reachability within two response‑time radii (5 min and 10 min) while ensuring all demand points are reachable within the legal 15 min limit. From 17 candidate sites, four stations were selected together with 13 fixed stations. Solving produced 16 Pareto‑optimal solutions. A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock rises sharply, forcing short sellers to buy back borrowed shares to cover their positions, which further elevates the price and can generate large, theoretically unlimited losses for the shorts. Short selling itself involves borrowing shares, selling them, and hoping for a price decline; profits are capped at roughly 100 % while losses can exceed that amount, and most assets tend to rise over time, creating a headwind for short positions. Short squeezes are rare events, and backtesting a specific short‑squeeze strategy is practically impossible because the events are random and lack clear, quantifiable patterns; high short‑interest ratios do not reliably forecast a squeeze and historically have underperformed low‑interest stocks. The typical duration of a squeeze is two to four weeks, often less than a month, with examples such as the Volkswagen squeeze lasting about 31 trading days and the GameStop squeeze lasting under a month (GameStop rose from around $5 to $80 in early 2021, and in a separate account from $17 to a peak of $483 within a month). An exit strategy for shorts involves monitoring price movements and short‑interest data, using stop‑loss or trailing‑stop orders to lock in gains or limit losses before the price reverses. The opposite of a short squeeze is a long squeeze (or bear squeeze), in which a heavily shorted stock falls, forcing shorts to buy to cover and thereby driving the price even lower. In the U.S., a short squeeze may be illegal if it results from deliberate manipulation of price or stock availability; naked short sales—selling shares without first borrowing them—are prohibited, while derivatives markets have no borrowing requirement. Adding short strategies to a portfolio can provide diversification, though they are generally not profitable as standalone approaches.

Stereo‑electroencephalography (SEEG) resting‑state data from 43 drug‑resistant focal epilepsy patients were analyzed to investigate information flow and excitation‑inhibition balance in the epileptic network. Within‑frequency (directed transfer function) and cross‑frequency (cross‑frequency directionality) connectivity were computed over 1–250 Hz in 10‑minute interictal epochs. The seizure‑onset zone (SOZ) was clinically identified; 1/f power slope (FOOOF) estimated excitability. Balanced random‑forest classification was used to predict electrode‑level SOZ membership and patient‑level seizure outcome. Results showed dominant information flow from non‑SOZ to SOZ across frequencies, with higher inward connectivity and more negative 1/f power slope in SOZ indicating lower excitability. Greater asymmetry of within‑frequency flow (weaker SOZ→non‑SOZ, stronger non‑SOZ→SOZ) correlated with Engel I (seizure‑free) outcome. Random‑forest models achieved 0.85 accuracy and 0.94 AUC for SOZ identification and 0.77 accuracy/0.78 AUC for outcome prediction. The findings suggest that resting‑state directed connectivity combined with machine learning can localize SOZ and predict seizure outcome without prolonged ictal recordings, potentially improving patient care.

The lecture discusses the differences between Riemann and Lebesgue integration. Riemann partitions the time axis into intervals, while Lebesgue partitions the range axis and measures the set of input values mapping to each range interval. Lebesgue integration always gives the same result as Riemann when the Riemann integral exists, but also exists for "weird" functions where Riemann fails, such as a function equal to 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals. The measure of rational numbers in [0,1] is zero, and there are uncountable sets with measure zero like a modified Cantor set. A function is measurable if the set of times where the function lies in any interval is measurable. For non-negative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists as either finite or infinite. L1 and L2 function spaces are defined by whether the integrals of |u(t)| and |u(t)|² are finite; for time-limited functions, L2 implies L1. The Fourier series theorem states that for L2 functions over finite intervals, all Fourier coefficients exist and the series converges in the mean (energy sense). Functions can be segmented into time intervals and expanded into Fourier series, which underlies voice compression algorithms. The lecture concludes by introducing Fourier transforms as the next topic.

The paper introduces a variadic nominal anti‑unification technique for generalizing code fragments that contain binders and variable‑arity constructs. It formalizes variadic nominal terms (atoms, individual and hedge variables, function symbols, abstraction) and an A‑based generalization ordering. The rule‑based VNAU algorithm processes anti‑unification problems, applies decomposition, abstraction, solving, merging, and narrowing rules, and computes an A‑based least‑general generalization together with a description of differences. The algorithm is proven to terminate, be sound and complete, and can be guided by a user‑supplied rigidity function to control the granularity of similarity. Example encodings of code clones (type‑2 and type‑3) illustrate how the method captures structural similarity, handles bound‑variable renaming, and provides a difference measure. Limitations include high nondeterminism and limited control over selection of similar parts, which motivate further refinements. The approach is applicable to program analysis, clone detection, refactoring, and other domains requiring structural abstraction over binders and variadic arity.

The ADS868xW device communicates via a synchronous serial interface that requires a 32‑bit command word for any register write. Half‑word (HWORD) commands operate on 16‑bit register pairs and always ignore the LSB of the 9‑bit address, treating it as 0. Supported commands include CLEAR_HWORD, READ, READ_HWORD, WRITE, WRITE_HWORD, WRITE_MSB, WRITE_LSB, and SET_HWORD; each command determines whether 8‑bit or 16‑bit data is transferred. Write operations to protected registers (e.g., RST_PWRCTL_REG) must be preceded by writing the key value 69h to address 05h.

Output data is shifted out on the SDO‑x pins synchronized to SCLK. The 32‑bit output word can contain conversion results, register data (8‑ or 16‑bit), or a fixed pattern, and can be appended with device address, input‑range flags, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, and parity bits according to the DATAOUT_CTL_REG configuration. The DATA_VAL[2:0] bits in the same register control whether a conversion result, register data, or a fixed data pattern is output.

The multiSPI interface provides four legacy SPI protocols (SPI‑00‑S, SPI‑01‑S, SPI‑10‑S, SPI‑11‑S) selectable via the SDI_MODE[1:0] bits. For reads, the device supports single‑SDO, dual‑SDO, and source‑synchronous (SRC) protocols. In SRC modes the output clock on the RVS pin can be derived from the external SCLK or the internal device clock, and the bus width may be expanded to two bits. All SPI‑compatible protocols maintain the same timing specifications for both single‑ and dual‑SDO modes, with dual‑SDO halving the required SCLK cycles.

Nine configuration registers are mapped: DEVICE_ID_REG (00h), RST_PWRCTL_REG (04h), SDI_CTL_REG (08h), SDO_CTL_REG (0Ch), DATAOUT_CTL_REG (10h), RANGE_SEL_REG (14h), ALARM_REG (20h), ALARM_H_TH_REG (24h), and ALARM_L_TH_REG (28h). These control device ID, reset/power‑down behavior, SPI protocol selection, SDO mode, output data formatting, input range selection, and alarm thresholds/hysteresis.

The device integrates a differential analog front‑end, precision reference, programmable input ranges, and alarm functions (AVDD and input alarms) with user‑programmable thresholds and hysteresis. It offers low‑power NAP and power‑down modes activated by specific register settings. Power‑supply decoupling guidelines (10 µF and 1 µF capacitors on AVDD, 1 µF on DVDD) and PCB layout recommendations (separate analog/digital sections, short ground paths, proper capacitor placement) are provided to ensure performance and noise immunity.

The study examined Hungarian educators’ and students’ familiarity with AI tools, their integration into education, overall attitudes, and the effectiveness of popular chatbots (ChatGPT, Bard/Gemini, Microsoft Copilot) in programming tasks. Interviews (N = 14) and questionnaires (N = 53) showed that participants recognized a wide range of AI applications, especially ChatGPT, and used them mainly for debugging, code generation, explanations, summarizing material, and creating practice tasks. Advantages cited included time savings, faster debugging, and easier self‑learning; concerns covered cheating risk, over‑reliance, and reduced critical thinking. Over 90 % of respondents held a positive view of AI in education. Performance tests on programming‑theorem tasks found ChatGPT correct on 92 % of items versus 64 % for Bard/Gemini and 74 % for Copilot. On complex programming tasks (HTML, JavaScript, PHP, C), ChatGPT solved all after additional prompts, while the others failed on the most demanding C task. The authors conclude that AI tools are useful for users with sufficient prior knowledge and critical‑thinking skills, assisting both teachers (task creation, lesson preparation) and learners (practice, assessment).

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converter design. They support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. Key features include external fault protection via the FAULT pin with a 0.6 V rising threshold and internal fault delay logic, slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation when duty cycle exceeds 50%, and frequency compensation using a transconductance error amplifier (Type 2A or 2B). The devices include internal thermal shutdown at 175 °C (typical) with restart at 160 °C. Operating input voltage range is 4 V to 14 V, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. The controllers require external gate drivers and are suitable for GaN power semiconductor designs. A detailed design example for a synchronous push-pull converter operating at 500 kHz with a 5 V output is provided, covering transformer selection, main and synchronous rectifier FETs, output inductor and capacitance, RCD clamp, soft-start, hiccup mode, and frequency compensation. Layout guidelines emphasize separation of analog and power grounds, minimization of high di/dt switching loops, and placement of bypass and compensation components near the controller.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, delivers up to 312 TFLOPS of mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x the mixed-precision performance and 20x the standard FP32 throughput of the Tesla V100. Obamacare touches nearly all Americans, reducing Medicare costs for seniors, covering free preventive services such as mammograms and contraceptives, and providing subsidies and Medicaid expansion for low‑income adults. The law created health‑insurance exchanges, limited out‑of‑pocket spending, required insurers to cover pre‑existing conditions and banned gender and high age‑rating, and added an individual mandate imposing a penalty (up to $695 or 2.5% of income) for lacking coverage. Medicare beneficiaries saved about $700 this year in premiums and cost‑sharing, and 11 million people saved over $2,100 on prescription drugs; the “donut hole” in drug coverage is being phased out. The ACA also required employers with 50+ workers to provide affordable coverage, though most already did, and allowed children to stay on parents’ plans until age 26, helping 2.3 million young adults. About 10.4 million people were enrolled in exchange plans and 6.9 million bought individual policies outside the exchanges. Medicaid expansion extended coverage to adults earning up to 138% of the poverty line in 31 states and the District of Columbia, adding roughly 17 million enrollees, with the federal government initially covering 100% of the cost.

Repeal would raise Medicare spending by $802 billion over ten years, restoring higher premiums, deductibles and the donut hole for seniors, and eliminating free preventive benefits. Employers would lose the coverage mandate, could raise the hours threshold, and could reinstate annual or lifetime limits; workers could lose free contraceptives and preventive screenings. The individual mandate and most subsidies would end, the Medicaid expansion would be eliminated, and millions could become uninsured. Republicans plan to start by repealing the spending and revenue provisions with a Senate majority and eventually dismantle the entire law except the child‑on‑parents provision.

The passage is an MIT lecture by Hong Liu on holographic duality. Key points include: no textbooks or recitation; grades are 75% PSETs and 25% final project. Gravity differs from other interactions (electromagnetism, weak, strong) which are described by gauge theories, as no complete quantum theory of gravity exists. The 1997 holographic duality proposal states quantum gravity equals quantum field theories on fixed spacetime, with gravity emerging from non-gravitational systems. Sakharov in 1967 proposed gravity could emerge from material systems. The Weinberg-Witten theorem (1980) proves that theories with Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensors cannot contain massless particles with spin greater than 1, preventing emergent gravitons in conventional QFT. This theorem assumes particles exist in the same spacetime as the original theory, which holographic duality evades by placing gravity in a different spacetime.

BioRecall is a pilot cross-sectional biobank-recall study in Central Finland that aims to collect lifestyle and environmental data via an electronic questionnaire from genotyped donors with type 2 diabetes. The questionnaire covers physical activity, diet, anthropometrics, smoking, medical history, work characteristics, emotional states, sleep, and residential environment, with postcode data enabling spatial environmental analysis. Data will be combined with existing genetic and clinical data from the biobank, and participants receive automated feedback on their habits relative to national recommendations. The study has ethics approval and may expand to other Finnish biobanks if successful. Key strengths include a scalable electronic approach and comprehensive exposome data; limitations include a small pilot sample and lack of wearable data.

Sony's PS3 faced intense competition from Microsoft's Xbox 360 (launched a year earlier with 4 million units sold) and Nintendo's Wii (launching two days after PS3 at half the price). The PS3 also served as a vehicle for Sony's Blu-Ray format against Toshiba's HD-DVD. Sony's previous format failures included Betamax and UMD. The PS3's $599 price was significantly higher than competitors. Sony's PlayStation captured 60% of the US market by 1999 and the PS2 dominated with 55% share by 2006. The video game industry evolved from Atari's collapse in 1983 through Nintendo's quality-focused strategy to Sony's 3D CD-based approach. Online gaming became critical, with Xbox Live offering a unified experience while Sony took a more open approach and Nintendo targeted casual gamers with innovative motion controls. The industry faced public backlash over video game violence and the ESRB rating system. Forecasts predicted Sony would lead the next-generation market, but Microsoft's head start posed significant challenges as the November 2006 PS3 launch approached.

DNA origami uses a long scaffold strand and shorter staple strands to self‑assemble predefined nanometer‑scale structures. A team led by Ralf Jungmann employed the super‑resolution DNA‑PAINT technique to image each strand of a rectangular DNA origami, revealing that assembly proceeds robustly across a range of conditions, but strand incorporation efficiency varies with its position in the structure. Physical parameter variations have little effect on overall quality, yet not all binding sites are occupied in every particle. The researchers recommend adding components in large excess and aligning modifications with the measured incorporation map to optimize assembly. DNA‑PAINT thus provides a tool to assess and improve DNA nanostructure construction and offers potential for quantitative structural biology.

The paper defines modal extensions of lattice‑based logics, introduces notions of regular versus non‑regular modal valuations, and shows that a normal modal extension is regular iff the set of designated values is a filter containing its meet. It establishes that for lattices with a top value and a special implication, any upward‑closed set of designated values is implicative, and that filter implicativity characterizes the validity of the axiom (2ϕ ∨ 2ψ) → 2(ϕ ∨ ψ). For axiom K, it proves that linearity outside the filter (with a strictly deductive implication) and anti‑monotonicity/involutivity/down‑distribution (with the standard implication −x+y) are each equivalent to all frames satisfying K. An example with twist algebras derived from Boolean algebras illustrates these results.

The passage discusses data-driven modeling of noisy, high‑dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems using transfer operator theory and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). It describes Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) as a Galerkin method that combines principal component analysis with the discrete‑time Fourier transform to approximate the Koopman operator, enabling linear analysis of nonlinear systems. Kernel‑based DMD algorithms are non‑parametric but become computationally expensive for large datasets. The authors propose integrating Gaussian Process (GP) regression with DMD to obtain a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, providing automatic hyperparameter optimization, sparse dictionary learning, and uncertainty‑aware multi‑step predictions. They employ the variational free energy method to reduce the O(N³) complexity and treat the operators as random variables. The resulting algorithm is a special case of Extended DMD, inheriting some of its limitations.

Bob Jones, a serial entrepreneur, discusses entrepreneurship through two case studies: Regain, a nutrition bar for dialysis patients that failed due to misidentifying the customer (focusing on clinicians instead of patients who couldn't afford or want it), and NiteBite, a timed-release glucose product for diabetics that succeeded by understanding customers' real needs (peace of mind), building demand through diabetes educators, and leveraging customers to bypass slotting fees. Key lessons include the need to identify actual customers, understand what they truly want, build demand before approaching retailers, and focus on benefits. The only non-negotiable requirement for success is having customers who want your product.

Recent interest in rare‑earth barium cuprates (REBCOs) stems from advances in high‑temperature superconducting (HTS) tapes and their proposed use in fusion reactors and particle accelerators. Their superconducting properties are highly sensitive to oxygen stoichiometry; YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋ₓ (YBCO) changes from an antiferromagnetic insulator to a superconductor with oxygen content. Synthesis produces defects such as twin boundaries and oxygen‑sublattice disorder, which can either pin vortices or scatter Cooper pairs. Oxygen vacancies in CuO chains introduce holes in the CuO₂ planes and control critical superconducting parameters; annealing irradiated samples partly restores superconductivity, indicating that oxygen defect diffusion and recombination are crucial.

Classical interatomic potentials fail to reproduce the high‑temperature orthorhombic‑to‑tetragonal transition observed in experiments. To overcome this, we trained a machine‑learning potential based on the Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) method on a large density‑functional‑theory (DFT) dataset. The dataset (1368 configurations, 545 267 atoms) includes equilibrium structures, all possible vacancies and interstitials, amorphous‑like environments, and oxygen Frenkel‑pair (FP) configurations with transition‑state geometries.

The ACE potential achieves RMSEs of ~10 meV/atom for energies and ~70 meV/Å for forces on both training and test sets. It reproduces the DFT equation of state and lattice parameters, outperforming the previous Buckingham‑Coulomb potential, especially far from equilibrium. For defect energetics, migration barriers are reproduced within 20 meV and formation energies are within ~0.2 eV of DFT values.

Large‑scale NPT simulations (~25 000 atoms, up to 75 ns) using the ACE potential spontaneously exhibit the orthorhombic‑to‑tetragonal transition at ~800 K, close to the experimental ~1000 K. The transition is identified as an order‑disorder process: oxygen atoms from CuO chains (O1) and, to a lesser extent, from apical sites (O4) migrate to interstitial O5 positions between chains, making the a and b directions equivalent. The transition is entropy‑driven; the formation energy of O1v–O5i FPs decreases with lattice expansion, facilitating disorder at elevated temperatures.

The developed ACE potential enables accurate investigation of oxygen diffusion in YBCO and can guide optimization of annealing procedures for restoring superconductivity in radiation‑damaged HTS tapes. Future work should extend the potential to variable oxygen content and employ advanced simulation techniques to access experimentally relevant timescales.

The article reviews existing literature to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) impacts inclusive education. It notes that AI is widely recognized as a powerful tool that can personalize learning, provide timely feedback, increase student engagement, and support diverse learners, including those with disabilities and English learners. AI‑enabled features such as text‑to‑speech, speech‑to‑text, writing aids, and chatbots are cited as means to raise awareness of diversity, equity, and inclusion and to assist educators in addressing varied learning needs. The authors argue that effective AI integration requires thoughtful design, teacher involvement, and alignment with cultural and contextual factors.

Inclusive education is defined as a sustained process that upholds diversity, reduces barriers to teaching and learning, and provides equal opportunities for all students regardless of color, race, ethnicity, location, or disability. The literature identifies several barriers to inclusion: teachers’ limited technological competence, overcrowded classrooms, inadequate infrastructure, insufficient resources, lack of parental and community involvement, and labeling of students with special needs.

Benefits of AI highlighted include automated routine tasks, data‑driven monitoring of student performance, cost‑effective administration, and support for self‑directed learning. However, limitations are noted: AI can perpetuate bias if training data are not diverse, implementation can be expensive, and over‑reliance may diminish the human element of teaching, critical thinking, and problem‑solving. Privacy concerns, potential job displacement for educators, and the inability of AI to fully replicate human creativity and emotional support are also mentioned.

The discussion emphasizes designing an inclusive syllabus that incorporates assistive technologies, Universal Design for Learning principles, multiple representation and engagement options, and flexible delivery methods such as asynchronous lessons and offline resources. Recommendations from the article include integrating AI in teaching, adopting child‑centered approaches, providing continuous professional development on inclusion, ensuring safe learning environments, and promoting inclusive policies at institutional and governmental levels.

In conclusion, the authors assert that while AI can significantly enhance inclusive education, its successful implementation depends on balancing technological capabilities with the core human aspects of teaching and learning, and on actively fostering inclusivity in curriculum and practice.

The lecture discusses ion traps and their differences from neutral atom traps. Unlike neutral atoms confined by magnetic/optical forces with depths of microkelvin to kelvin, ions use Coulomb forces that can achieve ~10,000 kelvin confinement with 100 volts per millimeter. Ion cooling methods include Doppler cooling, evaporative cooling, and sideband cooling. Applications include atomic clocks and quantum information processing.

Two main dynamic ion trap types exist: Penning traps using electrostatic and magnetic confinement, and RF/Paul traps that alternate between confinement and anti-confinement at radio frequencies. Paul traps work because the ion's micromotion causes force averaging along its trajectory rather than at fixed positions, resulting in net inward force.

For quantum computation, ion systems use single qubit rotations and two qubit gates like CNOT or controlled phase gates. The Cirac-Zoller gate uses center of mass motion as a data bus: swap ion two's qubit state to phonon motion, perform the controlled phase gate between ion one and the motion, then swap back. This pioneering approach requires ground state cooling and slow operations due to center of mass vibration frequency, limitations not shared by other quantum gate implementations.

National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day, scheduled for May 29 2018 by the Black Star Project and the National Newspaper Publishers Association, responded to a Starbucks arrest incident by urging Black‑owned coffee houses to attract customers while Starbucks closed 8,000 U.S. stores for diversity training. Over 400 Black‑owned coffee shops, cafés and tea houses were expected to participate, stocking extra pastries, coffees and teas and hosting “Black Economic Empowerment Forums” in the evening. Cadillac sold 35,020 units in September 2017, extending a 16‑month growth streak, on pace to exceed last year’s 308,718 total. Year‑to‑date sales rose 44,336 to 256,613 units; U.S. sales grew 1.1% and China surged 37.6%. XT5 led with 103,645 YTD units; ATS rose 15% and CT6 6.6% month‑over‑month. U.S. average transaction price stayed near $54,000, second‑highest among major luxury brands.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors amended and restated the company’s Bylaws to add proxy access and revise stockholder nomination notice periods. The new Section 5(h) permits stockholders (or groups of up to 20) owning at least 3 % of the voting power continuously for three years to include director nominees in the proxy materials, up to the greater of two directors or 20 % of the Board. Stockholders nominating directors outside of proxy access must now provide written notice 90‑120 days before the anniversary of the prior year’s annual meeting (previously 120‑150 days). The Restated Bylaws also provide for timely notice if the meeting date shifts more than 30 days. A copy of the Amended and Restated Bylaws is attached as Exhibit 3.1.

The study examined race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive performance in older adults. Data from three harmonized cohorts (MARS, MAP, Black Clinical Core) provided 2,284 participants aged ≥55 years who self‑identified as Black or White, completed ≥2 cognitive assessments, and had ≥2 BP readings. Participants were classified into three BP groups based on mean systolic BP and its variability relative to the sample standard deviation: normal (mean < 130 mm Hg and low variability), high (mean ≥ 130 mm Hg and low variability), and variable (high variability). Cognitive function was assessed with 19 tests covering episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, and visuospatial ability; composite z‑scores were computed for each domain and for global cognition. Linear mixed‑effects models tested time‑by‑group interactions, adjusting for age, sex, education, and baseline diagnosis, with false‑discovery‑rate correction.

Across all groups, greater time and older age were linked to faster cognitive decline. No racial differences were observed among participants with normal BP. White adults with high BP declined faster than Black adults with normal or high BP in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory, but not episodic memory. White adults with variable BP showed faster decline across all cognitive domains compared with all Black groups. Secondary analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive scores did not explain the race differences. Limitations included the use of BP categories without medication‑adherence data and absence of detailed medication history. The findings suggest that older White adults are more vulnerable to cognitive decline associated with elevated or fluctuating BP than older Black adults, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to reduce racial disparities in cognitive health.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) announced a multiyear AI chip supply agreement with OpenAI, under which AMD will provide its next‑generation MI450 series accelerators to power OpenAI’s growing data infrastructure. OpenAI will also receive warrants to acquire up to 10 % of AMD’s equity upon meeting production and performance milestones. The announcement lifted AMD’s stock more than 20 % in premarket trading, reflecting investor confidence in AMD’s expanding foothold in AI computing. The partnership positions AMD as a challenger to Nvidia in the AI chip market and could generate tens of billions of dollars in revenue if OpenAI scales its hardware demand. AMD also disclosed a $6 billion share‑buyback plan announced earlier this year. Analysts caution that execution risks, technical complexity, and potential supply‑chain bottlenecks remain, and sustained growth will depend on delivering on milestones and maintaining demand from major clients such as OpenAI, Microsoft, and hyperscale cloud providers.

Judges are sanctioning attorneys who file briefs with faulty case citations likely generated by AI. In Puerto Rico, firms including Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison and Sidley Austin shared $24,492 in fees after opposing counsel submitted at least 55 defective citations; the judge reduced the firms’ $88,000 request. In California, lawyer Amir Mostafavi must pay $10,000 to the court for AI‑generated fake quotes and irrelevant cases; opposing counsel received no fees because they did not detect the errors. The cases raise a lawyer’s duty to identify AI‑fabricated citations.

Following the death of President Franklin D. Roosevelt, the speaker addresses Congress with a heavy heart, noting that the world looks to America for decisive leadership. He declares that the war against Germany and Japan will continue until the enemies’ unconditional surrender, and that America will not accept a partial victory. The speaker emphasizes that war criminals must be brought to justice and that a United Nations organization must be built to maintain peace under law, with the great powers serving rather than dominating. He calls for national unity, urging every American, regardless of party, race, creed, or color, to support the effort to create a durable peace. The speech stresses that hope and faith are essential, but that hope alone is insufficient; peace‑loving nations must cooperate and defend each other to prevent future aggression. The speaker asserts that America has learned to fight alongside allies and must now learn to trade and cooperate with other nations for mutual economic benefit. He acknowledges the sacrifices of the armed forces, promises they will be remembered, and says the war strategy remains under the direction of Admiral Leahy, General Marshall, Admiral King, General Arnold, General Eisenhower, Admiral Nimitz, and General MacArthur. Concluding with a prayer for wisdom, the speaker asks Congress and the nation to work together to achieve a just and lasting peace.

Audi, BMW, Volkswagen, and Volvo have discontinued various manual transmission models in South Africa due to low demand. Audi removed the manual A4 1.4T FSI, BMW discontinued the 120i and M140i manuals and removed the manual option for the 220i, 230i, and M240i, while Volkswagen ended manual versions of the Polo GTI, Scirocco 2.0TSI Highline, and Jetta 1.6TDI Comfortline. Volvo discontinued the S60 T3 Kinetic manual. Porsche and Jaguar SA continue to offer manual transmissions.

Stranger Things season 3 cast pay tiers: adults Winona Ryder and David Harbour $350,000 per episode; young core $250,000; teen actors $150,000. Some raises up to 12× levels. Millie Bobby Brown negotiating separately; Netflix declined comment.

U.S. and Belgian officials discussed increasing Congo supplies through development work, with the Belgium government pledging to facilitate such activity. Telegrams and airgrams show that Day will forward a commodity list by August 10, and that data on reciprocal supplies should be sent simultaneously to the British Foreign Office and the State Department for the Combined Raw Materials Board and Combined Production and Resources Board. The Department recommended a tripartite agreement clause to freeze export duties on palm nuts and geranium oil. The signing of the agreement was postponed but made retroactive to the expiration of the existing Anglo‑Belgian pact, a step the Department found satisfactory. Negotiations continued through 1942‑1943 without reaching agreement, after which an Office of Economic Warfare mission visited the Congo and an informal Tripartite Supply Committee was formed. The passage also notes U.S. recognition of a state of war with Hungary, Bulgaria, and Romania, and a mutual‑aid agreement with Czechoslovakia.

A University of Birmingham academic, Dr Chris Bradley, said drainage was not the cause of recent flooding in Birmingham, attributing it to an extreme weather event that produced a month’s rainfall in one hour. Birmingham City Council reported that drains were inspected and no blockages were found, and floodwater receded quickly. A yellow weather warning for Thursday warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain (30‑40 mm per hour, possibly 60‑80 mm in 2‑3 hours), lightning, large hail and a risk of flooding across southern and eastern England.

The article describes a simple ETF momentum rotation strategy that monthly ranks SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20‑year Treasury bonds) and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) by the previous month’s performance and holds the best‑performing ETF for one month. Back‑tested over two decades the strategy outperformed a buy‑and‑hold approach with lower drawdowns; its compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from early 2003 to early 2022 was about 11 % and maximum drawdown before 2022 was 22 %. However, 2022 proved difficult, with the portfolio falling 41 % from its peak, reducing overall performance in the last five to six years. The authors recommend using the strategy in a tax‑deferred account because of frequent trades and note that the trading code is available to members.

Charlie Javice, founder of fintech startup Frank, was sentenced to 85 months (just over seven years) in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase in a $175 million acquisition. A 12‑person jury found her and chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty of three counts of fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit fraud. Javice expressed remorse, apologized to JPMorgan, employees, shareholders and investors, and the judge imposed three years of supervised release, $22.36 million forfeiture and $287 million restitution. The fraud involved inflating Frank’s customer base from fewer than 300,000 real users to over five million by creating synthetic identities, and Javice directed employees to fabricate millions of accounts before the sale. JPMorgan said it “acquired a crime scene” rather than a functioning business, noting it failed to verify the true customer count before paying the $175 million.

A crack forced the operator Ineos to shut the 450,000‑bpd Forties Pipeline System for weeks, prompting Brent crude to rise above $64.50 per barrel and widening the Brent‑WTI spread to about $7 per barrel. The pipeline carries roughly 40 % of UK North Sea oil, links 85 offshore fields, and more than 80 platforms may be halted. An outage of three weeks could disrupt up to 10 million barrels, tightening the Atlantic basin market and increasing U.S. crude exports. The incident mirrors the recent Keystone spill and has global price implications.

S&P 500 fell 1.96% on Friday, dragged down by Apple declines, to 6,212.69, dropping 214.3 points (3.33%) from its record high of 6,427.02 in two days; it closed at its lowest since early July. Last week the index lost 2.36% after a 1.5% gain the prior week, suggesting consolidation after April lows with a possible deeper correction. The AAII sentiment survey showed 40.3% bullish versus 33.0% bearish. VIX rose to 21.90, its highest since late June, historically indicating increased chance of an upward reversal when high. Crude oil fell 2.79% on Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ announced a 547,000 bpd output increase for September, the sixth consecutive monthly rise, raising supply pressure. The U.S. threatened 100% secondary tariffs on India and China for buying Russian oil, risking 1.7 million bpd of demand. Goldman Sachs forecasts $64 oil in Q4 2025, cautioning on geopolitical and demand risks. Market outlook for Monday suggests a short‑term bounce, but low volatility, weak seasonal signals and high valuations support defensive positioning.

Three repeat participants in the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee described their extensive preparation. Erin Howard, 13, who misspelled “Klydonograph” last year, spent three to four hours on weeknights and six to eight hours on weekends studying, focusing on trademarked words, and sacrificing social activities. Cameron Keith, 12, wakes at 5:30 a.m. to review his 200 word lists, logging six hours on weekdays and nine on weekends after previously tying for 18th in 2016 and misspelling “noncompos.” Naysa Modi, 12, is competing for the fourth time; her father described her ability as “absolutely inhuman” and said years of intense effort are required. All repeat spellers highlighted that the competition is driven by love of words and language rather than solely by winning.

President Trump announced a 100% tariff on Chinese goods, effective November 1, prompting US stock indexes to fall and reigniting US‑China trade war concerns. July US employment data missed expectations with only 73 000 jobs added, and May‑June figures were revised down by a total of 258 000, pulling the 12‑month average to its lowest level since the pandemic; almost all gains came from health care. June economic indicators were stronger, with 12 of 20 key data points beating forecasts, making June the best month of 2025 so far. Corporate earnings were strong: 17 mega‑cap firms reported Q2 results, 15 beat earnings estimates (94 % beat rate) and 16 beat sales forecasts by an average of 2.4 %, lifting S&P 500 Q2 earnings‑growth expectations from 7.7 % to 11.2 % and sales‑growth from 4.5 % to 5.6 %. July posted a positive close for the 11th consecutive year, but the market now faces a historically weak seasonal period from August‑October. The S&P 500 reached its long‑term average annual return of 9.1 % and the equal‑weighted index retested its prior record‑high resistance. The US dollar rallied to its 2024 low but was rejected after the tariff news and weak data, while the 10‑year Treasury yield remained rangebound. AI‑related stocks have driven the market; overall earnings growth has surprised to the upside, yet valuations at 22‑25× earnings with a negative equity risk premium suggest limited further upside. Economic slowdown is evident but not yet a recession, and the report expects possible market weakness in the coming months that could create a better entry point for year‑end.

Wiechmann v Wiechmann: In a divorce action, plaintiff Wesley Wiechmann sought physical custody of the couple’s four children. A custody specialist recommended that all four children be placed with defendant Sylvia Wiechmann. After evaluating the statutory best‑interest factors (MCL 722.23; MSA 25.312(3)), the trial court awarded the parties shared legal custody, gave plaintiff physical custody of the two older children and defendant physical custody of the two younger children. The defendant appealed, arguing the trial court abused its discretion by separating the siblings. The Court of Appeals held that while generally it is in a child’s best interests to keep siblings together, when separation better serves an individual child’s interests, that child’s best interests control. Applying the great‑weight‑of‑evidence and palpable‑abuse‑of‑discretion standards, the appellate court affirmed the trial court’s custody order.

SFS is an AMD firmware feature enabling non-persistent runtime updates to AMD-provided firmware without system reboot or BIOS reflash, targeting high-priority and security issues while excluding x86-based code (SMM, AGESA, UEFI). Updates are cryptographically signed by AMD with optional customer co-signing for datacenter approval. Three version tracking levels exist: SFSPL (overall patch level), SPL (individual firmware component security patch level), and SYSPL (run-once code version). BIOS developers enable SFS via specific configuration tokens, and customers deploy an SFSDA to manage updates through the ASP. Updates apply sequentially, require memory alignment, and must be reapplied after reboot as they are non-persistent.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets fell Thursday as investors feared capital outflows after Federal Reserve minutes indicated policymakers may start trimming the central bank’s $4.5 trillion balance sheet later this year. Markets tracked overnight U.S. declines and stayed cautious ahead of the planned Trump‑Xi meeting. MSCI’s Asia‑Pacific index slipped about 0.6 %, while Indonesian shares hit a record high and Philippine shares edged down. Vietnam and Thailand were closed for holidays.

The emergence of Covid‑19 in late 2019 forced many countries to suspend formal schooling and adopt distance education, showing online learning as a viable supplement to face‑to‑face instruction. The paper reviews literature on AI in education, defines AI as systems that automatically perform tasks taught in their programs, and notes that modern AI uses machine learning, deep learning and artificial neural networks, enabling computers to learn from large data sets. Examples given include IBM Watson (which won Jeopardy and now assists in oncology and education) and AlphaGo (which mastered the ancient game of Go). AI terminology—algorithms, machine learning and artificial neural networks—is explained.

In education, AI can support personalized teaching, intelligent education systems (IES), exam analysis, game‑based learning, and other applications. IES consist of domain, pedagogy and learner models and provide adaptive instruction based on feedback. Three modes of AI‑based education are identified: AI‑supported face‑to‑face (human teachers with AI assistance), AI‑led face‑to‑face (virtual teacher on screen or robot), and simulation education (AI in virtual or augmented reality). Andriessen and Sandberg’s scenarios—transfer, studio and negotiation—describe how instruction may be delivered: with fixed goals, server‑independent environments, or interactive, evolving curricula. Two algorithmic approaches are distinguished: supervised learning where humans define objectives, and unsupervised deep learning where AI creates its own curricula.

Potential learning environments include real‑time classroom AI and fully simulated settings that can instantly transport learners to any location. Benefits discussed include increased efficiency, reduced cost, personalized pacing, elimination of peer bullying, and scalable instruction. Concerns raised include possible domination by AI, privacy breaches, teacher unemployment, mental‑health risks, isolation, and confusion between virtual and real worlds.

The authors conclude that distance education will remain important, AI‑based education merits serious interdisciplinary discussion, and society should prepare for a future where machines may share or take over teaching roles.

Mariners beat Rangers 2‑1 on May 28, 2018. Marco Gonzales pitched into the seventh without allowing an earned run for his third straight start, extending his streak to 19 ⅓ innings. Seattle won its ninth game in ten tries, moved 13 games above .500 for the first time since late 2014, and leads MLB with 16 one‑run victories. Texas’s only run came in the third when Rougned Odor scored on a passed ball; Seattle’s two runs in the sixth resulted from a fielding error that prevented a double play and produced RBI singles. The Mariners debuted new acquisitions Alex Colome (All‑Star closer) and Denard Span, both obtained from Tampa Bay. Rangers shortstop Elvis Andrus and third baseman Adrian Beltre took ground balls for the first time since injury, while Seattle shortstop Jean Segura was scratched after a head injury and is expected back Tuesday. The Mariners anticipate Dee Gordon’s return Thursday.

FCA 2017 Financial Lives Survey shows 70% of adults planning to access their defined‑contribution pension have not been asked about options; 2% were asked by some providers, 20% by all. 67% have not received advice from pension provider’s adviser; 40% not taking advice said they could decide alone, 10% cited cost. On retirement income, 33% expect state pension as largest source, 21% DC pot, 15% final salary. 44% know their annual income, 28% little or none, 17% do not know.

Taxify, Europe's fastest-growing ride-sharing app, is launching in Sydney as its first Australian market entry. The company will offer half-priced fares for one month and charges drivers a 15% commission, significantly lower than Uber's. Over 4,000 drivers have registered, and the app already operates in 20 countries with $1 billion in revenue and 4 million users. Founded in 2013 by Markus Villig in Estonia, Taxify is backed by Chinese company Didi Chuxing.

Neuromarketing applies neuroscientific techniques to understand consumer behavior in markets. This study investigates its state in Spain's audiovisual sector through 18 in-depth interviews with consultancies, audiovisual sector representatives, neuroscientists, and academics. The research confirms that neuroscientific methods are feasible for studying audiovisual consumers but require multidisciplinary teams and scientific protocols. Neuromarketing in Spain remains incipient, with its application limited mainly to major private television groups like Atresmedia and Mediaset España. Key barriers include lack of awareness, distrust, high costs, and weak university-business transfer. Film and TV producers show interest but lack resources to invest. The sector expects positive growth contingent on technological advances, data interpretation improvements, cost reduction, and demonstrated ROI. Emotions serve as the core element of audiovisual production and are central to neuroscientific research applications.

Research indicates that installing air filters and upgrading ventilation in schools significantly improves test scores and attendance. A natural experiment from the 2015 Aliso Canyon gas leak showed students in schools with air purifiers gained approximately three months of learning in math, matching results from expensive class-size reduction programs while costing roughly $30 per student versus $7,000. Studies also found air purifiers reduced student absenteeism by 12.5% and Swedish daycare centers saw a 55% drop in illness-related absences. Air quality improvements provide cognitive benefits, reduce respiratory illnesses, and particularly benefit students in low-income communities with higher pollution exposure. The intervention requires minimal administrative burden and experts recommend schools reconnect existing devices, install proper filtration, and monitor outcomes including absenteeism and test scores.

Governor Ige attended the groundbreaking for the Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport, a $220 million, 260,000-square-foot project adding gate capacity for larger aircraft, scheduled for completion in 2020 as part of a $1.3 billion upgrade.

Index Markets Research’s report on the global Plastic Granules market outlines its definition, applications and key players (Dar Al Khaleej Plastics, Nahata Plastics, etc.). It segments the market by product type (PP, HDPE, etc.), end‑use (Plastic products, Clothing, etc.) and geography (North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan & India). The study provides revenue and volume forecasts, cost structure, production capacity, competitive landscape, and a SWOT analysis with investment feasibility.

Australia’s ecosystems are undergoing abrupt, potentially irreversible collapses driven by 1 °C warming since 1900 and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. Recent studies document six sudden regime shifts: kelp forests turned to seaweed turfs after the 2011 marine heatwave; loss of Gondwanan refugia to 2016 wildfires; floodplain‑forest die‑back along the Murray River during the 2001–2009 drought; conversion of alpine forests to shrubland after repeated fires 2003–2014; boom‑and‑bust in arid zones after 2011–2012 extreme rainfall; and mangrove die‑back across a 1,000‑km stretch of the Gulf of Carpentaria after the 2015–2016 monsoon. Except for the Murray River site, these ecosystems had little prior human disturbance, showing even pristine areas lack resilience. Longer heatwaves, intensified fire weather, altered rainfall and shorter intervals between extremes are pushing systems toward tipping points. Targeted actions—assisted recolonisation, reseeding, fire protection—may prevent collapse but are costly and must be decided quickly. The recent surge in catastrophic biological changes indicates many Australian ecosystems are on the brink of collapse.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program data to develop machine learning models that predict healthy aging among adults aged ≥50 based on social determinants of health (SDOH). Healthy aging was defined as a composite of comorbidities (modified Charlson comorbidity index), absence of mild cognitive impairment, and no assisted‑living residence. Three algorithms were trained (logistic regression, multi‑layer perceptron, XGBoost); XGBoost with random oversampling achieved the best performance (AUROC = 0.793, F1 = 0.697, recall = 0.739, precision = 0.659, accuracy = 0.716). SHAP analysis ranked health insurance type as the most predictive feature, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The model demonstrated predictive parity across race and sex groups, indicating fairness across demographic groups. The study concludes that XGBoost accurately predicts healthy aging and that health insurance is a key determinant of healthy aging in older adults.

Joe Flacco has been traded from the Browns to the Bengals in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round draft pick. The Bengals sent a 2026 sixth-round pick to Cleveland as part of the deal. Flacco will start at quarterback against the Packers on Sunday, marking his second start against Green Bay in four weeks. Cincinnati is 2-3 with a three-game losing streak while Joe Burrow remains on injured reserve with a turf toe injury. Bengals coach Zac Taylor confirmed Flacco will take all the reps in practice and is hopeful the veteran quarterback can help end the team's losing streak and keep them in playoff contention.
