Wham is a run play resembling a trap but executed by a tight end or fullback pulling to kick out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. Its main strength is providing quick, unexpected favorable angles for the run and acting as an effective change‑up. Its main weakness is the difficulty and time required to teach and install the play, requiring precise identification of front, assignments, timing, and a powerful player for the block. Detailed alignments are provided for the Wham play versus a 3‑4 odd front and a 4‑3 even front, describing each position’s responsibilities. Two variations are presented: a Gun H‑Back Wham RPO where the center releases to the second level and the fullback kicks out the nose tackle, and a Shotgun Influence Wham where the fullback traps a widened 3‑tech after a guard pull.

Microsoft’s 8‑K filed on March 13 2020 disclosed that co‑founder Bill Gates resigned from the Board of Directors, effective that date; a press release announcing the resignation was attached as an exhibit.

The study examined horizontal intra‑familial transmission of hepatitis C virus (HCV) among household members of HCV‑positive patients in Rwanda. A descriptive cross‑sectional design was used at the Centre Universitaire de Santé Public (CUSP) in Huye district, Southern Province. One hundred and eighty participants were planned; 30 families provided 148 participants aged 5–60 years, predominantly married, from rural sectors. Inclusion criteria covered spouses, breastfeeding mothers and close contacts of index cases. HCV antibody screening was performed with a rapid test and reactive samples were confirmed by ELISA; a questionnaire assessed risk factors and awareness. Data were analysed with descriptive statistics using Excel and SPSS.

The overall HCV prevalence among tested household members was 10.8 % (16/148). Statistically significant associations (p < 0.05) were observed between HCV positivity and co‑infection with HBV (6 of 7 HBV‑positive participants) and with HIV (4 of 4 HIV‑positive participants), and with reporting unprotected sex (12 of 116 participants practising unprotected sex). Blood transfusion was not significantly related to HCV infection (p = 0.058). Awareness of HCV transmission was low: 139 of 148 participants answered incorrectly; the association was not significant (p = 0.079).

The findings indicate that household members living with an HCV‑positive patient have a higher prevalence than the general Rwandan population (4 %). Unprotected sex was identified as the most important risk factor, while HBV and HIV co‑infections also showed strong association. The study recommends early HCV screening of household contacts, health education on transmission routes, and follow‑up of identified cases to support the national elimination goal by 2030. Limitations include the cross‑sectional design, which prevents determination of infection direction; phylogenetic studies are suggested for future work.

President Donald Trump nominated Travis Hill to be chair of the FDIC. Hill is a senior Treasury adviser, requires Senate confirmation. Banks face tighter credit and higher rates. Hill expected to adopt a pragmatic, deregulatory approach, balancing stability with lighter regulation. He would oversee deposit insurance, bank assessments, and potential failures. The nomination may face congressional scrutiny. The appointment could influence debates on deposit insurance limits, risk management, and crisis intervention. For the banking industry, his leadership could bring continuity in FDIC's mission while shifting regulatory approach.
Summerland Antique Collective: man bound two female employees with duct tape, stole cash, fled; victims freed after 20 min, no injuries. Suspect: black male, late 20s‑early 30s.

Iqaluit‑Tasiluk MLA George Hickes warned the Nunavut legislature on May 29, 2018 that public‑servant employees are being pressured by senior Government of Nunavut managers not to communicate with MLAs. He said the issue resurfaced after he raised a similar concern in 2014 when he was accused of obtaining insider information. Hickes cited specific directives ordering employees to avoid speaking with legislators and noted a lingering culture of discomfort among the GN’s more than 3,000 staff. He asked the minister responsible for the Public Service Act, David Akeeagok, whether the law prohibits public servants from contacting MLAs and whether any senior‑manager directives to discourage such contact exist; Akeeagok responded that employees are free to provide information to MLAs and are protected under the Act and by an ethics officer. Hickes emphasized that constituents have a right to contact their elected members and that fear of retaliation, particularly in small communities, can prevent people from seeking help. He stated that MLAs depend on constituent feedback to do their work and pledged to keep speaking out, indicating he expects other members to raise similar concerns.

The Chamber of Mines announced that the Mining Expo & Conference will be held April 25‑26 at Windhoek Show Grounds under the theme “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector”. Nedbank Namibia Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) will showcase its mining‑finance expertise, offering insights on attracting foreign investment and providing a complete funding solution – sourcing, structuring and negotiating packages. Investment banker Dominic Shikola highlighted Nedbank’s commitment to delivering capital, noting that mining contributes about 11 % of GDP as a foreign‑exchange earner, employer and tax‑revenue source. The expo will host a networking lounge and provide a platform for sharing trends and fostering partnerships to sustain the industry.

The coach discusses the physical nature of playoff hockey, stating fights and physical play are part of the game. He identifies the game's turning point as an offensive faceoff where his team turned the puck over, took a penalty, and the opponent scored on the power play. He notes both teams played sloppily at times and emphasizes the importance of winning the next game and maintaining momentum throughout a series. The coach stresses that faceoffs and puck possession are critical to success, and mentions adjusting a player to a grinding role to help him score after he struggled. He describes playoff hockey as a series where teams go through dips and must learn to respond, noting momentum is key in games and series. The coach comments on Marty St. Louis as a player who received an opportunity and used it to prove critics wrong, calling that motivation valuable. He concludes by emphasizing the importance of responding when facing adversity within a playoff series.

On Oct 18 2001 Commissioner.COM sent an e‑mail to Paul Lucci containing a fantasy‑football update. The message includes promotions for a free e‑mail football game, discounts on NFL memorabilia, a Vegas vacation offer and a Norton software deal, followed by a detailed NFL player‑news section. The player‑news provides injury and playing‑status information for many teams—examples include Drew Bledsoe listed as doubtful, Tyrone Wheatley expected to miss 3‑4 weeks with a knee injury, Terrell Davis aiming to return by early November, and numerous other players with injuries or questionable status along with fantasy‑relevant recommendations. A separate “Luccis Losers” player‑news section updates status for players in that league, noting that Duce Staley will start but share carries, Kurt Warner briefly left a game and returned, and other similar updates.

Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) is a formal framework that analyzes computational problems through three linked spaces: syntactic (Ssyn), semantic (Ssem), and logical (Slog), connected by mappings αf, βf, and γf. Intensional definitions generate the syntactic structure; extensional behavior corresponds to the semantic and logical outcomes. Stability of a mapping means its output size is polynomially bounded; explosiveness means it grows super‑polynomially. A problem is CDF‑complete when its three spaces are disjunctively definable, the mappings are mutually coherent, and all are stable. Compositional coherence (γf = βf ∘ αf) defines the class ComCDF; lack of coherence or an unstable αf defines ExpCDF, with a intermediate Semi‑ExpCDF class. αf and βf represent the potential space of semantic realizations, while γf records the actual logical outcome. Applying CDF to SAT shows that 2‑SAT clauses decompose into local binary implications, yielding stable αf and polynomial‑time tractability, whereas 3‑SAT clauses involve non‑local triple constraints that make αf explosive, causing exponential growth of the semantic space and intractability. This structural difference explains why 3‑SAT is NP‑complete and 2‑SAT lies in P, linking the CDF classification to the P/NP boundary. Recursive examples (e.g., factorial) illustrate how input variability destabilizes the mappings, mirroring the complexity growth of NP problems.

Patents grant inventors a monopoly that ends upon expiration, allowing free use of the invention. Scott Crump’s 1992 FDM patent underlies today’s desktop printers; Stratasys builds industrial machines, printing up to 36×24×36 in at $400,000. Average selling price $104,222 for industrial printers, $566,570 for metal printers, $1,094 for desktops. Stereolithography and powder‑bed fusion are processes; patents expired, enabling $3,500 vat polymer systems and stereolithography machines up to $990,000. Materials include plastics, metals, ceramics. BAAM prints up to 240×90×72 in at 80 lb/h, needing 2,725 desktops. One HP Jet Fusion 4200 equals 163 Ultimaker 3 units; a service provider makes 600,000 small parts weekly with six HP machines. NASA uses metal AM for propulsion; GE prints LEAP fuel nozzles 25 % lighter, 5× longer, and reduced CT7 engine from 900 parts to 16, cutting weight and cost ~35 %. AM projected to serve $12.8 trillion global market. Patents expire, advances become public; entrepreneurs commercialize them. The Wohlers Report (343 pages, $500) is industry reference.

European shares rose on Wednesday, with the STOXX 600 gaining 0.4% to its highest close in nearly 16 months, as Britain formally began Brexit negotiations. The German DAX climbed 0.4% to 12,203 points, its highest since April 2015, boosted by Daimler’s record‑sales outlook and broker upgrades for auto suppliers. EU antitrust regulators blocked the proposed LSE‑Deutsche Boerse merger; both stocks rose. ECB policymakers signalled caution on policy changes, while Deutsche Bank rallied on its €8bn cash call. Engie and 3I Group advanced on upgrades, whereas Scout24 fell after results missed forecasts and Aurelius slumped more than 35% after a short‑seller report.

China is leading the clean energy transition, spending heavily on renewables and reshaping the global market. At the UN Climate Summit, President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China’s green commitments, including a pledge to reduce greenhouse‑gas emissions by 7–10 % by 2035, a shift from earlier peak‑emissions targets. China aims to install 3,600 GW of wind and solar capacity by 2035 (six times its 2020 level), raise the renewable share of its energy mix to more than 30 %, make electric vehicles mainstream, expand its carbon‑trading market to more sectors and increase forest cover to 34 billion cubic meters. The country invested about $625 billion in clean energy last year—nearly a third of global spending. Analysts note China often overdelivers on its targets, and its large domestic market is driving down renewable costs worldwide, while other major economies have stalled or reversed climate policies.

A randomized controlled trial in Kampong Speu Province, western Cambodia, compared the efficacy of 3·5 mg/kg (0·25 mg/kg/day for 14 days) versus 7·0 mg/kg (0·5 mg/kg/day for 14 days) primaquine added to a 7‑day artesunate regimen (2 mg/kg/day) for Plasmodium vivax radical cure. G6PD‑normal patients were randomly assigned (2:2:1) to low‑dose primaquine, high‑dose primaquine, or no primaquine; G6PD‑deficient patients were assigned to the no‑primaquine arm. Patients were relocated to a non‑endemic site (Aoral town) for 90 days to prevent reinfection and monitored every 48 h by microscopy and qPCR. The primary outcome was the proportion with at least one P. vivax recurrence within 90 days.

Between 10 Nov 2021 and 10 Feb 2024, 160 patients were enrolled and 156 allocated: 37 G6PD‑deficient (no primaquine), 49 low‑dose, 46 high‑dose, and 24 G6PD‑normal (no primaquine). At day 90, recurrence rates were 81·4 % (95 % CI 69·6‑89·2) without primaquine, 24·4 % (14·2‑38·7) with low‑dose, and 4·7 % (0·8‑15·5) with high‑dose (p = 0.0141 for high vs low). The hazard ratio for recurrence for high‑dose versus low‑dose was 0·17 (95 % CI 0·04‑0·79, p = 0.0229); the risk was 5·9‑fold lower with high‑dose. Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated; methaemoglobin elevation was more common with high‑dose (35 % vs 10 %) but clinically silent. No serious adverse events were reported.

The study provides evidence that a total dose of 7·0 mg/kg primaquine over 14 days is markedly more effective than 3·5 mg/kg in preventing P. vivax recurrence in Cambodia, with comparable safety in G6PD‑normal individuals. The authors recommend that Cambodian and other Southeast Asian treatment guidelines adopt the 7·0 mg/kg regimen. The trial was funded by the NIH (R01AI146590) and registered as NCT04706130.

Paulo Dybala is fit and ready to start in Juventus's Champions League quarter-final return leg against Barcelona. He expressed satisfaction with his contract renewal until 2022, saying he chose to stay at Juventus, which he considers equal to top European clubs. He scored two goals in the first leg.

Sebi allows debt issuers to review ratings by submitting supporting documents, to prevent 'rating shopping'. Reviews must be by a CRA committee with a majority of independent members, having no pecuniary relationship with the CRA. Non-accepted ratings must be disclosed on the CRA's website for 12 months, including issuer details. CRAs must publish half-yearly summary sheets within 15 days, with separate disclosures for securities and other financial instruments.

Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from the Pink Hearts Fund, a cancer charity based in Long Beach, Mississippi. She admitted writing 132 checks to herself between March and July 2016, using the money for gambling and bills. She was ordered to repay $181,000 to the charity and pleaded guilty in April.

English councils are owed a refund after the Ministry of Justice overcharged court fees for council tax summons since 2013‑14 due to an administrative error. The overcharge was £2.50 per application, totalling £9 m a year. A review identified a small number of incorrect fees; fees will be cut and a refund scheme announced. Councils issued about 3.5 million summons last year and legal and admin costs for council tax arrears were £292 m in 2016‑17. In 2016‑17, over 4,800 were threatened with prison and 62 imprisoned.

The U.S. government has frozen about $18 billion in federal funding for New York City projects, saying contract awards may have relied on unconstitutional diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) criteria. The Office of Management and Budget confirmed the freeze, which impacts the Second Avenue Subway extension and the Hudson River Tunnel. The action follows a Department of Transportation interim rule limiting race‑ or gender‑based preferences, and a $300 million payment has been suspended pending audits. City officials and local leaders warn the freeze will delay thousands of jobs, disrupt construction schedules and cause cost overruns, calling it politically motivated. The freeze comes as a partial federal government shutdown has already complicated contract management, raising further uncertainty for the projects. Ongoing federal reviews could require the city to renegotiate terms or risk losing funding. Analysts say the delay highlights the vulnerability of infrastructure timelines to federal support and signals a broader shift in Washington’s approach to DEI‑linked programmes.

LG's upcoming webOS TVs, launching this month, provide integrated Sky TV EPG, quick input switching, and a Today menu aggregating content from Netflix, Sky Now TV, YouTube and live TV, controlled via the Magic Remote's gesture and voice features.

Ed Silverman's Pharmalot column reports that enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; Sweiti previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head for oncology clinical development. The piece is part of a weekly hires feature and is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

A group of college accreditors (CRAC) representing seven agencies that oversee 3,000 institutions is endorsing AI to reduce credit loss during transfer, which is a major barrier to degree completion. Current credit evaluation processes are inconsistent, time-consuming, and often result in students having to retake courses, delayed information, and increased costs. In 2024, 40% of adults attempted to transfer credits, with 58% experiencing some credit loss, 20% repeating courses, 13% running out of financial aid, and 16% abandoning degree pursuit. The CRAC statement encourages institutions to use AI to analyze course equivalencies and commit to applying credits by default unless learning outcomes aren't met. A pilot program with 59 institutions is testing AI platforms to identify course matches. The goal is to enhance human decision-making, reduce administrative burden, and provide students with timely information about transfer credits, while maintaining accreditation standards.

Cryotherapy involves standing in a chamber cooled to about -180°F for up to three minutes. Developed in the 1970s by Japanese physician Toshima Yamauchi to treat arthritis, it spread from Europe to United States. Enthusiasts claim it speeds muscle recovery, reduces inflammation, eases joint pain, improves circulation, alleviates anxiety and depression, boosts mood, strengthens the immune system, and can burn 500–800 calories per session. The FDA has not approved cryotherapy and warns of frostbite, burns and eye injuries; it is considered alternative medicine. Polar Brrr Cryo opened in Southwest Michigan in February, charging $55 per session; introductory rates $25 for one class or $90 for three. Clients include professional athletes and people with various health concerns. Research in the US National Library of Medicine shows limited scientific evidence for the benefits, and a 2015 death occurred in an unsupervised cryotherapy unit. Polar Brrr requires staff presence and advises patients with heart problems or hypertension to consult a doctor.

A 2,100‑year‑old chalk bowl fragment inscribed with “Hyrcanus” was uncovered under a mikvah at the Givati parking lot in Jerusalem’s City of David. Discovered in 2015 and announced later, it is among the earliest chalk vessels known from the city. Hyrcanus was a common Hasmonean name and could refer to either John Hyrcanus or John Hyrcanus II, but the artifact’s ownership remains uncertain. It was found near the remains of the Akra fortress built under Antiochus IV Epiphanes.

Bollinger Bands, created by John Bollinger in the 1980s, are a technical analysis tool consisting of a middle simple moving average (typically 20-day) with two outer bands set two standard deviations away. The bands expand during high volatility and contract during low volatility. Traders use them to identify overbought/oversold conditions and potential entry/exit points through various strategies including Squeeze, Breakouts, %B, and Reversal strategies. The passage notes Bollinger Bands can be profitable in some markets like gold but may fail in others like stock indices, and that default settings can be adjusted for different timeframes and sensitivities. The tool should be used with other indicators for confirmation, as it has limitations including delayed signals and potential false indications during strong trends.

Apple Inc. held its annual shareholders meeting on March 1, 2019. Shareholders elected eight directors (James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, Sue Wagner). They approved the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent accounting firm for 2019 and approved the advisory resolution on executive compensation. Two shareholder proposals—“Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “True Diversity Board Policy”—were not approved.

The holiday effect is a documented stock‑market anomaly where returns tend to be higher around certain holidays. The article tests seven U.S. holidays using S&P 500 data from 1960 onward (SPY and ^gspc) and compares the results to the monthly benchmark (the strongest months are October‑April). Backtest results show that only three holidays produce tradeable positive effects:

- July 4th (Independence Day): average gain 1.01 % per trade, win ratio 68 %, profit factor 2.97, max drawdown 4 %, CAGR 0.5 % while invested 0.6 % of the time.  
- Thanksgiving (including Black Friday): average gain 0.82 % per trade, win ratio 65 %, profit factor 2.72, max drawdown 5 %, CAGR 0.4 % while invested 0.6 % of the time; the retail sector (FSRPX) shows a higher average gain of 1.14 % with a win ratio of 71 % and profit factor 3.24.  
- Christmas/Year‑end rally (long from the close of Dec 20 to the first trading day of the new year): average gain 1 % per trade, win ratio 67 %, profit factor 4.8, max drawdown 2.9 %.

Other holidays (Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President’s Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day) show negligible or negative results. Proposed explanations for the effect include lower liquidity, increased optimism, absence of macro news, and selling of risky assets before holidays. A post‑holiday strategy that buys on the close after a holiday and holds for one day yields an average gain of 0.56 %, win ratio 71 %, profit factor 4, annual return of 3.5 % while invested only 1 % of the time, with risk‑adjusted return about 250 %. The article concludes that the holiday effect is real but modest, not a get‑rich‑quick scheme, and that only Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas offer viable seasonal trading strategies.

Councils in Scotland can raise the basic council tax rate by up to 3%, ending a freeze since 2007 that was funded by £70m. Properties in bands E to H will see mandatory increases due to MSP-approved changes to multipliers, raising £100m annually. This affects about 700,000 households (26% of 2.6m homes). Average weekly increases are around £2 for band E and £10 for band H. The impact varies by area, with 56% of properties in East Renfrewshire affected compared to 18% in East Ayrshire, and 37% in Edinburgh versus 14% in Dundee. Council tax bands are based on 1991 property values; studies suggest 57% of properties would change band if revalued in 2014. Local authorities rely primarily on government grants, with councils like Glasgow raising only 17% of budgets from council tax. The Scottish government's budget includes a reduction in core grant to councils but offset by direct local service funding and an additional £160m agreed with the Greens; Labour estimates a £170m cut while Greens view it as improved.

Amazon is creating an AI chip for Alexa. A Super Bowl Alexa ad was the most‑viewed on YouTube. At CES, Sony unveiled an Aibo robot dog and foldable TVs; Jeff Bezos highlighted Alexa. Amazon and Google cut speaker prices, losing money per unit, while the Echo Dot sold well and Apple delayed its speaker. German reported Alexa playing music at 2 a.m., and Amazon announced Alexa integration into Big Mouth Billy Bass.

This document is a specification agreement for the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) between AMD and recipients. It standardizes the GHCB memory area for guest-hypervisor communication in SEV-ES and SEV-SNP environments, which protect guest register state from hypervisor access. The specification defines the GHCB protocol, version negotiation, hypervisor feature support, and various Non-Automatic Exit events such as page state changes, AP creation, doorbells, timers, and APIC ID lists. It also covers VMPL levels, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, SMP booting, NMI handling, and debug registers. Several versions and revisions are documented, and System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

On Oct 29 2001, Moody's cut Enron's senior unsecured long‑term rating to Baa2 (two notches above junk) and placed it on review for further downgrade; S&P kept its BBB+ rating but revised the outlook to negative. Enron's shares fell to about $13–$14, a near‑seven‑year low, having lost more than half their value in two weeks. The company drew $3 billion from its credit lines last week, using $2 billion to repay commercial paper, and is in talks for an additional $1–2 billion credit line to shore up liquidity. Moody's and S&P cited deteriorating financial flexibility, large write‑downs and equity charges tied to undisclosed partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, whose resignation followed an SEC inquiry into the related‑party transactions. European energy firms have restricted or frozen dealings with Enron because of credit concerns, while U.S. wholesale traders say business continues at normal levels but they are monitoring the situation. Analysts warned that lenders will demand stricter terms, and a market newsletter reported Royal Dutch/Shell may consider acquiring Enron. Separately, rating agencies forecast a broader decline in U.S. corporate credit quality, with about $100 billion of debt expected to default in 2001.

India’s income inequality rose sharply after the early 1980s, with the top 1% holding 22% of national income, a record since 1922. Their share fell from 6% in the early 1980s to 22% today, coinciding with new policies after Rajiv Gandhi’s 1984 appointment. Earlier, strong regulations and fiscal progressivity reduced top shares during the 1950s‑70s, while the middle 40% captured 49% of growth. Growth has been uneven within the top 10%, and India shows among the largest increases in top‑income concentration over the last three decades.

Russian forces have increasingly targeted Ukrainian drone pilots as high-value threats, ramping up attacks using missiles, bombs, and other weapons against suspected operator positions. Ukrainian soldiers and drone operators report that pilots have become "target No. 1" due to their critical role in hindering enemy missions and launching numerous strikes. Casualties among drone pilots have increased at a rapid rate, according to Artem, an officer in Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps. Drones equipped with explosive payloads account for roughly 70% of casualties on both sides, and are used for intelligence gathering and strikes at a fraction of the cost of other munitions. Russia extensively bombs areas where pilots are suspected, deploying every available weapon to eliminate them. Ukrainian drone pilots have responded by building stronger shelters, working from deeper underground, and rotating locations frequently. Ukraine also targets Russian drone operators, viewing them as high-value targets as well.

Health agencies recommend 6–8 glasses (≈1.2 L) of water daily. Excess water can cause water intoxication, diluting blood salts, causing lethargy, light‑headedness and, rarely, death after intake. A Monash University study found swallowing becomes effortful after excess water, indicating the body guides intake by thirst. A 12‑week trial of 48 adults (55–75) showed that drinking two cups of water before meals produced an average loss of 15.5 lb versus 11 lb for controls; three pre‑meal drinks added about 5 lb extra loss. Advice: drink more water and fewer sugary drinks. Warning: athletes who overhydrate can die.

The preprint describes a Bayesian model‑averaging method called Doublethink that simultaneously controls the Bayesian false‑discovery rate and the frequentist family‑wise error rate when testing for direct (non‑mediated) risk factors in biobank‑scale data. The approach uses a prior that creates a one‑to‑one mapping between model‑averaged posterior odds and traditional p‑values, allowing joint Bayesian/frequentist inference and avoiding the need to pre‑specify a candidate exposure or to select an “independent” variable set.

The method was applied to 1,912 variables (including 865 factor levels and 863 ICD‑10 codes) from UK Biobank to identify direct risk factors for COVID‑19 hospitalization in 2020. Using 100 Markov‑chain Monte‑Carlo chains with 100,000 iterations, nine individual variables (e.g., unspecified dementia, acute lower respiratory infection, tendency to fall) and several a‑priori groups (age, deprivation, sex, obesity, kidney disease, psychiatric history, infection, dementia, and general comorbidity) were identified as significant at a posterior‑odds threshold of 10 (corresponding to a family‑wise error rate of ≈10⁻³·³). Post‑hoc grouping recovered additional signals, such as combined obesity measures and a proxy for poor physical health.

Comparison with 127 published UK Biobank studies found that established risk factors such as age, sex, deprivation, obesity and smoking were supported, while diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease showed no significant direct effects, suggesting their influence may be mediated through other variables. Psychiatric disorders, infection and dementia, rarely analyzed in prior work, showed strong direct effects. The analysis is limited to direct effects, excludes pre‑2020 exposures to avoid collider bias, and required ~3,500 CPU hours, making computation the main practical constraint. The authors conclude that Doublethink enables systematic, agnostic risk‑factor discovery while bridging Bayesian and frequentist testing frameworks.

Software development patterns have evolved from Knuth's algorithms to object-oriented design patterns (Gang of Four), enabling reusable components. Patterns provide value through learning from others' mistakes, providing shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components.

Single-node container patterns include: sidecars that augment applications (adding HTTPS, configuration sync, monitoring); ambassadors that broker external communication (sharding, service discovery, request splitting); and adapters that modify interfaces to conform to standards (monitoring, logging, health checks).

Multi-node distributed patterns include: replicated load-balanced stateless services providing redundancy and scale; sharded services for handling large datasets by distributing data across multiple machines; and caching layers for performance optimization.

These patterns enable modular, reusable systems that improve reliability, agility, and developer productivity through shared best practices and community collaboration.

Teams must be ready for three jump‑ball situations: defensive (opponent has the advantage), even (both teams have equal chance), and offensive (team has the advantage). In defensive jump balls the priority is to stop the opponent after the tip, watch the jumper’s eyes and hand to anticipate direction (right‑handed jumpers typically tip left, left‑handed right), rotate early, and use Box, Diamond or Y alignments depending on the opponent’s size or jumper ability. Box alignment places X1 back to protect the basket while X2 and X3 box out and X4 anticipates the tip; Diamond alignment puts X3 and X4 on the basket line with X1 and X2 denying passes. The Y alignment places two defenders back to prevent easy shots when the opponent has a clear jumper advantage. Even jump balls require boxing out, early rotation and a pre‑determined clockwise or counter‑clockwise signal (e.g., hand on hip). With a six‑inch height advantage teams can run set offensive plays such as Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem and Loop; after gaining possession they flow into a set or motion offense if a good shot is unavailable.

The passage documents US diplomatic communications in early 1942 regarding Finland's potential peace talks with the Soviet Union. The US informed a Finnish official that an intercept suggesting Finnish Legation comments on Anglo-American machinations was considered a mistake if true. The Finnish Minister inquired about travel restrictions for legation staff and American citizens, noting that restrictions in Finland apply to all foreign diplomats and that Helsinki is in a war zone. The British Embassy relayed Soviet willingness to enter peace negotiations with Finland through Sweden with more favorable terms, requesting secrecy. The US and UK coordinated to signal to Finland that they are not disposed to leniency regarding Finland's current policy, and the US instructed its minister in Finland to convey this stance to Finnish officials.

After winning the Stanley Cup, the player recalls a game‑winner in Carolina and a moment when the opponent scored first, prompting him to ask goalie Fleury to make the save. He notes that his two goals do not improve his stick‑handling and that he must work on it during the summer, but says he does not care about the goals because the team won. He credits Fleury’s saves, Geno’s Conn Smythe win, and Miroslav’s shot block as key contributions, and says the team has a great core for the next couple of years. He emphasizes feeling fortunate before each game, the bond with teammates who grew up together, and praises Sidney Crosby as the heart and soul of the Pittsburgh Penguins, highlighting his leadership and respect for the game. He also notes that Mario Lemieux kept the team in Pittsburgh and that the Cup victory fulfilled a promise made four years earlier, calling it the best day of his life.

Survivors and family members of the 72 Grenfell Tower victims offered tributes during the first phase of the public inquiry. Testimony highlighted criticisms of local authorities for failing to heed fire safety warnings and fire brigades for instructing residents to stay inside despite spreading flames. Chair Martin Moore-Bick stated the inquiry would begin with individual testimonies before examining technical causes. Survivors emphasized the need to address the gap between wealthy and poor areas in the investigation.

Trump's initial response to the Charlottesville rally drew backlash for not explicitly denouncing white supremacy. Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from Trump's Manufacturing Council to protest intolerance. Trump responded by attacking Frazier on drug pricing. Elon Musk and Robert Igor previously resigned from Trump's advisory councils over the Paris Climate Accord decision.

The Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018‑2022 report forecasts the market will exceed $1 billion revenue by 2022, based on an in‑depth analysis with industry expert inputs. It covers the market landscape, growth prospects, key vendors (AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons’, Nidec, Schneider Electric) and includes segmentation by application (industrial machinery, robotics) and region (APAC, EMEA, Americas). Key trends are a focus on miniaturized stepper motors, advances in design for robotics, and the emergence of IoT‑enabled motors. A primary driver is rising demand for automated equipment in industrial premises, prompting adoption of automated material‑handling to cut costs and improve cash flow. A major challenge is stiff competition from servo and conventional stepper motors.

Rule of thumb: dividend yields above 6% signal higher cut risk. Two FTSE stocks forecast a 7.1% yield.

Taylor Wimpey targeted £1.3bn shareholder return 2016‑2018 and plans a £450m dividend for 2017 (≈13.9p per share). 2016 free cash flow of £511.6m covered the payout. Strong housing demand keeps cash surplus high, making the 7.1% yield affordable and sustainable, though the housing cycle may reduce future dividends.

Connect Group, a logistics firm, paid a 9.5p dividend last year (6.9% yield) backed by £49.6m free cash flow. Forecast dividend for year ending August 2017 is 9.8p, giving a 7.1% yield. The stock trades at a forecast P/E of 7.6, reflecting market concerns. Net debt was £141.7m against pre‑tax profit of £41.9m, with net tangible assets of -£151.8m. A trading slowdown or tighter credit could force a dividend cut; the pending sale of its Education business may improve the balance sheet but likely not enough. The author sees risks outweighing rewards.

Regina Police survey of 462 residents (Sept‑Oct 2017) found 79% rated service very good to excellent, over 80% saw RPS as honest, and nearly 25% said RPS lacks sensitivity to Indigenous peoples. Chief Evan Bray will offer reconciliation training.

The defense enjoys a 5‑on‑4 numerical advantage on baseline out‑of‑bounds plays, which makes defending these situations different from regular half‑court defense because shooters cut directly toward the basket and there is little margin for error. Four effective defensive tactics are presented: (1) Jam – aggressive, hard‑nose denial with no switching, sag‑off protection before the pass, smothering the inbounder, then pressuring the ball with match‑up or box pressure once the ball is inbounded; (2) Jump Switch – aggressive switching on screens, denying passing lanes, smothering the inbounder, then applying box pressure; (3) Trap – double‑team the inbounds pass, trap the receiver, rotate according to the near‑player rule and create triangle help; (4) Combination defenses – Box & One, Diamond & One, or Triangle & Two, using a mix of man‑to‑man chasers and zone alignments to deny the pass and then transition to normal defensive pressure.

In Morton’s neuroma patients, RNA sequencing revealed over 3300 differentially expressed genes, with upregulated immune and inflammatory pathways and downregulated nervous system development pathways. Deconvolution analysis identified increased macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain. Specific M(GC) macrophage markers (MARCO, CD163, STAB1) were upregulated and correlated with paroxysmal pain. Immunohistochemistry confirmed demyelination, increased intraneural T-cells, and CD163+MARCO+ macrophages. CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain. Diffusion models and flow matching are generative approaches that can be viewed as special cases of learning stochastic dynamics between distributions. The Schrödinger bridge (SB) problem seeks an optimal stochastic bridge between two distributions and is solved computationally by the iterative proportional fitting (IPF) algorithm, which iteratively updates forward and reverse processes until they become time reversals of each other. Standard diffusion training corresponds to a degenerate IPF that converges in one step. Existing IPF variants require samples from both marginals, limiting use when marginals are specified by unnormalized densities or energy functions. This work extends IPF to data‑to‑energy and energy‑to‑energy settings by adapting off‑policy reinforcement‑learning losses and stabilization techniques, providing the first general method for such bridges. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithms learn low‑cost bridges comparable to data‑to‑data IPF, that learning the diffusion coefficient improves data‑to‑data IPF, and that the approach enables scalable data‑free image‑to‑image translation via prior‑to‑posterior translation in generative model latent spaces.

Overnight trading involves buying at the close and selling at the next day's open or close, exploiting the overnight edge where average gains from open to close have been zero over 30 years. Strategies include Turnaround Tuesday, holiday effects, end-of-month effects, mean-reversion, and options expiration effects, each showing positive backtest results (e.g., win ratios of 57-70%, average gains of 0.2-0.55% per trade). A portfolio of these strategies, combining different types like mean-reversion and breakouts, can improve risk-adjusted returns. Key principles for building a portfolio include using uncorrelated strategies, diversifying across asset classes and time frames, and avoiding significant drawdowns to enhance compounding. Backtests are approximations but can be useful with logical strategies. The short holding period and focus on capturing infrequent excessive returns define overnight trading's potential.

Small-sided games (SSGs) are soccer matches with fewer than 11 players per team on a reduced field, used in practice to develop tactics and in competition for youth (U6‑U12). The format gives players more ball touches and follows US Soccer standards. Practice SSGs range from 3‑v‑3 to 9‑v‑9, are fast‑paced, confined to areas of 20‑ to 60‑yard squares or rectangular fields, and target themes such as attack, defense, possession and transition. Age groups progress from U6 to U16 with increasing field size and complexity. In August 2017 U.S. Soccer introduced Player Development Initiatives (PDIs) setting national standards for youth SSGs: smaller fields, goals and balls; shorter games; build‑out lines at U9; no offside before U9; bans on headers and goalkeeper punts/drop kicks. These standards apply to all US Soccer member organizations and also cover field markings, substitutions and refereeing.

The passage describes an analyte monitoring system (for glucose monitoring in diabetes patients) and methods for sterilizing it. The system includes a sensor applicator, a cap, a sensor control device with an electronics housing, a sensor and sharp extending from the housing, and a collimator positioned within the cap defining a sterilization zone. The invention addresses the problem that radiation sterilization (e.g., electron beam) can damage electronic components while chemical sterilization (e.g., ethylene oxide) can damage sensor chemistry. Previous solutions required separate sterilization and packaging of components, necessitating user assembly. The disclosed solution uses a collimator to focus radiation on the sensor and sharp while blocking radiation from reaching sensitive electronics within the sealed housing. This enables a one-piece architecture that can be shipped in a single package without user assembly. The collimator has a sterilization zone (passageway) that receives the sensor and sharp, with the body material preventing radiation penetration to electronics. Seals create a sterile region encompassing the sensor, sharp, and portions of the electronics housing interior.

The application discloses metal‑assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters based on cyclic Pt(II) and Pd(II) complexes that employ benzo‑imidazo‑phenanthridine and analogous ligands. General formulas I–XVII define the core structures: M is Pt(II) or Pd(II) (or Ir(III) in octahedral complexes for formulas XIV–XVII). The emitters can exhibit both singlet and triplet excitons, yielding unity internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. The triplet state is localized on the benzo‑imidazo‑phenanthridine moiety; extending conjugation reduces singlet energy with little effect on triplet energy, producing a small singlet‑triplet energy gap that enables thermally assisted delayed fluorescence and efficient phosphorescence. The compounds are suitable for full‑color displays and lighting, and can be incorporated into OLEDs, photovoltaic devices, and luminescent displays. A light‑emitting diode implementation is described comprising an emissive layer containing one of the disclosed complexes. Synthesis examples (Examples 1–31) detail Ullmann‑type coupling of benzo‑imidazo‑phenanthridine‑based ligands with aryl halides followed by cyclometalation with Pd(OAc)₂ or K₂PtCl₄, producing complexes MC1–MC30 in yields from 10 % to 86 %. Emission spectra and external quantum efficiency data for selected complexes demonstrate delayed fluorescent and phosphorescent behavior.

The lecture explains constructing SNARGs using BARGs and somewhere extractable hash functions (SSB hash). A BARG proves multiple NP instances belong to a language with proof size polylogarithmically dependent on the number of instances and semi-adaptive soundness. An SSB hash has algorithms for generation, evaluation, opening, verification, and extraction, with properties including completeness, index hiding, and binding preventing opening a specific index to both 0 and 1. The SSB hash can be extended to multiple indices by repetition while preserving index hiding for unrevealed indices. The SNARG construction hashes all circuit wires with SSB hash, then uses a BARG to prove all gates are satisfied and the output is 1, with the verifier efficiency relying on the index language property of the BARG.

Cavity coupling to quantum critical matter systems enables superradiant phase transitions at arbitrarily weak light-matter interaction when the cavity mode directly couples to the critical degree of freedom. Systems show enhanced intrinsic squeezing and quantum Fisher information compared to the standard Dicke model. When coupling to non-critical modes, complex phase diagrams emerge with tricritical points. Experimental realization is feasible using materials like CoNb2O6, LiHoF4, and CrI3 coupled to cavity modes.

The Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) is an autonomous system that swaps depleted universal Swap Cartridges (SCs) on UAVs to extend flight range and endurance. It features a configurable landing zone with visible or non‑visible markers that generate scalable composite images to guide UAVs during approach and landing. After landing, the UAV is retained and electrically connected; a swapping mechanism removes the depleted SC from the UAV’s Universal Integrated Swap (UIS) and transfers it to a modular power bay (MPB) for recharging. The RPS then retrieves a charged SC from an MPB, elevates it to the landing zone, and inserts it into the UAV’s Swap Cartridge Receptacle (SCR). A central processor coordinates landing queues, monitors environmental conditions, communicates with the UAV’s Universal Swap Processor (USP), and manages MPB and SC status. The RPS can house multiple SC types (batteries, fuel cells, fossil fuels) in modular, line‑replaceable bays and can operate on internal or external power. It also supports non‑UAV unmanned systems and provides data storage, telemetry, and safety functions.

Experimental progress in orbitronics has shown that injected currents generate wavevector‑dependent orbital angular momentum, giving rise to the orbital Hall effect and the orbital Rashba‑Edelstein effect. Orbital torques are measured using spin‑torque ferromagnetic resonance or second‑harmonic analysis in magnetic heterostructures; conversion of orbital to spin angular momentum via spin‑orbit coupling is required to act on the magnetization. Materials such as permalloy, Ni, Ni‑Fe, CuOx, Pt and 4f transition metals exhibit strong orbital torques, while CoFeB requires an additional conversion layer. Thickness‑dependence studies reveal that orbital currents travel longer distances than spin currents. Direct imaging of orbital accumulation has been achieved with magneto‑optical Kerr effect and electron magnetic linear dichroism. In two‑dimensional van der Waals systems, the orbital Hall effect in transition‑metal dichalcogenides has been distinguished from the valley Hall effect and linked to topological invariants; orbital torques have also been observed in antiferromagnets and perpendicular ferromagnets.

Theoretically, the orbital Hall effect is a universal property of conductors arising from momentum‑space orbital texture and can exist without spin‑orbit coupling. The magnitude of orbital torque depends on both orbital angular‑momentum generation and relaxation processes. Crystal‑field coupling (~1 eV) should dissipate orbital angular momentum quickly, yet experiments report long orbital diffusion lengths, leading to conflicting first‑principles predictions. Key open questions concern the orbital relaxation mechanism and the factors that determine torque efficiency.

For applications, orbital torque offers advantages such as low‑resistivity channels using light metals (Ti, V, Cr) and potential for low write currents. Challenges include achieving large torque magnitude (reported ξ up to ~0.3, but higher values needed), compatibility with high tunneling magnetoresistance in CoFeB/MgO structures, and reducing the required layer thicknesses. Demonstrations show up to 50 % lower switching power than spin‑orbit torque devices, and applications in THz emission and unconventional computing have been explored.

Outlook emphasizes that orbital textures exist without spin‑orbit coupling, enabling use of abundant, inexpensive materials; orbital effects can be tuned by crystal and interface engineering; orbital angular momentum is less sensitive to magnetic perturbations and can be coupled with photons or phonons, promising new avenues in condensed‑matter physics.

NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, built on the Ampere architecture, delivers >1.7× memory bandwidth (1555 GB/s) via 40 GB HBM2 organized in five stacks, supports SECDED ECC for memory, L2 and L1 caches, and includes a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7× larger than V100) with 2.3× read bandwidth, hardware‑coherent partitioning, and Compute Data Compression (up to 4× DRAM/L2 bandwidth, 2× L2 capacity). Third‑generation Tensor Cores provide 16× mixed‑precision throughput versus FP32, support fine‑grained structured sparsity, and are organized in 108 SMs with data‑sharing across 32‑thread warps, asynchronous copy to shared memory, and 1.7× larger shared‑memory allocation, reducing instruction count by 8× and register accesses by 2.9×. The Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) feature can split each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated GPCs, L2 slices, memory controllers and Sys Pipes; further subdivision creates Compute Instances that support Volta‑style MPS and enable simultaneous context execution. A100 implements third‑generation NVLink (12 links, 600 GB/s total), PCIe Gen 4 with SR‑IOV, robust error detection/isolation, hardware JPEG decoding (NVJPG), an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics (FP16 11×, FP32 2.7× over V100) and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 exposes these capabilities via task graphs, asynchronous copy/barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and cooperative groups, enabling strong scaling and reduced kernel launch overhead. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch (4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth), delivering 5 PFLOPS, up to 6× training performance versus V100, and scales to thousands of nodes via Magnum IO. The architecture also supports 2:4 fine‑grained structured sparsity, providing near‑full accuracy at higher compute efficiency.

President Rutherford B. Hayes, on April 26, 1879, warned that any persons preparing to forcibly settle or move onto Indian Territory west of Arkansas without permission from the Indian Department will be promptly removed by agents, and if necessary, by U.S. military forces, under existing laws.

Cosmetic tooth bleaching is a $3.2 billion global industry that continues to grow as consumers seek brighter smiles. OTC whitening products are largely unregulated by the FDA, which classifies them as cosmetics, and only one OTC product—the Crest 3D White Glamorous White Whitestrips—holds the American Dental Association (ADA) seal of acceptance. The ADA seal indicates an independent panel verified the product’s safety and effectiveness, though many other OTC products can be effective when used as directed. Common side effects include temporary tooth sensitivity, and products may irritate gums if applied incorrectly. OTC bleaching typically takes two to six weeks; custom‑made trays from a dentist cost about $400 and require up to four weeks of daily one‑ to two‑hour wear. In‑office bleaching, using hydrogen peroxide concentrations up to 40 percent, costs over $1,000, produces results in one to two hours, and can lighten teeth several shades more dramatically; insurance rarely covers it. In‑office procedures rose 29 percent in 2015. Surface stains from coffee, tea, red wine, turmeric, and smoking can be reduced with good oral hygiene and professional cleanings, while deeper stains from aging, enamel cracks, or grinding may be lightened two to seven shades with bleach. Permanent discolorations from trauma, tetracycline, or excess fluoride require crowns or veneers. All bleaching methods are temporary, and the ADA notes no evidence supports “natural” remedies such as charcoal, baking soda, or lemon juice.

In February 1974, the tug Ocean Prince, pushing the oil barge New London, struck a charted rock in the Hudson River outside the navigable channel, causing damage to the barge and a significant oil spill. Red Star Towing & Transportation Co., the tug's owner and charterer, sought exoneration from or limitation of liability under 46 U.S.C. § 183 et seq., while Pittston Marine Transport Corp. claimed damages for the barge and cargo, and the United States sought pollution cleanup costs. The district court granted Red Star limitation of liability to the tug's value, dismissed claims against the United States, and limited cleanup cost liability to $100 per gross ton. On appeal, the Second Circuit held that the casualty resulted from negligence and unseaworthiness within Red Star's privity and knowledge, finding that Red Star failed to provide a qualified captain, inadequately managed crew assignments, and neglected to post a required lookout despite hazardous conditions. The appellate court reversed the limitation of liability, finding Red Star's omissions constituted willful misconduct under 33 U.S.C. § 1321, thereby increasing its pollution cleanup cost liability, while affirming the dismissal of claims against the United States. The case was remanded for further proceedings.

The Single/Double Offense is an NBA playbook strategy designed to free up shooters using baseline and double screens. The basic action involves a shooter cutting to the basket and then popping out off either a single or double screen, while the small forward goes opposite. This approach attacks both sides of the defense simultaneously, making defensive help nearly impossible. The offense includes multiple reads and counters for various defensive reactions (chasing, cheating over, switching, showing and recovering), allowing players to exploit defensive adjustments. Screeners also have opportunities to score by breaking double screens. Successful execution requires precise coordination, non-verbal communication, and defensive recognition. The offense offers continuities including Motion, Side Screen, and Drive & Kick actions, and emphasizes offensive rebounding with players assuming all shots may be missed and boxing out defenders. Teaching requires the whole-part-whole method and comprehensive understanding of all components.

Cannabidiol (CBD) drug Epidiolex, made by GW Pharmaceuticals, is a purified, 99% pure, THC‑free cannabis derivative that the FDA indicated it would approve for treating seizures associated with Lennox‑Gastaut syndrome (LGS) and Dravet syndrome (DS) in patients age two and older. The drug is manufactured under good‑manufacturing‑practice guidelines, unlike many over‑the‑counter CBD products, and three clinical trials provided substantial evidence of efficacy and acceptable safety. Panelists heard from parents, including a mother whose teenage daughter had failed 17 medications, describing life‑threatening seizures. Physicians report that some children who were wheelchair‑bound have become able to attend school after treatment. The FDA limits the approved use to LGS and DS, while researchers are exploring CBD for autism, anxiety and inflammatory disorders. It differs from recreational marijuana because it contains no THC.

The paper proposes a feasible method to simultaneously trap laser-cooled ions and electrons in a two-frequency Paul trap, enabling quantum operations faster than current trapped-ion computers. Electrons offer advantages due to their small mass (16,000 times lighter than light ions), enabling harmonic oscillator energy gaps in the hundreds of MHz range and potentially 700 ns gate operations. The physical concept involves one Ca²⁺ ion and one electron trapped by separate radio-frequency potentials, with the electron existing in three categories of electronic states: bound to the ion, in a transition region showing Rydberg-like and trap-induced characteristics, or bound by the trap potential rather than Coulomb interaction. The design uses planar trap technology for large-scale manufacturing with sub-micrometer features and integration with photonic and electronic layers, addressing challenges of maintaining symmetric trapping fields at approximately 1 mm from electrodes. President McKinley reports to Congress on the three‑year war between Spain and insurgents in Cuba, stating that the conflict has forced the United States to enforce neutrality laws, caused large losses to American trade and property, and produced domestic unrest. He notes that mediation attempts by his predecessor in 1896 failed because Spain demanded submission of the insurgents before any settlement.

After the change of government in Spain, the new administration released American prisoners, offered home‑rule for Cuba, and revoked the reconcentration policy that had forced about 300,000 rural Cubans into towns, where they suffered severe food shortages and mortality exceeding 50 % among the reconcentrados by March 1897. The United States organized a central Cuban relief committee, raised nearly $200 000 in money and supplies, and arranged free transport and duty‑free entry for relief goods; thousands of lives were saved and the Spanish Government appropriated $600 000 for further aid.

In an effort to end the war, the United States, through Minister Woodford, proposed a suspension of hostilities until 1 October for peace negotiations and immediate revocation of reconcentration. Spain’s 31 January reply offered to place peace preparation in the insular parliament, whose powers would not diminish central authority, and did not object to a cease‑fire if requested by the insurgents; it did not grant the immediate armistice requested.

The President reviews the options of recognizing the insurgents as belligerents, recognizing Cuban independence, or intervening as a neutral or as an ally. He cites President Jackson’s criteria that independence should be recognized only when the new state can sustain itself and the danger of re‑subjugation has passed; he concludes that the current insurgent government does not meet that test, and that premature recognition could tie the United States to a particular regime and limit its influence.

The destruction of the USS Maine in Havana harbor on 15 February, caused by an exterior submarine mine, is presented as evidence that Spain cannot guarantee safety even for a U.S. warship on a peaceful mission. Spain has offered arbitration of the incident and expressed willingness to submit the facts to an impartial investigation.

The President outlines four reasons for U.S. intervention: humanitarian concerns over barbarities and starvation; protection of American citizens and property in Cuba; injury to U.S. commerce and property; and the persistent threat to U.S. peace and the heavy cost of maintaining a semi‑war footing. He emphasizes that the conflict shows no prospect of decisive victory for either side and that the only path to lasting peace lies in enforced pacification.

McKinley asks Congress to authorize the President to use U.S. military and naval forces to secure a full termination of hostilities, establish a stable Cuban government capable of maintaining order and honoring international obligations, and continue distributing food and supplies to the island’s starving population. He notes that Spain’s Queen Regent has ordered a suspension of hostilities, the details of which have not yet been received, and says this development will be considered in the congressional deliberations.

The ADS9803 is an 8‑channel, 20‑bit ADC that outputs conversion data in straight‑binary or two’s‑complement format selectable via a DATA_FORMAT register. A free‑running sampling clock (differential or single‑ended) drives the device; a SMPL_SYNC pulse synchronizes multiple ADCs. An internal precision voltage reference can be filtered with a 10 µF capacitor, and an external reference may be used by disabling the internal reference through SPI. The ADC supports 2‑lane or 4‑lane modes with SDR or DDR data rates; output is a 24‑bit packet (20‑bit result MSB‑first, last six bits zero) on D[3:0] pins with DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT. Data‑clock frequency = (24 bits × 8 channels)/(lanes × data‑rate) × frame‑clock; frame‑clock = sampling‑clock/4. The device includes a data‑output randomizer (XOR with PRBS or LSB) to reduce ground‑bounce, two averaging modes (simple and moving) to improve SNR, and test‑pattern modes (fixed, ramp, alternating) for debugging. Speed‑boost mode enables up to 8 MSPS on a user‑selected channel pair while the remaining six channels are idle. Power‑down is controlled via the PWDN pin or PD_CH register field; reset is via the RESET pin or RESET register bit. After power‑up or reset, initialization requires a sequence of register writes with a free‑running sampling clock applied. Register access uses a 16‑bit SPI interface organized in three banks; bank selection is via address 0x03 in bank 0. Multiple devices can be configured in a daisy‑chain for SPI, with DAISY_CHAIN_LEN set accordingly. The ADC is suitable for ATE applications, offering low total‑unadjusted‑error (TUE), low‑noise and wide‑bandwidth modes, and compatibility with external multiplexers. Power requires three supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with recommended decoupling and layout guidelines. Development tools and support resources are available from Texas Instruments.

The study developed an automatic NLP classifier to detect utterances documenting goal‑of‑care (GOC) discussions in EHR notes of patients with serious illness. It framed the task as binary classification of utterances. The corpus consisted of 776 inpatient notes—400 Advance Care Planning (ACP) notes and 376 general notes—sampled from five University of Pennsylvania Health System hospitals (April 2017–December 2019). Two annotators independently labeled each utterance; disagreements were adjudicated by a palliative specialist (Cohen’s κ≈0.66). The dataset was extremely imbalanced: 9:1 positive/negative ratio in ACP notes and 155:1 in general notes. Five base classifiers (regular‑expression, logistic regression, BERT‑base, BioClinical BERT, RoBERTa) were combined into an ensemble. The authors compared passive learning, active learning (iteratively querying the most informative unlabeled examples), and training on all examples. Active learning substantially improved precision; the best model (weighted‑average ensemble) achieved an F1 of 0.557 for utterance classification and 0.629 for note classification. On the test set it correctly identified 13 of 18 GOC‑containing notes (72%) while incorrectly flagging 13 of 158 non‑GOC notes (8%). Active learning reduced annotation effort to about 30% of the unlabeled utterances. The definition of a GOC discussion required evidence of a conversation about goals, values, prognosis, or care preferences; code‑status documentation alone was not counted as positive. Limitations include the 512‑token context restriction and reliance on a local utterance view. The authors conclude that the moderate performance is sufficient for deployment and plan to release corrected labels on MIMIC‑III notes for reproducibility.

In HQET, matching and running involve renormalizing heavy quark fields and local operators, with the choice between on-shell and MS schemes affecting calculations. Heavy-to-light transitions yield a constant anomalous dimension, while heavy-to-heavy transitions produce an anomalous dimension dependent on v dot v prime (w). Options trading in Apple offers contracts (calls and puts) that give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying stock at a predetermined strike price on or before expiration. Call options rise in price when the stock price rises, while put options fall; as expiration approaches, call prices decline and put prices rise. Higher market volatility increases both call and put prices, while higher interest rates decrease them.

Traders can use a range of strategies: buying calls to speculate on direction, selling calls to generate income, buying puts to hedge, selling puts for income with the risk of having to buy at the strike price, covered calls, protective puts, and straddles to profit from volatility. Straddles and strangles involve simultaneously holding a call and a put (or different strike prices) to benefit from implied‑volatility changes.

Option trading carries high risk because options are leveraged instruments, can experience rapid losses exceeding the initial investment, and are subject to time decay and market risk. Naked short calls are particularly risky because a stock’s price can rise without limit. Options are a zero‑sum game.

Compared with stocks, options are contracts rather than ownership stakes, they are more leveraged, and they expire, making them more complex and requiring a deeper understanding of risks and strategies.

Apple options are considered highly volatile and highly liquid due to the size and liquidity of the underlying stock. Trading costs include the option price, broker commissions and fees, taxes (capital‑gains taxes applying to profits, with wash‑sale rules for losses), and hidden slippage.

Macroeconomic factors such as interest rates, inflation, and market volatility influence option prices, as do corporate news events (positive news raises call prices, negative news raises put prices). Dividend payments affect prices: dividends increase call prices and decrease put prices.

Various analysis tools are available—technical analysis (charting), fundamental analysis (financial reports), and options‑specific models such as Black‑Scholes and Monte Carlo simulations. Backtesting and quantitative strategies are recommended for evaluating performance.

Order types for trading Apple options include market orders, limit orders, stop orders, and stop‑limit orders. American‑style options can be exercised any time before expiration and are more expensive than European‑style options, which can only be exercised at expiration.

Risk‑management techniques include protective puts, delta‑hedging, and the use of stop‑loss or trailing‑stop orders, though stop‑loss orders may be bypassed by erratic news. Strategies such as straddles and strangles can limit risk while allowing profit from large moves in either direction.

The Apple options market is highly competitive and liquid, offering greater volatility than many other stocks. The article advises that most traders should consider trading the underlying AAPL stock before engaging in options, and emphasizes the importance of backtesting, quantitative analysis, and understanding one’s competitive edge.

Derivatives such as futures, forwards, and swaps can also be used alongside options. The strike price determines whether an option is in or out of the money and is a key factor in pricing. Overall, options trading in Apple can be profitable for experienced traders but requires careful understanding of strategies, risks, costs, and market dynamics.

The study examined the integration of AI in a university‑level Digital Photography in Nature elective offered at a public university in eastern Turkey. Using a qualitative case‑study design, the researchers conducted semi‑structured interviews with the instructor and 38 students who completed the course. Data were analyzed by content‑analysis, with trustworthiness ensured through triangulation, peer debriefing, and member checking.  

The instructor described the instructional design process, emphasizing problem identification, learner analysis, goal setting, constructivist strategies (flipped classroom, project‑based collaboration), and AI‑based assessment. She noted AI’s contributions to personalized feedback, improved academic language, and more systematic evaluation, while also highlighting risks such as inadequate infrastructure and AI hallucinations that produced inaccurate technical information.  

Students reported advantages including increased AI awareness, enhanced technical knowledge, faster feedback, time efficiency, and multiple role perceptions of AI (assistant, guide, teacher). They also identified disadvantages: reduced initiative and over‑reliance on AI, potential loss of originality, and exposure to misinformation and contradictory outputs.  

The findings indicate that AI‑supported instruction can enhance technical skill development and personalize learning but requires careful pedagogical oversight, structured AI literacy training, equitable resource access, and strategies to preserve critical thinking and creative autonomy.

Scientists led by the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences discovered that bacteria residing in tumors produce a metabolite, 2‑methylisocitrate (2‑MiCit), which makes colorectal cancer cells more susceptible to chemotherapy. Using a large‑scale screen of over 1,100 conditions in microscopic worms, they identified that E. coli generates 2‑MiCit, and computer modeling confirmed that tumor‑associated microbiomes from patients also produce the molecule. Experiments in human cancer cells and a fly model of colorectal cancer showed that 2‑MiCit inhibits a key mitochondrial enzyme, causing DNA damage and disrupting cancer cell metabolism, and that it synergizes with the chemotherapy drug 5‑fluorouracil to kill cancer cells more effectively than either compound alone. Collaboration with medicinal chemists produced a synthetic version of 2‑MiCit with even greater potency, demonstrating the potential to develop microbe‑derived drugs that improve cancer treatment and support personalized therapy.

Rapid advances in deep learning have produced powerful neural networks for biomedical image processing, yet specialized models for restoration, super‑resolution, fusion and registration overlook three critical factors: the need for multi‑step pipelines, the inter‑relations among degradations, and the large scale of biomedical data. These limitations motivate a universal foundational model. We introduce Orochi, a versatile biomedical image processor designed to address these issues through four key aspects: (1) dataset‑level processing of over 100 publicly available studies (>100 TB, 2‑5D modalities) using random multi‑scale sampling; (2) task‑related joint‑embedding pre‑training (TJP) that learns jointly from various degradations; (3) a multi‑head hierarchical architecture built on linear‑complexity Mamba blocks with Swin‑Transformer‑inspired design; and (4) a three‑tier fine‑tuning framework (full, normal, lightweight) providing parameter‑efficient adaptation. Orochi is the first model to offer a unified solution for diverse low‑level biomedical imaging tasks, achieving performance comparable to state‑of‑the‑art specialist models while reducing training and inference costs.

The Town of Knightdale obtained a preliminary injunction preventing Paul Alton Vaughn from operating a used car lot in violation of the town's zoning ordinance. The Court of Appeals vacated the injunction because the town's conclusory allegation of irreparable harm was insufficient under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 1A-1, Rule 65. The court held that a plaintiff seeking a preliminary injunction must show likelihood of success on the merits and provide specific facts supporting irreparable harm, not merely allege it. Although municipalities may enforce ordinances through injunctive relief, they must still comply with Rule 65's requirements for showing specific facts of irreparable injury.

The application is a continuation of prior applications relating to storage/retrieval. The invention is an automated storage, retrieval, and processing system for objects, comprising storage bins, a retrieval conveyance, a programmable motion device with an end effector for grasping objects, and linearly arranged destination bins. The system uses bin displacement mechanisms and conveyors to move selected storage bins to a processing area where a perception unit identifies objects and determines grasp points. The programmable motion device moves along a gantry to pick objects and place them into destination bins according to a manifest. Grasp optimization uses surface normal approach and fiducial features such as barcodes, with machine learning to improve grasp selection. Multiple embodiments include rows of storage bins, parallel processing sections, box tray assemblies, and box kicker mechanisms to transfer bins. A computer system controls the system, continuously updating locations and identities of storage and destination bins.

Japanese minister Otori demanded on the 28th that Korea declare whether it is tributary to China; after consultations Korea answered that, under the 1876 Kang‑hua treaty and the King’s letter to the U.S. President, Korea is an independent state with full sovereign rights in both internal administration and foreign affairs. Japan accepted the reply. A 1882 Korean communication to the U.S. President stated that Korea is a Chinese dependency but controls its own governmental affairs and will negotiate treaties on an equal basis, with the U.S. pledging non‑interference in Sino‑Korean matters. Korean minister Ye Sung‑Soo later reported that a meeting of foreign representatives in Seoul had been held; the Japanese minister refused to withdraw Japanese troops and demanded a meeting to change Korea’s political system. He appealed to the U.S. President to help resolve the crisis, warning of a serious situation as Chinese and Japanese forces remained in Korea. A conference of foreign ministers was arranged, and Ye Sung‑Soo asked the United States to instruct its representatives in China, Japan and Korea to use their influence to prevent conflict and secure the withdrawal of the troops.

The swinging gate is an unconventional special teams formation used primarily on two-point conversion attempts after touchdowns. The offense lines up with kicking team personnel, placing the kicker as an eligible receiver while the offensive line aligns to one side. The formation allows teams to either execute a trick play (such as a side snap or quick screen pass) or shift into a field goal formation for an extra point attempt. Defensive strategy involves matching personnel to the formation's "heavy side" and positioning safeties to cover alleys while box players align across from blockers. NFL rules restrict the formation's use on extra points, which must be snapped from the 15-yard line, making it more common in college and high school football.

ZEA‑DNK‑02170 SAP (Version 1.0, 16 Aug 2019) outlines the statistical analysis plan for a trial comparing dasiglucagon with placebo in patients with diabetes. Adverse‑event (AE) causality is graded by investigators on a 0‑3 scale (0 = not related, 1 = unlikely, 2 = possible, 3 = probable); possible and probable are considered related. Missing causality is queried and, if unresolved, set to related. Severity is graded 1 = mild, 2 = moderate, 3 = severe; missing severity remains missing. AE summary tables present the number and percentage of patients with at least one event and total event counts for screening AEs, treatment‑emergent AEs (TEAEs), TEAEs of special interest, other important TEAEs, injection‑site reactions (investigator and sponsor‑defined), drug‑related TEAEs, serious TEAEs, serious drug‑related TEAEs, and deaths. Frequency tables are produced by MedDRA system organ class (SOC) and preferred term (PT); patients with multiple events in the same PT are counted once and tables are ordered by descending incidence in the dasiglucagon arm. Special‑search categories include QT‑interval prolongation (SMQ Torsade de pointes/QT prolongation) and drug‑related hepatic disorders. Laboratory data are summarized with descriptive statistics per visit, flags for values above/below reference ranges, and change from baseline (screening to follow‑up). Hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy test, and alcohol breath test are described. Vital signs are summarized descriptively and pulse rate is analyzed categorically. ECG results are presented as overall interpretation and descriptive statistics for PR, QRS, QT, and QTcF intervals; categorical QTcF thresholds (>450 ms, >480 ms, >500 ms) and change from baseline (>30 ms, >60 ms) are reported. Immunogenicity (ADA) is analyzed descriptively, counting treatment‑induced and treatment‑boosted ADA‑positive patients; evaluable patients are defined as those with at least one post‑dose sample. Protocol changes are limited to re‑wording of the primary efficacy analysis, addition of sensitivity analyses, and changing secondary efficacy terminology from “within X min” to “at X min”. Appendices detail SAS programming QC requirements (program naming, header, log review, output review, dataset verification, documentation) and provide a comprehensive list of tables, figures, and listings for sections 14 and 16.2, covering patient disposition, demographics, medical history, efficacy (time to plasma glucose recovery, plasma glucose), adverse events, ECG, laboratory, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity.

Secondary endpoints assess glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase) at 10, 15, 20, and 30 min after dasiglucagon or placebo. Rescue IV glucose censors patients. Recovery rates are compared by Cochran‑Mantel‑Haenszel test (or Fisher's exact test if low cell counts). Change from baseline is analyzed by ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site. Least‑square means with 95% CIs are presented.

During late 1942, U.S. and Finnish diplomatic offices exchanged numerous telegrams covering a range of subjects. On 3 January 1942 the U.S. Secretary of State notified the Finnish Minister (Procopé) that Finnish Legation staff must obtain Department of State approval before traveling beyond Washington, D.C. and its immediate suburbs, and that Finnish consular officers must seek approval for travel outside their assigned districts. The U.S. official explained the scope of the restrictions and indicated that minor travel details could be resolved as needed.
