Football offenses use various formations to align players, with formation names being generic and varying by coach. Basic formations include the I Formation, where backs line up behind the quarterback for power running, historically used by teams like the 1995 Nebraska Cornhuskers; the Split Backs Formation, with backs split on each side, now rare in professional football; and the Twins Formation, featuring two receivers on one side and a tight end on the other, allowing flexible run or pass options.  
Spread offense formations aim to space out defenses. The Ace Formation has two receivers on each side with a tight end, creating balance. Trips Formation puts three receivers to one side, forcing defenses to choose coverage. Empty Formation uses five receivers with no running backs, prioritizing passing but allowing creative runs. Quads Formation places four receivers to one side, limiting defensive disguise. Bunch Formation clusters three receivers, creating route confusion and picks.  
Backfield formations describe quarterback positioning. Shotgun places the quarterback several yards behind the center; it can combine with various personnel. Pistol Formation, developed by Coach Chris Ault, keeps the quarterback deep with a running back directly behind him, enabling downhill runs and passing. Single Back Formation features one running back, often under center.  
Older formations are common in high school football. The Wishbone uses three backs in a wishbone shape for misdirection and option plays. Flexbone, adapted from wishbone, moves two backs closer to the line for pass threats; Paul Johnson famously used it. Double Wing features a wing blocker on each side with tight offensive line splits, making it hard to defend. T Formation, once standard, now appears mainly near the goal line. Wing‑T, adapted from T Formation by Coach Harold “Tubby” Raymond at Delaware, uses quick motion and play action. Power I adds an extra blocker near the goal line. Single Wing has one wing and multiple backs who can take snaps, influencing many modern offenses.  
Gadget formations are unusual but effective. Wildcat uses an unbalanced line and a non‑quarterback snap, famously revived by the 2008 Miami Dolphins. Emory and Henry spreads players across the field in pods, confusing defenses; Cincinnati Bengals used it under Marvin Lewis. Swinging Gate lines up in an atypical way, often after touchdowns, to attempt a two‑point conversion. Unbalanced Formation places four or more ineligible players on one side, commonly used at the goal line.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture enables hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and real‑time ray tracing, using dedicated RT cores to accelerate BVH traversal and ray‑triangle intersection, and Tensor cores to power AI features such as Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, AI Slow‑Mo and AI Super Rez. Turing also introduces Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh shaders) for flexible geometry processing, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for per‑region shading control, Texture Space Shading (TSS) to decouple visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi‑View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass. Turing GPUs (TU102, TU104, TU106) incorporate these units, support second‑generation NVLink, USB Type‑C VirtualLink for VR headsets, and provide the RTX‑OPS workload‑based metric that accounts for Tensor, CUDA, RT and INT32 pipeline usage. The architecture enables ray‑traced shadows, ambient occlusion and reflections with denoising, delivering real‑time, cinematic‑quality graphics for games and professional applications while improving VR performance through foveated rendering, 3‑D audio acceleration and efficient resource binding.

SEV-TIO enables guests to bind trusted devices; SNP guest requests handle device info, MMIO, and IOMMU. Secure AVIC manages guest APIC state via backing pages. Termination requests allow guest exit with reason codes. Guests identify SEV-ES via CPUID features. SMP booting uses AP jump tables or AP creation events to avoid measured register updates. The invention concerns a phase‑stable colloidal polysaccharide suspension that contains (1→3)‑glucan, a method for its preparation, and its applications. The glucan is obtained by enzymatic conversion of sucrose with GtfJ glucosyltransferase isolated from Streptococcus salivarius and is used in its never‑dried, initially moist state. A press cake with a solids content of 4–80 wt % (preferably 15–45 wt %) serves as the starting material. The desired polysaccharide concentration of the final suspension is adjusted to 0.01–50 wt % (preferably 1–20 wt %) by addition of water, after which the material is comminuted with a low‑shear dispersing unit such as an Ultraturrax® mixer or a colloid mill. No chemical or enzymatic pretreatment, no dissolving/precipitating steps, and no high‑pressure homogenization are required, although an optional high‑pressure homogenizer may be used to improve homogeneity. The resulting suspension is isotropic, forms a three‑dimensional network, exhibits shear‑diluting behavior, and has water‑retention capacities up to 500–5000 %. The glucan may constitute 1–100 wt % of the polysaccharide; other polysaccharides such as cellulose gels (amine‑oxide process), cellulose derivatives, starch, or other glucans can be incorporated. Additives (pigments, TiO₂, BaSO₄, ion exchangers, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, latex, activated carbon, superabsorbents, flame‑retardants) may be included up to 200 wt % of the polysaccharide. The suspension is film‑forming, can be applied by doctoring, spraying or brushing, and the dried films act as uniform, dense barriers. It also serves as a binder for nonwovens, a viscosity modifier, and a base for spray‑dried, freeze‑dried or supercritically‑dried powders or aerogels. Functional additives such as chitosan, nanosilver or zinc‑oxide can be introduced. Experimental examples demonstrate that never‑dried glucan yields homogeneous, stable gels (e.g., 4 wt % gels prepared with a colloid mill) while dried glucan produces unstable, phase‑separated suspensions. Increased solids content raises viscosity but reduces water‑retention capacity. Spray drying of a 3 wt % gel yields particles in the sub‑micron to low‑micron range. The disclosed suspension thus provides a simple, energy‑efficient route to stable colloidal polysaccharides for coating, packaging, adhesive and other applications.

Virgin Galactic completed its second rocket‑powered test flight of VSS Unity over Southern California on May 29, 2018. Unity had completed extensive engine testing and seven glide flights before the powered test.

Mechanical: Socket 940 is a 940‑pin ceramic µPGA socket with LCP (UL 94 V‑0) base and cover; cover thickness ≤1.17 mm, seating‑plane flatness <0.25 mm, lidless package thickness ≥2.20 mm. The cover incorporates a latch and a stainless‑steel actuation lever; lever actuation force <3.6 kgf, package insertion/extraction force ≤2 kgf (lever open) and ≥0.013 kgf per pin (lever closed). Pin displacement during actuation <1.0 mm; durability ≥50 cycles. No cracks, flashing, missing tabs, or misaligned parts; visual inspection at 1×, solder balls must be complete and co‑planar ≤0.20 mm. SMT solder balls Sn‑Pb 63/37 ±5%, 0.76 mm dia, PCB pad 0.64 mm dia, with solder‑barrier. Current rating 1.5 A per contact, ≤30 °C rise. Low‑level circuit resistance ≤25 mΩ per contact. Inductance: single pin <4 nH; nearest‑pair loop 3 nH ±10%; three‑pin matrix 3 nH ±10%. Capacitance between nearest pins <1 pF; three‑pin matrix <1 pF. Differential (odd‑mode) impedance 100 Ω ±10% for three‑pin (S1,S2,G) configuration. Propagation‑delay skew ≤10 ps + 3 ps error; differential‑pair skew ≤10 ps + 3 ps. Crosstalk measured via partial‑loop inductance and Maxwell capacitance matrix. Dielectric withstanding voltage ≥650 Vac; insulation resistance ≥1000 MΩ.

Newly elected Student Association State Quad senators found residents confused about asbestos despite existing notices. Residential Life has posted asbestos warnings for 20 years, but residents want direct university communication rather than notes on doors. Asbestos, found in some quad ceiling insulation, is only harmful through long-term exposure when disturbed. Facilities Management proposed adding asbestos FAQs to the university website. RAs claimed housing directors told them to avoid discussing asbestos to prevent panic, which Residential Life director Carol Perrin denied. RAs prefer more prominent information in housing contracts over current signage. Colonial Quad received abatement last year, with Schuyler and Beverwyck Hall next. The university released an asbestos awareness guide seven years ago.

Mick Schumacher says he is not yet ready for Formula One, noting he is older than rookie Lance Stroll and younger than Max Verstappen’s debut age. After leaving Formula 4 without a title, he is focusing on his F3 season, to finish among the rookie leaders. He has no plan for super licence points but interest from Mercedes and Ferrari flatters him. Media attention is part of the sport and he intends to adapt now.

In this cross‑appeal from a Family Court order, mother Laurie A. Miosky sought modification of a 2003 sole‑custody award to father Jon M. Miosky after he relocated the two daughters (now 17 and 15) to Florida without notice, obstructed the mother’s visitation and communication, and violated the custody agreement. The lower court found multiple intentional violations but declined to change custody and left visitation “subject to the children’s wishes.” The appellate court agreed that visitation for the younger daughter should not be subject to her wishes, noting the father’s alienation, his failure to testify, and the mother’s turnaround, and it remanded for immediate court‑ordered visitation after an updated in‑camera hearing. Child‑support payments were suspended pending further order.

Apple Inc. Q1 2021 Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2020 shows total net sales of $111,439 million, a 21% increase year-over-year. Net income was $28,755 million with diluted earnings per share of $1.68. Product net sales were $95,678 million (iPhone $65,597M, Mac $8,675M, iPad $8,435M, Wearables/Home/Accessories $12,971M) and Services net sales were $15,761 million. Gross margin was $44,328 million (39.8%). Operating income was $33,534 million. Total assets were $354,054 million with cash and cash equivalents of $36,010 million and total marketable securities of $159,561 million. Total liabilities were $287,830 million and shareholders' equity was $66,224 million. The company repurchased $24 billion of common stock and paid $3.6 billion in dividends during the quarter. Segment net sales included Americas $46,310M, Europe $27,306M, Greater China $21,313M, Japan $8,285M, and Rest of Asia Pacific $8,225M. As of December 26, 2020, the adjusted recovery amount related to the European Commission State Aid Decision was €12.9 billion held in escrow pending legal proceedings.

Following the Charlottesville rally, educators are seeking ways to confront racism and white supremacy. Derek Weimer, who taught accused driver James Alex Fields Jr., described him as intelligent but deeply interested in Hitler and white supremacy, and said he felt he failed to steer him away. Facing History and Ourselves offers an evidence‑based curriculum emphasizing moral choices and producing academic and social gains. Teachers are advised to use identity charts, curated book lists, lesson plans on bias, civil rights, and media literacy, and online resources such as #CharlottesvilleCurriculum, Share My Lesson, and Teaching Tolerance.

Denise Ricco, whose son was diagnosed with autism in fourth grade, and her family joined SPARK, a three‑year study seeking genetic markers for 50,000 families affected by autism. The study uses at‑home cheek swabs, works with any family structure and offers a $50 gift card per family. As of early April, 25,328 individuals with autism and their families were enrolled; Rush University Medical Center manages the Chicago arm. Additional testing dates are May 6 in Evanston and Northbrook, and June 17 in Chicago. Researchers note that autism’s genetic basis remains unclear, but the study aims to link specific chromosomal deletions to treatment efficacy, share data with other researchers and possibly inform early indicators, while emphasizing that prevention is not its goal.

Microsoft Corporation Q1 FY2017 (quarter ended September 30, 2016) reported revenue of $20.5 billion, essentially flat year-over-year. Net income was $4.7 billion, down from $4.9 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $0.60 compared to $0.61. Operating income decreased 10% to $5.2 billion. Revenue growth in Productivity and Business Processes (6%) and Intelligent Cloud (8%) was offset by a 2% decline in More Personal Computing. The company repurchased $3.6 billion of common stock and paid $2.8 billion in dividends. Cash and short-term investments increased to $136.9 billion. Commercial cloud annualized revenue run rate exceeded $13 billion. Microsoft announced a $26.2 billion acquisition of LinkedIn, expected to close in calendar 2016.

Strix Group Plc Q2 2025 earnings call held on 2 Oct 2025 at 6:30 AM EDT. CEO Mark Bartlett presented interim results for the period ending 30 June, describing the first half as mixed with a lot of activity and noting they would give details quickly to allow time for Q&A. He highlighted Billi’s strong double‑digit growth, supported by new products and further geographic expansion. Updated notes and forecasts are available on equitydevelopment.co.uk.

The Global Geiger-Mueller Counters Industry 2018 Market Research Report provides a comprehensive analysis of the global market for the period 2018–2025. It covers product definitions, classification into end‑window and windowless types, and applications in industrial, healthcare, defense and law‑enforcement, and other sectors. The report examines market size (sales and revenue) and growth trends for 2012‑2022 across regions including the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia and India, and presents competitive profiles of key players such as Ludlum Measurements, Mirion Technologies, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Arrow‑Tech, ECOTEST, FLIR Systems, Fuji Electric, Gamma‑Scout, International Medcom, John Caunt Scientific, Quarta‑Rad, Polimaster, S.E. International and SOEKS USA. Additional sections address upstream raw‑material and downstream demand analysis, manufacturing cost structure, marketing channels and forecasts for 2017‑2022.

The Passing Game is an unstructured, team‑oriented offensive system that relies on continuous ball and player movement, off‑ball screens, and unselfish play rather than set patterns. All five players are involved at all times; movement must have purpose—creating leads, cutting to the basket, setting screens, or establishing rebounding position. Basic rules include passing and moving, maintaining 12‑15 ft spacing, eliminating dribbles except for a strong drive or a better passing angle, and using screens and back cuts to attack defensive overplay. Strengths are involvement of every player, effective ball movement, adaptability to any defense, and difficulty for opponents to scout; weaknesses include disruption by selfish players, limited offensive rebounding, and reliance on patience and reading defense. The offense can be run from multiple alignments and works against both man‑to‑man and zone defenses with specific adjustments such as sharper passes, reduced screen use, and frequent skip passes. Success requires teaching fundamental skills—passing, shooting, screening, rebounding—and an unselfish attitude. Variations include a three‑player Hi/Lo, a four‑out system with rotating post, and a five‑player Motion offense for smaller, quicker teams. Zone adjustments stress quick, accurate passing, attacking gaps, and using back cuts. Coaches gain long‑term stability but initially sacrifice control; the approach creates mental pressure on opponents, exposes weak defenders, and exploits tempo to generate easy baskets.

The plaintiff Luis Antonio Avendano appealed from a Kings County Supreme Court order dated May 17 2005 that denied his motion to set aside the jury verdict for the defendant and from the resulting judgment of October 18 2005 dismissing his complaint. The appeal from the intermediate order was dismissed, the judgment was affirmed, and one bill of costs was awarded to the defendant. The appellate court found that the jury’s verdict in favor of the defendant, based on a fair interpretation of the evidence, was not against the weight of the evidence.

This systematic review examines digital leadership in education, highlighting its necessity due to technological integration in schools. Definitions of digital leadership vary across literature, often lacking elements such as interaction, ability, follower roles, and goals; the review proposes a technology-organization-environment (TOE) driven model to address these gaps. Effects of digital leadership are observed at three levels: student (academic performance), teacher (technology integration, professional development, job satisfaction), and school (management efficiency, digital culture, transformation). Influencing factors are categorized as internal (individual characteristics, professional experience, digital literacy) and external (infrastructure, school culture, policies, training, COVID-19). Future research should explore digital leadership's role in lifelong learning, digital security, followership dynamics, and multicultural contexts.

The author recommends using existing channels to assess Soviet intentions before improving bilateral relations, as no basis exists for major deals. The author sees no room for compromise on INF arms control or major regional issues (Afghanistan, Central America, Middle East). The author opposes intensifying U.S.-Soviet dialogue, as it would create false expectations and pressure for concessions. Specific disagreements include: rejecting a bold framework on Afghanistan as it would erode U.S. credibility with Pakistan; avoiding renewed discussions on Namibia/Angola; opposing restoration of the Joint Commercial Commission before the East-West Economic Study is completed; and noting that dialogue should address human rights and Soviet behavior as a litmus test of intentions. Multiple-level dialogues and summit meetings are deemed counterproductive until the Soviets demonstrate genuine willingness to reduce threats to Western security.

Mike Regnier, chief executive of Santander UK since 2022, will step down in the first quarter of 2026 as the bank prepares for its merger with TSB, citing the merger’s timetable extending beyond his preferred tenure. Santander UK has begun searching for his successor, aiming to appoint the new CEO early next year. The leadership change follows the August appointment of Thomas Scholar as chairman, and the incoming CEO will inherit the challenge of integrating two large retail operations while maintaining customer confidence and meeting regulatory requirements.

Fitch Ratings assigned an expected 'BB(EXP)' rating to two senior secured term loans – Term Loan AI (minimum USD1,000m, 8.25‑year tenor) and Term Loan AH (minimum EUR750m, nine‑year tenor) – issued by Telenet International Finance S.à.r.l. and Telenet Financing USD LLC, subsidiaries of Telenet BVBA. The transaction will partially refinance existing bank debt in a leverage‑neutral manner as part of Telenet's strategy to refinance prior to maturity and maximise tenor. The final rating is contingent upon receipt of final documentation conforming to the preliminary documentation reviewed. The loans are guaranteed by Telenet Financing USD LLC, Telenet BVBA, Telenet International Finance S.à.r.l. and Telenet Group BVBA.

Telenet operates a cable network in Flanders and parts of Brussels, serving about 70% of households with TV, broadband and fixed‑line telephony, and generates a pre‑dividend free‑cash‑flow margin of 12‑14%. The company is investing EUR500m over five years to raise network capacity to 1 GHz, enabling downstream speeds of at least 1 Gbps.

Belgium's cable wholesale regulation, introduced in 1Q16, is expected to have a limited impact. Telenet targets net debt/EBITDA of 3.5‑4.5x and maintains FFO‑adjusted net leverage below 5.25x (≈4.3x). The secured debt is rated one notch above the issuer default rating, with a recovery rating of 'RR2'.

Rating sensitivities include a potential downgrade if leverage exceeds 5.25x, fixed‑charge cover falls below 2.5x, or operating conditions worsen. Positive action is unlikely unless a more conservative financial policy is adopted.

Liquidity is supported by EUR120m internal cash generation and EUR400m undrawn facilities; the first debt maturity is in 2022.

Targeting, as defined by the NCAA rulebook, is a player aiming at an opponent to deliver forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block, or ball play, including helmet‑to‑helmet hits and contact with a defenseless player. The penalty is a 15‑yard flag; a player called for targeting in the first half is ejected, and a foul in the second half results in a suspension for the first half of the next game. A targeting foul in the final game of a season leads to a postseason or next‑season suspension. Repeat offenders receive an automatic one‑game suspension for each third targeting foul in a season and for each additional foul. No fines are imposed. The rule was introduced in 2008, amended in 2013 to add disqualification and replay overturn ability, and in 2019 video review became mandatory with further punishment for repeat offenders. The NFL's equivalent is called unnecessary roughness and does not automatically disqualify a player. Notable examples include a 2024 Peach Bowl helmet‑to‑helmet hit by Texas safety Michael Taaffe that was not reviewed for targeting, and a 2019 Fiesta Bowl targeting penalty on Ohio State defensive back Shaun Wade for a hit on Clemson quarterback Trevor Lawrence.

Keith Chegwin, 60, died on 11 December after a long battle with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a progressive lung condition that scars and stiffens the lungs, leading to shortness of breath, chronic cough, fatigue and clubbing of the fingers and toes. About 6,000 people are diagnosed with IPF each year in the UK; it is more common in men and in people over 70. Research suggests IPF may result from the body’s response to lung damage caused by acid reflux, certain viruses (including Epstein‑Barr, herpes and hepatitis C) or exposure to dust from wood, metal, textiles, stone or farming. His family thanked Severn Hospice for its care and asked to be left to mourn privately.

The passage is a transcript of a MIT OpenCourseWare poker class lecture. The instructor discusses an in-depth combinatorial hand analysis of a cash game hand, covering bet sizing, position, and range deduction. He explains concepts like polarized ranges, stone-cold nuts versus weaker draws, and when to raise versus call. The lecture then shifts to general poker topics: why poker has money available due to overconfidence, gambling self-control issues, the game's fast evolution, and avoiding results-oriented thinking. The instructor recommends resources including CardRunners, Two Plus Two forums, Twitch streams, and books like "Small Stakes Hold'em" and "Harrington on Hold'em." He shares personal philosophy about poker being a game of decision-making and discusses the importance of honest self-assessment. The lecture concludes with a Q&A session addressing topics like dealing with downswings, online poker legality in Massachusetts, and casino play strategies.

Facebook shares fell 6.8% on Monday, on pace for their biggest one‑day percentage decline since March 2014, erasing about $40 billion in market value. Regulators in the U.S. and U.K. criticized Facebook for allowing Cambridge Analytica, a data firm linked to the Trump campaign, to access user information without users’ consent and retain it after stating it had been deleted. Analysts gave mixed assessments: Wells Fargo said the episode creates a public‑relations and regulatory risk but kept a buy rating; GBH Insights warned of potential further platform changes; Pivotal Research’s Brian Wieser said near‑term business impact is unlikely but regulatory risk is heightened; Stifel’s Scott Devitt said Facebook has been slow to address security concerns and may face engagement and monetization headwinds. The sell‑off dragged other tech stocks lower, with the Nasdaq Composite down 1.8%.

The speaker discusses being ready when called upon by the coach, playing their game despite tough calls, expecting a strong opposing team with fast forwards, focusing on the current game and each shift, and emphasizes their team's persistence and ability to comeback in games.

Admiral Harry Harris, commander of U.S. Pacific forces, will become the next U.S. ambassador to South Korea instead of Australia, Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said. Bishop acknowledged the decision follows U.S. challenges on the Korean peninsula. The United States has had no ambassador to Australia since September 2016, and Acting Secretary of State John Sullivan said a new appointment will be a priority. Charge d'affaires Jim Caruso will continue in the role, while Australian officials expressed a need for a new ambassador soon.

In 2016, the Rams traded a package of draft picks to the Titans for the No. 1 overall pick, selecting quarterback Jared Goff. The Rams also acquired players like Pharoh Cooper and Mike Thomas, while the Titans got Corey Davis, Jack Conklin, Derrick Henry, and others. Analysis suggests the Rams have the edge due to Goff's success and Pro Bowl selections, but the Titans' grade remains incomplete pending the performance of their acquired players.

The passage investigates the coarsening dynamics of phase-separated DNA droplets in a self-stirring active fluid (composed of microtubules and kinesin motors) compared to a passive fluid. In both environments, coarsening is driven by Smoluchowski coagulation (collision-driven coalescence), with Ostwald ripening playing a negligible role.

Experimental results show that while the mean radius scaling exponent ($\beta_R \approx 0.33$) is identical for active and passive droplets, the total number scaling exponent ($\gamma_N$) is more negative for active fluids, and the droplet size distribution loses self-similarity over time in active conditions. This occurs despite active droplets being advected by flows with a size-independent effective diffusivity, violating the classical Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland (SES) relation.

Simulations and theoretical analysis reveal that the collision kernel exponent ($k$) is the fundamental control parameter. For Brownian droplets ($k=0$), a linear relationship $\beta_R = -\gamma_N/3$ holds and size distributions are self-similar. Active fluids, self-propelled particles, and systems with inverted SES relations exhibit $k=2$, leading to a non-linear relationship between exponents and a loss of self-similarity due to the preferential coalescence of large droplets. This framework unifies coarsening in active and anomalous passive systems.

The author founded a company at 16, created an herbal product that earned over $350 million in under a year. In 2010 he observed Amazon selling supplements and listed his nootropic Excelerol on the platform. After generating 65 reviews and $5,000 in sales in one night, he faced a dilemma between his subscription model and Amazon sales. Amazon later shifted policies to be buyer‑centric, treated customers as its own, and could suspend sellers. A market for suspension insurance emerged. Over five years the author learned to navigate Amazon’s rules and now leads a consultancy that advises Fortune 500s and startups on winning in the Amazon marketplace.

ECC memory resiliency (SECDED) protects the A100’s HBM2, L2, L1 caches and register files. The L2 cache is 40 MB (≈6.7× larger than V100), divided into two 20‑slice partitions, delivering 2.3× higher bandwidth (5120 Bytes/clk vs. 2048 Bytes/clk) and supporting L2‑cache residency controls and Compute Data Compression (up to 4× DRAM/L2 bandwidth and 2× capacity).  

The Ampere architecture adds third‑generation Tensor Cores that provide 16× the mixed‑precision throughput of standard FP32 FMA. Data‑sharing improvements raise warp‑level sharing from 8 to 32 threads and reduce register accesses; a new asynchronous copy instruction bypasses L1 and the register file, directly moving data from global memory to shared memory. Asynchronous barriers enable fine‑grained thread synchronization.  

Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) can partition a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute resources (GPCs, SMs), L2 slices, memory controllers and DRAM bandwidth, guaranteeing QoS and fault isolation for multi‑tenant or multi‑user scenarios.  

Third‑generation NVLink runs at 50 Gbit/s per signal pair, uses 12 links for 600 GB/s total bidirectional bandwidth, and includes link‑level error detection and packet replay. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction and supports SR‑IOV for virtualized GPU sharing.  

Error/fault detection, attribution, isolation and containment are improved across the GPU and NVLink‑connected clusters, with page‑fault communication returned via NVLink.  

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches (4.8 TB/s total bandwidth), delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, scalable to thousands of nodes via Magnum IO SDK, Mellanox ConnectX‑6 HDR InfiniBand and Kubernetes‑based orchestration. The software stack includes CUDA 11, Container Toolkit, GPU‑optimized NGC containers for deep learning, inference, analytics and HPC workloads.  

Fine‑grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) is supported in A100, allowing near‑zero accuracy loss while increasing compute throughput and reducing memory traffic.

The player reflects on winning a championship with a team that included veteran players Ray Bourque and Rob Blake, who had never previously won. He cites advice from Bourque to act immediately, his gratitude toward goalie Patrick Roy, and the emotional moment when Bourque received the Cup first. He credits the organization, scouting, and contributions of players such as Chris Drury and Milan Hejduk, noting that the team secured home‑ice advantage and the first championship for the region. He notes the weight of the Cup, his plans to celebrate with family and friends (including playing golf with the Cup), and the need to stay focused for future games.

The Vintage Optical Shop, the US’s largest online retailer of authentic vintage eyeglasses and sunglasses, offers new email subscribers a one‑time $20 discount on their next purchase. Subscribing also provides early notification of new arrivals, sales and special offers. The store’s inventory includes vintage styles from the 1850s to the 1980s, and all items are genuine, handcrafted and priced competitively.

President Trump claimed that “big homebuilders” are withholding about 2 million empty lots and compared them to OPEC, urging Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to stimulate construction to restore the American Dream. Libertarian economist Bryan Caplan rejected the analogy, arguing that U.S. homebuilding consists of thousands of firms eager to build and that the real barrier is local zoning, permitting and overlapping regulations rather than collusion. A National Association of Home Builders survey shows a persistent shortage of buildable lots, with 64 % of single‑family builders reporting low or very low lot supply—a level higher than any year from 1997 to 2016—despite housing starts averaging under 1.5 million annually. Caplan contends that additional financing will not resolve the shortage in heavily regulated markets and that zoning reform is needed to meaningfully increase housing supply.

The passage describes a study analyzing RNA-sequencing data from 390 whole blood samples to diagnose rare disease patients by examining transcriptome-wide splicing outlier patterns, particularly focusing on intron retention in minor intron containing genes (MIGs). The study identified five individuals with excess intron retention outliers in MIGs; four were diagnosed with RNU4atac-opathy due to biallelic pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC, and one case (D1) revealed a novel candidate gene, RNU6ATAC. The findings demonstrate that transcriptome-wide splicing patterns can serve as an unbiased diagnostic approach for identifying spliceopathies and new gene-disease relationships in rare disease cohorts.

A Pepperdine sophomore studying abroad in Buenos Aires received help from locals, felt appreciated and not singled out due to his race, noted a small presence of people of African descent, and encourages African American students to travel abroad.

Emma Stone signed a two‑year, up to $10 million deal to become Louis Vuitton’s new face after LVMH pursued her for almost a year. Playing Billie Jean King in Battle of the Sexes, she bulked up with weightlifting and protein shakes, initially struggled then found it addictive and felt stronger.

Vijay Mallya, the Indian businessman wanted for defaulting on about Rs 9,000 crore of loans, appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court for an extradition hearing. Chief Magistrate Emma Louise Arbuthnot granted him bail until 4 December and set the next case‑management hearing for 6 July, with the final hearing also scheduled for 4 December. Mallya denied all allegations, saying he has sufficient evidence and that no loans were diverted, and told reporters “you can keep dreaming about a billion pounds.” He was accompanied by his son, a female companion and supporters. Mallya was arrested by Scotland Yard in April and has been on conditional bail, now extended to December. His defence, led by Boutique Law LLP, expects a second extradition request from India related to an Enforcement Directorate case. The Crown Prosecution Service, acting for India, pushed for a December conclusion; the defence sought a March/April 2018 final date. The judge excused Mallya from the July hearing pending a decision on media barriers. Mallya has been in the UK since March 2016, gave a £650,000 bail bond and surrendered his passport. The UK‑India Extradition Treaty of 1992 has previously resulted in only one extradition.

AGESA™ is a BIOS procedure library designed to help customers implement AMD technology. The document defines interfaces for wrapper implementers, specifies procedure call mechanisms, and provides guidelines for host environment integration. AGESA uses a three-level version numbering scheme (X.Y.Z) and supports multiple AMD processor families. The software provides two build methods: binary modules for indirect integration or source integration for direct compilation. Key features include initializer functions for simplified interface calls, standard header structures containing configuration parameters, and two error reporting methods (return codes and error logs). Call entry points are time-based rather than function-specific. The architecture supports both traditional BIOS and UEFI environments across multiple execution phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP). Configuration is customized through platform-specific files (<Plat>Options.c) that control defaults tables and build options. The software includes PEIM modules for processor and memory initialization, DXE drivers for late initialization, and various procedures for system configuration, memory management, PCIe topology, and power management.

Sprint and its foundation announced the 1Million Project, an effort to connect one million high‑school students lacking home internet. This school year it will give 180,000 students in 1,300 schools across 32 states a free smartphone, tablet or hotspot with 3 GB of LTE data for four years, starting Aug. 15. Participating districts include New York City, Miami‑Dade, Los Angeles, Chicago, Phoenix and Baltimore. A pilot with 3,750 students showed 86 % improved learning attitudes. Sprint will donate about $2.16 billion in services over five years.

BiondVax received a $2.8 million investment from Angels High Tech Investments Ltd. (owned by Check Point co‑founder Marius Nacht) for 33.8 million shares, giving Angels a 19.99% stake. CEO Ron Babecoff called the investment a vote of confidence in its universal flu vaccine.

The Enforcement Directorate accused Nirav Modi of using his company Firestar Diamonds to indirectly challenge the money laundering case against him. The ED told the Delhi High Court that Firestar Diamond International Pvt Ltd's plea for an interim stay of proceedings was "premature" and "misconceived," and warned it would cause "grave miscarriage of justice" and hinder the investigation. The ED stated Modi, accused in the Rs 12,000 crore PNB fraud case, has not joined the investigation despite summons from both the ED and CBI, and described him as a "fugitive and absconder." The money laundering case is based on a First Information Report filed by the CBI.

Korean government asked foreign representatives to secure simultaneous withdrawal of Chinese and Japanese troops. Chinese troops entered to suppress rebellion; Japanese troops arrived without invitation, against Korean protest, and now retain large forces. China will withdraw only if Japan does; Japan refuses. Representatives of the United States, Russia, France, and England submitted this proposal to their governments, warning that foreign troops endanger peace. U.S. official Sill reported tension, 5,000 Japanese troops near Seoul, danger to 80 Americans, and persuaded Admiral Skerrett to delay departure. The Korean insurrection has become minor compared with Sino‑Japanese complications.

The speaker says the team expects a loud arena, similar to previous playoff venues, and notes that Marty’s two shutouts have earned respect. He emphasizes staying focused and not celebrating until the championship is secured, crediting veteran leaders such as Scottie Stevens, Scottie Niedermayer and Patrik for maintaining focus with minimal need for extra motivation. The opponent received some breaks while the team did not, and a mistake on the final goal proved costly. The team struggled with faceoffs throughout the season, missing Joe Nieuwendyk, and while the goaltender’s error was noted, the speaker declines to blame him. The team has won two games and needs four more to win the title.

The SEC upgraded its informal inquiry into Enron to a formal investigation regarding partnerships with former CFO Andrew Fastow. S&P cut Enron's long-term credit rating to "BBB" from "BBB+" and its short-term rating to "A-3" from "A-2," with further cuts possible. Enron secured $1 billion in credit lines backed by its Northern Natural Gas and Transwestern Pipeline assets from J.P. Morgan and Salomon Smith Barney. Enron shares fell 14% to $11.99, having lost about two-thirds of their value in two weeks. Analysts expressed concern the probe could expand to Enron's core trading business. Key energy trading partners said they were continuing business as usual with Enron while monitoring the situation. The investigation involves related-party transactions with Fastow-led partnerships that resulted in a $1.2 billion writedown of shareholder equity. Enron has retained former SEC enforcement chief William McLucas as counsel and formed a special committee to address the investigation.

Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement on March 17, 2016, with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank, J.P. Morgan, and Merrill Lynch for the issuance of $750 million 2.250% notes due 2021, $1.25 billion 3.250% notes due 2026, and $1.5 billion 4.650% notes due 2046. These are further issuances of existing series, resulting in total outstanding amounts of $3 billion, $3.25 billion, and $4 billion respectively. Interest is payable semi-annually, starting August 23, 2016. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured debt. The filing, signed by CFO Luca Maestri on March 24, 2016, includes exhibits such as the underwriting agreement, note forms, legal opinion, and ratio of earnings to fixed charges.

Milford, who lost last year's Intermediate final, face St. Naul's in the 2017 decider at O'Donnell Park, Letterkenny on Sunday. Milford are strong favorites, having competed well in Division One while St. Naul's play two divisions below them. St. Naul's have a poor championship record, winning just one of eight finals in the past 30 years. Milford last won this grade 25 years ago in 1992. Both managers have returned key players from injury, and while St. Naul's possess a compact side with a good running game, the passage suggests Milford's overall strength makes them unlikely to be upset.

U.S. higher education funding reflects historic discrimination and elitist choices. Flagship public universities receive substantially more per‑student state funding than other public institutions (e.g., UConn vs. SCSU). Funding formulas typically use a “base plus” method that indexes to prior‑year allocations, perpetuating inequities and ignoring institutional and student need. Historically, universities excluded women, Black students, and low‑income groups, leading to separate, under‑resourced institutions such as HBCUs and community colleges. Today, most Black, Hispanic, and low‑income students attend open‑access schools that spend roughly half as much per student on education as selective research universities. The report argues that reforms should prioritize equity by directing additional state money based on measured student need and accounting for outside revenue sources, and only after establishing an equitable formula pursue adequacy (higher overall funding). Approaches such as free college for all and outcomes‑based funding are insufficient because they do not address resource distribution. Equity must be the foundation of any systematic overhaul of higher‑education funding.

Scholars argue that climate education currently emphasizes scientific knowledge and “green” solutions while ignoring the long‑standing colonial histories and power structures that shape climate change. They introduce “climate coloniality” to describe how colonial frameworks continue to determine climate impacts, adaptation strategies, and environmental governance, noting that solutions such as lithium mining reproduce extraction and dispossession in the Global South. Mainstream approaches, including Education for Sustainable Development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, focus on modernization and development without confronting colonial legacies, leading to climate apartheid and eco‑apartheid. The authors propose a “decolonial educational ecology” that uses contrapuntal reading and critical inquiry to foreground Black and Indigenous knowledge systems, reject technocratic fixes, and address systemic inequities through reparative and distributive justice. This framework seeks to uncover hidden histories, question universalized growth models, and nurture alternative, context‑specific futures for climate education.

Robert Epstein argues that the dominant “information processing” (IP) metaphor, which likens the brain to a computer, is flawed and should be abandoned. He contends that humans are born with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms, not with software, algorithms, or stored representations. The IP metaphor, which emerged after the 1940s computer era, treats thoughts as software and the brain as hardware, but brain studies show no localized storage of memories or images. A demonstration where a student draws a dollar bill from memory shows the inaccuracy of mental retrieval. Multiple scientists, including Eric Kandel, estimate that understanding brain change may take centuries. Alternative “anti‑representational” views see behavior as direct interaction with the environment rather than internal computation. solution-processed semiconductors are promising alternatives to epitaxial for LEDs, solar cells and photodetectors but laser diodes require high current densities that are difficult in organics due to low carrier mobility and losses from triplet excitons and annihilation. inorganic colloidal quantum dots have reached 1.93 kA cm⁻² under pulsed excitation. metal‑halide perovskites (MHPs) sustain high injection but suffer carrier‑imbalance, Joule heating, low thermal conductivity and ion migration that degrade efficiency and prevent amplified spontaneous emission. to exploit the soft ionic lattice, we built an electrically driven polariton laser using a CsPbBr₃ microplate (5 × 9 µm, 435 nm thick) integrated in an optical microcavity with single‑walled carbon‑nanotube (SWCNT) electrodes on a distributed Bragg reflector. a two‑stage cryo‑cooling protocol (first to 280 K, then to 8 K at a constant 0.5 µA for 3 h) transforms the metal‑semiconductor‑metal Schottky diode into a rectifying p‑i‑n junction by drift of mobile ions, yielding forward‑bias currents four orders of magnitude larger than at 8 K without bias. at 8 K the device shows strong coupling with two polarisation‑split cavity modes (ΔEc‑XY = 33.7 meV) and an exciton energy EX = 2.341 eV. angularly resolved electroluminescence exhibits discrete lower‑polariton states consistent with parabolic confinement (≈0.9 µm for X, ≈1.2 µm for Y polarisation). above an injection current of 60 µA (≈2.8 kA cm⁻², 3.95 V) the emission intensity jumps more than two orders of magnitude, the MPB‑X linewidth narrows ten‑fold to 2.5 meV, and all polariton branches blueshift, signalling the onset of polariton lasing. the carrier density remains ~4–6 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻³, well below the Mott transition. this demonstrates a continuous‑wave, electrically pumped perovskite polariton laser and provides a strategy for solution‑processed semiconductor lasers.

A surgical instrument system and associated methods are disclosed for measuring torque, power and energy in real time while a working tool penetrates tissue such as bone. The system comprises an instrument with a working tool, a torque sensor that generates real‑time torque signals, a controller that processes the signals into torque, energy, power or a combination thereof, and a display that presents the processed signals to the user. The instrument houses a rotational drive motor and an axial drive motor, the latter driving a guide harp that retracts to reveal the length of the working tool extending beyond a distal guide element, thereby providing real‑time depth control and measurement. Axial force sensors positioned on the guide harp and on the working tool sense applied forces and communicate them to the controller, which can also display force information. The torque sensor may be a direct reaction torque sensor positioned between the motor and a motor mount, creating a floating motor sub‑assembly that isolates the sensor from the instrument body. The controller transforms torque data into energy using the work‑energy theorem; the accumulated drilling energy is displayed versus depth or time and correlates with regional bone density, screw pull‑out strength, and material strength. The system detects impending cortical or joint penetration by monitoring changes in the slope of torque on any of the x‑, y‑, or z‑axes, allowing the user to redirect the tool before inadvertent plunge. A drop in power can trigger automatic motor shutdown to prevent over‑penetration. The instrument can be linked to an external computing device via wired or wireless communication, and a graphical user interface shows torque, power, energy, depth and force in real time. Working tools include drill bits, saws, burrs, reamers, drivers and self‑drilling implants, and the system may include an irrigation system, removable battery pack, and modular components that can be sterilized. Methods include penetrating tissue, generating torque signals, processing them into energy or power, displaying the information, determining regional tissue strength from the energy, providing real‑time depth control and plunge prevention, and stopping the motor upon a sensed power decrease.

Scientific knowledge advances through recombination of existing theories, findings, and concepts, but not all combinations prove equally generative. This study proposes that "gap-opening" papers—those that create empty regions or holes in concept networks—stimulate more future research than other forms of recombination. Using persistent homology to analyze 34,363,623 articles from Microsoft Academic Graph spanning 1900–2020, researchers categorized papers into three types: gap openers (creating topological holes), non-gap openers with novel pairs, and papers without novel combinations. Gap openers constitute only 0.84% of articles—twice the random baseline—suggesting gap formation reflects meaningful structural properties of scientific knowledge networks. These papers bridge newer, less established concepts, use creation-related verbs in titles, and demonstrate higher recombinational novelty while citing fewer prior works. Gap openers significantly outperform other types in achieving top citation rankings, disruptive influence, and Nobel Prize association. However, they receive fewer citations within five years but substantially more within twenty years, exhibiting higher "Sleeping Beauty Index" scores indicating delayed recognition. These papers emerge from smaller teams with younger, less connected members and greater geographical proximity. The findings suggest topological significance—not novelty alone—determines generative capacity, with implications for science policy and evaluation frameworks that may undervalue breakthrough contributions with delayed impact.

A recent Thorax study of 971 adults from the French EGEA cohort found that higher cured‑meat intake was linked to worse asthma outcomes. Low consumers (≤1 serving/week) had a 14 % worsening rate, medium consumers (1–4/week) 20 %, and high consumers (>4/week) 22 %. After adjusting for smoking, physical activity, age, sex and education, high consumers were 76 % more likely to experience symptom worsening than low consumers. Biological sex and gender identity are distinct. Biological sex is determined by sexual‑differentiation pathways guided mainly by genes on sex chromosomes, notably the SRY gene on the Y chromosome that promotes testis formation. Studies of individuals with XY chromosomes but female anatomy and of XX males who carry SRY on an X chromosome showed that a single nucleotide change in SRY can disrupt testes development, while insertion of SRY into female mouse embryos produced male anatomy and behavior. These findings, together with cases such as David Reimer, suggest gender identity is more influenced by biological factors than by upbringing, though the specific genes involved are not fully understood. Some candidate genes may reside on X or Y chromosomes, but the author cautions against using biological variables to arbitrate gender identity.

The passage describes distributed system patterns for containerized applications. The ambassador pattern routes requests through a proxy that handles sharding, service discovery, or request splitting, enabling separation of concerns between application logic and routing. Examples include sharding Redis via twemproxy and splitting traffic between production and experimental services using nginx.

The adapter pattern modifies application interfaces to conform to standardized conventions for monitoring and logging. Adapters enable heterogeneous applications to present consistent interfaces to monitoring systems like Prometheus or logging systems like Fluentd, improving modularity and reuse without modifying core application containers.

Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy and scaling by deploying identical service instances behind a load balancer, with readiness probes determining when instances can serve traffic. Session tracking ensures user requests route consistently to the same replica using IP hashing or cookies.

Advanced patterns layer additional components: caching via Varnish improves performance; SSL termination via nginx secures traffic. Sharded services distribute data across replicas, with each shard serving a subset of requests, enabling scaling for large datasets. Consistent hashing minimizes resharding impact when scaling.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes requests across multiple leaf nodes, with the root merging partial results. Trade-offs include straggler delays and overhead scaling with parallelism. FaaS and event-driven architectures offer automatic scaling and simplified deployment but face challenges with background processing, memory requirements, and operational complexity.

Simons Observatory (SO) is a cosmic microwave background project located at 5200 m in the Atacama Desert with three small‑aperture telescopes (SATs) and one large‑aperture telescope (LAT). SO observes in six bands (30–280 GHz); the UHF detector modules cover the 220 and 280 GHz bands. Each UHF module contains 1720 transition‑edge‑sensor (TES) bolometers (430 feedhorn‑coupled orthomode transducers each feeding four TESs) plus 36 dark calibration devices. The TESs are read out via microwave SQUID multiplexing (µmux) with two RF readout chains per module. Laboratory characterization of 25 production‑design UHF modules, comprising over 36 000 TESs, showed an average TES yield of 83 % (minimum 71 %). Resonator identification reached 98 % before cuts, falling to 86 % after applying frequency‑spacing and SQUID‑response criteria; 95 % of resonators have internal quality factor Qi > 50 000. Readout noise peaked at 35 pA/√Hz, with 87 % of channels below the 65 pA/√Hz baseline target. Median TES parameters were RN ≈ 7.7 mΩ, Tc ≈ 163 mK, Psat ≈ 24–26 pW, τeff ≈ 0.4 ms, and optical efficiency ηopt ≈ 0.62–0.63. About 89 % of detectors met the NEP requirement (<53–64 aW/√Hz) and the noise is photon‑noise dominated on sky. Low‑ηopt tails were linked to post‑fabrication re‑annealing; one outlier module (Uv63) will not be deployed. Overall, 23 modules satisfy performance specifications; the best 19 will be installed—13 already deployed on the LAT and a UHF SAT, and six more planned for a LAT upgrade. On‑sky characterization will be reported in forthcoming commissioning papers.

Erik Demaine's lecture proves a cell probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity: any data structure handling edge insertions/deletions and connectivity queries requires Ω(log n) time per operation even when connected components are paths, even amortized or randomized. The proof reduces dynamic connectivity to a permutation composition problem using a grid graph with perfect matchings between columns. An access sequence based on the bit-reversal order is used, and a balanced binary tree over time is constructed to analyze information flow between left and right subtrees. An information theoretic argument with separator families and perfect hash functions shows that the data structure must read or write Ω(√n log n) cell probes for a block of √n updates and queries, implying the Ω(log n) per-operation lower bound. This establishes the optimality of link-cut trees and related dynamic tree structures.

In 2015 PayPal adopted a mission to democratize financial services using technology. CEO Dan Schulman, whose career included prepaid‑card work at American Express and a focus on serving the unbanked, led the company to pursue universal financial health. In 2019 the company discovered that 65 % of its entry‑level and hourly employees ran out of money between paychecks, prompting the creation of an Employee Financial Wellness Initiative. The four‑point plan, announced company‑wide in October 2019, included a wage increase where appropriate, a 60 % reduction in U.S. healthcare premiums for grades 15‑19 employees plus a company‑funded health‑reimbursement account, one‑time equity grants averaging $3,100 for roughly 8,600 employees (with a second grant in 2020), and a financial‑wellness coaching program offering education, digital tools, and confidential one‑on‑one support. PayPal emphasized that the initiative was company‑sponsored and not cross‑subsidized.

Measurement showed rapid improvement: turnover in customer‑service centers fell from 19.4 % in 2019 to 7.3 % in 2020, overall engagement scores rose to 84 (top 5 % of benchmark tech firms), and the share of employees intending to stay at least five years increased from 51 % to 76 %. By early 2021 the minimum estimated net disposable income for hourly and entry‑level staff reached 11 % (global goal 20 %). Additional benefits included on‑demand wage access via the Even app in the U.S. and the Hastee app in the U.K. and Ireland, and a third equity grant in 2021.

The initiative was part of PayPal’s broader multistakeholder capitalism approach, which also encompassed achieving gender‑pay equity globally and ethnic‑pay equity in the U.S. in 2016, committing $535 million to close the racial wealth gap, and providing $25 million in interest‑free advances to furloughed federal employees during the 2018‑19 government shutdown. Externally, PayPal co‑founded the non‑partisan Time to Vote movement and, together with the Financial Health Network, Good Jobs Institute, and Just Capital, formed a coalition that by the end of 2021 had 11 companies (including Chobani, Prudential, Verizon, and Chipotle) committed to employee financial‑wellness assessments.

Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) of the thalamus effectively manages tremor in essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease, but its mechanism remains unclear. This study recorded local field potentials (LFPs) from the thalamus (VIM and VOP) using a bipolar DBS lead in 34 patients and simultaneously recorded tremor with an accelerometer. Results showed a moderate correlation between tremor and low-frequency LFP spectral power in the alpha and theta bands, and a strong correlation between tremor and peak coherence between LFPs and acceleration. Postural tremor was decoded from LFP signals with an area under the curve of approximately 0.7. High-frequency DBS (~130 Hz) reduced low-frequency spectral power compared to baseline. Computational modeling revealed that low-frequency spectral power varied with electrode location, spatial distribution of tremor cells, and the proportion of tremor versus non-tremor cells. The findings suggest that LFP signals from the same lead used for stimulation could serve as internal biomarkers for closed-loop DBS control.

High‑performance computing (HPC) is emerging as a key competitive factor for industrial enterprises that rely on complex simulation, modeling and data analysis. Currently only a small share (8 %) reports high demand for such calculations, but within two years almost half of surveyed firms expect to do so. About 42 % of respondents already use outdated or inaccurate simulations, creating trade‑offs between speed and accuracy.

Four‑fifths of decision makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96 % among firms that have already implemented it. HPC enables more complex calculations, higher‑quality and faster simulations, unlocks new industrial usage scenarios, and increases innovation and agility across the value chain.

Deployment patterns show that the majority prefer external infrastructure: 87 % use or plan cloud‑based HPC, 74 % operate or plan own HPC in colocation datacenters, and 43 % partner with scientific institutions. Only 6 % currently run on‑premises HPC, though 28 % plan to do so. Key challenges include security concerns (72 %), high capital and licensing costs, energy consumption and sustainability (58 %), limited computing performance, availability, and a lack of internal expertise (42 %).

The future HPC landscape is expected to be dominated by public‑cloud and hybrid‑cloud architectures. HPC‑as‑a‑Service (HPCaaS) offers advantages such as cost‑flexibility, rapid access to cutting‑edge technology (52 % value this), and support for new business models—81 % of existing HPC users intend to launch HPC‑based offerings. Recommendations emphasize adopting virtual product development, establishing a holistic data strategy, evaluating make‑vs‑buy HPC models, ensuring scalability/security/energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The findings are based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland in firms with more than 500 employees.

The paper introduces the popular dimension of a matching market as the minimum size of a set of matchings that is at least as popular as any other matching. It studies three classic settings: house allocation, marriage, and roommates.  

For the house‑allocation problem the popular dimension is shown to be exactly 2 for all four cases (unweighted or weighted agents, strict or tied preference lists).  

For the marriage problem, when agents are unweighted and preferences are strict the dimension is 1 (a stable matching always exists and is popular). In the more general cases (weighted agents or ties) the dimension is at least 2 and at most 3.  

For the roommates problem, with unweighted agents and strict preferences the dimension is 2; for the general case (weights or ties) the dimension is again at least 2 and at most 3.  

Polynomial‑time algorithms are given: Algorithm 1 builds a size‑2 popular winning set for house allocation; Algorithm 2 builds a size‑2 set for the unweighted‑strict roommates problem; Algorithm 3 builds a size‑3 set for the general roommates problem by reducing it to house allocation and edge‑colouring.  

The paper leaves as an open problem whether the dimension for the weighted/tied marriage and roommates cases is exactly 2, conjecturing that it is 2 for the marriage case.

The study examines how climate change affects internally displaced learners' education in lower- and middle-income countries. It employs a Human Rights-Based Approach combined with Education in Emergencies research through a literature review of 73 sources. Climate change impacts education through displacement, resource scarcity, and health consequences, creating barriers including physical disruptions, socioeconomic pressures, and environmental factors affecting learning. Displaced learners face additional challenges in new environments: financial constraints, administrative hurdles like registration systems, discrimination, and limited access to alternative education. Children experience psychological trauma and health issues that affect academic performance. Girls face heightened vulnerabilities due to economic pressures and cultural norms that prioritize boys' education. The study identifies research gaps including limited focus on climate-related displacement within emergency education frameworks and reactive rather than proactive policy responses. It advocates for comprehensive approaches including financial support, streamlined administrative processes, and gender-sensitive policies, treating climate displacement as an educational emergency requiring long-term systemic solutions.

The passage describes two all-optical thermometry methods using fluorescent diamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers and machine learning pattern recognition to address calibration limitations. The core innovation involves analyzing multiple temperature-dependent features from the diamonds' photoluminescence (PL) and Raman signals. Two regression algorithms are introduced: a standard multi-feature regression (MFR) model using explicit feature selection, and a two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) model using partial least squares regression, Lasso regression, and spline correction. The experiments tracked nine physical quantities (intensity, peak position, and FWHM of ZPL, PSB, and Raman signals) across a temperature range of 25–85 °C. The MFR model achieves approximately a 26% improvement in accuracy over traditional single-feature (SF) models using only three features (ZPL wavelength, ZPL linewidth, and Raman linewidth) and minimal calibration data (3–4 diamonds). The 2SMFR model achieves the highest performance (0.7 K accuracy and 0.6 K∙Hz−1/2 resolution, representing roughly a 70% improvement over SF models and a 59% improvement over the MFR model) but requires larger calibration sets (up to seven diamonds and temperature points). The sensitivity of the 2SMFR model is approximately seven times higher than the best SF model. The methods provide a flexible, data-efficient, and instrument-agnostic framework for nanoscale thermometry.

On April 27, 2001, the Dabhol Power Company (DPC) board authorized its managing director to issue a termination notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) following disputes over unpaid bills and a Rs 401 crore penalty imposed by MSEB for alleged non-supply of power. International lenders favored termination, while Indian lenders led by IDBI opposed it and pushed for renegotiation. The Indian government and Maharashtra chief minister expressed concern and indicated willingness to renegotiate, but also said termination would not significantly impact foreign investment. The termination could cost the Center Rs 2,840 crore (one year's electricity bill plus a $300 million termination fee). MSEB made a protest payment of Rs 134 crore for March bills. The DPC's high tariff (Rs 7.1 per kilowatt-hour) was a key point of contention. The DPC had issued a political force majeure notice, and multiple arbitration and conciliation notices were in progress. MSEB held a 15% stake in DPC, with Enron holding 65% and GE and Bechtel holding 10% each.

The case addressed whether a widow’s share in her deceased husband’s real estate is subject to his estate’s debts. The relevant statutes (Code §§ 2387, 2391, 2440, 2441, 2453) and prior common‑law dower principles were examined. The court held that the widow’s interest attaches upon the husband’s seizure of the land and the wife’s coverture, becomes vested upon his death, and is not made subject to estate debts or charges; it is secured by absolute language in § 2440. Sections 2387 and 2391 authorize sale of the estate’s interest in the land, not the widow’s portion. Section 2441 merely prohibits awarding the widow more than one‑third of the land’s value, not subordinating her right to creditors. Section 2451 provides for payment of the widow’s share and subsequent homestead exemption from her own debts, not from her husband’s debts. The lower court’s order setting apart the widow’s interest was affirmed.

On September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon prompted major energy companies, including Enron, Dynegy, and El Paso, to shut down trading operations, evacuate employees, and enhance security at facilities such as nuclear power plants. Energy markets suspended trading at the New York Mercantile Exchange and online platforms like EnronOnline, causing oil prices to spike to $31 per barrel and gasoline prices to rise amid fears of supply disruption. Companies increased security domestically and reviewed operations in South Asia, with Enron India taking precautions at its Dabhol project. Some energy trading resumed on September 12, and OPEC indicated readiness to boost production to stabilize prices.

The quarterback is regarded as the most important position in football, touching the ball on every play and serving as the leader of the offense. His responsibilities include taking the snap, throwing or running the ball, relaying play calls from coaches, making audibles at the line of scrimmage, ensuring correct formation, and extensive study of playbook, scouting reports, and opponent film. Key skills required are a high football IQ, sound decision‑making, accuracy, leadership, solid footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. The position is also called the signal caller, field general, or gunslinger; the name originated from early formations where the quarterback stood a quarter‑back behind the running back. Body type has evolved from traditionally tall, strong players to a range of sizes and athletic profiles. Notable quarterbacks cited include Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady. Because the quarterback controls the ball each play, orchestrates the offense, and influences its success, he is viewed as the most crucial position in sports.

Uber’s self‑driving Volvo struck and killed a 49‑year‑old woman, Elaine Herzberg, who was walking outside a crosswalk in Tempe, Arizona, on Sunday night. The vehicle was in autonomous mode with a safety driver present. Uber immediately suspended all road‑testing in the U.S. and Canada. The fatality is the first involving a fully autonomous test car and may affect future regulation and development of self‑driving technology.

In Josephine Slosson’s estate, her father’s will gave her a life interest in a trust fund and a power of appointment. She validly exercised the power by directing payment of her debts from the fund, bequeathing $5,000 to her predeceased husband, $500 to Margaret Gillesse, and the remainder to her surviving issue per stirpes. Her three children elected to take under the grandfather’s will, but the court held that the power was effectively exercised, so the trust passed under the decedent’s will; the contingency for the grandfather’s alternative disposition never occurred. Consequently, the beneficiaries’ interests were subject to a transfer tax. The children had not renounced their legacies, so the tax consequences of renunciation were not considered. Money ($682.04) advanced by Alice Slosson to pay the decedent’s creditors was improperly included as taxable interest; the order was modified to deduct that amount and affirmed in all other respects.

Carol Christ, 73, has become the first female chancellor of UC Berkeley, the crown jewel of the UC system. A Victorian literature scholar, she previously served as president of Smith College and returned to Berkeley after nearly five decades, having taught there as a 26‑year‑old Ph.D. graduate from Yale. She inherits multiple challenges: a $110 million budget deficit that must be halved, a state audit revealing $175 million in undisclosed funds and a $50 million withholding by Governor Jerry Brown, ongoing free‑speech controversies, a student housing shortage and a campus community she describes as fractured. Christ plans a “free‑speech year” with point‑counterpoint debates, partner with Berkeley and Oakland on housing and homelessness, and increase private philanthropy while cutting administrative costs. She is concerned about low Black enrollment (≈3 %) and says sexual‑assault policy will be addressed through cross‑group conversations. Faculty have expressed optimism about her tenure.

Penalty kick takers are players who take a restart awarded after a foul inside the penalty area. Law 14 governs the kick: the ball is placed on the penalty mark, the goalkeeper must stay on the goal line between the posts, all other players must be outside the penalty arc, the ball must be kicked forward and is in play once it moves. The kicker must develop a consistent routine that includes setting the ball, choosing a starting position, and executing one of three basic kick styles – inside‑of‑foot, instep drive, or instep‑face – with accuracy prioritized over power. Preferred target zones are the lower corners; the upper corners are harder to stop but more likely to be missed. Mental techniques such as focused breathing and visualization help block distractions and maintain composure. Coaches identify a primary kicker and at least one alternate based on demonstrated ability and confidence; any player on the field may take the kick. During the run‑up, feints are permitted only before the final step; once the run‑up is completed, feinting is not allowed. After the whistle, the kicker jogs to the ball, plants the non‑kicking foot toward the target, strikes with the chosen technique, and follows through. If the ball rebounds off the posts or is saved, the kicker may follow up only after another player has touched it. Regular practice should simulate game conditions, involve a goalkeeper, and emphasize repetition to build muscle memory. Advanced tactics include scouting the opponent’s goalkeeper, maintaining at least two different kick options, using a “tap” or “two‑man” play, and modifying the approach to reduce tells. Success depends on preparation, a consistent routine, calm focus, accurate placement, and regular practice.

Expiry is the moment an options contract becomes void; in the US the expiration date is the third Saturday of the month, with the last trading day usually the preceding Friday (or Thursday if Friday is a holiday). The expiration time is 11:59 a.m. EST on the expiration date.

The third week of the month – the options expiration week – typically shows higher average weekly returns for large‑cap stocks with actively traded options (the Options Expiration Week Effect or OPEX). When stock, index‑futures and index‑options all expire on the same day (March, June, September, December) it is called a quad‑witching week.

Strategies around expiry include selling bear/bull call credit spreads and gamma‑neutral combinations. Developing such strategies requires researching models, backtesting over at least 15 years through bull and bear cycles, and forward‑testing the best‑performing model.

Backtests on SPY and the healthcare ETF XLV illustrate the effect: SPY averaged a 0.3% weekly gain during expiration weeks; XLV showed a 0.7% average gain per trade; an overnight SPY strategy averaged 0.46% per trade; a short‑term day‑trade on SPY yielded 0.18% per trade. Expiry days exhibit slightly higher volatility than normal trading days, especially quad‑witching days.

Seasonality‑based expiry strategies are presented as robust and among the least likely to stop working.

Chenai Mathabire, a 35‑year‑old Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for demonstrating that a rapid urine‑based tuberculosis test can be implemented in health centers in southeast Africa. The test yields results in under an hour, requires only a few hours of staff training, and is easy to read. Over two years Mathabire and a team evaluated the test in Malawi and Mozambique, where HIV is the leading cause of death and TB is the top killer of HIV‑positive patients. They found the rapid test reduced diagnostic delays from days to minutes, was accepted by patients, and has already been adopted by some Doctors Without Borders facilities, potentially improving survival for HIV‑positive patients. Mathabire still works for Doctors Without Borders, is planning further HIV/TB research, and recently moved to Sweden to marry an infectious‑disease specialist while sewing her own wedding dress.

Player said his team held off an opponent, scored a goal and played its best game, needing a response. The nominee thanks Governor Stevenson, Senator Johnson, Adlai Stevenson, Senator Symington, President Truman, Senator Humphrey and Chairman Butler for their support and introductions, and acknowledges his distinguished running‑mate, Lyndon Johnson. He accepts the Democratic presidential nomination with a pledge to devote his full effort to lead the party to victory and to uphold the Constitution. He affirms the platform’s commitment to civil and economic rights, insists its pledges are made to be kept, and notes his record on separation of church and state and on public education as proof that his religious affiliation will not affect his policy decisions. He asks voters not to base their choice on his faith, stating that his decisions will be his own as an American and a Democrat.

He warns that the Republican opponent has not produced a challenger with both competence and courage, characterizes the opposition’s rhetoric as generic and its platform as a collection of left‑over Democratic planks, and predicts a difficult campaign. He outlines major challenges at home and abroad: a shifting global balance of power, new and terrible weapons, expanding Communist influence, technological revolutions in agriculture and urbanization, demands for civil‑rights progress, extensions of medical care for the elderly, and automation that displaces workers without replacing their income. He also cites a decline in moral and intellectual vigor and a “dry rot” in Washington.

He introduces the concept of a “New Frontier” for the 1960s—an array of unmet scientific, economic and social frontiers that require bold leadership, sacrifice and pioneering spirit rather than promises of security. He calls for courage, decisive leadership and collective effort, urging citizens to give their help, voice and vote. He closes by invoking the biblical promise of renewed strength for those who wait upon the Lord.

The study, published in the American Journal of Psychiatry, tracked 33,908 Norwegian adults for 11 years. Non‑exercisers were 44% more likely to develop depression than those who exercised 1–2 hours weekly; small amounts of exercise could have prevented 12% of depression cases. Author Prof. Samuel Harvey noted that even one hour of weekly exercise offers protection and suggests integrating exercise into mental‑health strategies.

This is an appeal from a judgment denying recovery in a head-on collision case. The appellants sued for damages arising from a May 28, 1955 collision on a three-lane highway, alleging King was negligent. King denied liability and claimed Wilson caused the collision. The jury found that Wilson drove into the west lane, was negligent, and was the sole proximate cause of the collision, while King was not negligent. The appellants raised six assignments of error regarding jury instructions and improper argument. The court found that the appellants waived their objections by failing to timely object under Texas Rules of Civil Procedure 272 and 273, and that the improper argument could have been cured if objected to at the time. The judgment was affirmed.
