The Hawk Offense is a high‑post rub offense derived from the UCLA system and the shuffle offense. Introduced to the NBA by Hubie Brown in Atlanta, it primarily exploits mismatches at the off‑guard/shooting‑guard spot while also offering wing isolations and post‑up options. The offense is organized into three phases: (1) dribble‑entry point isolation, with the ball handler reading defensive responses (e.g., baseline sag, double‑team) and making drop passes or kick‑outs; (2) a high‑post shuffle cut in which the off‑guard uses a back screen from the high post to cut to the basket, with multiple reads and counters (chase over, under, switch, zone, show‑recover, double‑team); and (3) ball‑reversal down‑screen action that creates weak‑side post isolation and Hi/Lo feeds. When the basic flow does not produce a good look, teams transition to continuities such as Flex (continuous pick‑the‑picker screening), the Triangle Game (inside‑screening with wing shooters) and Motion (five‑player passing game). Several NBA‑style variations expand the base action: Side Screen, Single/Double, Back Screen, Pin Down, Base Screen, and Post Lob, each offering specific entry, roll, post‑up or reversal options. Successful implementation requires precise spacing, timing, non‑verbal communication, defensive recognition and a whole‑part‑whole teaching method supported by drills (2‑on‑2, 3‑on‑3, scrimmages). Game strategy emphasizes scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, varying alignments and entries, and using organized continuity as the shot clock winds down. The offense is complemented by an awareness of how to defend it.

Grin is a secretive blockchain whose developers adopt Harry‑Potter aliases; Blockstream mathematician Andrew Poelstra has clarified he is not a pseudonymous member of the project. Mimblewimble, a “scriptless” privacy protocol built on Blockstream’s Confidential Transactions, allows spent outputs to be removed because the spend cancels the receive, yet verifiers can still authenticate key ownership and prove that the sum of outputs minus inputs equals zero, with no new money created. It replaces arbitrary Bitcoin scripts with simple group‑to‑group or person‑to‑person transfers, giving a symmetry where inputs and outputs cannot be altered without breaking the balancing equation and where a balanced transaction cannot be produced without the blinding keys.  

For Mimblewimble‑compatible chains, verification requires only the current unspent outputs and one signature per transaction, compressing the entire history into a small set of signatures; Poelstra estimated this could shrink Bitcoin’s then‑80 GB blockchain to roughly 1 MB plus the unspent‑output set. The design is not yet usable because wallet support is absent, and Poelstra has proposed a soft‑fork‑friendly Grin implementation that would initially host the Grin currency and a test currency, later adding a Bitcoin peg so all assets appear indistinguishable to outside observers, providing shared privacy.  

Poelstra’s 2016 paper highlighted the compression property, but removing scripts threatened functionality such as Lightning; he discovered that signatures can sign script‑like conditions, enabling simple Lightning‑like constructions and that the difference between Schnorr signatures can be used for atomic swaps without revealing the signatures themselves, allowing signature transfer between chains. He has also worked out how to link transactions across different elliptic curves (e.g., Bitcoin and Monero) and how to chain multiple transactions like Lightning channels, using discrete logarithms for routing. A Mimblewimble sidechain would be smaller for future verifiers by deleting spent outputs and inputs, while real‑time size remains similar to Bitcoin plus Confidential Transactions.

Gamma‑ray astrophysics emerged in the 1950s to study high‑energy astrophysical processes; because gamma rays are not deflected by magnetic fields they can point directly to emission sources. Atmospheric absorption creates electron‑positron pairs and electromagnetic showers, so ground‑based detection relies on Cherenkov light emitted by the relativistic charged particles in the showers, using the atmosphere as a natural calorimeter and achieving effective areas of ~10⁴ m². This is the principle of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs), which employ large reflectors and photomultiplier or silicon sensors to reconstruct gamma‑ray direction and energy while rejecting the much more abundant charged‑cosmic‑ray background. Current major IACT systems are MAGIC (two 17 m reflectors in La Palma), H.E.S.S. (four 12 m plus a 28 m in Namibia) and VERITAS (four 12 m in Arizona), each requiring multiple telescopes for stereoscopic reconstruction.

The future Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will improve energy (20 GeV–300 TeV) and spatial resolution, provide full sky coverage and be the first ground‑based gamma‑ray facility open to external proposals. Three telescope types are planned: Large‑Sized Telescopes (23 m, 4.3° field of view) for the frequent low‑energy showers (20–150 GeV), Medium‑Sized Telescopes (12 m, 8° field of view) for the core range (150 GeV–5 TeV), and Small‑Sized Telescopes (4.3 m, 9° field of view) for the rare high‑energy showers (5–300 TeV). Northern and Southern arrays will be sited at La Palma and the Atacama desert, respectively; prototypes such as LST‑1 are already commissioning, and additional prototypes exist for dual‑mirror SSTs and a Schwarzschild‑Couder medium‑sized telescope.

During its first ten years 40 % of CTAO observing time is allocated to Key Science Projects (KSPs). A major KSP focuses on indirect dark‑matter searches via WIMP annihilation, described by a particle‑physics factor (WIMP mass, velocity‑averaged cross‑section ⟨σv⟩ and photon spectrum) and an astrophysical J‑factor (squared dark‑matter density integrated over the line of sight). Simulated observations of the Galactic Center (825 h), Large Magellanic Cloud (340 h), Perseus Galaxy Cluster (300 h) and several dwarf spheroidal galaxies (100 h each) indicate CTAO can improve upper limits on ⟨σv⟩ for TeV‑scale WIMPs by roughly an order of magnitude and set limits below the thermal benchmark using spectral‑line searches.

CTAO will also probe fundamental physics by observing active galactic nuclei, constraining axion‑like particles (via photon‑ALP oscillations) and other effects on photon propagation over cosmological distances, including extragalactic background light, intergalactic magnetic fields and Lorentz‑invariance violation. Overall, CTAO promises revolutionary sensitivity, resolution and survey capabilities for gamma‑ray astrophysics and dark‑matter studies.

In November 2015 Brazil declared a public‑health emergency because of Zika virus (ZIKV) outbreaks, and prenatal ZIKV infection was linked to congenital Zika syndrome (CZS)—a condition characterized by microcephaly, brain malformations, hearing loss, locomotor disability and increased risk of in‑utero fetal death. No prenatal standards of care exist, and the reasons for variable brain injury among exposed infants are unclear. A scoping review was therefore conducted to identify candidate genes that may modulate susceptibility to virally induced prenatal brain injury. Included studies were experimental or observational designs that reported genetic factors associated with ZIKV‑related prenatal brain injury; gray literature and review articles were excluded. Searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Academic Search Ultimate, Agricola, Health Source: Nursing/Academic Edition, Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection and CINAHL were performed, following PRISMA guidelines. After screening 3 777 records, 13 articles met the inclusion criteria. These articles described 23 candidate genes (six maternal and 17 fetal/neonatal) that may influence brain injury after prenatal ZIKV exposure. The genes fall into several functional groups: neurodevelopmental genes (DISP3, miR‑124‑1, TP53, NOS2, VEGFA, MTOR, CDK5RAP2, FOXG1, LHX2), inflammation‑ and immunity‑related genes (IL12RB2, CXCL8, CXCL10, TNF, TLR3, TREM1, IL4, ADCY3, ADCY7, IL28B) and cellular‑stress genes (DDIT4L). Specific alleles were associated with increased risk of CZS or severe microcephaly, whereas other variants showed protective trends. Limitations noted include small cohort sizes, use of a candidate‑gene approach and the need for larger replication studies and functional validation. The authors suggest that larger pooled genomic studies and functional analyses could eventually guide neuroprotective strategies and early identification of infants at risk for severe brain injury.

The case involves Iturea Atwood Hicks, widow of deceased Benjamin E. Atwood, appealing an order that revoked her letters of administration and appointed H.B. Sanders as administrator. Deceased died in 1894 leaving no children. The estate was valued at $390 (community property). Sanders petitioned to revoke the letters claiming Hicks failed to publish notice to creditors for more than two months. The trial court revoked the letters. The Supreme Court reversed, holding that under Code of Civil Procedure section 1469, when an estate's value does not exceed $1500 and there are no children, the widow is entitled to the whole estate without further administration proceedings. Therefore, notice to creditors is not required, and persons without interest in the estate cannot invoke court machinery to revoke letters of administration.

According to a Finnish study of 5,800 public‑sector employees who retired between 2000 and 2011, sleep difficulties declined after retirement. In the final working year 30 % reported sleep problems, falling to 26 % after retirement; overall problem likelihood dropped 11 %, early‑morning awakenings fell 24 % and non‑restorative sleep fell 53 %. Sleep duration increased by about 20 minutes on average, and by 45 minutes for those with prior sleep difficulties or heavy alcohol use. Reductions were most marked among retirees who had poor health, shorter sleep, psychological stress or job strain before retirement. The researchers note that retirement removes work‑related stress and offers an opportunity to obtain more restorative sleep. Commenting on the findings, Dr. Jean‑Claude Marquie highlighted that some effects of poor working conditions may be reversible and that more research on middle‑aged workers is needed.

Deep ripping only addresses subsoil conditions and does not overcome topsoil water repellence, which can worsen when dry topsoil is loosened. Soil inversion treatments are more effective than deep ripping for improving soil moisture in water repellent soils, showing significantly higher moisture content at various depths in trials. Growers with water repellent soils are advised to avoid dry seeding, delay cereal seeding, increase seeding rates, use soil wetting agents, or implement soil amelioration measures.

Digital leaders treat data culture as the centerpiece that aligns employee beliefs, espoused values and day‑to‑day actions; employees consistently reflect stated values, while digital laggards exhibit misalignment despite recognizing the importance of a data‑driven culture. Changing entrenched mindsets and behaviors is the most challenging part of transformation, yet many former laggards have successfully evolved. Mature firms—whether digital natives or transformed traditional enterprises—enjoy a competitive edge by embedding learning, risk‑taking, transparency and measurement into their culture, values and daily practices. Organizations fall into four patterns: data novices (need culture and system change), insight ready (supportive culture but limited analytics), tech enabled (advanced tools but low experimentation) and data reliant (over‑reliance on data that discourages critical thinking). Each pattern can target specific actions to strengthen data culture. Keystone Strategy is a consulting firm offering technology‑led strategy and digital transformation services.

Whole-body MR imaging at ultrahigh fields (7T, 10.5T) benefits from higher SNR but challenges arise from increased Larmor frequencies, large inductance, parasitic capacitance, radiation losses, and electromagnetic coupling. Microstrip resonators provide high Q‑factors and reduced radiation, while high‑impedance coil designs suppress inter‑element coupling. The authors present a high‑impedance microstrip transmission‑line resonator that combines these features and was validated with a 2‑channel prototype (8 cm × 8 cm, copper strip on 2 mm Teflon). The array was tuned to 447 MHz (10.5T proton frequency) and matched to 50 Ω; at a 10 mm gap the high‑frequency mode achieved –21 dB decoupling, whereas the low‑frequency mode (~116 MHz) showed stronger coupling (~‑7.6 dB). Reducing the gap to 2 mm caused the low‑frequency mode to split, while the high‑frequency mode retained decoupling. Simulations confirmed well‑defined B₁ distributions and a B₁⁺ of about 2 µT/√W per channel. The high‑impedance microstrip coil array therefore offers a simple, robust approach for multichannel transceivers at ultrahigh‑field MRI.

Due to the expiration of pandemic-era ESSER funds and declining enrollment, school districts face budget shortfalls while serving increasing numbers of students with disabilities and multilingual learners. The master schedule, which controls teacher time, class sizes, and 70-85% of district budgets, is often inefficiently managed. Two Texas districts, Lubbock and Edgewood, used AI-optimization tools to redesign their schedules, saving $2.2 million in Lubbock across 14 schools and $1.05 million in Edgewood districtwide, without laying off any teachers—adjustments came through normal turnover. AI analyzed thousands of scheduling scenarios to rebalance class sizes and workloads, freeing staff to focus on strategic, student-centered decisions. The authors argue that AI can help districts navigate financial constraints while improving educational quality.

Investors have placed record-high bets against the pound due to Brexit concerns, despite a historical pattern of sterling rising approximately 2 percent in April. Nomura analysts warned this seasonal bounce poses risks for short sellers. Speculators' net short positions hit record highs in late March before pulling back. Analysts cite UK tax year-end and corporate dividend repatriation as contributing factors to April gains, which emerged consistently after 2004.

Active Surfaces, founded 2022 as an MIT spin‑out, makes flexible solar panels using roll‑to‑roll printing. Co‑founders Dr. Richard Swartwout (Ph.D., MIT) and Shiv Bhakta (MS/MBA, MIT) lead the firm. In 2023 it issued 500k shares at $2, paid $24,000 for insurance, opened a $1 M line of credit and drew $400,000, purchased $2,000 of office supplies on credit, bought $650,000 of equipment, paid a $25,000 legal retainer, billed a pilot project $500,000, later repaid $420,000 on the line, received a 20% down payment on a $1 M order, spent $325,000 on raw materials, received a $1,500 retainer refund, recognized one‑year insurance expense, and recorded $65,000 depreciation. The assignment asks to record these events, prepare a balance sheet, and compute net income and cash flow.

Audi’s e‑tron prototype has a drag coefficient of 0.28—best for SUVs—enabling >400 km WLTP range; each 0.01 reduction adds ~5 km. Tested >1,000 hours in Ingolstadt wind tunnel (2.6 MW, 300 km/h). Features: exterior mirrors (15 cm narrower, OLED displays), air suspension (lowers 26 mm >120 km/h), enclosed underbody with bowl‑shaped dimples protecting battery, cool‑air inlet with louvers, side ducts to wheel arches, and 19‑inch wheels with low‑rolling‑resistance 255/55 tires and negative lettering. These improve range by ~35 km per charge versus comparable conventional vehicle.

Year 6 volunteers and PTA cleaned a bus Swallowdale Primary is converting into a reading area. The bus will be painted as a woodland scene with book characters chosen by pupils, and the school seeks an upholsterer to recover seats.

The passage discusses challenges in quantifying graph similarity/distance and reviews prior approaches: exact graph matching (Sussenguth, Zelinka, Sobik, Kaden), graph edit distance, graph kernels, and topological‑index based measures. It notes that a recent multi‑index method loses information when converting indices to a binary representation. The authors propose a new similarity/distance measure built from multiple topological indices, scaled to [0,1] via Ji(G) = (Ii(G) – m)/(M – m). They define distance dp(G1,G2) using a p‑norm on the scaled indices and provide conversion formulas (d = 1 – s; for bounded d, s = (M – d)/M; for unbounded, s = 1/(1 + d)). The measure is claimed comparable to an established metric, more sensitive to structural differences, computationally less demanding, and applicable to random‑graph models (Watts–Strogatz, Barabási–Albert) and molecular similarity of decane isomers.

Disney’s brand sentiment fell to its lowest in at least two years among Republicans and Democrats, according to a Jefferies analysis of Morning Consult data. The decline followed Disney’s temporary suspension of Jimmy Kimmel’s show after his comments about a slain conservative activist and a subsequent Disney+ price hike. Both parties saw sharp drops, with Democrats soured more than Republicans. Analysts say the PR hit may limit streaming churn, while Disney shares fell 6% over the past month. Jefferies maintained a buy rating and $144 price target.

Functional emulsifier blends are mixtures used to create oil‑ and water‑based emulsions. They are employed notably in ice‑cream and bakery products, where they improve handling, product feel and maintain fat content. North America dominates the market owing to concentration of major food‑ingredient producers such as ADM and Cargill, while the APAC region shows the fastest growth driven by rising private investment. Increasing food‑safety concerns and demand for processed foods are key drivers, and multifunctional properties are the primary consumer preference. Major players invest in R&D and expand capacity; however, complex food matrices and GMO restrictions present challenges. Food‑and‑beverage, especially bakery, is the largest application segment, with personal care projected to grow faster.

In early America the choice between submission to a foreign legislature and total independence prompted founders to fear internal disputes over government forms. Revolutionary zeal maintained order until a Confederation modeled on the Batavian and Helvetic confederacies proved inadequate for the country’s size, leading to neglect, economic decline, and political discord. This crisis inspired the creation of a more perfect union embodied in the Constitution, which established justice, domestic tranquility, common defense, general welfare, and liberty. The author first encountered the Constitution abroad, supported it, and after returning served under it, finding its operation meets expectations and earning an habitual attachment to it. The passage extols the representative system of government, warns that free, fair elections must be protected from party intrigue or foreign influence, and notes potential abuses. It praises George Washington’s prudent, just, and fortitudinous leadership, recommending his example to successors. The author declares personal commitments to a free republican government, support of the Constitution, respect for state governments, equal regard for all states, love of virtuous men, encouragement of education and knowledge, promotion of justice, improvement of agriculture, commerce, and manufactures, fair treatment of Native peoples, maintenance of peace, neutrality, and friendship with all nations, esteem for France, determination to seek reparations for commercial injuries, confidence in the American people, and veneration for Christianity. The passage concludes with a prayer for continued divine blessing on the nation and its government.

President addresses coal miners during World War II, stating the country faces a serious crisis as the war has reached a critical phase. The president returned from a two-week inspection tour through twenty states, observing military training and war production including airplanes, guns, and ammunition. Farmers are planting crops to feed armed forces and civilians.

After Pearl Harbor, three major labor organizations including the United Mine Workers of America pledged no strikes during the war. The War Labor Board was established to settle disputes with representatives from workers, employers, and the public. However, when a coal crisis arose, the UMW national officers refused to participate in the Board's fact-finding process despite the Board's assurance of fair proceedings and retroactive wage adjustments to April first.

A general strike began on Friday night, prompting the government to take over the mines on Saturday morning. The president appeals to miners' patriotism, noting their sons are fighting overseas in locations including New Guinea, the Aleutian Islands, Guadalcanal, Tunisia, and China. The president states that stopping coal production even briefly endangers soldiers and victory chances, and that production will continue regardless.

The Secretary of the Interior has authority over the mines, existing contract terms will be followed, and miners who return to work will receive protection. The president affirms support for workers' rights and union membership while stating miners must resume production. The president expresses belief that miners will heed the call to duty and that the nation will achieve victory.

Her Highness Sheikha Jawaher Al Qasimi visited 10th Sharjah Children’s Reading Festival (SCRF) at Expo Centre Sharjah, themed ‘Your Future… Just a Book Away’. She said children’s learning today shapes future values and ideas, desire to learn builds civilization. She visited publishers and workshops, highlighting SCRF’s role in inspiring a thirst for reading, knowledge and innovation. She said books restore harmony and bring humanity together, praising the Sharjah Book Authority for organizing an event that combines fun, science and arts, encouraging youth to develop skills and express creativity.

Google partnered with the Pentagon on a drone footage‑analyzing AI (Project Maven). Over 3,100 employees signed a petition opposing the work, and about a dozen resigned in May. Google responded by saying it is developing ethical guidelines that would preclude AI use in weaponry.

The passage discusses a study on human rights education (HRE) in early childhood education and care (ECEC), proposing four content selection dimensions: children's ages, progression, human rights knowledge anchored in social studies, and children's own interests. Using the Norwegian ECEC context and UN Day observance as an example, the study analyzes 73 posts from the Idebroen website via theoretical content analysis. Findings show that ideas for observing UN Day primarily focus on human rights, diversity, or fundraising, with limited explicit connection to specific human rights articles. The analysis highlights opportunities and challenges in adapting content to children's developmental levels, ensuring progression, and grounding knowledge in social studies. The study concludes that the dimensions provide a structured framework for selecting HRE content, but ECEC teachers need more support and guidance to effectively implement HRE.
The passage is a collection of headlines from The 74 covering a wide range of topics, including crime, education, public policy, sports, cultural events, and community initiatives.

The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN), viewed as a message to the US and North Korea to pursue negotiations amid rising nuclear tensions. The award emphasized concerns about nuclear escalation on the Korean Peninsula and was interpreted as coded support for the Iran nuclear deal. The US stated it would not sign the treaty banning nuclear weapons backed by ICAN. North Korea recently conducted its largest nuclear test and is preparing long-range missile tests capable of reaching the US west coast. Tensions have escalated with aggressive rhetoric from both sides, including Trump's "calm before the storm" remark and Kim's threats. The Nobel committee aims to draw global attention to nuclear dangers and encourage diplomatic efforts to prevent irreversible consequences.

President Coolidge commemorated the late President Harding, pledged to continue his policies, and outlined a broad domestic and foreign agenda.

Foreign policy emphasizes peace, non‑entanglement, and refusal to join the League of Nations while supporting a permanent World Court with appropriate reservations. Relations with Russia are conditional on honoring debts, respecting international obligations, and abandoning hostility; American principles are not for sale. The United States will adjust foreign debts but not cancel them, protect claims against Germany and American citizens, and seek Europe’s economic recovery.

Domestically, the Budget system achieved a $3 billion reduction in expenditures, enabling tax cuts on earned incomes and the elimination of nuisance taxes; excess‑profits taxes are opposed in peacetime and a constitutional amendment is proposed to end tax‑exempt securities. The tariff will be kept with limited adjustments via its elastic clause, and the merchant fleet will be transferred to private ownership.

Public‑improvement projects (waterways, flood control, St. Lawrence power/navigation) and modest infrastructure spending are endorsed. Railroad regulation, labor‑board mediation, and freight‑rate restructuring are recommended, with consolidation legislation to follow Supreme Court rulings. The Department of Justice needs law revision, additional judges, simplified court procedures, prison‑industry employment, and a criminal‑identification division.

Prohibition enforcement requires treaty negotiations, a strengthened Coast Guard, and cooperation with states. Civil‑rights protection for the 12 million African‑Americans, anti‑lynching legislation, vocational training, and a bipartisan commission for race relations are urged. The classified civil service should be expanded to postmasters and prohibition enforcement personnel.

Regulatory proposals cover maritime‑pollution control, aviation, radio interference, vessel load‑line standards, navigation‑law recodification, the Federal Trade Commission, and Alaskan fisheries. The Army and Navy should be strengthened with additional aircraft and submarines, and Panama’s defenses completed.

Education and welfare merit a cabinet‑level department, federal encouragement of schooling, child‑labor limits, and a minimum‑wage law for women under federal jurisdiction. Immigration must stay selective and restricted, with mandatory alien registration. Veterans deserve adequate hospital care, expanded facilities, and a generous but non‑bonus approach.

Coal‑industry problems require reduced prices, continuity of production, voluntary arbitration, and possible emergency commissions. A reorganization plan for executive departments is pending. Agriculture needs tax relief, freight‑rate adjustments, cheaper fertilizers, farmer organization, diversification, and limited export assistance through the War Finance Corporation. Muscle Shoals should be sold with covenants guaranteeing cheap nitrate production for agriculture, and reclamation‑project users may receive charge adjustments. Highway funding and reforestation remain national priorities.

The Monroe Doctrine must be upheld with a balance of idealism and responsibility; America’s moral leadership and commitment to justice will maintain its free, independent, and powerful position in the world.

Toronto's TTC will return 67 of 89 new Bombardier streetcars for repairs of inferior frame welds; no safety risk, repairs at Bombardier's La Pocatiere, Que., facility, covered by Bombardier, completed by 2022, involving 25‑30 workers and work done in Mexico.

Scientists at Ohio State University discovered that exhausted T cells become overwhelmed by misfolded proteins, activating a previously unknown stress pathway named TexPSR (proteotoxic stress response in T‑cell exhaustion). A leading opinion journal described TexPSR-driven exhaustion as a “proteotoxic shock”. Unlike typical stress responses that slow protein production, TexPSR drives protein synthesis out of control, causing toxic buildup that disables T‑cell tumor‑killing activity. Blocking key drivers of TexPSR in preclinical models restored T‑cell function and enhanced cancer immunotherapy. Elevated TexPSR levels in patients’ T cells correlated with poor immunotherapy outcomes. The mechanism was validated across multiple cancer types, including lung, bladder, liver cancer, and leukemia, suggesting that targeting TexPSR could improve therapeutic response.

Buchanan transmits to Congress the Kansas constitution, certified by J. Calhoun, expressing hope for admission. He describes the political situation in Kansas as a rebellion by supporters of the Topeka constitution against the Territorial government authorized by Congress, citing reports from Governor Walker detailing the existence of a revolutionary organization, the failure of opponents to vote in the delegate election, and violent resistance including attacks at Lawrence and organized militia under General Lane. He maintains that the Lecompton convention was legally constituted under the organic act, that the June 1857 delegate election was free and fair despite the opposition’s abstention, and that the people subsequently elected a governor, legislature, and other State officers under the Lecompton constitution on January 4, 1858, indicating a majority accepted the new government. Buchanan argues that admitting Kansas fulfills the principle of popular sovereignty, will localize the slavery question, restore domestic peace, allow withdrawal of U.S. troops, and avoid renewed national agitation. He notes that the constitution includes a provision recognizing the people’s right to alter or abolish their government, and that a majority can amend the constitution after admission if they wish. He then issues a proclamation on the same date regarding Utah, stating that settlers there have repeatedly defied the Constitution and laws, driven out federal officers, organized an armed force, destroyed a supply train, and now stand in open rebellion. He offers a full pardon to those who submit to lawful authority, warns that continued resistance will be met with rigorous enforcement, and declares that troops will remain until the inhabitants demonstrate proper obedience.

Flexible working enables employees who care for someone to balance work and caring duties. All employees in England, Scotland and Wales have a statutory right to request flexible working after 26 weeks of employment, and only one request may be made in any 12‑month period. A request must be made in writing, stating that it is a statutory request, describing the desired change (such as altered hours, compressed weeks, home working, part‑time or job‑share), the proposed start date and how the change might affect the business. The employer must give the request serious consideration and decide within three months, but may refuse if a valid business reason exists. If the request is approved, the employer must update the contract; if refused, the employer must explain the reason. Employees who believe the process was unfair can appeal through the employer’s appeal procedure or take the matter to an employment tribunal within three months of the decision.

Veterans in Galesburg and Abingdon, Illinois have experienced missing prescription medications delivered from the Iowa City Veterans Affairs Health Care System. Robert Stevens and Gary Kilpatrick reported pills stolen, with Kilpatrick noting significant quantities taken repeatedly. Abingdon Police Chief Ken Jones confirmed two cases, and VA spokesman Bryan Clark stated multiple theft reports are under investigation.

NVIDIA’s Q1 FY2021 (three months ended April 26 2020) generated revenue of $3.08 billion, up 39% year‑over‑year and down 1% sequentially. Gross profit was $2.00 billion with a 65.1% gross margin (670 basis‑points higher than the year‑ago quarter). Operating expenses were $1.03 billion (research & development $735 million, sales, general & administrative $293 million). Income from operations rose 173% to $976 million, and net income increased 133% to $917 million ($1.47 diluted EPS). Cash and cash equivalents totaled $15.5 billion; together with marketable securities, liquidity was $16.35 billion. Operating cash flow provided $909 million, while investing activities used $1.06 billion (chiefly purchases of marketable securities and property) and financing activities provided $4.74 billion (mainly the $5.0 billion March 2020 debt issuance). The company paid $98 million in quarterly dividends ($0.16 per share) and is authorized to repurchase up to $7.24 billion of common stock through December 2022 (no repurchases in the quarter). Subsequent to quarter‑end, NVIDIA closed the acquisition of Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for approximately $7.0 billion cash on April 27 2020. Effective tax expense was $64 million (6.6% effective rate) versus a $5 million tax benefit a year earlier, mainly due to reduced stock‑based compensation tax benefits. By segment, Graphics revenue grew 25% to $1.906 billion and Compute & Networking grew 69% to $1.174 billion. Geographically, Taiwan led with $813 million, followed by China (including Hong Kong) $758 million, Other Asia Pacific $607 million, U.S. $497 million, Europe $254 million and other regions $151 million. By market platform, Gaming contributed $1.339 billion (up 27%), Professional Visualization $307 million (up 15%), Data Center $1.141 billion (up 80%), Automotive $155 million (down 7%) and OEM & Other $138 million (up 39%). No single customer accounted for 10% or more of total revenue in the quarter. The company maintains a $575 million revolving credit facility (unused) and had total debt of approximately $7.0 billion (September 2016 notes $2 billion, March 2020 notes $5 billion). Operating segments were reorganized from GPU/Tegra to Graphics and Compute & Networking. The COVID‑19 pandemic caused supply‑chain and logistics disruptions and temporarily affected demand for gaming, automotive and OEM products, while also driving increased demand for gaming and data‑center offerings. Legal proceedings related to securities class actions and derivative lawsuits are ongoing; no material accruals have been recorded.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture, spanning the TU102, TU104 and TU106 GPUs, introduces a new streaming multiprocessor with dedicated RT Cores for real‑time ray tracing, Tensor Cores supporting FP16/INT8/INT4 inference, and a unified L1/shared memory subsystem, alongside hardware USB‑Type‑C/VirtualLink support and second‑generation NVLink (up to 100 GB/s bidirectional). Turing features GDDR6 memory delivering ~50 % higher effective bandwidth than Pascal, an 8K‑capable display engine with DSC and HDR, an enhanced NVENC encoder, and new shading techniques such as Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading and Multi‑View Rendering, enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization, ray tracing and AI‑based image enhancement (e.g., DLSS). The architecture defines the RTX‑OPS metric that weights Tensor, FP32, RT and INT32 operations by their frame‑time utilization.

Ferrari, founded by Enzo Ferrari in 1947 and renowned for its prancing horse emblem and racing heritage, pursued a "controlled growth" strategy in 2024-2025, having doubled vehicle shipments over the prior decade while growing revenues from $3.2 billion to $7.2 billion. The company held a 14% share of the global luxury performance automotive market and 23% of the two-door sports car segment. Ferrari operated through 178 authorized dealers across 60 markets, sold vehicles exclusively through dealers (except limited editions), and relied heavily on repeat customers—81% of new car sales went to existing clients, with 48% of sales to multi-car owners. The company offered extensive personalization through programs including Tailor Made and One-Off, with waitlists typically 12-18 months. CEO Benedetto Vigna, a physicist formerly of STMicroelectronics, emphasized balancing tradition with innovation, stating that Ferrari must "look at the past" with one eye and "the future" with the other. Ferrari planned its first fully-electric vehicle for 2025, following hybrid models that grew from 2% of shipments in 2020 to 51% in 2024, targeting a 2026 portfolio of 55% hybrid, 40% internal combustion, and 5% fully electric. The company maintained technology neutrality, allowing customer preference to ultimately determine the mix. Ferrari's Formula 1 involvement, including the Netflix "Drive to Survive" effect, provided global visibility, while the Lifestyle division licensed branded merchandise and operated retail stores and museums.

First Lady Melania Trump ended a absence by tweeting she is at the White House with her family, feeling well. She last appeared May 10 at the welcome of three US detainees from North Korea and underwent a minor kidney procedure May 14. Her office dismissed speculation.

The European Commission issued final warnings to Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and Britain for repeated breaches of nitrogen‑dioxide limits caused mainly by diesel‑engine traffic; the countries have two months to respond or face EU Court of Justice proceedings.

The passage outlines five key principles for early childhood education and care (ECEC) for children aged 1–5: prioritize the early years for holistic development, create a nurturing environment, focus on quality in ECEC, engage families, and support continuous professional development for educators. The early years are characterized by rapid brain development, high plasticity, sensitivity to external stimuli, and are crucial for cognitive, linguistic, social, emotional, and motor growth. A safe, inclusive, stimulating environment supports exploration and confidence. High‑quality ECEC emphasizes warm teacher‑child interactions, evidence‑based curriculum, inclusive practices, and ongoing educator training. Engaging families, recognizing the home learning environment, and building partnerships enhances children’s learning, cultural responsiveness, and empowerment. The conclusion stresses that applying these principles benefits both individual children and society.

Tyrus Capital S.A.M. bought 182,400 Reynolds American shares for about $11.86 M in Q2, representing 0.9 % of its portfolio. Institutional investors increased stakes: Vanguard added 1.7 M shares (2.9 % rise, now 59.9 M, $3.90 B), BlackRock added 4.66 M shares (10.1 % rise, now 50.86 M, $3.31 B), State Street added 0.11 M shares (0.3 % rise, now 33.25 M, $2.16 B), and FMR LLC added 1.94 M shares (16.0 % rise, now 14.05 M, $0.91 B). American International Group raised its stake by 1.2 % in Q1, holding 9.26 M shares worth $0.58 B. About 46.34 % of Reynolds American is owned by institutional investors. Analysts give a consensus “Hold” rating with an average price target of $59.82; ratings from BidaskClub, Cowen, Jefferies, and Vetr vary. The stock closed at $65.40 on Friday, with a 12‑month range of $43.38‑$67.81, a 50‑day moving average of $65.25 and a 200‑day moving average of $64.00. Reynolds American operates three segments: RJR Tobacco, Santa Fe and American Snuff.

Vanguard offers ten exchange‑traded funds suited for long‑term, buy‑and‑hold investors. The firm leads the U.S. mutual‑fund and ETF market with over $7 trillion in assets under management and was founded in 1975 by John Bogle, the originator of passive index investing. Bogle advocated a lifetime holding of a market‑wide fund with a modest bond allocation and advised investors to avoid speculation and active management.

Each fund is designed to track a specific benchmark using full replication or sampling, and performance is back‑tested from each fund’s inception to the present with dividends reinvested. The ten funds are:

- VOO: tracks the S&P 500 Index, holding all stocks in capitalization‑weight.  
- VOOV: tracks the S&P 500 Value Index, replicating large‑cap U.S. value stocks.  
- VOOG: tracks the S&P 500 Growth Index, replicating large‑cap U.S. growth stocks.  
- VT: tracks the FTSE Global All Cap Index, covering large, mid, and small‑cap stocks worldwide, including developed and emerging markets.  
- VXUS: tracks the FTSE Global All Cap ex‑US Index, covering international stocks outside the United States.  
- VNQ: tracks the MSCI US Investable Market Real Estate 25/50 Index, investing in commercial REITs for high income and moderate capital growth.  
- BLV: tracks the Bloomberg U.S. Long Government/Credit Float Adjusted Index, providing high current income from long‑maturity U.S. Treasury, agency, and investment‑grade corporate bonds.  
- VGLT: tracks a market‑weighted long‑term Treasury index, sampling securities to match key risk factors.  
- VCLT: tracks a market‑weighted long‑term corporate bond index, sampling securities with at least 80% of assets in index bonds.  
- BNDX: tracks the Bloomberg Global Aggregate ex‑USD Float Adjusted RIC Capped Index (USD‑hedged), covering global investment‑grade fixed‑rate debt outside the U.S. dollar.

The FAQ notes that a buy‑and‑hold approach minimizes short‑term volatility, emphasizes patience, and that VOO, VOOV, and VOOG differ by focusing on the broad S&P 500, its value segment, and its growth segment, respectively. VNQ adds real‑estate exposure for diversification and income but carries sector‑specific volatility.

Pakistan hoisted a 120‑by‑80‑foot flag at 400 ft, the highest in South Asia and eighth worldwide, at the Attari‑Wagah border on its 70th Independence Day. Army chief Gen Qamar Javed Bajwa raised the flag after midnight and outlined the country’s resolve to combat terrorism and pay tribute to those killed during migration.

Ted Hannah, a 1959 Summerland high school graduate, writes to the class of 2018 sharing his wartime childhood in Summerland. He describes parents who survived the Great Depression and WWII, families displaced or arriving as refugees, and his carefree early life: hunting, gardening, wearing hand‑me‑downs, biking, skating, swimming, and no television or internet. Schooling began in 1947; students used inkwells, learned from strict but caring teachers, and participated in sports, clubs, and Student Council. After graduation some attended UBC or UVic, others entered business, orchard work, or trades. He and his classmates married, stayed connected through cards, marked 25th, 50th, and upcoming 60th anniversaries, and faced health issues. He advises the 2018 grads to nurture relationships, volunteer, and support others regardless of background.

The lecture discusses methods for finding minimal trellis representations of linear block codes. Key points include the state space theorem, which defines state space dimension via a formula involving subcodes, and an algorithm for reducing a generator matrix to trellis-oriented form by minimizing generator spans until all starting and ending times are distinct. From this reduced matrix, state and branch space dimensions are determined by counting active generators at each time. The minimal trellis is constructed by realizing each generator as a one-dimensional memory element active during its span, summing their outputs. Branch complexity is noted as more fundamental than state complexity for Viterbi algorithm complexity. Sectionalization can simplify trellis appearance without reducing branch complexity. Average dimension bounds relate coding gain to trellis complexity, suggesting exponential growth in decoding complexity for codes with linearly increasing minimum distance. The lecture concludes by connecting these concepts to projections, Reed-Muller codes, and the trade-offs between coding gain and decoding complexity, particularly for capacity-approaching codes like turbo codes.

On May 7 2019 Tesla Inc. closed an underwritten public offering of 3,549,381 shares of common stock and $1.84 billion of 2.00% convertible senior notes due May 15 2024, after the underwriters exercised their option in full on May 3. The notes bear interest at 2.00% per year payable semi‑annually, have an initial conversion rate of 3.2276 shares per $1,000 principal (≈$309.83 per share) and are convertible only under specified conditions before Feb 15 2024, thereafter at any time until maturity. Settlement is at Tesla’s election in cash, shares or a combination. The notes rank senior to subordinated debt, equally with other unsecured debt, and junior to secured debt and subsidiary liabilities. On May 7 Tesla entered a Fifth Supplemental Indenture governing the notes. Concurrent with the option exercise, Tesla entered additional note hedge transactions with four counterparties, paying ≈$62.1 million (total ≈$475.8 million) to mitigate dilution and cash‑payment risk. Tesla also issued additional warrants allowing purchase of up to ≈1.5 million shares at $607.50 per share; the warrants may be dilutive unless cash‑settled, and generated ≈$22.8 million (total ≈$174.4 million). The filing includes the indenture, supplemental indenture, form of note, legal opinion and hedge and warrant confirmations, and is signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP features protect guest VM register state from the hypervisor through encryption during world switches. This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), a 4KB decrypted memory area for guest-hypervisor communication via VMGEXIT instructions. The specification defines required Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events, guest state exposure in the GHCB, and specific handling requirements for operations like SMP booting, NMI handling, and page state changes. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement and support for SEV-SNP features including Restricted Injection, AP Creation, Secure AVIC, and SEV-TIO. The document details protocol negotiation, GHCB registration, page state change operations, guest request mechanisms, AP boot procedures, interrupt delivery through doorbell pages, and termination handling.

The article previews Week 15 of the NFL season, presenting odds and predicted scores for each game. In the AFC, the Colts beat the Broncos 20‑17, the Chargers edge the Chiefs 21‑20, the Jaguars rout the Texans 38‑7, the Steelers defeat the Patriots 24‑23 and the Bills beat the Dolphins 24‑17 (if Tyrod Taylor plays). In the NFC, the Lions top the Bears 24‑13, the Vikings beat the Bengals 34‑10, the Seahawks outlast the Rams 24‑23, the Raiders beat the Cowboys 24‑23, the Falcons beat the Buccaneers 27‑17, the Panthers beat the Packers 31‑27 (if Aaron Rodgers starts), the Saints beat the Jets 31‑7 (if Bryce Petty starts) and the Eagles beat the Giants 24‑10 (if Nick Foles starts). The Cardinals beat the Redskins 24‑17 and the Ravens beat the Browns 20‑10. The 49ers are predicted to beat the Titans. The preview highlights significant injuries (Carson Wentz possible torn ACL, Aaron Rodgers uncertain, Tyrod Taylor uncertain) and notes must‑win situations for the Lions and playoff‑chasing Bills.

Social media users debated reactions to Mike Pence during St. Patrick's Day, including a book by John Oliver about the Pence family's pet rabbit. Conservative commentator Chad Felix Greene criticized LGBT activists for wasting time protesting Pence, arguing he remains polite and unaffected by their efforts. Others defended the protests, citing Pence's connections to James Dobson and concerns about religious freedom. The exchanges included sarcastic comments, emojis, and accusations of misinformation on both sides.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10‑Q for the quarter ended May 1 2016 reports Q1 FY2017 revenue of $1.305 billion, up 13% year‑over‑year; gross profit $751 million (gross margin 57.5%); operating income $245 million; net income $196 million; diluted EPS $0.33. By segment, GPU revenue was $1.079 billion with operating income $348 million; Tegra Processor revenue $160 million with an operating loss of $38 million; All Other (primarily patent licensing) revenue $66 million. Cash and marketable securities totaled $4.754 billion. The company returned $562 million to shareholders via a $500 million accelerated share repurchase and $62 million in quarterly dividends. NVIDIA’s $1.5 billion 1% Convertible Senior Notes due 2018 remain outstanding; conversion notices for $0.2 million principal have been received. Litigation with Samsung and Qualcomm was resolved. The lecture discusses reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains, focusing on two case studies: ReCellular and Whirlpool. ReCellular collects and repurposes secondhand cellphones, with students debating its viability given technological evolution and changing consumer behavior. The Whirlpool case addresses extended producer responsibility regulations in Canada regarding appliance disposal, with three options: joining an Industry-Funded Organization (IFO), implementing a closed-loop system, or opposing regulation. Cost analysis shows IFO costs approximately $47-80 per unit compared to Whirlpool's forward supply chain cost of $70 per unit. Whirlpool ultimately chose a closed-loop approach despite higher initial costs, gaining consumer connection but facing operational challenges including warehouse space and tracking issues.
XPC=0/1: 0.36 W/no Class vs 0.54 W/Supported Class; XPC change requires reinit. UHS‑I host sets S18R=1, card replies S18A=1, S18A=0 after switch. UHS‑II always S18A=0.

Coach says Matt has been excellent throughout the playoffs, highlighting his resilience, timely saves and ability to stay focused. The staff wants players to trust their instincts, make calculated decisions and play the right way, while Geno is praised for buying into the team concept and being an elite threat when balanced. The team faces few penalties in the playoffs, limiting power‑play chances, and struggled to generate zone time and clean entries on their only man‑advantage. Individual defending in soccer involves a defender controlling an opposing ball carrier by getting goal-side and assuming a proper stance. Before engaging, defenders must assess teammates' positions; if covered, they use aggressive defending (cutting off the ball, tackling, interposing, or preventing turns). If not, they use attack stalling to delay the dribbler while teammates recover. Key techniques include staying goal-side, maintaining a balanced stance, denying passes, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler's vision, jockeying, shepherding, and stealing the ball. Defenders can only backpedal so far, usually near the penalty area; beyond that, they must stand ground or tackle. Oral communication from teammates is critical and uses terms like "Contain," "Delay," "Jockey," "Stand him up," "Challenge," "Tackle," and "Take him" to coordinate actions. Coaches must teach defenders approaches, stances, techniques, and communication meanings through practice involving half-speed movements with and without the ball, gradually increasing speed.
Michigan State Police placed 13 semi trucks under the bridge on I‑696, negotiated with a suicidal man, and he walked off and taken to Beaumont Hospital.

The passage discloses methods and systems for controlling uplink data transmission when a wireless device is in an enhanced‑coverage state, aiming to reduce power consumption caused by repeated transmissions. Two main approaches are described: Solution 1 – an application queries the modem for radio‑coverage information (e.g., coverage‑enhancement level, mode, coverage class, signal strength/repetitions) and decides to refrain from sending uplink data based on predefined conditions; Solution 2 – the application sends the modem an instruction that includes conditions and parameters for the modem to conditionally transmit or withhold data. Additional conditions for refraining include data type (e.g., non‑emergency), QoS indicators, timers, counters, device speed (from sensors or accelerometer), battery level (thresholds or charging status), and whether the device is plugged into a power supply. Configuration of transmission restrictions may be pre‑defined in the device, specified in industry standards (e.g., 3GPP), or sent by the network via downlink messages such as Attach Accept, Activate Default EPS Bearer Context Request, or RRC information elements. New AT commands (+CREG, +CIOTQCEL, +CSODCP, +CEUDR) are introduced to exchange coverage‑related status and transmission‑restriction instructions between the application and modem. The disclosure also describes example network node and UE hardware components.

This study analyzed NHANES data from 2007-2010 (4,136 subjects, 305 with RA) to investigate associations between rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and three chronic inflammatory conditions: depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG). RA prevalence was found to increase with C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and subjects with depression, obesity, or HTG all showed elevated CRP. Depression coexisting with obesity or HTG significantly increased RA prevalence in a synergistic manner, with the effect maximum at medium CRP levels (1-3 mg/L). For example, at medium CRP, RA prevalence was 27.2% in subjects with both depression and obesity, compared to 19.5% and 5.5% for each condition alone. HTG showed a more complex relationship: it increased RA prevalence with depression at medium CRP (34.9% vs 16.3% and 5.6% separately) but decreased it at high CRP levels. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and researchers recommend longitudinal studies and broader inflammatory marker panels to better understand these interactions and potentially improve RA prediction models.

The passage describes a shift in Information Systems (IS) research from positivist, technology‑centric views toward human‑focused perspectives, quoting Ray Paul’s definition of IS as the emergent outcome of IT usage, formal and informal processes, and user adaptation. Two parallel developments are identified: (1) the application of complexity science—originating in environmental biology and accelerated by computing—to IS, which provides a theoretical basis for studying mixed‑method and human‑centric usage; and (2) the rise of User Experience (UX) as a practice that supersedes traditional usability by addressing subjective, durational, experiential concerns. Complexity theory is presented as distinguishing “complex” from “complicated” systems, emphasizing open, far‑from‑equilibrium systems, self‑organisation, irreversibility, and the arrow of time. Key theorists (Prigogine, Kauffman, Goodwin, Cilliers) argue that such systems exhibit unpredictable bifurcation points, emergent properties, and persist as dissipative structures, and that analytical methods suitable for complicated systems are inadequate for complex ones. The UX approach, informed by mixed methods, is driven by business needs and technological trends (e.g., Web 2.0/3.0, HTML5, AI tools) and highlights the importance of human behavior, impulse, and emotional intelligence, noting the irreversibility of user experiences. Recent IS literature treats IS as a complex adaptive system (Benbya & McKelvey), but Kallinikos critiques retained representational views of user requirements, arguing that human parts cannot be abstracted from technology. A Knowledge Transfer Partnership between the University of Salford and UX firm Sigma Ltd will examine how irreversibility and durational complexity affect design, usability, and success in live projects. The conclusion calls for IS research to adopt complex, durational understandings and integrate them into future design practices.

The paper proposes a framework for ontology alignment using Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs). While LLMs have become popular for this task, KGEs remain underexplored despite their ability to represent semantic and structural information numerically. The approach combines source and target ontology triples into a unified "triple factory" to formulate alignment as a link prediction problem, enabling KGE models to learn joint representations across both ontologies. The modular three-stage pipeline consists of a Parser (extracting RDF-style metadata), an Encoder (creating unified triplet representations), and an Aligner (using PyKEEN for representation learning via 17 different KGE models, followed by cosine similarity-based inference). The system is integrated into the OntoAligner Python library. Related work shows various KGE models (TransE, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, ConvE, among others) have been applied to ontology alignment, often in combination with structural or contextual embeddings.

The DAWN‑PLASMA trial was a randomized, open‑label, multicenter phase 2 study comparing best supportive care plus convalescent plasma with best supportive care (SOC) alone in hospitalized adults with COVID‑19. The primary objective was to evaluate clinical efficacy and safety of adding convalescent plasma; the primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on Day 15. Secondary endpoints included daily clinical status on Days 15 and 30, time to sustained clinical improvement, and incidence of ventilation or death at 30 and 90 days, among others.

Eligible participants were ≥18 years, had laboratory‑confirmed SARS‑CoV‑2 infection or typical CT findings with respiratory symptoms, and met oxygenation or radiographic criteria, but could not be on invasive or non‑invasive ventilation at enrollment. Exclusion criteria included prior anti‑CD20 therapy, severe allergic reaction to fresh frozen plasma, and restrictions against mechanical ventilation.

Participants randomized 2:1 to plasma plus SOC or SOC alone received 800–1000 mL of convalescent plasma in four doses (≈200–250 mL per unit) within 12 hours of randomization and a second infusion 24–36 hours later; plasma had neutralizing‑antibody titers ≥1:160 (most units ≥1:320). SOC reflected current (inter)national guidelines and was unrestricted for concomitant therapy.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed, 489 were randomized (326 plasma, 163 control), and 10 were not randomized. The Day 15 visit was performed in 434 patients; the Day 30 visit in 423. Protocol deviations led to exclusion of 26 plasma patients who received fewer than four units and three control patients who received plasma before Day 30.

Two analysis sets were used: a Full Analysis Set (FAS) and a Per‑Protocol Set (PPS). The primary analysis showed no difference in the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 (plasma 83.7 % vs control 84.1 %; odds ratio 0.99, p = 0.976). Pre‑specified subgroup analysis revealed a significant interaction with age. Safety and other secondary outcomes were comparable between groups. The trial was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP and received Independent Ethics Committee approval.

The Match-up zone defense combines person-to-person and zone principles using a series of defensive rules. It prevents offensive alignments from splitting defenders, makes overloads easier to defend, and tends to confuse opponents. Success depends on smart, knowledgeable players and communication. The system assigns defenders X1-X5 to guard specific offensive positions based on the opponent's alignment, including 2-3, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, and 1-4 formations. Defenders can switch or interchange assignments when guarding cutters and screens. The match-up zone can be extended into full or half court with trapping applied when the ball enters primary trap zones.

Distributed systems design involves patterns for organizing containers on single nodes and across multiple nodes. Single-node patterns include the sidecar pattern, where an auxiliary container extends an application's functionality without modifying the original application; the ambassador pattern, where a container brokers interactions between an application and external services; and the adapter pattern, where a container modifies an application's interface to conform to standardized conventions.

Multi-node patterns encompass replicated load-balanced services, where identical server replicas distribute traffic through a load balancer, and sharded services, where different replicas serve distinct data subsets. Replicated services typically support stateless applications, while sharded services handle stateful workloads where data size exceeds single-machine capacity.

Container patterns provide benefits including modularity, reuse, and separation of concerns. Effective pattern implementation requires parameterizing containers through environment variables, defining stable APIs, and documenting container functionality. These patterns enable teams to build reliable, scalable distributed systems by combining small, focused containers rather than monolithic applications.

The disclosure relates to systems and methods for providing a user interface that prompts a user to confirm whether to review or proceed with an action associated with an untrusted email. A driver on a device monitors creation and termination of application processes. When an application of interest is launched, the driver notifies a user console which determines whether to monitor the process. If monitoring is required, an injector process injects a monitor library into the application. The monitor library detects when a user attempts to access a domain that is not on a trusted list, pauses the request, and notifies the user console. The user console resolves the URL and queries a server to determine if the domain is trusted. The server returns the disposition and, if the client settings hash differs from the server hash, updated notification settings. The user console then displays a configurable notification using locally stored settings, allowing the user to confirm or revert the action. The user's response is recorded on the server and passed to the monitor library which either resumes or discards the request. The system supports desktop applications and browser‑based email clients via injected code or browser extensions, and includes a core library that manages shared memory communication between the monitor library and the user console. Administrators can customize notification content, colors, button labels, and visibility through a server console; changes are propagated to clients via a hash comparison so that only altered settings are transmitted. The invention provides users a second chance to reconsider actions related to phishing emails, enables real‑time training, and allows organizations to measure and improve security awareness.

The disclosure describes a fluid flow measuring and control device for installation in a plumbing line. The device has a main flow channel with an inlet and outlet, a parallel bypass channel containing a flowmeter, a solenoid valve for stopping flow, upstream and downstream pressure sensors, and a transceiver that sends flow data to a computer. The flowmeter comprises a chamber, a rotating wheel with blades, and a pair of movement sensors that detect wheel rotation direction, enabling net flow measurement including backflow. The computer stores pre‑recorded fluid‑usage signatures for individual appliances, compares incoming data to these signatures to identify which appliance is in use, and can determine abnormal usage by comparing current data to prior data. When abnormal usage or a leak is detected, the computer can close the solenoid valve and send a notification to a user’s mobile device via a remote server. Leak detection is performed by temporarily closing the valve, comparing the pressures upstream and downstream, and maintaining the valve closed if a low‑to‑medium pressure drop indicates a leak, otherwise reopening it. A baseline leakage can be stored so that only additional leaks trigger alerts. The system also supports pattern‑recognition and machine‑learning algorithms to recognize water‑usage signatures, predict consumption, detect appliance deterioration, and schedule maintenance. The device can be enclosed in a casing with a detachable transceiver that contains memory and a processor for local data handling. Installation is at a single point common to all fluid‑consuming appliances, allowing identification and control of each appliance without individual meters.

Nationwide district analysis and Mississippi 2025 test data show a strong correlation (0.87) between school-level reading and math proficiency. Districts that excel in one subject typically excel in the other; 140 districts performed well across subjects, while only 14 were strong in one subject and weak in the other, mostly in math. Growth data reveal similar patterns: schools with high reading growth also have high math growth, and none of the top 50 reading gain schools fell below state average math growth. Florida data show comparable results. The findings indicate that schools strong in one academic area tend to be strong across subjects, making specialization in a single subject rare.

Crystal morphology strongly affects the sensitivity and performance of energetic materials, influencing safety and detonation properties. Existing morphology prediction methods (BFDH, surface‑energy, attachment‑energy models) imperfectly capture experimental shapes, especially for low‑symmetry crystals, and neglect growth kinetics. This work introduces a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation technique that predicts crystal morphology using only intermolecular interaction parameters. The system is encoded as a colored, undirected graph where nodes represent lattice sites with occupation variables and edges carry static interaction weights. Surface sites are identified via coordination numbers derived from an adjacency matrix. Adsorption rates are proportional to solute diffusivity and solubility, while evaporation rates follow harmonic transition‑state theory. The evaporation prefactor is dynamically adjusted to reach a target crystal size. The method is implemented in an open‑source Python package, and simulations of PETN growth show excellent agreement with attachment‑energy predictions and experimental observations.

Corner‑kick defense requires a ready plan that every player understands and executes instantly when a corner is awarded. All players have a specific job – goalkeeper commands the area, post players guard near balls, three defenders line the six‑yard line, one blocks the kick, and a striker stays high for a fast‑break counter‑attack. Defenders must react quickly, win the first ball, and clear the ball high, far, and wide. Teams generally use one of three systems: zone defense (players cover defined areas), man‑to‑man defense (each defender marks a specific opponent), or a mixed combination (post players and six‑yard line in zone, remaining defenders in man‑to‑man). Zone is easiest to teach but can be overwhelmed; man‑to‑man is simple yet forces defenders back toward goal; mixed approaches have shown the lowest goal‑concession rates. Coaches should drill the chosen system repeatedly, adjust tactics per opponent, ensure the goalkeeper stays in charge, and practice quick transitions to attack so the response becomes intuitive.

Mid Screen Offense is a widely used NBA/WNBA set that creates dribble penetration via an on‑ball screen by a high‑post player. The point guard can drive, pull up, pass to the post, or kick out to shooters; the offense includes reads and counters for defensive actions such as chasing, sagging, switching, trapping, and showing. It flows into ball‑reversal continuities (motion, single/double, flex, triangle, side‑screen) and has variations like post‑pop, Horns, 1‑4 low, high‑post isolation, and Two‑Game. Effective execution depends on coordinated timing, non‑verbal communication, drills, individual skill work, and strategic scouting of opponents.

NVIDIA’s combined L1 cache and shared memory, introduced in V100, boosts performance and simplifies tuning; A100 offers 192 KB/SM versus V100’s 128 KB/SM, providing low‑latency, high‑bandwidth access for streaming and reused data.

Design requirements for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices include a 500 kHz switching frequency with RT resistor of 205 kΩ, 5V output with RTOP of 10 kΩ and RBOT of 1.4 kΩ, dead time of 25 ns with 20.5 kΩ resistors, leading edge blank time of ~50 ns with 49.9 kΩ RLEB, soft-start capacitor of 33 nF providing ~7.5 ms, transformer with 2.5 turns ratio and 40 μH primary inductance, main switching FETs rated 170 V, synchronous rectifier FETs rated 80 V with Schottky diode in parallel, RCD clamp circuit, output inductor of 0.47 μH with 40% ripple, output capacitance of 1.3 mF minimum (2.3 mF total for radiation mitigation), additional LC output filter, cycle-by-cycle current limiting at 35 A with 7.5 Ω sense resistor, hiccup capacitor of 3.3 nF, Type 2A compensation with RCOMP of 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP of 15 nF, CHF of 47 pF, and slope compensation resistor of 102 kΩ. Power supply operates from 4-14 V with 0.1 µF minimum bypass. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loop areas, and routing high di/dt and dv/dt traces away from sensitive signals.

Companies are developing self‑driving cars using five SAE levels. Levels 1 and 2, already in production, provide basic cruise control and limited steering, requiring constant driver attention. Level 3, expected on BMW’s iNext in 2021, allows hands‑off driving but demands rapid takeover. Many firms skip to Level 4, which extends takeover time to minutes and lets the vehicle stop safely if the driver fails. BMW is working on Level 4, anticipating regulations and maps by the mid‑2020s. Waymo already has Level 4 cars, offering a limited commercial taxi service in Phoenix later this year with an engineer on board. Level 5, fully driverless, is projected for the end of the next decade.

The passage describes a system and method for detecting abnormal cardiac activity (e.g., atrial fibrillation) using a deep‑learning architecture. Cardiac data (ECG, PPG, etc.) and motion data (accelerometer) are collected from wearable sensors and divided into time windows. For each window the system computes signal‑quality indices (SQI) for cardiac and motion data, extracts cardiovascular features, and applies a tensor transform (e.g., wavelet) to generate a tensor representation. A trained deep‑learning model—comprising a convolutional neural network, a bidirectional recurrent neural network (RNN), and an attention network—classifies each window into classes such as normal, abnormal, or noise, using the SQI values, motion SQI, and optional subject contextual information (medical history, demographics). The attention network produces a score for each window, and the window with the highest score indicates the location of abnormal activity. A report is generated summarizing the classification, type of abnormal activity, and burden (percentage of time in abnormal activity) for each period. The system may be implemented on a wearable device (e.g., smartwatch) and includes processors, memory, and communication interfaces.

The study examined associations between postpartum blood pressure measurements and incident hypertension in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Using retrospective cohort data from the Carolinas Collaborative (2014-2017), the analysis included 2,514 women. Key findings: 13% developed incident hypertension within 12 months; higher systolic BP (140 vs 120 mmHg) was associated with increased risk (HR 1.70); severe preeclampsia/eclampsia conferred higher risk than gestational hypertension (HR 1.49); older maternal age increased risk (HR 1.46); and 40% of eligible women lacked documented BP checks at 15-90 days postpartum. Most women (55%) had BP readings in Stage 1 or 2 hypertension range. Limitations include retrospective design and demographic differences between included and excluded participants.

iOS 11 drains iPhone battery significantly faster than iOS 10, according to a Wandera study of 50,000 devices. A fully charged phone lasts about 240 minutes on iOS 10 versus 96 minutes on iOS 11. Older iPhone models experience greater drain. Apple released two updates; iOS 11.0.1 improved battery life to 159 minutes (65% better than iOS 11). Wandera warns against downgrading due to security risks. Suggested battery‑saving steps include disabling background app refresh, limiting location‑services access, and enabling low‑power mode.

Enron shares fell to multi-year lows after Moody's downgraded the company's debt to two notches above junk status. Enron is in talks with banks for additional credit lines after drawing $3 billion last week. European energy firms are restricting trades with Enron due to credit concerns. The SEC is investigating related-party transactions involving partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, and multiple shareholder lawsuits have been filed against Enron and its executives.

AMD Geode CS5535/CS5536 companion device lists ten hardware issues (106‑108, 109, 111‑116). Issue 106: reading Port 60h clears AuxOutputFull bit, possibly breaking PS/2 emulation; use interrupts. Issue 107: UDMA tACK bits have no timing effect; no impact. Issue 108: ATAC hangs if PRD addresses are not DWORD‑aligned; enforce DWORD alignment. Issue 109: LPC controller may abort I/O when only two clocks follow turn‑around; a PLD workaround exists. Issue 111: SMB controller NEGACK bit may be cleared incorrectly; write twice to SMB_STS. Issue 112: GLPCI retry counter counts all PCI retries; can be disabled. Issue 113: after suspend, atomic writes to GPIO High Bank registers clear non‑selected bits; use read‑modify‑write. Issue 114: SMBus data hold time shorter than 300 ns spec. Issue 115: LOWBAT_FLAG not set after abnormal standby. Issue 116: if PM_SCXD/Y or PM_IN_SLPCTL delay counters exceed PM_SED, Sleep_X/Y stay asserted and PCI/IDE inputs stay disabled; set counters lower than PM_SED.

Connaught Public School in Hintonburg attempted to break the Guinness World Record for most students playing tunnel ball simultaneously, with over 250 students participating against the existing record of 120 set by an Australian school. The school believes they broke the record, which awaits verification. A ValueInsured survey found 71% of Washington homeowners are concerned about a housing bubble, though the survey sampled only 1,079 people nationwide (about 21 per state). King County median home prices rose 18.6% year‑over‑year to $658,000 (July 2016‑July 2017) and inventory fell more than 13% while pending and closed sales rose, according to the Northwest Multiple Listing Service. The article also lists median sale prices and required annual household incomes for 25 U.S. cities, ranging from Detroit ($25,000 median, $7,359 needed) to San Francisco ($1.19 million median, $226,577 needed).

Jeff Bezos calls it a “debilitating phrase” and prefers “work‑life harmony,” arguing that satisfaction at home boosts work performance and vice‑versa. LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman warns that founders who speak of balance are not committed to winning and should invest every hour in venture. Nespresso UK CEO Anna Lundstrom also targets harmony, noting that splitting work and life is unrealistic. Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman says the notion that a 38‑hour week can yield greatness is mind‑boggling, asserting that building products requires all waking hours. Zoom CEO Eric Yuan describes work as life and life as work, yet prioritizes family when conflicts arise. American consumer confidence rose to 128.7 in April, up from March's 127.0 and near February's 18-year high. Analysts attributed the increase to a strong labor market, December tax cuts, reduced stock volatility and diminished trade war concerns.
