A player praised a teammate for his steady play and reliability. He said his family enjoys the city, the team has a family atmosphere, and fans have become more supportive since Christmas, with neighbors seeking season tickets. He noted hockey’s growth in southern markets, referencing his coaching of kids in Tampa after the Lightning’s win. He expressed a desire to finish his career in Carolina, describing it as a great place for families, and said his team has no big names but up‑and‑coming stars.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth‑generation farmer at Boglily Farm outside Kirkaldy, runs The Buffalo Farm. He uses social media to market the farm and promote buffalo meat’s health benefits, targeting a “gym‑and‑slim” niche. The farm won the 2016 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Award in the Meat category for its buffalo fillet steak, gaining credibility with larger clients. The 2018 awards are now open for entries.

A white van struck multiple pedestrians on Yonge Street near Finch Avenue in Toronto on April 23, 2018. Witnesses described the driver zigzagging on the sidewalk and hitting people deliberately, with victims thrown into the air and body parts visible. Police took the driver into custody. Sunnybrook Hospital received 10 patients with two pronounced dead, five in critical condition and three serious. North York General received four patients. Police created a hotline for witnesses and a web portal for photos and videos. The investigation will take days and a busy stretch of Yonge Street remains closed. Ralph Goodale said there is no indication of a national security connection despite G7 cabinet ministers being in Toronto. The TTC temporarily suspended subway service between Finch and Sheppard stations.

Edmonton city officials claim its calcium chloride road salting experiment saved $4.2 million in operating costs and reduced sand use by 68 percent. However, chemical engineer Arthur Potts warned council it's too early to call it a success, stating vehicle damage costs could be 10 times the savings. Potts, a former corrosion engineer, said the chemical stays liquid longer, causing rust damage to vehicles and concrete. City officials claimed the salt is less corrosive but admitted they did not test it in Edmonton, and corrosion depends on local conditions. Officials plan to request new equipment funding and continue monitoring environmental and collision data.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned over 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged more than 28,000 as potentially describing harmful side effects. Researchers verified that 86% of 250 flagged posts represented problematic experiences. Waldo outperformed ChatGPT on this task but did not surpass human reviewers. The tool demonstrates that social media can provide valuable public health information that agencies like the CDC currently do not monitor. Developers envision using such tools ethically to flag rare side effects, protect consumer safety, and connect people to health resources.

The United States withdrew from United Nations negotiations on a global migration compact, saying the process could undermine its sovereignty and conflict with U.S. law and policy. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson announced the decision on Dec 3, noting the U.S. would not support a framework that could limit its control over immigration enforcement and border security.

The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) expressed disappointment and urged the administration to reconsider, saying participation would allow the U.S. to help build international cooperation that respects migrants’ rights and protections. Archbishop Timothy Broglio and Bishop Joe Vásquez, chairing USCCB committees, stressed that Catholic teaching respects a nation’s right to regulate migration but also obligates protection of vulnerable migrants such as refugees, victims of trafficking, and families seeking safety.

Pope Francis sent a video message to the three‑day UN talks in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico (Dec 5‑7), calling on participants to “welcome, protect, promote and integrate” migrants and refugees. The talks are a step toward adopting a non‑binding Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration in 2018, based on the 2016 New York Declaration for Refugees and Migrants. Bill Canny of USCCB said the compact focuses on migrant children’s education, support for host countries, preventing exploitation and humanitarian aid, and that the U.S. decision may strengthen other nations’ resolve.

The Center for Immigration Studies welcomed the withdrawal, arguing the draft language was too broad and would infringe on U.S. laws regarding unauthorized employment and border detention. UN officials said the framework leaves implementation to member states, and UN General Assembly President Miroslav Lajčák called the UN the only forum for such a response.

U.S. bishops’ 2014 “Mission for Migrants” document affirms a nation’s right to control its borders for the common good, but not as an absolute right; wealthy nations have a higher obligation to the universal common good and should provide legal pathways for safe, orderly migration. Boston College Law School dean Vincent Rougeau said global migration requires international cooperation and that the U.S. has historically been generous but should do more.

A four‑member team from King Edward VI Grammar School, Louth, finished second in the national schools University Challenge, beating St Ivo and Nottingham High School before losing the final 280–315 at the University of Lincoln. Headmaster James Lascelles praised their confidence and quiz performance.

Indian Railways has adopted a ‘if no bill, food is free’ policy requiring display of the message and billing for every transaction; it must be implemented by March 31 on all trains serving food on payment. IRCTC is promoting the policy on its booking site and deploying inspectors. Between April‑October over 7,000 overcharging complaints were recorded. Minister Goyal has ordered penalties, including licence cancellations, and the CAG recommended a system to prevent overcharging; auditors noted food tariffs unchanged for over five years and that some food was prepared with articles unsuitable for human consumption.

During the recent U.S. government shutdown, air traffic controllers were required to work without pay, causing many to call in sick and resulting in staffing cuts of up to 50% at some airports, leading to flight delays and heightened safety concerns. The shutdown has worsened a pre‑existing shortage: at the start of 2025 only 285 of 313 U.S. air traffic control facilities met FAA staffing targets, and at 73 locations at least a quarter of the workforce was missing, especially in the New York and Long Island regions. Aviation experts attribute the shortage to costly, time‑consuming training—taking up to several years with a wash‑out rate of about a third—and a mandatory retirement age of 56, which forces the FAA to hire only applicants under 31. Despite these obstacles, controllers earn an average of $144,580–$145,000 per year, and the profession is projected to grow 3% through 2033 with roughly 2,200 new openings annually. Candidates must be U.S. citizens under 31, pass medical and security checks, and complete a rigorous multi‑year training program; less than 10% of applicants are accepted. The combination of shutdown‑driven absenteeism and long‑standing hiring challenges has intensified operational pressures across the national airspace system.

Hascall Steel Company is a U.S. steel service center with over 45 years of experience, offering a diverse inventory including cold reduced, blanked, slit and flat‑rolled steel coils, plus hot rolled black, cold rolled aluminized and coated steel. It partners with domestic and foreign producers, delivers cost‑effective solutions, conducts quality testing via an in‑house lab, and employs technicians to achieve tolerances, reducing lead times and supply‑chain costs.

Mixed‑precision Tensor Cores in the NVIDIA A100 GPU (Ampere architecture) accelerate HPC and AI workloads by supporting TF32, FP16, BF16 and FP64 formats. The Tensor‑Core‑Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver (TCAIRS) in cuSOLVER demonstrates up to 4× speedup with TF32 versus a full FP64 solver on matrices around 40 K elements, with a geomean speedup of 2.0× for TF32, 1.9× for FP16 and 1.8× for BF16. A100’s third‑generation Tensor Cores deliver 16× the mixed‑precision compute performance of standard FP32 FMA operations.

Fine‑grained structured sparsity uses a 2‑out‑of‑4 non‑zero pattern, compressing trained weights 2× and doubling Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero‑value computations. The A100 architecture adds a combined L1 data cache and shared memory of 192 KB per SM (up from 128 KB on V100) and simultaneously executes FP32 and INT32 instructions at full throughput.

Memory subsystem details: 40 GB HBM2 DRAM at 1555 GB/s bandwidth (1.7× V100), 40 MB L2 cache (6.7× larger than V100) providing 2.3× L2 read bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection on HBM2, L2, L1 and register files, and Compute Data Compression offering up to 4× improvements in DRAM read/write and L2 bandwidth.

Interconnect and I/O: third‑generation NVLink provides 12 links with 600 GB/s total bidirectional bandwidth (double V100), PCIe Gen 4 delivers 31.5 GB/s per direction and supports SR‑IOV for GPU virtualization. A100 also includes error detection, isolation and containment features for large clusters and Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) environments.

MIG can partition each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, L2 cache slices and memory controllers, ensuring QoS and fault isolation for multi‑tenant use cases. Each GPU Instance can contain multiple Compute Instances that support Volta‑style MPS for concurrent CPU processes.

CUDA 11 introduces asynchronous copy (direct global‑to‑shared memory transfer bypassing L1 and registers), asynchronous barriers for fine‑grained thread synchronization, L2 cache residency controls that allow persistent caching of recurrent weights, CUDA Graphs for define‑once/run‑repeatedly workflows, and expanded Cooperative Groups collectives with hardware‑accelerated warp reductions.

Additional hardware accelerators: NVJPG 5‑core JPEG decoder, Optical Flow Accelerator for dense optical‑flow and stereo‑disparity estimation, and five NVDEC video decoders (5× V100). Atomic operation throughput improves 11× for FP16 and 2.7× for FP32 over V100.

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with 4.8 TB/s NVSwitch bandwidth, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U form factor, scaling to thousands of nodes via Magnum IO SDK and Mellanox InfiniBand/ Ethernet fabric. The software stack provides GPU‑optimized containers for deep learning, inference, data analytics and HPC via NGC Private Registry, with CUDA 11 supporting all new A100 features.

Tesla announced Feb 28, 2019, that the $35,000 Model 3 (220‑mile range) and $37,000 Model 3 Standard Range Plus (240‑mile range) are available. Tesla will shift all sales online, cut vehicle prices ~6 % on average, close most stores while keeping some as galleries, and improve service with same‑day/hour capability and a 7‑day/1,000‑mile return policy. Firmware upgrades will increase the Long Range RWD Model 3’s range to 325 mi, raise the Model 3 Performance’s top speed to 162 mph, and add ~5 % peak power to all Model 3 vehicles. Tesla does not expect Q1 2019 profitability but projects profitability in Q2 2019.

Researchers built nano‑scale resealable packets that open when exposed to a wavelength of light. The packets have a water‑soluble outer polymer layer and a glassy inner layer linked by light‑responsive molecules; illumination softens the glass, releasing contents, and the packet reseals when light is off. Biocompatible polymers—polyethylene oxide outer layer and polylactic acid inner layer—enable uses including drug delivery and release of chemicals in soil. The study appears in Nature Chemistry and was funded by the US Army Research Office.

Appellate court reversed judgment, ordered a new trial after finding the trial court improperly restricted plaintiff’s proof for an accounting; the credibility of oral testimony will be determined by the new judge.

A training intervention research project implemented a Training of Trainer (TOT) model for maternal and newborn health (MNH) in Palghar District, Maharashtra, scaling up from a Pune pilot. The six-step approach included: pre-TOT screening of 48 candidates (selecting 32), training with pre/post assessments, staggered induction of master trainers (MTs), continuous support from Pune core trainers, virtual quality assessment by UK experts, and refresher training via virtual platform. This produced 32 Palghar MTs (25 medical doctors, 7 GNMs) who trained 505 health providers. Post-training assessment scores showed significant improvement in clinical knowledge and skills. MTs reported increased clinical competency, confidence as trainers, and career recognition. The study concluded that methodical TOT approaches using adult-learner-centric principles, hybrid platforms, longer time frames, and supportive ecosystems are effective for developing sustainable trainer cadres within public health systems.

Cascaded inference uses collections of sub‑models with different complexity to balance accuracy, latency, and cost, but existing routing and termination policies are heuristic and lack guarantees. T‑Tamer formalizes the bi‑objective trade‑off as a weighted sum of loss functions and recasts routing, stopping, and consulting as a costly exploration problem over directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). The paper proves an information‑theoretic impossibility: no‑recall policies cannot achieve any constant‑factor approximation to the offline optimal, even for two nodes. To overcome this, T‑Tamer develops a with‑recall dynamic indexing strategy derived via dynamic programming that is provably optimal for single‑line DAGs; the strategy stops when the current minimum loss falls below a dynamically computed index. This approach generalizes to directed trees and the transitive closure of a line, preserving theoretical optimality and polynomial‑time computation (pre‑processing O(n·|V|²T), inference O(n) per sample). The method is model‑agnostic, trained on input–output pairs from sub‑models without retraining them, and functions as a plug‑in component. Experiments on synthetic data and real vision/NLP early‑exit workloads (VGG‑11/13, BERT‑base, GPT‑2) demonstrate that recall‑based strategies consistently yield favorable accuracy–latency trade‑offs, e.g., reducing latency to 45% of the original while sacrificing less than 7% accuracy.

S&P 500 trades near 6,715, sparking bubble talk as valuations surpass pre‑2000 levels; the market holds above 6,620 support while Fed policy and government‑shutdown headlines add caution. Traders Union, founded in 2010, is a financial portal offering unbiased broker reviews and market‑trend content.

The ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP) provides an open, FAIR platform for dark matter research, supporting particle physics experiments (ATLAS, DarkSide, Fermi LAT, KM3NeT, CTA) through the European Open Science Cloud. The TSP develops tools and workflows for constraining dark matter properties, aiming to bridge particle physics and astrophysical communities. Astrophysical constraints from gravitational lensing and dwarf spheroidal galaxies complement particle physics experiments in testing CDM and alternative models (WDM, SIDM). Software tools like pyHalo, GAMBIT, and AxionLimits facilitate dark matter constraints, with the TSP working to incorporate astronomical searches into its services.

In February 2017, St. Kitts and Nevis Minister Mark Brantley told a Charlestown town‑hall that the Team Unity coalition—launched in September 2013 and led by Timothy Harris—had achieved an unprecedented coming together of the federal and Nevis Island administrations. After Unity’s electoral victory on 16 February 2015, Harris became Prime Minister. Brantley noted that in 2013 the St. Kitts‑Nevis Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (SIDF) spent $95.5 million solely in St. Kitts. Under Unity, the SIDF directed $62.2 million to Nevis projects (e.g., a pier, sports facilities, geothermal development, a hospital, an electricity generator) and the Nevis Island Administration received $51.16 million in regular budgetary support, totaling $113.36 million in less than two years—far exceeding the $17.3 million provided between 2006‑2015. He praised Premier Vance Amory and stated the government’s goal is a fair share of the country’s resources for all citizens regardless of birthplace.

A hockey player is described as working harder than younger players to maintain fitness, characterized as classy, intelligent, and helpful. He had an excellent reputation in Russia, where he played on the most famous line in Russian hockey history and was considered among the country's best five players. He connected defense to offense, performed well in important competitions like world championships and the Olympics, and was among Russian hockey's elite. The speaker suggests his generation, born in the 1970s, was the last to be truly influenced by him, and believes this is why Russian hockey is currently struggling.

The United States and Imperial Russian Government agreed by notes of September 8, 1900 to arbitrate U.S. claims for indemnity arising from the arrest and seizure of American vessels by Russian authorities. The claims involve four cases – the Cape Horn Pigeon, James Hamilton Lewis, C. H. White and Kate and Anna – which detail the forced detention of crews and other injuries. The United States maintains that the seizures violated international law and its treaty rights. The submission argues that interest on the indemnity is customary, citing numerous past arbitration awards that allowed interest. The United States presented detailed statements of facts, damages and arguments to the arbitrator.

US equity markets reached a record high despite a likely government shutdown. The USD/JPY fell sharply after a weaker-than-expected US jobs report, testing key support levels around 147.13. GBP/USD remained cautious ahead of the Bank of England’s Thursday meeting, where markets anticipate a 25 basis-point rate cut to 4.0% amid slowing UK economic momentum. Bitcoin prices slid alongside equities, finding support near the 50-day moving average, while AI-selected stocks continued to outperform the S&P 500. Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to speak this week, and the resignation of Fed board member Adriana Kugler could lead to a more dovish policy direction.

They scored two goals but only capitalized once, failing to equalize. Buffalo won the first home game, and they fell short by a goal. They were nervous early, settled down, created scoring chances, but couldn't convert, and the game remained tight with missed opportunities at the end.

Delhi High Court seeks response from Centre and Jammu & Kashmir on whether J&K High Court judges take oath upholding the Indian Constitution. The bench issued the direction while hearing a PIL by advocate Surjeet Singh challenging Constitution Order 1954, which added a proviso to Article 368 requiring Presidential orders under Article 370 for constitutional amendments to apply in the state. The petition contends the proviso is an unconstitutional encroachment on Parliament's constituent power to amend the Constitution.

Progressive advocates at Wells Fargo's annual shareholders meeting in Des Moines demanded the bank address investments in fossil fuels, private prisons, and discriminatory practices. Organizers from People's Action called for the CEO and board to resign. The protest followed a $1 billion CFPB fine for predatory mortgage practices. Activists criticized the bank's $4.6 billion investment in fossil fuel projects (2015-2017) including the Dakota Access Pipeline, which Indigenous leaders called a "manifest destiny agenda." Sierra Club and ACRE representatives said the bank must be held accountable for its environmental and social harm.

ADS868xW series ADCs support standard SPI interface for single devices or daisy-chain topology for multiple devices with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK signals. The devices operate in three functional states: RESET (controlled by RST pin, supporting application reset or power-on reset), ACQ (analog input acquisition), and CONV (conversion, ignoring further CONVST/CS transitions until completion). Nine configuration registers control device operation: DEVICE_ID_REG (address 00h) for daisy-chain identification, RST_PWRCTL_REG (address 04h) for reset and power management including NAP and power-down modes, SDI_CTL_REG (address 08h) for SPI protocol selection (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S based on CPOL/CPHASE), SDO_CTL_REG (address 0Ch) for output configuration including single/dual SDO-x modes and source-synchronous protocols, DATAOUT_CTL_REG (address 10h) for output data flags (device address, input range, AVDD/input alarms, parity), RANGE_SEL_REG (address 14h) for input range selection up to ±12.288V, ALARM_REG (address 20h) for alarm flags, and ALARM_H_TH_REG (address 24h) and ALARM_L_TH_REG (address 28h) for programmable alarm thresholds with hysteresis. Data transfer frames begin at CONVST/CS falling edge and end at rising edge, with optimal frames containing exactly 32 SCLK cycles. The device integrates analog front-end and precision reference, accepts bipolar and unipolar inputs (±2.5V, ±5V, ±10V, 0-5V, 0-10V, 4-20mA, 0-20mA), and offers power supply decoupling requirements of 10µF and 1µF on AVDD and 1µF on DVDD.

Knee health can be maintained through active lifestyles, keeping muscles strong, flexible, and maintaining a healthy weight. Early physiotherapy aids recovery from injuries and may prevent surgery. Recommended exercises target the hamstrings, quads, glutes, and hip flexors, while low-impact activities like cycling and swimming benefit knee health by improving circulation and limiting joint stress. Higher body weight increases force on joints and injury likelihood. The majority of knee replacement patients are over 50, with around half over 70. Modern knee replacements are highly durable, with over 80% of total and 70% of unicondylar replacements lasting 25 years. Physiotherapy remains important for both injury recovery and post-surgery rehabilitation.

An absorbent core for hygiene articles comprises substantially continuous high fluid distribution structures (interconnected channels) and discontinuous fluid absorption structures surrounding them, with channels distributing fluid faster than surrounding absorbent material. The core has front, back, and crotch portions with a longitudinal axis, and channels extend through at least part of the crotch portion from one side to the other, forming shapes like U-bends with funnel-shaped open ends. Channels are substantially free of absorbent material to maintain efficient fluid distribution. The core may include multiple interconnected channels arranged concentrically. Articles include disposable diapers, incontinence products, and sanitary napkins, where channels remain visible before and after use. Manufacturing involves using a mold with a 3D insert and vacuum to form channels substantially free of absorbent material. The design provides faster fluid distribution, improved comfort, and perception of longer-lasting dryness.

The Government has launched a six‑week consultation on proposals to update the Package Travel Regulations, aiming to give online package‑holiday bookers the same protections as high‑street agents. The plans require clearer refund information, extended coverage, and hold the package‑assembler responsible for the whole trip even if third‑parties deliver parts. Consumer groups, including Which? and spokesperson Alex Neill, support the changes, and Consumer Minister Margot James says the regulations must reflect the shift to online booking.

Japan’s GDP rose 4% in Q2, beating expectations, extending an 18‑month expansion. Household spending climbed 3.7%, near‑10% jump in big‑ticket purchases and higher wages. Topix fell 0.8% amid volatile data. The run is Japan’s longest growth streak in a decade, showing resilience under Abe’s reforms, global economy and BOJ stance. Wage growth lags labor market and the BOJ has delayed its 2% inflation target; consumer spending is a step toward wage‑price cycle.

Enron Corp. restated its third-quarter earnings and faces a $690 million debt payment due by late November following a credit downgrade. The energy company, which agreed to be acquired by Dynegy Inc., also disclosed that Arthur Andersen, its auditor, has not completed its review of financial statements amid ongoing investigations. Congressional representative John Dingell has called for a probe of Arthur Andersen's audits of Enron and Waste Management.

The New Jersey Gold Coast along the Hudson River offers Manhattan skyline views and has become a market. Hoboken, Bayonne and Jersey City have recovered from the 2008 crash with demand for rentals. Major projects include Toll Brothers City Living’s 28‑story Provost Square near the Grove Street PATH station (242 condos, $400,000s‑$1M+), Hoboken’s 1425 Hudson Street (studios‑to‑three‑bedrooms) and 1400 Hudson (sold). Bijou Properties and Intercontinental are building a 424‑unit rental tower at 700 Jackson St. with a gym and a 2‑acre resiliency park, finishing 2019. Ironstate Development is constructing the 45‑story 235 Grand (549 rentals) and a complex at 70‑90 Columbus (545 rentals, roof deck, pool, retail). JMF Properties plans the Harbor Station project in Bayonne with 500 residences, 200,000‑sq‑ft commercial space and an 80,000‑sq‑ft Costco‑anchored shopping center on the former Military Terminal.

The author says that most immigration “solutions” from both parties are flawed, and the immigration debate is broken due to widespread lies. He argues that honesty is needed to develop a fair system and outlines a 20‑point plan that includes: keeping refugee families together with hearings; tying legal immigration to labor market needs; limiting family reunification to spouse, children, parents and siblings; raising legal immigration from about 1 million to 3 million annually; applying asylum laws equally; securing the border with modern surveillance and tunnel detection rather than a wall; deploying National Guard only sparingly; continuing deportations while preserving discretion; creating a path to earned legal status (not citizenship) for undocumented residents who have lived in the U.S. for at least ten years and pass background checks; granting permanent legal status to DACA recipients in exchange for one year of community service; banning benefits for newly legalized immigrants; allowing those legalized to become citizens if they meet effort requirements; eliminating the annual deportation quota; stopping local police enforcement of immigration law; introducing a tamper‑proof identification card; removing the “knowingly” clause from the 1986 Immigration Reform and Control Act; imposing a “three‑strikes” penalty for employers of illegal immigrants; using tax incentives to encourage U.S. companies to create jobs in Mexican states to reduce migration; and promoting better parenting and youth work ethic to reduce competition for low‑wage jobs.

Amber Rose underwent breast reduction surgery in January, reducing her size from 36H to 36DDD. The procedure was prompted by chronic pain that intensified during her 2016 "Dancing with the Stars" run. She had the surgery performed by Dr. Garth Fisher and has since expressed satisfaction with the results, sharing her new look on social media.

Fireworks on July 4 may cause unhealthy air in parts of Southern California, where smoke and particulates from the displays will add to existing vehicle‑emission particulates. Inland areas could see ozone levels reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category. Sensitive groups—athletes, children, teens, the elderly and people with asthma, lung disease or heart ailments—should limit outdoor exercise and avoid heavy exertion. The SCAQMD regularly issues air‑quality advisories for Independence Day, and a heat wave arriving Thursday may prompt additional warnings, as high temperatures convert vehicle emissions into ozone, worsening respiratory conditions.

Ohio districts favor one party, reducing accountability. Two proposals: the League’s Fair Districts Fair Elections plan calls bipartisan commission preserving communities; the alternative creates oddly shaped, tilted districts backed by the Statehouse despite opposition. The author urges citizens to contact legislators supporting the Fair Districts plan.

The 22nd District Agricultural Association board unanimously rejected both construction bids for the Surfside Race Place remodel due to a $4 million funding shortfall. The project, now called a "multipurpose entertainment venue," was estimated at $23.6 million including HVAC upgrades, while a required storm-water treatment plant came in $4 million over budget at $14.6 million. The board has an $18.5 million IBank loan approved and has already spent $1.3 million on the remodel. Current return on investment is approximately 3 percent, far below the desired double-digit returns. Board members expressed concerns about proceeding with the project given the funding challenges and low profit margins. Directors voted to re-evaluate the project and return with a revised plan in four to six months. The loan deadline is June 27.

Sector trading and investing involves focusing on buying and selling securities within a specific sector of the economy, such as technology or energy, and carries higher risk than broader market investing. The worst sectors to invest in based on median returns are information technology, energy, utilities, and materials.

Industry refers to a specific branch of economic activity, while sector is a broader category grouping multiple industries together. S&P divides the stock market into 11 sectors.

JP Morgan's research (1980-2015) based on Russell 3000 components examined catastrophic losses (70% decline with less than 60% recovery). Telecom, information technology, and energy suffered the most catastrophic losses, while utilities had the least. Overall, 40% of the stock universe experienced catastrophic losses. Examining excess returns compared to Russell 3000 showed utilities as the worst sector, followed by energy and materials. While utilities are stable due to heavy regulation and low competition, this stability comes with poor long-term returns.

The research found that median stocks produce negative lifetime returns, while a minority generate spectacular gains. This illustrates the difficulty of shorting stocks. The article suggests focusing on avoiding the worst sectors rather than trying to identify winners. Based on various metrics, utilities, information technology, energy, and materials are identified as the worst sectors to invest in.

AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures on firmware and on each SFS update. OEMs/ODMs own the firmware root of trust for update; unless AMD PSB is enabled they also own detection for their own firmware. During early boot OEM/ODM code can enable ROM Armor to restrict ROM write access to the SMM handler; after lockdown untrusted third‑party code runs. SFS offers optional co‑signing: the OEM/ODM provides its RSA public key during early boot, allowing the ASP to require updates signed by AMD and the OEM/ODM. SFS_ENABLE and COSIGN_REQUIRED BIOS tokens default to off; customers opt‑in. Update packages are applied at runtime, are non‑persistent across reboots, and must be applied sequentially. Each package checks current patch levels before applying and can modify registers, replace firmware images, or update parts of a firmware package. SEV/SNP updates have additional constraints. The ASP verifies the customer signature (if present), then the AMD signature, loads the executable patch, updates the patch level, and returns status. Package naming follows the pattern fam_<family>-<AGESA‑Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. SFS commands require a 2 MB‑aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and optional co‑signing header before the AMD package.

This paper addresses the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP), where unknown physical parameters of complex systems must be inferred from observational data when direct measurement is impossible. Scientists use computer models encoding physical laws to link parameters to observations—for example, the heat equation relates material properties to temperature measurements.

The eSIP seeks a probability distribution on parameter space Λ such that observations sampled from an unknown data-generating distribution correspond to the induced distribution from that solution. When the quantity of interest map Q is not one-to-one, multiple parameter values yield identical observations, creating indeterminacy that is addressed through conditioning on prior information using a Bayesian framework.

The paper establishes four main results: (1) under general conditions, a unique posterior distribution solving the SIP exists with an explicit density formula derived from observation and prior densities; (2) this posterior density is continuous almost everywhere; (3) the solution corresponding to a uniform prior has maximum entropy, making it the least informative choice; and (4) a numerical estimate using importance sampling is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent.

The theoretical framework relies on measure disintegration and regular conditional probabilities rather than standard Bayes' theorem. The solution involves generalized contours—sets of parameter values producing identical observations—that form manifolds whose surface properties determine the solution structure.

Applications span diverse fields including estimating thermal conductivity, modeling groundwater contamination, characterizing nuclear reactor materials, detecting subsurface mineral deposits, and forecasting epidemic surges. The approach differs from traditional Bayesian inverse problems and computer model calibration by focusing on probability distributions over physical parameters rather than point estimates, with solutions exhibiting complex heterogeneous structures requiring nonparametric computational methods.

The Trump administration, which came into office looking to dismantle the Affordable Care Act, must ensure the 2018 open enrollment period ends on Dec 15 for the 39 states on HealthCare.gov. The enrollment window was cut from 90 to 45 days, raising concerns about website congestion and long call‑center wait times. Consumers in hurricane‑affected areas can get an extension to Dec 31. About 9–10 million people are enrolled in ACA marketplace plans. While list‑price premiums rose, subsidies increased, and many eligible consumers can obtain zero‑premium bronze plans. Deadline remains midnight Pacific time (3 a.m. Eastern). It is unclear whether the administration will continue the grace period for incomplete applications. States running their own exchanges have extended deadlines, with California and New York keeping Jan 31.

Colorado State beat Wyoming 78-73 to take sole first place in the Mountain West, its first Border War win in five meetings. Prentiss Nixon hit a three and four free throws in the final minute. Emmanuel Omogbo recorded his 15th double‑double with 19 points and 16 rebounds, while Braden Koelliker played through illness. The Rams, plagued by foul trouble, shot 46.7% from three (7‑15) but made only 21 of 34 free throws (61.8%). Role players contributed 19 points and 14 rebounds. CSU has won four straight and eight of its last nine, and next plays at New Mexico.

Following the Panama and Paradise Papers leaks, experts suggest tax evaders are shifting unaccounted money into Bitcoin. Vijay Mukhi, an Indian IT pioneer, claims Bitcoin exchanges in tax‑haven jurisdictions serve as a new conduit for concealing black money and calls the cryptocurrency a Ponzi scheme, urging the government and RBI to curb its use. Bitcoin's price surged from Rs 7,304 in April 2013 to Rs 1.1 million in December 2017, an increase of roughly 9,000 % over four years. Zebpay, which holds about half of India’s Bitcoin market, reports the industry adds roughly 200,000 new users monthly, has ~2 million total users, and monthly volumes of about Rs 2,000 crore. Zebpay states it follows strict KYC norms and that Bitcoin is not illegal. Mukhi recommends not banning Bitcoin but implementing further demonetisation to stop black‑money flows, while Indian exchanges say they will cooperate with investigators.

The passage documents the AMD AGESA boot‑and‑initialization software. Only the published entry functions are guaranteed to remain stable; internal procedures may change. The boot‑block code resides in flash ROM and provides a minimal processor reset routine that establishes basic settings and execution‑cache regions. Execution‑cache regions are defined by a three‑structure array, must be located in non‑volatile storage, and are allocated according to alignment, size, and boundary rules. A structure for the FCH controller hub configures SATA, IDE, GPP and XHCI controllers.  

AmdInitReset performs the minimal core initialization, separating the Bootstrap Processor (BSP) from Application Processors (APs) and returning status codes (SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR). AmdInitEarly sets up the host environment and includes a PlatformConfig structure with many settings such as VRM properties, C‑State modes, Core Performance Boost, DMI, PState, CRAT, CDIT, WHEA, power limits, and a large set of build‑configuration elements (BLDCFG_ ).  

AmdInitPost brings main memory online, configures MTRRs, and prepares the system for OS boot. AmdInitEnv performs late platform configuration (graphics, FCH, PCIe) and generates ACPI/DMI tables.  

The host environment must implement required call‑outs (AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, Reset, ReadSpd, RunApTask, etc.) and may use optional call‑outs for customizations. Build options (BLDOPT_REMOVE_ ) allow code removal for unsupported DIMM types, processor families, sockets, and features, while build‑configuration elements describe VRM capabilities, CPU frequency limits, and other platform‑specific parameters.

Researchers from Clarkson University studied 75‑year‑old adults performing a six‑minute walking test before and after cognitive tasks. LED sensors recorded gait speed and stride length; participants reported mood, motivation and energy. No gait change was observed in the first 30 seconds after mental fatigue. Later, walking speed and stride length declined significantly with higher cognitive fatigue, while physical fatigue did not affect gait. Further research is needed to clarify why physical energy and fatigue are unrelated to gait.

HF-band RFID communication, particularly NFC in mobile devices, causes significant battery drain—smartphones need 50% more power when NFC is active without a transponder and up to 107% more when reading one. The article proposes dynamic magnetic field strength scaling to reduce power consumption by properly supplying transponders based on actual needs rather than using maximum power. Three investigations are presented: scaling during card detection, during communication (when distance changes or operations vary), and for multiple transponders. The PTF-Determinator method determines the Power Transfer Function to enable proper field scaling. Simulation shows up to 80% transmission energy savings, while measurements on real hardware demonstrate 26% transmission energy reduction and 13% overall battery drain reduction on smartphones. A feature to cut off power when exceeding maximum transmission distance achieves 75% transmission energy reduction and 39% battery drain reduction.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin of the Central District of California dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit alleging that Nirvana’s “Nevermind” album cover, which shows a nude infant underwater, constitutes child pornography. He compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing and concluded it does not meet the legal standard for lasciviousness. A 9th Circuit earlier reinstated a related suit.

The Trump administration’s “Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy” recommends increasing breastfeeding rates through WIC and other policies, but experts say federal paid parental leave is critical and note the report lacks such support. About 84% of U.S. parents initiate breastfeeding, but fewer than 40% continue to a year, and 60% stop earlier than planned. Experts cite structural barriers like lack of paid leave, especially for low-income parents and parents of color. The U.S. is the only high-income country without a federal paid parental leave mandate. Recommendations include paid leave, Medicaid coverage for breastfeeding services, healthcare provider training, and improved state-federal coordination. The report also promotes donor human milk, but experts warn that proposed cuts to SNAP and other safety net programs could hinder progress.

Pfizer agreed to price its medicines at parity with other countries and to launch new drugs at comparable rates. In return, if Pfizer continues investing in U.S. manufacturing, it will avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs for three years, a grace period tied to a $70 billion investment announcement. The agreement includes a new Trump‑branded purchasing platform offering discounts of 50 % or more on many Pfizer products, with examples such as Duavee, Eucrisa and Toviaz discounted by 80 % or more. Specific price changes and revenue impacts are confidential. The White House said the deal would save Medicaid “many millions” of dollars; Medicaid spent over $50 billion on prescriptions in 2023. The 4‑2‑5 defense consists of four down linemen, two linebackers and five defensive backs. It evolved from the 4‑3 defense (which provides the six‑man box) combined with the 3‑3‑5 defense (which supplies the five defensive backs). The Sam (or Rover) linebacker is a hybrid player required to cover, match larger blockers and rush the quarterback. This alignment keeps six players in the box for run support while the five backs cover pass threats, making it effective against modern spread offenses. Strengths include versatility against run and pass, maintenance of a six‑man box against 2×2 formations, and high‑pressure options that enable multiple blitz packages. Weaknesses are its lack of mirror balance, asymmetry that places the weak‑side safety in a large alley, and smaller personnel that can be exploited by bigger offensive lines. Offenses commonly attack the side opposite the Sam with runs such as buck sweep or outside zone. Common blitzes are the 6‑man Cover 0 and a 6‑man Cover 0 field blitz that can become seven‑man pressure; frequent coverages are Cover 4 and Cover 3 Sky. Notable coaches using the scheme include Gary Patterson at TCU, whose defenses led the nation in total defense three straight years and five times overall, making TCU the third program to achieve a defensive three‑peat, and now serving as a special assistant at Texas; and Greg Etter, who ran the 4‑2‑5 at Carthage College (2004 unit led the nation in interceptions) and later as head coach at Concordia University (NACC Coach of the Year 2013).

Sleep problems are common in the US and negatively impact mood, quality of life, productivity, and health, particularly in older adults with chronic conditions and low health literacy. Minoritized groups and low socioeconomic status populations experience worse sleep outcomes. This study evaluated a mobile app delivering tailored sleep psychoeducation to 195 adults aged 40+ with chronic health conditions and low health literacy at Fort Lauderdale, Florida and Atlanta, Georgia. Participants received the sleep module at 3rd, 6th, or 8th grade reading levels with multimedia content. Results showed significant decreases in Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores over time (mean decline 0.85 points) with a small to medium effect size (d=0.40). Socioeconomic status, health literacy, and number of health conditions were significantly associated with sleep quality. Although effect size was modest, findings suggest brief tailored sleep interventions at appropriate reading levels may improve sleep in populations with limited resources and low health literacy, though more intensive interventions might yield larger effects.

The lecture discusses pleat folding, focusing on the hyperbolic paraboloid origami model that self-folds from a square with concentric squares and diagonals. It covers paper's elastic memory and plastic deformation from creasing, simulations of pleated folding, and physical models made via 3D printing. Mathematical sculptures called hyperhedra are formed by joining hyperbolic paraboloids to represent polyhedra. A key theorem proves that the concentric square crease pattern cannot fold into a proper 3D form without triangulation; a construction method using sphere intersections and interval arithmetic verifies triangulated versions exist. The lecture also addresses curve creases, David Huffman's curve crease work, and open problems like maximizing volume in pillows and inflating polyhedra.

Micro E‑mini futures are 1/10‑the‑size versions of standard e‑mini contracts, launched by the CME Group in 2019 to give retail traders access to the futures market with lower margin requirements. They trade on the CME Globex electronic platform and are mostly financially settled.  

The initial set covered the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 indexes; the product line has since expanded to include bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury‑yield and FX futures.  

Contract specifications differ by underlying asset. For the Micro E‑mini S&P 500, one contract unit equals $5 times the index value, the tick size is $1.25 per contract for outright trades and $0.25 for calendar spreads, and the minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points (outright) or 0.05 index points (calendar spread). Contracts are listed quarterly (March, June, September, December) for five consecutive quarters and are cash‑settled using the special opening quote on the third Friday of the contract month at 9:30 a.m. ET.  

Trading runs Sunday through Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET (5:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. CT) with a daily break; CME ClearPort hours are 6:00 p.m. to 5:15 p.m. ET.  

Risk arises mainly from adverse price moves and leverage; a 1 % adverse move on a 20× leveraged contract can wipe out an account.  

To begin trading, a trader opens a futures broker account, deposits the initial margin, and executes orders via the exchange. CFDs that track micro futures are also available and can be held indefinitely, unlike futures which have fixed expiration dates.  

Strategy development often includes back‑testing; an example uses an overnight entry/exit on the Nasdaq 100 (@NQ) contract. Seasonality varies by asset—for example, Treasury futures tend to perform better in the second half of the year.  

Price‑moving factors depend on the underlying: Treasury micro contracts are influenced by interest‑rate changes, inflation, economic conditions and sociopolitical events, while equity‑index micro contracts are driven by broader market sentiment.  

All‑time high for the Micro E‑mini S&P 500 was 4808.25 in January 2022 (per TradingView). Charts and trading symbols are available on platforms such as TradingView and the CME website.

An international team used Bell’s test on 73 qubits to confirm that large quantum systems obey quantum mechanics, demonstrating genuine quantum correlations that cannot be explained classically. By preparing a low‑energy state in a superconducting processor, they measured a deviation of 48 standard deviations, and they also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations up to 24 qubits. The results show quantum computers are authentically quantum and could improve secure communication and quantum algorithms.

Advanced attacking runs require offensive players to decide moves three or more passes ahead and are divided into three categories: individual, planned, and supporting runs.

Individual runs are reactive to defender behavior and include blind‑side runs, drawing defenders out, inverted runs, overlap/underlap runs, third‑attacker/third‑man runs, late/delay runs, and deep‑lying runs.

Planned runs are pre‑designed by coaches for set pieces or specific situations: designed routes, runs to receive crosses, and fast‑break counters (quick two‑run sequences).

Runners must monitor offside, time their bursts, avoid predictability, and keep the run un‑telegraphed.

Supporting runs retain possession via back‑pass, square‑pass, or swinging the ball across the field.

Effective attacks require a completed pass; only one run receives the ball, but all players must finish runs; scouting defenders optimizes execution.

Student mistreatment is common in medical education (≈38 % of graduating students report it in the most recent AAMC Graduation Questionnaire) and is linked to anxiety, depression, post‑traumatic stress, burnout, reduced empathy, and career regret. However, only 27 % of those who are mistreated file a formal report; the most common reasons are that the incident seemed unimportant, that nothing would be done, and fear of reprisal.

To understand why students decide to report or not, a single‑site qualitative study was conducted at a large urban U.S. medical school. Peer‑to‑peer semi‑structured interviews were carried out by student researchers; 21 current medical students (13 women, 8 men, median age 25) who self‑identified as having experienced mistreatment participated. Participants described 34 incidents, of which 12 were reported (via online software, student affairs, or a course director) and 22 were not reported.

Inductive analysis of the interviews identified four overarching factor groups that shape reporting decisions:

* **Personal factors** – Concerns about possible repercussions (e.g., effects on grades or career) deter reporting, but a sense of justice and the desire to protect other students can motivate it. Low personal motivation, such as feeling there is nothing to gain, also discourages filing a report.

* **Situational factors** – The type, severity, and perceived ambiguity of the mistreatment influence decisions; race‑based mistreatment is more likely to be reported. Students often seek confirmation from confidants (friends or family) and are influenced by bystander behavior—inaction from peers, residents, or attendings reduces willingness to report. Perceptions of the perpetrator’s intent or a prior positive relationship can also suppress reporting.

* **Structural factors** – Distrust that a report will lead to action, lack of clarity about the reporting process, uncertainty about where and how to report, and the effort required given heavy clinical duties deter students. Missing feedback on outcomes reinforces the sense that reporting is futile.

* **Climate factors** – The hierarchical culture of medicine normalizes mistreatment, leading students to feel powerless and to expect that reports will not change the system. This perception discourages reporting even when mechanisms exist.

The study also highlighted the negative impact of bystander inaction and the unique motivating effect of a personal sense of justice.

The authors recommend improving reporting systems (making them accessible, transparent, confidential, and protected from retaliation), providing bystander training—especially for those higher in the hierarchy—and fostering a top‑down cultural shift to reduce mistreatment and support learners.

Limitations include reliance on a single institution, a self‑selected volunteer sample with a higher reporting rate than the general student body, and a focus on clinical‑setting incidents.

In summary, medical students weigh personal, situational, structural, and climate‑related considerations when deciding whether to report mistreatment; motivators are few, but a sense of justice and the negative influence of passive bystanders are notable. Changing the institutional culture is essential to increase reporting and improve the learning environment.

Research published in Climate Change proposes that the 10th Eldgjá eruption (939–940 CE) may have spurred Iceland’s conversion to Christianity. The eruption, the largest known lava‑flood of the Common Era, released ash that reduced sunlight, lowered temperatures and harmed early settlement agriculture. The researchers connect this event to the 10th‑century Völuspá poem, which contains two stanzas describing severe volcanic activity as a sign of the doom of the Norse gods. They argue the poem intentionally references the Eldgjá eruption to encourage Christianisation, culminating in the official conversion (kristnitaka) of 999/1000 CE after the Þingvellir parliament. Later sources such as Kristni saga also link the conversion to a volcanic episode during the debate.

The speaker advocates that remaining coal lands be permanently withdrawn from sale by legislation, with the United States retaining ownership while permitting private mining under a royalty system. The government would control prices charged to consumers and regulate the freight rates and conduct of common carriers, an approach modeled on the earlier withdrawal of forest lands. He notes that Congress has made significant progress in regulating interstate corporations, citing the railway‑rate bill, pure‑food bill, and enhanced oversight of the beef‑packing industry, and points out that the interstate‑commerce law has already produced substantial voluntary freight and fare reductions by railroads. He argues that further measures—such as a national licensing system, greater Interstate Commerce Commission authority, and requirements for corporations to disclose stockholders and assets—are needed to prevent over‑capitalization and abuses of consolidation, and that adequate public control of interstate carriers can forestall demands for government ownership. He contends that addressing genuine abuses will diminish socialist‑type agitation while still preserving individual initiative and avoiding the harmful effects of unregulated competition.

Michelle Bishop, a Gamilaroi woman, presents research conducted on D'harawal Country in south-west Sydney that explores Indigenous education sovereignty. The research, involving surveys and yarns with over 35 community members, critiques mainstream Australian schooling as a site of ongoing colonial harm while centering Indigenous peoples' long history of successful education practices. Using Indigenous, decolonizing, and relational theories, the study employs envisioning and storytelling to imagine alternative educational futures. Findings are re-presented through the community story "Our Education, Our Way," which depicts a collective vision of Aboriginal-controlled, identity- and Country-based learning.

Meb Faber’s 200‑day moving average trend‑following system for the S&P 500, introduced in a 2012 paper, buys when the index price rises above its 200‑day average and sells when it falls below it. The rule relies solely on price, ignoring news, earnings and sentiment. Paul Tudor Jones cites the 200‑day average as a defensive tool that helps avoid large drawdowns. Backtesting from 1960 shows the strategy sold before the 2008/09 financial crisis and re‑entered in June 2009, limiting losses; during the COVID‑19 sell‑off it exited and re‑entered quickly, with a maximum drawdown of 19 %. A ten‑month moving‑average version turned $100 000 invested in 1960 into $4.7 million (not including dividends) and produced a 6.3 % CAGR versus 7 % for buy‑and‑hold, with the largest drawdown of 26 % in October 1987. The article concludes that the simple 200‑day moving‑average trend system works reasonably well and keeps investors on the sidelines during major downturns.

The passage describes the AMD AGESA™ software core architecture used in UEFI BIOS environments. It explains that when the binary image build model is used, all interface call‑out functions from “Chapter 15 Call‑Out Procedures” are funneled through a single portal, giving the host a consistent point for filtering and dispatching. All AGESA core call‑outs are made through a call port, requiring the host to implement a router function that translates function numbers into execution addresses. The router must expose a specific interface and support three parameters: an index or identifier, a function‑specific data element, and a pointer to a configuration data block (ConfigPtr).  

The UEFI BIOS offers four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) spanning three modes. AGESA files are organized into three core libraries for the three execution modes, with additional UEFI libraries for four build targets. Build tools vary by phase: MASM 6.15 for 16‑bit SEC, Microsoft Macro Assembler and C/C++ compiler (32‑bit versions) for 32‑bit SEC/PEI, and 64‑bit versions for DXE and RT phases.  

Two primary build methods exist: the indirect “Binary Modules” method, where source and control files produce binary modules routed through a common entry point, and the “Source Integration” method, where the host integrates distributed source files into its own tool chain. Build customization is handled through a <Plat>Options.c file; environment variables AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir, and the platform name must be set before building.  

The host must implement several required call‑out procedures: AgesaAllocateBuffer (post‑memory buffer allocation), AgesaDeallocateBuffer (buffer de‑allocation), and a reset function (cold or warm). Optional call‑outs provide services such as heap management, event logging, MMIO mapping, and reading SPD or data‑eye information.  

The passage details entry procedures that follow a chronological order:  

* AmdInitReset – minimal processor initialization after reset, allocating execution cache regions and configuring FCH, SATA, IDE, GPP, and XHCI settings.  
* AmdInitEarly – full processor initialization, publishing PPIs (AMD_PEI_INIT_RESET_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_POST_PPI) and a HOB for memory info.  
* AmdInitPost – memory subcomponent initialization, publishing AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI and coordinating with a reset‑coordinating PEIM.  
* AmdInitEnv – graphics, display, IOMMU, LVDS, PCIe reference clock, audio, SATA, USB, and GPP configuration; moves HOBs from cache to main memory.  
* AmdInitLate – generates ACPI/DMI tables (IVRS, DMI, PState, WHEA‑MCE/CMC, CRAT, CDIT, ASL library), executed after PCI enumeration and before OS boot.  
* AmdInitRtb – last‑minute configuration for Ready‑To‑Boot, saves processor context to SMM area for suspend.  
* AmdS3Save – saves critical processor registers and context to non‑volatile storage for S3 resume.  
* AmdS3Restore – re‑initializes memory and restores processor state from saved context; called after PCI control structures are re‑established.  

Additional service routines are provided: AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct for allocating/removing parameter block storage (PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, ByHost methods); AmdGetExeSize (pre‑memory cache size); AmdGetApicAddress (APIC ID); AmdGetPciAddress (base PCI address); AmdIdentifyCore (socket/die/core identification); AmdIdentifyMemoryAddress (FRU location); AmdReadEventLog (event log retrieval); and AmdAddMmio (MMIO range merging).  

The passage also describes stack establishment macros: AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK creates a pre‑memory stack in Cache‑As‑RAM, preserving EBX and requiring the host to set SS:ESP correctly; AMD_DISABLE_STACK removes the pre‑memory stack, flushing cache and disabling CAR mode. These macros are specific to x86‑64 APUs; AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use them.  

Finally, the document outlines the file structure for reference implementations (Cpcar32.asm wrapper, <Plat>Options.c and <Plat>RecoveryOptions.c), control files for UEFI builds (AgesaPei0Libs.inf, AgesaPei1Libs.inf, AgesaDxe0Libs.inf), and configuration options for platform customization, including VRM settings, voltage planes, memory interleaving, ECC, power management, and display parameters.

The article argues that English as a Second Language (ESL), World Languages (WL), and Bilingual Education (BE) have historically developed as separate fields in the United States, each shaped by distinct sociopolitical forces and monolingual ideologies. It contends that a historically aware, cross‑disciplinary perspective is needed to understand the connections and tensions among these areas and to improve language‑teacher education. The authors apply Valdés’s “curricularization of language” framework—which examines what is taught, how, and for whom under the influence of ideologies, policies, and local contexts—to analyse ESL, WL, and BE programs.  

Setting and context: The work is situated in an urban Illinois institution that serves a growing emergent‑bilingual population (e.g., over 205,000 Spanish‑speaking English Learners, 2,900 Chinese‑speaking English Learners, and a statewide Chinese‑teacher shortage of roughly 48:1 compared with 22:1 for Spanish teachers). Although ESL/BE and WL programs operate as separate units, enrollment crossover—WL candidates take ESL methods—has created an opportunity for collaborative redesign.  

Phase 1 – Crossing from ESL to translanguaging: The ESL methods course was re‑designed around translanguaging pedagogy, emphasizing learners’ diverse linguistic repertoires. Course outcomes, activities, and the culminating assessment were revised to include multiple languages, culturally responsive strategies, and documentation of learner backgrounds. The shift moves the course from a monolingual, behaviorist model to an equity‑oriented, heteroglossic approach that serves pre‑service and in‑service teachers, including WL candidates.  

Phase 2 – Crossing from translanguaging to WL: A combined ESL and WL Methods course was created, initially focusing on Chinese language teaching. Instruction is bilingual in Chinese and English; candidates explore ESL‑WL intersections, use case studies (e.g., teaching Pinyin), observe mentor teachers in various program models, and build a teaching portfolio that demonstrates support for learners’ bilingualism and biliteracy. The course encourages a multilingual turn, asset‑based perspectives, and critical analysis of professional standards.  

Phase 3 (future) – Crossing from WL to BE: Planned redesign of the BE methods course will integrate WL and BE candidates, emphasizing decolonizing methodologies, linguistic autobiographies, drama‑based pedagogy for critical consciousness, and case‑study analysis of existing dual‑language programs using Valdés’s framework. The goal is to train teachers who can operate across program models while advancing bilingualism, biliteracy, biculturalism, and critical consciousness.  

Implications: Cross‑disciplinary collaboration, a guiding analytic framework, and explicit modeling of equity‑oriented practices enhance teacher‑education curriculum. Institutional constraints (schedule flexibility, advising, field‑experience oversight) shape implementation, but heterogeneous enrollment contexts foster pedagogical flexibility and a heteroglossic vision. The authors conclude that bridging ESL, WL, and BE in teacher education historicizes the fields, harmonizes theoretical foundations, and cultivates critically conscious, language‑equity‑focused educators prepared to serve diverse linguistic profiles.

This lecture introduces MIT course 6.451 (Principles of Digital Communications II), covering logistics, policies, and fundamental concepts. The course focuses on coding for additive white Gaussian noise channels, with the goal of achieving channel capacity (Shannon limit). Key policies include a strict prerequisite of 6.450, weekly problem sets (15% of grade), a midterm on March 16 (1/3 of grade), and a final (1/2 of grade). No textbook is required. The course covers topics including algebraic block codes, convolutional codes, capacity-approaching codes (LDPC), lattice codes, and trellis coded modulation. Chapter 1 introduces channel models (deep space and telephone channels) and the Shannon capacity formula C = W log2(1 + SNR). Chapter 2 covers converting continuous-time AWGN channels to discrete-time equivalents using PAM modulation and orthonormal pulses. Spectral efficiency (rho = R/W) is identified as a key parameter. The course emphasizes practical implementation of Shannon's theoretical results on coding over 50 years.

The article compares dollar‑cost averaging (DCA) and lump‑sum investing, citing studies (e.g., Morningstar 2020) that show lump‑sum beats DCA in roughly 70‑90 % of periods. It defines DCA as spreading investment over time and lump‑sum as investing at the earliest opportunity. Backtests from Jan 2000 to Dec 2019 with $60 k show lump‑sum growing to $193 k (CAGR 6.0 %) versus DCA reaching $174 k (CAGR 5.5 %). When the S&P 500’s return sequence is reversed—placing the later decade’s gains before the earlier decade’s flat performance—lump‑sum’s result remains similar (CAGR 5.9 %) while DCA’s final value drops to $87 k (CAGR 1.9 %). The article concludes that lump‑sum is generally superior and that DCA’s outcomes are more vulnerable to the order of returns and random variation.

Weber State University cancelled its 27th annual Unity Conference (formerly the Diversity Conference) after being required to censor presentations under HB 261. Days before the event, a student presenter received an email directing them to remove references to "DEI," "diversity," "equity," and "inclusion" from their slides. Associate professor Sarah Herrmann and her student refused and withdrew their presentation. Other faculty also pulled out in protest.

The conference was organized by the Student Access and Success division, which is subject to HB 261 restrictions on non-academic programming. Events sponsored by academic units are exempt from the law. University officials acknowledged communication could have been clearer and said they are working through how the legislation applies to different university divisions.

The university is considering restructuring future conferences under Academic Affairs or a specific college to qualify for exemption. HB 261 has been in effect for about 18 months and has led to cuts affecting programs such as queer studies, ethnic studies, and women's and gender studies minors.

A study reveals that AI chatbots trained on biased online images perceive women as younger and less experienced than men in workforce settings. Researchers analyzed 1.4 million online images and videos, used nine language models for text analysis, and conducted experiments with over 450 participants. ChatGPT consistently generated younger, less experienced resumes for female names and ranked them lower than male resumes, despite Census data showing male and female employees are similar in age. The bias was strongest in prestigious occupations like doctors and CEOs. Participants who uploaded images of female employees estimated average ages as two years younger than controls. The researchers argue this "gendered ageism" helps explain the glass ceiling, noting organizations hire young women but fail to promote them. They recommend tackling intersecting biases like gender and age rather than addressing single issues in isolation.

The SPY and XLU rotating system is a weekly strategy that switches between the S&P 500 (SPY) and the utilities sector (XLU) based on recent performance. It originated from Michael Gayed’s SSRN paper, which highlights utilities’ low beta, risk‑aversion and sensitivity to interest rates—making them attractive when rates fall and vulnerable when rates rise. Trading rules are simple: buy the better‑performing of the two in the prior week and sell the other. Historical backtests starting in 1926 show the system outperformed the market, especially before the paper’s publication. A 1999‑based backtest (adjusted for dividends and splits) reports a low compound annual growth rate because it began near the dot‑com peak, and the strategy slightly underperformed the market though its risk‑adjusted return was comparable. From the paper’s release in 2014 through early 2021 the system returned about 6.7% per year versus 4.6% for a buy‑and‑hold SPY, but after 2021 it lagged by more than 5% annually (5.1% vs 10.4%). It did not recover from the 2020 COVID crash and its maximum drawdown since the 2021 peak matched SPY’s (‑23.6% vs ‑23.9%). While the strategy historically generated superior returns, it has underperformed SPY since the paper’s publication; however, this may be a short‑term effect, and it is premature to conclude the strategy no longer works.

Researchers at the 255th ACS National Meeting reported that the global wine industry generates about 14 million tons of grape pomace annually, which can pollute water, acidify soil and attract pests if left as waste. Pomace is rich in natural antioxidants such as proanthocyanidins, anthocyanins and ellagic acid that neutralize free radicals. Using a holistic extraction approach, Changmou Xu’s group separates nutrients and removes pesticides for cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and dietary supplements. They added isolated phenolic compounds to high‑fat foods (mayonnaise, ranch dressing), significantly inhibiting lipid oxidation and extending shelf life, especially at elevated temperature. A previous study showed these polyphenols cut acrylamide formation in potato chips by 60 %. The team aims to make the natural antioxidants perform comparably to artificial EDTA while providing a clean‑label ingredient.
