Study design: The trial used BNT162b1, BNT162b2, and BNT162b2SA vaccines and placebo. The first two doses were given in an observer‑blinded manner; later phases became open‑label for the initial vaccine. Booster doses were given open‑label, except for a small group whose booster assignment remained observer‑blinded. The study was conducted at 153 sites in 6 countries between 29 April 2020 and 10 February 2023 (≈33 months). Participants were healthy children and adults aged 12 years and older with no prior COVID‑19 infection or vaccination. Gender was balanced in Phase 1 and Phase 2/3; ages ranged from 19‑82 years in Phase 1 and 12‑91 years in Phase 2/3.

Enrollment and retention: In Phase 1, all 195 participants received a study vaccine and none left during the blinded period. In Phase 2/3, 46 406 participants enrolled, 46 297 (99%) received a study vaccine, and 1 156 (3%) discontinued during the blinded period (most could not be reached for follow‑up). A subgroup of 333 participants who had not previously received BNT162b2 received BNT162b2SA; 330 (99%) of them received the vaccine and 102 (31%) did not complete the study, mainly because they could not be reached for follow‑up.

Efficacy: Compared with placebo, BNT162b2 was 95 % effective in preventing COVID‑19 from 7 days after Dose 2 to the end of the monitoring period (December 3 2020). Efficacy was similar for participants with or without prior infection.

Immune responses: One month after a booster (Dose 3) with BNT162b2, immune responses to the original SARS‑CoV‑2 strain were comparable to those seen one month after Dose 2. A booster with BNT162b2SA produced immune responses to the Beta variant comparable to those against the original strain after Dose 2. Similar comparable responses were observed after Dose 2 of BNT162b2SA in participants who had not previously received BNT162b2.

Safety: Temporary decreases in lymphocyte count occurred in a few participants after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, returning to normal by 6‑8 days. Injection‑site reactions (pain most common) and systemic events (tiredness and headache most common) were generally mild or moderate and resolved quickly. All tested doses in Phase 1 were tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1 due to reactions. BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3; few participants (≤1 %) left because of medical problems. Most adverse events were mild or moderate.

Serious medical problems and deaths: In Phase 1, two participants (appendicitis, nerve inflammation) had serious problems unrelated to the vaccine. In Phase 2/3, a few participants experienced serious problems; none exceeded 1 % of any group, and most were not considered related to the vaccine. During Phase 2/3, 85 of 23 141 participants who received BNT162b2 at study start, 62 of 21 371 who received placebo then BNT162b2, and 23 of 23 141 who received only placebo died; causes varied and deaths were not attributed to the vaccine. No deaths occurred in the BNT162b2SA Phase 3 group.

Overall, the study showed that BNT162b2 was well tolerated, produced strong immune responses, and demonstrated high efficacy against COVID‑19, with a safety profile similar to other vaccine platforms.

Cassini started its final five close Saturn flybys on August 14, passing at 1,010–1,060 miles altitude and may perform a “pop‑down” pass to gather unprecedented atmospheric data, temperature profiles, aurora images, vortex details and composition. The spacecraft will become the first Saturn atmospheric probe and also aims to determine the planet’s rotation period. Saturn is about 75 % hydrogen with the rest helium and traces. In 13 years at Saturn it completed 127 close Titan encounters and, with fuel low, will avoid contaminating Titan or Enceladus by plunging into Saturn on September 15 after a final Titan farewell on September 11.

The present disclosure provides a method for characterizing a state of an end effector of an ultrasonic device by applying a power level to an ultrasonic transducer, measuring the impedance value, comparing it to a reference value, classifying the impedance value, characterizing the state of the electromechanical ultrasonic system based on the classification, and adjusting the power level applied to the ultrasonic transducer based on the characterization. The method may characterize the state of the end effector, the function of the end effector, or tissue in contact with the end effector.

The lecture introduces plasma diagnostics as tools to indirectly measure plasma properties since direct measurement is impossible. Diagnostics transform physical effects into measurable signals, exemplified by thermometers using thermal expansion.

The history of plasma diagnostics includes: the UK's ZETA pinch (1950s) initially misinterpreted neutron bursts as fusion before developing Thomson scattering to verify Russian tokamak claims of kiloelectron volt temperatures, leading to global conversion to tokamaks; and the National Ignition Facility's initial failure due to insufficient diagnostics, which later improved alongside successful ignition.

Diagnostics serve experimentalists, computational scientists for code validation, and theorists who must critically evaluate experimental claims while designing testable predictions. The ideal measurement would track every particle's position and velocity, but practical needs include distribution function moments (density, velocity), and magnetic fields.

Key diagnostic limitations include sparse spatial/temporal sampling, line-integrated light measurements, instrument response functions, poorly understood atomic physics in spectroscopy, and model-dependent interpretation. The course focuses on enduring principles rather than specific implementations.

The interactive segment surveyed participants' diverse plasma systems spanning 16 orders of magnitude in density (10^16-10^32 m^-3), temperatures from 0.1 eV to 10+ keV, and magnetic fields from 0.01 to 100 tesla, covering tokamaks (Columbia HBT, DIII-D, ASDEX, Spark), stellarators (W7-X, CNT), inertial confinement fusion (NIF, magLIF), pulsed power (Z machine), helicon plasmas, Hall thrusters, and plasma accelerators. Diagnostics mentioned include Thomson scattering, Langmuir probes, interferometry, bolometers, electron cyclotron emission, spectroscopy, and Faraday rotation imaging.

Rams seek permission from Jaguars to interview Doug Marrone for head coach. Marrone went 1-1 as interim coach, with Jaguars (3-13) showing improvement during his tenure. Jaguars are considering removing his interim tag and making him permanent, though Rams (4-12) are not the only interested team.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported Q1 2015 net sales of $22.7 billion, a 15% increase from $19.7 billion in Q1 2014. The company reported a net loss of $57 million compared to net income of $108 million in the prior year period. Operating income was $255 million. By segment, North America had net sales of $13.4 billion with operating income of $517 million; International had net sales of $7.7 billion with an operating loss of $76 million; and AWS had net sales of $1.6 billion with operating income of $265 million. Total assets were $50.1 billion and cash and cash equivalents were $10.2 billion as of March 31, 2015.

Tesla, founded in 2003 to advance sustainable transportation, grew into a leading EV manufacturer under Elon Musk, who invested $80 million during a 2008 liquidity crisis. Early models included the Roadster, Model S and Model X. In 2016 it launched the mass‑market Model 3 at $27,500, and by 2017 became the most valuable U.S. automaker.

Tesla expanded into battery production and home energy storage (Powerwall), and in 2016 acquired SolarCity for about $2.1 billion. Despite a rising stock price, Tesla posted operating losses and negative cash flow, requiring equity and debt raises that pushed debt above $10 billion.

Model 3 production began in July 2017; Tesla repeatedly delayed its target of 5,000 cars per week, a threshold needed for cash‑flow positivity. Analysts warned Tesla might need over $10 billion in external capital by 2020. Musk said the company would not need a capital raise in 2018, and its survival depended on investors’ willingness to provide additional capital.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs introduce GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps, 20 % power improvement) with a redesigned interface, delivering a 50 % increase in effective bandwidth versus Pascal. The architecture adds a dedicated RT Core per SM for hardware‑accelerated ray tracing, enabling real‑time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray‑traced lighting, shadows, ambient occlusion and reflections, and provides roughly 10 × the ray‑tracing throughput of Pascal. Turing includes new AI features via Tensor Cores and the NGX stack, such as DLSS (≈2× performance gain), AI‑based InPainting, AI Slow‑Mo and AI Super Rez, plus Variable‑Rate Shading, Texture‑Space Shading and Multi‑View Rendering for efficient, flexible rendering. The display engine supports 8K HDR via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, and VirtualLink USB‑Type‑C simplifies VR connectivity. NVLink (25 GB/s per direction) replaces the prior SLI bridge for higher‑bandwidth GPU interconnects. TU102, TU104 and TU106 variants provide up to 13.6 B transistors, with full‑chip configurations ranging from 2304 to 3072 CUDA cores, 288 to 368 Tensor Cores, and 36 to 48 RT Cores. Turing also adds an enhanced NVENC encoder (HEVC 8K 30 fps, up to 25 % bit‑rate savings) and an updated NVDEC decoder (HEVC 4:4:4, VP9 10/12‑bit HDR). A workload‑based RTX‑OPS metric combines FP32, Tensor, RT and integer operations to reflect the hybrid rendering balance of the architecture.

Hurricane Harvey damaged or destroyed critical wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast. The storm damaged nesting sites and eroded marshes home to endangered species. Aransas National Wildlife Refuge sustained damage to salt marshes where whooping cranes feed. The Attwater Prairie Chicken National Wildlife Refuge received 50 inches of rain, with only about 10 of approximately 60 endangered chickens believed to have survived. Some marine species survived, but many oyster beds were lost. Agencies are conducting damage assessments.

Public transit planning often assumes a hierarchical arrangement of modes, but the alignment between planners' hierarchies and actual passenger usage is not well understood. This paper proposes an ascending‑descending method that uses smart‑card data to identify macroscopic hierarchies among transit modes. For each multi‑modal trip, the total travel distance is split at its midpoint; transfers before the midpoint are classified as ascending‑phase transfers, those after as descending‑phase transfers. Transfer rate matrices for the two phases are built, and the hierarchy distance between each pair of modes is derived. Average hierarchical distances are computed and rescaled to [0,1]; higher values indicate a superior hierarchical position. The approach is applied to the Seoul metropolitan area using 10,264,700 trip chains from the T‑money dataset (November 12 2019) covering six modes: walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro. Within Seoul, the hierarchical order is walking < community bus < urban bus < light rail < metro, with no significant difference between ascending and descending phases. Inter‑zonal trips reveal that intercity bus ranks highest, and that the relative positions of metro and urban bus vary between Seoul and the surrounding regions, indicating regional differences in transit hierarchy. The method successfully captures hierarchical relationships without assuming spatial homogeneity.

Jerry Wayne Hill sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury after his 15-year-old son Michael drowned when Bradd Rudolph drove through an unmarked "T" intersection into Bayou Bartholomew. The trial court found the police jury knew of the intersection's danger but failed to post adequate warnings, allocating 20% fault to the police jury and 80% to Rudolph, awarding Hill $31,587.53. The Court of Appeal found the allocation unreasonable and amended it to 35% fault to the police jury and 65% to Rudolph, while affirming the $150,000 general damage award.

Using a validated cohort of clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers (IntoValue dataset), this study assessed the potential of green open access (self‑archiving) to increase accessibility of trial results. Of 1,897 publications published 2010–2020, 54% were openly accessible (gold 23%, hybrid 7%, bronze 16%, green 8%), while 46% were closed‑access. Among closed‑access publications, 85% had a self‑archiving permission allowing deposit of the accepted or published version in an institutional repository; most permissions involved a 12‑month embargo. Only 16% of closed‑access publications with a permission were actually archived, indicating a large unrealized potential of green OA. The findings corroborate previous research showing that many journal and publisher policies permit self‑archiving, yet practice lags. The study employed Unpaywall to determine OA status and Shareyourpaper to derive article‑level permissions. The automated workflow can support institutions in identifying articles that can be self‑archived and is being piloted at Charité to improve trial transparency.

Natural gas prices settled at $3.27/MMBtu, staying within a descending wedge pattern since March highs. Europe's LNG demand is boosting U.S. exports, while North American oversupply and seasonal weakness pressure domestic prices. Canadian supply disruptions contribute to market volatility.

U.S. markets fell Tuesday, with Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq down. The 10‑year Treasury yield hitting 3% and Alphabet’s share drop unnerved investors. Canada’s TSX fell less as Barrick Gold and gold prices rose; the Canadian dollar edged up to 77.95 cents US. May copper contract up three cents to $3.14/lb.

Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne, speaking at Humber College, said that if older white people do not vote, younger and minority voters will be outvoted, suggesting that demographic groups have opposing interests. Critics label the comment ageist, arguing it presumes older and younger voters differ on policy, and racist, noting it implies certain demographic votes are harmful. Ali Taghva, describing himself as a person of colour, accused Wynne of employing identity politics to divide people. Labour lawyer Sunira Chaudhri said such a statement in a workplace could trigger Human Rights Tribunal complaints. The author describes the remark as shameful and calls for engaging all groups in voting.

Global stock markets rose after Fed Chair Janet Yellen said the central bank could raise interest rates as soon as next month, reflecting confidence in the U.S. economy. European indexes advanced, Asian markets mostly gained, and the dollar strengthened against the yen. Oil prices fell.

This lecture introduces MIT course 15.S12 on blockchain and money, taught by Gary Gensler. Gensler, a senior lecturer with experience in finance and public policy, outlines the course focus on blockchain's potential to change finance. He gauges student backgrounds: about 45% have owned cryptocurrency, and a third have worked on blockchain projects. The course addresses two core questions: what is blockchain, and why might it be a catalyst for change in finance.

The lecture provides historical context, tracing the internet's evolution (TCP/IP, HTTP), the first online sale (Pizza Hut's PizzaNet in 1995), and the challenge of moving money online. Gensler explains cryptography's role, from ancient ciphers to modern SSL/TLS, noting MIT's contributions. He defines blockchain as time-stamped, append-only logs creating an auditable, cryptography-secured database. Key components include hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols, which solve the Byzantine Generals Problem (addressed by Satoshi Nakamoto in 2008).

Gensler recounts Bitcoin's origin as a peer-to-peer electronic cash system and the first pizza purchase with 10,000 BTC in 2010, illustrating early use as a medium of exchange. He describes blockchain technology as a decentralized way to verify data, reducing some verification costs but adding others via consensus protocols. In finance, it relates to moving money and risk across networks, offering opportunities like financial inclusion (1.7 billion unbanked globally) and reducing payment system costs (US revenue of $100-200 billion). Challenges include scalability (Bitcoin handles ~7 transactions/second vs. Visa's ~20,000-70,000), privacy, interoperability, and governance.

Gensler contrasts permissioned blockchains (e.g., the Australian Stock Exchange using Hyperledger) with permissionless ones (e.g., Bitcoin). He notes the financial sector's current preference for permissioned systems. Crypto finance is ~$200 billion, modest compared to global capital markets (~$330 trillion). Public policy issues include guarding against illicit activity, financial stability, and investor protection, with regulators applying the "duck test" (if it quacks like a duck, it's a duck).

The course structure includes three acts: fundamentals, economics, and financial sector use cases. Assignments involve class participation (30%), two critical reasoning write-ups, and a team project proposing a blockchain use case. Gensler emphasizes critical thinking to separate hype from ground truths, covering perspectives from minimalists (e.g., Nouriel Roubini) to maximalists. Next week's focus is on the roles of money (medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account), fiat currency, and ledgers (double-entry bookkeeping).

Digital laggards hoard data as a source of power, storing it in departmental silos and restricting access on a need-to-know basis. They favor business judgment and expertise over data-driven decisions, using data only to justify pre-determined conclusions rather than to interrogate them. Digital laggards set unrealistic aspirational goals that employees believe are unachievable, leading them to avoid measurement and focus instead on process adherence. In contrast, digital leaders use standardized APIs (88% versus 27% for laggards) to enable easy data flow, encourage employees to collect and examine relevant data, and ground goals in measurable metrics. They track progress continuously and evaluate performance through data-driven metrics complemented by 360-degree reviews. This measurement focus provides flexibility and autonomy, enabling innovation and risk-taking rather than constraining it. Digital leaders align organizations around shared data-driven objectives, using transparent methodology to connect individual goals to company strategy both vertically and horizontally. They emphasize data culture as central, ensuring consistency between stated values and actual behavior. Organizations in transformation struggle most with changing entrenched mindsets. Companies typically fall into four patterns: data novice (needs culture and systems change), insight ready (culture supports risk-taking but lacks technical capability), tech enabled (has technology but lacks experimental culture), and data reliant (high maturity but may over-rely on data, discouraging critical thinking).

Psychedelic therapies have revived drug‑facilitated psychotherapy; pooled MDMA‑AT Phase II trials showed 54% PTSD remission, prompting FDA breakthrough status; Phase III confirmed safety and greater symptom reduction.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on January 28, 2016, under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, reporting its fourth‑quarter and full‑year 2015 financial results. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and information on non‑GAAP measures (Exhibit 99.2), signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Ireland is heavily exposed to exchange‑rate changes. A euro draws US tourists, while sterling keeps UK visitors away. Importers, exporters, tourism firms and holidaymakers are affected. The euro rose to $1.18, sterling to 91p per euro; euro appreciation could bring it to parity with sterling. ECB policy tries to keep the euro low, but appreciation threatens exports. Importers from the UK profit and should hedge; exporters to the UK face losses and need hedging. Weak sterling fuels UK used‑car imports, hurting car sector. Tourism firms have limited hedging; rates favour US visitors, disadvantage UK visitors, and leave eurozone visitors unchanged. Strategies should incur costs in the market's currency.

Browns traded quarterback Joe Flacco and a 2026 sixth‑round pick to Cincinnati for a 2026 fifth‑round pick, leaving only Shedeur Sanders and a fellow rookie on the active roster. Sanders, who has been inactive as the No.3 and emergency quarterback through the first five games, is now listed as the No.2 on this week’s depth chart; Stefanski declined to say whether the team will sign the other rookie to the active roster for the emergency role. Wide receiver Jeudy praised Sanders for being professional and ready to seize his opportunity. Flacco started the first four games before being benched for Dillon Gabriel, whose first career start was a 21‑17 loss in London. Stefanski described the trade as a surprise, with the Bengals initiating contact. Deshaun Watson remains on the physically unable to perform list while rehabbing an Achilles injury. OBJ accepted a six‑game PED suspension. Additional headlines note that the Cardinals are monitoring Kyler Murray’s foot injury, Giants receiver Darius Slayton is ruled out, and other NFL news items.

A University of Michigan study found that 21% of women and 10% of men in Generation X and late Baby Boomers (ages 50-64) meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, far higher than adults 65-80 (12% women, 4% men). This generation was the first to grow up surrounded by ultra-processed foods loaded with fat, salt, sugar, and flavorings. Researchers used the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 to assess addiction criteria including cravings, failed cut-down attempts, and withdrawal symptoms. The study suggests aggressive marketing of "diet" ultra-processed foods to women in the 1980s may have reinforced addictive eating patterns. Addiction was strongly linked to poor physical and mental health, social isolation, and self-reported overweight status—overweight women were 11 times more likely and overweight men 19 times more likely to meet addiction criteria. Researchers warn that children today consume even higher proportions of ultra-processed foods, potentially leading to higher addiction rates in future generations.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note and issue the £10 polymer note in September despite a tiny amount of tallow. It says alternatives would be costly and risk anti‑counterfeit measures. Over 134,000 signed a petition; the Bank has postponed £20 note contracts pending plant‑based alternatives and will decide by summer 2017.

Qarlingua (Inuktitut for “like pants”) is a natural sea arch on the Brodeur Peninsula, Baffin Island, Nunavut, about 80–90 km southwest of Arctic Bay. The formation stands over 50 m tall and consists of sedimentary rock with resistant quartz layers. Initially dismissed as a hoax, it was confirmed real by local hunters, tourism workers and four Canadian geologists, who identified it as a sea arch created by coastal erosion as the land sinks while sea level rises. Access requires a 4–5 hour boat trip with only a brief ice‑free window each year. Geologists say similar arches are rare in the Arctic, more common farther south, and the arch could collapse within decades to thousands of years. One tour company offers visits, and Nunavut’s tourism office, previously unaware, plans to promote the site to high‑income travellers.

The passage discusses a research study on career transitions of lecturers and education personnel in Indonesian higher education institutions. It highlights that lecturers serving as campus leaders while maintaining teaching duties experience role conflicts and declining performance. Bureaucratic reforms have caused mismatches for education personnel between positions and actual work. The study uses Schlossberg's transition theory (4S factors: situation, self, support, strategies) and qualitative grounded theory methods to analyze adaptation experiences. Findings show reciprocal relationships among the 4S factors in adaptation, with transitions causing changes in behavior, role, learning, and perception. Unlike traditional career anchor theory suggesting one career anchor, this study found lecturers and education staff use two anchors: competence and managerial. The study's limitations include its qualitative nature preventing generalization and lack of demographic considerations.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on September 10, 2019, reporting that Bob Iger resigned from its Board of Directors on that date. A player discusses recovering from a head injury, noting concerns about getting hit into boards rather than direct head hits. The decision to undergo the CT scan arose after learning of another player's injury, and the player's family was supportive of his return.
Appeal of judgment for plaintiff affirmed with costs; trial judge's opinion.

This bibliometric study examined mathematics anxiety in mathematics education literature from 2013 to 2023 using the Scopus database. Analyzing 324 journal articles, the study found a steady increase in research output, peaking in 2022. Social Sciences (35.1%) and Psychology (30.7%) were the dominant subject areas. Network visualizations identified seven clusters linking math anxiety to psychological aspects (e.g., self-efficacy, emotions) and cognitive aspects (e.g., skills, problem-solving), primarily focusing on secondary and high school levels. Frontiers in Psychology was the most prolific journal, while Garcia-Santillan was the most productive author. The United States produced the highest number of publications and collaborative networks, with Germany receiving the highest citations. The University of Barcelona was the leading institution. The core theme of 'mathematics anxiety' and 'math anxiety' remained the most prevalent research focus throughout the decade.

North Korea warned ready to counter nuclear attacks, displaying missiles at Kim Il‑sung’s 105th anniversary parade; Kim Jong‑un relaxed. Choe said it would meet an all‑out war. Trump called it “foolish” and “looking for trouble”. China warned conflict could erupt with no winner; Chinese officials absent.

Gross margin was 58.8%, down from 59.8% year-over-year, reflecting acquisition-related costs from the Mellanox Technologies acquisition completed on April 27, 2020, for $7.13 billion. The acquisition contributed approximately 14% of total revenue and resulted in goodwill of $3.43 billion allocated to the Compute & Networking segment, bringing total goodwill to $4.19 billion. Graphics segment revenue was $2.09 billion, up 16% year-over-year, while Compute & Networking segment revenue was $1.78 billion, up 130% year-over-year. Revenue by platform included Gaming at $1.65 billion (up 26%), Data Center at $1.75 billion (up 167%), Professional Visualization at $203 million (down 30%), Automotive at $111 million (down 47%), and OEM and Other at $146 million (up 32%). Operating expenses increased 67% year-over-year to $1.62 billion, primarily due to the Mellanox acquisition and additional hiring. Cash and marketable securities were $10.98 billion at quarter-end, and the company paid $99 million in dividends. The company noted uncertainty regarding the ongoing impact of COVID-19 on its business.

The disclosed embodiments provide a detection model training method, apparatus and terminal device for training a model to detect a target object (e.g., a lesion) in images such as colorectal polyp images. The method starts from an initial training model consisting of an initial detection model (which includes a feature‑extraction module and a detection/classification module) and an adaptive model (which includes a domain‑classification module and optionally a gradient‑inversion module). A training sample comprises source‑domain data (labeled first images containing a first identifier for lesion presence and a second identifier for domain) and target‑domain data (unlabeled second images containing only a third identifier for domain). The initial detection model processes each first image to determine whether a lesion is present and, if present, its type and location, yielding a detection result; the adaptive model processes every image in the sample to determine the domain to which the image belongs, yielding a domain‑classification result. A loss function is computed from the detection result, domain‑classification result and the identifiers; it includes a detection loss (first error), a classification loss, a positioned‑regression loss (third error) and an adaptive loss (second error). The parameter values of the initial training model are then adjusted, typically by back‑propagation and gradient descent, to minimize the loss. The adjustment repeats until a stop condition (e.g., convergence or a set number of iterations) is reached, producing a final detection model. Because target‑domain images need not be labeled, the method enlarges the usable training set and reduces labeling cost, while the adaptive model eliminates domain‑specific differences so that the model trained on source data works accurately on target data. The embodiments also cover a training apparatus that implements the described units (model‑determining, sample‑determining, model‑processing, loss‑function, adjustment and detection units) and a terminal device comprising a processor and storage medium that store instructions to perform the method.

Enron's $3 billion Dabhol Power project in India faced escalating disputes as the Maharashtra State Electricity Board canceled its power purchase agreement and accused Enron of misrepresenting capacity. Enron denied the board had the right to rescind the contract and indicated it may sell its stake. Separately, news reports detailed Kenneth Lay's influence on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, with Chairman Curtis Hebert claiming Lay offered support in exchange for policy changes. The White House signaled Hebert would likely be replaced. California's energy crisis continued with political disputes between state leaders and the Bush administration over price controls and deregulation. Australian firms announced plans to invest in India's power sector despite the Enron controversy.

The passage describes three types of jump ball situations in basketball: defensive (opponent has advantage), even (equal chance), and offensive (team has advantage). Defensive strategies include early rotation, watching jumpers for telegraphed tips, and using alignments like box, diamond, and "Y" to protect the basket and contest tips. Even situations require boxing out, early anticipation, and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations. Offensive jump ball plays, often used with a height advantage, involve set plays such as double tap, post split, jumper fly, forward fly, spread, tandem, and loop to secure possession and transition into offense.

Apple removed multiple ICE-tracking apps, including ICEBlock, Eyes Up, and DEICER, from its App Store following claims by US Attorney General Pam Bondi that the tools endanger officers. Developers of the apps, Joshua Aaron and Mark, stated they will appeal the bans and continue operating via Google Play, arguing the apps constitute protected First Amendment speech. Legal experts consulted by WIRED confirmed the apps publish truthful information on matters of public interest. Digital rights researchers and Stanford policy researcher Pfefferkorn criticized Apple, highlighting the risks of centralized platform control and calling the removals “needless kowtowing.”

Tropical Depression 02W struck eastern Visayas on April 15, 2017 with 25‑knot winds, weakened over the Philippines, and became a remnant low over the South China Sea. NASA's Terra satellite captured it on April 17 near 14.9°N 116.9°E, about 230 nm west of Manila, moving west while wind shear and dry air are expected to prevent re‑intensification.

Alberta’s education minister said the province could allow parents to pay bus fees despite Bill 1 eliminating fees for students over 2.4 km. Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million shortfall from inflation, a $360,000 carbon levy and Bill 1; parents want to keep paying prior fees. Options include changing bell times, extending rural bus commutes (up to three hours) and moving urban bus stops. Board may contact the Ministry and could delay its April 12 deadline.

The Supreme Court is examining whether the double‑jeopardy clause bars separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Generally, convictions for a lesser‑included offense are prohibited, but Congress may indicate intent for multiple punishments. The parties agree Congress allowed cumulative punishment for 924(c) and its underlying crime, but dispute which statutory language provides that indication. Justices considered 924(c)(1)(D)(ii), which mandates a consecutive sentence notwithstanding any other law, and the “in addition to” phrasing that applies only to the underlying crime. They noted that 924(j) lacks the latter language, and charging 924(j) removes the separate predicate conviction, the consecutive‑sentence requirement, and the mandatory minimums. Arguments also touched on whether Congress’s intent can be inferred from the penalty scheme and whether the clear‑indication requirement reflects separation‑of‑powers or double‑jeopardy concerns. These issues were not fully briefed and seem unlikely to dominate the Court’s opinion.

Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for Texas Instruments devices is provided and subject to change without notice. It includes status, material type (preproduction prototypes not yet approved for full production), RoHS compliance values, lead finish/ball material options, moisture sensitivity level ratings with peak reflow temperatures, and part marking details. All technical and reliability data is supplied “as is” with no warranties; users are solely responsible for product selection, design, validation, and compliance with applicable standards, safety, and regulatory requirements. Resources are intended for skilled developers and may be revised or discontinued without notice. TI’s products are provided subject to TI’s Terms of Sale or other applicable terms.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) affects ~1% of the global population and currently lacks objective biomarkers. Researchers aim to develop a clinically applicable classifier using resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI, addressing challenges of accuracy, generalisability, across-session variability, and specificity. They used a large harmonized dataset from four institutions, applying LASSO with a voting method and spatial averaging of 100 classifiers. Two independent multi-disorder datasets were analyzed: a discovery set of 1,015 participants and a validation set of 683 participants. Mass univariate analysis showed reproducible diagnostic effects across datasets (r=0.597). LASSO classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy (AUC 0.876) on the discovery set and 77.3% accuracy (AUC 0.824) on the validation set, with sensitivity and specificity reported per site. Forty‑seven functional connections (FCs) were identified as important; 44 maintained their direction of difference in the validation set. Voting classifiers improved sensitivity and AUC (0.841) compared with LASSO, especially at lower‑performing sites. Analyses of laterality indicated an imbalance between hemispheres for seven regions of interest. Age matching partially influenced voting classifier performance, and sensitivity varied with disease severity. The study also explored whether the classifier could function as trait, state, and staging markers. The findings suggest rs‑FC biomarkers may aid SSD diagnosis and treatment development.

Amazon’s mobile accessory kit allows wireless earbuds to embed Alexa; the Jabra Elite 65t are among the first devices to use it and cost $170. Currently the Alexa integration works only on Android, with iOS support promised later.  

The earbuds cannot make phone calls, send texts, or use popular music services such as Spotify; only Amazon Music can be streamed by voice. Voice‑shopping works well and can reuse previous orders, but navigation, reminders, and timer/alarm notifications are absent, and the assistant cannot trigger auditory alerts for those functions.  

Compared with Google Assistant or Siri, Alexa in earbuds lacks features such as full‑length translation, detailed navigation, and the ability to read and reply to messages. It also does not support Drop‑In calls. Google Assistant can provide auditory notifications for reminders and timers, while Siri sounds alerts on the phone but not in the earbuds.  

Sound quality is praised as “one of the best” and HearThrough lets ambient sound in via a double‑tap, but there is no built‑in tracker to locate lost earbuds. Battery life is 5 hours per charge, with an additional 10 hours in the case—less than the 24‑hour total of Pixel Buds or AirPods. The earbuds fit comfortably and improve on the earlier Elite Sport model.  

Future updates (e.g., reminder support) are planned, but for now the Alexa experience in the Elite 65t is more limited than in Amazon’s smart speakers.

Shohei Ohtani was the Dodgers' starting pitcher in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS against the Phillies. During the 2025 regular season, he appeared in 14 games with a 1-1 record and 2.87 ERA, striking out 62 batters in 47 innings. This was his first-ever postseason pitching appearance. The game took place on October 4, 2025, at Citizens Bank Park, with Ohtani facing Phillies pitcher Christopher Sanchez.

Following the Oct. 1 Las Vegas concert shooting that killed 58 and injured over 500 while Jason Aldean performed, country music artists are debating firearms and gun‑control responsibility. Charlie Daniels called the event an “anomaly” and the shooter a “nut,” urging people not to let fear prevail. He supports NRA‑backed regulation of bump‑stock devices but opposes broader gun‑control measures, arguing many politicians lack firearms knowledge and citing Chicago’s strict laws as a counterexample. The NRA’s “N.R.A. Country” program links the industry to the gun‑rights group. Rosanne Cash wrote a New York Times essay urging musicians to confront the NRA; Daniels said he had not read it and commented “things happen.” Daniels will headline a Booth Amphitheatre show on Oct. 21.

Digital leaders view risk-taking and experimentation as essential strategies, adopting a learning organization mindset that values data for continuous feedback. They emphasize experimentation's learning value, even when goals are unmet, and encourage thoughtful planning to maximize success and learning. Recognizing individual development as crucial for long-term success, they prioritize critical thinking skills in training programs.

Using Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO) minute‑by‑minute solar radiation measurements from 1980 onward, the author examined atmospheric clarity. The record shows that except for periods after the El Chichón and Pinatubo eruptions, the maximum downwelling solar energy has remained essentially unchanged, contradicting a claim that the current stratosphere is unusually clear. Comparing the two‑year post‑eruption intervals with the non‑volcanic periods reveals a lower maximum and average solar radiation during volcanic times; the average total solar radiation fell by about 24.5 W m⁻². Clouds partially compensated, increasing downwelling radiation by roughly 7 W m⁻² compared with the expected loss of 31.3 W m⁻² if cloud cutting had remained proportional. However, a net loss of about 25 W m⁻² persisted. Temperature records from MLO and several Hawaiian stations covering the same periods show no measurable cooling despite the sustained 25 W m⁻² reduction in solar forcing. The author notes that this contradicts the common assumption that a drop in solar energy must cause temperature fall, and suggests the climate system may respond to changes in a self‑regulating way, citing the Constructal Law and Le Chatelier’s Principle. Data sources and methodology are described in the appendix.

The Hawk Offense combines a wing isolation, a high‑post shuffle cut and a weak‑side post‑up, resembling the UCLA offense. Defending it requires three core phases: (1) one‑on‑one wing isolation defense using on‑ball alertness and weak‑side “show” and “recover” actions; (2) high‑post shuffle‑cut defense by forcing the cutter behind the screen, employing show‑and‑recover and contact‑switch techniques; (3) down‑screen defense with show‑and‑recover and contact switches on the screen. For total disruption, teams employ an All‑Out “SOS” approach that includes a double‑team trap at the sideline wing, contact switches on the high‑post rub, coordinated rotations after passes out of the trap, and specific on‑ball, pass‑denial and helpside positions for each defender.

Madison Snap and William Francis were convicted and fined for wounding a mare that was trespassing in their oat field. The safety is a defensive back positioned deepest on the defense, serving as the last line against big plays. The two primary types are the free safety, who roams the middle of the field with speed for deep coverage, and the strong safety, who is stockier, lines up near the line, and focuses on run defense. Alternative terms include Rover for strong safety, Star for extra safety; historically the free safety was a defensive fullback and the strong safety a defensive halfback. Safeties must cover receivers, make tackles, run quickly, and communicate. Notable safeties include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, and Sean Taylor, with 17 safeties in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. An elite safety gives the defense confidence, creates turnovers, and can take away portions of the field.

Webster and colleagues found the Great Barrier Reef recovered from near‑extinction five times over the past 30,000 years. Fossil core data from 16 sites show it migrated seaward or landward 0.2–1.5 m per year in response to sea‑level changes, with five death events caused by exposure, sea‑level rise and sediment dumps. Current rates of sea‑surface temperature rise and ocean acidification appear faster than any past episode. The reef, a World Heritage site, is now suffering repeated bleaching linked to climate change; a 2016 heatwave killed nearly a third of its coral. Coral reefs support about a quarter of ocean life and act as nurseries for many fish species.

- Following the 2024 Arab Summit, the Bahraini foreign minister cited UNESCO (2018) data showing over 10 million Arab children (ages 5–15) are out of school, prompting the “Hope” initiative under King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa.  
- The report, prepared by Jaber Mustafa and Younis Bukhari, examines early‑childhood education (ECE) challenges in Arab conflict zones, using Syria as a case study.  
- Key significance points: (1) inclusive community integration, (2) restoration of hope, (3) mental‑health impacts (60.5 % of Syrian children meet criteria for a psychological disorder; 12.5 % depression, 11.5 % PTSD, 9.2 % anxiety among refugees in Turkey), (4) resilience through family and caregiver support, (5) educational‑psychosocial challenges, (6) contribution to long‑term national recovery, and (7) proactive education during conflict.  
- Literature findings: conflict displaces families, destroys schools (≈4,000 attacks on Syrian schools; one‑third damaged or converted for military use), and creates inequitable access for girls and children with disabilities; quality suffers from teacher turnover, resource shortages, and fragmented curricula.  
- UNICEF 2021 data: over two million Syrian children remain out of school, 90 % of the population lives below poverty, 2.6 million children are displaced; in Turkey, nearly 400,000 Syrian refugee children are out of school, with dropout driven by poverty, early marriage, and child labor.  
- Methodology: triangulation design using interviews (a parent, a child), a ten‑question survey, and a case study of Ahmed, a Syrian child in Alkhabor who receives 2–3 hours/week of communal learning in unsanitary conditions without electricity or internet.  
- Results: interviews revealed destroyed schools, constant trauma, limited resources, PTSD signs, community‑learning groups, and lack of psychological support; the child’s case highlighted limited study time, poor environment, need for consistent tutoring, and hope for education as a future pathway.  
- Proposed solutions: immediate remedial actions (emotional support for all and vulnerable groups, academic interventions) and proactive sustainable strategies culminating in the “Hope Initiative,” a fully integrated system combining short‑term measures (mobile education units, psychological services) with long‑term frameworks to sustain education and anticipate problems.  
- Conclusion: education in conflict zones is both a casualty and a beacon of hope; addressing the crisis requires immediate interventions and long‑term solutions through regional and international collaboration.
Jane Goodall died Oct 1 at 91; taught about bones, loss, waste; legacy includes chimp skeletons from 2018 Uganda photo.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced in Manhattan to 50 months (four years and two months) in federal prison and a $500,000 fine on two felony counts of transportation to engage in prostitution under the Mann Act. A jury convicted him of those counts but cleared him of the more serious sex‑trafficking and racketeering‑conspiracy charges, which carried a possible life sentence. Prosecutors had sought an 11‑year term; the defense had asked for no more than 14 months. In court Combs apologized to his victims, his children and his mother, calling his conduct “disgusting, shameful, and sick.” The judge said his history of good works could not wash away evidence that he had abused women physically, emotionally and psychologically, and praised the women who testified for “standing up to power.” A key witness described multiple beatings, and the defense argued the sexual encounters were consensual. One alleged victim, referred to as “Mia,” declined to appear after the defense sent a letter the judge called inappropriate. Combs’ legal team presented a video highlighting his family and community efforts, which the judge said did not outweigh the abuse shown in the case. Additional civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault, rape, drugging and other violence remain pending.

The passage explains the backtesting methodology for DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 futures expiration. It notes that the after‑expiration backtest for DAX 40 does not use a futures backtest; instead it applies a 100 % margin strategy, investing €100 000 from March 2000 and reinvesting at each quarterly expiration. Four trades per year are placed: entry at the close of the Friday when futures expire, exit one week later at the close of the following Friday, with no commissions or slippage.

Both contracts expire on the third Friday of March, June, September and December. During the expiration week, DAX 40 averages a 0.39 % gain with a 57 % win ratio, compared with 0.12 % for a random week; December shows the strongest performance and all months outperform a random week. Euro Stoxx 50 averages a 0.30 % gain with a 54 % win ratio, versus 0.18 % for a random week; the effect is smaller, with December best and June a notable loss.

The week after expiration shows a negative average return for DAX 40 of –0.10 % with a 47 % win ratio; September is the worst month (profitability 25 %), while March and December are positive. Markets are said to be more volatile during expiration week due to “pin” risk. The passage recommends the DAX 40 contract for its high trading volume and observes a positive futures expiration week effect for both indices.

In UC1825BEVM‑CVAL, a resistor‑capacitor‑diode RCD clamp limits voltage; values are found by testing, using Equation 30 (Vc = Kclamp·Np·s·(Vout+Vd)) with Kclamp≈1.5, and calculations from parasitic inductance and allowed change.

A method is provided for producing elastomeric compositions by dispersing hydrophilic carbon black (CB) particles in curable hydrophobic silicone pre-polymers. The method involves treating the hydrophilic CB particles with a dispersant that is miscible in the silicone pre-polymer and contains carbon-black-affinic moieties (e.g., amino, acrylate, or epoxy groups). The treated CB particles are mixed into the pre-polymer to form a dispersed composition, which is then cured via addition-curing or condensation-curing. The CB particles typically have high volatile matter content, acidic pH (≤5.0), high oxygen content, and specific zeta potentials and Raman spectral ratios. The dispersant is generally a branched, siloxane-based molecule (e.g., amino-silicone oil) with a low amine number to avoid inhibiting curing. Applications include intermediate transfer members for printing and sealants.

Design requirements for the ADS8860 ADC specify VS±=±15 V, VLVDD=5.3 V, VLVSS=GND, and ADC REFIN=5 V. The PGA848 front‑end uses three filters: a first EMI/RFI filter at the PGA input (customizable for bandwidth and antialiasing), a second filter formed by CFB (75 pF) in parallel with the PGA’s 6.67 kΩ feedback resistors, giving a cutoff of ~318 kHz (≈277 kHz at the high‑side resistor tolerance), and a third RC charge‑reservoir filter at the ADC inputs to reduce kickback and distortion. The combined PGA848 delivers a nominal –3 dB bandwidth of 318 kHz (277 kHz high‑side) with –0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. The ADS8860 requires a 0–5 V full‑scale input; PGA848 REF is set to 2.5 V, generated by feeding a REF6250 5 V reference through a 10 kΩ/10 kΩ ±0.05 % low‑drift divider and buffered by an OPA192 op‑amp configured with dual feedback (RF = 2 kΩ, CF = 2 nF, RISO = 20 Ω) providing ≈86° phase margin; the noninverting input includes a 1 kΩ/10 nF low‑pass filter to suppress divider noise. Power‑supply guidelines require ±15 V for input and output stages, clamp output supplies to input‑stage levels, and warn that voltages >40 V permanently damage the device. Layout recommendations stress symmetrical input paths, local 0.1 µF low‑ESR bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive traces from noisy ones, minimization of leakage and parasitic capacitance on DA_IN pins, keep‑out areas under input pins, and avoidance of thermal gradients. Simulation tools (TINA‑TI, PSpice‑for‑TI) are advised before layout, and documentation and support resources are listed.

Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co. is a 1964 Supreme Court decision involving a veteran’s seniority claim. The petitioner was hired as an apprentice machinist in 1951, drafted into the military, and returned in 1953. After completing his apprenticeship in North Little Rock, he sought a seniority date of November 3 1955. The District Court awarded him that seniority; the Eighth Circuit reversed, relying on Tilton v. Missouri Pac. R. Co. The Supreme Court reversed the Eighth Circuit, holding the petitioner was entitled to seniority as of November 3 1955 at North Little Rock, and remanded the case.

Zone forecasts for southern California covering July 3‑10 2018 show a warming trend with low clouds or fog in the mornings turning mostly sunny each day. An Excessive Heat Watch is posted for most inland valleys, mountains, and desert regions from Friday morning through Saturday evening. Temperatures rise from the mid‑70s to low‑80s at the coast early in the period to the mid‑80s to low‑90s by Friday, while inland valleys and deserts reach the upper 90s to low‑110s (e.g., 99‑104 °F inland, 107‑112 °F in the Coachella Valley, 112‑117 °F in the San Diego deserts). ESPN was at its peak in the early 2010s with 100 million cable/satellite subscribers paying $7 monthly, but by 2024 subscriber numbers declined to approximately 70 million, facing challenges from rising sports rights costs, streaming competition, and changing consumer behavior. To adapt, Disney launched ESPN+ in 2018 as a supplementary streaming service, later announcing flagship ESPN would go direct-to-consumer in 2025, and partnered with Warner Bros. Discovery and Fox in February 2024 to create Venu Sports, a joint venture sports streaming service launching fall 2024. ESPN's history includes its 1979 founding by Bill Rasmussen and his son Scott, corporate ownership evolution through Getty Oil, ABC, RJR Nabisco, CapCities Communications, and eventual 1996 merger with Disney (Hearst retains 20%), first affiliate fee negotiations in 1983-84, and growth through NFL acquisition, DBS expansion, and new channel launches. ESPN operates primarily as a "renter" of live sports rights (NFL, NBA, MLB) and is transforming from a B2B model (cable operators, advertisers) to a B2C direct-to-consumer approach, though profitability in streaming remains challenging.

IEX, launched to disrupt stock trading, remains a minor exchange with less than 3% of volume. It has spawned two concepts: IEX One, a market‑mechanic that uses a speed‑bump to subsidize the buy‑side at the expense of resting orders, and IEX Two, a visionary that aims to replace the SEC’s National Market System (NMS) by offering equal execution quality to all traders. The speed‑bump provides superior execution for large market orders, but it is an implicit fee that depends on NMS barriers and does not change IEX’s strategic position; it merely shifts a subsidy within the existing system. Observers note that IEX One is a niche product, while IEX Two must abandon the speed‑bump and confront the NMS to dominate the market. The author contends that IEX can only succeed by bypassing SEC regulation, delivering true liquidity, and balancing the interests of both buy‑ and sell‑side participants. The article notes the author has no financial position in IEX.

January added 200,000 jobs, keeping unemployment at 4.1 percent while average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent year‑on‑year. Economists said a tightening labor market and minimum‑wage increases in 18 states (4.5 million workers) lifted pay. Analysts caution single‑month data and emphasize long‑term averages. Job growth under President Trump (2.1 million jobs in 2017) mirrors the 2.2 million added in 2016 under President Obama. African‑American unemployment rose to 7.7 percent in January from 6.8 percent in December, though down from 15.5 percent in 2010; Hispanic unemployment fell to 4.9 percent from 12.9 percent. The January estimate will be revised twice; December was revised up to 160,000 from 148,000, while November was revised down to 216,000 from 252,000, with a margin of error of about 100,000. Estimates come from employer payroll and household surveys.

Women’s education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu Kashmir faces significant challenges, with female literacy at 51.9% overall and 40.8% in rural areas, compared to 73.3% for men. Key barriers include patriarchal culture, poverty, lack of motivation, early child marriages, limited educational facilities, and traditional norms. Both literate and illiterate women identified similar issues like family barriers, resource management, financial problems, and religious factors. Solutions include raising awareness through media and seminars, compulsory education legislation, and utilizing open and distance learning.

After ending a 20‑year marriage, the author faced unemployment and had little knowledge of her household’s bank accounts, investments or retirement assets. With a friend’s help she gathered documents, copied statements and built a budget. A financial planner introduced by her father guided her in retirement planning. At age 49 she bought her first car, learning to handle purchases previously managed by her husband. She re‑entered the workforce after a 15‑year gap, secured a steady job that provided income and health insurance, and now handles purchases, home repairs and financial decisions independently. Her retirement will be on her own terms.

Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke will travel to Maine this week to review the newly designated Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, which was created after a private donation of more than 87,000 acres in northern Penobscot County. The monument is endowed with $40 million in private funds and is intended to boost rural Maine’s economy without cost to state taxpayers. Governor Paul LePage opposes the designation and seeks federal repeal, while Senators Susan Collins and Angus King and Representative Chellie Pingree publicly support retaining it. Zinke, who grew up near Glacier National Park, will canoe on the East Branch of the Penobscot River and hear from local business owners who view the monument as an economic lifeline. LifeCLEF 2014 plant identification task used a dataset of 60,962 images from 19,504 observations of 500 species, collected by 1,608 contributors via a citizen science initiative. The task involved multi-image plant observation queries, combining images of the same individual plant. Ten research groups submitted runs using methods like Fisher Vector encoding, convolutional neural networks (CNN), and bag-of-visual-words (BoW). IBM AU's Fisher Vector-based runs achieved the highest scores, outperforming CNN and other approaches. Combining images from the same observation improved results. LeafScan and Flower categories yielded the best performance, while metadata like GPS was not effectively utilized. The challenge advanced from previous years by increasing species count and including multiple plant views.

The document lists terminal‑function tables for a Texas Instruments SoC (TMS320DM814x DaVinci™ Digital Media Processors).  It covers a Cortex‑A8 memory‑map reference region that is not part of the L4 Slow bus and a TILER extended addressing map that adds an extra 4‑GByte range using a 33rd address bit; this extended range is accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, while other masters can reach only a single 512‑MByte view through the base 4‑GByte region.  Boot configuration is governed by BTMODE[15:0] pins sampled at reset; sampled values set the boot‑mode order, GPMC timing/width/multiplexing, Ethernet PHY mode (via BTMODE[9:8]), and XIP options (via BTMODE[10]).  The tables enumerate each peripheral’s signal name, pin number, pin type (I, O, Z, S, GND, A), internal pull state (IPU, IPD, DIS), supply voltage, and de‑selected input state (DSIS).  Pin multiplexing is controlled by PINCNTLx registers through MUXMODE bits, with the default setting placing pins in tri‑state (MUXMODE = 0).  Peripherals include camera I/F, DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers, EMAC (MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII), GPIO groups GP0‑GP3, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SPI, USB, video input/output, and others.  The document also provides guidance on external pullup/pulldown resistors: boot‑configuration pins should have external resistors even when internal pulls exist; other pins need external resistors only when the internal pull does not match the required state; typical values are ~1 kΩ to oppose internal pulls and ~20 kΩ to supplement them.

The Controller and Auditor General’s 2015/16 report finds weaknesses in Tanzania’s procurement. MDAs spent Sh2.48 billion without tender‑board approval, and ten entitiesprocured works, goods and services worth Sh11.253 billion without valid contracts, violating Public Procurement Regulations 2013. Offensive switches in soccer (crossover runs) are exchanges of positions used to beat defenders. They can be “called” (verbal) or “natural” (no call) and may involve the ball or not. The basic (horizontal) switch consists of two players running diagonally across each other, forming an X, exchanging wing and inside forward duties; the vertical switch exchanges front‑to‑back positions. Both aim to create 2‑v‑1 or 2‑v‑2 situations, causing defender confusion. After completing the maneuver, players signal “Switch back” to return to their original positions.

MatterMech is a benchmark comprising 4,800 questions across eight nanomaterial synthesis subdomains, developed using 17,000 papers and evaluated on 14 LLMs. It employs MCQ and text-infilling metrics. Findings show that while LLMs excel at logical reasoning, they struggle with conceptual understanding and principle-based reasoning. Model scale and principle-guided prompting consistently improve performance. The benchmark identifies gaps between named entity recognition and logical reasoning abilities, along with performance variations across subdomains. A curated dataset, MatterDB, with 31,735 papers is also released.

Many people abandon New Year’s weight‑loss resolutions after January. Dr. Edith Mbagwu recommends using the SMART framework—Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, Time‑based—to set realistic goals. Specific goals define exact exercise days, calorie targets, exercise types and food choices. Measurable indicators include weight, body‑fat percentage and clothing size. Attainable and realistic goals require honest assessment of resources and time, and setting smaller milestones (e.g., burning 500 calories per day to lose one pound per week). Motivation—such as training for a race or fitting into certain clothes—helps maintain commitment. For more guidance, visit www.ochsner.org/info or call 225‑761‑5200.

The study aimed to identify difficulties in foreign language education at university caused by the shift to distance learning during the COVID‑19 pandemic. The population comprised undergraduate and graduate students of German and English (teaching, literature, translation) in the spring term of 2020‑2021; 294 of them responded to an online survey. The instrument included five demographic items and a 53‑item “distance education problems scale” with six subscales. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics and t‑tests.

The highest problem subscale was internet/computer issues (mean = 0.473) and the lowest was teacher‑related problems (mean = 0.147); the overall scale mean (0.284) indicated moderate difficulty. Specific high‑rating items included internet disconnection/freezing (0.707), poor connection (0.588), insufficient mutual communication (0.544), lack of motivation (0.694) and low active participation (0.639). Measurement/evaluation problems (mean = 0.255) centered on the inability to assess skill‑based gains (0.371). Male students reported higher student‑related problems than females; no differences were found by language studied. Students without prior training on distance‑education programs experienced more program‑related difficulties. Those lacking an independent study room or a home internet connection reported more problems across all subscales.

Conclusions emphasized that distance education is viewed as unsuccessful for foreign language teaching, with face‑to‑face education deemed more effective; materials, assessment, teacher proficiency, participation, and student preparation were identified as major issues. Recommendations include training for students (self‑discipline, responsibility, program use) and teachers (program use, assessment methods, material design, virtual classroom management) and implementing a hybrid model combining face‑to‑face and distance education.

The lecture discusses the quantization of the Dirac theory. Replacing commutators with anticommutators ensures a positive definite Hamiltonian and enforces fermionic statistics and the Pauli principle. The operators a and c create particles and antiparticles with spin-1/2, identical mass, and opposite charge. The conserved Noether charge from U(1) symmetry distinguishes particles from antiparticles. The Dirac theory predicted the existence of the positron, experimentally confirmed in 1932. Correlation functions for fermionic fields are derived, related to scalar field propagators with spinor factors. The momentum-space Feynman propagator is given by (γ·k - m + iε)^(-1). Dirac spinors can be reduced to chiral or Majorana fermions, to be discussed further.

Data transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS is pulled low and end at its rising edge. The host provides SCLK clocks to shift data in (SDI) and out (SDO‑x). Based on SCLK count (<32, =32, >32) the frame is short, optimal, or long; the device interprets the input shift register as a command at the end of an optimal or long frame. Input commands must be 32‑bit words; half‑word (HWORD) commands ignore the LSB of the 9‑bit address. Output data are shifted from the 32‑bit output shift register and can include device address, range, alarm flags and parity bits, as controlled by the DATAOUT_CTL_REG. The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI protocols (SPI‑00‑S to SPI‑11‑S) and optional dual‑SDO‑x or source‑synchronous (SRC) modes, with internal or external clock selection. Nine configuration registers (addresses 00h–28h) control device ID, reset/power‑down (write‑key protected), SDI/SDO protocol selection, data output format, input range, and alarm thresholds/hysteresis. The device integrates an analog front‑end, driver and reference, operates from separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, and offers NAP and power‑down low‑power modes. Application guidance covers industrial analog input modules, programmable alarm thresholds with hysteresis, decoupling requirements, and PCB layout practices separating analog and digital sections.

A study examined interactions between a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS) and lifestyle/environmental factors on Parkinson's disease (PD) age at onset (AAO) using data from 9,745 patients across three cohorts. MGS was inversely correlated with AAO in LRRK2-PD but not in idiopathic PD (iPD). Smoking was associated with later AAO in iPD, black tea with later AAO in LRRK2-PD, and caffeinated soda with earlier AAO in both. MGS interacted with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption in LRRK2-PD and with caffeinated soda and pesticide exposure in iPD, modifying AAO. The findings highlight gene-environment interactions in PD onset.

The disclosure provides a method and apparatus for periodic beam‑failure detection in 5G NR systems. A UE determines a measurement‑period length from the periods of periodic BFD reference signals (RSs) that are quasi‑co‑located (QCL) with the DMRS of the PDCCHs it monitors. Within each measurement period the UE evaluates a subset of those BFD RSs (e.g., CSI‑RS, SS or PBCH blocks) for signal quality against a threshold; if all fail, the UE reports a BF instance to a higher‑layer entity (e.g., MAC). The measurement‑period duration is based on the shortest such BFD RS periodicity, or on the maximum of that shortest periodicity and a specified value. A BF is declared after a predefined number N of consecutive BF instances. The document also describes handling of measurement periods without any transmitted BFD RS: the counter may be ignored or incremented as a BF instance. Example embodiments implement the method in a UE comprising processors and memory, and include flow diagrams and timing illustrations of BFD RS sequences, measurement periods, and beam‑failure recovery steps such as candidate‑beam selection and BFRQ transmission. The priority chain of the related patent applications is also listed.

MOTO is a computational framework for systematic mapping of local transition-state networks. It consists of three components: a multi-objective explorer proposing diverse initial configurations, a bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel using Hessian-vector products for efficient saddle point identification, and bidirectional saddle descent for connectivity certification. Benchmarks on atomistic spin systems demonstrate that Hessian-vector product methods match explicit-Hessian accuracy while reducing memory usage and computational time. Applications to Pd/Fe/Ir(111) spin systems and Ni(111) Cartesian systems demonstrate the framework's generality across different system types and potential energy surfaces.

The 2017 Google internal memo by James Damore argued that women are underrepresented in technology because of innate biological differences, claiming women have a stronger interest in people and are more prone to neuroticism, while men have a higher drive for status. The memo asserted these differences are fixed and unchangeable. However, recent psychological and neuroscientific research challenges this view: studies show men and women are more similar than different, many cognitive differences exist on a spectrum, and the notion of a distinct male or female brain is unsupported; brains display a mosaic of traits and are highly plastic. Evidence demonstrates that spatial cognition can be improved with training, the gender gap in spatial skills is shrinking, and stereotype threat—the anxiety caused by negative stereotypes—reduces performance and alters brain activity. Empowerment techniques and diversity training can mitigate stereotype threat, alter brain function, and change self‑critical mindsets. The passage concludes that diversity initiatives address environmental influences that Damore wrongly assumed to be innate.

Home hospital programs across the United States have halted new admissions as a Medicare waiver that permits hospitals to deliver inpatient care in patients’ homes is set to expire September 30. The waiver, first granted during the COVID‑19 pandemic and extended several times, is tied to a stopgap funding bill; Congress must reauthorize it or a government shutdown will cause the program to end. UMass Memorial Medical Center stopped admitting patients on Saturday and is caring for roughly 20 patients per day at home, while other systems—including Hackensack Meridian Health, ChristianaCare, and Mass General Brigham—have also paused or reduced their census. CMS instructed hospitals to discharge or return patients to medical facilities by midnight Tuesday without congressional action. An estimated 1,000 home‑hospital beds exist nationwide, concentrated in capacity‑constrained regions. A bipartisan bill to extend the waiver for five years is under consideration, but leaders say tying the extension to continuing resolutions limits investment and creates uncertainty.

The study examines EFL pre-service teachers' and teacher educators' perceptions of ICT and CALL integration in Vietnamese tertiary initial teacher education. Findings indicate a high presence of opportunity to learn CALL-related knowledge among pre-service teachers (M=3.05), particularly in digital media technology competencies and ICT pedagogies (M=3.33), with strong emphasis on resource discovery, archiving lessons, and information exchange. However, less opportunity was reported for designing blended learning modules (M=3.11), troubleshooting equipment (M=2.28), and supervising online work (M=2.64).

Factors influencing ICT integration include: individual educator obstacles (limited skills, confidence, and fear of change); infrastructure problems (unstable internet, unreliable equipment, slow technical support); pre-service teacher-related barriers (attitude and disengagement); and inconsistent institutional policies lacking official requirements or guidelines for CALL technology integration. The study adopts Hong's (2010) theoretical framework, which identifies CALL teacher education factors, individual teacher factors, and contextual factors as key influences on technology integration. The findings suggest a need for continuing professional development for educators, stronger institutional support, and official policies to guide ICT integration into initial teacher education programs. Limitations include the small sample size and focus on a single Vietnamese institution, limiting generalizability.

In Flinn’s Estate (Pa. 1932), the Supreme Court decided when intact value of trust assets must be fixed to apportion undistributed earnings between life tenants and remaindermen. Senator William Flinn died February 19, 1924, leaving a residuary estate of which 60 % was placed in trust for his children (Mary Flinn Lawrence, Mrs. Patterson, and Ralph E. Flinn) while the remaining 39 % was outright to other heirs. The dispute involved stocks (Gulf Oil, Union Trust, Colonial Trust, and Booth & Flinn Co.) owned at death or later transferred. The court held that for assets owned at the testator’s death intact value is fixed as of the date of death, so life tenants are entitled to earnings accruing from that date. For stock held by Booth & Flinn Co., a separate legal entity, and received as a dividend in January 1925, the proper intact value is the book value at the time of receipt, not the death date. The lower‑court method of averaging yearly earnings on a per‑diem basis to determine undistributed earnings was upheld. The decree was affirmed as modified.

The article argues that global citizenship education (GCE) offers limited insight into current international conflicts such as the war in Ukraine and rising tensions with China. It contends that GCE, despite its focus on global issues and participatory citizenship, lacks concepts to explain why states engage in violent conflict or the conditions for peaceful cooperation. The authors suggest supplementing GCE with theories of international politics from political science—specifically realism, regionalism, and institutionalism. Realism explains conflict through state power and security competition; regionalism shows how economic integration can contain rivalry; institutionalism highlights how international organizations shape cooperation. The article outlines that these perspectives help students understand why conflicts arise, how cooperation occurs, and how citizens can influence foreign policy. It proposes that teaching should broaden GCE to include military and economic security, use historical examples, address media manipulation, and emphasize that states solve problems. The authors maintain GCE's values of peaceful cooperation and global engagement but argue for expanding its scope to incorporate international politics insights and citizen participation in national foreign policy.

Between November 11 and 20, 1918, a series of diplomatic telegrams documented reactions to the signing of the Armistice. President Woodrow Wilson announced the armistice, stating America’s goals had been achieved and promising to aid democracy worldwide. U.S. Secretary of State Robert Lansing sent congratulatory messages to the British and French foreign secretaries, praising their nations’ steadfastness. The French, Japanese and Greek governments replied with thanks, emphasizing the United States’ crucial contribution, the enduring alliance and hopes for future cooperation, including a Society of Nations. Wilson also sent a personal message to British Prime Minister Lloyd George expressing admiration for his recent address.

The study explored integrating music notation software (Sibelius) into a general music education course at a Caribbean university (University of Trinidad and Tobago) for pre-service teachers. Using a mixed-methods phenomenological approach, 24 students (22 female, 2 male) from Bachelor of Education Primary and Early Childhood Care and Education programs participated. Data collection included a questionnaire and a practical assignment requiring participants to compose eight bars of music in specified time signatures.

Results indicated successful integration: all participants completed the assignment to 90% accuracy, and the majority reported the software enhanced their understanding of music concepts. Most participants (67%) supported continued use of technology, though 75% indicated they required additional training. Half reported comfort using the software, and approximately half expressed concern about applying it during practicum.

The study concluded that music software positively impacts student performance and comprehension, supports 21st-century learning approaches, and aligns with the UN Sustainable Development Goal of quality education. Given COVID-19's impact on educational delivery, integrating technology in teacher training has become increasingly critical.

Four recommendations emerged: continued use of music software as an introductory contemporary strategy; implementation of progressive training programs for instructors and students; introduction of technology assessment criteria in practicum rubrics; and inclusion of technology-focused learning outcomes in course assessments.
