Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and archival Hubble images, a Northwestern‑led team identified the red supergiant progenitor of supernova SN2025pht in the spiral galaxy NGC 1637, about 40 million light‑years away, just before it exploded on June 29 2025. The star was intrinsically roughly 100 000 times more luminous than the Sun but was hidden beneath an extremely thick, carbon‑rich dust envelope that dimmed its visible light by over a factor of 100 and made it appear as the reddest such progenitor ever observed. This JWST observation is the first confirmed detection of a supernova progenitor star and suggests that many massive red supergiants explode while obscured by dust, explaining why they are rarely seen before explosion. The upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope may help uncover additional dust‑enshrouded massive stars nearing detonation.

The passage introduces the "Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model" for interpreting ventricular repolarisation on ECGs. This model simplifies the heart as an egg-shaped mass and views repolarisation as a signal expanding from its centre (Wilson Central Terminal). It explains how this process generates the T-wave and accounts for abnormalities like ST elevation/depression and various T-wave morphologies based on the location of heart damage relative to the centre. The text argues that current ECG interpretations, particularly the use of the corrected QT interval (QTc), are flawed, and proposes that the interval from the start of the Q-wave to the T-wave peak (QTp) is a more reliable measure for assessing arrhythmia risk and medication effects. It suggests that the entire repolarisation process should be viewed as a unified event rather than separate components. Future work will explore the U-wave origin and apply the model to atrial repolarisation.

A patent disclosure relates to methods and systems for creating a virtual game environment from a real-world scene by selecting and arranging physical objects to form a physical model, scanning the model to obtain a digital three‑dimensional representation, converting the representation into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual construction elements, and defining game‑controlling elements based on physical properties of the objects. The disclosure also includes an interactive game system with a capturing device, display, processor, and data storage to perform the method, a data processing system and computer program product for executing the method, and a cyclic interactive game system where game play outcomes initiate new cycles of environment creation and play. Additional aspects include recognizing known physical objects to create virtual objects and modify the environment, a method for voxelizing a surface representation by mapping points on surface elements to voxels, and a method for identifying a target color from a predetermined set representing an input color using a bounded search in color space. The virtual toy construction model can be stored in LXFML format. The interactive game system may be integrated into a single mobile device and may include a physical playable character model with tool models that translate into virtual powers or skills. The disclosure aims to provide computationally efficient conversion processes and a closer link between physical and virtual game play.

The article investigates the experiences of leaders of education‑related undergraduate programmes in further education (FE) colleges in England. Drawing on Hodgson and Spours’s (2009) four‑level lifelong‑learning ecology (macro, exo, meso, micro), it describes how policy initiatives from the 1990s and 2000s – including post‑Dearing expansion, foundation degrees, and widening‑participation agendas – have produced a diverse range of provision validated or franchised by higher‑education institutions (HEIs). The macro layer reflects national policy and structures; the exo layer covers local institutional relationships with employers and HE partners; the meso layer focuses on programme leaders as keystone species who provide high‑quality, personalised support; the micro layer highlights the diverse, non‑traditional learner base and the social‑justice mission of these programmes.

The study, funded by the British Education Studies Association, used an online questionnaire (70 respondents, 14 from FE colleges) followed by 11 semi‑structured interviews (four with FE programme leaders). Findings show that most FE programme leaders entered the role informally rather than via formal application; most hold master’s degrees but few have doctorates; most have post‑16 teaching qualifications and a minority hold Higher Education Academy fellowships. FE teams are small (average three permanent staff) and leaders often combine teaching with line‑management responsibilities.

Three core responsibilities were identified: administrative/organisational duties linked to colleges and validating HEIs; academic support for learners (including small cohort sizes and mixed‑level teaching); and pastoral care, with leaders acting as the main point of contact for students. The role is ill‑defined, with programme leaders relying on craft wisdom and often unable to undertake scholarship or continuing professional development. Tensions arise from competing macro, exo, meso and micro demands, such as pressure to conform to FE regulations while delivering HE‑level culture, and limited sightlines beyond institutional confines.

The authors argue that programme leaders function as keystone species anchoring local learning ecologies, but their effectiveness is constrained by insufficient opportunities for research, external engagement and professional development. Recommendations include fostering sightlines through greater research activity, partnerships with employers and other institutions, and enhanced support for scholarly work. The article concludes that programme leaders are essential to the health, sustainability and success of FE‑based undergraduate provision, and that further research is needed to understand and address the challenges they face.

UAE announced Mars 2117 Project to build first inhabitable Mars settlement by 2117. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al‑Maktoum unveiled it at 5th World Government Summit in Dubai on 14 February; Elon Musk attended. Project will partner with research institutions, focus on faster travel, start with Emirati scientists, expand. UAE plans launch its Mars probe in 2021. Nigerian couple Gbenga Ogundele (aka Benson Ogundele) and his wife Mojisola Popoola were sentenced in U.S. federal court to a combined 252 months in prison for orchestrating an internet‑dating fraud scheme that defrauded victims of millions of dollars. Ogundele received 234 months and Popoola 18 months, each followed by three years of supervised release, with Popoola’s supervised release to be served in home detention. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft, ordered to forfeit $2,195,103.36, and Popoola ordered to forfeit $165,000 and pay restitution of $34,100. The conspiracy operated from January 2011 to May 18 2015, using online dating websites to form romantic relationships and then soliciting money through false stories such as fake hospital bills, travel expenses and foreign business problems. Members opened “drop accounts” to receive payments ranging from $1,720 to $50,000 and laundered the funds by transferring money among accounts, obtaining cashier’s checks and writing checks to individuals. Co‑conspirator Victor Oyewumi Oloyede was sentenced to 234 months; Babatunde Emmanuel Popoola (Moji Popoola’s brother) received 12 years and was ordered to pay $465,170.76 restitution; Olusegun Charles Ogunseye, Olufemi Wilfred Williams and Adeyinka Olubunmi Awolaja Jr. each pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. Funmilayo Joyce Shodeke pleaded guilty to operating an unlicensed money‑transmitting business and was sentenced to 13 months’ probation and ordered to forfeit $29,900. The case was prosecuted by U.S. Attorney Rod J. Rosenstein and the FBI.

The passage discloses a compound represented by Chemical Formula 1 and an organic light emitting device that includes the compound in one or more organic material layers between a first electrode and a second electrode. The compound is described with various aryl, heterocyclic, and other substituents, and multiple synthesis examples are provided. Performance data for devices using the compound as an electron‑transport layer show lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime compared to devices employing comparative compounds.

GPS-directed truck traffic on Arkansas 43 through Ponca, Arkansas, has sharply increased, causing repeated runaway‑truck crashes on a steep, winding 2‑mile stretch north of the town. Since early 2015, seven trucks have wrecked there, including six tractor‑trailers and a dump truck; drivers suffered minor injuries and one crash contaminated the Buffalo River with diesel. The route drops 1,300 ft over 4 mi from the Arkansas 103 intersection, appearing as a straight line on mapping services and masking its steepness and curves. Independent drivers hauling loads such as beverages, canned goods and detergents frequently choose the road, contributing to the accidents. The Arkansas Highway and Transportation Department plans to post “Crooked and steep next 3 miles” warning signs near the intersection within the next month or two and is re‑evaluating further measures. Officials advise drivers hauling more than 30,000 lb or traveling in wet or snowy conditions to avoid the route.

This protocol describes a descriptive, register‑based cohort study using the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register (DHR) to analyse trends in revision surgery for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) from 1995‑2022. Revisions will be classified as DAIR, one‑stage exchange or two‑stage exchange, and yearly numbers, percentages by time since primary (<4 weeks, 4‑12 weeks, >12 weeks) and the risk of a second revision will be reported using Cox regression adjusted for calendar time, age and sex. Inclusion: all adults (≥18 y) receiving primary THA; exclusion: hemiarthroplasty or simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty. Data come from the mandatory DHR, which has completeness of 96.9 % for primary THA and 92.3 % for revisions. Strengths include the long observation period and simultaneous analysis of all three revision approaches; limitations include reliance on surgeon‑reported PJI diagnosis and possible incomplete reporting from private clinics. No external funding was received; investigator salaries are covered by the orthopaedic department. The preprint is not peer‑reviewed.

A floor cleaner comprising a vacuum source, a supply tank for cleaning fluid, a distribution nozzle, a suction inlet, and a recovery tank. The recovery tank has a tank body with a lower end wall, a sidewall extending upwardly from the lower end wall, an inlet duct extending upward from the lower end wall, a perforated strainer movable from a lowermost position to a removed position, and a shut‑off float that closes the suction air outlet when fluid reaches a high level. The strainer engages the inlet duct, and the tank includes a removable cover with a suction air outlet, a baffle that redirects airflow downward, and a filter with chamfered sidewalls that can be withdrawn by a single tab. The floor cleaner also has a body pivotally coupled to a base about a first axis between an upright storage position and an inclined operating position, and about a second steering axis orthogonal to the first. The base includes wheels, a brushroll rotatable about an axis parallel to the first axis, two squeegees, rollers, and a removable brushroll cover operable by two opposed actuators. The brushroll comprises a hydrophobic textile cleaning medium made of tufted fibers of two different diameters, the larger fibers providing agitation and the smaller fibers providing wiping. A rechargeable battery is housed in a chamber behind the handle axis, and the arrangement of the battery, supply tank, recovery tank, motor and handle positions the center of gravity behind the handle axis and generally along the steering axis for balanced handling. The distribution nozzle sprays fluid forward of the base and is illuminated by LEDs visible to the user. The recovery tank is retained in a recess of the body by a latch and projections that prevent unwanted release when the body flexes. The floor cleaner includes a link forming a yoke that couples the body to the base, providing steering control by rotating the body about the steering axis.

On July 2, 2018, the Philippine national basketball team lost to Australia 89-53 in a 2019 FIBA World Cup qualifier at the Philippine Arena in Bocaue, Bulacan. During the match, the Philippines was outplayed, with Australia shooting 61.5% from the floor and 13-of-26 from three-point range. After a shove by RR Pogoy, a brawl erupted, involving punches, chairs, and water bottles from both players and fans. Both teams apologized: the Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas (SBP) regretted breaching Filipino hospitality, and Australia apologized for its role. Head coach Chot Reyes defended the team, emphasizing brotherhood and understanding within the circle. The author argues the Philippines was more at fault and calls for accountability, suggesting FIBA will impose sanctions. The passage concludes that the incident damaged the Philippines' image and urges the team to learn from this for future competitions.

The Give & Go offense uses ball handlers in 2‑1‑2 spread, with the post on the weakside. O1 passes to O2, who looks to feed O1 cutting to the basket; if lane is denied, O2 dribbles out and repeats action. When wing is overplayed, a back cut is used. If defender plays soft, wing turns the corner and drives; spin or behind‑the‑back dribble beats defender cutting off lane. When cutter is unavailable, the post steps out as a pressure release and can feed cutter or back cut. Weakside players may exchange positions or set down/back screens to occupy sagging defenders, but screens must be stationary to avoid fouls.

Leam Richardson dismissed reports of a post‑match tunnel incident after Wigan’s game with Fleetwood, describing it as a brief clash between striker Ivan Toney and defender Nathan Pond that the two laughed off after. He said it lasted about three seconds, was not comparable to the Old Trafford “Milkgate”, and that he himself walked away from it. Richardson noted Toney is likely to start Tuesday’s FA Cup replay against AFC Fylde, with Wigan aiming to win and advance to a third‑round tie at Premier League side Bournemouth.

This passage reports a study examining Turkish teachers' opinions on culturally responsive education. Using Q methodology, 21 teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa sorted 30 statements about cultural responsiveness. Analysis revealed three factors: Unification (emphasizing global citizenship and unity), Student Support (focusing on equality and cultural competence), and Teacher Support (highlighting professional development and curriculum integration). Teachers agreed that students' cultural competence skills should be increased and life practices for general culture are presented, while disagreeing on measures against discrimination and viewing different cultures as a threat. The study concludes that the Turkish education system values diversity but has not fully developed a culturally responsive system, with inequalities persisting. Recommendations include increasing teacher training, supporting student expression, and promoting cultural awareness.

Progressive (PGR) is the fourth‑largest U.S. auto insurer and a top‑20 home insurer. Each month it publishes a detailed dashboard with key metrics. In February 2018 it reported a combined ratio of 87.8%, a 2.6‑point improvement year‑over‑year, and net income of $129 million (4% lower than Feb 2017). Net earned premiums were $2,204.7 million, up 19% YoY; year‑to‑date earned premiums rose 18% to $4,894.3 million. The insurer raised $1,083.4 million net proceeds from a $600 million senior‑note issuance and 500,000 Series B preferred shares, and added $70 million of net premiums by expanding commercial auto coverage for an Uber subsidiary in three states. It targets a group‑wide combined ratio below 95% and expects book‑value growth >10% and EPS in the upper part of a $2.50‑$4.30 range. Based on current and projected metrics the intrinsic value is estimated at $48 per share currently and $50‑$54 forward; the author views the stock as slightly overvalued. The FY 2018 dividend is projected between $0.76 and $1.85 per share.

The Dual Momentum strategy, introduced by Gary Antonacci, combines absolute momentum (an asset’s own price change over a chosen period) with relative momentum (its performance versus other assets). It selects the security with the highest relative momentum among those that have a positive absolute momentum for a long position, and the worst‑performing security among those with a negative absolute momentum for a short position. The approach originated from Jagadeesh and Titman’s 1993 research on relative momentum, and Antonacci extended it by adding absolute momentum in his 2012 book “Dual Momentum Investing.” Implementation typically uses ETFs that track broad indices; each month the investor compares two or more securities, buys the strongest if its absolute momentum is positive, and holds bonds when absolute momentum is negative. Two examples illustrate the method: comparing the S&P 500’s 10% gain with gold’s 5% gain leads to buying the S&P 500, while comparing crude oil’s 10% decline with natural gas’s 5% decline leads to shorting crude oil. Back‑testing of Antonacci’s Global Equities Momentum model shows it outperformed a 45/28/27 global allocation, had lower drawdowns and only about 1.5 trades per year, indicating higher risk‑adjusted returns and less volatility than a simple buy‑and‑hold portfolio. The strategy also applies to sector rotation by ranking ETFs by absolute momentum and rotating into the best performers.

The Break, a longtime restaurant and billiards hall in Birmingham’s Five Points South, will be demolished for high‑rise apartments. Former patron Donnell Head welcomes the change, citing the venue’s decline and hoping new luxury apartments will revive the area. Some residents oppose luxury apartments, citing rising rents and seeking affordable housing. No closure date has been set; management was unavailable.

US researchers studied more than 10 million secondary students over 13 years and found that a 0.5 °C rise in average annual temperature correlated with a 1 % drop in exam scores. In the UK, June’s typical temperatures above 21 °C coincide with most exams, and the scarcity of air‑conditioning may not buffer the heat effect. The academic year follows a September‑July pattern used by schools, universities and Westminster, making change difficult. However, UK grading adjusts yearly based on cohort performance, offsetting any long‑term disadvantage from hot summers.

The advance-decline indicator is a market breadth tool that plots the cumulative difference between daily advancing and declining stocks within an index. It measures market sentiment by showing whether more stocks are rising or falling, confirms current trends, and can signal potential reversals when it diverges from the index direction. The indicator is calculated as: Current Day's Advancing Stocks minus Current Day's Declining Stocks, added to the Previous Net Advances. A backtest on SPY using this indicator produced 229 trades with an average gain of 0.6% and a profit factor of 1.55, below the 1.75 minimum threshold. The authors concluded the advance-decline indicator did not prove effective for creating profitable trading strategies and suggested using other oscillating indicators like RSI, Williams %R, or IBS instead.

Dive operators are divided over the impact of the ex‑HMAS Tobruk being scuttled on her side. Hervey Bay Dive Centre and Dive Hervey Bay were chosen for wreck diving. Dive Hervey Bay owner Glenn Bowman says the side‑landing could cut revenue up to 50 % and blocks most divers from starboard, while Hervey Bay Dive Centre owner Ed Gibson says open divers can still enjoy the wreck; tourism will not suffer. After 15 days of settlement talks in Washington failed, California Governor Gray Davis said the state would pursue an $8.9 billion refund from electricity suppliers in court. A federal mediator indicated the state was likely owed closer to $1 billion. Analysts also warned of risks to the stability of California's power grid.

Rapid advancement of large language models and generative AI is reshaping finance, healthcare, and education while creating unprecedented legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, deepfakes, and amplified bias. Existing regulatory and voluntary efforts—such as EU, US, and Chinese AI legislation and corporate responsible‑AI policies—aim to align AI development with fundamental rights, inclusiveness, safety, transparency, and accountability. Nonetheless, macro‑level gaps between the technology industry and governments, together with the lack of international consensus, produce fragmented regulations that raise compliance costs and impede innovation. At the micro level, the complexity of LLMs means that certain risks, such as jailbreaking prompts, may only surface after users encounter them, complicating timely regulation. To address these issues, the passage advocates a governance approach that combines top‑down partnership among policymakers, industry, and academia with bottom‑up involvement of developers and users, emphasizing forward‑looking rules, transparent reporting of identified problems, and social‑computing tools to monitor community needs and update policies in real time.

Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1942, Volume II Europe is released as an ebook by the Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State, making the series lighter, portable, searchable, and usable offline while preserving the content of the printed edition. The paper presents a framework for learning Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf) by combining it with Boolean Set Cover. The authors treat Boolean operators differently from temporal operators, using Boolean Set Cover to construct formulas from enumerated LTLf components, enabling larger and more expressive formulas than direct enumeration allows. They implement this approach in a tool called Bolt, along with a benchmark suite of over 15,000 LTLf learning tasks. Experiments demonstrate that Bolt significantly outperforms state-of-the-art tools (Scarlet and a GPU algorithm) in both wall-clock time and formula size, solving more tasks and returning smaller formulas. The authors argue that Boolean Set Cover is a fundamental problem with applications beyond LTLf learning, and they provide a greedy beam-search algorithm with divide-and-conquer techniques to solve it approximately and efficiently.

The passage explains the specialized positions that make up the offense in American football. The offense’s goal is to advance the ball, score touchdowns, or kick field goals. The quarterback is the leader, handling every play, making quick decisions to throw or hand off, and can change the play at the line of scrimmage with an audible. The running back carries the ball on rushing plays, catches passes, blocks, and must secure the ball while finding gaps. The tight end is a hybrid receiver‑lineman, versatile enough to block and catch, with “attached” tight ends lining up on the line and “sniffer” (H‑back) tight ends playing off the line and often used in motion. The offensive line consists of five players—two tackles, two guards, and a center—who block for both runs and passes; they are typically the biggest athletes and are generally not eligible to catch passes. Offensive tackles protect the outer edges and the quarterback’s blind side (the left tackle for right‑handed quarterbacks). Guards line up between the center and tackles, frequently double‑team or pull on runs. The center, positioned in the middle, touches the ball every play and acts as the O‑line captain, communicating defensive alignments to teammates. Wide receivers primarily catch passes, run routes, change direction quickly, and block for the run; they are categorized as split end/X (big, physical, press‑coverage), flanker/Z (fast, lines up a yard back), and slot receiver (smaller, lines up inside, beats safeties or linebackers). Each position has distinct responsibilities that together enable the offense to move the ball and score.

New research by Cornell professor Adam Anderson, published in Psychological Science, shows that eye expressions convey emotions. Participants accurately identified six expressions—sadness, disgust, anger, joy, fear, and surprise—and matched them to mental states from features such as eye openness, eyebrow distance, and wrinkles. Narrowed eyes, which enhance visual discrimination, were linked to emotions like suspicion and disapproval, while open eyes, which expand visual sensitivity, were tied to emotions like curiosity and fear. The study found the eyes are more robust indicators of emotion than other facial regions. The work supports Darwin’s hypothesis that facial expressions originated for sensory function and later became tools for social communication. Anderson’s co‑author is Daniel H. Lee of the University of Colorado Boulder.

COVID‑19 pandemic increased antibiotic consumption in India, contributing to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). About 90 % of antibiotic sales are non‑regulatory, and 216.4 million extra antibiotic doses were consumed during the first wave; 16.29 billion antibiotics were sold in 2020. High‑priority pathogens identified by WHO include Enterobacteriaceae, especially Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, which show carbapenem and extended‑spectrum β‑lactamase (ESBL) resistance; colistin is the last‑resort drug but resistance has emerged.

Unmetabolised antibiotics enter sewage systems, and wastewater treatment plants in India are largely absent or inadequate, allowing resistant bacteria to spread into aquatic environments.

The study isolated antibiotic‑resistant Enterobacteriaceae from untreated wastewater in the Western Uttar Pradesh (WUP) region. Fifteen samples were collected in triplicates (2020‑2021) from three zones covering metropolitan and non‑metropolitan cities (Zone 1: Ghaziabad, Noida, Sahibabad; Zone 2: Agra, Hathras, Aligarh; Zone 3: Meerut, Bulandshahar, Bijnor). A total of 150 isolates were obtained: E. coli 93 (62 %), K. pneumoniae 36 (24 %), other Enterobacteriaceae 12 (8 %) and mixed populations 9 (6 %). Isolates were identified biochemically and confirmed by VITEK; antimicrobial susceptibility was tested against 19 antibiotics in eight classes by disc diffusion and broth microdilution.

Of the 150 isolates, 39 (26 %) were susceptible to all agents except ampicillin, and 111 (74 %) were resistant to one or more antibiotics. Among the resistant isolates, 88 (79.3 %) produced ESBL. Multidrug‑resistant (MDR) profiles were observed in 57.14 % of E. coli, 28.57 % of K. pneumoniae and 5.71 % of Pantoea agglomerans. Overall MDR prevalence was 74 %. Carbapenem resistance ranged from 37 % to 59 % across zones. Zone 1 showed the highest overall MDR, with the highest resistance in K. pneumoniae; Zone 3 had the highest MDR in E. coli. Colistin resistance was detected in some isolates, representing an emerging threat.

The findings indicate that indiscriminate antibiotic use during the COVID‑19 pandemic has elevated AMR levels in Indian wastewater, with high resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, quinolones and carbapenems. Approximately 80 % of isolates were MDR, including resistance to last‑resort agents such as colistin. Inadequate wastewater treatment and direct discharge of untreated sewage exacerbate environmental AMR and pose a human health risk. The study underscores the need for regular surveillance of AMR in wastewater and receiving water bodies, molecular characterization of resistance genes, and a one‑health approach to mitigate the global spread of AMR.

PLL and analog supplies should use ferrite beads and capacitors (minimum 0.1 µF, smallest body size, 0201 preferred, no larger than 0402) placed close to device pins; a Pi filter (capacitor before the bead) is recommended. PLL pins close together may share a supply while analog pins need individual filters. Bulk capacitors (≥10 µF) are advised for every ~10 power pins. Excessive capacitance can slow power‑up ramp and affect sequencing.

The device provides multiple reset types: Power‑On Reset (POR), External Warm Reset (RESET), Emulation Warm Reset, Watchdog Reset, Software Global Cold and Warm Resets, Test Reset (TRST), and Local Resets for individual modules. Reset priority from highest to lowest is: POR, external warm, emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold/warm, test, local. POR sequence requires supplies and clocks stable before de‑asserting the POR pin; during POR all pins except emulation go Hi‑Z, PRCM asserts reset and starts PLLs in bypass. Warm reset similarly resets all modules except test/emulation, EMAC switch (optional) and PLLs; BTMODE pins are latched on release. RSTOUT_WD_OUT reflects reset state and is 3‑stated during POR/RESET unless BTMODE[11] = “0”. Pin behavior during reset puts most I/Os into Hi‑Z; DDR address/control pins are 3‑stated then driven to pull values after reset. Reset isolation is supported for the PCI Express and EMAC switch.

Device clocks are generated from DEV and AUX inputs (crystal with internal oscillator or 1.8 V LVCMOS) and a high‑quality differential SERDES clock. PLLs (12 top‑level plus embedded) multiply reference clocks; all start in bypass. SYSCLKs are derived from PLLs through the PRCM and feed individual modules (e.g., ARM Cortex‑A8, C674x DSP). Clocks must meet specified frequency limits and voltage levels; slew rates are 4 V/ns for inputs.

Interrupts are handled by the ARM AINTC (up to 128 requests) and the C674x DSP interrupt controller (12 prioritized interrupts from 128 events, with multiplexing options). Debug support includes IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, AET (hardware breakpoints, watchpoints, counters, state sequencing), and trace (Cortex‑A8 and system level) exported via ETB or a 5‑pin trace interface.

Ethernet MAC Switch provides a 3‑port gigabit switch supporting MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII with a single MDIO interface for PHY configuration. GPIO modules (four, up to 128 pins) support input/output, interrupts, and open‑drain operation. GPMC functions as a glueless memory controller for NOR/NAND flash, SRAM, and custom logic, with an associated Error Locator Module for BCH‑based error detection. HDMI 1.3a transmitter requires TMDS differential pairs routed for 100 Ω differential and 60 Ω single‑ended impedance; DDC and CEC use standard I2C pull‑ups and ESD protection. HDVPSS offers dual display pipelines and a configurable video input port, plus an HDMI transmitter and video DACs with layout guidelines. Four I2C modules comply with Philips I²C‑bus spec v2.1, support 10–400 kbps, 7/10‑bit addressing, and multimaster modes with 32‑byte FIFOs.

The Court of Appeals of Indiana affirmed convictions of Eric Simmons and Anthony Davis for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine in excess of three grams. The court rejected arguments that individual sales under three grams couldn't be aggregated and that jury verdicts were inconsistent, finding sufficient evidence of an agreement involving multiple overt acts including transportation, preparation, and sale of cocaine. The court also upheld Davis's enhanced sentence, determining his criminal history alone justified the enhancement under Blakely v. Washington.

Fort Buford, built in 1866 at the Missouri‑Yellowstone confluence near Williston, Dakota, operated as post until Sitting Bull’s surrender in 1881. Soldiers grew, fished or hunted food, causing scurvy; cooking was poor, described as abominable. Supplies arrived by steamboat, stopped when the river froze. Boredom, alcohol and self‑injury problems. A 1876 report noted patients, one placing a hot coal in his pocket, and described a post library. The fort was abandoned; a museum opened in headquarters in 1963 and sections have been restored.

The robot can grill up to 150 burgers per hour and uses a 6‑axis arm, a sensor bar, thermal and 3‑D cameras, and AI that improves with use. Human staff still place patties, add cheese and extras, and wrap orders. Caliburger has exclusive use for six months before selling Flippy to other vendors; each unit costs about $60,000 and may become more expensive. Currently limited to one restaurant, the chain plans U.S. expansion after a trial. A McKinsey report rated fast‑food as highly vulnerable to automation.

The device is a TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processor supporting reset isolation for PCI Express and Ethernet Switch subsystems. PCI Express reset isolation allows the PCIE Subsystem to be reset independently when the device is a Root Complex via PRCM, requiring idle state before reset and bus re-enumeration after; when an Endpoint, it generates an interrupt on in-band reset. Ethernet Switch reset isolation, enabled by ISO_CONTROL bit, prevents switch and PLL reset during most system resets except POR, preserving traffic and some control registers; pin multiplexing and certain PINCNTL registers are unaffected. Power domain resets include warm reset on external warm reset or power domain OFF transition, and cold reset on POR or power domain ON transition. During reset, all I/O pins enter Hi-Z state except emulation pins (reset by Test Reset), EMAC Switch pins (Hi-Z during POR; some remain active during other resets if isolated), and RSTOUT_WD_OUT pin (3-stated during POR/RESET). DDR address/control pins are 3-stated during reset and driven to pull resistor values upon release; PINCNTL registers reset to default unless EMAC Switch isolation is enabled. Internal pull-up/down resistors are enabled during reset as specified. The device clock architecture uses DEV and AUX clock inputs from internal oscillators or external 1.8V LVCMOS sources; DEV clock is typically 20 MHz but can range 20–30 MHz under certain conditions, while AUX clock is optional and also 20–30 MHz. Twelve top-level PLLs and four embedded PLLs generate system clocks; PLLs support bypass mode and must stay within REFCLK, CLKDCO, and CLKOUT limits. SYSCLKs are outputs from PRCM after division/multiplexing, with maximum frequencies listed per OPP100; module clocks are sourced directly or via SYSCLKs, with maximum frequencies per module. The device provides 128 interrupt requests for ARM Cortex-A8 via AINTC with programmable priority, and the C674x DSP combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts with optional multiplexing. Debug features include Advanced Event Triggering (hardware breakpoints, watchpoints, counters, state sequencing), Trace at Cortex-A8 and system levels via ETB or 5-pin trace interface, and JTAG IEEE 1149.1 for emulation and boundary scan with internal pulldown on TRST. Peripherals include two DCAN interfaces supporting CAN 2.0A/B with FIFO mode and loop-back; EDMA controller with up to 64 channels and 512 parameter entries; Ethernet MAC Switch with 3-port gigabit switch supporting MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII, hardware flow control, QoS, and MDIO for PHY management; GPIO modules with up to 128 pins, de-bouncing, and interrupt generation; GPMC for NOR/NAND Flash, SRAM, and custom logic with 8/16-bit multiplexed bus up to 512 MB and pre-fetch/write posting; Error Locator Module for BCH error correction on NAND; HDMI 1.3a transmitter with TMDS, CEC, DDC, and up to 1920x1080p@75Hz video; HDVPSS with two display pipelines, HD/SD encoders, HDMI, video input capture up to 165 MHz, and three graphics layers; four I2C modules compatible with Philips I2C spec v2.1, 10–400 Kbps, seven/ten-bit addressing, and 32-byte FIFO; Imaging Subsystem with parallel camera (CAM) and serial camera (CSI2) interfaces, ISP for processing, timing control for flash/shutter, and up to 5376 pixels per line; DDR2/DDR3 memory controller with 16/32-bit data path, two chip selects, and dynamic memory manager. Timing specifications for all interfaces are provided in accompanying tables, including setup/hold times, delay times, and switching characteristics for clocks, reset, PCIe, Ethernet, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, HDVPSS, I2C, ISS, DDR, and JTAG. Register descriptions and PCB layout guidelines for HDMI TMDS and DDR2 interfaces are included, with DDR routing specifications requiring strict length and skew control.

Trials focus on traffic‑light management, real‑time sensor data processing and virtual‑reality monitoring, and will evaluate multiple network slices under live industrial conditions – the first such trial in Germany.

Prosecutors dismissed the most serious charges against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer, accused of plotting a shooting at Fair Haven Union High School in Vermont. The state Supreme Court ruled the prosecution "untenable." Sawyer now faces lesser charges of criminal threatening and carrying a dangerous weapon. Since 2000, only 12 albums have spent at least 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Taylor Swift and Morgan Wallen each have three albums on this list, while Adele has two. Adele’s “21” logged 24 weeks at the top, the most for a woman. Taylor Swift’s sophomore album “Fearless” led for 11 weeks, and her latest “The Tortured Poets Department” began with a 12‑week streak, later adding five more weeks for a total of 17. Morgan Wallen’s “Dangerous: The Double Album” spent its first 10 weeks at No. 1, joining Stevie Wonder’s “Songs in the Key of Life” as the only albums to achieve that start. Bad Bunny’s “Un Verano Sin Ti” topped the chart for 13 weeks, and Wallen’s “One Thing at a Time” surpassed it to become the biggest‑week country album this decade, eclipsing Garth Brooks’ previous record of 18 weeks. SZA’s “SOS” was the first R&B album by a woman to reach this milestone since Mariah Carey’s 1991 debut. The list also includes the “Frozen” soundtrack, among others.

On Oct 22 2001 U.S. stock indexes rose sharply as several companies posted earnings that beat or met analysts’ expectations, while the Conference Board’s leading‑indicators index fell 0.5 % in September, its largest monthly drop since early 1996. Enron disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission requested information about its related‑party transactions with limited partnerships run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow; the news sent Enron shares down about 20 % to $20.65, wiping out roughly $4.2 billion of market value. The company reported a $618 million third‑quarter loss after a $1.01 billion charge, a $35 million loss tied to the partnerships, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from repurchasing 55 million shares to unwind the partnerships. Shareholder derivative and securities‑fraud class‑action suits were filed alleging the board breached fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to manage the partnerships, which earned him and associates millions while costing Enron over $35 million. Enron said its board approved the arrangements and that they were disclosed in SEC filings, and it pledged full cooperation with the SEC. Analysts noted concerns about possible further write‑downs, credit‑rating risk and the dilution of common shares if certain affiliated structures are dismantled.

During a meeting between the US Secretary and Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin, the two discussed arms control negotiations, particularly INF and START, with the US preferring Geneva but open to other channels. Dobrynin proposed expanding bilateral cooperation and creating an inventory of bilateral agreements categorized as cancelled, lapsed, ongoing, or close to agreement. They also discussed other bilateral talks on radiological and chemical weapons, conventional arms transfers, and Indian Ocean naval deployments. Regional issues included the CSCE Madrid meeting, South Africa, the Middle East, nonproliferation, and the Warsaw Pact's Prague Declaration, as well as Poland, Kampuchea, Afghanistan, and Central America. Human rights issues, such as Soviet Jewry, were raised, with both sides emphasizing practical handling without publicity. Arms control negotiations were deemed most important, with START and INF as key topics for future meetings. Confidence-building measures were seen as an area for early progress.

A memo from President Reagan's National Security Advisor Clark to Reagan assessed the possibility of constructive US-Soviet relations, noting that after two years of restoring US strength, the Soviets may now be more amenable to negotiation, as they likely prefer restraint through talks over military conflict, given their recent setbacks.

Clio, a cloud‑based legal practice management company, acquired global legal research platform vLex for $1 billion in June, adding capabilities such as intake, research, drafting, case management, communications, accounting and billing. The purchase follows earlier acquisitions of AI platform ShareDo and document automation software Lawyaw; Clio was valued at $3 billion last year. CEO Jack Newton will discuss the company’s future and AI at the Clio Cloud Conference on Oct 16‑17 in Boston, with keynotes from legal‑technology pioneer, Esther Perel and JJ Velazquez.

Tyreek Hill was carted off with a leg injury in the third quarter of the Dolphins-Jets game after his left leg got tangled, resulting in a dislocated knee. He was taken to a hospital for imaging and evaluation. Dolphins coach Mike McDaniel confirmed the dislocation, describing it as far worse than a dislocated knee cap, and said the injury is expected to be season‑ending, with Hill not anticipated to return in 2025. Recovery timeline will depend on the extent of ligament damage; typical patella dislocations heal in six‑to‑eight weeks, but severe cases involving multiple ligament tears may require surgery and a longer absence.

Citizenship education has moved beyond constructing national identity to fostering democratic participation, knowledge, skills, and values needed for informed, responsible citizens worldwide. Contemporary global challenges (climate change, pandemics, migrations, wars) highlight the growing role of science and scientific literacy in citizenship. Science education aims to develop scientifically literate citizens, not only future scientists, and literature advocates integrating citizenship into science via Science‑Technology‑Society‑Environment (STSE) topics. The United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (2030) further link citizenship and science education.

Turkey’s citizenship education historically emphasized a duty‑driven national identity through history, geography, and social studies. From the 2000s it shifted toward democratic citizenship aligned with European Union harmonization, introducing an interdisciplinary approach in 2005 and later a standalone citizenship course. Science education reforms began in the 1990s with the Science‑Technology‑Society concept; the 2018 curriculum centers on scientific, technological, and environmental literacy, sustainable development, and the interplay of individual, environment, and society.

The study examined the Turkish science curriculum and conducted semi‑structured interviews with eight science teachers. Thematic analysis identified six curriculum themes (scientific literacy, technology, society, environment, values, skills) and a teacher‑identified “problems” theme. Key findings:

- Scientific knowledge and process skills are prominent; teachers view scientific literacy as essential for modern citizenship, linking it to problem‑solving, inquiry, and critical thinking.
- Technology receives limited explicit connection to citizenship.
- Society is linked to daily life, health, safety, and socio‑scientific issues (e.g., climate change, COVID‑19, GMOs, organ donation).
- Environment is the most highlighted theme; teachers connect environmental awareness to active citizenship, emphasizing protection, sustainable development, and global treaties.
- Values include scientific integrity, respect, compassion, responsibility, and patriotism; skills encompass observation, questioning, interpreting data, and critical thinking.
- Teachers report barriers: overcrowded classrooms, insufficient laboratories, an exam‑focused system, curriculum gaps, and challenges with refugee students.

The conclusion stresses that science education can enhance citizenship competencies (knowledge, skills, attitudes, values) but practical implementation is hampered by systemic obstacles. Recommendations include explicitly embedding citizenship skills in the science curriculum, providing teacher training, integrating socio‑scientific topics, and aligning instruction with the SDG‑2030 agenda.

UFC 216 is Saturday in Las Vegas, after a shooting that killed 58 and injured nearly 500; the UFC pledged $1 million for victims. This study examined future preschool and primary school teachers' conceptions of robots using a Draw-A-Robot Test with 121 students at the University of Belgrade. Most participants accurately depicted robots, with animal-shaped robots like Bee-Bot being most common. The primary functions identified were educational (dominant among preschool teachers) and assistive. Misconceptions (22 cases) mostly involved viewing robots as electrical appliances. Real-life experience with robots was prevalent, primarily gained at the Faculty of Education. Differences emerged between departments: preschool teachers prioritized cognitive domain in robot selection, while primary school teachers showed mixed domain influences. The findings highlight the need to integrate educational robots into teacher training to enhance digital competencies and algorithmic thinking in children.

Byron Bell, 29, signed with the Packers, adding competition for right tackle. He started games for the Panthers, playing for the Titans and Cowboys. The position is uncertain because Bryan Bulaga is recovering from a torn ACL; officials say Bulaga remains part of plans. Other candidates include Jason Spriggs and Kyle Murphy. Out of bounds situations are critical in basketball. Teams must be prepared to inbound from the baseline, sideline, and full court using simple plays that get the ball to the best players for high percentage shots. Practices are essential since new plays during timeouts rarely work. Inbounders need fundamental skills, commitment to team play, vision, communication, execution, and timing. Automatic reads should be the first option: cutting to the basket when a defender's back is turned, executing give-and-go when unguarded, and using lob passes when defenders face up. Players must communicate through eye contact and body language, and coaches should scout opponents to anticipate defensive strategies. Key rules include a five-second inbound limit, restrictions on inbounder movement, allowance for baseline movement after made shots, and the ability to inbound to the backcourt without violation. Defender contact over the out of bounds plane results in a technical foul. Coaches should test players on rule knowledge to ensure understanding and prevent costly mistakes during games.

Digital games support Education 4.0 by enabling competency-based, personalized teaching-learning and skill-based assessment. They enhance cognitive and non-cognitive skills through engaging, multimodal experiences and can assess learners objectively during gameplay using AI-driven stealth assessment. Stealth assessment relies on evidence-centered design and machine learning to continuously track competencies and provide adaptive feedback. However, integrating digital games in education faces challenges, including the need for multidisciplinary expertise, managing cognitive load, calibrating difficulty, and establishing validity and reliability.

Neutrinos can be obtained from several sources: supernova explosions, relic Big Bang neutrinos, cosmic‑ray showers, solar fusion, accelerator‑produced beams, and nuclear reactors. Nuclear reactors also allow global monitoring of reactor activity. Experiments characterize neutrino sources by three parameters: baseline length, neutrino energy, and sensitivity to a given Δm² range.

Solar neutrinos travel the Earth–Sun distance and have energies ~1 meV, probing Δm²≈10⁻¹⁰. Atmospheric neutrinos produced by cosmic‑ray interactions in the upper atmosphere travel 10⁴–10⁷ m with energies from 10² to 10⁵ meV. Reactor neutrinos are MeV‑scale, produced by fission of heavy isotopes (mainly uranium and polonium), and their baselines are limited by the reactor site. Accelerator neutrinos, generated at facilities such as CERN, Fermilab (NuMI) and Japanese labs, have energies 10³–10⁴ meV; experiments place detectors near and far to study appearance and disappearance.

Solar neutrino experiments (e.g., Homestake chlorine detector, later SNO) measured fewer electron neutrinos than predicted; SNO’s neutral‑current channel confirmed the total flux matches expectations, providing the first evidence of solar neutrino oscillation. Atmospheric neutrino observations show a deficit of muon‑type neutrinos that depends on zenith angle, confirming oscillation. Accelerator experiments such as T2K compare unoscillated predictions with measured oscillated spectra, demonstrating clear oscillation. Reactor experiments detect antielectron‑neutrino disappearance via inverse beta decay and have measured the survival probability as a function of L/E, especially in the 2000s.

The speaker says it took many years to reach this point and remains excited with butterflies still present, recalling past games in New Jersey and Colorado and childhood championship feelings. Their routine includes a morning pre‑game skate, brief skill work, stick practice, and staying even‑keel.

Kochi court convicted migrant labourer Muhammed Ameerul Islam from Assam for rape and murder of a 30-year-old Dalit law student in Kerala. He was found guilty under IPC sections 302, 376, and 376(A). Sentencing will be announced tomorrow. Islam was arrested 50 days later in Tamil Nadu. Investigation included over 100 police, 5,000 fingerprints, and 20 lakh phone calls. Governments are increasingly regulating AI through documents like the EU AI Act and US executive orders, necessitating developers who can navigate policy demands. However, AI policy discussions remain largely absent from computer science curricula. This paper synthesizes key AI regulatory developments in the US and EU. The US lacks comprehensive federal legislation, instead relying on non-binding policies; recent shifts include Biden's safety-focused EO 14110 being rescinded in favor of Trump's EO 14179 emphasizing AI dominance for economic and national security. The EU's AI Act, enacted in 2024, categorizes AI systems by risk level, prohibits certain high-risk practices, and requires transparency from general-purpose AI models. The paper identifies three implications: the volatile policy landscape requiring adaptable developers, challenges translating abstract policy goals into technical specifications, and cross-border regulatory effects exemplified by the GDPR's global reach. A framework is proposed to integrate AI policy into CS courses, organized across three perspectives (socio-political, translational, technical) and three dimensions (scope, power, agency), with guiding questions to help students connect policy to technical implementation.

Penalty kicks are a restart, with the ball live when kicked. All outfield attackers must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field and outside the penalty area; they may not enter the penalty area or arc until the ball is touched by the kicker and moves forward. Players must react to blocks, saves or rebounds and be ready to follow up. The kicker may not touch the ball again until another player contacts it – typically after a goalkeeper block – and must follow up immediately after a block or clear the way for a teammate after a rebound off the goal. If the ball is secured by the goalkeeper, the attacking team must shift to defense. Violations of positioning rules result in a retake if a goal is scored, otherwise an indirect free kick; certain other infractions always result in an indirect free kick. The USA‑Vietnam 2023 Women’s World Cup match illustrates a missed follow‑up opportunity.

An Italian man, Luca Traini, 28, opened fire on African migrants in Macerata on Saturday, wounding six people, one seriously, before police arrested him. Traini, wearing an Italian flag and making a fascist salute, also fired at the offices of the centre‑left Democratic Party without causing injuries. He previously ran as a Northern League candidate in local elections. The attack occurred days after the arrest of a Nigerian asylum seeker, Innocent Oseghale, in connection with the murder of 18‑year‑old Pamela Mastropietro, whose dismembered body was found in suitcases near Macerata. Prime Minister Paolo Gentiloni and political leaders called for calm, while Northern League leader Matteo Salvini blamed mass immigration for rising tensions.

Rutgers historian Mark Bray, who wrote a book about antifa in 2017, is trying to flee the US to Spain after receiving death threats from far-right influencers and anonymous accounts. The threats followed a Change.org petition by conservative student activists and online targeting by figures like Milo Yiannopoulos and Jack Posobiec after Trump's executive order designating antifa as a terrorist organization. Bray and his family were turned back at the airport when their reservations were mysteriously canceled after going through security. He plans to try again and stay in Spain until the end of the academic year, making his situation public to protect academic freedom and the right to dissent.

The ADS868xW device features a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) with configurable input ranges, a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with 500kHz cutoff, and an integrated ADC driver. It supports internal (4.096V) or external voltage references with internal buffering. The device provides input alarms (with programmable thresholds and hysteresis) and AVDD alarms (fixed thresholds: 4.7V low, 5.3V high). The multiSPI digital interface supports standard SPI and daisy-chain topologies, with the device operating in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Nine configuration registers control device functions including range selection, alarm thresholds, and data output formatting. The device supports NAP and power-down modes for power saving and requires AVDD and DVDD supplies with specific decoupling capacitors.

A unified multiscale framework that directly links atomistic solid‑melt interface energetics to macroscopic GaN growth kinetics is presented. Machine‑learning‑potential‑based molecular‑dynamics simulations reveal pronounced, polarity‑dependent layering of liquid Ga at the GaN‑Ga interface, with charge redistribution confined to the primary interfacial layer. Well‑tempered metadynamics quantifies free‑energy landscapes for N‑adatom adsorption and lateral migration at Ga‑polar and N‑polar surfaces; ordered Ga layers lower migration barriers to ≈0.34–0.56 eV versus ≈1.1 eV on a clean surface, a “Ga lubrication” effect. Step‑edge (Ehrlich‑Schwoebel) barriers above 0.6 eV are also determined. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations parameterized by these barriers show that typical MBE conditions produce diffusion‑controlled, layer‑by‑layer growth, whereas high N fluxes generate island‑type growth. A parameter‑free diffusion model, derived from modified Fick’s law with interfacial free‑energy profiles, predicts facet‑resolved growth rates of 0.01–0.04 nm s⁻¹, in quantitative agreement with experimental growth rates extracted from TEM/STEM analysis of partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles. The framework is transferable to other III‑V systems where the key group‑V element has low solubility in the metal melt, making interfacial free‑energy landscapes the decisive factor for growth kinetics.

In soccer, the second defender provides individual support by positioning behind and inside the field relative to the first defender, staying goalside and far enough back to react if the first defender is beaten. The support defender maintains appropriate distance, adopts the same stance, announces arrival with “support” or “you have help,” and adjusts position as the attacker and first defender move. They may signal “jockey/delay/contain” to tell the first defender to manage the attacker, or “tackle” to indicate a solid attempt to win the ball. Proper oral communication is critical. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender usually takes over, possibly executing a defensive switch. Instruction involves stationary and moving drills at half‑speed and full‑speed.

The study compared air‑ and bone‑conduction auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady‑state response (ASSR) thresholds in 64 infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing (NH) or conductive hearing loss (CHL). Infants were tested at 500 Hz and 2000 Hz using the BCEHP ABR protocol and ASSR with AM2 stimuli presented monotically. ABR was recorded first, followed by ASSR. AC thresholds were significantly higher in the CHL group for both methods, while BC thresholds did not differ between groups. Both ABR and ASSR showed larger air‑bone gaps (ABG) in the CHL versus NH infants, with ABR ABGs being larger and more clearly separated. Minimum normal intensities were higher for ASSR (40 dB HL AC, 30 dB HL BC at 500 Hz) than for ABR (35 dB nHL AC, 20 dB nHL BC). Sensitivity and specificity for detecting CHL were highest for AC ABR thresholds; screening measures had high sensitivity but low specificity, and ASSR AC thresholds/ABGs performed less well. The authors conclude that ABR remains the gold‑standard for infant hearing assessment in EHDI programs and that further research is needed before ASSR can be adopted clinically.

RS Components compared the wealth growth of the five richest Forbes billionaires—Jeff Bezos, Bernard Arnault, Bill Gates, Warren Buffett and Mark Zuckerberg. Last year Bezos added $39.2B, Arnault $30.5B and Gates $4B. Using the average US salary of $56,516, Bezos earns that amount in 46 seconds, Arnault in 59 seconds, while Gates, Buffett and Zuckerberg each need over a minute. For a $100,000 salary, Bezos needs 1 minute 21 seconds, Arnault 1 minute 43 seconds, Zuckerberg 3 minutes 30 seconds, Buffett 6 minutes 14 seconds and Gates 13 minutes 6 seconds. The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture implements a hybrid rendering model that combines traditional rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation to enable realistic graphics in games and professional applications. Turing includes dedicated RT Cores for ray tracing acceleration and Tensor Cores for AI operations, allowing real-time ray tracing with denoising and efficient acceleration structures.

Ray tracing hardware in Turing centers on the RT Core within each SM. RT Cores accelerate bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, performing visibility testing on behalf of threads in the SM. This offloads the SM, enabling it to handle vertex, pixel, and compute shading work. Turing GPUs use a highly efficient BVH acceleration structure developed by NVIDIA Research. Combined with advanced denoising filtering, Turing can achieve real-time ray tracing with far fewer rays per pixel than traditional software approaches. NVIDIA Real-Time Ray Tracing Denoiser modules significantly reduce rays required per pixel. Turing can deliver over 10 gigarays per second, approximately ten times faster than Pascal GPUs for ray tracing workloads, which require about 10 TFLOPS per gigaray in software emulation.

AI acceleration in Turing is provided by Tensor Cores and the NGX platform. NGX utilizes deep neural networks (DNNs) and neural services to accelerate and enhance graphics. Key features include Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), which produces higher quality output than temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) from a given set of input samples, enabling faster rendering at lower sample counts. DLSS is trained using thousands of 64x supersampled reference images (64xSS) to approximate that quality. NGX also offers AI Slow-Mo for interpolated video frames, AI Super Rez for upscaling images by 2x to 8x with sharper results than bicubic interpolation, and InPainting for intelligent content removal and replacement using trained DNNs.

Turing introduces several rendering techniques to improve performance and flexibility. Mesh shading adds task and mesh shader stages that use a cooperative thread model similar to compute shaders, eliminating CPU draw call bottlenecks and enabling efficient rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects. Task shaders dynamically generate work and can select appropriate levels of detail. Variable rate shading (VRS) allows developers to adjust shading rates per 16x16 pixel region, supporting content adaptive shading (reducing rate in slowly changing areas), motion adaptive shading (reducing rate for moving objects), and foveated rendering (reducing rate in peripheral areas based on eye tracking). Texture space shading (TSS) decouples visibility sampling from appearance sampling, storing shading values in texture space for reuse across frames, improving temporal stability and allowing fine-grained control over shading rates via MIP levels. Multi-view rendering (MVR) enables rendering from multiple viewpoints in a single pass, supporting up to four views and expanding on Pascal's simultaneous multi-projection for efficient stereo and wide field-of-view VR. Turing's MVR allows view-dependent attributes like reflection direction to be computed per view, while view-independent attributes are shared.

Turing enhances VR experiences through VirtualLink, a USB Type-C based standard that delivers power, display, and data through a single connector, simplifying VR setup on small form factor devices. Foveated rendering, enabled by VRS, reduces shading in peripheral areas based on eye tracking, and VRS can also increase shading rate for multisample anti-aliasing. NVIDIA VRWorks Audio uses RT Cores to accelerate ray-traced audio for realistic sound propagation, including indirect sound and reverberation.

Performance metrics for Turing are expressed using RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric that combines peak operations of CUDA cores (FP32), RT cores, Tensor cores, and integer pipelines, weighted by their utilization over a frame. For example, an RTX 2080 Ti delivers 78 RTX-OPS by combining 80% FP32 utilization, 40% RT, 20% Tensor, and 28% integer. Workload analysis shows DLSS occupies about 20% of frame time, rendering 80%, with ray tracing taking half of the rendering time (about 40% of total frame time), and integer pipelines active for 35% of shading time.

Turing GPUs are available in several configurations. The full TU102 features 72 SMs, 4608 CUDA cores, 576 Tensor cores, and 72 RT cores. The TU104 has 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor cores, and 48 RT cores, used in products like GeForce RTX 2080 and Quadro RTX 5000, with second-generation NVLink providing 50 GB/s total bandwidth. The TU106 has 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor cores, and 36 RT cores, used in GeForce RTX 2070, and does not support NVLink or SLI. The Tesla T4, based on TU104, includes 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA cores, and 320 Tensor cores, designed for inference with 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

Turing enables ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections that provide physically correct lighting and grounding of objects. Ray-traced shadows overcome shadow map limitations like resolution mismatch and contact hardening, providing correct shadows from area lights. Ray-traced ambient occlusion highlights geometric complexity more realistically than screen-space methods. Ray-traced reflections produce artifact-free results on specular and glossy surfaces, avoiding limitations of screen-space reflections and static cubemaps. These effects are demonstrated in games like Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider, where RTX enables realistic reflections and shadows.

In summary, Turing combines rasterization, ray tracing, AI, and simulation through dedicated hardware and advanced techniques to deliver real-time photorealistic graphics.

This passage discusses a study on inclusive education policies and the awareness of educational leaders in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Inclusive education aims to provide equal opportunities for all students, including those with disabilities, guided by global, regional, and national legal frameworks. Key global frameworks include the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Convention on the Rights of the Child, Salamanca Statement, Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and Sustainable Development Goals. Regional frameworks in Africa include the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and the African Disability Protocol. Ethiopia’s national frameworks include the Constitution, Education and Training Policy, Education Sector Development Plan VI, Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy, and National Children’s Policy. The study used qualitative methods, interviewing Ministry experts, school principals, itinerant teachers, and teachers. Findings show that while comprehensive legal frameworks exist, awareness among educational leaders varies. Ministry experts and itinerant teachers demonstrate better awareness than principals and teachers. The study recommends increasing awareness through professional development, aligning local practices with global standards, and monitoring policy awareness.

The passage discusses modeling light-matter interactions at the nanoscale for quantum technologies. Classical electromagnetic solvers based on Maxwell's equations cannot capture quantum features like photon correlations or entanglement. Existing quantum simulation approaches using master equations or quantum-optical models describe idealized systems and cannot account for realistic device properties. The authors introduce a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approach to bridge quantum and classical descriptions, avoiding wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, or operator-valued noise. The method links quantum dynamics to electromagnetic fields and can be integrated with Maxwell solvers. They validate this approach using the Mollow spectrum from a strongly driven two-level system. The passage also addresses the derivation of SDEs from Fokker-Planck equations, distinguishing between conventional symmetric diffusion matrices and non-symmetric matrices that capture asymmetric noise correlations from non-commuting quantum operators.

The passage describes the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification for AMD virtual machines. Key points include:

**GHCB Protocol**: A 4KB decrypted memory page used for guest-hypervisor communication, with protocol versioning (v2 through v2.04) enabling SEV-ES and SEV-SNP features. The hypervisor advertises supported features via a bitmap.

**NAE Events**: Non-Automatic Exits including MSR_PROT, CPUID, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request.

**AP Booting**: Challenges with INIT-SIPI-SIPI under SEV-ES/SEV-SNP. Solutions include AP Reset Hold NAE event, AP Jump Table for transfer from UEFI to OS, and SNP AP Creation feature allowing VMSA page supply.

**Restricted Injection**: Enables hypervisor notification via #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent (vector, NMI, #MC) and NoEoiRequired fields, with host behavior emulating APIC interrupt delivery semantics.

**Additional Features**: Debug register support, NMI handling via "NMI Complete" message, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, CPUID request protocol before GHCB establishment, and page state change operations for private/shared transitions.

Planetary scientist Ralph Harvey notes Soviet probes in the 1970s survived only minutes to a few hours, calling Venus “a hell hole.” NASA’s Phil Neudeck and his team demonstrated durable electronics that operated 21 days in the simulator, the first multi‑week electronic operation in a Venus environment, removing a mission constraint. Physicist and sci‑fi author Geoffrey Landis calls Venus Earth’s “evil twin,” a runaway greenhouse boiled its oceans, and notes that about 30 miles up the atmosphere is Earth‑like, allowing floating habitats, though clouds are concentrated sulfuric acid. He says studying Venus helps predict Earth’s climate and could reveal microbial life in that zone. The Glenn work is a game‑changing step toward longer exploration.

Authors evaluate fine‑tuning of a universal interatomic potential (MACE) on unary (Au), binary (RuO₂) and ternary (BiVO₄) surface datasets. They compare three strategies: training from scratch (TS), zero‑shot (ZS) and fine‑tuning (FT); they also test multi‑head fine‑tuning (MHFT) to suppress catastrophic forgetting. Across all three systems, FT yields lower energy and force errors than TS, reaching comparable accuracy with only 40–200 configurations versus 2 000 needed for TS. ZS predictions show reasonable performance but systematically underestimate surface energies. In the ternary BiVO₄ case, FT reduces force outliers (13 vs 2–3 for ZS/FT) and achieves the lowest force RMSE (0.17 eV/Å). Fine‑tuning on one unary surface degrades predictions for other novel metals; MHFT restores bulk‑data performance while further reducing surface‑energy errors (RMSE ≈ 16 meV/Å² vs 27 meV/Å² for ZS and 88 meV/Å² for FT). The study concludes that fine‑tuning foundation models improves accuracy and data efficiency for surface simulations, and that MHFT is advantageous when retention of bulk‑level performance is required, at the cost of increased training time.

The article discusses integrating trauma‑informed practice into human rights education (HRE) in higher education. It notes that HRE is widely offered in universities but remains mostly confined to law schools and that existing models do not address contemporary threats or the impact of trauma on learners. Over half of UK university students have experienced adverse childhood experiences, increasing the risk that HRE may retraumatise learners. The authors define trauma‑informed practice as principles and pedagogies that promote a healing learning experience and mitigate secondary trauma for teachers and learners.

The article recommends three main strategies: (1) educators should clarify their values and develop a rights‑respecting teaching persona by locating themselves, recognizing biases and privileges; (2) content design should embed trauma‑sensitive principles—using the UN’s “about, through and for” framework, SAMHSA’s six principles (safety, trustworthiness, peer support, collaboration, empowerment, cultural awareness), co‑creation with students, project‑based learning, reflective exercises (e.g., Gibbs’ Reflective Cycle), and careful use of trigger warnings and wellbeing check‑ins—to minimise retraumatisation and foster empowerment; (3) teaching should be dialogic, creating horizontal relationships, encouraging critical dialogue, inviting guest speakers (survivors and practitioners) and building communicative competence and advocacy skills.

The article concludes that trauma‑informed human rights teaching can empower learners and educators to move from avoidance toward advocacy, placing wellbeing, agency and dignity at the centre of the learning experience.

Manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria and Switzerland face geopolitical, energy, raw‑material, supply‑chain, labor and sustainability pressures while digital transformation reshapes value creation. An IDC survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers in manufacturing firms with more than 500 employees (Dec 2021) shows that IT‑based simulation, modeling and data analytics are tied to key business goals: 75 % rank innovation as most important, 57 % see them as a means to improve product/service quality, and 64 % plan to invest in modern simulation and high‑performance data analytics. Current deployment is highest in product development, production planning and quality management, and is expected to rise to about 90 % within two years, with nearly two‑thirds planning related investments. Thirty‑nine percent aim to virtually simulate as many physical processes as possible, and 42 % already use high‑performance data analytics. Digital twins and virtual prototyping can cut development time by up to 50 % and boost sustainability. Eighty‑one percent of respondents consider high‑performance computing (HPC) a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96 % among firms already using HPC. HPC enables complex calculations, faster iterations and new usage scenarios, but adoption faces challenges: security concerns (72 %), high investment/licensing costs and energy consumption (58 %). Most firms rely on external HPC (87 % use or plan cloud‑based HPC, 74 % colocation); only 6 % operate on‑premises HPC. IDC expects HPC‑based simulation and analytics to become routine and enable new business models such as product‑as‑a‑service.

The paper investigates whether textual content in earnings press releases predicts stock returns on announcement days. Using over 138,000 press releases from 2005–2023, the authors evaluate NLP techniques including LDA and BERT models. They find soft information from press releases explains stock returns similarly to earnings surprises, with FinBERT providing the most effective extraction. A long-short trading strategy based on press release content and earnings surprises yields no sustained profits when executed at market open, supporting market efficiency. However, when information is available in advance—as in documented hacking incidents—traders can correctly identify approximately 56% of top-performing stocks by combining both hard and soft information. The research demonstrates that both earnings surprise and press release text are equally important in predicting announcement-day returns, achieving an R² of approximately 4% over 134,354 observations.

Credit‑card holders, adjustable‑rate mortgage borrowers and home‑equity line users will face quarter‑point increases after the Federal Reserve's fourth rate hike in 18 months, lifting its benchmark to 1‑1.25 percent with one more rise expected this year. Savers see modest gains: average one‑year CDs rose from 0.27 % to 0.35 % while top‑yield CDs moved from 1.35 % to 1.5 %, with smaller banks offering higher rates than large national banks. Higher U.S. rates attract overseas capital, pushing up the dollar and pulling funds out of developing economies. Consumers with poor credit may face higher costs, especially for used‑car financing. Retirees with bond portfolios are advised to stay the course and maintain a mix of short‑ and long‑term bonds.

The researcher does not advise vegetarian diets but urges owners to consider climate impacts as premium foods become popular. A UC Davis expert notes pet‑food meat comes from rendered byproducts that would otherwise be wasted. Some dogs can thrive on plant‑based diets, but many veterinarians warn cats need taurine, and a 2015 review found vegetarian pet foods failed to meet minimum amino‑acid standards.

Twenty‑seven days after Kilauea’s massive eruption, fast‑moving lava is threatening the Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens neighborhoods, advancing at about 600 yards per hour and producing a 200‑ft‑high fountain from Fissure 8.
