Tests on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin from January 2015 to September 2021 show that RSI works differently on crypto than on traditional equities. RSI as a mean reversion indicator (buying low RSI readings and selling high readings) produced weak results with few trades and is considered ineffective. However, RSI as a momentum indicator shows promise. A momentum strategy using RSI(5) with entry when RSI crosses above 50 and exit when it crosses below 50 achieved 122% CAGR versus 101% for buy-and-hold, with lower drawdowns (39% vs 83%). The conclusion is that while mean reversion strategies fail in crypto, momentum-based RSI strategies can be effective.

Don Davis, Arkansas inmate who had a last meal, faces execution as attorney general asks US Supreme Court to lift stay; 8th Circuit reversed lower court block on eight executions, rejecting claims midazolam causes undue pain.

The manuscript illustrates the value and potential of critical approaches to quantitative research (quantitative criticalism) for education scholars. It is intended for scholars, students, instructors, and institutional researchers who employ quantitative methods or critical perspectives, offering guidance on integrating critical epistemologies with quantitative techniques. The authors share their own positionalities: Jay, a queer, white cisgender researcher who uses quantitative methods to center queer and trans students, and Jimmy, a Vietnamese‑Chinese American scholar who emphasizes disaggregating aggregated data and minimizing harm in institutional research.

The authors define quantitative criticalism as a combination of post‑positivistic quantitative techniques with critical perspectives that recognize subjectivity, advocate social justice, and challenge systems of oppression. They note that numbers are not neutral and that analyses must account for systemic inequities.

Several inherent tensions are identified: the white supremacist and cisheteropatriarchial origins of statistics, the lack of a clear “threshold of criticality,” and methodological challenges such as essentialist demographic categories, limited statistical power for intersecting identities, and the conflict between seeking broad generalizability and surfacing nuanced counterstories. The authors emphasize that these tensions should be acknowledged rather than dismissed.

Four illustrative examples are provided: a critical race theory (CRT) study that operationalized the community cultural wealth model into scales (Sablan, 2019); a queer‑theory‑informed study highlighting within‑group differences among LGBQ respondents (Garvey, 2017); an intersectionality‑focused investigation of gendered racism coping among Black women (Szymanski & Lewis, 2016); and a latent‑class analysis exploring opportunity gaps using intersectional frameworks (Wilson & Urick, 2022). Each example demonstrates how critical theories can be embedded in quantitative design, noting both benefits (e.g., surfacing counternarratives) and limitations (e.g., sample constraints and essentialist data).

Implications urge scholars and educators to embed criticality throughout research—from question formulation through publication—by practicing reflexivity, involving community partners, and addressing power dynamics in authorship. The authors propose three reflective questions for practitioners: (1) What are the intentions behind using quantitative criticalism and how do they advance equity? (2) Can methods rooted in white supremacy truly serve justice? (3) What is each researcher’s personal threshold of criticality? The manuscript concludes that quantitative criticalism seeks to advance social justice and collective liberation by confronting inherent tensions and promoting conscious, coalition‑based reflection.

SpinGPT is an LLM-based poker agent for Spin & Go tournaments, trained via Supervised Fine-Tuning on 320,000 professional hand decisions followed by Reinforcement Learning using a GTO solver. SpinGPT-SFT achieves 80% exact accuracy on professional data and outperforms the Slumbot benchmark after applying a heuristic patch. The final SpinGPT model reduces bet-sizing error and significantly beats the SFT-only version in head-to-head play. Limitations include numerical hallucinations and the absence of evaluation against specialized opponents or humans. Future work may involve stronger foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, chain-of-thought prompting, and explainability features.

The global learning crisis, exacerbated by pandemic-related school closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs US$129 billion annually. Youth unemployment nears 30% in lower-income countries, and 20% of youth worldwide are not in employment, education or training. Forty percent of employers lack workers with needed skills, and by 2030, 39% of current job skills will transform or become obsolete. In lower-income countries, educational mismatch affects two-thirds of young adult workers. The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) addresses this by financing, policy dialogue and public-private partnerships to build quality, inclusive education systems providing foundational learning skills (literacy, numeracy, socio-emotional) and 21st century skills (creative thinking, problem solving, collaboration, analytical ability) to prepare students for the workforce. GPE supports partner countries like Lesotho, Ghana, Kenya and El Salvador in developing relevant curricula and teacher training focused on employment readiness.

Common weight‑loss mistakes include drinking from plastic bottles, completely eliminating sweets, being overly self‑critical, eating when emotional, using protein bars and energy drinks with artificial sweeteners, consuming sweets at any time, surrounding yourself with unsupportive people, measuring success only by the scale, taking meal‑replacement supplements, cutting all carbohydrates, eating only fat‑free products, not getting enough sleep, undereating while over‑exercising, repeating the same workout, drinking calories, restricting diet too quickly, and copying someone else’s routine. The passage advises using stainless‑steel bottles, replacing artificial sweets with fruit, forgiving lapses, exercising to manage emotions, substituting coconut water or nuts for processed drinks or bars, limiting sweets to pre‑workout times, choosing supportive friends, tracking progress with non‑scale metrics, eating real food, including healthy carbs and fats, ensuring at least seven hours of sleep, maintaining a moderate calorie deficit, varying workouts weekly, eating solid meals, making gradual dietary changes, and customizing a plan to one’s body type and metabolism.

The MACD‑histogram trading strategy is a mean‑reversion system that aims to spot momentum shifts and reversal points. The system enters positions on the close and exits on the first day the close exceeds (for longs) or falls below (for shorts) the prior close. Over a portfolio of 77 liquid ETFs the strategy produced 6,669 trades, with long trades outperforming short trades and the approach staying in cash most of the time. A back‑test of the 2×‑leveraged Nasdaq‑100 ETF (QLD) from 2007 onward yielded 85 trades, an average gain of 2.2% per trade, 10.4% annual returns despite being invested only about 5% of the time, and a maximum drawdown of 19%. Traders favor the MACD histogram because it visually displays the difference between the MACD line and its signal line, indicating bullish momentum when bars are above the zero line and bearish when below, and crossover signals are generated when the histogram crosses the zero line.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs introduce a new display engine supporting 8K resolution, HDR, and VirtualLink over USB‑C for single‑cable VR headsets. Turing includes an enhanced NVENC encoder that adds HEVC 8K @ 30 fps encode with up to 25 % bit‑rate savings and an updated NVDEC decoder supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR. SLI is replaced by second‑generation NVLink providing up to 100 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth. Dedicated RT Cores enable hardware‑accelerated real‑time ray tracing; Turing uses a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization and ray tracing for reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion, assisted by BVH traversal and denoising. NGX AI features include Deep Learning Super‑Sampling (DLSS) for performance gains, AI Super Rez upscaling, AI Slow‑Mo video interpolation, and InPainting for intelligent image content removal. New Mesh Shaders and Task Shaders eliminate CPU draw‑call bottlenecks, while Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows per‑16×16‑pixel shading‑rate control for content‑adaptive, motion‑adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples shading from screen space for temporal stability and texel reuse, and Multi‑View Rendering expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi‑Projection to up to four views per pass, improving VR rendering. Turing offers three die variants—TU102, TU104, and TU106—with varying SM, RT Core, Tensor Core, memory‑controller counts and NVLink support, and introduces a workload‑based RTX‑OPS metric that combines FP32, integer, RT, and Tensor throughput. Overall, Turing enables real‑time ray tracing, AI‑enhanced rendering, and advanced VR capabilities through hybrid rendering, denoising, and BVH acceleration.

Onesmo Rupil, 23, began using drugs at 17, was discontinued from the University of Dodoma in 2013 for poor performance linked to substance abuse, and cannot resume studies because his father cannot cover tuition. He now manages the Philimisana Foundation Sober House in Mwanza, which houses about 30 youths undergoing rehabilitation, most of whom smoke marijuana. A UN report states that marijuana was the most widely produced, trafficked and consumed drug worldwide in 2010, with 119–224 million adult users. Dr Kassian Nyandindi reported that in 2014 about 550,000 Tanzanians were affected by drug abuse, an estimated 25,000 drug addicts existed nationwide, and only 3,500 received treatment at the four methadone hospitals in Dar es Salaam; HIV infection among drug users ranged from 20 % to 50 %. THC in marijuana damages the corpus callosum and can cause mental disorders, though many youths attribute such disorders to superstition. Onesmo progressed from marijuana to heroin, spending over Sh100,000 on heroin boosters, stealing over 200 laptops from fellow students to fund his habit, was arrested in 2015, imprisoned for six months at Isanga Prison and later in other regions, and completed rehabilitation in Dar es Salaam.

The study developed an automated guideline adherence monitoring system for intensive care that combines FHIR‑encoded clinical practice guideline recommendations with patient data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model. The system was implemented across five university hospitals to evaluate six COVID‑19‑related recommendations on more than 82,000 intensive care episodes recorded from January 2020 to May 2023. Validation against a ground‑truth established by experienced physicians showed the system achieved 97.0 % accuracy, significantly higher than the 86.6 % accuracy of human reviewers (McNemar’s test, p < 0.001), with a specificity of 99.5 % versus 87.6 % and a processing speed exceeding 2,000 patient‑days per second, compared with ~30 seconds per patient‑day for manual review. Over 80 % of disagreements between the system and reviewers were attributable to human error; system errors were primarily due to missing unstructured data. Adherence rates varied across recommendations and hospitals (mostly 10–60 %) but generally increased over time. The authors conclude that the system is feasible, scalable, and substantially improves the accuracy and efficiency of guideline adherence monitoring compared with manual review, providing a foundation for broader integration of evidence‑based care.

New paper by Nic Lewis and Judith Curry finds that high climate‑model warming projections are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850. Using energy‑budget estimates and globally‑complete temperature data extended to 2016, the study derives median equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) of 1.66 °C (5–95 % range 1.15–2.7 °C) and median transient climate response (TCR) of 1.33 °C (5–95 % range 1.15–1.9 °C). These values are substantially lower than the 31 CMIP5 model medians of 3.1 °C (ECS) and 1.9 °C (TCR). The authors show that the upper uncertainty bounds are lower than in a predecessor study and that possible bias sources (non‑unit forcing efficacy, temperature estimation, sea‑surface pattern variability) are minor. The results imply future warming will be 30–45 % lower than IPCC model projections, i.e., 55–70 % of the CMIP5 central warming estimate. The paper appears in the Journal of Climate, Early Online Release.

Statistical Analysis Plan for Protocol ZP4207-17086 outlines reporting of plasma glucose concentration summary statistics and pharmacodynamic metrics by treatment group and time point. Safety analyses are based on the safety set and include: extent of exposure (insulin administration prior to hypoglycemia induction, hypoglycemia induction procedure details, trial medication administration, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion with time to first IV glucose infusion described); local tolerability assessments at injection sites at specified time points; adverse events (TEAEs defined as events occurring after dosing or worsening existing events, with causal relationship classification 0-3 and severity grading 1-3, categorized by system organ class and preferred term using MedDRA, including special interest events and injection site reactions); laboratory results (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy tests with continuous and categorical presentations); vital signs with descriptive statistics and categorical analysis; electrocardiogram results including QTcF interval thresholds; and immunogenicity analysis for treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA. Protocol changes include rewording of primary efficacy statistical analysis and terminology changes for secondary efficacy variables. Appendices detail data presentation specifications, SAS programming QC requirements, and comprehensive table/figure/listings index.

Janet Yellen said the Fed must raise interest rates gradually to prevent the economy from overheating while allowing inflation to reach its 2% target. She noted that a sustainable monthly job gain is 90,000–120,000, and February added 313,000 jobs, above expectations. Despite a 1.7% price rise in the year to January, Yellen warned of risks of tightening too slowly or too quickly. She left the Fed after President Trump appointed Jerome Powell, who is expected to continue gradual rate hikes. Under Yellen, unemployment fell from 6.7% to 4.1% without pushing inflation above target.

Arizona pioneered school choice, operating open enrollment for district schools for 30 years, charter schools for more than 25 years and a private‑school tax‑credit program. It was the first state (2011) to enact direct parent‑appropriations through Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers and later the first to make the program universal (2022), despite voters rejecting a capped expansion in 2018. The state now supplies over $1 billion annually in subsidies to private education, with little accountability.

Research by the Grand Canyon Institute (GCI) shows that ESA vouchers are concentrated in higher‑income zip codes, though the disparity has narrowed as participation grew. About 90 % of new universal entrants in FY 2025 came from district or charter schools, yet roughly three‑quarters of all universal participants never attended a public school. Less than 40 % of ESA allocations in FY 2023 were used for private‑school tuition; the rest funded homeschool or extracurriculars.

FY 2023 spending on private schools totaled $173 million, with 51 % to religious schools (primarily evangelical Christian and Catholic) and 44 % to schools serving students with disabilities; secular private schools received under 5 %. Voucher amounts equal 90 % of charter funding, can exceed $30 000 for high‑need students, and most awards are under $8 000.

GCI estimates the universal ESA program cost the state at least $330 million in FY 2024 and about $350 million in FY 2025, because most participants never enrolled in public schools. Enrollment grew from 144 (2012) to 87,602 by Q3 FY 2025, driven initially by disability categories then by universal expansion. Account balances accumulated to $360 million by FY 2024, with a small number of accounts holding large balances. Overall, GCI calculates a net universal‑voucher cost of roughly $349.5 million in FY 2025, including administrative expenses.

Mega Geometry is a new RTX technology that enables real‑time ray tracing of high‑detail geometry in game engines like Unreal Engine 5’s Nanite by solving two main hurdles: cluster‑based LOD updates and high object counts. It introduces Cluster‑level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) built from batches of up to 256 triangles, reducing BVH construction cost by two orders of magnitude, and a Partitioned Top‑Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) that updates only changed partitions, avoiding full TLAS rebuilds each frame. Mega Geometry supports DirectX 12 (via NVAPI), Vulkan extensions, and OptiX 9.0, and runs on all RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Blackwell’s 4th‑generation RT Cores include hardware cluster engines with new compression schemes, delivering up to 2× the ray‑triangle intersection rate and cutting VRAM usage for typical Nanite scenes by several hundred megabytes. The technology also accelerates displaced subdivision surfaces by mapping tessellation directly to CLAS generation.

Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) are a new hardware primitive for rendering strand‑like objects such as hair; LSS is roughly 2× faster and uses 5× less VRAM than the previous Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips (DOTS) approach.

Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles the efficiency of the core reorder logic, improving coherence extraction and accelerating neural shading workloads. SER is controllable through a small API and already benefits path‑traced games and production renderers without code changes.

The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a programmable RISC‑V scheduler on the GPU that offloads GPU‑context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and CPU bottlenecking, enabling smoother frame rates and better multitasking.

Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode support for 4:2:2 chroma video, improving color accuracy over 4:2:0 while requiring only two‑thirds the data of uncompressed 4:4:4. The 9th‑generation NVENC raises AV1/HEVC quality by 5 % BD‑BR PSNR and introduces an AV1 Ultra‑High‑Quality mode for an additional 5 % gain; it supports up to three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds by over 50 % versus the previous generation. The 6th‑generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decode speed and adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC decoding. DisplayPort 2.1b (UHBR20) provides up to 80 Gbps, enabling 8K @ 165 Hz and 4K @ 480 Hz with DSC.

Power‑efficiency improvements include fine‑grain power gating, independent voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, rapid clock gating, and accelerated frequency switching that reacts 1000× faster than prior architectures. Low‑latency sleep states enter 10× quicker, yielding up to 50 % power savings for small language‑model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to three extra frames per traditionally rendered frame), a 40 % faster AI model, 30 % lower VRAM usage, and Blackwell‑enhanced Flip Metering for smoother pacing. A new transformer‑based neural network doubles the parameter count, improving temporal stability, reducing ghosting, and enhancing detail for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA.

Neural Shaders, accessible via the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, enable techniques such as neural texture compression (up to 7:1 ratio), RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache for real‑time global illumination, RTX Skin (real‑time subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI facial rendering). These are powered by 5th‑generation Tensor Cores and Blackwell scheduling optimizations.

GPU families: GB202 (92.2 B transistors, 12 GPC, 192 SMs, 24 576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores) drives the RTX 5090. GB203 (45.6 B transistors, 84 SMs, 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores) powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 (31 B transistors, 50 SMs, 6 400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores) powers the RTX 5070. All support the full set of Blackwell features, DLSS 4, and AI‑driven rendering capabilities.

The passage describes a research study examining pre-service teachers' opinions on the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (grades 5-8). Using a survey model with 100 students from Bayburt University's Faculty of Sports Sciences, the study found that novice teachers generally held positive views regarding program achievements and considered teaching processes enriched with activities. However, they often responded "undecided" regarding scientific accuracy of outcomes, content features, and compatibility with other programs, indicating insufficient knowledge in these areas. Findings suggest curriculum evaluation helps improve programs by identifying faulty aspects. The conclusion recommends increasing studies on this topic and organizing seminars for prospective teachers about training programs.

The application discloses a method for fabricating three‑dimensional vertical NOR‑type memory string arrays. The method forms damascene local vertical bit lines and etches local word lines in two steps to avoid ribboning, thereby lowering the aspect ratio of word‑line stacks and improving structural stability during patterning. Alignment variations between the two etch steps are absorbed by grouping thin‑film transistors on each side of a stack into separate circuits with dedicated reference elements. After forming word‑line stacks, silicon‑nitride layers are selectively removed to create cavities that are filled with a metal layer; sidewall metal is then removed so that metal remains only in the word‑line strips. Elongated vias are formed through the stacks, and conformal layers of tunneling dielectric, charge‑storage, blocking dielectric, channel, optional liner, and sacrificial dielectric are deposited. Vias are repeated to create source and drain regions connected to global interconnect lines above and below the memory structure. A staircase structure is formed by successively recessing masking layers and etching portions of each word‑line strip, allowing vertical conductors to contact each local word line. Additional embodiments employ dielectric pillars or stacked masks to mechanically support high‑aspect‑ratio word‑line stacks. The disclosed fabrication process enables dense vertical NOR memory arrays while mitigating ribboning and alignment issues.

Digital ecosystems aim to mimic biological ecosystems to solve complex, dynamic problems in information systems. They incorporate evolutionary computing, spatial dynamics, and self-organization, using fitness landscapes, networks, and complex adaptive systems to create robust, scalable, and self-organising software. The architecture includes a decentralized peer-to-peer network of agents with local evolutionary optimization, sharing solutions across similar requests. Simulations based on business ecosystems demonstrate behavior resembling biological ecosystems.

The lecture introduces an effective field theory (EFT) for two non‑relativistic nucleons that describes low‑energy elastic scattering by contact interactions and their derivatives. It emphasizes that ordinary dimensional power counting can misidentify operators: an operator that looks irrelevant (e.g. the leading four‑nucleon contact term) is actually relevant when the scattering length is large, a situation called “fine tuning”. To obtain the correct power counting the kinetic term must include both the gradient term (∇²/2M) and the time‑derivative term (∂ₜ); keeping only the latter produces a pinch singularity in loop integrals.

The theory is built from operators C₂ₘ N⁴ with 2M derivatives; dimensional counting gives C₂ₘ ∼ 1/M. In the naive MS‑bar scheme power‑law divergences are invisible, so the coupling C₀ appears irrelevant. Physical data show that the S‑wave scattering lengths (≈ 23 fm for ¹S₀ and ≈ 5 fm for ³S₁) are much larger than the natural scale 1/Λ∼ 1/mπ, indicating a fine‑tuning that requires C₀ to be treated as relevant. This is achieved by switching to a renormalization scheme that tracks power divergences: either an off‑shell momentum‑subtraction scheme or the power‑divergence‑subtraction (PDS) scheme, which subtracts both D=4 and D=3 poles. In these schemes C₀ obeys a renormalization‑group equation (β = 8π μ (1 − a μ)²), revealing that the coupling runs to larger values as the subtraction scale μ is lowered, and the operator becomes relevant when μ∼ P. The resulting amplitude sums all bubble diagrams, giving P cot δ = Σₘ (Ĉ₂ₘ P²ᵐ) with Ĉ₀ ∝ 1/μ and Ĉ₂ ∝ 1/(μ² Λ). The RG flow has three fixed points: a = 0 (non‑interactive), a = ±∞ (interacting, scale‑ and conformal‑invariant). The pole at a = 1/μ corresponds to a bound state—the deuteron. At the interacting fixed points new symmetries appear, notably a combined spin‑isospin SU(4) symmetry and conformal invariance.

Using the revised power counting, predictions for low‑energy nucleon‑nucleon observables and for processes such as deuteron formation can be made; higher‑order operators are systematically enhanced or suppressed according to the renormalization‑group flow. The lecture stresses that power‑law divergences can be crucial for the correct power counting, and that different renormalization schemes (MS‑bar, off‑shell subtraction, PDS) can be matched to recover the same physics.
Coral Davenport reports that Russell Vought, director of the Office of Management and Budget, plans to circumvent Congress’s budgetary authority to advance the Trump administration’s agenda.

President Donald Trump said the government shutdown provides an “unprecedented opportunity” to cut federal agencies. The administration froze about $18 billion for New York City infrastructure projects and canceled $8 billion for climate projects in Democratic‑leaning states. Trump plans to meet with Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought—who helped author Project 2025—to decide which “Democrat Agencies” to cut and whether the cuts will be temporary or permanent. Top Democrats Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries, both representing New York, are leading opposition to the shutdown. Congress failed to pass a funding bill Wednesday, prompting the shutdown; Republicans favor a short‑term stopgap while Democrats are demanding an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described Democratic negotiators as “terrorists,” and White House officials warned that thousands of federal workers could be laid off within days. The Senate is scheduled to vote again on Friday.

Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation petitioned the D.C. Circuit to review the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s (NRC) transfer of regulatory authority over nuclear materials in New Jersey to that state under §274 of the Atomic Energy Act. Shieldalloy, which had spent a decade seeking NRC approval for on‑site decommissioning of its Newfield, New Jersey facility, argued that the transfer was arbitrary and capricious because New Jersey’s program was not compatible with the federal program and because the transfer would disrupt the processing of its pending decommissioning license. The court agreed that the NRC’s explanation was insufficient. It found that the NRC failed to connect the facts—Shieldalloy’s long‑standing, NRC‑reviewed decommissioning plan, New Jersey’s consistent opposition, and the risk of interference with license processing—to its decision to transfer authority. The court also noted that the NRC did not adequately explain why a partial transfer (excluding the Newfield site) was not an appropriate arrangement under criterion 25, despite precedent allowing limited agreements. Although the NRC argued that statutory language foreclosed partial transfers at a licensee’s request, the court observed the agency had not exercised interpretive discretion and thus could not receive Chevron deference. The court declined to address other claimed incompatibilities (e.g., ALARA, dose standards) as unnecessary. It granted Shieldalloy’s petition, vacated the transfer, and remanded for further proceedings consistent with the opinion.

AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine facilitates moving memory pages between memory tiers to optimize performance. The TMPM operates via a ring buffer interface and supports commands for migrating pages, including PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO handles DMA-mapped pages and SNP hypervisor pages, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages between Pre-Migration and Guest states. The engine requires IOMMU enablement and supports up to 128 pages per command, with 4KB alignment requirements. Interrupts indicate queue thresholds, completions, or errors. Firmware reload capability exists with version verification. Hardware errors during batch processing may render entire command pages unrecoverable.

Spanish banks Caixabank and Sabadell also declined following disappointing quarterly results. All sectors except oil and gas are in negative territory on the STOXX 600. Markets await U.S. payrolls data for further direction.

The passage explores whether large language models (LLMs) can autoformalize physical systems into differential game logic (dGL) for cyber‑physical systems (CPSs). Formalizing CPSs is traditionally difficult, time‑consuming, and error‑prone. The authors create 20 benchmarks from undergraduate kinematics problems and test three OpenAI models (GPT‑4o, GPT‑4.1, and o3) using few‑shot prompting and parser feedback. OpenAI o3 achieves a top‑5 success rate of 70%, significantly outperforming GPT‑4.1 (45%) and GPT‑4o (20%). The autoformalization pipeline includes a dGL parser for syntax checking and a semantic checker that verifies symbolic equivalence to expected solutions and ensures sufficient variable mutations. Six problems remain unsolved, classified into optimization, non‑polynomial continuous dynamics, and complicated dynamics categories, limited by checker capabilities. Results suggest LLM‑based autoformalization could accelerate formal methods adoption and enable runtime formalization of unfamiliar scenarios in autonomous systems.

Britain had light snowfall; author reports from Creeting St Peter, Suffolk. Government ministers are said to sabotage Theresa May's EU deal; a quoted Article 46 stresses EU‑UK commitments must be upheld in all circumstances. Post criticises lack of awareness of breaking contract consequences. It previews House of Lords business, noting Liberal Democrat focus, a new award scheme for young by‑election activists, Samaritans' Christmas work, and a “goodbye” musical interlude. Mark Valladares is Monday editor of Liberal Democrat Voice.

Depression and anxiety affect over 300 million people globally. This study collected 15,000+ minutes of speech recordings from 1,160 outpatients at Shanghai Mental Health Center with 25 diagnoses. Using a pre-trained LLM with clinical annotations and extracted linguistic/acoustic features, they built an ensemble machine learning pipeline to predict diagnostic groups and symptoms, demonstrating that LLM-generated objective cues combined with behavioral markers can differentiate diagnostic groups and identify symptom disclosure.

Everton beat Newcastle 1-0 at Goodison Park on Monday. Theo Walcott scored the only goal in the 51st minute, finishing from a Yannick Bolasie cross. It was Walcott's third goal for Everton since joining in January. Everton visit Huddersfield on Saturday; Newcastle host West Bromwich Albion the same day.

Cover Zero is an all‑out pressure defense that blitzes every non‑coverage player and forces the quarterback to make split‑second decisions, offering speed and simplicity but also high risk because every coverage player is on an island. Offensive coordinators try to avoid 3rd‑and‑long and use quick, short routes such as slants, shallow crosses, and pick plays to exploit the open middle of the field. Effective man‑beaters and perimeter talent help counter the blitz. Several specific plays that attack Cover Zero are described: the Double Slants from Ole Miss, which uses mirrored slant routes for a quick throw to a slot receiver; the Full‑Slide Fade‑Out/RB Seam Gadget from Oregon, a timed gadget that uses slide protection and a slipping running back to score; the Trips Bunch Jerk Route from Michigan, a red‑zone play relying on natural picks and rubs from a bunch set; the Slant‑Rub from Wake Forest, a goal‑line concept that creates a natural rub for the Z receiver; and the Jerry Rice Motion Slant‑Flat from Dixie State, which uses pre‑snap motion to lose a defender and open a TE for a score.

Neale Cooper, 54, Aberdeen and Gothenburg player from the 1983 Cup Winners’ Cup team, died from a fall. Former Aberdeen manager Steve Paterson suggested his funeral be held at Pittodrie stadium. Fans, Alex McLeish, Willie Miller and Stewart Milne paid tribute.

FlowMotion ONE, a smartphone stabilizer, raised over $600,000 on Kickstarter in one hour against a $30,000 goal, attracting more than 2,700 backers. Its 3inONE design allows use as a wearable mount, a handle with joystick, or an extension pole, eliminating shake via sensors and high‑precision motors. The product weighs less than a pound, fits in a pocket, and can attach to bikes, tripods or selfie‑stick‑style poles. Founded in 2015 by Lars Flesland, Julie Bauge, Eirik Dyrseth and Didrik Dimmen, the 10‑person team operates from Palo Alto and Trondheim, Norway, with a mission to help people capture smooth cinema‑quality video. FlowMotion has received awards in Norway, Finland, Germany and the United States.

The study used Demographic and Health Survey data from Benin (2017‑2018) and Cameroon (2018) to assess women’s awareness of cervical cancer and cervical screening. A total of 21 322 women aged 15‑49 were included. Awareness of cervical cancer was 9.5 % in Benin and 46.1 % in Cameroon; roughly half of those aware also knew about screening. Higher awareness was associated with older age, higher education, frequent internet use, and, in Cameroon only, higher wealth. Media use (radio, television, internet) was positively related to awareness of both cancer and screening in both countries. The study concludes that awareness is low, especially among younger, less educated, and poorer women, and recommends strengthening awareness programmes through stakeholder involvement, public education, and targeted interventions. Limitations include the cross‑sectional design, a small sub‑sample for screening awareness, and potential recall bias.

SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19, is transmitted via respiratory droplets and shed in feces, allowing detection in wastewater. Monitoring SARS-CoV-2 RNA in wastewater is critical for surveillance. Initial processing involves concentrating viruses from 50-250 mL samples using methods like membrane filtration or skim milk, but these require centrifuges. Nanotrap particles offer a versatile, sensitive method for capturing and preserving viruses and nucleic acids from complex samples like wastewater, without compromising sensitivity. Sampling methods include grab, composite, and passive sampling; this study used Moore swab passive sampling and grab samples. The study evaluates parameters affecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and compares manual Nanotrap methods (10 mL) to membrane filtration (150 mL) and skim milk (250 mL) methods for low-resource settings. Samples were collected from Atlanta wastewater treatment plants and manholes.

A veterinarian at Gentle Care Animal Hospital in Edmond, Oklahoma surgically removed 21 pacifiers from a dog named Dovey. The dog had slowed eating and was vomiting; an X‑ray indicated 7–9 pacifiers, but surgery uncovered 21. Dovey recovered and was released home.

On December 12, 2000, utility stocks in the US were up 36% year-to-date but flattening due to a tech rebound and seasonal demand decline. Analysts noted opportunities remain due to tight capacity. Enron's Indian unit, Dabhol Power Company, had four local lenders cut loan rates by 450 basis points to 16.5% to lower power tariffs. Natural gas prices hit a record $9.413 per million BTU, prompting firms like Terra Industries and Mississippi Chemical to sell natural gas rather than use it in production. Activate, a digital media services company, reported 15-30X growth in 2000 with over 100 million streams and industry awards. A retired Indian judge suggested Enron's Dabhol Power Purchase Agreement could be nullified for not serving public interest. Green Mountain Energy applied to become the first renewable power retailer in Texas. The New Power Company, formed by Enron, was certified as a retail natural gas marketer in Georgia. In internet energy trading, EnronOnline and IntercontinentalExchange dominated, while smaller exchanges struggled with liquidity. Dynegy's new e-commerce site had $1.5 billion in November trading.

Between Jan 1 2010 and Sep 1 2022 the Wisconsin Poison Center (WPC) received 59 calls about Kratom exposure. Most callers were male (62.7 %) with a mean age of 35.3 years; three exposures involved infants under two. Calls rose from zero in 2010 to a peak of 15 in 2020, with the majority of cases in southeastern counties (Marinette County had the most, 10 calls). About 56 % of exposures involved Kratom only; the remainder involved polysubstance use, most commonly alcohol and benzodiazepines. The most frequently reported symptoms were agitation (39 %), tachycardia (35.6 %), confusion (23.7 %) and central‑nervous‑system depression (22 %). Among calls with known outcome, 38 % had moderate or major medical effects, and seven patients required critical care (including an infant and several older adults); one death was recorded with Kratom listed as contributory. The authors recommend that clinicians be aware of increasing Kratom use, gather detailed exposure histories, and counsel on safe storage and avoidance of concomitant substance use.

Randomized apixaban trial for NVAF: 1112 subjects, 48‑week, 1:1 randomized to SOC information or Additional Program; at 24 weeks Additional Program re‑randomized to continue/revert to SOC. Adherence tracked; 24‑hour window counted adherent if doses taken unless two consecutive doses missed; withheld days excluded; >30 consecutive days without treatment = permanent discontinuation.

The article discusses the upcoming Alabama vs Texas A&M football game, where the top-ranked Crimson Tide faces an unranked Aggies team. Given Alabama's dominance (outscoring SEC opponents by 122 points and not losing a conference game in over two years), the matchup lacks its previous luster. Coach Kevin Sumlin is under pressure, and while the Florida game isn't necessarily a must-win, strong performance in the final six games is crucial for his job security. The field will feature a tribute to former coach Gene Stallings and the 1967 team that beat No. 8 Alabama in the Cotton Bowl.

Asia‑Pacific markets were muted after mixed Chinese PMI data, with Australian markets nervous ahead of the RBA. The S&P 500 rose 2.2 % in July (7.8 % YTD, 8.6 % total return) but fell 1.6 % at the start of August. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, investors are increasing tech allocations, and U.S. electricity demand hit a record high. Short‑term technicals are weak, with the 50‑day breadth rolling over from overbought, while medium‑ and long‑term trends remain healthy. US large‑cap stocks placed third in monthly returns, behind frontier markets; August opened with a sell‑off that erased part of July’s gains. Gold topped $3,800/oz for the first time amid U.S. shutdown concerns and rate‑cut bets. An Investing.com advertisement promotes its AI‑driven ProPicks service, stating that three‑quarters of its global portfolios beat benchmarks and that its Tech Titans strategy doubled the S&P 500 in 18 months. Data on the site may not be real‑time, and trading involves high risk.

Swiss spy arrested in Germany May 2017; watchdog rejected OAG involvement. 54‑year‑old former policeman faces investigation since 2015 for handling stolen banking data sold to Germany. North Rhine‑Westphalia bought 11 CDs, recovering €7 bn tax. Whether he acted for the FIS remains unclear; government confirmed FIS assistance in 2014 and the Green Party seeks a parliamentary inquiry.

Players credit the team's performance to long‑term togetherness, which builds trust and helps them in tough moments. Dustin Brown notes that a lead provides emotional relief and that strong starts are important. He adds that matchups between major cities increase fan interest and heighten the sport’s profile. Anze Kopitar says the team stays focused on the next game and only reflects after advancing in the playoffs, then resets quickly. Brown points out Drew Doughty’s growth as a player and leader since the Olympics and the squad’s goal of winning the Stanley Cup rather than just a division title. The group emphasizes closeness off the ice, voluntary workouts, lack of cliques, and seamless integration of new players like Gaborik. Brown describes Justin’s calm, focused approach and big‑game ability. The core has stayed together for hundreds of games after earlier high turnover.

Memphis police say 2‑year‑old Laylah Washington died after being shot in the head while riding with her mother and brothers on Sunday. The mother reported a near‑collision in a parking lot, an argument with the other driver, and being followed before shots were fired. The girl was the only person hit and was taken to a hospital in critical condition. No arrests have been made; police are seeking a black Chevrolet Impala.

HMP Northward is operating about 22 inmates over its 212‑person capacity, prompting authorities to transfer low‑risk prisoners to a cordoned section of the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks. The move aims to relieve overcrowding, mitigate security risks and restore rehabilitation programmes, while maintaining separation from the centre’s migrants and asylum seekers, including nine hunger‑striking detainees. Officials say the plan is a short‑term solution while longer‑term options are pursued.

The passage describes a communication processing method for a wireless communications system that supports a duplication mode, in which PDCP data is transmitted on a first RLC entity (first path) and duplicated on a second RLC entity (second path). The method includes two main aspects.

First aspect – data‑volume reporting in duplication mode: a terminal determines that a data volume report needs to be triggered for one of the two paths. The path can be indicated by a first message from the radio access network, selected by the terminal based on priority, or selected based on the data volume on each path. The terminal triggers the report, which indicates the data volume on the selected path, and sends the report to the radio access network. The network may also send a second message indicating the cell or cell group corresponding to each path; the report can be sent in the cell/group of the selected path or in a different cell/group if resources are unavailable.

Second aspect – activation/deactivation of the duplication mode: the terminal receives a first indication message from the radio access network that indicates whether to activate the duplication mode for a radio bearer. The message contains fields that identify it as a duplication‑mode control message, activation bits for each path, and optionally identifiers of the radio bearer and the paths. Based on the indication, the terminal activates or deactivates the mode. When the mode is activated, the terminal may trigger a data‑volume report that includes the volume on one path or the sum of both paths. When deactivated, the terminal stops duplicating data, may discard duplicated data in buffers, and may continue sending non‑duplicated data on a designated path while still reporting the data volume on the active path.

The passage also details message structures, handling of duplicated data on deactivation, and optional implementations for carrier aggregation and dual‑connectivity scenarios, as well as the architecture of a communications apparatus, a computer‑storage medium and a device that implement the described methods.

Microsoft Corporation reported strong first quarter fiscal year 2021 results with total revenue of $37.2 billion, a 12% increase from the prior year period. Net income was $13.9 billion, up 30% year-over-year, with diluted earnings per share of $1.82, representing a 32% increase. Operating income grew 25% to $15.9 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion, driven by Azure growth of 48% and Office 365 Commercial growth of 21%. The company entered into an agreement to acquire ZeniMax Media Inc. (parent of Bethesda) for $7.5 billion in cash, expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2021. A change in accounting estimate for server and network equipment useful lives increased operating income by $927 million for the quarter. Segment revenue growth: Intelligent Cloud increased 20%, Productivity and Business Processes increased 11%, and More Personal Computing increased 6%.

A special weather statement has been issued for Edmonton and surrounding areas due to conditions favorable for funnel cloud development Wednesday afternoon. Environment Canada warns weak rotation could intensify into a landspout tornado with winds up to 100 km/h, though this is considered unlikely. Jesse Beyer advises people to be sky aware and prepared to take shelter. As a precaution, Sturgeon Composite High School gathered about 500 students indoors. Landspout tornadoes rarely cause significant damage but should be taken seriously.

Britain's FTSE 100 fell 0.2% on Friday, heading for its worst week since August 2017, with BT and AstraZeneca weighing on the index after disappointing results. BT dropped over 5% to a five-year low following concerns about growth and its pension scheme, while AstraZeneca fell 1.7% on a disappointing profit outlook. Capita rebounded 5% after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to "equal-weight" from "underweight."

This passage describes a data intake and query system designed to collect, index, and search large volumes of machine data from modern data centers. The system processes machine data from diverse sources (servers, networks, mobile devices, IoT, etc.) and stores it as events, each associated with a timestamp and metadata fields (host, source, sourcetype). Key system components include: forwarders that collect and forward data with metadata; indexers that parse data into events, assign timestamps, apply optional transformations, and generate keyword and field-value pair indexes stored in time-based buckets (hot, warm, cold, frozen); and search heads that execute queries against indexed events. The system employs a late-binding schema, applying field extraction rules at search time to preserve raw machine data and enable flexible analysis. It supports both on-premises and cloud-based deployments, and can access external data sources (e.g., Hadoop, SQL databases) via External Result Provider (ERP) processes operating in streaming, reporting, or mixed modes. Users query events using keywords, field criteria, and time ranges to gain operational insights.

Melissa Jennings, a former member of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill women’s soccer team, sued UNC and several individuals, including head coach Anson Dorrance, alleging Title IX sexual harassment, constitutional privacy violations under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, and common‑law invasion of privacy. Jennings claimed that Dorrance made frequent sexually explicit comments and inquiries about players during warm‑ups and once asked her “Who are you fucking?” in a private meeting. She also alleged that assistant coach William Palladino participated in some of the conversations. After Jennings was dismissed from the team in May 1998, she filed a complaint that later included a Title IX claim, § 1983 claims for privacy invasion, sexual harassment, and supervisory failure, and a state‑law intrusion claim. The court denied Jennings’s motions to strike the defendants’ amended answer and to strike exhibits C–H. On summary judgment, the court held that the alleged conduct was not severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive under Title IX; that Dorrance’s two inquiries did not violate Jennings’s constitutional right to privacy; that no actionable hostile‑environment sexual harassment occurred under § 1983; that supervisory defendants had no knowledge of a constitutional violation; and that the conduct did not meet the North Carolina standard for intrusion into privacy. Accordingly, the court granted summary judgment for all defendants on all claims.

Mel Stride, Treasury minister, said fish fingers would be safe under the Government during Brexit. Labour MP Mel Onn urged him to ensure customs arrangements protect Great Grimsby’s time‑sensitive fish trade and processing industry, which supports 5,000 jobs.

The article reviews the integration of information technology (IT) into language education, especially in Indonesia, under Education 4.0. It identifies challenges such as teachers’ limited digital proficiency, difficulty maintaining student engagement online, resource inequality (digital divide), and problems assessing speaking and listening skills remotely; it notes benefits including technologies like Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for pronunciation and vocabulary, task‑based and game‑based learning, augmented and virtual reality, AI, and gamification that make language learning more interactive. Management strategies highlighted involve using digital platforms that support synchronous and asynchronous learning, investing in teacher professional development, providing AI‑based language assistants and translation tools, fostering global collaborations and virtual exchanges, building cloud‑based infrastructure, deploying mobile learning solutions, applying data‑driven decision‑making, and establishing inclusive IT policies. Students generally exhibit a positive attitude toward IT in language learning, comparable to their enthusiasm for STEM subjects, though resistance to adoption and unequal access to resources remain concerns. The study employs a qualitative descriptive method, conducting a literature review of 1,010 manuscripts from Scopus, retaining 151 highly relevant papers, and presents bibliometric data, research trends, top‑cited articles, and a proposed framework for IT and management strategies in Indonesian language education.

Agreement is the entire understanding; void provisions do not affect the remainder. It is governed by California and U.S. federal law, excludes the UN Convention, and disputes must be filed in Santa Clara County courts. Export must follow U.S. regulations, and amendments require written, signed authorization.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 selective private colleges of conspiring to inflate tuition. The plaintiffs alleged the schools overcharged students of divorced or separated parents by considering both parents' finances, raising tuition by about $6,200. The judge found no plausible agreement among the schools and noted the complaint did not show they shared aid‑decision data or used a common formula.

During a human trafficking training session in Oshakati, Prosecutor‑General Martha Imalwa said it is the third‑largest international crime, generating $32 billion (N$401 billion), with 20‑30 million in slavery and 600,000‑800,000 trafficked, 80 % women, some children. Namibia reported an 11‑year‑old boy found in South Africa and underpaid Angolan children. She sought UN training for investigators, prosecutors and victim assistance. Ndeitunga reported 25 cases (2010‑2017): six pending, three declined, one convicted, one acquitted, fourteen under investigation.

A randomized, single‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of SA58 nasal spray—a broad‑spectrum anti‑COVID‑19 monoclonal antibody—as post‑exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in 1,222 healthy adult workers who had contact with SARS‑CoV‑2‑infected individuals within 72 hours. The study was conducted at 21 construction sites in Beijing during an Omicron BF·7 outbreak. Participants self‑administered SA58 (5 mg/ml, 1 mg per dose) or placebo intranasally 5–6 times daily. Among the 1,123 participants included in the efficacy analysis, laboratory‑confirmed symptomatic COVID‑19 occurred in 7 of 824 (0.22 per 100 person‑days) in the SA58 group versus 14 of 299 (1.17 per 100 person‑days) in the placebo group, yielding a protective efficacy of 80.82 % (95 % CI 52.41–92.27 %). SARS‑CoV‑2 RT‑PCR positivity occurred in 32 versus 32 participants (1.04 vs. 2.80 per 100 person‑days), representing a 61.83 % (95 % CI 37.50–76.69 %) reduction in infection. No severe COVID‑19 or deaths were observed. Adverse events were mild and similar between groups (25 % SA58 vs 22 % placebo); the most common were nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, and headache, all grade 1. The authors conclude that SA58 nasal spray provided satisfactory efficacy and safety as PEP, with advantages of non‑invasive administration and rapid self‑use, and recommend further evaluation in high‑risk populations.

A medical system for assisting rescuers with intubation or rapid sequence intubation (RSI) procedures includes airflow sensors (oxygen, capnography, flow), physiological sensors (pulse oximeter, ECG, acoustic, impedance, blood pressure), a patient monitoring device with processor, memory, display, and defibrillator capability, and optional portable computing devices. The processor receives sensor data, detects airway airflow, initiates a timer (default 5–15 seconds, user‑adjustable) to confirm proper endotracheal (ET) tube placement within the interval, and evaluates physiological information (ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, acoustic patterns) against predetermined criteria (fixed thresholds, trends, percentage of moving average, or deviation from an initial or dynamic baseline). Visual feedback, alarms, and guidance are presented on the device display, touchscreen, or wrist‑worn devices. The system automatically identifies steps of the RSI process (e.g., preoxygenation, intubation, post‑intubation) by analyzing intubation parameters (gas, physiological, positioning data) and transitions, providing context‑sensitive feedback. It verifies tube placement by confirming that ventilation airflow reaches the lungs (via capnography, impedance, or acoustic detection) and monitors ongoing placement by detecting deviations from baseline values. Components include a defibrillator/AED, electrode assembly, airway sensor module (optionally integrated in a bag‑valve‑mask), and communication links (wired or wireless). Sensors described include an oxygen sensor (0–100 % range), pulse oximeter, and near‑infrared tissue oxygen sensor.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, a law requiring major AI companies headquartered in California to publicly disclose how they will mitigate catastrophic risks from advanced AI models, report critical safety incidents to the state’s Office of Emergency Services and extend whistleblower protections to employees. The legislation also establishes CalCompute, a public computing consortium for safe AI research, and imposes civil penalties for non‑compliance enforceable by the state attorney general, though penalties are considered weak. Companies with training compute costs in the hundreds of millions and annual revenue over $500 million are covered; 32 of the world’s top 50 AI firms are based in California, giving the law potential global reach. Reactions are mixed: Anthropic backs the measure, OpenAI and Meta call it a positive step toward federal‑state harmonization, while Andreessen Horowitz and other critics argue it could burden startups and create a patchwork of regulations. Authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener, the law focuses on transparency rather than liability, succeeding a vetoed earlier bill (SB 1047).

Kevin Love has accumulated scratches and bruises from battling NBA big men as he prepares for his fourth NBA Finals with Cleveland. He is recovering from a concussion sustained against Boston that could keep him out of Game 1 and has disclosed anxiety and panic attacks. Traded to Cleveland in 2014, he joined LeBron James and Kyrie Irving and became a target of criticism, labeled soft, overrated and injury‑prone, with trade rumors. After a January team meeting questioning his absence from a game, he revealed his panic attacks in a Player’s Tribune essay, prompting thousands of supportive messages and community. He has undergone counseling, asks not to be treated differently, and calls basketball his refuge. In the playoffs his performance was uneven; a collision in Game 6 placed him in concussion protocol, and Jeff Green helped the Cavs win Game 7. Love’s Finals opener status is uncertain, but he remains optimistic about his time in Cleveland.

Tropical Storm Nate formed off Nicaragua, causing at least 17 deaths in Central America. Forecast models predict it will cross the Yucatan peninsula Friday night, move into the Gulf of Mexico, and reach the northern Gulf coast Saturday evening, intensifying into a hurricane by Saturday night or Sunday. The National Hurricane Center’s warning cone now stretches from the Florida Panhandle to central Louisiana, placing Pensacola on the storm’s eastern side where wind gusts, storm surge and tornadoes are most likely. Nate is expected to bring 3–5 inches of rain, flash flooding and possible tornadoes to Escambia and Santa Rosa counties Saturday through Sunday, with tropical‑storm‑force winds of 35–45 mph and gusts up to 65 mph in Escambia. A tropical‑storm watch is in effect for the area. Gov. Rick Scott declared a state of emergency in Escambia, Santa Rosa and 27 other Florida counties; the Florida National Guard has 7,000 members available for deployment. Several events and schools, including the University of West Florida and Pensacola State College, are closed or cancelled, and sandbag locations are open in Santa Rosa County.

Summer 2017 box office was marked by the dominance of three comic‑book superhero releases—Warner Bros./Time Warner’s Wonder Woman, Disney’s Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 and Sony’s Spider‑Man: Homecoming—which earned top‑tier domestic and worldwide numbers. Most other genres produced only one successful entry: the year’s biggest animated film, Universal’s Despicable Me 3; the top comedy, Girls Trip; the top horror, New Line/Warner’s Annabelle: Creation; the adult drama Dunkirk; the studio programmer Baby Driver; and the indie hit The Big Sick. The remaining releases largely underperformed or failed, including Cars 3, King Arthur: Legend of the Sword, Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight and War for the Planet of the Apes. Comedies, adult dramas and other genre films struggled, with only occasional modest successes such as Everything, Everything. The season highlighted a lack of content diversity, as non‑superhero films rarely achieved multiple hits in their categories.

Researchers at UC Irvine and other institutions have introduced a new satellite‑based drought severity index (GRACE‑DSI) that incorporates terrestrial water storage, including groundwater, into drought assessments. The index uses data from NASA’s GRACE mission (2002‑2014) and will be extended with the ongoing GRACE and a 2018 follow‑on mission. It provides globally consistent, continuous monitoring, even in data‑sparse regions, and has demonstrated agreement with the Palmer drought severity index and other metrics in the continental U.S. The work was presented at the AGU fall meeting and offers a more comprehensive view of hydrological drought impacts worldwide.

Guitarist Tony Iommi answered questions May 25 at Birmingham’s BIMM Music Institute, announcing his sponsorship of a scholarship and noting he has always considered his career worthwhile, citing needed drive to survive setbacks.

On May 24, 2001, news reports covered energy and political issues. California officials, including Attorney General Bill Lockyer, accused energy companies like Enron of manipulating electricity prices, while Governor Gray Davis faced criticism. A potential party switch by Senator James Jeffords could shift Senate control, impacting industries such as drugs, HMOs, defense, tobacco, and energy. Brazil began energy rationing, asking consumers to cut usage by 20% to avoid blackouts. In India, the federal government intervened in a dispute between Enron's Dabhol Power Co. and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Poland's gas market faced changes with proposed pipeline projects and sales of gas assets like Slovakia's SPP. Endesa announced the sale of its Electra de Viesgo subsidiary, and Dynegy expressed interest in acquisitions and mergers.

Ryan ToysReview, launched in 2015 by a six‑year‑old boy, earned $11 million in 2017 and ranked among Forbes’ top‑paid YouTube stars. The channel has over 10 million subscribers and over eight billion views in the tracked year. The family keeps their surname and location private, and the show will continue only as long as the child enjoys it.

The long-short equity strategy is an investment method where traders take long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline. It aims to minimize risk through hedging while maximizing profits from both rising and falling values. Traders identify undervalued stocks to buy and overvalued stocks to sell short, often applying the strategy across different sectors to avoid correlation. The strategy is popular with hedge funds and suitable for institutional investors who can use leverage and derivatives. A backtest example using Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola showed an average gain per trade of 0.45%, annual return of 3.8%, and maximum drawdown of about 11%. Leverage is typically needed because average gains per trade are normally low.

This study presents a machine learning-assisted inverse design workflow for discovering new 2D Dion-Jacobson (DJ) perovskites with tailored electronic properties. Researchers developed a 12-digit invertible molecular fingerprint system to encode organic spacers, enabling navigation from 21 known spacers to approximately 4 million hypothetical candidates through molecular morphing across generations G0-G6. High-throughput DFT calculations on 3,239 spacers provided training data for machine learning models to predict frontier orbital energy levels (HOMO/LUMO). The workflow includes synthesis feasibility screening using PubChem accessibility and a formability score based on five topological descriptors with a 0.88 cutoff distinguishing 2D from non-2D perovskite spacers. Analysis identified 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates that passed feasibility filters and DFT validation. No type Ib candidates were found in G0-G6 due to synthetic accessibility constraints, but inverse design guided by fingerprint constraints revealed 2 type Ib spacers in G7-G8, 12 additional type IIa candidates in G3-G9, and 42 additional type IIb candidates in G2-G6. Type Ib alignment requires at least five linearly fused benzene rings (pentacene backbone), type IIa typically requires extended conjugation through more rings or oligothiophenes, and type IIb requires a single primary ammonium group with pyridine-type nitrogen substitution. The workflow integrates database generation, high-throughput calculations, machine learning, and DFT validation, with the key innovation being the invertible fingerprint representation enabling direct mapping between molecular structure and target properties.

A circuit using the PGA848 amplifier to drive the ADS8860 16-bit SAR ADC is described, featuring ±15V input-stage and 5.3V output-stage power supplies. The REF6250 provides a 5V reference, with the PGA848 REF pin set to 2.5V via a precision voltage divider buffered by an OPA192 op amp configured in dual-feedback for stability, achieving 86° phase margin. Three filters are employed: an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback filter with 75pF capacitance yielding a 318kHz cutoff, and a charge reservoir filter at the ADC inputs. The circuit maintains -0.1dB flatness to 41kHz with a nominal 318kHz bandwidth. Power supply recommendations specify ±15V, warning against exceeding ±20V to prevent damage. Layout guidelines stress symmetrical input paths, bypass capacitors, trace separation, and minimizing parasitic capacitance and thermal effects. Simulation tools like TINA-TI and PSpice are recommended for design verification.

Federal judges responding to a New York Times survey expressed widespread dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions related to President Trump’s second term. Of the 65 respondents, only 12 said the Court had made appropriate use of the docket and only 12 said lower courts received sufficient guidance. Of 54 judges, just two said the docket improved the judiciary’s public perception, while 42 reported it caused harm. Judges described the orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” and “incredibly demoralizing,” and one characterized the relationship as a “war zone.” The survey, sent to over 400 federal judges, included 28 Republican appointees and 37 Democratic appointees. Most emergency orders lacked reasoning and benefited the administration, granting broad practical effects such as deportations and mass firings. The Times noted respondents may not represent the whole judiciary, and a Volokh Conspiracy critique highlighted potential sampling bias.

The case that made federalism go up in smoke involved a 2002 confrontation where DEA agents destroyed medical marijuana plants from Diane Monson's California backyard, despite state law permitting them. Monson and Angel Raich, who both used medical cannabis for serious medical conditions with physician recommendation, sued arguing Congress lacked constitutional authority to regulate their purely local activities under the interstate commerce clause.

The case reached the Supreme Court, which ruled 6-3 in favor of the government in 2005. Justice John Paul Stevens wrote the majority opinion joined by justices including Scalia and Kennedy, reasoning that Congress could regulate local medical cannabis because it was part of a larger regulatory scheme targeting the interstate market. The majority deferred to Congress's judgment that legal medical marijuana would reach the black market.

Justice Sandra Day O'Connor dissented, arguing the decision removed meaningful limits on the commerce clause by allowing Congress to package local activity regulation within broader schemes. Justice Clarence Thomas wrote a longer dissent, using originalist interpretation to argue "commerce" referred only to buying, selling, and transporting, not activities like growing marijuana for personal use. Thomas said Congress presented no evidence justifying regulation and warned the decision gave the federal government power over "quilting bees, clothes drives, and potluck suppers."

Chief Justice Rehnquist dissented without written opinion. The decision was described as "a major – possibly even terminal – setback" for efforts to limit commerce power, with federalism called "a casualty of the war on drugs."

Randy Barnett, who argued the case, later successfully challenged the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate on commerce clause grounds, securing a ruling that Congress cannot compel "inactivity." Justice Thomas has continued advocating for originalist commerce clause interpretation in subsequent cases, calling the federal marijuana ban contradictory in 2021.

VREF offers 1.4V and 2.5V internal references with external reference support. The comparator module compares voltage levels with six blanking sources and wakeup capability. The 12-bit DAC supports self-calibration, multiple data formats, and DMA operation. Security features include AES-128/256 encryption, secure key storage for up to four keys, and CRC-16/32. The TRNG generates 32-bit random numbers for FIPS-140-2 compliant systems. MATHACL provides hardware-accelerated 32-bit math functions. Communication peripherals include multiple UART instances supporting LIN mode and DMA, I2C with speeds up to 1 Mbit/s, SPI up to 32 Mbit/s, and CAN-FD compliant to ISO 11898-1. The Low-Frequency Sub System (LFSS) contains RTC_B and independent watchdog timer. Timers include general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) variants with features like PWM, quadrature encoder interface, and fault handling. Additional features include serial wire debug interface, boot strap loader with password protection, and factory constants memory region.

This passage describes systems and methods for improving occlusion rendering in passthrough visualizations for artificial reality head-mounted devices (HMDs). Passthrough allows a user wearing an HMD to view the physical environment via front-facing cameras by re-projecting captured images to the user’s viewpoint using a 3D model of the surroundings. A problem arises because the 3D model—typically a coarse mesh approximating object contours—may be imprecise, especially at edges, leading to incorrect occlusion between physical and virtual objects. This manifests as under-occlusion (virtual objects incorrectly visible through a physical object) or over-occlusion (empty space around a physical object incorrectly occluding virtual objects).

The disclosed embodiments address this by leveraging instance segmentation masks. A machine-learning model (e.g., Mask R-CNN) processes captured images to generate masks identifying specific object instances (e.g., people, pets). Each mask’s pixels are associated with a representative depth value computed from corresponding portions of the 3D model (e.g., averaged depth or depth at the centroid of the object). To mitigate over-occlusion, padded borders around each mask are generated (e.g., via morphological gradient), and these borders are assigned depth values significantly farther than the object’s representative depth, enforcing a hard edge. During rendering, visibility tests cast rays from the user’s eye viewpoints through screen pixels; if a ray intersects a portion of the 3D model corresponding to a segmented instance, the rendering system uses the instance’s representative depth (or its padded border’s depth) rather than the measured mesh depth to determine occlusion against virtual objects. If no instance matches, the measured mesh depth is used.

The passage also describes depth measurement techniques: high-performance devices may use GPU-based optical flow with stereo triangulation, while resource-limited devices may leverage a device’s video encoder to compute motion vectors between stereo images, followed by epipolar and temporal filtering to obtain reliable correspondences. The resulting sparse point cloud deforms a hemispheric 3D mesh approximating the environment’s contour, which is then used for rendering.

In summary, the embodiments improve passthrough occlusion accuracy by integrating instance segmentation masks with depth-based rendering decisions, reducing visual artifacts in mixed-reality scenes.

A study examined factors attracting and retaining rural special education teachers in Midwest US using surveys from three cooperatives (93 respondents). Statistical analyses showed significant relationships between support/satisfaction and intent to remain. Plaintiff Thomas H. Fisher sued Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane seeking an accounting for $6,500 paid to Fuller, Rodney & Co. in commodity transactions in December 1940–January 1941. After Fuller dissolved on April 30 1941, defendants took over certain customer accounts with customer consent, but plaintiff’s account was not transferred. Plaintiff claimed defendants assumed Fuller’s liabilities through a merger/consolidation and requested discovery of documents. Defendants moved for summary judgment, supported by affidavits and the April 18 1941 agreement showing no assumption of liabilities, no transfer of plaintiff’s account, and no merger. Plaintiff’s affidavit admitted lack of personal knowledge and relied on information and belief, failing to meet evidentiary standards. The trial court granted summary judgment; plaintiff appealed. The appellate court held that competent evidence demonstrated no genuine issue of material fact, the Civil Practice Act permitted summary judgment in equitable accounting actions, and no court order denying discovery appeared of record. The decree was affirmed.

Global operations include centers in Ireland, Singapore, and the United States; phone manufacturing is primarily in Vietnam, with the entry‑level feature‑phone business announced for sale in May 2016. Other devices are produced by third‑party contract manufacturers.

Customers include consumers, small‑ and medium‑size organizations, large global enterprises, public‑sector institutions, Internet service providers, application developers, and OEMs; no single customer accounted for more than 10 % of revenue. Tokyo residents who endure long commutes and live in small homes face increased risk of insomnia and daytime sleepiness, according to a study by Osaka Metropolitan University. Smaller housing size independently predicted insomnia, while longer commutes also heightened daytime sleepiness. The findings highlight a trade‑off between location and floor area affecting sleep health, suggesting that housing policies balancing commute distance and dwelling size could improve sleep and reduce related economic losses.

A defender must adopt a proper 1‑v‑1 stance after reaching a goal‑side position. Use a forward “lead” foot and a backward “trail” foot, with the dominant leg as the trail foot. Keep feet 18 inches apart, stay balanced on the balls of both feet, knees bent, elbows bent, arms out. This enables reactions, slowing or forcing opponent, avoiding being beaten, preparing to tackle. Lead‑foot placement varies by field side: left foot on the right side, right foot on the left side, optional in the centre. Coaches demonstrate the stance for right, centre, left; practice with and without a ball; use field markings. Youth need one‑on‑one instruction; basketball guards and football cornerbacks illustrate the stance, but defenders must not block or extend arms.

Iso is a downhill running scheme used in I‑formation and traditional pro‑style offenses. It isolates a fullback as a lead blocker on a linebacker, designed to overpower the defense and move the ball quickly to the second level. Its strengths are fast vertical push and simplicity, making it easy to teach and execute. Its main weakness is a heavy dependence on personnel—requiring large, powerful linemen and a rugged fullback to win one‑on‑one blocks. Iso includes detailed blocking assignments for a 3‑4 odd front and a 4‑3 even front. Two notable variations are Shotgun Iso (used by Baylor in a spread offense, often paired with RPOs) and Weakside Iso (run to the weak side with favorable double‑team angles).

"Shall" denotes mandatory provisions, "should" recommended, "may" optional. The document defines the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification V6.00, covering capacity classifications (SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC 2‑32 GB, SDXC 32 GB‑2 TB), voltage ranges (High‑Voltage 2.7‑3.6 V; UHS‑II VDD1 2.7‑3.6 V, VDD2 1.70‑1.95 V), and bus speed modes: Default Speed (≤25 MHz, ≤12.5 MB/s), High Speed (≤50 MHz, ≤25 MB/s); UHS‑I modes SDR12/25/50/104 and DDR50 (up to 104 MB/s at 1.8 V signaling); UHS‑II modes UHS156 (1.56 Gbps) and UHS624 (6.24 Gbps), supporting Full‑Duplex and Half‑Duplex configurations.  

The specification includes error‑correction, write‑protection (mechanical switch, internal permanent/temporary), password protection (CMD42 LOCK_UNLOCK), and content protection complying with SDMI. Card form‑factors are Standard (24 mm × 32 mm × 2.1/1.4 mm), miniSD, and microSD. Registers (CID, RCA, CSD, OCR, SSR, etc.) store identification, addressing, and operational data.  

Two operation modes are defined: Card Identification Mode (reset, voltage validation, RCA assignment via CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3) and Data Transfer Mode (single/multiple block read/write, busy signaling on DAT0, CRC protection). Commands are broadcast or addressed; command tokens are 48 bits with 7‑bit CRC, responses 48 or 136 bits. Data blocks are transferred with start/stop bits and 16‑bit CRC; bus width defaults to 1‑bit and can be switched to 4‑bit via ACMD6.  

UHS‑I initialization requires host to set S18R in ACMD41, card responds S18A, and CMD11 performs voltage switching to 1.8 V; sampling tuning uses CMD19. UHS‑II cards support both legacy SD and UHS‑II interfaces; initialization proceeds through PHY, Device, Enumeration, Configuration, and SD‑TRAN phases, with optional FD156, HD312, FD312, FD624 modes.  

Speed classes (0, 2, 4, 6, 10) indicate minimum performance; Application Performance Class defines random IOPS and sustained sequential write minimums. Optional features include Cache, Self‑Maintenance, Command Queue (CQ) with sequential or voluntary modes, Discard (CMD38 00000001h), Full‑User‑Area Logical Erase (FULE, CMD38 00000002h), and Card Ownership Protection (COP) with PWD and optional FEP registers controlling lock/unlock and force‑erase operations.  

Write protection methods comprise a mechanical switch, internal card‑controlled protection, and password‑based locking via CMD42. All communication is host‑controlled; the host may poll status with CMD13, abort transfers with CMD12, and select/deselect cards with CMD7. The specification also defines the Mc‑EX Interface as an extension for Mobile Commerce commands over the SD bus.
