The Post Office revenue has grown and exceeds expenditures. General Lafayette visited and was warmly received; a provision for him is recommended. The President expressed support for Greek independence and noted the success of the new South American republics.

The Supreme Court’s duties are burdensome; reorganization is needed to free judges from circuit duties. A military post at the mouth of the Columbia River is recommended to protect commerce and tribes on the Pacific coast. Improvements to Washington city, including a canal from the Tiber to the Eastern Branch, are suggested; public lots could fund them.

The President concluded by urging continued vigilance, preservation of the Union’s blessings, and harmonious cooperation between state and national governments.

Mali’s gold exports are declining as its major legacy mines approach the end of production. The world‑class Sadiola mine, a joint venture of IAMGOLD (41 %), AngloGold Ashanti (41 %) and the Government of Mali (18 %), requires a $380 million investment to process its hard‑rock (sulphide) reserves of 3.4 million ounces and extend operations for another ten years. Negotiations to secure this investment appear stalled within the government, jeopardising the project ahead of the 2017 Invest in Mali Forum in Bamako.  

Sadiola, located in the Kayes region near the Senegal border, was built for soft‑rock ore but the oxide material is now depleted. The mine’s production has fallen from about 600,000 oz in 2000 to under 200,000 oz today. Its surrounding infrastructure includes a water pipeline from the Senegal River and diesel‑generated power; expansion plans aim to connect the site to the national grid, benefiting nearby villages.

Other key mines are also winding down: Morila is set to close in 2019 and Yatela has already ceased operation. Mali’s total gold exports fell from 70 t (2015) to 67 t (2016), while industrial output is projected to drop to 45 t in 2017. Gold accounts for roughly 25‑30 % of government revenue.  

The Sadiola expansion would protect about 1,000 current jobs (93 % Malian) and create additional employment, which authorities view as important for security given high youth unemployment ahead of the 2018 elections. IAMGOLD’s CEO has stated the company remains committed to Mali and West Africa.

RTX IO, integrated with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, provides GPU‑based lossless decompression that moves data from NVMe SSDs directly to the GPU, reducing CPU work by up to 20× and delivering up to 100× higher I/O throughput. This improves game frame rates, enables near‑instantaneous loading, reduces pop‑in and stutter, and streams high‑quality textures while lossless compression reduces download and install sizes, and opens the door to a new era of large, incredibly detailed open world games. RTX IO also benefits artists and designers working with large CAD or scientific datasets and enables high‑resolution, high‑frame‑rate VR for collaborative product design. Fast storage is critical for moving mesh and texture data to the GPU for rendering jobs.

The GA10x Ampere architecture powers GeForce RTX 30‑series and data‑center GPUs. It adds second‑generation RT Cores that double ray‑triangle intersection performance and support ray‑traced motion blur, third‑generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity that double effective throughput, and up to 2× FP32, 2× ray‑tracing, and 5× AI training performance versus Turing. GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps per pin and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth. PCIe Gen4 doubles bandwidth compared with Turing, and 48 GB of GPU memory scales to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink.

GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 die with 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs and 10 496 CUDA cores, outperforming the previous‑generation TITAN RTX. GeForce RTX 3070 uses the GA104 die and delivers more performance than the RTX 2080 Ti while using GDDR6.

Display capabilities include 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, and HDMI 2.1 with the same resolutions; HDCP 2.3 is supported. The fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder accelerates MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, with GA10x being the first GPU to offer AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 with minimal CPU usage. The seventh‑generation NVENC encoder can encode 4K H.264 or 8K HEVC with quality comparable to x264 Medium while offloading the CPU.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x, is billed as the world’s most powerful data‑center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2× FP32, 2× ray‑tracing, and 5× AI throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB memory, vGPU virtualization, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX platform. The RTX A6000, also GA102‑based, provides 10 752 CUDA cores, 84 second‑generation RT cores, 336 third‑generation Tensor cores, 48 GB GDDR6, and supports large datasets with NVLink to 96 GB; it includes hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and shows performance gains in SPECviewperf, Blender, V‑Ray, Redshift, HPC and deep‑learning benchmarks versus the RTX 6000.

Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects memory transmission errors and retries them, letting users push overclocking until performance plateaus, indicating the memory limit.

Disclosed are systems and methods for providing ground support to vertical‑takeoff aerial vehicles. A ground station comprises a protective casing, an extendable landing pad, a charging mechanism and an elevator mechanism. The landing pad can switch between a closed configuration, where it is stored inside the protective casing, and an open configuration, where it expands beyond the casing to provide a platform large enough for the vehicle to land. The station may also include a centering mechanism that guides a landed vehicle onto the base platform and a wind‑breaker to reduce cross‑winds.  

Charging is performed by a power supply that maintains a potential difference between conducting terminals embedded in the base platform and/or the casing, allowing conductive coupling with corresponding terminals on the aerial vehicle. Power sources can be solar panels, wind turbines, fuel cells, electrochemical cells, piezoelectric units, or mains connection; photovoltaic panels may be integrated into the top‑closing of the casing.  

The protective casing is preferably made from material transparent to satellite navigation signals and may include a bottom panel, side panels, and a top‑closing with outwardly folding flaps. Side extensions and bridging lobes expand from the base platform when opened and fold back into the casing when closed.  

Homing aids such as visual patterns of contrasting dark and light areas, infrared, RF, LED, audio, or ultrasonic beacons help the vehicle locate the landing pad from high and low altitude. The ground station can be networked with a control server and other stations to coordinate multiple aerial vehicles.  

Extension modules (e.g., weather station, communication, sensor, radar, night‑vision, transportation wheels, battery packs) can be mechanically and electronically coupled to increase functionality. Methods are disclosed for deploying stations over a required range, raising the platform, extending the pad, landing and centering the vehicle, retracting the assembly, and charging the vehicle.

The study focuses on laboratory near-infrared (NIR) spectral measurements and modeling of water ice, epsomite (MgSO₄·7H₂O), and halite (NaCl) at cryogenic temperatures to support compositional analysis of Europa’s surface ahead of NASA’s Europa Clipper and ESA’s JUICE missions. Europa’s surface is predominantly water ice, with hydrated materials that may reflect the composition of its subsurface ocean, relevant to habitability. The research addresses how grain size and mixing impact spectral signatures, using the Cryogenic Reflectance Observations using Nitrogen-purged Optical Spectroscopy (CRONOS) facility to measure pure materials and 50%/50% volume mixtures across four grain size bins (<63 μm, 63–250 μm, 250–500 μm, >500 μm). Samples were prepared as discrete grains to avoid ambiguity in hydration states, ground under liquid nitrogen, and measured at temperatures typically between 100–120 K. Hapke radiative transfer theory was applied to generate linear and intimate mixture models for comparison with laboratory spectra, employing optical constants for crystalline water ice at 120 K and epsomite at 120 K; halite optical constants were not available. The results indicate that water ice spectra are generally well-reproduced by both linear and intimate mixture models, though some inconsistencies remain in continua or absorption features. Smaller grain sizes of water ice exert stronger influence on spectral features than larger grains, and mixtures of epsomite or halite with water ice are dominated by water ice signatures. Halite’s sole notable feature is a 1.95 μm adsorbed water band, and its mixtures with water ice are nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice. For epsomite, significant discrepancies between laboratory and modeled spectra suggest potential errors in published cryogenic optical constants, possibly mislabeled as ambient data. The study emphasizes the need for quantitative spectral mixture analysis using optical constants to accurately determine material abundances and grain sizes, cautioning that observational bias toward smaller grains may exist. It concludes that both linear and intimate unmixing should be applied to assess abundance uncertainties, and future work will involve deriving corrected epsomite optical constants.

The Sri Lankan rupee declined for a third consecutive session, ending at 158.60/75 per dollar. Dealers attributed the weakness to importer dollar demand exceeding remittance inflows and state banks refraining from dollar sales. Emerging market currencies face pressure from rising Fed rates, the US-China trade war, and higher oil prices. The rupee reached a record low of 160.17 on June 20 and has fallen 3.4% year-to-date. Moody's warned that a strong dollar increases credit risk for Sri Lanka and other emerging markets. Foreign investor outflows from government securities totaled 3.5 billion rupees in the week ended June 27, with annual outflows reaching 29 billion rupees. Sri Lanka received $584 million from a Chinese port operator last month as part of a Hambantota port deal.

An Uzbek-born U.S. citizen, Zokir Aliyev, 46, was convicted by an Uzbek court for publicly calling for the government's overthrow and participating in an extremist group. He was fined $67 for offences dating back nearly 20 years. Aliyev was detained in June, freed after six days, and denied involvement with the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, saying he only attended opposition meetings in Turkey in the 1990s. Uzbekistan's state security service said he had been wanted since 2005 over suspected IMU affiliation and suspected training in Afghanistan. His Facebook page indicates he lived in Virginia and studied at the University of Nevada. The U.S. embassy declined comment.

President’s message to the Senate responds to a resolution about an alleged forcible resistance to federal law in Boston. A deputy marshal, Patrick Riley, filed an affidavit describing the incident, but official confirmation is lacking and some implicated parties deny key facts. The President characterizes the event as an unexpected, high‑handed violation of law, noting that Boston’s general sentiment condemns it and that many citizens would have acted to prevent it had warning been given.

The message reviews federal statutes governing detention of federal prisoners. Congress resolutions of 1789, 1791, and 1821 require state jails to house federal prisoners at 50 cents per month per prisoner and authorize the marshal to hire temporary facilities when a state withdraws jail access. Massachusetts law of March 24 1843 repealed those arrangements, prohibiting state judges, justices, sheriffs, and other officers from exercising powers under the federal fugitive‑slave act and from allowing state jails to be used for fugitive‑slave detentions. The President argues that these state provisions, though creating obstacles, cannot relieve Congress of its constitutional duty to return escaped laborers.

The President reports that the marshal was reminded of his authority to obtain a temporary jail but has not confirmed compliance; instructions will be issued to secure such a place if needed. Enclosures include a proclamation of April 18 and communications from the War, Navy, and State Departments.

Turning to enforcement power, the message notes that the Constitution places the Army and Navy under presidential control and requires congressional authorization to call the militia. Existing statutes (1795, 1807) allow use of military force but mandate a proclamation against insurgents, which could alert targets and hinder arrests. The President suggests amending the 1795 act to permit militia use without a prior proclamation and to place militia under civil officers, and recommends clarifying the 1807 act regarding army and navy employment. The message also affirms that all citizens may be summoned as the posse comitatus and that the marshal may not summon organized militia without its officers’ consent.

A second proclamation dated April 25 1851 warns that any person joining a planned invasion of Cuba will be prosecuted under U.S. law and will forfeit government protection.

The President concludes by assuring that he will enforce the laws fully and believes the majority of Americans support the Constitution and lawful government.

NVDA options trading enables investors to leverage positions and potentially generate high returns from relatively small capital while capping losses at the option premium. The price of an option depends on the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividend payments; the Black‑Scholes model is commonly used for pricing. Popular strategies include buying calls or puts, writing calls or puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars, each with a distinct risk‑reward profile. Risk factors include adverse stock movement, time decay, volatility changes, and liquidity constraints. Dividends generally cause call prices to fall and put prices to rise. Margin requirements are lower for buying than for writing options, and NVDA options tend to be liquid due to active participation of buyers and sellers. Effective analysis combines quantitative (e.g., pricing models) and qualitative factors, and hedging can be achieved with protective puts. Proper risk‑management techniques—diversification, position sizing, stop‑loss and protective‑put orders—are essential. Market volatility drives option price changes, and tax treatment follows capital‑gains rules. Successful trading requires a solid understanding of option theory and practical experience.

The 2018‑19 Union Budget contains no dedicated women‑specific allocation, unlike the 2017‑18 and 2016‑17 budgets, and economists note that the Budget treats women mainly through existing social roles rather than structural change. The National Health Protection Scheme, a renamed version of RSBY, promises ₹5 lakh health cover for about 50 crore people in 10 crore families. While some economists call this a breakthrough for poor women’s access to private hospitals, others warn that the scheme resembles RSBY, which failed to cut out‑of‑pocket costs, and point out that overall health spending rose only 2.7 % and now represents 2.1 % of the budget, below the National Health Policy target of 2.5 % of GDP. Funding for the National Health Mission and Integrated Child Development Services fell. The Budget allocates ₹3,794 crore for credit, capital and interest subsidies to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which employ many self‑employed women and self‑help groups. Sanitation investments under Swachh Bharat are credited with improving women’s health, but the maternity entitlement budget was cut from the required ₹8,000 crore to ₹2,400 crore. The Ujjwala scheme, providing free LPG connections, is expanded to 8 crore families despite evidence that many recipients cannot afford refills. Overall, the Budget is described as a continuation of previous patterns, offering limited new pathways for women’s economic participation.

The speaker has been in Quebec for about seven months, feels at home and expects family at the game. He credits hard work, preparation and toughness in key moments for success, noting that effort creates luck. The team values home performance, must match the opponent’s intensity, and plans to focus one game and shift at a time. He says the team is comfortable on the road as well as at home, has size and speed, and will try to impose its style. The atmosphere is expected to be intense, with the first ten minutes crucial, and they aim to quiet the crowd and play their game.

USB‑C and USB‑A are physical connector shapes; USB‑C, introduced in 2014, is smaller, reversible and can deliver more power than USB‑A. All USB devices follow a versioned specification that defines data‑transfer speed and power capability; the whole connection runs at the slowest component’s speed. The current specification is USB4 (2022), offering up to 40 Gb/s and later USB4 Version 2 up to 120 Gb/s, but adoption is limited. USB‑3.x naming is inconsistent; speeds are best identified by their numeric rating (e.g., 5 Gb/s, 10 Gb/s, 20 Gb/s). USB‑2.0 maxes out at 480 Mb/s.  

Power Delivery (USB‑PD) enables charging up to 240 W with USB‑PD 3.1, supporting pass‑through charging on hubs and docks. DisplayPort Alternate Mode (DP Alt Mode) lets a USB‑C cable carry audio and video; the capability depends on the DisplayPort generation (DP 1.4 for USB 3.2, DP 2.0 for USB4). USB4 makes DP Alt Mode mandatory, enabling higher resolutions and refresh rates.  

Thunderbolt, an Intel‑Apple standard using the USB‑C connector, has stricter certification. Thunderbolt 4, built on USB4, reaches 40 Gb/s, 100 W and DP 2.0; it guarantees at least two 4K 60 Hz displays and up to 2 m cable length. Thunderbolt 5 (2025) raises bidirectional bandwidth to 80 Gb/s (up to 120 Gb/s with Bandwidth Boost), can drive three 4K 144 Hz displays or two 8K 60 Hz screens, and raises power delivery to 240 W. Thunderbolt ports work with ordinary USB‑C devices but default to the slower link.  

To achieve rated speeds, use the cable that shipped with the device, check the manufacturer’s listed speed or version, and prefer cables that state the maximum data‑rate rather than a generic USB version.

Lincoln argues the government cannot endure half slave and half free, contends the Nebraska doctrine and Dred Scott decision work together to extend slavery, outlines three key points of the Dred Scott decision regarding negro citizenship and territorial slavery, criticizes Senator Douglas's "care not" policy on slavery, and asserts the anti-slavery cause must be conducted by its own supporters.

United States v. Adams: The Tenth Circuit affirmed Henry J. Adams III's 140-month sentence for armed bank robbery. Adams argued he was entitled to a minor-participant reduction as a lookout and that the above-guidelines sentence was an abuse of discretion. The court held Adams was not entitled to a reduction because he helped plan the robbery, knew its purpose, and expected compensation, making him equally culpable. The sentence was characterized as an upward variance based on Adams's extensive criminal history, and the court found it substantively reasonable under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) factors.

Chelsea and Real Madrid are vying with Tottenham for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, 21, valued at £40m. Tottenham offered £28m; Chelsea and Real are preparing higher counter‑bids. Sanchez wants to leave for the Premier and Champions Leagues. Ajax are trying to retain him but face a losing battle.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing scheme designed for fast quarterback decision-making, featuring 5 eligible receivers where the tight end is the primary target with route flexibility. The concept works effectively against man coverage, Cover 3, and Cover 4 by having QBs read the flat defender post-snap. It struggles against Cover 2 due to cornerback undercutting potential. The offense includes specific routes for each position: tight ends run vertical sticks, backs run arrow routes at 3 yards, slot receivers stretch horizontally, X receivers run 3-step slants, and Z receivers run go routes. The concept has variations including 2x2 condensed formations and Trips Flex Sticko with double moves to counter defensive adjustments.

The President outlines four major domestic goals: a stronger economy, higher‑quality affordable health care, energy independence, and expanded compassion programs. To boost the economy he proposes making the 2004 and 2006 tax reductions permanent, eliminating the marriage penalty, raising the child credit, and ending double taxation of dividends; 92 million taxpayers would keep an average of $1,100 more this year, and a four‑person family earning $40,000 would see federal income tax fall from $1,178 to $45. He asks Congress to limit discretionary spending growth to 4 percent and to prioritize essential programs.

For health care he pledges $400 billion over the next decade to strengthen Medicare, give seniors a prescription‑drug option, and pass medical‑liability reform. On energy he requests $1.2 billion for hydrogen‑powered‑car research, supports the Clear Skies Act (a 70‑percent cut in power‑plant air pollution) and the Healthy Forests Initiative, and promotes clean technology and conservation.

He calls for a Faith‑Based Initiative and a Citizen Service Act, a $450 million mentor program for disadvantaged junior‑high students and children of prisoners, and a $600 million effort to provide drug‑treatment for an additional 300,000 Americans over three years. He also asks Congress to protect infants at birth, ban partial‑birth abortion, and prohibit human cloning.

On foreign policy the speech highlights the war on terror: key Al‑Qaeda members have been arrested or neutralized, cells disrupted in many countries, and new security measures include thousands of federal screeners at airports, smallpox inoculations for troops, and a missile‑defense system. The President says the United States is working with allies to prevent rogue regimes from obtaining nuclear, chemical, or biological weapons, citing concerns about Iran, North Korea, and Iraq.

Regarding Iraq, the address details 12 years of non‑compliance, unaccounted biological agents, chemical weapons and munitions, uranium procurement attempts, and evidence that Iraq is hiding material from inspectors and intimidating scientists. He announces a United Nations Security Council session on February 5 to consider Iraq’s defiance and warns that the United States will lead a coalition to disarm Iraq if it does not fully comply. He tells U.S. service members that critical hours may lie ahead, affirms the nation’s resolve to fight if forced, and promises humanitarian aid to the Iraqi people.

The President concludes by reaffirming confidence in American strength, the universal right to freedom, and reliance on God’s guidance.

Walgreens fell 5.8%, Rite Aid and CVS Health fell 4.9% after reports Amazon is exploring drug sales; Amazon is talking with pharmacy benefit managers, hiring talent, and an analyst predicts entry within two years; Amazon declined comment.

The study analyzed the value load of words in 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grade Turkish textbooks from the Ministry of National Education. A database of 3,637 unique words was created. Field experts classified the words as positive (172, 4.72 %), negative (159, 4.37 %), or neutral (3,306, 91.43 %). No clear relationship was found between grade level and the distribution of value loads. The study suggests using a corpus‑based method when preparing textbooks to support values education and recommends further digitisation of textbooks for future research.

MIT OpenCourseWare lecture covering the connection between graph theory and additive combinatorics, starting with Schur's theorem derived from Fermat's Last Theorem attempts and its equivalence to a finitary coloring problem, then proving Schur's theorem via Ramsey's theorem for monochromatic triangles using a graph-theoretic approach; the lecture then outlines the historical development of additive combinatorics, including Van der Waerden's theorem on arithmetic progressions (APs), the Erdos–Turan conjecture on positive density implying long APs, Roth's theorem for 3-term APs using Fourier analysis and graph theory, Szemeredi's theorem proving the conjecture, and generalizations via ergodic theory, higher order Fourier analysis, hypergraph regularity, and the polymath project; further topics include multi-dimensional extensions, polynomial patterns, the Green–Tao theorem on primes containing arbitrarily long APs, and connections to extremal graph theory including the question of maximum edges in graphs where every edge lies in exactly one triangle; the lecture includes administrative details and mentions upcoming course content on extremal graph theory and bounds for Roth's theorem.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email last week while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives posted old blog posts from his private “Hosts of Error” blog calling President Donald Trump “mentally unfit” and an “institutional terrorist.” The posts were written while he was an associate at Kobre & Kim; he joined the U.S. attorney’s office in September 2020. Rosenzweig’s dismissal follows the firing of dozens of federal prosecutors deemed at odds with the president. The Justice Department also removed three other Southern District prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith, recently condemning dismissals of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law.

Weekly trading focuses on weekly price action, allowing position, swing, or broader market analysis, trades less frequently than daily charts, and may deliver larger gains. Most weekly traders are long‑term position traders, and range trading is the most common strategy—identify a range, mark support and resistance, and enter on price‑action patterns or indicator signals. Trend‑following on the weekly chart is possible but can require holding positions for years. Weekly bar highs and lows act as key support/resistance on lower timeframes (e.g., H4), enabling breakout or reversal swing trades. Multi‑timeframe analysis (weekly with H4 or daily) is common, and backtesting determines which timeframe works best for a given strategy. Weekly charts suit position trading; daily charts suit day trading; swing traders are not subject to the $25,000 day‑trading margin rule. An example backtested sector‑rotation strategy on weekly ETFs generated 728 trades, 0.4% average gain, 15.1% annual return, 43% max drawdown; a monthly version returned 12.1% annually. The weekly chart helps identify long‑term trends, ranges, and key levels, while the choice between weekly and daily charts depends on the trader’s style and strategy.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment to AMCO Insurance Company. The court found no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO breached the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, because its investigation was reasonable, it relied on expert opinions, and there was no evidence of bad faith. Consequently, the court also upheld summary judgment on Morello’s claims for intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations, all premised on the same grounds. The appellate court further held that Morello’s evidence of AMCO’s mediation communications was inadmissible for the bad faith claim. The district court’s denial of Morello’s motion for reconsideration was not an abuse of discretion. The decision was affirmed.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10‑Q for the first quarter of fiscal year 2022 ended May 2 2021. Revenue was $5.66 billion, up 84% year‑over‑year; gross profit $3.63 billion (64.1% gross margin). Operating income was $1.96 billion and net income $1.91 billion, resulting in diluted earnings per share of $3.03. The company generated $1.87 billion in operating cash flow and held $12.67 billion in cash and marketable securities. By segment, Graphics revenue was $3.45 billion (operating income $1.79 billion) and Compute & Networking revenue was $2.21 billion (operating income $0.86 billion). Revenue by platform was led by Gaming ($2.76 billion), Data Center ($2.05 billion), Professional Visualization ($0.37 billion), Automotive ($0.15 billion) and OEM & Other ($0.33 billion). Geographically, Taiwan accounted for $1.78 billion, China (including Hong Kong) $1.39 billion, and the United States $0.77 billion. The company completed the acquisition of Mellanox Technologies Ltd. in April 2020 for $7.13 billion and continues to await regulatory approval for the pending acquisition of Arm Limited, a transaction valued at $40 billion (signing consideration $2 billion paid; $10 billion cash and 44.3 million shares to be paid at closing; potential earn‑out up to $5 billion). The Arm closing is expected in the first quarter of calendar year 2022. A four‑for‑one stock split was declared, subject to shareholder approval of an increase in authorized shares, with distribution planned for July 19 2021. The board also authorized a cash dividend of $0.16 per share, with $99 million paid in the quarter. The company had $7.24 billion remaining under its share‑repurchase program. On legal matters, a securities class action alleging false statements about channel inventory and crypto‑mining impact was dismissed; plaintiffs have appealed. Derivative suits remain stayed pending the appeal. NVIDIA noted it expects to remain supply‑constrained in gaming through the second half of the fiscal year.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes up to 128 page‑migration entries, moving pages and updating IOMMU host PTEs. It works in SNP‑enabled and non‑SNP systems; in SNP only Hypervisor‑owned pages may be moved and memory may be unencrypted or hypervisor‑encrypted. The command can migrate DMA‑active pages; for non‑SNP ATS devices, hPTE.PMS must be set and ATS invalidations issued before the call. CPU access must be prevented (pages made non‑present, TLB shootdown) and software updates page‑table addresses after migration. 2 MB pages must be split into 4 KB pages. Firmware validates addresses, marks hPTE, issues IOMMU and CPU TLB invalidations, copies page, updates hPTE, releases exclusive RMP access, clears migration flag.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves SNP‑guest pages, requiring contiguous 4 KB pages for 2 MB entries and prohibiting DMA during migration. Source must be Guest‑Valid/Invalid, destination Pre‑Migration; after migration destination takes source state and source returns to Pre‑Migration. Firmware checks RMP_ENFORCE, validates states, obtains exclusive RMP access, verifies size, issues CPU TLB invalidate, copies data, updates source/destination RMPs.

A terminating command can signal end of migration sequence. Command format errors reject; entry errors may cause partial success; ring‑buffer errors reported in PM_STATUS; hardware errors reported via status codes and MCA. If a batch of up to 128 pages times out, an MCA is logged, correction attempted, VMs may be terminated. Unrecoverable errors can render pages unusable, possibly leading to eventual system failure after a save‑state attempt.

The GST regime requires e‑way bills for consignments over Rs 50,000. The GST Council exempted 153 items—including live animals, produce, milk, honey, cereals, gas, kerosene, postal baggage, currency and jewellery. Bills optional below Rs 50,000 and will start after NIC software ready (likely Oct). E‑way bills must list goods, mode, origin, destination, supplier, recipient and transporter; no conveyance details needed for intra‑state trips under 10 km. The system helps tax officials track inter‑state movement after border checkposts were removed.

School systems across the United States are outfitting traditional yellow school buses with live‑camera feeds, GPS tracking, turn‑by‑turn navigation and real‑time student manifests. Drivers receive tablet‑based route guidance and can monitor their own children’s rides, while parents get rideshare‑style apps that show exact pickup times, bus location and photos of students boarding or leaving. Districts such as Kansas City Public Schools have signed multi‑year, multimillion‑dollar contracts with vendors like Zum and Transportant, paying about $3,600 per bus upfront plus annual subscription fees that can exceed $90,000 per district. The technology is credited with improving safety, driver recruitment and route efficiency, and can alert dispatchers to incidents within minutes, allowing school staff to contact parents quickly. However, privacy advocates warn that the growing volume of GPS locations, video footage and student data raises security and data‑retention concerns; many districts say they store footage separately from other student records and delete it on a set schedule. The market for bus‑tech services is expanding, with companies offering all‑inclusive suites that include on‑board Wi‑Fi, camera systems and parent‑tracking apps for a per‑bus subscription of roughly $69 per year.

Infiniti’s Q Inspiration concept, unveiled early this year, will lead an electrified platform launching up to five models in five years, built in China. It features clear, concise lines, a sculpted four‑door coupe, and signals a shift to compact, less intrusive powertrains, heralding a new era.

SOS Player Fundamentals outlines a man‑to‑man pressure defense system using three on‑ball actions – SET, ON, and SMOTHER – and three off‑ball actions – SNUGGLE, OFF, and STRIKE. SET forces the ballhandler to dribble by assuming a low, bent‑knee stance, wide feet, one hand tracing the ball and the other cutting passing lanes. ON drives the dribbler toward a sideline or baseline checkpoint with a backward slide, maintaining an arm’s distance and using quick mini‑slides; if beaten, the defender sprints and recovers. SMOTHER crowds the ballhandler when the dribble is picked up, extending both arms and moving them laterally to disrupt shooting or passing. Off‑ball SNUGGLE denies a pass one pass away with a low stance, extended arm and short slides. OFF slides away from the opponent to block cuts and then resumes a Snuggle stance to stop the return pass. STRIKE positions the weakside defender halfway between opponent and passer, pointing to both ball and opponent, and provides help responsibilities such as denying the three‑second area, taking charges, blocking lay‑ins, and rebounding. A closeout from Strike transitions back to Set. The system stresses coach attitude, enthusiastic drills, positive feedback, and pride in limiting opponents’ scoring.

Fiat Chrysler (FCA) recently rejected an acquisition offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker, citing insufficient financial terms. The rejection follows years of FCA pursuing mergers with General Motors and Volkswagen, with CEO Sergio Marchionne previously expressing a preference to be the acquirer rather than the target. Marchionne has stated he does not view Asia as a viable partner and suggested China may eventually acquire FCA. Chinese automakers are attracted to FCA under the government‑driven China Outbound policy, which encourages purchases of foreign assets, and because FCA offers a well‑known U.S. distribution network, a broad product line and a plan to erase debt by 2019. Chinese manufacturers have also been working to improve vehicle quality and enter the U.S. market.

Xiaomi is preparing for a major launch event in 2018 with the Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. The company has confirmed it will not launch the Mi A2 in India, stating there is no such phone but more Android One devices are planned. The Mi A1 launched in India last year as the first stock Android Xiaomi phone. Xiaomi is also preparing to launch the Redmi S2/Y2 in India as its most affordable dual camera smartphone, competing against Realme 1, Honor 7A, and Honor 7C.

In GIVENS v. MISSOURI‑KANSAS‑TEXAS R. CO. OF TEXAS the Fifth Circuit reversed the district‑court judgment for the railroad. A passenger train broke down in zero weather because a driving‑wheel tire came off, and the brakeman‑plaintiff, ordered to flag the rear, suffered severe frost‑bite to his feet. The jury found $12,000 in damages and that the engine breakdown was a proximate cause of his injuries, but the trial court entered judgment for the defendant. On appeal the court held that the locomotive’s breakdown while in service established a violation of the Federal Boiler Inspection Act as a matter of law, that the plaintiff’s injuries were compensable under that Act, and that the trial court erred in not entering judgment for the plaintiff. The case was reversed with instructions to enter judgment for $12,000.

North American markets closed sharply lower on Friday, with the Dow falling 666 points (2.5%) and the S&P 500 losing 2.1%, the worst weekly decline since early 2016. The Nasdaq dropped 2%. Losses followed stronger‑than‑expected January wage growth, raising inflation and rate‑hike expectations, and a rise in Treasury yields to multi‑year highs. Weak earnings from Exxon, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple (iPhone sales below forecasts) added pressure. The Canadian dollar fell, and the S&P/TSX lost 255 points (1.6%) as oil, gold and marijuana stocks declined.

This study analyzes 3,395 course syllabi from India's top 100 engineering institutions to examine AI ethics integration in computing education. Only 75 courses (2.21%) included substantive AI ethics content, typically covered superficially—60% through a single session and 7% as dedicated courses. Topics included privacy and data governance (42%), accountability and policies (32%), ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%), human-AI interaction (24%), algorithmic bias and fairness (18%), AI safety (16%), generative AI concerns (11%), and social impact (8%). Most courses lacked dedicated ethics resources and clear assessment methods. Researchers conclude AI ethics remains marginally and inconsistently addressed in Indian computing curricula, necessitating coordinated efforts to embed it as a core educational component.

In southern Zambia, the sugar industry in Mazabuka attracted a mobile workforce that fueled a sex trade, helping spread HIV and contributing to the African “AIDS belt”. At the 2003 peak Zambia recorded about 70,000 AIDS deaths per year; hospitals and mortuaries were overwhelmed and a nearby graveyard filled with graves of adults and children. A military‑style prevention campaign by the NGO DAPP conducts door‑to‑door testing, supplies mobile kits, distributes condoms to truckers, involves former sex workers and chiefs, and has reached over 1.5 million of the country’s 16.5 million people. UN data show new infections have fallen 27 % since 2010 and AIDS deaths 11 %. District Commissioner Protacia Mulenga, who lost two brothers to AIDS, praised the effort’s reach.

FBI arrested 23‑year‑old Jerry Drake Varnell, Oklahoma, for attempting to detonate an explosives‑laden van outside Oklahoma bank; he is charged with attempting to destroy a building and scheduled to appear Monday.

Heart attacks and strokes have fallen by about 30% in the UK over two decades, yet they remain a major health risk. Effective cholesterol‑lowering and blood‑pressure medicines, especially statins, have contributed to this decline. Research shows that many reported statin side‑effects are linked to the nocebo effect, and blinded trials found equal side‑effect rates when participants did not know which pill they were taking. New injectable lipid‑lowering drugs (evolocumab, alirocumab, inclisiran) that target a protein associated with high LDL can cut LDL by roughly 50% with a six‑monthly dose and are reserved for very high‑risk patients. Lifestyle measures further lower risk: maintaining a healthy weight, quitting smoking (with free NHS support), regular aerobic plus resistance exercise (about 30 minutes most days), consuming oily fish and plant sources of omega‑3, and eating soluble fibre from oats, barley, legumes, fruit, nuts and seeds. Cooking from scratch reduces hidden sugar and salt; using potassium‑based salt substitutes could cut early deaths by 12% and heart‑attack/stroke risk by 13%. Plant sterols in fortified foods and soya products also help reduce cholesterol absorption. The article notes the TLC (Therapeutic Lifestyle Changes) diet as a structured plan for lowering cholesterol, is peer‑reviewed, mentions Dr Sarah Jarvis as a LoSalt medical advisor, and clarifies that community views are not medical advice.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoffs of nearly all remaining Voice of America employees, reinstating over 500 journalists and staff. Judge Royce C. Lamberth found the administration violated his April order requiring continued broadcasting. The judge warned Kari Lake and other officials they risked contempt charges for failing to maintain VOA's global news operations. The agency, which provides independent reporting to countries like China, Russia and Iran, had reduced operations to approximately one hour of daily broadcasting from around-the-clock service after the closure order.

American football originated from rugby and soccer; Walter Camp, called the Father of American Football, codified its modern rules in the late 1870s, introducing the line of scrimmage, 11‑player teams, quarterback position, and scoring system. The sport’s name derives from its European ancestors, not from kicking the ball. American football is not an Olympic sport, but flag football may debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games; 96.5 % of NFL players are American, reflecting the sport’s deep roots in the United States. A team fields 11 players on the field (12 in the Canadian Football League). A professional or college game lasts 60 minutes, divided into four 15‑minute quarters; high school games are 48 minutes with 12‑minute quarters. The field measures 100 yards between the goal lines, plus 10‑yard end zones, and is 160 feet wide. Scoring: touchdown 6 points, extra point 1 point, two‑point conversion 2 points, field goal 3 points, safety 2 points. Key rules include offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer and illegal formation; each incurs yardage penalties. A catch requires control, two feet in bounds and a football move, with sideline and end‑zone exceptions. Turnovers consist of interceptions, fumbles and turnover on downs. The line of scrimmage separates the teams before the snap; the neutral zone is the space equal to the ball’s length, with only the center allowed inside it. Special teams cover kickoffs, punts, field goals, extra points and returns. A quarterback may call an audible to change the play after lining up. Each offense receives four downs to advance the ball ten yards; a first down resets the count. The red zone, between the goal line and the 20‑yard line, is a condensed area where scoring decisions are critical. Notable players cited include Tom Brady (greatest quarterback), Jerry Rice (greatest wide receiver), Jim Brown (greatest running back) and Lawrence Taylor (defensive MVP).

CBS’s drama “Doubt” premieres Wednesday, Feb. 15 at 10 p.m. ET/PT after “Code Black.” Katherine Heigl stars as Sadie Ellis, a defense attorney at a New York City firm handling the case of pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan, accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years ago, while romantically involved. Firm staff include Isaiah Roth (Elliot Gould), Albert Cobb (Dulé Hill) and transgender lawyer Laverne Cox, first transgender actor on broadcast TV. Each week brings new cases while the show reveals Sadie’s backstory, including mother’s imprisonment. Critics find the show competent but formulaic, with a likeable cast and dialogue shortcuts, and note it addresses issues.

Police seized a white Holden Commodore linked to Aaron Marks' murder on a Ballina footpath. Forensic officers are checking it for fingerprints, DNA and blood, seeking passengers; the driver is assisting. Chief Inspector Cameron Lindsay declined to comment on Marks’ statements and thanked the public.

Callum Knott, 21, admitted taking his aunt’s car without consent and driving without a licence or insurance. He was spotted by his aunt and abandoned car when battery died. He received 12‑month community order, 80 hours unpaid work, four‑month driving ban, and to pay £85 costs and £85 surcharge.

Cover 2 is a 5‑under, 2‑deep defense that stops quick passes by turning corners into flat defenders. Offenses attack it by high‑lowing the corners, using 3‑receiver formations to force linebackers to cover vertical routes, sending four vertical receivers to stress the two safeties, and exploiting the open middle with post/corner routes. Specific concepts include the smash combination, snag‑and‑go, fade‑out, QB draw with an RB pop pass, and jet‑sweep four‑verticals.

The East Demerara Football Association held its AGM; six of seven clubs attended; Alfred King was re‑elected president with executive including vice presidents, secretary, treasurer, assistant, and committee members.

Curaleaf Holdings rallied on renewed hopes for U.S. cannabis rescheduling, gaining after a Trump Truth Social post touting CBD’s benefits for seniors following a September slump; the company reported in‑line Q2 2025 earnings and announced an expansion into Turkey, while the analyst maintains a Hold rating citing sector uncertainty. The author discloses a long position in CURLF.

Tesla, Inc. reported second-quarter 2020 revenues of $6.0 billion, a decrease from $6.4 billion in Q2 2019, primarily due to lower automotive sales. The company returned to profitability with net income of $129 million, compared to a net loss of $389 million in the prior-year quarter. As of June 30, 2020, total assets were $38.1 billion, and cash and cash equivalents increased to $8.6 billion. The company temporarily suspended manufacturing operations at global facilities during the first half of 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic but resumed operations and increased output by the end of the second quarter.

Andrew Dawes, CEO of Intels Nigeria Ltd, says the company is partnering the Federal Government to boost port investment. Intels has invested billions of dollars in infrastructure under NPA concession agreements and refutes monopoly allegations, stating it pays higher fees than private jetties and invests heavily in oil and gas terminals, similar to container terminals. Challenges include historic low oil prices and a 70% drop in cargo volumes, but Intels continues long‑term investment. Phase 4B is the only facility ready to receive a full FPSO alongside, with 4 km of quay length built in partnership with the government. The Badagry deep‑seaport, being developed with APM Terminals, is planned as Africa’s largest port with the deepest draft. Intels, founded 30 years ago, provides an integrated “one‑stop‑shop” logistics package for the oil and gas industry.

The passage presents a methodology for studying a closed Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) interacting via asymmetric buyer–seller relationships. It argues that Markov random fields are unsuitable for modeling such systems due to their symmetry, proposing instead a neural network-inspired model using non-linear coupled differential equations. In this model, each company's "fitness" variable evolves based on decay, self-excitation, and mutual excitatory/inhibitory signals derived from product matching and quantified trust (using the Weber–Fechner law). The methodology includes creating a simulated DBE with 100 companies trading 20 products, using statistical data to match real-world properties. Experiments solve the resulting equations iteratively to observe system dynamics, including company survival rates and the emergence of monopolies. The authors conclude the simulated DBE enables quantitative study of real-world ecosystems where direct data is unavailable.

Background: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death; most cases are diagnosed at late stage, resulting in low 5‑year survival. Current low‑dose CT screening has low adherence (≈5.8 % overall, 22.3 % annually). A peripheral blood multi‑omics biomarker test may improve early detection.

Study design: MOSAIC was a case‑control study of 2,513 adults from 77 U.S. sites; 2,094 subjects were clinically eligible (816 lung‑cancer cases, 1,278 controls). Plasma samples were analyzed by deep untargeted proteomics (Proteograph assay), total RNA‑seq, untargeted metabolomics and four targeted immunoassays. Subjects were randomly split into a training set (1,225) and a held‑out validation set (398) while preserving site separation.

Results: The assays detected 113,671 peptides (≈8,385 protein groups), 219,729 mRNA transcripts, 71,756 introns and 1,801 metabolites. Univariate analysis identified thousands of differentially abundant analytes between cancer and control cohorts. A classifier built on clinical variables alone achieved an AUC of 0.78; a proteomics‑only classifier reached AUC 0.91. A multi‑omics classifier (proteins, transcripts, metabolites, immunoassays) achieved AUC 0.96 for all stages and 0.93 for stage I disease. In the validation set, using a decision threshold set to 87.5 % sensitivity on training data, overall sensitivity was 89 % (95 % CI 83‑93) and specificity 89 % (84‑93). Stage‑specific sensitivities were 80 % for stage I, 88 % for stage II and 99 % for stages III‑IV.

The classifier comprised 682 analyte features representing 149 distinct proteins, 346 distinct genes and 77 metabolic pathways; no single omics type dominated the top features. Over 60 % of these features showed a significant association with cancer stage.

Conclusion: A deep multi‑omics plasma classifier achieved high sensitivity and specificity for detecting lung cancer, including early‑stage disease, in a case‑control cohort. Prospective validation in the intended high‑risk screening population is required before clinical implementation.

The Camarilla pivot point, introduced in 1989 by bond trader Nick Scott, extends the classical floor‑trader pivot point and provides day traders with nine price levels—four support and four resistance. It helps identify key intraday price levels, entry and exit points, and suitable risk‑management settings. Trading approaches vary with market conditions and often consider the opening relative to yesterday’s close. Backtests of ordinary pivot points have not shown “super profits,” but the authors encourage traders to test their own ideas. Day traders use pivot points to define support, resistance, and potential changes in trend direction.

Long-standing criticisms of academic publishing—such as research fraud, paper mills, peer reviewer shortages, and high costs—are fueling the Trump administration’s attacks on scientific publishing. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya have proposed solutions like capping article processing charges and launching a government journal to address bias and access. However, experts are skeptical, warning that the administration’s actions are ideologically motivated and may worsen problems like pharmaceutical industry influence. They argue that meaningful reform requires changing academic incentive structures, which cannot be achieved by the NIH alone.

The coach praised three players for earning increased minutes in the playoffs, noting they play tough, unheralded roles and are being rewarded for their hard work. He described the difficulty of executing game‑plans under opposition pressure, emphasized the group’s consistent work ethic and commitment, and discussed in‑game adjustments, including the opponent’s line changes and his team’s counter‑moves, citing a decisive shot by Sammy Pahlsson. Security researchers at Lookout identified over a thousand Google Play apps infected with a new spyware family called SonicSpy. The malware can secretly record audio, capture photos, make calls, send texts, and exfiltrate call logs, contacts, and Wi‑Fi data. It can execute more than 73 remote commands via a command‑and‑control server. One example, the Soniac messaging app, disguises a customized version of Telegram, removes its icon to hide, connects to arshad93.ddns[.]net:2222, and installs a hidden Telegram APK. The associated account, iraqwebservice, previously uploaded two other SonicSpy samples. Enterprises are warned that such threats can cause regulatory violations and costly fines.

The Supreme Court on Friday cleared the way for the Trump administration to strip hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan nationals of their protected status under the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program. In a brief, unsigned order, the justices paused a ruling by a federal judge in San Francisco that barred the Secretary of Homeland Security from terminating the TPS designation for Venezuela. The court's three Democratic appointees indicated they would have denied the administration's request, with Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson writing a dissenting opinion. The TPS program allows the DHS secretary to designate a country's citizens as eligible to remain in the US and work when they cannot return due to natural disaster, armed conflict, or other extraordinary conditions. In February 2025, Secretary Kristi Noem terminated both the 2023 designation and the 2025 extension of the TPS for Venezuela. A federal challenge followed, and in March, U.S. District Judge Edward Chen temporarily prohibited Noem from ending the TPS designation and its extension. On September 5, Chen issued a final ruling that Noem had acted unlawfully. After the 9th Circuit declined to block Chen's ruling, the Supreme Court once again put Chen's ruling on hold, with the court explaining that although the posture of the case has changed, the parties' legal arguments and relative harms generally have not. Jackson argued that the court should step in only if the government can show a time-sensitive need, which it had not, and she concluded that the court had used its equitable power to allow the administration to disrupt as many lives as possible.

Manjot Kalra scored an unbeaten century in the 2018 ICC Under-19 World Cup final, helping India win its fourth U19 World Cup title. The 19-year-old Delhi player appeared nervous during a post-match interview with former cricketer Simon Doull. Kalra was picked by Delhi Daredevils in the IPL auction for his base price of Rs 20 lakh. Social media compared his batting to Yuvraj Singh, Sourav Ganguly, and Gautam Gambhir. Previous U19 World Cup century-makers, including Unmukt Chand, did not go on to play for India's senior team. Head coach Rahul Dravid said the win should be cherished as a memory but not define the players' careers.

The buyouts target employees 55 and older with at least 10 years at the company, offering severance packages. This is the insurer's first buyout offer since the late 1980s, prompted by soaring healthcare costs and steep losses, signaling financial struggles in the health insurance industry.

The disclosed embodiments describe a method and system for rendering computer generated graphics while detecting saccades. A processor renders a simulated scene, monitors the user's eye movement, and, upon detecting the onset of a saccade that causes saccadic masking, reduces the computing resources used for rendering frames for at least part of the saccade duration. The reduction can be achieved by skipping frames, repeating frames, decreasing detail or resolution, or adjusting the frame rate. Saved processing capacity may be reallocated to low‑frequency updates such as complex lighting calculations. Detection may employ optical sensors, EMG sensors, or other eye‑tracking technologies and may be based on an eye‑movement model that predicts saccade duration. Confidence in the detection can affect the amount of resource reduction, and calibration procedures can individualize the model for each user. The technique is applicable to head‑mounted displays, virtual‑reality and augmented‑reality devices, and can be combined with foveated rendering.

Share repurchases totaled $3.4 billion in the first half of fiscal 2018, leaving $33.4 billion of the $40 billion authorized program unused. Students at Max Hayes High School in Cleveland's Auto Collision Repair program spent 18 months refurbishing a police cruiser damaged during the 2016 Cavs championship celebrations. After the city planned to scrap the vehicle as a total loss, teacher Greg Boykin arranged for students to repair it. Companies donated materials, and the work saved the city approximately $10,000.
