UOB strategists expect GBP/USD to stay above 1.2900; momentum may lift it to 1.3040/45, with 1.3060 resistance. Support at 1.2975 and 1.2939; bearish phase from 1.3045 remains intact, but a break above 1.3060 would end it.

TradingView is a free technical analysis platform with charting, indicators, backtesting, portfolio tracking, news, and a community, available via web and mobile. To build an RSI‑based strategy, add the Relative Strength Index from the Indicators menu, setting its period and overbought/oversold levels. A simple strategy for the DOT market on a 5‑minute chart uses a 14‑period RSI with long entries when the RSI crosses above 35 (leaving oversold) and short entries when it crosses below 65 (leaving overbought). Positions are closed when the RSI crosses the mid‑level of 50. The strategy is coded in Pine Script using the ta.rsi function, strategy.entry and strategy.close commands, and IF statements to enforce the conditions. User inputs allow changing the period and thresholds without editing code. After compiling and adding to the chart, TradingView displays an equity curve, net profit, drawdown, and win rate. Free accounts are limited to the chart’s visible data; Pro or higher accounts enable a deep backtest using all available historical data (since 2019 for DOT) and provide performance metrics such as Sharpe Ratio and average risk‑reward, plus a trade list that can be exported as CSV (Pro only). The guide notes that RSI alone is inconsistent and benefits from additional indicators.

Nannette Perkins, 40, was arrested April 16, 2017 at her Taylorsville home after a tip linking her to the pajama‑wearing robber behind six Salt Lake bank robberies, five in two‑hour span; wearing pajamas, glasses and a blue bandanna, she remains in jail pending a court appearance.

The passage compares university life to a small town and states that student newsrooms serve as essential community news sources, warning that their removal creates news deserts. It cites former Rocky Mountain News editor John Temple, who said locals are deprived of the ability to make informed decisions, and notes that about six large corporations control most news outlets, limiting diversity and threatening an informed citizenry.

The passage describes a research‑and‑development study that aimed to identify the basic needs for achieving excellence in vocational education management in Thailand and to develop corresponding strategies for institutions under the Office of Vocational Education Commission (OVEC).  

Background — Rapid global change driven by Industry 4.0 and technology disruption (including AI) is reshaping jobs, skill requirements and national education systems. Thailand’s vocational education faces external pressures (globalization, scientific‑technological advances) and internal pressures (demographic, environmental, economic, social and political shifts). Labour demand in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) is high, especially in tourism/health‑tourism, modern automotive and agricultural‑biotechnology industries, with 24 596 workers needed in 2022 and projected to rise to 59 476 by 2027 (tourism) and 21 897 (automotive/biotech) rising to 47 732 by 2027.  

Research objective — To study current and desired conditions of vocational education management and to formulate strategies that enable OVEC institutions to reach excellence.  

Method — Phase 1 used document analysis and a validated questionnaire (content validity IOC 0.80–1.00; reliability α = 0.987/0.983) administered to a stratified random sample of 206 respondents from 424 OVEC institutions nationwide. Data were analysed with mean, standard deviation, modified Priority Needs Index (PNI​modified) and SWOT analysis, yielding six strategic priorities. Three exemplary institutions (Udonthani Vocational College, IRPC Technology College, Chachoengsao Technical College) were examined through structured interviews.  

Phase 2 drafted a strategic framework, which was evaluated by nine experts in focus‑group discussions; suitability and feasibility were assessed using mean and standard deviation.  

Results — Overall current conditions were high and desired conditions were the highest, with an overall PNI​modified = 0.179. The three highest‑ranked need areas were Curriculum Development (0.198), Cooperation Networks (0.196) and Personnel (0.193).  

The proposed strategies comprise five inter‑related components (Vision, Mission, Objectives, Strategies, Key Performance Indicators) organized around six key areas:  

1. Enhancing professional management efficiency – governance‑based administration, digital platforms, budget and PMQA 4.0 evaluation.  
2. Developing competency‑based curricula to international standards – flexible, industry‑linked curricula, dual‑vocational education, outcome‑based education (≥80 % coverage).  
3. Elevating teaching‑and‑learning quality – active learning with industry experts, English/language capability, digital assessment tools, innovative learning platforms.  
4. Developing teacher and staff expertise – certification by internationally recognised bodies, digital‑content production, English‑Program capability, continuous professional development.  
5. Building comprehensive collaboration networks – dual‑vocational education partnerships, academic exchange with domestic/international institutions, resource mobilisation, digital labour‑market information linking.  
6. Improving graduate quality – ethics/morality foundations, up‑skilling programmes, active‑learning scientific processes, certification by professional standards, ≥85 % employment rates.  

Expert evaluation judged the overall suitability and feasibility of the strategies at the highest level.  

Discussion — Findings align with prior studies (Sommut 2020, Teerasawasdi 2015, Khoriklang 2021, Chonnithi 2015, Daoreung 2019) that emphasise curriculum modernisation, stakeholder collaboration and personnel certification.  

Recommendations — Administrators should prioritises Strategy 2 (competency‑based curricula) and adapt the strategies to each institution’s SWOT context. Future research should focus on curriculum‑design models linking professional competencies with qualification systems and on methods for enhancing digital‑content production and professional competency certification.  

The study was conducted by Dr. Puttawat Kanyakan, Dr. Chuankid Masena, Dr. Phongthon Singhaphan, Dr. Somruthai Taochan and Dr. Nares Khantharee; no external funding was received and no competing interests were declared.

American Mint offers the Band of Brothers Men’s Ring, a 24k gold‑layered band in sizes 8–14, priced at $129.90, with a jeweler’s box. Order online (www.americanmint.com) or 1‑877‑807‑MINT; limited to stock. American Mint, based in Mechanicsburg, PA, supplies collectibles worldwide.

David Dickinson, a freelance science writer and US Air Force veteran, reports on the August 21, 2017 total solar eclipse that will sweep across the United States from Oregon to South Carolina in a 70‑mile‑wide path over roughly 90 minutes, providing up to 2 minutes 40 seconds of totality. Umbraphiles (“shadow lovers”) have spent years planning for this event, describing the brief darkness as a singular experience. Dickinson, who has witnessed partial and annular eclipses but never totality, will observe the eclipse at the Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in southwestern North Carolina, expecting 107 seconds of totality, while many chasers travel to Wyoming or Idaho for better weather. He stresses that certified solar glasses (ISO 12312‑2) or proper filters are required during all partial phases, and a pinhole projector offers safe viewing. A subsequent total solar eclipse on April 8, 2024 will cross the United States from southwest to northeast, passing over Dickinson’s hometown of Presque Isle, Maine. He notes that total eclipses will end in about 600 million years as the Moon recedes.
Cancer cells transfer mitochondria to neighboring fibroblasts through tube-like structures, reprogramming these cells to fuel cancer growth and alter gene activity.

A mean‑reversion QQQ trading strategy that exits when the close exceeds yesterday’s high or yesterday’s close has generated a CAGR of about 12.4% since 2000, with a high profit factor and a drawdown far lower than buy‑and‑hold, though future performance remains uncertain.

The study evaluated the maturity of AI in healthcare publications from 2019–2021 using a semi‑automated pipeline. PubMed searches for “machine learning” or “artificial intelligence” limited to English and human research returned 13 400 papers, of which 7 062 (1 647 in 2019, 3 232 in 2020, 2 182 in 2021) met inclusion criteria after excluding non‑relevant topics. A BERT‑based classifier, trained on 2 500 manually labelled abstracts (1998‑2020) and validated on a test set (n = 784) and a prospective 2021 set (n = 2 494), achieved ≈99 % accuracy and 91‑93 % F1 scores.

Overall, 385 of 7 062 papers (≈5 %) were classified as mature (i.e., providing actionable output for patient care). Year‑specific mature rates were 6.01 % in 2019, 7.7 % in 2020, and 1.81 % in 2021; systematic reviews were excluded from detailed analysis.

Radiology accounted for the highest number of mature publications across all three years. Other leading specialties differed by year: Pathology (2019), Ophthalmology (2020), and Gastroenterology (2021). COVID‑19 related AI publications were numerous in 2020–2021 but only 4 % (2020) and 1.6 % (2021) were mature. Cardiovascular disease AI papers remained numerous, yet their relative maturity ranking fell over the period.

Geographically, mature publications were concentrated in the United States and China; the United States led in 2019–2020, while China led in 2021. Developing regions such as South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were markedly underrepresented, indicating potential bias and limited generalizability of current AI solutions.

Manual annotation of mature papers revealed that image data predominated (≈89 % in 2019, 88 % in 2020 and 2021), whereas textual data rose modestly (11 % in 2021) and tabular data declined to zero by 2021. Deep‑learning models were the most common AI approach (66 % in 2019, 71 % in 2020, 62 % in 2021), followed by classical machine‑learning methods.

The authors conclude that only a small fraction of AI in healthcare publications meet maturity criteria, highlighting a need for more clinically relevant and deployable models. The dominance of imaging data and deep‑learning techniques, especially in radiology, stems from readily available open‑source image repositories and pre‑existing convolutional neural network frameworks. Geographic disparities and the under‑representation of text and tabular data suggest opportunities to broaden dataset diversity and expand research capacity in under‑served regions. The findings provide a quantitative baseline to guide future AI research, resource allocation, and the development of heterogeneous, multi‑modal AI solutions across healthcare specialties.

London breakout strategy is a forex day‑trading method that trades upward or downward breakouts of the range formed during the Asian session, occurring within the first three hours of the London session. The London session (8 am–5 pm GMT) overlaps the late Asian and New York sessions and offers the highest liquidity and volatility, often setting the day’s trend. Traders mark the Asian session’s high‑low or open‑close range and enter long on upside breakouts or short on downside breakouts. A custom London breakout indicator provides exact entry, stop‑loss and take‑profit levels,发出一 signal at 3 am EST (8 am London time) and can be automated. Backtesting on EUR/USD with various exit times shows the strategy loses money or yields near‑zero average gains; the authors recommend additional parameters or risk‑management and suggest alternative markets such as stocks and bonds may offer better risk‑reward. Session times: London 8 am–5 pm GMT (adjusted for daylight saving), Asian 8 pm–8 am GMT, New York 8 am–5 pm EST. The authors have published over 1200 articles and offer packaged trading rules, including the London breakout code.

The passage investigates MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown via the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method (IVBM). Four growth stages were identified: turbulent flow enables pure MnBi₂Te₄ formation; rapid MnTe precipitation reduces Mn concentration from ~14% to ~7%; stationary flow promotes ordered assembly of quintuple layers (QLs) and septuple layers (SLs); and cessation of flow causes structural degradation. An inverse relationship exists between SL spacing and MnTe supersaturation in the melt, attributed to diffusion-limited competition between septuple layers. Structural analysis of samples from different ingot positions revealed varying SL spacings (0 to 7±2 QLs) and Mn concentrations (1.14% to 13.5%). Magnetic behavior correlates with layer spacing: antiferromagnetic ordering occurs in closely spaced, compositionally complete SLs (Néel temperatures 26 K and 13.5 K), while ferromagnetic behavior emerges in structures with larger SL separations (Curie temperatures ~10 K). The system exhibits long-range stacking order preserved over tens of micrometers, demonstrating self-organization that can be controlled through melt composition and flow dynamics.

Antiferromagnetic (AFM) domain walls have been studied for decades; recent advances enable efficient observation and manipulation via optical and electrical methods. AFM order offers advantages over ferromagnets, notably the absence of stray fields. The dynamics of AFM textures are described by extensions of the nonlinear σ‑model for the Néel vector, allowing Newtonian and relativistic regimes and enabling spin‑orbit‑torque‑driven domain wall motion faster than in ferromagnets. This work investigates AFM domain wall dynamics under spin‑orbit torque, obtaining a precessional steady state, a constant‑velocity propagating wall (not a simple Lorentz‑boosted static wall), and oscillatory motion when the spin current has both in‑plane and perpendicular components. The study uses a discrete spin chain with antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, and perpendicular anisotropy; the continuum limit yields an extended σ‑model including damping and a spin‑torque term. The magnetization associated with AFM textures is expressed as \(M = (s/\sqrt{2})\int n\times\partial_t n\,dx\). Numerical simulations of a 14 200‑site lattice (x from –355 to 355) with parameters \(s=1\), \(K/J=0.0025\) (\(\epsilon=0.05\)) are performed. For spin polarization \(\hat{p}=\hat{e}_3\) and zero DM interaction, the system evolves to a steady precession of the Néel vector with frequency \(\omega = -\beta/\alpha\).

A bank support staff posted a warning about a fraud scheme at ATMs. A stranger approaches a user, claims to have exceeded a 150,000 naira withdrawal limit and asks the user to receive a transfer into their account and withdraw the cash. The transfer comes from a stolen phone or hacked account. When the account owner reports it, the recipient’s account is frozen, BVN is flagged, and a police memo may be issued for arrest. Two recent cases involve an 18‑year‑old forced at gunpoint to withdraw 40,000 naira and a customer who received 50,000 naira and now faces arrest despite holding about one million naira. The warning advises never to help strangers with ATM transfers.

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife re‑approved Newhall Ranch after the Supreme Court ordered review of greenhouse‑gas emissions and mitigation for protected stickleback. Developer Newhall Land (FivePoint) revised its plan to net‑zero emissions, verified by the California Air Resources Board, and altered bridge and bank‑stabilization work to avoid water contact, eliminating measures. The 15,000‑acre project near SR 128 and I‑5 includes up to 12,000 homes and 11.5 million sq ft of commercial space; Los Angeles County Supervisors vote July 19.

Young African entrepreneurs showcased climate‑focused agricultural innovations at the MasterCard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Summit in Kigali in 2017. Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona Ltd employs 25 youth who collect market waste, separate plastic and metal, and convert organic waste into 50 tonnes per month of cooking fuel briquettes and organic fertiliser, reducing greenhouse‑gas emissions from open‑burning. Pilirani Khoza founded the Bunda Female Students Organisation in 2014, sending sponsored university students to train 360 rural women farmers in simple techniques such as bottle‑irrigation, drought‑tolerant crops and water‑conservation. Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo (knowledge farming) provides a handheld sensor that tests soil and delivers advice via mobile phones; the service helped a farmer increase earnings to $300 per month and aims to reach 200,000 Kenyan smallholders by 2019. The summit highlighted that climate change is intensifying water and food insecurity in Africa, and that a 10 percent rise in agricultural productivity can cut poverty by 7 percent. Experts noted that youth, armed with new technologies and equipped to address the whole agricultural value chain, are uniquely positioned to drive a green revolution and meet Sustainable Development Goals of ending hunger and poverty.

The study developed a comprehensive MEN-associated pathogenic variant (MAPVar) database by classifying 3,280 variants across RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B genes from ClinVar, Mastermind, and the Indian IndiGen population dataset, using ACMG/AMP guidelines. Analysis of IndiGen data estimated the genetic prevalence of RET-linked MEN in India at roughly 1 in 341 individuals, with two pathogenic RET variants identified in individuals from Jammu & Kashmir and Odisha. Comparison with 18 global populations showed one variant was novel in India and the other had significantly higher allele frequency there. The database includes 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 variants of uncertain significance, accessible at https://clingen.igib.res.in/MAPVar/. Validation against the GUaRDIAN cohort identified 5 pathogenic variants across 7 patients with endocrine disorders, and a multiplex primer panel covering all coding regions of the three genes was designed and successfully solved 3 cases, demonstrating its utility for rapid MEN diagnosis and carrier detection.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on February 13, 2020 reporting that it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to publicly offer 2,650,000 shares of its common stock. The underwriters were granted an option to purchase up to an additional 397,500 shares, which they exercised in full on February 18, 2020. The offering closed on February 19, 2020, generating net proceeds of approximately $2.31 billion after discounts and expenses. In connection with the offering, certain investors waived registration rights under the company’s investors’ rights agreement. Related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, the waiver, a legality opinion and a press release, were filed.

Enron Corp. warned that credit worries, declining asset values, and reduced trading activity could hurt fourth-quarter earnings. The energy company restated its third-quarter loss to 87 cents per share and faces a $690 million debt obligation due by late November after a credit downgrade triggered a demand clause. Enron may also face a $700 million derivative loss from its Whitewing partnership and up to $3.9 billion in additional debt if its rating drops below investment grade. The company is being acquired by Dynegy Inc. for approximately $9.8 billion, though bankers are concerned Dynegy could abandon the deal. Congressman John Dingell requested an investigation of Arthur Andersen, Enron's auditor, which faces scrutiny over its audits of Enron and Waste Management. Enron has overstated earnings by $586 million since 1997 and faces numerous shareholder lawsuits.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported $14.9M net income in 2016, includes $2.7M acquisition and conversion charges; assets rose $175.3M to $1.8B; loans grew 14% ($139M); EPS 42 cents after 19‑cent costs; non‑interest income up 38% ($3.4M), flat ex‑securities gains.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. The case involves Lebene Konan, a Texas landlady who filed suit after experiencing mail delivery problems at her property, alleging the failure was intentional and part of racial harassment. The government argues a "postal exception" shields it from such lawsuits under the Federal Tort Claims Act. Lower courts disagreed on whether intentional nondelivery falls under this exception. During Wednesday's argument, justices debated the meaning of "loss" and "miscarriage" in the postal exception, with some expressing concern that a broad ruling could lead to numerous lawsuits over delayed Christmas cards or lost packages. A decision is expected by early July.

At the Silverbluff Audubon Center in Aiken County, fans Paul Koehler and Brandon Heitkamp support the Philadelphia Eagles for the Super Bowl, citing bald eagles that have nested there since 1994 as their inspiration. The eagles, a national symbol, are featured by WJBF reporter George Eskola. Patriots also appreciate the eagles.

R. Thomas Beach submitted rebuttal testimony on behalf of Indicated Electric Generators to the California Public Utilities Commission, responding to the Southern California Generation Coalition and The Utility Reform Network's Post-Interim Settlement Agreement. Beach argues the Commission should adopt the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement rather than PISA, stating that SCGC/TURN exaggerate differences between PG&E and SoCalGas systems, overstate the costs of transmission unbundling, and fail to recognize benefits including competitive city-gate markets, reduced rates for electric generators, and reduced operational risks. The testimony contends that electric generators can avoid demand charge impacts through interruptible service, capacity trading, or city-gate market purchases.

VOT broadcasts shortwave programs to Tibet on 11.510 mHz (8:30-9:30 pm Tibet time), 9.510 mHz (9:30-10:00 pm), and 15.565 mHz (10:00-10:30 am), with different time slots for India and Nepal. VOT's satellite service operates on ASIASAT 7 at 105.5°E, C-Band, with a down frequency of 4146 MHz, horizontal polarisation, and 24-hour availability under the service name "MOMO," offering content alternating between 30 minutes of Mandarin and 30 minutes of Tibetan.

Radford University has selected two finalists for the Vice President for Student Affairs position, left vacant after Dr. Irvin Clark’s departure. Susan Trageser is serving as interim. The finalists met with campus constituents in forums on September 11 and 12. Dr. Thomas C. Segar, current VP at Shepherd University with over 26 years of experience, emphasizes student learning, belonging, social justice and a motto of “students persist; institutes maintain,” and enjoys outdoor activities with family. Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, Dean of Campus Life at NYIT, grew up in Detroit as a first‑generation student and stresses mentorship, adaptability, and using social media to tell Radford’s story. Both candidates are experienced and eager to serve.

Four writers predict Beneil Dariush to defeat Evan Dunham at UFC 216, with three predicting unanimous decision victories and one predicting a second-round submission. Writers cite Dariush's superior all-around skills and underrated ground game.

Jacob Allen sued Richard Knight and his wife Hannah, executrix of her former husband Hope Allen’s estate, for withholding about £64 he was owed under his father’s will; the jury awarded him his proportional share of the estate and court costs of 41 shillings 5 pence.

Nick Kyrgios defeated Jan‑Lennard Struff 6‑4, 6‑4, 6‑4 to level the Australia‑Germany 2018 Davis Cup tie after Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur in a five‑set, four‑hour match that gave Germany a 1‑0 lead. The tie continues Saturday with the Ebden‑Peers vs. Gojowczyk‑Puetz doubles, and concludes Sunday with a reverse singles between Kyrgios and Zverev; a possible deciding match between Struff and de Minaur could follow.

Raymond James chief investment strategist Jeffrey Saut warned that US‑North Korea tensions have caused technical damage to markets, with volatility rising. He sees a possible pullback but maintains a long‑term secular bull market and cautioned that a conflict could push oil to $150 per barrel, though he deems war unlikely. Chantico Global CEO Gina Sanchez forecasts heightened volatility.

The article addresses the gap between universities' commitment to global education and low student participation in study abroad, with only about one percent of U.S. students currently participating. It identifies financial barriers and lack of sustainable business models as primary obstacles. The authors present a structured methodology for building sustainable education abroad programs based on three interdependent drivers: curricular logistics, operational logistics, and financial logistics.

Curricular logistics focus on aligning program design with learning outcomes, considering factors such as whether participation is elective or required, credit allocation, assessment methods, strategic alignment with host institutions, location selection, engagement modalities, and program duration. Operational logistics address risk management, program leadership, travel timing and organization, flights, lodging, local transport, communication, meals, entertainment, emergency preparation, student preparation, wellbeing support, and problem resolution. Financial logistics examine expenses including faculty time, operational support, external party costs, project expenses, and coordination, as well as income sources such as student tuition and fees, and internal and external funding opportunities.

The article presents a typology of twelve business models categorized into three types: external party-led programs run by private or nonprofit companies; faculty-led programs with options including student payment-driven, revenue-driven, corporate donation-driven, and grant-driven models; and student-led programs typically associated with campus clubs. Key principles for sustainable programs include leveraging revenue from community engagement or corporate sponsors, utilizing dedicated staff support, and delegating planning responsibilities to students to reduce faculty workload while fostering student development. The authors emphasize that programs must balance academic excellence with operational and financial feasibility while remaining accessible to diverse student populations.

A UCLA study shows black tea acts as a prebiotic, changing gut bacteria to boost lean‑mass microbes and cut obesity‑linked ones, and may aid weight loss. Black tea works in the gut; green tea also acts in the liver; combining both may be optimal.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8‑K on July 8, 2021 reporting that it will redeem all of its outstanding 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021 (ISIN XS1001749107) issued in the principal amount of €1,750,000,000. The redemption date is September 6, 2021; the cash redemption price equals the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, that date. The redemption is made under the indenture dated May 18, 2009, as supplemented by the seventh supplemental indenture, with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. acting as trustee. The filing notes that the 8‑K does not itself constitute a notice of redemption. Exhibit 99.1 is a press release dated July 8, 2021. Securities listed on NASDAQ under ticker MSFT include Microsoft common stock, the 2.125% notes due 2021, 3.125% notes due 2028 and 2.625% notes due 2033.

Parker Hogan, 19, has been accused of aiding his roommate Michael Buskey's suicide in Plymouth, New Hampshire. Buskey died May 8 from a gunshot wound in the woods near their apartment. Police say Hogan helped plan the suicide, brought a gun to the scene, and instructed Buskey on how to hold it. Hogan was arraigned and entered not guilty pleas to charges including falsifying physical evidence. He's scheduled to appear in court in July and has posted bail.

Speaker describes adjustments after Zdeno was harder to see; notes big saves by Timmy and overtime goal excitement for Tico; emphasizes practicing fundamentals, adjusting shot angles, and maintaining focus; says the team is happy with the win in a four‑out‑of‑seven series and will focus on the next game without distraction.

This study examines the impact of advanced technologies—artificial intelligence, blockchain, metaverse, virtual/augmented reality, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips—on open and distance education and management in higher education institutions. Conducted as a qualitative case study, it involved semi-structured interviews with four academics from Anadolu University with over 20 years of experience in distance education. The findings indicate that these technologies will significantly transform educational environments and management processes, requiring organizations to adapt and reorganize. Experts predict that AI will assume managerial roles, augmented and virtual reality will be used for practical training, and blockchain will provide centralized control. They anticipate a shift from hierarchical to horizontal organizational structures, increased network organizations, and a transition toward knowledge-based employment, with some entry-level jobs being automated. Economically, while initial investments may be high, long-term benefits include cost savings, increased productivity, and profit growth, though unemployment may rise for those lacking technological skills. Socio-culturally, advanced technologies may alter lifestyles, potentially increasing laziness and psychological issues, and lead to the emergence of a "meta-culture" in virtual societies. The study recommends further development and testing of AI managers, blockchain certification systems, adaptive synthetic content, metaverse teaching environments, and research into brain-computer interfaces.

Solar arrays at the Dry Lake Solar Energy Zone north of Las Vegas were commissioned Dec 11 2017 with 179 MW capacity dedicated to Switch’s data centers in Reno and Las Vegas. Former Sen. Harry Reid, EDF Renewable Energy and First Solar Inc. attended. An NV Energy executive said the addition brings Nevada’s solar plants to 16.

The telegram from the US Embassy in the Soviet Union argues that the Andropov regime is not departing from Brezhnev's foreign policy and is utilizing conservative internal methods. It states that the Soviets are likely to accelerate overtures to China, which is not in US interests, but their priority remains the US relationship. The author urges a return to first principles focusing on US security and the prevention of nuclear war, warning against the 1970s mistake of over-relying on arms control without emphasizing defense. The telegram recommends giving heightened priority to arms control, specifically advocating for a change to the US "zero-zero" INF negotiating position, which is deemed to be losing effectiveness. It explains that Soviet strategy aims to manipulate Western European public opinion to prevent US INF deployment without concessions on their part, noting that the original decision to deploy INF systems was primarily a political move to establish US credibility rather than a strict military necessity.
Apple Watch LTE (38/42mm); Apple LTE only, limiting markets like India; KGI's Kuo forecasts 17.5–18 M sales next year, half Series 3; LTE units 2.8–3.6 M (35–40%); sales after fall iPhone launch.

A neural modulation system includes electrodes on leads, a modulation generator, and a programming system to deliver energy for modulating neural tissue. The system uses target multipoles with multiple fractionalized electrodes to create linear electric fields. Examples detail configurations with directional electrodes, user-adjustable parameters (angle, focus, spread), and optimization algorithms to maximize field effectiveness while minimizing activation of non-targeted tissue (e.g., dorsal columns). The system can receive user-drawn regions or pain areas to automatically determine multipole configurations. Methods involve programming modulation parameters based on target multipoles and delivering energy to produce the desired field. The technology aims to selectively modulate dorsal horn or dorsal root tissue over dorsal column fibers for pain relief without paresthesia.

Senate committee report criticizes Supreme Court for imposing rigid trial deadlines the system cannot meet, warns tens of thousands of charges may be dismissed under the Jordan ruling (18‑30‑month limits), proposes 50 recommendations, and says the Court lacked sufficient data.

John Bryant, a pro se inmate, sued DOCS, Sing Sing, and Officer Hernandez under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleging that a Code Blue lockdown from Dec. 24, 1999 to Jan. 13, 2000, based on Officer Hernandez’s false ammunition report, violated inmates’ First, Fourth, Fifth, Eighth, and Fourteenth Amendment rights by denying showers, recreation, library access, mail, phone, hot meals, clean linen, religious services, and non-emergency medical care. He also claimed DOCS violated state labor laws by underpaying inmates (35 cents/day) and denying collective bargaining. DOCS moved to dismiss based on Eleventh Amendment immunity. The magistrate judge recommended dismissal, and the district court, after de novo review of the plaintiff’s objections, agreed. The court held that DOCS and Sing Sing are state agencies entitled to Eleventh Amendment immunity; New York did not consent to suit; and Section 1983 does not abrogate state immunity. The claims against DOCS and Sing Sing were dismissed. The claim against Officer Hernandez may proceed if properly served, and the plaintiff was ordered to advise on service status.

The government plans to give powers to the Insolvency Service, including disqualifying irresponsible directors, reversing asset stripping and clawing back money for workers, in response to corporate failures such as Carillion and BHS. A consultation will be launched. Business Secretary Greg Clark says reforms will strengthen enforcement and accountability. The Insolvency Service disqualifies 1,200 directors annually. MPs Frank Field and Rebecca Long‑Bailey called for greater director accountability.

The Grand River Conservation Authority is spending $1.8 million on a five‑year LiDAR mapping project to produce up‑to‑date digital floodplain maps for the Speed, Conestogo and Grand rivers. The airborne laser data will generate detailed 3‑D models of land and riverbed, replace 40‑year‑old paper maps and be linked to U.S. Army Corps flood‑forecasting software for real‑time warnings. The initiative, already planned, was not a direct response to the June flash flood that highlighted the need for current flood data.

A novel optical technique using ultra‑fast femtosecond and picosecond lasers enables rapid screening and separation of protein sequences, including those inside living bacteria, revealing structural properties relevant to manufacturing and medicine. The method, called time‑domain thermo‑transmission, performs crystallinity measurements in milliseconds without killing cells. It addresses the need for fast, low‑volume screening of large protein libraries. Natural structural proteins such as silk, collagen and wool form a $40 billion industry, but silk loses strength in water while squid‑ring‑teeth proteins retain mechanical performance in wet environments. The researchers, studying both natural and synthetic semicrystalline proteins, received a DURIP grant to build a larger high‑throughput instrument. The work was supported by the Army Research Office.

The speaker discusses an upcoming must-win game, emphasizing focus on execution rather than results. He expresses the team's collective desire to win the Stanley Cup, describing it as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The coaching staff will review defensive tapes to make adjustments, particularly addressing short-side board play that needs improvement. Detroit is noted as a team with strong lines, making matchups less critical than against previous opponents like Buffalo.

The paper proposes a methodology for trusting agents to determine the probability of failure in e-commerce interactions within digital business ecosystems. It introduces the concept of 'FailureLevel' and a failure scale to quantify risk, dividing time into non-overlapping slots to account for risk's dynamic nature. In the pre-interaction phase, FailureLevel is determined using past interaction history or recommendations from other agents, considering factors like trustworthiness and recency. For the post-interaction phase, the methodology uses Gaussian distribution to predict future FailureLevel based on previous levels. An example demonstrates this with two agents, calculating probability distributions for each failure level.

Iowa State fell to Cincinnati 38‑30 in week 6, ending its unbeaten season and opening the Big 12 race. Last year the conference was chaotic: BYU and Arizona State shared the regular‑season title, while expected powers underperformed—Kansas State finished 5‑4 in conference, Oklahoma State won no conference games, and Utah’s only victories came against Oklahoma State and UCF. Heisman‑winner Travis Hunter lifted his team from a bowl absence to conference relevance. The early 2025 upset suggests the Big 12 may again be highly unpredictable.

The study examines how special education teachers in Kazakhstan evaluate disabled education according to inclusive education quality during distance learning. It reviews Kazakhstan’s policies to increase inclusive schools, UNESCO’s three inclusiveness categories, UN Convention rights for persons with disabilities, and the shift to online learning caused by COVID‑19. A qualitative case study with ten teachers collected data through semi‑structured online interviews and used thematic analysis. Findings show teachers primarily used online lessons, videos, homework, and mobile apps. Most teachers (7) considered formal education more advantageous than distance education; six found distance education insufficient to meet individual student needs. Family participation was hindered by high anxiety, lack of technology, communication gaps, and insufficient online family education. Interaction between teachers, students, and peers was reported as weak, time‑limited, unqualified, and irregular. Recommendations include diversifying technology‑based methods, creating individualized content, offering online family seminars, and organizing regular social activities to improve interaction.

A memorial match will be held at Stark’s Park on Sunday to remember Aidan Sutherland, the 20‑year‑old Kirkcaldy footballer who died in July from diabetes complications. Organised by his friend Ben Graham, the event will include a pipe band, stalls, face‑painting and a sweetie bar, with friends, former teammates and ex‑professionals Colin Cameron and Darren Dods playing. Proceeds will go to the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation to raise awareness of the illness and the need for rapid response to hyper‑ or hypoglycaemia. Kick‑off is at 1 pm, with activities starting at noon.

The speaker discusses the importance of learning from difficult situations and maintaining discipline, noting that conversations about poor performance help the team improve. They emphasize controlling emotions and staying focused, while highlighting team depth and praising a player for stepping up during injuries. They express excitement about playing for home fans.

The study analyzed high‑throughput transcriptomic data from three Alzheimer’s disease (AD) cohorts (Knight ADRC, MSBB, ROSMAP) to examine whether shared transcriptomic signatures could explain the bidirectional link between AD and epilepsy. Using RNA‑seq from parietal cortex, parahippocampal gyrus, and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, they applied integrative clustering (iClusterBayes) and differential expression analyses to compare a severe cognitive subtype of AD, termed the synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD) profile, with other sporadic AD cases and controls.

Across the three cohorts, 45–67 % of a set of 105 epilepsy‑associated genes were dysregulated in the SPD profile; 16 genes were commonly dysregulated in all cohorts. Of these, 15 were consistently downregulated (including ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, NECAP1, SCN1A, SCN8A, KCNQ3, UBA5, PPT1, SLC25A12, MEF2C, FGF12, WWOX) and one (CERS1) was upregulated. Most dysregulated genes were highly expressed in iPSC‑derived neurons and enriched for synaptic pathways such as glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapses, as well as ion channel activity and sodium transport. Effect‑size comparisons in ROSMAP showed that epilepsy‑related gene dysregulation was present in both early and late AD, with larger magnitude at later stages.

The findings indicate that epilepsy‑causing genes are disrupted in AD, especially in advanced disease, supporting a bidirectional relationship and suggesting that shared molecular pathways (e.g., GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling, ion channel function) may contribute to both cognitive decline and seizure susceptibility. The authors propose that these shared pathways could be therapeutic targets and emphasize the importance of early detection and management of epilepsy in AD patients.

Uranium’s price rise has corrected from a February high; the Global X Uranium ETF (URA) shows short‑term weakness but seasonal patterns indicate a spring‑summer rebound. The World Nuclear Association projects a 100% increase in the global nuclear fleet—160 reactors already planned and over 300 proposed—adding roughly 37% more capacity. Analysts expect a 6% annual demand rise through 2020, a supply gap covering up to 20% of current reactor demand, and price gains to about $65/lb by 2019. Negative sentiment stemming from the 2011 Fukushima disaster is viewed as disconnected from fundamentals. Investing in uranium is most accessible via URA; short interest has fallen 15% with less than one day to cover. Technical indicators (RSI, stochastic, MACD) signal near‑oversold conditions, with support at the April low, S1 near $14.40 and S2 at the 200‑day moving average.

In his farewell address the President notes that after fifty years of public service he will soon transfer the authority of office in a traditional ceremony. He thanks Congress for its cooperation over his career, recalling his early Senate appointment to West Point, wartime collaboration and eight years of joint effort that advanced national interests. He observes that despite four major wars the United States is now the strongest, most influential and most productive nation, and that its leadership must be exercised not only through material and military strength but also for world peace and human welfare. He stresses the need for balance in national programs, warns against the acquisition of unwarranted influence by the military‑industrial complex, and describes the recent technological revolution that has shifted research toward large‑scale federal efforts, requiring vigilance against both scientific elitism and the capture of public policy by specialists. He calls for long‑term thinking, warns against mortgaging future generations’ resources and advocates steady progress toward disarmament and peaceful resolution of conflicts. The President concludes by expressing gratitude for citizens’ opportunities for service, affirming confidence in a future of peace with justice and offering a prayer that all peoples may attain freedom, prosperity and mutual respect worldwide.

The Tax Court held that gifts made by check were not complete in 1980 because the petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery, and under Oklahoma law, a gift by check is not complete until payment or acceptance by the bank. Consequently, the transfers were treated as occurring in 1981, affecting the gift tax annual exclusion and estate tax deficiency periods.

The GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to twice the performance of the prior Turing generation in programmable shading, ray tracing and AI. It includes second‑generation RT Cores that double ray‑triangle intersection, support hardware‑accelerated motion blur and enable concurrent ray tracing and shading, and third‑generation Tensor Cores that implement fine‑grained structured sparsity with a 2‑out‑of‑4 non‑zero pattern. Structured sparsity compresses weights by 2×, doubles the effective Tensor Core throughput and has negligible impact on inference accuracy across vision, detection, segmentation, language and translation workloads.

Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) uses Tensor Cores and a deep neural network to upscale rendered frames, enabling 8K60 gaming on the GeForce RTX 3090 with a new 9× super‑resolution scaling factor. GDDR6X memory, co‑developed with Micron, employs PAM4 signaling to reach data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth—over 52 % higher than previous GPUs. A Maximum Transition Avoidance (MTA) encoding scheme reduces transition errors on the high‑speed memory interface.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage for Windows to move compressed data directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU, providing GPU‑based lossless decompression and achieving up to 100× I/O throughput and 20× lower CPU utilization. This improves frame rates, shortens load times and supports larger, more detailed open‑world games.

The data‑center A40 GPU, based on GA10x, offers up to 2× FP32 throughput, 2× ray‑tracing performance and 5× AI training throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000, supports PCIe Gen 4 and can scale to 96 GB via third‑generation NVLink. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU features 48 GB GDDR6, second‑generation RT Cores, hardware‑accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and can be paired for 96 GB of combined memory.

Display capabilities include DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a for single‑cable 8K60, HDMI 2.1 for 8K60/4K120 and HDCP 2.3 support. GA10x GPUs include a fifth‑generation NVDEC hardware decoder supporting MPEG‑2, VC‑1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and the first hardware‑accelerated AV1 decode, enabling 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. The seventh‑generation NVENC encoder provides hardware‑accelerated video encoding up to 8K HEVC, matching the quality of x264 Medium preset while reducing CPU load.

Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and retries transactions, allowing users to identify memory limits during overclocking by observing performance plateauing rather than crashes.

Amazon Prime Day discounts on toys include multiple Squishmallows: a 20‑inch Diane Peach Bigfoot plush at over 50% off, a 20‑inch Caedyn Cream Cow for $24 ($10 off), a 5‑inch Austin the Avocado for $5, and a 12‑inch Maui the Pineapple for $9. this prospective observational cohort study evaluated single‑nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in PTPN2 (rs72872125), VDR (rs7975232, rs731236, rs11568820) and FCGR2A (rs1801274) as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for aggressive cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) behavior. 103 patients were stratified as symptomatic (hemorrhage or seizure) or asymptomatic and followed up to 4 years; 42 patients formed a prognostic subgroup. Genotyping and plasma cytokine profiling (18 cytokines) were performed. PTPN2 rs72872125 CT genotype and VDR rs7975232 CC genotype were more frequent in asymptomatic patients and were associated with altered plasma levels of IL‑10, IL‑18, IFN‑γ, IL‑27 and IL‑23. A discriminant model combining PTPN2 rs72872125 CC genotype with serum GM‑CSF distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients (AUC = 0.663, sensitivity 41.3 %, specificity 85.7 %). The FCGR2A rs1801274 GG genotype predicted symptomatic events during follow‑up (AUC = 0.796 in the full subgroup and AUC = 0.875 after propensity‑score matching). VDR rs731236 AA genotype delayed symptom onset (hazard ratio 0.52), while VDR rs11568820 CC genotype accelerated it (hazard ratio 1.58). In silico structural analysis showed the FCGR2A rs1801274 variant (H131R) is conserved among higher primates. The study proposes PTPN2/VDR genotypes as diagnostic biomarkers and FCGR2A GG as a prognostic biomarker for aggressive CCM phenotype, emphasizing the influence of inflammatory pathways.

The study presents a coupled mechanical‑biogeochemical model for CH₄ bubble growth in consolidated aquatic muds. Bubbles nucleate as penny‑shaped seeds and grow beyond the pore scale through elastic cavity expansion followed by localized tensile fracturing described by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM). The model integrates (i) a solute‑conservation equation for dissolved CH₄ diffusion with uniform boundary concentration and a no‑flux condition on the symmetry plane, and (ii) a force‑equilibrium equation for elastic deformations, solved concurrently in a symmetric sediment block with an applied overburden stress. Bubble pressure is derived from Henry’s law, the inner pressure balances the normal compressive stresses, and the Mode‑I stress‑intensity factor (K_I) is calculated by displacement/stress extrapolation at the crack front. Crack propagation direction follows the strain‑energy‑density criterion, and the local crack increment Δa is proportional to (K_I/K_I,max)², limited by the mesh size. The finite‑element implementation uses COMSOL Multiphysics with quadratic Lagrange elements for mechanics, linear elements for transport, and a refined mesh near the bubble surface and front. Input parameters correspond to summer conditions at 1 m sediment depth in Eckernförde Bay. Validation against analytical solutions for mature bubble shape and size shows good agreement for varying fracture toughness. The model applies to individual bubbles; upscaling to effective gassy‑mud properties for remote‑sensing, sediment‑destabilization assessment, and methane‑flux prediction remains a future challenge.

This passage describes a teacher education program integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to enhance pre-service teachers' diagnostic skills and instructional design capabilities. The program involved 22 teacher education students (TESs) over one semester, comprising four cycles of collaborative lesson preparation, teaching practice with classroom observation using panoramic cameras, post-teaching review of footage, group discussions, and subsequent adjustments to teaching plans. The study assessed TESs' diagnostic abilities through observation reports and their perceived instructional design capabilities via a questionnaire. Results indicated improved diagnostic performance across cycles, with average scores rising from approximately 0.47 to above 1.88 out of 2 points, and significant positive changes in perceived capabilities for lesson preparation, linking observation with teaching practice, and adjusting plans based on discussions (p < 0.05). The conclusion suggests that the integrated model is feasible and effective in teacher education.

Amazon has been granted a patent for a “directed fragmentation” system for delivery drones. It uses a continuously updated fragmentation sequence to decide which components to release, based on flight path, weather, and terrain data. Terrain topology data can target safe drop sites such as water, forests, or open fields, and the drone can control where parts fall using latches, hooks, springs, small explosives, or compressed gas. The order of release is chosen by factoring in component cost, weight, drag, and purpose, to modify the drone’s descent in a controlled manner. Triggers include high winds, heat, rain, hail, battery or rotor failure, or sensor errors. The patent acknowledges catastrophic failure risk and suggests a solution for drone deliveries, though implementation is not guaranteed.

President's annual message to Congress reviewing the nation's condition at its 60th anniversary. The United States maintains peace with all nations and blessings of harvest and restored health following pestilence. Relations with Great Britain improved through navigation act changes allowing mutual vessel admission. Diplomatic intercourse with France resumed. Regarding Germany, the U.S. maintained neutrality during the Schleswig-Holstein war by halting naval assistance to a German war steamer and recalling the minister from Frankfort to Berlin as no definitive German Empire government exists. The expedition to Cuba was suppressed to honor treaty obligations with Spain. An abducted foreigner was restored from Cuba and returned to American jurisdiction.

The U.S. remained neutral during European conflicts including the Austria-Hungary war, standing ready to recognize Hungarian independence had it succeeded. Claims against Portugal remain unsettled and will require special message. Relations with Russia, Austria, Prussia, Sweden, Denmark, Belgium, Netherlands, and Italy remain amicable. Diplomatic relations with the Papal States remain unsettled due to revolutions. Relations with Mexico are friendly under the Guadalupe Hidalgo treaty, with boundary commissioners making progress and claims commissions ongoing.

The Treasury shows receipts of $59.6 million and expenditures of $57.6 million, with projected deficits requiring borrowing authority. The President recommends tariff revision with specific duties, continued river and harbor improvements, and careful economy in expenditures.

California's people have formed a constitution and will apply for statehood; New Mexico is expected to follow. The President recommends establishing an agricultural bureau, a branch mint in California, land title commissions, and geological surveys of mineral lands. A transcontinental railroad reconnaissance is recommended to assess feasibility.

Regarding the African slave trade, existing laws are inadequate to prevent abuse via sea letters, and stronger enforcement is needed. A convention with Brazil for claims satisfaction awaits Senate approval. Separate treaties with Central American states and a canal treaty with Nicaragua have been negotiated. The Panama railroad under the New Granada treaty and routes at Tehuantepec remain important for interoceanic communication.

The military requires increases at western posts and an officer retirement system is recommended. The Navy reports satisfactory conditions and reorganization is suggested. Post office service to California is inadequate and postage reduction to five cents is recommended with Treasury funding for congressional franking. The census board has completed preparations and awaits Congressional legislation.

The President emphasizes constitutional separation of powers, using the veto only in extraordinary cases, and expresses unwavering commitment to preserving the Union as the greatest duty of every American.

Major social media platforms are tightening policies, hiring more staff, and redesigning algorithms to address hate speech, extremist propaganda, fake news, and other community‑standard violations. AI can scan text for slurs and extremist terminology and recognize prohibited images such as the swastika, but it is not reliable: it mis‑tagged dark‑skinned users as “gorilla” and still struggles with evolving language, as shown by Twitter’s search outage for terms like #gay and #bisexual. Because AI systems learn from human‑labeled data, they inherit human bias—if training sets over‑represent white males, the system performs poorly on other skin tones, and this bias spreads across programs. Moreover, AI cannot assess intent; it incorrectly removed a post that paired a swastika with an anti‑hate plea, flagged the statue of Neptune as explicit, and repeatedly deleted the historic “napalm girl” photo. Although AI serves as an initial filter and helps prioritize posts for human reviewers, human moderators remain essential. Facebook has doubled its review team to 20,000, and AI‑driven tools that flag suicidal content have triggered emergency responses. Experts note that AI speeds moderation but cannot fully automate it, and that ethical oversight must keep pace with rapid technological growth, increasing demand for staff with humanities or ethics expertise.

Lobbyists for Connecticut towns and cities asked Governor Malloy to ease administrative burdens. The Council of Small Towns (COST) and the Connecticut Conference of Municipalities (CCM) want changes to municipal retirement system, easier arbitration of collective‑bargaining issues and land‑transfer fees. Malloy said six‑week budget stalemate created uncertainty, noting regulatory relief. CCM executive Joe DeLong said municipalities face reduced aid but are not seeking hold‑harmless status; Senate President Pro Tempore Martin Looney called inaccurate. The state budget deficit is estimated at $3.5 billion after union concessions, and COST wants the prevailing‑wage threshold updated and employee retirement contributions removed from state law.

SanDisk’s warranty requires contacting the company by phone or email, returning the product in tamper‑resistant packaging, freight prepaid, and obtaining a tracking number. SanDisk may, at its option, repair, replace, or refund the product; the warranty period for a replacement continues for the remaining time on the original product. The warranty does not cover loss of data, and SanDisk disclaims all express or implied warranties to the extent permitted by law; liability is limited to the purchase price paid. The software is licensed under a limited, non‑exclusive, non‑sublicensable agreement, provided “as is,” with no warranties, and may not be reverse‑engineered, modified, or used in high‑risk activities. The agreement is governed by California law and can be terminated for breach.

A method and a system for manufacturing an orthodontic appliance are disclosed. The method comprises measuring a patient’s tooth positions, receiving tooth‑movement constraints, and measuring a first element of the patient’s malocclusion. Based on the measured positions and constraints, a plurality of treatment plans is generated. For each plan, a first interim final tooth position is generated; a second element of the malocclusion in that interim final position is measured; the interim final position is then modified to correct the element; and a final position for the plan is generated. One of the plurality of plans is selected, a model of an appliance for each stage of the selected plan is generated, and instructions for fabricating the appliance for each stage are output. Optionally, the appliances for one or more stages are fabricated from the instructions.

The method can create additional treatment‑plan branches based on decisions about treating various malocclusion elements (e.g., openbite, molar class, canine class, overjet, posterior crossbite) and based on options such as bicuspid extraction or interproximal reduction. For each branch, interim final positions are determined, corrected, and used to produce the final positions. The system includes a processor and memory that store instructions to carry out the described steps.

Orthodontic appliances are described as shell‑type devices having tooth‑receiving cavities and can be fabricated by direct methods (e.g., stereolithography, selective laser sintering, fused deposition modeling, multi‑material additive manufacturing) or by indirect methods (e.g., thermoforming over a mold). Appliances may have heterogeneous thickness, stiffness, or material composition and can include integrally formed features or auxiliary components. Fabricated appliances may be used in a series of stages to incrementally reposition teeth from an initial arrangement toward a target arrangement.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10‑Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018. The company, incorporated in Delaware, reported total assets of $29.26 billion and total liabilities of $23.41 billion, resulting in total stockholders’ equity of $4.51 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion and restricted cash $158.6 million. For the three months ended September 30, 2018, Tesla recorded net income attributable to common stockholders of $311.5 million (basic earnings per share $1.82, diluted $1.75). For the nine months then ended, the net loss was $1.12 billion (basic and diluted loss per share $6.56). Total revenues for the quarter were $6.82 billion (automotive sales $5.88 billion, automotive leasing $220.5 million, energy generation and storage $399.3 million, services and other $326.3 million); nine‑month revenues were $14.24 billion. The company adopted ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) on January 1, 2018 using the modified retrospective method, recording a cumulative adjustment to accumulated deficit of $623.2 million. Tesla operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. As of October 26, 2018, 171,732,775 shares of common stock were outstanding. The registrant is a large accelerated filer subject to the SEC’s filing requirements.

In a French monitored access program, 112 patients with hematological malignancies and COVID-19 received convalescent plasma (CCP) transfusion. The 90-day overall survival was 64.9% overall, 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasm, 20% for myeloid neoplasm, and 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasm. Inverse probability treatment weighting analysis showed CCP was associated with a 63% reduction in death risk among B-cell lymphoid disease patients pre-treated with anti-CD20 therapy. CCP transfusion decreased inflammatory markers (temperature, CRP, ferritin, fibrinogen) and increased PCR cycle threshold values, indicating reduced viral load. Adverse events were limited to 3 allergic reactions and 2 transient oxygen requirement increases. Limitations include the retrospective observational design, absence of vaccinated patients, and coverage of only original and Alpha SARS-CoV-2 variants.

The document lists known hardware issues and design deviations in the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device (Silicon Revision A3). Issue numbers such as 40, 44, 54, 70, 85, 89, 90, 92, 98–116 appear with brief titles covering problems with the GLIU, UART, DMA, I/O cycles, PIC, UDMA, ACPI, USB, LPC, and other subsystems. Detailed descriptions are provided for several issues: a PIT read‑back command that does not cancel a latch command, returning the counter value first; a debug port that hangs the system on detection of a special GeodeLink packet (no workaround); an incorrect immediate load of a new count value in PIT mode 3; an XPIC bug where the IRR bit is cleared one clock after the second interrupt‑acknowledge pulse, causing double interrupts with auto‑EOI; a DMA rotating‑priority mode that does not rotate correctly; a thermal alarm that cannot be detected while the system is in Standby, leading to repeated faulted‑standby cycles; and a Sleep Clock control side effect requiring the Sleep Clock option to be enabled in the PMC register even when disabled at the GPIO. Implications range from negligible impact to functional failures; most issues have no resolution or only suggest avoiding the problematic usage.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8‑K on September 5, 2017 reporting that on September 12, 2017 it issued $5 billion of senior unsecured notes in four series: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027 and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. The notes were sold under an underwriting agreement dated September 5, 2017 with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank Securities and Merrill Lynch as representatives. They are governed by an indenture dated April 29, 2013 and an officer’s certificate dated September 12, 2017. Interest is payable semi‑annually on March 12 and September 12, beginning March 12, 2018, and the notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of notes, legal opinion and consent as exhibits. The report is signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Luca Maestri.

Diana Containerships Inc. (NASDAQ:DCIX) reported a Q loss of $0.66 per share, beating the $0.77 consensus estimate by $0.11. Quarterly revenue was $5.40 million, missing the $7.50 million forecast and falling 63.8% year‑over‑year. The company posted a negative return on equity of 11.99% and a negative net margin of 350.33%. Diana Containerships operates a fleet of containerships through subsidiary Unitized Ocean Transport Limited.

This document contains news headlines and articles from March 27-28, 2001, covering various topics including Viacom/Blockbuster, energy markets, and Enron's activities.

Viacom abandoned its plan to split off Blockbuster, stating the video-rental chain's business has improved significantly. Blockbuster's market share rose from 26% in 1997 to 36% by end of 2000, with CEO John Antioco expecting it to approach 40% by end of 2001 and 50% within three years. Blockbuster stock rose from around $8 at end of 2000 to $15.10 in late February 2001.

President Bush named Patrick H. Wood III and Nora M. Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), which oversees electricity markets. Wood, head of the Texas Public Utility Commission and a Bush ally, supported price caps during Texas deregulation. The appointments came as FERC faced pressure to intervene in California's power crisis, where wholesale electricity prices rose more than tenfold.

Enron awarded Chairman Kenneth Lay a $7 million bonus for 2000, up 79% from $3.9 million in 1999, citing the company's "extremely strong" performance. Lay's base salary was $1.3 million, and he received $7.5 million in restricted stock awards and options for 782,830 shares.

Enron presented plans to build a liquefied natural gas-fired power plant in Aomori Prefecture, Japan, with initial capacity of 2 million kilowatts. Construction was scheduled to begin in 2004 for 2007 operation. The project cost was expected to exceed initial estimates of 20 billion yen, possibly reaching over 100 billion yen.

Enron and PowerGen withdrew their bids for a 26% stake in the 500 MW Vijayanagar Thermal Power Project in Karnataka, India. Karnataka Power Corporation initiated talks with Larsen & Toubro (L&T) to pick up the stake instead. An Enron spokesperson stated the company would not make further investments in India until the power sector became economically viable.

Enron Wind applied to establish a wholly owned subsidiary in India for assembling, installing, and operating wind turbines. The initial investment was proposed at $2 million, with the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to consider the proposal.

CEO Jeffrey Skilling said Texas energy markets were well-positioned for deregulation starting January 1, 2001, contrasting Texas with California's problems. Skilling stated California's system was "the most regulated markets in North America" and suggested California's 40% rate hike would help reduce shortages.

California's Public Utilities Commission approved electricity rate increases of up to 46% to prevent utility bankruptcies. SoCal Edison and Pacific Gas & Electric reported losses exceeding $13 billion since summer 2000 due to wholesale price caps.

Enron projected 2001 revenue of $160 billion to $170 billion, up from $100.8 billion in 2000. The company was pressing the Export-Import Bank to allow private lenders to offer export financing.

Dubai was described as "desperate" for natural gas supplies for power generation, with the Dolphin Energy project (involving TotalFinaElf and Enron) planning to supply gas from Qatar's North Field starting 2005.

The Indian government considered barring state governments from directly accessing multilateral agency funds, citing deteriorating state finances including the Enron payment crisis in Maharashtra.

Steve Yzerman emphasizes building the Tampa Bay Lightning through homegrown talent and patience, relying on draft picks and player development rather than quick fixes via trades or free agency. He credits Al Murray’s scouting staff for finding players such as Steven Stamkos, Victor Hedman, and later‑round picks like Ondrej Palat and Nikita Kucherov, who have become key contributors. Coach Cooper describes the team’s evolution, noting how young players were given opportunities in the AHL, allowed to develop together, and then advanced to the NHL as a group, creating a strong core. Leadership has transitioned from veterans to Steven Stamkos, who has accepted different roles and sacrificed personal scoring to enable others. The organization maintains a winning culture, with players like Ben Bishop and the forward group rising to challenges throughout the playoffs. Yzerman stresses the importance of character, program quality, and patience to attract talent and sustain success.

Bittle tree, a tulip poplar planted by Roanoke’s first president Dr. David Bittle, stood over 100 years before being removed after lightning and wind damage. Its wood was used to create Bittle Tree of Life Cross installed in Antrim Chapel for 175th anniversary. Designed by Reverend Chris Bowen and George Arthur, cross shows a tree with roots and branches, symbolizing college’s foundations and future.

May Baxter‑Thornton and Emma Lewis, survivors of child sexual abuse, appointed to IICSA’s panel to advise on reaching Welsh victims, promised to champion cause. Baxter‑Thornton was abused in late 70s‑80s and 16 years’ experience. Lewis entered care at 10, disclosed abuse at 12, works with care‑leaving youth. The inquiry opened in Wales November 2016 consulted towns.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana granted the writ of review in the case Robert Daniel Chappuis v. Sears Roebuck & Co. (No. 60725) on November 11, 1977, and ordered the Court of Appeal to transmit the record in duplicate and notify the parties’ counsel.

ERW pipes transport petroleum and gas at various pressures with high efficiency, low cost, and material savings. They use hot-rolled coil with wall thickness controlled to ±0.2mm and burr removal to 0.2–0.5mm, meeting API or GB/T9711.1 standards for urban pipe networks.

This patent application describes a system and method for identifying audio content facilitated by a playback device. The application is a continuation of several related SONOS patent applications regarding audio content identification. The technology enables a playback device to receive digital audio data, send portions to an identification system to retrieve metadata, and forward the information to a control device while playing the audio via speakers. This approach avoids the need for a control device to use a microphone to capture and identify audio. The disclosure includes detailed descriptions of playback devices, control devices, playback zone configurations, and methods for extracting digital data from various points in an audio processing pipeline, including handling audio discontinuities and frequency segregation.

During a March 25 meeting, Rep. Ken Buck called health care a commodity, not a right. The writer calls health care a right, arguing that the system endangers lives and supports Medicare for all. The writer criticizes a headline about Denver paying $1 million to family of a teen shot by police, saying it should note the teen was driving a stolen car toward an officer, argues police acted in self‑defense, calls the settlement unjustified, and for respect for police.

A directional illumination apparatus and display device are disclosed, comprising an imaging directional backlight with a waveguide that guides light from an illuminator array to exit through a first guide surface, a transmissive spatial light modulator, input and output polarizers, an additional polarizer, and at least one retarder arranged between the additional polarizer and the input or output polarizer. The retarder may include crossed A-plates, C-plates, O-plates, or switchable liquid crystal retarders, enabling privacy mode by reducing off-axis luminance while maintaining head-on luminance and efficiency. A control system can switch between privacy and wide angle modes by controlling light sources and applied voltage. Applications include autostereoscopic 3D displays, multi-viewer displays, and privacy displays for devices such as automotive displays.

A Deloitte survey shows consumer confidence in driverless cars has risen; only 49% now doubt safety versus 73% last year. Trust in brands and manufacturers drives the shift: 53% cite brand trust (up from 44%) and 51% prefer manufacturers over tech firms (21%). Respondents prefer conventional engine vehicles (73%) over electric (2%), citing range, price and charging infrastructure as barriers, though 37% would consider an electric car if ongoing costs fell. Customer service remains a buying factor, and the UK government is launching a safety inquiry for the driverless rollout.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory, based on historical data, suggests that U.S. stock market performance follows a predictable pattern over a president's four-year term. Typically, the first two years underperform the last two years, with midterm election years showing weak performance until the fourth quarter. Yale Hirsch, founder of the Stock Trader's Almanac, quantified this effect, noting that pre-election years are the best-performing, followed by election years, especially when an incumbent runs for reelection. Volatility tends to increase during midterm years. The theory attributes this pattern to presidential policies aimed at stimulating the economy for re-election. While the cycle is a consistent seasonal pattern, it cannot predict market performance exactly, and its impact is more sector-specific (e.g., healthcare, energy) rather than economy-wide.

Intel embeds a small microcontroller called the Management Engine (ME) in its CPUs. The ME is connected to all peripherals, remains active even when the computer is off, and can be awakened over a network. Parts of the ME were added at the NSA's request. At BlackHat Europe, researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy demonstrated an exploit that allows arbitrary code execution on the ME, requiring physical access. The ME runs the Minix operating system and originated from Trusted Platform Modules and Active Management Technology. It can theoretically exfiltrate keystrokes from a powered‑down machine. The exploit enables arbitrary code execution via USB. Mitigation options include firmware updates from System76, Dell laptops with ME disabled, Intel's detection tool, and the me_cleaner tool that tricks the ME by deleting its first ROM page. No universal method to disable the ME exists, and disabling it is manufacturer‑dependent. The current exploit requires physical access; a network‑based exploit has not yet been observed. The case illustrates concerns about unauditable code in hardware.

Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities. The bill was proposed after 22-year-old Stephen Komninos died in a Haddonfield group home in 2007. The law allows state inspectors to conduct unannounced visits twice yearly and requires treatment agencies to notify parents within two-to-eight hours of patient injuries. Family meetings are required at least twice a year.

Mortimer J. Adler’s perennalist philosophy underpins a qualitative literature‑review study that analyses Christian education and global education management. Adler stresses the continuity of ideas across time, essentialising knowledge as opinion and affirming that lectures and memorisation remain valuable despite technological acceleration. He links educational management to learners’ rational capacities and argues for democratic education that develops full human potential rather than merely preparing for employment.  

Adler defines docility as a postponement of judgment toward a trusted authority (e.g., a teacher) and as a virtuous, enduring value that complements pietism. He maintains that docility does not destroy democratic agency, but he acknowledges dilemmas and cultural ambivalence toward obedience. Critics in the paper note that Adler does not differentiate between genders, suggesting women may need prior support before entering education.  

The study reviews four prior works: Fruh et al. on family‑meal interventions in Christian families, Stephen on spirituality in managing chronic disease, Espinosa & González on moral education in 160 Christian schools across 17 countries, and Patra on subjective versus objective character education. These illustrate global, multidimensional approaches to education management that extend beyond administrative tasks.  

Posthumanist theory is examined as an unfinished, locality‑dependent framework that questions anthropocentric supremacy and explores technology‑mediated human identity (robots, AI, implants). The paper sees posthumanism as a critical lens that, combined with Adler’s perennialist values, deepens reflection on educational praxis beyond mere systematisation.  

Christian‑based management examples include: a Kenyan transformation of a Bible‑school institution into a university, a New‑Zealand diaspora‑community disaster‑resilience model using the Tama Fanau concept, business‑family social assets grounded in Christian values, and identity‑diversity practices in investment ethics.  

The conclusion argues that a just society requires empowering women, removing the expectation that children become miniature adults, and ensuring that teachers, parents, and the state—not children—bear responsibility for educational failures. Educational management must reach beyond the classroom and engage the fragile, evolving identities of learners, integrating Adler’s emphasis on docility, intellect and conscience with perennialist timeless values. The analysis highlights that post‑humanist critique, when viewed through Adler’s philosophy, pushes education management toward deeper, value‑driven exploration of curricular spaces, including Indonesia’s independent curricula.

Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield is the Browns’ No. 1 pick. GM remains open to options, and coach says top QBs are still in play. Darnold favorite; Allen rising. Dorsey values winning, accuracy, arm strength. Mayfield, 2017 Heisman winner, threw 4,627 yards and 43 TDs, led Oklahoma to Big 12 title and CFP berth.

Jefferies raised Ferguson Plc’s price target to GBX 5,240 (hold); Liberum Capital reissued buy, target GBX 5,300. J P Morgan and Barclays set overweight at GBX 5,600. Peel Hunt raised target to GBX 5,200 (hold) and Deutsche Bank reissued hold at GBX 4,700. Three analysts hold and four recommend buy; average rating “Buy”, target GBX 5,265.71.
