Background: Traditional LVEF and wall‑motion assessment often fail to detect early systolic dysfunction in CHD patients, and there is no rapid bedside index for evaluating myocardial recovery after revascularization.

Objective: To examine the relationship between LVEF‑1 (the proportion of left‑ventricular volume change from aortic‑valve opening to peak aortic flow velocity relative to end‑diastolic volume) and the degree of coronary artery stenosis, and to assess LVEF‑1 changes after PCI.

Methods: Consecutive patients (June 2021–June 2023) undergoing coronary angiography for chest pain were enrolled if they were ≥18 years old, had angina or evidence of myocardial ischemia, and had LVEF > 50%. Exclusions included prior MI/heart failure, significant valvular disease, atrial fibrillation, chronic total occlusion, or poor echocardiographic images. Patients were classified by maximum stenosis: mild (< 50%), moderate (50–70%) and severe (≥ 70%). Echocardiography (LVEF, GLS, E/e’, LAD, LVDd, LVDs, LVEF‑1) was performed before and on day 4 after PCI. Statistical analyses included Pearson correlation, restricted cubic splines, logistic regression, paired t‑tests, multiple linear regression, and ROC curve evaluation.

Results: 207 patients (73 mild, 39 moderate, 95 severe; 82 severe patients underwent PCI). As stenosis severity increased, male sex, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, SBP, DBP, glucose, CRP, BNP, LAD, LVDd, LVDs, E/e’, and Gensini score rose (P < 0.05), while GLS and LVEF‑1 fell (P < 0.05); LVEF did not differ. LVEF‑1 correlated negatively with Gensini score (r = ‑0.694) and BNP (r = ‑0.244). Restricted cubic splines confirmed a non‑linear negative relation with Gensini score and a linear negative relation with BNP. Logistic regression showed LVEF‑1 independently predicted stenosis ≥ 50% (OR 0.406, 95% CI 0.313–0.526) and ≥ 70% (OR 0.366, 95% CI 0.275–0.486). ROC analysis gave a cutoff of 27.9% for LVEF‑1 (sensitivity 82.8%, specificity 83.6%) for ≥ 50% stenosis and 26.9% (sensitivity 89.5%, specificity 83.9%) for ≥ 70% stenosis; AUC was higher than for LVEF, GLS, E/e’, or LVDd. After PCI, E/e’ decreased while GLS and LVEF‑1 increased (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified Gensini score and stent diameter as independent factors influencing ΔLVEF‑1.

Conclusion: LVEF‑1 is a sensitive indicator of cardiac dysfunction related to coronary artery stenosis; its decrease reflects stenosis severity and its increase after PCI indicates therapeutic benefit, particularly in more severe disease.

Medical problems within one month after the second or booster doses were mostly mild or moderate; no single problem affected more than 2 % of participants in any group. The study investigates transfer learning to address domain shift in neuroimaging, focusing on age and sex prediction from structural MRI. The authors use Simple Fully Connected Neural Networks (SFCNs) pretrained on the UK Biobank (≈40 000 subjects) and then fine‑tune on three smaller datasets (OASIS‑3, IXI, ABIDE). They propose a three‑step transfer‑learning pipeline: (i) pretrain the SFCN on the large source dataset, (ii) if the output dimensionality differs, reshape the classifier and retrain only this layer on the target data, and (iii) fine‑tune the entire model on the target data. Data augmentation (random translations and sagittal mirroring) expands the effective training set by a factor of ~250.

Direct transfer of a sex‑classification model pretrained on UKB achieved 99.5 % on UKB, 90.2 % on OASIS, 59.9 % on ABIDE and 59.1 % on IXI, showing substantial performance drops due to domain shift. Visualisation of high‑dimensional features via t‑SNE revealed that learned features are highly task‑specific (age‑trained models do not separate sexes) and that OASIS/IXI preserve spatial separation while ABIDE does not because of its younger age range.

Fine‑tuning only the classifier improved performance; full fine‑tuning gave further gains especially for ABIDE (age MAE reduced from 4.43 ± 0.22 to 1.70 ± 0.07). Across all target datasets, the transfer‑learning pipeline outperformed elastic‑net regression on PCA features (e.g., OASIS age MAE 6.24 → 3.25; sex accuracy 67 % → 92.6 %) and also outperformed training from scratch, with faster convergence. Ablation experiments showed that the benefit comes from actual feature reuse, not merely from scaled random initialization.

The authors conclude that the UK Biobank can serve as an “ImageNet” for neuroimaging, enabling effective and simple transfer learning that improves both predictive accuracy and training efficiency even with small target datasets. Limitations include the limited scanner variety in UKB and challenges for disease‑specific prediction tasks.

This study introduces the first large-scale publicly available Turkish dataset for citation intent classification in Computer Science, containing 2,650 annotated examples from 723 research articles. The researchers address a significant gap in Turkish academic literature by developing AI models to classify citations into five categories: Background, Basis, Support, Differ, and Discuss.

The methodology employs Large Language Models (GPT-4o and Gemini) with In-Context Learning (ICL), progressing from manual prompting to automated optimization using the DSPy framework. A stacked ensemble model combining multiple base classifiers through an XGBoost meta-model achieves the highest performance.

Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains: manual prompts (v001) reached 83.9-85.0% accuracy, DSPy optimization improved this to 86.5%, majority voting ensemble achieved 90.2%, and the final stacked ensemble reached 91.3% accuracy. Challenges encountered include severe class imbalance with the Background class dominating, difficulty distinguishing semantically similar categories like Support and Differ, and LLM inconsistencies in repeated classifications.

The study concludes that integrating diverse models through learned weighting produces more robust classifiers and establishes a foundational resource for Turkish scholarly NLP, with future directions focused on addressing class imbalance through hierarchical classifiers, synthetic data augmentation, and expanded contextual features.

Uncertainty about a key injured teammate is acknowledged; the player’s presence is a boost, but if he can’t contribute the team will rely on other players. The speaker advocates staying even‑keeled, businesslike and avoiding cockiness, pointing out that veterans who have experienced both winning and losing help keep the group focused on present tasks. He contrasts home‑game pressure—crowds, high expectations—versus the more relaxed environment on the road, noting that while winning is enjoyable, the priority is executing the game plan.

Prof. Ross Levine and co‑authors from the University of Hong Kong and Chinese University of Hong Kong published an NBER paper titled “Bank Liquidity, Credit Supply, and the Environment.” The study shows that easier borrowing encourages firms to invest in pollution‑reducing projects by increasing credit availability for green loans and lowering financing costs via reduced interest rates. These investments cut pollution fines, improve worker health and productivity, and enhance corporate reputation. The authors used the shale‑gas boom as a natural experiment: landowners deposited lease payments in banks, expanding banks’ lendable funds. Comparing non‑gas‑producing counties whose banks received deposit windfalls elsewhere with average counties, they found benzene levels fell 26 % and other toxic pollutants fell similarly. Individual firms that obtained better credit terms reduced toxic emissions more, received higher environmental performance ratings, and publicly advocated green issues more than control firms. The research does not evaluate the direct environmental effects of fracking. Levine plans to examine how credit conditions affect worker safety.

Ryan Malone, a 37-year-old 2010 Olympic silver medalist, signed a 25-game tryout with the AHL’s Iowa Wild to stay eligible for the 2018 PyeongChang Games. Brian Gionta, 38, who led the 2006 U.S. Olympic team in goals, was announced as the lone men’s hockey player at a Nov. 1 countdown event. Both have over 1,500 NHL games. Malone came out of retirement to try out for the Minnesota Wild but joined the AHL instead. Gionta, unsigned, had a meeting with an AHL club in Rochester on Sept. 25. USA Hockey confirmed Gionta is on its radar but he likely needs to play for a non-NHL team. The 25-player U.S. Olympic team will be named around Jan. 1. Malone and Gionta are older than all previous U.S. Olympic hockey players except Chris Chelios, who was an assistant on the PyeongChang team.

David and Larry Ellison recently completed the acquisition of Paramount, and media observers expect the younger Ellison to next pursue Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). At a Bloomberg event, David Ellison declined to discuss any such plans. Analysts note that a Paramount‑WBD combination has industrial logic: merging their streaming services, film and TV production assets, sports rights and back‑office functions could create a competitor to Netflix, Disney and Amazon. Antitrust hurdles might be eased by Larry Ellison’s close relationship with the Trump administration, which he cited. WBD carries a market value of about $44 billion and roughly $35 billion in debt; Larry Ellison, the world’s second‑richest person, could provide financing, and private‑equity firm Apollo is reported to be interested in joining a bid. Inside WBD, CEO David Zaslav is expected to resist a sale, similar to Jeff Bewkes’s stance in 2014, despite recent attempts to split streaming and cable assets. Industry observers say further consolidation could reduce the number of buyers for content creators.

This paper introduces an edit distance between constructible Rd-persistence modules and proves it equals the interleaving distance (Theorem 4.1). The connection is established via Galois connections and free presentations of persistence modules. This provides an order-theoretic viewpoint on interleaving distance, complementary to the combinatorial bottleneck-interleaving isometry, and enables characterization of interleaving-stable invariants in terms of edit-stable invariants (Theorems 4.2 and 4.4). The edit distance is defined on categories JSd and (1D)d of finite posets embedded in Rd, with morphisms being monotone functions with right adjoints.

Shauna Sinfield, a single mother with multiple sclerosis, had her 1998 light tan Toyota Corolla (plate BLJ 2687) stolen in Calgary. The car contained her 12‑year‑old son Caden's hockey gear, worth about four times the vehicle's value, costing $1,500‑$2,000 to replace. Police are investigating but say recovery is unlikely. The speaker notes that every playoff series has become tougher and the team needs to recognize the officials' calls, especially early. They are pleased with their systems and defensive play, aware Detroit is playing well, and plan to stick to their game plan. They enjoy the home crowd and the electricity, acknowledge streaks and bounces don’t always go their way, and emphasize staying strong defensively while supporting a teammate.

TPS7H500x-SP are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz for GaN designs. Primary outputs are turned on by an internal clock and off when sensed peak current reaches the COMP/2 voltage; the CS_ILIM pin detects primary-side current for PWM and overcurrent protection, with a 1.05 V threshold triggering hiccup mode. The hiccup mode uses a CHICC capacitor to control cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and the non-switching period before restart; a minimum of 3.3 nF is recommended. The FAULT pin provides external fault protection with a 0.6 V rising threshold and 0.4–1.4 µs pulse width filter. Slope compensation (via RSC pin) is required for duty cycles above 50% to prevent subharmonic oscillation; the recommended value is 1 × inductor falling slope. Frequency compensation (Type 2A or 2B) is applied at the COMP pin using RCOMP, CCOMP, and optional CHF. Thermal shutdown activates at 175°C (typical) and resets below 160°C. The device operates from a 4 V to 14 V supply with a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high di/dt and dv/dt switching loops, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and routing feedback and noise-sensitive traces away from switching nodes. A design example for a synchronous push-pull converter operating at 500 kHz is provided, including component selection for transformers, FETs, inductors, capacitors, current sense resistors, hiccup capacitors, compensation networks, and slope compensation resistors.

The team expressed disappointment after a tough playoff loss, citing second‑period lapses that cost them despite a strong third‑period push and solid goaltending from both sides. They said they felt comfortable playing at home, need to be consistent for a full sixty minutes, work harder to create their own bounces, and will rely on a high‑energy player while being aware of the opponent’s skilled player.

Highlights: DomTerm, a terminal emulator using a browser engine; open‑source origins from a MIT print‑jam fix; container runtimes explained; Christine Peterson's 1998 coining of “open source software” and its 20‑year milestone; and Ontario middle‑school teacher Andrew Dobbie's Tech Stewardship program keeping over 200 computers running with Linux. The article advocates for a sociocultural perspective on English language education policy in Asian countries, examining the gap between policy intentions and actual outcomes. It employs an ecological framework considering three key factors: macro-level curriculum goals and equity, English proficiency targets and national language contexts, and micro-level teacher perspectives. Case studies from Malaysia and Thailand demonstrate that CEFR-based proficiency targets remain unmet, particularly among rural and lower socioeconomic students. Communicative language teaching approaches mandated by policymakers often conflict with sociolinguistic realities where English is not used in daily life. Teachers face challenges including large classes, limited resources, and curricula misaligned with student abilities. The article concludes that educational policies frequently fail to account for contextual realities, resulting in teachers adapting mandated methods to fit classroom conditions. Effective English language education requires policymakers to align curriculum outcomes with the sociolinguistic, sociocultural, and educational capacities of their specific contexts.

The study develops an exponential‑clock model of Plasmodium vivax relapse in which each hypnozoite activates independently with a constant rate (η). The model is fitted to the daily‑surveillance data from the 1993–1995 SPf66 vaccine trial, which enrolled 1,344 children aged 2–15 years on the Thailand‑Myanmar border and followed them for 21 months. Fitted parameter estimates include a hypnozoite activation rate of 1/171 day⁻¹ (half‑life ≈118 days), an average sporozoite inoculum of 6.9 per bite (generating on average 2.7 hypnozoites), and a ratio of relapsing to primary infections per bite of 3.4, indicating that roughly 75 % of observed symptomatic vivax episodes were relapses. The model incorporates post‑treatment prophylaxis (chloroquine ≈15 days, mefloquine ≈35 days) and age‑dependent anti‑disease immunity, reproducing the non‑linear rise and subsequent fall in symptomatic vivax incidence with age and accommodating up to 13 recurrent vivax episodes per child. The analysis supports an intrinsic exponential activation mechanism while noting higher‑than‑expected vivax after P. falciparum monoinfections, consistent with possible external triggering.

Researchers isolated bacteria from grape leaf surfaces (phyllosphere) that degrade guaiacol, a volatile phenol responsible for smoke‑taint in wine after wildfires. In laboratory tests, two strains reduced guaiacol to near‑undetectable levels after 96 hours; the gene enabling this degradation was identified, and deleting it prevented guaiacol consumption. The microbial approach could selectively remove smoky compounds without stripping colour or other desirable traits, unlike activated‑charcoal filtration, which also removes valuable components. The wine industry lost over $3 billion in California and Oregon in 2020, underscoring the need for tools to manage smoke taint. Further work is required to find microbes that degrade other smoke‑related phenols.

The department has shifted toward treatment and group therapy rather than discipline. The Education Department’s first round of talks on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ended Friday with cautious optimism and no consensus on the core issue: which postbaccalaureate programs count as professional for higher federal loan caps (up to $200,000 versus $100,000 for graduate programs). The department initially proposed limiting the definition to the 10 programs listed in the Higher Education Act, then offered a one‑year expansion (July 2026–June 2027) allowing any program that a college had designated professional before July 4 2025 to meet the three‑part standard. Committee members questioned the clarity, legal standing, and impact on health‑care and master’s‑level programs; no agreement was reached. A second round of negotiations is scheduled for Nov. 3–7. Transparency suffered because the government shutdown prevented posting of meeting materials, forcing members to share information directly. The July 1 2026 effective date heightens pressure to reach a timely resolution, especially for the transition of existing borrowers to remaining income‑driven repayment plans and the new Repayment Assistance plan.

Study of 451,355 UK Biobank participants examined cardiovascular (CV) biomarkers and outcomes across ethnicity‑adjusted BMI categories (normal, overweight, obese) stratified by diabetes mellitus (DM) status. In the 5% with DM, 10% were normal weight, 34% overweight, 55% obese; in the non‑DM group 34% were normal, 43% overweight, 23% obese. Overweight/obesity was associated with higher carotid intima‑media thickness, arterial stiffness and cardiac contractility index, and lower left‑ventricular ejection fraction in non‑DM participants, with weaker relationships in DM. Within each BMI class, DM was linked to an adverse CV phenotype, most marked in normal‑weight DM. Over 5.3 million person‑years (median 12 years), incident myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke and CV mortality rose across BMI categories in both groups. Normal‑weight DM had higher CV mortality risk than obese non‑DM (adjusted IRR 2.81 vs 1.84). Both obesity and DM independently contributed to adverse CV biomarkers and outcomes, with adiposity measures showing stronger (though modest) correlations than diabetes‑oriented metrics.

Defendant Yuk Bui Yee moved to sever 13 counts of extortion-related offenses from six incidents at three Chinese restaurants, arguing joinder should be under CPL 200.20(2)(c) rather than (b), which would allow severance. The court analyzes joinder rules, tracing CPL 200.20's evolution from the Code of Criminal Procedure section 279, including adoption of the "Molineux rule." The offenses are grouped: Group A (December incidents at one restaurant, nine counts), Group B (January incident at another, two counts), and Group C (February incidents at a third, two counts). The People justify joinder under Molineux exceptions: common scheme, identity, and intent. The court finds common scheme exists within Groups A and C but not across all groups; identity is supported by modus operandi (Mandarin demands for "brothers," claiming "Eagles" membership) despite potential alibi for Group B; and intent is admissible because demands were not unequivocal. The court holds all offenses are properly joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b) and denies the motion to sever.

Team must be patient, get puck deep, limit opponent speed in neutral zone, and find ways to get pucks through shot blocks and lanes; acknowledges opponent's defensive collapse, emphasizes execution, admits poor performance in front of goalie and expresses frustration.

This study investigates the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between arterial stiffness (measured by baPWV) and kidney function (measured by eGFR) in 67,060 adults from China. Results show a bidirectional relationship: higher baPWV predicts increased CKD risk, and lower eGFR predicts higher arterial stiffness risk. Cross-lagged panel analysis indicates that kidney function decline (lower eGFR) precedes arterial stiffness increase (higher baPWV). The study concludes that arterial stiffness is associated with CKD, and the temporal sequence suggests that eGFR decrease may drive baPWV increase.

Lower‑limb amputation affects millions and increases fall risk due to loss of somatosensory feedback. Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) can evoke sensations in the missing limb and improve balance and gait. This case study examined a 60–65‑year‑old woman with a unilateral transtibial amputation who received three 8‑contact epidural SCS leads at T12–L2 for 84 days. Stimulation was triggered by plantar pressure during the prosthetic stance phase. Surface EMG and motion capture recorded muscle activity and kinematics over time. After multiple weeks of in‑lab SCS use, the residual tensor fasciae latae (TFL) muscle became markedly more active (≈94% increase vs early no‑stimulation). Co‑contraction of the residual vastus lateralis and biceps femoris decreased significantly (from 1.57 to ≈0.95–1.05). Pelvic obliquity range‑of‑motion increased and residual‑limb pelvic drop rose toward values of the intact limb. These changes indicate improved knee and hip stability during walking and reduced compensatory muscle strategies. The findings suggest long‑term SCS‑mediated sensory feedback can modulate muscle activation and produce functional gait improvements, though data are limited to one participant.

Bear Grylls has criticized schools for not adequately preparing children for adult life, saying they need to "empower" young people more. This preprint introduces SCIseg, a deep‑learning model for automatic segmentation of the spinal cord (SC) and T2‑weighted hyperintense lesions in spinal cord injury (SCI) patients. The model uses a region‑based training strategy with nnUNet and a three‑phase training protocol that includes active learning to expand the training dataset. The study retrospectively analyzed 191 patients with 231 MRI scans from three sites, encompassing traumatic and ischemic etiologies, pre‑ and post‑operative scans, and heterogeneous imaging parameters (different manufacturers, field strengths 1–3 T, varying voxel sizes and orientations). After training on 196 scans, SCIseg achieved SC segmentation Dice scores of 0.92 (average) and lesion segmentation Dice scores of 0.60 (average), with higher performance on site 2 than site 1. The model performed significantly better than 2D SCIseg and comparable or superior to existing Spinal Cord Toolbox methods (sct_propseg, sct_deepseg_sc, contrast‑agnostic). Active learning improved lesion volume and length estimates, showing higher agreement with manual ground truth. Correlations between automatically derived MRI biomarkers (lesion volume, intramedullary lesion length, maximal axial damage ratio) and clinical scores (pinprick, light‑touch, lower‑extremity motor) were not significantly different from those obtained with manual segmentations. SCIseg also produced reasonable segmentations for non‑traumatic SCI, specifically degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM). The method is open‑source and available via the Spinal Cord Toolbox and a GitHub repository, enabling reproducible multi‑site studies.

SEC Form 8-K filed July 25, 2019 by Amazon.com, Inc. announcing the company's second quarter 2019 financial results. The filing includes a press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as exhibits.

Athlete Unlimited (AU) is a network of professional women’s sports leagues founded in 2020 by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros that operates in softball, volleyball, lacrosse and basketball. Its model eliminates owners, places players in charge through Player Executive Committees, uses a weekly draft to reshape teams, and ranks individuals on a leaderboard that awards points for performance. Seasons are five weeks long and all games are held at a single venue, with players deciding schedule, uniforms, venues and social‑impact initiatives such as the Power in My Voice program. Legally organized as a public benefit corporation, AU caps investor returns under a Mission Equity structure and directs at least half of any surplus beyond the cap to a long‑term player profit‑participation plan; players also receive base compensation and performance bonuses. AU secured broadcast deals with ESPN, CBS, Fox and others, raised $30 million in 2022 and was named one of the ten most innovative sports companies in 2023. Research indicated fans value player stories and organizational values, and surveys show high engagement through broadcasts and strong approval of AU’s uniqueness and athlete empowerment. Despite expanding to more than 200 athletes across four sports, AU faces challenges around scaling, economic sustainability and maintaining its player‑driven mission while growing.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for allocating random access resources in a multiple basic service set identifier (BSSID) wireless network. An access point associated with a transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) allocates random resource units (RUs) using association identifier (AID) values based on a group AID mapping contained in a partial virtual bitmap of a traffic indication map (TIM) element. The access point transmits a trigger frame containing AID values to stations belonging to the multiple BSSID set. AID value zero allocates random RUs to stations associated with the Tx BSSID, AID value 2045 allocates random RUs to all unassociated stations, and AID values set to BSSID indices allocate random RUs to stations associated with corresponding non-transmitted BSSIDs (non-Tx BSSIDs). The trigger frame enables prioritized allocation of random RUs to selected BSSs based on factors including the number of stations, traffic types, and quality of service parameters.

The speaker, at an Amherst College ceremony honoring Robert Frost, emphasizes that graduates of elite institutions bear a responsibility to serve the public interest due to the advantages society provides them. He cites statistics showing private colleges draw half their students from the wealthiest 10% of Americans, while high school dropouts comprise a disproportionate share of the unemployed, and the lowest fifth of families hold only 4.5% of national income. Honoring Frost as both an artist and American, the speaker argues that artists provide essential truth and moral guidance by questioning power, resisting propaganda, and preserving individual conscience. He expresses hope for an America that balances military and economic strength with wisdom, protects cultural and natural heritage, and values artistic achievement, concluding that Frost's life and this college's mission have strengthened the nation's foundations.

Look Good… Feel Better offers free skincare, makeup, and hair‑loss support for women in cancer treatment; sessions at Dignity Health Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital on May 8; register at 1‑800‑227‑2345.

The CAT offense is a simple, effective system for defeating traps, double‑teams and zone presses. It begins in a 2‑1‑2 spread with a skilled, triple‑threat post as the central hub and emphasizes sharp, accurate passing. Basic rules: when the ball goes to the middle, baseline players back‑cut to the basket; when the ball reaches a corner, the post rolls to the basket (or pivots and back‑cuts if denied) and returns to the high post if the pass isn’t received. A post‑interchange can occur on a roll— if a corner does not feed the post, the post clears to the opposite corner and the other wing fills the middle. The “opposite‑corner rule” directs a skip pass to the far corner whenever a player is trapped or hard‑double‑teamed. Dribble penetration is used sparingly as a “drive‑and‑kick,” keeping the ball and clock moving, avoiding fouls, and—if the defense stops double‑teaming—holding the ball or transitioning into a penetrating spread offense.

Tight ends line up next to the offensive line and perform both blocking and receiving duties. They run short‑to‑medium routes against linebackers, exploit size in the red zone, and block defensive linemen and linebackers in the run and pass game. Their name originates from early football when players on the line’s end were called “Ends”; those staying tighter to the formation became “tight ends.” The position requires strong hands, athleticism, speed, blocking ability, route‑running, and physicality, with typical dimensions of 6’3″–6’8″ and 240–270 lb. Versatile tight ends let offenses vary schemes and create mismatches, making them a key weapon, as they present the biggest matchup problem for opposing defenses. Notable TEs include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe, each with records or multiple Super Bowl titles. The abbreviation TE and the term H‑back (a tight end lining up behind the line) are common synonyms.

Guangdong Province is experiencing China’s largest chikungunya outbreak, with over 4,000 confirmed cases since late July, concentrated in Shunde District (over 3,600 cases) and spreading to Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Macao. The disease is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, causing fever, intense joint pain and rash; it does not spread person‑to‑person. Authorities are urging residents to eliminate standing water to reduce mosquito breeding, while climate change, urbanization and travel are driving the spread. The World Health Organization has issued new clinical guidelines and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative to improve surveillance. Chikungunya, first identified in Tanzania in the 1950s, now occurs in over 110 countries, rarely fatal but can cause long‑term joint pain. There is no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral; treatment focuses on symptom relief. Aedes mosquitoes, which also transmit dengue and Zika, thrive in stagnant water and are expanding their range with warmer temperatures, prompting public health strategies emphasizing community participation, repellents and protective clothing.

On World No Tobacco Day, CTC‑Pak called for health over business, noting tobacco contributes 16% of non‑communicable disease deaths and cardiovascular disease accounts for 19% of total deaths in Pakistan. Tobacco kills over seven million people yearly, causing 108,800 deaths in Pakistan and costing $1.4 trillion annually. CTC‑Pak urged enforcement of tobacco control laws, implementation of 85% pictorial health warnings on cigarette packs, and higher tobacco taxes, noting recent compromises have made cigarettes cheaper and increased youth consumption. Pakistan ratified the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in 2004 but still needs stronger policies. CTC‑Pak comprises over 250 civil‑society partners across Pakistan’s provinces.

The authors implemented a minorization‑maximization (MM) algorithm in Julia for variance components linear mixed models, handling phenotypes. Applied to PsychENCODE, it partitions genetic variance and covariance between cis‑ and trans‑SNPs: cis‑SNPs have sparse strong effects, trans‑SNPs weak individually, strong collectively. Isoform‑level analyses reveal more genetic signals than gene‑level analyses, including autism, suggesting isoform resolution aids disease‑gene discovery and GWAS interpretation.

Texas Longhorns sports update covering football recruiting (major visit weekend Dec 15-17, list of remaining targets including DT Tommie Harris and LB Derrick Johnson, and 19 early commitments), bowl prospects (likely Cotton, Holiday, or Alamo if Texas beats Texas A&M), and women's basketball advancing to the Preseason WNIT semifinals after defeating Tulane and Wichita State. The authors introduce SoDaDE (Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings), a new data-driven fingerprint for solvents developed using a transformer model trained on the Spange dataset of 191 solvents with 12 molecular properties. They employ data augmentation by randomly shuffling property-value pairs (up to 12! combinations per solvent) and mask token training. The model combines word tokens, ChemBERTa fingerprints, and scalar values through projected embeddings, using causal, prediction, and attention masks. SoDaDE achieved a validation MSE of 0.107 and outperformed Gaussian process and Random Forest baselines on solvent property prediction. On the Catechol Benchmark for predicting reaction yields, SoDaDE achieved the lowest MSE (0.0026-0.0029 for full data, 0.0044 for single solvent) compared to previous methods including DRFPs, Fragprints, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa fingerprints. The results demonstrate that effective molecular fingerprints can be created from small datasets when trained on task-relevant properties.

Discrete-time linear shift invariant systems are represented by the convolution sum. Two key properties are stability (bounded input yields bounded output, equivalent to absolutely summable unit sample response) and causality (output depends only on current and past inputs, equivalent to unit sample response zero for n<0). These systems can also be represented by linear constant coefficient difference equations, whose solutions depend on boundary conditions and may yield causal or non-causal systems. An alternative representation is the frequency response, derived from the unit sample response, which is periodic with period 2π and shows that complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of such systems. The Fourier transform generalizes this concept.

GameStop will ship at least five Nintendo Switch consoles to its over 4,400 stores on Aug 15, available by Aug 16 – all stores have stock. Supplies are in‑store only; online sales are bundles shipping in September. Switches also appear at Target and via product‑tracking services.

Plasma radiation is self-emission used for diagnostics, spanning radio to gamma rays. Radiation transport involves emission, absorption, and non-local processes; the transport equation is dI/ds = j - αI, with optical depth τ = ∫α ds. Solutions yield optically thin (radiation streams through) and thick (radiation absorbed) regimes; Kirchhoff's law relates emissivity and opacity. Radiation arises from accelerated charges; the far field propagates as 1/r^2 with constant total power, while the near field decays as 1/r^4.

The speaker said his team’s transition game was solid in the first period, but a neutral‑zone mistake let in a goal and the team appeared to play on its heels after a second goal, losing north‑south flow. He expressed confidence about playing for the Stanley Cup with home‑ice advantage and emphasized his team’s effort despite limited results. He credited the opponent’s goaltender as one of the league’s best and said his team needs to get more pucks and bodies to the net. MMFP‑Tableau is a data‑integration and visualization platform developed by the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program (MMFP) at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. It extracts, cleans, and integrates clinical data from the EPIC electronic medical record (EMR), research data from REDCap databases, and spreadsheet‑based records into a centralized server managed by a dedicated analyst. The platform uses Alteryx (version 2021.4.2.47844) for extract‑transform‑load workflows, automated scheduling, and machine‑learning analytics, and Tableau (version 20222.23) for secure, role‑based interactive dashboards. Integrated data include demographics, diagnoses (ICD‑10/SNOMED), laboratory results, medications, imaging, patient‑reported outcomes, and biological sample information, with phenotype terms harmonized to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) codes. MMFP‑Tableau provides real‑time, user‑customizable views at both individual‑patient and cohort levels, supporting tasks such as clinical cohort characterization, clinical‑trial eligibility screening, genotype‑phenotype mapping, medication‑trend analysis, and risk‑factor delineation. The system is housed behind an institutional firewall, enables authorized clinicians and researchers to query live data without needing advanced informatics expertise, and has improved EMR documentation practices. Current limitations include inaccessible non‑discretized EMR text, some imaging data, scanned PDFs, and external institution data; ongoing work aims to expand data types, increase computational efficiency, and enable predictive diagnostics. The platform demonstrates a scalable, generalizable paradigm for linking siloed health‑system data to advance precision medicine in rare diseases such as primary mitochondrial disease.

Ninth‑generation NVENC in Blackwell raises AV1/HEVC quality by ~5 % BD‑BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encode support, and introduces an AV1 Ultra‑High‑Quality mode that provides an additional ~5 % gain. RTX 5090 includes three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds >50 % over the previous generation and 4× versus RTX 3090. The passage explains the head‑and‑shoulders (H&S) chart pattern and its inverse. A standard H&S forms during an uptrend with three price‑swing highs (left shoulder, head, right shoulder) and two intervening swing lows; the line connecting the lows is the neckline. When price falls below the neckline it signals a bearish reversal and the start of a downtrend. Traders may close long positions or open short positions; some enter when the right shoulder appears if a bearish candlestick pattern is present, placing a stop‑loss just above the right shoulder.

The inverse (or bottom) H&S forms in a downtrend with three swing lows and two intervening swing highs; the neckline is a resistance line. A break above the neckline indicates a bullish reversal, and traders may buy or cover shorts. Stop‑loss can be placed below the right shoulder or at the neckline; a break higher should occur on high volume.

Backtesting the pattern is difficult, so the site uses Thomas Bulkowski’s 1990s study of 500 stocks over five years (≈2,500 stock‑years) containing over 15,000 formations. For H&S, Bulkowski reported a 93 % win rate (30 false signals out of 431), an average price drop of about 23 % after the break, and noted that volume and neckline slope do not affect reliability. For the inverse H&S, the data show few false signals, a typical gain of 20‑30 % within 73 days, and a stop‑loss below the right shoulder; the neckline direction and volume do not matter, but a breakout on high volume is preferred.

A 1995 Federal Reserve article confirmed that technical analysis, including the H&S strategy, can generate statistically significant profits. The authors caution that Bulkowski’s results are after‑the‑fact, so the pattern should be used cautiously, and they advise strict risk management when applying any technical‑analysis strategy.

The passage outlines two defensive strategies used against the Base Cross offense. The All Out SOS Disruption method employs a sideline trap on the ball handler before entry, a hi‑lo switch when the cutter goes low, post‑trap rotations, and near‑player rotations after the pass out, with weakside defenders assuming helpside triangle positions to deny reversal passes. Both strategies rely on coordinated pressure, switching and help defence to disrupt the Base Cross offense.

This paper introduces automatic detection of "hype" language in biomedical research texts, defined as hyperbolic or subjective language used to promote or embellish research. The authors developed formal annotation guidelines with six criteria (value-judgment, hyperbolic, gratuitous, amplified, coordinated, broader context) to classify 11 novelty adjectives (groundbreaking, innovative, novel, etc.) as Hype or Not Hype in 537 sentences from NIH grant abstracts. Experiments compared traditional classifiers (SVM, Naive Bayes), finetuned language models (BERT, BioMedBERT, GPT-2), and large language models (LLAMA, GPT-4) against a human baseline. Finetuned BERT achieved 86.1% accuracy, outperforming the human baseline (82.4%), while traditional methods performed worst. The study concludes that formal annotation guidelines improve consistency, and language models can achieve promising results for hype detection, though the task requires domain knowledge and temporal awareness of facts.

The article explores why offering career advice to adult children is hard and presents guidance from expert Ruth Nemzoff. Three core principles are recommended: parents should know themselves (recognize how their own experiences bias advice), know their child (adapt style to each child and consider current life circumstances), and know the environment (account for economic conditions and workplace norms). To set a positive tone, Nemzoff suggests asking whether advice is desired, opening with curious questions, acknowledging what you don’t know, and sharing personal career mistakes. Practical tips include helping children focus on the next step, suggesting they consult a neutral third party, and avoiding expectations that they will follow the advice.

The passage describes a theoretical-computational study examining how chlorothalonil (CLT), a toxic fungicide and human carcinogen, interacts with single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) of varying chiralities (8,0), (10,0) and (12,0) using DFT calculations and molecular dynamics simulations. The study finds that CLT adsorbs onto both nanotubes through moderate physical adsorption, with the molecule's aromatic ring parallel to the nanotube surface. While CNTs exhibit higher adsorption energies that increase with tube radius due to enhanced π-π stacking, their band gap and work function remain nearly unchanged upon adsorption, making them unsuitable for electronic sensing applications. In contrast, BNNTs show significant band gap reduction and work function changes, providing high electronic sensitivity and short recovery times suitable for reversible sensing. Both nanotubes remain stable in aqueous solution and can remove CLT from contaminated environments, but only BNNTs are recommended for detection purposes due to their superior electronic response. The interaction strength increases with nanotube radius for both systems, governed by improved π-π stacking on less curved surfaces and the polarizability of the nanotube material.

Pneumonia and tuberculosis remain major global health burdens, especially in low‑resource settings; pneumonia accounts for 14 % of deaths in children under five and TB caused 1.25 million deaths in 2022. Misdiagnosis between the diseases is common, leading to treatment delays and high mortality. Recent AI and deep learning methods, including CNNs and Vision Transformers, have achieved high accuracy in classifying chest X‑ray images into normal, pneumonia, or TB categories, often exceeding human performance. However, existing models rely on limited, imbalanced datasets, suffer from high computational demands, and lack the ability to detect non‑X‑ray or anomalous cases. This study proposes a multi‑class classification framework that categorizes chest X‑rays into four classes (normal, pneumonia, TB, and non‑X‑ray) to improve robustness and reliability. Data were compiled from multiple public sources, anonymized, and used in compliance with ethical guidelines, with no external funding.

Hounds of the Bay is a dividend‑based stock‑picking strategy applied to the S&P/TSX 60, named after Bay Street. It selects the highest‑dividend‑yielding large‑cap Canadian stocks, often including commodities and energy because of the index’s composition. The strategy assumes blue‑chip companies keep dividends stable, so a high yield signals the firm is near a business‑cycle low, which may lead to faster price appreciation. Backtests are scarce, but academic research indicates it performed similarly to Dogs of the Dow, with its effectiveness diminishing over recent decades. The approach underperformed in 2014 when a sharp oil price decline hurt results.

The smash concept is a versatile pass concept used across all football levels, from youth to NFL. It creates big plays while allowing quarterbacks to release the ball quickly and works effectively against man coverage, Cover 2, and Cover 4. Against man coverage, corner routes exploit space after CBs commit to hitch routes. Against Cover 2, corner routes operate in voids left by safeties. Against Cover 4, QBs can high-low CBs using hitch and corner routes. However, Cover 3 poses challenges as OLB flat defenders can undercut hitch routes if thrown late. Coaching points specify routes for TEs, TBs, slot receivers, and X/Z receivers. QBs read one side pre-snap and high-low the CB by throwing the hitch if the corner deepens or the corner route if the corner plays low. Variations exist for 3x1 sets with answers for different coverages, and for pocket movement using sprint-out designs with the QB reading the corner and the backside TE as a third option.

The ISM Manufacturing Index (also called the Purchasing Managers’ Index, PMI) is a monthly indicator of the U.S. manufacturing sector’s health. It is based on a survey of purchasing managers at over 300 manufacturing firms that evaluates production, new orders, employment, supplier deliveries and inventories. Each factor is seasonally adjusted and given equal weighting in the composite index. The index is calculated with the formula PMI = (P1 × 1) + (P2 × 0.5) + (P3 × 0), where P1, P2 and P3 are the percentages of respondents reporting improvement, no change and deterioration, respectively. The PMI is released on the first business day of each month and reports data for the prior month.

A reading above 50 indicates the manufacturing sector is expanding; a reading below 50 indicates contraction; 50 means no change. The PMI is widely watched by investors, traders, businesses and policymakers because it provides insight into the direction of the economy and can move financial markets.

The PMI can be used together with other economic indicators—such as GDP, employment data, consumer confidence indices and inflation rates—to obtain a comprehensive picture of economic conditions. Weighting of the PMI’s components is equal, and seasonal adjustments remove regular patterns caused by weather, holidays and other factors.

The PMI is a backward‑looking indicator, reflecting past activity, but because purchasing managers often see changes first it can give an early signal of economic direction. Backtesting shows that a simple strategy of buying when the PMI is above 50 and selling when below yields modest results: about 7.3% annual return versus 8.5% for the S&P 500, with exposure 72% of the time. Holding S&P 500 for 12 months after an above‑50 reading produced an average gain of 10.99% with 86% exposure. Low PMI readings do not reliably produce contrarian moves, and gold is the only asset that performs better following low PMI readings.

The PMI is considered a reliable indicator, but it is not a perfect predictor of future conditions; markets quickly price in released data, limiting short‑term predictive value. Consequently, it is best used in combination with other data and market analysis when making investment or business decisions.

The passage introduces SQuID (Survey and Questionnaire Item Embeddings Differentials), a method using LLMs to create semantic embeddings of psychometric questionnaire items as alternatives to costly human raters. The core technique subtracts the average questionnaire embedding from individual item embeddings to extract negative correlations that are otherwise absent in raw embeddings. Tested on the PVQ-RR (value orientations questionnaire), the best model (Linq-Embed-Mistral) achieved internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) comparable to or exceeding human data across 19 value dimensions. Dimension correlations between embeddings and human data reached 0.74, and MDS configurations recovered the theoretical circular structure of values. Procrustes comparison showed high congruence coefficients (0.88, 0.82) between embedding-derived and human-derived configurations. The method requires no domain-specific finetuning and works with various models. The authors propose this as a complement to traditional psychometrics, enabling cheaper, scalable analysis while opening research directions such as investigating cultural biases in LLMs and extending measurement to diverse languages.

The paper describes a team’s participation in the 2023 SMM4H shared tasks, focusing on Task‑1 (COVID‑19 self‑reported diagnosis detection) and Task‑4 (social‑anxiety disorder classification). Both tasks are binary classification problems. Task‑1 data comprises 7,600 training, 400 validation and 10,000 test tweets; Task‑4 data consists of 6,090 training, 680 validation and 1,347 test posts from the subreddit r/socialanxiety. Preprocessing removed non‑alphabetic characters, tags, emojis, URLs, stopwords and punctuation. Three models were evaluated: RoBERTa for sequence classification, a fine‑tuned BERT model (digitalepidemiologylab/covid‑twitter‑bert‑v2), and a hybrid BERT + LightGBM approach. The hybrid method fine‑tuned BERT, extracted hidden [CLS] tokens from the last three layers, fed them to LightGBM and optimized hyperparameters with Optuna. Results show BERT + LightGBM achieved F1 = 0.93 on the validation set and 0.94 on the test set for Task‑1, outperforming the other methods. The same architecture applied to Task‑4 yielded an F1 = 0.80 on the test set. The authors conclude that combining BERT’s language representations with LightGBM’s gradient‑boosting optimization provides effective health‑related binary classification.

A100 GPU architecture introduces fine‑grained structured sparsity with a 2‑out‑of‑4 non‑zero pattern, compressing weights for a 2× reduction in data footprint and bandwidth, and enabling the Sparse Tensor Core to double math throughput by skipping zero entries. The accompanying training recipe (dense training followed by pruning and fine‑tuning) preserves accuracy across vision, detection, segmentation, language and translation models.  

The A100 includes a combined L1 data cache and shared memory (192 KB per SM) providing low‑latency, high‑bandwidth access, and separate FP32 and INT32 execution units that run simultaneously. The device houses 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth (1.7× V100) with SECDED ECC protection for the DRAM, L2 cache and SM registers.  

The 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7× larger than V100, divided into 40 slices and two partitions for higher bandwidth and lower latency, providing 2.3× L2 read bandwidth. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth, L2 bandwidth and L2 capacity by up to 4×.  

Third‑generation Tensor Cores run on 108 SMs, supporting larger matrix operations and delivering 16× peak mixed‑precision performance versus standard FP32 FMA. Warp‑wide data sharing expands to 32 threads, the k‑dimension grows up to 4×, and the core issues 8× fewer instructions with 2.9× fewer register accesses, improving compute efficiency.  

A new asynchronous copy instruction transfers data directly from global memory to shared memory without passing through L1 or the register file, and asynchronous barriers allow fine‑grained synchronization of any thread subset. L2 cache residency controls let programmers reserve up to 1/16th of L2 (≈2.5 MB) for persisting data, reducing DRAM traffic for recurrent weights and other reuse patterns.  

The Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) feature partitions a single A100 into up to seven independent GPU Instances, each with dedicated GPCs, L2 slice groups, memory controllers and frame‑buffer memory, providing QoS, fault isolation and consistent performance. Compute Instances inside a GPU Instance enable concurrent contexts and support Volta‑style MPS.  

Third‑generation NVLink provides 50 Gbit/s per signal pair, 12 links per GPU for a total bidirectional bandwidth of 600 GB/s (2× V100), while PCIe Gen 4 with SR‑IOV offers 31.5 GB/s per direction. Error detection and fault isolation include link‑level CRC, packet replay and page‑fault propagation over NVLink.  

Additional hardware accelerators include a five‑core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an Optical Flow accelerator for dense optical flow and stereo disparity, improved FP16 (11×) and FP32 (2.7×) atomic throughput, and five NVDEC video decoders.  

CUDA 11 exposes task graphs for define‑once/run‑repeated workloads, asynchronous copy and barriers, L2 residency controls, and cooperative groups for collective memory operations and hardware‑accelerated warp‑reductions.  

The DGX A100 system houses eight A100 GPUs interconnected via six NVSwitches delivering 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional bandwidth, providing up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. MIG can create up to 56 isolated GPU instances per DGX, and the NGC Private Registry supplies optimized containers for deep learning, HPC and analytics workloads.  

The A100 architecture also supports a sparse neural‑network primer that explains fine‑grained and coarse‑grained sparsity; fine‑grained structured sparsity on A100 yields virtually no accuracy loss when using 2:4 pruning across classification, detection, segmentation and language tasks.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU implements the Ampere architecture with third‑generation Tensor Cores that support a wide range of data types: IEEE FP16, BF16, the new TF32 (8‑bit exponent, 10‑bit mantissa), FP64, INT8, INT4 and binary. A single A100 SM contains four Tensor Cores delivering 1024 FP16 FMA per clock (2048 FP16 ops) and a full A100 chip with 108 SMs provides up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed‑precision FP16/FP32 performance – 2.5× the mixed‑precision and 20× the standard FP32 throughput of the Tesla V100. TF32 gives the range of FP32 with the precision of FP16, enabling AI training on Tensor Cores by default, while FP16 or BF16 mixed‑precision training can reach up to 2× the TF32 throughput.  

A100 introduces fine‑grained structured sparsity with a 2‑out‑of‑4 non‑zero pattern that doubles Tensor Core throughput for inference and can be applied to training with a universal pruning‑and‑fine‑tuning recipe that retains accuracy.  

Memory hierarchy includes 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM (1555 GB/s bandwidth), a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7× larger and 2.3× higher bandwidth than V100), and a 192 KB combined L1 cache/shared memory per SM, all protected by SECDED ECC.  

Multi‑Instance GPU (MIG) can partition each A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, L2 slices, memory controllers and DRAM bandwidth, providing QoS for multi‑tenant workloads.  

Third‑generation NVLink offers 12 links delivering 600 GB/s total bandwidth (versus 300 GB/s on V100) and PCIe Gen 4 with SR‑IOV enhances connectivity.  

New CUDA 11 features include asynchronous copy to shared memory, hardware‑accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, cooperative groups, and task‑graph optimizations that reduce launch overhead and latency.  

The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches (4.8 TB/s bidirectional bandwidth) to achieve 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, scalable to tens of thousands of GPUs and configurable into up to 56 isolated MIG instances, all supported by CUDA‑optimized containers, deep‑learning frameworks, HPC libraries, and the NGC software stack.

Two near‑miss attempts to appoint a U.S. Labor Secretary occurred during the Trump administration. Andrew Puzder, CEO of Hardee’s and Carl’s Jr., was nominated but withdrew after Senate Republicans opposed his candidacy, citing his hiring of an undocumented housekeeper, domestic‑violence allegations and his opposition to raising the federal minimum wage. Puzder’s restaurants had been fined for thousands of labor‑law violations, primarily for failing to pay minimum‑wage or overtime, and he advocated replacing workers with automation. When Puzder’s nomination collapsed, the White House considered Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker as a replacement. Walker had previously curbed public‑employee collective bargaining, signed a right‑to‑work law, cut state education funding and linked his anti‑union policies to fighting terrorism. Walker publicly declined, stating on Twitter that his future was in continuing as governor.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end and precision reference. It features an internal 4.096V reference with optional external reference mode, programmable input ranges supporting bipolar and unipolar signals, and alarm functions for input over/undervoltage and AVDD monitoring. The device operates via multiSPI interface with RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, supports daisy-chain topology, and offers SPI-compatible and source-synchronous protocols for data transfer. Nine configuration registers control device operation including reset, power modes (NAP/power-down), alarm thresholds, and data output formatting. The device targets industrial analog input modules requiring up to ±10V input ranges with fast settling time and overvoltage protection.

The Rate of Change (ROC) is a momentum‑based technical indicator that measures the percentage change between the current price of a security and its price a selected number of periods (n) earlier. It is plotted as an oscillator moving above and below a zero line; positive values indicate rising momentum and negative values indicate falling momentum. Traders use ROC to detect overbought/oversold levels, identify centerline crossovers and divergences, and anticipate potential price reversals. The indicator is most effective in trending markets and can be applied to any market with price data, but it tends to generate whipsaws in volatile or sideways conditions. The choice of n affects sensitivity—smaller n yields a more volatile indicator and more signals, while larger n produces fewer, later signals. ROC can be combined with trend‑following tools such as moving averages to improve reliability. Compared with the RSI, ROC directly measures price change, whereas RSI uses the ratio of up‑ to down‑periods. Backtesting of several ROC strategies (oversold mean‑reversion, breakout, zero‑line crossing) on the S&P 500 showed performance inferior to RSI, Stochastic, and Williams %R. The indicator does not set stop‑loss or position size directly, but it can inform a trading system and risk‑management decisions when backtested.

A couple flying to Costa Rica for their wedding was removed from a United Airlines flight after sitting in Economy Plus seats they hadn't paid for. The lecture covers the SLIP (Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum) model for running dynamics. This model, consisting of a mass with a massless leg containing an ideal spring, serves as a simplified template for running behavior. Comparative biomechanics demonstrates that despite vast differences in mass (five orders of magnitude) and kinematics across animals like cockroaches, horses, and crabs, they exhibit dynamic similarity when analyzed through the SLIP framework using dimensionless quantities like the ratio of kinetic to potential energy. The system is completely conservative with perfectly elastic collisions and no energy loss during flight or stance phases. The state space can be reduced to a one-dimensional map using apex height as the state variable, since other parameters can be derived from energy conservation and the touchdown angle assumption. Surprisingly, this conservative system achieves stability through coordinate switching (piecewise holonomic systems), possessing both stable and unstable fixed points. Extensions include adding toe mass to create dissipative collisions, allowing control through spring constant variation. The concept of "preflex" describes how springy tendons in animals provide faster-than-neural responses to perturbations, as demonstrated in cockroach experiments using cannon impacts. Raibert's hoppers from the 1980s-90s illustrated these principles through robots capable of running, jumping, and performing acrobatic maneuvers. Recent work on SLIP walkers explores how robots can transition between walking and running behaviors by varying spring constants.

SARS‑CoV‑2 seroprevalence was measured in pregnant women attending first antenatal care (ANC) visits in four Zambian districts (Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, Lusaka) from September 2021 to September 2022. Using a multiplex bead assay targeting nucleocapsid and spike (RBD) proteins, 8 304 valid samples were obtained from 9 221 enrolled women. Overall adjusted seroprevalence was 63.8 %, rising to near‑100 % in Lusaka, Chipata and Chongwe by August‑September 2022, while Chadiza peaked at 77.2 % in April 2022 and declined to 56.6 % by July 2022. Vaccination coverage increased from 4.4 % to 26.6 % over the period, but most antibodies were infection‑induced (77.7 %); hybrid infection‑plus‑vaccination responses grew over time. Seropositivity was associated with COVID‑19 vaccination, older age in Chipata, higher education in Chadiza and Chongwe, and occupation in most districts. The ratio of seroprevalence to reported cumulative incidence ranged from 29:1 (Lusaka) to 92:1 (Chongwe). Strengths included a 13‑month window covering Delta and Omicron waves, use of a multi‑target assay distinguishing infection from vaccination, and integration into routine ANC services. Limitations comprised non‑systematic district selection, cross‑sectional design, possible underestimation from waning antibodies, and early termination of surveillance in Chadiza. The authors conclude that most pregnant women in these districts have been exposed to SARS‑CoV‑2, ANC platforms can be used for ongoing COVID‑19 surveillance, and subnational strategies may better target prevention efforts.

Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) has a poor 5-year survival rate of approximately 14%, highlighting the need for improved biomarkers. Genomic diversity in tumors is associated with more aggressive disease and poorer outcomes. Liquid biopsies offer a minimally invasive method to analyze tumoral genomic diversity through circulating tumor cells (CTCs), which can provide intact cells for whole-genome profiling and are considered precursors of metastasis. While CTC enumeration is a validated prognostic marker in CRC, CTC populations can exhibit significant genomic variation within patients. This study evaluated the clinical relevance of CTC genomic variation in 29 mCRC patients using whole-exome sequencing of CTC pools. The results demonstrated that CTC populations with higher MATH scores (measuring genomic diversity) or with non-silent mutations in the BCL9L gene were significantly associated with poorer overall survival. Multivariate analysis confirmed these as independent prognostic factors. Additionally, a 55-gene panel showed strong correlation with whole-exome sequencing-derived MATH scores and survival prediction, offering a cost-effective alternative. This is the first study to show an association between CTC genomic diversity and cancer outcome, suggesting CTC genomic profiling has potential as a novel prognostic tool in mCRC. The relatively small sample size may limit generalizability.

BerkeleyGW demonstrates exascale quantum many‑body GW simulations with true performance portability across AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPU architectures. Using directive‑based OpenACC and OpenMP together with hardware‑specific kernels (HIP, SYCL, CUDA), the code scales to the full machines of Frontier (9 408 nodes, AMD MI250X) and Aurora (9 600 nodes, Intel Ponte Vecchio). On Frontier the optimized off‑diagonal GPP kernel attains 1.069 EFLOP/s (59.45 % of the theoretical peak) and on Aurora 707.52 PFLOP/s (48.79 % of the attainable peak); the diagonal GPP kernel reaches roughly 500 PFLOP/s on both systems. Strong and weak scaling are reported up to tens of thousands of GPUs with high fraction of peak performance.

Key methodological advances include: (i) GW perturbation theory (GWPT) for systematic many‑body electron‑phonon coupling; (ii) a fast full‑frequency GW scheme using a static subspace approximation that reduces cost from O(N²_G) to ~10–20 % of the full planewave basis; (iii) a mixed stochastic‑deterministic pseudobands algorithm that compresses high‑energy bands and lowers the formal O(N⁴) scaling; and (iv) optimized GPP kernels for both diagonal and off‑diagonal self‑energy matrix elements, recasting the latter as dense matrix multiplications (ZGEMM) for increased arithmetic intensity.

These developments enable large‑scale applications such as silicon divacancy (2 742 atoms, ~80 k bands), lithium‑hydride defects (17 574 atoms), and twisted BN moiré structures (867 atoms). The combined performance, portability and scientific reach justify the ACM Gordon Bell Prize nomination.

ABXLAB is a framework for studying how AI agents respond to environmental nudges and choice architecture in online shopping scenarios. Experiments with 17 models across 80,000+ trials reveal that LLM agents exhibit systematic biases 3–10× greater than human baselines: they show strong preferences for higher-rated products (30–80pp effect), cheaper options (15–35pp), and are significantly influenced by persuasive nudges like authority cues and incentives (10–60pp shifts). These findings indicate agents lack robust mechanisms for handling presentation order and are hypersensitive to superficial cues without the cognitive limitations that explain similar human biases.

Sampling and aliasing are demonstrated using a programmable digital filter consisting of a continuous‑to‑discrete (C‑to‑D) sampler, a digital filter, a discrete‑to‑continuous (D‑to‑C) converter, and a smoothing low‑pass filter. With the digital filter set to the identity, a sinusoidal input is sampled and returned to continuous time. When the input frequency is low enough, the output tracks the input. As the input frequency rises toward half the sampling rate, beating appears because the low‑pass filter is non‑ideal. Once the input passes half the sampling rate, aliasing causes the output frequency to decrease while the input frequency continues to increase. A low‑pass digital filter with a symmetric impulse response (linear‑phase) is then inserted. Its discrete‑time frequency response is periodic with 2π and has a cutoff at π/5 (one‑tenth of 2π). The overall continuous‑time frequency response has the same shape but its frequency axis is rescaled so that 2π in digital frequency maps to the sampling frequency. Consequently the continuous‑time cutoff becomes one‑tenth of the sampling rate, doubling when the sampling frequency doubles, halving when it halves. The lecture demonstrates this scaling by sweeping the filter and listening to audio as the sampling rate is changed from 40 kHz down to 2.5 kHz, resulting in correspondingly changing cutoff frequencies.
