Justice Deborah Austin imposed three months of house arrest with a curfew, followed by one year probation, praising his outstanding transformation. He must continue counseling and avoid drugs.

Toews emphasized staying focused on the game during the Stanley Cup Final, noting the playoff experience goes by quickly and family members are often more nervous than players. He said they play their best hockey in the most meaningful games. Richards highlighted the team's experience and maturity, saying they don't need many reminders because they've been through it together. Versteeg described Tampa Bay as a skilled team that makes plays in tough situations and expects close games. Players discussed staying ready when not in the lineup and maintaining confidence through practice and communication. Richards emphasized the need for patience and smart play against Tampa Bay, while also praising a veteran teammate's all-around game and positive attitude.

Research by NYU's Michelle Munson and U of Houston's Sarah Narendorf demonstrates that understanding marginalized young adults' mental health narratives—how they perceive the origins and management of their conditions—is critical for effective treatment. Their studies found that young adults' interpretations of symptoms and perceptions of help sources strongly influence treatment engagement and self-care. Key questions for providers include asking about perceived causes, management approaches, treatment efficacy, and consequences of not seeking help. "Marginalized" refers to youth navigating challenges like poverty, safety-net systems, disabilities, and young parenthood, with structural discrimination limiting access to resources. The researchers advocate training providers to collaboratively uncover patient narratives, proposing a professional-patient team approach as the optimal model for mental health care. Their ongoing NIMH study "Just Do You" in Brooklyn and the Bronx examines whether narrative types generalize beyond formative research and how they relate to health behaviors over time. Munson and Narendorf are also developing technology-based interventions, in partnership with the Jed Foundation, to help young adults construct narratives around new mental health diagnoses. A critical finding: many marginalized young adults who need help do not receive it partly because they do not feel heard, respected, or understood by professional providers.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who immigrated from Uzbekistan to the United States in 2010 and recently became a U.S. citizen, realized his dream of visiting NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener connected him with his brother, NASA astrophysicist Jeremy Schnittman. During the tour, Murad and his mother saw spacecraft testing facilities, a laser lab, and discussed black hole research. Murad, who aims to attend Caltech and eventually lead a Mars mission, expressed his passion for space and the upcoming total solar eclipse visible from Kansas City. He credits his citizenship with making his astronaut aspirations more achievable.

BBC removed Radio 4 presenter Anita Anand since 2012 from an Any Answers edition before broadcast because she publicly criticised the gender‑pay gap and the programme was to discuss the dispute; Julian Worricker presented instead. Critics said the BBC was implying women journalists cannot be impartial. Anand, who supports equal pay, is barred by BBC impartiality rules from covering topics she has spoken out on. The BBC says editors decide case‑by‑case.

On April 20, the NRA told members that YETI coolers had cut ties with the organization. YETI responded that it eliminated discounting programs and offered the NRA Foundation a customization program, contradicting the NRA claim. Some NRA supporters called for a boycott; a South Carolina man, Bryan Atkinson, filled a YETI cooler with ammonia nitrate and aluminum powder and shot it with an AR‑15, prompting a #YetiCoolerChallenge on social media. The dispute follows other companies ending NRA member discounts after shootings. YETI says it continues to support the Second Amendment.

Researchers performed a benchmarking study of fifteen summary‑level Mendelian randomization (MR) methods on real‑world genetic datasets. The methods were grouped into four categories: IVW‑class, outlier‑detection‑removal, model‑based, and outlier‑robust. Performance was evaluated on three aspects: type I error control, accuracy of causal‑effect estimates, and replicability/power.

Type I error was assessed in three confounding scenarios. Scenario (a) used 1,130 exposure–outcome trait pairs affected by population stratification (hair‑color and tanning traits as negative controls). Scenario (b) used 77 trait pairs with pleiotropy (adult behaviours and aging traits as exposures, childhood traits as outcomes). Scenario (c) used 82 genetically uncorrelated trait pairs analyzed with both population‑based and family‑based GWAS to test family‑level confounders.

Across the three scenarios, Egger, Weighted‑mode and MR‑APSS generated well‑calibrated p‑values at their default IV thresholds, while CAUSE produced deflated p‑values. The remaining eleven methods showed inflated type I error, especially under strong population stratification. When family‑based GWAS data were used, all methods produced calibrated p‑values, indicating that within‑family designs can mitigate family‑level confounding.

Varying the IV selection threshold from the stringent 5 × 10⁻⁸ to the relaxed 5 × 10⁻⁵ generally increased type I error inflation for most methods, but MR‑APSS, Egger and Weighted‑mode retained calibration across thresholds. CAUSE’s confidence intervals were reliable even when its p‑values were deflated.

Accuracy of causal estimates was examined using six trait pairs where exposure and outcome were the same trait, with a known true effect of one. MR‑APSS produced point estimates closest to the true value and covered it in all confidence intervals across thresholds. Weighted‑mode also gave accurate estimates at the default threshold, whereas Egger gave unbiased but larger errors. CAUSE covered the true effect only at the stringent threshold; many other methods (IVW‑fixed, IVW‑random, MR‑Lasso, cML‑MA, MR‑PRESSO, RAPS, Weighted‑median, MR‑Robust, MRMix, MR‑ConMix) biased estimates toward the null and had poor coverage when IV thresholds were relaxed.

Replicability was assessed with six LDL‑C GWAS datasets (sample sizes from ~20 k to ~1.3 M) and a coronary artery disease outcome. CAUSE and MR‑APSS showed the most consistent causal estimates and confidence intervals across datasets and thresholds. Egger, Weighted‑mode, Weighted‑median and MR‑Mix missed significance in several tests, though performance improved with larger sample sizes.

Based on the results, the authors recommend: (1) incorporating negative controls to detect confounding; (2) applying multiple IV selection thresholds to assess method sensitivity; (3) using data from independent sources to prioritize methods with high replicability; and (4) considering family‑based GWAS designs when family‑level confounders are suspected.

Limitations noted include possible co‑existence of multiple confounders in the real‑world datasets, lack of true positive cases for power analysis, reliance on the self‑self design which does not test robustness to pleiotropy, and restriction to summary‑level MR methods.

Asparagus provides 33 % daily value (DV) folate per cup; broccoli supplies about 14 % DV; citrus fruits (oranges contain ~50 mcg folate, also papaya, grapefruit, grapes, banana, strawberries) are folate‑rich; legumes (beans, peas, lentils) give most daily needs; avocado ~110 mcg per cup (28 % DV) and provides fiber and fatty acids; lady’s finger ~103 mcg per half‑cup; nuts and seeds (sunflower, flax, pumpkin, sesame, peanuts, almonds) are high in folate; cauliflower ~55 mcg per cup (14 % DV); beetroot ~14 % DV per cup with antioxidants; carrots ~5 % DV per cup; corn ~34 mcg per cup, preferably fresh.

Zita Kovács started winemaking seven years ago, designs labels and is respected as a winemaker; Zsófi Laposa studied harvests abroad, earned a Master’s in Bordeaux, and notes the profession’s growing openness to women; Krisztina Csetvei founded a winery in 2011, brings her toddler daughter to tastings and will present the Panna Rose wine at VinCE Budapest; and Andi Gere co‑manages her family estate with her father, adding feminine elegance to Hungarian wines.

The passage discloses a continuation patent application concerning structurally colored articles (e.g., footwear, apparel, sporting equipment) and methods of making and using them. The articles achieve color through optical elements that interact with light by scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, or diffraction, rather than by pigments or dyes. The optical element may comprise one or more optical layers (such as multilayer reflectors or filters) and may be combined with a textured surface and/or a primer layer to produce the structural color, which can be single‑hue or multi‑hue (including iridescent) and may be angle‑dependent or independent. Color can be characterized using CIE 1976 L*a*b* or CIELCH color spaces with specified thresholds for single‑color classification. The textured surface can contain micro‑ or nanoscale profile features (projections or depressions) that influence the optical response, while the primer layer may be a dark coating (e.g., metal‑oxide, crosslinked polymer) that assists in color control. Polymers such as thermoplastic polyurethanes, elastomers, and related materials are used in the article components. The invention is applicable to a variety of products such as shoes, clothing, and sports gear, and can be applied to external or internal surfaces of components (e.g., uppers, soles, bladders, foams). The present application is a continuation of earlier applications including U.S. application Ser. No. 17/176,057 (filed Feb. 15 2021), which claims priority to, among others, U.S. Pat. No. 10,955,587 and international application PCT/US2018/053529.

A flurry of new deals Monday signals a potential uptick in M&A activity among junior mining companies, especially gold. Hecla Mining (Idaho) announced a US$462 million cash‑and‑share bid for TSX‑listed Klondex Mines (Nevada), while Alio Gold offered $128 million for Rye Patch Gold. A third deal would have Anaconda Mining acquire Maritime Resources. In Canada, 2018 has seen only six mergers versus 19 a year earlier, but the new transactions would raise Hecla’s gold output to about 370,000 oz/yr and create an Alio‑led company with roughly 165,000 oz/yr, with analysts noting silver’s speculative competition from cryptocurrencies and cannabis. Klondex shares jumped 61 % on the news.

Detroit is viewed as the strongest opponent with strong offense and a top goaltender. The team must adapt to referee's calls, especially avoiding penalties after the whistle to prevent Detroit's powerplay. They need better decision making, particularly in shooting and puck possession. Detroit's line led by Kris Draper is highlighted. The team is focused on the game and excited to play at home in the finals. They need to improve faceoffs against Detroit's puck possession game. Detroit has skilled faceoff men like Yzerman and Fedorov. Lidstrom is praised as the league's best defenseman. The home arena is considered louder than Detroit's, creating a great atmosphere. The player is dealing with a growing beard.

MSPM0C1105/6 MCUs are ultra‑low‑power 32‑bit devices based on Arm Cortex‑M0+ core, running up to 32 MHz, operating from 1.62–3.6 V over –40 °C to 125 °C. They provide up to 64 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, a high‑speed on‑chip oscillator (±2.1 %/ +1.6 %), 3‑channel DMA, CRC‑16, a 12‑bit 1.6 Msps ADC with VDD reference, a comparator with 8‑bit DAC, an on‑chip temperature sensor, a 16‑bit advanced timer (up to 64 MHz), four 16‑bit timers, a windowed watchdog, three UART, one SPI, two I2C, and support for LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus and PMBus. Supported by a LaunchPad, free MSP SDK in Code Composer Studio, MSP Academy and TI E2E forums.

Former Nagaland minister Pusa, 63, died leaving his wife, two sons and a daughter. AICC member, he served as Veterinary/Animal Husbandry minister (1998‑1999) and Roads/Bridges minister (2000‑2003), opposition MLA 2003‑13. He won as independent in 1993. Funeral held at residence, burial at Viswema. Leaders condoled.

India's state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in fiscal year 2017/18, with non-performing loans rising 15% to 8.96 trillion rupees. The losses followed RBI's withdrawal of loan restructuring schemes. New Delhi has announced a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan, though some banks may lack growth funds due to Basel III requirements.

Zillow’s analysis of homes sold from June 2017 to May 2018 in the 35 largest metros found that homes with central air‑conditioning sold for a 2.5 % premium—about $5,500 more than comparable homes without AC. Premiums were highest in San Antonio (5.8 %), Cincinnati (5.7 %) and in Detroit, Indianapolis and Las Vegas (≈5 %). Air‑conditioning was a required feature for 62 % of buyers, out‑ranking private outdoor space (48 %). Across the U.S., 66 % of sold homes had AC; in hot climates the share approached 100 % (99 % Las Vegas, 98 % Phoenix). Renters also paid a premium: rentals with central AC rented for 2.8 % more, roughly $40 per month, with the largest rent premiums in New York, Las Vegas and Phoenix. The premium reflects AC’s shift from luxury to necessity as extreme heat becomes more common.

Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options that give the right to buy or sell a set number of shares at an agreed‑upon price on or before expiration. Call options allow buying, while put options allow selling; investors use them to profit from price movements, hedge risk, or speculate without owning the shares. The leverage of options lets investors make large gains with small investments, and options function like insurance, with premiums paid for protection.

Orders for IWM options include market orders, limit orders, stop orders, and trailing‑stop orders; trades are not permitted when the stock’s closing price is below $2.00. Strategies range from buying call options when a price rise is expected and buying put options when a decline is expected, to selling covered calls (holding the underlying stock) and buying protective puts. Risks include loss of the entire premium, potential loss of the whole investment if the price moves opposite to the prediction, and unlimited risk from short calls.

A trading plan should use technical indicators such as moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger bands, monitor news and economic data, and include backtesting of strategies. Short selling is allowed, and taxes apply to short‑term and long‑term capital gains as well as to premiums. A margin account is required, and margin trading increases risk; the minimum account balance varies by broker but is commonly around $2,000. Allocating no more than 10 % of a portfolio to IWM options is advised, and investors must meet eligibility requirements (age, funds, and possibly Level 2 approval) and understand contract terms, expiration dates, strike prices, and associated fees.

Resources for staying informed include online news sources, research websites, financial publications, and trading forums. Effective profit‑maximizing strategies combine buying and selling options, using spreads, applying technical analysis, and employing risk‑management tools such as stop‑loss orders and diversification. Beginners should avoid options trading until they have thoroughly learned the mechanics and should backtest any strategy before committing capital.

Governor Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program to train administrators in school security. The program allows administrators at schools without a resource officer to keep a firearm in a secured safe for active‑shooter response. Participants must complete training and receive approval from the local superintendent, school board and sheriff. Sentries must store weapons securely and provide their own approved firearm, ammunition and a bullet‑proof vest. Hal Taylor and Dr. Eric Mackey supported the program, stating it will enhance safety without new funding.

This patent application describes systems and methods for tracing cryptocurrency transactions to detect money laundering and terrorism financing using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The system receives blockchain transaction data and intelligence labels from a database, selects transaction flows between source, intermediate, and destination addresses, and applies AI graph search algorithms to trace asset paths based on user-defined parameters. When suspicious addresses are identified, the system can alert users or suspend transactions. The risk management system uses machine learning models to classify entity behaviors and assign risk scores (ranging from Safe to Risky), enabling automated actions like blocking or freezing transactions based on configured thresholds. The system incorporates address clustering, feature analysis across statistics, topology, temporal, and behavioral categories, and employs AutoML for model selection and training.

Bank of England warns that AI‑related stock valuations have reached unsustainable levels reminiscent of the dot‑com era, with concentration among a few U.S. firms (Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta) creating systemic risk; a sharp correction could spill into UK markets via capital outflows. Plum School District officials aim to avoid a third tax increase by beginning 2018‑19 budget discussions early. The district is $4 million in debt. It approved a $66 million budget June with a 0.866‑mill tax hike and bond approval. Plans include recruiting Chinese students for tuition in 2018‑19; this year’s attempt failed due to visa delays. Tuesday’s workshop covers construction, consolidation, redistricting and process for closing Regency Park Elementary, which requires state notification and public hearings. It follows a 6 p.m. voting meeting on personnel moves.

Infosys Finacle survey of 100 finance professionals: more than 80% of bankers expect commercial blockchain by 2020; over half are investing this year, with average spend about $1 million. Half partner with fintech firms. Priorities: transparency, automation, faster settlement. Top use cases: cross‑border payments, digital identity, clearing/settlement, letters of credit, loan syndication. Private blockchain preferred by 69%, consortium by 20%, public by 10%.

A pump‑and‑dump scheme involves a promoter acquiring a position in a low‑priced, often thinly‑traded stock or cryptocurrency and then artificially raising its price by spreading false or misleading information. As the price rises, the promoter and early participants sell their holdings to later investors, causing the price to collapse. Such schemes are illegal on regulated exchanges but are common in the OTC (penny‑stock) market and the largely unregulated cryptocurrency market, especially among low‑volume “shitcoins.” They exploit the fear‑of‑missing‑out bias, and participants typically suffer large losses – a study of German bank accounts found that 6 % of investors entered at least one scheme, with an average return of –28 % and total losses of at least €1.2 million per tout campaign. Pump‑and‑dumps account for roughly 15 % of spam e‑mail. Regulatory actions have reduced the practice on major exchanges, but the risk remains elevated in OTC and crypto venues. Investors are advised to avoid such schemes, trade on regulated markets, and focus on systematic, long‑term strategies.

The disclosure pertains to methods, apparatus and a system for transmitting paging information in new‑generation wireless communications that employ high‑frequency carrier frequencies and beamforming. In such systems a single transmit port covers only a small angular sector, so paging must be sent on all beams/ports to reach an idle user equipment (UE). The existing LTE discontinuous reception (DRX) mechanism cannot be directly applied because a UE cannot predict beam/port scheduling across timeslots.

To solve this, the disclosure defines a paging occasion (PO) as a group of paging resources that spans one or more preset beams or ports; the PO can correspond to a synchronous signal (SS) burst set or to sweeping resources of a beam group. A first communication node (e.g., a base station) calculates the time‑domain position of the PO of a second node (UE) based on parameters such as the DRX cycle (T_DRX), paging transmission interval (T_paging), number of paging transmissions (N), the UE identifier (Device_ID) and a PO offset (t_offset). Formulas for determining the starting radio‑frame number (SFN) of the PO are provided. The first node then transmits paging information (paging downlink control information and/or a paging message) within the PO, covering all beams/ports.

The second node independently calculates the same PO time‑domain position and receives the paging information during that PO. Quasi‑co‑location relationships between the paging‑related signal and other sweeping signals (SS, DMRS, BRS, MRS, CSI‑RS) may be indicated or pre‑configured, allowing the UE to determine the proper receive beam/resource.

The disclosure also covers corresponding apparatus, a system, a base station and a terminal device, a computer‑readable storage medium, and a computer program product that implement the described methods, thereby enabling effective DRX for paging in high‑frequency beamformed networks.

Orbital ATK reported Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, up 3% year‑over‑year, beating the $1.11 billion analyst consensus. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.56, $0.13 above expectations, while GAAP EPS fell 3% to $1.51; operating margin declined 140 basis points to 12.2%. Free cash flow turned negative, dropping from a $107.2 million positive result a year earlier to a $55.8 million loss. The company booked $1.4 billion in new firm and option orders plus $220 million in option exercises, yielding a book‑to‑bill ratio of 1.45 and lifting firm backlog 10% over the prior year. Management raised full‑year guidance to sales of $4.6‑$4.65 billion and EPS of $5.95‑$6.25, while keeping free cash‑flow guidance unchanged at $250‑$300 million. In response, Argus Research upgraded the stock to “buy” with a $120 price target, implying about 12.5% upside, citing expected H2 milestones and increased defense spending. The author observes that the valuation appears stretched—market cap $6.1 billion, trailing P/E of 22, projected P/E of 17, and an enterprise‑value‑to‑free‑cash‑flow ratio above 40 (falling to 25 at best)—and concludes the stock is too expensive to justify a buy rating. The Motley Fool recommends Orbital ATK, and the article’s author, Rich Smith, holds no position.

Shepard Fairey's 2009 arrest outside Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) during his exhibition's opening night drew attention but didn't diminish public interest, with 130,000 visiting the show over six months. Under Director Jill Medvedow, who took leadership in 1998, the ICA transformed from an institution with minimal funding, no permanent collection, and only 25,000 annual visitors to a major cultural destination. The museum secured a $51 million waterfront building on Fan Pier's Parcel J in 1999 and selected Diller + Scofidio—architects with no U.S. building experience—to design the structure. Through unconventional fundraising strategies and public engagement efforts, the ICA exceeded its $62 million capital campaign goal, raising over $75 million. When the new building opened in December 2006, it attracted over 280,000 visitors in its first year, surpassing the 200,000 needed to break even. Medvedow's leadership emphasized risk-taking, expanding accessibility to contemporary art beyond traditional museum audiences.
Jenkins v. United States appeal docketed and dismissed on motion of appellee with appellant's consent.

This study proposes "whole human pedagogy," a novel framework for education abroad centered on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. Informed by decolonial theory and the works of hooks (1994) and Thompson (2016), the framework approaches students as integrated human beings with bodily, emotional, relational, and meaning-making knowledge. The qualitative study involved in-depth interviews with 17 education abroad practitioners in Fall 2023. Findings showed practitioners consistently valued the whole human approach and naturally engaged with two or three of the four tenets. Participants emphasized physical immersion, emotional processing, communal relationships, and transformative learning as central to their work. The framework offers a decolonial alternative to dominant Euro-U.S. epistemological values and provides practical applications for program development and professional development in education abroad.

Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters under the Mann Act. He was acquitted of sex‑trafficking and racketeering charges that could have carried a life sentence. The passage describes container design patterns for building distributed systems. The sidecar pattern extends existing application containers without modification, used for HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, and monitoring. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between application containers and external systems, applicable to sharding, service discovery, and request splitting. The adapter pattern modifies application interfaces to conform to standardized conventions for monitoring, logging, and health checks. For larger-scale distributed systems, the replicated load-balanced pattern provides redundancy and scalability for stateless services using layers for caching and SSL termination. Sharded services handle stateful workloads where data exceeds single-machine capacity, enabling both scaling and data isolation. The scatter/gather pattern achieves parallelism by distributing requests across multiple replicas simultaneously, combining partial results into complete responses. All patterns emphasize modularity, reusability, and separation of concerns through container composition.

Confidential March 8, 1892 dispatch by Mr. Stevens reported revolutionary plans kept in check by a U.S. naval presence, hostility to the “half‑English” heir, and sentiment for annexation to the United States. The queen’s reliance on half‑caste Tahitian Wilson caused dissatisfaction; cabinet was voted out in August/September, leading to a deadlock. A vote of want of confidence on October 17 forced crisis; the minister’s October 19 dispatch warned the queen must yield or the monarchy would fall. On November 20, Stevens detailed islands’ condition and advocated annexation or a customs union, ocean cable, perpetual cession of Pearl Harbor, and an implied U.S. protectorate. Naval reports corroborated accounts. On January 28, telegraph news announced a revolution and queen’s dethronement. U.S. policy from 1820‑1893 emphasized friendship, protection, and distrust of foreign intervention, contemplating annexation under threat under President Pierce. The appendix notes time, provides a general view, includes copies of papers, and records three unperfected treaties (1849, 1855, 1867) and correspondence in Navy archives.

Seven months after the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) eliminated more than 100 research contracts at the U.S. Department of Education, several recent actions have sparked cautious optimism among researchers. In June the department said it would reinstate 20 of the canceled contracts, and a court order gave a short reprieve to 10 federally funded regional education labs (RELs). The department also opened a public comment period on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) and posted job listings for eight senior assessment positions at the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) to support the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP). An external adviser, Amber Northern from the Thomas B. Fordham Institute, was hired to guide a six‑month IES reform effort. Researchers rate IES’s current capacity at 3‑4 on a 1‑10 scale, citing severe staff shortages that still threaten data quality. The administration has acknowledged the “chaos” of the first six months and is moving toward outcomes‑based contracting. While NAEP testing is expected to continue, reporting functions have been cut, including the end of district‑level results for some subjects. A recent executive order requiring retroactive collection of college‑admissions data may further strain NCES resources. The potential reinstatement of the 10 RELs, previously funded at $336 million, is seen as a positive step, though observers note the “education improvement industrial complex” still influences funding debates.

Theratechnologies Inc. announced on May 30 2018 that it will issue US$50 million of convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30 2023 at US$1 000 per note, with an option for the underwriters to purchase up to an additional US$7.5 million of notes. The notes bear interest at 5.75 % per annum, payable semi‑annually on June 30 and December 31, with the first payment on December 31 2018. The notes are not redeemable before June 30 2021; after that they may be redeemed, in whole or in part, on 40‑60 days notice if the 20‑day volume‑weighted average share price is at least 130 % of the conversion price. The notes will be offered by short‑form prospectus in all Canadian provinces and may also be placed privately in the United States. NGC 5949, a dwarf galaxy ~44 million light‑years away, has ~1% of the Milky Way’s mass and displays loosely bound barred spiral arms. Discovered by William Herschel in 1801, its brightness permits observation with modest telescopes. Dark‑matter distribution and missing satellites pose cosmological puzzles.

The ultimate oscillator is a momentum indicator that measures price momentum across three timeframes (7, 14 and 28 periods), combining them with a weighted average of 4:2:1 (shortest period most heavily weighted). It was created by Larry Williams in 1976 and popularized in 1985. Calculation involves: (1) buying pressure (BP) = close – minimum of current low or prior close; (2) true range (TR) = maximum of current high or prior close – minimum of current low or prior close; (3) average BP and TR sums for each period; (4) UO = 100 × [(4 × Average7)+(2 × Average14)+Average28] / 7. The indicator oscillates between 0‑100, with levels below 30 considered oversold and above 70 overbought. Signals are generated only when a divergence between price and the oscillator occurs; a bullish divergence from oversold territory and a rise above the divergence high trigger a buy signal, while a bearish divergence triggers a sell signal. Backtests with optimized settings show profit factors well above 2.5, win rates around 78 %, average gains of about 0.77 % per trade, maximum drawdown ~25 % and only two down years, indicating the ultimate oscillator is a consistent, stable mean‑reversion tool.

The Supreme Court dismissed a plea seeking cancellation of interim bail for the Pinto family in the murder case of 7-year-old Pradyuman Thakur. The CBI investigation held a class 11 student responsible, giving a clean chit to initially arrested bus conductor Ashok. Pradyuman's family alleges Pinto family complicity.

Americans with 3.5 million truck drivers face automation within decades. Global companies invest in autonomous vehicles; Rio Tinto runs driverless mining trucks, Volvo tests autonomous passenger rides, and a former Google self‑driving engineer founded Otto. AI has also entered law firms, hotels, and newsrooms. The World Economic Forum predicts the Fourth Industrial Revolution will eliminate over five million jobs in five years. To stay employable, workers may augment themselves: Elon Musk proposes a brain‑enhancing “neural lace” inspired by Harvard’s injectable electronic mesh that can monitor and potentially boost brain function. Exosuits developed by Hyundai, Harvard, the US Army, and SuitX provide strength assistance and reduce physical strain; Harvard’s soft exosuit decreased walking effort by about 23 percent. Augmentation also includes upskilling; Tom Davenport recommends developing non‑codifiable abilities, learning machine operation, and collaborating with AI. While knowledge workers may find new roles, many physical laborers such as truck drivers could face a difficult transition.
Trump rejected a NYT article saying he watches four to eight hours of TV, claiming he does not. The Times defended reporting citing 60 associates. Trump tweeted about fake news.

Meb Faber's Tactical Asset Allocation is an active trend-following strategy using market timing to allocate across four asset classes: stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities. These are organized into five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. The strategy uses five diversified index ETFs with 20% allocation to each position, moving to cash when no signal exists. Faber is co-founder and chief investment officer at Cambria Investment Management. Backtesting shows a -13.24% drawdown versus 40-50% for passive buy-and-hold strategies.

The case involves a modification of child support. Following a divorce in 1981, the mother was awarded custody of three children. The father, a state trooper, originally paid $145 per child per month. In 1985, the mother moved to increase support due to increased expenses and the father's higher income. The trial court increased support to $516 per month (30% of net income), citing the father's income increase from $1,246 to $1,721 monthly. The father appealed, arguing the increase was unjustified. The Court of Appeals found the support amount within discretion but remanded the case because the trial court failed to make specific findings required by Moylan v. Moylan to justify the increase.

Richard Mosse’s Heat Maps project uses a military‑grade thermal camera attached to a robotic arm to photograph refugees in Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. According to UNHCR, 65.3 million people are currently displaced by war or persecution. The camera renders human flesh translucent grey and blackens eye sockets, turning people into ghostly avatars. Mosse says the device strips identity and reveals how Western governments view refugees, deliberately making viewers feel complicit. The large‑scale panoramas are built from nearly a thousand frames stitched together, evoking Bruegel‑like detail but flat like medieval tapestry. He repurposed a surveillance camera originally designed for weapons targeting, employing a Verfremdungseffekt to render the familiar strange. Logistics were difficult, including month‑long attempts to join a Swedish convoy to reach Timbuktu, and access to camps such as Calais Jungle was obtained just before its demolition. The work, displayed at the Jack Shainman Gallery until March 11, aims to be culturally resonant without being politically committed.

India demanded the UN Secretariat disclose information about misconduct cases involving UN personnel and the immunity invoked against prosecutions. India's UN Mission legal advisor Yedla Umasankar criticized the UN for not vigorously following up allegations of serious wrongdoing by staff with diplomatic immunity, saying the UN appears reluctant to waive immunity even for serious misconduct. He requested data on the number of registered serious misconduct cases, how often the UN refused to waive immunity, how often host countries wanted immunity waived, and how often countries refused UN requests to waive their citizens' immunity. While the UN has published data on sexual misconduct in peacekeeping operations since 2015, it has not made public a comprehensive roster of all allegations across the entire organization. Umasankar attributed the lack of accountability to legal complexities regarding sovereignty and jurisdiction, the necessity of immunity for UN operations, and countries' varying capability and willingness to prosecute.

President Trump announced that the United States will impose a 100% tariff on all Chinese imports starting November 1, 2025, on top of existing duties, and will also apply export controls on critical software the same day. The measures are retaliation for China’s new export restrictions on rare‑earth minerals, which supply roughly 70% of global demand and are vital for high‑tech sectors such as automobiles, defense and semiconductors. China also requires a license for exports of products containing more than 0.1% rare‑earths sourced from China or manufactured using Chinese processing technology, effective Dec 1. The current effective tariff on Chinese goods is about 40%.

Double bottom is a bullish reversal pattern comprising two swing lows at approximately the same level and a swing high between them; the lows create a support level and the connecting swing high defines a resistance called the neckline. The pattern completes when price breaks above the neckline, indicating the possible end of a downtrend or prolonged pullback. Traders often measure the pattern’s height and project it upward from the neckline to set a profit target, and place stop‑loss orders either at the middle of the pattern for a 2:1 reward‑risk ratio or below the pattern for greater safety. Aggressive traders may enter when the second low forms, looking for reversal signs (e.g., bullish candlesticks or RSI exiting oversold), while conservative traders wait for a confirmed neckline breakout with increased volume. Coding double bottom detection is complex, though Amibroker code exists for marking patterns and backtesting. Thomas Bulkowski’s study on 500 stocks over five years found that roughly 68 % of double bottom formations reached their target, higher than the double‑top counterpart, but the study relies on manual identification and may suffer from survivorship bias, so the results are only an indication rather than definitive proof.

A new remote‑sensing system uses an inexpensive time‑lapse camera and weather sensors to monitor colony behavior online. Observations reveal penguins huddling when it is warmer, suggesting reduced body fat and possible food scarcity linked to sea‑ice loss and plankton decline. The court sentenced defendant Pomeroy to $1,000 fines for each of six offenses, totaling $6,000, and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company to $18,000 fines for each of six crimes, totaling $108,000. The passage critiques the criminal law for setting aside judgments on technicalities unrelated to merits, and proposes a law requiring that errors must cause a miscarriage of justice before a judgment can be overturned. It discusses injunctions, arguing that while necessary to combat mob violence, they are subject to abuse; judges should use them to curb violence but not to suppress peaceful labor activity or aid corporations. UDMA write CRC corruption occurs when an IDE device terminates a write, causing ATAC to reuse previous CRC for next portion instead of starting a new one. Corruption originates from host termination during a preceding UDMA read. Consequently, UDMA writes are unreliable; recommended fix is enabling UDMA I/O blocking feature via bit 8 of ATAC Error MSR.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of an antitrust lawsuit against Mitsubishi entities and Exportadora de Sal (ESSA), a Mexican corporation majority-owned by the Mexican government. The plaintiffs alleged that ESSA and Mitsubishi conspired to monopolize Mexico's solar sea salt production and distribution, breaching distribution contracts with Innofood and Sea Breeze Salt. The court held that the act of state doctrine barred the suit because it challenged Mexico's sovereign decisions about exploiting its natural resources. The doctrine precludes U.S. courts from adjudicating the official acts of foreign sovereigns performed within their territory. ESSA's policy decision to distribute salt exclusively through Mitsubishi was deemed a sovereign act, as Mexican Constitution commits salt resources to state ownership. The relief sought would require invalidating Mexico's official acts regarding its natural resources. The court also declined to adopt a commercial exception to the doctrine, finding ESSA's conduct involved sovereign powers not exercisable by private citizens. The judgment was affirmed, and the court noted the holding was narrow and limited to these specific facts.

hBN is a promising 2D material with a wide bandgap, high thermal conductivity, chemical stability and mechanical robustness, but achieving large‑area, high crystalline quality remains difficult because its threefold symmetry allows antiparallel domain nucleation on sixfold symmetric metal substrates, leading to grain boundaries that degrade optical and electronic properties. Conventional structural probes such as TEM, STM, LEED and Raman spectroscopy either sample limited areas, require demanding preparation, or cannot resolve orientational polarity. Interferometric second‑harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry overcomes these limitations by exploiting the coherent, anisotropic second‑order nonlinear response of hBN. Dual‑polarization SHG imaging of CVD‑grown hBN reveals SHG intensity variations up to three orders of magnitude, while Raman intensity varies only by a factor of four, indicating additional disorder not captured by Raman. Polarimetric maps show multiple orientational domains with angular spreads up to ~5° and boundaries with weak SHG signals. Interferometric detection with a local oscillator identifies π‑phase shifts between neighboring domains, confirming antiparallel alignment. Mixed‑domain simulations demonstrate that the observed intensity suppression arises from destructive interference among antiparallel sub‑domains. By correlating SHG intensity, Raman intensity, Raman linewidth and orientational spread, a quantitative framework for crystalline quality assessment is established. The technique enables wide‑area, non‑destructive structural imaging and is applicable to other non‑centrosymmetric 2D crystals such as transition‑metal dichalcogenides, offering a scalable method for growth optimization and domain engineering.

Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a common complication of advanced liver disease that can be exacerbated by transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement, which increases HE risk by 30-55% post-procedure. This study used untargeted metabolomics to analyze blood samples from hepatic and peripheral veins before and after TIPS in 22 participants to identify metabolite changes associated with HE development. The most significant metabolomic changes occurred between post-TIPS and discharge, with bile acids showing the largest shifts. Participants who developed HE (grades 1 or 2+) had greater dissimilarity in their hepatic vein metabolome pre- to post-TIPS, suggesting less pre-existing intrahepatic shunting compared to those who did not develop HE. Patients who developed HE also exhibited greater decreases in specific conjugated bile acids and glycerophosphocholines post-TIPS. Two readmitted patients showed consistent bile acid decreases that improved with HE treatment. The findings suggest that intrahepatic shunting may be protective against HE by acclimating patients to portal toxins, and that certain bile acids may have a protective role against HE development. Bile acid supplementation and measurement of intrahepatic shunting are proposed as potential strategies for HE prevention and risk stratification. The study is limited by incomplete metabolic coverage, reliance on spectral library annotations, and the need for validation in larger cohorts.

AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update lists multiple hardware limitations and recommended workarounds. Issues include UART registers being inaccessible during DMA but not blocked on current platforms; legacy DMA write from LPC fails; I/O cycles to addresses ≥10000h cause hangs; over‑voltage protection specification not met, requiring external circuits; I/O base registers can be set to illegal values; PIC fails when an edge‑triggered interrupt source stays high after the clock is gated; PRD prefetch can cause errors if tables are not 8‑byte aligned; UDMA write CRC corruption occurs after device termination; DMA‑related SSMI generation is unreliable; the main GLIU clock domain does not wake on ASMI from statistics counters; ACPI PM1_STS/PM1_EN registers only support WORD/DWORD accesses; WORD/BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt other registers; KEL emulation does not correctly report I/O port 064h writes; Snoop mode incorrectly affects KEL registers; PCI back‑to‑back reads may fail in simulation but not in real systems; 8259 PIC polling mode is unsupported; automatic clock gating for UART does not work in CEIR mode; IRDY# and DEVSEL# timing violates PCI spec; SSMI may be lost when an interrupt occurs simultaneously; enabling bus master before sending a PIO command causes UDMA failure; most wake inputs from S3 do not work; RTC CMOS RAM read after extended write returns incorrect data; block/demand DMA blocks I/O to LPC; USB controller clock gating prevents register reads; an ATAPI packet command can reset the bus master; AuxOutputFull bit is cleared by Port 60h reads; tACK does not affect UDMA timing; ATAC hangs if PRD address is not DWORD aligned; LPC may abort on short sync patterns; SMB controller NEGACK bit requires two writes to clear; GLPCI retry counter counts all retries; GPIO high‑bank atomic writes clear non‑selected bits after suspend; SMBus data hold time is shorter than spec; LOWBAT_FLAG may be missing after standby; Sleep_X/Y signals may stay asserted if delay counters exceed PM_SED. Resolutions generally advise avoiding certain modes, ensuring proper alignment, disabling clock gating, using DWORD accesses, adding external circuitry, or adjusting timing parameters.

The passage covers container design patterns and distributed system architectures. It begins with the adapter pattern, used to adapt services like Redis to Prometheus for monitoring and to normalize diverse logging formats via tools like Fluentd. It also describes using adapter containers for rich health checks on databases like MySQL. The discussion then shifts to multi-node distributed patterns: replicated load-balanced services for stateless applications, session tracking for user request affinity, and layers for caching (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx). Sharded services are introduced to scale stateful data storage, with sharded caches improving memory utilization and consistent hashing minimizing resharding impact. The scatter/gather pattern is explained for parallel request processing across distributed nodes. Finally, the passage explores function-as-a-service (FaaS) and event-driven architectures, highlighting benefits like simplified deployment and automatic scaling but also challenges such as debugging complexity and limitations in background processing and sustained high-load scenarios. Patterns like decorators for request transformation, event handling for asynchronous tasks like two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines for orchestrating decoupled workflows are demonstrated using frameworks like Kubeless. The overarching theme emphasizes modularity, reuse, and decoupling in distributed system design.

The President addresses the Senate and House of Representatives, expressing anxiety about being called from a private retreat to assume the presidency and acknowledging his limited qualifications. He commends Congress’s talents, rectitude, and patriotism, believing they will safeguard liberty and base policy on moral principles. He notes the link between virtue and national prosperity and stresses the importance of preserving liberty. James T. Hodgkinson, a 66‑year‑old Illinois man, was shot and killed by police after wounding Rep. Steve Scalise and several others during an early‑morning congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia. Authorities say Hodgkinson had been living out of a white cargo van in northern Virginia since March and frequented a nearby YMCA, where he was seen working on a computer and largely kept to himself. He expressed online grievances about President Donald Trump and Republicans, and his brother told the New York Times he was upset about the election. Hodgkinson previously ran a home‑inspection business, was a supporter of Bernie Sanders, and wrote letters to a local newspaper about income inequality. Court records show a history of minor arrests and a 2006 battery charge that was later dismissed. He was armed with a handgun and a rifle, and two Capitol Police officers and a congressional aide were also injured. The FBI is tracing the weapons and seeking public information about his recent activities.

President transmits to Congress a June letter from the Texas governor to the late President, together with his own reply. Texas’s legislature authorized a commissioner to extend its civil jurisdiction over the unorganized counties of El Paso, Worth, Presidio and Santa Fe on its northwestern frontier; the commissioner reported that U.S. military officers at Santa Fe opposed the effort, favoring a separate state government east of the Rio Grande. The legislature has been convened to defend Texas’s claim and to establish jurisdiction by force.

The President outlines his constitutional duties and existing statutes (Acts of 1795 and 1807) that empower him to call forth the militia or employ land and naval forces whenever U.S. laws are opposed by combinations too powerful for civil authorities. He stresses that Texas’s authority is confined to its own borders; Texas militia entering another state or a U.S. Territory would become trespassers, and the President would be obligated to suppress any obstruction of U.S. law.

He affirms that New Mexico is a U.S. Territory under the Treaty of Guadalupe‑Hidalgo, whose provisions (Articles 5, 8 and 9) guarantee Mexican residents north or east of the treaty’s demarcation line security of liberty, property and religion. The treaty is supreme law and must be upheld until replaced by legitimate authority.

The boundary between Texas and New Mexico remains unsettled; only Congress (with Texas’s assent) or a legal adjudication can resolve it. Until then, the President must protect all inhabitants living within the territory as it existed at the treaty’s date.

The President urges Congress to settle the boundary promptly, suggesting it may offer Texas fair, liberal indemnity for relinquishing its claim, and warns that delay risks disturbance. He expresses hope that an amicable settlement will restore harmony and confidence in the Union.

James D. Rone sued Boncar Construction Co. for personal injuries sustained on May 6 1970 at a sewer project in Hobart, Indiana. Rone, employed by Dan Raymond Construction Co. as a line foreman, was part of a joint venture with Boncar. While assisting in moving a 6‑to‑8‑ton metal box with a back hoe, Rone climbed onto the gantry to lift telephone wires, then held a cable while descending; the cable moved and severed the fingers of his right hand and caused loss of fingers on his left hand.

Rone filed three counts: (I) violation of the Illinois Structural Work Act; (II) negligence under the Indiana Dangerous Occupation Act; (III) willful and wanton negligence (later dropped). The trial court struck Count I, reasoning the Illinois act did not apply extraterritorially. Plaintiff appealed the dismissal; the appellate court dismissed the appeal without prejudice and remanded for trial on the remaining counts. After trial on Counts II and III the jury returned a verdict for Boncar.

On appeal Rone argued the dismissal of Count I was appealable, that negligence should have been decided as a matter of law, that he was free from contributory negligence under the Indiana Employers Liability Act and common law, and that the court erred by refusing two of his proposed instructions. The appellate court affirmed, holding: (1) the dismissal of Count I was final but plaintiff waived his right to appeal; (2) negligence and contributory negligence were jury questions; (3) the refusal of the instructions was not erroneous. The judgment for Boncar was affirmed.

The AEGEAN trial compared primary standard of care (SOC), secondary SOC and an additional educational program for patients initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation. Time from consent to first dose averaged 1.6–1.8 days and total drug exposure at 24 weeks (≈158–168 days) and 48 weeks (≈301–328 days) was similar across groups; interruptions were <2 days on average. Most subjects received apixaban 5 mg BID (≈87–88 %) with low dose modifications (<5 %). Compliance exceeded 95 % at weeks 4, 12, 24 and >94 % at week 48 in all groups.

Mean adherence at 24 weeks was ≈91–92 % with no significant differences; adherence remained comparable at 12 weeks and through 48 weeks. Persistence at 24 weeks was ≈91–92 % and at 48 weeks ≈85–88 % without significant differences. Fully adherent subjects accounted for ≈26–28 % at 24 weeks (median full‑adherence duration 58–59 days) and ≈14.5–15 % at 48 weeks (median 45–78 days). Predictors of non‑adherence varied by group (e.g., alcohol use, occupation, MMSE score) but no consistent advantage of the educational program was seen.

Safety: adverse events up to 24 weeks occurred in ≈51–52 % of subjects (≈8–9 % related, ≈12–15 % serious); bleeding events were 6–9 % with major bleeding 0.7–1.1 %. Between 24 and 48 weeks, any AE was reported in 34–41 % of subjects, serious AE in 12–14 %, and bleeding in 3–4 %; fatal bleeding occurred in two subjects (one each in primary and secondary SOC). Overall, 24 deaths were reported (11 before week 24, 13 after week 24); one additional death without a reported adverse event was noted. No clinically relevant hepatic or renal laboratory signals were observed.

The study concluded that high adherence and persistence were sustained to 48 weeks, and a proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.

Chinese official Yuan informed Heard that two Chinese men‑of‑war would arrive in Chemulpo and that a strong decree would caution against further discussion of heterodoxy, while Yuan pledged responsibility for foreign safety. Subsequent dispatches note continued agitation, petitions for harsh measures against the sect, a royal decree in the Gazette, and a violent Tong Hâk manifesto urging the extermination of foreigners, posted at the governor’s gate. The Japanese consul privately warned his nationals to prepare for possible evacuation to Chemulpo, and some Japanese families have already moved there. Despite the unrest, most foreigners remain calm; H.M.S. Severn visited the port and departed, with the captain promising to return within 48 hours if needed, though the reliability of telegraph communication in a crisis remains uncertain.

Opening range breakout (ORB) trading strategies, popularized by Tony Crabel's 1990 book, have diminished effectiveness for major futures contracts and ETFs. Backtests on S&P 500, Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil futures show simple ORB strategies on minute bars produce minimal returns (best around 0.04% per trade) with low win rates. Strategies fail due to false breakouts, computer-driven arbitrage eliminating edges, and the fact that daily highs and lows typically occur in morning and closing hours rather than mid-session. However, adding daily time-frame filters significantly improves results—example shows 198 trades with 0.27% average gain, 65% win rate, and 2.0 profit factor. Traders are advised to use strategy optimization while avoiding curve fitting to find robust approaches, potentially focusing on individual stocks rather than indices for better opportunities.

The Amoeba defense was developed by coach Jerry Tarkanian at UNLV and contributed to their 1990 NCAA Championship. It is an aggressive, trapping match-up zone defense using a 1-1-3 alignment that disrupts opponents and creates steals and fast-break opportunities. The formation includes a point guard (X1) who pressures the ballhandler at midcourt, a defender (X2) at the free throw line, two wings (X3, X4) positioned between the free throw line and baseline, and a post defender (X5) protecting the basket. The defense features various trapping scenarios and rotations depending on where the ball is passed, including wing traps, corner traps, and post rotations, requiring quick guards for effective execution.

Momentum investing buys stocks with the best recent 3‑12‑month performance and periodically rebalances to maintain exposure to the highest‑momentum securities, based on the hypothesis that past performance predicts near‑future returns. Research shows that roughly 20% of stocks listed between 1989‑2015 accounted for all market gains, while the remaining 80% returned zero, illustrating a negatively skewed distribution. A simple S&P 500 monthly‑bar moving‑average crossover momentum strategy backtested from 1960 to 2023 grew a $100,000 portfolio to $5.575 million, yielding a 6.6% annual return versus 7% for buy‑and‑hold, but was only invested 69% of the time, producing a risk‑adjusted return of 9.5% and smaller maximum drawdowns (26% vs 55%). The average loss per trade was under 5% and the average gain about 25%, with simple moving averages outperforming exponential ones. The S&P 500 Momentum Index (ticker SP500MUP) tracks stocks with relative strength across all markets. A compilation of over 1,200 articles contains backtestable trading rules and strategy packages.

Overbought denotes a significant price rise over a defined period, often identified by indicators such as the Relative Strength Index (RSI). It is considered bearish, suggesting a potential short‑term correction. Mean‑reversion (or regression to the mean) explains that strong deviations from the trend tend to reverse over time, so overbought markets typically produce weaker returns in the first days after the signal but eventually return to long‑term averages. Media coverage can amplify overbought conditions by publishing positive articles, fostering fear of missing out, and during downturns, negative coverage can increase panic. Backtesting shows that after an overbought trigger (e.g., 2‑day RSI > 95), short‑term returns are lower than average, but the edge diminishes as time progresses.

The passage covers multi-node distributed system patterns: the adapter pattern (e.g., Fluentd for logging Redis queries, MySQL health checks), microservices architecture (benefits: modularity, independent scaling, team decoupling; challenges: debugging, design complexity), replicated load-balanced services (stateless serving, readiness probes, session tracking, caching with Varnish, SSL termination with nginx), sharding (data partitioning, sharded caches, consistent hashing, hot sharding), scatter/gather (parallel request processing, leaf sharding, straggler problem, replicated sharded scatter/gather), event-driven/FaaS (benefits: simplified deployment, automatic scaling; challenges: operations complexity, background processing limits, memory constraints, per-request cost model), patterns like the decorator (request/response transformation), event handling (e.g., two-factor authentication), event pipelines (e.g., new-user signup), and master election (distributed ownership, singleton reliability trade-offs). The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. The controllers operate from 4V to 14V input with switching frequencies from 100kHz to 2MHz. Three oscillator modes are available: internal oscillator mode uses an RT pin resistor to set frequency; external synchronization mode accepts a clock signal at the SYNC pin at twice the desired switching frequency; and primary-secondary mode allows two controllers to operate in sync with 90° or 270° phase shift. Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) provide approximately 150mA peak current capability each. Dead time and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors, while duty cycle limits of 50%, 75%, or 100% can be set using the DCL pin. Protection features include cycle-by-cycle current limiting, hiccup mode for overcurrent recovery, external fault protection input, pulse skipping for high-frequency operation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C (typical). Current sensing uses the CS_ILIM pin with a 1.05V threshold, and slope compensation is configurable via the RSC pin. The controllers use transconductance error amplifiers supporting Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation.

Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating with multiple levels, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster than previous architectures), and 10x faster entry into low-power sleep states. The architecture enables neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors API, supporting technologies like RTX Neural Materials (offering 3x memory savings), Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 compression), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI for facial rendering). The lecture derives Thomson scattering for coherent (collective) scattering when the scattering wavelength exceeds the Debye length, sampling collective plasma motion. The relevant modes are ion acoustic waves (ω ∝ k√(ZTe + Ti)/mi) and electron plasma waves (ω² = ωp² + 3Te k²). The derivation uses the Klimontovich distribution to calculate scattered power in terms of density fluctuations, employs a test particle treatment to determine plasma response, and produces the spectral density function s(k,ω). This function contains electron and ion contributions corresponding to scattering from these waves, with peaks occurring where ε(k,ω) = 0 (the normal modes). The susceptibility calculation uses the Vlasov equation and Landau contour integration. For a Maxwellian distribution, the susceptibility yields the plasma dispersion function (w function), which appears frequently in plasma physics calculations.

Massachusetts General Hospital’s (MGH) Pre‑Admission Testing Area (PATA) is an outpatient clinic that performs pre‑operative anesthesia assessments for about 43 % of surgical patients. PATA has suffered from long patient wait times (average ≥ 2½ hours; only ~1.5 hours of actual face‑to‑face care), frequent staff overtime (often until 6–8 p.m.) and limited capacity (only ~65 % of out‑patients seen on‑site). In June 2009 a patient complaint letter highlighted these inefficiencies and prompted Dr. Jeanine Wiener‑Kronish, chief of anesthesia, to address the problems. In 2008 she had formed a PATA Task Force (including senior administrators, nursing and OR directors) and in May 2009 added an MBA intern who conducted a time‑study and workflow mapping. The data confirmed that patients spent more time waiting than with providers and revealed high variability in provider tasks. The clinic runs 7 a.m.–5 p.m., with about 55 patients per day, staffed by five lab technicians, five RNs and eight anesthesiologists, and follows a sequential process: check‑in, vitals/EKG, nursing assessment, physician assessment, blood draw and check‑out. Prior attempts to add a second site or embed PATA improvements in larger peri‑operative projects were rejected. At the June task‑force meeting, members suggested extending clinic hours, adding resources, reducing patient volume or redesigning the process without new resources; the intern offered to model these options using the collected data before a decision is made.

A 4-year naturalistic follow-up study of the ePOD-methylphenidate RCT examined long-term effects of stimulant medication on brain development in individuals with ADHD. Of the original 50 children (aged 10-12) and 49 adults (aged 23-30), 33 children and 25 adults returned for follow-up. Using pharmacological MRI, researchers assessed cerebral blood flow (CBF) response to an acute methylphenidate challenge as a measure of dopamine-reactivity. The study found no evidence for long-term age-dependent effects of stimulant treatment on resting CBF or dopamine-reactivity over time, contradicting their initial short-term RCT findings. However, age-dependent associations were observed: adults with higher thalamic resting rCBF received less stimulant medication, while adolescents with lower mPFC dopamine-reactivity received more medication. Whole-brain CBF-response was associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution but not dopamine receptor/transporter distributions. The findings suggest that previously identified short-term effects may be transient, and mPFC dopamine-reactivity may have predictive value for stimulant treatment patterns in adolescents.

Proto-Indo‑European (PIE), spoken roughly 4500–2500 BC on the steppes north of the Caspian Sea, was the common ancestor of more than 440 modern languages—including English, French, Spanish, German, Punjabi, Persian, Russian and Ukrainian. Because no written records exist, linguists have struggled to reconstruct its sounds. Linguistics researcher Martin O’Leary posted Twitter charts showing how seemingly unrelated English words share PIE roots. For example, the PIE term *teks* (“to weave”) gave rise to German *dachs* (“badger”) + *hund* → “dachshund”, and to Greek *tekton* (“craftsman”) + *arki* (“chief”) → “architect”. The ancient root *bhel* (“to shine”) produced “blue”, “phlegm” and “flamingo”, while *sek* gave both “science” (via Latin *scire*) and a vulgar term (via Proto‑Germanic *skit*). Other cognate pairs include “bumpkin/husband”, “souffle/bladder”, and “doom/orifice/chauffeur” derived from *dhe* (“to put”). O’Leary’s graphs have been widely shared, accumulating thousands of retweets and enthusiastic comments.

The ADS7828 is a 12‑bit ADC that samples the voltage on a selected CHx pin using an internal ~25 pF capacitor; input current depends on conversion rate and the source must charge this capacitor. The device can use its internal 2.5 V reference or an external reference; an external reference is required for full dynamic range when powered from +5 V, and can be as low as 50 mV. The LSB size equals the reference voltage divided by 4096, so lower references increase apparent offset/gain errors and noise; internal noise contributes roughly 0.32 LSB at 2.5 V and up to ~16 LSB at 50 mV, and averaging can reduce noise.

Communication uses the I²C bus in standard (100 kHz), fast (400 kHz), and high‑speed (3.4 MHz) modes. The ADS7828 operates as a slave with open‑drain SDA and SCL lines; the bus protocol defines START, STOP, data‑valid, and acknowledge conditions, with the master generating the clock and START/STOP signals. Data can flow from master to slave or from slave to master. The address byte contains a factory‑preset code (10010) followed by device‑select bits A1‑A0, allowing up to four devices on the same bus; the R/W bit selects read or write.

Operating mode is set by a command byte, with tables defining power‑down and channel selection. In slave receiver mode the device acknowledges each byte; in slave transmitter mode it sends data after the address is received. Converted 12‑bit data are output as two bytes (MSB first). In standard/fast mode a typical read sequence ends with a repeated START for continuous conversions. In high‑speed mode the ADS7828 stretches SCL low after the read‑address byte until conversion completes; to stay in HS mode a repeated START must be used instead of STOP.

The internal reference is off by default; to use it the PD1 bit must be set to ‘1’ and sufficient settling time allowed before a conversion; toggling the reference requires additional settling time.

For optimal performance the ADC needs clean power, 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitors near the device (optionally 1–10 µF), and a clean analog ground separate from digital ground; layout should minimize glitches near the sampling window, and any noise on an external reference directly appears in the digital result.

The passage also notes standard product lifecycle information, prototype status, RoHS and MSL ratings, mechanical dimension guidelines, and a disclaimer.

Interfacial mobility is a key parameter controlling material microstructural evolution, but connecting atomistic simulations to continuum models remains challenging. Mobility is typically extracted from molecular dynamics using either the capillary fluctuation method or linear response regime. Both methods assume Markovian, memory-free dynamics, but memory effects persist due to hierarchical relaxation processes. These effects manifest as sub-diffusion at short to intermediate times. To address this, generalized approaches from biochemistry were adapted to extract memory kernels and extrapolate to long-time behavior. A simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model was developed to study interface migration in the presence of interacting solute, demonstrating inconsistencies with conventional methods and presenting an alternative mobility extraction approach based on a time convolutionless propagator.

Newton D. Baker’s memorandum to Walter Lippmann outlines the Inquiry’s organization and analyzes the probable course of the war. It notes that European allies refrain from public replies because domestic political situations are too tense, and that peace terms are regarded as secondary to the objective of defeating the German army.

The preprint describes an agent‑based, high‑resolution analysis of the first COVID‑19 wave in the Netherlands (Feb 27 – Jun 1 2020). The model stratifies the 17 million Dutch residents into 11 demographic groups across 380 municipalities and reconstructs hourly movements using anonymized mobile‑phone data and survey‑based mixing matrices. Transmission follows a stochastic SEIR framework, with four time‑varying transmission parameters (β1–β4) calibrated to observed hospital admissions.

The study evaluates three non‑pharmaceutical interventions implemented in four phases: (i) mobility reductions (‑31.7 % to ‑42.4 % inter‑municipality travel), (ii) behavioral changes (social distancing, mask use, hygiene), and (iii) school closure (Mar 16–May 10). Simulations show that mobility restrictions contributed most to epidemic control; without them cumulative hospital admissions would roughly double. Behavioral changes had a substantial but smaller effect, whereas school closures had little impact because they were introduced relatively late.

The authors also explore subnational implementation of interventions at the municipality level, triggered when the local prevalence of infectious cases exceeds a threshold (3 %, 1 %, 0.33 % or 0.1 % of the population). Higher thresholds reduce the number of municipalities under lockdown but increase cumulative hospital admissions (e.g., a 3 % threshold yields ~19 000 admissions, 157 % above the observed national lockdown). Lower thresholds approximate national‑level outcomes with modest additional admissions (≈410 at 0.33 % threshold) and provide large societal benefits (≈36 million additional person‑days free from interventions; about 6 % of municipalities never required a lockdown). A 0.1 % threshold yields only a few extra admissions while 18 municipalities remain intervention‑free for over five weeks.

The study concludes that subnational interventions, combined with real‑time infection monitoring (e.g., sewage surveillance, mass testing), could substantially lower societal burden while maintaining comparable epidemiological control, especially in larger or more heterogeneous countries. Limitations include the absence of household‑level detail, use of 2018 mobility data, and assumptions about daily mobility randomness. The analysis framework, data and code are publicly available.

The paper introduces the LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method to distinguish large reasoning models (LRMs) by their reasoning patterns. LOT uses an LLM to propose distinguishing features from paired reasoning traces of two LRMs, annotates these features across traces, and trains a logistic classifier to predict the source model, iteratively refining the feature set. Applied to 12 open-source LRMs across five reasoning datasets (GPQA-Diamond, MATH-500, AIME, CRUXEVAL, LiveCodeBench), LOT achieves 80–100% classification accuracy, outperforming few-shot prompting, VML, and human-defined taxonomies. The method identifies systematic reasoning differences: smaller models exhibit circular reasoning, while code-specialized models sometimes use Python to solve math problems. A case study on Qwen3 models shows reasoning style differences correlate with performance gaps, and test-time intervention on reasoning traces improves accuracy by 3.3–5.7% on GPQA. Contributions include the LOT method, high classification accuracy, human-readable explanations of reasoning differences, and demonstration of a causal link between reasoning behaviors and model performance.

The lecture discusses policy with behavioral agents, focusing on paternalism. Paternalism involves government intervention to help people make better choices for themselves, distinct from addressing externalities. Internalities—where consumers fail to internalize effects on their future selves—justify intervention, unlike standard economic market failures. Hard paternalism forces choices through mandates or price changes, while soft or libertarian paternalism (e.g., nudges) preserves freedom of choice. Arguments against paternalism include government knowledge limitations, potential for corruption, and infringement on freedom. Arguments in favor highlight people's tendency to make mistakes and the low cost of soft paternalism. Examples include Social Security, cigarette taxes, and the Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) plan, which uses defaults and loss aversion to increase retirement savings without restricting choice. Market solutions may fail because firms exploit naive consumers, and nudges can be used negatively (sludges). Soft paternalism can improve welfare but must respect preferences and avoid harming others. The class emphasizes psychological considerations in economic decisions and the importance of behavioral insights in policy and design.

A recent study funded by Boeing and conducted by researchers from Emory University and Georgia Tech examined germ transmission on commercial flights. During ten observed flights, only one cough was recorded and no cold or flu viruses were detected. Mathematical modeling based on passenger movement indicated that a hypothetical infectious aisle passenger in row 14 would, on average, infect only one of roughly 150 travelers. About 38 % of passengers never left their seat; 80 % of aisle‑seat occupants moved at least once versus 62 % of middle‑seat and 43 % of window‑seat occupants. The eleven people sitting adjacent to an infected passenger—two on each side and those directly in front and behind—faced the highest risk. Researchers recommend staying in a window seat to reduce exposure, though outside scientists caution that the small sample limits broader conclusions.

S-O-S Pressure Defense is presented as an innovative defensive approach designed to counter increasingly powerful modern offense. The system emphasizes six core elements: (1) logical progression of fundamental one‑on‑one skills to full‑team pressure, reinforced daily; (2) consistent use of S‑O‑S action words (SET, ON, SMOTHER for on‑ball; SNUGGLE, OFF, STRIKE for off‑ball) to trigger and communicate defensive moves; (3) “Operation Checkpoint” directing opponents to low‑percentage areas beyond 18 feet; (4) aggressive two‑on‑two switching to neutralize screens; (5) immediate backcourt pressure to stop fast‑break outlet passes and funnel ballhandlers to checkpoints; and (6) assigning each defender a specific role so the five players function like clockwork. The program aims to act as an equalizer, enabling less talented teams to compete, adding edge to equal teams, and providing a decisive advantage for strong scorers on off‑shooting nights.

New research co‑authored by University of Calgary professor Darla Zelenitsky and Florida State University professor Gregory Erickson determines dinosaur egg incubation durations. By counting daily growth lines in thin sections of embryo teeth from a Protoceratops (Mongolia) and a Hypacrosaurus (Alberta), they found incubation lasted nearly three months for the 194‑gram Protoceratops and six months for the >4 kg Hypacrosaurus. These periods match primitive reptile incubation and exceed typical bird egg periods, indicating dinosaurs were not bird‑like in this trait. Longer incubation exposed eggs and parents to prolonged predation and risk, slowing reproduction and putting non‑avian dinosaurs at a disadvantage at end of Cretaceous. Hypacrosaurus specimens came from Devil’s Coulee nesting site. Future embryo studies on other dinosaur species are planned.

The disclosure describes an enhanced overlay network-based transport mechanism for IPsec traffic, such as traffic from customer branch office locations. The method involves using DNS-based ingress edge region selection, where customer routers perform initial hostname lookups to resolve a service hostname to an IKEv2 destination of an outer IPsec tunnel associated with an overlay network edge. Upon tunnel establishment, the overlay network edge performs a secondary DNS lookup to determine whether it is an appropriate ingress region. If not, the edge sends an IKEv2 redirect message to redirect the router to a more optimal edge region. Additionally, the edge performs periodic lookups to determine continued appropriateness and may drop liveness probes from routers to trigger reconnection to a different edge region. The technique leverages existing CDN infrastructure and provides improved reliability for Internet-based WAN connections.

Professor discusses solving inviscid Burgers' equation from a delta‑function source. The solution is a fan followed by a shock: the fan gives u = x/t, and mass conservation yields the shock position X = √(2t). The shock speed s = dX/dt satisfies the jump condition (u_left + u_right)/2 and meets the entropy condition u_left > s > u_right. He then shows how adding a viscosity term to Burgers' equation permits a nonlinear change of variables that turns it into the linear heat equation; solving the heat equation and letting viscosity tend to zero recovers the inviscid solution. This leads to an explicit minimisation formula valid for any initial data.

The lecture briefly introduces the Korteweg‑de Vries (KdV) equation, which arises in one‑way shallow‑water waves, its integrability, and the notion of solitons—traveling waves whose shapes survive interaction. KdV and the nonlinear Schrödinger equation are cited as examples of completely integrable nonlinear PDEs.

The professor also mentions the Navier–Stokes equations, the Clay millennium prize for proving global regularity, and recent numerical experiments indicating that a previously conjectured blow‑up example does not occur. He signals the next topics: finite‑difference methods for these PDEs, the level‑set method, a guest lecture on PDEs in finance, and the later part of the course on solving large linear systems.
